# Cinders of Chaos server scripts (TFS 1.4.2, the base server style)

Server side for the client modules in `client/overlay/modules/`. One revscript per module,
each registering a `login` CreatureEvent plus an `extendedopcode` CreatureEvent (same pattern as
`scripts/customs/stats_inspect/inspect.lua` in base server).

**What has run on a server (2026-10-14).** Most systems were tested in game on a local test server: the TFS 1.4.2
fork with the engine patches, MySQL with the `sql/` tables, the Linux client. ROADMAP.md says per item whether it was
"tested in game". An integrated live test (server, two clients, website) passed on 2026-10-14; its fixes are in
`0ff264b2` and `6f4c0435`. Nothing has run on a production host or with the Windows client. What never ran live
(pack combat, the four deep dungeons, many systems checked only against the mocked engine, the hosting tools) is listed
in docs/BETA_READINESS.md "Never run on a real server or real client"; treat their engine calls as unverified.
Every `.lua` parses in Lua 5.3 and LuaJIT, and the `*_core.lua` logic is unit tested against a mocked engine API
(`tests/`).

```
    item_tooltip.lua  item_tooltip_core.lua (rich item tooltips with the equipped-item compare, client game_itemtooltip)
    weapon_dps_core.lua  (the tooltip's "Estimated DPS", see "Estimated DPS")
    weapon_skill_core.lua  weapon_skill_config.lua (wand and rod hits scale with the magic level; see "Weapon damage scales
                                      with skills")
    charges_look.lua  charges_look_core.lua ("It has N charges left." in the Look text, see "Item charges")
    shop.lua  shop_config.lua  shop_services.lua  autosell.lua  sell_prices.lua (store, see "Store services")
    bounty.lua  bounty_core.lua  bounty_config.lua  bounty_pool.lua (bounty board; pool from tools/gen_bounty_pool.py)
    rift.lua  rift_core.lua  rift_config.lua  rift_layout_core.lua (rifts: keys, a generated map per run built by a
                                      slot pool, run HUD; see "Rifts")
    crafting.lua (crafting bench and orbs; rules in data/lib/chaos_crafting.lua, installer tools/install_crafting.py)
    salvage.lua  salvage_core.lua  salvage_config.lua (salvage into rune shards, the item lock; installer tools/install_salvage.py)
    potions.lua  potions_core.lua  potions_config.lua  (no empty flasks, the Everfull potions that never empty;
                                      potion_flasks.lua is a retired stub; helpers in
                                      data/lib/chaos_potions.lua, installer tools/install_potions.py, see "Potions")
    lootline.lua  lootline_core.lua (one loot line per kill: the stock "Loot of", the Chaos bonus and the pouch line
                                      merged, see "One loot line per kill" under the loot filter)
    craft_bonus.lua  craft_bonus_core.lua  craft_bonus_config.lua (the base crafting tables' bonus: rarity of crafted
                                      equipment, extra potions and runes; tools/patch_base_crafting_bonus.py, see "Crafting bonus")
    item_mods.lua (Chaos item modifiers on the character; catalogue and rolls in data/lib/chaos_item_mods.lua, see "Item modifiers")
    treasure_goblin.lua  treasure_goblin_core.lua  treasure_goblin_config.lua (treasure goblins, see "Treasure goblins")
    invasion.lua  invasion_core.lua  invasion_config.lua  worldevents.lua (invasions and the small world events, see "Invasions and world events";
                                      the Wandering Merchant NPC is data/npc/Wandering Merchant.xml + npc/scripts/wandering_merchant.lua)
    leaderboard.lua  leaderboard_core.lua  leaderboard_config.lua (weekly boards with titles, class ladder)
    season.lua  season_core.lua  season_config.lua (seasons; sql/chaos_season.sql, tools/patch_season_events.py)
    hunt.lua  hunt_core.lua  hunt_config.lua  hunt_supplies.lua (hunt tracker; supply prices from tools/gen_supply_prices.py)
    daily_core.lua  daily_config.lua (daily reward login streaks, milestones, grace, login window order)
    patchnotes.lua  patchnotes_core.lua (patch notes window; the notes are data/patchnotes/*.md, see "Patch notes")
    changelog_core.lua (the window's Changelog tab: data/changelog/changelog.json, see "Changelog")
    nameplate.lua  nameplate_core.lua  titles.lua (name plates over players, title registry, the Achievements window; sql/chaos_nameplate.sql)
    guild.lua  guild_hall.lua  guild_core.lua  guild_config.lua (guild levels, perks, guild bank, guild halls; sql/chaos_guild.sql)
    cityportals.lua  cityportals_core.lua  cityportals_config.lua  cityportals_fx.lua (labelled portals near the temples, see "City portals")
    achievements.lua  achievements_core.lua  achievements_data.lua (achievements, points, titles, rewards; sql/chaos_achievements.sql)
    pets.lua  pets_core.lua  pets_config.lua (pets: companions that level from kills, small abilities; sql/chaos_pets.sql)
    buffbar.lua (buff / debuff bar, client game_buffbar; registry and rules in data/lib/chaos_buffs.lua)
    partyframes.lua  partyframes_core.lua (party frames, client game_partyframes; see "Buff bar and party frames")
    partymarkers.lua  partymarkers_core.lua  partymarkers_config.lua (party members on the minimap, client
                                      game_mapmarkers; see "Map markers")
    poi.lua  poi_core.lua  poi_config.lua (points of interest on the minimap: data/chaos_poi.lua from tools/gen_poi.py,
                                      discoveries in sql/chaos_poi.sql; see "Map markers")
    market.lua  market_core.lua  market_config.lua (our player market for gold and Chaos Coins; sql/chaos_market.sql,
                                      tools/patch_market.py, engine patch 0017; see "Market")
    bestiary.lua  bestiary_core.lua  bestiary_config.lua  bestiary_spawns.lua (bestiary, kill tasks, task tracker;
                                      sql/chaos_bestiary.sql; spawn data from tools/gen_bestiary_spawns.py)
    monster_damage.lua  monster_damage_core.lua  monster_damage_config.lua (late-game monster damage boost: physical hits
                                      of high-level monsters on players, see "Percent armour")
  data/monster/monsters/chaos/pets/   the pet monster types (not attackable, no attacks)
```

## Install

1. Copy `server/data/scripts/chaos/` to `<server>/data/scripts/chaos/`.
2. Run `server/sql/chaos.sql` against the game database (`mysql -u USER -p DB < chaos.sql`).
   Foreign keys assume `players.id` is `int(11) NOT NULL` (stock TFS schema).
3. Spells: `python3 -I server/tools/register_spells.py <server>/data` (Chaos spells) and
   `python3 -I server/tools/rename_spells.py <server>/data --sql rename_spells.sql` (Chaos names for the stock
   spells and runes; apply the SQL once). See `data/spells/README.md`. Then
   `python3 -I server/tools/patch_free_spells.py <server>/data`: no spell or rune needs premium ("Free spells").
4. Experience bonuses: `python3 -I server/tools/patch_base_events.py <server>/data` (once; idempotent). The base
   server's `Player:onGainExperience` (`data/events/scripts/player.lua`) never runs the script callbacks, so
   without it every Chaos experience bonus is silently ignored: Blood Moon, the passive tree's experience nodes,
   monster tier experience, and the store's world buffs. The patch adds the dispatch after the stage, stamina
   and potion multipliers (verified on the test server: +2% passive bonus -> exactly 1.02x the experience).
   The same tool makes the base loot callback (`data/scripts/eventcallbacks/monster/default_onDropLoot.lua`) apply
   the waystone character upgrades "Loot" (item drop chances x(1 + level/100)) and "Rarity" (+level % to roll a
   rarity, +level/2 % per tier); `data/scripts/chaos/waystone_bonuses.lua` applies the "Experience" upgrade
   (+1% per level, x2.0 at level 100). Before, all three only stored their level and nothing read it.
   Steps 13 and 14 of the same tool make the base stamina scripts ask the Chaos Pact (`pact_perks.lua`): the offline
   regeneration of `data/creaturescripts/scripts/regeneratestamina.lua` multiplies the offline time by
   `ChaosPactPerks.staminaMult(player)` (x1.5 while the Pact is active), and the stamina trainer tile
   (`data/scripts/customs/actions/trainer_tile_stamina.lua`) waits `ChaosPactPerks.staminaRestMs(player, 120000)` ms per
   stamina minute (80 s). Without `pact_perks.lua` both behave as stock (`tools/pact_stamina_patch_test.py`).
   Steps 16 and 17 ("Time-friendly progression"): the stock loot callback no longer drops nothing at 14 h of stamina or
   less; it asks `ChaosCatchup.staminaLootMult(player)` (x0.5) and multiplies every loot chance by it; the offline
   regeneration also multiplies the offline time by `ChaosCatchup.offlineStaminaMult(player)` (x2, the Pact's x1.5 on
   top). Without `catchup.lua` both behave as stock (`tools/stamina_catchup_patch_test.py`).
   Verified on the test server: Experience 50 -> x1.5; Loot and Rarity 100 over 300 Dragon kills: items
   985 -> 1279, items with a rarity 81 -> 212.
   Its step 12 sends System > Report a Bug of every account to `reports.lua` (`chaos_reports`, reason "bug"; the stock
   callback refused normal accounts): "Bug reports" under "Anti-bot and player reports".
   It also removes the demotion from the base `creaturescripts/scripts/login.lua`: without premium (`freePremium =
   false`) the stock login set every vocation without a promotion back to `vocation:getDemotion()`, so a free account
   lost its ascended class (Berserker, Ninja, ...) at every login. The premium branch is left as it was; the engine
   itself never demotes. Verified on the test server: a Berserker on a free and on a premium account stays Berserker
   (before: Warrior after the login, saved so in `players.vocation`).
   The loot callback's two "Loot of ..." lines name the monster through `Chaos.monsterNameDescription`, so a renamed
   monster (a rift monster, an invader) shows the name it wears ("Loot of an abyssal gazer"; see "Rift names").
   And the base `scripts/creaturescripts/autoloot.lua` hands each item to `ChaosLoot.finalizeRarity` before moving it,
   so autolooted gear gets its rarity stats (the engine only rolls items still in the corpse; see "Rarity stats are
   rolled once").
   And the base rarity element script (`scripts/customs/rarity/rarity_onCombat_elementdamage.lua`) no longer deals 0 damage
   with two different rarity elements: each element gets its own share, see `data/scripts/chaos/rarity_elements.lua`.
4a. Item links: `python3 -I server/tools/patch_help_itemlinks.py <server>/data` (once; idempotent; `install_all.py` runs it with
   the events step) keeps item links out of the Help channel (see "Item links in chat").
   `python3 -I server/tools/patch_help_ai.py <server>/data` (same step, idempotent) adds the hook of the Help channel
   assistant to `chatchannels/scripts/help.lua` (see "Help channel assistant").
4b. Stock promotion off, the ascension quest's base parts: `python3 -I server/tools/install_class_ascension.py <server>/data
   [--dry-run]` (idempotent; `install_all.py` runs it as a class hook). It copies the Ascendant Oracle
   (`server/data/npc/Ascendant Oracle.xml`, `npc/scripts/ascendant_oracle.lua`) into `<server>/data/npc/` and runs
   `server/tools/patch_promotion.py <server>/data`, which makes every stock promotion path refuse: `StdModule.promotePlayer`
   in `npc/lib/npcsystem/modules.lua` (King Ormund, Queen Isadora, the emperors, Pellen, The Forgotten King, ...) says a
   short line pointing to the Ascendant Oracle and changes nothing; every NPC script that promotes answers "promotion" with
   that line first (a keyword added right after `NpcSystem.parseParameters`), direct `setVocation(<promotion|demotion>)`
   calls in NPC scripts (the "Promo Bug" NPC) are commented out, and the premium branch of the stock
   `creaturescripts/scripts/login.lua` (promotion storage 30018 -> `setVocation(promotion)`) no longer promotes. The tool
   then lists any other promotion in the data folder for a manual check: none in this base server (no talkaction, action
   or store offer promotes; the Oracle of the starting island only sets the first vocation). Verified on the test server:
   King Ormund answers "promotion" with the pointer and "yes" does nothing; a premium Warrior with storage 30018 = 1 stays
   a Warrior at login. The guardian monsters (`data/monster/monsters/chaos/ascension/`) come with step 5 / the monsters
   step. See "Ascension quest".
4c. Base NPC dialogues: `python3 -I server/tools/patch_base_npcs.py <server>/data [--dry-run]` (idempotent; `install_all.py`
   runs it with the events step). The base NPC scripts were written for a newer NPC library than the one shipped: replies
   given as a list of lines (every "twist of fate" priest such as Dorrik, Yorvane, Ulette, A Bearded Woman, the greetings
   of Ald Weyr and Bamir: 50 replies in 20 scripts) stopped with `npchandler.lua: bad argument #1 to 'gsub' (string
   expected, got table)`, the blessing priests charged the string `'|BLESSCOST|'` / `'|PVPBLESSCOST|'` ("attempt to compare
   string with number" on "yes") and `|TIME|` was printed as it is. The tool patches `npc/lib` (exact match on the stock
   lines): lists of lines are said line by line, the tags are filled (blessing 2000 gold up to level 30, then 200 per
   level above 20, at most 20000; the twist of fate at most 50000), a node without text says nothing instead of failing
   (Sevias's dead rats), the delayed lines of a long reply stop when the player logs out. An NPC whose `script="..."` names its
   file in another letter case (the base `Addoner.xml` asks for `addoner.lua`, the file is `Addoner.lua`: fine on Windows,
   "Can not load script" twice at every Linux start) gets the file's real name (`tools/patch_base_npcs_test.py`). `tools/rename_spells.py` writes
   an NPC `spellName` with an apostrophe escaped (it broke Casnath, Whiskerton, Valon, Jashelm, Korbek and Ixesseth, which did
   not load) and repairs the lines an older run wrote. Tested by `tests/npc_lib_test.lua`; verified on the test server
   (Dorrik answers "twist of fate" in four lines, "yes" charges the level's cost and gives the blessing).
4d. Base crafting script: `python3 -I server/tools/patch_base_crafting.py <server>/data [--dry-run]` (idempotent;
   `install_all.py` step `basecrafting`, after `events`). Closes the duplication hole of the base crafting tables; see
   "Base crafting script".
4e. Crafting Table window: `python3 -I server/tools/patch_base_crafting_ui.py <server>/data [--dry-run]` (idempotent;
   `install_all.py` step `basecraftingui`, right after `basecrafting`, whose patch it needs). The base crafting script
   talks to the client's Crafting Table window; see "Crafting Table window".
4f. Crafting bonus: `python3 -I server/tools/patch_base_crafting_bonus.py <server>/data [--dry-run]` (idempotent;
   `install_all.py` step `basecraftingbonus`, right after `basecraftingui`, whose patch and the guard's it needs). Crafted
   equipment rolls a Chaos rarity and item level, potions and runes may give extra pieces; see "Crafting bonus".
5. Late game: copy `server/data/monster/monsters/chaos/*.xml` to `<server>/data/monster/monsters/chaos/` (17 of them
   are tuned for levels 650-1000), then `python3 -I server/tools/late_game.py <server>/data` (idempotent; `--dry-run`
   shows what would change, `--remove` undoes it). It writes the new `experienceStages` into `config.lua` and puts the
   level-scaled monsters of `server/tools/late_game_spawns.csv` into the loaded map's spawn file. See "Late game".
5b. Classes: `python3 -I server/tools/add_vocations.py <server>/data [--dry-run]` (idempotent). It writes the classes of
   `data/XML/chaos_vocations.xml` into `data/XML/vocations.xml` between marker comments (Warrior 4 / Juggernaut 8 / Berserker 14,
   Ranger 3 / Deadeye 7 / Beastmaster 15, Mystic 1 / Elementalist 5 / Illusionist 10, Thief 11 / Ninja 12 / Samurai 13; the base
   entries with those ids are replaced, 2, 6 and 9 removed), converts the stock vocation lists of `spells.xml`, `weapons.xml` and
   `movements.xml` to the classes once (Berserker: two-handed weapons, no shields; Beastmaster: bows and arrows), adds the Berserker /
   Beastmaster to the knight / paladin potions of `actions/scripts/other/potions.lua` and to `Player.isKnight/isPaladin`, and lets the
   Thief line use one-handed swords, throwing weapons and whatever the Ranger may wear. Run it **together with** the scripts of this
   folder: `class_migration.lua` moves the characters of the retired ids 2, 6 and 9 at the next start, before anyone logs in (a
   character still on a retired id cannot log in). See docs/CLASSES.md, "Phase 2a". For the Ninja's dual wield and the line's attack speed with weapons that have their own speed, build the engine
   with `src-patches/0002-dual-wield-and-vocation-attack-speed.patch` (without it the off-hand sword cannot be equipped; everything
   else works). Ascension: the quest of the Ascendant Oracle (see "Ascension quest"; staff and the free switch use Character > Services) at level 100 (Warrior: juggernaut|berserker, Ranger:
   deadeye|beastmaster, Mystic: elementalist|illusionist, Thief: ninja|samurai; final, the store's Vocation Change is the only way
   back, except the one free switch of migrated Elite Knights / Royal Paladins). See docs/CLASSES.md.
   The same run installs the Monk (17-19), Necromancer (20-22) and Templar (23-25) lines from `data/XML/chaos_vocations_*.xml`
   and opens the equipment to them: every sword, axe and club (one- or two-handed) is open to the Warrior, Thief, Monk and Templar
   lines ("One melee skill"; the Berserker two-handed only), the Monk line also wears what the Ranger may wear, the Templar line
   what the Warrior may wear (shields too), the Necromancer line every wand and rod, what the
   casters may wear and the Mystic's stock healing and support instants (no rune conjuring, no stock summon); the potions follow
   (Monk: the Royal Paladin's, Templar: the Elite Knight's and the Royal Paladin's, Necromancer: the Elementalist's).
   The Thief, Monk and Templar lines also get the stock utility spells of the other classes (`LINE_STOCK_SPELLS`: light, great
   light, haste, find person, levitate, magic rope, strong haste for the Thief and Monk
   lines; the cure spells are retired, see "Spell progression audit (C6)"); `client/tools/gen_spell_data.py`
   writes the same table into the client's spelldata.lua. Test: `tests/stock_spells_patch_test.lua`.
   Then `python3 -I server/tools/patch_base_classes.py <server>/data [--dry-run]` (idempotent; `install_all.py` runs it in the
   vocations step): the base server's own vocation checks (NPCs, quests, familiars, exercise weapons, ...) learn the classes.
   See "Base scripts and the classes".
5c. Classes five to seven: their spells come with step 3 (`spells_chaos.xml`), their scripts with step 1. The Necromancer's minions
   are monsters: copy `data/monster/monsters/chaos/necro_*.xml` with the other Chaos monsters (step 5) and register them with
   `python3 -I server/tools/register_monsters.py <server>/data/monster/monsters.xml <server>/data/monster/monsters/chaos`.
   The class lock: run `server/sql/chaos_class_unlocks.sql` (the server also creates the table at startup). The three classes
   need an account-wide unlock, free once a character of the account reaches level 200 (not sold: the store's "Classes" category was removed on 2026-10-15, owner rule "follow your recommendations"; level 500 -> 200 the same day, "Time-friendly progression"); see "Class lock".
5d. Dark tile set: `python3 -I server/tools/install_dark_tiles.py <server>/data [--dry-run]` (idempotent; `install_all.py` step
   `darktiles`) adds the 74 items of `data/items/dark_tiles.csv` to `items.otb` / `items.xml`. The client needs the matching
   `Tibia.dat` / `Tibia.spr` (`client/tools/sprites/gen_dark_tiles.py`). See "Dark tile set".
5e. Gems: `python3 -I server/tools/install_gems.py <server>/data [--dry-run]` (idempotent; `install_all.py` step `gems`)
   adds the 35 gems (32001-32035) to `items.otb` / `items.xml`, names the Orb of Sockets (24692) and gives it its own orb
   look (client 38641, pair 38). The client needs the multi-use flag on the small diamond:
   `client/tools/sprites/set_multiuse.py`. See "Gems and sockets".
5f. Auras: `python3 -I server/tools/install_auras.py <server>/data [--dry-run]` (idempotent; `install_all.py` step `auras`)
   adds the 19 Chaos auras of `data/XML/chaos_auras.csv` (ids 6..24) to `auras.xml`; the store sells them (category Auras).
   It also adds the four faction auras of `data/XML/chaos_auras_donor.csv` (ids 25..28, looks 2136..2139 of things_custom14;
   quartermaster rewards in `factions_config.lua`, never sold).
   The client needs the pair from `client/tools/sprites/import_vfx.py`. See `data/spells/README_FX.md` "Animated pack effects".
5g. Crafting orbs v2: `python3 -I server/tools/install_orbs.py <server>/data [--dry-run]` (idempotent; `install_all.py` step
   `orbs`, after `crafting`) adds the six new orbs (32251..32256) to `items.otb` / `items.xml`, gives the base server's
   currency items their new names (`items.xml` and every loot list or shop that names them) and needs no client change.
   See "Crafting orbs v2" and "Legendary powers".
5h. Professions: `python3 -I server/tools/install_professions.py <server>/data [--dry-run]` (idempotent; `install_all.py` step
   `professions`, after `charms`): the 20 materials and 10 gathering nodes (32351..32380) in `items.otb` / `items.xml`, the
   Material Broker in `data/npc`, one hooked line in the stock pick, sickle, skinning and fishing scripts; then
   `sql/chaos_professions.sql` (also created at startup). See "Professions".
5i. The Gambler: `python3 -I server/tools/install_gamble.py <server>/data [--dry-run]` (idempotent; `install_all.py` step
   `gamble`, after `professions`) copies the Gambler NPC (`data/npc/Mordecai Ashwager.xml` and its script) into `data/npc`;
   `gamble.lua` places him next to the main temple at startup. No items, no tables, no client change outside `game_gamble`.
   See "The Gambler".
5i2. Candlemarks: `python3 -I server/tools/install_candlemarks.py <server>/data [--dry-run]` (idempotent; `install_all.py`
   step `candlemarks`, right after `gamble`) copies Osric the Chandler (`data/npc/Osric the Chandler.xml` and its script)
   into `data/npc`; `candlemarks.lua` places him for towns 1-5 at startup (town 2: his stall in the hub; else next to the temple). Tables:
   `sql/chaos_candlemarks.sql` (the sql step; also created at startup). See "Candlemarks".
5i3. Idle kick: `python3 -I server/tools/patch_base_idle_kick.py <server> [--minutes N] [--dry-run]` (idempotent;
   `install_all.py` step `idlekick`, after `candlemarks`) sets `config.lua` `kickIdlePlayerAfterMinutes` to 1440 so idle
   characters stay online and earn Candlemarks (the stock 15 kicks them after 16 minutes). See "Candlemarks".
5i3b. Cast port: `python3 -I server/tools/patch_cast_port.py <server> [--port N] [--dry-run]` (idempotent; `install_all.py`
   step `castport`, after `idlekick`) sets `config.lua` `castPort` to 7179 (127.0.0.1 only; needs src-patch 0064 and a
   restart). Without it the port stays off. See "Live spectator", phase 2.
5i2b. Service NPCs: `python3 -I server/tools/install_service_npcs.py <server>/data [--dry-run]` (idempotent; `install_all.py`
   step `servicenpcs`, after `castport`) copies the five NPCs of `service_npcs_config.lua` (`data/npc/<name>.xml`, their
   scripts and the shared `scripts/chaos_service_npc.lua`) into `data/npc`; `service_npcs.lua` places them at startup. No
   items, no tables, no opcode. See "Service NPCs".
5j. Infinite arrows and quivers: `python3 -I server/tools/patch_base_archery.py <server>/data [--dry-run]` (idempotent;
   `install_all.py` step `archery`, after `vocations` and `spells`) gives bows and crossbows the attack, hit chance and
   missile of their ammunition, makes the quivers off-hand equipment (items.xml, items.otb, movements.xml; needs engine
   src-patch 0023), maps the base's slot tables to the second ring slot (moot since src-patch 0058: slot 10 takes
   nothing), marks the might rings (items.xml `chaosMightRing`: one at a time, "Second ring slot"), keeps both rings of a ring slot swap in the base rarity
   script and clears there a hand the base two-handed swap emptied ("Right-click equips"), keeps a quiver in the base's two-handed swap and takes arrows and bolts out of loot, shops, conjure spells and rewards; then run `server/sql/chaos_archery.sql` once, with the server stopped
   (the `sql` step does), before the first start with the patched items.otb. See "Infinite arrows and quivers".
5j2. Unique equip rules: `python3 -I server/tools/install_unique_equip.py <server>/data [--dry-run]` (idempotent;
   `install_all.py` step `uniqueequip`, after `archery`) gives the uniques with `equipLevel` / `equipLines` in
   `chaos_items.xml` their own rule: movements.xml entries of their base items and
   `data/movements/scripts/chaos_unique_equip.lua`. See "Unique equip rules".
5k. Base item names: `python3 -I server/tools/patch_base_item_names.py <server>/data [--dry-run]` (idempotent;
   `install_all.py` step `itemnames`, after `archery`) gives the base items of `data/items/base_item_names.csv` their
   Chaos names by id and moves the monster loot that named them to their ids. See "Base item names".
5k2. Base monster names: `python3 -I server/tools/patch_base_monster_names.py <server>/data [--dry-run]` (idempotent;
   `install_all.py` step `monsternames`, right after `lib`, before `lategame` and `spawns`) gives the base monsters of
   `data/monster/base_monster_names.csv` (keyed by the sha256 of the old name) their Chaos names everywhere the base data
   names them. See "Base monster names".
5l. Town names: `python3 -I server/tools/patch_base_towns.py <server>/data [--dry-run]` (idempotent; `install_all.py`
   step `towns`, after `itemnames`) renames the map's towns by id from `tools/base_towns.csv` in the `.otbm` itself
   (`<map>.otbm.bak` keeps the original). See "Town names".
5l2. The rest of the base world: `python3 -I server/tools/patch_base_npc_names.py <server>/data`, then
   `patch_base_texts.py <server>/data`, then `patch_base_houses.py <server>/data` (each idempotent, each with
   `--dry-run`; `install_all.py` steps `npcnames`, `worldtexts` and `houses`, right after `towns`): the NPCs, every text
   that names the old world (dialogue, travel, quest log, raids, achievements, books and signs of the map) and the house
   names. See "Base NPC names", "Base world texts" and "Base houses".
5l3. The base server's own name: `python3 -I server/tools/patch_base_server_name.py <server>/data [--dry-run]`
   (idempotent; `install_all.py` step `servername`, after `worldtexts`): the welcome text over the first temple and a
   console banner, and `serverName` in `config.lua` while it is still the base value. The status protocol's name is
   engine patch 0030. See "Server name".
5m. Spawns: `python3 -I server/tools/patch_base_spawns.py <server>/data [--dry-run] [--remove] [--report]` (idempotent;
   `install_all.py` step `spawns`, after `monsters`) fixes the dead monster registrations, the glitched spawntimes and the
   spawns on blocking tiles, shortens the 300-600 band's respawn and adds spawns in thin areas, all from
   `tools/spawn_tuning.json`. Engine patch 0022 is needed for the dynamic respawn. See "Spawn density and respawn".
   Then `python3 -I server/tools/patch_spawn_fields.py <server>/data [--dry-run]` (idempotent; step `spawnfields`)
   puts the small fire without damage under nine spawn entries in fire lairs. See "Spawns on fire fields".
6. Restart the server (or `/reload scripts`). Check the console for Lua errors.
7. Player commands: `python3 -I server/tools/install_commands.py <server>/data` takes the base server's spoken player
   commands out (talkactions.xml lines with "!" words, the "!" words of base revscripts, the "!commands" login lines);
   every one of them is in the client menu (see "Player commands: the menu"). It also covers the stock `!autoloot`
   and makes the base `/pos` staff only.
7a. Autosave: `python3 -I server/tools/patch_base_save.py <server>/data [--dry-run]` (idempotent; `install_all.py` step
   `autosave`, after `commands`) switches the base hourly autosave to `Game.saveIncremental` and keeps the game state;
   the logout writes the outfit columns and the skill history row only on a change. Needs engine patch 0026 for the
   steps (without it the stock full save runs). See "Autosave in steps".
7b. Base scripts that stalled the game loop: `python3 -I server/tools/patch_base_stalls.py <server>/data [--dry-run]`
   (idempotent; `install_all.py` step `stalls`, after `autosave`): the expedition announcements look at the players
   online instead of every tile of an island, the upgrade-slot check keeps its parse per item description and runs
   once a second per player (at once on an equip move) instead of every 100 ms, and adds and removes each slot bonus
   under one condition id, forgetting the bonus of an emptied slot. See "Game loop stalls". The base extended opcode
   script reads and pushes the ancestral points at most once every 2 s per player instead of for every request a
   client sends (see "Stress test").
7c. Base lever and step-in boss rooms: `python3 -I server/tools/patch_base_bossrooms.py <server>/data [--dry-run]`
   (idempotent; `install_all.py` step `bossrooms`, after `stalls`): the lever (or entry tile) is locked while a group is
   inside, a time limit with warnings, the exit and the clean-up. See "Instance limits".
7c2. Soul pit and tower defence: `python3 -I server/tools/patch_base_eventrooms.py <server>/data [--dry-run]`
   (idempotent; `install_all.py` step `eventrooms`, after `bossrooms`): both run as boss rooms (lock, time limit,
   warnings, exit, clean-up of the waves and of the script's own state). See "Instance limits", "Soul pit and tower
   defence".
7d. Base dungeon entry: `python3 -I server/tools/patch_base_dungeon.py <server>/data [--dry-run]` (idempotent;
   `install_all.py` step `dungeonentry`, after `bossrooms`): the step-in tile of the base modal dungeon entry opens the
   Chaos dungeon window instead, so every dungeon run goes through the queue. See "Instance limits", "Base modal
   dungeon entry".
8. Client: apply the client-side gaps listed below, otherwise bank, autoloot, daily and stash
   cannot talk to the server at all.
9. Client pair guard: `config.lua` records the sprite pair the shipped client is on (`chaosClientPair = 54`). Items of a
   newer pair (the pickups of pair 55, the fist weapon looks and the weapons above level 800 of pair 56) are installed only
   once the record is that number or more; before, `install_all.py` skips those rows and prints a warning. The owner raises
   the record when a client update ships: see "Client pair guard" (admin app first, then `chaos-ctl.sh client-pair set N`).

`data/scripts/chaos/admin/` and `sql/chaos_admin.sql` are the in-game admin panel (client `game_admin`, extended opcode
120, which does not collide with any opcode below); its own README (`admin/README.md`) has the files, the permission
model and every action. Besides the base server tools it has seven Chaos categories (Currencies, Progression, Classes,
Buffs & Gear, Bosses & Events, Instances & PvP, Guilds & Market: 93 actions over the Chaos systems' own APIs) and the
staff chat commands as Tools actions (the talkaction files unchanged). Group 4 inspects and fixes, value needs group 5,
resets of progress are dangerous (group 6); every run is in `chaos_admin_log`. Tests: `tests/admin_panel_test.lua`,
`tests/admin_probe_test.lua`, `tests/staff_permissions_test.lua`.

Every script starts with `if not Chaos then dofile("data/scripts/chaos/chaos_constants.lua") end`,
so load order inside `data/scripts` does not matter (the `dofile` path is relative to the server's
working directory, as with the rest of the base server libs).

### Extended opcodes in use

Every Chaos extended opcode is a key of the global `ChaosOpcodes` table in `chaos_constants.lua` (most in the table
itself, the newer ones as `ChaosOpcodes.<key> = n` below it), except the admin panel's 120, which is
`CHAOS_ADMIN_OPCODE` in `admin/core.lua`. One opcode per module; the payload is JSON `{action, data}` unless the row says
otherwise. This list was rebuilt on 2026-10-11 from `ChaosOpcodes` (loaded with LuaJIT and sorted) and a search of the
client modules for opcode constants and `registerExtended*Opcode`; a new opcode must take a free number (see "Opcode
collision check") and be added here.

### Player summons are allies (owner debug items 84, 86 and 83, 2026-10-18)

**Summons (item 86).** Owner report: "the wolf and the player take each other for enemies: the wolf attacks the owner and the
player keeps it as a target; the only skill the wolf has (the red claw) it uses on the player instead of the monsters".
Every summon is `Game.createMonster` + `setMaster`. The engine's own rule (a summon of a player is an opponent of everyone
but its master) and the base `Creature:onTargetCombat` (a summon never hits its master or the master's party members) were
already there, and the engine source is not in this repo, so the cause could not be reproduced here. What the scripts
left open, now closed (`summons_core.lua`, `summons.lua`, `tests/summons_test.lua`):
- the monster is made before its master is set, so the owner standing next to it is in its target list from then on:
  `ChaosSummonsCore.bind(owner, monster)` (Wild Bond, Moonfang Pack, Mirror Image, the Necromancer's minions, the Cinder
  Effigy, the Reliquary Warden, the pets; `ChaosSpell.bindSummon` in the spells) sets the master and clears its attack and
  follow target;
- a player could take its own summon (or a party member's) as its attack target (a click, the client's auto target) and
  then Feral Command, the companions' bites and area spells went at it (the "red claw" effect `claw_rake` plays on the
  target of Feral Command, next to the owner): `summons.lua` refuses every hit between a player and its allies' summons
  (`EventCallback` onTargetCombat, priority -60) and drops such a target every 0.5 s; `ChaosSpell.canAttack` never takes the
  caster's own or its party's summons (its comment always said so; the code did not); Feral Command picks the nearest enemy
  within 7 sqm when its target is an ally (or says "No enemy in range."); the companion's bite skips an ally target;
- the Moonfang wolves now carry the companion guard too (the owner's area spells do not hurt them).
Client side the Auto Target already skips summons and effigies (base patch 0076); its locked target and attack next
followed in 2026-10-21 (base patch 0112, see "Summons: targets, walk-through, levels"). **Second pass (O86, 2026-10-27).**
A likely engine cause, still a hypothesis (the engine source is not here; written from the TFS 1.4.2 code as remembered):
`Monster::updateTargetList` only drops creatures that are dead or out of sight, never non-opponents, and `isOpponent` of a
player's summon is "everybody but its master", so the owner, the party and the owner's other summons sit in the summon's
target list and the engine's own `selectTarget` may pick them; the scripts only refused the *hit* (`onTargetCombat`), the
wolf kept chasing. Closed in Lua, no engine patch (it cannot be compiled or tried here): `ChaosSummonsCore.purge(summon,
owner)` removes every ally of the owner from the summon's engine target list (`getTargetList` / `removeTarget`) and drops an
ally attack target, never the follow target (a summon follows its master); `bind` calls it, and the 0.5 s tick of
`summons.lua` calls `purgeAll` for every player with summons or a party, so a relog, a teleport, a town portal, a party
join and the move in or out of a PvP zone are covered within half a second. `sameParty` compares the party objects and,
when the engine hands out a new object per `getParty()` call, the party leaders, so `isAlly` no longer depends on `==` of
userdata. Every engine call is behind `pcall` (an engine without one of them is not an error). Mocked tests in
`tests/summons_test.lua`: creation with the owner, a member and their summons in the list; a fresh party object per call;
listed again after a relog or teleport; a member who joins later; a member who left (not purged any more); a skulled
stranger and a wild monster (kept); failing and missing API. **Live check**: the tester bots (below, "System checks") run the
wolf for 20 s and fail with `BUG beastmaster_wolf` on any wrong target or any ally left in its engine target list, and the
helper reports `summon_targets_owner` for every tester with a summon, all the time. **To check live by hand**: summon the wolf, stand
next to it with Auto Target on, hunt, press Feral Command with the wolf clicked (it should hit the nearest monster), and watch
whether the wolf ever walks at the owner. If it still does, read `Monster::selectTarget` / `isOpponent` in the engine and
tell me what the fork changed.

**Class change (item 84).** `ChaosClasses.afterVocationChange` (ascension, the Oracle, the free switch and the store's
Vocation Change) runs `ChaosClassSpells.sync`: spells with `needlearn="1"` the new class does not list are forgotten, the
ones it lists and the level allows are learned (`class_spells_core.lua`; none exist today: every Chaos and every stock
player spell is `needlearn="0"`, so the vocation and the level decide and the engine already swaps the whole kit at the
moment of `setVocation`, the old class's spells being refused by the vocation check). What stayed old was the client:
`ChaosSpellbook.refresh` now pushes the new vocation to a Spellbook window that is open, the store's message tells the player to
replace the action bar slots, and the client's Helper takes the old class's rules out (client/MANIFEST.md). Passive tree
reset, storages and the free-respec rule are untouched. `tests/class_spells_test.lua`, `tests/spellbook_test.lua`.

**Cinder Effigy (item 83).** Price x0.65 -> x0.75 and pulse 22% -> 24%: +10.6% of the spell damage in a pack (was -6.1%),
+27.8% with the Idol, one target -22% (was -31%). Numbers and caveats: server/data/spells/README.md "Effigy rebalance".

### Opcode collision check
Searched the reference server for every `onExtendedOpcode`, `sendExtendedOpcode(` and opcode
constant. Opcodes in use there: 1, 67, 73, 89, 91, 92, 99, 106, 107, 136, 181, 201, 202. (The
`ServerOpcodes` 125/126 in `global.lua` were first read as game-protocol opcodes, a different number space. They are not:
the base NPC scripts send them with `player:sendExtendedOpcode`, and 125 is the monster bar's. O189 moved them to 126 / 127
and gave the custom currencies their own opcode 113, see "NPC currencies".)
No other Chaos opcode collides. Weather (O208) took **114**: not in the reference server's list above, not one of the base client's `ExtendedIds`, not a `ChaosOpcodes` value, not named by any client module (`tests/weather_test.lua` checks all four, and that no two `ChaosOpcodes` share a number); it is the smallest number above 113 (the NPC currency opcode) that nothing else uses; 188-254 are all taken. Hideouts (192) also checked the reference client's own opcodes (`gamelib`
`ExtendedIds` 144-146, 210, 212, 213, 230, 246 and 0x8C = 140): 145 was taken there by the skill wheel. 110 was chosen for the stash because
the client has no fixed value and 110 is free. Storage keys (see "Storage keys" below) and DB tables
`chaos_*` are new; the one deliberate overlap is autoloot's storage base 80000 (shared on purpose).

Base client `ExtendedIds` (`gamelib` `const.lua`): 144 StaffVisuals, 145 WheelSkills, 146 MonkData, 210 Cavebot,
212 SmartFollow, 213 NpcConversationEnd, 230 BotCheckAlert, 246 Teleportation. Of these only 213 is registered by a base
module (`game_npctrade` `npcdialog.lua`, plain text); `game_raid` registers 213 too (JSON). That is harmless today (the
server never sends the NPC dialog end on 213), but the later registration replaces the earlier one, so a new system must
not take any of 144-146, 210, 212, 213, 230 or 246 (230 and 246 are already Chaos: ground labels and seasons; the base
defines both but registers neither).

### Weather on the client (O208) (`weather.lua`, `weather_core.lua`, `weather_config.lua`, `tools/patch_base_rain.py`, client `game_chaosweather`)

**What the base did.** `customs/globalevents/rain.lua` of the base server, all of it inside `if configManager.getBoolean(configKeys.WEATHER_RAIN)`
(config.lua `weatherRain = true`):
- one world-wide state in the global storage `Weather`: at startup 15% rain; every 5 minutes (`GlobalEvent` interval 300000) a dry
  world starts to rain with 15%, a rainy one stops with 10% (a long-run share of about 60% of the rolls rainy);
- while it rained, a `GlobalEvent` every 100 ms called `Player.sendWeatherEffect` for every online player
  (`data/lib/core/player.lua`): a random tile within 7 x 5 of the player, the first floor from 0 to 7 that has a tile there, one
  distance effect (drop, id 56) falling onto it from 7 tiles up-left and one magic effect (splash, id 2) on it, a second effect on
  water, and with `thunderEffect = true` a 50% chance per drop, when a player stood on that tile outside a protection zone, of a
  1-5 energy damage hit. So: no zones. It rains for everyone, but a drop lands on floors 0-7 only, so a player underground
  (floor 8 and below) saw none, and a player under a roof saw the drops on the roof, which the client hides.
- cost: two packets per player per 100 ms (about 14 million an hour at 200 online) and 6 s of game loop and 57 MB of garbage a minute
  ("Game loop stalls", measured).

**The design.** The server only decides; the client draws.
- `weather_core.lua` (pure, `tests/weather_test.lua`): the state `{raining, intensity, nextRollAt}`, the base's dice (`startup`,
  `roll`; a tick that comes late rolls once), a strength 1-3 picked when a rain starts (`weather_config.lua` `intensities`, 20 / 60 /
  20 percent; 2 is the base's density), the areas (`areaAt`: a list of `{name, kind, minZ, maxZ, box}`; the default is one area,
  floors 0-7, the base's), the message for a position, and the per-player rule `decide`: a message goes out only when what that
  player should see changed (a player is taken to see nothing until a first message, so a dry world sends nothing).
- `weather_config.lua`: every number (`tickMs = 3000`, the base's 15 / 10 / 300000, the strengths, `fadeMs = 2500`, the areas).
- `weather.lua` (engine glue): a `GlobalEvent` every `tickMs` (the dice, then one `getPosition` per online player and a `decide`), a
  startup event, a login event (a forced send after 1.5 s; the client also asks), `onExtendedOpcode` for `hello` (rate limited to
  one a second), logout forgets the player, and the staff command `/weather rain [1-3]`, `/weather clear`, `/weather info`.
  `Chaos.send` is the only send. The tick runs in a `pcall`.
- `tools/patch_base_rain.py` (install step `baserain`, after `idlekick`): sets `weatherRain = false` in config.lua (keeping a
  trailing comment; no key means off already). The base script is not edited: it registers nothing with the flag off. Idempotent,
  `tools/patch_base_rain_test.py` (stock text, CRLF, comment, a missing key, `--dry-run`, the install step). `thunderEffect` stays;
  only that script reads it.
- Protocol (opcode **114**, JSON `{action, data}`; see "Extended opcodes in use"): server -> client `set {k = "rain" | "none",
  i = 1..3 (rain only), f = fade ms}` (about 55 bytes); client -> server `hello {}` (answered with the current `set`, even when
  nothing changed). A player gets `set` when he logs in, asks, crosses between an area and no area (the tick notices it
  within 3 s: stepping from floor 7 to a cave, or back), or the weather or its strength changes. Steady rain sends nothing.
  An hour of rain for 200 players at 3 s ticks is 200 messages (the test counts them), the base sent 14 million packets.
- Storage keys: none (the state is in memory and rolls again at a restart, as the base's did). The global storage `Weather` is
  no longer written; no other script read it.

**What changed on purpose.**
- No thunder damage (1-5 energy about once in 30 s out in the rain; the base's drops decided it).
- No drops placed on tiles, so no splash effects on the ground and no extra effect on water; the client draws streaks over the screen.
- The strength varies per rain (the base had one density).
- The weather area follows the player's floor at the 3 s tick, not each step.

**The client** (`game_chaosweather`, client/MANIFEST.md): three repeated pictures scrolled over the game map only; fades with the
server's `f`; hidden under a roof; the option `weather` in Options > Graphics ("Rain and weather", base patch `0130`, through
`game_visualfx`).

**To check live.** Install (`install_all.py --only baserain`, then `files`), restart or reload, `/weather rain 2` as staff: players on
floors 0-7 get `set` within 3 s (`/weather info` says how many), a cave player none; `/weather clear`; wait for a roll (5 minutes)
or watch the console for `[ChaosWeather]` lines. In a client: the rain fades in, goes under a roof, returns, and the
checkbox switches it. Not run yet: the glue's engine calls (`Game.getPlayers`, `GlobalEvent`, `addEvent`, `TalkAction`) are the ones other
scripts here already use, but this file has only run against the mock.

### Ambient particles (O226) (`weather_core.lua`, `weather_config.lua`, `weather.lua`, client `game_chaosweather`)

The client draws slow embers, motes or dust over the game window (client/MANIFEST.md "Ambient particles (O226)"). The mood of a
place is decided here, as the weather is (option 1 of the brief: the weather code made it a small step).
- **Config:** `weather_config.lua` `ambient = {enabled, areas}`; an area is `{name, kind, minZ, maxZ, box}` like the rain areas, `kind` is
  `embers`, `motes` or `dust`, the first area that holds the player's tile wins, a tile in none has no mood. It is independent of the
  rain (a mood stands in rain or dry weather). `W.ambientAt(cfg, pos)` in `weather_core.lua` looks it up; a kind that is not in
  `W.AMBIENT_KINDS` (a typo) is dropped, never sent.
- **Protocol:** opcode 114 (no new opcode), server -> client `set {k, i?, f, a?}`: `a` is added only in a region with a mood. A player in no
  region gets the old message byte for byte, an older client ignores `a`. The per-player signature is `k:i:a`, so crossing between
  moods or into a cave is one message and walking inside one is none (the same 3 s tick and one `getPosition` per player as before).
  A cave floor (8-15) now sends a first message to a player of a dry world (`none` + `dust`), once.
- **Opcode budget and JSON guard:** nothing new to guard. The message is server -> client (about 60 bytes); the only inbound message of the
  opcode is still `hello`, which goes through `Chaos.opcodeDispatch` (`Chaos.opcodeBudget`, the 16 KB request cap) and `Chaos.decode`
  (`Chaos.guardJson`), and is rate limited to one a second as before.
- **Places in the default config:** Emberdeep Hollows (z 9-10) and Cinderfall Wastes (z 7), exact from `areagen_config.lua`: `embers`;
  every floor 8-15: `dust`. The surface swamp, jungle village, river forest and the jungle cave (`motes`) are boxes of 100 x 100
  or less around the sample sites of `docs/MAP_GUIDE.md` (swamp town 32935,32055; jungle village 32578,32728; forest by the river
  32602,32222; jungle cave 32666,32846 z 9). **They are guesses, the map is not in the repository: widen or move each box to the real
  swamp and forest** (one line each, the map editor shows the tile), and add the other forests. Order matters: put a small box before a
  wide one.
- **Staff:** `/weather ambient` says the mood of your tile.
- **Tests:** `tests/weather_test.lua` (the moods and boxes, an unknown kind, the signature rule, byte-for-byte old payload outside a region,
  the cave payload, `/weather ambient`).
- **Not run on a live server or in a client.**

### Area colour mood (O234) (`weather_core.lua`, `weather_config.lua`, `weather.lua`, client `game_visualfx`)

A gentle colour grade of the map picture by area (client/MANIFEST.md "Visual effects", "Area colour mood (O234)"). The server only
names the mood; the numbers are on the client (`grademood_logic.lua`), which eases to a new mood over about 2 s.
- **Config:** `weather_config.lua` `mood = {enabled, areas}`, next to `ambient`. An area is `{name, kind, minZ, maxZ, box}`, the same
  shape and the same lookup as `ambient.areas` (`areaIn` in `weather_core.lua`; first area that holds the tile wins, boxes inclusive,
  a tile in none has no mood). `kind` is `ice`, `swamp`, `desert`, `fire` or `crypt` (`W.MOOD_KINDS`; a typo is dropped, never sent).
  `W.moodAt(cfg, pos)` looks it up. It is independent of rain and of the ambient particles.
- **Protocol:** opcode 114 (no new opcode), server -> client `set {k, i?, f, a?, m?}`: `m` is a short string, added only in a region
  with a colour mood (about 12 bytes more; far below the 8192 limit). A player in no mood region gets the old message byte for byte, an
  older client ignores `m`. The per-player signature is `k:i:a:m`, so crossing between moods is one message and walking inside one is
  none (same 3 s tick and one `getPosition` per player as before). Leaving a region sends the message without `m`, which eases the
  client back to the plain grade.
- **Places in the default config:** exact from `areagen_config.lua` (origin and size): Emberdeep Hollows z 9-10 and Cinderfall Wastes z 7
  `fire`, the Iron Crucible and the Pyre Throne z 9 `fire`, the Ossuary z 9-10, the Hollow Vault and the Marrow Crypts z 9 `crypt`.
  The Fallen Sanctum has none. **Marked for the owner to fit (guesses; the map is not in the repository):** `swamp town` (swamp,
  32880,32010-33000,32110 z 7), `desert west` (33000,31330-33100,31420 z 7) and `desert east` (33200,31310-33300,31410 z 7),
  `ice settlement` (31950,31310-32040,31400 z 6-7) and `ice field` (32000,31060-32100,31150 z 6-7) are boxes of about 100 x 100 around
  the sample sites of `docs/MAP_GUIDE.md` (swamp 32935,32055; deserts 33050,31374 and 33248,31360; ice 31994,31358 and 32048,31104).
  Widen or move each box to the real swamp, desert and ice land (one line each, the map editor shows the tile) and add the other
  ones; a small box goes before a wide one. Plain caves have no colour mood, only the dust.
- **Client numbers** (added on top of the grade of `0126`, `grademood_logic.lua`): `ice` tint r -0.020 g +0.004 b +0.034, colour -0.02;
  `swamp` -0.012 / +0.026 / -0.018, colour -0.03, contrast +0.01; `desert` +0.032 / +0.016 / -0.022, colour +0.02, contrast +0.01;
  `fire` +0.036 / +0.004 / -0.030, colour +0.02, contrast +0.03; `crypt` -0.006 / -0.002 / +0.004, colour -0.10, contrast +0.02.
- **Staff:** `/weather ambient` also says the colour mood of your tile.
- **Tests:** `tests/weather_test.lua` (config sanity, the sample sites, floors, box edges, first area wins, off switch, unknown kind, the
  message field, the signature rule). Client: `grademood_test.lua`.
- **Not run on a live server or in a client.** The client needs base patch `0153` and the option `screenGrade` (off by default).

### Extended opcode size limit (`extended_opcode.lua`, `Chaos.sendChunked`)
One extended opcode message carries at most 8192 bytes (`NetworkMessage::addString` refuses longer strings without an
error). The base `Player.sendExtendedOpcode` wrote `0x32` and the opcode first, so a longer payload went out as the two
bytes `32 <opcode>`: the client read the next two bytes as the length, logged `ProtocolGame parse message exception (...
3 unread, last opcode is 0x32 ...)` and dropped the rest of that network message. At every admin login this lost the
whole admin catalog (opcode 120, then about 20 KB, now about 60 KB in 8 parts; so the admin panel never appeared) and whatever was bundled after it (the
ancestral points push 89, sometimes the loot filter settings 238 and name plates 248). `extended_opcode.lua` replaces
`Player.sendExtendedOpcode`: a payload over 8192 bytes is not sent and a `[Warning - Chaos] extended opcode ...` line names
it. Big JSON goes through `Chaos.sendChunked(player, opcode, json)` (parts `S...`, `P...`, `E...` of 8000 bytes, joined by
the client's `ProtocolGame.registerExtendedJSONOpcode`); the admin panel uses it. `tests/extended_opcode_test.lua`; tested in
game (admin and player logins without the exception, admin panel filled and running actions).

### Extended opcode dispatch (`chaos_constants.lua`, `tests/opcode_dispatch_test.lua`)
The engine runs every `extendedopcode` creature event a player registered for every extended opcode the client sends.
With about 80 Chaos handlers that was 80 Lua calls per request, all but one returning at once (about 0.2 ms of game loop
each request; "Stress test"). `chaos_constants.lua` (loaded before any module defines its handler) keeps each handler a
module defines with `function ev.onExtendedOpcode` in `Chaos.opcodeDispatch` instead of the engine, under the opcode of
its guard: the upvalue `OPCODE` of the handler (every such handler starts with `if opcode ~= OPCODE then return end`, or
`... ~= OPCODE or ...`; the test checks every source). A handler without that upvalue (notifications.lua with its two
opcodes, the admin panel) is called for every opcode, as before. `player:registerEvent` of such a name records it for
the player and registers the one engine event `ChaosOpcodeDispatch`, which calls the handlers of the opcode the player
registered, in the order they were defined (the shared opcodes 246, 218 and 153 keep their order), each in its own
protected call (an error is printed with its traceback and the next handler still runs). `unregisterEvent` and logout
work as before. A request over `Chaos.opcodeRequestMax` (16,384 bytes) is dropped before any handler decodes it, with
one console line per player a minute. After a reload of the scripts with players online (their records are gone) every
handler runs for them until they log in again. Handlers made with the table constructor (`CreatureEvent({...})`) and the
base server's own events (`ExtendedOpcode`, the tasks module) stay with the engine. Without the engine API (the unit
tests' mocks) nothing changes, so the fuzz test still calls every handler directly.
- Load order fix, 2026-10-13. A spell loads this file first: `thief/shadow_veil.lua` calls `ChaosSpell.loadClasses`,
  which runs `classes.lua`. That is the spells' interface, where `CreatureEvent()` gives nil. The load stopped there and
  the Scripts interface's own load returned at `if Chaos then return end`. So `ChaosOpcodeDispatch` was never made and
  `Player:registerEvent` was never hooked: no client request reached a Chaos handler. Now `D.install()` makes the events
  and the hook once, on the first load that can. The guard at the top calls it.
  Test: `tests/opcode_dispatch_load_test.lua`, which fails on the old file.
- No error at start, 2026-10-16. The console still printed "CreatureEvents can only be registered in the Scripts
  interface" with a traceback (shadow_veil.lua, _common.lua `loadClasses`, classes.lua, chaos_constants.lua). Now
  `D.install()` returns before any `CreatureEvent()` call when a chunk of another interface's folder is on the call
  stack (`D.outsideScripts`: `data/spells/`, `data/npc/`, `data/lib/`, `data/monster/` and the XML event folders).
  Chaos and the class rules still load there; every spell works as before. Test: `tests/spells_interface_load_test.lua`
  (a mocked spells' interface whose `CreatureEvent()` throws; it fails without the check).
- Checked in a live client, 2026-10-13: before the fix the bestiary, achievements, leaderboard, siege and pets windows
  never opened and the market stayed empty. After it all six open with their data; `Chaos.opcodeDispatch.players`
  holds the player.

### Protocol fuzz test (`tests/opcode_fuzz_test.lua`, client `game_chaosguard/opcode_fuzz_test.lua`)
The server test loads every script under `data/scripts` against a mocked engine and feeds every `onExtendedOpcode` handler
(fixed seed, about 5 s per interpreter): malformed and truncated JSON, every action found in the script with each field it
reads missing or of the wrong type (negative, fractional, NaN, inf, 2^53, 60 KB strings, 5000-entry arrays, 300-deep
nesting), database rows of another character, rapid repeats with the clock stopped, requests after logout, removal and
death. It fails on a Lua error (also one a module catches and prints), anything granted to the fuzz player (who owns
nothing), an answer over 8192 bytes, a client string in SQL unescaped, NaN / inf / a fraction handed to the engine as an
integer, a player passed where a position is expected, a database read after a refused rate limit or on every one of five
rapid calls, and an opcode that differs from the table above or from `ChaosOpcodes` (fallbacks `ChaosOpcodes.x or n` and
`cfg.opcode` too; handlers sharing an opcode never answer the same action). The client test loads every module with a
stubbed client API and feeds every registered handler, through the client's own dispatcher (client base patch 0043, read
from the patch), bad buffers, `data` and every field of the wrong type or shape (rows that are numbers, ...) and chunk
sequences with parts missing, repeated or out of order; any Lua error fails it, also one the module or the dispatcher
catches and logs (under Lua 5.3 `"%d"` takes fractions as the client's LuaJIT does). It also checks each module's opcode
against this table and `ChaosOpcodes`. The client modules check the shape of what they draw from (lists keep their
tables, objects must be tables), so a bad row cannot leave a window half drawn.
- `Chaos.toInt` (and `int` in `market_core.lua`, `orbexchange_core.lua`) refuses numbers beyond +-2^53: `1e308` stayed a
  float, which `"%d"` refuses under Lua 5.3 and turns into -2^63 under LuaJIT.
- `ratelimit.lua` keeps at most 512 keys per player and none longer than 64 bytes: keys are built from the client's action
  names, so made-up actions grew the table until logout.
- The stash's "Stash" request answers with the list (a database read) at most every 100 ms, whatever item it names.
- Values the client sent are echoed only after a check (`seq` of the market, the item link request number, the loot filter
  kill id, the command page id, the crafting orb key): inf or a table made `json.encode` raise, a 60 KB string made the
  answer too big to send.

## Shared security rules (`chaos_constants.lua`)

- **Instances.** Every system with its own way in and out registers with `Chaos.registerInstance(key, {label, inside(player),
  at(pos)})`: rift, dungeon, tower, arena, worldboss, siege, raid, descent, ascended, guildboss, battleground, trials, ascension,
  marches, hideout. `Chaos.inAnyInstance(player[, except])` (a member of a run or standing in its area) is asked by the Town Portal,
  the hideout entry and the store teleports (`ShopServices.teleportBlocked`: temple teleport scroll, guild hall scroll; a hideout stays
  allowed there). `Chaos.instanceAt(pos)` is asked by the hideout before it returns a player to a stored spot. A check that errors
  counts as "no". `ChaosSiege.isInside(player)` and `ChaosSiege.isInsidePos(pos)` exist now (guild hall scroll, arena, treasure goblin).
- **Strangers in a slot.** Raid, Ember Descent, Ascended Omen, guild boss and battleground runs sweep their slot every 3 s
  (`Chaos.instanceSweepMs`, from their tick): an online non-staff player standing there who is not in the run goes to the temple
  (`Chaos.sweepIntruders`). Login inside a slot without a run already did that.
- **Save before a database credit.** The stash goes one step further: every deposit and withdrawal is a journal row written
  BEFORE the item moves, with a serial saved with the character ("Stash", "Write order"). Value that leaves the character
  in memory and is credited to a row (star bank deposit, gold transfer to an offline character, guild bank deposit, guild depot, guild boss gold and materials) is
  credited only after `player:save()` succeeded (`Chaos.saveCharacter`); a failed save gives it back and credits nothing, as the
  market and the orb exchange do. Otherwise a crash between the two duplicated it. The other way round, value credited to
  a character after a row or another saved character paid it (a gold transfer to an online character, a guild bank
  withdrawal) is saved at once after the credit, so a crash cannot lose it ("Stress test").
- **Staff talkactions.** `Chaos.staffCommand(player, words, param, economy)`: `/coins`, `/charm give` and `/pact` (all but
  `info`) need group 5 (`Chaos.economyMinGroup`), `/market` and `/orbx` staff access; every staff use goes to `ChaosAdmin.log`.
  Staff never give value (docs/GM_HANDBOOK.md section 2, decided): `/rift key|omen|fragments`, `/ascended sigil|relic|shards`,
  `/newplayerkit` (the kit, a milestone, `reset`), `/guild bank|xp` and `rent <guild>, paid`, `/classunlock`, `/cosmetic`,
  `/exclusive` (a grant or `roll`) and `/transmog` grants, and `/pet give` need group 5 the same way (2026-10-12); what only
  looks, tests or takes away (status, sync, revoke, info) stays at group 4 and is logged too.
  The admin panel's `players.give_item` and `world.create_item` need group 5 too (like `economy.*`).
- **Rate limits.** `Chaos.limited(player, key, ms)` (over `ratelimit.lua`) drops a request inside 300 ms of the same action in the
  opcode handlers of season, siege, arena, bounty, rift, season journey, season modes, daily, hunt, invasion, infinity tower, patch
  notes and bestiary; the passive tree's save and reset at most once a second. A save always goes to the active preset (no free
  respec through another preset number).
- **Stash reach.** A floor item is stashed only from the own tile or a tile that does not block (wall, bars, window), in clear
  sight, and not diagonally between two walls.

Tests: `tests/instances_test.lua`, `save_before_credit_test.lua`, `staff_permissions_test.lua`, `rate_limits_test.lua`,
`passivetree_preset_test.lua`, and new cases in `hideout_test.lua`, `security_test.lua`, `guildboss_test.lua`, `shop_test.lua`,
`shop_payments_test.lua`.

## Gold payments: carried coins, then the bank (`data/lib/chaos_pay.lua`, `Chaos.pay`, `tools/patch_bank_payments.py`, `src-patches/0053`)

Owner 2026-10-22: "todas as lojas que usam gold aceitam o dinheiro diretamente do banco". Every kill's coins go to the
bank (`autoloot.lua`), so every price in gold is paid from the coins the character carries first and the rest from the
bank account, the order of the stock `removeTotalMoney`. One helper does it everywhere:

- `ChaosPay.pay(player, amount[, quiet])` (`data/lib/chaos_pay.lua`, pure, also `Chaos.pay` / `Chaos.canPay` /
  `Chaos.totalMoney` in `chaos_constants.lua`): whole gold, all or nothing. Short (carried + bank < amount), a bad amount,
  or a coin removal that fails: false, nothing taken. A bank write that fails after the coins went puts the coins in the
  bank (cannot happen within one script call). A negative balance counts as 0. When the bank paid a part it says so
  in the player's language ("Paid %d gold: %d carried and %d from your bank. Bank balance: %d gold.", pt-BR in
  `i18n_strings.lua`), unless `quiet`. Returns true, fromCoins, fromBank. Refunds and payouts are unchanged (most go to
  the bank already).
- `ChaosPay.install()` makes `Player.getTotalMoney` and `Player.removeTotalMoney` these. The base defines both twice
  (`data/lib/core/player.lua`, and `data/npc/lib/npc.lua` when the first NPC loads; the stock one ignored a failed coin
  removal and printed English), so both files load `chaos_pay.lua` at their end (install step `bankpayments`).
- **NPC trade window.** The stock shop module already checks `getTotalMoney` and pays with `removeTotalMoney`, and the
  engine sends carried + bank as the window's money (`ProtocolGame::sendSaleItemList`); the client greys every offer by
  that number (`game_npctrade` `canTradeItem`, `GameDoublePlayerGoodsMoney` on for 10.98). The engine sent the list
  again only when an item moved, so a purchase paid from the bank alone left the old money in the window:
  `src-patches/0053` makes Lua `setBankBalance` send it again while a shop is open.
- **Base scripts** (`tools/patch_bank_payments.py`, install step `bankpayments`, late: after every step that writes a
  `removeMoney`): in `npc/scripts`, `actions`, `talkactions`, `movements`, `creaturescripts`, `globalevents`, `scripts`
  (not `scripts/chaos`) and `spells`, `X:removeMoney(` becomes `X:removeTotalMoney(`, `doPlayerRemoveMoney(` becomes
  `ChaosPay.payCid(`, and outside bank scripts `X:getMoney()` becomes `X:getTotalMoney()` and `getPlayerMoney(` becomes
  `ChaosPay.totalCid(`. On the base server: 78 scripts, 151 calls (boats, carpets, horse renters, ferrymen, outfit and
  addon sellers, the blessing priest, the table shops with their own trade code, the crafting table and its window's
  money). A bank script (deposit, withdraw or transfer: the bankers and coin changers) keeps its `getMoney`, which is the
  coins a deposit takes; a `removeMoney` followed by a bank balance change (a deposit in Lua) and a commented line are
  left alone. Idempotent; `tools/patch_bank_payments_test.py`.
- **Chaos systems** pay with `Chaos.pay`: gem and support removal (before: the bank only when it held the whole price,
  else the coins only), paragon and passive tree reset, passive builds and build sharing (fallbacks), and every former
  `removeTotalMoney` wrapper (trials, gentle death blessings, atlas, Ember Descent sigils, factions, guild payments and
  the guild hall, transmog, restock, the Gambler, community brazier, house broker, respec), the Everfull potion seller
  (now paid before the potion is given; no room gives the gold back to the bank) and the admin panel's Remove gold.
  Their money checks read `Chaos.totalMoney`.
- **Left as they are:** the market and the orb exchange (a bank wallet with escrow; their listing fees and purchases
  are taken from the bank on purpose), the bank's own deposit, Candlemarks, conquest tokens, the store's Chaos Coins
  and every payout.

Tests: `tests/chaos_pay_test.lua` (carried only, bank only, mixed, short = nothing taken, failures, overrides, pt-BR),
`tests/potions_test.lua`, `tools/patch_bank_payments_test.py`.

## Player commands: the menu (`commands_ui.lua`, `commands_ui_core.lua`, `tools/install_commands.py`)

Players type no commands. Every player command of the server is in the client's top menu (`client_chaos_topbar`):
a Chaos window where one exists, else a page of the **Info & Services** window (client `game_chaosinfo`, extended
opcode 237, `ChaosOpcodes.info`). The window asks `catalog` (which command ids this server has, the vocation words)
and sends `run {page, ids, params}`; `commands_ui.lua` runs each command's function and
catches what it would have shown (text messages, cancel messages, `popupFYI`, `showTextDialog`) to send it back as
the page text. Chaos scripts register their command with `ChaosCommands.register(id, fn)` (`commands_ui_core.lua`)
instead of a `TalkAction`. Base server commands are loaded on demand: an XML talkaction's script from
`data/talkactions/scripts/` (its line, commented out, still names the script), a revscript in a sandbox that keeps
its other events away from the engine. `tools/install_commands.py <server>/data` takes the spoken forms out of the
base server (idempotent; `--dry-run` lists the changes).

**Ancestral Store** (Economy > More > Ancestral Store; `commands_ui.lua`, pure part `commands_ui_core.lua`,
tests `tests/commands_ui_test.lua` and `tests/ancestral_store_test.lua`). The window asks `store` and gets
`{points, entries = [{id, kind, name, item (client id), price}], maxCount, message}`; its Buy button sends
`buy {id, count}`. Entries, prices and items are read once from the base store scripts named in `talkactions.xml`
(`ITEM_PRICE` and `ItemType(id)` of `data/talkactions/scripts/<entry>.lua`; a script outside that folder, a price
outside 1..1,000,000 or an unknown item leaves the entry out). The purchase is made by `commands_ui.lua`, never by the
base script: those read the points of the wrong row (`fiery_wings.lua` used the account id as a player id) and took
the points with an unconditional `UPDATE` after a separate read. Now: unknown ids and counts that are not a whole
number in 1..10 are refused (`K.validateBuy`); one purchase a second per player (`ChaosRateLimit`, or a local throttle
when that file is missing), checked before the request is read; a refused request reads no database (its answer
carries the points last sent; `tests/opcode_fuzz_test.lua`); the points are read, checked, and taken with `UPDATE ... WHERE ancestral_points >= cost`,
then read again and nothing is given unless exactly the cost was taken; capacity is checked first; items go to the
backpack only (`addItem(id, 1, false)`), and the points of what did not fit are returned; a character that is gone buys
nothing. The old `run ancestralstore "<group>, <n>"` goes through the same path. Every purchase is one console line.

**Services state** (`services` action): Name / Vocation Change tokens, the free switch, the tutorial, whether the
familiar commands answer (level 200, the base script's rule), web shop orders waiting (`znote_shop_orders`, only when
the base `!shop` script is there) and the owned / shown name plate frames (`ChaosShopCore.FRAMES`). The client
disables the buttons that cannot be used. Rate limited to one read per 500 ms, as `store`.

Texts: the base `!exp` line "You didn't have any current Double EXP enhancement." shows as "No Double EXP active."
(`K.REWRITE`); `classes` groups the locked classes that unlock the same way in one line (`ChaosClassUnlocksCore.lockGroups`);
`ascension` below the level says "Ascension unlocks at level 100 (you are level X)." (the NPC keeps its own line).
