## Client-side gaps found while reading the client (not changed, `client/` is out of scope)

1. **`sendAction(opcode, action, data)` does not exist in the overlay.** `game_bank`, `game_autoloot`
   and `game_daily` call a global `sendAction(op, action, data)`; the only `sendAction` in the tree
   is passivetree's own two-argument one. It must send `json.encode({action = action, data = data})`
   on that extended opcode (the server expects exactly that envelope). Without it those three
   modules send nothing.
2. **game_stash** uses the donor client's `modules.client_manager`, which is not in the overlay. The
   server speaks `{"action":"Stash","data":{"make":...}}` both ways on opcode 110. Minimal port:
   set `Stash.Opcode = 110`, replace `modules.client_manager.Manage.NewModule(...)` with
   `ProtocolGame.registerExtendedOpcode(110, function(_, buf) local j = json.decode(buf); if j and j.action == "Stash" then Stash.DataManager(nil, 110, j.data) end end)`
   and drop/replace `modules.game_extramenu`, `Keybind`, `modules.game_windowfocus` if absent.
   The envelope is an **assumption** about what client_manager does; only the client's outbound
   JSON proves it for the client-to-server direction.
3. (fixed) `game_dungeons` loads banners from `/images/dungeons/<name>.png` (`dungeonsview.lua` `V.BANNERS`, title to
   name): the base dungeons' images, and for the Vault and dungeons 6-9 renders of their own maps
   (`client/tools/gen_dungeon_banners.py`).
4. `game_passivetree` sends via `protocolGame.sendExtendedJSONOpcode`, an OTClient call. Stock OTClient
   10.98 may lack it.
5. (fixed) the JSON error branches of the bank, autoloot and daily client modules used an undefined variable.

## Stubbed or assumed (read this before relying on anything)

General
- Engine API assumed to match TFS 1.4.2: `Player:getBankBalance/setBankBalance/getMoney/addMoney/removeMoney`,
  `Game.getPlayerByGUID`, `Game.getSpectators(pos, multifloor, onlyPlayers, minX, maxX, minY, maxY)`,
  `Tile:getThing(stackpos)`, `Container:getItems(true)`, `Item:remove(count)`, `Item:hasAttribute`,
  `ItemType:isRune/isStackable/isPickupable/getWeaponType/getClientId`, `Party:getInvitees/addMember/removeInvite`,
  `MonsterType:getOutfit`, CreatureEvent types `kill` and `death`, `os.mtime` (falls back to `os.time`),
  `result.getNumber`. None verified against a real server.
- `json` global is the base server `lib/core/json.lua` (rxi). Empty tables encode as `[]`.
- Packets stay far below the ~24 KB network message limit (stash `addItems` is cut at 40 entries and 6000 bytes of JSON, see "Stash", "List packets").
- All client input is validated (integers, ranges, ownership). Flood control: `ratelimit.lua` (`ChaosRateLimit.allow`,
  `Chaos.limited`) drops repeats of the same action within a few hundred ms in the opcode handlers of most modules
  (about 70 scripts use it; "Shared security rules"), and the engine's `maxPacketsPerSecond` limits every connection.

bank
- Stars are off: the star tab came with the imported client and item 35572 exists in no item list of this game.
  `Chaos.bank.starItemId = 0`; the client hides the tab. The star code stays for a real item id later.
- The server does the maths. Amounts are integers in 1..balance (`bank_core.lua` `checkAmount`); anything else is dropped.
- Withdrawals, also Withdraw all, are paid as coin stacks through `addItemEx(item, false)`, never onto the floor.
  A stack that does not fit is tried smaller (`payOut`). Only what arrived is charged; the rest stays in the bank.
- Deposit all takes `player:getMoney()`: every gold, platinum and crystal coin carried. Chaos Coins are account points, no coin item.
- Gold moves inside one dispatcher call on the in-memory balance: no double spend between two requests.
- One rate limit key for every money request (`bank.move`, `rateLimitMs`), `bank.open` for opening. Checked first.
- Transfer checks the name (`validName`) and the balance before the lookup, then that the character exists.
- Offline transfers update `players.balance` directly; transfers have no fee, limit or log.

autoloot
- Client numeric ids sent by the Auto Loot window are treated as **client** ids and mapped to server ids
  through a one-time scan of item ids 100..100000.
- Looting itself is not done here; it needs the base server `scripts/creaturescripts/autoloot.lua` callback.
- The window's add / remove / clear go over the opcode (no spoken command is involved).
- `sync` answers `list` (the same data, the window stays shut); add / remove with `quiet = true` answer `list` too.
  The client uses them for the item menu's "Add to Loot List" / "Remove from Loot List", which the base client wired
  to its Quick Loot (packets a 10.98 server does not have; live test winpkg-35). "Manage Loot containers" opens the
  Loot Bag rules (`pouches.lua`).

daily
- Reward table is a placeholder. The shipped client adds 2 to `Day` and maps claims through
  `{6,7,1,2,3,4,5}`; the server compensates (documented in the file). Day 7 of that client logic is
  otherwise unreachable, so do not "simplify" the offset.
- "Midnight" is server local time; the client's countdown uses client local time minus 1 hour.

notifications
- No catacomb system exists in the reference server: `start_catacomb` and `leave_queue` only call the
  overridable `ChaosNotify.onStartCatacomb` / `onLeaveQueue` (the latter also leaves the dungeon queue).
- No `Party:onInvite` hook exists in the reference server, so `partyInvite` toasts are never sent
  automatically (call `ChaosNotify.partyInvite`). Its text says "catacomb"; for plain parties it reads oddly.
- Task / battle pass toasts need one call added to the reference `tasks.lua` / battle pass code.
- `/gmnotify` is allowed for any group with `Group:getAccess()`.

passivetree
- Tree shape comes from the client's `nodes.lua` (664 nodes, 659 on the server, plus the four flask nodes 669-672 of O251: the four class section start nodes fold into the root,
  and node 239, a stray copy of the original tree on top of 240 with no links, is `hidden`; the generator records 1024 stat entries,
  per-class keystone variants included). `server/tests/passivetree_layout_test.lua` checks the whole tree: every client link is a
  server link and the other way round, every link is drawn (the client draws from `out` lists), no overlapping nodes, no line
  through a node, no node without links, and the class sections reachable only through themselves.
  Every link is also listed on both ends in `nodes.lua` (2026-10-21): 50 -> 115 and 365 -> 364 were listed on one end only.
  The server had them (its links are undirected), but the window let a node join only through its own lists, so a saved
  allocation down 50 -> 115 (skipping 116) showed 115 and everything past it dim, and the planner priced those saved
  nodes again (the server charged 0 or 1: "You already have those nodes"). Saved trees were always right; nothing to
  repair or refund. The client now shows the allocation over undirected links (`TreePlan.connected`), lists every link
  back at load (`TreePlan.linkBack`), and the planner counts the ids of the last `sendNodes` as owned
  (`client/overlay/modules/game_passivetree/treelinks_test.lua`: both ends, client = server, every server path of
  every class shown whole).
  Regenerate `passivetree_data.lua` with `tools/gen_passivetree_data.lua` whenever the client tree changes.
- Points formula is invented: `(level - 8) * 1` plus storage `7100020`. Change `Chaos.passive`.
- Only one preset slot exists in the client UI; presets 0 and 1 are the same slot. `refund` is just a resync.
- Stat keys such as `strength`, `incrementFire`, `absorbIce`, `criticalHitChance`, `lifeLeechChance`
  are **not applied**. base server' `CHARSTAT_*` values are stored by its own system and would conflict.
  Use `ChaosPassiveTree.getBonuses(player)` or `ChaosPassiveTree.appliers[statName] = function(player, value)`.
- The client's "exclude" (two big nodes of one path) rule is not enforced: no node in the data uses it.

dungeons
- Entry is by queue, not by the base server modal/PZ/party rules: no PZ requirement, no real party needed,
  players are matched individually (same difficulty). Solo and groups (beta feedback 2026-10-22, O147): the largest group
  is `AmountParty` when `NeedParty`, else 1, and **one player may always enter alone**; see "Solo dungeons" below.
- Bosses are assumed to exist inside the dungeon box (map spawns or `SpawnMonsters`). Boss names per
  dungeon id are in `Chaos.dungeons.extra` (guessed from the base server boss scripts) and must match the monster
  names on your server. Progress % = monsters that disappeared from the box / monsters at start (summons
  ignored; it never goes back down). At `Chaos.dungeons.progressNeeded` (85%, owner 2026-10-14; was 100) the boss is
  unlocked (`dungeons.lua` `unlockBoss`): every member gets "Boss unlocked!" (console line through `Chaos.t`, pt-BR in
  `i18n_strings.lua`; the kill counter of `game_dungeons` shows it, pt-BR "Boss liberado!"), and a generated dungeon opens
  its boss room gate and spawns its boss (`extra.unlock`). A run is won when the boss dies after the unlock (`onKill`, or
  seen and gone); a base dungeon's boss killed before 85% wins the run once the 85% are reached.
- One run per dungeon at a time (they share a single map area). All monsters in the box are removed when a
  run ends.
- Difficulty (1..6) is stored and unlocked (finish on your top difficulty to unlock the next) but changes nothing in-game.
- The difficulty panel of a dungeon with its own health curves (the Vault and the generated dungeons 6-9,
  `areagen_config.lua` `bossHealth` / `trashHealth`) shows those: `dungeonPayload` sends
  `health = D.healthCurves(bossHealth, trashHealth)` (`dungeons_difficulty.lua`; a side without a curve keeps the table's
  percent, as `scaleMonster` does), the client shows "Monster Health" / "Boss Health" from it, damage, experience, gold
  and loot from the table. No field (base dungeons, an older server): the table's texts. Tested in
  `tests/dungeons_difficulty_test.lua` (every curve of areagen_config.lua against `D.bossHealth`, the client's copy of
  the table) and the client's `game_dungeons/dungeonsview_test.lua`.
- Loot panel and challenge list are configured in `Chaos.dungeons.extra`; real loot comes from the boss XML.
- The base server `DUNGEON_SYSTEM` is used for level, group size, positions, time and cooldown. Its modal script reads
  `Storages.TimerCooldown` while the table defines `timerCooldown` (existing bug); this module accepts both.
  `DUNGEON_SYSTEM.Dungeons[3]` has `DungeonPos` z=0 but `FromPos/ToPos` z=7; the box is widened to include
  DungeonPos so players are not treated as "outside".
- The area of a run (who is inside on every tick, the login and shutdown checks, the monster count, the clean-up) is
  the base box plus `Chaos.dungeons.extra[id].area` (`dungeons.lua` `areaOf`). Measured on the base map, its spawn file
  and the dungeons' lever boss scripts: dungeon 2 fits its box. Dungeon 1's boss room (31856-31908, 32197-32236, z 8) is
  east of its box. Dungeon 3's box is floor 7 only; its spawns, lever and boss room reach floors 8-10 (area 31950-32078,
  33098-33245, z 0-10). Dungeon 4's box is its entry hall only: `DungeonPos` is 3 tiles south of it, so a queue run
  ended on its first tick, and every spawn, the lever and the boss room lie outside (area 31452-31736, 31495-31644,
  z 8-12). No other spawn lies in the added boxes. The generated dungeons 5-9 (The Hollow Vault and the deep dungeons
  6-9, `areagen.lua`) get the whole generated grid of every floor as their box: entry, exit, boss and spawns inside. Tests: `tests/dungeons_area_test.lua`,
  `tests/areagen_test.lua`.
- Cooldown (2026-10-15, "Time-friendly progression"; owner 2026-10-24: none after a clear): a cleared run starts no
  cooldown (`cooldownOnSuccess` false, `cooldownSeconds` 0; it was 15 min, and the base `DUNGEON_SYSTEM.CooldownTime`
  of 1 h after every run stays replaced), the next run can start at once. A failed run, a time-out, a member
  who leaves or dies, and a member who logged out inside and logs in again while the server runs (sent to the temple)
  start the short `failCooldownSeconds` (300 s, `cooldownOnFail`): farming 85% of the monsters and leaving does not pay
  (owner rule "follow your recommendations"). A restart sets none. Tests: `tests/dungeons_area_test.lua` (a cleared run
  sets 900 s for every member, leaving 300 s), `tests/instance_limits_systems_test.lua` (time-out, relog).
- The run's time is `DungeonTime` capped at `Chaos.dungeons.maxTimeSeconds` (45 min). The base modal entry tile opens
  this window instead of its modal window (`tools/patch_base_dungeon.py`, "Instance limits", "Base modal dungeon
  entry"), so its own `DungeonTime` timer never starts.
- Ranking: solo = best time per player (party size 1), group = best runs with 2+ players. Times in ms.

Solo dungeons (O147, beta feedback 2026-10-22: "dungeons need two players; my testing partners are often offline")
- **Entry.** The base table's `NeedParty` / `AmountParty` (2 for the Bones Dungeon, Master of the Elements, Forbidden
  Chevalier and Rootmaw) is now the largest group, not a minimum (`dungeons.lua` `groupSizeOf`). A queued player waits
  `Chaos.dungeons.party.soloWaitSeconds` (5) for a partner of the same difficulty; a full group starts at once. The window's
  "Party" requirement shows "1-2". The generated dungeons 5-9 (`party = 1`) were solo already.
- **Scaling formula** (`dungeons_difficulty.lua` `D.partyHealth` / `D.partyDamage`, numbers in `Chaos.dungeons.party`),
  n = the players that went in:
  `health(n) = 1 + 0.6 (n - 1)` and `damage(n) = 1 + 0.1 (n - 1)` (the damage the run's monsters deal to its players).
  The health and damage curves of every dungeon (`extra[id].bossHealth` / `trashHealth`, the difficulty table) are the
  measured solo ones ("Solo kill times", "Pack combat (pace)"), so **1 player = x1.0**. Two players: monsters x1.6 health
  and x1.1 damage; four: x2.8 and x1.3. Health grows slower than the group's damage output (n players deal about n times
  one), so a group clears faster than a solo player (two players: about 20% faster) and takes slightly more per hit.
  It multiplies with the difficulty step (`scaleMonster` for the health, `scaleHit` for the damage). The ranking keeps
  solo and group apart already (party size 1 against 2+).
- **Respawn and boss check (the old bug).** The map's own respawn inside a running dungeon is refused (`onSpawn`, owner
  2026-10-17), the run's monsters are created once, and the unlock (generated dungeons: the boss) fires once. A gap was
  found and closed: a won run stays in `runs[]` for `exitDelayMs` (10 s) with `ended` set, and `runAt` skipped ended runs,
  so the map could respawn the boss and the trash beside the group while it walked out. `runAt` now holds until the
  teardown. `tests/dungeons_area_test.lua` (blocks "solo entry and party scaling" and "the old bug") fails on the old code.
- **All monsters at the entry (O179, owner 2026-10-24: "make them all spawn at once when the player enters").** A run
  places every monster in the entry tick, before the players are teleported in: `startRun` clears the area, makes the
  map's monsters from the start-up record (`ChaosDungeonMapSpawns`, now a global, so a `/reload` of the scripts keeps it),
  then the base list (`SpawnMonsters`; it used to be made before the clean-up, which removed it again), then a generated
  dungeon's points (`areagen.lua populate`). No `addEvent` spawns anything later. The run counts only that **roster**
  (`run.roster`, monster ids at the start): `run.total` is fixed, "Monsters Alive" (`left`) only goes down, and a monster
  that appears later (a boss fight's add) is not counted. Other mid-run paths closed: the Treasure Goblin replacing a
  respawn (`treasure_goblin.lua` `onSpawn`) and the tier ambush copy (`monster_tiers.lua`, at the kill and again after its
  600 ms delay) ask `ChaosDungeons.runAt(pos)` and do nothing inside a running dungeon. Boss rules are unchanged (base
  dungeons: the boss stands there from the start; generated: it appears at the 85% unlock). Teardown still clears the
  area. Most monsters at once: 119 (Bones Dungeon, `keep` in `tools/spawn_tuning.json`); the generated dungeons place
  fewer. Estimate, not measured live: 0.1-0.3 ms per `Game.createMonster` with its `onSpawn` callbacks, so 120 monsters
  take about 12-40 ms in one tick (one dropped frame of the 50 ms loop at worst), plus the health scaling (about 2 ms).
  No install step: scripts only (`files` step and a restart).
- **Stuck safety (O180, owner: "stuck at 83% with 20 monsters alive").** The percent is a scan of the area, so an alive
  monster nobody can reach (a map spawn behind a wall or in a closed room of dungeon 1's widened boxes) keeps it below 85%.
  `Chaos.dungeons.stall` (`seconds` 150, `minPercent` 60, `hintEveryMs` 30000, `hintMax` 5): with no progress for that
  long the members get "N monsters are left. Nearest: x,y,z ..." and an effect on those tiles, and from `minPercent` on
  the boss is unlocked anyway (`stallCheck`). Kill credit is not involved; summons are not counted; a monster removed
  without a death is gone from the scan. The real cause on the live map is not confirmed: run dungeon 1 and read the hint
  coordinates, they are the unreachable spawns (fix them with a `patch_*.py`, never by hand).
- **Placement, one boss, boss level (O183, beta 2026-10-24: "I killed every monster that appeared and the bar did not fill. 2 bosses. Level 2.").** Cause, from the numbers of the screenshot (bar 66% with 57 alive = a total of 168; dungeon 2 keeps 110 after `patch_base_spawns.py`): since O179 `startRun` made the base list (`dg.Monsters`, one entry per species) after the clean-up, on top of the map's record; before, the clean-up always removed it. It was the dungeon a second time (about 58 monsters, unthinned, at base table positions that can be a line of tiles or out of reach) and its boss entry made a second boss next to the map record's boss. The map record's `fillFromMap` also made the boss with every other entry, and every placement was forced (`createMonster` force), which puts a monster on a wall or on another monster. The boss was made without a level, so `monster_levels.lua` showed the estimate of its type (2, 8): display only (`MD.levelOf` reads the engine level; health follows `extra[id].bossHealth` through `scaleMonster`, unchanged). Now: (1) the base list is made only when the dungeon has no start-up record (the old behaviour of every normal start); (2) `placeMonster` makes a monster unforced on its tile if that is walkable and free, else on the nearest such tile of the same floor inside the area within `Chaos.dungeons.placement.radius` (4), else not at all, and a monster not made or placed outside the area is not counted; (3) `settleMonsters` does the same for what stands there at the start (a generated dungeon's points, monsters left standing without a record): moved, or removed; (4) the boss is never in the entry placement or the roster: `placeBoss` makes it once per run (`run.bossSpawned`) at its record tile with `Chaos.createMonsterNamed(..., level)`, the dungeon's `Level`, and the tick removes a second one (`bosses > 1`, base dungeons); (5) the unlock is asked once per run (`fireUnlock`), also when the stall unlock (O180) and the 85% unlock meet; the stall hint lists only roster monsters still standing in the area. **Reachability** is approximated by the tile (ground, no solid item, one monster per tile, inside the boxes of "the area of a run"); a path check from the entry (`Creature:getPathTo`) is not used, because the engine's path search is bounded and would refuse far rooms of the 61,325-tile dungeon 2 (engine behaviour recalled, not measured here). A closed room or a one-way floor that passes that test is still caught by the O180 hint and unlock. Not run live: install `files` and restart, run dungeon 2 and compare the start total with 110. Tests: `tests/dungeons_area_test.lua` block O183.

infinitytower
- The gameplay is `infinitytower_run.lua` ("Infinity Tower gameplay"); its engine calls are assumed from the engine

stash

## Tunables
Everything adjustable is in `chaos_constants.lua`: rewards, limits, boss names, season length, storages, table names.

## Monster tiers and monster bar

`data/scripts/chaos/monster_tiers.lua` (opcode 125, client `game_monsterbar`): magic, rare and legendary monsters (health, speed, damage and experience multipliers in `ChaosTiers`), a roll on every spawn (`spawnChance`), and an ambush: when a player kills a monster a magic, rare or legendary copy may appear next to the corpse (`ambush`, `ambushTier`, `maxChain`). All numbers are at the top of the file. Not run on a server; it assumes the base server `onSpawn` and `onGainExperience` event callbacks, `Creature:setMaxHealth`/`changeSpeed` and `Game.createMonster(name, pos, extended, force)`. Tier state is kept in memory only and is lost on reload. No name prefix is set in the world (there is no `Monster:setName`); the client prefixes the tier on the bar only. Tier and boss multipliers also do not change loot.

When the tier is applied: the engine runs `onSpawn` before the placement and gives a monster its id only at the placement, so nothing keyed by the id can be written in `onSpawn`. The natural roll is decided there and the monster gets a think event for that tier (`ChaosTierRollMagic` / `Rare` / `Legendary` / `Boss`); at its first think, after the placement, the tier is applied and the event removes itself. A map respawn or `Game.createMonster` thinks within about a second; a startup spawn once a player comes near. A tier set in between (`ChaosApplyTier`: rift, invasion, tower) wins over the roll. Ambush copies get their tier right after `Game.createMonster` returns. Loading the script drops any entry an older version left under id 0 in `ChaosTierState` (the table survives a reload, so a server that ran the old roll would otherwise keep it). `tests/monster_tiers_test.lua` runs the file against a mocked engine whose `getId()` is 0 until the placement. Checked in game: a forced legendary roll lands under the monster's id with modifiers, monster bar tier and announcement; a normal kill after it still brings an ambush.

### Modifiers and shaders (monster_tiers.lua)
Every magic, rare, legendary and boss monster rolls modifiers: magic 1-2, rare 2-3, legendary 3-4, boss 4-5 (`modCount`). Thirteen modifiers in `ChaosMods`: Blazing, Chilling, Venomous and Shocking (on-hit conditions), Vampiric (heals 15% of the damage dealt), Berserker (more damage below half health), Brutal (+40% damage), Stoneskin (-30% damage taken), Reflective (reflects 15%), Regenerating (1% health every 2.5 s; never together with Vampiric: `exclusive`, beta report 2026-10-20 of a monster that could not be brought below 90%), Swift (+40 speed), Explosive (fire blast on death), Juggernaut (+60% health). The monster is drawn with the outfit shader of its strongest modifier, from the 17 shaders already in `data/XML/shaders.xml` (animated, glowing), and a rotating magic effect plays one modifier's icon at a time, so the look follows the modifiers. Only one shader fits one monster, so a monster with five modifiers shows the colour of the strongest one. Bosses get modifiers too (`bossMods`), without stat scaling. The names are listed under the bar. The client must register those shader names (base server does it in `game_shaders`; the base client base needs the same list, see below). Shader ids 5 ("blue Dortmond", name differs from the client's "blue_Dortmond") is not used.

The server also pushes `info` for tiered monsters to players within about 10 tiles every 15 s (from the monster's own 2.5 s tick), so the client can label them in the world without a query.

The `info` answer also carries `role` (`guardian` for a rift guardian, `omen` for an Omen guardian, read from `ChaosRift.monsterRun` and the run's `bossIds`; absent otherwise) and `level` (`ChaosLoot.monsterLevel`, absent when loot.lua is not loaded). The client picks the bar's look from them (`game_monsterbar/monsterbarstyle.lua`). Both are tested in `tests/monster_tiers_test.lua`.

## Chaos loot rate caps (`loot.lua`, `loot_config.lua`, details in `data/scripts/chaos/LOOT.md`)

Every loot bonus multiplies into one rate (`loot_config.lua` `rateMult`): the Loot Frenzy event 1.5, World Loot 1.25, a
rift's Quantity (up to 2.28, its own rules unchanged), Golden Hour 1.25, community stage 1.10 and family 1.30, the Marches
1.5 and shrine 1.1, Ember of Plenty 1.4, and the guild perk wrapper (`guild.lua` `G.wrapLoot`, x1.05). Together that came
to ~8-10x, and the rate multiplied both the extra-roll chance and the stack counts (an expected value of ~rate^2 x item
find). Now:

- `ChaosLoot.rateMult(ctx)` clamps the final rate (wrapper included) to `maxRate` (3.0). Extra rolls, currency, gems and
  supports all read that value.
- The rate scales the chance of an extra roll only; the stack count is `extraCountMult x levelCountMult`.
- The currency chance scale (rate x item find x orb find of the charms x Ember of the Forge) is capped at
  `currency.maxScale` (3.0), so orb find no longer saturates the entries (a normal-tier Orb of Fate stays rare; boss-tier
  entries above 1/3 still always hit).

**Rare and magic monsters, orbs and waystones (owner 2026-10-17: "Monstros raros e mágicos estão dropando loot demais";
"orbs drop too often, waystones only from high level monsters").** Numbers in `loot_config.lua`:

| | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| extra loot passes (`extraRolls`) magic / rare / legendary / boss | 1 / 2 / 3 / 2 | 1 / 1 / 2 / 2 |
| chance of an extra pass (`extraChanceMult`) magic | 1.0 | 0.5 |
| stack size of an extra pass (`extraCountMult`) rare / legendary | 1.25 / 1.5 | 1.1 / 1.25 |
| expected loot per kill vs a normal monster (1 + passes x chance) magic / rare / legendary / boss | 2.0 / 3.0 / 4.0 / 3.0 | 1.5 / 2.0 / 3.0 / 3.0 |
| orb chances per kill, magic (x normal) | about x8 | x3 (1 orb per about 18 kills) |
| orb chances per kill, rare (x normal) | about x30 | x6 (1 per about 9 kills) |

Legendary and boss orb chances, the guaranteed boss / legendary draw and the unique-item tier multipliers are unchanged.
**Orbs** (`currency`): the normal-tier column adds up to 183 in 10000, about 1 orb per 50 kills; they drop only from
monsters of level 100 or more (`currency.minMonsterLevel`; the level is `ChaosLoot.monsterLevel`, the bounty-pool level
for monsters without a scaled level; bosses are exempt, `levelGateSkip`). **Waystones** (the base server's Waystone Tier I-VI
items, dropped by the stock loot pass or a monster's own list, neither is in this repository): `loot.lua` takes them out
of the corpse again (`ChaosLoot.gateWaystones`, matched by item name, `waystone.namePattern`) when the monster is below
`waystone.minMonsterLevel` (150, owner decision open); no base file is edited, so nothing to install. Diagnostics
(`ChaosLootRoll`) have no monster and are not gated.

`tests/loot_caps_test.lua` loads `loot.lua` against a mocked engine (also the level gates).

## Time-friendly progression (catchup) (`catchup.lua`, `catchup_core.lua`, `catchup_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_catchup.sql`)

Owner goal (2026-10-15): the game respects the players' time. An adult with little time progresses fluidly, a heavy
player still feels rewarded, everyone is rewarded for effort. Every number is in `catchup_config.lua`; the numbers to
review are in docs/OWNER_TODO.md "Time-friendly progression". No command: it shows in the buff bar, in login messages and
in the windows of the systems it touches.

**Stamina.** The stock rule gave NOTHING from a kill at 14 h of stamina or less (and half experience). Now low stamina cuts,
never zeroes: the stock loot callback rolls every chance x0.5 (`tools/patch_base_events.py` step 16), the Chaos loot layer
multiplies its rate x0.5 after the `maxRate` cap (`loot.lua`, `ChaosCatchup.lootMult`), the experience stays at the base
script's x0.5 (`stamina.xpMult / baseXpMult` on top, 1). Offline regeneration is x2 (step 17; the Pact's x1.5 on top): an
8 h night gives 5.3 h back (was 2.7 h), a player of up to about 9.5 h a day never runs dry (was 6 h). A "Low Stamina"
debuff on the buff bar and one message a day say what holds. The store's **Stamina Refill** (40 coins, 42 h at once) and
**Stamina Extension** (8 coins, +2 h) are removed: paying to farm longer at full loot. Nobody holds one (the service filled the stamina at purchase); a gift of it
still queued for an offline character is refunded to the sender at delivery (`shop.lua`, "It is no longer sold."). The
Novice Pack's 5 Stamina Extensions (40) became 100 Supreme Health Potions (30). Owned extensions keep working, and the level
100 kit still gives two (earned, not bought).

**Rested experience.** Offline time past the 10 minute grace fills a pool of "model minutes": the experience per minute
the leveling model ("The leveling model and the hours", the sorcerer's base hours per band) gets at the character's level,
so the pool means the same hunting time at any level. 2.5 minutes per offline hour, at most 180 (three days away). While
it lasts, monster experience is +100%, and the bonus itself is what the pool pays. A one-hour-a-day player (23 h away)
gets about 57 minutes: the whole session doubled; a 12 h player 30 minutes. Storage 7102400 (centi-minutes), the buff
"Rested" with the minutes left as stacks.

**Returning player.** An account none of whose characters was online for 14 days gets 7 days of +50% monster experience,
+25% Chaos loot (outside the loot cap) and +50% token drop chance (faction tokens; `ChaosCatchup.tokenMult(player)` for
any other token source, guarded). The boost is per account (`chaos_catchup.returning_until`); each character is welcomed
once (storage 7102402). When the Next Goals panel is loaded (`ChaosGoals`, `goals.lua`) the welcome points the player at
it, and asks it for a hint first when it defines `ChaosGoals.hint(player, why)` (`why = "returning"`); without the panel
no such line is sent. Buff "Welcome
Back" with the time left.

**Alt catch-up.** A character below the best level of its account (season characters do not count; the best is read at
login and follows level advances) gets +100% monster experience while it is at least max(20, best x 0.2) levels below,
shrinking linearly to 0 at the best: best 500 -> +100% to level 400, +50% at 450. Needs a best of 50. Buff "Catch-up" (the
percent as stacks).

**Rested Vial.** `ChaosRested.addVials(player, n)` (the Candlemarks shop's "Rested Vial") adds `vialMinutes` (60) of rest per
vial, never past the 180 cap; it returns false (the shop gives the marks back) when nothing fits or for a season
character. Tests: `tests/catchup_test.lua`, `tests/candlemarks_apis_test.lua` (the three Candlemarks call offers light up
with the real modules loaded, and each API works as the shop calls it).

**Order and ceiling.** One `onGainExperience` callback at index 87: after the experience cap (85, so the cap does not eat
the player's own time), before the dungeon difficulty (90), the rift cap (100) and the hunt tracker. Returning, alt and
rested multiply, together never above x3 (`maxXpMult`); rested pays only what fits under that ceiling (the pool is kept
otherwise). Season characters get none of the three bonuses (a fresh race); the stamina rules apply to everyone.

**Also for limited time** (each in its own system's section): the faction weekly cap rolls over (3 weeks at most), the
season pass daily caps bank over 3 days, the bounty weekly chest needs 4 contracts (was 7), the Vocation Trials' repeat
rewards bank (15 at most), no dungeon cooldown after a clear and 5 minutes after a failed run (was 1 h after every run, then 15 minutes after a clear), the Ember
Descent's free daily runs bank up to 3, the Necromancer, Monk and Templar unlock free at account level 200 (was 500) and
are no longer sold.

**Tests.** `tests/catchup_test.lua` (LuaJIT and Lua 5.3): the config's own checks, the model, the pool, returning and alt
rules, stamina factors, the experience with its ceiling, loot and token factors; `catchup.lua` on a mocked engine (login
with the pool and the boost written, welcome once per character, the alt and its best, advance, the callback spending the
pool, buff items, season characters, a new account, the Next Goals hint, switched off, logout).
`tools/stamina_catchup_patch_test.py` (steps 16 and 17 on stock copies, run with Lua). Not run on a live server.

## Experience cap (`xpcap.lua`, `xpcap_core.lua`, `xpcap_config.lua`)

The base `player.lua` (patched by `tools/patch_base_events.py`) computes the staged experience (monster level factor
x0.03 L, stage, stamina, the store potion x2) and then runs the `onGainExperience` callbacks; 19 Chaos callbacks multiply
it (Blood Moon 1.5, Victory 1.1, World Experience 1.25, blessing 1.25, professions 1.10, community up to 1.495, Marches 1.5,
shrine 1.1, passive tree 1.33, item mods 1.15, waystone 2.0, bestiary 1.06, guild 1.05, siege 1.05, mentor 1.10, the
season modifier, the admin `double_exp` event at index 50: ~55x with the potion). The cap callback at index 85 clamps a
monster kill to `cap` (4.0) x its base: rawExp x the monster level factor x the stage of the player's level x the monster
tier (magic 2, rare 4, legendary 10: the monster, not a bonus). The potion and the admin event count against the cap like
any bonus; a season character's potion is still halved back first (`shop_services.lua`, index 5). The dungeon difficulty
(90, it goes with the monster's 1.3-13x health), the rift cap (100) and the hunt tracker (1000) run after the cap. When
the engine passes no rawExp, a recorder at index -1000 keeps the experience as it entered the chain and that x tier stands
in for the base. Player kills are not capped. `tests/xpcap_test.lua` runs a mocked chain. Pack combat ("Pack combat
(pace)"): a paced monster's base is also x its experience curve, so the cap is 4 x the paced kill.

## Custom spells and spell effects
36 spells (`data/spells/chaos/`, installer `tools/register_spells.py`, table in `data/spells/README.md`) and 52 extra magic effects plus 10 projectiles (`data/lib/chaos_fx.lua`, catalog `data/spells/effects_catalog.csv`, build commands in `data/spells/README_FX.md`). All spell effects are our own procedurally drawn art (`client/tools/sprites/gen_effects.py`): it appends the 52 + 10 and also redraws, at the same ids, the 83 stock effects and 25 stock missiles that spells and spell hits use, so stock spell scripts need no change. The spells load `chaos_fx.lua` themselves and fall back to standard effects if it is missing, so they work before the generated dat/spr is in use; the custom art shows only with that pair on the client. Effect ids above 255 work because the base server sends them as 16 bits and the client profile enables `GameMagicEffectU16`. Not run on a server. The client spell list and action bar need entries and icons for the new spells (see `data/spells/README.md`).

## Combat feedback (`combat_fx.lua`, `src-patches/0001-critical-hit-to-lua.patch`)

What the engine already does: a weapon with an element (items.xml `elementFire` etc.) hits with one combat whose
primary is physical and whose secondary is the element; `Game::combatChangeHealth` sends both values in one damage
message with their own colours (physical by race, e.g. red on blood; fire orange, ice sky blue, energy purple, earth
light green, death dark red, holy yellow) plus the stock hit effect of each type, and the client draws two numbers side
by side (verified on the test server: fire sword on a dummy shows an orange and a red number). The rarity modifier
"adds X% <element> damage" (`customs/rarity/rarity_onCombat_elementdamage.lua`) adds its part to the same secondary
damage, so it shows the same way. Nothing had to change for the numbers.

`combat_fx.lua` adds, for any player attack (event registered on the target from `onTargetCombat`, index 50, after the
rarity and passive-tree damage events):
- elemental weapon hit (origin melee, ranged or wand, secondary damage of an element type; water and arcane use the
  ice / energy art): `imbue_<element>` (418..423) on the target. Falls back to the rarity storages when the rarity
  script has not added its part yet.
- critical hit: `crit_burst` (415) and a yellow "CRIT!" (animated text, opcode 0x84, sent to the spectators). Needs the
  engine patch below; without it `critical` is nil, nothing is added and the engine keeps its own
  `CONST_ME_CRITICAL_DAMAGE`.
- `ChaosCombatFx.dodge(creature)`: `dodge_whoosh` (416) + grey "DODGE"; `ChaosCombatFx.reflect(creature)`:
  `reflect_aegis` (417) (label off by default). Neither the engine nor our scripts had a dodge; the only reflect is the
  monster modifier "Reflective" (`monster_tiers.lua`, which now calls `reflect`). Keystones or items that add dodge or
  reflect call these (`if ChaosCombatFx then ChaosCombatFx.dodge(player) end`).
- `ChaosCombatFx.crit(pos[, sourceId])`, `.element(pos, combatType[, amount[, sourceId]])`, `.label(pos, text, color)`.
- `ChaosCombatFx.config`: `enabled`, `crit`, `critLabel`, `dodge`, `dodgeLabel`, `reflect`, `reflectLabel`, `element`,
  label texts and colours, and the throttle: per source and kind at most `perSource` (3) visuals per `windowMs`
  (300 ms), one per tile and kind per `tileMs` (200 ms), one label per source and kind per `labelMs` (600 ms). An area
  spell that crits 20 monsters shows 3 bursts and one "CRIT!".

Engine patch (only where the server is built from source): `patch -p1 < server/src-patches/0001-critical-hit-to-lua.patch`
in the server source root, rebuild. It pushes `damage.critical` as the 8th argument of `onHealthChange` (existing
scripts ignore it) and removes the two `CONST_ME_CRITICAL_DAMAGE` effects in `combat.cpp`. Tested on the test server
(TFS build from this source, objects of `combat.cpp` and `creatureevent.cpp` recompiled and relinked).

## Critical and leech chances (`src-patches/0004-uniform-chance-rolls.patch`)

The base engine rolled the critical hit chance (single-target hits: melee, distance, runes and single-target spells),
the life and mana leech chances (every hit) with `normal_random(1, 100) <= chance`. `normal_random` is a bell curve
around 50 (sd 25; a draw outside 1..100 lands on 50/51), so a chance fired far less often than written, the more so
the smaller it was (measured in game: a 10% leech gem leeched in ~5% of the hits, a small sample; the exact rate is
3.0%). Area spells already rolled their critical hit uniformly. Patch 0004 rolls every one of them with
`uniform_random`: a chance now means what it says. The old effective rate, exactly (P(normal_random(1, 100) <= c)):

| written chance c | old effective rate | new value of a Chaos source (round(2c/3)) |
|---|---|---|
| 1% | 0.1% | 1% |
| 2% | 0.3% | 1% |
| 3% | 0.6% | 2% |
| 5% | 1.2% | 3% |
| 7% | 1.8% | 5% |
| 10% | 3.0% | 7% |
| 15% | 5.6% | 10% |
| 20% | 9.0% | 13% |
| 25% | 13.3% | 17% |
| 30% | 18.7% | 20% |
| 40% | 32.0% | 27% |
| 50% | 50.0% | 33% |

The engine rolls once against the sum of every source (gear, gems, tree, waystone), and the old curve is not linear,
so no per-source mapping can reproduce it; every chance was scaled by one factor, two thirds (at least 1, 100 stays
100), which gives the old effective rate at a total of ~30% (end-game builds); smaller totals now fire more often
than before (10% -> 7% instead of 3%), totals above ~35% a little less. Leech amounts and critical damage are unchanged.
What changed: gems (amethyst 1/2/3/4/5 -> 1/1/2/3/3%, cap 15 -> 10%; onyx 2/4/6/8/10 -> 1/3/4/5/7%, cap 30 -> 20%),
the passive tree nodes (client `treedata/nodes.lua`, `passivetree_data.lua` regenerated: 2 -> 1, 3 -> 2, 5 -> 3,
7 -> 5), the uniques (`chaos_items.xml`, specs regenerated), the rarity roll (engine patch and Orb of Grafting, above), and
on install `tools/patch_base_events.py` scales the stock items' `criticalhitchance` / `lifeleechchance` /
`manaleechchance` in `items.xml` and the waystone "Critical / Life / Mana Chance" upgrades the same way. Uniques and
rarity items that already exist keep the values they were made with. Class crits (Bushido, Shadowfist focus, stealth,
the Keen Edge support) are rolled in Lua with `math.random` and were always uniform: unchanged. The patch also rolls the
chance of a `<monsters>` set in a spawn file uniformly (no spawn file of ours uses sets).

## Attack speed cap (`src-patches/0011-attack-speed-cap.patch`)

Life and mana leech roll on every hit a player deals (melee, distance, single-target spells, every scripted
`doTargetCombat` with the player as attacker; an area spell rolls once per cast; damage over time never), so more hits
per second meant more healing per second. Every source of extra or faster hits, at its maximum:

| Source | Max |
|---|---|
| Vocation attack speed (patch 0002 scales a weapon's own interval by it) | Shadowfist 1300, Ninja 1400, Monk 1500, Thief 1600, Iron Sage 1700, Samurai 1800, others 2000 ms |
| Weapon: Chaos `attackspeed` modifier + topaz gems (`M.syncAttackSpeed`) | -15% of the weapon's own interval (2000 without one; -20% before 2026-10-28) |
| Dexterity of the stat window (engine: interval - dex%) | 20 points = -20% (the passive tree's dexterity is a damage multiplier only) |
| Ninja off-hand strike (`thief_combat.lua`) | +1 hit per melee hit |
| Bloodrage cleave / Cleaving Arc keystone | +4 / +3 hits per melee hit |
| Ricochet / Arcane Echo keystones, support repeats and Reprisal | +2 bounces; one hit per enemy of the echoed spell; one repeat per cast |
| Shadowfist Flurry | 2 + chi hits, one every 200 ms |
| Pets, Beastmaster companion, Necromancer minions (hit as their owner) | one hit per 2 - 2.5 s each, pet auras up to 3 targets |
| Waystones, store, world buffs | no attack speed |

Before: fastest single-target swing 832 ms (Shadowfist, weapon -20%, dexterity 20), a Ninja 896 ms + off-hand = 2.2
hits and 2.2 leech heals per second. Three engine rules (config.lua; 0 turns one off; defaults when not named):

- `minPlayerAttackInterval = 1000`: no player swings faster than once a second. The fastest vocation unbuffed is 1300 ms,
  so 1000 is reached only by the fastest classes with most of the bonuses; everyone else never sees it.
- `maxPlayerAttackSpeedBonus = 40` (25 until 2026-10-28; owner: "40%, reachable but min-maxed"): all bonuses together
  (weapon attribute against its type's interval, dexterity, the player bonus of patch 0078) shorten the vocation-scaled
  interval by at most 40%. A 2000 class bottoms out at 1200 ms; the Shadowfist and the Ninja reach the 1000 ms floor first.
  Reachable only min-maxed: weapon modifier and topaz together at most 15% (gems config `attackspeed` cap, 20 before),
  dexterity 20 (the stat window), passive tree and worn pieces together at most 12% (`playerSpeedCap`, 20 before; tree
  `maxAttackSpeed` 8, 12 before). All at their maximum reach -40%; a weapon 4 short, dexterity 5 short or tree and gear 3
  short miss it (`tests/attack_speed_cap_test.lua` "only min-maxed").
- `minPlayerLeechInterval = 900`: life leech heals at most once per 900 ms, mana leech too; a roll inside the window is
  skipped. One rule for every extra-hit source above (off-hands, cleaves, procs, pets, multi-hit spells), so leech is
  about one heal per second however many hits land. 900 rather than 1000 so a swing at the 1000 ms floor that the
  timer fires a few ms early still leeches.

**Maximum attack speed: one attack per second** (owner 2026-10-28). `minPlayerAttackInterval = 1000` is the hard floor for every
source together (vocation, weapon modifier, gems, dexterity, the passive tree, worn pieces) and is never lowered;
`tests/attack_speed_cap_test.lua` sweeps the combinations and asserts none goes under 1000 ms.

**Player attack speed bonus (patch 0078).** `Player:setAttackSpeedBonus(percent)` (0 .. 100, not saved) is counted like
dexterity points before the rules above, so it only shortens the interval inside the 40% cap and above the 1000 ms floor.
Sources, summed by `ChaosItemMods.setPlayerAttackSpeed` and held at `config.playerSpeedCap` (12): the passive tree's
`attackSpeed` stat (at most `maxAttackSpeed` = 8 in `passivetree_effects.lua`, see "Passive tree: attack speed nodes") and
the `gearspeed` modifier of rings, amulets and other worn pieces (cap 10). The weapon's own `attackspeed` modifier stays local
to the weapon (`M.syncAttackSpeed`). Without the patch the Lua call does nothing. Item share among suffix rolls (before ->
after): weapon 9.1% -> 20.0%; jewel 0% -> 11.0%; other (belts, gloves..) 0% -> 17.6%; the other kinds 0%.

Lua mirror: `ChaosItemMods.effectiveInterval` / `attackCapConfig` (`data/lib/chaos_item_mods.lua`, reads the config
keys through `configManager`); weapon tooltips add "Your Attack Interval" for the viewer's vocation and dexterity,
"(capped)" when the cap raised it. Tests: `tests/attack_speed_cap_test.lua`, `tests/item_tooltip_test.lua`.

Measured on a test server (engine built from the base source + patches 0001-0011 in order, 100% leech chance, a dummy,
30 s each; "before" = the same build with the three keys at 0):

| Build | Hits/s before | after | Life (= mana) leech heals/s before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ninja, two swords, main hand -20%, dexterity 20 | 2.20 | 1.93 | 2.20 | 0.93 |
| Shadowfist, sword -20%, dexterity 20 | 1.20 | 0.97 | 1.20 | 0.97 |
| Shadowfist unarmed, dexterity 20 (1040 ms, under the caps) | 0.97 | 0.97 | 0.97 | 0.93 |

## Movement speed (`src-patches/0018-movement-speed.patch`, client `base-patches/0029`, `data/lib/chaos_speed.lua`)

Walking was slow early (1.8 tiles/s at level 1), diagonals were broken and nothing bounded speed. The engine's own
diagonal rule was `lastStepCost = 1.5` stored in an integer, so the server walked a diagonal in a straight step's time
while the client waited 3x for it: diagonals were 3x slower for players and jerky for everyone. The 50 ms step rounding
made high speeds come in coarse jumps (a 107 ms step became 150). Patch 0018, for players only:

- Base speed = vocation base + `playerSpeedBonus` (50) + `playerSpeedPerTenLevels` / 10 (2.5) per level up to
  `playerSpeedSoftLevel` (300), then `playerSpeedPerTenLevelsAbove` / 10 (1) per level. Stock: vocation + 2 per level.
  The vocation values in `chaos_vocations*.xml` are unchanged (Thief / Monk lines keep their +10 / +12).
- Walk speed (base + haste, slows, items, mounts, passive tree, Paragon, Lua `changeSpeed`) is held between
  `minPlayerSpeed` (120) and `maxPlayerSpeed` (2600). The sum is clamped in `Player::getStepSpeed`, so no source can
  push past it and the client is sent the clamped value. Staff with `PlayerFlag_SetMaxSpeed` keep the stock limits.
  `creature:getStepSpeed()` returns it in Lua; `getSpeed()` stays the raw sum.
- A player's step is rounded up to 10 ms, not 50. A diagonal step takes 7/5 of a straight one (about sqrt 2).
- Below speed 16 the step formula went negative and wrapped to a 0 ms step; now at least 1.
- Monsters and NPCs keep their rules: 50 ms rounding, diagonal at 1x, no clamp. They hardly ever step diagonally anyway
  (seen in game: rats chasing walked only straight).

Client patch 0029 predicts the same: 10 ms rounding and 7/5 diagonal for players, 1x diagonal for others. The walk
offset spans the whole step, so a diagonal glides. Click-walk path finding costs a diagonal 1.4 (was 3), so paths use
diagonals. The constants must match on both sides; `tests/movement_speed_test.lua` reads both patches.

Tiles per second, ground speed 150 (grass; the engine's default), a 220 vocation, ms per step in brackets:

| Level | Speed before | Before | Speed now | Straight | Diagonal (was 3x on the client) | Strong haste | Paralyze rune |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 220 | 1.82 (550) | 270 | 2.22 (450) | 1.59 (630; was 1650) | 3.03 (330) | 1.02 (980; was 0.65) |
| 100 | 418 | 2.86 (350) | 517 | 3.70 (270) | 2.65 (378; was 1050) | 5.26 (190) | 1.02 (980) |
| 300 | 818 | 5.00 (200) | 1017 | 5.88 (170) | 4.20 (238; was 600) | 7.69 (130) | 1.02 (980) |
| 1000 | 2218 | 6.67 (150) | 1717 | 7.69 (130) | 5.49 (182; was 450) | 10.0 (100, capped) | 1.02 (980) |

- +15% to +30% on straight lines; level 100 gains most because 312 ms was rounded up to 350 before.
- Diagonal factor 1.4: a diagonal covers about 1.41 tiles of distance, so walking a slope costs what it should.
- Floor 120 = about 1 tile/s on grass. The paralyze rune (speed 80) and the siege's downed slow (-90%) stop there.
  A slow can still take a level 300 player from 5.9 to 1 tile/s, but never freezes anyone.
- Ceiling 2600 = 100 ms steps, 10 tiles/s on grass. Below about 100 ms one confirmed step per round trip makes
  latency the limit, and the screen scrolls a tile every 3 frames at 30 fps. A level 1000 with strong haste already
  reaches it, and so do haste + 10% Paragon + 12% item speed + 80 tree speed. Haste still adds +18% at level 1000.
- Ground speed scales all of it: on a 100 road level 1000 walks 90 ms (11 tiles/s); the cap still binds in speed.
- Lua that matches a player's speed should use the effective value: `ChaosSpeed.effective(creature)`; the
  treasure goblin's flee speed now does. Rift / tier / trial monster speed changes are untouched.

Config (engine defaults, also written by `tools/prod_config.py`): `minPlayerSpeed = 120`, `maxPlayerSpeed = 2600`,
`playerSpeedBonus = 50`, `playerSpeedPerTenLevels = 25`, `playerSpeedSoftLevel = 300`, `playerSpeedPerTenLevelsAbove =
10`. 0 for min or max means the engine's 10 / 12000. The stock base formula is `playerSpeedBonus = 0`,
`playerSpeedPerTenLevels = 20`, `playerSpeedSoftLevel = 1`, `playerSpeedPerTenLevelsAbove = 20`.
Lua mirror and tests: `ChaosSpeed` (`data/lib/chaos_speed.lua`), `tests/movement_speed_test.lua`.

Tested: engine built from the base source + 0001-0018, Linux client from the base client + 0001-0029, a Warrior at
levels 1, 100, 300 and 1000 on grass. Server timing, a protocol bot, mean ms between moves straight / diagonal:
450 / 631, 271 / 378, 172 / 239, 131 / 183 (predicted 450 / 630, 270 / 378, 170 / 238, 130 / 182), autowalk and
step by step alike. In the client, a held arrow key for 3.5 s per case, plus strong haste and a paralyze rune:
every step sent was confirmed by the server, 0 walk cancels, 0 position jumps. The client predicted exactly the
server's step and diagonal times. Measured gaps ran 10-30 ms above prediction from the confirm round trip and
software rendering. Slowed diagonal steps ran up to 220 ms over, since walk updates come once per frame.
Level 1000 with strong haste: speed 2862 clamped to 2600, 100 ms predicted, 111 ms measured. Paralyze rune at
level 1-1000: speed 80 clamped to 120, 980 ms predicted, 1000-1070 ms measured. A clicked walk 6 east, 8 south took
6 diagonal and 2 straight steps (630 / 450 ms), no cancels.

## Account passwords (`src-patches/0014-salted-password-hashes.patch`, `src-patches/0029-login-worker-database.patch`, `sql/chaos_passwords.sql`)

The stock engine (and the stock website) stored an unsalted SHA-1 of every password. Now `accounts.password` holds

```
pbkdf2-sha256$<iterations>$<salt, base64>$<key, base64>      e.g. pbkdf2-sha256$120000$XUwE...aQ==$exa6...m0zU=
```

PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256, a 16-byte random salt per password, a 32-byte key, about 90 characters. The engine computes it
with Crypto++ (already linked for RSA; there is no OpenSSL in the engine), the website (`website/`, section
"Passwords" of its README) with PHP's `hash_pbkdf2`; both read each other's hashes (checked on the test server in both
directions).

- **Migration, nothing to run by hand**: a 40-hex-digit value is the old SHA-1. It still logs in (game and website); on
  the first successful login it is replaced by a PBKDF2 hash (only if the stored value did not change meanwhile). A hash
  with fewer iterations than configured is upgraded the same way. `sql/chaos_passwords.sql` widens the column from
  CHAR(40) to VARCHAR(255) (idempotent; `tools/install_all.py` runs it with the other `sql/*.sql`, and the website's
  installer makes the same change). Until it ran, old passwords keep working but stay SHA-1 (one console warning).
  Accounts inserted with `SHA1(...)` (the Windows package's `test_accounts.sql`, `tools/loadtest.py setup
  --hash-iterations 0`) work the same way. `tools/loadtest.py setup` writes PBKDF2 hashes by default, as the website
  does, so the bots' first logins cost what a new player's does.
- **Where it is checked**: the login server (character list) and the game server (entering the game: the client's
  session key carries the password, so it is checked a second time). The engine has no other password path, and no
  Lua script reads or writes passwords (the admin panel's account lookup never shows them), so there is no Lua binding.
- **Timing**: an unknown account, a wrong password on an old SHA-1 account and a wrong authenticator token each cost one
  PBKDF2 run, so the answer time does not show whether an account exists (test server, 12 logins each: wrong password
  206 ms, unknown account 208 ms, right password 231 ms median, on a loaded 4-core machine).
- **Threads**: one hash at 120000 iterations took ~150 ms on the test machine (no SHA CPU extensions; a few times less
  on CPUs with them), far too long for the dispatcher. The check (database lookup + hash) runs on a login worker
  (2 threads, at most 64 waiting logins; more are refused with "Too many logins at the moment") and the answer goes back
  to the dispatcher. With 100 parallel wrong logins the dispatcher (status protocol round trip) kept a median of 1.8 ms.
- **Login rush on a busy machine**: the worker shared the engine's one database connection with the dispatcher, so it
  waited while the dispatcher ran the login scripts' queries and whole save transactions. Since engine patch 0029 each
  worker thread has a connection of its own (opened at its first login, the same reconnect and retry rules as the main
  one; two more connections to the database server). The account row, the character list, the character check and the
  re-hash `UPDATE` run on it; every game and Lua query stays on the main connection. If the worker cannot connect it
  uses the shared connection (one console warning) and tries again 30 s later. Checked: logins after a `KILL` of both
  worker connections reconnect without a message; with the database account locked the logins went through the shared
  connection with the warning, and after the unlock the worker connected again.
  Measured with 0029 (the test server with every install step, a 64 x 64 test map, a fresh database each run, 398
  bots with PBKDF2 passwords, `--ramp 0.15`, the bots' own start took 79-114 s on this 4-core machine; before and after
  interleaved, same machine): with no extra database load nothing to tell apart (3 runs each: login p50 0.94-1.33 s
  before, 0.98-1.14 s after; p90 1.2-2.1 s / 1.4-2.4 s; 398 of 398 every time). With the game's database work slowed
  as on the busy machine (a TEST ONLY script: the dispatcher runs `SELECT SLEEP(1.5)` on the main connection, then
  waits 1 s, again and again), 2 runs each:

  | | in game | login p50 | login p90 | character list p50 / p90 |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | before 0029 | 237, 244 of 398 (126 / 123 "Too many logins" at the character list, 35 / 31 at the game login) | 24.4 s, 24.4 s | 27.0 s, 25.9 s | 11.9 / 14.0 s, 11.5 / 13.0 s |
  | with 0029 | 398, 398 of 398 | 6.9 s, 6.8 s | 8.4 s, 9.7 s | 2.8 / 4.2 s, 2.9 / 4.3 s |

  What is left is the dispatcher itself (it was blocked 60% of the time and posts every answer); with a lighter hold
  (`SLEEP(0.3)`) both were alike (p50 1.3-1.5 s). `tools/loadtest.py` prints the login time p50 / p90 / p95 / max and
  the character list part of it. The SHA-1 migration adds a hash and an `UPDATE` (a commit) to every first login.
  Measured before 0029 (test server, full map, fresh database, 398 bots 0.15 s apart, a disk writer running beside
  it): bots with SHA-1 passwords 249 of 398 in game (89 timeouts waiting for the character list, 51
  "Too many logins at the moment", 9 game login timeouts); the same bots right after (already PBKDF2) 398 of 398; fresh
  bots with PBKDF2 passwords and the archery fix below 395 of 398. This was the load test of the map markers (about 150
  of 398 on the first run, 395 after a restart, on a 4-core machine at load 13). A real launch has PBKDF2 accounts from
  the website; the migration of old accounts happens once per account.
- **config.lua**: `passwordHashIterations = 120000` (iterations of new hashes; 1000 .. 10000000; the website's
  `CHAOS_PASSWORD_ITERATIONS` should be the same). `passwordType` is not read by the engine; `tools/prod_config.py`
  sets it to `"pbkdf2-sha256"` as a reminder of the scheme.

## Spell ids below 256 (`tools/patch_spell_ids.py`, install step `spells`)

The engine keeps a spell id in one byte (`Spell::spellId` is `uint8_t`; `spellid` in spells.xml is cut to 8 bits) and
the 10.98 cooldown packet sends one byte. Fifteen base spells had ids 258-397 and two shared 106, so for the engine
Radiant Shard (258) was spell 2: casting it put Deep Mending on its 26 s cooldown; Arcane Ripple (394) locked Smoulder
Brand (138), Break Glamour (395) Hex of Withering, Gravity Snare (396) Galvanic Mark, Shatterfrost (262) Fleetfoot
(6); and the client showed the cooldown on the wrong spell. `patch_spell_ids.py DATA_DIR [--dry-run]` (run by the
`spells` step after `register_spells.py`) finds each of them by its script and gives it a fixed free id: Radiant Shard 34,
Lance of the Grave 35, Headsman's Hurl 37, Shatterfrost 40, Quakeburst 41, Hallowed Ground 46, Fading Step 47, Crossfire
Hex 52, Bewitching Hex 53, Wash Taint 58, Dread 60, Arcane Ripple 85, Break Glamour 164, Gravity Snare 165, Riftbolt 168,
Sunder Guard 171 (Earthrend keeps 106). Three base scripts also start their own cooldown condition with the old id as sub
id (`divine_grenade.lua`, `executioners_throw.lua`, `divine_empowerment.lua`); that number changes with it. Idempotent;
refuses when a new id is taken. The client's spell table uses the same ids (`client/overlay/modules/game_chaosspells/
spellfix.lua`). Run on the test server: 16 ids and 3 sub ids changed, a second run changed nothing, Radiant Shard came
back as spell 34 with its 26 s cooldown in the client. Sunder Guard's attack group cooldown was 12 s (base data), so a
Mystic who cast it had no attack spell for 12 s; 2 s since the rotation pass ("Spell timings" below).

spells (Raise Bone Warrior 192, Raise Bone Archer 193, Raise Bone Mage 176) took the ids of the base's Fletch Crystal Arrows
(O254: Raise Bone Archer was removed; id 193 is the attack spell Splinter Volley and the trio is warrior, warrior, mage. Wildstride, Blood Pact, Mistborne Step and Zealotry became attack spells too: server/data/spells/README.md "Support to attack (O254)".)
(192), Fletch Wraith Bolts (193) and Arrow Call (176): ammunition conjure spells, switched off by the `archery` step
(`patch_base_archery.py`, `conjureScripts` of `data/lib/chaos_archery_config.lua`). The `spells` step runs before `archery`,

### Hawkeye retired, Tautstring (beta report 2026-10-20: the Ranger's auto attack stops)

Report (owner, beta, live commit 53e35f94): "sometimes in a box or a small place the auto attack does not work", then "it
stopped completely", then "it came back, then stopped again". A level ~25 Ranger, bow, Demon Skeletons and a Nightmare in a
narrow corridor; the owner found that the bow stopped while the helper's Support tab kept the stock Sharpshooter up (Chaos
name Hawkeye, stock words `utito tempo san`, Chaos words `vyr ira sol`, spell id 135) and fired again when it ran out.

What the base script (`data/spells/scripts/support/sharpshooter.lua` of the base server) puts on the caster for 10 s (12-20 s
with the base's upgrade storages 37036-37039): `CONDITION_ATTRIBUTES` with `SKILL_DISTANCEPERCENT` 150 (152-158),
`DISABLE_DEFENSE` and `BUFF_SPELL`, and a `CONDITION_PARALYZE` of `-0.7 x speed + 56` (the upgraded variants call
`setFormula` on the first condition by mistake, so theirs slow nothing). spells.xml adds the healing group as secondary
group (10 s). No `CONDITION_PACIFIED` and no exhaust: nothing in it refuses an attack by itself. The likely way it stopped
the bow (engine reading, not reproduced on a live server): the 70% slow. With Chase Opponent on, a slowed Ranger keeps
stepping after a target it cannot reach in a corridor full of monsters (the monsters walk faster than it now), and every
step that is not a kite walk step holds the distance swing until the step ends (src-patch 0042, `stepEndTime` in
`Player::doAttacking`; 0028 frees only kite walk steps). The next step starts the moment the last one ends, so the swing
waits again and again; when the buff ends the Ranger reaches its spot and the bow fires. Nothing in the server Lua aborts
the attack: the 2026-10-20 keystones (Longshot, Barbed Quiver, Opening Shot, Hobbling Shot) only scale a hit in
`onHealthChange` (`archetypes.lua`), and an error there would leave the hit as it was, not stop the swing.

Owner decision: the spell goes and a Chaos one takes its place.
* `tools/retire_cure_spells.py` (first action of the `spells` step) comments it out of `spells.xml` by script
  (`support/sharpshooter.lua`, `OTHERS`, marker `Chaos: spell retired`), whatever name and words it has; its row left
  `spell_names.csv`. The spell was `needlearn="0"`: nobody "learned" it, and the words no longer cast anything.
* **Tautstring** (id 135, `vyr sag`, Ranger / Deadeye / Beastmaster, level 60, 300 mana, cooldown 30 s, support group 2 s;
  `data/spells/chaos/paladin/tautstring.lua`): +25% distance skill for 12 s (`CONDITION_ATTRIBUTES`, sub id 71072, buff bar
  row `tautstring`). No slow, no pacify, no defence loss, no other group cooldown. Numbers: `data/spells/README.md`
  "Tautstring".
* Client: `gen_spell_data.py` writes Tautstring and `ChaosRetiredSpells` (the stock entry `utito tempo san` leaves the
  spell list; `spellfix.lua` moves it to 1135 like every stock spell the server lacks, and the helper's lists drop the
  stock 135); the `vyr ira sol` fix entry is gone. The helper's Support / Auto setup entry for id 135 is Tautstring now
  (`supportspells.lua`, timer, 12 s), so a Support row or an Auto setup that had Hawkeye has Tautstring. A Timer rule a
  player typed by hand with `vyr ira sol` stays as written (the words are plain speech now). Icon cell 308, buff icon
  `tautstring.png`.
* Test: `tests/tautstring_test.lua` (the cast on a mocked player: one attribute condition, no paralyze / pacify / group
  cooldown; the spell entry, the retirement, the client data), `tools/retire_cure_spells_test.py` (now in CI),
  `spell_ids_test.lua`, `spellfix_test.lua`.

The other stock self buffs: Protector (Bulwark) and Swift Foot (Windrunner) pacified the caster; retired the same day
("Bulwark and Windrunner retired, Ironhold and Wildstride" below). Blood Rage (Bloodlust, `utito tempo`, Warrior line) has
`DISABLE_DEFENSE` only (no attack block) and stays; Charge (`utani tempo hur`) is a haste and stays.

What to look for on the live server: nothing in the log (no Lua error comes with it). In game: while the buff bar shows
"Spell Buff" and "Slowed" (Hawkeye), the Ranger walks in short slow steps and the bow is silent; turning Chase Opponent
off (Stand) brings the shots back at once. After the update, `vyr ira sol` says the words as chat and `vyr sag` casts
Tautstring.

### Spell cap (owner 2026-10-20: "mysthic tem magias demais. abaixe pra 15. faça isso pra todas as classes")

Every class and ascension has at most 15 spells of its own (kits, counts and what each class dropped: docs/CLASSES.md
"Spell cap"; the 12 spells every character shares and the two mana shields are not counted; the three light spells are retired).

* `tools/patch_spell_cap.py DATA_DIR [--dry-run|--list]` (install step `spells`, right after `retire_cure_spells.py`,
  idempotent): `CAP` names the 79 stock instants the cap changes, by script, with the classes that keep each one. Every
  other class's `<vocation>` line leaves the instant; an instant no class keeps (68 of them) is commented out (marker
  `Chaos: spell cap`, the tag kept in the comment). The Chaos block is never touched: the Chaos spells' class lists are
  in `data/spells/chaos/spells_chaos.xml` (14 lists changed, no Chaos spell lost its last class). It must run after
  `add_vocations.py` (vocations step), which writes the class lists it cuts; on a re-run the vocations step adds nothing
  back (its conversion runs once). `OUTSIDE_CAP` names the spells kept outside the 15: Ward of the Mind (stock
  Magic Shield, see "Magic Shield" below) for the Mystic, Necromancer and Ranger lines, and Soulward for those lines and the Templar line.
  `retire_cure_spells.py` also retires the three stock light spells (Light "utevo lux" = Lantern, Great Light = Greater Lantern, Ultimate Light =
  Radiant Lantern; ids 10, 11 and 75 free; owner 2026-10-28, "Tire também as magias de luz, já que são inúteis"): found by script, commented out
  with every vocation row, on an existing server too (the tool runs on every install). Torches and light items stay. A character that knew a
  light spell has nothing left to cast: the instant is gone and the words are unknown to the server (the spells need no learning, nothing is stored
  per character). The client hides them (`ChaosRetiredSpells`, `gen_spell_data.py` `RETIRED_STOCK`) and the Helper never lists them. No quest,
  tutorial text or achievement uses a light spell (checked in the data).
* `patch_spell_ids.py` skips the retired scripts of its table (Lance of the Grave, Shatterfrost, Quakeburst, Fading Step,
  Crossfire Hex, Dread, Gravity Snare, Riftbolt, Sunder Guard); `spell_timings.csv` lost the rows of Sunder Guard,
  Earthrend, Reaver's Spin and Bramble Fan (patch_spell_timings.py refuses a script it cannot find). `spell_names.csv`
  keeps the retired rows: `rename_spells.py` still renames the NPC teachers' lines and the learned rows of
  `player_spells`.
* `data/spells/stock_spells.csv` re-exported from an install (`rotation_sim.py --export-stock`): 20 stock attack and
  healing spells left. The helper's Auto rotation presets were regenerated (`rotation_sim.py --write`): every class keeps
  a set of at most 5 with the same gaps as before; best-set damage in `data/spells/README.md` "Spell cap".
* Client: `gen_spell_data.py` writes `ChaosCappedSpells` (Chaos words -> the class ids that keep the stock spell, `{}` =
  retired); `game_chaosspells` cuts the stock entries' class lists to it (`ChaosSpellFix.capVocations`), hides the
  retired ones from the spell list and marks them never cast (`ChaosSpellFix.removedWords`). `spellfix.lua` lost the
  `EXTRA` entries of Riftbolt, Crossfire Hex, Fading Step and Gravity Snare; its `STOCK` class lists follow the cap.
* Other changes: the tutorial spell of the Ranger and Mystic kits is Minor Mending (Arcane Stitch is retired;
  `newplayer_config.lua`); the Hall of Mirrors class effect moved to the Illusionist's swaps (`chaos_class_fx.lua`).
* **Live server (install step):** run the `spells` step (or the whole `install_all.py`) and restart. Characters keep the
  rows of spells they learned in `player_spells`; nothing deletes them. A dropped spell is simply unusable: the engine
  checks the vocation on every cast ("You have the wrong vocation to cast this spell."; it skips that check only for a
  `needlearn="1"` spell, and no player spell of the installed `spells.xml` is one; the retired spells a monster uses
  are, see "Monster spells" below) and the spellbook and the client's
  spell list leave it out. Action bar slots and helper rules a player made with a dropped spell stay until the player
  removes them; the server refuses each cast. No database change is needed.
* Tests: `tools/patch_spell_cap_test.py` (the tool on a small `spells.xml`; every class at most 15, counts pinned),
  `tests/class_spell_progression_test.lua`, `spellfix_test.lua`, `autorotation_test.lua`, `snares_test.lua`,

### Magic Shield (owner 2026-10-21: "quero aquele antigo, que o usuário toma dano primeiro da mana e depois da hp. somente pra mages e rangers")

Ward of the Mind (spell 44, stock Magic Shield, words "tor ael") is the classic one again: the stock
`CONDITION_MANASHIELD` of the base server, 200 s, level 14, 50 mana. Every hit goes to the mana first; only what the
mana cannot take goes to the health (then the energy shield, before the health). No pool, no cap. The engine does the
split (`Game::combatChangeHealth`); no Chaos patch changes it.

* Who: the Mystic line (Mystic 1, Elementalist 5, Illusionist 10), the Necromancer line (Necromancer 20, Lich 21,
  Bone Lord 22; the owner counts it as a mage) and the Ranger line (Ranger 3, Deadeye 7, Beastmaster 15). Before, the
  spell cap kept it for the Elementalist only; Rangers never had it. `tools/add_vocations.py` `LINE_STOCK_SPELLS` adds
  the nine classes (the Necromancer conversion skips the spell, `NECRO_SPELL_SKIP`, so this entry is the one place);
  `tools/patch_spell_cap.py` `CAP` keeps them and `OUTSIDE_CAP` leaves the spell out of the 15.
  The vocations step adds only the classes a list lacks, so an install the cap already cut is repaired with no
  duplicate. Client: `ChaosCappedSpells["tor ael"]` and `ChaosStockSpellLines["tor ael"]` (`gen_spell_data.py`); the
  helper's Magic Shield panel follows the spell's classes.
* Soulward (spell 234, "tor anh", level 80) gives 15 s of the same condition, since 2026-10-28 only to the magic and hybrid lines (owner:
  "Deixe o mana shield somente pra classes de magia e híbridas"): the Mystic, Necromancer, Ranger and Templar lines, ascensions included
  (`manashield_config.lua` `soulwardVocations`; `spells_chaos.xml` lists the same twelve classes). The Warrior, Thief and Monk lines have no mana
  shield at all; the Templar line does not get Ward of the Mind. `tests/manashield_test.lua` pins the list against the xml and `spelldata.lua`. A character
  of another line who knew Soulward (it needs no learning, `needlearn="0"`): the spellbook and the Helper no longer list it, and a cast by its words
  fails with the engine's "You have the wrong vocation to cast this spell." (`Spell::playerSpellCheck` tests the vocation list on every cast); a shield
  already running ends by its own timer. Reload spells (or restart); the `spells` install step rewrites the Chaos block from the xml.
* Parity (`manashield_core.lua`, `manashield_config.lua`, glue `manashield.lua`): the engine runs the onManaChange events
  on the whole hit and the onHealthChange events only on what the mana could not take. The Chaos systems that scale a
  monster's hit on a player do it in onHealthChange, so a mana shield skipped all of them. Each now registers a provider
  (`ChaosManaShield.provide`): monster tiers (`tiers`), boss mechanics stacks and enrage (`bossmech`), the raid sunder and
  enrage (`raid`), the pocket boss curve (`pocketboss`), the invasion scale (`invasion`), the Vocation Trials run scale
  and take multiplier (`trials`), Rampage (`rampage`) and Shadow Twin (`shadowtwin`). The event
  `ChaosManaShieldMana` runs them in key order on a monster's hit on a shielded player (not healing, mana drain, a
  self hit or a player without the condition), and the mana pays the scaled hit.
  * The mana takes it all: the providers' side effects run (boss stacks, raid sunder, tier on-hit effects).
  * It cannot: the hit is marked (player, attacker, time, keys; `markMs` 10 ms) and each system's health event of the
    same hit asks `ChaosManaShield.scaled(creature, attacker, key)` and leaves the rest unscaled. A mark is consumed per
    key, a stale one dropped, a logout clears it.
  * Login `Chaos1ManaShieldLogin` sorts after `Chaos0MonsterDamageLogin` and before every other Chaos login event, so
    the combat log, the arena and the death recap see the scaled hit.
  * Not changed: reductions that live in onHealthChange (resistances, Vigil of Iron, Hollow Vessel) do not reduce the

### Attack kit (owner 2026-10-23: "devem ter a mesma quantidade"; `attack_kit_config.lua`, `attack_kit_core.lua`, `data/spells/chaos/_attackkit.lua`)

Every class and ascension has 10 attack spells (rule, list, balance: `data/spells/README.md` "Attack spell parity").
37 spells in `spells_chaos.xml`, each with a stub script under `data/spells/chaos/<line>/` that calls
`AttackKit.cast(key, creature, variant)`; the numbers are in `attack_kit_config.lua` (also `rotation_model.csv`; the
test `tests/attack_kit_test.lua` keeps config, XML and model equal, and casts every spell on a mocked engine). Shapes:
single, dot, circle, around, wave, line. Hits go through the school's helpers (Templar holy strike, Necromancer damage and
dots, Monk chi and finisher, Thief weapon strikes, `doTargetCombat` with ORIGIN_SPELL for the rest), so the class spell
factor applies as for the other spells. `chaos_supports_config.lua` `kindOverride` keeps them out of Support.
The spell cap is now 20 (`patch_spell_cap.py` `MAX_SPELLS`). The 37 ids are base ids the cap retires; `register_spells`
runs after the cap and skips commented-out instants, so they are free at install. Opcodes and storage keys: none new.
CI step "Attack spell parity": `tools/ci/check_attack_counts.py` (21 classes x 10) and its test. Not run on a live
server.

### Retired spells (O145, player beta report 2026-10-23: "some of my support spells disappeared")

Audit of O133-O140: no Chaos spell changed its class list or level (`spells_chaos.xml` compared before and after); the attack
kit only added spells and reused ids of retired stock spells; the only support retired in the last update is Galeborne
Stride (O136, 11 classes; the replacements Fleetfoot and Vigil of Haste are universal). Every Chaos class spell is
`needlearn="0"`, so nobody had a learned row to lose and the engine simply stopped listing the spell: the player had no way
to learn what went. Fix, three parts:

* `retired_spells.lua` (+ `_core`, `_config`): at login `forgetSpell` for every retired spell the character still has a
  learned row of (`names`: the 69 stock spells `patch_spell_cap.py` retires plus Hawkeye, Bulwark, Windrunner; the test parses
  `CAP` and fails when they drift, or when a live Chaos spell is on the list), and a one-time message to the classes that lost
  a spell (`notices`; Galeborne Stride for level 20 and up of the 11 classes, pt-BR in `i18n_strings.lua`). The notice version
  is storage 7100205 (`retired_spells_config.lua`, next to the classes' 7100200-7100204); a new retired support adds a notice
  and raises `version`. Nothing is taught: the replacements need no row.
* Client, `game_helpersupport` `deadReason`: a saved Support tab row of a retired spell (`notOnServer`) or of an id that is an
  attack spell now leaves the list at load, like the utilities did.
* Patch note bullet "Retired supports, and what replaces them" (`data/patchnotes/2026-10-22.md`).

Action bar slots and hotkeys are saved by the words they say (not by id), so the attack kit's reused ids never moved a slot
to another spell; a slot of a retired spell stayed and did nothing. Client base patch `0123` makes the action bar call
`ChaosSpellFix.pruneRetiredSlots` (`game_chaosspells/spellfix.lua`) when the character enters the game: it removes the
slots and hotkeys that say a retired spell (old stock words too) and saves the options. Tests: `tests/retired_spells_test.lua`,
`game_helpersupport/supportspells_test.lua`, `game_chaosspells/spellfix_test.lua`. Needs a server restart (login script) and
a client update (helper, action bar). Not run on a live server.

### Monster spells (owner report 2026-10-21: "Unknown spell name: arc bolt" / "dread" after the spell cap)

Monsters cast player spells by name: an `<attack name="arc bolt">` (XML) or `{name = "arc bolt"}` (Lua) without a
script is looked up as a rune or instant of `spells.xml` first (`Monsters::deserializeSpell`, `getSpellByName`,
case-insensitive), then as a built-in attack type. The spell cap commented Arc Bolt (stock Energy Strike) and Dread
(stock Fear) out; the engine printed "Unknown spell name" and World Devourer, the Eradicators, Rupture, The Rage, The
Hunger, Nightdweller, Phantom Shade, Plant, Black Stag, Golden Dragon and the Twisted Shapers loaded without the attack.
On a copy of the base server eight retired spells are in use: Arc Bolt, Dread, Frostbite (stock Ice Strike: the knight
familiar and summons), Stormlance and Reaver's Spin (Mooh'tah Master; Reaver's Spin also Mazzinor), Cinder Fan
(Thawing Dragon Lord, Feral Sphinx), Bramble Fan (Ogre Shaman) and Dawnbolt (Mazzinor).

* `tools/monster_spells.py` reads the names (XML monsters registered in `monsters.xml`, Lua monsters the engine loads
  from `data/monster`, built-ins left out). `needed_names()` adds every `monster/**/*.xml`, the repo's Chaos monsters and
  the stock / Chaos alias of each name (`spell_names.csv`: before `rename_spells.py` a base monster names "energy
  strike").
* `retire_cure_spells.py` and `patch_spell_cap.py` keep such a spell instead of commenting it out, in the **monster-only
  form** (the base server's own monster spells look the same: `###` words, `needlearn="1"`, no vocation):
  `words="###chaos <script name>"`, `needlearn="1"`, no `<vocation>`, no `spellid`, a comment
  `Chaos: monster-only spell` before it. Player-proof: the old and Chaos incantations find nothing; the engine casts a
  `needlearn` spell for a player only when `player_spells` has its name (the vocation list is not read then) and
  `player:canLearnSpell` refuses a spell without vocations, so no NPC teaches it; `rename_spells.py --sql` (the `sql`
  step) deletes the learned rows of the monster-only spells. An empty vocation list alone would not do: the engine
  lets every vocation cast a spell with no vocation entries. No `spellid`: the retired ids stay free for the Chaos block
  (`patch_spell_ids.py`, `register_spells.py` skip a spell without one). The server's Spellbook skips `#` words
  (`spellbook.lua` `Book.isPlayerSpell`), and the client keeps them retired (`ChaosCappedSpells`, `ChaosRetiredSpells`
  come from the repo tables, not from `spells.xml`).
* Repair: both tools first bring back a retirement comment (`Chaos: spell cap`, `Chaos: cure retired`, `Chaos: spell
  retired`) of a spell a monster names, in the monster-only form. A monster-only spell no monster names any more is
  commented out again. **Live server:** `python3 -I server/tools/install_all.py SERVER_DIR --only spells,sql` (`sql`
  runs the learned-row DELETEs that `spells` writes; or the whole `install_all.py`), restart. Idempotent.
* Check: `python3 -I server/tools/monster_spells.py DATA_DIR` lists every monster spell name the installed server does
  not know (exit 1); the `spells` step runs it and prints a warning per name. An install on a copy of the base server:
  0 unknown (with the tools before the fix: the eight above).
* Tests: `tools/monster_spells_test.py` (references, the form, both tools: kept, repaired, idempotent, the command
  line repair, the SQL), `tools/patch_spell_cap_test.py`, `tools/retire_cure_spells_test.py`. Not run on a live server.
