### Class spell factor (owner 2026-10-20: the cooldown ladder's retune proposals applied)

One factor on a class's spell damage: `data/scripts/chaos/spell_factor_config.lua`. Since the combat pass (O136,
2026-10-23) it is a level curve: `ChaosSpellFactorConfig.byLevel[vocation id]` is a list of {level, factor} points (flat
below the first point, linear between points, the last value above) and `byVocation` is the end value (level 1000 and
up; 1 for a class with no curve). End values: Templar 0.63, Sentinel 0.60, Inquisitor 0.77, Illusionist 0.73, Lich 0.92,
Bone Lord 0.71, Shadowfist 0.80, Necromancer 0.69, Beastmaster 1.17, Ranger 1.12, Deadeye 1.25, Juggernaut 1.09,
Berserker 1.08, Elementalist 0.70, Thief 0.91, Ninja 1.09, Samurai 1.05 (C2, 2026-10-24), the rest 1. The points keep each class's best-set rotation score at its value before the
attack kit at levels 15-1000 (no early dips, no level 200 spikes); the table is in `data/spells/README.md` "Combat pass
(O136)". Rules in `spell_factor_core.lua` (`ChaosSpellFactor.forVocation(voc, cfg, level)` and `.factor(..., cfg,
level)`; the event passes the attacker's level), tested by `tests/spell_factor_test.lua` (the table, the curve, the rule,
the event on a mocked engine, the guards).

* Where: the `ChaosPassiveDealt` onHealthChange event of `passivetree_effects.lua`, the event every damage a player deals
  already passes (the passive tree, Paragon, the class tree's factor). The factor goes on damage with origin
  `ORIGIN_SPELL` from a player of a listed class, before the tree's bonuses (they multiply, so the order does not
  matter), also for a player without tree data.
* The Thief line (C2, 2026-10-24): a spell's weapon strike is dealt by `ChaosSpell.weaponStrike` (`spells/chaos/_common.lua`),
  which multiplies it by `ChaosSpellFactor.forVocation(voc, nil, level)` itself, because the event never sees a weapon
  origin; the guard (`ChaosSpellFactor.depth`) turns it off there as well. The line's auto attacks stay unscaled.
* Not on: weapon and auto-attack hits (`ORIGIN_MELEE`, `ORIGIN_RANGED`, `ORIGIN_WAND`; a Thief-line spell strike is the
  exception above), conditions (`ORIGIN_CONDITION`:
  a burn or rot a spell leaves ticks unscaled), healing, keystone / support / archetype procs (`ChaosKeystones.depth`:
  a share of a hit that had the factor already), and hits inside the factor's guard (`ChaosSpellFactor.depth`): the
  Templar line's holy strike on a weapon hit (`templar_combat.lua` radiantStrike) and every Necromancer minion hit
  (`necro_minions.lua`; the rotation model has no minions). The Beastmaster's companion bites are `ORIGIN_NONE` and no
  event sees them; Feral Command and Pack Frenzy are spells and take the x1.25.
* Assumption: runes. The engine gives a rune's hit `ORIGIN_SPELL` as well; a rune used by a listed class takes its
  factor (onHealthChange cannot tell a rune from an instant).
* `tools/rotation_sim.py` reads the same table (`spell_factors()`) and multiplies every spell of the class: `--report`,
  the presets and `--check` match the server; `rotation_sim_test.py` checks the table and the multiplication. The
  presets did not change. Numbers: `data/spells/README.md` "Class spell factor".
* Live server: the `files` step (copies the scripts) and a restart. No database change. Not run on a live server.

## Wide spell ids and the spell id pool (2026-10-28, engine src-patch 0079)

Two measures for the 21 line-quest spells (spec: three quests per class line; the spells are added by the next phases).

**The pool (now).** "All 255 ids are taken" was wrong. `tests/spell_ids_test.lua` counted the 14 ids of
`patch_spell_ids.py` as taken, but nine of those spells are retired by the cap (`patch_spell_cap.py` `CAP` rows with no
class). Read from the tools, 34 ids of 1-255 are free in the install after the Chaos block (a run of the `spells`,
`vocations`, `runes` and `archery` steps on a copy of the base server also showed 41, because the ammunition conjure
spells 48, 49, 51, 79, 95, 108 and 109 are commented out too; they are not counted, the client keeps them for icons).
No stock spell needed retiring: nothing is left that no class uses and the tools already retire it. The pool is
`data/scripts/chaos/spell_id_pool_config.lua`: `ids` (21: 142 143 148-160 172 173 174 177 178 237, the ids of the
retired stock attack and healing spells, as the attack kit did before) and `spare` (11: 35 39 40 41 47 52 60 101 165 168 171). The test checks that every pool id is free: no live
stock spell, no Chaos spell, freed by a retiring tool. A phase that adds a spell takes the next id of `ids` and writes
it in `spells_chaos.xml`, `attack_kit_config.lua` (a kit spell) and nowhere else; `register_spells.py` refuses a taken
id, the client moves a stock entry that held it (`spellfix.lua` `chaosIds`).
Used by phase 2 (2026-10-28), in the order line by line (quest 1, 2, 3 of the Warrior line = the first three of `ids`, then the Ranger line, ...): the level 500 spells took 142, 149, 152, 155, 158, 172 and 177; the next free are 143 and 148 (Warrior), 150 and 151 (Ranger), 153 and 154 (Mystic), 156 and 157 (Thief), 159 and 160 (Necromancer), 173 and 174 (Monk), 178 and 237 (Templar). `spell_ids_test.lua` lets a quest spell (name in `spellquest_config.lua`) use a pool id and nothing else. The client's `spellfix.lua` lost its entries for the retired Bog Splatter (172) and Arcane Stitch (174).

**Wide ids (later, off by default).** The spell id is 16 bits in the engine now and on the wire when the owner turns it on.
* `Spell::spellId`, `getId` / `setId` and `spell:id()` are `uint16_t` (a spells.xml `spellid` was read as 16 bits and
  cut to 8 when stored). Conditions held a u32 sub id already.
* The 10.98 cooldown packet `0xA4` has one id byte. With the gate on it is `0xA4`, u16 id, u32 time.
* **Gate.** The client sets bit 6 of the capability byte of its login packet (the byte that has bit 7 for typed impact
  numbers, 0051). The server answers with feature 152 in the `0x43` features packet only when the bit is set AND
  `config.lua` has `chaosWideSpellIds = true`. The client clears feature 152 before every login and reads a u16 only
  while it has it. Default `false`: nothing changes on the wire; an old client never sets the bit, a new client against
  an old or off server never gets the feature. With the gate off an id above 255 sends no packet (stock sent its low
  byte and put the icon on another spell).
* Not widened: the group cooldown `0xA5` (group ids 1-4), the known spells list of the `0x9F` packet (a fixed 0-254 list
  nothing reads), the live cast (it forwards no `0xA4`).
* `tools/patch_wide_spell_ids.py SERVER_DIR [--on | --off] [--dry-run]` (install step `widespellids`, after `baserain`)
  appends `chaosWideSpellIds = false` when the key is missing and keeps an existing value. Turn it on by hand: run the
  tool with `--on` (or edit `config.lua`) and restart; the admin app has no button for it. Only do it when the
  shipped client has the feature (client/BASE.md "Wide spell ids"), then ids above 255 may be used in `spells_chaos.xml`;
  until then `spell_ids_test.lua` still refuses them. Spell ids must stay below 1000 on the client (`spellfix.lua`
  `OFF_SERVER`).
* Tests: `tools/patch_wide_spell_ids_test.py` (CI: the tool, the patch text, the install step), `tests/spell_ids_test.lua`.
  The patch applies on top of 0001-0078 and compiles (syntax check of the six changed translation units). Not run on a
  live server.

## Necromancer summons and the summon cap (2026-10-18)

Raise Bone Warrior / Archer / Mage (`data/spells/chaos/necromancer/raise_*.lua`, helper `NecroSpell.summon` in `_necro.lua`),
one minion per cast; the minion types are `monsters/chaos/necro_risen_warrior|archer|mage.xml` (looks 298, 33, 99 of the
client pair, no new art; registered by the `monsters` step like the other `necro_*.xml`, the spells by `register_spells.py`
from `spells_chaos.xml`). All numbers: `data/scripts/chaos/necro_config.lua` (`minions`, `summonSpells`). The total cap of a
class (all minion kinds together; Necromancer 3, Lich 1, Bone Lord 6 / 7 from level 400, plus the passive tree's Legion) is
enforced in `ChaosNecro.raise` (`necro_lib.lua`): the OLDEST minion is dismissed first (puff, no corpse, no loot), then the
new one is created, whichever spell raises it. `necro_minions.lua` keeps the minions of a class within its caps as a safety
net (vocation change, level loss) and gives the new kinds their animation (arrow, energy bolt). Tests:
`tests/necro_test.lua` (caps, order, numbers, spell entries), `tests/necro_summon_test.lua` (the cap on a mocked engine).
Docs: `docs/CLASSES.md` "Necromancer", `data/spells/README.md` "Necromancer line". Needs a live check: the three casts and the
minions' hits (arrow and energy animations), the replacement of the oldest minion at the cap, a Lich and a Bone Lord at their
caps, look 33 for the archer.

**No room, beta 2026-10-22** (owner: "when the necromancer has no room, the summons are blocked"). `ChaosNecro.spotAt`
took only a free tile on or next to the spot, so a caster in a pack of monsters got "not enough room". Now it looks two
and three steps away (a free tile in sight), then takes a tile with a creature on it (the spot, a tile next to it, the
caster's own); `Game.createMonster` already places with force, so the minion shares it and walks off. Never a protection
zone, a wall, stairs or a teleport. Bone Golem goes through the same rule. Test: `tests/necro_summon_test.lua` "no room".
Fields (owner: "summons do not appear in fields"): the minion types have under 50 health until `setMaxHealth`, so a fire
field on the spot killed them as they rose. `spotAt` now takes an empty field tile (on or next to the spot) before a
crowded one, and `ChaosNecro.raise` removes the field on the spot first (a puff).

**Minion spells, beta 2026-10-22** (owner: "two spells for each necromancer summon, one single target and one area"; "a
taunt for the summoned warrior"). `necro_config.lua` `minionSpells`: every kind (skeleton, shade, golem, warrior, archer,
mage) has a single target spell and an area spell, each with its own cooldown. When a minion's hit is due it casts the
area spell if at least `minArea` (2) enemies stand in it, else the single target one, else the plain hit
(`necro_core.lua` `N.minionSpell`). Damage is the kind's hit with all its factors (class, Banner of Bones, passive tree)
x `mult`, dealt as the owner like the hit; the area spells hit monsters and enemies only, never other players
(`enemiesAround(..., false)`). Melee kinds centre their area on themselves, ranged kinds on their target.

| Minion | Single target | Area |
|---|---|---|
| Skeleton | Marrow Rend x2.2, 8 s | Bone Sweep x1.2 r1 around it, 12 s |
| Lich Shade | Grave Bolt x2.4, 8 s | Soul Wail x1.3 r2 at the target, 12 s |
| Bone Golem | Crushing Fist x2.5, 9 s | Ossuary Quake x1.4 r2 around it, 14 s |
| Risen Warrior | Sundering Cleave x2.4, 8 s | Whirling Bones x1.3 r1 around it, 12 s |
| Risen Archer | Piercing Shot x2.4, 8 s | Arrow Rain x1.2 r2 at the target, 12 s |
| Risen Mage | Arc Bolt x2.4, 8 s | Static Nova x1.3 r2 at the target, 12 s |

The Risen Warrior also taunts like the golem (Bone Challenge: `tauntMs` 8000, `tauntRadius` 2, while the owner has a
target). Engine side: `necro_minions.lua` `act` / `cast`; timers in `ChaosNecroMinions.spellAt`. Tests:
`tests/necro_test.lua` "minion spells". Needs a live check: the effects of each spell, the warrior pulling monsters off
the caster.

**Minions in a hunt (O160, 2026-10-24).** A paced monster's hit on a minion is x the monster's pace damage curve (what it
deals to the owner), and minions regenerate (`minions.incoming`, `minions.regen` in `necro_config.lua`; `N.minionTaken`,
`N.minionRegen`, `N.minionIdle` in `necro_core.lua`; applied in `necro_minions.lua`: the guard and `think`). Regeneration
is 0.5% of maximum health per second in a fight, 10% per second once no minion was hit for 2 s and the owner has no
target. The Necromancer's class hit is 0.92. Balance model: `server/tools/minion_model.py --check`; method and numbers in
`data/spells/README.md` "Necromancer minions (O160)". Assumption: the model is computed, not measured in game.

* **First strike delay (class identity pass, 2026-10-28).** A freshly raised minion waits `minions.firstStrikeMs` before its first hit:
  Necromancer 2000 ms, Lich 4000 ms, Bone Lord 0 (its army takes 13 s to raise). `necro_minions.lua` sets the first `nextHit` when it first sees a
  minion (`ChaosNecroCore.firstStrike`, tested in `necro_test.lua`), so a pull, a replacement after a death and a wake from a protection zone rest
  all pay it, while minions that persist between packs do not. The class reaches 80% of its steady damage after 4-8 s (Necromancer) (the Lich ramp is 0 s, its shade strikes 5 s after the raise) in
  `weakness_model.py` (the Lich ramp stays 0 s: its shade strikes 5 s after the raise, pinned on that); the steady damage and `minion_model.py` are unchanged. Reload scripts.

## Summons: targets, walk-through, levels (2026-10-21)

Owner report: "the Necromancer's risen warriors do not attack, they get targeted and they block the way", and "the risen
skeletons' level does not follow the player's". Causes found in the code (the engine sources of the chain and the client
base read, not reproduced live):
- **Targeted, then idle.** The 10.98 creature packet carries no master id, so the client knows a summon only by its
  creature type (3 own, 4 another player's). The helper's own pick skips both (client base patch 0076), but a click on
  the minion (map or battle list) and the battle list's attack next (the minion stands closest, so it comes first) set
  the helper's locked target, and the lock path sent the attack again whenever the player was not attacking it. The
  server refuses an own summon (`summons.lua`, "You may not attack this creature." and a cancel), so the attack went out
  again on every helper tick: the player never held a real target, and the minions, which take their owner's target
  (the engine's `Creature::setAttackedCreature` passes it to the summons; `necro_minions.lua` hits the owner's target),
  stood idle. When `summons.lua` dropped such a target itself (`player:setTarget(nil)` every 0.5 s), the client was not
  told and kept the red square on the minion. Fixes: client base patch 0112 with the overlay module `game_targetguard`
  (a lock on an own summon is dropped; a lock the server refuses 3 times within 3 s is dropped; attack next / previous
  skip own summons; client/BASE.md, client/MANIFEST.md "Target guard"); engine patch 0057 (`creature:setTarget(nil)` on a
  player sends the cancel target packet). The server's refusals stay as they were.
- **Blocking.** A melee minion stands next to its owner and only moved one tile per push. Engine patch 0055: a player
  walks through its own summons (`Player::canWalkthrough`, the server's step and path check) and the creature packets
  tell its client so (`canWalkthroughEx`, the "unpassable" byte; the client's `Tile::isWalkable` honours it, no client
  patch). `setMaster` runs after `Game.createMonster` placed the monster, so `Game::updateCreatureType` now also sends the
  walk-through state. Only the owner: another player's or a party member's summons still block (party changes would need
  every summon re-sent), the summon still needs a free tile of its own, and every other rule of the tile stays (walls,
  items, other creatures, protection zones, floor changes). Exploits checked: no step into a blocked tile (only the
  summon itself is skipped), body blocks in PvP unchanged for everyone but the owner, summons still never push creatures
  (`canpushcreatures` 0, and the engine never lets a summon push), a player is never pushed onto another's summon.
- **Levels.** The spawn callback (`monster_levels.lua`, `onSpawn`) runs inside `Game.createMonster`, before `setMaster`,
  so a minion got the display level a wild 10 hp, 0 experience monster is estimated at, and nothing changed it after.
  Its hits and health already came from the owner's level and magic level. Now `ChaosNecro.raise` shows the owner's level
  (`ChaosNecroCore.minionLevel`) after setting the master, and `necro_minions.lua` keeps every living minion in step on
  each think (`ChaosNecro.refresh`): a level up (or a new magic level or passive tree) re-shows the level and rescales
  the maximum health, keeping the same share (`ChaosNecroCore.rescaleHealth`); hits are computed from the owner's numbers
  at each hit. Engine patch 0056 sends a changed display level to the spectators at once (`monster:setDisplayLevel` only
  stored it; the name had gone out with the first packet). Without 0056 the look text is right and the name updates when
  the minion comes into view again.
- **No farming.** Every minion type has `experience="0"` and no loot table, `ChaosNecro.raise` turns its loot drop off,
  the owner's and its other summons' hits do not hurt it (`ChaosNecroMinionGuard`), the owner and its party cannot target
  it (`summons.lua`), and the kill counters (bestiary, bounties, hunt, achievements, season pass, item mods) skip
  summons. The shown level is display only (`getMonsterLevel` stays 0; loot, pace and monster damage read that).
Tests: `tests/necro_summon_test.lua` (levels, rescale, the XML experience and loot of every minion type),
`client/overlay/modules/game_targetguard/targetguard_test.lua` (the targeting choice). Needs a live check: a click and
attack next on an own minion with Auto Target on, walking through a warrior in a corridor (and a second player who
cannot), a level up with minions out.

## Monster debuff durations (`tools/patch_debuff_durations.py`, install step `debuffs`)

Owner, 2026-10-20 (beta): stock debuffs lasted up to a minute; they now last at most 10 s. Every `<attack>` of a monster
file whose name is a debuff (`speed`, `drunk`, `outfit`, `strength`, `skill`, `weakness`) and whose `duration` is over
10000 gets `duration="10000"`: a slow, a rabbit or chicken disguise, drunkenness. A monster's own haste or disguise
(`<defense>`) and damage attacks are untouched; shorter debuffs keep theirs. On the base files it changes 150 attacks in
129 monsters; the Chaos monsters of the repository follow the rule already (17 attacks in 15 files cut when it was
added). Idempotent; `tools/patch_debuff_durations_test.py`. Needs a server restart (monster files load at start).

## Corpse decay (`tools/patch_corpse_decay.py`, install step `corpses`)

Owner, 2026-10-20 (beta, the ground label "Corpse: 1 item 20:41"): corpse timers and the time a corpse stays on the
ground are at most 5 minutes. A corpse decays through stages (items.xml `decayTo` + `duration`: the fresh corpse with
the loot, a decayed one, the remains); the stock chains lasted up to 75 minutes. Every chain of corpse items
(`corpseType` set) longer than 300 s is scaled down, every stage by the same factor (at least 1 s), so the loot stage
keeps most of the time; chains that share their later stages are rescaled until every chain fits. Base items.xml:
1774 stages changed, the longest chain 300 s. Shorter chains and non-corpse items are untouched; the two corpses
defined by fromid/toid ranges are kept. Runs late (before `sql`), after every step that adds items. Idempotent;
`tools/patch_corpse_decay_test.py`. Needs a server restart.

## Spell timings (`tools/patch_spell_timings.py`, install step `spells`)

The rotation pass (2026-10-14, owner: "Faça todas as classes terem até 5 magias na rotação e nunca ficarem 2s sem uma";
`data/spells/README.md` "Rotations"). `patch_spell_timings.py DATA_DIR [--dry-run]` (run by the `spells` step after
`rename_spells.py`) sets the cooldown, group cooldown and secondary group of base spells from
`data/spells/spell_timings.csv`; each row names its spell by script, an empty cell leaves the attribute alone, the Chaos
block is never touched. Idempotent; refuses when a script of the csv is missing. The csv also sets `level` and `mana`
(2026-10-17, owner debug items 44 and 45; `data/spells/README.md` "Level 8 spells", "Mana runway"): Bonebreaker (level
8, 10 mana) and Phantom Javelin (level 8, 20 mana) so that the Warrior and Ranger lines have a spell at the start level,
and the mana of Earthrend, Reaver's Spin, Scything Arc, Butcher's Gyre, Headsman's Hurl and Bramble Fan lowered to what the
Warrior's and the Illusionist's pools sustain. Rows today: Sunder Guard's attack group cooldown 12 s -> 2 s (the 12 s
above is gone), Bonebreaker's cooldown 6 s -> 2 s (second pass: the Warrior line's only attack spell at levels 16-27) and
the eight above. The client knows them all (`game_chaosspells/spellfix.lua`). Assumption: the base spells.xml has one
`<instant>` with `attack/brutal_strike.lua` (Bonebreaker), `ethereal_spear.lua` (Phantom Javelin), `groundshaker.lua`,
`berserk.lua`, `front_sweep.lua`, `fierce_berserk.lua`, `executioners_throw.lua` and `terra_wave.lua`.
`tools/rotation_sim.py --mana` checks the mana runway of every class (a full pool must sustain the best rotation for 15 s
with the vocation's regeneration) and `rotation_sim_test.py` runs it in CI, with "every class has an attack spell at level 8".
`tools/rotation_sim.py` reads the installed stock numbers from `data/spells/stock_spells.csv` (`rotation_sim.py
--export-stock SERVER_DIR` after an install) and checks in CI that every class and ascension has a rotation of at most 5
attack spells with no window over 2 s at levels 15 / 30 / 60 / 100 / 300 / 600 / 1000 and at every level where a
preset changes, from level 15 up (`tools/rotation_sim_test.py`; below 15 exempt, and every class has an attack spell
at level 8 since 2026-10-17). The snares are flagged `utility` in
`rotation_model.csv`: no preset takes them. Assumption: the
4 s attack group cooldowns of the supreme strikes and the big stock area spells stay (balance); the rotations leave
those spells out.

## Free spells (`tools/patch_free_spells.py`, install step `spells`)

Owner decision (2026-10-16): free players can use every spell. The playtest found a free level 20 Mystic unable to
cast 12 of the 28 Mystic spells. The engine refuses a premium spell to an account without premium time
(`Spell::playerSpellCheck`, "You need a premium account."). `patch_free_spells.py DATA_DIR [--dry-run]` runs in the
`spells` step after `patch_mystic_stock_fx.py`. It sets `premium="0"` on every `<instant>`, `<rune>` and `<conjure>` of
`data/spells/spells.xml` that had it set. It turns `spell:isPremium(true)` of revscript spells (`data/scripts/**`,
`data/spells/scripts/**`) into `isPremium(false)`. It drops the premium test of `StdModule.learnSpell` in
`data/npc/lib/npcsystem/modules.lua`, so an NPC teacher never asks for premium. The Chaos block is left alone:
`data/spells/chaos/spells_chaos.xml` itself has no premium spell any more (71 were premium; all 97 are free now).
Idempotent; refuses only when `spells.xml` is missing; a base without the `learnSpell` test is reported.
Test: `tools/patch_free_spells_test.py` (CI). On a stock 1.4.2 data folder it freed 83 entries of `spells.xml`.
Only spells and runes change. `freePremium` stays false. The other premium perks stay ("Premium" under the Pact).
The client follows: `game_chaosspells/spellfix.lua` clears the premium flag of the client's stock spell and rune
entries, the Chaos entries come free from `spelldata.lua`, and the Spellbook window no longer shows a Premium row.

## Engine: decay manager, hardening, spell events (`src-patches/0006`, `0007`, `0008`)

**Decay manager (0006).** The base engine kept every decaying item (fields, corpses, rings and amulets with a duration,
summons' remains) in four lists and walked one of them every 250 ms, subtracting the elapsed time from each item's
duration. Now `src/decay.cpp` keeps a `std::map<decay time, items>`; one scheduler event waits for the earliest entry
(at most an hour), so the cost is nothing while nothing is due and one map operation per start / stop. A decaying item
carries the runtime attribute `ITEM_ATTRIBUTE_DURATION_TIMESTAMP`; `Item::getDuration()` returns the time left from it, so
the description ("will expire in ..."), `item:getAttribute(ITEM_ATTRIBUTE_DURATION)`, the player and house saves and
the client see the exact remaining time (the old countdown was off by up to a second). What is unchanged: decayTo chains,
`item:decay()`, `canDecay()`, containers (a corpse's contents decay with their own timers), `transformEquipTo` /
`transformDeEquipTo` with `stopduration` (a time ring keeps its remaining time when taken off), saved durations across
logout and restart, an item in a depot or whose owner logged out stops and keeps its remaining time (a 10 s sweep plus the
checks at every move / remove), clones continue from the original's remaining time. Lua: `setAttribute` /
`removeAttribute` of `ITEM_ATTRIBUTE_DURATION` on a decaying item restart the countdown with the new value; the timestamp
attribute is not exposed. Verified on a test server: fire field and corpse chains with shortened durations, a ring equipped
and taken off, a corpse with a decaying item inside in the backpack and on the ground (also cloned), a transformed
decaying item, an item removed before it expired, logout / login (remaining time frozen while offline, within 1 s),
server restart with an equipped time ring, a backpack corpse and a depot item (all kept).

**Hardening (0007).** `Protocol::key` and the `NetworkMessage` buffer start zeroed. A `globalevent` time that is empty,
not a number or has more than three parts, or an hour / minute / second out of range, is rejected with an error line
(`GlobalEvent::configureEvent` and `globalevent:time()` share `parseGlobalEventTime`); before, an empty or non-numeric time
was an uncaught exception at startup, and a failing `localtime()` a null dereference. Not ported: the debug logging of
closed connections and failed async queries behind a `debugMode` key (it only adds console noise).

**Spell events (0008).** Four optional `Player` events in `data/events/events.xml`, all with `self` = the player and
`(spellName, spellId, spellGroup, aggressive, ...)` (`spellGroup` is `SPELLGROUP_NONE / ATTACK / HEALING / SUPPORT /
SPECIAL`, new Lua constants):

| Event | Extra arguments | Return |
|---|---|---|
| `onSpellCost` | `manaCost` | `manaCost[, healthCost]`: the mana that must be available and is paid (and trains magic level); a health cost is paid on top, never lethal |
| `onSpellPreCast` | `manaCost, healthCost` | `false` cancels the cast (nothing paid, no cooldown) |
| `onSpellCast` | `manaCost, healthCost` | none; runs after the spell, the payment and the cooldowns |
| `onSpellCooldown` | `cooldownType` ("spell", "group", "secondary"), `cooldown` (ms) | the cooldown to set in ms (0 sets none); once per cooldown the cast sets |

`tools/patch_base_events.py DATA` adds the four entries to `events.xml` **disabled** and the four stubs to
`events/scripts/player.lua`; a stub calls `ChaosSpellEvents.<event>` when a script defines that table and otherwise
returns the unchanged value, so enabling them without a script changes nothing. `--enable-spell-events` switches the entries
on (only for an engine with patch 0008: the base engine warns about unknown methods). Verified: a test script got all four
events with the right arguments, raised the mana cost by 7 and added 3 health (paid), halved both cooldowns (the cooldown
condition held 1000 of 2000 ms), and `onSpellPreCast` returning `false` cost nothing.

How the supports and the item modifiers could use them (their Lua is not changed): `ChaosSupportsSpell`
(`data/spells/chaos/_supports.lua`) wraps `onCastSpell` and, one tick after a cast, gives mana back (Thrift) and rewrites the
cooldown condition (Quickening). With the events the same effects become exact and need no wrapper timing: a
`ChaosSpellEvents.onSpellCost(player, name, id, group, aggressive, mana)` returning `mana - floor(mana * thrift / 100)` makes
Thrift a real discount (no refund tick, and the check "enough mana" sees it); `onSpellCooldown(..., cooldown)` returning
`max(cooldownMinMs, cooldown - floor(cooldown * quick / 100))` replaces the condition juggling of Quickening, and the same
function is where "spell cooldown reduction" of the item modifiers (README "Item modifiers": "no engine hook") plugs in, per
`cooldownType` ("spell" for the spell's own cooldown, "group" for the shared one). `onSpellCast` is the place for effects
that follow a cast (Reprisal's remembered spell and time, the cast context storage now written by the wrapper before
the script runs), `onSpellPreCast` for casting restrictions (return `false`), and the second return value of `onSpellCost`
for a future "costs health instead of mana" modifier. Spell id and name come straight from the engine, so `spells.xml` does not have to be parsed
(`spellsByScript`). One `ChaosSpellEvents` table is shared by everything that wants a hook: it holds one function per
event and chains the callers itself.


**Lua objects after `:register()` (0010).** The register functions of Action, TalkAction, CreatureEvent, MoveEvent,
GlobalEvent and Spell passed the script's own object to the engine, which owns and deletes it, so the Lua variable
dangled: `action:clearItemIdRange()` inside the engine's own register call, a second `moveevent:type(...)` for the next
registration, or `spell:name()` after `spell:register()` read and wrote freed memory (18 AddressSanitizer reports per
script load; arbitrary crashes when the block had been reused, e.g. after a `/lua` test that created a Spell). The engine
now registers a copy and leaves the script's object alone. Scripts need no change.

## Engine: reloads and oversize messages (`src-patches/0012`, `0013`)

**Reloads keep what creatures point to (0012).** A player or monster holds raw pointers to its registered creature events.
After `/reload creaturescripts`, `/reload scripts` or `/reload all` (also the admin panel's "Reload system"),
`CreatureEvents::removeInvalidEvents()` freed every event left without a script (an XML event whose file no longer loads or
was removed, a revscript that no longer registers it) and kept iterating over the erased entry; the next extended opcode,
kill, death, health change ... of a logged-in player then read freed memory. Reproduced on an AddressSanitizer build: a
syntax error in `creaturescripts/scripts/game_store.lua` + `/reload creaturescripts` + one extended opcode, and a syntax error in
`scripts/chaos/hunt.lua` + `/reload scripts` + a kill, each gave `heap-use-after-free` in `Creature::getCreatureEvents`. Now an
event without a script stays, unloaded and skipped; when a later reload brings the script back, the same object is reused
and works again for players who are still online (checked: 47 -> 48 extended opcode events on the player after fixing the
file). A name that comes back with another event type gets a new entry and the old one is kept, never freed. Monster spells
had the same flaw: an attack or defense that names a spell (`soulroots`, `renegade knight`, `vorgrunwave`, ... in many base
monsters) kept a pointer into the spell list, which `/reload scripts` and `/reload all` (revscript spells), `/reload spells`
(for monster types made in Lua) and the SIGHUP reload (spells after monsters) freed: a Rotten Golem next to a player after
`/reload scripts` gave `heap-use-after-free` in `Monster::doAttacking`. Monster types now re-resolve these spells by name after
each of those reloads. The same build with 0012 had no report through the three cases, a death and a kill with broken
scripts, `/reload spells`, `/reload all`, logout / login and a name re-registered with another type. Actions, movements,
talkactions, globalevents and weapons are looked up at each use, nothing keeps their pointers; no change there.

**Oversize network messages are dropped, not cut (0013).** `NetworkMessage::add*` returned silently when the buffer was full
and `addString` / `addBytes` refused more than 8192 bytes, so the message went out without its tail and the client misread the
rest of the packet (the `0x32` parse error of "Extended opcode size limit"). A message now remembers that something did not fit
(`isOverflow()`); `ProtocolGame::writeToOutputBuffer` and `Protocol::send` drop it and print one line, e.g.
`[Warning - Protocol] network message too big, not sent: opcode 0x32 (extended opcode 120), 2 bytes written before it
overflowed, to player Tester`. The packet length on the wire is 16 bits, but this base's buffer is 90459 bytes: a message, or a
batch of small messages collected for one send, past 65535 bytes wrapped its length (seen before the patch: a 64 KB extended
opcode reached the client as a 6492-byte packet and a parse error). Messages and batches now stop at 65522 bytes of body.
`extended_opcode.lua` and `Chaos.sendChunked` still keep scripts under the limit; this is the engine's safety net. Tested on a
server built with 0001-0014 and the full map: logins (the admin catalog in three chunks, 8192-byte opcode 92 parts), teleports
to ten floors and eight towns, walking up and down stairs, a browse field of 255 items with item attributes and a backpack of
20, the crafting bench, 7600- and 8192-byte extended opcodes, ten 8192-byte opcodes in one dispatcher task (all ten arrived) and
a market browse of 1200 offers (25 KB, arrived whole; the client has no market window, it logs "unhandled opcode 249" with or
without the patch): no message dropped, no client parse error. A 9000-byte string and a 72 KB message were dropped with the line
above and the client went on without an error.

## Energy shield (`src-patches/0015-energy-shield.patch`, `data/lib/chaos_energy_shield.lua`, client `game_energyshield`)

A second pool above the health that only items give. The engine keeps it per player (monsters have none) and takes a hit
in this order:

1. the mana shield (utamo vita), as before;
2. the onHealthChange scripts: resistances, dodge, block, "Damage Taken from Monsters", reflect and thorns, Last Breath and
   the other lethal-hit catches see the whole hit (what the mana shield left);
3. the energy shield;
4. the health.

Everything that takes mana, shield or health restarts the recharge delay (melee, spells, damage over time, fields, PvP).
`COMBAT_UNDEFINEDDAMAGE` (scripted health costs) bypasses it, as it bypasses the mana shield. Healing never fills it.
The recharge starts `energyShieldRechargeDelay` ms (config.lua, 2000) after the last hit taken and gives 20% of the maximum
per second (`ChaosEnergyShield.config.basePerMille`), more with "Faster Energy Shield Recharge"; the engine adds it on the
player's think (once a second) and counts only the part of the think after the delay. Death empties it, a login starts at 0
(it is full about 5 s later).

**Modifiers** (`data/lib/chaos_energy_shield.lua`, added to `ChaosItemMods.config.mods` like the legendary powers, so the
roll, the crafting bench, the orbs, tooltips, the loot filter and the Codex know them; T1-T8 like the others, on armours,
shields, helmets, amulets and rings):

| Modifier | Side | T1 .. T8 | Cap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Maximum Energy Shield +N | prefix | 12-25, 25-50, 50-85, 85-135, 135-195, 195-270, 270-360, 360-480 | 1500 |
| Maximum Energy Shield +N% | prefix | 2-4, 4-6, 6-9, 8-12, 10-15, 13-19, 16-23, 20-28 | 60 |
| Faster Energy Shield Recharge +N% | suffix | 5-8, 8-12, 12-16, 16-20, 20-25, 25-30, 30-36, 36-45 | 100 (40%/s) |

Maximum = flat total x (100 + percent total) / 100: the percent raises the flat amount only. Balance (health at level L is
about 185 + 5 / 10 / 15 x (L - 8) for a Mystic / a 10-per-level class / a Warrior):

| | Rolls | Shield | Mystic | 10 per level | Warrior |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| level 300 (item level ~74: T1 .. T5) | four flat T4 + one percent T4 | ~480 | 29% of 1,645 | 15% of 3,105 | 11% of 4,565 |
| level 300 | four flat T5 + one percent T5 | ~740 | 45% | 24% | 16% |
| level 1000 (item level 128+: T3/T4 .. T7/T8) | four flat T7 + one percent T7 | ~1,500 | 29% of 5,145 | 15% of 10,105 | 10% of 15,065 |
| cap | 1,500 flat, +60% | 2,400 | 47% | 24% | 16% |

Casters get the largest share of their health from it, as wanted, without a class rule. Five slots can carry the flat
modifier, so a character that stacks it gives up other prefixes (damage, reflect, thorns ...).

**With the other rules**:
- life / mana leech: a hit on a shielded player leeches as a hit on the health (`CombatDamage::absorbed` counts for the
  attacker's leech, single target and area); the mana shield part does not, as before;
- reflect (`item_mods.lua`): the reflected share is of what the hit takes from health and shield together;
- the lethal-hit catches count health + shield, so they fire only when the hit really is lethal: Last Breath
  (`item_powers.lua`), the arena (`arena.lua`), the ascension Trial (`ascension_quest.lua`), the trials' Last Stand
  (`trials_effects.lua`) and the tutorial island (`newplayer_tutorial.lua`); a caught hit is cut to health + shield - 1,
  so the shield is used up and the health ends at 1;
- damage over time and fields hit the shield (each tick restarts the delay); PvP works the same; healing, potions and
  regeneration never fill it.

**Other systems** change the maximum and the recharge through `ChaosEnergyShieldModifiers` (name -> function of the
player, the totals, the maximum and the recharge; applied in name order by `ChaosEnergyShield.apply`): Hollow Vessel and
its uniques (`archetypes.lua`, "Build archetypes").

**Engine**: `Player` holds the value, the maximum and the recharge (per mille of the maximum per second); Lua
`player:getEnergyShield()`, `setEnergyShield(n)` (clamped to 0 .. max), `getMaxEnergyShield()`, `setMaxEnergyShield(n)`
(lowers the current value), `getEnergyShieldRecharge()`, `setEnergyShieldRecharge(perMille)`. `item_mods.lua` sets the
maximum and the recharge from the equipped items' totals (`ChaosEnergyShield.apply`) whenever they change. A hit on the
shield shows "You lose N energy shield due to an attack by X." and a light blue-violet number (colour 131). The client gets
extended opcode `energyShieldOpcode` (config.lua, default 224; `ChaosOpcodes.energyShield`), plain text
`es:<current>:<max>`, at most every 200 ms (a skipped update goes out with the next think) and at once when the maximum
changes; `game_energyshield` draws the bar above the health slot of the character plate, eases rises over 0.9 s and hides at
max 0. Buff bar: no entry (the bar shows the recharge).

Tests: `tests/energy_shield_test.lua` (catalogue, maths, the engine's recharge timeline, item_mods glue, reflect, the
lethal-hit checks, the opcode), `client/overlay/modules/game_energyshield/shieldmath_test.lua`; `tests/item_mods_test.lua`
counts 45 modifiers.

**In game** (test server, engine 0001-0016, Warrior level 300, helmet +300, amulet +200 / +20%, armour +25% recharge:
maximum 600, recharge 250 per mille): a 352 physical hit took the shield to 248 (health unchanged), the next one took 248
from the shield and 104 from the health, the third all from the health; the recharge started 2-3 s after the last hit (the
think is once a second) with +150 per second (80 for the part-second) to 600. A fire condition of 6 x 150 took the shield
600 -> 450 -> 300 -> 150 -> 0, then the health; mana shield on with 200 mana: the first hit took 200 mana and 152 shield, the
next ones shield, then health. Last Breath (30%): a 700 hit at 300 health + 600 shield left 200 health and did not trigger;
at 300 + 100 it triggered, left 1 health and healed to 1,405 (30%). Reflect 10% on a 348 hit taken fully by the shield sent
34 back. The bar, its numbers and the violet hit number: screenshots of the test run. Not tested in game: PvP leech against
a shield (needs two clients; the engine path is the same as for a monster target).

## Percent armour (`src-patches/0016-percent-armour.patch`, `tools/armor_sim.py`)

The stock formula took a random flat amount off a physical hit, uniform(armour / 2, armour - 1): it blocked weak hits
completely and hardly mattered against late-game hits (200 armour: -150 of a 2,000 hit). Now a player's armour takes a
share of every physical hit:

    reduction = armour / (armour + K), at most armorPercentMax      (K = armorPercentConstant)

config.lua: `armorPercent = true` (false = the stock formula for players), `armorPercentConstant = 250`,
`armorPercentMax = 80` (all optional, these are the defaults; `tools/prod_config.py` writes them). 50 armour 16.7%, 100
28.6%, 150 37.5%, 200 44.4%, 1,000 80% (cap). Only physical damage that armour blocks (melee, distance weapons, "physical"
monster spells, spells with `COMBAT_PARAM_BLOCKARMOR`); elemental damage is not reduced by armour any more (the stock
formula also took its flat amount from an elemental hit with blockArmor, e.g. a few monster spells). Defence (the shield
or weapon block, two per second at most) is unchanged and still comes first. Monsters keep the stock formula: their armour
values (25-100) are tuned for it, and a percentage would have cut every player's damage.

**K.** Typical armour totals from the base items (`movements.xml` levels, median of the five best per slot, without a
shield: ~55-70 at level 100 to 300, 60-100 at 1000) plus the rarity armour bonus the engine adds to each item (item.cpp:
+1-3 at Common-Rare, +3-7 at the middle rarities, +8-19 at the top ones, on 6-8 armour pieces): about 70-95 at level 100,
95-120 at 300, 140-200 at 1000. The base items stop growing after level 100-150, so no single K gives 15% at 100 and 45%
at 1000; K = 250 gives 22-27% at 100, 28-32% at 300 and 36-44% at 1000.

**Balance** (`python3 -I server/tools/armor_sim.py <server>/data`: a Monte Carlo of the engine's rules over each monster's
attacks, 20,000 s per monster: melee and physical spells through defence and armour, elemental attacks untouched, the
monster level damage bonus, the engine's normal_random hit values; level 100 and 300: the 12 monsters with the most spawns
of the bounty pool's band (hunting level 80-130 / 250-360), level 1000: the 17 late-game monsters). Damage taken per
second from one monster, average over the set:

| Level | Profile | Stock | Percent (K 250) | Change | Physical only |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100 | caster, armour 72 | 116 | 120 | +3% | +4% |
| 100 | tank, armour 93, shield 37 / shielding 80 | 74 | 83 | +13% | +25% |
| 300 | caster, armour 96 | 228 | 208 | -9% | -13% |
| 300 | tank, armour 118, shield 39 / shielding 100 | 179 | 167 | -7% | -11% |
| 1000 | caster, armour 140 | 983 | 830 | -16% | -24% |
| 1000 | tank, armour 200, shield 53 / shielding 130 | 754 | 661 | -12% | -22% |

Other K (total change, tank at 100 / 300 / 1000): K 200: +9% / -11% / -17%; K 300: +17% / -4% / -9%. Nobody becomes
invulnerable: the cap is 80% and late-game monsters still hit a level 1000 tank for ~660 per second each. The late game
(tuned for the stock armour, README "Late game") gets 12-16% easier for everyone; a level 1000 tank in the best gear is the
reference of that tuning, so its monsters' damage could go up ~10% if the owner wants the same pressure (done: "Late-game
damage boost" below). Weak hits are no
longer blocked completely: a level 100 tank takes ~13% more from level 100 monsters (mostly small melee hits that the flat
armour used to stop), and high-level characters now feel low-level monsters (a 100 hit on 200 armour: 56 instead of 0).

**In game** (test server, a dummy monster with a fixed 400 physical spell hit, armour only, and one with a fixed 300 fire
hit; the player's armour set by an item attribute): armour 120: percent 270 every hit (30 hits), stock mean 310.3 (281-338,
29 hits); armour 200: percent 222, stock mean 251.2 (203-299, 30 hits); the fire hit 300 with both. The formula's values:
400 x (1 - 120 / 370) = 270, 400 x (1 - 200 / 450) = 222; stock 400 - 89.5 = 310.5 and 400 - 149.5 = 250.5.

### Late-game damage boost (`monster_damage.lua`, `monster_damage_core.lua`, `monster_damage_config.lua`)

The percent armour made the late game 7-16% easier (above). The owner's decision: give high-level monsters that damage
back. Monsters deal more **physical** damage to players by their level, linear between the points of
`Chaos.monsterDamage.points` (`monster_damage_config.lua`), flat beyond the ends:

| Monster level | 150 and below | 225 | 300 | 475 | 650 and above |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Physical damage to players | +0% | +7% | +14% | +22% | +30% |

- **Level**: `ChaosLoot.monsterLevel` (the one the item level uses): `Monster:getMonsterLevel()` of a level-scaled
  monster (the late-game monsters 650-1000), else its hunting level from `bounty_pool.lua`, else the experience / health
  estimate. So it covers every monster from one place: base-server monsters (no level of their own; their XMLs are not in
  the repo), world bosses, Omen guardians, dungeon bosses, rift packs and guardians (picked from the bounty pool by tier),
  tiered monsters. A monster's summon counts at least at its master's level, an invader at least at its invasion area's
  level (`invasion.lua` stores it on the invader). The other multipliers (tiers and modifiers, rift tiers and Brutality,
  invasion scaling, dungeon difficulty) apply on top, unchanged.
  The level of each monster is cached by id in two generations of `levelCacheSize` (32768) entries
  (`monster_damage_core.lua` `C.newCache`): at most 65,536 entries, and a monster still fighting survives the turnover.
  The old cache cleared itself at 5000 entries and recomputed every level with pace's ~100k monsters alive.
- **Which hits**: a monster's melee and ranged physical attacks (origin melee / ranged: the hits armour reduces) on a
  player. Elemental damage is unchanged (`elemental = false`): the engine sets blockArmor only on melee and "physical"
  monster attacks, so armour never reduced a monster's elemental spell and the percent armour did not change them. Not
  boosted: a player's summons (whatever their level), PvP, scripted damage (reflection, Cinderdeath, boss scripts:
  origin spell), bleeding and other conditions, healing.
- **Order**: a `healthchange` event on the player, registered at login by `Chaos0MonsterDamageLogin`. The engine runs the
  login events in name order and a creature's events in registration order, so the boost comes before every other Chaos
  `healthchange` of the player (resistances, "Damage Taken from Monsters", dodge, block, Last Breath and the other lethal
  catches) and before the energy shield; defence and armour come before any script (engine). With the mana shield the
  engine hands the whole hit to the `manachange` events first: that event scales it (`manaShield = true`) and the rest
  the mana could not take is not scaled a second time (`tests/monster_damage_test.lua` checks the order and this).
- **Off**: `enabled = false`; `elemental = true` also scales the elemental part of melee, ranged and spell hits.

Simulation (`armor_sim.py` reads the points from the config; "percent + boost" = the percent armour, then the boost on
the physical hit that lands; "boost" = the average over the band's monsters; damage taken per second from one monster,
average over the set):

| Level | Profile | Boost | Stock | Percent | Percent + boost | Physical vs stock |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100 | caster, armour 72 | 0.0% | 116 | 120 (+3%) | 120 (+3%) | +4% |
| 100 | tank, armour 93, shield 37 / shielding 80 | 0.0% | 74 | 83 (+13%) | 83 (+13%) | +25% |
| 300 | caster, armour 96 | 13.2% | 228 | 208 (-9%) | 226 (-1%) | -1% |
| 300 | tank, armour 118, shield 39 / shielding 100 | 13.2% | 179 | 167 (-7%) | 180 (+0%) | +1% |
| 1000 | caster, armour 140 | 30.0% | 983 | 830 (-16%) | 978 (-0%) | -1% |
| 1000 | tank, armour 200, shield 53 / shielding 130 | 30.0% | 754 | 661 (-12%) | 759 (+1%) | +1% |

The level 100 band (hunting level 80-130) is untouched. The physical share of a late-game hit lost 22-24% to the percent
armour, so it needs about +30% to come back (1 / 0.77); at level 300 it lost 11-13% (+13% back). Per hit the shape stays
that of the percent armour: a 2,000 physical hit on 200 armour lands for 1,850 with the stock armour, 1,111 with the
percent armour and 1,444 with the boost, while small and medium hits land harder than with the stock armour.

## Passive tree points

One passive point every `Chaos.passive.levelsPerPoint` (4) levels above level 8, plus `passiveExtraPoints` from quests/GMs:
about 248 points at level 1000 against 618 nodes, so the tree cannot be completed and each build has to choose a path.
On login, a preset holding more nodes than the character's points is emptied for free with a message (this covers
characters made under the old 1-point-per-level rate). Past the tree's budget, the Paragon track (below) gives small capped
bonuses.

### Boss passive points (`bosspoints.lua`, `bosspoints_core.lua`, `bosspoints_config.lua`)

The first kill of each major boss gives the character +1 passive point, once per boss (10 points in all): the five world
bosses (Kaelgor, Skaldra, The Rotmother, Nyxareth, Vharok), the Ascension Trial's Warden (type `Ascension Warden`, whatever
class name it wears) and Moloveth, Apocalypse, Vhalkareth Mortal Shell and Ul'thazmor. Bosses are matched on the monster
TYPE name, so renamed spawns count.
A kill in a pocket ("Pocket bosses") counts too, so the world boss and Moloveth points are no longer tied to the event clock
or a random raid.

- Credit, as the bestiary and the bounty board (`ChaosBounty.credit`): every player in the boss's damage map (summons for
  their master), the last hit and the most damage, plus the party members of each within `partyRange` (30) tiles on the same
  floor. A player who logged out or died before the kill is not credited.
- Storage: one flag per boss, `storageBase + id` (7101400 - 7101419 reserved; +0 = old kills checked). `ChaosBossPoints.count`
  is added to the tree budget by `passivetree.lua totalPoints` with the level points and `passiveExtraPoints`, so resets,
  single-node refunds and build codes keep them. The Paragon track is not changed: its points come from levels above 1000
  only, the boss points are tree points (248 + 10 + 1 is still far below the 618 nodes, so they never overflow).
- Old kills: once per character, at the first login (again if `retroVersion` is raised), the missing points are given from
  the `chaos_bestiary` row of the boss (kills > 0), the world boss stats of `chaos_achievement_stats` (`wb_kaelgor` ...) and
  the Ascension quest stage (3 = Trial won, 4 = ascended). Bestiary rows only exist for the last hit / most damage and their
  party (and only since the bestiary was installed), so a helper who only did some damage before that is not found: those
  characters get the point at their next kill of that boss.
- Client: a toast (`game_chaosnotify` action `bosspoints`) and a message on the first kill; the passive tree window shows
  "Boss points n/10" under the points box, with the list (slain or not) as its tooltip (`game_passivetree/bosspoints.lua`,
  `bossPoints` sent after every `sendPoints`). The tooltip first says where the kills come from (2026-10-15): the world
  boss event every 6 hours (level 300), pocket bosses any time from Adventure > Boss Spawns (daily charges), the Trial
  Warden of the Ascension Trial (level 100), the other bosses' spawns, and that party help counts.
- Spending (owner report 2026-10-18, "not working"): a boss point is not a separate currency. It is a free tree point
  like a level point (the "points" box counts it, any node can take it); the server path was checked (`totalPoints`, the
  budget check of `validateNodes`, `sendPoints` after a grant) and passes its tests. The window now says so: the label reads
  "Boss points 3/10 (+3 passive points)" (translated in the client, no longer the server's English text) and the tooltip's
  second line says they are already in the points counter. If a live character still sees no free point after a first
  kill, check the kill was credited (damage map or party within 30 tiles) and the message "First kill of ..." appeared.
- Removing a boss from the list takes its point back at the next login (a tree with more nodes than points keeps them and
  cannot grow until the level or points are back, O190); never reuse an id.
- `server/tests/bosspoints_test.lua`: the list (the five world bosses of `Chaos.worldBoss`, the Trial guardian type and stage
  storage), counting, damage-map and party credit, first kill only, the Trial Warden, the tree budget, the old kills once.

### Death and the point budget (O190)

- Beta 2026-10-24: the tree reset after a death. Cause: the login emptied every preset with more nodes than `totalPoints`
  (`refundOverBudget`), and the Paragon login saved an empty allocation when `spent > total`; a death takes levels, so a
  character with every point spent lost everything when a death crossed a point threshold (one point per 4 levels; Paragon
  per level to 1100, then per 6). Not class specific.
- Now an allocation over budget is kept at login (`noteOverBudget`, `ChaosParagon.debt`): the player gets a message with the
  number over, free points read 0, saves that grow the tree are refused until the points are back, nothing is written.
  `refundForeignNodes` skips a login whose vocation cannot be read (every class node would look foreign).
- `server/tests/passivetree_death_test.lua`: all classes and ascensions, levels around the thresholds and past 1100, losses of
  1 to 150 levels, a Thief tree on a Ninja, transient states. A tree emptied by the old login is not stored anywhere.

## Passive tree effects (`passivetree_effects.lua`)
The tree now has an effect: after every save, reset and login the summed node stats are applied.
- **Character stats** (strength, intelligence, dexterity, vitality, spirit, wisdom) become a value on a two-tier curve
  (`ChaosPassiveCharStat`, below) and get the engine's effect without being written into the character's stats (those are the
  stat window's points and are saved with the player; writing them made the bonus stack on every login and let the stat window
  refund it as free points): strength / intelligence multiply damage dealt by `1 + value/230` (physical / other types, the
  engine formula), dexterity multiplies weapon hits by `1 / (1 - value/100)` (the damage equal of the engine's faster attacks,
  which a script cannot set), vitality / spirit are +value% max health / mana conditions, wisdom has no effect in the engine.
  Characters whose stats an older version inflated are clamped once to the stat window maximum on login (`passiveStatsFixed`
  storage).
- **Attribute curve (2026-10-22, owner feedback):** the path nodes alone filled the old caps (strength / intelligence 60,
  dexterity 20, vitality / spirit 50) after 50-100 points, so later attribute nodes were wasted. Measured on the Auto builds
  (`passive_builds_data.lua`, the most of each class's builds): at 100 points strength reached 86-100 (Berserker, Inquisitor,
  Juggernaut, Ninja, Shadowfist), intelligence 71-104 (casters), dexterity 97-138 (Deadeye, Monk, Ninja, Thief), vitality
  80-93, spirit 82-95; at 248 points (level 1000) 100-350 of a class's main stats. Now, per stat (`charStatKnee`,
  `charStatCap`, `charStatMax`, `charStatKneeShare` 0.8): up to the knee (the old cap) a point gives 0.8 of what it gave,
  so the knee gives 80% of the old maximum; from the knee to the new cap (strength / intelligence 120, dexterity 80, vitality /
  spirit 100) the points share the other 20%; nothing above. Strength 60 = +20.9%, 120 = +26.1%; dexterity 20 = weapon hits
  x1.19 (value 16: the 80% is of the value, so 76% of the +25%), 80 = x1.25; vitality / spirit 50 = +40%, 100 = +50%. The
  Vocation Trial and Paragon shares of max health / mana stay outside the curve. Nothing is stored: the values are summed
  from the nodes at every login and save, and the conditions (sub ids 7220 / 7221) are replaced. Median Auto build, before
  / after: level 300 (73 points) Juggernaut physical x1.21 -> x1.16, Ninja weapon hits x1.25 -> x1.23, Lich intelligence
  +23.9% -> +19.1%; level 1000 (248 points) the Deadeye, Juggernaut, Ninja, Shadowfist, Lich and Illusionist stay at the
  maximum, the Necromancer intelligence +26.1% -> +24.0%, the Bone Lord +26.1% -> +24.4%. (A first version, 2026-10-22, was a
  straight line to the new cap, half a point each: level 300 builds got half their attribute effect.) The rotation numbers in
  `data/spells/README.md` were measured with the old caps.
- **Skills, magic level, critical hit, leech:** a permanent attribute condition (sub ids 7200 to 7219).
- **Absorbs:** the second absorb storage per damage type (977562 to 977575) that the stock absorb event already reads; `absorbAllElements` adds to the nine elements; capped at 75% from the tree.
- **Damage dealt:** `incrementX` for the type, `multiIncrement` for all elements, `incrementHealth` for healing; the event is registered on the target when a tree player attacks it.
- **Experience, loot, speed:** experience multiplier, the item-find storage that `loot.lua` reads (loot plus rarity loot), and `changeSpeed` by the difference (capped at 80).
- **Paragon:** the Paragon track's percentages arrive in the same bonus table and are added here (see "Paragon").
- The conversion factors from node value to game value are in `cfg` at the top of the file (for example 1 point of experience = 0.1%), and the client tooltip shows the same numbers.
- `server/tests/passivetree_effects_test.lua` checks the maths and the apply/remove logic against a mocked engine API and runs in CI. It does not prove the real API calls (`Condition`, `setCharacterStat`, `changeSpeed`, `onTargetCombat`) behave as assumed: that needs a server run. Speed bonuses are not restored after a death or a speed-resetting spell until the next save or login.

## Paragon (`paragon.lua`)
The long-term goal past the passive tree: the tree budget ends around level 1000 (about 248 of 624 nodes), and from there
every level gives one Paragon point (`Chaos.paragon.startLevel` = 1000, `pointsPerLevel` = 1, so level 1001 has 1 point).
Points go into eight small stats in four categories; a stat takes at most `maxPoints`, its cap is `perPoint x maxPoints`:

| Category | Stat (key) | Per point | Max points | Cap | Applied as |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Offense | Damage (`damage`) | +0.5% | 40 | +20% | multiplier on damage dealt (every type, not healing), after the tree's own bonuses |
| Offense | Critical Damage (`critDamage`) | +0.3% | 50 | +15% | added to the tree's `criticalHitAmount` (one condition, sub id 7215) |
| Defense | Max Health (`health`) | +0.5% | 40 | +20% | added to vitality in the same max health condition (sub id 7220) |
| Defense | Damage Reduction (`reduction`) | +0.25% | 32 | +8% | added to every absorb storage (977562-977575), with the tree's absorbs, capped at 75% together |
| Utility | Movement Speed (`speed`) | +0.5% | 20 | +10% | percent of the base speed, added to the tree's flat speed (`changeSpeed` by the difference) |
| Utility | Max Mana (`mana`) | +0.5% | 40 | +20% | added to spirit in the same max mana condition (sub id 7221) |
| Fortune | Gold Find (`goldFind`) | +1% | 20 | +20% | extra coins in the kill's corpse (onDropLoot index 2: after the stock loot and the Chaos loot layer, before autoloot) |
| Fortune | Item Find (`itemFind`) | +0.5% | 40 | +20% | added to the Chaos loot layer's item-find storage (`loot_config.lua` `itemFindStorage`) |

All maxed: 282 points. Since O135 ("Progression smoothness") the points come one a level up to level 1100 and then one every 6 levels (`Chaos.paragon.slowFrom`, `levelsPerPointSlow`), so the track is full at level 2192, not 1282 (before: 900 levels with nothing to spend). Characters that already own more points than the new rate gives keep them (a request that adds points is refused until the level catches up).
- **Stacking with the tree:** `ChaosPassiveTree.apply` (passivetree.lua) asks `ChaosParagon.addBonuses` to put the Paragon
  percentages into the tree's summed bonus table (keys `paragonDamage`, `paragonHealth`, ...), and `passivetree_effects.lua` applies
  the sum once. So the health and mana conditions (fixed sub ids 7220/7221), the crit condition, the absorb storages and the
  item-find storage each hold tree + Paragon together and never overwrite each other. The tree's own caps (vitality 50, absorbs 75,
  speed 80) still apply to the tree's share. A health/mana sum with a half percent (Paragon has 0.5% steps) uses the flat parameter
  with the engine's own formula (current maximum x percent / 100), whole percents keep the percent parameter.
- Whole numbers: crit damage, damage reduction and item find are engine integers, so the sum (tree + Paragon) is rounded down
  (8 reduction points = 2%, 1 point = 0.25% = nothing until the 4th). Damage, health, mana, speed and gold find are exact.
- Gold find: `value x percent / 100` of the coins in the corpse, the fraction as a chance of one more gold coin, paid as crystal /
  platinum / gold coins. Only coins on the corpse's top level count (where the stock loot puts them).
- **Allocations only go up.** Taking points back is a reset, priced like the tree's full reset by `respec.lua` (see "Respec"; it
  was level x 250 gold, still the fallback in `paragon.lua` without `respec.lua`). **Decision:** the store's Passive Tree Reset service resets the tree *and* Paragon for free (one paid
  respec for every passive point; its description says so). The vocation change resets only the tree: Paragon stats do not depend on
  the vocation.
- A character whose level fell below the points it spent keeps its allocation (O190; before, the login saved an empty one, so a death above level 1000 wiped it). The login tells it how many points are over (`P.debt`); spending waits for the level. On every level above 1000
  the player is told how many points are unspent, and the speed share follows the new base speed.
- Protocol (opcode 65, documented at the top of `passivetree.lua` and `paragon.lua`): `paragonRequest` -> `paragonState`
  `{unlocked, level, startLevel, total, spent, free, resetCost, categories = [{key, name, stats = [{key, name, desc, perPoint,
  maxPoints, points}]}]}`; `paragonApply {alloc = {statKey = points}}` (the absolute allocation; the server checks: unlocked, known
  keys, whole numbers 0..maxPoints, no stat lower than now, sum <= points owned) -> saved, applied, `paragonState`; `paragonReset` ->
  costs the gold, `paragonState`. Errors use the tree's `sendMessage` box. The client gets the numbers from the server.
- Table `chaos_paragon` (`server/sql/chaos.sql`): one row per player and stat key with points > 0. Run once on an existing database:

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `chaos_paragon` (
  `player_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `stat` varchar(32) NOT NULL,
  `points` smallint(5) unsigned NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  PRIMARY KEY (`player_id`, `stat`),
  CONSTRAINT `chaos_paragon_players_fk` FOREIGN KEY (`player_id`) REFERENCES `players` (`id`) ON DELETE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8;
```

- Client: the Paragon button next to Apply Plan / Reset in the passive tree window (`game_passivetree/paragon.lua`,
  `paragon.otui`, maths in `paragonmath.lua`). Below level 1000 it shows "Unlocks at level 1000". The "Info & Bonuses" list has a
  Paragon section.
- `server/tests/paragon_test.lua`: points, caps, validation, the handlers against a mocked db, gold find maths, the death -> relogin keeps the allocation matrix (O190) and
  the stacking with the tree in `passivetree_effects.lua`. `client/.../paragonmath_test.lua`: the panel's +/- maths.
- Measured on the test server (Elite Knight, 120 tree nodes with vitality 22, spirit 12, absorb physical 3, item find 3, crit 5):
  tree only max health 22055 / mana 6787 / speed base+80 / 1000 fire hit on the dummy 1316 / 1000 physical taken 970. With
  damage 10, health 20, reduction 8, speed 10, item find 2 points: health 23862 (18078 x 1.32: one condition, 22% + 10%), speed base +
  80 + 5%, absorb 5, item find 4, fire hit 1382 (x1.05), physical taken 950. Capped damage 40 / crit 50 / reduction 32 + health 21 +
  mana 1: hit 1579 (x1.20), crit 20, absorb 11, health 18078 x 1.325, mana 6060 x 1.125, taken 890. Gold find 20: the callback added
  207 gold to 1035 in 40 dragon corpses (20.0%). Reset (gold), the store reset, the forged requests, relog, restart and the login
  refund were checked too.

## Soft caps, Paragon Mastery and totals (O146)
Beta report (level 1500): strength about 280 against a cap of 120, physical damage 300-400 against 150, the Paragon track
full at level 1100-1200 with about 300 points left, and the gear's critical chance (about 28%) and damage (about 40%) not
shown in the tree window. All real: the caps were hard (`ChaosPassiveCharStat`, `ChaosPassiveDamagePercent` in
`passivetree_effects.lua`), `Chaos.paragon` had no sink for points past its eight stats, and the window listed node sums only.
No passive that needs a critical chance threshold exists in the repo, so there was none to change.

**Soft cap** (`ChaosSoftCap(raw, cap, H)`, numbers in `passivetree_effects.lua` `softCap`): `eff = raw` up to the cap, then
`cap + H x ln(1 + (raw - cap) / H)`. Continuous, never decreasing, slope 1 at the cap, no upper bound.
- Damage percents (physical, the elements, all elements): cap 150, H 60. Raw 300 gives 225.2, 400 gives 248.5, 1000 gives 313.1.
- Attributes: the points past the cap are soft capped with H = the cap (wisdom 40), then follow the curve's slope at the cap
  (`max x (1 - knee share) / (cap - knee)`). 280 strength counts as 221.7 points, about +7% damage over 120. Dexterity is a
  divisor and stays under a value of 50. Vitality 300 gives +72% max health (cap +50%).
- Hard on purpose: absorb (75, engine patch 0049 ceiling) and speed (80).
PvP stays bounded: three times the cap in points gives under +45% of the capped value (+35% dexterity). `tests/softcap_test.lua`
checks the properties and numbers; `weapon_sim.py --power --check`, `rotation_sim` and the PvP balance tests are unchanged.

**Paragon Mastery** (`Chaos.paragon.mastery`, `paragon.lua`): seven endless masteries, a rank costs 1 point, `n` ranks give
`scale x ln(1 + n / h)` percent on the same bonus as the category stat (damage 6/50, crit damage 8/50, health 8/50,
reduction 3/60, mana 8/50, gold find 10/50, item find 8/50). 300 damage ranks give +11.67%. At most 60000 ranks per mastery
(`chaos_paragon` rows, smallint: no DB migration). No crit chance or speed mastery: crit chance is a PvP lever and speed is
an integer condition. **Exchange** (`Chaos.paragon.exchange`, ratio 1): free passive tree points become Paragon points for
good; the count is in storage 7102500, subtracted in `passivetree.lua totalPoints`, added in `ChaosParagon.pointsOf`.
Points earned after the track is full stay free and are never lost.
Protocol (opcode 65): `paragonMastery {key, n}`, `paragonConvert {n}` in; `paragonState` gains `mastery {maxRanks, rows[]}` and
`exchange {ratio, treeFree, converted}`. Build codes carry the category stats only (`buildshare.lua`); loadouts check both.

**Totals** (`passivetree_totals.lua`, rules `passivetree_totals_core.lua`): request `statTotals`, answer `statTotals
{attributes[], damage[], crit {chance {total, tree, other}, amount {total, tree, paragon, other}}}` (rate limit 300 ms). The
crit totals are the engine's own value (gear, gems, blessings, tree, Paragon). Client: `totals.lua`, `totalsview.lua`.

**Critical reach** (`luajit tools/crit_reach.lua`, from the item mod, crafting, gem and tree tables). The T8 critical modifier
(item level 140+) rolls amount 8-10 and gives chance 5-7 (9 at +30% quality) on each of 8 slots:

| Source | Critical chance |
|---|---|
| Gear, 8 slots T8: lowest / average / highest roll | 40 / 48 / 56 (72 with quality) |
| Gear, T7 only: average / highest | 40 / 48 |
| Gems | 10 (damage 75) |
| Tree crit nodes of a class: best / median / worst | 40 / 29 / 15 |
| Trial node, Keen Edge mastery | 5, 2 (damage 30, 5) |
| Ceiling / dedicated build / casual build | 129 / 68 / 30 |

A gated passive should ask for at most 45% (halfway between the casual and the dedicated build); 70-80% needs the ceiling
case. Critical damage ceiling 214 from gear, gems, trial and mastery, plus Paragon 15.
Deploy: server `files` step and a restart, client update, no DB migration.

## Passive tree keystones (`passivetree_keystones.lua`)
Two new paths at the edge of the tree, each two notables and a keystone (1 point per node, like every node): **Wrath**
(619 Gathering Fury, 620 Edge of Ruin, keystone 621; starts at node 600, north-east) and **Resolve** (622 Iron Resolve,
623 Unbroken Will, keystone 624; starts at node 489, south-west). Both keystones sit about 25 nodes from the start, like the
divine nodes. A keystone node has one variant per vocation (`knight = {...}`, `paladin = {...}` in the client's `nodes.lua`; the
generator writes them to `v` in `passivetree_data.lua`, and `ChaosPassiveTree.getBonuses` takes the variant of the player's
vocation, by the vocation's client id). The server also sends the vocation key with `sendNodes`, so the client shows the same
variant the server applies (the client's own vocation number did not match: an Elite Knight reported 4, "druid").

| Vocation | Wrath (621) | Resolve (624) |
|---|---|---|
| Knight | Cleaving Arc: two-handed melee hits also hit up to 3 other enemies next to you for 40% | Bulwark: with a shield, 15% to block a melee/ranged attack completely; 30% of melee damage taken reflected |
| Paladin | Ricochet: bow/crossbow hits, 100% to bounce (owner 2026-10-17; it was 30%) to the nearest other enemy within 4 sqm for 65%, then once more for 42%; never the same target twice | Deadeye: a crossbow (no ammunition needed), 15% for a shot with double damage |
| Sorcerer | Arcane Echo: a spell hitting 2+ enemies, 35% to repeat 0.6 s later on the same spots for 50%; 3 s cooldown | Elemental Overload: a spell hit primes the other elements, the next spell of another element within 8 s deals +20% |
| Iron Sage (621) / Sentinel (624), the old druid pair, since 2026-10-12 | Overgrowth (Iron Sage): heals on others heal 10% more over 6 s (3 pulses; 30% for the old druid) | Thorns (Sentinel): melee/ranged attackers take 30% of their hit + 2 x magic level as earth damage |
| Illusionist (support) | Shared Phantasm: your hits mark the enemy for 6 s; other party members deal +12% to it | Inspiring Illusion: other party members within 8 sqm deal +8% damage |
| Thief, Ninja, Samurai (2026-10-20) | Shadow Twin: weapon hits (melee or ranged, not a wand), 30% for the shadow to strike the same target again 0.3 s later for 60%; price: you take 6% more damage | Viper's Verdict: weapon hits on a poisoned target, 20% to strike a vital for x2; weapon hits on a target that is not poisoned x0.85 |
| Necromancer, Lich, Bone Lord (2026-10-20) | Corpse Detonation: a monster you or your minions kill explodes, 12% of its maximum health (at most 15 x your level) as death on up to 6 enemies within 2 sqm; an explosion's kill does not explode; price: your and your minions' hits x0.92 | Reaper's Toll: your and your minions' hits on a monster at 40% health or less x2, above x0.92 |
| Monk, Shadowfist (2026-10-20; the Iron Sage keeps Overgrowth) | Seventh Palm: every 5th melee hit (fists or a melee weapon, 4 s window) is a finisher, x2.2 and a shockwave of 50% of it on up to 4 enemies next to the target; the other melee hits x0.90 | Piercing Palm (the Iron Sage too): a melee hit passes through, the nearest enemy next to the target and farther from you takes 70%, the next one behind it 40%; the hit x0.95 |
| Templar, Inquisitor (2026-10-20; the Sentinel keeps Thorns) | Radiant Rebuke (the Sentinel too): with a shield, 20% to block a melee/ranged hit completely; a block sends a holy nova (at most one a second) on up to 8 enemies within 2 sqm for the blocked hit + 4 x magic level; your weapon hits x0.90 | Dawnchain: melee weapon hits chain holy light to the nearest other enemy within 3 sqm (in sight) for 55%, then 55% of that (30%); your spells x0.90 |

- **Signature keystones of the Thief, Necromancer, Monk and Templar lines (2026-10-20).** The owner asked for nodes "like
  Ricochet and Deadeye for all classes". Those four lines had only their class section keystones and the main tree
  archetypes: a poison buff (Blackblood Creed), minion and aura scaling, a no-evasion trade, a stance tweak; nothing that
  shows in every fight the way a bouncing bolt or a doubled shot does. Each class of the four lines now has its own pair
  on 621 / 624 (the rows above; variant key = class key, `ChaosClasses.keystoneKey`), so every one of the 21 classes may
  take both nodes. Numbers `class_keystones_config.lua`, rules `class_keystones_core.lua`, glue here. No character of
  those classes could hold 621 / 624 before (the class check of every save and the login sanitize refused them) and the
  ids, links and meaning for every other class are unchanged, so nothing is refunded (no `reworked` version) and the build
  code format stays 6. Weapon procs (Shadow Twin, Seventh Palm's shockwave, Piercing Palm, Dawnchain, Radiant Rebuke's
  nova) are dealt like Ricochet (guarded, `ORIGIN_SPELL`, PvP rules). The pure factors (Corpse Detonation's price,
  Reaper's Toll, Dawnchain's spell price) are a second event, `ChaosClassKeystones`, on every monster from its spawn
  (EventCallback onSpawn index 11) and on every player from login, so area spells and minion hits on monsters nobody
  targeted count too (a factor does not depend on the event order); `ChaosClassKeystonesDeath` (same registration)
  sets off Corpse Detonation. Every new branch runs in `pcall`: an error is printed and the hit lands unchanged.
  Visuals: Shadow Twin `shadow_smoke`, Viper's Verdict `poison_burst` + crit, Corpse Detonation `necro_skull`, Reaper's
  Toll `shadow_flame` once per monster, Seventh Palm `crit_burst` + `ground_slam`, Piercing Palm `shockwave`, Radiant
  Rebuke block + `holy_spiral`, Dawnchain `holy_bolt` missile + `holy_cross`. Icons: `keystones.png` cells 52-59.
  Computed balance against Ricochet and Deadeye (`ChaosClassKeystones.model`, asserted in the test):
  `data/spells/README.md` "Signature keystones of the Thief, Necromancer, Monk and Templar lines". Not measured in
  game. Test: `tests/class_keystones_test.lua`.
- Every extra hit (cleave, ricochet, echo, reflect, thorns) is dealt from an `addEvent` with `ChaosKeystones.depth > 0` and
  `ORIGIN_SPELL`: no keystone, no passive bonus (`passivetree_effects.lua` skips it) and no weapon style (two-handed factor, arrow
  splash) applies to it, so nothing chains. Targets: monsters that are not a player's summon; players only where
  `ChaosSpell.canAttack` (the PvP rules) allows it. The illusionist bonuses need a party, never apply to the illusionist and are
  not given or received by multi-client characters (`Chaos.isMultiClient`).
- Overgrowth's regrowth (since 2026-10-12) is plain health (`Chaos.heal`, no health event): the healer's bonuses (stat window,
  tree, healing rules) count once, in the heal that planted it; a heal in PvP combat plants the reduced share. Before, each
  pulse was a new heal by the healer and got them again (41% instead of 30% in game). A new heal on the same player adds its
  share to what is left and starts the 3 pulses again, so no share is lost (before, it replaced the running regrowth).
  Heals over time (`ORIGIN_CONDITION`) and self heals plant nothing. The pulses are not in the combat log.
- The event order matters: the keystones' `onTargetCombat` callback registers with index 1, after the passive tree's and the weapon
  style's (index 0), so the cleave/ricochet share is taken of the hit after the passive bonuses and the two-handed factor.
- Visuals: cleave `blood_slash`, ricochet a bolt/arrow missile between the targets, Deadeye `holy_cross`, echo `arcane_burst` on each
  tile, overload `arcane_circle` on the caster, regrowth plants then `heal_sparkle`, thorns an earth missile and plant attack, Bulwark
  the block / shockwave effect, Shared Phantasm `arcane_circle` on a newly marked enemy; plus `ChaosCombatFx.dodge/reflect/crit`
  when that module is loaded. Icons: `client/tools/gen_keystone_icons.py` -> `data/images/passivetree/keystones.png`.
- Measured on the test server (level 1000, 60-120 s of auto attack against the balance dummies, 5 dummies, two next to the knight):
  knight two-handed 456/s on the main dummy, with Cleaving Arc 503/s main + 454/s on the 2 neighbours; paladin crossbow 766/s single,
  Deadeye 833/s (+9% in 90 s, +15% expected), Ricochet 742/s main + 312/s on the others; sorcerer Rime Bloom 5150 per cast on 5 targets,
  every cast echoing 7490 (+45%), with the real 35% chance +16% expected; alternating ice and fire spells +15% with Overload; Thorns
  reflected 569 per 970 melee hit (magic level 157), Bulwark blocked 2 of 20 hits and reflected 329 per hit.
- Verified in game (2026-10-12, level 300, two clients; numbers and screenshots in `data/spells/README.md` "Keystones
  verified in game"): Ricochet chains on 33% of crossbow hits (83 of 254), each bounce 65% of the one before; Deadeye
  doubles 14% of the shots (golden cross and "CRIT!"); Bulwark blocks 14% (10 of 70 hits, "DODGE") and reflects 30% of
  the rest (shockwave, aegis); Inspiring Illusion +8% (1296 for 1200) and a marked enemy +20% (1440: the two add up)
  for the other party member, nothing for the Illusionist's own hits and nothing between two characters of one IP
  (multi-client rule); the mark heals the ally 4% of its hits (before the healer's bonuses). Overgrowth and Thorns work
  when forced on a character for the test (3 pulses at 2 / 4 / 6 s; 30% + 2 x magic level as earth damage); no class
  could take them then. Since 2026-10-12 the Iron Sage has Overgrowth and the Sentinel Thorns (computed, not measured;
  "Passive tree: class sections"). Every proc is dealt by a player,
  so the base engine's stat window (+1% per strength or intelligence point) and, on heals, the healer's healing rules
  (Weaver's Grace +16%) still apply to it; the passive tree's bonuses do not.
- `server/tests/passivetree_keystones_test.lua`: chance maths, cleave and ricochet target choice, echo cooldown, overload priming, party
  bonus, the engine glue against mocked creatures, the recursion guard, the per-vocation data and that the client tooltips state the
  server's numbers.
