## Passive tree planner and mastery nodes (`passivetree_core.lua`, `passivetree_config.lua`, client `game_passivetree`)
The tree window plans a whole allocation and applies it in one request; four mastery nodes let the player pick one
effect. Rules in `passivetree_core.lua` (pure), numbers in `passivetree_config.lua` and the tree data.
- **Planner (client `treeplan.lua`, `planner.lua`).** A left click on a node that is not allocated plans the shortest
  path to it from the allocated set and the plan: a breadth-first walk over the nodes the class may take (another line's
  section, a locked ascended path and start nodes are not walked). Planned nodes get a blue-tinted frame (the `checked`
  state of the node styles), their links the allocation's edge style. A click on a planned node takes it out with every
  planned node that hangs on it. The plan bar (bottom right) shows "Plan: n / free points" (red when short) with Undo,
  Redo (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y, whole plan states, 100 deep) and Clear Plan. "Info & Bonuses" lists the plan's bonuses under
  PLANNED. Apply Plan sends the whole plan once. The Paragon track does not interact (its points are separate).
- **Server check (`planApply {nodes, masteries}`).** Ids the character already holds are first left out of the plan (`dropOwned`; a client view that was a step behind is no reason to refuse the rest; a plan of nothing else answers "You already have those nodes" and sends `sendNodes` so the client catches up; 2026-10-20 beta report "Node N is already allocated"). `validatePlan` then checks the whole plan like a save, then the plain
  save's `validateNodes` runs on the final list: a table of 1 to `maxPlanNodes` (300) ids, every id known and not the
  root, no id twice, none already allocated, every node one the class may hold (`ChaosClassTree.allowed`: class sections
  and ascended paths), saved + planned <= points owned, every planned node connected to the start through saved and
  planned nodes, every planned mastery with a valid effect, no effect for a saved mastery. All of it is saved at once, or
  nothing, with the reason in `planResult {ok, message}`. Same rate limit as a save (one a second, key
  `passivetree.save`); the tree has no zone or combat rule today and the planner adds none.
- **Nodes 669-672 (O251, changed in O273)**: four nodes in own groups 105-108 on a side branch of Mercy of Embers (358). They gave
  Everfull flask charges; the flasks never empty now, so they give vitality and spirit (669 and 671 +1 spirit, 670 +1 vitality,
  672 "Bottomless Flasks" +2 vitality and +2 spirit). The class lanes never touch them (a dead-end branch). See "Potions".
- **Mastery nodes 665-668** (one per class section, above its third line node; any class of the line may take it): 1
  point like every node; 3 or 4 effects of ordinary tree stats, about one notable each (no new combat code). The effect
  is picked while the node is planned (free, changeable until Apply). Changing the effect of a saved mastery
  (`masteryChoose {id, choice}`) costs the single-node refund price of `respec.lua` (free below level 50); a refund or a
  reset drops the choice. Numbers: `treedata/nodes.lua` (`masteries`), generated into `passivetree_data.lua` as `m`.

| Line | Mastery (node) | Effects |
|---|---|---|
| Thief | Shadow Discipline (665) | Keen Edge: crit chance +2, crit amount +5 / Light Step: dexterity +3, speed +20 / Tough Hide: vitality +4, physical absorb +2 / Venom Glands: earth +6, physical +3 |
| Necromancer | Grave Mastery (666) | Withering Touch: death +6, magic level +1 / Ossified Hide: physical absorb +3, vitality +3 / Soul Well: spirit +5, death absorb +2 |
| Monk | Inner Discipline (667) | Iron Knuckles: physical +6, strength +2 / Swift Palm: crit chance +2, crit amount +4 / Still Water: healing +6, spirit +3 / Stone Body: vitality +4, physical absorb +2 |
| Templar | Sacred Oath (668) | Oath of Flame: holy +6, strength +2 / Oath of the Wall: shielding +2, physical absorb +2, all elements absorb +1 / Oath of Mercy: healing +6, vitality +3 |

- **Saved data.** The `nodes` column of `chaos_passive_tree` stays "2,3,9"; with masteries it is "2,3,9,665|665:2" (the
  chosen effect after "|"). Old rows read as before, so no SQL is needed. `sendNodes` carries `masteries = [{id,
  choice}]`. Loadouts keep the same text in their `tree` column (a switch, save, park and the crash undo keep the
  choices; a choice the node no longer has is dropped on load). Build codes carry them in format version 2.
- **Search (client `search.lua`).** A box at the bottom left (Ctrl+F) frames every shown node whose name, stat lines,
  description or mastery effects hold all typed words (any case, any order); Next / Prev (Enter / Shift+Enter) centre
  the view on each match, the label counts them ("3 / 12").
- **Zoom (client `passivetree.lua`).** Each zoom level of the shown class keeps its widgets in its own pair of panels
  (at most three); a zoom step back to a level built before swaps the visible panels instead of destroying and creating
  about 1,480 widgets again, and a zoom keeps the same point of the tree in the middle. The client has no render-to-texture
  binding for Lua, so the links stay widgets; off-screen widgets were already skipped by the engine's draw.
  Measured in the Linux client (software GL under Xvfb, other builds running): a build of a level 1,479 widgets in
  1,658-2,452 ms (sliced over frames, as every zoom step before); a step to a cached level 27-70 ms and no widget.
- Tests: `tests/passivetree_plan_test.lua` (text format, mastery data, every plan rule, mastery changes, the handlers,
  loadouts text), `tests/buildshare_test.lua`, `tests/inspect_test.lua`, client `treeplan_test.lua` (paths, plan
  undo / redo / remove, masteries, search) and `game_playerinspect/playerinspect_logic_test.lua`.
- Tested in game (two clients): a planned path to a mastery with its choice, Apply (one request, saved with the
  choice), the effect changed for 9,000 gold at level 105, a forged disconnected plan refused, a plan over the points,
  search, zoom, a version 2 code exported and previewed on another character, the inspected tree read-only and a
  private character refused. Screenshots in the session's scratchpad (`treework/shots`).
- Not done: the Warrior, Ranger and Mystic lines have no class section and so no mastery yet; the masteries were not
  measured on the dummies (one node of 73 / 248 points; each effect is sized like a notable of its section).
- **Reworked nodes.** A node whose meaning changes a lot keeps its id and is listed in `passivetree_config.lua`
  `reworked` (`{version, ids}`, append only). At the first login after a version (`Chaos.storage.passiveRework`, 7100023,
  holds the last one handled) `ChaosPassiveTree.refundReworked` takes those nodes, and the ones only connected through
  them, out of every preset (`passivetree_core.lua` `reworkedSince`, `dropNodes`) and every saved loadout
  (`ChaosLoadouts.dropNodes`), for free, with one message. It runs before the class check of the login. Version 1:
  369, 376, 383, 390 (the line keystones). Version 2: 77, 78, 81, 82, 106-109, 253, 262, 355, 362 (the build
  archetype keystones, "Build archetypes" below). A new character only records the version.

## Passive tree notables on the paths (2026-10, client `treedata/nodes.lua`)
Runs of three or more small nodes along a path (outside the class sections and the ring next to the start) had one
node turned into a notable with its own name and a combined effect; 27 nodes in all, spread over every damage type,
the crit paths and the defences. Only the node's type (`isUncommon`), name, stats and icon changed: same id, same
place, same links (`tests/passivetree_layout_test.lua` passes), so saved trees and build codes keep them and nothing is
refunded (each notable holds its old stats plus a premium). Each one is sized against the small nodes of its run and
the notables around it, never above them: in the elemental clusters (small nodes 1, notables there 4 / 2 + 4) a
notable is the run's stat +2 and its absorb +1 (for example 393 Cinder Vein: fire 1 -> fire 3, fire absorb 1); on the
middle rings (small nodes 2) the stat +1 and 1-2 attribute points; on the crit runs crit chance 1 -> 2 and amount 1 ->
2-3 with a small extra.

  Power per point: the greedy class builds of the balance runs (the C4 build weights of

## Build archetypes (`archetypes.lua`, `archetypes_core.lua`, `archetypes_config.lua`, docs/BUILDS.md)
The owner asked for the genre's most played build styles, at least two per class line (2026-10-12). Twelve keystones
on converted leaves of the main tree, twelve uniques that push them, two summons. The build guide per line is
docs/BUILDS.md. Computed numbers: `data/spells/README.md` "Build archetypes" (not measured in game).

| Node | Keystone (flag) | Classes | Effect | Price |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 108 | Pyre Oath (`arPyreOath`) | Warrior, Templar lines | every second, out of a protection zone and in a fight or with an enemy near: enemies within 2 sqm take 4% of your maximum health as fire (a spell of yours: tree bonuses and the class factor apply); you take 2.5% of it as fire (`doTargetCombatHealth` without an attacker, so absorbs apply; never lethal) and heal 2% | other damage x0.75 |
| 81 | Sanguine Covenant (`arSanguine`) | all | 5% of the damage that landed on every hit as health (`Chaos.heal`, a tick later; the target's health is read again then, so an immune target, a zero hit or overkill leeches only what was really lost), at most 6% of the maximum health per second; the fraction of a point is carried to the next hit (before, a hit under 20 damage gave 0 and the keystone looked dead at low level; owner item C2, the leech in the bottom-left of the tree) | healing received (`COMBAT_HEALING` on the player, any source) x0.7 |
| 77 | Thornbound Oath (`arThornbound`) | all | a melee, ranged or spell hit from a creature: 20% of what landed (health + energy shield) + the items' Reflect Damage again, physical, at most 50% of the own maximum health a hit; players (only where `ChaosSpell.canAttack`): a third, at most 5% of their maximum health; bosses (`MonsterType:isBoss`): half, at most 2 x level per second per boss; never damage over time, never a reflect inside a reflect | damage dealt x0.9 |
| 109 | Open Hand Creed (`arOpenHand`) | all but the Monk line | no weapon in the hands (a shield or quiver is fine): the engine's fist hit (attack 7) is scaled to the Monk's fist attack (40 + level x 0.025, at most 60) with the best of fist, sword, axe and club skill, x1.1. `ChaosSpell.meleeAttack` (the Thief and Templar strike spells) returns that attack for an empty hand (it reads the flag storage 7100024 and the worn ring); the Warrior's skill spells keep the engine's fist values | none |

- **Casts.** A hit counts as a spell cast only inside the spell supports' cast context (storage 7109990, written by
  `data/spells/chaos/_supports.lua` around every wrapped spell script): effigies, sigils, ignites and the Effigy price
  read it. Other spell-origin hits (item reflect, other systems' procs, minions dealt as their owner) are not casts.
- **Chain budget.** Poison and burn spreads and shatters wait in one queue: at most 24 run per 50 ms, at most 40 per
  chain (a pack), 200 waiting (more are dropped). A spread is one spectator query and a condition or a hit, so one
  tick stays near 2 ms, far under the 20 ms task class of "Game loop stalls". Unit test: a 30 monster pack killed in
  waves ends within 6 waves and inside the budget.
- **Guards.** Shares of a hit (Cascade, arcs, effigy and sigil pulses, reflect) are dealt with `ChaosKeystones.depth`
  up like the keystone procs: no second tree bonus, nothing reacts to them. Own damage (aura, relic, shatter, Aether
  Edge) is a spell of the player with `ChaosArchetypes.source` set: tree bonuses and the class factor apply, the
  archetype's own price does not, only the leech and the marks react. The rift's Spiteglass reflect runs inside a
  guarded reflect, so a reflect never bounces back and forth.
- **Events.** `ChaosArchetypesHit` (onHealthChange) on every monster as it spawns (onSpawn index 10, after the passive
  tree's callback, so its event comes first and shares are of the hit with its bonuses; registered on the creature
  itself, since the monster has no id before its placement), on attacked targets and on players at login;
  `ChaosArchetypesDeath` on the same monsters; a passive tree listener writes the holders, the flag storage
  `Chaos.storage.archetypeFlags` (7100024, a bit per keystone for the spells' Lua state) and the Aether Edge
  condition; one global think a second runs Pyre Oath, the effigies, sigils and the relic for holders only.
- **Summons.** `monsters/chaos/archetype_cinder_effigy.xml` (speed 0, look 95) and
  `archetype_reliquary_warden.xml` (look 1074, to be checked in game): not attackable, not hostile, no attacks, health
  10 (below the monster tiers), registered by the monsters step like the other Chaos monsters. Removed at logout,
  death, a tree change and (relic) in a protection zone. `pets_config.lua` counts them as class summons.
- **Uniques** (`data/items/chaos_items.xml` `archetype`, specs by `tools/gen_unique_specs.py`, drops in
  `data/lib/chaos_unique_items.lua`): Pyreheart Mantle (8881), Vein of the Unsated (27652), Spitethorn Bulwark
  (15413), Knuckles of the Unbound (28023), Rotbloom Phial (21691), Splintered Instant (28049), Stormcaller Recurve
  (8858), Shard of the Long Winter (26756), Effigy Carver's Idol (22423), Brand of the Ashen Choir (18403), Aetherbound
  Plate (2466), Reliquary Censer (27251). `archetypes.lua` reads the worn copies (with `chaos_unique`) at login and
  after every equipment move. Knuckles and the Recurve also work without their keystone. The second round: Snarewalker
  Greaves (28115) and Fusewright's Charm (7890) for the snares, Choirmaster's Circlet (27667) and Oathkeeper's Standard
  (15453) for the vigils, Hollowglass Diadem (27668) and Stillheart Robe (27390) for the energy shield; the spells'
  Lua state reads them with `ChaosArchetypesCore.wornUniques` (the snare and vigil spells), the scripts with
  `archetypes.lua`. The snare uniques and the Diadem work without a keystone. The six have their own level and class
  lines, not their base items' ("Unique equip rules").
- **Save data.** The twelve nodes keep their ids and links (`tests/passivetree_layout_test.lua`); reworked version 2
  refunds them once; build code format 4 (older codes leave them out). Client: `game_passivetree` tooltips and names,
  icons `keystones.png` cells 28-39 (`client/tools/gen_keystone_icons.py`). The second round (96, 99, 102, 105, the
  ends of the four other elemental clusters): reworked version 3, build code format 5, `keystones.png` cells 40-43,
  flag bits 13-16 of storage 7100024.
- **Third round: the Warrior and Ranger lines (2026-10-20).** Beta feedback: the Warrior line had no keystone of its own
  and the Ranger line few. Eight keystones on converted leaves, flag bits 17-24 of storage 7100024 (numbers in
  `archetypes_config.lua`, rules in `archetypes_core.lua`, glue in `archetypes.lua`). Warrior, Juggernaut, Berserker:
  Executioner's Verdict (428: a melee or spell hit that would leave a non-boss monster at 15% or less kills it; x0.60 above 15%;
  x0.90 otherwise), Earthbreaker (409: every 4th melee hit within 3 s deals +50% and a 60% slam to up to 6 monsters
  within 2 sqm; the other hits x0.90), Rampage (466: a monster kill gives a stack, 5 at most, 6 s, +6% damage and +4%
  damage taken per stack), Last Stand (523: a hit that would take you under 20% health is cut to leave you there, then
  5 s of -40% damage taken, healing taken x0.80, 90 s cooldown; not against players). Ranger, Deadeye, Beastmaster:
  Longshot (561: distance weapons +6% per sqm beyond 2, at most +30%; at 2 sqm or nearer x0.85), Barbed Quiver (542:
  distance weapon hits bleed for 60% of the hit over 4 s, the hit x0.90), Opening Shot (599: the first hit on a full
  health monster +80%, other hits x0.93), Hobbling Shot (447: 25% to hobble 3 s, 40% slower, +20% damage on hobbled
  targets, other hits x0.92). Reworked version 6 refunds the eight nodes once, build code format 6 (`CB6-`),
  `keystones.png` cells 44-51. `classlanes.lua` lost the lanes of the eight nodes and some lane skill values were
  trimmed by hand to keep the supply cap (`gen_class_lanes.lua --check` would differ).
- **Hollow Vessel and the other rules.** Every percent-of-maximum-health hit on a player takes `Chaos.percentBase(player)`
  (`chaos_constants.lua`, over `ChaosArchetypes.percentBase`): health + maximum energy shield for a holder, so the fixed
  100 health is no way around them. That is the rifts' `percentHit` (Scorched Earth, Rimefloor, Veilstorm, the Wrathful
  Guardian's nova) and, since 2026-10-12, the scripted `shareHit` of the raid (`raid.lua`: Crushing Verdict, cleave,
  sweep, soak and the other telegraphs), the Ascended Omens and the Cinderheart (`uber.lua`) and the guild boss
  (`guildboss.lua`). The world boss event (`worldboss.lua`) has no percent hits (its pulse is a flat range). Festering Wounds is a poison
  condition: a holder takes none. The hexes and Parched Veins work as on anyone. Pyre Oath, Sanguine Covenant's cap
  and Thornbound Oath's cap read the maximum health (100). The mana shield and the Trials' Mana Ward come before the

  `tests/trials_flow_test.lua`, `tests/ascension_quest_test.lua`. No percent hit reads the health alone now.
- **Not done.** A spell cast by name on a critical hit needs an engine call; not added (it would skip the cast
  checks), Cascade Edge deals its own burst.
- Tests: `tests/archetypes_test.lua` (rules, data, tooltips, uniques, the glue against a mocked engine; the second
  round's prices, the vigils' hit multipliers and Hollow Vessel), `tests/snares_test.lua`, `tests/vigils_test.lua`,

## Snares (`data/spells/chaos/_snares.lua`, `snares_core.lua`, `snares_config.lua`, docs/BUILDS.md "Snares")
Traps and mines for the Ranger and Thief lines (2026-10-12): Snare Trap (spell 99, `drai snar`, level 40), Seeker Mine
(100, `kah snar`, level 60), Detonate Mines (104, `vok snar`, level 60). A snare is a record in the spells' Lua state
(`ChaosSnares.state`): kind, owner, position, element, its hit, when it arms and ends. Nothing is created on the map.

- **Placement.** Thrown up to 4 sqm: onto the attack target (in range and sight), else straight ahead to the last open
  tile in sight, never into a protection zone. Per player 3 traps / 5 mines (Snarewright's Creed +2 / +3, the Greaves
  +1 trap, the Charm +2 mines; the oldest goes); 400 for the whole server (refused with a message).
- **The scheduler.** One `addEvent` loop every 200 ms while snares exist, started with the supports' raw `addEvent`
  (`ChaosSupportsSpell.rawAddEvent`) so it never carries a cast context. Each tick it visits 60 snares round robin: an
  armed trap makes one 3x3 spectator query (a monster within 1 sqm sets it off), a mine past its fuse goes off, a
  trap past its 20 s goes; a visit also drops the snare when its owner logged out, died, changed floor, went 30 sqm
  away or into a protection zone (`archetypes.lua` clears them at once at logout and death when the two sides share
  a Lua state). At most 16 bursts a tick (a 5x5 query and up to 8 hits each), 200 waiting. Worst case about 2 ms a tick,
  far under the 20 ms task class of "Game loop stalls".
- **The hit.** level x 0.2 + power x 0.045 + 10 .. level x 0.2 + power x 0.0675 + 20 (halved on 2026-10-13 after the
  in-game measure: the Ranger and Deadeye snare builds were 40-90% over their computed rows), power the best of distance skill x
  distance attack, sword skill x blade attack and the shuriken power; a mine x1.15; the keystone x1.25, Greaves traps
  x1.1, Charm mines x1.1; physical x1.15, energy x0.85 with 1 sqm more radius. Dealt with `doTargetCombat` from the
  owner (`ORIGIN_SPELL`; tree bonuses and the class factor apply in the scripts' events) to monsters that are not a
  player's summon, in sight of the snare. Storage 7100027 is 1 while they are dealt: Snarewright's price spares them.
  Outside a cast context: no spell supports, no Effigy or Sigil from them. The DPS meter and combat log still name
  them by their spell (`ChaosCombatLog.asSpell`, fixed 2026-10-12; they were "Other"): Snare Trap, Seeker Mine (a
  mine past its fuse) or Detonate Mines (a mine it set off, `snares_core.lua` `spellOf`).
- **The element** (storage 7100026 remembers the last spoken one): the word after the spell words, else the
  remembered one, else the first brand rune socketed in the spell (supports storage 7110000 + spell x 4 + 1..3; the
  snare spells are kind "area" in `chaos_supports_config.lua` so brands fit), else physical. Fire: a burn of 30% over
  4 s (a fire condition of the owner); ice: slowed 40% for 3 s; earth: a poison of 36% over 6 s; death: 4% of the
  damage back as health; holy: the owner and party members within 2 sqm of the snare heal 2% of their maximum health.
- PvP: monsters only. Tests: `tests/snares_test.lua` (rules; the glue against a mocked engine: thrown, armed,
  triggered, bursts, sight, the marker, the combat log's spell name per hit, elements, mines, the fuse, caps, the
  protection zone, the cleanup, the work per tick with 400 snares, the spells in the XML). Not run on a live server.

## Mana flow (`mana_flow.lua`, `mana_flow_core.lua`, `mana_flow_config.lua`; beta report 2026-10-20)

Report: a level 800 Juggernaut (7M health shown) could only keep his skills up with infinite mana potions, and "the mana
cost scales, one skill costs 400k". Findings: (1) the cost does not scale in the engine. Spell costs are flat
(Juggernaut kit 30-500); the 400k is the display scale (`display_scale_core.lua`, factor 215 at level 800, 1000 at 1000)
shown on the spellbook and the mana bar, and the pool is shown scaled the same, so cost against pool never moved.
(2) The real gap was regeneration: pool 5 mana a level, vocation regeneration 2.5 a second, the best rotation 44 a second
at level 300 (`rotation_sim.py --mana`, which only checks up to level 300 and without regeneration from the tree).

- **Regeneration**: from level 100 every player gets mana a second on top of the vocation's, flat for every class, linear
  between 100 -> 4, 300 -> 24, 600 -> 45, 1000 -> 60 (level 800: 52.5; mana is shown as it is since 2026-10-21, "Fixed
  spell costs"). A think every second
  (`GlobalEvent`), none at a full pool, dead, or under the rift's Parched Veins (`fx.noMana`). Juggernaut: level 300 pool
  1530 against 44 a second: runway 37 s -> 87 s; level 600 and up the Juggernaut rotation is paid by the regeneration alone.
  Casters (Elementalist rotation about 183 a second at level 1000, pool ~30000) still drain: runway about 4 minutes.
- **Cost cap: removed 2026-10-21** ("Fixed spell costs" below). It capped a cast at 25% of the maximum mana from level
  100, so a cost depended on the pool (Colossus Fall 332 at level 260). `mana_flow.lua` registers no "cost" handler and
  drops the old one (`ChaosSpellEvents.remove("cost", "manaflow")`: handlers survive a /reload).
- Numbers: `mana_flow_config.lua`. Test: `tests/mana_flow_test.lua`. No storage, no DB.
- **Righteous Fire style skill**: that is Pyre Oath (keystone `arPyreOath`, `archetypes.lua`), not a spell: it burns and
  heals every second and costs no mana. Support runes are keyed by spell id and wrap a spell's `onCastSpell`; a keystone
  has neither, so it cannot take runes without a new socket kind (storage, window, client). Not done. The mana the
  report mentions is the Juggernaut's other spells (and mana-on-hit gear), which the regeneration above now pays.

## Fixed spell costs (owner 2026-10-21: "Mas o custo de mana das skills ainda tá escalando com o level do char")

Every player spell costs **one fixed number at every level, for every class**: the `mana` of its spells.xml entry
(`data/spells/chaos/spells_chaos.xml` for the Chaos spells; the stock spells through `tools/patch_spell_timings.py`,
`data/spells/spell_timings.csv`, as before). The client shows that number. Only percentages of it change a cast: Thrift
runes, Mana Cost Reduction (items, sets), the trial nodes. The cost table, the reasons of the numbers and the mana runway
up to level 1000: `data/spells/README.md` "Fixed spell costs".

What scaled before, and the change:
- **The shown cost** (the beta tester's "one of my skills costs 400k"): the display scale showed the own mana x the factor
  of the level, so the spellbook and the client's action bar showed every flat cost x that factor: Colossus Fall (400)
  read 400,000 at level 1000. Now mana is out of the display scale: engine `src-patches/0052` (stats packet mana and
  max mana, the mana drain / gain messages of patch 0051's types 3 and 4), `display_scale_core.lua` (no spell list site;
  party frames keep the mana `m`, `M`; item tooltips keep max mana, mana on hit / kill and mana gems), `spellbook.lua`
  (one packed list for every viewer), client `game_chaosscale` (no `SpellInfo` scaling). Health, damage, heals and the
  energy shield keep the scale ("Display scale").
- **Shadow Mend** cost 2% of the maximum mana (`manapercent="2"`): now 40 mana.
- **The cost cap** of "Mana flow": removed.
- Kept: the vigils reserve a share of the maximum mana while they are up (an aura; their cast costs 0); Raise Dead from
  nothing costs its own 60 once more (flat); runes unchanged.
- Guards: `tests/mana_flow_test.lua` (no `manapercent`, a number in every mana field of `spells_chaos.xml`,
  `stock_spells.csv` and `spell_timings.csv`, no cap, no cost handler), `tests/display_scale_test.lua` (no spell list
  site, mana rows and party mana unscaled, the spellbook has no display scale), `tools/display_scale_patch_test.py`
  (0052), `tools/rotation_sim.py --mana --check` (runway up to 1000, no cost above a class's pool at the spell's level).
- Install on a running server: `python3 -I tools/install_all.py SERVER_DIR --only files,spells` (scripts and the Chaos
  spell block of spells.xml; idempotent), apply `src-patches/0052-mana-outside-display-scale.patch` to the engine source
  (after 0001-0051), rebuild and restart. The client needs its update too (`game_chaosscale`, `spelldata.lua`): an old
  client with the new engine still multiplies the costs on the action bar by the factor while the mana bar no longer
  is, so from level 153 it greys out spells it can cast (casting by words works). Ship the two together.

## Vigils (`vigils.lua`, `vigils_core.lua`, `vigils_config.lua`, `data/spells/chaos/_vigils.lua`, docs/BUILDS.md "Vigils")
Auras that reserve mana (2026-10-12), every class: Vigil of Wrath (spell 179, `vigh vyr`, level 60, reserves 35%,
+5% damage), Vigil of Iron (255, `vigh tor`, 60, 35%, -6% damage taken), Vigil of Haste (161, `vigh ruan`, 40, 20%,
+15% speed), Vigil of Clarity (162, `vigh lum`, 35, 20%, 1% of the maximum mana a second). `mana="0"`: a cast
switches the vigil in storage 7100025 (a bit each) and costs nothing.

- **Reservation.** `vigils.lua` thinks every second over the online players. A holder's reserved share (the vigils'
  shares x0.7 with Covenant of Vigils, x0.85 with the Choirmaster's Circlet, x0.9 with Oathkeeper's Standard) becomes
  one `CONDITION_ATTRIBUTES` (sub id 71092) with a negative `STAT_MAXMANAPOINTS`, sized from the maximum without it and
  renewed when that changes; the engine lowers the current mana with it. Reserved mana is never spent: spells, the
  mana shield and the Trials' Mana Ward see the lower maximum. Iron Tithe reserves health instead (sub id 71093, at
  0.6 of the share). More than 100% cannot be switched on; vigils that stop fitting (a unique taken off) are switched
  off, the last first, with a message. The condition goes at death; the next think puts it back.
- **Coverage.** The holder and its party members on its floor within 5 sqm (+3 Covenant, +2 Standard), alive; Iron
  Tithe and a multi-client holder cover only themselves. Per member and vigil the strongest holder counts. A member
  keeps the cover 1.5 s after the last think that saw it. Haste: a haste condition (sub id 71094, +15% of the base
  speed, refreshed each think). Clarity: `addMana` each think, none while the member's rift run has Parched Veins
  (`ChaosRift.runOf[id].fx.noMana`).
- **Buff bar** (2026-10-12; `data/lib/chaos_buffs.lua` source `vigils`, opcode 234, client `game_buffbar` unchanged): one
  row per vigil that covers the player, `vigil_wrath`, `vigil_iron`, `vigil_haste`, `vigil_clarity`, named after the vigil,
  stacks = its effect in whole percent (the text has the exact one, e.g. "+7.5% damage dealt"), no timer; the text says
  whether it is your own (and what it reserves of your mana, or health) or a party member's, and Clarity under Parched
  Veins. Iron Tithe adds `vigil_tithe` ("Iron Tithe", stacks = the health reserved). `ChaosVigils.buffItem` reads what
  the last think saw (no engine call); the texts are `vigils_core.lua` `V.buffItem`. A row goes when the cover does
  (1.5 s after the holder leaves the range); a quiet vigil costs no traffic. Icons `buff:vigil_*`: a banner with the
  vigil's emblem (`client/tools/gen_buff_icons.py`).
- **Hits.** `archetypes.lua` onHealthChange (on every player and every monster already) multiplies a covered
  attacker's hits by `ChaosVigils.dealt` and a covered player's damage taken by `ChaosVigils.taken`. Wrath does not add
  on top of Inspiring Illusion (a giver in range: only what is above its +8% counts); Iron does not add on top of the
  Templar line's defence aura (`ChaosTemplar.activeAura`: only what is above its reduction counts).
- Tests: `tests/vigils_test.lua` (rules; the toggle spells; the glue against a mocked engine: reservation, renewal,
  death, Iron Tithe, the party, haste, Clarity under Parched Veins, what no longer fits, the hit factors with the
  Templar aura and Inspiring Illusion, the buff bar rows; the spells in the XML), `tests/buffs_test.lua` (the source).
  Not run on a live server.

## Unique equip rules (`data/lib/chaos_unique_equip.lua`, `tools/install_unique_equip.py`, `chaos_items.xml` `equipLevel` / `equipLines`)
A unique is a copy of a stock base item, and the engine's equip check (movements.xml: level and vocations) belongs to
the base item id. Measured in game (2026-10-13) the second round's archetype uniques followed their base items:
Stillheart Robe (soulmantle) level 400, Hollowglass Diadem (eldritch hood) no Elementalist, Choirmaster's Circlet
(eldritch cowl) Mystic and Necromancer lines only, Snarewalker Greaves (shadewalker boots) level 300. Since then a unique
may carry its own rule: `equipLevel` (its drop level) and `equipLines` (class lines) in `chaos_items.xml`, generated
into `chaos_unique_specs.lua` as `equip = {level, lines, vocations}`.

| Unique | Level | Worn by (the classes its archetype names) | The base item's stock rule (kept for stock copies) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Snarewalker Greaves (28115) | 120 | Ranger and Thief lines (Snarewright's Creed) | 300; Ranger, Thief and Monk lines |
| Fusewright's Charm (7890) | 150 | Ranger and Thief lines (Snarewright's Creed) | 60; everyone |
| Choirmaster's Circlet (27667) | 200 | Warrior, Mystic, Necromancer, Monk and Templar lines (Covenant of Vigils, Iron Tithe) | 230; Mystic and Necromancer lines |
| Oathkeeper's Standard (15453) | 180 | Warrior, Mystic, Necromancer, Monk and Templar lines (Covenant of Vigils, Iron Tithe) | none |
| Hollowglass Diadem (27668) | 250 | Mystic, Necromancer, Monk and Templar lines (Hollow Vessel) | 230; Mystic (no Elementalist) and Necromancer lines |
| Stillheart Robe (27390) | 300 | Mystic, Necromancer, Monk and Templar lines (Hollow Vessel) | 400; Mystic and Necromancer lines |

- **Install** (`install_unique_equip.py`, step `uniqueequip`, after `vocations` and `archery`): the stock Equip entry of
  each base id is taken out of movements.xml and recorded as a comment in a marked block before `</movements>`; the
  block's entry has the lower of the two levels, both vocation lists (none when either side lets everyone wear it),
  `function="onEquipItem"` and `script="chaos_unique_equip.lua"`. A base id without a DeEquip entry gets one. The
  unique's classes show in the look text, stock-only ones are hidden. `data/movements/scripts/chaos_unique_equip.lua`
  is written with the recorded stock rules. A re-run rebuilds the same block; `add_vocations.py` leaves it alone. A stock
  entry with its own script, two Equip entries or a range over the id stop the tool.
- **The check.** The engine checks the looser rule, then the script's `onEquip` (`ChaosUniqueEquip.onEquip`) decides on
  the check pass: a copy with `chaos_unique` whose spec has `equip` is held to that rule, every other copy to the stock
  rule. Refused: the engine's "You cannot dress this object there." Staff with the weapon check flag pass, as in the
  engine. A copy worn before the rule stays worn until taken off.
- **Look text.** The engine's "can only be wielded properly by" line shows the entry's level (the lower one: 60 for the
  Charm, 230 for the Diadem, where the unique asks more); the unique's description says its own level and lines.
- Tests: `tests/unique_equip_test.lua` (every round-two unique can be worn by the classes its archetype names and not
  below its level; unique and stock copies; the tool on a small movements.xml, idempotent; the generated script).
- **No lines, every class** (2026-10-23): `equipLevel` without `equipLines` writes an empty class list; that lets every
  class wear it from the level (before, an empty list let nobody). A weapon base without a stock entry gets a `hand`
  entry. The leveling and endgame uniques below use both.

## Leveling and endgame uniques (`chaos_items.xml` `mods`, `chaos_unique_items.lua`, 2026-10-23)
Before this the uniques stopped at level 1000 with flat stats, and the first one dropped at level 40.
- **Built-in modifiers.** `<attribute key="mods" value="key:value,..." />` names modifiers of `chaos_item_mods.lua` and
  legendary powers of `chaos_powers.lua`. `tools/gen_unique_specs.py` checks the keys and writes `mods = {{key, value}}`
  into the spec; `ChaosMakeUnique` stores them as T8 modifiers (`ChaosItemMods.set`). They count in the equipped totals
  like rolled ones, under the same caps. The tooltip shows them (a power in the power colour), the Codex and the wiki
  list them. No orb touches a unique, so they never change.
- **Leveling, 12 uniques, level 10-35**, one per weapon kind and slot (sword, axe, club, bow, wand, helmet, boots, ring,
  amulet, body, legs, shield): life / mana on kill, health on hit, regeneration, experience +5-8%, movement speed +10%,
  attack speed +8%, ailment chances. Flat numbers that carry a character to about level 100-150 and then fade. They drop
  from magic monsters and up of the level 5-40 hunts at chance 25 (the other uniques 4-10, x the tier multiplier).
- **Endgame, 12 uniques, level 1200-2400**, each with near-cap modifiers and one legendary power (Critical Echo,
  Bloodrush, Arc Lightning, Echo Shot, Crimson Burst, Smoldering Aura, Last Breath, Hunter's Rush, Glacial Ward, Death
  Blast). They drop from the waystone bosses of their band (x6) and the band's waystone monsters (rare and up,
  `minMonsterLevel = 1000`) at chance 6; the Choirless Pendant (2400) from the high band bosses and Ysgrath only.
  Weapons and class armour have `equipLines`.
- **Reworked**: the 13 uniques of level 800 and 1000 got built-in modifiers, a legendary power on 11 of them.
- Every new unique has `equipLevel`, so a copy traded to a low character cannot be worn. The bases have no abilities of
  their own (a unique keeps its base item type's abilities) and no stock equip script; none is a transmog set look.
- Lists: `data/items/README.md` "Leveling and endgame uniques". Tests: `tests/unique_mods_test.lua` (every spec.mods key
  and cap, ChaosMakeUnique writes T8 modifiers the totals count, levels, rules, one power per endgame unique, drop
  sources), `tests/unique_equip_test.lua` (an empty class list).

## Unique passives (`unique_passives*.lua`, O278, 2026-10-27)
Owner: "nos itens unique, coloque passivas build changers. muito boas mesmo". Every one of the 183 uniques has ONE passive
that changes how a build plays: a conversion, a trigger, a rule with a price. The rules are in `unique_passives_core.lua`
(pure, tested), the numbers in `unique_passives_config.lua` (`families` = defaults, `passives[item id]` = the item's own
numbers, `lv` checked against the item's level), the tooltip lines in `unique_passives_text.lua`, the engine glue in
`unique_passives.lua`. The item keeps its name, flavor text, stats, class rule and archetype line; the passive is one more
sentence in its description (`tools/gen_unique_specs.py` renders it from the config through `tools/dump_unique_passives.lua`,
so a number changed in the config changes the item text, the Codex and the wiki after the generators run).
- **Who gets it.** A passive works while the unique is worn as a real copy (custom attribute `chaos_unique`) and only for the
  class lines it names (`lines`); the item stays wearable for every class its equip rule allows, the passive sleeps for the
  others (so `gear_coverage` is unchanged). At most 5 passives are active, one per family: a character wearing more picks
  by item level. Equipment is read at login, on every inventory move and every 3 s.
- **Families (22).** convert, lowlife, overflow, opener, focus, statscale, critrule, crowd (damage rules with a price);
  extra, nova, riposte, spread (hits that start from a hit, a kill or a hurt); ward, hitcap, immunity, panic, manashield,
  feast, mend (defence, each with a price such as less healing received); stacks, mark (a state you build);
  minionPact (Necromancer). Every number of a family is in the config comment.
- **Safety.** The product of the damage multipliers is clamped to 0.5-1.8, the damage taken to 0.4-1.5, the bonus against
  players is 1/3. Condition ticks and procs get no multiplier and start no passive (guard flag plus `ChaosKeystones.depth` /
  `ChaosSpellFactor.depth` / `ChaosPowers.depth`, the same guard as the legendary powers). Every proc has an internal
  cooldown; a price in health never takes the character under `minHealth`; extra hits only hit wild monsters (no summon, no
  hunt-room display, never a player); a ward is capped (25% of the health at most, 4% per hit), fades, and is not an item;
  heal per kill is capped per second; a spread is bounded (targets, ticks, 120 monsters remembered). No passive creates
  gold or items. The unique's drop and sell values are untouched, so the economy does not change.
- **Necromancer.** `ChaosNecro.minionFactor` is wrapped once (minion hit and health); the "own spells deal less" price is
  taken in the damage event, so it does not reach the spell scripts' own Lua state (their `ownSpellFactor`).
- **Languages.** The generated description is English. The pt-BR Codex lines are generated into `pt_br.lua` (between the
  GENERATED UNIQUE DESCRIPTIONS markers) from `data/items/unique_flavor_pt.tsv` (the pt-BR flavor of each description) plus the
  pt-BR passive line; the in-game tooltip swaps the passive line for pt-BR on the server (`item_tooltip.lua`). The passive
  names stay English (proper nouns). The 18 uniques without a pt-BR flavor line show the English flavor with the pt-BR passive.
- **Balance.** `tools/unique_passives_model.lua --check` (luajit and lua5.3): expected power gain = damage dealt x
  survivability in a typical hunt (assumptions at the top of the file). Each passive: 1.03-1.55 on every line it works for;
  the best five of a line in a level band: 1.35-3.2 (limits: `model.*` in the config); every line has 3+ passives per band.
  `--list` prints every passive, no flag the table per class line and band, `--tune` the numbers that bring an outlier into range.
  Average gain of one passive by class line: warrior 1.12-1.20, ranger 1.14-1.30, mystic 1.14-1.25, thief 1.10-1.20, monk
  1.11-1.19, necromancer 1.13-1.24, templar 1.12-1.17. The model is an estimate, not a measurement: nothing here was run live.
- **Bug found and fixed on the way.** `archetypes.lua` read the worn archetype uniques only at login and on inventory moves;
  an item that left its slot another way kept its effect. The think event now checks them again.
- Tests: `tests/unique_passives_test.lua` (every unique has a passive and its text matches the config, pt-BR numbers in the
  English order, 3+ passives per class line and band, per family the trigger, cap or cooldown, price and no self-trigger, the
  glue against a mocked engine). Install: Lua, XML-free; copy `data/scripts/chaos/unique_passives*.lua` and the regenerated
  `data/lib/chaos_unique_specs.lua`; no new install step, no engine patch, no new opcode or storage key. Existing unique copies
  work at once; the tooltip and the Codex read the spec, only the plain look text of a copy made before keeps the old sentence.

## Thief dual wield, attack speed and daggers (2026-10-23)
Owner: "thief deveriam ser criados já com dual wield de daggers. devem atacar mais rápido que a outras classes, empatado com o monk"
and "adicione também mais daggers pros thiefs". Class rules: docs/CLASSES.md; balance numbers: `data/spells/README.md` "Thief dual wield
and attack speed". Lua and XML only: no engine rebuild (src-patch 0002 already reads the dual-wield storage and scales the weapon speed
by the vocation's); a server restart after `install_all.py` loads the new vocation speeds.
- **Dual wield for the Thief.** `ChaosClasses.isDualWielder` (`Chaos.classes.dualWield.vocations`: Thief 11 and Ninja 12; the Samurai
  keeps one sword). `syncDualWield` keeps storage 7100200 at 1 for them (login, ascension, vocation change), which lets the
  engine put a one-handed sword in the shield hand; `thief_combat.lua` adds the off-hand strike. A Thief who ascends to the Samurai
  keeps a dagger already in the shield hand (it does nothing there).
- **Kit.** `newplayer_config.lua` `thief`: dagger 2379 in the left hand and in the right hand (`NP.giveWearable` syncs the storage
  first, the login event of the class may come after the kit's); no spare dagger in the backpack any more. The Ninja inherits it.
  The Samurai has `{slot = "right", none = true}`: a `none` row drops the base kit's slot (`NP.resolveKit`), so it keeps one katana.
- **Existing Thieves.** At login `ChaosClasses.grantOffhand` gives one dagger 2379 into an EMPTY shield hand, once per character
  (storage `Chaos.storage.offhandGranted`, 7100204, set before the add so a failure never repeats it), only to a base Thief
  (11) with a one-handed sword in the main hand. Nothing when the shield hand holds a shield (the grant stays open until it is
  empty; it is still one dagger, ever), a weapon already there marks the flag without giving anything, and a Ninja or Samurai gets
  none (the Ninja's old kit had the spare in the backpack). Not exploitable: one common dagger (2 gold) per character, flag
  per character, not reset by a vocation change. Test: `classes_test.lua`.
- **Attack speed.** `chaos_vocations.xml`: Thief 1500, Ninja 1300, Samurai 1700 (the Monk line 1500 / 1300 / 1700, everyone else
  2000). `Chaos.classes.attackSpeed` lists was / now; `ChaosClasses.speedComp` (now / was) cuts the weapon hits of those three
  in `thief_combat.lua` so their damage per second is unchanged, and `dualNeutral` (Thief only) cuts the main hit by
  1 / (1 + share x ratio) while both hands hold a light blade. A test reads the vocation XML and fails if the table and the XML
  disagree, if the Thief is not tied with the Monk or if any class outside the two lines is not at 2000.
- **Thief daggers.** Five uniques on dagger-sprite bases (one unique per base id), see `data/items/README.md` "Thief daggers":
  Cutpurse's Sliver (knife, level 10) and Moonlit Shiv (silver dagger, 28) from magic monsters and up of the low hunts (every class);
  Gravewhisper Stiletto (combat knife, 600), Nightbloom Stiletto (poison dagger, 1250) and Misericorde of the Pale Vow (drownkin
  ceremonial dagger, 1900) for the Thief line, with attack speed and the line's poison / penetration modifiers (the last two with a
  legendary power, from waystone kills). Bands: 1-9 the shop dagger (2379), 10-27 and 28-599 the two leveling daggers and the stock
  daggers (assassin dagger 7404 from level 40, ceremonial 27193 from 180), 300 the Duskstalker Fang, 600+ the Thief-only ones up
  to 2400+. Attack by the gear curve (`install_gear_sets.py`); the auto attack power factors (`weapon_power_config.lua`,
  `weapon_sim.py --power --check` passes) scale it as every melee weapon. Only the level 600+ ones are Thief-line only. Drop pool,
  codex, wiki and tooltip come from the same files as every unique (`gen_unique_specs.py`, `gen_codex_data.lua`,
  `gen_wiki_data.lua`); uniques have no NPC price (`gen_item_prices.py --check`).
- Storage 7100204 is in the 7100000-7100999 block (`Chaos.storage`), next to 7100200-7100203.

## Build sharing (`buildshare.lua`, `buildshare_core.lua`)
A build can be exported as a short text code and imported on another character (or after a reset). The server encodes, decodes,
validates and applies; the client only shows what the server sends.
- **Client:** the **Build Code** button of the passive tree window opens a panel (`game_passivetree/buildshare.lua`,
  `buildshare.otui`): **Export** puts the code in the text box and on the clipboard (`g_window.setClipboardText`), **Paste** /
  **Import** asks the server for a preview. The tree then shows the nodes the import would allocate, and the panel says the
  points needed vs. owned, what changes (new / taken back), the nodes left out and the price. **Apply Build** (with a confirm
  box showing the price) applies it, **Cancel Preview** shows the saved tree again.
- **Chat:** the spoken `!build` commands are gone (everything is in the Build Code panel); a "build link" `[build CB1-...]`
  pasted in chat still opens the panel with that code.
- **Code format, version 5** (since the second round of build archetype keystones, 2026-10-12; versions 2 to 4 have the
  same layout): `CB5-` + base64url of:
  class line (1 byte, index into `ChaosBuildShare.CLASS_LINES` = warrior, ranger, mystic, thief; 0 = no class; never a
  vocation id), flags (1 byte, 1 = Paragon part, 2 = mastery part), the optional
  Paragon part (count, then stat index into `PARAGON_KEYS` + points, 1 byte each), the optional mastery part (count, then node
  id in 2 bytes and the chosen effect in 1 byte), a bitset of the allocated node ids (bit `id % 8` of byte `id / 8`, trailing
  zero bytes dropped) and a 3 byte checksum (`h = (h x 257 + byte) mod 16777213` over "CB5" and the bytes). Only the
  canonical base64 form is accepted, so every single-character typo is rejected (test). A 100 node build is ~60 characters, a
  248 node level 1000 build ~110, the whole tree ~120. **Version 1** (`CB1-`, the same without the mastery part) is still
  read: an import of it keeps the character's own mastery effects, else takes the first one (the preview says so). An import
  that changes the effect of a mastery the character holds counts as taking points back (the full reset price).
- **Stability rule:** the bitset is indexed by the stable node ids of `passivetree_data.lua` (the client's `nodes.lua` ids), not
  by array positions. New nodes are appended with new ids; existing ids are never renumbered or reused, so old codes stay valid
  and mean the same nodes. A retired id makes codes that use it invalid ("node N is not in the passive tree"). Class lines and
  Paragon stat keys are append-only lists, and so are a mastery's effects. A new format gets a new version number; `decode`
  reads every version ever handed out (`ChaosBuildShare.READS`: 1 to 5), others are rejected with a clear message.
  **A node whose meaning changes** keeps its id and gets an entry in `ChaosBuildShare.REWORKED` (id -> the first version
  made with the new meaning; append only) and a new format version: an older code that holds it leaves it out on import,
  with the nodes only connected through it, and the preview says so ("The code is older than a tree change: n nodes
  whose effect changed are left out."). Version 3 came with 369, 376, 383 and 390 becoming the line keystones; the 27
  path notables kept their meaning (old stats plus a premium) and need no entry. Version 4 came with the twelve build
  archetype keystones (77, 78, 81, 82, 106-109, 253, 262, 355, 362); codes of versions 1-3 leave them out. Version 5
  came with the second round (96, 99, 102, 105); codes of versions 1-4 leave those out.
- **Import rules (server):** same class line as the importer (Juggernaut and Berserker share the Warrior line; keystone variants
  follow the importer's class via `ChaosClasses.keystoneKey`), else "This build is for a Warrior line class; you are a ...";
  every node known and connected to the start through the build's own nodes; a keystone only if the importer's class has a variant
  of it; the saved list passes the tree's own save validation (`validateNodes`) again. **Not enough points (decision): the first N
  nodes in path order are applied** (the nodes the character already has first, then nearest to the start, then lowest id; the
  prefix is always connected) and the preview / result says how many were left out. The Paragon part is applied when the track is
  unlocked, stat by stat in key order up to the points owned.
- **Price:** an import that only adds to the current tree (and Paragon) is free, onto an empty tree too. One that takes nodes or
  Paragon points back costs the full reset price of that part (`respec.lua`: tree, Paragon), with the same free cases (below level
  50, the free reset after a class change). The store's Passive Tree Reset service (a free reset of both) can be used first. The
  client sends back the price the preview showed; a higher price at apply time is refused ("preview again").
- Protocol (opcode 65, through `ChaosPassiveTree.extraActions`, which `passivetree.lua` checks before its own actions):
  `buildExport` -> `buildCode {code, nodes, paragon}`; `buildPreview {code}` -> `buildPreview {code, nodes, current, wanted,
  applied, skipped, added, removed, treeReset, paragon, paragonChange, paragonReset, cost, free, points, notes, change, summary}` or
  `buildError {message}`; `buildApply {code, cost}` -> `sendNodes`, `sendPoints`, `paragonState`, `respecInfo`, `buildApplied
  {message}` or `buildError {message}`. No new opcode.
- `server/tests/buildshare_test.lua`: round trip (40 / 248 nodes, Paragon part), every single-character typo, swapped and truncated
  codes, old / newer version, wrong class, unknown and disconnected nodes, keystones, too many points, reset detection, the Paragon
  part, an old code on a tree with an appended node, the reworked nodes (versions 1 and 2 leave 383 out with a note, version 3
  keeps it for the Thief line and refuses it to another line, a node behind a reworked one goes with it).
- Tested on the test server (Deadeye, level 599, 147 points): a 100 node tree exported (63 characters, clipboard checked), reset
  (3,945,000 gold), imported (free) and saved identical to before; imported over a 147 node tree (took 47 back, 3,945,000 gold) and
  identical again; a 200 node code applied its first 147 nodes; bad checksum, wrong class and old version gave their messages; the
  Build Code panel flow (export / import / apply) and "You need 3,945,000 gold coins" with too little gold. Screenshots in the
  session's scratchpad. Not tested in game: the Paragon part (the character is below level 1000; unit tests only).

## Passive tree: Auto build, class lanes, Primary / Secondary and stat help (2026-10)

Files: `passive_builds.lua` (engine), `passive_builds_core.lua` (pure), `passive_builds_config.lua` (numbers), `passive_builds_data.lua`
(generated by `tools/gen_passive_builds.lua`, `--check` in CI), `passivetree_stats.lua` / `_core.lua` / `_config.lua`, the lane
generator `tools/gen_class_lanes.lua` (+ `tools/passivetree_lanes_lib.lua`, client `treedata/classlanes.lua`). Client: `autobuild.lua`
/ `.otui` (+ `autobuildview.lua`), `statinfo.lua` / `.otui` (+ `statinfoview.lua`) in `game_passivetree`.

- **Auto build** button (tree window): a dropdown with Recommended (2 to 4 builds per class, 3 roles, 21 classes) and Focus
  themes (leech, mana, damage, ...), each with its points and a one-line summary. Opcode 65 actions `autobuildList` /
  `autobuildPreview` / `autobuildApply {build, mode = "add" | "reset", cost}`. Apply only adds the nodes you can pay and takes
  nothing back. Reset and apply takes the tree back at the normal respec price (a free reset is used first) and builds the
  chosen one; the price shown in the preview is the one sent back. Rate limited: Apply `passivetree.autobuild` (1 s),
  the preview its own `passivetree.autobuildPreview` (`previewRateMs`, 500 ms). Every preview request is answered: a
  refused one with `autobuildError {message, build, retry}` (retry: too fast), a Lua error with `autobuildError` too.
  Fix 2026-10-20 (owner report: stuck at "Asking the server for a preview..."): the client asked for a preview only on
  its first list, so after an Apply or on reopening the window it waited for an answer to a request it never sent. It
  now asks whenever no preview is shown, asks again after 4 s (3 tries) and then shows an error. The skipped count of
  the plan also says "points" for the rest of a path once the points run out (it said "disconnected", which the client
  showed as nodes the class cannot hold). A preview is at most about 2.3 KB (one message, tested for every build).
- **Drown nodes** are gone: 23 nodes hidden in `nodes.lua`, refunded once (`reworked` version 4), the tree has 640 nodes.
- **Primary / Secondary** per class: `passivetree_stats_config.lua` `classes[...]` (the Templar line counts mana leech as
  secondary: its spells cost mana). The window shows a header, a gold (primary) or silver (secondary) border on nodes and a
  legend; the Stats button lists every stat with its description (en + pt-BR in `i18n_strings.lua`), and the node tooltip adds
  the description lines. `statInfo` message, 10 stats a part.
- **Class lanes**: every class has its own re-skin of the plain nodes (`v` in `passivetree_data.lua`, from
  `treedata/classlanes.lua`, which `tools/gen_class_lanes.lua` writes; Mystic and Elementalist share one lane). The test
  `tests/passivetree_paths_test.lua` checks, for every class, that the shortest route to every keystone and notable it can
  reach has no irrelevant node and at least `paths.minShare` (70%) primary / secondary nodes. `reworked` version 5
  (`lanes = true`) refunds once the lane nodes (and what hangs on them) of each character at login.
- **Hand-set lanes** (`gen_class_lanes.lua` `Gen.OVERRIDES`, 2026-10-22): even with the new dexterity cap (80) the Thief and
  the Ninja collected far more dexterity from their lanes (Thief 137 / 199 at 100 / 150 points, Ninja 138 / 213), so their
  most taken 10-point Attribute nodes give all-element resistance (`absorbAllElements` 2, now a secondary stat of both)
  instead of dexterity 10: Thief 130, 132, 157, 173, 238; Ninja 130, 132, 238. Same ids and cost, no refund (a held node
  just gives the resistance). `classlanes.lua` carries them by hand too (the generator's output already differs, see above).
- **Attribute worth in the Auto builds:** `caps` and `statCurve` match the effect file's curve (`passivetree_stats_test`
  checks the numbers and `Gen.curveValue` against `ChaosPassiveCharStat`); an attribute node scores the value it adds from
  where the build stands on the curve. Scores are rounded to 1e-9 so LuaJIT and Lua 5.3 (different `pairs()` order,
  different float sums) write the same bytes.
- **Lane names** (client only, 2026-10-20): a lane re-skinned a named node's stats but the tooltip, search and refund box
  kept its old name ("Pyre Litany", holy, gave a Beastmaster physical damage; "Speed" gave a Berserker strength). The
  client's `treelanes.lua` now names every re-skinned named node after the stats the class gets ("Physical Damage and
  Vitality", "Strength"); the generic "Attribute" stays. The server tree has no names; the data files did not change.
  `treelanes_test.lua` checks every node of every class.
- **Passive tree: attack speed nodes (2026-10-28, patch 0078).** New stat `attackSpeed` (percent, a real attack speed; the
  stat help and the totals panel say "at most 1 attack per second"). No new node ids: `gen_class_lanes.lua --attack-speed`
  (only the attack speed lanes, on top of `classlanes.lua` as it is; a full run would drop the hand trims) gives the classes
  that fight with weapon hits (Warrior, Juggernaut, Berserker, Ranger, Deadeye, Beastmaster, Thief, Ninja, Samurai, Monk,
  Shadowfist, Templar; `Gen.ATTACK_SPEED`) 10 small nodes (+1%, +2% from 3 dexterity) on the plain Attribute nodes that gave
  them dexterity and are walked most, and up to 2 notable nodes (+4%, +5% from 6 dexterity) from the named or big
  dexterity-only nodes (a Juggernaut has one). The other classes see no attack speed. Cap: the tree counts at most +8
  (`maxAttackSpeed`), tree plus worn pieces +12 (`playerSpeedCap`), then the engine rules (40% together, 1000 ms floor).
  The stat is a primary (Ranger, Deadeye, Thief, Ninja, Shadowfist) or secondary (others) stat in
  `passivetree_stats_config.lua`; the Speed Focus build (`mobility`) values it. Client: the node tooltip line, the totals
  panel line ("Attack speed: +N% (tree, gear)", `totalsview.lua`). Dexterity keeps its damage equal.
- Regenerate in this order after a tree or config change: `gen_class_lanes.lua`, `gen_passivetree_data.lua` (from the client
  treedata folder), `gen_passive_builds.lua`, `gen_wiki_data.lua`, `gen_codex_data.lua`.
- Tests: `passive_builds_test`, `passivetree_stats_test`, `passivetree_paths_test`, `passivetree_plan_test`; client
  `autobuildview_test.lua`, `autobuild_test.lua` (the window's requests against a mocked client), `statinfoview_test.lua`.
  Not checked in game: the dropdown, the node borders (`setBorderColor`), the
  tree preview of a build, the lane balance (damage and resist caps are reached with fewer points).
- Ascension refunds the tree once (O305). The plain nodes (shared stats `s`) are read with the character's own lane key, and
  the ascended lanes differ from the base class's on 289 nodes (Ranger -> Beastmaster turned Vitality / Dexterity nodes into
  Spirit, tester report), so the lanes stay (Auto build and the presets are built on them) but an ascension no longer
  changes allocated nodes silently. `ChaosPassiveTree.refundLaneChange(player, live)` (`passivetree.lua`) runs from
  `ChaosClasses.afterVocationChange` (ascension, `!ascend` switch, store class change) and at every login. Storage
  `Chaos.storage.passiveLane` (7100029) records the vocation id the tree was made under, -1 = none. When the variant key of
  the recorded vocation differs from the current one (`Core.laneChangeFrom`), the allocated nodes that give other stats under
  the new key (`Core.laneDiff`) and the nodes only connected through them are removed from every preset and saved loadout, for
  free, once, with a message (pt-BR in `i18n_strings.lua`): "Your ascension changed your passive tree to the <Class> lane:
  your N points were refunded for free. Open the tree to spend them, or use Auto build." A character that ascended before the
  record existed (-1 and an ascended vocation) is taken to have planned under its base class's lane and is refunded at its
  next login; an unascended character is only recorded. Mystic / Elementalist share a key and get nothing. Assumption: a
  pre-fix ascended character that already re-planned under the ascended lane loses the differing nodes too (once; free).
  Tests: `passivetree_death_test` (login and ascension, once, not for an unascended class), `passivetree_paths_test` "ascension".

## Passive tree pick statistics (`treestats.lua`, `treestats_core.lua`, `treestats_config.lua`)
Beta telemetry of the tree: how often each node is taken, per class line and level band, read from the saved trees on
demand (one query over `chaos_passive_tree` joined with `players`; no hook on allocations, nothing stored). Staff only
(`Chaos.staffCommand`: access, every use in the admin audit log), at most one request per 5 s per staff member.

- `/treestats`: characters with a saved tree per line and band. `/treestats <class> [band] [n]`: the n most taken nodes
  (default 10, at most 40) with count, share of the characters and the node's stats, and the never-taken nodes of the
  line (the count and the first 40 ids). The class may be the line or any class of it ("ninja" = the Thief line); the
  band "1-99", "100-299", "300-499", "500-999", "1000+", a level ("350") or "all" (the default). `/treestats export`
  writes every line, band and node the line may take (counts of 0 included) to `data/chaos_tree_picks_<YYYYMMDD-HHMM>.csv`
  in the server folder: `line,band,characters,node,count,share,stats`.
- Who counts: one tree per character, the active preset (the lowest preset number, as the tree reads it); characters
  with an empty tree, of a retired vocation, marked for deletion or of group 4 and up (staff test characters) are left
  out. Unknown (retired) node ids are not counted. Bands and the rest: `treestats_config.lua`.
- **Counts only.** No character name, id or account is in a report or the CSV. A line and band with fewer than 3
  characters (`minCharacters`) is not written to the CSV (its counts would show one character's build); the command marks
  it "(few characters: not in the CSV)" and the export lists what it left out.
- Example (test data: 4 Warrior-line and 5 Thief-line characters, one staff tree left out):

```
> /treestats berserker 300-499 5
Passive tree picks: warrior, level 300-499, 4 characters.
Top 5:
 1. node 2  3 (75%)  strength+1
 2. node 9  3 (75%)  incrementPhysical+2
 3. node 11  3 (75%)  absorbPhysical+1
 4. node 13  3 (75%)  strength+1
 5. node 61  3 (75%)  weaponsmithSkill+1
Never taken: 594 nodes: 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 12, 14, 15, ...
> /treestats export
Written data/chaos_tree_picks_20261012-0745.csv: 2490 rows (counts only).
Left out (fewer than 3 characters): thief 100-299, thief 1000+.
```

- `server/tests/treestats_test.lua`: bands, the active preset, staff / empty / retired left out, counts per line and band
  and "all", top N and ties, never-taken, the node descriptions, the report, the CSV (every node of the line, small
  groups left out, seven fields a row, no names) and the command against a mocked engine (class and band words, a level,
  unknown words, the export file, staff only).
- Not run against a live database: the query's join (`players.deletion`, `players.group_id`) is the base schema's.

## Respec (`respec.lua`, `respec_core.lua`, `respec_config.lua`, `tools/respec_income.py`)
What taking passive points back costs. Every number is in `respec_config.lua`.
- **Full reset** of the tree (Reset button) and of the Paragon track (its Reset button): a level curve worth about 37.5 minutes of
  hunting gold at the level, linear between the points below (and the last slope past level 1000). Paragon uses the same curve
  (`paragonFactor` 1.0). Rounded down to 1,000 gold. Paid from carried gold, then the bank (`Chaos.pay`).

| Level | 49 | 50 | 100 | 200 | 300 | 500 | 600 | 1000 | 1200 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Full reset | free | 50,000 | 225,000 | 395,000 | 565,000 | 3,450,000 | 3,950,000 | 5,950,000 | 6,950,000 |
| Single-node refund | free | 2,000 | 9,000 | 15,000 | 22,000 | 138,000 | 158,000 | 238,000 | 278,000 |

- **Single-node refund:** right-click a saved node in the tree, confirm (the dialog shows the price). The server checks that the
  node is allocated and that every other allocated node stays connected to the start without it (a leaf, or a node on a loop),
  then charges 4% of the full reset price (~1.5 minutes of hunting) and frees the point. Not-yet-saved nodes are still taken back
  for free with a left click, as before.
- **Free cases:** everything below level 50; **one free full reset after the vocation changed** (ascension, class migration): the
  vocation id of the last free reset is kept in storage `7100550` (`freeVocationStorage`), recorded at the first login with
  `respec.lua`, and a different vocation means the next full reset (tree, Paragon or a build import that takes points back) is free.
  The store's vocation change keeps resetting the tree for free, and the store's Passive Tree Reset service stays a free reset of
  tree and Paragon; both go through `ChaosPassiveTree.resetAll`, which `respec.lua` wraps so it also uses up a pending free reset
  (no double free reset after a vocation change).
- **Client:** the server sends `respecInfo {level, full, paragon, node, free, freeBelowLevel}` with every `requestPoints` and after
  each reset / refund (`game_passivetree/respec.lua`). The Reset button tooltip and the reset dialog show the tree price and the
  node price, the refund dialog the node price, the Paragon reset dialog the Paragon price (`paragonState.resetCost`).
- Protocol (opcode 65, `ChaosPassiveTree.extraActions`): `respecInfo` -> `respecInfo`; `refundNode {id}` -> `sendNodes`,
  `sendPoints`, `respecInfo`; `resetPreset` and `paragonReset` are handled here (the old handlers in `passivetree.lua` /
  `paragon.lua` remain as the level x 250 fallback when `respec.lua` is not loaded).
- **Measured income** (`python3 -I server/tools/respec_income.py <server>/data`): for each level the best of the hunts that are
  spawned in the map, gold per hour = kills per hour x (expected coins + NPC sell value of the drops from `sell_prices.lua`, i.e.
  what the Auto Seller pays) x 1.11 (the Chaos loot layer's extra rolls at the tier spawn chances). Coin counts use the stock
  level count multiplier; health the engine's level bonus. Kills per hour = 3600 x 0.47 x average 5-target rotation DPS
  (`data/spells/README.md`: 1804 at level 300, 4337 at 1000, linear) / health; the late-game monsters 3 at a time (x0.75). This is
  the leveling model's estimate, not a measured hunt.

| Level | Best hunt (spawned) | Kills / h | Coins / h | Item sale value / h | Total / h | Full reset = minutes | Node refund = minutes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100 | Dragons (Dragon, Dragon Lord, Wyrm, Hydra) | 1,033 | 67,777 | 291,062 | 358,839 | 37.6 | 1.5 |
| 300 | Demons (Demon, Hellspawn, Behemoth, Dark Torturer, Juggernaut) | 355 | 158,430 | 723,436 | 881,866 | 38.4 | 1.5 |
| 500 | Soul War (8 monsters, 905 spawns) | 158 | 1,410,416 | 4,137,915 | 5,548,330 | 37.3 | 1.5 |
| 600 | Soul War | 181 | 1,612,325 | 4,730,281 | 6,342,606 | 37.4 | 1.5 |
| 1000 | Soul War | 272 | 2,419,962 | 7,099,748 | 9,519,711 | 37.5 | 1.5 |

  The late-game tier 3 monsters (Nightglass Core, `tools/late_game_spawns.csv`) are an experience hunt, not a gold hunt: about
  162,000 gold per hour at level 1000 (33 kills, little coin loot), so the curve follows Soul War, which a level 1000 character can
  still hunt. The jump at level 500 is where Soul War opens. Vexclaw (in `monsters.xml` as `Vexclaw.xml`, file `vexclaw.xml`) is not
  loaded by the server and left out.
- `server/tests/respec_test.lua`: the curve points, linear parts, monotony, the minutes against the measured income, free cases,
  `canRemove` (leaf, middle, loop, root, unallocated), and the handlers against a mocked engine (refund, paid / free / used-up
  reset, the store wrapper, below 50, Paragon, `requestPoints`).
- Tested on the test server (level 599): Reset tooltip and dialog showed 3,945,000 / 157,000, the reset charged 3,945,000 from the
  bank, a right-click refund of node 4 (on a loop) charged 157,000 and freed the point, a refund of node 11 (others depend on it) was
  refused with its message. Not seen in game: the free reset after a class change (unit test only; the test server was killed by the
  machine's memory limit during that run) and the Paragon reset dialog (character below level 1000).

**Respec waiver for testers (O255).** The tester bots have 20,000 gold, so above level 50 they could not pay the reset after
every node of the keystone run (O249). Instead of giving them gold, `Respec.pay` waives the price for a tester, and credits
nothing: no gold exists that could leave the account. `R.testerWaived(player, cost)` (core: `R.testerWaiver`) requires all of:
