and fewer than `testerWaiver.perDay` (400) waivers today (storages 7102905 = day, 7102906 = count, reset on a new day). A normal
account, a tagged character with another name, any staff character and a tester over the cap pay as always. Every waiver prints
`[Chaos respec] waived N gold for tester NAME (guid, level), K of 400 today`; a refusal or the cap prints a line as well.
The price shown in the window is unchanged. Nothing sets the tag but `tools/testers.py setup`. No dev key is involved.
Test: `tests/respec_test.lua`.

## Arena looks (O276: `arenalook_core.lua`)

Owner request 2026-10-27: "as arenas de bosses, infinity tower e tudo mais precisam de um rework". The runtime-built fight rooms were flat floors with a wall ring (the dark tile set, when installed, only scattered decoration with `math.random`). `arenalook_core.lua` is the shared, pure look generator, modelled on the Scorched Marches (`pvpzone_core.lua`).

- **What it builds.** For a floor (any list of tiles): a base ground and patches of other grounds with border pieces (`ChaosAreaGenCore.borderPieces`), a rim of another ground along the wall plus rubble (the wall has depth), a paved lane between two points, lights (blocking braziers) standing against the wall, cover pieces and walkable decoration. Everything is a function of the coordinates (a hash, no `math.random`) and of the seed, so a look is the same in every slot and in every test; looks are cached.
- **Guarantees** (`tests/arenalook_test.lua`): the free floor stays one 4-connected field; keep points (arrival, boss spot, gates, fixtures) and lanes stay open; no two solid pieces touch, not even on a diagonal, so a lane is never narrower than one tile; with `mirror` every solid piece has its image turned 180 degrees (fair for PvP and for the two ends of a hall).
- **Themes.** `ember` (scorched rock, basalt, lava cracks), `stone` (flagstone and marble) and `crypt` (slate, rock, bones), all with stock ids that the generated hunting areas or the Marches already use (a test checks the ids against `areagen_config.lua`, `pvpzone_config.lua` and the arena configs). `dark` is the dark tile set (`data/lib/chaos_dark_tiles.lua`) as a fourth theme; without the set installed it falls back to `ember`. `ChaosArenaLook.themeFor(name)` picks by keyword (fire, lich, abyss...) and else by a hash of the name.
- **Rooms.** `ChaosArenaLook.dress(roomKey, rect, z, theme, opts)` paints a rectangular room: it removes what a former painting left (only ids the looks own), paints the new look and gives any tile without a ground the plain one (never a hole). A room painted with the same theme and layout is left alone, so a slot that serves many bosses is repainted only when the theme changes. The caller places its fixtures (basins, pillars, gates) after the call.
- **Where it is used.**
  - Infinity Tower (`infinitytower_run.lua`, `cfg.look`): inner size 19 -> 25 (slot spacing 40 holds it), one theme and one of six layout variants per run in turn. The group starts in the open middle (keep radius 3); monsters appear around it and never on a cover piece; a paved lane runs from the south wall; each floor shows a floating label; the entry message states the goal. Before the first build of a slot the whole footprint is checked (a tile of the map refuses the run with a message instead of building over it); a slot stays "ours" across a script reload. After a run the slot is wiped (items, walls and ground) so the next run repaints. Balance numbers are untouched (`tools/tower_model.py --check`).
  - World boss arena and lobby (`worldboss.lua`, `Chaos.worldBoss.arena.look`): theme by boss name, repainted when the boss changes; the arrival, boss spot, the lane between them (the boss sees the entry), the four pillars and the basins stay open. The lobby gets ground, rim and rubble only.
  - Pocket boss, guild boss and Ascended arenas (`pocketboss.lua`, `guildboss.lua`, `uber.lua`; `look` in their configs; `ChaosArenaLook.dressBossArena`): theme per boss (the Ascended omens and the guild boss are set in the config), mirrored cover and lights, the arrival, starts, boss spot, middle, corner basins and the pocket's second gate open, a free lane from the entry to the boss. The footprint checks of the three also accept the looks' grounds, so a script reload cannot mark a built slot as foreign.
  - Ranked PvP arena (`arena.lua`, `arena_config.lua` `look`): a theme per slot in turn, cover and lights mirrored for the two teams, spawns, the centre line and the stone pillars open.
- **Clean-ups keep the look.** The `cleanSlot` / `cleanArena` of these systems keep every id `ChaosArenaLook.isOwned` returns true for.
- **Second part (O276, all remaining fight rooms).** The Battleground, the Ember Descent hall, the Vocation Trials and the Sepulchre raid no longer paint with `ChaosDarkPaint` (the dark paint stays for rifts, the dungeon and other areas, see "Dark tile set"). New in `arenalook_core.lua`: `dressTiles(roomKey, tiles, z, theme, o)` dresses a floor of any shape (`dress` is a rectangle through it; `o.plain` lists tiles that keep their own ground, with no border piece or decoration), and `freeSpot(roomKey, pos, maxR)` moves a position that lies on a cover piece or light to the nearest open tile (monster spawns of the Descent, the Trials and the raid use it). Their clean-ups keep every id `isOwned` returns true for and their footprint checks accept the looks' grounds.
  - Battleground "Ember Wells" (`battleground.lua`, `battleground_config.lua` `look`, `ChaosBattlegroundCore.lookSpec`): theme `ember`, `cover` 3, `lights` 6, mirrored. The field and the bases are dressed; the closed graveyards and every wall are left out (one connected field for the flood check); bases and capture circles keep their grounds (`plain`). Open of cover: all spawns (radius 1), both bases, the three wells (capture radius + 1), pillars, flags; a paved lane runs between the two spawns through the three wells. The layout is a 180-degree turn for team 2 and the look is mirrored about the same middle, so every cover piece and light has its twin: both teams get the same field. A test in `battleground_flow_test.lua` checks it on the real script (cover mirrored, nothing on walls, graveyards, bases or circles, spawns and wells reachable).
  - Ember Descent (`descent.lua`, `descent_config.lua` `look`): one theme per rift theme in turn (Abyssal Rift `dark`, Obsidian Hall `ember`, Ashen Crypt `crypt`, Forsaken Sanctum `stone`; `dark` is `ember` while the dark set is not installed). Each room repaints the hall (the old pieces are removed only when theme or layout change) with layout variant `seed + depth mod variants`, so two rooms of a theme differ. Not mirrored. Open: the arrival (radius 3), the gate (2), the middle where the altar, stand, chest and boss stand (2) and the corner lights; a lane runs from the arrival to the gate.
  - Vocation Trials (`trials.lua`, `trials_config.lua` `room.look`): theme by tier (`stone`, `crypt`, `dark`), layout by vocation (seed + vocation mod 3), `cover` 3, `lights` 4, repainted at the start of a run when theme or layout changed. Open: the player's start (3), the guardian's spot (2), the middle (2), the four seals and the corner lights (1) and a lane between start and guardian, so no mechanic (seals, marks, zones, the pyre) meets a solid piece; thralls and marks made on a cover piece step to an open tile.
  - Sepulchre raid (`raid.lua`, `raid_config.lua` `look`): the whole floor (hall, five corridors, five boss rooms) is one shape in one `dressTiles` call so the openings between rooms are real openings; theme `crypt`, `cover` 3, `lights` 14, painted when a slot is built. Open: exit, arrival, the fallen spot, each room's entry, middle and boss spot, the Font of Ash tiles, the pack spots, the door tiles of every corridor (their middle with the corridor's half width) and a lane from the hall to the last boss; `spawn` moves a monster off a cover piece. The mechanics' own free-tile search (adds, totems) already skipped blocked tiles. A block in `raid_test.lua` checks it on the real script.
  - Tests: `tests/arenalook_places_test.lua` (Descent hall and Trial chamber for every theme and layout, `dressTiles` on an L-shaped floor with plain tiles, `freeSpot`, repaint removes the old theme's pieces, 2x2 walls), blocks in `battleground_flow_test.lua` and `raid_test.lua`. The Descent hall layout is repeated in the test (it is built in the engine file); keep it equal to `X.layout`.
- **Not changed.** The rift, dungeon and waystone maps are generated by the area generator or are map areas of the base server; the Tower Defense room is a base map room. No VPS install step: the looks use stock items and are applied at runtime.
- Tests: `tests/arenalook_test.lua` (generator), `tests/arenalook_arenas_test.lua` (Ascended, guild boss, pocket boss and PvP layouts for every theme and slot), `tests/arenalook_places_test.lua` (Descent hall, Trial chamber, irregular shapes, `freeSpot`), plus blocks in `infinitytower_run_test.lua`, `worldboss_test.lua`, `battleground_flow_test.lua` and `raid_test.lua`.

## Infinity Tower gameplay (`infinitytower_run.lua`)
The tower exists now. The Enter Tower button of the client window (action `enter`) takes you, or your party (leader only, members within 12 tiles, up to 4), into an arena that is built at runtime with `Game.createTile` in an empty part of the map (x from 2000, y 2000, z 7; sixteen arenas side by side), so no map editing is needed. Floors are waves: kill everything to open the next one (6 s pause, half of the missing health and mana restored, `floorGold` x floor gold); every 10th floor is a boss floor with its helpers (twice the floor time since 2026-10-13: 10 minutes). Pools get harder every 8 floors, and the chance of magic, rare and legendary monsters (with their modifiers and shaders) rises with the floor. A floor has a 300 s limit and a whole run 60 minutes (`runTimeLimit`, warnings at 5 min, 1 min and 10 s, the floor's at 1 min and 10 s; "Instance limits"); at most 16 arenas, the wait and the waiting line when all are busy. Dying, leaving (the Leave Tower button), logging out or running out of time ends your part of the run and records the cleared floors with `ChaosTower.recordRun` (points, best floor, ranking, milestones). Logging in inside an arena sends you to the temple. Milestone rewards now use item ids that exist (gold, Orbs of Upheaval and Fate, Soulreaper). Everything is configured at the top of the file (`ChaosTowerRunConfig`).
- `server/tests/infinitytower_run_test.lua` covers the floor planner, entering, clearing floors, dying, leaving, the time limit, logout and login with a mocked engine; CI runs it with LuaJIT and Lua 5.3. The real `Game.createTile`, `Tile:addItem`, `Game.createMonster` and teleport calls are assumed from the engine sources, not run.
- **Next floor now and the tower panel (O274).** Floors have no waves (all monsters of a floor appear together), so there is no "call next wave"; the button skips the wait. Opcode 214 got three actions, no new opcode: client `{"action":"skip"}` starts the next floor at once, `{"action":"state"}` asks for the state; the server pushes `{"action":"state", inRun, canSkip, isLeader, floor, nextBoss, boss, cleared, waiting, remaining, total, nextIn | floorLeft}` on entry, floor start, every kill, floor cleared and leaving (the client counts the countdowns on its own clock). `ChaosTowerRun.skip` (`infinitytower_run.lua`, config `ChaosTowerRunConfig.skip`) refuses unless: the player is in an active run and inside the arena; the run is waiting (start delay or pause, so the floor is cleared: never two floors alive, no kill skipped, nothing stacks); the player is the run leader (any member once the leader died or left, so a member cannot rush a group); the next floor is not a boss floor (`intoBoss = false`: the pause before a boss is kept); and `minInterval` (2 s) since the last press, on top of the 300 ms per-action limit of `infinitytower.lua`. A timer sequence number makes the skipped pause timer do nothing. Records and rewards: floor gold, rewards, the heal and `ChaosRecords.towerFloor` all run when a floor is cleared, before the pause, so a skip only drops the 6 s of regeneration; the run clock is real time, so a fast climb is faster by at most 6 s a floor, the same for everyone, and `tower_model.py` (which models the fight, not the pause) is unchanged and passes. Tests: `tests/infinitytower_run_test.lua` ("Next floor now"). Client: see `client/MANIFEST.md` game_infinitytower.
- Not done: a visible ladder of floors in the client window (since O144 it shows the next reward, see "Infinity Tower balance and floor rewards"). Check that x 2000..2700, y 2000..2020, z 7 is really empty in your map (it is in the map analysed: the content starts at x 18992).

## Infinity Tower balance and floor rewards (O144: `infinitytower_balance_config.lua`, `infinitytower_balance_core.lua`, `tools/tower_model.py`)

Beta feedback of 2026-10-22: tower monsters were much stronger than outside ones, a level 800 player was always stuck
between floors 20 and 29, a level 500 friend needed a minute for one level-100 monster, the drops looked like outside
and there was no reward per floor.

**Root cause (computed; `tower_model.py --before` is the planner of 2026-10-22).**
- The tower is excluded from `pace.lua`, so floors held the stock pool health, while a hunt pack is thinned to 0.36 - 0.21
  of it. With 12-16 monsters and tier chances that rose every floor, a floor held 4x, 12x and 24x the health of an outside
  pack of the same species at floors 15, 25 and 35.
- A single legendary monster (health x6 plus modifiers such as Juggernaut x1.6 and Stoneskin) is the minute-per-monster report.
- The wall at floor 29: floor 30 held Zeburoth, who heals 1,750 health a second. A median class below about level 1100
  cannot out-damage that, so the fight never ended (`never` in the table). Ashvoran (floor 90) is the same.
- Damage taken was the stock monster damage, not the pace curve of the hunts.

**What changed.**
- Health per floor is a curve by the floor's meant level (`level`) and the seconds a median class needs for the floor
  (`clear`), times a sawtooth over each climb of five floors (0.75, 0.88, 1.00, 1.10, 1.22: the floor after a milestone
  floor is a breather). `health`, `bossHealth` and `damage` are generated by `python3 -I server/tools/tower_model.py --derive`
  (the unit test diffs them with the config).
- 4 monsters on floor 1 up to 9 from floor 120 (was 12-16), two more for every player after the first. A boss floor has a third
  as helpers.
- Tiers: health x1.5 magic, x2.2 rare, x3.5 legendary in the tower (stock x2, x3.5, x6; `infinitytower_run.lua` sets the health
  before the stock tier applies). The chances rise slowly (legendary 1% on floor 30, 4% on floor 120).
- Bosses in a new order, the healers last: the Ashen Count, the Grey Widow, Massacre, Vharagoth, Moloveth, Vhalkareth,
  Jungle's Revenge, Ssylvath the Corruptor, Pestrogh, Morgashal (floor 100), Zeburoth (110), Ashvoran (120).
- Tower monsters hit x0.99 of the stock damage on floor 1, x0.67 on floor 44 and x0.72 from floor 52: the pace damage curve of the
  pool's hunting level (`ChaosTowerRun.damageMultOf`, read by `monster_damage.lua`). Bosses hit as before.
- Also fixed: a late timer of an earlier run in the same arena slot no longer starts or ends the next run.

**Time to clear a floor, median class (computed, not measured in game; seconds for a solo player at the level in the column).**

Before (planner of 2026-10-22):

| Floor | L100 | L300 | L500 | L800 | L1000 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 4 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| 10 B | 23 | 9 | 7 | 5 | 5 |
| 20 B | 236 | 81 | 54 | 36 | 30 |
| 25 | 41 | 16 | 10 | 8 | 7 |
| 30 B | never | never | never | never | 486 |
| 35 | 111 | 39 | 24 | 16 | 13 |
| 40 B | never | 250 | 135 | 81 | 64 |

After:

| Floor | Hunt pack | L100 | L300 | L500 | L800 | L1000 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 3.0 s at L100 | 6 | 4 | 4 | 3 | 3 |
| 10 B | 3.8 s at L300 | 145 | 50 | 34 | 24 | 20 |
| 20 B | 4.6 s at L540 | 307 | 92 | 60 | 40 | 33 |
| 25 | 5.3 s at L640 | 53 | 20 | 13 | 9 | 8 |
| 30 B | 10.6 s at L740 | 402 | 136 | 90 | 60 | 49 |
| 35 | 10.4 s at L820 | 97 | 34 | 21 | 14 | 12 |
| 40 B | 10.3 s at L900 | 673 | 186 | 119 | 78 | 63 |
| 60 B | 9.9 s at L1250 | 1026 | 287 | 183 | 119 | 97 |

A boss floor keeps the long time: a boss is one target with a heal. A player far under the floor's level (the L100 column
on floor 40) is meant to be slow. `python3 -I server/tools/tower_model.py` prints the whole table, `--before` the old
one, `--levels` and `--floors` pick columns and rows.

**Where a player gets to** (floors cleared within 1.1 x the time of a hunt pack of the player's level, median class):
level 100 floor 1, 300 floor 12, 500 floor 18 (21 until O285), 800 floor 38 (was 29), 1000 floor 44 (was 29), 1500 floor 64, 2000 floor 93
(was 40). The weakest class at level 800 reaches floor 34.

**O285 (2026-10-28, hunting level = pool level).** The hunt pack a floor is compared with is the base pack at the floor's level, and
the species of a band are read at their pool level (`_pool_level` no longer doubles it). The floors did not change; the
tower `damage` line did, to the `--derive` line (the pace damage curve at the half level: 1.0 / 1.0 / 0.86 / 0.83 / 0.79 /
0.76 / 0.8 / 0.86 at floors 1 / 12 / 20 / 28 / 36 / 44 / 52 / 120, it was 0.99 ... 0.78). The base health curve of `pace_config.lua`
was re-fitted to the old pack times (README "Pack combat (pace)"), which keeps the three floors the new pool levels had
pushed out of the 0.6-1.7 band (6, 11, 25: 0.56, 0.56, 1.90) inside it.

**CI (`python3 -I server/tools/tower_model.py --check`, limits in `infinitytower_balance_config.lua` `limits`).** Bounds, per
floor: the seconds a group of the meant level needs (1.5-24), the ratio to a base hunt pack of that level (0.6-1.7), the
seconds of a boss (30-150) and the share of the class's damage its heal eats (at most 50%), the weakest class against a
boss (300 s), the breather after a milestone floor, the step from floor to floor (at most x1.35), a player at 60% of the
floor's level (at most 60 s), the reach of a level 800 median class (30-40) and of a weak class (20+), a single legendary
monster's lifetime (30 s) and the damage curve against the pace curve (12%). `tower_model_test.py` covers the parser, the
tier factor, the old planner reproducing the floor 29 wall and bad configs failing. Lua side:
`tests/infinitytower_balance_test.lua` (the core) and `tests/infinitytower_run_test.lua` (the run on a mocked engine).

**Floor rewards.**
- First clear, once per character and tower season, on every 5th floor: Crystal Coins (the floor number: 5 on floor 5, 10 on floor 10);
  on every 10th floor Orbs of Upheaval (2 on floor 10, plus 1 per 10 floors) and Orbs of Fate (at least 1, 1 per 20 floors); on floors
  25, 50, 75, ... 2 more Orbs of Fate plus 1 per 25 floors. The rules are `rewards.firstClear`, all numbers in the config.
- Repeatable, on every clear of a milestone floor: Crystal Coins (a quarter of the floor number, at least 1) and on every 10th
  floor at least 1 Orb of Upheaval (`rewards.repeatable`).
- Delivery: `Chaos.giveItem`, what does not fit goes to the inbox. Each player in a group is paid by their own storage.
- Storage `rewards.storage` = 7102820: season x 1000 + the highest floor paid, so a new season pays again.
- Tower drops (`drops`, in an `onDropLoot` callback): an Orb of Upheaval (0.25% a kill) and Crystal Coins (4%, 1-2) from every
  monster, an Orb of Fate (0.12%) from floor 20; a magic monster x1.5, rare x3, legendary x6 the chance. The stock loot stays.
- The next milestone reward is shown in the tower window ("Season Informations" panel, `nextRewardLabel`), after every milestone
  floor and in the entry message, in English and Portuguese (`i18n_strings.lua`, `pt_br.lua`).

**Experience.** Not changed: the pool monsters give far less experience than a hunt of the player's level, so an hour in the
tower stays well under an hour of hunting (the tower is for points and rewards).

**Deploy.** `files` step and a script reload or restart; the client needs the new build for the reward label (an old client
shows no label, nothing else breaks). No SQL, no engine patch. New storage block 7102820. Not modeled: the player's armour and
resistances, damage taken in the tower, and uptime beyond the factors in the config. Computed, not measured in game.


**Monster level follows the floor (O168, beta 2026-10-24: "level does not scale").** The tower made its monsters with a
plain `Game.createMonster`, so `monster_levels.lua` showed the species' own level (the same on floor 1 and floor 100),
although health, damage and drops already followed the floor. `B.level` (the `level` curve, the level the floor is
meant for, the one the health is derived from) is now in every spawn of `B.plan`, and `infinitytower_run.lua` creates
each monster with `Chaos.createMonsterNamed(..., nil, level)`, so `Chaos.spawnLevel` shows "[level]" in the first
creature packet (engine patch 0044 lets it win over a level of the monster's own). The level is the floor's, not the
players'. Tests: `infinitytower_run_test.lua`, `infinitytower_balance_test.lua`. Server restart, no client change.

**Second report, same day: floors 1 to 130 felt the same, the bosses "just walked in circles".** Checked against the TFS
1.4.2 Lua API instead of trusting the first analysis:
- Health: `Creature:setMaxHealth` is a stock method (it works on monsters) and `Creature:setHealth` is clamped to the maximum,
  so the order matters; `spawnPlan` sets the maximum first, then the health, so the health curve held. The new
  `tests/infinitytower_floor_test.lua` has a mock that clamps `setHealth` like the engine and checks floors 1 to 42 (every
  monster above its species' own health, the boss floors' `bossHealth`, `levelOf`, the damage factor).
- Damage was the gap. `monster_damage.lua` boosts a monster's physical hit by its level (`ChaosLoot.monsterLevel`, the species'
  own level for a tower monster), so a floor 100 troll hit like a level 20 one. `ChaosTowerRun.levelOf(monster)` returns the
  level of its floor (summons too) and `MD.levelOf` takes at least that, the way it does for invaders. The floor's own
  factor (`damage`, the pace curve) stays on top. Bosses get the level boost as well, but not the factor.
- The natural tier roll of `monster_tiers.lua` (registered in `onSpawn` for every eligible monster, and 4-5 modifiers for a boss)
  ran at the first think of tower monsters too: a boss got Juggernaut (health x1.6), Regenerating or Stoneskin on top of
  the tuned `bossHealth` (the world bosses skip it for the same reason). `spawnPlan` now unregisters the four roll events
  (`ChaosTierRoll...`); the planned tier of the floor is applied by `ChaosApplyTier` as before.
- Walking in circles: a monster without a target only takes random steps. A 2 second tick per floor (`engageTick`) gives every
  tower monster without a target the nearest living player of the run (`Monster:selectTarget`), like `trials.lua` and
  `nemesis.lua`. The base boss XMLs are not in the repo and the tower bosses have no profile in `boss_mechanics_config.lua`,
  so a cause inside a boss file or the engine (for example a ranged boss that keeps its distance without a path) cannot be
  proven here. Owner check on the live server: the flags of the boss XMLs in the installed base (`targetdistance`,
  `staticattack`, `runonhealth`) and whether the build has 8d286bf7 and this commit (the first report matches a build without the display level: "level 80-100 from floor 20" is the dragon pool).
- Tests: `infinitytower_floor_test.lua`, `monster_damage_test.lua`. Server restart, no client change, no engine patch.

**Endless floors (O172, owner 2026-10-24: "the higher the floor, the stronger the monsters, without end").** Every curve was flat
above its last point: `level` and `health` above floor 120, `damage` from floor 52, the boss table repeated (and floor 110
had 187000 against 277000 on floor 100). Now `infinitytower_balance_config.lua` `beyond` takes over above `maxFloor` (120), d =
floor - 120:
- level = curve + 12.5 x d (the slope of the last segment); capped at 2e9.
- normal monster health = curve x growth x sawtooth, boss health = the floor 120 boss x growth, monster damage factor = curve x growth.
  growth = exp(rate x d + accel x d^2 / 2): health and boss health rate 0.007 and accel 0.000002, damage rate 0.002 and accel 0.000004.
  The step from a floor to the next is rate + accel x d, so it climbs (0.7% a floor at 121, 0.84% at 800): a soft wall, not a
  cliff. The first step is above the level's own growth (12.5 of 2200 is 0.57%), so the time a floor takes the player of its
  level rises from floor 121 on. Boss names still repeat in the order of the list; their health does not.
- a boss hits x1 up to floor 120 (its own attacks) and x the damage growth above it (`B.bossDamage`; `damageMultOf` no longer
  skips bosses, it stays 1 for them up to 120).
- Floors 1-120 changed only where they were flat or dipped: health at floor 100 19500 to 19600 (it equalled floor 90),
  bosses 110 and 120 187000 and 216000 to 278000 and 279000 (non-decreasing; `--derive` keeps a boss at least 0.5% over the
  one before; the floor 110 boss now takes the median class 128 s against 86 s and floor 120 116 s against 90 s, inside bossMax 150), monster damage rises from 0.72 at floor 52 to
  0.78 at 120 (`--derive`: last band + 0.06). Floors 1-51 still follow the pace curve down (0.99 to 0.67), which the level boost of
  `monster_damage.lua` (+30% at level 650) offsets, so strictly rising damage is checked from floor 52.
- "Stronger" with the sawtooth: the health trend (before the sawtooth), the level, the damage factor from floor 52 and the
  boss health of every boss floor rise on every floor; the health of a floor is above the floor five before it; inside a climb
  each floor is above the one before; only the breather after a milestone floor is easier than the floor before it.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 100 | 474 | 31,300 (floor 10) | 0.99 | 1 | - |
| 10 | 300 | 1,958 | 31,300 | 0.92 | 1 | - |
| 50 | 1,075 | 15,128 | 126,000 | 0.71 | 1 | - |
| 120 | 2,200 | 26,230 | 279,000 | 0.78 | 1 | 13.3 s |
| 200 | 3,200 | 46,214 | 491,573 | 0.93 | 1.19 | 16.2 s |
| 500 | 6,950 | 433,245 | 4,608,288 | 2.23 | 2.85 | 70.4 s |
| 1000 | 13,200 | 26,938,285 | 286,533,799 | 21.33 | 27.35 | 2,311 s |

(Monster health is the floor's value with the sawtooth of that floor, 0.75 to 1.22 of the trend; floors 1 to 120 as before.)

**Clamps (engine limits).** TFS creature health is int32. The tier multiplies after: `healthMax` 580,000,000 x 3.5 (legendary)
= 2.03e9 < 2^31 - 1, `bossHealthMax` 2,000,000,000 (a boss has no tier), and `engineMaxHealth` 2,147,000,000 is the last guard in
`preTierHealth` / `tierMaxHealth` and in `setHealth` of `infinitytower_run.lua`. The damage factor is capped at 1000
(`damageMax`; a hit is scaled with `floor(hit x factor + 0.5)`, so no inf or nan; `damageMultOf` also turns a nan or negative factor
into 1). The shown level is the engine's display level (patch 0040/0044: `int32`, sent as the text "Name [level]" in the creature
packet, not a uint16), capped at 2e9 (`levelMax`; a level climbs 12.5 a floor, never in reach). The floor argument is made finite and
at least 1 (`B.sane`: nan, text, infinity), and the growth exponent is capped at 60, so a floor of 1e300 still gives finite numbers.
The caps start at floor 1338 (normal health, at a milestone floor), 1217 (boss health) and 1577 (damage factor);
`tower_model.py --check` requires every cap past floor 1000 and prints the floors. From the cap on, values stay at the cap
(no longer strictly rising: past that point a floor is not stronger than the one before; the checks stop at the cap).

**Rewards do not follow the climb.** First-clear and repeatable counts and the tower drop counts use `min(floor, maxFloor)`: a
floor above 120 pays the counts of floor 120 (`rewardItems(rules, floor, capFloor)`, `dropRolls`), so the economy does not
inflate (a linear `perFloor` of 1 Crystal Coin would pay 1,000 on floor 1000, and a season pays each milestone floor once, up to
floor 999: the storage value is season x 1000 + floor). The rewards of floors 125, 130, ... are therefore paid at the amount of 120. The
store, roulette, skill and progression checks stay green. Not changed: `nextMilestone` stops at 120 (the window shows no next
reward past it).

**CI.** `tower_model.py --check` runs `endless()` over floors 1-1000 (`limits.endless`; every cap past `limits.capMin` 1000):
strictly rising health trend, level, damage (from floor 52) and boss health and boss damage per boss floor, the climb rule above,
no climb above maxFloor more than `stepMax` over the one before (no cliff), no value above its cap, the caps under int32 (the health
cap with the legendary tier), and the clear time at the floor's own level rising from floor 125 on at most `stepMax` per climb. The
unit test (`tower_model_test.py`) breaks each of them. Lua: `tests/infinitytower_balance_test.lua` (floors 1-1200 strictly, caps,
floors up to 1e12, nan, rewards) and `tests/infinitytower_floor_test.lua` (plans at floors 121 to 100000 fit int32 with every tier).
Not measured live; a level 2000 median class gets about 93 floors deep (unchanged), so floors above 120 are for the future.

## Infinity Tower season rewards (`infinitytower.lua`, `infinitytower_core.lua`, `Chaos.tower` in `chaos_constants.lua`)

The client window's "Top Rank Rewards" podium (Gold, Silver and Copper Tower Chest) is paid at the end of every tower
season. Before 12 Oct 2026 no script paid it.

- **Seasons.** `K.seasonOf`: fixed `seasonLengthDays` (30) windows from `seasonEpoch`, a unix time or `{year, month,
  day, hour}` in server local time; before the epoch it is season 1. The epoch is the launch (Fri 20 Nov 2026 15:00,
  docs/BETA.md section 5); it was 1 Jan 2025, which made the launch season 22. The tower does not follow the realm
  Seasons of `season_config.lua`: those last 13 weeks, have gaps between them and staff can start or end them by hand,
  while the tower's points, milestones and ranking reset every 30 days. Changing the epoch renumbers the seasons in
  `chaos_tower_players`: only on a wiped database.
- **Who gets a chest.** The ranking of the window: best floor, then best time. Characters of group 4+ (`seasonEnd.staffGroup`)
  and accounts held by the anti-bot (`antibot.lua` `filterRanked`, only with `log.holdLeaderboards`) are left out.
  Equal floor AND equal time share a place and the next place is skipped (1, 1, 3): two tied 1st both get gold and
  nobody gets silver; a tie for 3rd gives every tied character copper.
- **What is in it** (`seasonEnd.chests`): a stock pickupable container named by the item name attribute, with a
  description "Infinity Tower Season N, 1st place": Gold = treasure chest (1746) with 20 Orbs of Fate and 40 Orbs of
  Upheaval, Silver = chest (1740) with 12 and 25, Copper = box (1738) with 6 and 12. Orbs are the milestone and weekly
  board currency (`install_orbs.py`). Stacks that do not fit the chest go into the inbox loose.
- **Once per season.** `ChaosTower.checkSeasons` runs at startup and every `checkSeconds` (60). server_config
  `chaos_tower_season_done` holds the last season paid out; a new server stores the current season minus 1 and pays
  nothing earlier. Every ended season after it is paid oldest first (a long downtime pays them all at the next
  startup): one `chaos_tower_season_rewards` row per season and character (`INSERT IGNORE` on the primary key, so a lost
  marker never pays twice), then the marker. A broadcast names the winners (not at startup).
- **Delivery.** Rows with `rewarded = 0` go into the character's inbox: at once for the characters online at the season
  end, else at the next login (`ChaosTowerLogin`). The row is marked first, then the chest is made, so a failure never
  pays twice (the server log names it). The player gets a message, a notification toast (`ChaosNotify.send`) and
  fireworks.
- **Client.** The `update` / `open` payload carries `topRewards` (place, chest name, the chest's client id, the
  contents as tooltip); `game_infinitytower` shows those looks on the podium (the old fixed client ids 63194-63196 do
  not exist in the 10.98 items).
- **Staff.** `/towerseason` (group 4+): the season, its end and the last season paid out; `/towerseason pay` runs the
  check now (pays only ended seasons; idempotent).
- **Tests.** `tests/infinitytower_season_test.lua` (luajit and lua5.3): seasons and the epoch, ranking, ties, staff,
  awards, pending seasons, the configured chests, and `infinitytower.lua` against an in-memory database: paid at the
  end only, once (second check, restart, lost marker), online and offline delivery, several seasons after a downtime,
  a full chest, the payload, `/towerseason`.

## Event calendar, boosted creature/boss and the login screen (`events_schedule.lua`, `clientservices.lua`)
- **Events** (`Chaos.events` in `chaos_constants.lua`): recurring server days with real bonuses. Blood Moon (Saturday and Sunday, +50% experience), Chaos Rift (Wednesday, magic/rare/legendary spawns x2 and ambushes x1.5), Loot Frenzy (Friday, +50% Chaos loot and one extra loot roll on every monster) and Tower Ascension (days 1-3 and 15-17 of the month, double Infinity Tower points). Days are given as `weekdays` (1 = Sunday) or `monthdays`. Active events are announced on login and with Adventure > Events. The bonuses are read by `ChaosEvents.bonus(kind)` in the experience callback, `loot_config.lua` (`rateMult`), `loot.lua`, `monster_tiers.lua` and `infinitytower.lua`.
- **Boosted creature and boss:** the base server already picks them at startup (its lists and global storages). `clientservices.lua` reads that pick and falls back to `Chaos.boosted` when it is missing or names a monster that does not exist.
- **Login screen:** the client asks an HTTP endpoint for `boostedcreature`, `eventschedule` and `cacheinfo` (players online). The game server has no HTTP listener, so `clientservices.lua` writes the three answers to `data/chaos_clientservices.json` at startup and every 5 minutes, and `server/tools/clientservices.py` (standard library only) serves that file:
  ```
  python3 server/tools/clientservices.py <server>/data/chaos_clientservices.json --port 8090
  ```
  A Rust port with the same behaviour is opt-in (`chaos-ctl.sh clientservices-impl rust`, see "Rust services (O153)").
  The client's `init.lua` (base patch 0001) points `clientServicesLink` and `Services.status` at `http://127.0.0.1:8090/clientservices`; change the host for a public server. A GET on the same URL returns everything, handy to check it from a browser.
- **Runtime events:** `ChaosEvents.dynamic[key] = {id, name, description, bonus, untilTime}` adds an event with an end time to `ChaosEvents.active` (and so to the bonuses, Adventure > Events and the login lines) until `untilTime`: the invasion Victory buff and the world events use it (see "Invasions and world events"). Scheduled invasions are whole-day entries of `Chaos.events.list`.
- `server/tests/events_schedule_test.lua` checks the weekday/month-day rules, the bonus product, the calendar ranges sent to the client and the experience callback.

## Test kit (`admin/testkit.lua`)
`/testkit [kind][, player]` (admins only) equips a strong set for the class (uniques where they fit), a backpack of supplies (potions, runes, crystal coins, Orbs of Upheaval and Fate), raises the level to 500 and the main skills, and resets health and mana to the vocation's values. Relog afterwards so the stock rarity script applies the item bonuses.
Kinds (`ChaosTestKit.kindByVocation`, picked from the vocation when none is given): `mage` (Mystic, Elementalist, Illusionist with the rod; magic level 110), `knight` (Warrior, Juggernaut; melee 120, shielding 110), `berserker` (the knight set with Executioner's Reckoning, two-handed, no shield), `paladin` (Ranger, Deadeye; crossbow, distance 125, a Legendary Haloed Quiver rolled at the kit's item level), `beastmaster` (Doomtide Longbow and a Legendary Mercurial Quiver), `thief` (Thief, Samurai: Soulreaper and the paladin's armour, sword 120, distance 110, magic level 30, 100 assassin stars), `ninja` (the same plus Bloodmoon Edge in the shield hand; without `src-patches/0002` it goes to the backpack), `monk` (Monk line: no weapon, fist 120, club 110, the paladin's armour), `necromancer` (Necromancer line: the mage set with the wand) and `templar` (Templar line: the knight set, sword and club 120, shielding 110, magic level 25).

## Store (`shop.lua`, `shop_core.lua`, `shop_config.lua`, `shop_cosmetics.lua`, `shop_coins_config.lua`)
The client's Store (menu Economy > Store, module `game_shop`) talks JSON on extended opcode 218 (`ChaosOpcodes.shop`; the
base server's own store script uses 201 and is left alone). Prices are in Chaos Coins, kept per account in
`chaos_shop_coins`. Administrators (group 5+) give coins with `/coins <player>, <amount>` or the admin panel (Store > Give
Chaos Coins); a gamemaster is refused, and every use is in the admin audit log.
Rules without engine calls are in `shop_core.lua` (tested by `tests/shop_test.lua`); offers in `shop_config.lua`; the
services, unlocks and boosts in `shop_services.lua` (next section).
A look offer (outfit, addons, mount, wings, aura, shader) carries its `kind` in the offer the client gets, so the
Store's look preview (client/MANIFEST.md "Look preview") seats the player's own character on a mount and puts the
others on it; a pet's offer has none and is drawn alone.
**Icons and previews (2026-10-17, owner: "os icones da store estao repetidos ... use os proprios cosmeticos como
icones").** Every appearance offer also carries `look`, its own cosmetic (`shop_core.lua` `K.lookOf`; cosmetic unlocks
through `cosmetics_core.lua` `K.offerLook` / `ChaosCosmetics.offerLook`): `outfit`/`addons`/`mount`/`wings`/`aura`
(client ids from the XML files)/`shader`, `outline {art, pulse}`, `footprint {art}`, `effects {play}` (a spell skin or
kill effect, the same `play` steps as the Cosmetics window), `swatch {color}` (chat colour, loot label accent),
`nameplate {frame}`, `subject {look}` (a pet) and `bundle {parts}` (the parts that are an appearance; an items-only
bundle has none). Before this, only outfits, mounts, wings, auras and shaders sold as such had a picture of their
own: the cosmetic unlocks (outlines, footprints, spell skins, kill effects, the Chaos shaders), the plate frames and
the bundles were drawn as a stand-in item (one id per kind, so many offers shared one picture) and, being no creature, had
no preview at all. A look that is worn by a creature (an outline on the plain figure, a Chaos shader, a bundle's parts
merged: `K.iconOutfit`) is sent as `type = "outfit"` with that outfit; the client draws the rest (print, plate, effect,
sample) from `look`. A category whose icon is an item and whose first offer has a look shows that cosmetic (Name Plates,
Outlines ...). Items, services, premium time and convenience unlocks have no `look` and keep the item picture. Tests:
`tests/shop_looks_test.lua` (every appearance offer of `shop_config.lua` has a look, none repeats within its category,
bundle icons wear their parts), `tests/shop_test.lua` (mount, plate frame, bundle, item through `shop.lua`).

**Category tree (2026-10-21, owner: "De uma limpada na store do jogo. Separe em categorias e subcategorias. Use o
layout do server").** The layout of the base server's store window (the base client's store draws its categories as a
tree: a parent row that opens to its subcategory buttons, one parent open at a time, a click on the parent shows its
first subcategory; its categories carry a `parent` name). Our store, per player, in this order (empty categories and
parents are left out):

- **Starter** (only while one of its packs is for sale to the player), **This week** (the weekly rotation, below),
  **Bundles**
- **Premium & Services**: Premium Time, Chaos Pact, Storage & Slots, Season Pass, Services (name, vocation and sex
  change, skull remover, passive reset), XP Boosts (the Double Experience Potions), Blessings (All Blessings, Eternal
  Blessing), World Buffs; Depot Tabs only while the depot takes items (below)
- **Consumables**: Potions, Runes, Training (exercise weapons), Everfull Potions (the ten Everfull upgrades, one page,
  O286), Convenience (the three pouches, the Everfull Ration, Auto Seller, Rarity Autoloot, Backpack of Holding)
- **Cosmetics**: Outfits, Outfit Addons, Mounts, Wings, Auras, Outfit Shaders (the base shaders and the six Chaos
  shaders), Footprints, Outlines, Kill Effects, Spell Effects, Loot Labels, Chat Colours, Name Plates, Pets,
  Appearances (the transmog store sets), Portal Styles, Hideout Decorations
- **Crafting** (Whetstones, Excision, Binding with weekly limits)

The parents are `shop_config.lua` `groups` ({name, icon}); a category names its parent in `parent` and stands under it
in config order (`ChaosShopCore.arrange`: a parent's subcategories together, where its first one is). **Adding a
subcategory**: a category table with `parent = P_COSMETICS` (or `P_PREMIUM`, `P_CONSUMABLES`) at the place it should
stand in `shop_config.lua` (a category built in another file: `under(P_COSMETICS, dofile(...))`), or from another file
`ChaosShopCore.addSubcategory(cfg, "Cosmetics", category, "Auras")` (right after Auras; without the last argument after
the parent's last subcategory). `ChaosShopCore.validate` refuses an unknown parent, a parent without a subcategory, a
category named like a parent, a doubled category, and a sale or "New" naming a category that is gone; a sale or "New"
naming a parent (`categories = {"Cosmetics"}`) covers its subcategories (`ChaosShopCore.price` gets the parent).
Every offer has a stable key (`ChaosShopCore.offerKey`: `wings:4`, `outfit:909`, `item:32256x10`,
`service:pouch:loot`, or its own `key`), used by sales, featured lists, bundles, limits and the log; the clean-up kept
every key and every price.

**Protocol (backward compatible).** `init` (and every later list) sends `category_groups` (the parents: name, icon,
`size` offers, `children`) and then `categories`: still the flat list of the categories that sell, now in tree order,
each with `parent` and `size` (the offer count; not `count`, the icon's item count, nor `offers`, which an old client
fills with its pages). An old client ignores `category_groups` and `parent` and shows the flat list; the indexes of
`get_page`, `buy` and `preview` are unchanged. `search {text}` -> `search_results {text, offers}`: every offer whose
title, category or parent holds every word (case-insensitive, plain text; `ChaosShopCore.search`, the rotation is
skipped as its offers are in their own categories at the same price), at most 30, each with `at = {category, page,
offer}` (what `buy`, `gift` and `preview` send for it) and `path` ({parent, category}); rate limit 300 ms. A payload over
the engine's 8192 bytes goes out in parts (`Chaos.sendChunked`; the client's `registerExtendedJSONOpcode` joins them,
old clients too).

**Clean-up audit (2026-10-21).** Removed or fixed: Depot Tabs (an extra tab 150, four 500) are not sold while the depot
is withdraw-only (`stash_config.lua` `depot.withdrawOnly`, the stash took over: a bought tab could hold nothing); the
category comes back by itself under Premium & Services when the depot opens again (the end of `shop_config.lua`), and
the depot window hides its Buy Tabs button meanwhile (`depot.lua` sends `store = ""`). The "Chaos Shaders" category
(six offers) is merged into Outfit Shaders; Supplies is Potions (the Backpack of Holding moved to Convenience); Boosts is
split into XP Boosts and Blessings. Wings 3 and 15 show own names (Elderleaf Wings; Strength Wings, the base XML has a
typo and the other one a place name of another game). Checked and kept: no duplicate keys, no offer without a price,
every wing, aura and shader id in the base XML or the Chaos blocks, every outfit and mount generated, every service with
a handler, every unlock known to its system, every spell of the twelve spell skins still cast by a class after the
15-spell cap; Themed Sets stays a hidden rotation-only category. Tests: `tests/shop_tree_test.lua` (the tree functions,
the tree of `shop_config.lua`, every offer resolvable), `tests/shop_test.lua` (the messages, tree order, search, buying
from the results), client `game_shop/shoptree_test.lua`.

**Cosmetics: what exists and how it is got.** Counted on the installed base data with the Chaos blocks:

How the rest is got today: class looks at login and on a class change; achievements (`achievements_data.lua`), the
season track (`season_config.lua`) and the season pass with its packs (`seasonpass_config.lua` `cosmetics`) hand out their outfits, mounts, titles and portal styles; the ascension quest gives a
title (and the class outfits); base server quests, NPC addon traders, taming items and boss drops of the base world give
base outfits and mounts (those stay in the store too, as they were before: Shadowlotus, Blade Dancer, the store mounts).
Staff outfits are not in `outfits.xml`.

**Generated list.** `server/tools/gen_shop_cosmetics.py <server>/data` writes `shop_cosmetics.lua` from the base
`outfits.xml` and `mounts.xml` (pairs by name, `PAIRS` for the corrupted outfits whose two looks have other names), leaves
out the exclusives above (read from `class_looks_core.lua`, `chaos_constants.lua`, `achievements_data.lua`,
`season_config.lua`, `seasonpass_config.lua`, plus the tool's `EXCLUDED` list) and prices by tier: outfits 300 (look type < 400), 500 (< 900),
750 (newer, the old Shadowlotus / Blade Dancer price); addon sets 150; mounts 350 (client look < 500), 450 (< 900),
550 (< 1200), 690 (newer or speed 30, the old store mount price); `PRICE` overrides one offer (Spirit of Purity keeps
450). `--list` prints what was left out and why, `--check` fails when the file is stale. Add a new outfit or mount to
the XML (or `install_outfits.py`), run the tool, done. `shop.lua` checks the same exclusives again when it loads
(`ChaosShopCore.exclusions`; a class look added later is never sold, the console says "not sold: ...") and
`ChaosShopCore.validate` reports bad keys, prices, sales and bundles. Wings, auras and shaders are hand-picked offers
with names and prices in `shop_config.lua` (200-350; shaders 120-180).

**Delivery and duplicates.** An outfit gives both looks (male and female) with both addons, so a later sex change keeps
it; owned = the character's own look with both addons. Outfits and mounts the base XML marks premium need a Premium
account to wear: the store refuses them to a free account (gifts are allowed). Wings, auras, shaders and frames are
bought once (storages 7100600+, 7100650+, 7100700+, 7100761-7100765; the engine keeps the cosmetic itself). A purchase
that fails refunds the coins; a page reads "Owned." with the Buy button off for what the character has, and is sent again
after a purchase. All of it survives a reload and a restart (the engine and the storages hold the state).

**Delivery to the purse** (owner 2026-10-16: "Make the things bought in the store go to the purse."; `store_delivery.lua`,
rules `store_delivery_core.lua`, tests `tests/store_delivery_test.lua`). **The purse** is the engine's store inbox (item
26052 "your store inbox", inventory slot 11 of the 10.98 protocol): the client's "Open purse" button under the
equipment (base `game_inventory`, `GamePurseSlot` in client base patch 0006) opens it. Every character has one, it sits
in the equipment, it is never dropped at death, and the engine only lets the server put items in (a player cannot move
a normal item into it), so it is a one-way delivery box: the player takes things out into the backpack. The store
pouches are not the purse: they are optional store items a character may not own. (In the older texts of this file
"store inbox" means the depot inbox, `player:getInbox()`.)
- **What goes there.** Every store offer that becomes an item: `kind = "item"` offers (supplies, potions, runes in
  stacks of 100, Whetstones, crafting orbs, Backpack of Holding, exercise weapons, Double Experience Potions), the item
  parts of bundles and starter packs, the store pouches (`ChaosPouches.storeGive`, also the free Loot Bag of former
  Bottomless Loot Pouch owners), the Everfull Ration (`ChaosStoreFood.storeGive`), the temple scroll service, and gifts
  (online at once, offline at the next login). Items keep every attribute (`chaos_storebound`, `chaos_locked`, the
  owner of a pouch or ration): the "cannot be traded" rules apply in the purse and after it. **Unlocks stay unlocks:**
  outfits, addons, mounts, wings, auras, shaders, frames, pets, transmog sets, cosmetics, hideout decorations, tokens,
  services, world buffs, Pact days, premium time.
- **Fallbacks** (`ChaosStoreDeliveryCore.route`; never the ground, never lost): the purse; when there is no purse
  (an engine without `getStoreInbox`), the character cannot carry the item (the base engine counts the store inbox in
  the inventory weight, so the purse respects capacity as the backpack delivery did) or the engine refuses it: the depot
  inbox (weight free, at any depot); then the backpack (capacity checked); nowhere: nothing given, every item of the
  purchase (or bundle) placed so far taken back, coins refunded. Items are placed with `FLAG_NOLIMIT` and
  `FLAG_IGNOREAUTOSTACK`, so they never merge into a stack already there and a failed bundle takes back exactly its own
  items (`ChaosStoreDelivery.takeBack`; before, `player:removeItem` could not reach the purse).
- **Message** (one line per purchase, pt-BR in `i18n_strings.lua`): "Delivered to your purse (the button under your
  equipment).", or where it went and why ("Delivered to your depot inbox (you have no purse).", "Delivered: 1 to your
  purse, 1 to your depot inbox, 0 to your backpack (not enough capacity for the purse)."). A pouch in the purse collects at
  once, there or in the backpack (coordinator 2026-10-16, for new players; "Store pouches", Store-bound); one that went
  to the depot inbox says to move it to the backpack. The one-per-character checks of the pouches and the ration also
  look in the purse.
- **Other shops** (checked 2026-10-16): Osric's Candlemark shop and the Conquest vendor are NPC trades for in-game
  currencies: they stay as they were (backpack, then the depot inbox). The beta coins are Chaos Coins: what they buy is a
  store purchase and goes to the purse. The website shop (ZnoteX orders, `!shop`) is switched off (website/README.md:
  shop and points disabled), so no order can exist; the base talkaction was left alone.
- Not tested in game yet: the purse button with the delivered items, taking them out, eating the ration and using a
  scroll from the purse. Known limit: a container bought in the store (Backpack of Holding) can be filled while it lies
  in the purse; its weight still counts.

**Name plate frames.** The frame bought last is shown (titles.lua frame source "store"); Info & Services > Services >
Plate frame switches between the owned frames or back to the title's own (command id `plateframe`: a frame name typed in
the field, "My Frames" lists the owned ones; `commands_ui_core.lua` `K.PARAM` lets the name through, before that the
parameter was dropped and the frame buttons did nothing). Ember, verdant and bone (300 each) are drawn by
`client/tools/gen_nameplate_art.py` like the others (storages 7100763-7100765). Ashen, sapphire, rose, jade, copper,
obsidian, amber and storm (300 each) are slots 6-13 and the exclusives laurel, sepulchre and infernal 14-16 of
`shop_core.lua` `FRAMES` (the ownership slot is the index: 1-8 in 7100761-7100768, 9 and up in 7102010-7102039).

**Storefront** (`shop_config.lua` `storefront`, all server side; the client only shows what it gets and echoes title
and cost, so a changed price is refused, never charged): `featured` = `count` offers of `pool`, a new choice each week
(weeks start Monday `weekHour`), `pct` off; `sales` = offers / categories / kinds, `pct`, `from` / `to`
("YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM", server time), a tag (shipped: Wings -20%, 10 to 24 October 2026, "Launch sale"); `new` = a "New"
tag until a date. Discounts never stack (the biggest wins); bundles keep their price. The client shows the old price
struck through and the tags. **Bundles** (`kind = "bundle"`, `parts` = offer keys or inline offers, `pct` off the parts
or a fixed `cost`): Frostborn, Infernal and Gravewalker sets (wings, aura, shader, mount; 20% off); refused when a part
is owned or cannot apply; items are given first and taken back if a later part fails.

**Starter packs** (category Starter, `oncePerAccount`, `maxLevel`, not giftable; hidden once the account bought one and
for characters above the level): Novice 250 (worth 355; up to level 50: Gale Ring aura, 100 Great Spirit Potions,
100 Supreme Health Potions (5 Stamina Extensions until 2026-10-15), 3 Pact days), Adventurer 450 (worth 855; up to level 150: Loot Bag, Armoured War Horse, 100
Ultimate Health and 100 Great Mana Potions, 7 Pact days), Champion 750 (worth 1500; up to level 300: Auto Seller,
Discoverer outfit with addons, 100 Supreme Health Potions, 14 Pact days). No gear, no power, no orbs. Pact days go
through `ChaosPact.grantDays(player, days, "store")` (`shop_config.lua` `pact`); without the Pact that part is skipped.
The coin side of a starter offer is the one-time Starter Coins pack below.

**Fairness.** The orbs with a random result are not sold any more (Upheaval, Fate, Awakening, Gilding, Erasure, Unmaking,
Sockets, Grafting, Tempering, Reforging): Crafting keeps 10 Whetstones (5 per week), Orb of Excision and Orb of Binding (3
per week each), per account (`weeklyLimit`, counted in the purchase log). Season characters cannot buy Double Experience
Potions (`seasonBlocked`); World Experience does not apply to them and the base double experience potion's doubling is
undone for them in `shop_services.lua` (also when the potion came from gold). The Chaos Pact's +10% experience (owner
2026-10-13) skips them too, as the owner confirmed ("Chaos Pact and account storage", VIP perks).

**Gifts.** GIFT on an offer: a character name, a confirmation, then the server checks again (rate limit 3 s, 20 gifts per
account per day; not to yourself, staff (group 2+) or a banned account; services, unlocks and starter packs cannot be
gifted; the one exception is an unlock offer with `gift = true`, the hideout decorations). Online: delivered at once with a message. Offline: kept in `chaos_shop_gifts` and delivered 2 s after the next
login; when it cannot be delivered then (owned meanwhile, no room) the sender gets the coins back.

**Coin gifts** ("Transfer Coins", action `gift_coins`). Refused for `coinGifts.holdDays` (14) days after the sender's last
credited coin order, above `coinGifts.perDay` (5000) coins in 24 hours, to the own account and to a banned account
(`shop_config.lua`, `ChaosShopCore.coinGiftProblem`). Every gift is a row of `chaos_coin_gifts` (sender and receiver account,
amount, the sender's last credited order id, time, `clawed`). When a donation is refunded or charged back
(`shop_payments.lua processReversals`) and the donor's balance does not cover its coins, the rest is taken back from the
receivers of the donor's gifts made since that order, newest first, never more than a receiver has (`ChaosShopCore.clawbackPlan`);
the receiver is told, and what could not be recovered is logged for staff.

**Purchase log and dashboard.** Every purchase and gift is a row of `chaos_shop_purchases` (account, character, name,
level, offer key, category, title, price, list price, gift account and character, time); `chaos_shop_history` keeps
feeding the client's history. Admin panel tab "Store" (`admin/actions_store.lua`, group 5+): Sales dashboard (totals, per
day, per category, top 10 offers over N days), Recent purchases, Donations (coin orders), Donations: Pix / PayPal,
Donations: refunds and chargebacks, Record a donation (group 6), Give Chaos Coins.

**Chaos Coin packs** (`shop_coins_config.lua`, read by `shop.lua`, `shop_payments.lua` and the website's donation page):
100, 250, 500 +5%, 1000 +10%, 2500 +15%, 5000 +20%, a one-time Starter Coins pack (250 + 250), and double coins (at most
+1000) on the first pack an account gets (not the starter). Chaos Coins are a thank-you for a voluntary donation; the game is fully playable for free.
Prices: one USD table in integer cents (`usdCents`, decided 2026-10-14, docs/PRICES.md); Pix charges `usdCents * payments.brlPerUsd` (5) in BRL,
PayPal `usdCents` in USD (`ChaosPayCore.priceCents`; the website derives them the same way). Crediting: the payment side
marks a row of `chaos_coin_orders` `paid` (the donation flow below, the website hook `chaos_coin_order_paid` or the
admin action); `shop.lua` re-reads the row locked (`FOR UPDATE`: a refund that came meanwhile is not credited), credits
it in one transaction (coins + bonus + first-purchase bonus), rejects unknown packs and a second starter, and thanks
the account's online character ("Thank you for your voluntary donation! ...", then the "voluntary donation, not a
purchase" refund sentence and where the Donation Terms are).

**Donations: Pix and PayPal** (`shop_payments.lua`, rules in `shop_payments_core.lua`, numbers in `shop_coins_config.lua`
`payments`; website/README.md "Donations"). The client's Store has a Donate button: a window with the voluntary donation
notice (English and Portuguese), the refund sentence of the website's donation page with where the Donation Terms
are (`ChaosPayCore.terms`: "A donation gives no right to a refund..." before the donation, "This was a voluntary
donation, not a purchase..." once paid or credited, then "Donation Terms on the website:
page.php?plugin=chaos&p=legal&doc=donations"; the same strings as website legal_lib.php and the client's
payview.lua), the method (Pix (BRL) / PayPal (USD)) and the packs with their price and a Donate
button. JSON actions on opcode 218 (the store's own; `shop.lua` ignores them): `pay_packs`, `pay_create {pack, method}`,
`pay_status {id}`, `pay_cancel {id}`; the server answers `pay_packs` (with the notice and the refund sentence), `pay_order` (the order view: status, price text,
coins, Pix code as hex, PayPal link, seconds left), `pay_error`, and pushes `pay_paid` (the thank-you and the after-payment refund sentence, with the balance)
and `pay_reversal`. The client never sends a price: `pay_create` writes a `pending` order with the amount from the
config into `chaos_coin_orders` + `chaos_coin_payments`. Limits: one open order per account (asking again for the same
pack and method shows it again), `maxPerHour` (6) started per hour, the starter once, `ChaosRateLimit` on every action.
The game server has no HTTPS client: the website's payment worker makes the charge (Pix code / PayPal link) and the
provider's webhook marks the order `paid` after fetching the payment again. A poll every `payments.pollSeconds` (3)
starts the crediting step as soon as a `paid` row exists (so the client gets its confirmation in seconds, without a
relog), handles refunds and chargebacks after crediting (`chaos_coin_payments.reversal`, set by the website: the
refunded share of the credited coins is taken back, at most the balance, when `removeCoinsOnReversal` is on; logged and
listed in the admin panel; a second, larger refund flags the row again and only the difference is taken back,
`reversal_coins` counting every coin taken back so far, gift clawbacks included) and fails orders that got no charge in 10 minutes (worker not running).
Table `chaos_coin_payments` (`sql/chaos.sql`, also created at startup): one row per donation order (method, token,
amount in cents, currency, provider ids, Pix code / link, expiry, reversal). **Tests:** `tests/shop_payments_test.lua`
(prices derived from the USD table, money texts, the notice and thank-you texts, the refund sentences equal to
legal_lib.php's, limits, reuse, starter, views, reversal
amounts; the engine file on a mocked database: packs, create, reuse, refusal, cancel by the owner only, the thank-you
push, a refund and a chargeback after crediting), `shop_test.lua` (a refund between the crediting step's read and its
locked re-read credits nothing). **Tested in game** (own server and database copy, mock providers, Linux client):
Pix and PayPal donations from the client (QR code drawn and decoded back to the stored code, countdown, link opened),
automatic confirmation with toast and balance without relog, the first donation bonus, the starter once, a refund and
a chargeback after crediting (coins taken back) and the admin lists.

Tables: `chaos_shop_purchases`, `chaos_shop_gifts`, `chaos_coin_orders`, `chaos_coin_payments` (`sql/chaos.sql`, also
created at startup).
Storages: 7100760-7100769 (frames). **Tests:** `server/tests/shop_test.lua` (LuaJIT and Lua 5.3: keys, exclusives from
the real files, the generated list, no random orbs, prices and sales, featured rotation, packs, and `shop.lua` on a
mocked engine and database: every kind bought, duplicates, weekly limit, season, bundles, starter packs, gifts online and
offline with refund, coin orders, a reload), `shop_services_test.lua` (season experience), `website/tests/chaos_coins_test.php`.
**Tested in game** (own server and database copy, Linux client): Starter (Novice bought, pack hidden after, aura, items
and Pact days given; refund when the bag was missing), outfit (both looks with addons; second purchase refused, still
owned after a restart), mount, wings on sale, aura, shader, frame (shown on the plate), addon set, a bundle (refused
while a part was owned, then bought), weekly limit, gift to an offline character (delivered at login), gift to staff
refused, a paid coin order credited (750 + 75 + 150 first purchase), the admin Sales dashboard. Screenshots outside the
repository.

### Weekly rotation, bundles, coin packs (owner approval 2026-10-13)

The owner approved the monetization recommendations ("Pode fazer todas as mudanças recomendadas"): cosmetics and
convenience only, never power. Every price was decided on 2026-10-14 (owner delegated): the sheet and the reasons are
`docs/PRICES.md`.

- **This week** (`storefront.featured` in `shop_config.lua`: `name`, `count = 5`, `pct = 10`, `pool`). Five offers of the
  pool, 10% off, a new choice every Monday at 06:00 (`ChaosShopCore.featured`: a seeded shuffle of the pool by the week
  number, the same for everyone all week). The category carries `endsIn` (seconds to the next Monday, `ChaosShopCore.weekEnds`)
  and the client counts it down on the category label ("This week (3d 04h)", `game_shop/rotation.lua`). The pool: wings,
  auras, mounts, outfits, a stock shader, a plate frame, the six Chaos outfit shaders and the 12 themed appearance sets.
  A category with `rotationOnly = true` ("Themed Sets") is never shown on its own: its offers are sold only the weeks they
  rotate in (`Shop.view` skips it; a purchase is always taken from the view).
- **Themed sets of pair 24** (`data/lib/chaos_theme_art.lua` `M.sets`, 18 transmog sets). Split: 12 sold in the rotation
  (Cryptbone, Wildroot, Moonsilver 350 each; the Rimeglass, Emeraldine and Thornwild kits 250 each), 6 prestige
  achievement rewards, never sold: Voidmourn (`cinder_1`, the Cinderheart), Sunsworn (`level_1000`), Oathsteel
  (`ascended_all`), Starwing Warplate (`raid_first`), Starwing Vestments (`trial_merciless`), Starwing Hunter's Garb
  (`rift_t15`). The three boss exclusives of pair 24 (Blood Vortex, Rune Seal auras, Runic Wings) stay boss drops and
  never enter the pool (`theme_art_test.lua` checks it).
- **Chaos outfit shaders** (`cosmetics_config.lua` `outfitShaders`): switched on, 250 coins (Ember Glow, Frost Rime, Void
  Flicker, Heartblood) and 300 (Holy Radiance, Spectral Ghost), sold in Cosmetics > Outfit Shaders (`cosmetics_store.lua`
  "outfitshader"); account-wide, not giftable. The stock shaders cost 120-180.
- **Bundles.** The discount bundles (`pct`) are priced per player (`Shop.personalBundle`): the parts the player owns
  already are left out of the bundle and of its price, the description says how many; a bundle whose parts are all
  owned is not shown. Fixed-price bundles (the starter packs) keep their old rule (refused when a part is owned). New:
  three regalia at 25% off, an outfit with both addons + a mount + wings + an aura (Glacial: Astral Ice, Glacier Wyrm,

- **Coin packs** (`shop_coins_config.lua`, decided 2026-10-14, docs/PRICES.md): Handful of Coins 100 coins for US$ 1.98
  (R$ 9,90 by Pix at `brlPerUsd` 5, the entry pack), Pouch 250 / 4.98 (R$ 24,90), Sack 500 +5% / 9.98 (R$ 49,90), Chest
  1000 +10% / 19.98 (R$ 99,90), Hoard 2500 +15% / 49.98 (R$ 249,90), Vault of Coins 5000 +20% / 99.98 (R$ 499,90),
  Starter Coins 250 + 250 / 2.98 (R$ 14,90) once. One coin is about R$ 0,10; coins per R$ with the pack bonus: 10.1,
  10.0, 10.5, 11.0, 11.5, 12.0, so every bigger pack is a better thank-you.
- **First donation: double coins** (`firstPurchase.bonusPct = 100`, was 20), **at most +1000** (`firstPurchase.maxBonus =
  1000`, owner 2026-10-13: "Limite a 1000"): a pack up to 1000 coins is doubled, a bigger one gets +1000 flat (the Vault:

## Store services (`shop_services.lua`, `autosell.lua`, `sell_prices.lua`)

Five store categories sell services, unlocks and boosts besides the cosmetics. `shop_config.lua` has two new offer kinds,
both dispatched by `ChaosShopServices` (`shop_services.lua`):
- `{kind = "service", service = "<handler>", icon = <item id>}`: done for the character at once (`S.services` table).
- `{kind = "unlock", unlock = "autoSeller" | "rarityAutoloot"}`: a permanent per-character flag (storage).
- `{kind = "service", service = "pouch", pouch = "loot" | "orbs" | "keys"}`: a store pouch item ("Store pouches" below).

`shop.lua` asks `ChaosShopServices.check(player, offer)` **before** it takes coins: an unlock already owned, full stamina, a
world buff at its cap, an unused token, no skull to remove, an empty passive tree... is refused with a message and costs
nothing. Then the coins are taken and `ChaosShopServices.deliver` runs; a delivery error (no room for a scroll, a script
error, caught with `pcall`) refunds the coins, as for the other offers. Icons and descriptions come from the server; the
client module needed no change.

| Category | Offer | Coins | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Boosts | ~~Stamina Refill~~ | - | removed 2026-10-15 ("Time-friendly progression": paying to farm at full loot); the `stamina` service handler stays, unused |
| | ~~Stamina Extension~~ | - | removed 2026-10-15 (the base server's item 27990, +2 h; owned ones still work) |
| | Double Experience Potion / 5 potions | 50 / 225 | the base server's item 28095: x2 experience for 1 h per potion (storage 6000, Character > Character Info); `weeklyLimit` 4 / 2 per account (14 hours a week, O140) |
| | All Blessings | 60 | blessings 1-5 (refused when all are owned) |
| World Buffs | World Experience | 300 | +25% monster experience for everybody, 1 h, up to 3 h |
| | World Loot | 300 | +25% Chaos loot (`rateMult`) and one extra loot roll on every monster, like the Loot Frenzy event, 1 h, up to 3 h |
| | World Training | 250 | +25% skill and magic level tries for everybody, 1 h, up to 3 h |
| Services | Name Change | 250 | a token for Character > Services |
| | Vocation Change | 400 | a token for Character > Services |
| | Sex Change | 100 | at once; every owned outfit and addon is copied to the other sex (pairs by name in `data/XML/outfits.xml`) |

| | Passive Tree Reset | 100 | empties every preset for free (the in-window reset costs level x 250 gold; 60 before O140, see "Store balance (O140)") |
| Convenience | (the Temple Teleport Scroll is no longer sold) | | see below |
| | Loot Bag / Orbs Pouch / Rift Key Pouch | 250 / 200 / 150 | store pouch items, one of each per character ("Store pouches" below) |
| | Auto Seller | 400 | unlock (also lent by an active Chaos Pact), see below |

| Training | 18 exercise weapon chests | 25 / 75 / 450 | the base server's chests: melee (the one sword / club weapon since 2026-10-23; Warrior, Thief, Templar), fist (Monk line only since 2026-10-28), bow, rod, wand, shield with 500 / 1800 / 14400 charges ("Training weapons") |

Premium (250 for 30 days) stays where it was.

**Store balance (O140, 2026-10-23).** `cd server && luajit tools/store_model.lua` prints the price tables (coin packs, coins per hour of
benefit of every time saver, gold per coin of the supply packs, services against their gold way, bundles); `--check` (also
`lua5.3`) enforces the rules of `data/scripts/chaos/store_balance_config.lua` and CI runs it; `tests/store_model_test.lua` breaks each
rule on purpose and expects the problem. Rules: coin packs have `usdCents` ending in .98 and round Pix prices, the packs without a
bonus are within 1.5% of 10 coins per real, bonuses rise 0-20%, the Starter pack is at most 3.5x and the first donation at most 2.25x
the base rate; a supply pack is worth 700-2,000 gold per coin (a coin is 1,000 gold, store at most 2x cheaper than gold) and no store
item sells to an NPC for more than 500 gold per coin; the Double Experience Potion has weekly limits that add up to at most 14 hours,
the world buffs stay at 25% (Hunt 50%) and 3 hours, the experience cap at 4; the Passive Tree Reset is within 2x of its gold way up to
level 800; the Eternal Blessing is 8-15 All Blessings; a static plate frame costs no more than the cheapest wings; the Pact days of a
starter pack are listed at the Pact's price per day. Prices, before and after, and the reasons: docs/PRICES.md "Store balance (O140)".
Changed: Double Experience Potion weekly limit (new), Passive Tree Reset 60 -> 100, plate frames 300 -> 200. Server: `files` step and a
restart; the website wiki data is regenerated (`tools/gen_wiki_data.lua`).

Exercise weapons (O150): valued with `tools/skill_model.lua` (`skill_model_config.lua`; `tests/skill_model_test.lua`; computed, not measured): a dummy hour is worth 10-27 hunting hours, 5.6-24 coins per hunting hour, so the prices stay; `store_model.lua --check` bounds them (half of Premium's coins per hour to the Double Experience Potion's, tier discount at most 40%). Assumes the base server's `skills_stages.lua` with the O154 factor (below) and 70% of a hunting hour swinging. Skill 100 to 130 by hunting alone is 180-300 hours with it (900-1,500 with the stock stages; docs/PRICES.md "Skill training (O150)").

**Skill stages x5 (O154).** Owner 2026-10-24 ("pode acelerar 5x o treino de skill"): `tools/patch_skill_stages.py` (install step `skillstages`, right after `meleeskill`; `python3 -I tools/patch_skill_stages.py DATA_DIR [--dry-run]`) multiplies every stage multiplier of the base server's `data/scripts/customs/skills/skills_stages.lua` (every skill and the magic level) from trained level 101 up by `factor` (5, in `data/scripts/chaos/skill_stages_config.lua` with `fromLevel` 101; the stages up to 100 stay). Hunting, exercise weapons and offline training all pass that script, so all three get it and the price of an exercise weapon per hunting hour does not change. Assumptions: the file is the stock shape (`local skillStages = {`, `[SKILL_X] = {` blocks of `[{ a, b}] = {multiplier = n}` rows, the last row `[{150}]`, and the `onGainSkillTries` callback); any other shape is refused (exit 1, the file untouched, the reason printed). A stage spanning 100 and 101 would be split. Each changed row ends with `-- Chaos: was N` and a header line on top carries the marker, so a second run changes nothing and a new factor derives from the originals (set it to 1 to restore the stock numbers). CRLF is kept. Test `tools/patch_skill_stages_test.py` (synthetic copies, and the real base copy when `/tmp/wk` has one); `tools/skill_model.lua` reads the same config (`tests/skill_model_test.lua`). Deploy: `install_all.py SERVER_DIR --only skillstages` (the admin app's Update button runs every step) and a restart; no client change. Not run on the live server; the figures are computed, like O150.

**Temple Teleport Scroll (retired from the store).** Every character has the free Town Portal now ("Town Portal" below), so the store no longer offers the scroll or the 25-use scroll. Scrolls bought earlier keep working: the handler, `S.teleportBlocked` and the action id stay in `shop_services.lua`, and `shop_config.lua` keeps the `templeScroll` service kind. The old description: an ordinary "scroll" (item 6119, used by no other script) with action id 47301, the name
"temple teleport scroll", a description and the uses left in the custom attribute `chaos_uses`; no new item id. Using it
takes you to your town's temple. Refused with a battle sign or PZ lock, inside a dungeon run (`ChaosDungeonIsInside`), the
Infinity Tower (`ChaosTowerRun.isInside`) and the world boss lobby/arena (`ChaosWorldBoss.inside`). 2 s cooldown. The stash
refuses it (action id), so it stays an item.

**World buffs.** A purchase broadcasts "<buyer> activated the World Experience ..." to everybody (and fireworks); buying
while it runs extends it ("<buyer> extended ..."). A purchase that would leave more than 180 minutes is refused before
coins are taken. The expiry times are global storages 7100921 (xp), 7100922 (loot), 7100923 (skill), 7100924 (hunt) and
rows `chaos_worldbuff_xp|loot|skill|hunt` of the stock `server_config` table: they survive `/reload` and a **restart** (checked on
the test server). Adventure > Events lists the active ones with the time left; players get the list at login; the end is
broadcast (30 s check). Experience: `EventCallback.onGainExperience` (needs `patch_base_events.py`), monsters only.
**World Hunt** (beta 2026-10-22, owner: "a world boost in the store that raises the chance of rare and magic monsters"):
300 coins, 1 hour, up to 3; `monster_tiers.lua` multiplies the magic and rare spawn chances by 1.5 (not legendary, and
on top of the capped event multiplier, so a Chaos Storm under it can reach 6% x 3 x 1.5 = 27% magic). Monsters are
shared, so it also reaches season characters' hunts. Buff bar icon `buffs/world_hunt.png` (`gen_buff_icons.py`).
Training: `EventCallback.onGainSkillTries`, which the base `player.lua` already dispatches (no patch needed); one try
x1.25 becomes 1 or 2 tries at random, so small gains are not rounded away. Loot: `loot_config.lua` `rateMult` and the
extra-roll rule in `loot.lua`.

**Name change.** Character > Services (needs the token, out of combat, in a protection zone). Rules
(`ChaosShopServices.validateName`, settings `Chaos.shopServices.name`): 3-20 characters, letters and single spaces, at most
3 words of at least 2 letters, each word is capitalised for you ("kael vorn" -> "Kael Vorn"), no letter three times in a
row, no staff word as a word (GM, CM, God, Admin, Tutor, Gamemaster, ...), no forbidden substring, not a website address
as the whole name (`reserved`: Highscores, Page, Myaccount ...; the site serves `/highscores` as a page, website/README.md
"Web server"; the website's character creation refuses the same list), not a monster name, not taken (`players.name`). Then: the token is used, the character is saved and kicked, and 0.5 s later (retried each second
while it is still online) `players.name` is updated together with the tables that keep names as text: the member list of
`chaos_dungeon_runs` (runs the character took part in), `player_deaths.killed_by` / `mostdamage_by` (player killers) and
`guildwar_kills.killer` / `target`. If the name was taken in between, the token is given back. `chaos_admin_log.player_name`
is an audit log and keeps the old name. All other Chaos tables use the player id.

**Vocation change.** Character > Services (pick the class: warrior, juggernaut, berserker, ranger, deadeye, beastmaster, mystic, elementalist, illusionist, thief, ninja or samurai)
(token, out of combat, in a protection zone; your own vocation is refused). Every base class has two ascended classes
(`Chaos.shopServices.vocations`: warrior 4 -> juggernaut 8 | berserker 14, ranger 3 -> deadeye 7 | beastmaster 15, mystic 1 ->
elementalist 5 | illusionist 10, thief 11 -> ninja 12 | samurai 13): an ascended character names the ascended class it wants (the base
word asks it to choose), an unascended one becomes the base class with any word of the line, and a Juggernaut can become a Berserker
this way (the only way after the Ascendant Oracle). The change also resends the vocation to the client, keeps the Ninja's dual-wield storage in
line, dismisses a companion when the character is no Beastmaster any more (`ChaosClasses.afterVocationChange`) and spends a pending free
switch of the class migration. Health and mana are recomputed as the engine counts
them, 185 / 90 at level 8 plus (level - 8) x the new vocation's gain; capacity keeps whatever the character has outside the
level gains: cap + (level - 8) x (new gain - old gain). Skills and magic level are **kept** as they are (a knight turned
sorcerer keeps its sword skill and its low magic level). The passive tree is reset for free (`ChaosPassiveTree.resetAll`).
Items restricted to the old vocation stay equipped.

**Bottomless Loot Pouch (retired).** The old unlock (autoloot that did not fit went to the stash or inbox, `onDropLoot`
index 4) is gone, with its callback and its stash/inbox fallbacks in the loot filter. Storage 7100100 stays reserved: at their
next login its former owners get a Loot Bag item for free, once ("Store pouches").

**Auto Seller.** `onDropLoot` index 2 (after the Chaos loot layer at 1, before the autoloot at 3): items on your auto-sell
list are taken out of corpses you own and sold at the NPC price; the gold goes into your bank balance and one loot
message per corpse lists what was sold. The list is separate from the autoloot list (no autoloot slot needed), up to 40
items. Items with a rarity are sold only for the rarities the player ticks (below); uniques (`chaos_unique`) and items
with a custom name / description / text and no rarity are never sold, nor items the player worked on (a custom
attribute of `ChaosAutoSell.OWN_CUSTOM`: the base upgrade level, the Chaos quality, transmog, set, a gem in a socket).
The item level every gear drop gets does not count (until 2026-10-14 any custom attribute did, so plain gear drops were
kept as "named" and never sold; found in a live test). Containers are not sold. What the store pouches
collect (orbs, whetstones, rune shards, gems, Rift Keys, omen items: `ChaosPouches.neverSell`) is never sold, even when it
is on the list.

**The Auto Seller window** (owner 2026-10-13: "Tire os comandos do autosell e coloque no topmenu"; client `game_pouches`
`autoseller.lua` part of `pouches.lua`, `autoseller.otui`, logic `autosellerview.lua` with `autosellerview_test.lua`).
Top menu Economy > Auto Seller (icon `topbutton_autoseller`, `client/tools/gen_theme_art.py icons=autoseller`), or the
Loot Bag window's Auto Seller button. There is **no chat or Info & Services command** any more: the `autosell` command
and its Info & Services page are gone. The window: **Sell all** (the Loot Bag, below) with the 30 s cooldown counted
down on the button; the last sale's total; one checkbox per rarity in its colour; "Also sell the items of my list as
they drop" (the corpse selling on / off); the list with Add / Remove by name (only items an NPC buys) and Clear. Without
the Auto Seller (not bought, no active Pact) every control is greyed out with the reason as tooltip. Protocol: the pouches
