opcode 226 (`pouches.lua` routes `PO.AUTOSELL_ACTIONS` to `ChaosAutoSell.handleAction`, rate limit 250 ms): `as_open` /
`as_sync`, `sell`, `asrar {tier, on}` (or `{tiers = {key = bool}}`), `aslist {op = add|remove|clear, item}`,
`aspause {on}`; every answer is the window state `autoseller` (`A.state`: unlocked, the reason, paused, tiers, list,
cooldown, last sale, a notice). The server checks everything: the unlock (refused with the reason, nothing stored), an
unknown rarity or a non-boolean value, an unknown list change, an unknown item, one no NPC buys, orbs, a full list.

**Rarities** (owner 2026-10-13: "Deixe o jogador configurar o autosell por raridade"; `autosell_core.lua` `TIERS`). Six
choices per character (since the seven rarities of 2026-10-18), for the list and for the Loot Bag: Common, Uncommon, Magic,
Rare, Legendary and Divine (bits 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32; the bits keep their old place, so the old Rare is now Magic, the old
Epic is Rare, and the old "Legendary+" choice is Legendary; a version bit 128 marks a choice saved with Divine: without it
Divine follows Legendary). Default: Common and Uncommon on, the rest off. Uniques are never sold, whatever is
ticked. Stored in storage 7100103 (`Chaos.storage.autosellRarity`, the old opt-in key): 64 + one bit per tier
(`packTiers`); unset or the old "off" 0 = the defaults, the old "on" 1 = every tier on. `ChaosShopServices.sellBlocked`
takes the tiers (or `true` for every rarity).

**Auto Seller: selling the Loot Bag** (owner 2026-10-13: "vende tudo dentro da loot bag e pode ser usado a cada 30s";
`autosell_core.lua` rules, `autosell.lua` `ChaosAutoSell.sellBag`, `tests/autosell_test.lua`). With the Auto Seller
(bought, storage 1, or lent by an active Chaos Pact, 2): the Auto Seller window's "Sell all" (`game_pouches`, opcode 226
action `sell`) sells everything in the carried Loot Bag, bags inside it included, at the
NPC price of `sell_prices.lua` (the auto-sell list is not needed). Once per 30 s per character (`ChaosAutoSellCore.COOLDOWN`;
"ready again in N s"). Gold goes to the bank balance, as every Auto Seller sale; gold, platinum and crystal coins in the
bag go to the bank at their value. Kept in the bag: containers (their contents are sold), locked items (`chaos_locked`),
uniques, what the store pouches collect (orbs, whetstones, rune shards, gems, Rift Keys, omen items), items no NPC buys,
items of a rarity the player does not tick and items with a custom name / description / text and no rarity. Equipped
items are never in the bag, so they are never sold. One chat line (and the window's notice): "Auto Seller: sold 23 items
from your Loot Bag for 625 gold (to your bank). Kept 6: locked 1, unique 1, rarity 1, named 1, no NPC buys 1, orbs / gems
/ keys 1." The window keeps the last sale (gold, items) while the server runs.
Prices: each copy's own price, `ChaosItemPrices.sellPrice(item, count)` (`data/lib/chaos_item_prices.lua`, "Item
prices": a rolled copy of a higher rarity or item level sells for more), for the list and for the Loot Bag; without that
library the plain table `sell_prices.lua`, written by `python3 -I server/tools/gen_item_prices.py` (`gen_sell_prices.py`
is only a shim for it now). The list is managed in the Auto Seller window (above).
Store-bound items (custom attribute `chaos_storebound`: the Everfull Ration, Nemesis items; engine store items) are never
sold, from the bag or a corpse (counted as "orbs / gems / keys"). The contents of a locked or store-bound container and
of a store pouch inside the bag are not walked: the item lock and the binding cover what is inside. Gold is paid only for
what was really removed (each removal is guarded, so one failing item never leaves the rest unpaid).

**Auto Seller: one update per sale** (owner beta 2026-10-21: "o client ainda dá umas travadas quando o auto seller vende
muitas coisas ao mesmo tempo"). The earlier fix (2026-10-20) sorted the Loot Bag once per kill instead of once per item,
but each sold item was still removed on its own: per item one container packet for the open Loot Bag and, as the bag is
carried, one full stats packet (`Player::postRemoveNotification` -> `sendStats`). The client redraws every slot of the
window on `onSizeChange` and again on `onRemoveItem`, and the loot filter and depot tabs walked the window per call too:
a sale of 255 items was 510 packets and about 1500 full window passes in one frame. Now `A.sellBag` removes the items
inside `Chaos.containerBatch(player, fn)` (`chaos_constants.lua`): with engine patch 0054 the engine holds the packets
and sends one container packet per changed window and one stats packet at the end; without the patch fn just runs. The
same batch wraps the stow and sort of one kill (`pouches.lua` `collect`), click-to-loot (`PO.stow`) and the sort when the
bag opens. A sale stays one chat line and one window state. Measured on the mocked engine (`tests/autosell_test.lua`): a
sale of 255 items, unpatched 255 container + 255 stats packets, patched 1 + 1; gold identical. The client side is cheap
on its own too (client base patch 0109, `game_lootfilter`, `game_depottabs`: one redraw per container per frame).

**Loot burst: one update** (owner 2026-10-23: "o client dá uma travada rápida quando a janela do loot bag está aberta e o auto
loot pega muita coisa de uma vez"). The stow of one kill was already one held batch (`Chaos.containerBatch`, engine patch 0054),
but every kill ended its batch with its own full container packet for the open Loot Bag, and the client answers a full packet
for an open window by refreshing up to 255 slots (before client base patch 0122, by rebuilding all of them). An area spell
that kills ten monsters in one tick was ten such packets. `pouches.lua` `collect` now runs inside
`Chaos.containerBurst(player, fn)` (`chaos_constants.lua`): the first kill of a burst begins an outer batch for the player and
a 150 ms timer (`Chaos.burstWindowMs`) ends it, so every kill in that window shares one packet per open window and one stats
packet. Cost: the Loot Bag window shows the loot up to 150 ms later. The timer looks the player up again (a player gone by
then is skipped); without engine patch 0054 `fn` just runs. Checked in `tests/pouches_test.lua`: four kills in one tick, one
hold and one release timer, balanced afterwards; a later kill holds again. Client side: `client/BASE.md` 69n.

**Sell every X minutes** (owner 2026-10-17: "Auto seller: opção de vender a cada X minutos"; `autosell.lua`, `autosell_core.lua`
`INTERVALS`, window dropdown "Sell the Loot Bag automatically every" in `autoseller.otui`). Off by default; choices 5, 10,
15, 30, 60 minutes, stored in storage 7100152 (`Chaos.storage.autosellInterval`), action `asevery {minutes = 0|5|10|15|30|60}`
(anything else: "Bad request.", nothing stored; needs the Auto Seller unlock like every control). The timed sale is the
button's sale (`A.sellBag`: same rules, same prices, same 30 s limit shared with the button, one chat line only when gold
was made). Cost: one global timer (`ChaosAutoSellTick`, every 30 s) walks only `A.auto`, the table of the characters that have
it on (filled by `asevery` and by the login event `ChaosAutoSellLogin`; the first sale comes one interval after login),
at most 10 sales per tick; a character that left or lost the unlock is dropped from it. No scan of the online players
and no work in the kill hook. `state` also sends `interval`, `intervals` and `nextIn` (seconds to the next sale).

**Storage keys** (all in `chaos_constants.lua`): 7100100 reserved (the retired Bottomless Loot Pouch), 7100101 Auto Seller,
7100102 auto seller's corpse selling off, 7100152 "sell every X minutes" (5/10/15/30/60; unset = off), 7100103 the rarities it sells (packed, see Rarities), 7100104 name change tokens, 7100105 vocation change tokens, 7100106 Rarity
Autoloot, 7100107-7100109 store pouches, 7100111-7100150 auto-sell list, 7100151 Everfull Ration owed back after a death
(`store_food_config.lua`; not in `chaos_constants.lua` yet, as the pouches' keys live in `pouches_config.lua`); global
7100921-7100924 world buffs. Settings: `Chaos.shopServices`.

**Tests.** `server/tests/shop_services_test.lua` (LuaJIT and Lua 5.3): name rules, buff stacking and the cap, buff
effects and the reload from `server_config`, vocation mapping and stat recomputation, sell prices and the keep rules,
unlock/service checks (the pouch service), the auto seller (and that it never sells pouch items) against mocked items and corpses.

**Verified in game** (test server, client screenshots): every new category and offer renders with icon and description;
buying stamina, blessings, potions, a training chest, both scrolls, both unlocks, the three world buffs, both tokens, sex
change, skull remover and passive reset; refusals without coin loss (full stamina, unlock owned, buff at the cap, token
unused, nothing to remove/reset); refund when the backpack had no room; the scroll teleports, counts down and is refused
with a battle sign and in the world boss arena; world experience x1.25 on a real kill, skill tries x1.25 through the
engine, loot multiplier 1.25; buffs still active after a server restart, listed at login and by Adventure > Events; the auto
seller sold plain items to the bank and kept rarity/unique items (rarity sold after the opt-in, nothing sold while off);
Character > Services renamed the
character (and its dungeon run entry) and back; a vocation change paladin -> knight -> paladin returned exactly the
original health, mana and capacity.

## Cosmetics (`cosmetics.lua`, `cosmetics_core.lua`, `cosmetics_config.lua`, `cosmetics_store.lua`, `sql/chaos_cosmetics.sql`, client `game_cosmetics`)

Four cosmetic kinds, cosmetic only (they change a picture or a colour, never damage, area, timing or drops). Unlocks are
account-wide (table `chaos_cosmetics`, also created at startup); each character chooses what it shows in Character >
Cosmetics (storages 7100940 - 7100949). Every cosmetic is data in `cosmetics_config.lua` (`id`, `key`, `kind`, `icon`, `name`,
`desc`, `source` store with `price`, or achievement with `achievement`; also pvp, boss, pact, and candlemarks: three bought
for Candlemarks at Osric the Chandler, never for coins, see "Candlemarks"). The store categories are built from it by
`cosmetics_store.lua` (the Cosmetics hunk of `shop_config.lua`): `{kind = "unlock", unlock = "cosmetic_<key>"}`, not giftable,
sold through `ChaosCosmetics.storeUnlock` (`shop_services.lua` `unlockEntry`); season characters may buy them
(`season_config.lua` `store.unlockPrefixes`). Achievement cosmetics are granted at login and when the window opens.

| Kind | What | Store (coins) | Achievement |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spell effect skins | a class line's listed spells (2-3) show recoloured variants of their effects; everyone sees them | 12 skins, 250 each: Warrior Voidborn / Stormborn War Cries (Iron Bellow, Red Frenzy, Bloodrage), Ranger Sunfire Hunt (Skewering Line, Feral Command, Wild Bond), Mystic Voidfire (Doomtide, Forked Storm, Falling Pyre) / Bloodfire, Thief Dawnstep (Shadow Veil, Shadow Step, Shadow Mend) / Venom Smoke, Monk Crimson / Void / Gilded Palms (Ashen Fist, Sundering Palm, Pressure Points, Shadowfist Flurry), Templar Umbral Rite (Zealotry, Purging Nova, Vow of Mending) / Pyre Rite | none |
| Kill effects | an effect on the monster's tile when the character lands the killing blow (the engine's last hit, not most damage, not a summon's) | Soul Spark, Sun Ring, Frost Shatter, Blood Bloom, Radiant Ring, 200 each | Void Ring (Legend's Bane), Harbinger's Toll (Chaos Culler), Sovereign's Pyre (The Last Door, the raid) |
| Loot label accents | the background of the character's own highlighted ground loot labels (`game_groundlabels`); text and border keep the rarity colour, the corpse loot rays keep theirs | Ember, Verdant, Azure, Royal Labels, 150 each | Gilded Labels (Greed Is Good) |
| Chat name colours | the character's name in chat, for every viewer (player lines only, the name only; item link colours stay) | Cinder, Frost, Verdant, Amethyst, Rose Name, 200 each | Veteran's Gold (Veteran of the Wastes) |

**Spell skins.** Only effects of the client pair: every swap stays inside a recolour family of `families` (the same
procedural style in another palette, or the colour sets of the pack effects: `aura_burst_*`, `dome_blast_*`, `punch_hit_*`,
`shade_*` / `blink_*`, `px*_*`); the test checks each family against `effects_catalog.csv` (same style) and `vfx_catalog.csv`
(same size and frames). During a supported cast `_supports.lua` knows the caster and the spell (`ChaosSupportsSpell.cast()`,
also inside the cast's `addEvent` callbacks); `_common.lua` asks `ChaosCosmetics.swapFor(pid, spellId, type, name)` in
`ChaosSpell.fx` / `vfx` / `vshoot` and in the global `Fx` / `FxMissile` (wrapped once), so heal and area effects of the cast
change too. A variant the server does not know sends the default effect. Effects set at load time (a combat's
`COMBAT_PARAM_EFFECT`) stay the default. A spell belongs to one line; the skin chosen for that line is per character
(storage 7100943 + line slot). The Necromancer line has no skins yet (its effects were being redrawn).

**Choosing and previews.** Character > Cosmetics: one tab per kind, a Default row, Use, Preview, Open the Store. Preview (and
the store's SHOW button on a skin or kill effect) plays the effects at the player's tile for that player only
(`Position:sendMagicEffect(id, player)`), one every 0.7 s, at most one preview per 1.5 s. The store tints a chat colour
offer's title with the colour and puts a label accent behind the title; the window shows the player's own chat line in the
colour and three rarity labels on the accent.

**Reward track** (cosmetics earned by playing, "Achievements" below). An achievement cosmetic is earned one of three
ways: `achievement = <id>` (above), `points = N` (the account has N achievement points: each achievement once, whichever
character earned it) or `category = <key>` (the account has every achievement of that category, hidden ones too). 17 of
them, all palette variants of effects and colours that already exist (no new art):

| Account points | Cosmetic | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| 100 | Ashen Name (#cfc4b4) | chat colour |
| 250 | Chronicle Labels (deep teal) | label accent |
| 500 | Verdigris Splash (`px448_green`, the green Honor Brand) | kill effect |
| 1000 | Chronicler's Teal (#5cc8c0) | chat colour |
| 1750 | Arcane Vortex (`px03_arcane`) | kill effect |
| 2500 | Obsidian Labels | label accent |
| 3500 | Gilded Ascent (`aura_burst_gold`, the gold Cinder Throne) | kill effect |

Category completion: Combat & Leveling War Surge (`aura_burst_red`), Monsters Thornbloom (`px286_green`), World Bosses
Titan's Pyre (`dome_blast_holy`), Rifts Rift Sigil (`px674_arcane`), Raids Sepulchre Labels, Bounties Huntsman's Copper,
Items & Crafting Tempered Labels, PvP Bloodsteel Name, Exploration & Social Lantern Name, Secrets Falling Stars
(`starfall_crown`); the category's title is in "Achievements". `ChaosCosmetics.sync(player)` / `syncAccount(accountId,
player)` grant what the account earned (`K.syncs` with the facts `{points, categories}` from `ChaosAchievements.accountOf`):
at login, when the Cosmetics window opens and after every new achievement unlock (achievements.lua `syncTrack`). It only
adds (`INSERT IGNORE`, the owned set is checked first): fewer points later (a staff reset) take nothing back. Staff:
`/cosmetic <character>, sync` re-syncs an account (online or not). Never sold: no price, no store unlock (`ofUnlock` is
store-only), `cosmetics_store.lua` builds store cosmetics only, and the validator refuses a price, an offer, a second way to
earn it, a milestone used twice or above the points that exist, a category rewarded twice or unknown.

**Readable by rule.** `ChaosCosmeticsCore.validate` (startup and the test): ids and keys unique; kinds, sources, prices and
achievements known; 1-3 spells of the right line; swaps inside one family; kill effects in the pair; accents at least 200/255
opaque and every label rarity colour at contrast 3 or more on them; chat colours at contrast 4.5 or more on the console
background; every store cosmetic has its store offer at its price and name, nothing else is sold as a cosmetic.

Protocol (JSON on `ChaosOpcodes.cosmetics` = 225): client -> server `open | state | select {kind, id, line} (id 0 = the default) |
preview {id} | hello | close` (`state`: the same `state` answer without opening the window, for the Customise Character window's
dropdowns; `hello`: the client is in the game, the full `style`, `colors` and `looks` again); server -> client `state {open, line, lineName, rows}`, `style {accent}` (the character's own label
accent), `colors {names = {[name] = "#rrggbb" | false}, full}` (sent in full at login, a change to everyone online),
`result {ok, text}`. API: `ChaosCosmetics.swapFor / storeUnlock / storePreview / offerPreview / grant / revoke / owns`.
Staff: `/cosmetic <character>, <key | all>[, revoke]` and `/cosmetic <character>, sync` (group 4+; a grant needs group 5,
`Chaos.staffCommand`). Store action `preview {category, page, offer}`
(`shop.lua`, cosmetic unlocks only).

Install: the `files`, `spells` (the `_common.lua` / `_supports.lua` hook) and `sql` steps of `install_all.py`. Client:
`game_cosmetics`; `game_groundlabels` (`setAccent`), `game_chatlinks` (keeps its parts on the label), `game_shop` (SHOW and
the colour previews), `client_chaos_topbar` (Character > Cosmetics).
**Tests:** `tests/cosmetics_test.lua` (LuaJIT and Lua 5.3: the shipped config against the real effect catalogues, the spells
of each line, achievements and store; refusals of non-recolours, unknown effects, power fields, unreadable colours, a wrong
store price; ownership, choosing, the skin lookup; `cosmetics.lua` on a mocked engine: store unlock, choosing, kill effects on
the last hit only, chat colours to everybody, the accent, previews to the asking player only, achievement grants, `/cosmetic`;
the reward track: milestones, categories, idempotent grants that are never taken back, no store exposure, `/cosmetic ..., sync`;
`_common.lua` swapping during a cast and the default without a cast or without the variant), `season_test.lua` (cosmetics
allowed to season characters), client `game_cosmetics/cosmeticslogic_test.lua` (name position and recolouring next to item
links), `game_groundlabels/groundlabels_test.lua` (the accent keeps the rarity colours).
**Tested in game** (own server and database copy, two Linux clients): the four store categories, SHOW on a skin (seen by the
buyer only), purchases ("Owned." after), the window and its tabs; Iron Bellow with Voidborn War Cries drawn violet in the
other client; Frost Shatter on a killing blow seen by the other client; the Frost name colour in the other client's chat next
to an item link; the Azure accent on Legendary / Rare / Mythic labels; Veteran's Gold granted from the achievement at login;
the Ember plate frame. Screenshots outside the repository.

### Chaos outfit shaders (`cosmetics_config.lua` `outfitShaders`, OFF as shipped)
Six engine outfit shaders written for this server (client `game_chaosshaders`, `data/shaders/chaos_outfit_*.frag`; client
`MANIFEST.md`): Ember Glow, Frost Rime, Void Flicker, Holy Radiance, Heartblood, Spectral Ghost, shaders.xml ids 19-24
(`chaos_ember_glow` ... `chaos_spectral_ghost`, written into the Chaos shaders block by `install_outfits.py` whatever the
switch; a shaders.xml shader stays locked until `Player:addShader`). Unlocked like a cosmetic (account-wide, a
`chaos_cosmetics` row `shader_<name>`, store unlock `cosmetic_shader_<name>`) and worn through the Outfit window, like the
store's other shaders. Deliberately not a kind of `kinds` / `cosmetics`: the Cosmetics window has nothing to choose for
them; they show in its Collection tab as kind `shader` rows (owned or how to get them). **Off switch:**
`outfitShaders.enabled = false` (shipped): nothing is listed, granted, sold or added. On: an owned one is added to every
character of the account at login and to the buyer when bought (`addOwnedShaders`). **Not priced** (the owner decides): an
entry without `price` is never sold ("Store: not on sale yet"). To sell: set `price = N` on the entries and add
`dofile("data/scripts/chaos/cosmetics_store.lua")("outfitshader")` (its offers, appended to Outfit Shaders since 2026-10-21) to the Cosmetics hunk of
`shop_config.lua`; `K.validate` refuses an offer while the switch is off, without a price or at another price.
`K.validateOutfitShaders` (run by the startup check and the test): keys unique and not a cosmetic's, ids 19..255 and unused,
names `chaos_*` registered by the client, whole prices, a swatch colour, no power fields. **Tests:** `tests/cosmetics_test.lua`
(off: nothing listed, sold, granted or added at login; the client registers every name and has the files; on: listing,
owned ids, Collection rows, a priced unlock sold and added to the buyer and to the account's other character at login, an
unpriced one not sold; validator refusals).

**Worn through the Outfit window (fixed, ROADMAP 86).** No shader could be worn, the store's neither, for two reasons.
(1) Server: `Player:addShader` keeps a character's shaders as bits in the reserved storage keys 10002034-10002044, but
the base `Player::addStorageValue` accepted only the mount, wing and aura ranges there and dropped them ("Warning:
unknown reserved key: 10002034"), at the grant and when the keys were read at login. `hasShader` was false for every
shader, so the outfit window packet (it sends wings, auras and the owned shaders to our client) listed none, and a
set-outfit request with a shader was refused. Engine src-patch `0036` accepts the range. (2) Client: the base Outfit
window had no row for shaders, though the client read them from the packet; client base patch `0045` adds a Shader row
(client/BASE.md 27, MANIFEST.md "Outfit shaders in the Outfit window"). **Ownership** is checked by the engine on every
set-outfit request (`Game::playerChangeOutfit`: an unknown name is no shader; a shader without `hasShader` refuses the
whole change); the client sends only a shader of the list. **Earlier buyers:** a store or season pass shader left its
mark (`Chaos.storage.shopShaderBase` + id) but no ownership; `shop.lua` `Shop.syncShaders` adds the ownership again at
login for every marked id (`shop_core.lua` `markedShaders`), idempotent. **Tests:** `tests/shop_test.lua` (marks, the
login sync, delivery), `tools/outfit_shader_patch_test.py` (the chain's allow line has the shader range; every
configured shader id fits the 310 the range holds), client `outfitshaderlist_test.lua`. **Tested on a live test
server** (0001-0036, Linux client 0001-0045): with 0035 only, `addShader` returned true and the storage stayed -1, the
packet listed 0 shaders; with 0036, four granted (11, 19, 21, 23) listed and shown in the window with previews, Ember
Glow picked and worn (`lookShader` 19), an unowned `chaos_frost_rime` sent straight from the client refused (19 kept),
an owned one and none accepted, and ownership and the worn shader kept over a relog. A second run on fresh builds of
both chains also checked the login sync: a store mark for 19 with no ownership got the ownership at the next login
(listed, picked, worn). The switch stays off (prices are the owner's call).

## Footprints and outlines (`cosmetics*.lua` kinds `footprint` / `outline`, client `game_cosmeticfx`, client base patch 0038, art `client/tools/gen_cosmeticfx_art.py`)

Two more cosmetic kinds of `cosmetics_config.lua`, account-wide like the others, chosen per character in Character >
Cosmetics (tabs Footprints and Outlines, a Default row takes them off; storages 7102000 footprint, 7102001 outline, the
wardrobe block 7102000 - 7102049 of `chaos_constants.lua`). Everyone on screen sees them.

| Kind | What | Store (coins) | Never sold |
|---|---|---|---|
| Footprints | prints on the tiles a walking player leaves, turned to the step, fading out in 3.2 s | Ember Steps, Frost Steps, Blood Trail, Ash Prints, Petal Trail, Venom Drips, Shadow Wisps, Gilded Steps, Storm Sparks, 200 each | Hunter's Tracks (Never Off Duty), Inkstep (reward track, 750 points), Rimewalker (boss: Skaldra), Omen Ash (boss: the Ascended Omens) |
| Outlines | a 2 px line around the character's silhouette (body, addons, mount and rider, the walking frame), one colour or a vertical gradient; two of the store's and three earned ones pulse | Gilded, Crimson, Void, Frost, Verdant Glow, Ember Gradient, Storm Gradient, Radiant Pulse, Abyssal Pulse, 250 each | Paragon's Radiance (Absolute), Chronicler's Halo (reward track, 2000 points), Void Corona (boss: Nyxareth), Cinderheart Blaze (boss: the Cinderheart) |

**Why client-drawn.** Two ways were weighed for the prints. Server magic effects on the tile left: one effect packet per step
per spectator (a crowd of 30 walkers on one screen is about 60-80 packets a second to each viewer), effects of the pair that
are spell art and too loud for a trail, and no way for a viewer to hide them. Client drawing: the server only says who
wears what (`looks {names = {[name] = {f, o, p}}, full}` on the cosmetics opcode, sent in full at login and as a change to
everyone online, like the chat colours), and each client draws its own generated pictures: no work per step on the server,
nothing new in the pair, and a viewer setting. `game_cosmetics` hands `looks` and `tryfx` to `game_cosmeticfx`. Once in the
game the client sends `hello` and gets the full `style`, `colors` and `looks` again: what the login event sends can reach
the client before it is in the game and is dropped there, and a reconnect into a character still online runs no login
event (found in the outline test: after a relogin nobody's outline showed until someone changed theirs).

**How the client draws them.** A print is a tile widget (`Tile:setWidget`, the way `game_groundlabels` draws its labels) on the
tile the player left, put down once the step is done, turned with `UIWidget:setRotation`, fading out; at most 160 prints on
screen and 8 per walker; never on a tile that holds another module's widget (ground labels, hideout marks). No new prints
while the viewer stands in a protection zone (temples and depots are crowded; the client only knows its own zone flag). An
outline is a line the engine draws around the player's silhouette (client base patch 0038, `client/BASE.md`):
`Creature:setOutline(r, g, b, a, widthPx, pulseMs)` and `setOutlineGradient` for the colour at the top. The colours of each
art key are on the client (`game_cosmeticfx` `CF.OUTLINES`), so the server still sends only the art key and a client
without the patch keeps its old picture. Character > Cosmetics has "Show other players' footprints / outlines" (this client
only; the own character always shows). Preview (the window) and SHOW (the store, `tryfx {kind, art, pulse}` to the buyer
only) draw the look on the own character for 6 s; the window's sample shows the outline on a small copy of the character.

**Outlines (owner feedback: "they look like auras, they must follow the contour of the outfit").** The first version was a
soft glow picture behind the character; it is now a real silhouette line. The outfit queues one outline item before its
mount and body; at draw time it draws every part again (mount, body, each addon, the rider, the current walking frame,
shaded or not) as a quad grown by the width, through a program that reads the part's alpha in 8 directions and paints only
where the part is transparent and a neighbour is not. The parts are drawn over it, so the lines inside the silhouette
(rider over mount, addons) are covered and only the outer contour stays. It is a separate pass, so the outfit shader still
draws the body; wings and auras are not outlined (the line runs under the wings), names and bars never. Width: 2 sprite
pixels, scaled by the sprite size, so HD upscaling (xBRZ) keeps the same look. Gradients (feet to top): Ember (red to gold),
Storm (deep blue to white), Paragon's Radiance (gold to white), Void Corona (dark violet to violet), Cinderheart Blaze (red
to gold); pulsing ones (Radiant, Abyssal, Paragon's Radiance, Void Corona, Cinderheart Blaze) breathe between 45% and 100%
every 1.8 s in the engine. A client whose engine lacks `Creature:setOutline` (checked per creature) shows the old glow
picture (`client/tools/gen_cosmeticfx_art.py` still makes those for it). Cost: one extra quad per outfit part; 39 outlined
monsters and two players on one screen measured within the noise of the same scene without outlines (software OpenGL).

Tests: `tests/cosmetics_test.lua` (art keys, one picture per cosmetic, pulse for outlines only, prices, the track milestones,
the `looks` broadcast to every client, a reconnect keeping the look, the `hello` resend, `tryfx` to the buyer only, the boss
source), client `game_cosmeticfx/cosmeticfxlogic_test.lua` (looks merge, preview, settings, step directions, fading,
pulsing, the caps, sizes, a picture and outline colours for every art key of the server, the two store gradients, the
engine feature check) and `game_cosmetics/cosmeticslogic_test.lua` (the tabs, the Default rows).
Tested in game (own server built with src-patches 0001-0021, a private database, two Linux clients with base patches
0001-0038): footprints in a walking trail; outlines on a standing and a walking character, with an outfit shader, on a
mounted character, gradient and pulsing ones, 39 outlined monsters at once, at sprite scale 1 and 2 (xBRZ); the setting
hiding the other player's outline; a relogin and a reconnect getting everyone's outline back; an engine without 0038
showing the glow. Screenshots outside the repository.

**The window's effect preview** (2026-10-16). Each state row of a spell skin or kill effect carries `play`
(`cosmetics_core.lua` `C.playOf` / `C.playSpec` / `C.playRows`): one step per swap, `{a = the stock effect, b = the
skin's}`, each `{id, dx, dy, ms, m, n}` resolved through the same tables the cast and the Preview button use
(`ChaosFx`, `ChaosFxMissile`, `ChaosVfx`, `ChaosVfxMissile`); a kill effect is one step with no `a`; a name the server
does not know is left out. The client plays them in a loop beside the list (client `MANIFEST.md` "Cosmetics effect
previews"). `cosmetics_test.lua` checks the steps and the resolution.

## Wardrobe catalogue (`wardrobe.lua`, `wardrobe_core.lua`, client `game_unlocks`, base patch 0060)

The 10.98 outfit window packet lists only what the character owns; the Customise Character window shows everything
(client `MANIFEST.md` "Owned and locked lists"). On the cosmetics opcode (225, no new opcode) the client sends
`wardrobe` (at game start and when the outfit window opens; rate limit 300 ms, `cosmetics.lua` routes it) and gets
`wardrobe {sex, hash, outfit, mount, wings, aura, shader}`, sent with `Chaos.sendChunked` (about 20 KB):
outfits `{l, n, o, a, s}` (look, name, owned, owned addons, source), mounts / wings / auras `{l, n, o, s}` by client
look, shaders `{n, o, s}` by shader name.
- **Catalogue**: `data/XML/outfits.xml` (the character's sex, enabled, each look once), `mounts.xml`, `wings.xml`,
  `auras.xml`, `shaders.xml`, read once per sex and kept (`ChaosWardrobe.clearCache()` drops it).
- **Owned**: the engine's rules. `Player:hasOutfit(look, 0)` and the addons (3, else 1 and 2), `Player:hasMount(id)`;
  wings, auras and shaders by the bits of the reserved storages `Player::hasWing / hasAura / hasShader` read
  (10002012 / 10002023 / 10002034 + (id - 1) // 31, bit (id - 1) % 31); an access player owns everything, a premium
  entry needs premium.
- **Source**: exclusives (`exclusives_core.lua` `K.how`: "Achievement: ...", "Boss: ..., rare drop"), class looks
  ("Class: <name>", `class_looks_core.lua`), store offers at any depth of `shop_config.lua` ("Store"); an outfit with
  `unlocked="yes"` is "Free" ("Free; addons: Store" when its addons are sold). Unknown otherwise.
- Nothing is granted or worn here: `Game::playerChangeOutfit` refuses an outfit change with a part not owned.
`tests/wardrobe_test.lua`.

## Exclusives (`exclusives.lua`, `exclusives_core.lua`, `exclusives_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_exclusives.sql`, client `game_cosmetics` Collection tab)

Every visual kind of the store also has options that are never sold, only earned from an achievement or a rare boss drop.
Unlocks are account-wide and not tradeable (table `chaos_exclusives`): a drop is a direct unlock for the account of the
player who rolled it, never an item (the codebase has no tradeable cosmetic token, and an item would be lost to a trade or a
death). What an unlock gives is applied at once to the account's characters online and to every character at its login
(idempotent): outfits and addons (both looks with both addons), mounts, wings, auras, outfit shaders (the engine's own
ownership), plate frames (the frame slot storages of the store), portal styles (route `boss` of `townportal_config.lua`, owned
through `ChaosExclusives.owns`), transmog sets (`ChaosTransmog.grantSet`, source `boss`), pets (`ChaosPets.grant` on each
character, `source.boss`), footprints and outlines (`ChaosCosmetics.grant`, source `boss`).

| Kind | Achievement (never sold) | Boss drop (never sold) |
|---|---|---|
| Outfits | Wingbound 1455/1456 (Unrivalled), Jadeforged 1039/1040 (Master Artificer); before: Death Herald, Rift Warrior, Arena Champion, Demon Hunter | Ashen Seraph 1459 (Varkhul), Omen Lancer 1457/1458 (Ascended Omens), Mirewarden 1464/1465 (the Rotmother) |
| Outfit addons | Mage addons 130/138 (Monster Scholar) | Knight addons 131/139 (Gorvath, guild boss) |
| Mounts | Tuskhide Boar 146 / look 1323 (Nothing Surprises Me), Duskcrest Drake 147 / 428 (Untouchable); before: Doombringer, Corpsefire Skull, Rift Runner, Nightstinger, Siegebreaker | Rimebone Stalker 148 / 1444 (Skaldra), Bloodwing Fiend 149 / 1441 (Vharok), Bannerdrake 150 / 596 (Gorvath), Gloomwyrm 151 / 1450 (Nyxareth) |
| Wings | Bloodthorn Pinions 17 / look 2140 (Colossus Hunter), Gravecrow Wings 18 / 2141 (Nobody Kneels), Riftglass Wings 19 / 2142 (Lord of Thresholds) | Cinder Plumes 16 / look 1486 (the Cinderheart) |
| Auras | Ashen Murmuration 29 / look 1487 (Witching Hour) | Scarlet Glimmer 30 / look 712 (Sepulchre wardens) |
| Outfit shaders | Verdant Sparks 16 `green_pixent` (Master of the Wilds) | Cinder Sparks 18 `ember_pixent` (Ascended Omens) |
| Plate frames | Laurel (Keeper of the Flame); category titles bring their frames | Sepulchre (Sepulchre wardens), Infernal (the Cinderheart) |
| Portal styles | the six achievement styles (Abyssal Maw ...) | Drowned Gate 51 (Skaldra), Seraph's Door 52 (Varkhul) |
| Transmog | Thornmoth Vestments (Keeper of the Wort), Haloed Arms (Lifeline), Spiritthorn, Rimebound | Hellforged Visage (Kaelgor), Pyrarch Arms (Nyxareth), Deathlord Arms (Varkhul), Gilded Eldritch Arms (the Cinderheart) |
| Pets | Ash Cat, Gilded Goblin, Riftling | Rotling (the Rotmother), Ashweaver Spiderling (Sepulchre wardens) |
| Footprints / outlines | see "Footprints and outlines" | see "Footprints and outlines" |

Every look is existing art of the client pair: base looks that no outfits.xml / mounts.xml / wings.xml / auras.xml line had and
no monster or NPC uses (a scan of the pair against the base data and the repository), the shaders are client code. The XML
lines come from the install tools: `install_outfits.py` (a third outfits.xml block "Chaos exclusive outfits", mounts 146-151
appended to MOUNTS, a wings.xml block, a shaders.xml block for the ids the base file lacks; all read from
`exclusives_config.lua`), `install_auras.py` (`data/XML/chaos_auras_exclusive.csv`, ids 29 and 30). The store never sells them:
`shop.lua` adds them to its exclusions (`ChaosShopCore.exclusions` reads `exclusives_config.lua`), `gen_shop_cosmetics.py`
leaves them out, the validator refuses an exclusive that is sold and `tests/exclusives_test.lua` checks the store, the
generated list and the other reward sources (class looks, achievement, season and season pass rewards, faction auras).

**Achievements.** `achievements_data.lua` `reward.exclusives = {{key, name}}` names them (the achievements window shows the name
next to the other rewards, `achievements_core.lua` `rewardText`). The account owns an achievement exclusive once any of its
characters has the achievement: at login, when the wardrobe opens and after every new unlock (`ChaosAchievements.syncTrack` is
wrapped once at runtime, no edit in `achievements.lua`); older unlocks count. Footprints and outlines use the cosmetics' own
`achievement` / `points` fields (the reward track), transmog sets and pets their own `achievement` fields.

**Boss drops.** `exclusives_config.lua` `bosses`: groups of kill keys with a chance and a reward list. One guarded line in each
boss script rolls for every player that gets the kill's own rewards (personal loot, each player on its own): `worldboss.lua`
(rewarded players online at the kill; the boss's name gives `wb_<boss>`), `raid.lua` (`raid_<boss>`, the players that loot it
this week), `uber.lua` (`ascended_<kind>`, `cinder`), `guildboss.lua` (`guild_gorvath`, rewarded members online). A hit
(rng below the chance) unlocks one reward of the group the account does not own yet, picked evenly; with all owned, nothing.
Chances: world bosses 2%, the Sepulchre's first four bosses 1.5%, Varkhul 3%, the Ascended Omens 3%, the Cinderheart 5%, the
guild boss 2% (the validator keeps every chance at or below 25%). The player gets a message and a "Rare drop!" toast.

**The wardrobe.** Character > Cosmetics, tab Collection: every exclusive with its kind, owned or not, "Achievement: <name>
(<goal>)" (a hidden achievement stays "???" until owned) or "Boss: <boss>, rare drop", where it is chosen, and a preview on the
own character (outfits, mounts, wings, auras, shaders); owned ones first, "Earned N / M (never sold)". Exclusives never show in
the store.

Staff: `/exclusive <character>, <key | all>[, revoke]` (revoke removes the account row; what was applied stays on the
characters) and `/exclusive <character>, roll, <kill key>` (group 4+; a grant or a roll needs group 5, `Chaos.staffCommand`). API: `ChaosExclusives.grant / revoke / owns / sync /
bossKill / worldBossKill / rows / apply / applyAll`.

**Achievement wings (things_custom17).** The three achievement wings are donor I wings (8.60, the wings and auras
library) imported as looks 2140-2142 (client/MANIFEST.md "Achievement wings": picks.csv rows of family `exclusive`, the
silhouette and in-pair checks, the stock wings placement, so no displacement edit). Ids 17-19 follow the Cinder Plumes
(16) in the wings.xml block of `install_outfits.py`. They go to achievements with no exclusive yet: Colossus Hunter
(`wb_all`), Nobody Kneels (`raid_flawless`, hidden, so the window shows "???" until owned) and Lord of Thresholds
(`rift_100`). **Needs the new pair:** a client on things_custom16 draws no wings for 2140-2142. Ship the server change
with things_custom17 (not on `windows-assets` yet; docs/OWNER_TODO.md). The Scarlet Glimmer aura (look 712) has no
displacement in the dat. Checked in game:

**Scarlet Glimmer checked in game (2026-10-13, things_custom21, Linux client under Xvfb).** On a player (look 130),
four directions, next to the stock aura Fire Essence (932) and the Ashen Murmuration (1487). The client reads
displacement 0,0 for 712; the stock auras have 10-17 x 12-20 (932: 17,17; 933: 13,15; 934: 10,12; 935: 12,13;
936: 17,20; 1487: 17,14). **It is drawn off its tile, down and to the right.** The centre of its pixels (48 frames, the
player's own pixels taken out) sits 44 px right and 32 px down of the tile centre, at 85.3 px a tile: about 17 x 12
dat units. Fire Essence sits 15 px left, 0 px down; the Ashen Murmuration 15 px left, 16 px up. So the Glimmer is
about 22 units right and 12-18 units down of where the stock auras draw: its red orb and sparkles hang off the
player's lower right corner, half on the next tile. The direction does not change it (an aura has one direction).
Proposed fix: displacement 17,17 (as Fire Essence) on outfit 712 in the next pair, with
`client/tools/sprites/fix_pair_warnings.py` kind `displacement` (flags only, needs the owner's approval). The pair was not
edited. Screenshots (test-only, not in the repo): `aura_grid.png` (rows: no aura, 712, 932; columns: the four
directions), `aura_montage.png`, `aura_heat.png` (where each aura's pixels fall over 48 frames).

Tests: `tests/exclusives_test.lua` (LuaJIT and Lua 5.3): the shipped config against the store, the generated store list, the
achievements, the cosmetics, transmog sets, pets, portal styles and frames; refusals (a sold look, a price, a chance too high,
a boss drop nobody drops, a kill in two groups, wrong names); every kind has an achievement and a boss exclusive (wings:
three achievement ones, ids above the store's 15, each look the picks.csv row of the pair, wings 17-19 refused by the
store); the looks are no other reward; every world boss, raid boss, Ascended Omen, the Cinderheart and the guild boss has a
group and its script the guarded hook; the roll (miss, hit, owned skipped, nothing left, rates over 20,000 rolls); the
achievement sync and the rows; `exclusives.lua` on a mocked engine (a drop for the account and its online characters, the
frame switched on for the roller only, transmog / pets / cosmetics handed to their systems, the sync and the wrapped
`syncTrack`, a later login, the rows, the staff command). Also `transmog_test.lua`, `pets_test.lua`, `townportal_test.lua`,
`cosmetics_test.lua`, `season_test.lua`.

**Scarlet Glimmer displacement (things_custom23, on windows-assets since 2026-10-13, c91dd6f9).** The owner approved the fix. Pair things_custom23
gives look 712 displacement 17,17, the value of Fire Essence 932 (client/MANIFEST.md "Aura displacement
(things_custom23)"). Measured, not guessed: in every direction the Glimmer's art runs along the centre of the frame's
bottom-right tile, as the stock ground auras' does. With 0,0 the client drew it 15 px right and below the tile centre;
with 17,17 its centre sits 4 px up-left, inside the stock range. The art does differ per direction (the orb leads
facing north or west and sits on the body facing south or east); no single value centres both axes. A scan of every
aura and wings look of the pair found no other look with this fault. No server change: auras.xml 30 keeps look 712.
Not on `windows-assets` until the owner says "pode mandar o par para o windows-assets". A client on things_custom22
still draws the Glimmer off its tile.

## Hideouts (`hideout.lua`, `hideout_core.lua`, `hideout_config.lua`, `hideout_store.lua`, `sql/chaos_hideout.sql`, client `game_hideout`)

A personal room for every character (a season character is another character, so it has its own), built at runtime and
decorated by its owner. Cosmetic only: decorations change how the room looks and nothing else; the utilities are the ones
every town has (the owner's own depot, the supply stash, two exercise dummies), no buffs. Client `game_hideout`
(Character > Hideout, next to the Town Portal; a "Go to Hideout" button in the Town Portal window), extended opcode 192
(`ChaosOpcodes.hideout`). Numbers, themes and the catalogue: `hideout_config.lua`; pure rules: `hideout_core.lua`.

**Grid and slots.** x/y 12288-12799, z 7: 256 slots of 32 tiles (16 columns), rooms 15 x 11 inside walls. Clear of every
other runtime grid (tower 2000+, tutorial 4600+, world boss 5000+, siege 5100+, arena 6000-6100, ascension 7000-7100,
Ascended Omens 7600-7700, rifts 8192-8447, trials 9000-9160, guild halls 9216-9536, Ember Descent 10000-10255 x
10000-10127, raid 10400-10911 x 10000-10511, guild boss 11264-11456 x 10000-10144, battleground 11264-11456 x
11264-11456); `tests/hideout_test.lua` reads those configs and checks the overlap. A slot is taken from the pool when
someone enters (the owner keeps it while the room is up), built once with `Game.createTile` (a slot with a map tile in
its footprint is skipped for good), furnished from the database, and torn down after `emptySeconds` (30) without a player
inside: its items are removed and the slot goes back to the pool (tiles, ground and walls stay for the next owner).

**Themes** (floor, walls, the four corner lights; every theme has the same layout, so a change never moves a decoration):
Ashen Crypt (every character, 24 decorations), Ember Forge (Ember Descent depth 5, 30), Veiled Sanctum (the Veiled Choir
Honored, 36), Thornbound Grove (the Thornbound Circle Honored, 36). Walls are a base wall family (vertical, horizontal,
post, corner pieces by position); with the dark tile set installed the floor and the north / west walls use it (its
tall wall is never put on the south / east side, where it would hide the floor).

**Decorating.** The owner, inside the own hideout: Place / Move / Remove in the window; the window steps aside and the
hovered tile shows the decoration (green fits, red does not, `HideoutLogic.check` mirrors the server); left click places,
the wheel or Rotate turns it, right click or Done ends. Rules (`K.placeProblem`): one object per tile, a rug under it,
wall decorations on the north or west wall (the side picks the item), the fixture tiles (arrival, exit, depot, stash,
dummies, lights, the waystone device and the four tiles around it) stay free, a path of walkable tiles from the arrival to the exit, the depot, the stash and the dummies
(8 directions), a limit per decoration and per theme. Decorations carry an action id: using them does nothing, moving
them puts them back; items dropped on a hideout floor go back to the player; no PvP inside; the Town Portal inside is a way
out (below). Entering is refused from inside any registered instance (`Chaos.inAnyInstance`:
rift, dungeon, tower, arena, world boss arena, siege, raid, Ember Descent, Ascended Omen, guild boss, battleground, trials, ascension
trial, the Scorched Marches), so no return spot inside one is stored. Leaving never goes back to a spot that lies in an instance area
now (`Chaos.instanceAt`): such a player goes to the temple instead.

**Waystone device** (owner request 2026-10-17: the waystone texts said "house", the hideout is where it should work, and the
default hideout should come with the device in the middle). The base waystone system (`customs/waystone_system/tier_maps.lua`)
works only in a house: the device (item 29624 "Waystone Portal", 29626 is its other rotation; action id 42707, set by the base
`player.lua` when a kit 29628 is unwrapped) refuses unless `tile:getHouse()` and its portal pads are made only on tiles of a
house the player owns. The hideout has no engine house, so `tools/patch_waystone_hideout.py` (step `waystonehideout`, idempotent,
`tools/patch_waystone_hideout_test.py` in CI) gives `tier_maps.lua` a helper `chaosWaystonePlace(player, pos, ownerOnly)`: true on
a house tile (an owned one for the pads), **or** on a tile of the player's own hideout (`ChaosHideout.isOwnRoomTile(player, pos)`,
read when used, so load order does not matter); houses keep working as before. It also refuses the "wrap" answer for a
hideout's device (`ChaosHideout.isFixture(item)`), and changes the texts: "You may only use the Waystone Portal in your hideout or
inside a house.", "There is no space in your hideout or house to spawn portals.", and the six Waystone Tier descriptions of
`items.xml` ("Use this waystone on the waystone device in your hideout or house to teleport to a random tier N map."). The
portal kit (29628) still says "in your house": building a device from a kit needs a house. Every hideout, in every theme, is
built with the device as a fixture at the middle of the floor (`fixtures.waystone` = 8,6; item `ids.waystone` 29624, action id
`aid.waystone` 42707 are values of the base data, kept in `hideout_config.lua`): a solid tile like the depot (the path rule
counts it), never removable or movable (`onItemMoved` puts it back, wrap refused), and the four diagonal tiles around it (7,5 9,5
7,7 9,7, where the base script puts the portal pads for 60 s) stay free of decorations. A visitor who uses it gets the refusal
(only the owner's own hideout counts). The pads lead to the waystone maps and the 30-minute timer of the base script; the exit
leads out of the hideout, like the Town Portal. **Part 2 (2026-10-22, player report: "clicking the device and Use does
nothing, clicking waystones does nothing either").** The base script answers a use with `show` on extended opcode 202 and
waits for the client to send `teleport {clientId}`; this client had no window for it, so nothing happened, and a Waystone
Tier item had no action at all. Client module `game_waystone` is that window now (client/MANIFEST.md). The patch's part 2
(own marker, so a server patched before gets it on the next run): `show` carries `tiers` (`{clientId, look, tier, count}`
for the six tiers, counted by `player:getItemCount` through every backpack; `look` is the item's client id in this
server's items.otb, for the icon) and `pick`; `teleport` refuses a tier the player does not hold ("You have no waystone of
that tier.") before any pad is made (the base made the four pads first and took the waystone after, so a pick without one
still opened them for 60 s); and the six Waystone Tier items (29845-29850) get an action: used on the device, or used
anywhere in the player's own hideout (`ChaosHideout.waystoneDevice(player)`), it runs the device's own use with that tier
as `pick`; elsewhere it says "Use this waystone on the waystone device in your hideout or house." Tests:
`tools/patch_waystone_hideout_test.py` (part 2 on a mocked engine, a part-1 install upgraded once; `WAYSTONE_BASE_DATA`
checks the real files), `tests/hideout_test.lua` (`waystoneDevice`). **Install:** `install_all.py` step `waystonehideout` (after `files`, so
`hideout.lua` has the API; the patch itself needs only the base files). **Needs a live check:** the device opens its window in a
hideout, the pads appear and lead to a tier map, a visitor is refused, the wrap button is refused, the pads are not blocked by
decorations on the other tiles.

**Unlocks** (the catalogue shows each lock reason): every character (thrones, tables, racks, basins, tapestries, rugs,
banners, bones, trees), achievements (Skull Pillar: rift tier 5; Skull Candle: an omen guardian; Hero Statue: level 300),
faction ranks (Compact Trusted / Honored, Choir Trusted / Revered, Vigil Revered, Circle Trusted / Revered), trophies of the
character's own kills (the five raid bosses, the three Ascended Omens, the Cinderheart, the five world bosses as wall
trophies; the look text names the boss and how often the owner slew it), the Ember Descent (depth 9, the boss slain),
events (invasions defended 1 / 5, 10 Treasure Goblins), the season journey (chapters 1 and 3, `chaos_season_journey`;
`ChaosHideout.sourceProbes.journey` may replace the probe), and the store. An earned unlock is kept in
`chaos_hideout_unlocks` (a faction rank later lost to the rival keeps it).

**Store.** Category "Hideout Decorations" (`hideout_store.lua`, the Hideouts hunk of `shop_config.lua`): Stone Seat 120,
Wyrmbone Throne 300, Tall Candelabrum 150, Gargoyle 200, Mourning Angel 200, Black Crystal 250, Wyrm Banner 150, Azure
Tapestry 100, Woven Rug 80 Chaos Coins. `{kind = "unlock", unlock = "hideout_<key>", gift = true}`: account-wide,
giftable (`shop.lua` lets an unlock offer that says `gift = true` be gifted; online at once, offline at the next login),
allowed to season characters (`season_config.lua` `unlockPrefixes`). Earned decorations are never sold;
`K.validate` checks that the store sells exactly the store decorations at their price and that no decoration carries
a power field.

**Visiting.** Permission private / friends (the owner's VIP list and party) / guild / public (default friends); season and
standard characters never mix while a season runs; staff (group 4+, `/hideout <character>`) may enter any. Entering is
refused in a fight (pz-lock or the fight icon), with a skull, and where the Town Portal is refused. The **Hideout
Portal** of every town leads to the own hideout ("City portals": in Cinderhold the portal gallery at the temple, next
to the Ember Descent portal; side by side with the Guild Hall Portal next to
every other temple; a look text and a blue effect every 4 s; placed at startup, checked once a minute).

**The way out** (fixed 2026-10-16: the owner's test found no way out; the portal stored its own tile as the return spot,
and a teleport onto a portal runs its step-in, so the exit sent the character straight back in). The exit forcefield
(south of the arrival), the window's **Leave** button (Character > Hideout) and a login inside all go to
`K.exitDestination`: the spot the character entered from (storages 7100180-7100183: the tile stepped from when entering
by the portal, else where they stood), else a free tile next to it (a spot stored before the fix is the portal itself),
else the temple of the home town, else Cinderhold's (`mainTown`). Never a tile of the hideout grid, a portal, stairs or
an instance area. The Hideout Portal also ignores a character put on it by a teleport out of a hideout. A character who
entered from another town's portal goes back to that town. Logout inside: the next login leads out the same way (the
room may be torn down by then). A server restart or a death: the engine puts the character at the temple (the room's
tiles are gone), and the login drops the stale return spot. The Town Portal (spell or menu) inside is a way out too (coordinator
2026-10-16): `townportal_core.lua` `K.hideoutExit` lets it act at once, with no channel, no cooldown and no portal pair
(a return portal would lead back into a hideout), through the same `ChaosHideout.leave`, so never into a hideout or an
instance. The Visit tab: hideouts of the VIP list, party and guild the character may enter, the showcase of public hideouts (most liked
/ most visited), the recent visits. A visit counts once per visitor and day; a like once per account and hideout, only
from inside it, 10 a day per account, one request per 2 s. The owner may send visitors out; a visitor who loses access
(the owner changed the permission) is sent out at once.

**Protocol** (JSON `{action, data}` on 192, server -> client chunked): client -> server `open | get | enter | leave |
visit {guid} | place {key, x, y, r} | move {id, x, y, r} | remove {id} | clear | theme {key} | perm {level} | kick | visits
| like {owner}`; server -> client `state {open, me, hideout, inside, layout, themes, catalogue, placed, permissions,
categories}`, `visits {friends, showcase = {likes, visits}, recent}`, `result {ok, text}`.

**Install.** The `files` and `sql` steps of `install_all.py` (plus `waystonehideout`, above; `sql/chaos_hideout.sql`, 5 tables; `hideout.lua` also creates
them at startup). The depot locker needs engine patch 0017 (`item:unserializeAttributes` sets its depot id to the owner's
home town); without it the locker says to use a town depot.

**Tests:** `tests/hideout_test.lua` (LuaJIT and Lua 5.3): the shipped config against achievements, factions and the
store; the opcode against every ChaosOpcodes entry and the reference lists; the grid against the other grids; placement
(layers, walls, reserved tiles, limits, the path, multi-tile and rotation), unlock sources, permissions, likes, visits,
the showcase, the slot pool; then `hideout.lua` on a mocked engine and database (enter, build, wall pieces, the locker's
depot id, place / move / remove, trophy text, store unlock and gift, themes, VIP / guild visits, likes, permission
change sending a visitor out, no PvP, dropped items, teardown and slot reuse, login inside, staff entry, the waystone device:
built in the middle with the base ids, its pad tiles kept free, `isOwnRoomTile` for the owner / a visitor / outside, never moved);
the way out:
`K.exitDestination` (stored spot, next to a stored portal tile, never the grid, home temple, Cinderhold) and, with a
mocked teleport that runs the step-in of the tile's items like the engine, the portal -> exit round trip (back on the
tile stepped from, one step-in, no loop), an old return spot on the portal, a teleport from a hideout onto the portal,
another town's portal, logout inside with the room torn down, death / restart (stale spot dropped), the window's Leave,
no home town. `tests/cityportals_test.lua`: the portal placement. `shop_test.lua`
(a hideout decoration may be gifted, other unlocks not), `season_test.lua` (the category is allowed). Client
`game_hideout/hideoutlogic_test.lua` (filters, texts, rotation, positions, the placement check). **Tested in game** (a
server copy with MariaDB and the reference client): window, enter, an empty Ashen Crypt, decorating 34 pieces (the theme
limit refused the 25th in the Crypt), the Veiled Sanctum, the ghost preview green and red, placing by click. Not tested in
game: two players (visits and likes), the depot window, the store purchase screen.

## Store pouches (`pouches.lua`, `pouches_core.lua`, `pouches_config.lua`, `tools/install_pouches.py`, client `game_pouches`)

Four containers sold in the store (Convenience), each collecting its own kind of loot from the corpses the character owns,
**while the character carries it** (in the backpack or a bag inside it, any depth; not in the depot or inbox). No base
autoloot list is needed.

| Pouch | Item id (look) | Slots | Coins | Collects |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Loot Bag | 32081 (client 38608: a leather sack, gold coins spilling) | 255, weightless | 250 | all the loot of your kills by default (its rules, below, can narrow it); the Auto Seller sells what is in it |
| Orbs Pouch | 32082 (client 38609: a violet pouch with a glowing orb) | 100 (was 40) | 200 | every orb (the currency orbs 29851-29859, Erasure, Gilding, Sockets, Unmaking, orbs v2, the Whetstone, every `loot_config.lua` currency entry), rune shards (32051) and gems (32001-32035), the gems only while no Gem Pouch is carried |
| Rift Key Pouch | 32083 (client 38610: an iron strongbox, gold key, key ring) | 100 (was 30) | 150 | Rift Keys (item 10155 with action id 47401; tier and modifiers kept), Omen Keys (32072) and omen fragments (32071) |
| Gem Pouch | 32095 (the stock jewelled backpack's own look, no new sprite) | 100 | 150 | gems (32001-32035) only |

- **Items.** New items.otb nodes, copies of stock bags (group and flags of the expedition bag, the brocade bag and the fur bag)
  with their own looks: three item things of our own art, drawn by `client/tools/sprites/gen_pouch_art.py`, snapped to theme
  palettes by `gen_store_items_art.py` and appended to pair 34 as client ids 38608-38610 (client MANIFEST.md "Store item
  looks"; `clientId` in `pouches_config.lua`; the earlier looks 33651-33653, `oldClientId`, are replaced in place). Only the
  client id of the node changes, the server ids stay 32081-32083, so pouches already owned show the new look after the install;
  the store icons and the container window icons follow (`ItemType:getClientId()`). **The client pair must have the three things
  first** (a client without them shows nothing for a pouch); the Windows package pair has had them since pair 34;
  `install_pouches.py --stock-looks` keeps the stock bag looks only for clients on an older pair. And
  items.xml entries with `containerSize` (the protocol sends a container's size as one byte, so up to 255 would work). Installed by
  `tools/install_pouches.py` (step `pouches` of `install_all.py`, after `omens`; idempotent; `items.otb.bak` keeps the original).
  Weight 1 oz. The Orbs Pouch and the Rift Key Pouch carry their contents with their weight; a full pouch, or one the character
  cannot carry more in, passes the item on.
- **Bigger pouches and the Gem Pouch** (tester feedback 2026-10-28: "aumentar o espaco das bags de Rift/Orb e talvez criar uma
  outra so pra gema, que nao misturasse com orb"). `capacity` of the Orbs Pouch and the Rift Key Pouch is 100 now:
  `install_pouches.py` rewrites its marked block of items.xml when the config changed, so a second run on an installed server
  sets `containerSize` 100 (a restart loads it; pouches already owned have the new size, their contents stay;
  `tools/install_pouches_test.py` checks the rewrite of an old 40 / 30 block). The **Gem Pouch** is a fourth kind (`gems`,
  id 32095, free of every id table: pouches 32081-32083, Everfull Ration 32084, potions 32085-32086, globes 32088-32090,
  faction tokens 32091-32094), a copy of the stock jewelled backpack (5801; `clientId = 0` in `pouches_config.lua` means "keep the
  stock bag's client id", so no sprite is added). Store-bound, `bindLock`, one per character, regrant bit 8, Convenience offer at
  150 coins (like the Rift Key Pouch; `perCharacterConvenienceMax` 1,400 -> 1,550, `docs/PRICES.md`). Routing
  (`ChaosPouchesCore.plan`): `priority = {"gems", "orbs", "keys"}`; an item goes to the first **carried** pouch of that list that
  wants it. A gem is wanted by the Gem Pouch and the Orbs Pouch, so with a Gem Pouch carried it never reaches the Orbs Pouch,
  even when the Gem Pouch is full (the overflow then is the Loot Bag, as for every specialist); without a Gem Pouch the Orbs
  Pouch takes gems as before. The Gem Pouch takes nothing but gems.
- **The Loot Bag** (owner 2026-10-13: "uma bag sem fundo que pode carregar todo o loot que o jogador recebe automaticamente";
  called Loot Pouch before). Bottomless: 255 slots (`capacity`; the 10.98 protocol sends a container's size as one byte, so
  255 is the most a container can have) and **weightless** (`weightless = true`): engine src-patch 0038 keeps the weight of
  what lies in it (and in bags inside it) away from the character, and an item put into it skips the capacity check.
  `pouches.lua` registers the bag's item id with `Game.setWeightlessContainer` at load and at every login, only where the
  installed items.xml has it as a container; on an engine without 0038 the function is missing and the bag weighs as before.
  Its rules default to everything (`lootDefaults`: the autoloot list, coins, uniques, gear of any rarity, supplies, gems,
  everything else, overflow), so with no settings opened it takes all the loot of the character's kills; the rules window
  can still narrow it. It is a store item: kept at a relog, back (empty) after a death that drops the backpack (below), never
  traded or sold. 255 different stacks is its only limit: a full bag passes the item to the backpack, then the corpse.
- **The Loot Bag stays in the purse** (owner 2026-10-17, "Loot bag não pode sair da purse"). The store delivers it to the purse
  (the engine's store inbox, item 26052, `purseIds`). From the purse it cannot be moved anywhere else: not into the backpack,
  an inventory slot, a depot, a container on the ground, not dropped, mailed or traded. `Player:onMoveItem` answers the warning
  line "The Loot Bag stays in your purse: ..." (`ChaosPouchesCore.moveRefusal`: `lootBag` + `inPurse` in the move description;
  the trade request refuses it with the same line). A bag that sits elsewhere (a character from before the rule) keeps the
  old rule (backpack or depot only): the engine does not let a player drag into the purse, so it stays where it is. The Orbs and
  Rift Key pouches may still leave the purse.
- **The Loot Bag sorts itself by rarity** (owner 2026-10-17, "ordenar automaticamente por raridade"). Rarest first, uniques above
  every rarity, plain items last, equal ranks keep their order. `ChaosPouchesCore.rank` and `sortPlan` are pure (tested): the plan
  lists the items that must move to the front (the engine adds an item at the front of a container) and leaves the already sorted
  tail alone, at most `sort.maxMoves` (120) moves per call; a new plain item in front of a sorted bag moves only the rarer items.
  `ChaosPouches.sortBag` runs once per kill after the loot is stowed, after a click-to-loot, and when the bag is opened (an Action on
  the bag's id that sorts and returns false, so the engine opens it as usual). There is no timer and no scan of the whole bag
  except the O(n) rank read of those events. Only the top level of the bag is sorted; the moves use `FLAG_NOLIMIT` (a full bag).
  **Auto Seller:** "Sell all" in the Auto Seller window (Economy > Auto Seller, or the Loot Bag window's Auto Seller
  button) sells what is in it ("Store services", Auto Seller).
- **Order in the `onDropLoot` chain** (lower index first): 0 stock loot, 1 Chaos loot layer, 1.5 Echoing Spoils, 2 auto seller +
  rift key drop + paragon gold, 2.4 hunt tracker / achievements read the corpse, 2.45 pet fetch, 2.5 loot filter snapshot,
  **2.7 store pouches**, 3 base autoloot, 3.5 Rarity Autoloot pickup, 4.5 loot filter finish. After the auto seller, so an
  item on the auto-sell list is sold first; orbs and keys never are (`ChaosPouches.neverSell`, asked by `autosell.lua`, also
  refuses them on the list). After the snapshot, so the loot channel row shows the items the pouches took as looted. Before the
  base autoloot, so autoloot-list items land in the Loot Bag instead of the backpack.
- **Routing and priority** (`ChaosPouchesCore.plan`, `priority = {"orbs", "keys"}` in `pouches_config.lua`). The Orbs Pouch and
  the Rift Key Pouch always get their kinds of items first: orbs, the whetstone, rune shards and gems go to the Orbs Pouch, Rift
  Keys, Omen Keys and omen fragments to the Rift Key Pouch, before the Loot Bag, even when a Loot Bag rule would match too (its
  gems rule, the autoloot list). When that pouch is full (or the character cannot carry more), the Loot Bag takes the item only
  with its **overflow** rule (on by default, so nothing stays in the corpse that could be stored); with the rule off the item goes
  to the backpack (and the bags in it, capacity checked, never an equipment slot), else it stays in the corpse. Without the
  specialist pouch in the inventory, the Loot Bag rules decide as for any other item (an orb on the autoloot list, a gem with
  the gems rule). Every other item goes to the Loot Bag when its rules want it, else it is left to the base autoloot; a full
  Loot Bag passes it to the backpack, then the corpse. Click-to-loot in the loot channel (`lootfilter.lua` take ->
  `ChaosPouches.stow`) follows the same plan, then the backpack. Picking up an item through its ground label (`game_groundlabels`)
  is the normal move into the backpack and does not route into pouches. Gear is rolled on the way out
  (`ChaosLoot.finalizeRarity`). Containers and pouches are never collected. Only the corpse owner's pouches collect, as the base
  autoloot (party members do not loot each other's corpses here). The pouch line (`MESSAGE_LOOT`) ends the kill's one loot line ("One loot line
  per kill" below; its own line only without `lootline.lua`). It lists what was taken, not the pouch (owner 2026-10-16): "Looted: {[Legendary] wyrmscale helmet}, 10 gold coins, 2 dragon
  scales (Orbs Pouch is full; 3 to your Loot Bag; 1 to your backpack)." (`ChaosPouchesCore.lootList` / `summary`). Grouped
  by item (id, rarity, unique), plural names for counts, uniques and rarity gear first with the rarity tag; from Rare
  (`lootLine.flagRarity` 3) and uniques wrapped in `{}` (the client's loot highlight, as the Chaos bonus loot line); at most
  `lootLine.maxEntries` (5) entries, then "and N more". Pouch names appear only in the short notes ("is full" at most once
  a minute per pouch; "to your Loot Bag" counts the overflow). No loot message option exists to respect.
- **Loot Bag rules** (storage 7100107, one packed value; unset = the defaults above; window: right-click the Loot Bag > "Pouch settings", or the Loot
  Filter's "Loot Bag" button; extended opcode 226 `ChaosOpcodes.pouches`): items on the autoloot list, gold / platinum /
  crystal coins, uniques, gear with a rarity of at least N (1 = all gear, plain pieces too), supplies (potions, runes, ammunition, food), gems (when the character
  carries no Orbs Pouch), everything else, and overflow (what a full Orbs or Rift Key Pouch passes on; default on; stored as an
  inverted bit, 128 set = off, so rules saved before the rule existed read it as on). Item categories are the loot filter's (`ChaosLootFilter.itemInfo`). The Loot Filter's
  Rarity Autoloot minimum still holds list gear back (its snapshot runs first).
- **Store-bound.** Bought pouches arrive in the purse ("Store", Delivery to the purse) and collect there: `PO.carried`
  looks through the inventory (its bags, breadth first) and then the purse one level deep (a pouch lying directly in
  the purse; not one inside a bag in the purse; the inventory's pouch first when there are two). Weight rules are
  unchanged: the purse counts in the inventory weight, so what a pouch there takes counts as in the backpack (the
  Loot Bag stays weightless). A pouch in the depot inbox does not collect. One of each kind per character: the store refuses a second while one is in the inventory, the purse, the inbox or a depot
  chest (and while a lost one is owed back); a copy made by a GM collects only when it carries the character's guid
  (`chaos_pouch_owner`) and only the first one found is used. Every pouch has the custom attributes `chaos_storebound = 1` and
  `chaos_locked = 2` (`bindLock`; the item lock, engine patch 0009: no NPC buys it, trash holders refuse it, the stock market
  does not list it; no NPC lists the new ids anyway). Not 1: the client draws 1, a player's own lock, grey (`game_shaderfx`),
  and the pouches showed grey in the backpack and the purse (owner report 2026-10-22). Pouches of before get 2 at login
  (`ChaosPouches.rebind`: inventory, purse, inbox, depots; tested in `pouches_test.lua`). `Player:onMoveItem` (a hook `install_pouches.py` writes at its top, because only the last
  `onMoveItem` callback's value counts) keeps a pouch, or any container holding one, in the character's own inventory or depot
  (lockers, depot chest, depot boxes): the ground, a mailbox, trash, a house or corpse container and another player's container are
  refused ("Store items stay with you ..."); a pouch never goes into another pouch. The trade window refuses it
  (`onTradeRequest` / `onTradeAccept` callbacks; `patch_season_events.py` enables those events). Player market: it asks
  `ChaosPouches.isPouch(item)` / the attribute `chaos_storebound`.
- **Death** (`death_keep.lua`, `death_keep_core.lua`; `tests/death_keep_test.lua`, `tools/death_keep_patch_test.py`). The
  engine decides what drops (blessings, the amulet of loss, skulls as usual). Live test 2026-10-14: a death on shallow water
  lost the Loot Bag and the Everfull Ration. The stock `droploot.lua` moves each dropped slot item into the corpse and removes
  it when that fails, and a tile that cannot hold a corpse (water) has none. `patch_base_events.py` step 15 makes it ask
  `ChaosDeathKeep.beforeDrop(player, item, corpse)` first: every store-bound item (attribute `chaos_storebound`: the pouches,
  the Everfull Ration, the nemesis trophy; any copy of a pouch or ration item) leaves the dropping container for the
  character's inbox (attribute `chaos_death_kept`), its own contents stay in the drop; a store-bound item worn in a slot stays
  there (its contents drop). At the next login a marked item moves to the backpack when it fits, else it stays in the inbox:
  "Kept through your death: your Loot bag, Everfull ration (backpack)." (pt-BR too). So a store item is never lost and never
  looted by a killer, with or without a corpse, and it does not protect its contents. Fallback without the hook: the pouch
  leaves the corpse a moment later (`onDeath` + `addEvent`) and comes back, empty, at the next login (storage 7100109).
- **Former Bottomless Loot Pouch owners** (storage 7100100 = 1) get a Loot Bag for free at their next login, once (storage
  7100108), backpack or inbox, with a short message.
- **Tooltip.** The rich item tooltip shows "Store item: cannot be traded" and what the pouch collects (`item_tooltip_core.lua` asks
  `ChaosPouches.tooltipLines`); the look text is the items.xml description.
- `server/tests/pouches_test.lua` (LuaJIT and Lua 5.3, mocked engine): rule packing (overflow default on, old values), routing per
  pouch, the priority plan (specialist first whatever the Loot Bag rules, overflow on / off, a pouch not carried), the drop step
  (right pouch, stacking, key attributes kept, full Orbs Pouch -> Loot Bag overflow or backpack -> corpse, a gem with the gems
  rule still to the Orbs Pouch, capacity, owner only, carried only, a pouch in the purse collects, one level deep only, the backpack's first), the defaults (all the loot: plain gear, supplies,
  creature products), the weightless registration (installed kinds only, once), the window protocol, click-to-loot (same priority), never
  auto-sold, the store (one per character, delivered to the purse, depot inbox without purse or capacity, attributes), move / trade refusals, death and the login grants. Client: `game_pouches/pouchesview_test.lua`, `game_itemtooltip/tooltiplogic_test.lua`.
- Live test 2026-10-14 (engine 0001-0038): five kills filled the Loot Bag with all their loot and the free capacity did
  not change (weightless); Sell all sold to the bank, kept a unique, a named item and an Epic copy (Epic unticked), the
  30 s cooldown on the button and on the server. Found there: plain gear drops were kept as "named" (any custom
  attribute counted, and every gear drop has an item level: `ChaosAutoSell.OWN_CUSTOM` now); the Loot Bag and the
  Everfull Ration in a backpack overflowed the client's Lua stack (game_shaderfx); the Everfull Ration broke every packet
  that showed it (not stackable on the server, stackable look in the client). Death: a death on land gave both back at
  the next login; after a death on a shallow water tile no corpse was found there and the pouch and the ration did not come back
  (an open question, not investigated further).
- Verified in game (test server copy, screenshots in the session scratchpad `pouches/shots`): the three offers with icons; buying
  all three (into the backpack) and the refusal of a second Loot Bag; a kill whose corpse held orbs, a whetstone, a gem, rune
  shards, a Rift Key, omen fragments, gold and autoloot-list gear filled the right pouches (the key kept its tier and modifiers,
  the gear its rarity); the Loot Bag rules from the window (gear of rarity Rare+ taken, Uncommon left); a full Orbs Pouch sent an
  orb to the backpack, with the backpack full too it stayed in the corpse; the tooltip; "Pouch settings" in the right-click menu
  and the Loot Filter button; the trade window and dropping a pouch or the backpack holding it on the ground refused; a death
  without blessings dropped the backpack, the pouches left the corpse with their contents in it, and came back empty at the
  next login; a former Bottomless Loot Pouch owner got the free Loot Bag (inbox) at login. Not tested in game: the mailbox and
  house paths (the move rule is the same as for the ground), selling to an NPC (the lock and the missing NPC price), the depot.
- Verified in game for the new looks and the priority (client with the new pair, screenshots in the session scratchpad
  `pouchlook/`): the three pouches next to the three stock bags in a bag, the store offers and the container window icons with the
  new looks (existing pouches updated by the install); a kill with two gems, a Rift Key, omen fragments, an orb, gold and Rare
  gear with the Loot Bag gems rule on: gems and orb to the Orbs Pouch, key and fragments to the Rift Key Pouch, gold and gear to
  the Loot Bag; with the Orbs Pouch full a new orb overflowed into the Loot Bag ("Orbs Pouch is full; 3 to your Loot Bag");
  with overflow off the next orb went to the backpack; click-to-loot (`ChaosPouches.stow`) refused the Loot Bag with overflow off
  and used it with overflow on; the overflow checkbox saved on the server both ways.

## Store pouches and the Everfull Ration (`store_food.lua`, `store_food_core.lua`, `store_food_config.lua`, `tools/install_store_food.py`)

The store's infinite food (Convenience, "Everfull Ration", 100 coins, decided 2026-10-14, docs/PRICES.md).

- **Item.** Server id 32084 (after the pouches), a new items.otb node copied from the stock dragon ham (2672: flags and
  attributes), stackable like it, with an items.xml entry (name, description, weight 3 oz). Stackable because its look
  is a stackable client thing (the dragon ham, and our art made with its flags): the 10.98 protocol writes a count byte
  for such an item, and the first version (not stackable, no count) broke every packet that showed the ration ("parse
  message exception ... opcode 0x6e" when a backpack holding it opened; live test 2026-10-14). One ration a character,
  count 1; `install_store_food.py` updates an older node in place. Installed by
  `tools/install_store_food.py` (step `storefood` of `install_all.py`, after `pouches`; idempotent; `items.otb.bak` keeps
  the original; `tools/install_store_food_test.py` on a synthetic items.otb). Look: `ownLook = true` in
  `store_food_config.lua` (on since 2026-10-14: things_custom25 is on windows-assets at ebe1b2b2; run
  `install_store_food.py` again; false gives back the dragon ham's look) gives it client id 38611 of pair 34: a glazed bowl
  with a roast haunch and gold sparks, drawn by `client/tools/sprites/gen_store_food_art.py` (the store pouches' helpers;
  32 px, deterministic) into `art_import/store_food.png`, snapped to the cinderwrought palette by `gen_store_items_art.py`
  and appended with `art_import/store_items.csv` by `import_art_things.py` (client MANIFEST.md "Store item looks"; the
  earlier look 33904, `oldClientId`, is replaced in place). The store icon is the item, so it follows the look.
- **Eating.** Use it like food: one bite is the best stock food (60 x 12 s = 720 s of regeneration, the dragon ham, marlin
  and roasted meat of the base `food.lua`), "You are full." at the cap every food has (1200 s of regeneration), so it is
  eaten exactly as often as normal food; one bite a second at most (`exhaustMs`). Never used up. Only its owner can eat
  from it ("This ration belongs to someone else.").
- **Delivered to the purse** ("Store", Delivery to the purse; depot inbox without a purse or the capacity).
- **Store-bound** like the pouches (the store's convention for a permanent item): one per character (the store refuses a
  second while one is in the inventory, the inbox or a depot), the custom attributes `chaos_food_owner`, `chaos_storebound`
  and `chaos_locked = 2` (`bindLock`: locked, but not drawn grey; a ration of before gets 2 at login, `ChaosStoreFood.rebind`). The pouches' move hook, trade callbacks and the player market refuse any `chaos_storebound` item, so
  it cannot be dropped, mailed, traded or sold (the refusal text now says "Store items ..."). A service offer, so never
  giftable. Not for season characters (the Convenience category is refused there).
- **Death.** Kept out of the drop like the pouches (`death_keep.lua`, see "Store pouches", Death). Fallback without that
  hook: a ration dropped with the backpack leaves the corpse and comes back at the next login (storage 7100151, written
  to the database); the store refuses a second one meanwhile.
- **Tests:** `tests/store_food_test.lua` (the bite, the cap, the exhaust, owner only, never used up, the store check, the
  offer, delivery to the backpack or the inbox, death and the login), `tools/install_store_food_test.py`.

## Potions (`potions.lua`, `potions_core.lua`, `potions_config.lua`, `data/lib/chaos_potions.lua`, `tools/install_potions.py`)

Owner request 2026-10-16: "Remove the potion flasks and make the first pots infinite."
