- **No empty flasks.** No potion leaves an empty flask any more (strong 7634, great 7635, small 7636). The stock potion
  script (`data/actions/scripts/other/potions.lua`, `player:addItem(potion.flask, 1)`) and any other base Lua that adds a
  flask (an `addItem` / `createItem` / `doPlayerAddItem` call with an argument named like `flask` or a flask id) get that
  statement commented out (marker "Chaos: no potion flasks"; inside a longer expression the call becomes `nil`). This
  covers every stock tier, the spirit and the fork's herbalist potions (exalted, advanced, divine, mythic).
- **No deposit.** No NPC sells a flask (shop_buyable entries removed, `addBuyableItem` lines commented out, the `buy` of a
  `{id = ..., buy = ...}` row removed). A text about a flask deposit (it says "deposit" and names a flask, vial or potion:
  NPC dialogue, keyword replies, script messages, the flask descriptions in items.xml) loses its deposit and flask
  sentences, or becomes `flaskText` ("Potions no longer leave an empty flask. A potion store still buys old flasks.").
- **Open potions** (owner 2026-10-24: "let every class use any type of potion", ROADMAP O175). `tools/patch_open_potions.py`
  (install step `openpotions`, after `vocations`) removes the `vocations = {...}` list of every health, mana and spirit
  entry of the base `data/actions/scripts/other/potions.lua`, so no class is refused; the refusal text of the entry becomes
  "Only characters of level N or above may drink this fluid." and the Look text in `items.xml` "This potion can be consumed by
  characters of level N or higher." **The level gates stay** (50 strong, 80 great and great spirit, 130 ultimate, 200
  supreme; the base file has its own for the later tiers): they keep a low character off the strongest potions, and the
  Apothecary refuses a buyer below them too. The buff potions (berserk, mastermind, bullseye: a condition, no heal) keep their
  lists, as does `strengthening_potions.lua`. `add_vocations.py` only appends to a list that exists, so its re-run brings
  nothing back. Tests: `tools/patch_open_potions_test.py`; `tests/potions_patch_test.lua` runs the patched script on a mock
  engine and checks that every vocation id (0-25: the stock ones, Thief, Ninja, Samurai, Necromancer, Lich, Templar and the
  rest) drinks every healing potion. The helper client lists all of them (`helper_potions.lua`).
- **Everfull upgrades (O245).** She also gives the Everfull flask tiers: ask her about an {upgrade} (the task: 40 stock potions of the
  tier plus the previous flask, the level of the stock potion) or a {lost} flask. Nothing is added to her trade window. README "Potions",
  "Higher tiers".
- **Old flasks keep their value.** Nothing removes the flasks players hold. The NPCs' `shop_sellable` entries stay and
  the Loot Buyer and the Auto Seller still pay the old 5 gold each (`sell_prices.lua`), so nobody loses gold. No source
  creates new ones.
- **Everfull potions.** The lowest tier of health and mana potion (the stock Health Potion 7618 and Mana Potion 7620, level
  1, every class) has an Everfull copy: **everfull health potion 32085** (125-175 health) and **everfull mana potion
  32086** (75-125 mana), the rolls of the stock potions. New items.otb nodes copied from 7618 / 7620 (flags, attributes,
  the stock look), stackable like them for the same reason as the Everfull Ration (count 1, never used up), items.xml
  entries "A flask that never empties. ..." (the item tooltip shows them). No spirit potion at tier 1: the first one is the great spirit
  potion (level 80, a higher tier below); the hybrid classes start on health and mana potions too (docs/CLASSES.md, `newplayer_config.lua`).
- **Drinking.** On yourself or another player like the stock potion (not on a monster or an NPC). Never used up, no flask.
  The health and the mana potion each have their own wait (the action interval - 100 ms = 900 ms, a per-player timer in
  `potions.lua`; owner 2026-10-17: a mana potion after a health potion said "You are exhausted."), so each is no faster
  than a stack of stock potions and no `CONDITION_EXHAUST_HEAL` is added. "You are exhausted." for the same kind. Higher
  tiers stay consumables: they are the gold sink.
- **Hotkeys and the action bar** (engine patch 0043, playtest 2026-10-16): the client uses a potion from its action bar,
  hotkeys and helper by client id, and the engine maps 266 / 268 to the stock 7618 / 7620. So a hotkey drinks the stock
  potions first (consumed) and, without 0043, answered "Sorry, not possible." once none were left, with the Everfull
  potion in the backpack. With 0043 a hotkey first looks for a carried item of that look that is never used up
  (stackable and store-bound, `chaos_storebound`: the Everfull potion), so the free potion is drunk before the stock
  ones; then the stock type; then any item of that look. The hotkey message of such an item no longer counts it
  ("Using the last everfull health potion...", always one): "Using an everfull health potion (never runs out)." Using
  the Everfull potion from its container slot always drinks it. `tools/hotkey_lookup_patch_test.py`.
- **Store-bound** like the Everfull Ration: `chaos_storebound` and `chaos_locked`, so no trade, ground, mail, market, NPC
  sale or trash (pouches.lua, engine patch 0009), and `death_keep.lua` keeps it on death. The lock value is
  `bindLock` = 2, not 1 (live screenshot 2026-10-16: the Everfull potions showed as black, empty-looking flasks in the
  backpack while the stock ones looked right). Cause: not the look (items.otb gives 32085 / 32086 the stock client ids
  266 / 268, stackable like them, one look per count; `check_item_wire.py` agrees on both), but the client's
  `game_shaderfx`, which draws every item with lock attribute 3 > 0 grey, and a grey red flask reads as a black one. The
  client now greys only a player's own lock (1, the crafting bench's Lock button); every server and engine check treats
  any value but 0 as locked, so 2 stays bound. Potions given before get 2 at their owner's next login
  (`ChaosPotions.rebind`, sent again to the client). Beta 2026-10-20: still grey, because patch 0003 sent key 3 as 1 for any
  lock value, so the client never saw the 2; engine patch `0050-item-lock-value-on-wire` sends the value (needs a new
  engine build). Patch 0043's hotkey lookup goes by client id and `chaos_storebound`
  and is unchanged. `tests/potions_test.lua`, client `game_shaderfx/shaderfx_test.lua`.
- **Sources.** The starter kit, its wearable part on arrival at the tutorial island (`newplayer.lua` calls
  `ChaosPotions.giveAll` into the kit backpack; the only starting potions, no kit carries stock potions); a one-time grant at
  login for characters made before (storage 7102480 = 1 once given; a brand-new character waits for its kit); and the Veyra
  quests below (O273: no NPC sells an Everfull potion any more; `install_potions.py` removes the entries it added before from the
  trade window of every NPC and takes the `ShopModule` hook out of `modules.lua`, once, idempotent).
- **Existing stock potions stay consumables.** Stacks of Health / Mana Potions are not converted: monsters, NPCs, the
  mentor shop and the milestone gifts still hand them out, so a login conversion would fight every source. They are
  still drunk and used up as before, and still sell to NPCs. The Everfull copies sit next to them.
- **Amount: fixed + percent** (owner 2026-10-22: "quanto mais lvl o personagem tem, menos as pots healam. façam elas
  healarem uma quantidade fixa + uma porcentagem. e elas também são afetadas por healing da skill tree"). Every health and
  mana potion gives its own roll (the fixed part) + a percent of the target's maximum health or mana: 3% + 0.01% per
  level the potion needs, at most 10% (`potions_config.lua` `amount`; health potion 3%, great 3.8%, ultimate 4.3%,
  level 200 5%, 500 8%, 700 10%). **Everfull potions** (owner 2026-10-25: "faça as everfull recuperar um fixo + uma
  porcentagem") take the percent from their tier instead, at any character level: tier 1 6%, 2 8%, 3 10%, 4 12%
  (`amount.everfullPct`; a spirit potion gives it on health and on mana). The tree's Healing (`incrementHealth`) raises both: health through the heal event like
  every heal, mana in `ChaosPotions.amount` from the drinker's storage 7102481 (the tree writes it at every rebuild;
  the potion script runs in the actions' Lua state). `install_potions.py` rewrites the stock script's two
  `doTargetCombat(... potion.health[1], potion.health[2])` calls (marker "Chaos: potion amount", a loader line on top;
  it falls back to the stock roll when the library cannot load); the Everfull potions use the same rule. Tests:
  `tests/potions_test.lua`, `tools/install_potions_test.py`.
- **The Everfull potions never empty (O273).** Owner 2026-10-27: "retire as everfull da veyra. retire tambem as cargas delas. deixe-as
  ilimitadas mesmo." The charges of O242 are gone: a drink never spends or needs a charge, a kill and the temple refill nothing, and
  there is no empty-flask fallback to a stock potion. What stays: the level gate of the tier and the wait of each pool (the health
  pool, the mana pool, a spirit flask both), so a flask is no faster than a stack of stock potions. The amount of a drink is
  unchanged (the roll plus `amount.everfullPct`, 6 / 8 / 10 / 12 percent of the maximum). **Not rebalanced:** the percents were set
  when a flask held 5 to 8 charges; with unlimited drinks the wait and the 1 s potion cooldown (patch 0042) are the only limit.
  Nothing was measured on the live game; tune `amount.everfullPct` in `potions_config.lua` if the owner finds it too strong.
  - **Removed:** `potion_flasks.lua` (the kill and temple events, now a comment-only stub so an installed copy loads nothing), the
    charge functions of `potions_core.lua` and `chaos_potions.lua`, the "Charges: x/y" look line, the drink and refill messages,
    the passive tree hooks of `passivetree_effects.lua`, and `flask` in `potions_config.lua`. Storage 7102482 .. 7102485 is retired
    (README "Storage keys"); a value a character still has is never read and does no harm.
  - **The tree nodes 669-672** (O251) gave charges. They keep their place, name and art ("Bottomless Flasks" is still the notable) and
    now give vitality and spirit: 669 and 671 +1 spirit, 670 +1 vitality, 672 +2 vitality and +2 spirit. Points already spent stay
    valid. The stats `flaskMaxCharges` and `flaskChargeGain` no longer exist (config, texts, pt-BR).
  - **`ready` of the held message** (opcode 116) is always true now; the client still reads it, so an older server that says false
    keeps working.
- **Higher tiers (O245).** Owner 2026-10-25: "Podemos vender everfull potion na store ou em quests também" (can we sell Everfull
  potions in the store, or give them through quests too). Seven more Everfull items, copies of the stock potions' nodes
  (`install_potions.py`, server ids **32261-32267**, the range the lead set aside: 32087-32100 belong to other work), each with
  the stock potion's roll and level and the same "fixed + percent of the maximum" amount (percent by the tier, `amount.everfullPct`):

  | Id | Item | Stock potion | Level | Roll | Made from |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 32261 | everfull great health potion | 7591 | 80 | 425-575 health | 32085 |
  | 32262 | everfull great mana potion | 7590 | 80 | 150-250 mana | 32086 |
  | 32263 | everfull great spirit potion | 8472 | 80 | 250-350 health, 100-200 mana | 32085 |
  | 32264 | everfull ultimate health potion | 8473 | 130 | 650-850 health | 32261 |
  | 32265 | everfull ultimate mana potion | 26029 | 130 | 425-575 mana | 32262 |
  | 32266 | everfull ultimate spirit potion | 26030 | 130 | 420-580 health, 200-350 mana | 32263 |
  | 32267 | everfull supreme health potion | 26031 | 200 | 875-1125 health | 32264 |

  Rolls and levels are the base server's `data/actions/scripts/other/potions.lua`. Its comments call 26030 "supreme spirit" and
  26031 "ultimate health"; this repository's names (the Apothecary table above, the store packs) are the real game's: 26030 ultimate
  spirit, 26031 supreme health. The classes are all open to every potion since O175, so the spirit line is a choice of any class,
  not a hybrid-only item. The hybrid classes (Rangers and the like) are who it suits: it heals and restores mana in one key.
  - **A slot, not a tier.** A character holds ONE Everfull item per slot: health (the health line and the spirit line) and mana.
    An upgrade replaces the item with the next tier of its line; the old item is removed, the new one is store-bound and locked
    with the old item's `chaos_storebound` / `chaos_locked` values (a lock of 1, the client's grey, becomes the bind value 2). The
    health slot has two lines from tier 1: health (great 32261, ultimate 32264, supreme 32267) and spirit (great 32263, ultimate
    32266). The choice is made at level 80 and the lines never cross (`from` in the config; a spirit flask cannot become a health
    flask: there is no downgrade, and `K.upgradeCheck` says "needs a different flask").
  - **Pools are waits.** `pools = {"health", "mana"}`: one wait per kind and player, never per tier or item (`lastDrink`, forgotten at
    logout). An upgrade does not touch them. A health flask waits on the health pool, a mana flask on the mana pool, a spirit flask on both.
  - **Spirit and double dipping.** A spirit potion heals health and mana in one drink and waits on BOTH pools (`K.drink`), so it is no
    faster than a health drink plus a mana drink, and holding a spirit flask next to the mana flask gives no second source: the
    slot rule allows one Everfull item per slot, and the mana slot's wait is shared. Nothing is spent.
  - **Level.** Each tier keeps the stock potion's level: a drink below it is refused ("Only characters of level N or above may
    drink this fluid", the stock script's text), and the upgrade is refused below it (both ways).
  - **The quest: Veyra the Apothecary** (`data/npc/scripts/veyra_the_apothecary.lua`; no new NPC, no opcode). Ask her about an
    {upgrade} (also {everfull}, {task}). She lists what the previous tier the character holds can become and what it needs:
    **40 stock potions of the tier** (`upgrade.materials`; the stock potion of the item, in the backpack, 40 great health potions
    for 32261 and so on), the flask in the backpack, inbox, store purse or a depot, and the level. The materials are loot and
    purchases, so the task is a gold sink at her prices (docs/PRICES.md); a character with a choice (health or spirit at level 80)
    says which. {yes} does it. The same code runs again at {yes}, nothing is trusted from the first answer. Anybody can say any
    words; the only inputs are the NPC's keywords and a word match, and an unknown word does nothing.
  - **The store sells the same swap.** `{kind = "service", service = "everfullUpgrade", upgrade = <id>, cost = coins}` in
    Consumables > Everfull Potions (`shop_config.lua`; Convenience until O286, where the last four were on page 2), registered into `ChaosShopServices.services` by `potions.lua` (as the Ration). 30
    coins for the great tier, 50 the ultimate, 70 the supreme (`upgrade.coins`; a spirit or health line costs 150 coins in all, the
    limit is 200). The same `ChaosPotions.upgrade(player, id, "store")` as the task, minus the materials, with the same level
    gate, previous tier and once per tier. Pay to skip: it gives exactly what the task gives and nothing beyond (no better roll). The offer key includes the tier (`shop_core.lua`), services are not giftable, and the service checks that the
    offer's cost is the config's (`K.upgradeCoins`) before it does anything.
  - **Atomic, no duplicates.** `ChaosPotions.upgrade`: check everything (`K.upgradeCheck`: tier known and installed, not done, the
    ONE Everfull item of the slot is the tier's `from`, level, materials) -> place the new item (no room: nothing changed) -> take the
    materials -> set the tier's flag (7102510 + n) -> remove the old item. An error or a refusal anywhere undoes what was done (the
    new item removed, the flag cleared, the materials given back); everything runs in one call, so a double click finds the swap done
    (flag set, old item gone) and is refused. The store takes coins before `apply` and refunds on any result but `true`
    (`shop.lua`), and `apply` changes nothing unless it returns true. Paths that could duplicate a flask: trade, mail, the market,
    the trash and the ground are refused for any `chaos_storebound` item (pouches.lua, engine patch 0009); death keeps it
    (`death_keep.lua`); a relog changes nothing (the flags are storage); the stash is not used. A character
    that holds two Everfull items of a slot (a GM gift, an old copy) is refused ("Keep only one"), never a third. The starter
    kit and the login grant (`PT.giveAll`) check the SLOT, not the id: an upgraded character is never given a starting flask next to its
    great one. A restore ({lost}) checks the slot too.
  - **Where the previous tier may be.** Equipped or in any backpack, the store purse, the inbox or a depot chest (`PT.everfullItems`
    walks them). Anywhere else (the floor, another player's container) it is not found and the swap is refused with "Carry your
    Everfull potion in your backpack, your inbox or a depot".
  - **A lost flask.** Flasks are bound and kept through death, so this should not happen (a GM delete, a bug). A character that
    earned a tier and holds no Everfull item of that slot says {lost} / {restore} to Veyra: she gives back the highest tier it earned
    in that slot for `price` gold (the task's materials at her prices). Tier 1 is restorable the same way (it was
    only sold before O273), so a character that lost its starting flask has a path back.
  - **Not sold anywhere.** No NPC trade window lists an Everfull potion (O273); the ids are marked `bound`
    in the item price table (no NPC pays for them), listed by the item finder (source "Veyra the Apothecary": the starter kit for tier 1, her upgrade quest and the store service for the rest),
    and have the potion cooldown channel like the others (`cooldown_channels.lua` reads the config). The engine's hotkey patch (0043)
    finds them by their look like the first two.
  - **The helper and the tiers (O246).** Owner 2026-10-25: "Lembre de colocar as everfull no helper tambem". How a drink reaches the
    Everfull: the client uses an inventory item BY CLIENT ID and the engine maps it to one server type, the stock potion. Patch 0043
    (`Game::internalGetThing`) therefore tries first a carried item of that look that is never used up (stackable and
    `chaos_storebound`), then the mapped type, then any item of the look: a use of look 239 drinks the Everfull great health
    potion before a stock one, a use of 266 the tier 1 flask (this already held for the tiers 2-4, which copy the stock node). What
    was broken for the helper: after an upgrade nothing carries look 266 / 268 any more, so the helper's Health / Mana Potion rows
    (and Auto setup's fallback) drank stock potions or got "Sorry, not possible.", and the flask was never used. The client cannot
    see the tier (a closed backpack is not counted, and the look is the stock potion's), so the server tells it:
    `ChaosPotions.heldView` (`potions_core.lua` `heldView`/`heldKey`/`heldPayload`, tested in `tests/potions_helper_test.lua`)
    reads `Player:getItemCount` of the nine ids (inventory and backpacks, the places the use by look searches; not the inbox, the
    purse or the depots) and `ItemType:getClientId`, and `potions_helper.lua` sends opcode **116** (`held`, per
    slot `{look, tier, level, line, ready}`; free in the "Opcode collision check", listed in the opcode table) at login (after 1.5 s),
    after an upgrade, on the client's `sync` (one a second) and from a 3 s think when the view changed (an item moved), never otherwise. `ready` is always true since O273 (it was false for an empty flask). The client (`helper_potions.lua` `P.resolve`) lets a Health / Mana Potion row follow a ready, plain, allowed
    Everfull of its slot; any other row keeps its look (the engine prefers the Everfull of that look). Spirit
    flasks are chosen by a spirit row only. Auto setup counts the carried Everfull as carried. **Smallest design:** no engine change
    and no new client input (`sync` reads nothing); the engine's drink already checks the level, so a client that lies
    about a tier gets at most what it carries. **Audit:** the use finds only items the character carries; the level
    is checked in `K.drink` from the character, not from the client; the per-pool wait table `lastDrink` was never cleaned (now forgotten at logout). **Unique looks later:** when the nine
    get client ids of their own, the held message already carries the real look; change `look` in the client table
    `EVERFULL_ITEMS`, and then patch 0043's look preference, the follow rule for the 266 / 268 rows
    is no longer needed (the use of a look maps to one server id).
    Auto setup (owner 2026-10-27, "o auto setup nao coloca as everfull"): it also counts the flasks seen by their own O247 looks in open containers (for a slot the message says nothing about), asks `sync` and waits 0.6 s when no message has arrived yet, sets a row on the flask's own look when the row cannot follow it, and the potion and rune dropdowns of the helper are sorted alphabetically (`ChaosHelperPotions.sortOptions`).
  - **Install:** the same step `potions` (nine nodes now; twelve since O247). New: the `tier` of each row, the store offers; no seller since O273.
  - **Texts:** English keys, pt-BR in `i18n_strings.lua` ("Everfull potion tiers"). The item descriptions are in items.xml.
  - **Not done / risks:** the new
    looks were the stock great, ultimate and supreme potions' (own art since O247, below). The levels and rolls of the stock potions are read from the
    base `potions.lua` here; the names of 26029-26031 are the real game's. Prices are a first estimate (`store_model.lua`), nothing
    is measured on a running server and the whole path is only tested on a mocked engine.
- **Own art and four tiers a line (O247).** Owner 2026-10-25: the Everfull potions get art of their own, and every line gets four
  tiers. **Art:** twelve PixelLab 32 x 32 flasks, client items **38645-38656** of pair 44 (client/MANIFEST.md "Everfull potion
  looks"; `gen_everfull_art.py`, `art_import/everfull*`), one phase, stackable like the stock potions (flags copied from them; the
  ANIMATION flag is cleared on the nodes, because the server sends a phase byte for it and the art has one phase).
  `potions_config.lua` gives every entry a `clientId`; `install_potions.py` writes it into the node (new and existing nodes: a
  re-run on a server installed before O247 moves the nine flasks to their new looks). **Three new items** (server ids 32268-32270,
  nodes copied from stock nodes by `sourceId`, flags 7102517-7102519 appended last so the nine flags of O245 keep their place):

  | Id | Item | Client | Level | Roll | Made from | Veyra's task | Coins |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 32268 | everfull spirit potion (spirit tier 1) | 38653 | 0 | 75-105 health, 45-75 mana | 32085 | 40 health potions (7618) | 20 |
  | 32269 | everfull supreme mana potion | 38652 | 200 | 575-775 mana | 32265 | 60 ultimate mana potions (26029) | 70 |
  | 32270 | everfull supreme spirit potion | 38656 | 200 | 560-760 health, 275-475 mana | 32266 | 60 ultimate spirit potions (26030) | 70 |

  The spirit rolls are about 60% of the health and mana rolls of the same tier, as in the lines of O245; supreme mana sits above
  ultimate mana by the factor supreme health sits above ultimate health. **The chain:** health 32085 -> 32261 -> 32264 -> 32267;
  mana 32086 -> 32262 -> 32265 -> 32269; spirit 32085 -> 32268 -> 32263 -> 32266 -> 32270. So the spirit line now starts at tier 1
  (from the health flask of tier 1, level 0, 20 coins) and great spirit is made from it; there is no stock potion for the tier
  1 or the supreme mana and spirit tiers, so those entries name their own task potions (`materialId`, `materialCount`,
  `materialName`; `K.materialOf` falls back to the stock potion and the standard 40). Level gates 0 / 80 / 130 / 200. The store offers
  one swap per upgrade (ten) at 20 / 30 / 50 / 70 coins by tier; a whole line stays under 200 coins (`store_model.lua --check`,
  docs/PRICES.md). **Helper:** `EVERFULL_ITEMS` in `helper_potions.lua` has the twelve own looks; the rows on the stock 266 / 268
  looks keep the follow rule, and an Everfull look appears in the dropdown (engine patch 0043 stays). **Ship order:** pair 44
  and a client build FIRST (older clients draw nothing for the new client ids), then `install_potions.py` (step `potions`).
  Tests: `tests/potions_test.lua`, `tests/veyra_upgrade_test.lua`, `tests/potions_helper_test.lua`, `tools/install_potions_test.py`,
  `gen_everfull_art_test.py`.
- **Install:** `tools/install_potions.py DATA_DIR [--dry-run]` (step `potions` of `install_all.py`, after `runes`, before
  `itemprices`; idempotent; `items.otb.bak` keeps the original; it also removes the Everfull shop entries and the ShopModule hook
  an earlier run added, and warns about a hook it does not know). `tools/gen_item_prices.py` marks both ids `bound` (never priced).
- **Tests:** `tests/potions_test.lua` (the rules and the O245 tiers: config, check rules, swap, rollbacks, store service; drinking on a mocked engine: healed, not consumed, no flask, the exhaust;
  the kit and login grant; the restore; the stock potions.lua patched by the tool: no flask, a higher tier still
  used up, the exhaust unchanged), `tools/install_potions_test.py` (a synthetic base server: items, NPCs, the old
  entries and hook removed, idempotent).

## Stash (`stash.lua`, `stash_core.lua`, `stash_config.lua`, `item_codec.lua`, `sql/chaos_stash.sql`, `tools/migrate_depot_stash.py`, client `game_stash`)

**Reversed again 2026-10-17 (later)** (owner: "remova o depot e deixe só o stash", "quando a gente abrir o baú, abra o stash"): the stash is the one
storage. `stash_config.lua` has `depot.migrate = true`, `depot.withdrawOnly = true` and `toDepot.enabled = false` (the stash -> depot
migration below stays in the code, off). The chest still lists what is left to take out.

**Locker opens the depot only (2026-10-20)** (owner beta report: clicking a depot chest opened the depot window and the stash
window together). A depot locker opens the depot window alone and shows the withdraw-only line. The stash opens from its own
entry points: the top bar (Economy > Supply Stash), the "Toggle Stash" keybind and the stash keeper NPC. `depot.lua` `afterOpen`
asks `depot_core.lua` `D.lockerOpen`; it calls `ChaosStash.openWindow` (a `Toggle` with `open = true`) only when
`stash_config.lua` `depot.openStash = true` (off). Tests: `depot_test.lua` (the rule and a locker opening on the mocked engine).

**Reversed 2026-10-17** (owner: "Depot e stash estão iguais: migrar o stash para o depot"): the depot is the one storage again.
`stash_config.lua` `toDepot` (enabled): when a depot locker is opened, `ChaosStash.migrateToDepot` moves the character's stash
entries into the open depot tabs with room (`ChaosDepot.slots`), once per character (storage 7100013, version in
`toDepot.version`), at most `toDepot.batch` (40) entries per opening, plain stacks as stacks of `toDepot.stackSize` (100), stored
items made again with every attribute. It runs every entry through the stash journal (`K.withdraw` with a depot box as the
destination), so a crash or a failed save puts the entry back: no item lost, none doubled. What does not fit (the open tabs are
full: with one free tab that is likely) stays in the stash, withdraw-only, and the player is told how many entries remain. The
stash window stays as a thin view of that leftover: deposits are closed (window drop, Stow Everything, `ChaosStash.storeItem`;
the `tabs` message carries `closed = true`, the client greys the deposit out), withdrawals work as before. The depot is no longer
withdraw-only (`depot.withdrawOnly = false`) and no longer moves into the stash (`depot.migrate = false`); the migration waits for a
locker opening because the engine saves the depot only then. Rollback: `toDepot.enabled = false`, `depot.migrate = true`,
`depot.withdrawOnly = true`. The text below describes the stash as built on 2026-10-15.

The owner's decision (2026-10-15, reversed above): the stash is the one item storage of a character; the per-character depot boxes retire
into it. Every number and text is in `stash_config.lua`; the rules are pure functions in `stash_core.lua` (tested by
`tests/stash_test.lua`, which also runs `stash.lua` against a mocked engine and an in-memory database); `stash.lua` is the
engine glue. Window: Economy > Supply Stash (client `game_stash`, extended opcode 110). No player command (owner rule):
the window opens from the game menu and Stow Everything is its button.

**Scope.** Per character (`player_id`), as the stash and the depot always were (a season join empties it). The room is per
account: the Chaos Pact limit `stashTabs`, the extras bought, the Pact itself and achievements, so every character of an
account has the same tabs.

**Whole items.** A plain stack (nothing but its id and count; the engine's blob of patch 0017 is only `ATTR_COUNT`) merges by
type into `chaos_stash` (player, item) -> count, tab, as before: 5,000 gold coins are one entry. Every other item (a weapon,
a rift key, a written letter, a stack with attributes, an empty bag) is one row of `chaos_stash_items` with every attribute:
codec `blob` (the engine's own binary form, `item:serializeAttributes()`, hex; rarity, item level, every modifier with its
tier, sockets and gems, quality, powers, uniques, charges, durations, names, texts and any custom attribute), else `attrs`
(the market's key list, without engine patch 0017). Withdrawing makes the item again (`item:unserializeAttributes()`), with
a new per-item id. The codec is shared with the market escrow (`item_codec.lua`, `item_codec_core.lua`; `market.lua`'s
`MK.encode` / `MK.decode` call it, same behaviour). The charms grid keeps its own fallback form for its rows of before.
A row also keeps the item's name, look text and rarity, so the list never re-creates items.

**One drag, one deposit (2026-10-22,** player report: "dragging an item into the stash also takes the item to its right,
and that one does not show in the stash"). The base client offers a drop to every widget under the mouse until one
answers true; the client's list and window both answered false, so one drag sent two `Stash {Pos}` requests for the same
container slot. The first took the item; the bag closed the gap, and the second took the item that moved into the slot.
It went into the stash, but the list echo of the second request was inside the 100 ms echo limit, so the list did not show
it. Fixed on both sides: the client's drop answers true and names the item (`ItemId` = its client id, `Count`); the
server ignores a deposit of the same position within `repeatDepositMs` (400 ms) of the last one that went in (old
clients, `stash_core.lua` `K.repeatDeposit`) and refuses when the slot holds another item than the one named
(`K.sameItem`; the count of a stack only; "That item moved before it reached the stash. Drag it again."). Nothing is
lost or doubled: an ignored or refused request moves nothing. Tests: `tests/stash_test.lua` (one drop sent twice keeps
the neighbour in the bag, a later drag of that slot goes in, a named item that is not in the slot stays, a stack of
another count stays) and client `stashview_test.lua`.

**Access** (owner decision 2026-10-15: remote deposit is a paid unlock). Everybody uses the stash in town: deposit and
withdraw in a protection zone or inside a hideout (`withdrawInHideout`; the hideout's supply stash). **Remote deposit**
(from anywhere, mid-hunt, Stow Everything included) needs the unlock (`stash_config.lua` `remoteDeposit`): the store offer
"Remote Stash Deposit" (Storage & Slots, permanent, account-wide, pact_config.lua extra `stashRemote`, PLACEHOLDER price
300) or an active Chaos Pact (lent: it stops when the Pact ends; nothing stored is lost). Withdraw stays in town for
everybody, unlock or not. Deposits come from a drag of an item from the backpack, the inventory or a reachable floor tile
onto the window (the reach and house rules of before), Stow Everything, or a script (`ChaosStash.storeItem`, the same
rule); the depot migration is no deposit of the player. The server refuses elsewhere ("You can put items into the stash
only in a protection zone. Remote deposit from anywhere: Store > Storage & Slots, or an active Chaos Pact." / "You can take
items out of the stash only in a protection zone.") and tells the client (`access {canDeposit | canWithdraw}`); the `tabs`
message carries `canDeposit`, `depositWhy` ("pz", "hideout", "remote") and `remote` ("bought", "pact"). The client greys
out the items (withdraw) and the Stow Everything button (deposit) with a tooltip that says where to unlock, refuses a drop
with that line, and follows the local player's protection zone flag while walking (the window may stay open).

**Tabs.** An entry is one slot: a merged stack type or a stored item. General tabs (`tabSize` 100) take anything;
affinity tabs take one class and every deposit of that class goes to the first owned one with room, else to a general tab:

| Tab (id) | Takes | Owned by |
|---|---|---|
| Orbs (101) | currency orbs, orbs v2, Whetstone, rune shard (the Orbs Pouch ids, the loot filter's orb ids) | bought (Orbs Stash Tab) |
| Gems (102) | `ChaosGems.isGem` | bought |
| Keys (103) | Rift Keys, omen fragments and keys, key items, maps | bought |
| Supplies (104) | runes, potions and fluids, ammunition, food | free for everybody |
| Weapons (105) | weapons, quivers, fist weapons | bought |
| Armor (106) | helmets, armour, legs, boots, shields, other worn gear | bought |
| Jewellery (107) | rings and amulets | bought |
| Materials (108) | profession materials, ores, shards, ingots, dust | bought |
| Creature Products (109) | the pack products and any sellable loot that is nothing else | bought, or lent by the Chaos Pact |
| Collectibles (110) | dolls, figurines, trophies, configured ids | bought, or earned (Reliquary, 50 uniques) |
| Old depot (200) | what the depot migration could not place | never takes items: withdraw-only |

General tabs = `stashTabs` (4 free, +2 Pact, up to +6 bought) + 1 per depot tab achievement (Cabinet of Curiosities, Hall
of Trophies, Keeper of the Vault) + 1 per depot tab bought before (`depotTabsCount`), at most 30. Ids 101-103 are the
special tabs of before: their rows keep working. A tab beyond the count, an affinity tab no longer owned (the Pact ended)
and Old depot are withdraw-only; nothing is deleted when a limit shrinks. A merged stack in a withdraw-only tab moves with
its next deposit into a writable tab with room. Buying an affinity tab moves the matching entries of the general tabs
into it at the next opening. The client shows the tab bar with the affinity's item as icon, its name, a tooltip (what it
takes, who owns it, why it is withdraw-only) and the line under the list.

**Free room** (`stash_config.lua`, measured from the repo's loot data): 20 orb ids, 25 gem types, 20 profession
materials, 27 pack products, the base monsters' products (2,945 priced item ids, most of them gear), supplies, and gear kept
one entry per piece. The old free room was 2 stash tabs of 48 types + 4 depot tabs of 100 items = 496 slots; the new one
is 4 general tabs of 100 + Supplies 100 = 500 entries, and a merged stack is one entry where the depot counted every
stack of 100.

**Stow Everything** (the button; `StashAllRequest`): every item of the backpack, through its bags, into its tab, in one
batch with one save. Kept: equipped items and the backpack itself, containers (their contents go, the bag stays), items
that cannot be moved or picked up, store-bound items (store pouches, the Everfull Ration, store items), locked items, items
on the never-stash list, items with an action or unique id (quest items) except a Rift Key (`stowActionIds`). The room is
counted as the batch fills: what does not fit stays in the backpack ("no room"). The client gets
`StowReport {stowed, kept, reasons = [{reason, label, count, names}]}` (an info box) and the chat a line per result.

**Write order (the journal).** No item lost or doubled by a crash, a disconnect or a failed save. Every deposit and
withdrawal is first a row of `chaos_stash_items` in a journal state with a serial; the serial is set in the character's
storage 7100011 in memory and saved with the items in ONE transaction (`player:save()`):
deposit: 1. the depositing row (state 9, serial n) is written 2. the item leaves the character in memory, storage = n
3. `player:save()` 4. the row becomes an entry (a plain stack merges into `chaos_stash`, one transaction). Withdrawal:
1. the entry becomes a taking row (state 8; a plain stack's amount leaves its entry in the same transaction) 2. the item is
made on the character, storage = n 3. `player:save()` 4. the row is deleted. A failed save undoes the memory side and the
row. Whatever a crash leaves, the saved serial says which side is true (`stash_core.lua` `K.recoverAction`): depositing
with serial <= saved is activated, else dropped (the item is still on the saved character); taking with serial <= saved is
deleted, else restored. Recovery runs at login, and before every operation (between operations the serial in memory is
the saved one), so a row left by a failed write after a failed save is settled before a new serial is used; while one
cannot be settled no new operation starts ("busy"). `tests/stash_test.lua` crashes a deposit and a withdrawal after every
single step and recovers from the saved state: always exactly one copy.

**Security.** Every request is checked on the server: the item must be in an open container of the player, an inventory
slot (never the equipped backpack) or a reachable floor tile; a withdrawn row must be the player's and active; counts are
integers (`Chaos.toInt`) clamped to what is stored and to the free capacity; tab ids come only from the server. Every
query is built from integers formatted with `%d` and texts through `db.escapeString` (the store functions in `stash.lua`;
the test feeds them hostile text). Rate limits (`rate`): list 300 ms, withdraw 250 ms, stow 1.5 s, never-stash list 100 ms,
the list echo of a deposit 100 ms. The protocol fuzz test covers the handler. A container slot is resolved like the
engine's move: the page's first index (`player:getContainerIndex`) plus the slot the client names, so a deposit from a
later page of the Purse or the depot inbox takes the item shown there (fixed 2026-10-22; before, the item of page one).

**Withdrawal delivery** (player report 2026-10-22, "what I withdrew disappeared"; `ChaosStash.stowWithdrawn`). A
withdrawn item goes into the backpack or a bag in it (breadth first), added with `FLAG_IGNOREAUTOSTACK`; a plain stack
comes out as stacks of 100. Never an inventory slot (the engine's own search, `player:addItem` / `addItemEx`, put a
wearable into an empty slot, one no client draws on an engine without src-patch 0058), never a store pouch or what is
in it (`ChaosPouches.isPouch`: the Loot Bag the Auto Seller sells from), never the Purse. Nothing fits: the entry stays
in the stash and the player gets the room line (capacity line when the weight refused it). A failed save removes only
the items just made (`rec.made`), never other items of that id the character carries. Tests in `tests/stash_test.lua`.

**Depot transition** (`stash_config.lua` `depot`). `withdrawOnly = true`: the depot boxes and the chest take no new items
(`depot_core.lua` `D.decide`, code "closed"; taking out and tidying inside a tab still work); the inbox and the market
are untouched. `migrate = true`: at the first depot locker opening of a character (the engine writes the depot with the
character only once a locker was opened that session, so this is the safe moment) every item of all its depot chests
(the tab boxes stay, their contents go; a bag after its contents) goes through the journal into the stash, at most
`migrationBatch` (400) per opening; what fits no tab goes to the withdraw-only Old depot tab; items with a unique id stay
in the depot. Logged in `chaos_stash_log` and the console; the player gets a line. Storage 7100012 = the version done
(raise `depot.version` to run it again). Offline, for everyone at once: `python3 -I server/tools/migrate_depot_stash.py
SERVER_DIR --server-stopped` (server STOPPED; `--dry-run` counts, `--sql FILE` writes the SQL): one transaction copies
`player_depotitems` (but the boxes) into `chaos_stash_items` (source "depot", the engine's attributes column as hex) and
deletes them there; the stash describes and places those rows at the next opening (plain stacks merge, Old depot for the
rest). Needs engine patch 0017.

**Rollback.** Before the switch: a database backup (`tools/backup.sh`). To stop the transition: set `depot.withdrawOnly`
and `depot.migrate` to false; the depot works as before and the stash keeps what moved (withdraw in a protection zone and
put it back by hand). A full rollback is the backup. Removing the depot boxes later is a separate step (not done).

**Season join** counts the stash's whole items as stored items (the join needs them gone) and empties the stash as before.

**Client** (`game_stash`): the window of before plus whole items in the list (a whole item withdraws as one), the tab bar
with affinity icons, greyed items outside a protection zone, the Stow Everything button and its report. Logic
`stashview.lua` (tested by `stashview_test.lua`). Not run in a client yet.

**Staff** (admin panel Economy > Stash: add item, tabs and search, remove item; `stash.lua` `ChaosStash.staffGive`,
`staffSummary`, `staffFind`, `staffRemove`). Reads work by character id, offline too, and lay nothing out. Writes need the
character online and go through the journal like a player's: an item made for the stash (`Game.createItem`, never on
the character, so the journal's remove / restore have nothing to do) is a depositing row first, the serial is saved with
the character, then the row becomes the entry; a removal is a taking row, the save, then the row deleted (nothing is
given). A tab named by staff must be a general or affinity tab with room (never Old depot); Auto routes it as a deposit.
At most 100 whole items at once; a plain stack is one merged entry. `chaos_stash_log` rows `staff` / `staffdel`.
`tests/stash_test.lua` runs them on its in-memory database (a failed save leaves nothing behind, the backpack untouched).

**Tables.** `chaos_stash` and `chaos_stash_block` (`sql/chaos.sql`), `chaos_stash.tab` (`sql/chaos_pact.sql`),
`chaos_stash_items` and `chaos_stash_log` (`sql/chaos_stash.sql`; `stash.lua` creates them at startup too).


**List packets (fix 2026-10-20).** `sendItems` answers with `tabs` and then `addItems` packets (`isFirst` / `isLast`). A packet
is cut at `chunkSize` (40) entries or `chunkBytes` (6000) bytes of JSON, whichever comes first. Before, only the count cut it:
40 whole items with a look text of up to 1000 bytes were 40 KB, and a payload over the engine's 8192 byte string limit goes
out through `Chaos.sendChunked` in "S/P/E" parts that the window (a plain `registerExtendedOpcode` listener) cannot read.
Those packets were lost: with about 10 whole items the list showed only what arrived (a first row, or nothing), nothing could be
clicked, and a counter that comes from `tabs` (13/100) stayed right. The deposit and withdraw paths take the item by the
resolved engine item or by item id / row id, never by a list position; `tests/stash_test.lua` ("the list") deposits 25 entries
one by one, withdraws the 13th, then entries and half stacks, and checks character + stash sums after every step, and that
every `addItems` packet is under 8192 bytes. No duplication was found on the server. A neighbour item leaving with a deposit can
only come from a stale container slot in the client request (the slot is the index at the time of the drag); not reproduced.

## Chaos Pact and account storage (`pact.lua`, `pact_core.lua`, `pact_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_pact.sql`, client `game_pact`)

Two things sold for Chaos Coins, both account-wide and comfort only: nothing here adds damage, defence or loot. Every
number is in `pact_config.lua`; the rules are in `pact_core.lua` (tested by `tests/pact_test.lua`); `pact.lua` is the engine
glue. Window: Character > Chaos Pact (client `game_pact`, extended opcode 222 `ChaosOpcodes.pact`).

**The Chaos Pact** (store category "Chaos Pact", 300 coins): 30 days; a purchase stacks on the time left, up to 365 days
ahead (`maxStackDays`, refused before any coin is taken). While it runs the account gets the Pact bonus of every limit below,
the name plate title **Pactbound** (`ChaosTitles` source `pact`) and **5 Chaos Coins a day**: claimed in the window once per
server day (`Chaos.dayKey`), for the whole account, while the Pact runs; no back pay for missed days. A month of claims gives
150 coins back, so a player who logs in daily pays 150 net for the month: cheaper than the 250 of 30 premium days alone, and
never more coins than the Pact cost. Store bundles that contain Pact days (`shop_config.lua` `pact = {api = "ChaosPact",
fn = "grantDays"}`) go through `ChaosPact.grantDays(player, days, source)`.

**VIP perks** (owner approval 2026-10-13, changed 2026-10-13: "Vip ganha +10% de exp e restaura stamina mais rápido.
Retire o loot bag e autoloot."; `pact_config.lua` `perks`, `pact_perks.lua`, `pact_perks_core.lua`,
`tests/pact_perks_test.lua`, `tools/pact_stamina_patch_test.py`). The Pact is the server's VIP; on top of the limits
below, while it is active:
**+10% experience** from monsters (`perks.expBonus`; an `onGainExperience` callback at index 7, after World Experience
at 5 and the blessing at 6; it multiplies like every Chaos bonus and counts against the experience cap at index 85, so it
adds nothing for a kill already at the cap; player kills get nothing; season characters get nothing, as World Experience:
decided by the owner on 2026-10-13, "Ok");
**stamina back x1.5 faster** (`perks.staminaRegen`): offline (the base login script's offline time x1.5: 6 h offline give
180 stamina minutes instead of 120, and the slower regeneration above 40 h is also x1.5) and on the stamina trainer tile
(a minute every 80 s instead of 120 s), through `patch_base_events.py` steps 13 and 14 (Install 4);
one more loadout slot (`loadouts_config.lua` `pactSlots`, "Loadouts"; kept by the owner on 2026-10-13: "Pode manter");
the Auto Seller works for every character of the account (its storage set to 2; a bought unlock is 1 and is never touched,
and the store still sells it, since only 1 counts as owned there), so a Pact holder can sell the Loot Bag every 30 s;
**Rarity Autoloot is no longer a Pact perk** (`perks.retired`: a Rarity Autoloot the Pact lent before is taken back at the
next login or minute check, a bought one stays; still sold in the store), and the Loot Bag never was one (a store item of
its own); the chat colour **Pactbound Name** (cosmetic `chat_pactbound`, source
"pact", taken back when the Pact ends) and the **cosmetic of the month** (`perks.monthly`: YYYYMM -> a pact cosmetic,
November 2026 to April 2027 planned: kill effects and loot label accents), granted to accounts with an active Pact that
month and kept for good. Applied at login, at once after a purchase (`ChaosPact.grantDays` is wrapped, no edit of
`pact.lua`) and once a minute for the characters online. Still no premium days (`premiumDays = 0`). Remote stash deposit (deposit into the stash from anywhere, "Stash") is
included while the Pact runs (limit `stashRemote`, 2026-10-15); the store offer and the window's perk line say so. No priority login:
the engine has no login queue. Depot tabs: the Pact's +1 was already in `limits.depotTabs`.

**Premium.** The Pact gives no premium days (`pact.premiumDays = 0`, the owner's decision: the stamina bonus below is
power, not comfort). A value above 0 would add that many premium days per purchase. With `freePremium = false`,
premium on this base unlocks: the 64 outfits and 39 mounts marked `premium="yes"`, houses (`buyhouse.lua`), boats and the
premium travel / blessing NPC options, premium-only areas (bridge and teleport scripts), offline training, a VIP list
of 100, the depot limit, the base autoloot list of 20, and the stock stamina bonus (green stamina above 40 hours gives
x1.5 experience to premium players, `events/scripts/player.lua`). Promotion is off (`tools/patch_promotion.py`), so premium no
longer promotes anyone. Premium is already sold on its own (Premium Time), so the Pact adds nothing new to it; the
stamina bonus is the one premium effect that is not pure comfort, and it comes with any premium.

**Limits** (`limits`; yours = free + Pact bonus while active + bought extras, at most maxExtra):

| Limit | Free | Chaos Pact | Bought (max) | Used by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| General stash tabs (100 entries each; +1 per depot tab achievement and per bought depot tab, see "Stash") | 4 | +2 | +6 | `stash.lua` |
| Depot tabs (100 items each; +1 per depot tab achievement, see "Depot tabs") | 4 | +1 | +9 | `depot.lua` |
| Market listings per character | 20 | +10 | - | `market.lua` `ChaosMarket.maxActive` |
| Market listings per account | 40 | +20 | - | `market.lua` |
| Saved passive tree builds | 2 | +3 | +6 | `pact.lua` |
| Loot rules (the autoloot list) | 10 | +10 (premium too) | - | `autoloot.lua`, `lootfilter.lua` |
| Character slots | 5 | - | +10 | website, `pact.lua` at login |
| Affinity stash tabs (Orbs, Gems, Keys, Weapons, Armor, Jewellery, Materials, Creature Products, Collectibles; Supplies is free) | - | Creature Products lent | 1 each | `stash.lua` |
| Remote stash deposit (limit `stashRemote`; deposit from anywhere while > 0; withdraw stays in town) | 0 | +1 | 1 | `stash.lua` |

The loot rules count premium alone as the Pact (`premiumCounts`), because the base server's own autoloot callback
(`data/scripts/creaturescripts/autoloot.lua`) loots 10 / 20 by premium; keep free + Pact at most 20 or change that callback.

**One-time extras** (store category "Storage & Slots", service `pactExtra`, table `chaos_account_extras`): Extra Stash Tab 150,
Orbs Stash Tab 200, Gems Stash Tab 200, Keys Stash Tab 150, Weapons / Armor / Jewellery / Materials / Creature Products Stash
Tab 150 each, Collectibles Stash Tab 100 and Remote Stash Deposit 300 (these seven: PLACEHOLDER prices,
docs/OWNER_TODO.md), Character Slot 250, Build Slot 100. A purchase past the maximum is
refused before the coins are taken.

**When the Pact ends nothing is deleted.** Stash tabs above the limit become withdraw-only (an item whose entry sits there and
is deposited again moves to a writable tab with room, if there is one); market offers above the smaller limit stay until
they sell, expire or are cancelled (only new listings are refused); saved builds above the limit stay and can be loaded or
deleted, not overwritten or renamed; autoloot entries above the limit stay stored and work again after a renewal. A login
in the 14 days after the end says so.

**Stash tabs.** The tabs, what goes where and the depot transition are in "Stash" (`stash_config.lua`, `stash_core.lua`);
this file keeps the limit `stashTabs` and the extras that buy tabs. `pact.lua` sends the affinity tabs and who owns them in
`status.special = [{name, owned, source}]` (the Chaos Pact window's tab line).

**Saved builds** (`chaos_build_slots`, per account): Save stores the passive tree build code of the character
(`ChaosBuildShare.exportCode`, the same codes as "Build sharing") under a name in a slot; Load opens the passive tree and asks
for the preview of the code (the class line check, the price and Apply Build are those of `buildshare.lua`). No buildshare
file is changed. Slots above the limit are read-only (Load, Delete).

**Character slots.** The website sets `$config['max_characters']` per account (`website/overlay/plugins/chaos/lib.php`
`chaos_character_limit`: `characters.free` of `pact_config.lua` + bought slots + legacy slots), so ZnoteX's
`createcharacter.php` refuses one more character on the server side. The game server checks again at login: a character
past the account's slots (by creation order) gets a popup and is logged out; staff (group access or account type 5+) are
never stopped. At the first start with this feature every account that already had more characters than the free count
gets the difference as `charSlotsLegacy` (once, `server_config` row `chaos_pact_legacy`).

**Protocol** (opcode 222, JSON `{action, data}`): client `open | sync | claim | buildSave {slot?, name} | buildRename {slot,
name} | buildDelete {slot} | buildLoad {slot}`; server `status {active, ends, daysLeft, dailyCoins, canClaim, claimedTotal,
premiumDays, coins, title, limits = [{key, label, free, pact, extra, maxExtra, total, pactActive}], tabSize, special,
buildLimit, builds}`, `buildCode {slot, code}`, `message {text, error}`. Rate limits in `pact_config.lua` `rate`.

**Tables** (`sql/chaos_pact.sql`, also created at startup): `chaos_pact` (account, end, run start, days bought, last claim,
coins claimed), `chaos_account_extras`, `chaos_build_slots`, `chaos_pact_log` (purchases, claims, legacy grants, staff
changes). Staff: `/pact <player>, info | days <n> | end | extra <key> <amount> | claimreset`.

**Store hunk** (`shop_config.lua`, one block before "Premium Time"; the offers themselves are in `pact_config.lua` `store`):

```lua
		-- >>> Chaos Pact and account storage (pact.lua): offers, prices and texts live in pact_config.lua `store`
		dofile("data/scripts/chaos/pact_config.lua").store.pact,
		dofile("data/scripts/chaos/pact_config.lua").store.storage,
		-- <<< Chaos Pact and account storage
```

`pact.lua` puts the services `pact` and `pactExtra` into `ChaosShopServices.services` at startup, at every login and after a
reload (shop_services.lua builds that table when it loads).

**Tested in game** (own server copy and database, one client): the window without a Pact; a stash of 104 item types from
before tabs placed into tabs 1-2 and a read-only tab 3; a new item refused while tabs are full; the Pact bought in the store
(coins, premium days, log); the daily claim and the refused second claim; four builds saved; tab 3 writable with the Pact;
the Orbs tab bought, the orbs moved into it, Stash All sending an Orb of Grafting there, a second purchase refused without
taking coins; the Pact expired: limits back to the free counts, title gone, tab 3 withdraw-only (withdraw works, a deposit of
that item moves it to tab 2), builds 3-4 read-only (a forged save refused), a read-only build loaded into the passive tree;
`grantDays` from a bundle; the Pactbound name plate; a sixth character refused at login, then let in after a Character Slot
was bought; the window from another character of the account; the autoloot window with 20 rules.

## Depot tabs (`depot.lua`, `depot_core.lua`, `depot_config.lua`, `tools/patch_base_depot.py`, client `game_depottabs`)

The owner's decision: the depot works like a limited stash with tabs. Every number and text is in `depot_config.lua`; the
rules are pure functions in `depot_core.lua` (tested by `tests/depot_test.lua`, which also runs `depot.lua` against a
mocked engine); `depot.lua` is the engine glue.

**What the base has.** TFS 1.4.2 gives every town its own depot chest (`Player::getDepotChest(townId)`) inside the locker,
next to the shared inbox and the market. The engine never makes depot boxes. The items `depot box I` .. `XXI` (25453-25469,
29841-29844) exist in `items.otb` / `items.xml` as plain containers (32 slots, not pickupable, not moveable); the base only
put them into new characters' depots through an optional website SQL snippet (off here: `!season join` needs an empty depot).

**Tabs.** Boxes I-XVII are the tabs 1-17 (`boxIds`). `tools/patch_base_depot.py` (step `depot` of `install_all.py`, after
`pouches`; idempotent; `items.otb.bak` keeps the original) does four things: the 17 boxes get the pickupable flag in
`items.otb` (the engine refuses any non-pickupable item in a container, so no script could put a box into a chest; they
stay not moveable, so a player cannot drag one out), `items.xml` names them `depot tab 1` .. `17` with 100 slots, the base
locker Action (`data/scripts/customs/actions/sounds/depot.lua`, it plays a sound) calls `ChaosDepot.onOpenLocker` first, and
`Player:onMoveItem` calls `ChaosDepot.onMoveItem` first. When a locker opens, the missing boxes of that town's chest are
added (tab 1 first). No engine patch: Lua makes the boxes when the locker opens. `depot.lua` warns at startup when a hook
is missing, and registers its own locker Action when the base locker script does not exist.

**Limits.** An account may fill `ChaosDepot.tabs(player)` tabs: `pact_config.lua` limit `depotTabs` (1 free since 2026-10-17, +1 while the
Chaos Pact runs, up to 9 bought) + one per achievement of `achievementTabs` that any character of the account has, at most
17. A tab holds 100 items: every item counts once, a container counts as 1 plus everything in it (nested), a stack counts
as 1. Tabs above the count are withdraw-only. Nothing is ever deleted: contents above a limit stay, only adding is refused.
The tab count is the same in every town; each town's chest has its own 17 tabs.

| Source | Tabs |
|---|---|
| Free | 1 |
| Chaos Pact (while active) | +1 |
| Store "Depot Tabs" (Premium & Services; not sold while the depot is withdraw-only, "Store"): Extra Depot Tab, 150 coins (a stash tab costs 150 too); 4 Depot Tabs, 500 coins | up to +12 |
| Achievements: Cabinet of Curiosities (25 unique items), Hall of Trophies (100 bestiary entries), Keeper of the Vault (50 sealed rifts) | +1 each |

The store offers are service `pactExtra` with `extra = "depotTabs"` and `amount` 1 or 4 (`pact.lua` adds `amount`; a pack
that would pass the cap is refused before the coins are taken). They live in `depot_config.lua` `store`, inserted in
`shop_config.lua` as their own block:

```lua
		-- >>> Depot tabs (depot.lua): a single tab and a pack of 4 (service pactExtra); offers, prices and texts live in
		-- depot_config.lua `store`
		dofile("data/scripts/chaos/depot_config.lua").store,
		-- <<< Depot tabs
```

**Enforcement.** `Player:onMoveItem` runs for every move a player makes (the event is raised in `Game::internalMoveItem`
with the player as actor): from the inventory or the ground, a throw, dragging a bag in, dropping onto a box icon in the
chest window or onto the chest in the locker window (the destination is worked out as `Container::queryDestination` does),
into a bag nested inside a tab, between tabs, and the swap move. The rule (`ChaosDepotCore.decide`): into a tab from outside
it, the tab must be open and have room for the item and everything in it; inside the same tab every move is allowed (also
in a locked or over-full tab), except splitting a stack, which needs one free item; nothing new goes loose into the chest
itself or into an old container lying loose in it. The refusal is a warning line ("Depot tab 5 is locked: ... Buy more
tabs in the Store", "Depot tab 1 is full: 100 of 100 items, this needs 5 ...", "Put items into a depot tab, not loose into
the depot chest") and RETURNVALUE_NOTPOSSIBLE / CONTAINERNOTENOUGHROOM. Paths that add items without a player move, checked
in the base engine and the scripts: the market (sold items leave the depot chest and its tabs, bought and cancelled ones go
to the inbox), mail and parcels (inbox), the house transfer (inbox), the store and every Chaos script (inbox, or the
character), our stash (withdraws to the character). The engine never adds to a depot box itself. The inbox stays unlimited
(players cannot put anything into it; the engine refuses without FLAG_NOLIMIT). A script that ever puts an item straight
into a container that may be a tab must ask `ChaosDepot.checkAdd(player, container, item, count)` first;
`Item:moveTo` and `Container:addItem` skip `onMoveItem`. Not covered: such a script that does not ask.

**One default tab** (2026-10-17, "Diminuir as tabs do depot padrão para 1"): the free count is 1 (`pact_config.lua`
`depotTabs.free`; the bought maximum rose from 9 to 12 so the total stays 17 boxes). A locker opening makes only the boxes of
the account's open tabs (`Depot.ensure(chest, tabs)`), boxes that exist stay (a locked tab with items keeps its box), and the
`tabs` message's `max` is the number of boxes that exist, so a default depot shows one tab. Buying a tab or earning an
achievement makes its box at the next locker opening. The stash tabs (`stashTabs` free 4) are unchanged.

**The stash takes over** (2026-10-15, "Stash"; reversed 2026-10-17, see "Stash"): with `stash_config.lua` `depot.withdrawOnly` the boxes and the chest
are withdraw-only (the move rule answers "closed"; taking out and tidying inside a tab work, the inbox and the market as
before), and with `depot.migrate` the first locker opening moves the character's depots into the stash
(`ChaosStash.migrateDepot`). The locker line says the depot is withdraw-only. The depot tab achievements and bought depot
tabs now count as general stash tabs. The rules below stay for a rollback (both flags false).

**Old depots.** At the first locker opening with tabs, everything loose in that chest is placed into tabs in chest order:
open tabs first, then locked ones (withdraw-only), as the stash did with its tabs. An item that fits no tab (a backpack
holding more than 100 items, or every tab full) stays loose in the chest, withdraw-only. Nothing is deleted or merged
away. The player gets a line ("Your depot was sorted into tabs: ..."). The sort waits until the engine has put the chest
into its locker: before that the engine treats the chest's contents as removed and `Item:moveTo` does nothing.
`!season join` still sees an empty depot (it counts items that are not containers).

**Client: the depot window.** `game_depottabs` (opcode **111**, `ChaosOpcodes.depotTabs`). Opening a depot locker
opens one centred window, "<town> Depot", instead of the stock locker, chest and box windows: 17 tab buttons in rows of 6
(the tab's name or number, a colour accent, a lock on locked tabs, a tooltip with the count or the store hint) and a
"+ Tabs" button while tabs can be bought; the active tab's 100 slots in a 10x10 grid; "87/100 items", "4 of 17 tabs";
Inbox, Market, Buy Tabs (the Store at its Depot Tabs category; hidden while the depot is withdraw-only and tabs are not sold) and Close. The locker, its chest and one box stay real
containers: the client opens them with the engine's own use packet and only hides the stock windows (it wraps
`game_containers`' onOpen handler at runtime; no base file, no base patch). So container ids, the range check and every
move rule above stay as they were: drag and drop, stacking, use and look in the grid are the stock Item widget's.
Switching tabs: the client sends `open {tab}`; `ChaosDepot.requestOpen` answers `open {tab, ok, text}` after a rate limit
(`Chaos.limited`, `openMs` 250) and checks that the player has the chest of the locker last opened (`Depot.at`, set by
`onOpenLocker`) open (`player:getContainerId(chest)`), stands next to that locker on its floor, and that the box exists
(`ChaosDepotCore.openRefusal`); then the client opens that box into the tab's container id. A locked tab opens too
(withdraw-only by the move rule). The engine has no Lua call that opens a container for a player; doing it server-side
would need an engine patch, so the open itself stays the client's use packet. Walking away closes the containers (the
engine's own auto-close) and the window with them. Without the module the depot works as before.

**Tab names and colours.** Right-click a tab button (or the pencil above the grid): a dialog with the name (at most 16
characters; empty = the tab number) and 13 colour swatches (default + `palette` in `depot_config.lua`: gold, ember,
crimson, rose, violet, frost, azure, jade, moss, bone, ash grey, bronze; no free colours). Client -> server
`style {tab, name, color}`, rate limited (`styleMs` 1000); `ChaosDepotCore.styleRequest` trims the name, makes runs of
spaces one, turns UTF-8 Latin-1 letters into Latin-1 (the client draws Latin-1) and refuses control characters, anything
outside Latin-1, more than 16 characters and unknown colour keys (the refusal is a warning line and the stored style is
sent back). There is no shared name filter in the scripts to reuse (pet names have their own letters-only rule), so tab
names allow printable ASCII and Latin-1. Locked tabs can be styled too. Stored per account and tab in
`chaos_depot_tabs (account_id, tab, name, color)` (`sql/chaos_depot_tabs.sql`, `Chaos.tables.depotTabs`; `depot.lua`
also creates it at startup; a reset deletes the row), cached per account, loaded at login and at every locker opening:
every character of the account sees the same names. The name shows on the tab button, in the line above the grid and in
the box's title and look text ("Potions. 87 of 100 items.").

Server -> client `tabs {tabs, max, size, used, ids, chest, lockers, inbox, market, hint, store, names, colors, palette,
nameMax, town}` (at login, at every locker opening, after every move into or out of the depot, after a purchase and after
a style change). Each box's look text says the count ("87 of 100 items.", "Locked: ... Buy more in the Store."). A locker
opening prints "Depot: 4 of 17 tabs open, 100 items each ...". A box opened in a stock window (with the module off, or
the window closed) gets "Tab 3 (87/100)" or "Potions (locked)" as its title. Opcode 111 was checked free like the others
(base server list, base client ExtendedIds, every Chaos opcode; `tests/depot_test.lua`). No storages; one table.

**Tested in game** (own server copy and database, full map, one client): a depot of 133 loose items from before tabs
(130 items, a backpack of 4 stacks, a backpack holding 147 items) sorted into tab 1 (100) and tab 2 (35), the big backpack
left loose; tabs 5-17 dimmed; a move into locked tab 5 refused with the store hint; a move into the full tab 1 refused;
a move into tab 3 accepted and its count updated; the 4 Depot Tabs pack bought through the service (8 tabs), then tab 5
took an item.

**Depot window, tested in game** (own server copy and database on a private port, full map, the things_custom15 pair,
one client): the locker opened one window and no stock container windows; items dropped into tab 1 through the grid's
Item widgets (count 0 -> 6/100); a gold stack moved in with the stock count dialog and stacked to 100; an item dragged
from the grid to the backpack (6 -> 5); tabs 3 and 6 opened through `open {tab}`; a move into locked tab 6 refused;
tabs 1, 3 and 6 renamed and coloured (rows in `chaos_depot_tabs`), the names and colours shown on another character of
the account; Inbox opened the inbox, Market the market, Buy Tabs the Store at Depot Tabs; three steps away from the
locker closed every depot container and the window.

## Referral program (`referral.lua`, `referral_core.lua`, `referral_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_referral.sql`, client `game_referral`)

A player shares a code; a new account that takes it gets a welcome gift, and the code's owner gets cosmetic rewards when
the new account's first character levels. Approved by the owner. Nothing in it gives power. Every number and text is in
`referral_config.lua`; the rules are pure functions in `referral_core.lua` (tested by `tests/referral_test.lua`).

- **Codes.** An account gets its code (8 characters without look-alikes, shown `XXXX-XXXX`; `chaos_referral_codes`) when the
  window opens and one of its characters reached `minReferrerLevel` (20). Staff accounts have none.
- **Entering a code.** On the website's account creation form (optional field, pre-filled from `register.php?ref=CODE`;
  website/README.md "Referral codes") or in game in Character > Referral within `entryDays` (7) of the account's creation
  (`accounts.creation`, else `znote_accounts.created`). The website only checks the format and that the code exists, then
  writes a `pending` row; the server checks it at the account's first login. One referrer per account; a rejected code can be
  replaced by another while the account is new.
- **Anti-abuse** (`antiAbuse`, each refusal logged): not the own code; no staff on either side (account type >= 2 or a
  character of group >= 2); referrer not banned; no referring back; no shared IP (`sameIp`: login IPs of every character of
  both accounts, online characters and the website registration IP); no shared e-mail domain unless it is a public one
  (`sameEmailDomain`, `publicDomains`); at most `monthlyLinks` (10) new friends per referrer and calendar month. An IPv6
  address counts by its /64 network (`ChaosReferralCore.netKey`), as the website's login and register guards do.
- **The friend's gift** (`starterGift`): 50 health and 50 mana potions (backpack, the rest into the depot inbox) and the
  account-wide title Kindled, once, to the character that logs in after the link is accepted.
- **The referrer's rewards** (`milestones`): when the referred account's first character (the lowest character id, fixed when
  the link is accepted; another character does not count) reaches level 50: the title Torchbearer and 25 Chaos Coins; level
  250: the title Ember Herald and 50 Chaos Coins. Rows in `chaos_referral_rewards`: `paid` at once; `void` when the referred
  account is banned; `due` (waiting) when the referrer is banned or already had `monthlyRewards` (10) rewards this month.
  Waiting rewards are tried again at every login of the referrer, at startup and every `retryMinutes` (30). Coins go to
  `chaos_shop_coins`; titles come from the paid rows (`ChaosTitles` source `referral`). The referrer is told at once or at
  the next login. Level 250 is the main reward (owner decision 2026-10-13: "level X"; X = 250 decided 2026-10-14,
  docs/PRICES.md: with pack combat level 150 took only 1.5-3 hours).
- **Checked again when a reward is due** (owner rules 2026-10-13; one person never sits on both sides, as the
  multi-client rule and docs/GM_HANDBOOK.md section 4 say): the referred account must be `minReferredAccountDays` (7) days
  old (else the reward waits and is paid by the retry); a shared connection by then (`sameIpAtPayout`: every login IP of
  both accounts, the online characters and the website IPs, IPv6 by /64) or a shared payer (`samePayer`: a payer hash of
  `chaos_pay_payers` on a donation of each account; the table is empty until the donation service writes it, see
  website/README.md "Creator codes") makes it `void`.
- **Tier rewards** (`tiers`, `qualify` = `l250`): once 3, 5 and 10 referred accounts reached the qualifying milestone
  (paid, not void), the referrer gets the titles Flamecaller (+50 coins), Hearthwarden (+100) and Lord of the Pyre
  (+200), once each (`chaos_referral_tiers`, `Ref.checkTiers` after a payment; titles from the rows). The client lists
  them under the milestones ("And with friends at level 250 (n so far): ..."). The referral link is shown on the
  website too (The World > Creator Codes, `register.php?ref=CODE`).
- **Client** (`game_referral`, opcode 220 `ChaosOpcodes.referral`; `open` / `sync` / `enter {code}` out, `status` /
  `message` back): the code with Copy code, what both sides get, the code box while the account may enter one (or who
  referred it), the referred friends with level and each milestone (rewarded / waiting / no reward), this month's counts.
- **Staff:** `/referral <player>` (code, link, counts), `/referral <player>, unlink` (removes the link and the unpaid rows).
  Every link, refusal, gift and payment is in `chaos_referral_log`.
- **Tests:** `tests/referral_test.lua` (config sanity, codes, IP byte orders, IPv6 /64, payers, e-mail domains, every refusal,
  milestones, the reward decision with the account age, connection and payer, the tiers, titles, the client view), the client's `referralview_test.lua`, `website/tests/chaos_referral_test.php`.
- **Tested in game** (test server, cropped map, own DB copy): codes for a level 60 account; a code entered in game by a one-day
  old account refused for the shared IP, then (IP check off for the test) accepted with the gift and the Kindled title; level
  50 paid 25 coins and Torchbearer; level 150 with the monthly cap set to 1 waited, then was paid at the next start (Ember
  Herald, 75 coins); an account made on the website with a wrong code was refused on the form, with the right one it got a
  pending row, accepted at its first login with the gift; its level 50 waited for the cap, the account was banned, and the
  reward became void; the referrer's window showed both friends. Screenshots are not in the repository.

## Creator codes (`creator_codes.lua`, `creator_codes_core.lua`, `creator_codes_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_creator_codes.sql`; website `creator_lib.php`, `pages/creator.php`)

A streamer or content creator gets a code; a donor picks it on the website; for `supportDays` (30) every donation of that
account gives the creator `sharePct` (10, decided 2026-10-14, docs/PRICES.md) % of the donation's coins (the pack's coins, not its bonus), as
Chaos Coins in game. The donor's pack is never reduced. Owner decision 2026-10-13: paid in coins in game, not money.

- **Codes** are made on the website by an administrator (an admin panel account with a character of group `adminGroup`,
  5): code, the creator's character (its account is paid), a shown name, its own % (0 = the default), on / off. Donors
  pick a code on `page.php?plugin=chaos&p=creator` (the donate page's code field is a hook left to the store helper, see
  website/README.md "Creator codes"). The donor's own code is refused at once (self-use).
- **The game server's round** (every `pollSeconds`, 300, and at startup; `ChaosCreatorCodes.round`): (1) every credited
  donation (`chaos_coin_orders` status `credited`) of an account whose pick covers the donation's creation time gets one
  `chaos_creator_uses` row (the order id is the key: once per donation) with its share (`C.share`, at most `orderCap` 500);
  (2) every pending / waiting share is decided by `ChaosCreatorCore.decide`: **void** for the creator's own account, a
  shared connection (login IPs of every character, online IPs, the pick's IP; IPv6 by /64), a shared payer
  (`chaos_pay_payers`), a refund or chargeback (`chaos_coin_payments.reversal`, or the order ended without coins), a code
  switched off or deleted; **wait** within `holdDays` (14) of crediting (chargebacks come first), while the creator is
  banned, or when the creator's month (`monthlyCap` 5000) has no room (a share is never cut); else **paid** into the
  creator's `chaos_shop_coins` (the store's balance table; no store file is edited) and the creator is told in game.
  Every step is in `chaos_creator_log`.
- **Staff:** `/creatorcodes` (group 5: the settings and each code's paid shares), `/creatorcodes run` (a round now).
- **Install:** `install_all.py` (`files` and `sql` steps; the website's `install.sql` creates the same tables).
- **Tests:** `tests/creator_codes_test.lua` (codes, shares and caps, the pick window, IPv4 / IPv6 /64, every decision,
  the tables of the engine and SQL files), `website/tests/chaos_creator_test.php`. Live test 2026-10-14 (local site, mock provider): a code made on the website, picked on the donate page, the first donation (Vault: 10,000 + 3,000 + the capped 1,000 first bonus) credited in game, the round matched it (share 500) and voided it as the same connection as the creator (one machine).

## Character Bazaar (`bazaar.lua`, `bazaar_core.lua`, `bazaar_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_bazaar.sql`; website `bazaar_lib.php`, `pages/bazaar.php`)

Player-to-player character auctions for Chaos Coins on the website (website/README.md "Character Bazaar": listing rules,
escrow, fee, transfer). The game server's part is the lock: a character whose listing is `active` or `settling` cannot
log in.

- `bazaar.lua` onLogin: a locked character is refused (`return false`; the engine kicks it in `Player::onPlacedCreature`
  before it can act), logged as `login_refused` in `chaos_bazaar_log`. Staff characters (group >= `adminGroup`, 5) are
  never locked. Missing tables (a server without the site) lock nothing.
- The player reads why (live test 2026-10-14: the client only said "connection lost"): engine patch 0039
  `player:refuseLogin(text)` sends the client's login error box at once (anything sent the normal way is dropped with the
  kick). The text (`messages.locked`, the auction's end) is in the character's language (`Chaos.lang`, stored by the
  client's hello); a character that never told its language gets English and pt-BR together. Without the patch the text
  goes as a normal message (lost, as before). Tests: `tests/bazaar_test.lua`.
- A sweep every `sweepSeconds` (60) saves and removes a listed character that is online (a login that raced the
  listing; the website also refuses to list a character in `players_online`).
- The transfer itself is the website's: `players.account_id` changes while the character is offline and locked; the
  character leaves its guild; everything it carries goes with it (items, depot, houses it owns). A referral link does
  not follow it (the referral program tracks a character by the referred account).
- Numbers (`feePct` 10, decided 2026-10-14 at the top of the approved 5-10 range, docs/PRICES.md; 1-7 days; `minPrice` 100; `minLevel` 50; the bid step; the snipe
  minutes; `chargebackDays` 180) are in `bazaar_config.lua`, which the website reads. `ChaosBazaarCore.validate` refuses
  a fee outside 5-10 % or other days (startup and test).
- **Tests:** `tests/bazaar_test.lua` (config, fee, step, the lock against a mocked engine: active / settling locked,
  sold / cancelled / expired free, staff, off, missing tables, the sweep; the tables of the SQL, engine and website
  install files), `website/tests/chaos_bazaar_test.php`. Live test 2026-10-14 (local site): a level 300 character listed, its login refused (`login_refused` in the log; the client shows only the lost connection, not the reason), a buyout bid, the worker's transfer to the buyer's account (fee 8%, the seller paid 276 of 300) and the bought character's login on the new account.

## Mentors (`mentor.lua`, `mentor_core.lua`, `mentor_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_mentor.sql`, client `game_mentor`)

Veterans guide new characters; both get something for hunting together, nothing that adds power. Social > Mentors in the
client (opcode **194**, `ChaosOpcodes.mentor`); the website lists the mentors who opted in (website/README.md "Mentors").
Every number and text is in `mentor_config.lua`; the rules are pure functions in `mentor_core.lua` (tested by
`tests/mentor_test.lua`, which also runs `mentor.lua` against a mocked engine).

- **Mentors.** A character registers when its ACCOUNT is a veteran: a character at level 150 (`mentor.minAccountLevel`),
  100 hours of play (sum of `players.onlinetime`), 30 days old; the mentoring character itself needs level 20, so a
  veteran can mentor with a character near the apprentice's level (the bonus needs that, below). The mentor card:
  language / region, hours, a note (printable text, cut to 24 / 24 / 80), "Taking apprentices", "Show on website".
