  At most 3 active apprentices (`maxApprentices`) and 6 new ones per calendar month (`monthlyLinks`). Retire: only without
  apprentices; marks and graduates stay. A character with a mentor cannot mentor, a mentor cannot pick one.
- **Apprentices.** A character up to level 79 on an account up to 60 days old picks a mentor from the list (filters:
  class line, language / region text, online now / seen this week / any; online first, then the most graduates; full,
  closed and own-account mentors left out) or accepts an invitation (a mentor invites an online character by name; 10
  minutes; an invitation ignores "Taking apprentices", not the free place). "Looking for a mentor" sets the Party Finder
  tag. At most 3 mentors per character ever; 24 h after a dismiss or a release before the next; never the same pair twice.
- **Referral.** A referred account's first character (the one the referral tracks) gets the referrer's mentor character
  at login when it has no mentor and every check passes (`referral.autoPick`, source `referral`); the window also offers
  the referrer's mentor as a "Choose" row. It can be dismissed like any mentor.
- **Anti-abuse** (`ChaosMentorCore.linkCheck`, each refusal in `chaos_mentor_log`): not the own account; no staff (account
  type >= 2 or a character of group >= 2) on either side; nobody banned; the referral program's household rules through
  `ChaosReferral.accountFacts` (added to `referral.lua`): no shared IP (login IPs of every character, online ones, the
  website registration IP) and no shared private e-mail domain (`referral_config.lua` `publicDomains` are fine); the caps above.
- **The bonus** (apprentice only): +10% experience from monsters (`onGainExperience` callback, needs the
  `patch_base_events.py` experience dispatch like every Chaos experience bonus) and 5% less damage from monsters
  (`onHealthChange` / `onManaChange`), while: the mentor is online, in the same party, within 30 tiles on the same floor,
  not on the same IP right now, and **not over the content**: mentor level <= max(apprentice level, monster level) x 1.5 +
  20 (`overLevel`; the monster level is `bounty_pool.lua`'s, else the experience / health estimate of
  `tools/gen_bounty_pool.py`). A level 400 mentor carrying a level 40 apprentice on level 45 monsters gets nothing.
- **Mentor Marks** (per mentor character, earned only). Shared hunting: a minute in which an apprentice got the bonus
  counts (once a minute, `ChaosMentorTick`); one mark per 30 such minutes, at most 4 a day for all apprentices. Milestones,
  once per apprentice character whoever the mentor is: levels 25 / 50 / 100 (5 / 10 / 20 marks), the first sealed rift,
  finished dungeon, bounty contract, world boss reward (10 / 10 / 5 / 5; rift, bounty and world boss from a
  `ChaosLeaderboard.record` wrapper like guild.lua's, the dungeon from `chaos_dungeon_run_players`). A milestone pays only
  after 30 shared minutes on that link (`unearned` otherwise); one reached before the link is `before`. Everything respects
  300 marks per calendar month (`capped` beyond). The mentor is told at once or at the next login.
- **Graduation** at level 200: the link ends (`graduated`). With 120 shared minutes the mentor gets 50 marks and +1
  graduate (achievements Guiding Hand / Lamplighter / Keeper of the Flame at 1 / 5 / 15, titles Mentor / Seasoned Mentor /
  Master Mentor) and the apprentice 100 health and 100 mana potions and the achievement Fledged (title Fledgling);
  without, the link ends with no reward. Top Mentors in the window and the website rank by graduates.
- **Marks Shop** (`shop`, checked by `ChaosMentorCore.validate` at startup and in the test: titles, cosmetics, supplies
  only; supplies only the potions of `supplyIds`, with a weekly limit): titles Lanternbearer 40, Pathfinder 90, Wayshower 160
  (`ChaosTitles` source `mentor`); Ember Labels 100, Cinder Name 140, Soul Spark 140 (the store's cosmetics, unlocked for
  the account with `ChaosCosmetics.grant(..., "mentor")`); 50 health / 50 mana potions for 6, 3 a week each. The week is
  the shared one (Monday 06:00, `ChaosBounty.week`; `K.shopWeekStart`); it was Monday 00:00, and until
  `shopWeekGraceUntil` (19 Oct 2026 06:00) the later of both starts counts, so the switch costs nobody a purchase. Marks are
  taken with one conditional UPDATE before the delivery (given back when a cosmetic cannot be granted).
- **Party Finder.** Listings, members and applications carry the tag `mt` (`ChaosMentor.tagOf`: `mentor` while
  registered, taking apprentices and with a free place; `seeking` while "Looking for a mentor" is set and the character
  may pick one); the client shows "Mentoring" / "Looking for mentor" (`party_finder.lua` `plain`, `party_finder_core.lua`).
- **Protocol (JSON {action, data}).** Client `open`, `sync`, `list {line, lang, online}`, `register {lang, hours, note,
  accepting, public}`, `retire`, `choose {guid}`, `invite {name}`, `accept {guid}`, `decline {guid}`, `dismiss`,
  `release {guid}`, `seek {on}`, `buy {key}` (rate limited 0.5-2 s). Server `status` (`ChaosMentorCore.view`), `mentors
  {rows, filter}`, `message {text, error}`, through `Chaos.sendChunked`.
- **Opcode.** Referral's 220 is not reused: the client registers one handler per opcode and the mentor window is its own
  module. 194 is free in the reference server ("Opcode collision check"), in every Chaos script and in every client module
  of the reference client (grep for `sendExtendedOpcode`, `registerExtended*Opcode` and opcode constants; 190-199 had
  only guild wars' 197). Storages 7100360 - 7100369 (+0 "looking for a mentor").
- **State.** `chaos_mentors` (card, marks, graduates, today's minutes and marks, the month's marks), `chaos_mentor_links`,
  `chaos_mentor_milestones`, `chaos_mentor_purchases`, `chaos_mentor_log` (`sql/chaos_mentor.sql`; `mentor.lua` creates
  them at startup). Invitations live in memory. Staff: `/mentor <player>` (marks, graduates, link), `/mentor <player>, unlink`.
- **Tests:** `tests/mentor_test.lua` (config and the fairness rule, opcode and storages, every mentor / apprentice / link
  refusal, the household rules, the bonus and the over-level rule, hunting marks with the daily and monthly caps, the
  milestone and graduation decisions, the shop, the list filters, the tags, the view; `mentor.lua` against a mocked engine:
  events, the experience and damage bonus with party / floor / IP / over-level, the Party Finder tag, the leaderboard
  hook, logout), client `game_mentor/mentorview_test.lua`, `game_partyfinder/partyfinderview_test.lua` (tags),
  `website/tests/chaos_mentors_page_test.php`. The window was rendered in the Linux client with payloads built by the core
  (offline); not run against a live server.

## Town Portal (`townportal.lua`, `townportal_core.lua`, `townportal_config.lua`, spell `shared/town_portal.lua`, client `game_townportal`)

An ability, not an item: every character has it from creation (the spell "Town Portal", id 254, words `ash domh`, level 1, no mana, every
vocation; `needlearn="0"`, so existing characters have it at the next login after `register_spells.py`). The menu entries Character > Town Portal
(cast) and Character > Portal Style (window) call the same code. Numbers: `townportal_config.lua`.

- **Inside a hideout** (2026-10-16): the cast is a way out at once (`K.hideoutExit`: no channel, cooldown or pair), through
  `ChaosHideout.leave` (the spot entered from, else the home temple, else Cinderhold; never a hideout or an instance).
  The engine checks the spell's 60 s cooldown condition before the script runs, so a cast inside within a minute of
  the last portal answered "You are exhausted." (playtest 2026-10-16). Entering a hideout now lifts that condition
  (`ChaosTownPortal.liftSpellCooldown`) and leaving puts back what is left of the storage cooldown
  (`restoreSpellCooldown`); outside, the storage cooldown refuses as before. `tests/townportal_test.lua`, `tests/hideout_test.lua`.
- **Cast:** `ChaosTownPortal.cast(player)` refuses at once (reason below) or starts a 3 s channel (`castMs`, polled every 250 ms). A step or any
  damage (health change, or a mana hit from an attacker) ends it with nothing spent. At the end the rules are checked again, then the pair opens:
  a portal on the first free tile around the caster (`fieldOffsets`, action id 47810) leading to the temple of the character's town, and a return
  portal on the first free tile in rings 1..4 around the temple (action id 47811) leading to the exact tile of the cast (a creature standing there
  moves the arrival to the nearest free tile). Tiles must be walkable, no house, floor change, teleport, field or creature; two pairs never share a tile.
- **Cooldown:** 60 s from the moment the portal opens (storage `7101601` = os.time of the next cast, plus the spell cooldown condition so the action
  bar shows it). A refused or interrupted cast costs nothing.
- **Lifetime:** 5 min (`portalMinutes`, checked by a 2 s think), or when the owner steps through the return portal. A new cast closes the old pair first.
  Logging out keeps the pair until it fades.
- **Who:** the owner and the owner's party members (`partyCanUse`, at the moment of the step); others are pushed back with a message. A party
  member who uses the return portal arrives at the owner's spot and leaves the pair open; only the owner's return closes it.
- **Refused to cast:** already channelling, cooldown, tutorial island (`ChaosNewPlayer.onIsland`), arena match, world boss lobby/arena, guild siege
  (`ChaosSiege.locate`), inside a rift or omen arena, a dungeon, the Infinity Tower, pz-lock, white/red/black skull, inside a protection zone,
  and inside any other registered instance (`Chaos.inAnyInstance`, see "Shared security rules"): raid, Ember Descent, Ascended Omen, guild boss,
  battleground, Vocation Trial, ascension trial, the Scorched Marches, a hideout. Taking part in a run or standing in its slot both count, so a raid
  member cannot open a pair that lets non-member party members walk into the raid.
  The field portal refuses a pz-locked or skulled player at the step as well.
- **Instances (decision):** the portal cannot be opened inside rifts, dungeons or the tower, and so there is no pair that could point into one: the
  return portal always puts the player back on an open-world tile. (A portal opened outside stays usable while a run is going on elsewhere, but its
  target is the open world, so it can never lead into a finished run.) Leaving an instance uses its own exit, as before.
- **Temple Teleport Scroll (decision):** removed from the store (no new sales; old scrolls still work, see Store services). Starter kits that listed a
  scroll are unchanged (it is the same item).

**Portal Style.** `townportal_config.lua` `styles`: id, key, name, route, item (the portal's look: a stock teleport item of the base server), and
open / close / loop / travel effect lists. An effect entry is a `ChaosVfx` name, a `ChaosFx` name or a stock `CONST_ME_*` number, tried in order
(the last one must be a stock number, so a client without the effect art shows something). The selected id is in storage `7101600`; the style
is read at cast time and stored in the pair, so everybody sees the owner's style. A style that is no longer owned falls back to the default.
Exactly one route per style: `default` (Waygate), `store` (6, ids 1..6, `shop_config.lua` category "Portal Styles", offer `unlock = "portal_<key>"`,
owned in storage `7101610 + id`, resolved by `ChaosTownPortal.storeUnlock` from `shop_services.lua`) or `achievement` (6, ids 31..36, owned while
the character has the achievement whose `reward` is `{portal = {key, name}}` in `achievements_data.lua`, so older unlocks count too).
`ChaosTownPortalCore.validate` (run by `tests/townportal_test.lua` and printed at startup) fails a style with no route, with both, a store offer for a
non-store style, an achievement reward for a non-achievement style, or a missing effect name. No drops.

| Style | Route | Price / achievement | Look and effects |
|---|---|---|---|
| Waygate | everyone | | blue force ring; teleport_in / teleport_out |
| Emberforge Gate | store | 250 | molten lava gate; infernal_seal, fire_explosion, inferno_burst |
| Rimeglass Gate | store | 250 | ice-blue crystal gate; frost_glyph, ice_shatter, frost_ripple |

Route `boss` (ids 51 and up): owned while the account has the exclusive `portal_<key>` (`ChaosExclusives.owns`, the facts'
`bossOwned`); never sold, never an achievement reward; `how` is the window's line. See "Exclusives".

Store prices are in the range of the auras (200..300). All visuals come from items and effects already in the client pair (`things_custom12`,
`vfx_catalog.csv`); no new art. **Follow-up:** the sprite libraries R and S on the sprite-libraries branch have portal and gate effects (swirl,
arch, rune circles) that would give styles their own effect art instead of recoloured shared ones.

Protocol (opcode `ChaosOpcodes.townPortal` = 239, JSON): client -> server `open | get | select {id} | cast`; server -> client `state {open,
selected, cooldown, cooldownTotal, styles}`, `cast {ms}`, `castEnd {result}`. The client cast bar is in `game_townportal`.

Install: `register_spells.py` (already in `install_all.py`, step `spells`) installs the spell; no other installer. Client: regenerate
`gen_spell_data.py` and the spell icon sheets (`gen_all_spell_icons.py`, cell 280 is the Town Portal icon). Tests: `tests/townportal_test.lua`.
**Verified in game** (test server, cropped map): the Portal Style window (store styles "Store - N coins" with "Open the Store",
"Use this style" disabled; achievement styles locked, no store button; a locked style's `select` refused); Keybearer unlocked
by sealing the 25th rift -> Riftwalker's Gate "unlocked", selected and cast (field and return portal in its look); a store
style granted through `storeUnlock` (Emberforge) and the Waygate cast with their effects; the cast bar; an unlock while the
window is open now refreshes it at once (`achievements.lua` sends the state, `open = false`).
Not verified: a real party of two clients using the return portal while the owner is away; very crowded temples (80 return spots).

## Transmog (`transmog.lua`, `transmog_core.lua`, `transmog_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_transmog.sql`, engine patch 0019, client `game_transmog`, base patch 0030)

An equipped helmet, armor, legs, boots, weapon or shield can LOOK like another item of the same kind that the account has
unlocked. Appearance only: id, stats, name, tooltip, weight and every rule stay the item's own. Character > Transmog, or
right-click an equipped item > Transmog. Numbers and sets: `transmog_config.lua`.

- **The look is an item attribute.** Custom attribute `chaos_tmog` = server id of the look. Engine patch
  `src-patches/0019-transmog-appearance.patch` sends its client id as item custom attribute 8 (`CHAOS_ITEM_KEY_APPEARANCE`,
  after the keys of 0003) in every item packet. Client base patch `0030` draws that look in `Item::draw` and
  `Item::drawToImage`: map tiles, inventory, containers, trade, drag. The client keeps the item's own id for packets, so
  move / use / trade, which the engine checks against the real client id, are unchanged (no `game.cpp` change). A look that
  is stackable or a fluid / splash type is ignored by both sides. Decision: attribute + client drawing, not a different id
  in the packet (that would break the engine's client-id checks, the stack counts and every client module keyed on ids).
- **It travels with the item.** Moves, trades, depots and logout keep custom attributes; the market escrow keeps it through
  patch 0017 (or `chaos_tmog` in `market.lua` EXTRA_KEYS without it); the guild depot copies it (`guild_config.lua`
  `customKeys`). The 0003 version hash covers it, so tooltip caches refresh.
- **Wherever the item is drawn from server data:** tooltips add "Appearance: <look>" (`item_tooltip_core.lua` `tip.look`,
  client `tooltiplogic.lua`); Inspect Player draws the look (`tip.look`); market rows, My Offers, History and the sell picker
  draw it (`market.lua` `addLooks`: one query per page on the tip snapshot, `look` on sellable entries).
- **Kinds** (`kinds`): weapons by weapon type (sword, axe, club, distance, wand / rod, shield incl. spellbooks), armour by slot
  bit (head, armor, legs, feet). Not pickupable, stackable (throwing weapons), containers, fluids and ammunition have no kind.
  The catalogue is every item type up to `scanMaxId` with a kind, minus `exclude` / `excludeRanges` (1454 looks on the test
  server); collection progress counts it.
- **Wardrobe** (account-wide, table `chaos_transmog`): an item unlocks its look when it enters the character's inventory
  (`EventCallback.onItemMoved`, equipment or a carried container, 3 levels deep), at login (equipped items) and when the
  window opens (equipment and carried containers). Getting a transmogged item unlocks the item's own look, not its look.
- **Appearance sets** (`sets`, table `chaos_transmog_sets`): looks only the set's source unlocks (carrying such an item unlocks
  nothing). Sources: `store` (offer `{kind = "unlock", unlock = "transmog_<key>"}`, `ChaosTransmog.storeUnlock`, account-wide),
  `achievement` (owned while `ChaosAchievements.has` the named achievement; synced at window open), `season`
  (`ChaosSeasonPass.ownsTransmog(player, key)` when the season pass has that hook), `exclusive` (`ChaosTransmog.grantSet`, staff
  `/transmog`), `boss` (a rare boss drop: `exclusives.lua` calls `ChaosTransmog.grantSet`; `boss` names it for the window).
  Shipped: Falconer's Regalia (store, 300), Lionguard (store, 350), Spiritthorn (`level_500`), Rimebound (`rift_t10`),
  Arboreal (season), Arcanomancer (exclusive); the second store list Gravecloak (350, the star-less skeletal helmet, armor,
  legs, boots 26708-26711), Soulforged (400), Soulstalker (350), Mothwing (350), Cobra Regalia (300), Lionguard Arms (300),
  Grand Sanguine (350); achievement sets Thornmoth Vestments (`prof_wortcunning_100`) and Haloed Arms (`wb_heal_top_1`),
  with their own `how` line; boss sets Hellforged Visage (Kaelgor), Pyrarch Arms (Nyxareth), Deathlord Arms (Varkhul),
  Gilded Eldritch Arms (the Cinderheart). All are base server art that no monster drops and no NPC sells (checked against
  the installed base monsters and NPCs when they were picked; the test scans the repo data). `ChaosTransmogCore.validate`
  runs in the test and at startup.
- **Fee:** apply 2000 gold + 10 per item level, at most 20000 (backpack, then bank); remove free.
- **Refused:** empty slot, an item without a kind, another kind, the item's own look, the same look again, a look not
  unlocked, not enough gold.

Protocol (opcode `ChaosOpcodes.transmog` = 212, JSON, server -> client through `Chaos.sendChunked`): client -> server
`open | looks {kind} | apply {slot, look} | remove {slot} | close`; server -> client `state {open, money, fee, slots, kinds,
total, sets}`, `looks {kind, rows}`, `result {ok, text}`. API (other scripts): `ChaosTransmog.lookOf / setLook / clearLook /
isUnlocked / unlockLook / grantSet / revokeSet / ownsSet / storeUnlock / sendState`. Staff: `/transmog <character>, <set key |
all | look id>[, revoke]` (an unlock needs group 5, a revoke group 4; `Chaos.staffCommand`).

Install: the `files` and `sql` steps of `install_all.py` (no other installer). Engine: build with patches 0001-0019; client:
base patches 0001-0030. Tests: `tests/transmog_test.lua`, `tests/item_tooltip_test.lua` (key 8 in the engine, the constants and
the client), client `game_transmog/transmogview_test.lua`, `game_itemtooltip/tooltiplogic_test.lua`.
**Verified in game** (engine and Linux client built from fresh trees with the new patches, test server on the cropped map, two
clients): window, preview and apply (fee taken); the look in the inventory slot, a container, on the ground and in the trade
window of both players; picking it up from the ground and trading it (client sends the real id, the server accepts); the
receiver sees the look and only the real item enters its wardrobe; the tooltip keeps the real item with the Appearance line;
a store set granted through `storeUnlock` and an achievement set synced at open; the Collection page; market listing row
shows the look and cancelling returns the item with its look; Inspect Player draws the looks; refusal of a locked look; remove.
Store offers: category Appearances of `shop_config.lua` (Falconer's Regalia 300, Lionguard 350, not giftable), sold through
`ChaosTransmog.storeUnlock` from `shop_services.lua` `unlockEntry`; the startup notes and test warnings about them are gone.
Season set: `ChaosSeasonPass.ownsTransmog(player, key)` (`seasonpass.lua`) is true when the account's season pass holds a
reward `{kind = "transmog", key}`: the Ember Pack (and so Blaze and Inferno) holds Arboreal; synced when the window opens.
Item links in chat: the snapshot carries `tip.look`, and the tooltip icon draws it (`game_itemtooltip`, `setAppearanceId`).
**Tested in game** (cosmetics test server): Falconer's Regalia bought in the store (Owned. after), the Ember Pack granted to an
account and Arboreal owned at the next window open, a linked transmogged helmet showing the talon circlet in the other
client's link tooltip.

## Cast-time spells (`data/lib/chaos_casting.lua`, `casting.lua`, client `game_castbar`)

A spell script can have a cast time without an engine change: it builds its `onCastSpell` with
`ChaosCasting.spell({name, spellId, ms, prepare, check, fire, fx})` (`prepare(player, variant)` at the start: nil + text refuses
and nothing is spent; `check(player, ctx)` when the time is up: false + text fails and refunds; `fire(player, ctx)` the effect;
`ChaosCasting.targetCheck(player, targetId, range, attack)` is the usual "alive, attackable, same floor, in range, in sight").
The script returns true at once, so the engine takes the mana and sets the cooldowns as for any spell, and the spell supports and the
item modifiers apply as usual. The cost the engine took is stored per cast: the `cast` handler on `ChaosSpellEvents` (engine patch
0008, `Player:onSpellCast` gives the exact mana and health paid); without the events, the mana that went down by the second
dispatcher tick (after the supports' Thrift refund). The cast is polled every 100 ms (`addEvent`, so the spell supports' cast
context follows it to the effect). It is interrupted when the caster moves (any position change, floor included), gets a paralysis
that was not there at the start (`interruptOnParalyze`), is stunned by an Iron Palm (`monk_combat.lua` interrupts it, result `paralysed`), casts another spell of the cast's group (an attack spell or rune: a
`cast` event with that group; a heal, a healing rune or a support spell does not interrupt it, see "Cooldown channels";
without the spell events of patch 0008 this one interrupt is missing), opens a town portal (`townportal.lua` calls `ChaosCasting.interrupt`), dies (`death` event), logs out (`logout`) or cancels
(client). An interrupt or a failed check gives back the stored mana and health and the spell's own cooldown condition (replaced by a
100 ms one so the client's icon is told; the group cooldown stays), exactly once (`cast.refunded`; a refund asked before the
cost is known is paid when it is known). Damage taken does not interrupt. A new cast-time spell while one is cast replaces it
(refunded); one cannot start while a town portal channels. Numbers: `ChaosCasting.cfg` (poll, effect interval, paralysis switch,
cast time 200..5000 ms).

Extended opcode 231 (`ChaosOpcodes.castbar`), JSON `{action, data}`: server -> client `start {s serial, n name, ms, id}`,
`end {s, r result, t text}` (`done` / `moved` / `paralysed` / `spell` / `portal` / `died` / `logout` / `cancel` / `failed`),
`other {c creature id, n, ms}` and `otherEnd {c, r}` to the players who see the caster; client -> server `cancel` only (rate
limited). The client never completes a cast: the server's timer does, so a client can only cancel (refunded like moving). Opcode
231 was free (224 is the energy shield's, 239 the Town Portal's). Spells with a cast time and their numbers:
`data/spells/README.md` "Cast times". Tests: `tests/casting_test.lua` (mocked engine: completion, every interrupt, refund once,
the fallback cost, target checks, the client cannot complete). Tested in game (2026-10-10): completion, moving, a paralysis, another
spell, death, cancel, target out of range at the end, the Town Portal channel on the same bar.

## Spellbook (`spellbook.lua`)
Character > Spellbook in the client menu opens the client window `game_spellbook` on extended opcode 219 (`ChaosOpcodes.spellbook`). The list is read from the running server's own files, so renamed stock spells, the Chaos spells and anything added later show up without a client update:
- `data/spells/spells.xml`: every `<instant>`, `<rune>` and `<conjure>` (name, words, level, magic level, mana, soul, cooldown, group, premium, range, vocations, rune item id). Monster spells (words starting with `#`) and house spells (`house/` scripts) are skipped.
- `data/spells/scripts/<script>` is read as text, never run: element (`COMBAT_PARAM_TYPE`, `doAreaCombat`/`doTargetCombat`/`damageTarget` arguments), kind (damage, heal, buff, summon, conjure, utility), area (the largest `createCombatArea(...)`: an `AREA_*` table of the spell library, an inline table literal, which is loaded only when it holds nothing but digits, commas and braces, or a local table of the same script), scaling (magic level, skill x weapon attack, distance skill x weapon attack). Chaos spells use the first comment line of their script (`-- <Name>: <description>`); stock spells get a generated one ("Single-target fire damage.", "Fire damage in front of you (wave).", "Heals you and cures paralysis.", "Conjures 4 x 'searing orb rune'.").
- Parsed once at startup when the `AREA_*` tables already exist, otherwise on the first Character > Spellbook; `/spells reload` (staff) parses again after a spell change. A player can open it once every 2 seconds.
- Protocol (JSON `{action, data}`): `open` {vocation, level, magicLevel, total, chunks, vocationNames [{id, name}]}, then `spells` {index, spells [...]} until all are sent (about 6.5 KB of JSON per packet), then `done` {total}. A spell: name, words, level, maglevel, mana, manaPercent, soul, cooldown and groupCooldown (ms), group, type, element, target (`single`/`area`/`self`/`front`), center (`caster`/`target`), area (matrix, 1 = hit, 2 = centre, 3 = centre and hit; `front` spells drawn facing north), range, description, scaling, vocations (ids), premium (false for all since "Free spells"; the client no longer shows it), rune and runeClientId. The client sends `open` to ask for the same answer.
- With the reference spell set (234 player spells) that is 14 packets, about 76 KB.
- Descriptions of stock buff / utility spells (2026-10-18): the script's literal `CONDITION_PARAM_TICKS` / `setTicks` (a number or a product such as `6 * 60 * 1000`) is appended as "for 33 s" / "for 6 min"; an ATTRIBUTES condition names the stats it raises (`CONDITION_PARAM_STAT_MAGICPOINTS`, `SKILL_*`) and a script that calls `getParty` says "you and your party members"; Levitate, Find Person, Magic Rope, the challenges, Cancel Invisibility, Creature Illusion and Recovery have fixed texts (`Book.FALLBACK_TEXT`). A duration read from a config table is not guessed: the text then has no number. Chaos spells keep the header comment of their script as the description.
- Cache check (2026-10-16): `open`, `done` also carry `sig` (a checksum of the packed list, cached per display-scale factor), `open` carries `learned` (names of the `needlearn` spells the player learned) and spells carry `id` (spellid) and `needLearn`. The client sends `open {have = sig}`; when it is the current list only `open {unchanged = true, chunks = 0}` and `done` go out, without the 2 s throttle. An old client (no `have`) gets the full list as before.
- Spellbook items: using a stock spellbook (the base action `data/scripts/actions/others/spellbook.lua`, hooked by `tools/patch_base_spellbook.py`, install_all step `events`) or a Chaos set spellbook (27 gear-set and 10 themed ids, registered by `spellbook.lua`) sends `show` to a client that has spoken opcode 219 this login (its background fetch after login, `open {prefetch = true}`, which the new-player tutorial does not count); the client opens the window. A client without the window keeps the stock "Spells for Level n" text (`ChaosSpellbook.spellText`). Test: `tools/patch_base_spellbook_test.py`.
- The client window has a second drop-down All types / Attack / Support and an "AoE" tag (pt-BR "Área") on attack spells that hit an area, derived from the spell's `type` (damage = attack; healing, buffs, summons, conjures, utility = support; no type: the XML `group`), `target` (`area` / `front`) and `area` matrix (more than one hit tile): `spellbook_core.lua`, `spellbook_core_test.lua`.
- `server/tests/spellbook_test.lua` (fixtures in `tests/fixtures/spellbook/`) covers the XML parsing, named, inline and local areas, refusal of unsafe or malformed inline tables, the classification and descriptions, the chunking and the talkaction/opcode flow. Not run on a server.
- Chaos attack spells (O184, O185, 2026-10-24): a spell of the attack group with a `chaos/` script is always typed damage (the text scan misses helpers such as `ChaosSpell.weaponStrike`, and a spell typed Utility fell out of the client's Attack filter). A scripted pack hit with no `createCombatArea` takes its area from `data/scripts/chaos/spellbook_areas_config.lua` (shape and radius per spell name) or, for the attack kit, from `attack_kit_config.lua`, so its target, centre, grid and AoE tag show the pack. `tests/spellbook_areas_test.lua` checks all 99 Chaos attack spells against `rotation_model.csv` (2+ targets of the pack: an area; one target: none). Client: `game_spellbook/spellbook_classes_test.lua`, Learned + Attack gives each of the 21 classes its 10 attack spells.

## Multi-client (`multiclient.lua`)

At most `Chaos.multiClient.maxPerIp` (2) characters per IP can be online; a further login is refused with a popup
(the base server's own anti-mc script allows 4, the lower limit wins). While a character has another character online
from its IP it cannot queue for dungeons (`dungeons.lua` entry check), start or join the Infinity Tower
(`infinitytower_run.lua`) or attack players (EventCallback onTargetCombat; the Chaos spells that deal damage from
their script repeat the check in `ChaosSpell.canAttack`). A second character cannot log in while the first is inside a
dungeon run or the tower. Gamemasters and up are exempt; `Game.setStorageValue(7100990, 1)` switches the blocks off
(not the login limit). Tested with two live clients on one IP: spells did 0 damage to the other character, the tower
refused entry, a third login was refused.
The IP is the player's own one behind the gateways too: engine patch 0025 takes it from the gateway's PROXY header
(see "Gateways and the PROXY protocol"; tested: 5 bots from one address through HAProxy, 2 got in).

## Weapon styles (`weapon_styles.lua`, `tools/two_handed.py`)

- Two-handed weapons (swords, axes, clubs, bows, crossbows) attack 1.5x slower and hit harder: a two-handed sword, axe or club
  of one tier deals 1.07x the damage per second of one hand + shield at every level, a launcher still x1.6 (owner debug
  item 47, 2026-10-17: the flat x1.6 of the two-handed melee weapons was +28% at level 8 and +13% from level 75;
  `weapon_styles.lua` now multiplies by the factor of the wielder's level, 1.34 at level 8, 1.52 from 100:
  `weapon_balance_core.lua`, `weapon_balance_config.lua` written by `tools/weapon_sim.py`, numbers and the open launcher
  decision in server/data/spells/README.md "Weapon damage per second"). Run `python3 -I server/tools/two_handed.py
  <server>/data` once: it raises the `attackspeed` of the two-handed weapons in items.xml (2000 -> 3000 ms, 1800 -> 2700
  ms; idempotent). The extra damage is applied by `weapon_styles.lua` to weapon hits only (spells, runes and wands are not
  affected; a wand or rod hit gets only the magic level factor of "Weapon damage scales with skills").
- Bows splash: creatures around the target take 50% of the hit (normal PvP / protection zone rules). Crossbows hit only
  their target. Which kind a launcher is comes from `data/lib/chaos_archery_config.lua` (bows and crossbows fire without
  ammunition: "Infinite arrows and quivers" below).

## Weapon damage scales with skills (`weapon_skill_core.lua`, `weapon_skill_config.lua`, `weapon_styles.lua`)

Owner 2026-10-20: "faça o dano das armas/auto attack escalar com as skills dos players". Audit of every auto attack (the
base engine is TFS 1.4.2; no src-patch touches `weapons.cpp`'s damage):

| Weapon type | Classes | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| sword, axe, club | Warrior, Juggernaut, Berserker, Thief line, Templar line, Monk with a staff | engine `Weapons::getMaxWeaponDamage`: `level / 5 + (skill / 4 + 1) x attack / 3 x 1.03`, the best melee skill ("One melee skill") | unchanged: the skill term is 79-94% of the hit at levels 50 .. 1000 |
| bow, crossbow, throwing | Ranger line, Thief line (stars) | the same formula with the distance skill (min hit ceil(level / 5)) | unchanged |
| fist | Monk line, Open Hand Creed | the same formula with the fist skill; `monk_combat.lua` rescales attack 7 to the Monk's fist attack, the fist skill kept | unchanged |
| wand, rod | Mystic line, Necromancer line | **flat**: a uniform roll over weapons.xml `min .. max` (`WeaponWand::getWeaponDamage`), no skill, no magic level | **x the magic level factor** |

So the physical weapons already scaled with the skill (+10 skill is +20% damage at level 50, +8% at 300, +5% at 1000, see server/data/spells/README.md
"Weapon damage and skills"); only the wands and rods did not, although docs/CLASSES.md said they "use the magic level".
Now `weapon_styles.lua` (the `onHealthChange` of weapon hits; a wand hit has the melee origin in this engine) multiplies
a wand or rod hit by `ChaosWeaponSkill.wandFactor(level, magic level)`:

    factor = (magic level + 20) / (typical magic level of the level + 20), clamped to 0.5 .. 2.0

The typical magic level (`weapon_skill_config.lua` `typical.magic`) is the C4 measurement's caster magic level
(`rotation_sim.py` ANCHORS: 60 at level 100, 100 at 300, 120 at 600, 140 at 1000) starting from 0 at level 8, so a
character at the typical magic level of its level, and a new character, hit exactly as before: no balance jump. +10% magic
level is about +8% damage at level 300 (the same slope the engine gives the skill of a weapon). The magic level is the
effective one (equipment included), like the skill of a weapon hit. Spells (also a scripted weapon strike, storage
7100028) are not touched. A wand no longer goes through the two-handed / launcher style factor (no stock wand is two-handed;
the factor was meant for swords, axes, clubs and launchers only).

No engine build, no install step: a reload of the scripts is enough. Numbers: `python3 -I server/tools/weapon_sim.py
--skills`. Tests: `tests/weapon_skill_test.lua` (the core), `tests/melee_skill_test.lua` (the hit through
`weapon_styles.lua` against a mocked player), `tools/weapon_sim_test.py` (the report: a typical stat deals what it did,
0.8x / 1.2x the stat is clearly less / more for every type). Not measured in game. The item tooltip shows no wand damage
(the engine does not give weapons.xml `min` / `max` to Lua), so nothing there changed; the "Estimated DPS" of melee and
distance weapons already uses the skill.

## Auto attack power (`weapon_power_core.lua`, `weapon_power_config.lua`, `weapon_styles.lua`)

Owner 2026-10-23: "parece que auto attack nao esta escalando com a skill e lvl. ele esta muito fraco. reveja a formula dele
por favor?" Audit (the base engine is TFS 1.4.2 and no src-patch touches `Weapons::getMaxWeaponDamage`):

* **Old formula.** Melee and distance: max hit = `level / 5 + ((skill / 4 + 1) x (attack / 3) x 1.03) / stance factor`, the
  hit a bell curve over `0 .. max` (a launcher `ceil(level / 5) .. max`), then the two-handed / launcher style factor of
  `weapon_balance_config.lua` (launchers x1.6) and the best-melee-skill rule. Wand and rod: the flat `min .. max` of
  weapons.xml x `(magic level + 20) / (typical magic level + 20)`. Nothing else is level based.
* **Why it feels weak.** The level term is `level / 5`: 3% of the hit at level 1000. Everything else is skill x gear attack,
  and both flatten out: the typical skill is 110 at level 300 and 140 from 1000, the gear's attack 55 at 300 and 65 at
  1000 (`install_gear_sets.py` CURVES; ammunition no longer adds to a launcher). A class's spells keep growing with the level
  (`rotation_sim.py`: a Ranger's rotation is x4 from level 300 to 2000, its crossbow auto attack x2.3). The skill term is
  linear in the skill, so +10 skill at skill 140 is +5%: training the skill barely shows. Result in the model (single target,
  typical skill, no class factor, no tree, no armour): melee 41-43% of a Warrior's spell rotation from level 300 to 2000 (it
  was never the problem), a crossbow or bow 33% of a Ranger's at 300, 28% at 500, 24% at 1000, 19% at 2000, a wand 9-10% of
  a Mystic's from level 100 on. Monster armour (25-100, the stock formula, taken off every physical hit) bites the small
  hits of low levels hardest.
* **New.** Two multipliers on top of the engine hit, applied in the `onHealthChange` of `weapon_styles.lua` to auto attacks
  (a spell's scripted weapon strike, storage 7100028, is left out):
  * level factor, `ChaosWeaponPower.levelFactor(kind, level)`: kind `melee` (sword, axe, club), `distance` (bow, crossbow) or
    `wand` (wand, rod). Linear between the levels of `weapon_power_config.lua`, written by `python3 -I server/tools/weapon_sim.py
    --power --write` (CI `--power --check`). It lifts the kind to **a share of the single-target spell rotation of its
    reference class** and never cuts: melee 30% of a Warrior's (already 41-43%: factor 1 everywhere), distance 30% of a
    Ranger's (1.00 up to level 400, 1.07 at 500, 1.28 at 1000, 1.60 at 2000), wand 15% of a Mystic's (1.00 at level 50, 1.69
    from 100, 1.74 at 2000). Target used: 25-35% of the rotation for weapon classes (30%), 15% for the casters' wands (the
    measured tables had them at 13-23% of a caster's total).
  * skill factor, `ChaosWeaponPower.skillFactor(level, skill)` = `(skill / typical skill of the level) ^ 0.5`, clamped to
    0.7 .. 1.6 (`weapon_power_config.lua` `skill`), for melee (the best melee skill) and launchers (distance skill). 1 at the
    typical skill, so the balance numbers stand; +10 skill at level 1000 is now +9.3% instead of +5.6%, +28 skill +26.7%
    instead of +15.7% (table in server/data/spells/README.md "Auto attack power"). A wand keeps the magic level factor of
    "Weapon damage scales with skills".
* Fists (kind `fist`: the Monk's bare hands and fist weapons, applied in `monk_combat.lua`): the level factor is 1.00 (the
  Monk line is at 53-62% of its rotation already, target 30%); the skill factor applies with the fist skill. Not touched:
  spells, runes, conditions, procs. The tooltip's "Estimated
  DPS" (`weapon_dps_core.lua`) includes both factors when `weapon_power_core.lua` is loaded (`item_tooltip.lua` loads it).
* To retune: change `POWER_KINDS` (share, reference class) or `SKILL_POWER` in `tools/weapon_sim.py`, run `--power --write`.
  A class or spell change moves the rotation numbers, `--power --check` (CI) then asks for a new config.
* Live server: the `files` step and a restart (the scripts are read at start). No database or client change. Not run in game.
  Tests: `tests/weapon_power_test.lua` (config shape, factors, a hit scales with skill and level, the tooltip estimate),
  `tools/weapon_sim_test.py`, `tests/archery_test.lua` (the hit through `weapon_styles.lua`).

## Estimated DPS (`weapon_dps_core.lua`, `item_tooltip_core.lua` `T.dpsRow`)

Owner item 79 (2026-10-18): "Faça um medidor de DPS pra cada arma. Pode ser estimado." The tooltip of a sword, axe, club or
distance weapon (bows and crossbows included) in the inventory or a container has a base row **Estimated DPS: ~N** under "Your Attack
Interval". It is an estimate of the auto attack on a target that does not defend, the model `tools/weapon_sim.py` checks the styles with:

- max hit = round(level / 5 (integer) + ((skill / 4 + 1) x (attack / 3) x 1.03) / attack factor), the engine's `Weapons::getMaxWeaponDamage`, attack factor 1 (offensive stance);
- mean hit = (min + max) / 2, min 0 for melee and ceil(level / 5) for a launcher;
- hit = mean hit x the style factor of `weapon_styles.lua` (`ChaosWeaponBalance.hitFactor`: two-handed melee, bow, crossbow);
- DPS = hit x hit chance (launchers: the item's `hitchance`, else 100%) / "Your Attack Interval" in seconds, x the display scale factor of the character's level (like every combat number).

Inputs: the item's attack (a rarity roll or a unique writes it as an attribute), the viewer's level, best melee skill (one melee skill)
or distance skill (`item_tooltip.lua` puts them in `opts.wielder`), the interval of the tooltip (vocation, dexterity, attack speed cap).
Left out: critical hits, modifiers of the item, passive tree and gems, resistances, spells, runes, wands and rods (magic level
damage) and the fist. The row is not shown for a linked or inspected item (no viewer). The client caches a tooltip by item id and
version, so after a skill or level change the number refreshes when the item is asked for again (the same as "Your Attack
Interval"). Tests: `tests/weapon_dps_test.lua`, `tests/item_tooltip_test.lua`, client `tooltiplogic_test.lua`. Not checked live.

## Item charges (`loot.lua` `L.restoreCharges`, `charges_look.lua`, `charges_look_core.lua`)

Owner item 80 (2026-10-18): "cargas em amuletos não estão aparecendo" and "os amuletos com charges dropam com 1 charge só".
- **Drop with 1 charge.** The engine creates a non-stackable item that has charges with the *count* it was given as its charges
  (`Item::Item`), and a monster loot entry creates its item with count 1. `loot.lua` step 1c (`L.restoreCharges`, after the stock loot
  and the extra rolls, before the gear steps) sets every such item of the fresh corpse, bags included, to the item type's full charges.
  Items with fewer charges than the type and stackable items are only touched in a fresh corpse, so a used item is never refilled.
  Items other scripts create with `Game.createItem(id, 1)` or `addItem(id, 1)` (shops, quest rewards, ground loot) still get
  1 charge: pass the item type's charges as the count there. Test: `tests/loot_charges_test.lua`.
- **Charges not shown.** The engine writes "(that has N charges left)" only for types with `showcharges` in items.xml. The Look text
  now ends with "It has N charges left (of M)." for any non-stackable item with charges (`charges_look.lua`, an `onLook` callback at
  index 125, skipped when the engine text already has it). The rich tooltip already had "Charges: n of max" (`T.chargeInfo`).
  Test: `tests/charges_look_test.lua`. Not checked live.
- **Charges live while training** (owner 2026-10-20: "atualize as charges dos itens de training em tempo real"; an Exercise wand in
  training kept "Charges: 500" in its tooltip). The stock `exercise_weapons.lua` takes a charge with `setAttribute`, and the engine
  sends nothing for that. Protocol 10.98 has no charges in an item packet either (`NetworkMessage::addItem` writes a count only for
  stackables, fluids and splashes), so only the tooltip shows them. `patch_base_events.py` step 20 (v2) now calls
  `item:sendUpdate()` (engine patch 0003) after every charge: the client gets the item again, with no equip / de-equip event for a
  weapon held in a hand and no reset. Without that method it falls back to the step's first version, a transform to the same id
  with the new count. A file patched by the first version is upgraded in place. The client (`game_itemtooltip`) drops a cached
  tooltip with counted charges whenever its slot gets the item again and asks again when it is the hovered one; the plate stays
  until the answer, one small request per training hit while hovered (budget 12, 6 per second). Tests:
  `tools/exercise_charges_patch_test.py` (runs the patched lines under luajit and lua5.3), `tooltiplogic_test.lua`. Not checked live.

## One melee skill (`melee_skill_core.lua`, `melee_skill.lua`, `weapon_styles.lua`, `add_vocations.py`, client `game_simpleskills`)

Owner debug item 46 (2026-10-17): "Simplificar skills: melee, ranged, magic, wand e shielding. Itens de melee servem a todas as
classes de melee, e assim por diante." The skills of the game are **Melee, Ranged, Magic (wand), Shielding** (and Fist Fighting
for the Monk line). What is done without an engine patch, and what is not:

| Owner's skill | What it is on this engine | Done |
|---|---|---|
| **Melee** | sword + club + axe (the engine keeps three) | one skill by rule: a hit, a melee spell and the training use the **best of the three** |
| **Ranged** | distance fighting (bows, crossbows, throwing weapons, shurikens) | unchanged; shown as "Ranged" |
| **Magic** | magic level | unchanged |
| **Wand** | wands and rods hit by magic level, they have no skill of their own | nothing to merge; the skills window row reads "Magic / Wand" |
| **Shielding** | shielding | unchanged |
| Fist Fighting | the Monk line's bare hands | unchanged; shown for the Monk, Shadowfist and Iron Sage only |

- **The hit** (`weapon_styles.lua`, the one `onHealthChange` the weapon styles already have): a sword, axe or club hit
  (origin melee) is multiplied by `maxHit(best skill) / maxHit(the weapon's own skill)` of the engine's formula (the attack of
  the item with a rarity roll, the stance factor from `getFightMode`, the level term): a Warrior with sword 100 who picks up an
  axe hits as with sword 100, not as with axe 10. Effective levels (items, tree) count, the best of the three. The strikes of the
  spells (`ChaosSpell.weaponStrike`: Blade Flurry, Iaijutsu, Shadow Step) are worked out with the best skill already and mark
  storage 7100028 (`Chaos.storage.weaponStrike`) during the call, so the rule is not applied to them a second time. Spells:
  `ChaosSpell.meleeSkillLevel` (`_common.lua`; Blade Flurry, the shurikens, the Monk's staff strikes, the Templar's strikes
  already used `bestMeleeSkill`).
- **The training** (`melee_skill.lua`, `EventCallback.onGainSkillTries` at index 2, after the class lock and before the
  training multiplier and the island guard): tries of the sword, club or axe skill go to the best of the three
  (`ChaosMeleeSkill.routeTarget`); a tie keeps them where they are. The vocations' three multipliers are equal now
  (`chaos_vocations*.xml`: the Thief line sword 1.1, club and axe 1.3 -> 1.1; the Monk line sword and axe 1.3 -> 1.1; the Templar
  line axe 1.2 -> 1.1), so no skill is slower to level. **Saved characters lose nothing**: the three skills keep their stored
  values and tries, only the weaker two stop growing; the best one is what counts. The exercise weapons (sword, axe, club) are one
  melee weapon since 2026-10-23, for every melee class ("Training weapons").
- **Items by group, not by type** (`add_vocations.py` step 3, run by `install_all.py` and safe to run again on an installed
  server; `install_gear_sets.py` FITS the same): every sword, axe and club, one- or two-handed, that lists vocations is open to
  the Warrior, Thief, Monk and Templar lines (the weapon lists and the hand equip events); the Berserker stays two-handed only
  (the class rule). Armour, shields, launchers, wands and rods keep their lists. Tested: `tools/add_vocations_melee_test.py`.
- **The skills window** (client `game_simpleskills`, no base patch): the club and axe rows are hidden, the sword row reads
  "Melee" with the best of the three and its percent, "Distance Fighting" reads "Ranged", the magic level "Magic / Wand", the
  Fist row only for the Monk line. Tested: `simpleskills_logic_test.lua`; the widget code is not tested without a client.
- **Not done: a merged skill in the engine, and the stock Warrior skill spells.** The base spells (Bonebreaker, Reaver's
  Spin, Earthbreaker, Scything Arc, Butcher's Gyre, ...) get the skill and the attack from the engine by the weapon in hand
  (`Player::getWeaponSkill`): they still use the skill of the weapon's own type. The Chaos spells and every weapon hit use the best.

**Engine patch proposal "attack at once" (no number yet, not written: the engine source is not in this repository, nothing here compiles it).** One
change in `src/player.cpp` makes all of the above native and lets `weapon_styles.lua` drop its multiplier:
1. `Player::getWeaponSkill(const Item*)`: for `WEAPON_SWORD`, `WEAPON_CLUB` and `WEAPON_AXE` return the largest of
   `getSkillLevel(SKILL_SWORD)`, `getSkillLevel(SKILL_CLUB)` and `getSkillLevel(SKILL_AXE)` (the effective levels). Weapons, the
   stock skill spells and `Weapons::getMaxWeaponDamage` all read it.
2. `Player::addSkillAdvance(skills_t, uint64_t)`: a melee skill's tries go to the highest melee skill (what `melee_skill.lua`
   does from Lua), so the three never drift apart again.
3. `IOLoginData::loadPlayer`: after the skills are read, set the three melee skills to the highest level, tries and percent
   (idempotent, once per login; nothing is lost, the lower two are not used any more).
4. `ProtocolGame::AddPlayerSkills`: send the highest melee skill in the club, sword and axe slots, so a client without
   `game_simpleskills` shows one number three times (the module can then drop its max).
5. `CONDITION_PARAM_SKILL_SWORD / AXE / CLUB`: the bonuses of the three added together for the melee skill would triple the
   "+2 to every melee skill" items (Hornsworn Helm): keep the maximum of the three, as now.
Order: after 0047. The Lua rescale and the training callback then become no-ops and can be removed in the same change.
A full rename (a fourth stored `SKILL_MELEE`, a new column, a client protocol change) is not worth it: the three stored
skills cost nothing and the saves, the highscores and the exercise weapons keep working.

### Skill names in messages (src-patch 0065, `tests/skill_message_names_patch_test.lua`)

Owner report 2026-10-23 (a screenshot of "You advanced to axe fighting level 43."): the skills window shows one Melee row, the
messages still named the stock skills. The text comes from the engine: `Player::addSkillAdvance` and `Player::addSkillTries`
("You advanced to {skill} level {n}."), `Player::removeSkillTries` ("You were downgraded to ...") and `Player::setSkill*` ("Your
{Skill} skill changed from level ...") all called `getSkillName` (`tools.cpp`). Src-patch 0065 adds `getSkillMessageName` and uses it
in those four places only:

| Skill (engine) | Message name | Skills window |
|---|---|---|
| sword, club, axe fighting | melee | Melee |
| distance fighting | ranged | Ranged |
| fist fighting (Monk, Shadowfist, Iron Sage) | fist fighting | Fist Fighting |
| magic level | magic level | Magic / Wand |
| shielding, fishing, crafting skills | unchanged | unchanged |

The same names for every class: a Warrior, Thief, Templar or Monk with a staff advances "melee"; an unarmed Monk "fist fighting"; a
Ranger "ranged". The training goes to the best of the three melee skills ("One melee skill"), so a level-up message names the one
number the window shows. `getSkillName` itself is not changed: the item look texts read it, and `melee_skill_look.lua` rewrites
"club fighting +2, sword fighting +2, axe fighting +2" to "melee +2" from those names. **A server rebuild is needed** (C++); the patch
applies after 0064. The engine's messages are English only (the server has no translation of "You advanced to magic level N." or of
"Regenerating Stamina."); the Lua messages that name a skill already use the Chaos names. Not touched: the quiver's "Distance Fighting"
modifier label (`chaos_archery_config.lua`) and the passive tree's single-skill nodes.

### Melee and Ranged on equipment (`tools/patch_melee_skill.py`, `melee_skill_look.lua`, `tests/melee_skill_patch_test.lua`)

Beta report 2026-10-22: equipment still said and gave "+2 Club", "+2 Axe", "+2 Sword" or "Distance". The engine keeps
three melee skills and a bonus raised only its own, so a club bonus helped only a player whose best skill was club.
Now a melee bonus raises all three, so it raises the best one, the player's Melee:
- **Stock items** (`items.xml`, step `meleeskill`, right before `sql`): an item with any of skillSword, skillAxe,
  skillClub gets all three at the highest of them (181 items on the beta base copy). Fist and distance stay.
- **Rolled modifiers** (the base `base_rarity.lua` onEquip, same step): a rarity_swordSkill, rarity_axeSkill or
  rarity_clubSkill modifier sets all three skill parameters of its condition. Two melee modifiers add up. This covers
  the stock roll, the orbs and the uniques (their `skillSword` / `skillAxe` / `skillClub` keys are these attributes).
- **New rolls**: `C.candidates` rolls the sword key only (club and axe are `noRoll`, kept to read older items) and never
  a second melee modifier on one item. The Codex lists one "Melee Skill" modifier.
- **Item sets**: `skill_melee` (and the older `skill_sword`, `skill_axe`, `skill_club`) raises all three
  (`S.MELEE`); Bloodsworn's 6-piece bonus is `skill_melee = 3`.
- **Labels**: the modifier labels (`C.skills`), the tooltip's base stats (`T.SKILL_LABELS`: one "Melee" row with the
  highest of the three) and the set texts say "Melee" and "Ranged". The engine's look text is rewritten by
  `melee_skill_look.lua` (`M.lookText`): "club fighting +2, sword fighting +2, axe fighting +2" is "melee +2",
  "distance fighting" is "ranged". Fist fighting and shielding stay.

Not changed: the passive tree's single-skill nodes (`passivetree_data.lua`, sword or club nodes) still raise their own
skill; the market's modifier filter still names the sword, axe and club keys apart.

## Training weapons (`exercise_core.lua`, `exercise_config.lua`, `exercise_training.lua`, `tools/patch_exercise_weapons.py`, `tests/exercise_test.lua`)

Owner 2026-10-23 ("reveja os itens de training. o monk não pode usar nenhum. axe, sword e club podem ser trocados por um de
melee"; ROADMAP O125).

**What was wrong.** The base server has 21 exercise weapons (sword, axe, club, bow, rod, wand, shield in three charge tiers: 500,
1800 and 14400), used on an exercise dummy. Its script `actions/scripts/other/exercise_weapons.lua` lists the vocations of each
weapon, and `patch_base_classes.py` had given the classes lists of those. The Monk got only the club one, which trains the club
skill; but a Monk hits and casts with **fist fighting** (`monk_combat.lua`, `kindled_breath.lua`, `chi_ward.lua`, `mantra_of_stone.lua`
all read `SKILL_FIST`), so nothing a Monk could use trained anything it uses (and the melee reroute of `melee_skill.lua` sent the
club tries to the best of sword / club / axe, not to fist). The Monk could not train its shielding either. The Templar (magic
level: Radiant Rebuke, Thorns, Penitent's Wrath) had no rod or wand, and shielding was open to the Warrior and Templar lines only
(the Ranger, Mystic, Thief, Monk and Necromancer lines have a shielding multiplier too). The Monk's spells use fist fighting, never
the magic level, so it gets no rod or wand. The
sword, axe and club weapons were three items for one skill (since "One melee skill").

**The weapons now** (`exercise_config.lua`: `kinds`, `items`, `lines`):

| Kind | Items (500 / 1800 / 14400) | Classes | Trains |
|---|---|---|---|
| melee | sword 27732 / 27738 / 27744 (club 27734 / 27740 / 27746 works the same) | Warrior, Thief, Templar lines | the best of sword / club / axe (one melee skill) |
| fist | 27733 / 27739 / 27745 (the ids of the old exercise axe), chests 27762 / 27769 / 27776 | Monk line only | **fist fighting** |
| ranged | bow 27735 / 27741 / 27747 | Ranger, Thief lines | distance |
| rod, wand | 27736 / 27742 / 27748 and 27737 / 27743 / 27749 | Mystic, Necromancer, Templar lines | magic level |
| shield | 27758 / 27759 / 27760 | every class | shielding |

Every class line has a weapon for every skill it uses (`tests/exercise_test.lua` walks the 21 vocations). The melee weapon
trains the **best** melee skill, not the skill of its own look: the stage rate (x5 below 51, x3 to 100, x2 to 200, then the server
rate) is that of the skill that gets the tries, so a character with a weak sword and a strong axe is not trained at the weak
skill's fast rate (the old script did that for any weapon whose skill was low). `melee_skill.lua` would have rerouted the tries to
the best skill anyway, but after the wrong multiplier. A Monk who wields a staff still trains fist: fist is the skill its spells use.

**The Monk's own weapon (owner 2026-10-28: "monk também não tem training weapon").** What was wrong: nothing was broken in the
code (a Monk using the melee weapon trained fist fighting, `exercise_test.lua` walked it), but the store sold one "Exercise Melee
Weapon" with a sword look and a line in its text, so no offer, chest or item looked like the Monk's, and the Monk saw a sword.
Now the Monk line has a **fist** kind: Exercise Fist Weapon (500), Durable (1800) and Lasting (14400) in the store, same prices
as the others (25 / 75 / 450), text "Trains fist fighting. Monk line.". The melee offers no longer name the Monk and the melee
kind is closed to the Monk line. **No new item id, sprite or chest script:** the fist weapon lives on the item ids of the
retired exercise axe (weapons 27733 / 27739 / 27745, chests 27762 / 27769 / 27776), whose base chest script and charges already
work; `patch_exercise_weapons.py` (step `exercise`) renames them (`base_item_names.csv`), describes them and gives the three weapons
the look of the Monk's first fist weapons (items.otb client ids 33654 / 33655 / 33656: wraps, cestus, ember knuckles; the chests keep
the chest look; needs the client pair of `install_fist_weapons.py`, which every client has). **Nothing bought is lost**
(`exercise_config.lua` `tiers`, `E.convertTo(itemId, vocationId)`, tests in `exercise_test.lua`): on first use a sword or club
weapon in a Monk's hands turns into the fist weapon of its tier, and an old exercise axe (the fist weapon now) in the hands of
any other class turns into the sword one, charges kept; chests bought before open as before (an old axe chest gives a fist
weapon, which a Warrior turns into a sword one). The Exercise Roulette pool is unchanged (15 chests); a Monk who wins a melee
chest gets the fist chest or the shield chest of the tier (`roulette_exercise_config.lua` `chests`, the fist ids are not retired
any more). The client helper's Exercise list shows the fist weapon in place of the axe. `skill_model.lua` reads the fist offers
(`kindOfName`): 7.5 to 18 coins per hunting hour (Monk), inside the same bounds. Deploy: `install_all.py SERVER_DIR --only
itemnames,exercise,itemprices` (the admin app's Update button runs every step) and a restart; no SQL, no client change besides the
helper label. Not run on a live engine: check in game that the three fist chests give the wraps / cestus / knuckles weapon and that a
Monk trains fist on a dummy with it.
**Old items.** The store, the NPCs and the Ancestral Store no longer sell the axe and club chests (27762, 27763, 27769, 27770,
27776, 27777); chests bought before still open (they give an axe or club weapon), and the roulette prizes still hand them out.
An axe or club weapon turns into the sword (melee) one of the same tier **the first time it is used, charges kept** (`E.convertTo`,
`Item:transform(id, charges)`); if the transform fails the weapon is used as it is. The sword weapons and chests are renamed
"exercise melee weapon" / "Exercise Melee Chest" (`data/items/base_item_names.csv`, step `itemnames`; NPC lists follow). The axe and
club chests are `store` in `item_price_rules.csv` (never sold to an NPC: without it they would have had a 7700 and a 120 gold price).

**The script** (`exercise_training.lua`) replaces the base one: `tools/patch_exercise_weapons.py` (install step `exercise`, after
`runes`, before `potions` and `itemprices`) comments the 21 `<action ... script="other/exercise_weapons.lua">` lines out of
`actions.xml`, so the revscript owns the item ids (an id registered twice would keep the XML one); it also writes the item
descriptions (what it trains, who may use it) and takes the six retired chests out of the 17 NPC shop lists that sell them. The
stock script and the edits of `patch_base_classes.py` / `patch_base_events.py` stay in the folder, unused. Review of the old script
(each fixed in the new one):
- **A charge was taken before the vocation check**, so a refused class lost a charge per click. Now a step checks the class, the
  class lock (`ChaosClassUnlocks.isRestricted`: a locked class gains nothing), the dummy, the position and the protection zone first.
- **One click, one chain.** The "already training" branch reset the flag that the running chain keeps setting, so the next click
  started a second chain: N pairs of clicks trained N times as fast for the same charges. `E.beginChain` allows one live chain per
  player (alive while its last step is newer than 2 s; a stalled one is replaced and its old events stop by their generation number).
- **Range.** The bow, rod and wand had `allowfaruse` and no range check, so a modified client could use one on any dummy of its
  floor, house dummies included. Now a ranged weapon reaches 7 tiles, a melee or shield weapon the next tile, another floor never.
- **The flag `Exercise_Training.isTraining` (37100)**, which the Idle Hall reads, was left at 1 after a logout, a restart or a
  chain that ended silently, which kept the character out of the Idle Hall for good. It is cleared whenever a chain ends and at login
  and logout.
- Texts in English and pt-BR (`Chaos.t`; the stock script's were English only); no charge for a missing dummy.
Charges are shown live as before (`item:sendUpdate()`, engine patch 0003; fallback: a transform to the same id). The 10% of the
hall's and the houses' dummies and the free dummies (5787, 27750, 27757) are as in the base script. Not run on a live engine (the
tests mock it): check a Monk with the melee weapon (fist row in the skills window), a Ranger refused with the class list, an old
exercise axe turning into the melee weapon, a bow from 8 tiles refused.

## Attack delay after changing floor (owner debug item 50: "Demora para começar a atacar depois de subir ou descer escada"; fixed by src-patch 0066, not measured in game)

What happens, from the repository's own engine notes (`src-patches/0028`, `0042`; the stock source is not here): taking a
stair is a step (`Player::onWalk`), then the floor change moves the player (`Game::internalMoveCreature`) and
`Creature::onCreatureMove` sees the attacked creature on another floor and drops the target (`onCreatureDisappear`:
"target lost"; nothing attacks any more). The player (or the helper's Auto Target) picks a new target. In the stock engine the
first swing of a new target waits for the next creature think (`Creature::onThink` -> `onAttacking`, once per second per
creature: 0 to 1000 ms, 500 ms on average, then `Player::doAttacking` schedules the following swings itself by the attack
interval); patches 0028 and 0042 already removed the same wait after a step and after an item move, not after a new target.
Three delays add up after a stair:
1. **The target is lost** (engine, stock behaviour): the attack stops until a new one is picked.
2. **The first swing of the new target waits for the creature think** (engine, up to 1 s, 0.5 s on average): this is the only
   delay that belongs to the server and it is the one the owner feels, because the helper picks the new target at once.
3. **The helper's own wait** (base `mods/game_helper`, Auto Target and the magic shooter): not readable here (the base client
   is not in the repository); the overlay and base patches around it (0052, 0062, 0067, 0074) do not touch the target choice.
No server setting changes 2 (`prod_config.py` has no key for it: the think interval is a compile-time constant and
`classicAttackSpeed` only decides which task slot the swings use). **Implemented: engine src-patch `0066-attack-at-once.patch`**
(the proposal was called 0048; that number was taken by another patch). In `Game::playerSetAttackedCreature`, when the target is
a new one (not the one already set), the new `Player::getAttackReadyIn()` says how long the previous swing still owes (attack
speed minus the time since `lastAttack`; 0 when the player never swung). Ready: `Game::checkCreatureAttack(player id)` is queued
through the dispatcher, the same call `Player::doAttacking` schedules, so the first swing happens at once. Not ready, with the
cooldown channels on and `classicAttackSpeed` off: the player's own attack task (`setNextAttackTask`, patch 0042) is replaced by
one at the moment the cooldown ends, so it is never faster than the normal attack interval (`Player::doAttacking` still checks
it). Otherwise the creature think picks it up as before. It helps every new target (monsters switched, the first hit of a pull,
the target picked again after a stair); spells and runes are not affected. Re-selecting the same target does nothing new.
Keeping the target across a floor change (only when the creature is still visible) is not done: in the game a target on another
floor is not attackable.
Not done: item 3 (the helper's own wait) is unchanged, and a client-side guess of a new target after a stair was left out on
purpose (it would attack a monster the player did not pick when running away upstairs). Checked: the whole chain 0001-0065 plus
0066 applies on a copy of the installed server source and `game.cpp` compiles (`g++ -fsyntax-only`); not measured in game. To do
on the test server: a stair pull before and after, and the helper with Auto Target on and off for item 3.

## Infinite arrows and quivers (`data/lib/chaos_archery_core.lua`, `chaos_archery_config.lua`, `archery.lua`, `weapon_styles.lua`, `tools/patch_base_archery.py`, `sql/chaos_archery.sql`, `src-patches/0023-quiver-off-hand.patch`)

Bows and crossbows fire without ammunition. A quiver is off-hand gear (the shield hand, next to a bow or crossbow) with
modifiers for bow and crossbow users. Arrows and bolts are gone from the game. The ammunition slot was a second ring
slot until 2026-10-21 ("Second ring slot" below); since src-patch 0058 it takes nothing and the client draws the badge
slot there ("Badge slot").

**The off-hand quiver** (owner request "Quivers go in the off-hand now"; engine src-patch 0023). Bows and crossbows stay
two-handed, so the two-handed speed and damage of "Weapon styles", the keystones that ask for a two-handed weapon or no
shield, and the class kits see them as before; balance does not change. The one exception is the quiver, in
`Player::queryAdd` (classic equipment slots off, the Chaos setting):

| Weapon hand | Off-hand | Allowed |
|---|---|---|
| bow or crossbow | quiver | yes |
| bow or crossbow | shield, a dual-wield blade, anything else | no (both hands need to be free) |
| empty | quiver | yes (it does nothing alone; so the order of equipping does not matter and taking the bow off keeps it) |
| sword, axe, club, wand, a throwing weapon, any other two-handed weapon | quiver | no ("You cannot dress this object there.") |
| anything | (the quiver in the weapon hand) | never |

Why an engine exception and not one-handed bows with a Lua move hook: `Player:onMoveItem` only sees moves a player makes,
while queryAdd is asked by every path that equips something (drag and drop, the equip hotkey `Game::playerEquipItem`,
`Player::queryDestination`, a script's `addItem` / `addItemEx` with a slot: loadouts, kits, the store and stash only
deliver to containers). One-handed bows would also have changed every "two-handed" rule in Lua. The quiver has its own
weapon type (`weaponType="quiver"`, Lua `WEAPON_QUIVER` = 8): the engine never treats it as a weapon or a shield
(`Player::getWeapon`, `getShieldAndWeapon`: no defense, no shielding), and the Lua loops that find "the weapon in the
hands" (`weapon_styles.lua`, `passivetree_keystones.lua`, `monk_combat.lua`, `ChaosItemMods.kindOfType` / `fits`) skip
it. The base's convenience swap (`data/scripts/eventcallbacks/player/default_onMoveItem.lua`: a two-handed weapon taken
into the hand puts the off-hand item away) keeps a quiver beside a launcher (`patch_base_archery.py`). A shield taken
into the off-hand still puts the bow away, so a bow and a shield are never held together.

**At login** (`ChaosArchery.checkHands`, archery.lua; the engine loads a character without queryAdd): a quiver in the
ammunition slot (from the last change) goes to the off-hand when that is free and allowed (the engine asks again, with
the vocation and level of movements.xml); anything else in the ammunition slot, a ring of the old second ring slot
included, goes to the store inbox ("Purse"), else the depot inbox (`ChaosPrizes.toInbox`: no client draws slot 10 since
client base patch 0113; "Badge slot"); an off-hand item the rules refuse goes to the backpack, else the inbox. A copy is placed and the
item removed (one item, its rolls and per-item id kept), then the character is saved (`Chaos.saveCharacter`); a crash
before the save keeps the old state and the next login moves it again. Nothing to move: nothing changes (no mark
needed). The player is told what moved. Saved loadouts (`loadouts_core.lua` `C.legacyGear`): a quiver in slot 10 becomes
the set's off-hand item when the set left that hand empty; slot 10 is then no longer part of that set.

**No engine patch.** The engine asks for ammunition only when the launcher has an ammo type (`Player::getWeapon`), and
`Weapons::loadDefaults` gives every distance weapon without one a weapon of its own, which fires the launcher itself with
`WeaponDistance` (its attack, its hit chance, its `shootType` as the missile; nothing is used up, a weapon has no
`action`). So the install step only changes items.xml; every distance formula, the skill training, the hit and miss
effects stay the engine's.

**Launchers** (`tools/patch_base_archery.py`, step `archery` of `install_all.py`, after `vocations`, which still reads the
ammo types, and after `spells`). Every two-handed distance weapon with an `ammoType` loses it and gets the attack, hit
chance and missile of the ammunition of its level band (`bands` in the config: the best ammunition an NPC sold for that
level):

| Band (launcher level) | Bow: + attack, hit chance, missile | Crossbow: + attack, hit chance, missile |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | +29, 93%, arrow (the arrows of levels 1-39 on average) | +32, 87%, bolt (the bolts of levels 1-44 on average) |
| 30 / 40 / 55 / 70 | (no bow of the base needs 20-39) 38, 94%, onyx arrow from 40 | 33 piercing (30), 36 vortex (40), 40 power (55), 56 drill (70) |
| 90 and up | +65, 95%, crystalline arrow | +66, 90%, prismatic bolt |

`hitChance` = the band's + the launcher's own hit bonus, at most 100 (the engine added the bow's bonus to the arrow's
chance; a non-zero `hitChance` of the weapon is the whole chance now). A name with water, arcane or icicle gives the
elemental missile. The kind and level come from the config's `launchers` (75 ids; the level is the weapons.xml level, an
unleveled launcher with an attack of 4 or more counts as 100). A launcher the config does not name (the transmog set looks,
which only the transmog files may name) is a bow of its weapons.xml level, a crossbow when its name holds crossbow, bolter,
arbalest or piercer; the tool prints those. The five launcher uniques of `data/items/chaos_items.xml` got the same band on
their attack and lost their item hit chance (the engine fires with the type's). Rarity rolls no longer raise a launcher's
hit chance attribute (`ChaosCrafting.applyBaseBonus`), the engine does not read it.

**Old launchers** (`archery.lua`, at login for the inventory and whenever a launcher reaches a hand): an attack attribute
from before (a rarity roll or a unique) still holds the attack without ammunition. It is below the new type attack (the
smallest band, 29, beats the biggest rarity bonus, 19) and gets its band once; the hit chance attribute goes. A value at or
above the type attack is a roll of after the patch and stays. On an unpatched server nothing changes.

**Quivers.** Worn in the off-hand next to a bow or crossbow (above). The 12 base quivers (`quivers` in the config: id, level, implicit modifiers) stop being containers: items.otb group
2 -> 0 (the engine makes containers of that group only; `items.otb.bak` keeps the original), items.xml without container
size and stock abilities, `weaponType` quiver and `slotType` right-hand, a text with the implicits; movements.xml gets one Equip / DeEquip pair per
quiver (slot shield, the hands; `onEquipItem`, the quiver's level, the vocations that may fire a launcher: Ranger, Deadeye, Beastmaster). The stock
hunter's quiver stays a decoration (stackable in the client's data). `sql/chaos_archery.sql` (the `sql` step) moves what
players kept inside a quiver into the container around it, the backpack, or next to it in a depot or inbox: the engine
would drop it at login. Arrows and bolts among it are refunded at the next login.

| Quiver | Level | Implicit |
|---|---|---|
| 28693 (ashwood) | 20 | Attack Speed with Bows +2% |
| 27651 (thornhide) | 50 | Distance Fighting +2 |
| 27694 (ravenfeather) | 80 | Critical Strike Chance with Bows +3% |
| 27696 (splitwind) | 120 | Extra Projectile Chance +5% |
| 27663 (stormfletch) | 150 | Adds 8% of Bow Damage as Energy |
| 27686 (blightroot) | 200 | Adds 8% of Bow Damage as Earth |
| 27676 (bonewhisper) | 250 | Critical Strike Chance with Bows +5%, Distance Fighting +2 |
| 28379 (rimeshard) | 300 | Adds 10% of Bow Damage as Ice |
| 27695 (cinderflight) | 350 | Adds 12% of Bow Damage as Fire |
| 29566 (Haloed) | 400 | Distance Fighting +3, Attack Speed with Bows +4% |
| 28050 (Mercurial) | 500 | Extra Projectile Chance +10%, Critical Strike Chance with Bows +4% |
| 29873 (Seraphic) | 1000 | Distance Fighting +4, Extra Projectile Chance +8%, Attack Speed with Bows +5% |

A quiver is its own kind in the item system (`ChaosItemMods.kindOfType` "quiver"). It rolls only the modifiers that name
it: eight of its own and nine shared ones (Damage to Elites and Bosses, Physical / Elemental Penetration, Health / Mana on
Hit, Life / Mana on Kill, Chance to Bleed / Poison), never the engine's absorbs, skills, critical or leech pairs (the base
rarity script would apply those whatever the wearer holds). Weapons never roll the quiver modifiers.

| Modifier | Side | T1 .. T8 | Cap | What it does (`weapon_styles.lua`, `archery.lua`) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Distance Fighting | prefix | +1 .. +6-8 | 12 | an attribute condition of its own sub id |
| Critical Strike Chance with Bows | prefix | 1-2% .. 8-10% | 20% | a bow or crossbow hit deals +50% |
| Extra Projectile Chance | prefix | 2-4% .. 14-20% | 30% | a second missile, 60% of the hit, at the monster closest to the target (3 sqm), else the target |
| Adds N% of Bow Damage as Fire / Ice / Energy / Earth | prefix | 2-4% .. 20-28% | 40% each | the strongest element of the totals adds that share of the hit as its element, against the monster's resistance, with its hit effect |
| Attack Speed with Bows | suffix | 1-2% .. 8-10% | 12% | written on the launcher in the hands ("chaos_qspd") and folded into its attack interval (the engine's attack speed cap, patch 0011, applies); off again when the launcher leaves the hands |

A quiver counts only while a bow or crossbow is held (`ChaosItemMods.fits`: a quiver counts in the off-hand while a
launcher is in the weapon hand); its modifiers and implicits then join the totals like set bonuses, under the same caps. Without a
launcher it does nothing (the item_mods refresh after every slot move drops it). The engine refuses it to other
vocations (movements.xml). Quivers drop like other gear (`ChaosLoot.isGearId`; the base monsters already list them),
roll item levels and tiers like other gear (the item level gates of `chaos_item_mods.lua`), take the crafting bonus
(the Haloed and Seraphic recipes) and are in the Gambler's pool (a "Quiver" slot, the bow classes only). The tooltip
names them "Quiver" with a line "Off-hand: Quiver", compares them with the off-hand, lists the implicits in the modifier colour and adds "Works only while you hold a bow or crossbow.".

**Ammunition removed** (`patch_base_archery.py`): one-line loot entries of arrows and bolts in the base monsters (XML and
Lua, by id or by name: 142 entries on the reference server), the NPC shops (XML lists and Lua shop tables,
buy keywords commented out: 291 offers and rewards), the ten conjure spells (`spells.xml`, commented out; their names left
`spell_names.csv` and the client's spell data), and ammunition in base script rewards becomes gold coins worth its refund
(first items, the starter chest, the valuables, an NPC's trade; one postman mission asks 24 gold instead of 12 arrows,
and the NPC's texts say so: a string of an NPC script that names "<n> arrows" or "<n> bolts" when the script asks
`removeMoney` (or `removeTotalMoney`, patch_bank_payments.py) for the price of that many pieces names the gold instead, also on a script an earlier version patched).
No crafting recipe of the base makes ammunition, the Chaos store, kits and the Gambler never had any. The new player kit
and the staff test kit carry no ammunition (the test kits get a rolled quiver). `loot.lua` takes arrows and bolts out of
every corpse too (a loot table the tool could not read). `hunt_supplies.lua` was generated again (no ammunition is sold).
Throwing weapons (spears, stars, knives) are not ammunition and stay.

**What players own** (`archery.lua`). At the first login after the update every arrow and bolt in the inventory, the depot
chests of every town and the inbox goes, and the refund goes to the bank: half the cheapest NPC price (no NPC buys
ammunition; `ammo` in the config, 1 gold for an unlisted arrow), then the character is saved (`Chaos.saveCharacter`;
storage 7101100). A character with nothing to sweep (every character made after the update) only gets the two marks,
without a save (they go with the next save; a crash before it looks at an empty inventory again). Before, each first
login saved the character twice. Load test, fresh database, per bot over a short session: 13.7 InnoDB fsyncs and 12.5
DELETEs before, 10.4 and 2.0 with this; 3.9 fsyncs on a second run. On a busy disk those writes held the login worker
behind the dispatcher ("Account passwords", "Login rush"). All of it is in memory and saved as one: a crash before the save keeps nothing, the next login sweeps
again. The stash (`chaos_stash`) is a step of its own (storage 7101101): refund and mark first, saved, and only then the
rows are deleted; a failed save takes refund and mark back and leaves the rows. Later logins look at the inventory again
(a base reward the tool did not know), and ammunition that reaches the inventory by a move (a map chest, a trade) is turned
into its refund at once. Houses (their tiles are saved apart) and Chaos market listings are not swept; that ammunition
cannot be fired and turns into gold when a character picks it up.

**Spells.** `ChaosSpell.distanceAttack` (`_common.lua`) is the launcher's own attack (it carries the band); the shuriken
