spells' throwing weapon check also needs a one-handed weapon now. No Chaos spell consumed ammunition. The Deadeye
keystone needs a crossbow, the bow splash and Ricochet a launcher of that kind.

**Balance** (server/data/spells/README.md "Infinite arrows"): with the ammunition of its band a launcher deals exactly
what it did (same attack sum, same hit chance). The level 0 bow and crossbow carry the average of what levels 1-39 fired.

Tests: `tests/archery_test.lua` (bands, old items, the balance table, quiver kind, rolls and gates, slot rules, crafting,
tooltip, refunds, the save-safe sweep, the quiver's skill and speed, the hit: splash by kind, critical strike, element,
extra projectile, loot, the SQL ids), `tests/base_archery_patch_test.lua` (the tool on a small data folder, idempotent),
new cases in `gamble_test.lua`, `item_mods_test.lua`, `passivetree_keystones_test.lua`, `hunt_test.lua`,
`newplayer_test.lua`, `class_kit_test.lua` and the client's `tooltiplogic_test.lua`. Tested in game (base server built
from source with patches 0001-0021, the full map, client pair things_custom16, a private MariaDB): a level 650 Ranger
with a sanguine bow and an empty ammunition slot shot crystalline arrows (42 hits, average 423 after the troll's armour,
highest 686: the bow's attack is 74 now, 9 before); the login sweep took 150 arrows (50 of them out of an old quiver,
moved to the backpack by the SQL with 7 platinum coins), 20 onyx arrows in the depot and 200 crystalline arrows in the
stash, and paid 2,210 gold to the bank; a Legendary Haloed Quiver (item level 120) raised distance 114 -> 117 and the bow's
interval 3.0 -> 2.88 s, and its 19% ice share added 137 ice to hits of 722; the tooltip showed the implicits and the note;
the Gambler offered the Ranger a quiver and refused one to a Warrior.

Off-hand quiver and second ring slot: `tests/archery_test.lua` (the hand rules: bow or crossbow + quiver, bow + shield,
quiver without a bow, quiver beside a sword or a two-handed axe; the second ring slot takes rings only; the login plan
and `checkHands` against a mock engine: to the off-hand with the rolls kept, to the backpack, to the inbox, refused by
the engine, a ring stays, idempotent; two might rings: the one in slot 10 to the backpack or the inbox, a might ring
with another ring or alone in slot 10 stays, the might ring message; two rings and two copies of one ring add up under
the caps; the ring budget), `tests/base_archery_patch_test.lua` (the quiver entry, the movements, an earlier layout
rewritten, the base slot maps, the base swap run as code, the might ring key and the worn ids it follows), `tests/loadouts_test.lua` (old loadouts), `tests/item_tooltip_test.lua` and the client's
`tooltiplogic_test.lua`, `playerinspect_logic_test.lua`, `badgeslotlogic_test.lua` (until 0058: `ringslotlogic_test.lua`). Tested in game (base server from
windows-assets with src-patches 0001-0023 built, every install step, the full map, a private MariaDB, the client
`game22`): a Ranger with a bow and a quiver of before in the ammunition slot logged in with the quiver in the off-hand
(saved at once); a character with a sword and a shield had it moved to the backpack; dragged in the client: a sword
next to the quiver, a quiver, a torch into slot 10 refused; a bow taken into the hand kept the quiver; a shield onto the
off-hand put the bow away (stock swap); a crossbow beside the quiver; the equip hotkey put a time ring into slot 10
when slot 9 held one and refused a shield beside the crossbow; two time rings turned active in both slots (speed
+60 each), slot 10's ring lost duration and turned back with its time kept when taken off; the quiver tooltip read
"Off-hand: Quiver".

## Throwing weapons (`data/lib/chaos_throwables.lua`, `tools/patch_base_throwables.py`, `loot.lua`, `rarity_migrate*.lua`)

Owner decision 2026-10-20: the stackable throwing weapons are out of the game: small stone 1294, spear 2389, throwing
star 2399, throwing knife 2410, hunting spear 3965, viper star 7366, enchanted spear 7367, assassin star 7368, royal
spear 7378 (the block `T.items` of `chaos_throwables.lua` is the one list; the tool, the loot layer, the hunt tracker
generator and the tests read it). Arrows and bolts went the same way earlier ("Infinite arrows and quivers").

- **Install:** step `throwables` (after `archery`, whose editing functions it uses): `tools/patch_base_throwables.py DATA_DIR`
  removes them from base monster loot (XML and Lua), NPC shops (XML lists; script shop lines and keywords commented), and
  turns NPC and quest rewards into gold coins (the item's `sell_prices.lua` value, else 5 gold each). Idempotent
  (`tools/patch_base_throwables_test.py`). `items.xml` and `weapons.xml` are untouched; what a character holds stays.
  The Chaos monster files had their spear entries (15 goblins) removed in the repo; `tools/ci/check_content.py` fails on
  any throwable in Chaos monster loot, a new-player kit or `hunt_supplies.lua`.
- **Loot layer:** `loot.lua` step 0 takes a throwable out of a corpse (a loot table the tool could not read still drops none).
- **Thief kit (decision):** the Thief, Ninja and Samurai no longer start with 30 throwing stars (and the `testkit` Thief
  no longer gets 100 assassin stars). The shuriken spells (Shuriken Toss 236, Shuriken Barrage 242) never used them up:
  `ChaosSpell.shurikenPower` takes `Chaos.classes.shuriken.defaultAttack` (50) unless a one-handed distance weapon is in
  hand, so the spells and their numbers are unchanged (balance in `data/spells/README.md` "Thief line"). The kit keeps the
  dagger and the second dagger. `Chaos.classes.shuriken.items` was read by nothing and is gone.
- **Hunt tracker:** `hunt_supplies.lua` has no thrown weapon; `gen_supply_prices.py` no longer counts them.
- **No rarity on stackables (same decision):** a stack never carries a rarity. The Chaos gates already refused one
  (`ChaosLoot.isGearId`, `ChaosCrafting.isGear`), but the stock roll of the base drop script could still set the attribute
  on a stackable that passed its gear test, and nothing forged it: **that is why a royal spear always came without a
  rarity** (it is stackable). Now `ChaosLoot.stripStackableRarity` clears the attribute in every corpse before the engine's
  stat pass and in `finalizeRarity` (autoloot, pouch), and the login walk of `rarity_migrate.lua` (version 2, so
  characters walked before are walked again) clears it on existing stacks in equipment, backpacks, purse, inbox and
  depots. Not covered: stacks in house tiles, guild depots, market offers and stash tables (cleared when they pass a
  player's hands again). The stock roll function itself lives in the base file and is not edited.
- Tests: `tests/throwables_test.lua`, `tests/rarity_migrate_test.lua`, `tests/newplayer_test.lua`, `tests/class_kit_test.lua`,
  `tools/patch_base_throwables_test.py`.

## Second ring slot (`src-patches/0023-quiver-off-hand.patch`, `data/lib/chaos_item_mods.lua`, `archery.lua`, `tools/patch_base_archery.py`, client `game_ringslot`)

**Removed 2026-10-21** (owner: "tire o slot extra de ring e coloque o badge"; "Badge slot"). Src-patch 0058 makes slot 10
take nothing, the ring swap between slots 9 and 10 and the hotkey's second ring go, and the client draws the badge slot
there. A ring left in slot 10 moves to the Purse at login. What follows is the record of the slot as it was.

Owner request: "Don't remove the ammo slot. Turn it into a second ring slot." Inventory slot 10 (`CONST_SLOT_AMMO`, the
ammunition slot of the protocol) takes the item types the ring slot takes and nothing else.

- **Engine** (0023): `Player::queryAdd` takes an item with the ring slot position there, every other item is refused (the
  base's "Quiver" name exception goes). `MoveEvents::getEvent` looks up the ring events (`slot="ring"` in movements.xml)
  for slot 10, so a ring there gets its abilities, its vocation and level check and its transformation on equip and
  de-equip (time ring, stealth ring, the skill rings: they swap item ids when worn), and decays as in slot 9;
  `Player::getArmor` counts it. The equip hotkey (`Game::playerEquipItem`) of a ring worn in slot 9 or slot 10 takes
  it off to the backpack, as in stock (slot 9 first when both hold it); a ring not worn goes into slot 10 when slot 9
  holds another ring and slot 10 is free, else into slot 9. A ring taken off a ring slot (the hotkey, a drop on the
  inventory) never lands in the other ring slot (`Player::queryDestination` skips it). A ring dragged from one ring
  slot onto the ring in the other swaps the two, both ways (`Game::internalMoveItem`: the stock exchange cannot, as
  the source slot is still taken; the de-equip and equip events and `onMoveItem` / `onItemMoved` run for both
  rings). Both rings stay worn, so the one-might-ring rule holds. Since src-patch 0024 the hotkey's own moves run the Lua
  move events too, so the rarity bonuses of a ring put on by hotkey apply at once ("Right-click equips").
- **Base Lua** (`patch_base_archery.py`): the slot tables of `data/scripts/customs/rarity/base_rarity.lua` (the base
  rarity conditions) and `data/lib/core/itemtype.lua` (`ItemType.usesSlot`) map slot 10 to the ring bit. The base's
  `onItemMoved` in `base_rarity.lua` clears the slot an item left and fills the slot it reached, so in a ring swap
  either call would clear the other ring's slot; when the slot an item left holds another item now, it clears both
  slots and fills both again (step 12 of the tool).
- **Chaos systems**: `ChaosItemMods.slotBits` maps slot 10 to the ring bit, so both rings count for the item
  modifiers, the legendary powers, the gems, the veiled modifiers, the item sets (`itemsets.lua`) and the stat
  totals. The item tooltip compares a ring with both ring slots; inspect, the hover tooltips, loadouts (slot 10 is in
  `gearSlots`), the hunt supplies, the rift and uber key searches, the new-player kit slots and the testkit keep slot 10.
  A set piece counts once however many copies are worn (`ChaosItemSets.count` counts piece ids).
- **Two copies of one ring are allowed**, uniques included: no unique ring says otherwise, the modifiers of both add up
  under the catalogue's caps, and a set counts the piece once. The one exception is the might ring.
- **One might ring at a time** (owner decision; two would absorb 40% physical and magic damage instead of 20%):
  `Player::queryAdd` (0023) refuses a might ring in slot 9 or slot 10 while the other ring slot holds one, with the
  message "You can only wear one might ring at a time." (`RETURNVALUE_ONLYONEMIGHTRING`). Drag and drop, the equip
  hotkey (it also shows the message), automatic placement, scripts (`addItem` / `addItemEx` with a slot) and loadouts
  (the refused ring is listed as not equipped) all ask `queryAdd`. A might ring next to any other ring, or alone in
  slot 10, is allowed. Which ids are might rings is data: `chaos_archery_config.lua` `mightRings` (the base has one,
  2164 "might ring", 20% physical and magic, 20 charges, no worn id), and `patch_base_archery.py` writes the items.xml
  key `chaosMightRing` on each and on every id it turns into on equip or de-equip. The engine reads the key
  (`ItemType::chaosMightRing`, Lua `itemType:isMightRing()`). No Chaos unique or other ring has the might ring's
  absorb: none is based on 2164, and no other ring absorbs both physical and magic damage.
- **Migration**: anything in slot 10 that is no ring moves at login ("Infinite arrows and quivers", At login). A
  character who wears two might rings keeps the one in slot 9; the one in slot 10 goes to the backpack (or a
  container in it), else the inbox, and the character is saved at once (`ChaosArchery.loginPlan`, `checkHands`).
  Nothing to move: nothing changes, so it is idempotent; a crash before the save leaves both rings and the next login
  moves it again.
- **Client**: the slot stays where it was. The Chaos skin draws its placeholder with the ring's silhouette
  (`client/tools/gen_skin.py`: `data/images/game/slots/ammo(-blessed).png`), so the inventory window and the action
  bar's equipment presets show a ring slot; the overlay module `game_ringslot` gives the empty slot the tooltip "Ring"
  and drops "ammunition" from the soul label's tooltip; the inspect window names slot 10 "Ring". No client base patch.
- **Balance** (`server/data/spells/README.md` "Second ring"): every modifier a ring may roll already reaches its cap
  at T8 with the slots of one ring, so no ceiling rises; the stock rings stack (two skill rings, two time rings), the
  might ring does not (one at a time).
- **Tested** on a Linux test server (0001-0023, the base map, a private database), with a protocol client: a second
  might ring refused by drag into slot 10 and into slot 9 and by the hotkey, with the message; a might ring with a
  time ring allowed both ways, by drag and hotkey; a might ring alone in slot 10 allowed; `addItemEx` into slot 10 next
  to a might ring returns `RETURNVALUE_ONLYONEMIGHTRING`; the login split into the backpack, into the inbox without a
  backpack, and no change at the next login.
- **Tested** again after two fixes (a ring dragged between the ring slots answered "There is not enough room."; the
  hotkey of a ring in slot 9 moved it into an empty slot 10 instead of taking it off). Base server from windows-assets
  with 0001-0023 built on Linux, every install step, the full map, a private MariaDB, a protocol client on
  `tools/loadtest.py` (drag 0x78, hotkey 0x77): two ordinary rings (sword ring, club ring) swapped 10 to 9 and 9 to
  10 in both orders, their rarity skills (fist +7, club +9) and the ring bonuses unchanged; two copies of the sword
  ring swapped; a might ring and a time ring swapped both ways, the time ring stayed active (speed +60); a second
  might ring refused by drag into slot 10, into slot 9 and onto the time ring in slot 9, with the message; the
  hotkey put rings into slot 9 and slot 10 and took them off from slot 9 (slot 10 empty or full) and from slot 10
  (slot 9 empty or full), also with the worn ids of the time and sword rings; with both slots full the hotkey of a
  third ring exchanged it with slot 9 (stock).
- **Live test** of the equip hotkey: `tools/ring_hotkey_test.py` (test server only, not in CI; the bot of
  `tools/loadtest.py setup --count 1`). Six cases: a ring taken off slot 9 or slot 10 goes to the backpack and never
  into the other ring slot, a ring put on goes into slot 9, or into slot 10 when slot 9 holds another ring. Run on
  0001-0030: 6/6. With the `queryDestination` check of 0023 and the backpack-first take-off of 0024 both removed it
  fails the two take-off cases, the ring lands in the other ring slot, as on the old test server.

## Right-click equips (`src-patches/0024-equip-on-use.patch`, `rightclick_equip.lua`, `rightclick_equip_core.lua`, `rightclick_equip_config.lua`, client `game_rightclickequip`, base patch 0037)

Owner request: "Make items get equipped on right-click." A right-click on a piece of equipment in the backpack (any
open container) puts it on; a right-click on a worn piece takes it off into the backpack. Potions, runes, food, tools,
keys, containers and every item with a use of its own work as before.

- **Where it is decided: the server, on the use.** The client's mouse presets already send a use for that click (a
  right-click in Classic Controls, Ctrl + click in Regular Controls, a left-click in Left Smart-Click, "Use" in the
  context menu), with the exact item's position. `Actions::internalUseItem` (0024) calls `Game::chaosUseEquip` where it
  used to answer "You cannot use this object.": only when the item has no action at all. So the server's own action
  list decides what has a use of its own; nothing in the client has to know it. The equip hotkey packet (0x77) was not
  used for this: it names an item type, and the engine equips the first one it finds in the backpack, which is the
  wrong one when two rings or swords of one type carry different rarities.
- **What counts as equipment** (`Game::chaosEquipsOnUse`): a head, necklace, armour, legs, feet or ring item, or a sword,
  club, axe, distance weapon, wand, shield or quiver. Every item may be held in a hand by default, so the hands count by
  weapon type. A badge counts since src-patch 0058. Not ammunition, the base's other extra slots (deck, ship, belt,
  gloves), the backpack slot, an item that cannot be moved, a container. Not a hotkey use (`isHotkey`), not an item lying on the map. The item may be in any
  container the player has open (the backpack, a bag, the depot, a corpse), as with drag and drop.
- **Which slot:** the equip hotkey's (`getSlotType`). A ring goes into slot 9 (a worn ring swaps); a badge into slot 13
  (src-patch 0058, "Badge slot"; until then a ring could go into slot 10, "Second ring slot").
  A worn item goes into the backpack first, then wherever the stock hotkey put it when the backpack has no room.
- **The move** (`Game::chaosEquipMove`) runs with the player as the actor and the client positions, so it is the same
  as drag and drop: `Player:onMoveItem`, every onMoveItem and onItemMoved callback, `Player::queryAdd` (the hand rules,
  the quiver, the might ring), the base two-handed swap in `default_onMoveItem.lua` (a two-handed weapon or bow puts the
  shield into the container it came from, a shield puts the two-handed weapon away, a quiver stays beside a launcher),
  the exchange with the worn item, the depot tab limits. A refusal shows its message.
- **Multi-use weapons.** The stock weapons are multi-use (their action, `other/destroy.lua`, breaks furniture with a
  use with), so the client starts a use with on them and the engine refuses a plain use of a multi-use item. 0024 lets
  a plain use of one in an open container or the inventory through to `chaosUseEquip` (its use with is not run), and
  the client module sends that plain use for the multi-use weapons the server lists at login (`rightclick_equip.lua`:
  every multi-use item type that is equipment, minus those with any other action in `data/actions/actions.xml`, minus
  `keepUseWith`; 384 looks on the test server). The machete, the crowbar and the scythe are weapons with tool actions:
  they are not listed and keep their use with. "Use with ..." stays in the context menu of every multi-use weapon.
- **The option** "Right-click equips items" (Options > Interface, client base patch 0037, on by default): the client
  sends extended opcode **188** `{"on": true | false}` at every login and when it changes; `rightclick_equip.lua` keeps
  storage 7101810 at 1 while it is off, and the engine then answers a use as before. Opcode 188 is free in the reference
  server, the base client's `ExtendedIds` and every Chaos script and module. Storages 7101810 - 7101819 reserved.
- **The equip hotkey and the rarity bonuses.** A club ring put on with the equip hotkey showed +4 club (its own) instead
  of +9 (with its +5 rarity). Cause: `Game::playerEquipItem` moved the item with `internalMoveItem(..., nullptr)`, no
  actor and no positions, and the engine runs the Lua move events only with both. The base rarity script
  (`customs/rarity/base_rarity.lua`) turns the rarity attributes into conditions and storages only in `onItemMoved` and
  at login (its 3 s check only clears empty slots), so the ring's rarity never applied, and a worn item the hotkey
  swapped out kept its conditions for as long as the slot was taken. The item modifiers, archery (a launcher's quiver
  speed, a bow migrated on equip) and the base two-handed swap missed it too. Fix (0024): the hotkey moves through
  `chaosEquipMove` as well; every refusal of the hotkey shows its message. Checked live: the hotkey put a club ring with
  +5 club rarity on at 23 club with another club ring worn (10 + 4 + 4 + 5), and swapping it for a stealth ring with
  +1 left 15 (the +5 went at once). The same server built without 0024, same data: the hotkey put the +5 club ring on
  at 14 club (10 + 4, the rarity missing); with 0024 the same ring and steps gave 19.
- **A hand emptied by the two-handed swap** (`patch_base_archery.py` step 13): the base swap moves the other hand's
  item with `moveTo`, which runs no onItemMoved, so its rarity conditions stayed until the 3 s check. The base rarity
  script now clears the other hand at once when an item reaches a hand and the other hand is empty. Drag and drop gets
  the same fix. The item modifiers (`item_mods.lua`) work out every slot again on each move and needed nothing; the
  keystone and weapon style checks read the slots when they are needed.
- **Tests:** `tests/rightclick_equip_test.lua` (opcode and storage unique, the engine's key and rules in the patch, the
  message, the stored value, the equipment rule, actions.xml with ranges, lists, functions and comments, the
  multi-use list, the glue against a mocked engine), `tests/base_archery_patch_test.lua` (step 13 run as code), client
  `game_rightclickequip/rightclickequiplogic_test.lua`.
- **Tested** on a Linux test server (the windows-assets base with src-patches 0001-0024 built, every install step, the
  full map, a private MariaDB) with the Linux client (`game22` with this overlay and 0037's Lua part), real mouse
  clicks: helmet, armour, legs, boots, amulet, sword, shield, a two-handed sword replacing sword and shield (the shield's
  +6 shielding gone at once), a shield replacing the two-handed sword, a club ring into slot 9 and a second one into
  slot 10 (the exact copy clicked: the one without rarity), might rings exchanging with the worn might ring and never
  two, a ring into a free slot 10, a bow next to a quiver, a quiver with empty hands, a second quiver swapped in, a
  crossbow replacing the bow with the quiver kept, a shield replacing crossbow and quiver, every rarity and quiver bonus
  applied and removed at once; every worn piece taken off by right-click on its slot (a two-handed sword too). Potions
  and the rope still start a use with, food is eaten, a bag opens, the machete keeps its use with. Regular Controls:
  right-click opens the menu ("Use" equips), Ctrl + click equips; Left Smart-Click: a click equips and takes off;
  Classic Ctrl + right-click still opens the menu. The option off: a right-click equips nothing; back on: it does.

## Keep attacking while moving (`src-patches/0028-kite-walk.patch`, `kitewalk.lua`, `kitewalk_core.lua`, client `game_kitewalk`, base patch 0039)

Owner request: "Make the player not stop to attack when moving by clicking on the map or on the field." With an attack
target, a click on the map or the minimap (and a key step) now walks the clicked path while the attacks keep firing:
melee when the target is adjacent, a bow, wand or spell whenever it is in range. The target stays. Chase Opponent
starts again by itself when the walk ends.

- **What stopped it (stock engine).** With Chase Opponent the attacked creature is also the followed one. Its path is
  rebuilt on every step of the player or the target (`Player::onCreatureMove` -> `Game::updateCreatureWalk` ->
  `Creature::goToFollowCreature`, and every 2 s in `Creature::onThink`), which clears the walk list: a click walk was
  replaced by the chase after one step, and next to the target the click was eaten at once. Starting an attack mid
  walk dropped the path (`Creature::setFollowCreature`), and so did losing the target (`Player::onFollowCreature`).
  Every step (`Player::onWalk`) also cancelled the scheduled attack check (with `classicAttackSpeed = false` the next
  attack is the next action task) and pushed the next action to the end of the step: melee waited for the 1 s creature
  think, and a distance weapon (`interruptSwing`) or a rune fired only in the gaps between steps.
- **What stopped it (base client).** The click handlers never cancelled the attack. But the base option "Auto Chase
  Off" (Options > Gameplay, on by default; `game_inventory` `check()` on `onWalk` / `onAutoWalk`) switched the stance
  to Don't Chase on every manual walk while attacking, so the chase never came back.
- **The fix (0028).** `Game::playerMove` (a key) and `Game::playerAutoWalk` (a map or minimap click) mark the walk as
  the player's own, a kite walk. While it runs and for 400 ms after its last step, `Player::goToFollowCreature` does no
  chase pathing of the attacked creature, so held keys and the next click keep walking. Then a scheduled
  `Game::updateCreatureWalk` starts the chase again. Starting an attack mid walk keeps the path
  (`Creature::keepsWalkPathOnFollow`, a virtual that only the player overrides, so monsters and NPCs chase as before),
  and so do losing the target and switching Chase Opponent off. A step of a kite walk with a target neither cancels
  the next action task nor delays the next action, so the attack check runs on time. Every other walk keeps the stock
  lines: no target, the option off, and the server's own paths (chase, follow, walk to use).
- **The option** "Keep attacking while moving" (Options > Interface, client base patch 0039, on by default): the client
  sends extended opcode **186** `{"on": true | false}` at every login and when it changes; `kitewalk.lua` keeps storage
  7101820 at 1 while it is off, and the engine then walks as before. Storages 7101820 - 7101829 reserved. Opcode 186 is
  free in the reference server, the base client's `ExtendedIds` and every Chaos script and module. While the option
  is on, base patch 0039 skips "Auto Chase Off", so the stance stays Chase Opponent.
- **Unchanged:** the step timing (0018 and client 0029: one step and diagonal 7/5); the chase of monsters; follow
  outside combat (the client cancels a follow before it walks); Esc (`Game::playerCancelAttackAndFollow` clears the
  target and stops the walk); the right-click equip and the use-with crosshair (client only); the PZ rules (stepping
  into a protection zone still drops the target); cast-time spells (`data/lib/chaos_casting.lua` still ends a cast on
  a step, by design). Instant spells were never blocked by walking.
- **Tests:** `tests/kitewalk_test.lua` (opcode and storage unique, the engine key and the patch shape, the message and
  the stored value, the glue against a mocked engine), client `game_kitewalk/kitewalklogic_test.lua` (also checks patch
  0039).
- **Tested live** (the windows-assets base with src-patches 0001-0026 and 0028 built, every install step, a small
  test map, a private MariaDB; the Linux client built from the base with patches 0001-0039; real mouse clicks with
  xdotool and real arrow keys). Chase Opponent on, a troll as the target:
  - Ranger with a bow, map clicks 5 tiles east and west for 9 s: the path was walked, the target stayed, and the bow
    fired every 3 s (its attack speed) during the walk. An engine trace showed every step of the walk as a kite step
    and no blocked attack.
  - Option off, same clicks: the stance flipped to Don't Chase at the first click (stock "Auto Chase Off"), and the
    engine refused the attack mid step (7 times in 10 s) and fired late, in the gaps.
  - Option off and "Auto Chase Off" off: a click 3 tiles away from an adjacent target took one step, then the chase
    pulled the character back (the owner's report). Option on: the same click walked all 5 steps; the chase came back
    1.4 s after the stop.
  - Warrior with melee, a fast troll at the side: hits every 2 s while walking. Minimap clicks: the same as map
    clicks. Arrow keys held for 1.6 s: 5 steps away, the target kept, then the chase walked back.
  - Esc mid walk cleared the target and stopped the walk. Following a creature outside combat still follows. Walking
    into a protection zone dropped the target on the first protected tile. Chase Opponent off: the click walk keeps
    attacking. The option through the Options window and Ok wrote the storage (1 off, 0 on).

## Cooldown channels (`src-patches/0042-cooldown-channels.patch`, `cooldown_channels.lua`, `data/lib/chaos_casting.lua`, client `game_helpertimers`, base patch 0062)

Owner request (2026-10-16): attack spells, healing spells, the auto attack and moving things (items, containers,
equipment) must have cooldowns that never conflict: using one never delays or blocks another.

**Shared timers found (audit 2026-10-16).**
- Engine, `Player::nextAction` / `actionTaskEvent`: one next-action time and one queued task per player. Every item use
  set it (`Actions::useItem` 200 ms, `useItemEx` 1000 ms: runes and potions are "use with"), every step set it
  (`Player::onWalk`), and every use, item move and creature move waited for it (`Game::playerUseItem`, `playerUseItemEx`,
  `playerUseWithCreature`, `playerMoveItem`, `playerMoveCreature`; a blocked one was queued in the one task slot and the
  next queued one replaced it). So an attack rune held the healing rune and every potion for 1 s, a potion held the next
  rune, a step held both.
- Engine, auto attack (`Player::doAttacking`, `classicAttackSpeed = false`): a distance weapon waited for `nextAction`
  (a rune, a potion or a door delayed the shot), and the queued attack check sat in the same task slot: an item move or
  a use cancelled it (the next swing then waited for the 1 s creature think, up to a second lost) and the attack check
  cancelled a queued use or move (dropped). Melee never waited for `nextAction`; spells never touched the auto attack.
- Engine, spells: the spell cooldown (per spell id) and the group cooldowns (`CONDITION_SPELLGROUPCOOLDOWN` per group)
  are separate per group. Every Chaos spell has its group (55 attack, 8 healing, 34 support in
  `spells/chaos/spells_chaos.xml`, none without a group, no secondary group), every stock rune its right group (28
  attack, 3 healing, 5 support), the stock spells too. Kept on purpose: a spell without a group shares the
  "none" group cooldown with the other group-less spells (only the house spells; monsters do not use them). The stock
  buffs with a group lock are gone: Protector and Swift Foot (a 10 s attack group cooldown and a pacify from their
  scripts; "Bulwark and Windrunner retired, Ironhold and Wildstride") and Hawkeye (the healing group as its secondary
  group; "Hawkeye retired, Tautstring"), all retired on 2026-10-20.
- Lua, cast-time spells (`data/lib/chaos_casting.lua`): any other spell's cast event interrupted the cast and refunded
  it, so a heal cut the attack cast off, and the client helper held every heal while a cast charged.
- Lua, potions: the Everfull potions wait 900 ms per kind (a health and a mana timer per player in `potions.lua`, no
  `CONDITION_EXHAUST_HEAL` since 2026-10-17). The stock potions had no exhaust of their own (only the shared 1 s next
  action).
- Lua, other exhausts: Town Portal sets its own spell cooldown only (`townportal.lua`, group none with group cooldown 0);
  rift and store service items keep their own per-feature timers; crafting has none; the antibot, combat log and
  supports hooks only read or shorten a spell's own cooldown. None of them is shared with attack, heal or moves.
- Client helper (base `mods/game_helper`): one rate guard of 4 casts a second for every spell (base patch 0026), one
  object-use timer of 1 s for potions, the healing rune, the shooter's runes and the special foods, a 1.1 s potion
  "turn" after every rune, and a heal waited while a cast-time spell charged (base patch 0052).

**The four channels now.**
- **Attack**: attack spells and attack runes share the attack group cooldown (spells.xml); attack runes also wait
  `runeChannelDelay` (1000 ms) after the last attack rune. Nothing else holds them.
- **Heal**: healing spells and healing runes share the healing group cooldown; healing runes wait `runeChannelDelay`
  after the last healing rune. **Potions are a channel of their own** (`potionChannelDelay`, 500 ms):
  a potion never waits for a heal spell or rune and never holds one, as in the stock game where potions and healing
  spells never shared a cooldown; one potion a second stays the limit (health and mana potions together). Support runes
  have their own channel the same way.
- **The helper and runes (client base patch 0082, 2026-10-20, "o helper nao esta usando runas")**: the server never
  blocked them; the client did. The helper's rune use needed a count above 0 from `LocalPlayer:getInventoryCount`, which
  sees only equipped items and open containers, so a rune in a closed backpack was never used. The use by id finds it in
  any carried container, so the helper now probes an uncounted rune every 3 s (`ChaosPotionGate`, `client/BASE.md` 60)
  and waits 30 s after "Sorry, not possible.". A rune used on a creature only waits `runeChannelDelay` on this server.
- **Auto attack**: its own queued check and its own interval (`getAttackSpeed`, the 0011 floor and cap). No spell, rune,
  potion, use or move holds or cancels it. Only a step holds a distance shot, as before, and not a kite walk step
  (0028).
- **Movement**: item moves, creature moves, the equip hotkey and the right-click equip (0024) wait only for each other:
  `moveItemDelay` (50 ms) after each, and a step holds them as before. They never hold a spell, rune, potion or the
  auto attack. Plain uses (doors, levers, tools, food, opening containers) keep the stock delays on the action channel,
  which walking also sets; runes and potions never wait for it.
- **Anti-spam**: each channel has its own floor (at least 50 ms, `SCHEDULER_MINTICKS`) and one queued task (a blocked use
  is replayed when its channel is free, a newer one replaces it), so packet floods and fast clients stay limited per
  channel; nothing has a zero delay. The protocol's packet limit is unchanged.
- **Cast-time spells**: only another spell of the cast's group (attack) interrupts it (`ChaosCasting.interrupts`); a heal,
  a healing rune or a support spell goes through and the cast still fires.
- **Client helper** (base patch 0062, overlay `game_helpertimers`, `ChaosHelperTimers`): a cast guard per channel (heal,
  attack, support: 4, 4 and 3 casts a second, the same words not again within 500 ms) and an object-use timer per
  channel (potion, healRune, attackRune, supportRune, food). A heal no longer waits for a charging attack cast.

Which channel a use takes (`Actions::getUseChannel`): the item's own channel from `Game.setItemCooldownChannel(itemId,
channel)` (`cooldown_channels.lua`: every `<action>` of `other/potions.lua` in `data/actions/actions.xml`, else the list
of `cooldown_channels_config.lua`, plus the Everfull potions of `potions_config.lua`), else a rune by its spell group
(attack and special: attack, healing: heal, support: support), else the action channel. Lua constants
`COOLDOWN_CHANNEL_ACTION`, `_MOVE`, `_ATTACK`, `_HEAL`, `_SUPPORT`, `_POTION`, `_AUTO` (back to the default rule).

Config (`config.lua`, written by `tools/prod_config.py`; the engine defaults are the same): `cooldownChannels = true`
(false: the stock shared delay and attack task), `moveItemDelay = 50`, `runeChannelDelay = 1000`,
`potionChannelDelay = 500` (ms; also in `configKeys`). Balance note: a player may now drink a potion, use an attack rune
and a healing rune in the same second (one of each per second at most).

Tests: `tools/cooldown_channels_patch_test.py` (the patch: every stock gate goes, each use and move asks its channel,
the attack's own task, the 50 ms floors, the config, the Lua binding, prod_config.py), `tests/cooldown_channels_test.lua`
(the potion list, the engine file against a mocked engine), `tests/casting_test.lua` (a heal and a support spell leave the
attack cast running), client `game_helpertimers/helpertimers_test.lua` (channel guards and timers, base patch 0062).
The patch chain 0001-0042 applies and every engine source compiles (`g++ -std=c++17 -fsyntax-only`, Linux flags).
**Not run live yet**: rune + potion + heal spell + attack spell in one second, a distance attack while drinking and
moving items, the helper's rotation with heals during a cast-time spell, a flood of moves (the 50 ms queue).

## Progress bars over tiles (`tilebars.lua`, `tilebars_core.lua`, `tilebars_config.lua`, client `game_tileoverlays`, base patch 0041)

Owner request: our own small map overlays. The server half is a bar over a map position; the client half also draws
field timers (client only, see client/MANIFEST.md "game_tileoverlays").

- **API** (`ChaosTileBars`, any script): `set(id, {pos, label, progress = 0..1, color = "#rrggbb"})`, or a countdown
  `set(id, {pos, label, endsIn = s [, total = s], color [, keep = true]})` that goes away by itself when it ends;
  `owner = player` shows it to that character only. `set` again updates; `progress(id, v)`, `remove(id)`,
  `removePrefix(prefix)`, `get(id)`. Ids are strings up to 64 characters; labels up to 32 characters; at most 500 bars.
- **Sending.** A global event every 250 ms (`tickMs`) works out who sees each bar (`Game.getSpectators` on the bar's
  floor, 9 x 7 tiles; an owner bar by the owner's name and guid) and sends one message per player with something new:
  `bars {s = [{i, p = [x, y, z], n, c, v | l + t}], d = [ids]}` on opcode **156**, at most 40 bars per message (far
  under 8192 bytes). A countdown goes as ms left (`l`) and in all (`t`), so the client counts it down by itself with no
  further messages. A change of the progress alone reaches a player at most every 500 ms (`progressMs`) and only when
  it moved by 0.01 or reached 0 or 1; label, colour and place changes go out on the next tick. A player who walks away
  gets the id in `d`, and the bar again when back. The client sends `hello` at every game start (and when its module
  loads in game): the server forgets what that player had and answers `clear`; logout forgets too. No storages, no
  tables; bars live in memory (kept over `/reload scripts`, gone at a restart).
- **Users wired now** (each can be turned off in `tilebars_config.lua`):
  - Battleground: a bar over each brazier during the fight (`bg:<match>:<i>`), the capture progress towards the team
    that leans on it in its colour, "(contested)" in grey while both teams stand in it, "<name>: <team>" when held.
    Set at the 1 s capture tick, removed when the match ends.
  - Professions: after a vein or herb patch is gathered, "Ready in m:ss" over it for the gatherer only, as long as the
    node cooldown (`respawnMin`, 6 minutes).
  - Invasions: "Breach" over the target point while the waves come (red, the breach meter 0..100%); removed at the end
    and when stopped. Other events have no capture or channel time to show.
- **Opcode 156** was checked free: not in `ChaosOpcodes`, not 120 (admin), not in the reference server's list or the
  base client's `ExtendedIds`, not registered by any Chaos or base module; 154 and 155 are taken by other modules being
  added. `tests/tilebars_test.lua` checks it.
- **Tests:** `tests/tilebars_test.lua` (set / update / remove, countdown expiry, spectator range and floor, owner bars,
  the progress throttle and coalescing, walking away and back, hello and logout, message size, the brazier bar, the
  glue on a mocked engine, the three users wired); client `game_tileoverlays/tileoverlayslogic_test.lua`.
- **Tested live** (a small test map, the Linux client built from the base with patches 0001-0041, two clients):
  bars set from a script showed over their tiles, stacked when two share a tile, a countdown counted down by itself
  and was dropped at its end, and they came back after the module was reloaded (hello). A 1v1 battleground match
  (test minimum): the West Well's bar filled in the colour of the team in the circle, showed "(contested)" while both
  stood in it, "West Well: Ashbound" when held, and went away for both clients when the match was stopped. A vein
  gathered with a pick showed "Ready in 5:56" over it for the gatherer; the other character next to it got nothing.
  The invasion breach bar was not run live (unit tests only).

## Autosave in steps (`src-patches/0026-incremental-save.patch`, `tools/patch_base_save.py`, `tests/base_save_patch_test.lua`, `tools/chaossave_test.cpp`)

Owner request: "Optimize the autosave time. Keep the warnings." The base autosave (`data/globalevents/scripts/save.lua`,
every hour) broadcast three warnings and then saved every online player and every house in one dispatcher task. The
game stood still for the whole save: 1.2-1.4 s with 200 loaded players, about 2.1-2.5 s at 400. The backup's SIGUSR1 save
did the same 4 times a day, and the save set the game state back to normal, which reopened a server closed with
`/closeserver`.

What players see: the same three warnings at the same times (5, 3 and 1 minute before, same text), then no freeze.

How it works:
- **Players in steps.** `Game.saveIncremental([playersPerTick = 10[, tickBudgetMs = 25[, tickDelayMs = 50[,
  housesPerTick = 100]]]])` (engine patch 0026) writes the account storage in the first tick, then the online players
  one by one while the tick's budget allows: at most 10, and another player only when the time so far plus the last
  player's time fits 25 ms. Between ticks the game runs for 50 ms (the scheduler's minimum). Then the changed houses.
  It returns false while a pass runs; `Game.isSaving()` tells. One console line at the end: `> Saved in steps: N
  players (L logged out before, F failed), H changed house(s); T ticks, longest X ms, total Y s`.
- **Consistency.** Each player save is the stock one, one transaction per character, so `player:save()` and the
  "save before credit" rule (`Chaos.saveCharacter`: market, orb exchange, stash, bank, ...) work as before. A player who
  logs out before his turn was saved by the logout; one who logs in during the pass is not in it (he was just loaded).
  Characters are written a few seconds apart instead of in the same instant. That is what logouts already do, so a
  crash right after a pass can leave a trade between two characters half written, exactly as a crash after one of them
  logged out could before. A shutdown during a pass ends it; the shutdown saves everything.
- **Houses only when changed.** Every save (the pass and the full save of a shutdown, `/closeserver`, `/save`,
  `saveServer()`) writes only the houses whose database rows differ from memory: the `houses` row (owner, paid,
  warnings, name, town, rent, size, beds), the guest, subowner and door lists, and the `tile_store` rows (anything on
  the house tiles: items added, removed, moved or changed, container contents, texts, beds). The engine compares by
  content: it serializes each house as the stock save would and compares a signature of the sorted rows with what the
  database holds. So no change can slip past a missed event; the scan of all 1,057 houses (about 10,500 tile rows)
  takes about 15 ms and no database work. At startup the engine records what it read per house, so the first save
  after a start writes only what differs (0 houses on an unchanged map). A database it could not read (a new one)
  makes the first save write every house. The changed houses go in one transaction per chunk of 100 (one INSERT ... ON
  DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE for the rows, one DELETE + INSERT for the lists and one for the tile rows). Rows of houses the map
  no longer has are deleted by the first save, as the stock full rewrite did. A failed write marks those houses unknown,
  so the next save writes them in full; `house:save()` keeps the record in step. A crash loses what it lost before: the
  changes since the last save. Note: a house row changed in the database by hand while the server runs is now kept
  until that house changes in game (before, the next save overwrote it). Edit houses with the server stopped.
- **The game state.** The base `save.lua` set `GAME_STATE_NORMAL` after every save. `patch_base_save.py` takes that line
  out, and the pass never changes the state: a closed server stays closed (the stock full save still enters the
  maintenance state only when the state was normal).
- **Logout writes.** The base logout wrote two rows every time: the outfit columns (`creaturescripts/scripts/logout.lua`,
  an UPDATE of `wings_id`, `shader_id`, `aura_id`) and a skill history row (`scripts/customs/znote/player_history.lua`,
  an INSERT). The outfit UPDATE now runs only when the columns differ from what `login.lua` read; the history row only
  when level, experience, base magic level, skills, balance, town, skull or blessings changed since the login (the base
  magic level: equipment put on after the login event changes the effective one). The statement is the stock one,
  untouched. A character with no history row at its login (a new one; the stock login's INSERT ... SELECT needs the
  website's `znote_players` table and fails without it, a stock console error) writes its row at the first logout.
  The row at a death is written as before. Without a login record (a reload in between) both are written as before.
  On the test server: 20 new characters wrote 20 rows at their first logout; two more sessions with nothing changed
  wrote none (no SQL or Lua error at logout; before, every logout wrote a row).
- **SIGUSR1 (backups).** `backup.sh` sends SIGUSR1 at 00:15, 06:15, 12:15 and 18:15, then waits 15 s. SIGUSR1 now starts
  the same pass instead of the full save, so the noon and evening backups no longer freeze the game. The pass ends well
  inside the 15 s (3.3-3.9 s at 200 online, about 7-8 s at 400). If a dump starts earlier, every character in it is still
  whole, as of its last save.
- **Still full saves:** the daily save (it kicks every player, each saved at the kick, then saves the houses), a
  shutdown (SIGTERM), `/closeserver` and `/save`. With the house change the house part of those is about 15 ms.

Install: `install_all.py` step `autosave` runs `tools/patch_base_save.py DATA_DIR [--dry-run]` (idempotent, a marker in
every changed file; a file without the stock lines is reported and the step fails). The engine needs patch 0026;
without it the patched `save.lua` falls back to the stock full save (still without the state change). Tuning: the
four parameters of `Game.saveIncremental`; more players per tick or a larger budget makes the pass shorter and the
ticks longer.

Measured on the full base map with every Chaos system installed, a private MariaDB (default settings, one fsync per
commit), 200 bot characters (`tools/loadtest.py`: walking every second, talking every 20 s) with a seeded inventory
(7 worn items, a backpack with two bags, 47 items, about 8 KB of attributes) and depot (4 backpacks and 30 loose items,
110 items, about 20 KB; every 4th bot opened its depot each session, so its depot is written at each save). The
longest stall is the longest single dispatcher task (a temporary log of every task over 20 ms). Each line: 3 runs or
more.

| | before (stock save) | after (in steps) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 players: total | 320-372 ms (houses: every row rewritten) | 15 ms full save, 116-118 ms pass (0 changed houses) |
| 0 players: longest stall | 320-372 ms | 15-17 ms |
| 200 players: total | 1,218-1,415 ms | 3.3-3.9 s (44-51 ticks) |
| 200 players: longest stall caused by the save | 1,218-1,415 ms | 26-30 ms (longest task of any kind in the window: 37-123 ms, the game's own; outside saves p90 51 ms, p99 238 ms) |
| 400 players (extrapolated) | about 2.1-2.5 s stall | about 7-8 s total, ticks still about 30 ms |
| warnings | 5 min, +120.0 s, +240.0 s, save at +300.0 s | the same |

Tests: `tests/base_save_patch_test.lua` (the tool on the stock lines; the patched scripts against a mocked engine: the
warnings' text and timing, the save call, no state change, the outfit and history rules, idempotence, dry run, an
unknown file), `tools/chaossave_test.cpp` in CI (the tick budget, the pass queue, the house signatures, the change
test). On a live test server: a change on a house tile, a container's contents only, an owner and a guest list were
each saved by the next pass (1 or 2 changed houses), survived a restart, and the first save after the restart wrote 0
houses; reverting them was saved the same way.

## Game loop stalls (`src-patches/0027-game-loop-stalls.patch`, `tools/patch_base_stalls.py`, `item_mods.lua`, `respawn.lua`)

The autosave work measured, outside saves, game loop stalls of 250-650 ms every 20-25 s (once about 0.9 s) with 200 bots
on the full map. Found and fixed here.

**How it was found.** The test setup of "Autosave in steps": the full base map with every Chaos system, a private MariaDB,
200 bots of `tools/loadtest.py` (walking every second, talking every 20 s), here spread over ten town temples with a
seeded inventory (7 worn rarity items, a backpack with two bags and 36 more rarity items). Engine patch 0027 adds the
slow task log (below), which names the Lua script and line, the database queries and the collector's sweep of every
task over a limit. Two TEST ONLY scripts that are not in the repo: a 50 ms timer that records its own lag (the tick
jitter) and a per-script count of Lua heap growth (an engine build with a temporary allocation counter). `perf` showed
no C++ hotspot behind the stalls (pathfinding, decay, spawns and creature think stayed under 20 ms a task); the time
was in Lua.

**Causes, with the evidence.**
1. *The equipment check of `item_mods.lua`* (every 3 s, every player online in one task): 50-120 ms at 200 online, and
   160-270 ms whenever the Lua collector finished a cycle inside it (`[slow task] 265 ms | lua 265 ms ...
   item_mods.lua:203 | lua gc freed 59981 KB`). 94-97 of the 96-126 tasks over 50 ms in each 5 minute run were this one.
   It was also the largest source of Lua garbage: 265 MB a minute, half of all (540 MB), mostly a closure made per call
   by `pcall(function() ... end)` for every catalogue modifier of every worn item (`data/lib/chaos_item_mods.lua`
   `custom`). The heap went 60 -> 120 MB and back every 20-40 s; the end of each cycle swept 20-60 MB inside one task,
   which made the stalls of 250-650 ms every 20-25 s.
2. *The expedition announcements of the base server* (`data/scripts/customs/expeditions_system/`, 24 scripts, about 11
   spawn times a day each): every tile of an island box (627,000 tiles) was looked at for players, 0.6-0.9 s each time
   (`spawn_npc_aurostor.lua:39` 884 ms, `spawn_npc_abxal.lua:38` 839 ms, `spawn_npc_myrianus.lua:38` 608-665 ms). This
   was the 0.9 s stall.
3. *The dynamic respawn* (`respawn.lua`, every 20 s): one pass over all 50,522 map spawns per busy zone, 6-10 ms a pass
   (25-60 ms a tick at a few zones, 250 ms and more with dozens of hunting groups).
4. *The upgrade-slot check of the base server* (`customs/upgrade/upgrade_slot_item.lua`, every 100 ms per player): no
   stall by itself (0.1 ms a call) but 11 s of every minute of game loop at 200 online and 170 MB a minute of garbage
   (a pattern iterator and tables per worn item, ten times a second).

Not a cause (looked at): synchronous database queries outside logins (none over 20 ms in the steady state), JSON
payloads, the leaderboards, the bounty board, community goals, world events, the anti-bot, the market and orb exchange
sweeps, the season, invasions and the base raids (each under 20 ms a run). A login runs 85-110 queries on the
game loop (30-120 ms a login); see "Left as it is".

**Fixes.** Same behaviour in each case, except 7, which fixes a base bug.
1. `item_mods.lua`: the check runs in 12 groups of players (player id modulo 12), one group every 250 ms, so every player
   is still checked every 3 s with the same regeneration. `chaos_item_mods.lua`, `chaos_gems.lua`, `chaos_veiled.lua`
   and `chaos_item_sets.lua` call `pcall` on named functions instead of a new closure per call: the check makes 85% less
   garbage (40 MB a minute instead of 265) in half the time.
2. `tools/patch_base_stalls.py` (install step `stalls`): each expedition scan loops over the positions of the players
   online inside the box (the same x-then-y order) instead of every tile; the body is untouched, and a tile without a
   player never had a player as its top creature, so the same players get the same sound, marks and broadcasts.
3. Engine patch 0027 `Game.setSpawnIntervalZones(globalPercent, zones)`: the respawn tick's zones in one call, through an
   index of the spawns by 16 x 16 cell (`src/chaoszones.h`); only the spawns of the new and the last zones are touched.
   `respawn.lua` uses it when the engine has it, else the old calls.
4. `tools/patch_base_stalls.py` again: the upgrade-slot check keeps the slots it parsed per item description text (the
   same text gives the same slots; the description is still read every time): 56 MB of garbage a minute instead of 170,
   8 s of game loop a minute instead of 11.
5. The Lua collector's settings are not changed: with LuaJIT the pause and step multiplier only move the same sweep work
   between tasks. Less garbage (1, 4) is what shortened the sweeps: all Lua together made about 540 MB a minute before
   and about 215 MB after (200 online, no rain).
6. `tools/patch_base_stalls.py` step 3 (owner decision 2026-10-12): the upgrade-slot check runs less often. The stock
   script gave each player a 100 ms timer of its own. Now the check runs at login (as before), at once when an item
   is put on or taken off (an `EventCallback onItemMoved` with an inventory slot on either side, index 13: drag and
   drop, the equip hotkey and right-click equips since engine patch 0024), and once a second for every player in 12
   groups (player id modulo 12, one group every 83 ms, like `item_mods.lua`). The second-by-second pass catches what
   moves no item: decay, a script's `moveTo`, an upgrade rune or an orb used on a worn item; those apply within 1 s
   instead of 100 ms. The check itself is unchanged, and a player who left is dropped from its cache by the pass, as
   before. After `/reload scripts` the new chain takes over the players online and the old chain stops.
   **Estimate, not measured:** the check took 8 s of game loop a minute at 200 online (13%) after the cache of 4, at
   10 checks a second per player. At 1 a second plus the equip moves that is about 0.8-0.9 s a minute (1.3-1.5%): about
   7 s a minute (11-12% of the game loop) saved at 200 online, about 14 s a minute at 400. Its garbage drops in the same
   ratio (56 MB a minute to about 6), and the scheduler runs 12 events a second for it instead of 10 per player.
7. `tools/patch_base_stalls.py` step 4 (owner decision 2026-10-12): the upgrade-slot condition ids, a base bug found
   with fix 6. The stock check added a slot's bonus with the condition subid `90 + slot + 10 x index`
   (`CONST_SLOT_AMMO`) and removed it with `90 + slot + 16 x index` (`CONST_SLOT_GLOVES`). So an item taken off,
   swapped for one with fewer slots or decayed kept its skill bonus until logout. Ids of different slots also met,
   so an empty slot took another slot's bonus away (the helmet's second slot `90 + 1 + 20` is the right hand's
   first removal id `90 + 5 + 16`). Now the bonus is added with the removals' id. `16 x index` gives one id per slot
   and index for slots 1-16 (`CONST_SLOT_GLOVES` is the last slot). A removed or swapped item's bonus goes away on
   the next check: at once on the item move, within 1 s for decay or a script. The first check of a player after
   the script loads clears both ids of every slot once (a login, or `/reload scripts` with the player online). So a
   bonus still on under the old id is not kept next to the new one. These conditions have ticks -1, which the engine
   does not save, so after a restart no old id is left anyway. No other script uses the subids 101-154. The `Attr`
   compare by identity stays: every check removes and adds each slot bonus again, which also puts back a bonus that
   another script removed.
8. `tools/patch_base_stalls.py` step 5: an emptied slot is forgotten. The check keeps the bonus it added per player
   and subid (`slotAttribute.cache`). The removals (an emptied slot, the indexes an item no longer has) took the
   condition off but kept that entry. With the identity compare above this changed nothing, since every check adds
   every bonus again. With a compare by value (the base's intent, should `Attr.__eq` ever be fixed) the same item
   put back on would match the stale entry and stay without its bonus. The removals now drop the entry too. Own
   marker, so a base patched up to step 4 gets it on the next install.

**Measured** (the setup above, 200 bots, 3 runs each, before and after taken in turns; 5 minutes at 200 online per
run; the box ran other test servers and builds at the same time, so single outliers can be the machine). A stall is a
game loop task of 250 ms or more. Tick jitter: the lag of a 50 ms timer over the engine's 50 ms floor.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| stalls of 250 ms and more | 2.1 / 3.0 / 3.2 a minute (every 19-29 s), 2 of 0.8-0.9 s | 0 / 0.2 / 0 a minute (the one: a 272 ms task with 0 ms of Lua, the machine) |
| tasks of 100 ms and more | 6.4 / 7.8 / 13.1 a minute | 0 / 0.6 / 0 a minute |
| longest task | 314 / 884 / 420 ms | 86 / 273 / 77 ms |
| tasks over 20 ms: p90, p99 | 232, 312 / 247, 839 / 176, 385 ms | 73, 85 / 67, 272 / 63, 77 ms |
| all tasks: p99.99 | 56 / 61 / 76 ms | 12 / 19 / 12 ms |
| 50 ms timer lag: standard deviation, worst | 26 / 38 / 36 ms, 375 / 907 / 575 ms | 4 / 9 / 4 ms, 130 / 290 / 124 ms |
| game loop CPU (loadtest.py, % of one core) | 44 / 44 / 58 | 38 / 55 / 43 |

Runs 3 (before) and 2 (after) had the base weather's rain on (`customs/globalevents/rain.lua`: an effect per player every
100 ms, 10-20% more game loop), hence their higher CPU. At 400 online (estimate, not measured): before, the equipment
check alone would take 110-240 ms every 3 s and the collector's cycles end about twice as often, so stalls of 0.5-1 s
every 10-20 s; after, a group of the check takes 5-10 ms and the sweeps grow with the garbage, so the longest tasks
should stay around 100-150 ms with no stall over 250 ms from these causes.

**Left as it is.**
- Logins run 85-110 synchronous queries on the game loop (30-120 ms a login: the Chaos systems' login reads). In the 100 s
  login wave of a load test the database stalled for seconds at a time (a 13.6 s task, 5.6 s of it waiting for the
  connection the async query thread held, on this test machine's disk); with 1 bot a second it stayed under 120 ms. The
  account check moved to the login workers' own connection ("Login rush on a busy machine", engine patch 0029); the
  login scripts' reads moved there too since engine patch 0031 ("Login reads off the game loop").
- A logout saves the character in one transaction on the game loop; its COMMIT waits for the database's log flush. When
  100-200 bots left at once on this test machine (its disk shared with other test servers), single logouts took
  0.3-1.7 s with 0 ms of Lua and a few ms of timed queries; `perf` showed the game loop thread blocked in the database
  client's poll inside the save, so the COMMIT, which the slow task log did not count then (it does since this patch).
  A calm repeat with 100 bots: every logout under 30 ms, the longest part a 12 ms COMMIT. Not a steady-state stall.
- The base weather's rain (above) when it rains (6 s of game loop and 57 MB of garbage a minute at 200 online, ticks
  of 10-20 ms, a few of 70-180 ms): since O208 it is off (`tools/patch_base_rain.py`) and the client draws the rain, see
  "Weather on the client (O208)"; the base rarity check (`customs/rarity/base_rarity.lua`, 2 s and 42 MB a minute).
  Both are base scripts that work as designed; no stall over 250 ms from either in these runs.

Tests: `tests/item_mods_test.lua` (the 12 groups, every player once in 3 s, regeneration), `tests/respawn_test.lua`
(`R.zoneList`, the glue with `Game.setSpawnIntervalZones`), `tests/base_stalls_patch_test.lua` (the tool on the stock
code; the stock and patched scripts give the same players, marks, broadcasts and conditions against a mocked engine
with a clock, the conditions compared once each change has settled for 1 s; the upgrade check at login and at once
on an equip move, 24 players each checked once a second in groups of 2 per 83 ms tick, a player who left dropped,
one chain after a reload; after login, equip, unequip, swap, decay, relog and a reload every player has the bonuses
of the worn items, each once, which the stock script fails and the patched one passes; the sword put back on gets its
bonus again, also with a compare by value, which fails without step 5; every slot 1-16 and index 1-3 adds under its
own subid and is removed under the same one; idempotence, dry run, CRLF, a script patched by an older tool gets
steps 3 to 5), `tools/chaoszones_test.cpp` in CI (the index against the old way over 300 random zone lists).

### Slow task log (`slowTaskLogMs`, engine patch 0027)

Off by default. `slowTaskLogMs = 100` in `config.lua` logs every game loop task (the dispatcher's tasks, scheduler events
included) that took 100 ms or more, one console line:

    [slow task] 265 ms | lua 265 ms in 1 call(s), longest 265 ms data/scripts/chaos/item_mods.lua:203 | lua gc freed
      59981 KB | db 3 ms in 10 queries (waiting for the connection 0 ms), longest 1 ms: INSERT ... | task std::_Bind<...>

- *lua*: the Lua calls the task made (globalevents, creaturescripts, revscripts, `addEvent` callbacks, events), their
  time, and the longest by its file and the line where its function starts.
- *lua gc freed*: the Lua heap shrank by that much during one call: the collector swept there.
- *db*: the queries the game loop ran itself, their time, the part spent waiting for the connection (the async query
  thread uses the same one) and the start of the longest.
- *task*: the C++ type of the task (a `std::_Bind` names the function's signature; with GCC and Clang it is demangled).

Off, it costs one config read per task. On, about 1 us per Lua call (well under 1% of the game loop at 200 online). Use
it on a test server, or on the live one for an hour when players report lag. The log does not change what runs.

## Login reads off the game loop (`src-patches/0031-login-reads-prefetch.patch`, `tools/chaosprefetch_test.cpp`)

The onLogin scripts of the Chaos systems (and a few base ones) read about 70 result sets per login with `db.storeQuery`
on the game loop: one or two per system, by player id, account id or name. With 200 bots on the full map that was
14-15 ms of database time in a login task of 37-39 ms (p50), more when the database is busy ("Game loop stalls", "Left
as it is"). Engine patch 0031 runs them on the login worker instead. No script changed.

**How.** After the password check the login worker (patch 0014, its own connection since 0029) looks up the character
id and runs the SELECTs earlier logins ran, for this player. While the onLogin scripts run, `db.storeQuery` answers a
statement with exactly the same text from those rows. Anything else goes to the database as before: a different text,
a write, a query outside the onLogin scripts, a table written meanwhile, rows older than 5 s.
- *Which SELECTs.* Learnt from the logins themselves: each SELECT an onLogin script runs is kept with the player id,
  the account id and the quoted name taken out, and run for the next logins. One that no login runs again is dropped
  (after 2 prefetches if one login ran it, 50 if more did); at most 512, 256 per login. The first login after a start
  reads everything on the game loop.
- *Only plain reads.* A SELECT of tables of this database, nothing that depends on when or where it runs: no time,
  random, lock or connection function, no user variable, `FOR UPDATE`, `INTO`, comment, other schema or stored
  function of the database. A read that has the current time in its text (`referral.lua` bans check) never matches
  and stays on the game loop.
- *Same rows as on the game loop.* Every connection (the game loop's, the async query thread's, the login workers')
  counts its writes per table after they are committed (in a transaction at its COMMIT or ROLLBACK). A write also
  counts for the tables its foreign keys (`ON DELETE` / `ON UPDATE CASCADE`, `SET NULL`) and triggers reach, read
  from `information_schema` at start and again after every `CREATE` / `ALTER` / `DROP` / `RENAME` (scripts create
  tables at startup). A statement that cannot be told apart (a multi-table `UPDATE` or `DELETE`, `CALL`, DDL) counts
  for every table. The worker notes the counts of a read's tables before the read; the rows are used only if they are
  unchanged when the script asks. A write the website makes during the login has no order against it, as before: the
  early read is the same as a login a few milliseconds earlier.
- *Off.* `loginPrefetch = false` in `config.lua` (read at start) reads everything on the game loop as before. The
  console says which at start (`>> Login reads: ...`). The slow task log counts the answered reads (`db prefetched N`).

**Measured** (the setup of "Game loop stalls": the full map, every install step, a private MariaDB, 200 bots of
`tools/loadtest.py` near the second temple with account ids different from the character ids; 3 runs before and 3
after, taken in turns, 90 s at 200 online; a temporary timer around the login task and the onLogin scripts, not in the
repo).

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| login task on the game loop: p50 | 39.0 / 36.9 / 37.1 ms | 20.5 / 21.9 / 23.3 ms |
| p90, p99 | 56.6, 79.5 / 52.7, 69.7 / 52.4, 74.0 ms | 30.2, 50.1 / 33.1, 63.5 / 35.7, 64.5 ms |
| mean | 42.1 / 39.2 / 39.7 ms | 23.2 / 24.9 / 25.7 ms |
| onLogin scripts: queries to the database, their time (p50) | 70, 13.9-15.0 ms | 1, 0.2-0.3 ms (69 answered from the worker's rows) |
| the bots' login time p50 (connect to in game) | 531 / 521 / 543 ms | 497 / 525 / 556 ms |
| in game | 200 / 200 each run | 200 / 200 each run |

So about 16 ms less game loop per login (3 s over a wave of 200 logins); the worker's extra reads do not show in the
login time. The longest login task after (112 ms, once) was 74 ms of Lua with 0.6 ms of database (`hideout.lua`, a
collector sweep). What stays on the game loop per login: the scripts' own work (about 17 ms p50: `rightclick_equip.lua`,
`hideout.lua` and the others), their writes (`INSERT IGNORE` of new achievements, the daily account row, the skill
history), the reads of a table written meanwhile, and the engine's own player load (`IOLoginData::loadPlayerById`, about
17 queries, untouched).

**Checked.** A TEST ONLY build compared every answered read with a live read of the same text: 0 differences in
13,700 answers with 200 bots, on the build measured and on the final one. With a write to the player's `players` row
injected between the early read and the login (half as a plain `UPDATE`, half inside a `DBTransaction`), every read of
`players` went to the database and the rest were answered, 0 differences. With `loginPrefetch = false` all 70 reads went
to the database.

Tests: `tools/chaosprefetch_test.cpp` in CI (which reads are prefetched, what a write writes from its first tokens,
templates, the cascade and trigger closure, the clock with transactions and autocommit, the template set).

## Tester bots (`testers.lua`, `testers_core.lua`, `src-patches/0059`, `tools/patch_tester_filters.py`)

Owner request: bots that play on the live server to find bugs. They carry a visible TESTER tag. They never count as players.

**Marker.** A tester is a character with player storage 7102900 = 1 (`Chaos.storage.tester`).
Only `tools/testers.py setup` writes it. The engine reads the same key (`CHAOS_TESTER_STORAGE`, src-patch 0059).
Names are "Tester Xxx". Group 1, account type 1. Never staff.

**Never counted online.** A hard requirement. Each place:

| Count | How testers stay out |
|---|---|
| status protocol (XML `<players online>`, 0x20 info, 0x21 list, 0x22 name) | src-patch 0059 counts only non-testers |
| players record (`server_config` players_record, record broadcast) | src-patch 0059: only counted players beat it |
| `players_online` table (website online list and counts) | src-patch 0059: a tester is never inserted |
| waiting list, maxPlayers | src-patch 0059: a tester never queues, never takes a slot |
| client login screen (`clientservices.lua` cacheinfo) | `Chaos.countedPlayers()` |
| `!online` (base talkaction) | `patch_tester_filters.py` |
| chaos_health (Discord health posts) | reads the status protocol, so testers are left out |
| admin panel `stats` / `online` | labelled: "N (+M tester bots)", "[TESTER bot, not counted]" |

**Never ranked or announced.**
- Weekly leaderboards (`LB.record`), records (`memberOf`), the chronicle (`memberList`): tester guids skipped.
- Discord queue (`discord.lua` `X.queue`): an event naming a tester is dropped.
- `Game.broadcastMessage`: a broadcast naming a tester is dropped (level, achievement, prize lines).
- Base in-game highscores (opcode 73) and the top 3 statues: `patch_tester_filters.py` (install step `events`).
- Website: `website/patches/znotex-chaos-testers.patch` (highscores, latest deaths); `chaos_tester_sql()` on the
  sidebar top 10, class ladders, boards, records and mentors.

**Kept apart from players** (`testers.lua`):
- No combat between a tester and a player, summons included. Monsters hit testers for real.
- No trade, no mixed party. Market `buy`, `list`, `orderPost`, `fill` refused for testers.
- A look at a tester says it is a test character. The plate shows the title TESTER (priority 1000).
- Login refused for a tester in a staff group, on a staff account, or without a "Tester Xxx" name. Logged.
- Antibot and bot review skip testers: they are bots by design.
- Players cannot take a name with the word "Tester": game `staffWords`, website `chaos_character_name_tester`.
- No mail. A tester's parcel or letter is refused at the mailbox. So is one to a "Tester Xxx" name.
  `testers.lua` wraps `ChaosDepot.onMoveItem`, the move hook of `patch_base_depot.py`.

### The bots (`tools/testers.py`, `tools/tester_core.py`)

Built on `loadtest.py` (login, client guard answer, 10.98 packets). Standard library only.
- `setup`: N accounts `tstbot` + 10 random hex digits, one random password each.
  Characters "Tester Aaa" upward; a name a player owns is skipped. Levels 30/100/250/500/750/1000/1250/1500/1750/2000 in turn (each band 1/10 of the testers), the classes shifted
  by one each round (`plan_bots`).
  Rows: account type 1, group 1, the marker storage, the hunt spot (+2..+4) on a hunt of its level.
  The hunt is chosen by `tester_core.safe_hunts`: the whole band of the map mark (hunting levels since 2026-10-27; `baseLevelMult` is 1 since 2026-10-28, O285,
  so the pool levels of `bounty_pool.lua` are hunting levels too), at or under the tester's level, and on a spawn centre whose monsters all
  hunt at or under its level (`loadtest.spawn_levels`, from `bounty_pool.lua` and the spawn file); none within 30 sqm: the temple.
  State: `/var/lib/chaos/testers/state.json`, mode 0600, root. It holds the passwords.
- `run`: every bot logs in from its own 127.1.x.y address (the 2-per-IP rule). Secure mode on.
  Real damage, real death. A death is seen (0x28 or "You are dead."); the bot logs in again, rests in the temple
  (`tester_core.death_rest`: 20 s, doubled for each death within 5 minutes, at most 300 s) and then says `!tester hunt`.
  Heals itself: its best healing spell of spells.xml under 60 % health.
  Under 40 % a health potion by the hotkey packet: 0x84, position 0xFFFF, its own creature id.
  Casts its class rotation (`loadtest.rotation_for`).
  Then a weighted behaviour (`tester_core.BEHAVIOURS`, each with a cooldown): hunt, wander, town, depot (opens a
  locker, 0x82), shop (hi, trade, buy potions 0x7A, sell 0x7B, close 0x7C, bye), party, private message,
  client opcodes, loot (loot filter take, open the backpack), relog.
  A dropped connection is retried with a growing pause (up to 2 min). The bots survive a server restart.
  After `--minutes` (default 60) they log out. SIGTERM ends them early.
- `report`: the server log from the run's start offset, and `run.json` of the bots.
- `cleanup`: see below.

The bot's own "death within one hit from full health" needs a health update it really saw less than 0.5 s before; the exact
rule is the helper's (health, maximum and damage of one hit on the server). The helper's death line carries the hits of the
last 5 seconds (count, sum and biggest hit as % of the maximum health, seconds since the login) and the report summarizes them.

What a bot reads: health percent (0x8C), text messages (failures, Lua error texts, experience, loot, level),
the NPC trade window, extended opcode answers (chunked S/P/E joined).

**First live run (2026-10-27, 100 testers of level 30 to 99, 20 minutes).** 2998 deaths and 500 "death within one hit from
full health" anomalies. Causes found:
- The testers stood on the wrong ground. The map marks print the pool level of a band ("level 20-30"; the middle 70 % of its
  monsters, so up to 15 % are above it), the hunting level was twice that (until 2026-10-28, O285: `baseLevelMult` is 1 now and the tools read it), and `snap_to_spawn` moved a tester to the nearest
  spawn centre of any monster within 12 sqm. The killers had pool levels of 20 (Terror Bird, Frost Giant) to 284 (Juggernaut),
  hunting levels 40 to 568, for characters of 295 to 515 health with a plain weapon and no armour. Now `safe_hunts`, `spawn_levels`
  and `place_testers` (see "The bots").
- A dead tester went back to the same pack in the next second (17-35 s between two deaths of the same tester). Now it rests
  in the temple (`death_rest`).
- The anomaly was the bot's own: health starts at 100 % in the bot and a tester that died one second after the login never saw
  an update. The server side rule (helper `hitAnomaly`, exact numbers) fired 0 times: no single hit reached the maximum health. A
  bot-side anomaly now needs an update seen less than 0.5 s before; the helper's death line carries the last hits.
- Second live run (2026-10-28, after O285): every death line had `damage` 0 and `biggest` 0 with `hits` > 0. The engine passes
  `onHealthChange` damage as negative numbers and the helper summed `max(0, value)`; `H.damageOf` (`tester_helper_core.lua`) takes the
  size and leaves healing out, which also lets the "hit taken / dealt far above the level" rules fire at last. `online` in a death
  line is the seconds since the login, not a player count: now `secsOnline` (the report reads both). The killers (pool level 16 to
  509, tester level 30-63) stood next to testers because `snap_to_spawn` checked only the chosen spawn centre: now every spawn
  centre within `SNAP_CLEAR` (14 sqm) must be at or under the level too, and `!tester hunt` stays in the temple (answer
  "hunt spot too high") when a monster within 7 tiles of the hunt spot has a hunting level above the tester's (`H.hotSpot`), as a
  tester set up before the fix keeps its old spot. After a fix run `chaos-ctl.sh testers cleanup` and `setup` again.
- Keystone test: 1240 nodes "not tested: the bot left the game" and the FAILs "no answer to planApply / statTotals" were
  bots that died in the middle. The scenario now goes on after the login and drops the node it was cut off in.
  A hunt mark's band is the pool level, which is the hunting level since O285.

### A save that fails for one character (`src-patches/0080`, `tools/testers.py cleanup`)

Owner log 2026-10-28: every autosave printed `[Error - Game::saveIncremental] Could not save player Tester Ach.` (summary
`1 failed`) and the shutdown `Error while saving player: Tester Ach`, with no SQL error line.
- **Cause.** `IOLoginData::savePlayer` starts with `SELECT save FROM players WHERE id = <guid>`; an empty result returns false
  without a word (SQL errors print their own `[Error - mysql_real_query]` line, none was in the log). So the `players` row of
  Tester Ach was gone while the character was still in game. The only writer of such a delete is `testers.py cleanup`
  (`chaos-ctl.sh testers cleanup --yes`, the admin app's Apagar): it waits for the bots to log out, but a tester that stays in
  game (a fight, a stuck connection) lost its rows under the engine. It could not be saved at all after that, and the
  progress of that character was dropped. Other candidates (a column out of range, a storage value over 32 bits) all end in an
  SQL error line and are not it.
- **Fix, tool.** `cleanup` now kicks the testers it is about to delete: `kick NAME` lines in `remote.cmd` of the server folder
  (`remote_cmd.lua` runs them every 2.5 s; the logout saves a character whose row is still there), waits `--kick-wait` seconds
  (default 8), then deletes. `chaos-ctl.sh testers cleanup --yes` passes `--server-dir`. The admin app needs no change: its
  button "Apagar os testers" (Comandos tab, card Testers) runs this command (limit 240 s, the stop wait is 120 s). Tests: `tools/testers_test.py`
  (`kick_lines`, `kick_online`), `deploy/chaos_ctl_test.py`.
- **Fix, engine log.** `src-patches/0080-save-failure-step-log.patch`: every `return false` of `savePlayer` logs one line,
  once per character and step (at most 64 per run): `[Error - IOLoginData::savePlayer] NAME (guid N): failed at: STEP.`
  The missing row says `no players row for this guid (character deleted while online?)`. Needs an engine rebuild.
- **Owner, VPS.** Nothing to repair: the character is gone with its rows (a restart already dropped the ghost). Update from the
  admin app (Update button) for the tool, rebuild the engine for the log line. To get rid of the old testers: Comandos > Testers > Apagar os testers; fallback `chaos-ctl.sh testers cleanup --yes`. Checked on a mocked database only, not on the live server.

### The helper (TEST ONLY: `tools/tester_helper.lua`, `tools/tester_helper_core.lua`)

Not under `data/`, so no install step ships it. `chaos-ctl.sh testers start` copies both into `data/scripts` as
`zz_tester_helper*.lua`. `testers stop` and `cleanup` remove them. The loop ends when the file is gone.
- Acts ONLY on a character with the marker storage = 1 AND a "Tester Xxx" name. Anything else is left alone.
  `tests/tester_helper_test.lua` proves it on a mocked engine: a player, a player named like a tester without the
  storage, a player with the storage and another name. None is targeted, moved, given items, answered or logged.
- Never heals. Never prevents a death.
- Gives a target: the nearest unowned monster within 5 tiles, then faces it. Never a player, never a summon.
- Once: a backpack, the plain weapon of its class kit (`ChaosTestKit`, no unique roll), 100 health and mana
  potions, 20000 gold in the bank.
- `!tester info | town | depot | hunt | shop | bag | summons | party | chest | spellquest`: answers one line `[tester-helper] <kind> <json>`
  (`summons`, `party` and `chest` are the probes of the system checks, below).
  Teleports to the temple, next to a depot locker, next to an NPC, back to the hunt spot.
- `!tester places`: the map mark counts by kind (`ChaosPoi`). `!tester enter <kind> [N]`: next to the N-th mark of
  that kind (temple, depot, craft, bank, bless, travel, shop, boss, hunt, portal, dungeon; guild halls refused).
  `enter npc <name>`: next to that NPC; a player's name is refused. `enter rift [tier]`: a rift key of the tier
  (1-15, no modifiers) into the tester's backpack, then the temple. Only the tester moves or receives.
- Anomalies, one console line `[tester-anomaly] <json>` each:
  a hit taken over 3x max health (the 130M one-shot), a hit from full health to death,
  a hit dealt over 5000 + 400 x level, a negative or absurd experience gain,
  an item with an impossible count or attribute (backpack scan once a minute).
- A tester's death: `[tester-event] <json>`.

### On the live server (`chaos-ctl.sh testers`)

The client key. Never the development key: `testers start` refuses `clientGuardAllowDevKey = true`, and `testers.py`
