refuses the development key itself. The real key lives in a root-only file. Create it once, as root:

```
sudo bash -c 'umask 077; read -rsp "client key: " K; echo; printf "%s\n" "$K" > /etc/chaos/tester-client-key'
```

It must be 64 hex digits, owned by root, mode 0600. It never goes on a command line or into a log.
The bots announce the newest client build the guard accepts: the highest of `clientGuardBuilds` at or above the
`min_package` of `clientGuardManifest` (the engine's `ClientGuard::gateReason` refuses anything else), else that
`min_package`, else 1. `testers.py run` prints it.
The login block is encrypted with the key the engine really uses: the first file of `rsaKeyFile` (patch 0046), with
`CHAOS_RSA_KEY_FILE` from chaos.env (chaos-ctl.sh loads it), else `key.pem` of the server folder. Before 2026-10-22 the
bots always took `key.pem`: with our own key the server could not read the block and closed every login without a
message at "waiting for the character list". `testers.py run` prints the key file it uses (only the path).
`CHAOS_TESTER_KEY` in ctl.conf names another file.
A bot takes its own creature id from the helper's `info` answer (`cid`) when the game login answer does not come first
(the client guard's challenge can come before it). Before 2026-10-23 such bots had no id: they read no health packet,
so they never healed or drank a potion, every death looked like one hit from full health, and no bot was a pm or party
partner. `shop` goes to a trader first (`TRADERS` in tester_helper.lua: Material Broker, Loot Buyer, Wandering
Merchant), counts as ok when the trade window opens, and buys or sells one piece (u16 amounts, protocol 10.98). A
failed `town`, `depot` or `shop` names why in the failure list. The report lists the deaths the server logged by
killer, level and tester beside the bots' own count. It reads `error` as a whole word only (a "Terror Bird" death is no
error) and keeps up to three stack traceback lines under a warning.
Since 2026-10-23 (the run with 11,700 deaths in an hour): a bot heals in its own task four times a second, also while a
behaviour waits (a shop visit, a coverage scenario at the hunt); before, it healed only between behaviours. Under 50 %
health with a healing spell it casts no attack spell (the mana is for the heal), and the heal sets its group cooldown
(no "exhausted" from a support spell of the same group right after it). A heal or a potion counts ok when the health
rises within 3 seconds (`HEAL_SEEN`), else failed: before, both were only ever "tried". Under 20 % (`FLEE_AT`) with the
heal and the potion on cooldown the bot says `!tester town` (as a player's Town Portal), at most once a minute, and goes
back to its hunt 15 seconds later (behaviour `flee`). The helper puts a bot next to an NPC or a locker on a straight
neighbour first, never on a floor change or a teleport, next to an NPC only where that NPC is the nearest (only the
nearest answers, `chaos_npc_focus.lua`: a Material Broker in a row of stalls never heard the bot's "hi"), next to a
locker only on an adjacent tile, with the locker's stack position, and looks for a locker 45 tiles round the temple on
its floor and the ones above and below. A shop failure says whether the NPC answered at all.
The coverage table (`gen_tester_scenarios.py`) sends only the actions the client module really sends on an opcode
(a server comparison the client never sends, such as the item tooltip's `kind == "slot"`, is no request), reads a
handler's guard `action ~= "get"` as well as `action == "get"`, and fills a sub-action in the data (the stash's
`make`: Open, SendItems, ...). Before, 9 systems (charms, groundloot, item tooltip, loadouts, nemesis, pact, party
markers, stash, veiled) were tried with requests their servers ignore and never counted ok. The report puts the
systems that never answered, with no refusal and no log error, on one line "no answer, no error".

**First live run (2026-10-27, 100 bots), what each finding was.** Root causes found, none a server bug:
- *Shop 0 of 164.* A bot said `trade` as a plain say after `hi`. The NPC library (`npchandler.lua` onCreatureSay) takes a
  keyword from a focused player only in the NPC channel (talk type 12, `TALKTYPE_PRIVATE_PN`), as the client sends it.
  Now `trade` and `bye` go there (`NPC_CHANNEL`; the coverage NPC dialogs too, step `npc`). Purchase and sale packets used a
  16-bit amount where 10.98 reads one byte. The Loot Buyer lists only what a tester carries; with nothing he buys he says
  "You carry nothing I buy" (counted, expected).
- *Lua errors "attempt to sell a non-sellable item" (64) and "attempt to buy a non-buyable item" (4), 2026-10-28, 48 bots.*
  A real server bug, players could hit it. The stock ShopModule marks "not sold" and "not bought" with a price of -1
  (`addBuyableItem` leaves `sell = -1`, the Loot Buyer's list has `buy = -1`). The engine writes a price as
  `std::max<uint32_t>(price, 0)` (`ProtocolGame::AddShopItem`): the -1 goes out as 4294967295, and `sendSaleItemList` skips
  only a price of 0. So every window offered every item in both tabs, and a carried buy-only item (a pick at the Material
  Broker, the Wandering Merchant's orbs) was offered for sale; `callbackOnBuy` / `callbackOnSell` then raise the error (the
  buy one is worded "ShopModule.onSell" in the base). The bot read 4294967295 as a price, so it bought at the Loot Buyer and
  sold at the Material Broker and the Merchant every visit. Not an id clash: the shop items of the traders have unique
  client ids in `items.otb` (checked against the reverse map, first server id wins), and the sale of an item the bot does
  not carry reaches the same check. Fixed in the data: `tools/patch_shop_prices.py` (install step `shopprices`, test
  `patch_shop_prices_test.py`) makes `ShopModule.requestTrade` send 0 for a negative price (a copy; the shop list and
  `getShopItem` keep -1). The bot treats 4294967295 as no price, never trades on it and counts one failure
  `shop: the trade window prices an item ...` per visit while the server is not patched.
- *Connection closed without a message (65).* The engine logs a player out without a message 60 s after its last ping
  answer (`Player::sendPing`, see src-patch 0034). The bot pinged in its behaviour loop, which stops while the keystone
  scenario waits for minutes. The ping now runs in the always-on guard task as well.
- *"not possible" after wander (823).* A blind step into a wall or a counter: the engine answers "Sorry, not possible."
  A "not possible" within 3 s of a bot's walk is counted as `not possible (a blind step into an obstacle)`, expected.
- *"not enough room" (1225).* The bots loot and never sell, so the backpack fills. The helper has `!tester bag`: it empties
  the backpack of everything but the potions and tops the potions up to 100 (also at login; the supplies were given once,
  a potion count of 100 does not last 29 deaths). A bot calls it every 4 minutes and after 3 "not enough room". A "not
  enough room" within 30 s of a clean-up is reported as its own, unexpected, line.
- *"no helper answer" (town, depot, shop) and "no way".* A bot that died while it waited for the helper has no answer to
  wait for; such a behaviour is now `expected` (a fourth column of the behaviour table), not `failed`. The helper
  answers an error when its teleport next to the locker or the NPC is refused (before, the bot used the locker from
  where it stood and the engine said "There is no way.").
- *Potion and heal spell "failed".* The bot counts a heal ok when its health rises within 3 s. Not cast because of "You do
  not have enough mana." or "You are exhausted.", or dead before it worked: `expected`. What stays `failed` is a heal
  or potion that was used and did not out-heal the damage (a stock potion gives 3 to 10 % of the maximum health).
- *"no answer, no error" (castbar, charms, groundloot, item_tooltip, loadouts, map_marks, pact, partymarkers).* Four
  causes. (1) The generator read the words of a handler's comparisons, not the keys of a dispatch table
  (`actions[msg.action]`, `ACTIONS[m.action]`): charms, loadouts and pact were sent actions they do not have. It reads
  the tables now. (2) A data key no answer carries: the item tooltip needs worn slots, the ground loot `look` needs
  tiles (`HINTS`, `"$near"` = the 3 x 3 tiles round the bot; `tip` / `raise` take an item of the bot's own `look`
  answer), the map overlays need their switch sent as true (`FLAGS`). (3) A request the server answers with nothing by
  design (`SILENT`: castbar `cancel`). (4) A refusal that is the right answer (`EXPECT_REFUSAL`: veiled `choose` answers
  a window the Orb of Unveiling opens; counted ok).

```
sudo /opt/chaos/repo/server/deploy/chaos-ctl.sh testers start 100 60 --restart 300
sudo /opt/chaos/repo/server/deploy/chaos-ctl.sh testers status
sudo /opt/chaos/repo/server/deploy/chaos-ctl.sh testers report
sudo /opt/chaos/repo/server/deploy/chaos-ctl.sh testers log 400       # the newest run's actions and errors
sudo /opt/chaos/repo/server/deploy/chaos-ctl.sh testers stop
sudo /opt/chaos/repo/server/deploy/chaos-ctl.sh testers cleanup          # lists
sudo /opt/chaos/repo/server/deploy/chaos-ctl.sh testers cleanup --yes    # deletes
```

The trial kit reads `/etc/chaos/ctl.conf` (`ctl.conf.trial.example`): server `/opt/chaos-trial/server`, log `/opt/chaos-trial/logs/server.log`.
- `start [N] [MINUTES] [--restart SECONDS] [--keystones] [--checks]`: default 100 bots, 60 minutes; at most 150 and 1440.
  `--keystones`: the keystone and mastery test first (below, "Keystones and masteries").
  `--checks`: the system checks after it (below, "System checks"). Admin app: tab Comandos > card Testers > button
  "Iniciar testando os sistemas".
  The helper loads at a server start. Without "[tester-helper] running vN" (N = HELPER_VERSION in `tools/tester_helper.lua`, raised
  with every change of the helper files) in the log since the newest start, `start` copies the files but counts the helper as not
  loaded (a server still running an older copy prints no version) and refuses, unless `--restart SECONDS`: the usual restart countdown; the bots start 30 s after it.
  First run: `testers.py setup`. Then the run, detached (`setsid`, own process group), log `/var/log/chaos/testers.log`.
  When the minutes are over, the run calls `testers stop --finished` itself.
- `stop`: SIGTERM to the run's group (the bots log out), the helper files removed.
- `status`: running, pid, started, bots, minutes, `online` (testers in game now, as the run counts them; 0 when the run
  stopped saving over 90 s ago), `online_peak`, logins, deaths, `online_server` (the helper's last console count,
  while the run is up), helper copied, helper loaded.
- The helper counts the testers in game once a minute. The server console gets
  `[tester-helper] testers online: N` when the count changed, and every 5 minutes anyway. The activity log gets the
  run's own count once a minute (`online` lines).
- `report`: the server log since the run started (errors grouped as `chaos-ctl.sh errors`, warnings, anomalies),
  then what the bots saw: Lua error texts, failure texts (expected ones marked), kicks and disconnect reasons,
  each with the first bot and what it was doing; behaviours tried / ok / failed; the system coverage (below).
- Every run writes by itself `<state>/runs/run-<date>-<time>.log` (root, 0600): one line per tester action (its
  outcome), login, death, level up, and every error it received (Lua error, failure text, kick, anomaly), with the
  time, the tester, its level and class; at most 300,000 lines. At the end of the run its report (as `report`)
  goes next to it, `run-<date>-<time>-report.txt`. The 20 newest runs are kept. Admin app: Comandos > Testers.
- `log [N]`: the last N lines (default 200, at most 5000) of the newest activity log.
- `cleanup [--yes]`: stops a run; waits 2 minutes after a stop (a character in a fight stays in game).
  Deletes only characters with the marker storage AND a "Tester Xxx" name AND a `tstbot...` account. Exact ids, no
  LIKE. Rows of every table with a `player_id` / `*_player_id` or `account_id` / `*_account_id` column, a house a
  tester owns given back, a tester's house bid dropped. Then the characters, then the empty accounts.
- No config change is made: src-patch 0059 keeps testers out of `maxPlayers`.
  With `bindOnlyGlobalAddress = true`, loopback fails: `testers.py` refuses with that reason.

The admin app runs these through `chaos-ctl.sh` like the other commands (docs/ADMIN_APP.md).

### Coverage (`tools/gen_tester_scenarios.py`, `tools/tester_scenarios.json`, `tools/tester_scenarios.py`)

The table is generated from the sources. CI runs `--check`. Regenerate after a new system, opcode or action:
`python3 -I server/tools/gen_tester_scenarios.py`.
- Every system with a `*_core.lua` gets a kind:
  - `opcode`: the opcode its engine files answer, the actions in the client module's order, the data keys.
  - `place`: the helper's `enter` argument.
  - `staff`: only `/` talkactions. All are staff commands (`Chaos.staffCommand`). Testers are never staff.
  - `out`: what bots truly cannot do, with the reason. Payments, moderation, guilds, market, orb exchange, party
    finder, ranked arena, PvP zones, sieges, anti-bot. The list is `OUT_OF_SCOPE` in the generator.
  - `passive`: reached by play only. The report counts the server log errors that name its files.
- Per opcode, actions never sent (`skip`): those only out-of-scope files answer; money, report and ticket actions;
  world and staff actions (start, stop, reset, grant, give, transfer, gift and the rest of `ADMIN`).
- NPC dialogs: every NPC of `data/npc` with the keywords of its greeting.

`chaos-ctl.sh testers start` passes `--scenarios` with the table. The `opcodes` behaviour then runs a scenario:
- a module's requests: "open" first, then one to three actions in client order, 1.5 s apart;
- a place: `!tester enter`, the opcode of the system there, back to the hunt;
- an NPC: `enter npc`, hi (a plain say), one or two keywords and bye (in the NPC channel, type 12);
- a rift: `enter rift N`, then the key used by hotkey.
Data keys are filled only from the bot's own earlier answers on that opcode. Never invented.
Character keys (name, target, cid, ...) only get a tester. Owner, guid, gift, payment keys are never sent.
Report: per system tried / ok / refused / log errors. A system never reached says why:
out of scope with the reason, passive, or not picked in this run.

### System checks (O110, `tools/tester_checks.py`, `tools/tester_checks_test.py`)

`testers.py run --checks` (`chaos-ctl.sh testers start N M --checks`; the admin app button "Iniciar testando os sistemas"):
after the keystone test (if asked) each bot runs, once, the checks that apply to its class. The coverage layer above only
touches a system (a request, a place); a check asserts something about it. A failed check is a line `BUG <check>: <what>
(<bot>, <class>)` in the report (section "System checks"), in `run.json` (`checks`) and in the testers log (`CHECK` and `BUG`).
A check that cannot run is `skip` with the reason (no spell learned yet, no mana, no pet owned, no other bot in game,
the system is not installed): never faked. A death in the middle drops the check it cut off; it is done again after the login.

| Check | Classes | What it asserts |
|---|---|---|
| `beastmaster_wolf` | Beastmaster | casts Wild Bond (`vael ferh`), at most cap + 1 summons, then 20 s with the wolf: it never targets the owner, a party member or their summons; the owner never holds a summon as target; no ally stays in the wolf's engine target list. Then `!tester town` and back (teleport and leash), 6 s more |
| `necro_minions` | Necromancer, Lich, Bone Lord | the same for Raise Dead (`vael oss`), at most 5 + 1 minions |
| `pets` | all | the pets window answers; a pet the bot owns comes out as a summon, never targets its owner, is gone after `dismiss` |
| `party` | all | the bot invites another bot (0xA3), the other joins (0xA4): the helper sees a party of 2; a summoner casts its summon in the party and keeps the sides rule; after leaving (0xA7) the helper sees no party |
| `rift` | all | `!tester enter rift 1` (a key of tier 1, then the temple) answers without an error, the rift window answers |
| `waystone` | all | the atlas (`waystoneAtlas` `open`) answers without an error |
| `reward_chest` | all | the weekly chest (`weeklyChest` `open`) answers without an error, then `close` |
| `cursed_chest` | all | `!tester chest spawn` puts a chest next to the bot (`idle`), `use` starts the event (`running`, monsters tagged), `abort` ends it and leaves no chest and no monster |
| `auto_setup` | all | the preset of the client's Auto setup table (`autorotation_data.lua`) for the bot's class and level holds only spells that exist on the server (`spells_chaos.xml`, `stock_spells.csv`), are open to the class and are not gated higher (`auto_setup_problems`) |
| `spell_quest` | all, level 500 and up | the line spell quest end to end on the game's own code (`!tester spellquest`, below): reset, `set 1 1 0 0`, 3 kills count, 45 more count and the pity of 40 gives a fragment, a boss counts 25, `set 1 2` fills the counters, `!tester enter npc Archivist Odrenna` (a bot cannot reach her if she was not placed at startup or her XML did not load: BUG), the trial opens at her and is left again, the reward teaches the first spell of the line and pays 2000 gold a level; then the spell is in the server's spell list, open to the class, not gated higher, and in the class's Auto setup data (a preset, the extras or the ultimate; `quest_spell_problems`). The quest is reset at the end (the spell is forgotten again) and the bot goes back to the hunt. A level under 500 is a skip |

The helper commands (TEST ONLY, only for a `Tester Xxx` character with the tester storage): `!tester summons` answers the
bot's summons with the target of each (`none`, `owner`, `summon`, `ally`, `monster`, `player`, seen from the owner), how
many creatures are in each summon's engine target list and how many of them are allies; `!tester party` the party size,
leader and members; `!tester chest [spawn | use | state | abort]` a cursed chest of the bot (`ChaosCursedChest.spawnChest`,
`use`, `failEvent`); `!tester spellquest [state | reset | set Q STEP [KILLS [FRAGMENTS]] | kill [N] [boss] | trial | leave |
complete]` the line spell quests of the bot (`ChaosSpellQuest`; the staff command `/spellquest` is not open to a tester, so
the helper writes the same storages with `ChaosSpellQuestCore.applySet`). `kill` credits N hunt kills of the bot's own level
through `ChaosSpellQuest.credit` (the real counting, the fragment roll and the pity), at most 60 a call; `trial` is
`ChaosSpellQuest.enterTrial` (needs Archivist Odrenna within 6 tiles) and `leave` ends the run; `complete` is the reward
(`ChaosSpellQuest.complete`, only on the trial step). Every answer is the state: quest, step, code, kills, fragments, pity, the
quest's needs, the spell and whether it is learned. Rules of the words: `ChaosTesterHelperCore.parseSpellQuest`.

O86 rules, also in the helper's loop for every tester that has a summon (no check needed), one console line each,
throttled to one per rule and tester per 30 s: `[tester-anomaly] {"rule":"summon_targets_owner"}`,
`summon_targets_ally` (a party member, or the owner's or a member's summon) and `owner_targets_summon`. The report lists them
under the anomalies. Pure rules: `ChaosTesterHelperCore.targetKind` and `summonAnomalies` (`tests/tester_helper_test.lua`).
To run only what matters for the wolf: 20 or more testers (every class gets one), at least two in game at once for the party.

Tests: `tools/tester_checks_test.py` (mocked game: every check passes, fails with its BUG line, and skips; the Auto setup
rule against the real client data; the spell quest on a stateful mock with a switch per rule, and the first quest spell of
every class against the real Auto setup data), `tests/tester_helper_test.lua` (the probes on a mocked engine, a real player's
summons are never probed, and `!tester spellquest` on the real `spellquest.lua`), `testers_test.py` (flag, report section, flush).

### Keystones and masteries (O249, `tools/tester_keytree.py`, `tools/tester_keystones.py`)

Owner request: prove on the live server that the passive tree keystones and masteries do what they promise.

**How the owner runs it.**
1. Admin app: tab Comandos > card Testers > button "Iniciar testando a árvore" (set Quantos and Minutos first; 40 or more
   testers, so every class has a few; 60 minutes or more, a keystone with extra hits waits up to 150 s for its first one).
   When the minutes are over, Relatório (same card) shows the section "Passive tree keystones and masteries".
2. Fallback, on the VPS: `chaos-ctl.sh testers start 100 90 --keystones --restart 300`, then `chaos-ctl.sh testers report`
   (the same text is also in `<state>/runs/run-*-report.txt`, and `testers log 400` has one `KEYTEST` line per node).
   `--restart 300` only restarts the server when the TEST ONLY helper is not loaded yet.

**What a bot does** (before its other behaviours, until it is through; a death or a logout in the middle drops the node it was on
and the same scenario goes on at that node after the next login; the bot waits in the temple and walks to its hunt only for a
keystone with a combat log row, both with the helper's `!tester town` / `hunt`; otherwise only requests of the tree window and the
DPS meter, no development key, no god command):
1. read the tree (`requestNodesUnlocked`, `requestPoints`); clear it with `resetPreset` when something is left on it
2. `planApply` the route to the node; `statTotals` for the baseline
3. mastery: `planApply` the node with effect 1; every other effect with `masteryChoose`. The stats of the effect that the
   totals show (the five attributes, the damage percent per type, `multiIncrement` on every element, the critical chance and
   amount of the tree) must grow by exactly the effect's value. The rest of the effect is named as not observable.
4. keystone: `planApply` route and node together. A flag with a label (`keystone_labels_config.lua`, O255: 202 of the 242 keystone nodes) must make its row
   "Keystone: Name" of the combat log (`open`/`seg`, the tab of the label) grow while the bot hunts; the report names what the hunt needs (a shield, a bow, a second enemy).
5. `resetPreset`, always (also after a refused plan, a failure or a bot that left the game), and the tree is read back.
Bots of one class start at different nodes (their place in the class), the nodes go cheapest route first, a node needs its route
in points (`points = (level - 8) / 4 + boss points`; a keystone is 3 to 32 nodes away).

**Result per node:** `PASS`, `FAIL` (effect missing, wrong amount, plan refused by the server, accepted but not saved, no proc
in 150 s), `NOT OBSERVABLE` (with the reason; the node was allocated), `NOT TESTED` (not enough points, a change of effect or a
reset the character cannot pay, the run ended before the bot was through). A request without an answer while the bot is in the game
is a FAIL with its cause: for `planApply` the tree is read back ("the nodes are saved, the reply was lost" or "nothing saved, the request
was dropped"), `statTotals` is asked twice. Failures are listed first. Nothing unobservable is ever counted as a pass.

**Coverage of the table** (generated; `gen_tester_scenarios.py --check` in CI): 21 classes, 242 keystones, 4 mastery nodes
with 42 effects over 12 classes.

| Class (line) | Keystones | Seen in the combat log | Mastery effects | Seen in the totals |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mystic, Elementalist, Illusionist | 11, 11, 11 | 1, 1, 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Ranger, Deadeye, Beastmaster | 12, 12, 12 | 1, 0, 1 | 0 | 0 |
| Warrior, Juggernaut, Berserker | 12, 12, 12 | 2, 1, 1 | 0 | 0 |
| Thief, Ninja, Samurai | 9, 10, 10 | 1, 1, 1 | 4 each | 4 each |
| Necromancer, Lich, Bone Lord | 11, 12, 12 | 1, 1, 1 | 3 each | 3 each |
| Monk, Shadowfist, Iron Sage | 9, 10, 10 | 2, 2, 1 | 4 each | 4 each |
| Templar, Inquisitor, Sentinel | 14, 15, 15 | 2, 2, 2 | 3 each | 2, 2, 2 |

Not observable from a client (the reason is in the report): damage factors (Overload, Immovable, Hunter's Focus, Deadeye,
Viper Verdict, Reaper's Toll, Pack Alpha), a heal with no row (Undying Rage), party-only (Shared Phantasm, Inspiring Illusion,
Overgrowth), the build archetype keystones (`ar...`: their hits carry no label of their own in the combat log) and the
class-line keystones (`ks...` in the Thief, Necromancer, Monk and Templar files). A new keystone flag without a probe or a
reason stops the generator, so every new keystone gets a decision. Mastery stats the totals do not show (resists, speed, skills,
healing, life drain) are listed per effect.

**Assumed, not verified on a live server:** the shape of the answers (`statTotals`, `planResult`, `state` of the combat log)
is the one in the Lua files; the bot's own weapon is the helper's class kit weapon, so a keystone that needs a two-handed
weapon, a shield or a bow can fail on a bot that carries none (the report names the need); a reset costs gold above level 50
(`respec_config.lua`) and the helper puts only 20,000 gold in the bank, so most bots can test one node and report the rest as
"not tested: the tree could not be cleared". `testers cleanup --yes` deletes the tree rows with the characters.

Not verified against a running server: the bots' packets in game, the helper on the real engine, the cleanup on the
real schema, the scenario payloads against the real handlers. Tested only with mocks, stubs and synthetic packets.

Tests: `tests/testers_test.lua`, `tests/tester_helper_test.lua`, `tools/testers_test.py`,
`tools/chaostesters_test.cpp` (status answer without testers, CI), `tools/patch_tester_filters_test.py`, `tools/tester_keystones_test.py` (keystones and masteries),
`deploy/chaos_ctl_test.py` (testers), `tools/loadtest_test.py`, `tools/tester_scenarios_test.py`, website `chaos_leaderboards_page_test.php`,
`chaos_client_api_test.php`.

## Load test on the full map (`tools/loadtest.py`, `tools/loadtest_hunt.lua`, `src-patches/0032-network-message-buffer.patch`)

The launch audit's open item: how many players the full map holds, and `maxPlayers` for the beta and the launch.

**Setup.** Engine with patches 0001-0032 (the 0032 numbers below; the before/after pairs used 0001-0030), the base
server from the `windows-assets` branch with every `install_all.py` step and the production `config.lua` of
`prod_config.py` (client guard on, the bots use the development key), the full map (RSS 4.55 GB at 0 players), a private
MariaDB 10.11 (default settings: one fsync per commit), `slowTaskLogMs = 50`. A fresh database before the first run.
The bots: `loadtest.py setup --spread data/chaos_poi.lua`: a third round the 20 temples, the rest over the hunting areas of
level 150 and below (level 100 characters, 1500 health); `run --hunt`: they walk a step a second, talk every 20 s and
fight. `tools/loadtest_hunt.lua` (TEST ONLY, next to the probe) gives every bot near a monster that monster as its
target (chase on) and keeps the bots alive; about 70-90 of 300 were fighting at any time. Measured: every game loop
task (a TEST ONLY timing histogram in a local build, not a patch), the slow task log, the probe's timer lag, CPU per
core and per engine thread and RSS every 5 s, the database's status counters and its slow query log (50 ms and more),
an autosave pass (SIGUSR1) in each run. The machine: 4 vCPU Intel Xeon @ 2.1 GHz (no SMT), 16 GB, one disk; the
bots ran on the same machine (about one core at 300 bots), and other jobs ran beside it in several runs (noted).

| Bots | dispatcher busy | task p50 / p99 / max | tasks >= 100 ms | timer lag avg / max | engine CPU (busiest thread) | RSS | to the bots per player | autosave pass (longest tick) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100 | 11% | 0.01 / 0.81 / 131 ms | 0.1 a minute | 50.8 / 149 ms | 13% (9%) of one core | 4.63 GB | 0.7 KB/s | 2.0 s (29 ms) |
| 200 | 19% | 0.01 / 0.95 / 305 ms | 1.4 a minute (the save's COMMITs) | 51.4 / 309 ms | 24% (17%) | 4.64 GB | 0.8 KB/s | 6.8 s (305 ms: a 300 ms COMMIT) |
| 300 | 39% | 0.01 / 0.57 / 774 ms | 5.2 a minute (the save's COMMITs) | 57.8 / 803 ms | 46% (33%) | 4.65 GB | 0.6 KB/s | 22.4 s (774 ms: COMMITs of 430-670 ms, other jobs on the disk) |
| 300, other runs | 50-79% | 0.01 / 0.57-0.98 / 95-312 ms | 0-38 a minute | 52-75 / 146-432 ms | 65-92% (45-78%) | 4.63-4.66 GB | 0.6-1.0 KB/s | 3.4-5.2 s (26-55 ms) on a calm disk |
| 700 (ramp, 0.3 s apart) | 98% | 0.01 / 0.49 / 819 ms | 69 a minute, 63 of 250 ms and more in 4.5 min | 182 / 1,481 ms | 83% (67%: the machine was full) | 4.71 GB | 1.3 KB/s | 46.8 s (121 ms) |

The 300 line is the fresh database run; the other 300 runs (6, before and after 0032, with the base weather's rain on or
off and other jobs beside them) show how much it varies. The database was never the limit: 5 connections (main, the
async thread, the two login workers, the sampler), 5-12 queries a second at 100-300 online and 40 at 700, 0.2-2.6
commits a second, 0.3-8% of one core; the only slow queries were COMMITs (and a few INSERTs) while other jobs wrote to
the same disk.

**Where it breaks.** The game loop's one thread. In the ramp to 700 (per 100 bots): dispatcher busy 19% (0-99), 33%,
43%, 67% (300-399), 83% (400-499), 96% (500-599), 99% (600-699); the timer lag stayed at 52-74 ms on average up to 499
online, went to 151 ms at 500-599 and 180-200 ms with maxima of 0.6-1.5 s above 600 (36-69 tasks of 100 ms and more a
minute). CPU of the other cores, RAM and the database had room left. All 700 bots logged in (login p50 0.28 s, p90
1.2 s) and none were dropped; the game lagged. The machine was full in the ramp (bots, engine, other jobs; load 15), so
the engine's thread got 67-75% of a core: on a core of its own the knee moves up, not down.

**Login rush.** 300 bots 0.2 s apart into a fresh database (every character's first login): with 0001-0032, 300 of 300,
login p50 0.33 s, p90 0.58 s, max 0.80 s (character list p50 53 ms); the first-login writes of `achievements.lua:841`
were 207 tasks of 50-191 ms in the 90 s wave. The first fresh run, with 0001-0030 and another job beside it, was much
slower: login p50 9.8 s, p90 15.0 s, max 17.9 s, 300 of 300, the dispatcher 82% busy in the wave with 81 tasks of 250 ms
and more (`achievements.lua:841` and `daily.lua:371` waiting 140-190 ms on a single INSERT or `players_record` UPDATE).
A launch rush is limited by the disk's fsync time of the first logins' writes, not by the password check.

**Found and fixed: 0032, the network message buffer.** `perf` on the dispatcher thread at 300 online: 18.4% of the
samples in `memmove` inside `ProtocolGame::sendDistanceShoot` (and every other send) and 5.6-6.5% in `memset` from
`OutputMessagePool::getOutputMessage`. This engine's `NETWORKMESSAGE_MAXSIZE` is 90,459 bytes; 0007 made the buffer
`= {}`, so every `NetworkMessage` on the stack (one per packet piece the game sends) copied 90 KB of zeros, and
`allocate_shared<OutputMessage>()` value-initialised (cleared) every new output message, 90 KB. 0032 takes the
initialiser out and gives `OutputMessage` a user-provided constructor; every byte that is sent is still written first
(the add calls, XTEA padding 0x33, the one outgoing skip in `ProtocolGame::onConnect` filled again). After it the two
are 0.26% each. Two before/after pairs, 300 bots, 5 minutes each, in turns: the dispatcher thread 45.6% / 45.5% of a
core after against 52.8% / 51.2% before, dispatcher busy 51% / 50% against 60% / 55%, task p99 0.65 ms against
0.93 ms, RSS 25 MB less. Guard: `tools/netmsg_buffer_patch_test.py` (CI).

**The slow task log's top offenders** (300 online, 10 minutes):
- the save's COMMITs (`Game::saveIncrementalStep`, 0 ms of Lua): 0.3-0.8 s each while other jobs used the disk, 26-55 ms
  otherwise. A COMMIT waits for the log flush on the game loop ("Left as it is" above). Owner decision 2026-10-12: the
  database on a local NVMe (a hosting requirement, docs/LAUNCH.md section 2); `innodb_flush_log_at_trx_commit` stays
  1 (2 would take the flush off the commit, and an OS crash would lose up to a second of saves). With the slow task
  log on, `tools/chaos_health.py` warns at 3 COMMITs of 200 ms or more within an hour;
- the base server's `events/scripts/creature.lua:22` (`Creature:onTargetCombat`: registers three creature events on
  the target at every attack) and `deathrecap.lua:213` (the collector's sweep of 5-6 MB lands in these calls): 20-30
  tasks of 50-100 ms; at 700 online 240 and 435 tasks, up to 819 ms (part of the saturation, no fix here);
- logins: `achievements.lua:841`, `customs/tasks/tasks.lua:800` (base), `mentor.lua:1125`: 50-190 ms at a first
  login, under 100 ms after.
- With `--area-level 0` (level 100 bots in level 400 areas) the bots' near-deaths ran the 19 prepare-death events about
  150 times a second (tasks up to 300 ms, `deathrecap.lua:213`); `loadtest_hunt.lua` keeps them healed for that reason.
  A real player pays it once per death.

**maxPlayers.** Assumed production VPS: 4-8 dedicated vCPU at 3 GHz or more (a newer core runs the single game loop
thread about 1.3-1.6 times as fast as this 2.1 GHz Xeon), 16 GB RAM (the engine needs 4.7 GB at 700), a local NVMe disk
for MariaDB, 100 Mbit/s or more (0.6-1.3 KB/s per player, about 4 Mbit/s for 400). Real players cost more per head than
these bots (spells and area attacks, more monsters woken in more places, trading, depot and market work, the rain):
counted as 1.5-2 bots. The knee here is 450-500 bots (dispatcher 83-96%); on the assumed VPS about 600-750 bots, so
300-500 real players.
- **Beta: 300** (`prod_config.py --max-players 300`; owner decision 2026-10-12, with 400 at launch). The dispatcher stays under half busy with room for the unknowns;
  measure the beta weekend (the probe lag, the slow task log for an hour at the peak).
- **Launch: 400** (the `prod_config.py` default). Raise to 500 after a week whose peak hour kept the timer lag under
  70 ms on average and the slow task log (`slowTaskLogMs = 100`) under a few tasks a minute; lower to 300 if it did not.

## Load test with area classes (`tools/loadtest.py --classes`, 2026-10-14)

docs/BETA_READINESS.md B6: does the full map hold 300 players with pack combat (pace) on when they play area classes?
The melee-only test of "Pack combat (pace)" could not answer it.

**Setup.** The same as "Load test on the full map". The base server from `windows-assets` with every `install_all.py`
step (contentareas and spawns included), engine 0001-0039, `prod_config.py` (client guard enforce, the development key
allowed, a test server only), `slowTaskLogMs = 50`, and a private MariaDB. The machine has 4 vCPU at 2.1 GHz and also
runs the bots. The map holds about 98,500 monsters alive.

The bots (`loadtest.py setup/run --classes ... --levels 100,300,600,1000 --power 1.6 --pull 8,6 --hunt --dev-key`):
- Class weights: Elementalist 5, Berserker 4, Mystic 3, Beastmaster 3, Inquisitor 2, Bone Lord 2, and 1 each of Lich,
  Illusionist, Warrior, Deadeye, Thief, Monk and Samurai. That is 73% area classes.
- Each class gets every level band in turn.
- 10% stand in the towns. The others hunt their band, in map hunts (`chaos_poi.lua`) and in the planned hunts behind
  the hunt teleports (`chaos_hunt_places.lua`).
- They cast their real rotation by the say packet: 79 attack and 19 support casts a second at 300 bots. They lure 8
  steps, then fight 6 s, and never loot.

The TEST ONLY hunt script is a scratch copy of `loadtest_hunt.lua`. It picks targets within 8 sqm (else 14), faces the
bot to its target, keeps mana up and gives a class weapon. It also gives the bots x3 health and heals them below 75%
every 250 ms. Without that, 300 bare bots "died" about 90 times a second, and each near-death runs every prepare-death
event; that was half the slow tasks. The probe also prints its p95.

Each run holds 10 minutes after the ramp. The numbers cover the steady state, from ramp end + 60 s on (about 530 s).
- **Lag**: the probe's timer lag. Its floor is about 50 ms.
- **p95**: the p95 of each 5 s window, given as median / p90 / worst.
- **Stalls**: 5 s windows with a lag of 500 ms or more.
- **Thread**: the game loop thread in % of one core, average (p95).

| Run | Bots | Pace | Loot filter | Lag avg | p95 per 5 s | Max | Stalls | Thread | Kills/s | Bots fighting |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| a | 300 | on | stock | 58.9 ms | 102 / 138 / 230 | 506 | 1 | 73.5% (93.9%) | 5.9 | 97 |
| b | 300 | off | stock | 88.6 ms | 190 / 264 / 454 | 668 | 6 | 94.5% (98.9%) | 3.5 | 162 |
| a+fix | 300 | on | fix | 59.2 ms | 103 / 153 / 191 | 364 | 0 | 77.0% (94.9%) | 5.7 | 98 |
| c+fix | 400 | on | fix | 69.7 ms | 161 / 232 / 312 | 580 | 2 | 87.3% (97.9%) | 6.6 | 115 |
| d | 300 | on, +31 kills/s | stock | 74.8 ms | 124 / 217 / 303 | 1,042 | 18 | 66.8% (93.8%) | 31.0 | 4 |
| d+fix | 300 | on, +35 kills/s | fix | 67.9 ms | 114 / 197 / 248 | 395 | 0 | 66.9% (90.9%) | 35.0 | 5 |
| c+fix+perf | 400 | on | fix | 73.3 ms | 171 / 257 / 351 | 669 | 5 | 89.0% (98.8%) | 6.5 | 116 |
| a+fix+perf | 300 | on | fix | 60.5 ms | 107 / 169 / 252 | 327 | 0 | 79.2% (96.8%) | 5.9 | 99 |

Notes on the runs:
- An earlier pair with bare-health bots gave the same order: on 63.1 ms, 3 stalls, thread 79.8%; off 97.2 ms,
  14 stalls, thread 93.7%.
- Other numbers at 300 with pace on: RSS 4.82 GB (4.65 GB idle). To the bots 0.9-1.0 KB/s per player (2.0 with pace
  off). The database ran 85 queries, 0.9 commits and 15 fsyncs a second. The autosave pass (SIGUSR1) took 41 ticks,
  longest 62 ms, 3.4 s in all (8.6 s with pace off).
- At 400: 107 queries a second, autosave 52 ticks, longest 37 ms, 5.9 s.
- "perf" is four Lua optimisations added the same day: monster events registered once in `onTargetCombat`, nameplate
  and buff bar passes in shares, the hunt supply check in shares, a shorter pace experience lookup.
- "+N kills/s": the hunt script added kills on top of the bots' own. Each one is a bot's lethal hit on its target with
  real loot, experience, pace and loot filter. Idle bots were moved to a monster within 40 sqm. The bots then barely
  fought themselves, so these rows measure the cost per kill, not the cost of fighting.

**Findings.**
- **Pace lowers the load.** With the layer off, monsters keep their full health, so fights last longer. Twice as
  many bots are in combat, they take hits longer (near-deaths 16 a second against 4.5) and the bots receive twice the
  data. Turning pace off (`enabled = false`) is no fallback for load.
- **The pace hooks cost almost nothing.** LuaJIT's sampling profiler (`jit.profile`, TEST ONLY) puts `pace.lua`
  (first think, cleave, experience) under 1% of the Lua samples, and 1.3% at 35 kills a second. Lua is about two
  thirds of the game loop. Most of it is per-hit and per-attack callbacks that every attack pays (C functions called
  from Lua 50-60%, the collector 9-13%):
  - `events/scripts/creature.lua` `onTargetCombat`,
  - `player.lua:640`, `base_rarity.lua`, `combatlog.lua`,
  - `_supports.lua` (the spell wrapper; the spells themselves are about 3.5% of the time),
  - `monster_tiers.lua`, `passivetree_effects.lua`, the base attack sounds.
  `perf` on the game loop thread: luajit 37-43%, the engine 27-30% (spectators, pathfinding, walking, events), the
  kernel 17-21%.
- **The loot filter sweep was the stall.** `lootfilter.lua` tracks the last 50 kills of every player whose corpse
  still holds something. The bots never loot, which is the worst case; a player who leaves items in corpses comes
  close. Every 5th sweep (5 s) it re-read every tracked corpse with the full `itemInfo` of every item, in one task:
  - 200-380 ms (45-125 MB of garbage) at about 6 kills a second;
  - 730-890 ms at 31 kills a second, the 18 stalls of run d (max 1,042 ms) while the game loop thread was only 67% busy.
  Fixed (`lootfilter_core.lua` `F.decayDue`, `F.fingerprint`): each sweep checks a fifth of the tracked kills (kill id
  modulo `decayCheckEvery`), so every corpse is still checked every 5 s. A corpse with an active ray is still checked
  every sweep. A corpse whose item ids and counts did not change since the last check skips the reconcile.
  Results: no loot filter task over 50 ms at 6 kills a second, 54-221 ms at 35 kills a second, no stall of 500 ms.
  Tests: `tests/lootfilter_test.lua`.
- **Kill rate.** The bots kill 6-7 a second at 300-400, against the model's 134 at the launch peak. They clear their
  spot and wander, and only a third of them fight at any time. With injected kills, 31-35 a second cost about the same
  game loop as the bots' own fighting. 134 a second was not reached on this machine. `pace.lua` stayed under 1.5% of
  Lua at that rate; the loot filter (fixed) and `achievements.lua` `onKill` grow with kills.
- Other recurring slow tasks, not pace:
  - `nameplate.lua` (50-105 ms; 50-100 ms per 1 s share after the perf change);
  - `achievements.lua:856` and `tasks.lua:800` at logins;
  - `deathrecap.lua` at near-deaths (fewer with tough bots);
  - `onTargetCombat`.

**Verdict for B6 (this 2.1 GHz machine, the bots on it too).**
- 300 bots with pace on: borderline pass. Lag 59 ms, p95 about 100 ms, the game loop thread 74-77% (p95 94-95%).
- With the loot filter fix: no stall of 500 ms; without it, one stall at bot kill rates and many at higher ones.
- Keep pace on.
- Ship the loot filter fix before the beta.
- 400 bots fail on this machine: lag 70-73 ms, p95 about 165 ms, 2-5 stalls, the thread 87-89%. The game loop is
  saturated.
- The perf change did not move the averages; they stayed within run-to-run noise (300: 60.5 ms and 79% against 59.2 ms
  and 77%; 400: 73.3 ms and 89% against 69.7 ms and 87%). It cut the slow tasks: at 300, 44 tasks of 100 ms or more
  against 68, and 58 `onTargetCombat` tasks against 163.

The production VPS of "Load test on the full map" is assumed 1.3-1.6 times faster per core. Real area-class players kill
more and fight more of the time than these bots. So keep the beta at 300 and watch the probe lag and the slow task log
at the beta peak. Decide 400 for the launch from that, not from this test.

Scratch scripts and logs of the runs: `scratchpad/aoelt/` of the session (not in the repo).

## Stress test (`tools/loadtest.py` storms and spam, `src-patches/0033`-`0035`, `tools/patch_base_stalls.py` step 6)

A QA pass for bugs under load (2026-10-13). Setup as "Load test on the full map": the engine with 0001-0032 (then the
fixes below), every `install_all.py` step, the production `config.lua` with the bots' development key, a private
MariaDB, `slowTaskLogMs = 50`, the probe and `loadtest_hunt.lua`, 500 bot characters (`setup --spread`). The machine was
shared with another job (its clients kept all 4 cores busy), so the times are pessimistic.

**What ran.**
- 400 bots spread over the towns and hunting areas, 10 minutes: 400 of 400 in game, login p50 0.30 s, probe lag avg
  62 ms (max 1.5 s: a test script), RSS 4.64 to 4.73 GB, no Lua error. Meanwhile 20 solo and 10 party rifts (6 ready at
  once, the builder filled the 16 slots in 30-60 s, 640 ms of game loop per map at most, the 17th key heard the wait
  and joined the line), 5 raids (4 slots, the 5th waited), 6 Descents, 14 tower runs, the world boss with 55 bots
  (32 in the arena; random walkers leave by the side fields), deaths and logouts inside each.
- A burst of 400 logins in 2 s: 61 in game at first, 303 + 29 "Too many logins at the moment" (the login worker's
  queue of 64, "Account passwords"); the client retries by hand.
- Reconnect storms: 300 bots, each 5-25 s in game, 30% of the sessions dropped without a logout, 15% of the logins cut
  off half way (after the character list, right after the game login, after the first answer), 6 minutes: 5,583
  sessions, 1,707 dropped, 1,116 cut off. No Lua error, no crash, RSS +50 MB. The game loop fell behind by seconds when
  many logout saves met a slow disk (COMMITs of 0.5-2.3 s; "Load test on the full map").
- Spam: 60 bots at 20 extended opcodes a second each (null opcode, bank transfer, market browse), 300 bots with
  module requests, bank transfers, chat every 4 s, private messages every 5 s and party invites, joins and leaves.
- Economy: bank transfers between 100 bots, half of the targets offline, with reconnect loops and drops: the sum of
  every bank balance of the 500 bot characters was 50,000,000 before and after (38,000 and 32,000 transfers in two runs).
- Saves: the daily save (shutdown) with 300 online took 11 s, every character saved (the bank sum exact); `kill -9`
  in the middle of a save pass and in the middle of the daily save: every rift opener got the key back exactly once,
  every character woke at the temple; a global read lock on the database for 15 s froze the game loop 13.7 s (the
  first write waits), nobody was kicked, the loop caught up within 5 s.

**Found and fixed.**
- *A decay that loops forever* (0033, critical). The base items.xml has 23827 "dead dawnfly" decaying to itself.
  `Game::internalDecayItem` and `startDecay` then called each other without end: one Dawnfly corpse froze the whole
  server 15 minutes after the kill (no saves, no logins answered). Now its own id (or 0) removes the item and a
  failed transform stops the decay. Reproduced with one corpse and a 2 s duration; fixed build checked the same way.
- *A reconnect thrown out at once* (0034). A character whose client vanished stays 60 s (the no-pong kick). A login
  that took it over did not renew the last pong, so the next check logged the new client out before its first ping,
  without a message. Reproduced (logged out 1.5 s after a takeover 56 s after the drop); fixed build stays connected.
- *A character left in the game for good* (0035). A login that replaced a connected client waits 1 s; when its own
  connection closed in that second the character stayed marked as connecting, and the no-pong kick never removes such
  a character. Found as a bot still online 10 minutes after the storm; reproduced and fixed (removed after 60 s).
- *A database read for every extended opcode* (`patch_base_stalls.py` step 6). The base `ExtendedOpcode` script read
  the ancestral points with a SELECT on the game loop and pushed them on opcode 89 for every request any module sends.
  300 bots at 4 requests a second put the game loop 5 s behind. Now at most once every 2 s per player.

**Fixed after the run (owner approved, unit level; not yet run on a live server).**
- *One handler per opcode* (`chaos_constants.lua`, "Extended opcode dispatch" below). Every extended opcode ran all of
  about 80 `extendedopcode` creature events (each checking its opcode first): about 0.2 ms of game loop per request.
  Now one engine event calls only the handlers of that opcode. `tests/opcode_dispatch_test.lua`.
- *A size cap before the JSON decode.* A 60 KB JSON array costs about 5 ms to decode, so one modified client at the
  engine's 50 packets a second could take a quarter of the game loop. Requests over `Chaos.opcodeRequestMax` (16,384
  bytes; the client's largest, a passive tree plan, is about 3 KB) are dropped before any handler, one console line
  per player a minute. Same test.
- *A transfer to an online character* (`bank.lua`). A crash kept the sender's side when the sender had been saved
  (the save before the credit) but the receiver had not: about 10,000 gold of 300 bots' transfer spam lost per
  `kill -9`. The receiver is now saved right after the credit. `tests/save_before_credit_test.lua` (the gold sum a
  crash would keep).
- *The guild bank withdrawal* (`guild.lua`). The guild row is debited first and the gold credited in memory; the
  character is now saved right after, so a crash cannot lose it. Same test.

**Seen, not changed.**
- A reconnect while the dispatcher is more than 1 s behind can get "You are already logged in." (stock); a client that
  connects more than 5 times in 2 s is closed without a message (stock flood rule).
- Logout saves run on the game loop: a mass disconnect lands many in one creature check (tasks of 0.3-0.7 s).

**Tools.** `loadtest.py run` takes `--reconnect MIN,MAX`, `--drop P`, `--abort P`, `--opcodes FILE` with
`--opcode-every S` ("{name}", "{online}", "{other}" in the payloads), `--pm S` and `--party S`; a bot answers a late
client guard challenge. `tests`: `tests/opcode_dispatch_test.lua`, `tools/loadtest_test.py`, `tools/decay_loop_patch_test.py`,
`tools/reattach_ping_patch_test.py`, `tests/base_stalls_patch_test.lua` (step 6).

## Town names (`tools/patch_base_towns.py`, `tools/base_towns.csv`, `tests/base_towns_patch_test.lua`)

The base map came with the towns of another world. `patch_base_towns.py` (step `towns` of `install_all.py`) gives them
Chaos names by town id, from `tools/base_towns.csv` (columns `id,name`; the old names are in no repository file). It
rewrites the towns node of the `.otbm` (`<mapName>` of `config.lua`, else the only map in `data/world`, or `--map`):
town names are length-prefixed strings in that node, so the node is rebuilt and spliced in, and every other byte of the
map stays the same. Ids, temple positions and the town order are kept, so `players.town_id`, houses, depots (the depot
id is the town id) and every script that uses `Town(id)` are unaffected. The tool parses the rebuilt node again before
it writes, writes through a temporary file and keeps `<map>.otbm.bak` the first time. `--list PATH.otbm` prints the
towns of a map. On the reference map: 20 towns, all renamed; the map loads with the same 18,185,071 tiles, the same
23,317,821 item stack entries and the same temples (parsed with `tools/map/otbm.py`), and a test server showed the new
names in `Game.getTowns()`.

Since 2026-10-23 one of the two empty stalls is the Apothecary's (15 NPCs, one stall free; "The Apothecary"); on 2026-10-28 Archivist Odrenna took the last one (16 NPCs, every stall filled) and moved the same day to 31628, next to the Keeper of Trials, swapping with Archivist Maelis (now 31672).

## Service NPCs (`service_npcs.lua`, `service_npcs_core.lua`, `service_npcs_run.lua`, `service_npcs_config.lua`, `data/npc/scripts/chaos_service_npc.lua`)

Owner decision 2026-10-20 (from the menu / NPC list of 2026-10-20): five NPCs that stand in for menu entries, built in
this order. The menu entries are **not** removed; they stay until the owner has confirmed the NPCs in the game. No Guild,
Market, Store or Ancestral Store NPC. No player talkaction (the only one is still `!bless`). No new opcode, storage key
or table: every NPC opens the window of the module that owns the feature, through that module's own opcode and an
`npc` action (the pattern of Osric the Chandler and the Gambler); every action in the window is checked again by the
module's own script, never by the NPC.

| NPC | Stall in the hub (Cinderhold) | Opens / does | Module reused |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tavish Coldhand (stash keeper) | 31666, 32230, 7 | the stash window (`Toggle` with `open`) | `stash.lua`, opcode 110 |
| Vessa Hollowmark (pocket boss NPC) | 31660, 32236, 7 | the Boss Spawns window; says the daily pocket charges (`pocketboss_config.lua`) | `bossspawns.lua` / `pocketboss.lua`, opcode 217 |
| Cassian Auric (banker) | 31654, 32230, 7 | the bank window; says the balance | `bank.lua`, opcode 60 |
| Halvard Deedkeeper (house broker) | 31672, 32230, 7 | lists the free houses by town, sells one by name after a "yes", runs the base `!leavehouse` and `!sellhouse` | `commands_ui_core.lua` loader, opcode 237 page `house` |
| Pell Ashmere (services clerk) | 31653, 32236, 7 | the Services page (name, class, frame); says the token counts; runs the base `!summonfamiliar`, `!familiarlevel`, `!choosefamiliar`, `!shop` | `commands_ui.lua` / `shop_services.lua`, opcode 237 page `services` |

**Pure logic** (`service_npcs_core.lua`, `tests/service_npcs_test.lua`): what each NPC understands (`K.intent`: ordered
keyword rows, the narrow ones first), the house name after "buy", the house search (an exact name in any case, else the
one house whose name holds the text), the free houses of a town cheapest first, the towns with free houses, the price,
and the purchase rules (`K.buyCheck`: sales on, premium, no owner, none owned yet, enough gold). **Engine side**
(`service_npcs_run.lua`, loaded by the NPC script in the NPC's own Lua state: `R.open` sends the window message,
`R.houses`, `R.buyHouse`, `R.runBase`). The base commands run in a sandbox with their texts caught, through the loader
`commands_ui_core.lua` `K.baseHandler` that the Info & Services window (`commands_ui.lua`) uses too (moved there from
`commands_ui.lua` on 2026-10-20; the window's behaviour is unchanged). The commands that live in the main Lua state
(`changename`, `changevocation`, `ascend`, `plateframe`) cannot run in an NPC's state: the clerk opens the Services page
for them. `service_npcs.lua` places the NPCs at startup (4 s after the start) in the main city only (`C.towns = {2}`): the
stall first, else next to the temple (`offsets`).

**The house broker.** He sells from his stall, so a player need not stand at a door (the base `!buyhouse` does). Say
`list` for the towns with free houses, `list <town>` for the six cheapest of one, `buy <house name>` to hear the price
(tiles x `config.lua` `housePriceEachSQM`, `perSqm` 1000 when the base has no value), then `yes`. The house is read again
at the "yes", so a sale in between is caught. Gold is taken from the backpack, then the bank (`Chaos.pay`).
**Assumed, not verified (the base server is not in the repo):** the rules of the base `buyhouse.lua` of TFS 1.4 (premium,
no owner, none owned yet, enough gold) and the engine API `Game.getHouses`, `House:getTileCount/getOwnerGuid/setOwnerGuid`,
`Player:getHouse`, `configManager.getNumber(configKeys.HOUSE_PRICE)` (-1 = not for sale). Check on the first live start
that a bought house shows the player as owner and that the rent is charged as for a house bought at the door.

**Client** (one `npc` action each, an open window stays open): `game_bank` (`bankWindowShow`), `game_bossspawns` (`show`),
`game_chaosinfo` (`openPage(data.page)`, only a page the client knows); the stash needed none (`Toggle` with `open`).

**Stalls.** `npc_booths_config.lua` `booths` ("Hub NPC booths"); `tests/service_npcs_test.lua` checks that each of the
five has one.

**Install:** step `servicenpcs` (`tools/install_service_npcs.py`, `tools/install_service_npcs_test.py`). **Texts:** English
keys, pt-BR in `i18n_strings.lua` (`tests/service_npcs_test.lua` checks every line has one).

The other runes and the unscribed rune stay with Raloth and Isora (`chaos_rune_supply.lua` `vendors`) |

- **Prices.** The base server's lowest asking price per potion (`hunt_supplies.lua`), docs/PRICES.md. Great Spirit is 190
  (the price the store's pack is built on) and not the cheapest base NPC's 120. The store's packs of 100 stay the bulk
  way: 100 Great Mana Potions 15 coins, Great Spirit 15, Ultimate Health 20, Supreme Health 30; a pack is worth 800-1,667

The test fails for any NPC XML whose shop list has a name with leading or trailing whitespace.

## Cards and decks (`cards.lua`, `cards_core.lua`, `cards_config.lua`, `tools/patch_badges.py`, `tools/gen_card_descriptions.lua`)

Owner 2026-10-23 (pt-BR): "como alguém pega um deck pra colocar as cartas? usar elas não funciona e no character info só diz
se ela está ativada ou desativada", then "as cartas ainda referenciam as magias antigas" (a card said "convert Exori Mas
Spell to Earth damage"). The base deck system (76 cards, 3 decks) stays; Chaos fixes how it is reached, read and named.
No table, no storage key of its own: the base's card storages (37000-37059, 37065-37080) and action id 37866. One opcode, 172
(`ChaosOpcodes.cardState`), for the card borders below.

- **Root cause of "use does nothing".** The base registers a use action for every card (`deckSystem:id(cardId)`), but it
  only does something for a card that is already inside a deck: it looks for the card with `container:getItemsById` in the
  deck and flips its storage. A card loose in the backpack with a deck carried was not found, and the player got the
  base line "This card cannot be used on this deck slot..."; with no deck carried the action returned nothing and the engine
  said "You cannot use this object". Nothing ever said where a deck comes from (decks dropped from monsters and came from
  one task; the roulettes lost them with the badge slot change). `!deck` only printed "Activated" or "Deactivated" per card.
- **Use a card** (`patch_badges.py` step 4 puts one hook at the top of the base card action: `ChaosCards.use(player, item)`;
  nil means "not a card", so the base runs). The card is looked up in every bag the player carries at any depth, closed bags
  and decks included (`ChaosCards.scan`, at most `scanLimit` 600 items; slots 1-10, 12, 13, never the store inbox). Then
  `ChaosCardsCore.decide`: **off** (it was the copy that is on: storage 0, action id off), **dupe** (another copy is on:
  one copy counts), **max** (five cards on), **on** (it already sits in a deck), **move** (it goes into the first carried
  deck with room, the biggest deck first, then turns on), **nodeck** (the text says to buy one from Veyra with the three
  prices, read from `apothecary_config.lua`) or **full**. Messages go through `Chaos.t`, pt-BR in `i18n_strings.lua`.
- **Decks.** Veyra the Apothecary sells Bronze (5 cards) 1,000 gold, Silver (10) 6,000 from level 50, Golden (20) 30,000
  from level 100 ("The Apothecary"); decks still drop and one task gives one. A deck is carried, not worn.
- **Character Info.** The `deck` command (`ChaosCommands`, replaces the base `!deck` dialog) lists the decks carried with
  used and total slots, the cards that are on (at most five) with what each gives, the cards in decks that are off, the
  cards carried outside a deck, and, without a deck, how to get one. The text stays under `maxTextBytes` (6,000; the list
  ends with "... and N more."), below the extended opcode's 8,192 bytes, so `Chaos.sendChunked` is not needed. The client
  page runs `deck` when Character Info opens (`game_chaosinfo`, 6 auto commands, the server's `MAX_IDS`); an older client
  still gets the richer text from the Card Deck button.
- **State stays true.** `ChaosCards.reconcile` runs on use, on `deck`, at login and every 60 s (`reconcileMs`): a card whose
  storage is 1 but whose copy is no longer in a carried deck (dropped on death, a bag put away) is turned off with a
  message, and a stray action id (a second copy, a copy outside a deck) is cleared so the card can be moved again. Login is
  silent when nothing changed. A card counts once however many decks or copies a player has.
- **The cards name the spells you have.** The 60 common cards are 15 lines of 4 tiers; the base wrote the stock spell into
  each text. Every line belongs to one current spell in `cards_config.lua` (name and spell id). What each line does in the
  base: the spell scripts read the card storages (convert lines: the highest tier on sets the element; Deep Mending: a
  stronger heal; Blood Rage: longer and stronger; Challenge: a wider area). Six lines still have their stock script (Tempest
  Fan, Sanctum Burst, Frostfall Rune, Pyre Torrent, Bloodlust, Taunt of Iron) and work as they did. Nine lines belonged to
  spells that were retired (`rename_spells.py`, `patch_spell_cap.py`, `retire_cure_spells.py`), so their cards did nothing;
  they now act on the Chaos spell of the same role:

| Line (first card) | Stock spell | Now acts on | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| 27482 | Berserk | Reaping Gyre | element of the highest tier on |
| 27486 | Terra Wave | Rime Bloom | element |
| 27502 | Eternal Winter | Doomtide | element |
| 27506 | Rage of the Skies | Primordial Squall | element |
| 27510 | Groundshaker | Earthbreaker | element |
| 27522 | Strong Ice Wave | Frozen Crypt | element |
| 27526 | Intense Healing | Grand Mending | heals 10 / 20 / 30 / 40 percent more |
| 27530 | Divine Missile | Dawnpiercer | element |
| 27538 | Sharpshooter (no consumer even in the base) | Tautstring | 2 / 4 / 6 / 8 seconds longer, 2 / 4 / 6 / 8 more percentage points of distance skill |

  The `ChaosCardsHit` creature event (`cards.lua`, on the monsters a player attacks and on every player at login) reads the cast
  context the spells state writes (`ChaosSupports.ctxDecode`), and for these spell ids moves the whole hit to the element
  (`ChaosSupports.convert` with the target's resistances) or scales the heal (`ChaosSupports.scale`). Tautstring reads the
  line's storages itself (`cards_config.lua` `buffBonus`, the spells state). The base spell scripts, `supports.lua` and the
  rune effects are untouched. The eight "hit" lines are `C.byTarget`. The four legendary classes need a weapon in the left
  hand, not a vocation, and their chances are the base config's 7 / 9 / 14 / 20 percent (the base text said 2 / 3 / 4 / 5).
- **Descriptions.** `tools/gen_card_descriptions.lua` writes `data/items/card_descriptions.csv` (id, description) from
  `cards_core.lua` (`--check` in CI); `patch_badges.py` items step puts it into `items.xml` (English), and
  `item_tooltip.lua` sets the tooltip text per player language (`ChaosCardsCore.description`). Spell and element names come from
  the config and the item types, so no stock name is in the repo. `tests/cards_test.lua` scans every description (en and
  pt-BR) for the old stock names and words of `data/spells/spell_names.csv`, requires every line's spell to be a current
  spell with the right id (`stock_spells.csv`, `spells_chaos.xml`, `patch_spell_cap.py`), and checks the hint matches the tool.
- **Card borders** (owner 2026-10-24, pt-BR: "coloque uma borda pra mostrar se a carta está ligada ou não"). A card in a deck
  window gets a border: green when the card is on, a dim red-grey when it is off. The client cannot see action ids, so the
  server tells it which cards are on: extended opcode **172** (`ChaosOpcodes.cardState`, free in the reference server, the
  base client's `ExtendedIds` and every Chaos module; see "Opcode collision check"), JSON `{action = "state", data = {on, cards,
  decks}}`: `on` the card ids that are on, `cards` all 76, `decks` the three deck ids, all as client ids
  (`ItemType(id):getClientId()`; the server id when unknown). `ChaosCardsCore.statePayload` builds it (pure, tested).
  `ChaosCards.push(player, plan, force)` sends it at login (always), when the client asks (`sync`, one second after login, in
  case the module loaded late; limited to one per 500 ms), after a card is turned on or off, and whenever the 60 s sweep, the
  `deck` command or a use finds the set changed (`reconcile` plan.active); an unchanged set is not sent again (last key per
  player in memory, forgotten at logout). The payload is about 600 bytes, far under `maxTextBytes` and the 8192 limit.
  Client `game_cardborder` (`cardborderlogic.lua` rules, `cardborder.lua` widgets): hooks the `Container` signals like the loot
  filter, and draws a border child (`setBorderWidth` 2, `setBorderColor`) on the slot widgets of a container whose item is a
  deck; one redraw per container per frame, no per-frame loop. Cards outside a deck get no border, and nothing is drawn until
  the server's first message (an older server never sends one). **A card is told by its id, not by its copy:** a second copy
  of an on card inside a deck shows as on too, although the server counts one copy (a second copy can only sit in a deck
  by being moved there by hand; the action id sits on the first). No UI text, so no new `tr()` key.
- **Install:** step `badges` (`patch_badges.py`, idempotent; the hook and the descriptions). The Lua files are scripts.
- **Tests:** `tests/cards_test.lua` (data, reconcile and decide, the glue on a mocked engine, texts in en and pt-BR, the hit
  event, Tautstring's bonus, the stale-name scan, the card state messages: login, on, off, unchanged, sync, logout, opcode
  172 unique), client `game_cardborder/cardborder_test.lua` (rules and the real server payload), `tools/patch_badges_test.py` (hook once, descriptions, hint migration),
  `tests/apothecary_test.lua` (decks), `client/overlay/modules/game_chaosinfo/chaosinfoview_test.lua`.
- **Not seen in a client or on a live server.** The base is not in the repo: the right-click menu "Use" entry depends on
  the item's `.dat` usable flag (the base registered the action, so it is expected); the nine moved lines are tested on a
  mocked engine only. (The legendary weapon lists were left here once; fixed in O142 below.)

### Cards that did not fire (O142, beta 2026-10-23)

Beta: "a card in the deck does not work at all". Four root causes, all fixed; deploy: `badges` and `files` installer steps and
a server restart, no client update.

- **Legendary cards ignored most weapons.** The base `legendary_cards_system.lua` asks the left-hand item id against four
  hard-coded lists of stock ids (38 of 134 swords, 31 of 126 clubs, 34 of 114 axes, 26 of 37 bows, 24 of 29 crossbows, 41 of
  65 wands, 11 of 77 Chaos items matched). `patch_badges.py` step 9 rewrites the 16 checks to `chaosHolds(player, "<class>",
  leftHand, config.<list>)`, a local helper that calls `ChaosCards.holds` (cards.lua) and falls back to the base check while
  cards.lua is not loaded. `holds` decides by weapon type: Knight sword, club, axe or a fist weapon (the Monk line also
  fights bare-handed), Paladin distance, Sorcerer and Druid wand (wands and rods share one type; either mage card works
  with either). The stock ids still count. The fixture test is in `tools/patch_badges_test.py`.
- **The summon lock stuck.** The base sets `DeckSystem.Legendary.CanCreateSummon` to 1 on a summon and never releases it
  when the summon dies, so the card worked once and then never. `ChaosCards.releaseSummon` clears it when the player has no
  summons (a global event every `summonReleaseMs` 5000, and at login).
- **No card line for several classes.** Lines were tied to one spell. Thief, Ninja, Samurai, Monk line, Templar line and the
  Necromancer line had no usable line (Frostfall Rune is a rune everyone can use but gives no class value). Four hit lines
  now carry an `also` list of a second spell: Doomtide + Blade Flurry (Thief line), Earthbreaker + Consecration (Templar
  line), Frozen Crypt + Sundering Palm (Monk line), Dawnpiercer + Bone Spear (Necromancer line). `C.byTarget` maps every
  spell to its line; card texts name every spell ("these spells", "with several cards the highest one counts").
  No existing line was removed, so nobody loses a card.
- **Texts.** Legendary text now says what to hold ("Needs a melee weapon in your left hand (the Monk line: a fist weapon or
  bare fists)"); `card_descriptions.csv` regenerated; pt-BR in `i18n_strings.lua`.

`tests/cards_test.lua` now walks all 21 classes (`C.classes`) against all 60 common cards and the 16 legendary cards (about
45,000 checks): every line is castable by some class, every class has a common line and a hit that fires, every legendary card
fires for each class weapon, fist weapons, Chaos items, stock ids, bare fists for the Monk line, and the summon lock.
`luajit tests/cards_test.lua --table` prints the lines per class. The `elseif` limit is fixed in O149 below.

### Cards: two legendaries, class lines, wands and rods (O149)

Follow-ups of O142. Deploy: `badges` and `files` installer steps and a server restart; no client update.

- **Every active legendary card fires.** The base script was `if A then .. elseif B then .. end` over 16 storages, so only the
  first legendary card that is on was checked. `patch_badges.py` step 9 now also turns the 15 `elseif player:getStorageValue(
  DeckSystem.Legendary.Legendary..Lv6) == 1 then` into `end` + `if`, so each card rolls on its own hit (up to 5 cards are on
  at once). The base `CanCreateSummon` lock stays: only one summon at a time, so a second summon card rolls but its summon
  waits for the first to end; the stat bonus of a card that does not summon is not given either (it is inside the same
  branch). A script patched by O142 (helper there, `elseif` still in the chain) is upgraded by a second run; CRLF is kept;
  a second run changes nothing. Test: `tools/patch_badges_test.py` (fixture, an O142-style script, the real base copy when
  the machine has one, two cards on both fire under luajit or lua5.3).
- **Usable common cards per class** (`luajit tests/cards_test.lua --table`; the Frostfall Rune counts for everyone). Before: Warrior
  line, Ranger line 4 each, Mystic 3, Elementalist 7, Illusionist 2, Thief line 2, Necromancer line 3, Monk line 2, Templar line
  2 (median 3). After: all at least 3, Mystic 4 (gained Frozen Crypt), Necromancer line 4, Illusionist, Thief line, Monk
  line, Templar line 3. New `also` spells (`cards_config.lua`): Marrow Bolt and Soulrend Beam on Rime Bloom (Necromancer line),
  Radiant Smite on Dawnpiercer (Templar line), Shattered Psyche on Frozen Crypt (Mystic, Illusionist), Shuriken Toss on
  Primordial Squall (Thief line), Palm Shockwave on Earthbreaker (Monk line). No line was removed. The test asserts at least
  3 lines per class, a median of 3 and 4 for the Necromancer line; an `also` spell must belong to one class line (Shattered
  Psyche is the one exception: Mystic and Illusionist cast it, the Elementalist does not).
- **Wands and rods stay one type.** The engine has one weapon type for both and the items have no wand or rod flag, so the
  Sorcerer and Druid legendary cards fire with either. Decided as fine: cards belong to the weapon in the hand, not to a
  vocation, and a wand or rod user wants a mage card either way. No item id lists to keep in step with `chaos_items.xml`.
- `card_descriptions.csv`, the codex and wiki data, tester scenarios and wiki art are regenerated; pt-BR texts are built
  from the same spell lists.

## Tile labels (`tile_labels.lua`, `tile_labels_core.lua`, `tile_labels_config.lua`)

Orange name labels over tiles (owner 2026-10-18: the area of the new NPCs should show their names in orange text).
Since 2026-10-22 that area is the hub's market ("Hub NPC booths"). Every `intervalMs` (3 s) each label is sent as
animated text (`ChaosCombatFx.label`, opcode 0x84, palette byte 198 = `TEXTCOLOR_ORANGE`) to the players who see its
tile, so a stall nobody sees costs nothing. Labels come from `tile_labels_core.lua` `collect`, derived from
`npc_booths_config.lua`: the name of the NPC of every stall, and `labels = {{text, pos = {x, y, z}}}` for fixed tiles
(empty). A stall given an NPC there is labelled without an edit. The section titles of the old halls' rows and the
names over the temple arcade's stands are gone with them. The portals' own orange labels (where they lead) are
`cityportals_fx.lua`'s ("City portals"). Not seen in a live client (the animated text packet is the one of
`combat_fx.lua`, tested). `tests/tile_labels_test.lua`.

## City portals (`cityportals.lua`, `cityportals_core.lua`, `cityportals_config.lua`, `cityportals_fx.lua`)

Owner test 2026-10-16: the hideout and guild hall entries stood "in the middle of nowhere", with nothing saying what
they were. One shared helper now places every labelled portal near a temple, so a later portal gets the same for a
config line: `ChaosCityPortals.place({kind, aid, item?, towns?, offsets?, log?})` (one per town, kept when it already
stands, checked again by the caller once a minute) and `ChaosCityPortals.register(kind, aid, pos, town)` for a portal
placed by other means. Users: `hideout.lua` (kind `hideout`, action id 47610), `guild_hall.lua` (`guildhall`, 47602),
`memorial.lua` (`memorial`, 47944: Cinderhold and Mirewake), `harvestevent.lua` (`harvest`), `siege.lua` (`siege`, 47211: the Guild Siege Portals while a siege is open, from
its `portalOffsets`; closing removes them and the pulse drops them; `portalPositions` and the staff `/siege portal` only
register theirs), `worldboss.lua` (`worldboss`, the World Boss Portals while a boss is awake, the same way). Labelled
only (they keep their own placement, `ChaosCityPortals.register`): the Ember Descent and raid portals (`descent`,
`raid`, their `portal.positions`: in Cinderhold the temple's portal gallery), the hunting-area entrances of `areagen_config.lua` (`hunt`, 47950: one action id
for every area, so each portal carries its own title, "Emberdeep Hollows, levels 1000-1100", made by `C.bandTitle`
from the area's `name` and `spawns.level`; a new area gets one with no other change), the Idle Hall's exit
(`idlehall`, 47911, below). `chronicle.lua` places the **Chronicle Gates** (`chronicle`, 47920 + the area's index;
one spot per area, `spec.spot` "chronicle_<key>", and the area's name as `spec.title`) when a chapter opens an area,
for `gateTowns` (Cinderhold and Mirewake) beside the temple (Cinderhold: the gallery, Breach 32359, 32245, 7 and
Ossuary Stair 32377, 32245, 7; Mirewake 32959, 32073, 7 and 32961, 32074, 7); `ChaosCityPortals.remove(aid)` takes them away when the area closes. The installer's hunt teleports
(`hunt_teleports.lua`) already carry "Name, levels A-B" (both languages) and a sign, so they stay as they are.

**The Idle Hall's exit** gets its own action id 47911 (`idlehall_config.lua` `aid.exit`, `hall.exit` 22, 11, the plan's
exit tile, checked by `tools/idle_hall_test.py`): the installer leaves areagen's shared 47951 there; `idlehall.lua`
re-tags it at startup and every minute (a portal already re-tagged is found again, so the migration is idempotent) and
handles the step itself: the character's temple, else Cinderhold's. Look text "Idle Hall Exit: Step in to go back to
your temple. ..." and a blue effect.

**Where** (`C.candidates`, first match): the town's fixed spot (`towns`, offsets from the temple, by the spot:
`spec.spot`, default the kind; used only while the temple is where the config says, so another map falls through;
in Cinderhold the alcoves of the temple's portal gallery, "Temple portal gallery"); then the caller's offsets, then
the config's. A tile is free (`C.spotOk`) with ground, nothing blocking, no
house, teleport or stairs, and nothing movable or a door on it (borders, grass and other floor dressing are fine). The
fixed spots were chosen on the reference map (2026-10-16, `tools/map/otbm.py` and `itemdb.py`, renders checked by eye):
bare floor of the temple area, the two side by side along a wall or the edge of the square, off every shortest way from
the temple to its doors, stairs and edges, not next to stairs or a door, never the tile an NPC placement around the
temple takes first, and the area stays connected with both placed.

## Base item names (`tools/patch_base_item_names.py`, `data/items/base_item_names.csv`, `tests/base_item_names_patch_test.lua`)

Base items that our systems show (quivers, the Gambler's pool) and that carried names from another world get Chaos names
by id: `data/items/base_item_names.csv` (columns `id,article,name,plural`; an empty article or plural removes it; only
ids and new names are in the repository). `patch_base_item_names.py` (step `itemnames` of `install_all.py`, after
`archery`) reads the old name from the server's `items.xml`, writes the new name, article and plural, turns every monster
loot entry that named the item (`id = "old name"` in Lua, `<item name="old name"/>` in XML) into loot by id (an XML entry
with an id as well only loses its name; a doubled `id` an older version wrote is written once), and renames
the other mentions in the base data, whole words and case-insensitively, but not inside the name of another item
(`data/scripts/chaos`, `data/lib/chaos_*.lua` and `data/items` are not touched). The engine finds loot by name, so a
renamed item would otherwise drop out of the loot lists. On the reference server: 13 items, 122 loot entries by name
turned into ids, 9 other mentions (an NPC shop, a quest reward text, comments), 30 files.

| Id | New name | | Id | New name |
