| 28693 | ashwood quiver | | 27676 | bonewhisper quiver |
| 27651 | thornhide quiver | | 28379 | rimeshard quiver |
| 27694 | ravenfeather quiver | | 27695 | cinderflight quiver |
| 27696 | splitwind quiver | | 9778 | hollowspire mask |
| 27663 | stormfletch quiver | | 9776 | hollowspire armor |
| 27686 | blightroot quiver | | 9777 | hollowspire leg piece |
| | | | 8877 | molten scale armor |

The Haloed, Mercurial and Seraphic quivers keep their names: they belong to the base server's own late-game sets.

**Second round (owner decision: every name of the other world goes).** The CSV now holds 1,182 ids: the 13 above and
1,169 more, every base item whose name carried a proper noun or coinage of the other world (its races and factions,
its towns as place adjectives, its bosses and their trophies, corpses and remains, its persons, named sets) or a name
from another game (card sets, legendary weapons, a quiver, armour sets). Corpse and trophy names follow the monster
renames ("Base monster names"), place adjectives follow the town renames (the old capital's swords take the new town
name). An id may also be the fromid of a `fromid`/`toid` range entry (30 of them). Several ids may share a new name
only when `items.xml` gave them the same old name (one item kind with several ids); otherwise the tool stops before
it writes anything. Bonelord items keep their names (the Necromancer's Bonelord line uses the word; generic). On the
reference server, run after the whole install: 1,182 ids renamed (700 distinct old names), 801 loot entries by name
turned into ids, 516 other mentions, 318 files; a second run changes nothing. Item names that name NPCs of the other
world (letters, keepsakes) got new person names; the NPC rename ("Base NPC names") reuses them for those NPCs.

Part two added 18 ids whose names still carried a word of the old world or of another game (the trophies of two
renamed bosses, a mount's statues, a race of another game, a god's throwing star; 1,200 ids now). Since then the tool
changes only string literals in Lua files and only attribute values in XML files, never a path: a new name with an
apostrophe is escaped for the quote style of its Lua string, and a movements.xml script path that happened to contain
an item's old name no longer changes. Fresh install: 1,200 ids (711 old names), 806 loot entries by name turned into
ids, 387 other mentions; a second run changes nothing.

## Star inlay stones (`tools/patch_star_inlay.py`, `data/scripts/chaos/star_inlay_core.lua`, `tests/star_inlay_test.lua`, O181)

Beta 2026-10-24 (screenshots): "are these items working?" The Star Extractor (golden hammer) and the Common Three Stars
Inlay Stone (green stone with three stars) looked like leftovers of the base server. **They work.** It is a base system
(`data/scripts/customs/tier_system`: `inlay_stars.lua`, `upgrade_system_tiers.lua`, `star_extractor.lua`, each an
`Action()` registered by item id), and nothing in our code replaces, disables or duplicates it (no Chaos script uses
these ids except the price tables, `sell_prices.lua` and `chaos_item_prices_data.lua`).
- **What it does.** 20 base set pieces have twins with stars: Skeletal (26708-26711), Netherwave (26761-26764),
  Ironwrath (26766-26769), Blightwoven (26770-26773) and Ashborne (26774-26777) helmet, armor, legs and boots. A Star
  Inlay Stone (27133) turns a plain piece into its empty-star twin (27113-27132). A Common, Rare, Very Rare, Epic or
  Legendary stone of 1, 2 or 3 stars (27134-27148) turns the empty-star twin into one of 15 star variants (26813-27112,
  300 items: "Tier I ( 1 Star )" to "Tier V ( 3 Star )"; the variants differ in items.xml armor, absorbs, skills and speed,
  for example boots +35 speed at Tier I and +65 at Tier V). The Star Extractor (27149) turns a star variant back into
  the empty twin and gives the stone back. One stone per piece; a piece is never lost.
- **Where they drop.** The base monster loot, by item name (so the Chaos item finder shows it): the Master of the
  Elements (Star Inlay Stone 81% for up to 5, the 15 stones 5-57%, the Extractor 14% for up to 3) and the seven monsters
  of its cave (Herk, Alchemist, Brute, Forgepriest, Wardragon, Mega Dragon, Mitmah Vanguard; some also spawn in
  open hunts such as the Ironhorn Slagworks): the Common and Rare stones 3-9%, the Extractor 4%. The base boss bag
  script (`customs/enhanced_loot`) and the base task of the Master of the Elements list the same items, and the weekly
  chest the plaza had (unique id 34804, "Hall order") gave 2 + 2. The drop tooltip numbers (Herk 6% and Alchemist 6% for
  the Common Three Stars stone) are the base chances. The price tables sell the stones to the Loot Buyer and the Auto
  Seller (660 gold for a Common stone, 5,600 for 27133, 11,000 for the high ones).
- **How it fits the Chaos item system.** The stock scripts swap the item id with `item:transform`, which keeps every
  custom attribute: item level, rarity, modifiers, sockets and gems stay. The star variants have their own equip
  entries in `movements.xml` (the class lists of the vocations step cover them like any equipment), and the Chaos
  names are in `base_item_names.csv`. Stars add a few points of base stats, orbs and gems add modifiers: different
  layers, no conflict, no redundancy worth retiring a working system for.
- **Fixes** (`patch_star_inlay.py`, install step `starinlay`, after `itemnames`; idempotent; `--check`, `--dry-run`):
  1. The stone wrote the type's description over the item's own description attribute, which holds the Chaos crafting
     text ("Item Level: N. modifiers", sockets). Now `StarInlay.refineItem` keeps the text and adds one
     "Refined by <name>." line; a piece with no own text still gets the tier line, as before. The extractor removes
     the stale "Refined by" line from the empty twin.
  2. The stone and the extractor change the item type of a **worn** piece. The equip event had added the old type's
     speed and skills, so taking the piece off took the new type's away (boots: 30 speed of drift per change). Both now
     refuse a worn piece ("Take it off first: its stars change what it gives.", pt-BR in `i18n_strings.lua`;
     `StarInlay.isWorn(toPosition)`: x 65535 and y 1-63).
  3. The items.xml descriptions of 27133-27149 said "certain equipment"; they name the five sets and "not worn".
  4. `base_item_names.csv`: the typo "Epice" of one star variant (27048) is "Epic" (the tool now lets a one-letter typo of
     the base file share the new name of its kind, `_near`), and the four "Netherwave Bots" (26894, 26954, 27014, 27074)
     are "Boots".
- **Not changed.** Drops, chances, ids and what a character holds. Nothing is retired: the system is small (20 pieces) but
  complete, and the stones sell. If the owner wants it gone, the loot lines of the stones in the base monsters, the boss
  bag and the task reward are the only sources (`patch_base_throwables.py` shows the pattern); the stones keep selling.
- **Tests.** `tests/star_inlay_test.lua` (64 checks): the core, the patch on fixtures of the stock scripts (applies, idempotent,
  parses, `--check` / `--dry-run`, a changed base script is reported) and the patched stone and extractor scripts on a
  mocked engine (a piece with a rolled description keeps it, a piece without gets the tier line, the extractor returns the
  stone, a worn piece is refused and nothing is used up, the stock refusals stay, pt-BR). `tests/base_item_names_patch_test.lua`
  covers the typo rule. Run on a real base copy 2026-10-24: both scripts patched, parse in Lua 5.3 and LuaJIT, a second run
  changes nothing. Not run live.

## Base monster names (`tools/patch_base_monster_names.py`, `data/monster/base_monster_names.csv`, `tests/base_monster_names_patch_test.lua`)

Owner decision: the base monsters that carried names of the other world (its named bosses, races, factions, cults,
place adjectives, named sets) get Chaos names; generic fantasy names (rat, dragon, orc, skeleton, bonelord) stay.
Stats, looks and loot are untouched: only names change.

**The CSV holds no old name.** `data/monster/base_monster_names.csv` has the columns `sha256,name,kind`: the SHA-256 of
the old name in lower case, the new name, and `monster` or `look`. The tool collects every name the base data uses
(`monsters.xml`, the monster files, `Game.createMonsterType`, the spawn files, the raid files, the outfit and mount
lists), hashes each one and renames the ones the CSV knows. The CSV is also the hashed mapping for the later renames of
NPC dialogue, the quest log and raid texts: hash a name found in the data and look it up. 429 rows: 414 base monster
types, 7 of our own Chaos monsters whose donor names came from other games (they spawn by those names in the base
spawn file; their files in `monsters/chaos` were renamed with them), and 8 outfit and mount names with the old
world's words (`look` rows; outfits and mounts named like a renamed monster follow its row).

**What it changes** (step `monsternames` of `install_all.py`, right after `lib`): registrations in `monsters.xml` (a
line whose new name another line already registers, from an older install, is dropped; lines that already shared a
name stay); attribute values of the XML files (monster names, descriptions with the article fixed, summons, voices,
event names, spawn entries and their `lategame` marks, raid spawns and messages, item descriptions, monster spells by
name); Lua string literals (Lua monsters, scripts, actions, creature scripts, libs), never identifiers or comments.
Whole words, case-insensitive; a match inside a longer item or monster name (a corpse "dead <name>", a kept monster)
is left to that name, and so is a word joined by "_" or an apostrophe. Not touched: paths, NPC entries of the spawn
file (an NPC may share a monster's name), engine effect names
(`areaEffect` values), `data/npc` (dialogue keywords), `data/XML/quests.xml`, house files, `data/scripts/chaos`,
`data/lib/chaos_*.lua` and the Chaos monster folders. Monster file names stay: the engine registers monsters by the
`monsters.xml` name. It runs before `lategame` and `spawns` because `late_game_spawns.csv` names the monsters it
replaces by their new names.

**Measured on the reference server** (fresh install, the whole `install_all.py`): 414 names renamed, 272 registration
lines, 10,696 spawn entries, 47 raid spawns, 12,501 mentions in all, 16 outfit and mount names, 606 files; a second
run changes nothing. Started on the full map with a test database, compared with the same install before the
renames: the same 74,255 spawn entries and 872 spawned names, every one with a monster type, 1,046 registrations all
loaded, no "Can not find" or unknown monster warning, no Lua error, the raids load, and every loot row points to an
item (10,533 rows; the run before had 10,526 and 6 bad rows, which the loot by id now resolves). The regenerated `bounty_pool.lua` and `bestiary_spawns.lua` differ from
the old run only by the new names.

Our tables follow the new names: boss spawns (keys renamed too; four raid bosses the base never defined were dropped),
invasion bosses, boss points, tiers, infinity tower, bestiary words, transmog and exclusives (the Pyrarch Arms), late
game spawns, professions areas, unique item sources and the client tests. Still named after the other world (later
decisions): NPC names and dialogue, the quest log, raid folder and file names, house names, the other outfit and mount
names, one engine effect name the plant monsters use (an engine constant), one base event name that a Chaos monster
registers, and the two orb names of another game kept as `old =` keys in `chaos_orbs_config.lua` (install_orbs.py).
NPC names, dialogue, the quest log, raids and houses followed in part two ("Base NPC names" and the next sections).

**Fixed in part two:** a new name with an apostrophe (one boss's new name has one) was written into a single-quoted
Lua string of a base script, which then failed to load (`'}' expected near 's'`). String literals are now changed
through `base_rename_lib.patch_lua`, which escapes a quote of the string's own kind (single, double, long brackets),
and a string with an escaped quote is no longer mistaken for a path. `tests/base_monster_names_patch_test.lua` checks
it, and after an install every `.lua` of `data/` compiles with `luajit -b` (3,743 files).

## Base NPC names (`tools/patch_base_npc_names.py`, `data/npc/base_npc_names.csv`, `tests/base_world_names_patch_test.lua`)

Owner decision, part two of the rename: the base NPCs get Cinders of Chaos names. Generic names stay ("A Beggar",
"The Oracle", "Royal Guard", "Santa Claus", the test NPCs); persons get names by kind: dwarves, elves, djinns, lizards,
orcs and minotaurs names of their own flavour, the gnomes new gnome names (Gnomsalve, Gnomkettle, ...), women and
men by their outfit. Titles and roles stay (Captain, Guide, King, "the Worker", ", the guard"); captains got sea names
(Captain Brinehook, Captain Seawolf, Captain Kelpmane). NPCs named by an item of part one keep that person's name
(the letter's addressee, the keepsake's owner). Our own NPCs (`server/data/npc`) are not touched.

**The CSV holds no old name.** `data/npc/base_npc_names.csv` has the columns `sha256,name,kind,match`: the SHA-256 of
the old name in lower case (blanks folded), the new name, `npc` (a shown name, also used for dialogue) or `file` (an
NPC file name that is not its shown name), and `word` or `cap` (see "Base world texts"). 904 rows: 800 shown names, 69
name parts that dialogue uses alone (a captain's surname, a family name) and 35 file names.

**What it changes** (step `npcnames` of `install_all.py`, after `towns`): the engine loads an NPC by file name (a spawn
entry `<npc name="X"/>` loads `data/npc/X.xml`), so the NPC file is renamed with its shown name, every `<npc>` entry of
the spawn and raid files follows, and a Lua string that is exactly an old file name (`Game.createNpc("X", ...)`) too.
Script files keep their paths (players never see them; `patch_base_classes.py` patches some by path). A file whose new
name is taken keeps its name and is listed. Two tools that wrote to one base NPC by file name (the desert trader
Grimgan of `install_pack_items.py` and `install_fist_weapons.py`) find him by his new name, or before this step by the
sha256 of his old file name. Fresh install: 827 files renamed, 826 shown names, 798 spawn entries, 30 Lua references;
the server loads every NPC (960 spawn entries, no new warning).

## Task NPC names (`tools/patch_task_npc.py`, `data/lib/chaos_task_names.lua`, `tests/task_names_test.lua`)

Beta report 2026-10-22: at the base task NPC Mermod, saying most task names did nothing, so no task started and no
kill counted. Causes in the base scripts:
- The NPC took a name only after "normal" or "daily" said in a line of its own. A bare name got no answer at all.
- The name had to match letter for letter. Brackets as the list shows them, a hyphen or a missing apostrophe failed.
- The kill script compared the shown name, case sensitive. A list entry with a capital letter never counted.
- A party member got progress on the killer's task, not on their own.

The `tasknpc` step (after `npcnames`) finds the two scripts by their stock lines and patches them:
- After `local msg = msg:lower()`: a bare task name, or "normal <name>" / "daily <name>" in one line, starts that task
  the stock way (`ChaosTaskNames.route`, the normal list first). A daily name on the daily cooldown gets the stock
  cooldown reply.
- Both name loops also accept `ChaosTaskNames.same`: any case, brackets, quotes and apostrophes ignored, hyphens read
  as spaces, a plural "s" and a trailing word "task" tolerated.
- A kill also counts by `ChaosTaskNames.killCounts`: the shown name or the type name (`Chaos.monsterTypeName`), the same
  rules. Each party member counts their own normal and daily task.

Marker `Chaos: task names (patch_task_npc.py)`; a second run changes nothing. The test runs the tool on a reduced
copy of the stock lines with made-up names and says every listed name four ways. `TASK_NPC_DATA=<data dir>` runs the
same checks on a real installed server's scripts and task lists. On the beta base copy all 15 normal and 11 daily
names register and every normal task counts its first monster. Left as they are: two normal tasks share one name (the
first one starts), and one listed monster of the base lists does not exist on the server.

## NPC currencies (`tools/patch_npc_currency.py`, `data/lib/chaos_npc_currency.lua`, `tests/npc_currency_test.lua`, client `game_npctradewindow`)

Owner beta 2026-10-24 (O189), a screenshot of the azure NPC's trade window: "broken window. Where do players get azure
coins?" The window said "Currency: Gold Coin", priced the Blightwoven / Ironwrath / Netherwave / Ashborne set pieces and
bows "Price 30, 85.00 ..." and showed the player's 30.4M gold; names were cut ("blightwoven arm..."); and the NPC's
reply to "azure" talked about "knights", "sorcerers and druids" and "paladins".

**What azure coins are.** Item 26780, "Azure Coin" (weight 5, "Mystic Coin used to trade valuables things"), the
currency of the azure NPC (`data/npc/scripts/`, the script of the NPC the NPC list names Lanath): 30 coins for a
helmet, armor, legs or boots, 50 for a sword, bow, wand or rod; selling a piece back pays half. The NPC checks
`player:removeItem(26780, ...)`, so the coins are real items in the backpack, not a storage. They are also an ingredient of
the base crafting recipes (`data/items/base_recipes.csv`: 30 per armor, 50 per weapon, 15 per jewel of the base smiths).
`data/items/base_item_values.csv` lists them as `currency` (not sellable to the Loot Buyer).

**Where players get them (no new source was needed; the base's own, all still in the installed data).** Read from the
base server's data on 2026-10-24:
- the boss of the Azure portals (`data/monster/lua/azure_portals/boss/azure.lua`, the lever fight of
  `data/scripts/customs/portals/azure.lua`: level 200, four players, one try per player every 4 h): 65% for 1-22 coins.
  The base's Enhanced Loot script (`data/scripts/customs/enhanced_loot/`) gives the same boss a 50% chance of a bag with
  one of these set pieces directly, so the sets also drop where the NPC sells them;
- the Forbidden Chevalier (`data/monster/lua/dungeons/forbidden/`, a dungeon boss): 25% for 1-3 coins;
- the base tasks (`data/scripts/customs/tasks/tasks.lua`): the Azure Catacombs task pays 8 coins, three more pay 2, 3 and 3;
  the ancestral tasks (`data/lib/custom/ancestral_task.lua`) pay 10 for killing the Azure boss once, and 4 each for the
  150-kill depths task and the 300-kill portal task.
Our loot layer (`loot.lua`) runs after the stock drop and never removes a line of a base table, so none of this changed.
The Master of the Elements does not drop them (its table has none of these items), and nothing of ours (`scripts/chaos`,
`chaos_item_prices_data.lua`, the loot bands, the store, the roulette) names item 26780. Not checked in a live client:
that the portal lever and the dungeon work on the installed map. The Enhanced Loot and task rewards were not changed, so
no store, roulette, gold or loot model moved (store_model, roulette_model, loot_model and gen_item_prices pass unchanged).
The NPC says it now: "Azure Coins drop from the boss of the Azure portals and the Forbidden Chevalier, and some hunting
tasks pay them."

**Cause of the window.** The 10.98 shop packet (0x7A) has no currency, so the base client window always shows gold. Eight
base NPC scripts that trade for something else (the azure NPC; five mining-crafting NPCs that pay in town coins kept in a
storage, 48076-48080; the sweets NPC, dark chocolate coins, item 28697; the token NPC, silver tokens, item 25172) told the
old client by two extended opcodes, `ServerOpcodes.currencyType` 125 (a code such as "AZ") and `ServerOpcodes.coinAmount`
126, which no module of ours read. 125 is also the monster bar's opcode (`ChaosOpcodes.monsterbar`), so the code arrived
there as a broken JSON. The rows were cut by the base's `short_text(name, 15)` and `short_text(info, 16)`.

**Fix.**
- Server, step `npccurrency` (after `worldtexts`; `patch_npc_currency.py`, marker `Chaos: npc currency (patch_npc_currency.py)`):
  in those scripts the three opcode lines become `ChaosNpcCurrency.announce(player, {code, item | storage, name})`, which
  sends JSON on the new opcode 113 (`ChaosOpcodes.npcCurrency`): the currency's name (the item type's, or the script's own
  "... coins" text for a storage currency, so the world renames apply), the item for the icon, the balance. The two shop
  callbacks are wrapped so the balance is sent again (`again = true`) after every purchase and sale. The azure NPC's
  sell message named another currency ("... Coins"): it names the item's plural. Its reply to "azure" is now
  "Stuff for every class: Blightwoven and Ironwrath for Warriors, Netherwave for Mystics and Ashborne for Rangers." plus the
  source line, in the player's language (`ChaosNpcCurrency.setsReply`, keys in `i18n_strings.lua`; the set names are the
  renamed words found in the script; the Warrior line wears the first two sets, the Mystic line the third, the Ranger line the
  fourth, by the lists `add_vocations.py` rewrote). `data/global.lua`: `ServerOpcodes` 125 / 126 become 126 / 127, so a
  script the tool does not know stops writing to the monster bar. Files are found by their stock lines (any NPC name); a
  file without them is reported and left alone; CRLF and every other byte are kept.
- Client, `game_npctradewindow` (client/MANIFEST.md): opcode 113. The window shows the currency's name and icon (no icon
  for a storage currency), "Balance:" and the player's amount of it in place of the gold (the base's `getPlayerMoney`, so
  the buy button, the amount and the grey rows follow it); the gold comes back when the window closes. Every row (gold
  shops too) is rewritten to the whole item name and "Price 30, 85.00 oz" with a full tooltip. New texts "Balance:" and
  "Price %s" have pt-BR entries.
- Install: `python3 -I server/tools/install_all.py SERVER_DIR --only files,npccurrency` (or the admin app: Painel > Atualizar
  servidor > Aplicar e reiniciar, which runs the whole install), then a server restart. The client needs its Lua overlay
  published (the same update, box "publicar o update do client"), no engine build: no C++ and no base patch changed.
- Tests: `tests/npc_currency_test.lua` (balance, payload, JSON, announce, wrapped callbacks, the reply in English and pt-BR,
  opcode free), `tools/patch_npc_currency_test.py` (the patch on synthetic stock lines, CRLF, dry run, second run, both
  Lua dialects parse), `tradewindowlogic_test.lua` and `tradewindow_test.lua` (the currency life, the rows, the glue
  against a mocked client). Not run in a live client or on the installed server: the other seven NPCs' storage names are
  read from their own messages and were not looked at in game; Quick Sell and Sell All still say "gold" in their
  messages (they were not changed).

## Base world texts (`tools/patch_base_texts.py`, `tools/base_rename_lib.py`, `data/npc/base_world_names.csv`)

Every text of the base data that names the old world gets the new names: NPC dialogue and keywords, travel
destinations, the quest log (`data/XML/quests.xml`), raid messages, the base achievements, item descriptions, script
messages, outfit and mount names, and the texts of signs, books and plaques on the map. Step `worldtexts` of
`install_all.py`, after `npcnames`.

**Names.** Three hashed lists: `data/npc/base_world_names.csv` (266 rows: the 20 towns as in "Town names", their
demonyms, the world itself (Cindral), places (Sarvekh, Vhassa, Jadefen, Brassmoor, Gullhaven, Hagmoor Hills, ...), gods
(Kaedros, Vorthaal, Verdane, Ilvane, ...), factions, persons the old lore names, coined mount names, and words of other
games that part one left in texts), the NPC list and the monster list. A phrase of 1 to 5 words of the data is looked
up by its sha256; when two lists know it, the world list wins, then the NPC list, then the monster list. The world's
ruling caste of Hollowspire are the Spirekin; a demonym is used as an adjective ("the Cinderhold army").

**Rules.** Whole words, case kept (a lower-case keyword stays lower case, so a player says the new name), `a`/`an`
fixed, a "the ..." name not doubled and capitalized at a sentence start. `match = cap` rows (old names that are also
English words, such as a colour or a coin) change only where written with a capital letter, or as a keyword (a whole
string, a `;`-separated element, a short lower-case phrase such as "x sent me"), and not inside the title-case name of
an outfit or mount (a mount "Crimson X" stays). In Lua only string literals change (identifiers and comments never), escaped
for their quote style; paths, strings assigned to a file / map / path key (`mapName = '...'` is loaded as
`data/world/.../<name>.otbm`), spell and talkaction words, engine effect names (`key="areaEffect"`) and the item names
of `items.xml` stay. Names the data looks things up by stay too: item, monster and NPC names (an item named like an old
NPC yields where the NPC is meant, written with a capital letter). Our own files are skipped (`data/scripts/chaos`,
`data/spells/chaos`, `data/lib/chaos_*.lua`, the Chaos monster folders, `server/data/npc`).

**Raid spawns (O294).** Owner log 2026-10-27: `[Error] Raids: Cant create monster <name>`. A raid file names its boss in
`<singlespawn name="..."/>` and `<areaspawn><monster name="..."/>`; that is a monster type name, and the monster files
keep their base name. When the tool did not find the monster type (a boss defined where `monster/` scans do not look),
the spawn name was read as an old person's name and renamed, so the raid asked the engine for a monster that does not
exist. Now the spawn names (`singlespawn`, `monster`, `npc` tags of `data/raids/*.xml`) are never renamed, only the
announcement texts; Lua strings given to `createMonster(...)`, `doCreateMonster`, `doSummonCreature`, `summonCreature`
and `createMonsterType` stay too (`base_rename_lib.py` `patch_lua(skip_monsters=True)`). The step also repairs a server
an older run already changed: a raid spawn name that is the replacement of a row and that no monster type has (monsters.xml,
monster files, `createMonsterType`, the `-spawn.xml` files of `data/world`) goes back to the monster name whose sha256
the row has (`restore_raid_spawns`, printed as `raids: N spawn name(s) put back`). Idempotent. Test:
`tests/base_world_names_patch_test.lua`. Other file kinds: NPC scripts, quest and achievement Lua and the spawn files
(`data/world` is not touched) had the same weakness only for Lua strings that name a monster to create, now guarded;
other strings are prose and stay renamed. Install: stop the server, `install_all.py SERVER_DIR --only worldtexts
--dry-run`, then without `--dry-run`, start the server. The admin app's Update button runs every step, `worldtexts` included, so Update does it; no SQL, no client change.

**The map.** Item texts and descriptions are attributes of item nodes in the `.otbm`. The tool finds item nodes with
attributes by their marker bytes, parses each node's attributes (a node with an attribute it does not know is left
alone), rewrites the strings with their new lengths, escapes the bytes again and splices the node back; the rest of the
file is copied as it was. Before writing it checks that the item node count and the node markers are the same and that
every new text reads back, writes through a temporary file and keeps `<map>.otbm.bak` the first time (the towns step
usually made it already). Read back with `tools/map/otbm.py`: the same 18,185,071 tiles and 23,317,821 item entries,
every item id in place, towns and temples the same. Pure Python, about 15 s on the reference map.

**Fresh install:** 1,222 old names found (239 world, 831 NPC, 152 monster rows), 6,271 replacements in 642 files (towns
1,956, NPCs 2,350, places 739, worlds and demonyms 493, gods 192, monsters 149, factions 103, lore 129, persons 119,
mount words 41), 564 map texts (1,164 replacements). A second whole install changes nothing (0 files, the map's md5
unchanged). Every `.lua` of `data/` compiles with `luajit -b` (3,743 files).

**Tested on the full map** (test MariaDB, three bot characters over the game protocol, `tools/loadtest.py` setup): the
captain of Cinderhold's harbour sails to Mirewake ("Do you seek a passage to Mirewake for 170 gold?", the player lands
at 32954,32022,6), Thornmere's captain to Cinderhold, Bellwatch's to Wyrmscar; a shop NPC opens the trade window; the
Lions raid announces "There are more lions than usual west of Scorchveil."; no Lua error; compared with the install of
part one only one console line differs: the base script that the apostrophe broke loads again.

**Left as they are** (not seen by players, or owned by another name): file and folder names (NPC scripts, raid and
quest folders, the merchant's town maps, script paths, storage and event identifiers such as `portal_<town>`), the
names of items and monsters that are also old NPC names or plain English words (a staff, a shield and flowers named
after plain words, one barbarian boss, one expedition monster and a letter that names its family), common English words
written in lower case in prose ("skip the tutorial"), and one engine effect name.

**Fenmaw.** One of our Chaos monsters (`monsters/chaos/fenmaw.xml`, look 374) and the base mount 7 had the same coined
name of the old world. Both are now Fenmaw: a colossal swamp beast that hisses, chokes its prey in bog water and roots
it in creepers. The mount is that beast, saddled. The monster file, its name and `nameDescription` were renamed in the
repository. The mount has the hashed `look` row of `data/npc/base_world_names.csv`: as long as a monster of the data
carried the old name, the row could not apply (names the data looks things up by stay). Now this step renames it in
`mounts.xml` and in the two base mount menu scripts (3 replacements), and `tools/gen_shop_cosmetics.py` writes the store
offer `mount:7` with the new name. A server installed before this change keeps the old monster file and its
`monsters.xml` line (the `files` step never deletes): delete the other file of `data/monster/monsters/chaos` with look 374 and its line, then
run `install_all.py` again; the old name is then gone from the data and the mount follows.

## Base houses (`tools/patch_base_houses.py`, `tools/base_house_names.csv`)

All 1,057 houses get street names of their town by house id (`id,name`; ids carry no old names). Each old street became
one new street of the town's flavour, numbers and suffixes kept ("Tallow Row 4 (Shop)", "Gloom Hollows 3", "Kindle Isle
Cottage #7", "Sunscour Terrace 2, Flat 07", the guildhalls and clanhalls by their town). Step `houses` of `install_all.py`
writes the names into `<mapName>-house.xml`; ids, entries, rents, towns and sizes stay, so owners and rents in the
database are untouched. The server writes the loaded names into the `houses` table at its next save; the website's
house pages (ZnoteX `houses.php`) read that table. Checked: after a start and a shutdown the table has the 1,057 new
names.

## Server name (`src-patches/0030-server-name.patch`, `tools/patch_base_server_name.py`, `tools/base_server_texts.csv`)

The base server still told players and server lists the name of the server it came from. Now ours everywhere:

- **Status protocol** (engine patch 0030): the status document's `serverinfo` sends `server="Cinders of Chaos"
  version="1.0"` (were the base server's name and version and the engine version), and the software info answer (0x23)
  the same two. The console's first line is `Cinders of Chaos 1.0 (engine TFS 1.4.2)`; the root warning and the
  Windows console title use the name. Constants `CHAOS_SERVER_NAME` and `CHAOS_SERVER_VERSION` in `definitions.h`; the
  base constant stays there unused (a hunk that removed it would carry the old name into this repository).
- **Data** (step `servername` of `install_all.py`, after `worldtexts`): the floating welcome text over the first temple
  (`data/scripts/customs/actions/messages_text.lua`) says "Welcome to Cinders of Chaos!", the web login service's
  console banner (`data/scripts/customs/znote/znote_login.lua`) "= Cinders of Chaos Login =". The world renames could
  not do this: they replace single names, and a new row there would have doubled our name in the banner, where step
  `worldtexts` already turned its first word into "Cinders of Chaos". This tool replaces exact whole Lua strings: each
  row of `tools/base_server_texts.csv` is the sha256 of one old string's content as written (no old text in the
  repository), its file and the new text. The banner has two rows (the base form and the form after `worldtexts`), so
  the order of the steps does not matter and a tree installed before this change gets the same text. A second run
  changes nothing ("already done"); a file with neither the old string nor the new text is reported (exit 1).
  `tests/base_server_name_patch_test.lua` runs it on made-up strings.
- **config.lua `serverName`** (the world name of the character list, so the client's corner label, highscores and
  console tabs; the status `servername`; `znote_global_storage`): the same step sets it to "Cinders of Chaos" while it
  still holds the base server's value, so a test server installed with `install_all.py` alone shows our world name.
  The rows with file `config.lua` hash the base values (no old text in the repository); only the value of the
  `serverName = "..."` line is checked, nothing else in `config.lua`. Any other value (an owner's own name, the line
  `tools/prod_config.py --name` wrote) stays ("left as it is", exit 0); a second run says "already done"; `--dry-run`
  writes nothing; a `config.lua` without the line is reported (exit 1).
- **config.lua, the rest**: `motd`, `url`, `location` and the owner come from `tools/prod_config.py`; the base values
  stay on a server it was not run on.

Checked on a fresh base tree with every install step: no other old server name in the data, the scripts or the SQL
files. Left as they are (not shown to players): the Windows build files of the base (`vc17/`, the `.bat` restarters
naming the base executable), the base map's file name and the spawn and house file names inside it, the base
database name in the stock `config.lua`. The base map has one book that uses the English word for a mass departure
in its title and text (lore of a desert people), not the server's name; it stays.
Tested: the server built with 0001-0030 answered the status request with the new `server` and `version`, the software
info request the same, printed the new console line; the old name is not in the binary. On the installed test tree the
two strings changed, a second whole install changed nothing.

## Base server start warnings (`tools/patch_base_migrations.py`, `tools/patch_base_monsters.py`, `sql/chaos_website_tables.sql`, `tools/fresh_db_check.py`)

The first start of the Windows package (release winpkg-35, 2026-10-16) printed these; each is fixed at its source.

- **Database migrations** (install step `migrations`). The engine runs `data/migrations/<db_version>.lua` upwards at
  every start. The base `schema.sql` creates the columns of its migrations 33-40 (custom skills, wings, aura, shader,
  the smith skills) but writes `db_version` 33, so on a fresh database each of them failed with "Duplicate column name",
  and 41 (`znote_shop_orders.mountid`) failed on the missing table. `patch_base_migrations.py` rewrites every migration
  line that only adds named columns into `if db.tableExists("t") then db.query("ALTER TABLE t ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS
  ...") end` (MariaDB syntax; other statements stay). Same result on an old database, no error on a new one.
- **Website tables** (`sql/chaos_website_tables.sql`, install step `sql`). Base scripts use six tables of the website:
  `znote_global_storage` (login service banner at startup), `znote_players` (skill history at login and logout),
  `znote_shop_orders` (shop orders, migration 41), `znote_accounts`, `znote_guild_wars`, `znote_player_reports`. A game
  database without the website printed SQL errors at every start and login. The file creates them empty, with the
  definitions of the website's pinned schema (`website/install_site.sh`; its installer accepts tables that already
  exist and fills `znote_accounts` / `znote_players` for the existing accounts), and adds `mountid`. The packages get
  it through `sql-setup`.
- **Fresh-database check**: `python3 -I server/tools/fresh_db_check.py SERVER_DIR [--sql-dir DIR | --sql FILE ...]`
  starts a throwaway MariaDB, loads the first-start SQL (default `SERVER_DIR/sql-setup`) and runs the migrations as
  `DatabaseManager::updateDatabase` does, printing the engine's error lines; exit 1 on any SQL error. On the base
  download: stock migrations 9 errors (33-41, as in the start log); after `patch_base_migrations.py` and with
  `chaos_website_tables.sql`, db_version 33 -> 42 and no error. `tools/fresh_db_check_test.py` (skips the database
  part without MariaDB).
- **Monster load warnings** (install step `basemonsters`, after `itemnames`). `patch_base_monsters.py` changes the base
  monster files (not `monsters/chaos`, `lua/chaos`): a speed spell below -1000 becomes -1000 (11 bosses; the engine
  clamped it anyway, with a warning each), a loot name written with its article becomes the item id of that name (the
  jester doll parts of one undead monster: "Unknown loot item", "Cant load loot"), an unknown race gets a known one
  (two Lua bosses: `magical` -> energy, `dragon` -> blood). `tools/patch_base_monsters_test.py`.
- **Empty spawns**: ours, `patch_base_spawns.py` (see "What the spawns step changes").
- **CreatureEvents in the spells' interface**: see "Extended opcode dispatch".
- **Loot Buyer at Nightwrack**: see "Item prices".

### Monsters are not immune to fire (C7, 2026-10-20)

Pyre Oath (Righteous Fire style) burns its owner every second; against a fire-immune monster the burn was paid for
nothing. Owner decision: every monster that was immune to fire has a fire resistance of `FIRE_RESIST_PERCENT = 30` in
`tools/monster_fire_resist.py` (the engine's element percent: 30% of the fire damage is stopped, the monster takes 70%).
One constant; change it there only. "Immune" is `<immunity fire="1"/>`, `firePercent` 100+, Lua `{type = "fire"}` and
Lua `COMBAT_FIREDAMAGE` percent 100+; a monster with its own higher fire row keeps it. Our monsters: `tune_monsters.py`
(`--check` in `check_content.py`) changed 2 files (`monsters/chaos/plant.xml`, `lua/chaos/overcharged_energy_elemental.lua`).
The 14 pets (`monsters/chaos/pets`) are allies and never a target of the aura: they keep the immunity. The base server's
monsters (not in this repository): `patch_base_monsters.py` (step `basemonsters`) does the same, so the count there is printed at
install ("N file(s) changed"). Tests: `tests/monster_fire_resist_test.lua`, `tools/monster_fire_resist_test.py`.
Eight base spawn entries in fire lairs could not be placed at start any more: see "Spawns on fire fields".

## Monster lint (`tools/ci/check_content.py`, `tools/fix_monster_xml.py`, `tools/hash_base_monsters.py`)

`check_content.py` checks every Chaos monster against what the base loader reads and does (its docstring lists the
rules, each finding carries a code such as `[flag.tameable]`). Exceptions sit in its `ALLOW` table with a reason; an
entry that matches nothing fails, so the table cannot go stale. Rules that need data outside git run locally only:
`--base DATA_DIR` checks every loot and corpse id against that items.xml (and that a corpse is a container), `--pair
Tibia.dat` recounts the outfits and blank outfits of a pair against `PAIR_OUTFITS` / `PAIR_BLANK` (things_custom23:
2184 outfits, 687 blank). In CI the item rule covers our own ids (above 29926, `data/items/`).

**Base names.** `data/monster/base_monster_hashes.txt` holds the SHA-256 of every monster type of a fresh base server
(1487: `monsters.xml` and `Game.createMonsterType`). Rebuild it from an untouched base data folder with
`python3 -I tools/hash_base_monsters.py BASE_DATA_DIR` (`--check` compares). After the renames of
`base_monster_names.csv`, no Chaos monster may take a base name: `register_monsters.py` skips a name that is already
registered, and a base Lua type of the same name refills ours when the Lua monsters load (after the XML ones).

**Fixed 2026-10-13** (all through `fix_monster_xml.py`, idempotent, except the pet):
- the pet Bog Frog never loaded: the base has its own "Bog Frog", so `register_monsters.py` skipped our file and
  `pets.lua` summoned the base frog (attackable, its own look). The pet type is now "Pet Bog Frog" (`pets_config.lua`
  `monster`); the pet still shows "Bog Frog" or its given name;
- 20 summonable / convinceable flags on 13 imported monsters (Thal, Vyrm, Silicron, Facetis, ... with manacost 0):
  the summon spell and the convince rune could hand a player one of them; all off;
- 139 donor event names on 54 monsters (registered nowhere: one console warning per spawn) removed;
- Saga had loot but no corpse (the loot was lost): corpse 6068, the import fallback;
- Jungle Warrior's energy beam had min 9000 / max -15000 (a lost minus: some rolls healed the player): min -9000;
- Bone Lancer's area effect `hitarea` is no base name (nothing showed): `blackspark`, the hit-area effect;
- load warnings with the same behaviour: 14 spells without chance (now 100), 13 targetdistance 0 (now 1), 3 heals
  with min above max, a voices chance 200, a speedchange -500000 (now -1000), pushable next to canpushcreatures;
- 17 wrong articles in nameDescription; 240 donor `<monster>` attributes and 83 `<strategy>` / `<levelconfig>` lines
  the base never reads.

**Kept on purpose (in `ALLOW`):** the five Lua imports (butterflies, Scar Tribe Warrior, Overcharged Energy
Elemental) replace base types of the same name; the three goblins flee from the first hit.

**Follow-up 2026-10-13 (owner approval; `tools/tune_monsters.py`, idempotent, `--check` / `--table`).** Each change
is a row of its `TUNING` table; `check_content.py` fails on a file the tool would still change. Computed from the
spawned late-game set, not measured in game.
- Renamed: Wild Boar -> Gloomtusk Boar, Giant Hornet -> Blightwing Hornet (files `wildwood/gloomtusk_boar.xml`,
  `wildwood/blightwing_hornet.xml`; `invasion_config.lua`; the corpses "dead gloomtusk boar", "dead blightwing
  hornet" and the outfit names in `art_import/things.csv`, `art_items.csv`, `art_outfits.csv`; the wiki). The base
  Lua types keep their names, and so do `bounty_pool.lua`, `bestiary_spawns.lua` and `chaos_poi.lua`, which name
  the base hornet of the base map (level 192).
- Vharok: the dead `bleed="900"` is gone from its melee (its Hemorrhage stays the bleed). Vorathrax and Gloomfire:
  the 2,005,500 earth hit is now 26,000-32,000 and 36,000-42,000, the range of each one's own ranged fire.
- Lady bug keeps its element table: it is immune to earth, which beats the +20 of its peers.

|---|---|---|
| Ormathulak (910M health) | 500,000,000 exp | 22,000,000 |
| Talath (510M, armor 200, heals 200k) | 600,000,000 | 21,000,000 |

## Solo kill times (computed, not measured in game)

Kill time = boss health / (damage per second - the boss's heals per second). Damage: the measured one-target damage
of the classes (data/spells/README.md "Classes with the passive trees", C4 harness): median 913 at level 300 and 2,600
at level 1000, interpolated in between (825: 2,180) and scaled by the level below 300 (a rough guess: 100 -> 304).
The weakest class at level 1000 deals about 1,950, the best 4,570. Armor is left out (the C4 dummies have none), and
so are the monster tiers, the trash before a boss and moving out of telegraphs except where a model counts uptime.

**The generated dungeons (the Hollow Vault and the deep dungeons 6-9): runs of 10-15 minutes** (owner, 2026-10-14; since

the curves), so it can be recomputed after any change of monsters, counts or damage (`tests/areagen_test.lua` checks
every dungeon against it):
- damage `D.dps(L)`: 913 at level 300, 2,600 at 1000, the same slope (2.41 a level) above; L = the dungeon's level + 25;
- a monster's health at level L: its file's health x (1 + 0.0074 L) (the engine's level bonus);
- trash(d) = the monsters to the boss gate (85%) x health / dps x `trashHealth[d]` / 2.3 (packs: several at once);
- boss(d) = the boss's health (file x (1 + 0.0074 boss level) x `healthMult`) x `bossHealth[d]` / dps; the mechanics
  keep this time (boss_mechanics G.balance, "Boss mechanics");
- run(d) = trash(d) + boss(d) + 90 s of walking.
Curves: `bossHealth` 100 / 125 / 150 / 175 / 200 / 225%, `trashHealth` 100 / 105 / 110 / 115 / 120 / 125% (the
difficulty table's 100-1300% would make difficulty 6 hours long; the difficulty's damage, experience, gold and loot stay
the table's). Sizing: `healthMult` = 150 s x dps / (file health x (1 + 0.0074 boss level)): 2.88 / 2.91 / 2.88 / 2.83 /

## Boss mechanics (`boss_mechanics.lua`, `boss_mechanics_core.lua`, `boss_mechanics_config.lua`, client `game_monsterbar`)

One tested system gives the key bosses fight mechanics: marked area attacks you dodge by walking, adds phases, soft
enrage, stacking debuffs, soak circles, channels stopped by killing a totem and room-wide blasts you hide from behind a
pillar. The pure logic is `boss_mechanics_core.lua` (shapes, timing, fairness, the per-fight state machine, balance);
every number is `boss_mechanics_config.lua`, one profile per boss; `boss_mechanics.lua` drives the engine.
`tests/boss_mechanics_test.lua` runs all three (6,288 checks in both interpreters). No opcode, storage or table of its
own: the cast bar rides on the monster bar's opcode 125 (`ChaosOpcodes.monsterbar`) as the new action `mech`
(server -> client), next to `info` (monster_tiers.lua, worldboss.lua). raid.lua sends the same action.

**Who gets it.** `ChaosBossMech.attach(monster, key, opts)` from the systems that know their arena: `worldboss.lua` (the
31 x 31 floor, its four pillars count as cover), `uber.lua` and `guildboss.lua` (the arena floor; the hits go through
their own `shareHit`, so the lethal-hit catch still works), `rift.lua` (the Omen guardians by name, every other guardian
the light profile `rift_guardian` with the key's tier; the chamber of radius 9 round the boss spawn). Every other monster
whose shown name has a profile (Vault Keeper Ossrim, the bosses of the deep dungeons 6-9, the Emberdeep Maw, the Ossuary Warden, Cinderwing, the dormant
donor bosses) is attached at its first think after the spawn (an `onSpawn` EventCallback registers a think event, as
monster_tiers.lua does), with a box of radius 8 round it as the arena (walkable tiles only). The Ascended bosses, the
Cinderheart and the guild boss keep their own telegraphs, hazards, adds and enrage (`ownTelegraphs`); the profile adds
the mechanics below on top, and while one of those runs (`ChaosBossMech.busy`) they draw no telegraph of their own.

**Dungeon difficulty does not scale the mechanics (beta 2026-10-24).** The mechanics' hits are a share of the victim's
max health (telegraph `share`, soak `total` / `missShare`, channel and blast `share`), so they are already tuned to the
player. `dungeons.lua` multiplies the damage of a run's monsters by the difficulty (130% to 600%) and the party factor,
and used to do it to these hits too: a lone soaker in the Last Hymn circle (60%) died at difficulty 3 and up. Now
`ChaosBossMech.scriptedHit(attacker)` is true while the mechanic deals its hit and `scaleHit` leaves it unchanged; the
boss's ordinary attacks are still scaled. The soak circle (radius from the profile, Euclidean distance from the centre
tile, so a radius 2 circle is 13 tiles) is one tile list: the green tiles drawn, the tiles that count and the tiles
checked at the hit are the same set, on the same floor (`f.soakCircle`).

**The kit** (all per profile, all in the core):
- Telegraphs: circle, cone, line (beam), ring (donut), cross, puddles (on players and at random), follow (a circle that
  tracks the target for 1.5 s, then locks; the last 1.5 s+ count as the warning), plus uber's marks, half, lines, eye. A
  danger mark (`warning_zone`) pulses on every tile of the shape every 600 ms from the cast until the hit, the last
  pulse is the filling mark (`warning_fill`), the round ones also get the big warning circle of pair 24
  (`ChaosBigFx.telegraph`, effects 635-637). The hit effect is a big or pack effect of the boss's element (pair 24,
  effects 628-655, `chaos_big_fx_ids.lua`, `chaos_pack_fx_ids.lua`) with a stock effect as fallback. The hit lands only on
  the tiles still marked; it costs a share of the victim's max health (`Chaos.percentBase`).
- Adds phases at a health threshold, each once: `immune` (no damage while they live), `shield` (less damage), `empower`
  (+damage per living add), `heal` (a share of max health per add every 5 s). The adds and totems are the raid's
  immobile Hex Effigy renamed (Infernal Wardstone, Plague Heart, Void Anchor, ...) with the profile's health.
- Timed: `channel` (a cast bar of 8-10 s and a totem; kill it and the cast is interrupted, else a hit on everyone),
  `soak` (a green circle: the players inside split the total; nobody inside, everyone takes the miss share; `min`
  counts a lone soaker as several), `los` (pillars rise round the boss; after 3.5 s a blast hits everyone it can see, by
  a Bresenham line from the boss; the pillars go away after). One at a time; no telegraph meanwhile.
- Soft enrage (+x% a minute after a time) and stacking debuffs (each boss hit on a player adds a stack, +x% damage taken
  from that boss, one falls off every 6 s).
- Warnings: an orange yell over the boss and the same line in the console of everyone in the fight ("Kaelgor is shielded
  by 3 Infernal Wardstones! Break them!"), and the cast bar.

**Fairness** (enforced in the core, checked by the grid simulation of the test):
- The warning is 3.0 s at difficulty 0 down to 1.5 s at difficulty 1, never under 1.5 s (`G.warnMs`); the profiles sit
  at 2.4-3.0 s (rift guardians 3.0 s at tier 1, 2.6 s at tier 15). Enraged adds 0.3 difficulty. The Ascended and guild
  boss telegraphs now warn 2.5 s (were 2.0 s), enraged 1.5 s (were 1.0 / 1.2 s); the raid's enraged warning is held at
  1.5 s (was 2.2 x 0.6 = 1.32 s).
- Walking follows the player rules of patch 0018 (`data/lib/chaos_speed.lua`: 10 ms rounding, diagonal 7/5): the
  reference is a player of the content's level (vocation base 220, no haste, normal ground), 0.5 s to react.
- Every telegraph is made fair before it is drawn (`G.makeFair`): a player with no unmarked tile in walking reach gets a
  pocket (a tile and its four neighbours) cut out of the shape at a reachable tile, as far from the boss as the walk
  allows. With telegraphs still pending, the union counts and the budget is the earliest pending hit. The telegraph
  cadence is never shorter than the warning + 1.5 s, so the shared engine never overlaps two by itself.
- Shapes grow with the boss: size 4 (the Omen guardians, the Ascended, the Cinderheart, the 4 x 4 rift guardians) adds
  1 sqm to radii and lengths and measures from the whole 4 x 4 body.
- A big boss's target can stand on the boss's body tiles (the engine blocks only the anchor tile: a melee target north or
  west of it is inside the 4 x 4 footprint). Cones and lines aimed at such a target go from the body's centre and start
  at the target's row (`G.aimFrom`); before, they started past the whole body and missed the target (live test
  2026-10-14: Sangrith's Red Crescent marked 1 tile, the tank unmarked).
- Live test 2026-10-14 (two clients, levels 1000 and 300): Kaelgor and the Sangrith Omen guardian; the cast bar, the
  warning marks and big circles, hits only on players whose tile was marked (logged per hit), the Infernal Wardstones at
  55% (immune until the three died, then hurt again), no Lua error. The cast bar was off screen with no monster targeted
  (client fix, client/MANIFEST.md game_monsterbar). Not seen live: totems (channels), soaks, line of sight.
- Solo content (`ref.solo`) has no mechanic that needs two players: soaks count one soaker, a lone soaker takes at most
  60%; one player kills a totem in 60% of the channel; the adds of a solo phase die within 45 s.
- The test's grid simulation: four arenas (open 19 x 19, the world boss room with pillars, a round rift chamber, a
  9 x 21 hall), every telegraph of every profile at size 1 and its own size, 8 difficulties from 0 to 1.4, 1-8 players
  at random: 10,032 dodges, each bot walks its cheapest path (straight / diagonal costs) to a safe tile before the hit,
  and again 300 ms into its walk when a second telegraph lands on top; the slowest walk needed 980 ms. Every
  line-of-sight blast leaves a hidden tile in reach from every tile of a 19 x 19 room.

The raid bosses (Ashen Sepulchre) keep their own kit (sunder, cleave, sweep, soak, adds, marks, effigies, hex: "The Ashen
Sepulchre"); their telegraphs now pulse like the others (`G.pulses`, the filling mark in the last turn), send the cast
bar (Cleave / Sweep / Bone Bloom / Soak / Crushing Verdict) and never warn under 1.5 s. No new mechanic and no downtime
was added there, so the enrage times (9 / 10 / 11 / 11 / 16 min) and the 15-25% margin of `tests/raid_test.lua` stay.

**Kill times** ("Solo kill times": health / (damage x uptime - heal)). The mechanics cost time: moving out of the marks
(1.2 s per telegraph), the totems and adds (their health / damage), the hiding and soaking. To keep each fight's time,
the boss's health is multiplied at attach by the factor `G.balance` finds (`hpMult`, at least 0.6); for the solo Omen
and Ascended fights also at the weakest class's damage (`weakDps` 1,950), the lower factor wins. Group fights use the
"Solo kill times" group numbers (10 x 2,600 for world bosses, 20 x 2,600 for the donors, 5 x 1,400 at 75% for the guild
boss). The tests keep every final time within 5% above the old one and inside the limit:

**Client** (`game_monsterbar`, `monsterbarmech.lua` pure + `monsterbarmech_test.lua`, `monsterbarmech.otui`): a cast bar
under the monster bar (in its place when nothing is targeted): "Kaelgor: Meteor Rain 2.4s - move out", filling to the
hit; red = move out, purple = kill the totem, green = stand in the circle, blue = hide behind a pillar; an interrupted
channel turns grey. `previewMech({...})` shows it without a server.

**Checked.** The tests above, the existing suites of the systems it touches (uber, guildboss, raid, worldboss, rift,
big_fx) in both interpreters, and offline renders of the telegraphs from the core's real plans and the pair 24 strips in
git (Kaelgor's puddles and cone, Skaldra's ring and pillar blast, Nyxareth's cross in the world boss room; Thalcyra's
line, puddles and blast and Morvane's ring as 4 x 4 Omen guardians in a rift chamber). **Not checked:** a live server
and client (the machine had 3.6 GB free, under the 4 GB a test server needs); the `warning_zone` / `warning_fill`
strips are in the client pair only, so the renders draw a red tile in their place. The attach paths in worldboss.lua,
uber.lua, guildboss.lua and rift.lua are guarded (`ChaosBossMech` nil in their tests) and not exercised by those tests.

## World bosses (`worldboss.lua`, `data/monster/monsters/chaos/world_bosses/`)

**Pockets** ("Pocket bosses"): each world boss also has a private copy, open any time with daily charges, for 60% of the
experience and loot and a reduced share of the event reward. The event stays the full reward; a character it rewarded
waits an hour before the pocket of that boss opens for it (`W.deliver` is wrapped by `pocketboss.lua`).

**Limits** (`Chaos.worldBoss.limits`, "Instance limits"): the boss withdraws 45 minutes after it appears (unchanged); everyone inside now gets warnings at 5 min, 1 min and 10 s. One arena, at most 40 players; `/instances close worldboss event` is `/worldboss stop`.

A server-wide event: a portal opens next to every temple, players gather in a lobby, one of five world bosses appears in an
arena built at runtime, and everyone who took real part (damage, healing other players, tanking) is rewarded, not only the
corpse owner; the top 3 damage dealers, healers and tanks get extra rewards and a title. Settings: `Chaos.worldBoss` in
`chaos_constants.lua`. `tests/worldboss_test.lua` covers the layout, schedule, rotation, phases, role accounting, shares,
rewards and the whole event flow against a mocked engine (LuaJIT and Lua 5.3); the roles were tested in game (below).

**Install.** Copy the XMLs to `<server>/data/monster/monsters/chaos/world_bosses/` and register them:
`python3 -I server/tools/register_monsters.py data/monster/monsters.xml data/monster/monsters/chaos/world_bosses`.
The script itself loads with the rest of `data/scripts/chaos/`. Without the XMLs `/worldboss start` refuses with "not loaded".

**The base server's island bosses stay** (`data/scripts/customs/worldbosses/world_boss_timer.lua`, not in this repository;
compared with the Chaos event, decision recorded in ROADMAP.md). They are other content and do not clash: nine open-world
bosses (Lua monsters in `data/monster/lua/The_isles/worldbosses/`) that each appear once a week on their own island of the
base map (Sunday 00:00, Monday 16:00, Saturday 12:00, otherwise 20:00 server time) with a broadcast ("X has spawned on Y
Island."), a map mark and a sound; they never leave, their reward is their own loot. The Chaos world bosses run every 6
hours (03:00, 09:00, 15:00, 21:00) in the arena at x 5000 built at runtime, behind portals, with shared rewards, titles
and the weekly boards. No time slot is shared (closest: an island boss at 20:00 and the Chaos event at 21:00), and no
position, monster, storage, opcode, reward or board overlaps; island boss kills count for none of the Chaos boards, roles,
achievements or boss points. The base script defines the globals `spawnBoss` and `notifyPlayers`: Chaos scripts must not
define globals with those names (every current use is local). To turn the island bosses off, remove that file from the
server's data; nothing in Chaos depends on it.

### The bosses

All five have `<flag isboss="1"/>` (monster_tiers.lua also lists them in `cfg.bosses` as a fallback), so the client gets
the `boss` tier and draws them bigger; worldboss.lua also pushes the tier to players in the arena every 3 s. They are in
monster_tiers' `cfg.skip`: no random modifiers (Regenerating, Juggernaut or Explosive would wreck a tuned fight).

Every boss: 55-75 crystal coins, 12-15 Orbs of Upheaval, 5-7 Orbs of Fate (80-90%), 4-6% per set item; immune to paralyze,
invisibility, outfit and drunk. Adds get the configured health (100k-200k) so they matter at level 1000. Look types are
outfits other monsters already use (1472 needs the merged dat, see `data/monster/CUSTOM_MONSTERS.md`); corpses are stock
containers (slain demon, dead frost dragon, dead defiler, dead juggernaut).

**Why these numbers.** Measured single-target damage per second: level 300 about 400-700, level 1000 with the best gear
about 1300-3200. With ~70% uptime (movement, deaths, healers who do not attack):

| Group | Raw DPS | Effective | Nyxareth 15M | Skaldra 16M | Kaelgor 18M | Rotmother 22M | Vharok 24M |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20 x level 1000 | ~45k | ~31k | ~8 min | ~9 min | ~10 min | ~13 min | ~15 min |
| 15 x level ~700 | ~22k | ~16k | ~17 min | ~18 min | ~20 min | ~27 min | ~32 min |
| 10 x level 300 | ~5.5k | ~3.9k | > 60 min: fails the 45-minute limit |

(Self-healing is included: 1.2-3.2k health per second on average from the XML heals, Vharok up to ~3.5k more while
enraged.) Resistances shift this per vocation (Vharok resists 40% physical). The 5-target numbers (2400-6300 at level 1000)
only count against adds. Incoming damage: single hits 2.5-8k (the 8k rift beam and 7.5k cleave are the spikes), DoTs of
4-10k total over ~20-40 s, so a 9k-health level 1000 character survives one big hit and a 27k tank survives several,
with a healer. Level 300 characters (3-5k health) can be one-shot by the spikes; they should stay at range.

### Arena (built in code)

`Game.createTile` + ground/wall items, like the Infinity Tower; nothing is saved to the map. Coordinates (z 7):
- Arena x 5000-5032, y 5000-5032 (31 x 31 inside walls), black marble floor, stone walls, four stone pillars as cover at
  the centre +-7, coal basins in the corners. Boss spawn: centre 5016, 5016. Players arrive at 5016, 5029; the forcefield
  at 5016, 5031 goes back to the lobby.
- Lobby x 5009-5023, y 5040-5048 (13 x 7 inside), seven empty rows south of the arena so the boss can never see or reach it.
  Arrival 5016, 5046; forcefield to the arena at 5016, 5041; forcefields home (own temple) at 5010, 5044 and 5022, 5044.
- Free area: the map file was scanned for tile areas (OTBM tile-area nodes): the nearest content is around x 1024-2047,
  y 3072-4095; nothing exists within x/y 4500-5600. Other runtime areas: Infinity Tower x 2000-2660, y 2000-2020; the
  balance test harness 1490-1510. Before building, every tile of the footprint is checked: a tile that already exists and
  is not ours (other ground or a house) stops the build ("arena not built: tile x,y,z already exists").
- The lobby is protected by script (no combat against players in it); the engine has no Lua call to give a dynamic tile the
  protection-zone flag. PvP is blocked in lobby and arena (`allowPvp = false`). Deaths in the arena are normal deaths.
- Forcefields are item 1387 (magic forcefield, type teleport) **without destination** and with action ids 47201-47204;
  MoveEvents do the moving, so monsters that step on them stay put and the entry rules are checked.

### The event

- **Schedule:** every `intervalHours` (6) at full hours offset by `offsetHours` (3): 03:00, 09:00, 15:00, 21:00 server time,
  with broadcasts 10, 5 and 1 minute before. A GlobalEvent checks every 30 s. `events_schedule.lua` was not reused: it
  handles whole-day bonus events for the calendar, not timed spawns. `enabled = false` turns the schedule off.
- **Start** (`/worldboss start [name|number|random]`, staff only; no argument = the configured mode): the arena is built,
  a portal appears next to every distinct temple of `Game.getTowns()` (first free tile of `portalOffsets`: walkable, not a
  house, no other teleport; or exactly at `portalPositions`), broadcast + toast (game_chaosnotify `gmBroadcast`, no client
  change). Entry: level 300+, at most 40 players inside. The boss appears after 120 s; portals stay 30 minutes.
- **Boss choice:** `mode = "rotation"` (next one each time; the last index is a global storage, in memory) or `"random"`
  (never the same twice in a row).
- **End:** the boss dies (victory, rewards, broadcast with the top 3 and the time), or 45 minutes pass (it withdraws), or
  `/worldboss stop`. Town portals and adds disappear at once; after 90 s (10 s on stop) everybody still inside goes to their
  temple and the arena is cleaned (monsters, corpses, loose items). Logging in inside the arena when no event runs sends you
  to the temple.
- Adventure > Events (everyone): next start and boss, or the running fight (health %, minutes left). `/worldboss arena` (staff):
  builds the arena if needed and takes you to the lobby, to look at it without an event.

### Rewards

- The corpse works as for any monster: the engine's loot goes to the top damage dealer (corpse owner), plus the Chaos loot
  layer with the `boss` tier (extra rolls, gear rarity floor 6, currency, and the boss-only uniques of
  `chaos_unique_items.lua`, which now list the five world bosses).
- **Participation reward** for every player whose contribution score (see "Roles") reached `minScorePercent` (0.25%) of
  the boss max health (~40-60k, about 1.5 minutes of a level 300 hitting it, or as much healing, or twice as much tanking;
  the anti-AFK rule). share = own score / score of all eligible players. Each gets: 500k gold + share x 10M gold into the
  bank, 3 Orbs of Upheaval + 1 Orb of Fate + share x (60 Orbs of Upheaval, 25 Orbs of Fate), a 15% + share x 30% chance of one piece of
  the boss's set (rarity 6-9 via `Game.createItemWithRarity`) and a 0.5% + share x 3% chance of one of the boss-only
  uniques. Items that do not fit go to the inbox. Players offline at the kill get it at their next login (kept in memory
  until a restart).
- **Top 3 of each category** (`reward.podium`: damage, healing, tanking; eligible players only, one player can place in
  several): 1st 5 Orbs of Fate + 50 crystal coins, 2nd 3 + 30, 3rd 2 + 20 (the old top-3 damage bonus, now per category),
  an extra unique roll of 3% / 2% / 1% (one unique at most per player) and the category's title for 7 days on the name
  plate: **Bossbreaker** (damage), **Lifewarden** (healing), **Bulwark** (tanking). "Bossbane" stays the weekly World
  Boss board title, so the damage role got its own name. Ties: who reached the value first places higher, then the lower
  id; a value under `placeMinPercent` (0.1% of the boss max health) does not place. The titles are a `ChaosTitles`
  source "worldboss" (titles.lua; registered when the registry is loaded); the expiry is a player storage
  (7100930-7100932, `roles.titleStorage`), so it survives logout and restarts. The victory broadcast lists the three
  top 3 lists ("Top damage: A 1.2M, B 800k, C 50k. Top healing: ... Top tanking: ..."); the client toast has room for
  two lines, so each category gets its own toast ("World boss slain! Top healing: ...").
- **Multi-client:** characters with another character online from their IP may enter and fight (they already cannot attack
  players, and blocking entry would split friends sharing a connection), but get no participation reward (`mcReward = false`)
  and are told so at entry and at the end. A character counts if it was multi-clienting at entry or at any 3-second check
  while inside. Corpse loot is not affected (it follows the engine's damage rules).

### Roles: damage, healing, tanking (`Chaos.worldBoss.roles`)

Tracked per character (GUID) while the boss is alive (`state.stats`); a death keeps what was earned.
- **Damage:** as before, a healthchange event on the boss (summons count for their master, healing does not, overkill is
  clamped to the health left).
- **Healing:** a healthchange event registered on every player inside the arena (at the arena forcefield and every 3 s
  check). For healing the engine runs it before the heal with the healer as `attacker`, so the credit is the effective
  part: capped at the target's missing health, and at the boss damage the target took and was not healed for yet (the
  "debt": every heal from anyone, self-heals included, pays it off), so only healing of boss damage counts and nobody
  farms by healing damage from elsewhere. Healer and target must both be in the arena. **Self-healing does not count**
  (`selfHealWeight = 0`): what a tank survives is already its tanking credit. Attributed (engine source; the spells also in
  game): instant spells on others (Kindred Mend `saen kin`, Circle of Mending `saen gal vas kal`, the Chaos class heals
  that use `doTargetCombat`/combat objects such as the Templar and keystone heal pulses), healing runes used on someone
  (Grand Mending Rune) and potions used on someone (`potions.lua` calls `doTargetCombat(player, target, ...)`). Not
  attributed: `Chaos.heal` / `Creature:addHealth` (no origin and no attacker: the engine skips the healthchange event),
  health regeneration and food, life leech (no origin), and heals cast by summons only count when the summon has a player
  master. Mana restored is not healing.
- **Tanking:** damage from the boss or one of its adds (by creature id, conditions included: the engine passes the
  condition's owner) that the player survived: a hit that kills counts nothing, each hit is capped at `tankHitCap` (8000,
  the biggest designed boss hit), a hit from a boss or add that was not targeting the player (area splash) counts
  `offTargetWeight` (half), and it only counts while the player is active: attacked the boss or an add (EventCallback
  onTargetCombat) or healed someone within `activeSeconds` (30). So an AFK character parked in the boss's area earns
  nothing. Damage taken into a mana shield is not counted (only health).
- **Contribution score** = damage + healing x `healWeight` (1.0) + tanking x `tankWeight` (0.5; tanking overlaps with the
  healing that undoes it). Sizing: a level 1000 tank in front of the boss survives ~2-3k damage per second (~1.5M in a
  10-minute kill, score ~0.75M plus its own damage), a dedicated healer heals ~1-2k per second (~0.6-1.2M), a damage
  dealer does ~1.2M: the three roles end up in the same range of shares.
- **Leaderboards:** the World Boss board still records damage (and now counts a kill for every rewarded player, healers
  included; rows with 0 damage are not ranked). Two weekly boards were added to `leaderboard_config.lua` (one board = one
  value in this model, so a separate board per role fits it better than extending World Boss): **Boss Healer** (healing
  credit, title Lifebinder) and **Boss Tank** (tanking credit, title Ironwall), keys in `roles.boards`. Staff characters
  are left out of every board as before.
- **Achievements** (`achievements_data.lua`, fed from `distribute` via `ChaosAchievements.progress`, guarded): Lifeline
  (most healing at a kill, title), Immovable (most tanking at a kill, title), Pillar of the Raid (top 3 healing or tanking
  at 5 kills, 5 Orbs of Upheaval + 2 Orbs of Fate). `achievements.lua` still wraps `computeRewards` with the same signature; a share's
  `rank` is still the damage place, so "Lion's Share" (wb_top) keeps meaning the most damage.

**Tested in game** (test server with a cropped map, Kaelgor at 150k health and 1/8 damage in a test copy, gather 20 s,
`mcReward = true` because both clients share 127.0.0.1): a level 574 Deadeye tanked and attacked, a gamemaster healed him
with Kindred Mend and Circle of Mending (the driver also used a Grand Mending Rune and a health potion on him; their
share of the credit was not isolated), and both hit the boss. Live
stats during the fight (`state.stats`) grew for tanking and healing; the tank died twice (deaths counted, credit kept,
nothing earned while away) and came back. Result: "Top damage: Tester 15k, Duelist 12k. Top healing: Duelist 12k. Top
tanking: Tester 50k." in the broadcast; the reward message (61.6% of the contribution, 1st in damage and tanking, the
item counts match the formula), "You earned the title Bossbreaker / Bulwark for 7 days", both titles in the Achievements window and on
the name plate, the gamemaster's Lifewarden; World Boss and Boss Tank board rows (the gamemaster's healing is left out
of Boss Healer as staff, as for every board); a second kill showed the three per-category toasts.

### Not verified
`Game.getTowns()` temple spots on the real map (the test map is cropped: no portal spot, players were moved onto the
arena forcefield), the inbox path of the reward, and the actual fight balance at full health and damage. Monster damage
may be scaled by the server's own monster level system.

## Bounty board (`bounty.lua`, `bounty_core.lua`, `bounty_config.lua`, `bounty_pool.lua`, `tools/gen_bounty_pool.py`)

Daily rotating "kill X" contracts that pay gold and orbs (roadmap item 10). Client: `client/overlay/modules/game_bounty`
(Adventure > Bounty Board in the top menu), extended opcode 223, storage `7100300` (range 7100300-7100309),
table `chaos_bounty` (`sql/chaos.sql`). It is separate from the base server's task system (`scripts/customs/tasks`,
opcode 92, storages 187613+): no shared storage, opcode or event; its kills count for both.

- **The roll.** Every day at `rollHour` (06:00 server time) the board rolls, the same for everyone. It is seeded from the
  date with its own generator (`ChaosBounty.rng`, Park-Miller), so a restart gives the same board; it changes only when
  the config or the pool changes. Six level bands (8-49, 50-149, 150-299, 300-499, 500-799, 800+), each with 4
  contracts: two **hunts** (kill N of a monster), one **elite** (kill N monsters of a type that are at least magic, or
  at least rare, tier: `monster_tiers.lua`; the tier of a dead monster is read from `ChaosTierDead`/`ChaosTierOf`) and
  one **boss** (one kill of a boss that spawns on the map; a hunt when no boss fits the band). A player sees the band of
  their level and the bands next to it.
- **Monster pool.** `bounty_pool.lua` is generated by `python3 -I server/tools/gen_bounty_pool.py <server>/data` from
  the spawn file of the loaded map (`world/<mapName>-spawn.xml`, mapName from `config.lua`) and the monster
  definitions (`monster/monsters.xml` + XML files, and the Lua monsters under `monster/`). Only monsters that spawn
  are in it: hunts need at least 6 spawn entries (elites 20), bosses (boss/rewardboss flag) any. Each monster gets an
  estimated hunting level: the middle of `<level min max>` for the level-scaled monsters, otherwise 1.6 x sqrt(exp),
  raised by health for monsters much tougher than their experience. A band picks monsters in its `pick` window.
  **Rerun the generator after changing spawns (for example after `tools/late_game.py`) or monster experience/health**;
  it is idempotent and `--csv FILE` lists every spawned monster with the reason it was taken or left out. At the first
  roll the script drops pool monsters this server does not know (logged as `[ChaosBounty] N pool monster(s) ...`).
  The pool in the repo was generated from the test server's map with the late-game spawns: 708 hunt monsters, 30 bosses.
- **Accepting and progress.** Up to 3 contracts at once (`maxActive`); finished ones free the slot but cannot be taken
  again that day; Abandon drops one (progress lost). A kill counts for the players who made it (last hit and most damage,
  a summon's kill for its master) and for their party members within 30 tiles on the same floor (`partyRange`); each
  player once per kill. A party member whose level is below the contract band's min level gets no credit for the others'
  kills, only for its own (`B.partyCounts`, 2026-10-22: a low character cannot finish a higher band's contract, and
  take its experience, standing next to a strong one). Progress is saved per kill; messages at 25/50/75% and a toast (game_chaosnotify, action
  `bounty` on opcode 79) at 50% and on completion. Contracts expire at the next roll: unfinished rows of past days are
  deleted at login.
- **Rewards** (paid at once on completion; gold to the bank, orbs to the backpack or the inbox when it is full):

  | Band | Hunt | Elite / Boss (x1.5, Orbs of Fate rounded up) | Weekly chest |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 8-49 | 10k gold, 1 Chaos | 15k, 1 Chaos | 5 Chaos, 1 Divine |
  | 50-149 | 50k, 2 Chaos | 75k, 3 Chaos | 6 Chaos, 1 Divine |
  | 150-299 | 150k, 3 Chaos | 225k, 4 Chaos | 8 Chaos, 2 Divine |
  | 300-499 | 400k, 4 Chaos | 600k, 6 Chaos | 10 Chaos, 2 Divine |
  | 500-799 | 1M, 5 Chaos, 1 Divine | 1.5M, 7 Chaos, 2 Divine | 12 Chaos, 3 Divine |
  | 800+ | 2M, 6 Chaos, 2 Divine | 3M, 9 Chaos, 3 Divine | 15 Chaos, 4 Divine |

  **Experience** (2026-10-22, beta "as bounties dão muito pouca xp"; O105). It was 3% (hunt) or 4% (elite, boss) of one
  level, paid with `Player:addExperience`, which adds the amount as it is: no stage, no bonus. With the stages
  (x10 to x50 below level 100) that was 0.01-1.2% of what the contract's own kills gave (level 8, 90 Gazers: 87
  experience, the kills 111k). Now (`bounty_core.lua` `B.expReward`, `bounty_config.lua` `expShare` / `expFloor` /
  `expCap` / `tierXp` / `eliteSearch`):
  - kills = count x one kill's base experience x the stage of the player's level (`Game.getExperienceStage`, so an
    admin `xp-rate` x N scales it too). One kill's base is what the engine gives (`B.monsterKillBase`): the pool
    experience x the monster level factor x0.03 L of level-scaled monsters (when above 1; base `player.lua`, checked on
    the test server, "Late game") x the monster's pace experience curve (bosses are never paced). Elite: each counted
    kill x its tier's experience (magic 2, rare 4, read from `ChaosTiers`) plus `eliteSearch - 1` kills of the type made
    while looking for the tier (12 magic, 50 rare, from the spawn chances). No bonus is counted (potion, stamina, world,
    multikill, passive tree ...);
  - reward = `expShare` percent of it (hunt 40, elite 40, boss 100), at least `expFloor` (hunt 10, elite 15, boss 50)
    and at most `expCap` (2000 = 20 levels) percent of the experience from level L to L+1, L = the player's level capped
    at the band's top;
  - an elite or boss contract pays at least the mean hunt reward of its band for the same player (`B.huntMean`: the
    hunts of today's board in that band, else the band's pool median at the middle kill count, `B.huntPoolMedian`),
    still at most the cap: a boss is one kill and never pays less than a hunt;
  - the board shows the exact amount for the player's current level and stage (`B.rewardFor`); completion pays what
    the board shows at that moment (a level gained during the contract counts), with `addExperience`, so the stage is
    already in the number and no bonus is added on top.
  Exploits: a low character on the band above gets only its own kills (party rule above) and at most 20 of its own
  levels; a high character on a band below gets a share of the weak kills at its own stage, floor and cap at the
  band's top; rerolls keep the band and type (a rerolled monster missing from the pool pays the floor); multi-client
  contracts still pay nothing; each contract once a day, at most 12 a day.
  Model (30 days of boards, `luajit` with the real pool and pace config, the release stages; "min" = minutes of
  hunting that contract's monster at the pace model's kills per hour, `tools/spawn_tuning.json` `paceKillsPerHour`, to
  earn the reward; median of the player's own band):

  | Level | Type | Old | Old / kills | Kills' experience | New (min-max) | New, levels | Min |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 8 | hunt / elite / boss | 87 / 116 / 116 | 0.08% / 0.1% / 3.9% | 111k / 112k / 3000 | 44k (2.6k-58k) / 52k / 38k | 15.3 / 17.8 / 13.0 | 2 / 2 / 0 |
  | 30 | hunt / elite / boss | 1308 / 1744 / 1744 | 0.24% / 0.31% / 11.6% | 556k / 561k / 15k | 222k (13k-872k) / 447k / 345k | 5.1 / 10.3 / 7.9 | 2 / 2 / 1 |
  | 100 | hunt / elite / boss | 15k / 20k / 20k | 0.09% / 0.22% / 33% | 16.3M / 9.1M / 61k | 6.5M (1.2M-9.9M) / 6.8M / 6.1M | 13.2 / 13.8 / 12.3 | 7 / 8 / 4 |
  | 250 | hunt / elite / boss | 93k / 125k / 125k | 0.18% / 0.54% / 32% | 51.7M / 22.9M / 390k | 20.7M (8.4M-55.4M) / 23.4M / 22.9M | 6.7 / 7.5 / 7.4 | 15 / 15 / 3 |
  | 400 | hunt / elite / boss | 239k / 319k / 319k | 0.19% / 0.53% / 51% | 126M / 60M / 627k | 50.6M (18M-113M) / 54.7M / 53.7M | 6.3 / 6.9 / 6.7 | 15 / 14 / 4 |
  | 650 | hunt / elite / boss | 633k / 844k / 844k | 0.62% / 1.65% / 47% | 102M / 51M / 1.8M | 40.9M (15.5M-422M) / 43.1M / 43.1M | 1.9 / 2.0 / 2.0 | 13 / 13 / 1 |
  | 900 | hunt / elite / boss | 1.21M / 1.62M / 1.62M | 0.03% / 0.05% / 116% | 4.78B / 3.17B / 1.4M | 809M (24.6M-809M) / 809M / 809M | 20 (cap) / 20 / 20 | 17 / 18 / 29 |

  The band above, for comparison: level 8 and 30 on band 2 hit the cap (58k, 872k: 20 levels, own kills only); 100 on
  band 3 9.9M (cap); 650 on band 6 422M (cap). A band below: 100 on band 1 200k (0.4 level), 400 on band 3 17.5M (2.2
  levels), 900 on band 5 31.8M (0.8 level). Until O108 the 800+ band's level-scaled monsters gave about 20x the experience of a
