  base monster of the same hunting level once the engine's x0.03 L was counted, so its contracts paid the cap (the 900
  row above). With the re-fitted `scaled` curve (see "Pack combat (pace)", Scaled experience re-fit) level 900 gets
  116M (2.9 levels) for a hunt, 113M elite, 111M boss (with the re-sized kill goals of O108; 303M, 292M,
  265M with the old goals), and no contract of 30 boards at the cap.
  **Weekly chest:** 4 completed contracts in one bounty week (Monday 06:00 to Monday 06:00) give a "bounty chest"
  (present box) with the orbs of the player's band, once per week (`weeklyNeed`, 7 until 2026-10-15: two short sessions
  a week earn it now).
- **Multi-client** (`Chaos.isMultiClient`): as at the world boss event, such characters may accept contracts and hunt,
  but a contract that got a kill (or was accepted) while multi-clienting is marked (`mc = 1`) and pays nothing
  (`mcReward = false`); it does not count for the weekly chest. The player is told at accept and at completion.
- **Tests:** `tests/bounty_test.lua` (seeded roll, bands, kill matching, party credit and its band rule, milestones,
  rewards: the experience share, stage, elite tiers and search, floor, cap, the level factor and the pace hook, the
  elite / boss hunt mean (board and pool median), every contract of 30 real boards between floor and cap and no elite
  or boss below its band's hunt mean; the accept rules and expiry).

Verified on the test server (level 1000 knight): open from the menu (Adventure > Bounty Board); accept; 50 hunt kills -> 2M gold
in the bank, 6 Orbs of Upheaval + 2 Orbs of Fate (to the inbox, backpack full), 1.52M experience (the old 3% rule); elite: normal kills do not count,
magic/rare/legendary do; boss kill; weekly chest with 15 Orbs of Upheaval + 4 Orbs of Fate; the 3-contract limit (also an accept sent
straight from the client is refused); the same board (same checksum) after a restart; progress kept across relog and
restart; next-day expiry (simulated by shifting the day function); a multi-client contract pays nothing. Not verified in
game: party credit with two real players (unit-tested only) and the real 06:00 roll (the roll is a once-a-minute check
of the day key).

**Rerolls** (2026-10-15, for the Candlemarks shop). `ChaosBounty.addRerolls(player, n)` adds charges (storage
`rerollStorage` 7102403). An accepted, unfinished contract then shows a Reroll button in the window (action `reroll
{key}`): the contract gets another monster of the same band, slot, type and elite tier, picked by the board's own rules
and count (`B.rerollContract`), never a monster of the band's board or of the player's other contracts; progress goes
back to 0, the row in `chaos_bounty` keeps its key with the new `monster` and `required`. The rewards stay the slot's.
Kills of the new monster count (`B.overrideOf`, `B.onKill`); the board's monster no longer counts for that player.
Tests: `tests/bounty_test.lua` (every contract of a board rerolled, the override, nothing else fits),
`tests/candlemarks_apis_test.lua`.

## Treasure goblins (`treasure_goblin.lua`, `treasure_goblin_core.lua`, `treasure_goblin_config.lua`)

A cowardly, very rare monster (`data/monster/monsters/chaos/treasure_goblin.xml`, lookType 297, the stock goblin
scavenger with its sack, drawn with the golden outfit shader 12). It never attacks. All numbers are in
`treasure_goblin_config.lua`. Install: copy the XML and register it (`register_monsters.py`, see
`data/monster/CUSTOM_MONSTERS.md`); the scripts load with the rest of `data/scripts/chaos/`.

- **Spawn.** Own `EventCallback.onSpawn` (index -10, so it runs before the monster tiers). Only a *natural* map respawn
  (not `startup`, not `artificial`) of an eligible monster rolls: 1 in `spawn.oneIn` (3000). Never for bosses
  (`isboss` or monster_tiers' boss list), summons, non-hostile critters, monsters under 40 max health, names in
  `skipNames`, protection zones and houses, the rectangles of `excludedAreas` (quest rooms), and, guarded, the world
  boss arena, rift and arena slots. Rifts, arenas, the siege, the tower and ambush copies are created by scripts
  (`Game.createMonster` = artificial), so they never roll. At most `maxAlive` (3) goblins on the server and one per
  64x64 cell per floor every 30 minutes. On a hit the replaced spawn is cancelled (its spawn block retries after its
  normal interval) and the goblin appears on that tile. The roll is multiplied by an event bonus `goblin`
  (`ChaosEvents.bonus("goblin")`) if the event calendar ever defines one.
- **Treasure Goblin Chance** (item modifier `goblinchance`, helmets and amulets / rings, "Treasure Goblin Chance +N%":
  tiers 10-15, 14-20, 18-27, 22-33, 28-40, weight 5, cap +100% per character). A respawn's roll becomes 1 in
  `oneIn / (1 + bonus)`: +100% = 1 in 1500. The bonus is the **highest** total among the players within `spoor.radius`
  (24) tiles on the same floor of the spawn point (they do not add up, so a group gains nothing from stacking). Natural
  respawns happen out of sight but within that radius, so the player hunting there counts. The roll is done in two
  stages (`G.rollWithSpoor`: a first roll with the maximum bonus, players looked up only on its hit, then kept with the
  exact share), so the common miss costs nothing. `maxAlive` 3 and the per-cell cooldown are unchanged. Event bonus
  multiplies on top. Staff: `/goblin dry <monster>, <n>` measures the odds, `/goblin roll <monster>, <n>` rolls for real.
- **Variants** (`cfg.variants`, weights 70 / 20 / 10, one monster XML each, stock look types, distinct outfit shader):
  Treasure Goblin (Hoarder, look 297, shader 12, the hoard below), **Gem Goblin** (look 296, shader 9), **Shard Goblin**
  (look 61, shader 10). Same behaviour, experience, leaderboard (all variants count for Goblin Slayer and the goblin
  achievements) and loot rays. The announce, escape and kill texts use the variant's name. `/goblin [hoarder|gem|shard]
  [level]` spawns one. Variant loot overrides parts of the shared table (`variants[i].loot`):
  - Gem Goblin: half the gold, no Orbs of Upheaval and Fate, 2-3 gems (+1 per 250 levels, max 5; type random, tier by
    `ChaosGems.levelWeights(level)`, 25% one tier better), 1 Orb of Sockets (+25% for a second), 1 gear item, unique
    roll x1, no hoard roll.
  - Shard Goblin: half the gold, 1-2 Orbs of Upheaval (+1 per 300 levels, max 4), (10 + level / 10) x 80-120% Rune Shards
    (item 32051, max 60), 1 random crafting orb (salvage orb weights), 1 gear item, unique roll x1.
  - Expected per goblin (level 100 / 300): Gem Goblin 2.5 / 3.5 gems and 1.25 Orbs of Sockets; Shard Goblin 20 / 40
    shards. Over all goblins (70/20/10): about 0.5 gems and 2 / 4 shards per goblin. 25 shards make an Orb of Upheaval at the
    bench, so a Shard Goblin is worth about a Hoarder's orbs without its gear; goblins stay rare (1 in 3000, at most 1 in
    1500 with the cap), so the effect on the economy is small.
  Not done: **Goblin's Purse** (one-use vault item). The rift room builder is bound to a rift run (key, slot, lives,
  rewards); a clean standalone vault would need its own slot builder, which is not small.
- **Area level and health.** The replaced monster's level (`getMonsterLevel`), else the average level of the players
  within 30 tiles, else its max health / 20. Health = 300 + 40 x level, at least 3x the replaced monster's health.
- **Announce.** Players who come within 10 tiles get "A Treasure Goblin appears!" (once each) plus a toast through
  `ChaosNotify.gmBroadcast` (game_chaosnotify); the goblin says "Ooh, shiny...". Natural respawns happen out of sight
  of players (the engine blocks a spawn with a player in view), so the announcement is made on discovery, not at spawn.
- **Behaviour.** Non-hostile, it idles or keeps ~4 tiles from players. The XML `runonhealth` is 100,000,000 and the
  script keeps the goblin's health above it (shown as 100%) until the first hit, which drops it to the real health:
  from then on the engine's flee logic runs it away from its target. The first hit also gives it the attacker's
  speed x 0.95 (min +80, max 1500), a taunt, and a blink every 2.5-4.5 s (70%): a teleport 3-5 tiles to the free,
  visible tile farthest from the attackers. Taunts on further hits (60%, 2.5 s cooldown). 30 s after the first hit (18 s before O182) it
  escapes: portal effect, "Ha ha!", a message to players within 10 tiles, removed with no corpse and no loot. Never
  hit for 30 minutes: it vanishes quietly. `/goblin [level]` (god accounts) spawns one in front of you.
- **Loot** (added to the corpse in the death event, so the stock loot message and autoloot see it; owner = most
  damage): gold worth (2000 + 400 x level) x 80-130% in crystal/platinum/gold coins; 2-4 Orbs of Upheaval + 1 per 150
  levels (max 10); an Orb of Fate at 25% x item find; 2-4 gear items from the replaced monster's loot table (fallback:
  a level-banded pool), each rolled as magic (50, rarity at least 2), rare (35, at least 3) or legendary (15, at least
  5) through `ChaosLoot.upgradeRarity` / `stockRarity` and `Game.createItemWithRarity`; uniques via
  `ChaosLoot.rollUniques` as a legendary kill of the replaced monster with 3x item find, and if none, a 3% "hoard" roll
  for any non boss-only unique up to the area level + 20. Experience: the replaced monster's experience x 3 (min 50,
  cap 60 x level), given directly (the XML experience is 0). The goblin has no tier, so the loot layer's own pass adds
  nothing for it.
- **Leaderboard.** Each kill counts on the weekly **Goblin Slayer** board (`ChaosLeaderboard.record("goblin", player,
  1, "add")`, see "Leaderboards").
- **Optional hook** (called guarded, nothing is created): `ChaosLootRays.beam(position, kind, player)` with kind
  "unique" / "legendary" / "rare" / "magic" once the loot rays module exists (rename the call if it lands with another
  name).
- Tests: `tests/treasure_goblin_test.lua` (eligibility and exclusions, the 1-in-N roll, cooldown, health, the escape and
  lifetime timers, blinks, loot scaling). Verified on the test server: render, announcement and toast, flee, blinks,
  taunts, escape, a kill's corpse (level 100: 43,680 gold, 3 Orbs of Upheaval, Legendary / Rare / Uncommon gear; a Dragon
  next to it: 33 gold, a crossbow, 3 dragon ham), the onSpawn replacement (driven by hand: the cropped test map has no
  natural spawns), experience 2,100 for a goblin that replaced a Dragon. Not verified: a real natural respawn, party
  loot, the loot ray and leaderboard hooks (their modules do not exist yet). Outfit shader 15 drew as stripes in the
  test client, so 12 is used.

## Invasions and world events (`invasion.lua`, `invasion_core.lua`, `invasion_config.lua`, `worldevents.lua`)

Server-wide events in the open world. Client: `game_invasion` (HUD and the upcoming events window, extended opcode
251), toasts through `game_chaosnotify` (action `invasion` on opcode 79). Every number is in `invasion_config.lua`
(loaded as `Chaos.invasionConfig`; plain data, so the merchant NPC reads it too). The pure logic (schedule, waves,
scaling, breach meter, shares, rewards, occupation, world event rotation, HUD message) is in `invasion_core.lua` and
tested by `tests/invasion_test.lua`. No database table, no storage: the state is in memory (a restart ends a running
invasion, the Victory buff and the world event; offline rewards wait in memory like the world boss's).

**Install.** The scripts load with the rest of `data/scripts/chaos/`. Copy `data/npc/Wandering Merchant.xml` and
`data/npc/scripts/wandering_merchant.lua` into the server's `data/npc/` (the ascension quest's installer step, which
`install_all.py` runs, copies every file of `server/data/npc/`). Without them the merchant event refuses to start
("the merchant NPC could not be placed") and the rotation picks another event next time.

### When

- **Schedule** (`schedule`): Wednesday 19:30 and Sunday 17:30, area and faction `"random"`. A random pick depends only
  on the start time, so the warnings, the calendar and the start name the same area and faction.
- **Random invasion** (`random`): on 35% of the days, at a random minute between 12:00 and 23:00, at least 90 minutes
  from a scheduled one and outside the world boss hours 15 and 21. It is decided by the date alone (a restart does not
  roll again) and kept secret until its first warning.
- **Warnings** 30, 10 and 1 minutes before (broadcast + toast). The login-screen calendar and Adventure > Events get one
  whole-day "Invasion" entry per scheduled weekday (added to `Chaos.events.list` at load, as the siege does).
  Adventure > Events shows the running invasion and the upcoming events (scheduled invasions, the running or next world
  event, the Victory buff) and opens the client window.
- A GlobalEvent checks every 15 s. A start while another invasion (or an occupation) runs is skipped and logged.

### The fight

- **Areas** (`areas`): a rectangle on one floor, a level, a target point and its name, optional `edges` the waves come
  from, `exclude` rectangles, a faction list, `kind` (town / hunt), `invasion = false` / `worldEvents = false`.
- **Factions** (`factions`): existing monster types with their hunting level (the `bounty_pool.lua` estimates) and a
  boss. Orc Warband (Orc .. Orc Warlord, boss "Warchief Grashnak" = Orc Warlord renamed), Undead Legion (Skeleton ..
  Blightwalker; Sanguidrake as "Sanguidrake the Unburied", The Ashen Count from area level 200), Infernal Host (Fire Devil ..
  Juggernaut; Morgashal, Moloveth from 300), Minotaur Horde (Minotaur .. Hornbrute; Ironbrow as "Ironbrow the Gorer").
  The renaming runs in an `onSpawn` callback, before the monster is placed, so clients see the new name.
- **Waves**: 5. Wave i has (10 + 4 (i - 1)) x player factor monsters (1 + 0.15 per extra player within 30 tiles of
  the area, at most x3): 10, 14, 18, 22, 26 for one player. Monsters come from the faction's roster within [0.35, 1.25] x
  the area level (at least 3 types), wave 1 from its lower part, the last wave from its upper part. Packs of 3-5 appear
  together at one point of the outer 3 rows of the area border. A spawn tile must have ground and be walkable, and
  must not be a protection zone, a house, a depot, a teleport or a floor change, an `exclude` rectangle or within 6
  tiles of a temple (`templeRadius`). Tiers per invader: magic 10% + 4% per wave, rare 2% + 2%, legendary 0% + 1%
  (`ChaosApplyTier`). The next wave comes when 25% of the current one is left or after 150 s.
- **Scaling** to the area level: ratio = area level / monster level; health x ratio, damage x ratio^0.4, experience x
  ratio^0.8, each clamped to [0.5, 10 / 2.5 / 6]. The damage multiplier is applied on the players' `healthchange`
  (like the tier multipliers), experience in an `onGainExperience` callback.
- **The push**: every 0.4 s each invader without a target takes a step to the target point (at its own speed). It
  uses `Creature:getPathTo` and falls back to greedy steps. The step is made with `Creature:move(tile, 0)`, so the
  engine's own rules apply: no monster enters a protection zone, a house or a blocked tile (`move(direction)` would
  ignore all of that). An invader with a player target fights (engine AI) and walks on afterwards.
- **Breach meter**: every second, + 0.25% per invader within 2 tiles of the target (the boss counts 4), at most
  1.5% per second; - 0.25% per second while none is there. 5 invaders at the gate take 80 s to break it. HUD
  broadcasts at 50% and 80%.
- **Boss**: in the last wave, the faction boss with the highest level not above the area level, legendary
  (modifiers and shader), health 2500 x area level x player factor (at least 40,000), damage scaled from its level
  (exponent 0.6, [0.3, 2.5]), experience x3.
- **HUD** (every 2 s to every player online from level 30): area and faction, the target, wave N of M, invaders left,
  the time left, "Horde slain" (killed of all planned), the breach meter (amber, orange from 50%, red from 80%), the
  boss's health, the top 3 contributors with their share, your rank, share and kills. Click it to fold it. It sits
  under the character plate (the rift HUD's spot) and moves right of the rift HUD while a rift runs.

- **The count** (`I.sweep` every second, `stragglers`; beta 2026-10-20: "10 left" after every invader in sight was
  slain, no victory, no reward; commit 88f7fd76 had only dropped the removed ones). An invader that no longer exists
  (removed by another script, a despawn) or that has a master now (a summon, a tamed or convinced monster) leaves the
  count and counts with the slain for "Horde slain". One that exists but cannot be reached is called back to a free
  tile 2-6 tiles from the target: on another floor, more than 8 tiles outside the area, or stuck (no target, no step)
  for 30 s with no player hit for 30 s; with no free tile it is removed and leaves the count. Occupiers that became
  summons leave the occupation count too.
- **Rout** (`rout.seconds`): once the warlord is slain the horde breaks ("the last N invaders flee in 90 seconds"); 90 s
  later the invaders still alive flee and the invasion is **won** with the full rewards. At the time limit a slain
  warlord is a victory too; with the warlord alive the time limit is still a defeat.

### Win

All waves and the boss slain within 20 minutes (or the warlord slain and the rout over, see above). Contribution = damage dealt to invaders + 0.6 x healing done to other
players inside the area (+10 tiles, effective healing only) + kills x 0.25 x the average invader health. A player needs
0.2% of the total invader health in contribution to be rewarded. Multi-client characters fight but get nothing
(`mcReward`). Rewards per player, by share of the total:
- gold to the bank: area level x (200 + 8000 x share), e.g. area 100 alone 820,000; ten equal defenders 100,000 each;
- 1 Orb of Upheaval + share x 20 Orbs of Upheaval and 6 Orbs of Fate; top 3 extra Orbs of Fate (3 / 2 / 1), the first an Orb of Grafting;
- a unique at (100 + share x 600) / 10000: the Chaos loot layer's own roll for the boss as a boss-tier kill (x20 item
  find), else any non boss-only unique up to the area level + 20 (season uniques respect the season);
- the weekly **Defender** board (`leaderboard_config.lua`, title "Defender of the Realm"): 10 points per invasion + the
  share in percent (`ChaosLeaderboard.record("defender", ...)`, so the season and guild wrappers count it too);
- achievements, guarded: `ChaosAchievements.progress` with `invasion_defended`, `invasion_top` (rank 1),
  `invasion_boss` (did damage to the boss), `invasion_kills` (kills), `invasion_fought` (a lost one),
  `invasion_liberated`. No entries in `achievements_data.lua` use them yet.
- **Victory buff**: +10% experience for 60 minutes. With `scope = "server"` it is an entry of `ChaosEvents.dynamic`, so
  `events_schedule.lua` applies it and Adventure > Events lists it; with `scope = "area"` the invasion's own experience callback
  applies it inside the area only.

### Loss and occupation

The breach meter at 100% or the time up: the area is **occupied** for 30 minutes. The survivors stop pushing and get
x1.5 health, and a garrison of 6 rare (70%) / legendary (30%) invaders appears around the target. The HUD shows
"<area> is occupied", the occupiers left and the time. All slain: the area is **liberated**, and everyone who fought
them gets 25% of the gold and orbs (no unique, no board). Time up: they withdraw (removed).

**NPC shop prices while occupied.** An NPC inside an occupied town (its rectangle and floor, the temple too) charges
x1.25 and pays x0.75 (`invasion_config.lua` `occupation.buyMult` / `sellMult`), rounded, never below 1 gold; a hunting
area has no shops. The trade code is the base server's NPC library, so install step `occupiedprices`
(`tools/patch_occupied_prices.py`, after `shopprices`) makes its ShopModule ask `ChaosInvasion.npcPrice(price, npc
position, kind)` in the trade window, the buy (and a part buy when the backpack is full), the sell and the talk trade
("buy 5 torches"). Without `invasion.lua`, or when the call fails, the stock price is used. Travel prices and the Chaos
NPCs with their own trade scripts are not changed. Tests: `tests/invasion_test.lua`, `tools/patch_occupied_prices_test.py`
(runs the patched Lua). `ChaosInvasion.isOccupied(areaKey)` stays for other hooks.

### World events (`worldevents.lua`)

One at a time, the first 20-60 minutes after a start, then every 2-4 hours. It is never in the area of a running
invasion, never during one, and never within 45 minutes of an invasion start. The kind is picked by weight (storm 40,
merchant 30, golden 30), never the same twice in a row. A broadcast + toast at the start and the end, and an entry in
Adventure > Events while it runs (`ChaosEvents.dynamic.worldEvent`).
- **Chaos Storm** (15 min): magic, rare and legendary spawn chances x3 in the area. `monster_tiers.lua` multiplies its
  spawn roll by `ChaosWorldEvents.tierMult(position)` (with the event days at most x3 together, `maxSpawnMult`).
  Lightning and clouds around the players inside every 2 s.
- **Wandering Merchant** (20 min, town areas only): the NPC "Wandering Merchant" at a random free tile of the area (or
  one of `merchantSpots`). Only the area is announced. Goods: Orb of Upheaval 40k, Orb of Fate 120k, Orb of Grafting 200k, Orb of
  Gilding 250k (60k before the owner's decision of 2026-10-14, "Item prices"), Orb of Unmaking 80k, Double Experience Potion 350k, supreme health potion 900 (no stock limit). An item with
  `seasonBlocked = true` (the Double Experience Potion: it does nothing for season characters) is refused to a character of a
  running season, in the trade window and by "buy <name>", with the merchant's `seasonBlockedText` and a cancel message;
  the NPC reads the realm itself (`chaos_season_players`, `season_core.lua`, the `/season` overrides). Tested in game: a
  season character was refused the potion both ways and bought an orb; a standard character bought the potion
  (`tests/wandering_merchant_test.lua` covers both paths and a migrated character).
- **Golden Hour** (30 min): +25% Chaos loot in the area. `loot_config.lua` `rateMult` multiplies by
  `ChaosWorldEvents.lootMult(ctx)`, as for the rifts (under the loot rate cap, "Chaos loot rate caps"); golden rings
  around the players inside.

### Commands

Adventure > Events (everyone). Staff (`/invasion`, group with access): `start <area|random> [faction]`, `stop`, `status`,
`schedule <minutes> [area] [faction]` (a one-off start in memory, with the warnings), `check [area]` (is the area usable
on this map: target tile, valid border tiles and why the others are refused), `areas`, `event
<storm|merchant|golden|stop> [area]` (the merchant's spot is in the staff reply), `wave` (the next wave now), `breach <n>`.

### Coordinates for the real map

The areas in `invasion_config.lua` were read from the real map file (town temples from its towns list, tiles of
the rectangles from the map nodes, blocking from `items.otb`). The test server runs a cropped map, so they were not
walked in game.
- `cinderhold` (level 80): x 32324-32414, y 32196-32286, z 7, target 32365,32245 (the first walkable tile outside the temple's
  protection zone; the whole rectangle is one connected walkable area reaching all four borders).
- `thornmere` (level 60): x 32315-32405, y 31737-31827, target 32355,31782.
- `cinderholdfields` (hunting, level 150): x 32290-32400, y 32292-32338, target 32345,32315 (south of Cinderhold).
- `thornmerewilds` (hunting, level 100): x 32300-32440, y 31685-31735, target 32370,31710 (north of Thornmere).
- `mirewake` (level 120) is **disabled**. The streets are bridges over water, and the largest connected walkable piece
  around the temple holds only ~370 tiles. Try it with `/invasion check mirewake` and set `edges` / `target` before enabling it.
On the live server run `/invasion check` once: it lists every area with its problems. Levels are guesses: set them to
the hunting level around each area.

### Test server

`data/scripts/zz_ztest_invasion.lua` (srv2 only, not in the repo) builds a 46 x 41 grass field with a wall and a gate
on the empty cropped map and adds it as area `testtown` (level 300) with `ChaosInvasion.addArea`.

**Verified in game** (srv2, client game_ui, level 1000 character):
- the 30, 10 and 1 minute toasts of a scheduled invasion, and its start; a start skipped while another one ran;
- `/invasion check | schedule | start | status | breach` and Adventure > Events with the upcoming events window;
- packs arriving at the north edge and walking around the wall to the gate; invaders at the gate raising the breach
  meter (50% / 80% broadcasts);
- the HUD updating (waves, left, time, horde slain, breach, top, you) and the boss (Warchief Grashnak) with its health
  in the HUD;
- a win in 3:07: Victory toast, the reward message (7,590,000 gold, 31 Chaos, 13 Divine, 1 Orb of Grafting, before the
  gold and orbs were lowered to the current numbers), the Victory buff in Adventure > Events, the Defender board entry (110
  points, 1 invasion) in the leaderboard window;
- two losses (breach) with the occupation: garrison, HUD "occupied", the liberation with its reward (615,000 gold, 5
  Chaos, 1 Divine);
- Chaos Storm: 1000 Dragons created in the area had 175 with a tier shader against 58 without the storm (x3); lightning;
- Wandering Merchant: placed, greeting, trade window with the configured goods;
- Golden Hour: `rateMult` 1.25 inside the area, 1.0 outside.

**Not verified**: healing credit (needs two players), several defenders sharing the rewards, a unique reward (7% roll
not hit), the real map areas, the area-scope Victory buff, a natural world event rotation (started by command), a
withdrawal after 30 minutes. Found on the way, not fixed: `monster_tiers.lua` keys the tier state by the creature id
inside `onSpawn`, which is 0 before the placement, so naturally rolled tiers keep their health and shader but report
"normal" (no tier experience or damage multiplier, no monster bar label). Invasion monsters are not affected
(`ChaosApplyTier` after the creation). Ambush copies of slain invaders are ordinary monsters and stay after an
invasion.

**Edits to shared files**: `chaos_constants.lua` (`ChaosOpcodes.invasion = 251`), `leaderboard_config.lua` (board
`defender`), `loot_config.lua` (`rateMult` x `ChaosWorldEvents.lootMult`), `monster_tiers.lua` (spawn roll x
`ChaosWorldEvents.tierMult`), `events_schedule.lua` (`ChaosEvents.dynamic`: runtime events in `E.active`),
client `game_chaosnotify/notifications.lua` (toast type `INVASION`, action `invasion`).

## Leaderboards (`leaderboard.lua`, `leaderboard_core.lua`, `leaderboard_config.lua`)

Client `game_leaderboard` (opcode 229), opened with Social > Leaderboards in the top menu. Settings:
`leaderboard_config.lua` (loaded as `Chaos.leaderboardConfig`). Tables: `chaos_leaderboard`, `chaos_leaderboard_titles`
(`sql/chaos.sql`); the last processed reset week is the `server_config` row `chaos_leaderboard_reset`.

**Why not the base highscores.** The top menu used to open the base client's `game_highscores`. That window asks for
data with the game packet 0xB1 (the newer protocol's highscores), which this engine does not parse: it stays empty
(checked in game). The base server's own `customs/highscores` script answers extended opcode 73 for a different client
window, and builds its SQL from client input without checks. So the Chaos window is separate, and the menu entry
"Highscores" became "Leaderboards".

- **Boards.** Weekly: **World Boss** (damage dealt to world bosses, kills participated), **Boss Healer** and **Boss Tank**
  (healing and tanking at world bosses, see "World bosses"), **Bounty Hunter** (contracts
  completed), **Rifts** (highest rift tier completed, runs), **Goblin Slayer** (treasure goblins slain), **Guild Siege** (siege points), **Arena 1v1** and **Arena 2v2** (best rating of the week). All time: **Class Ladder** (highest level per class).
  Each board shows the top 20 (`rows`), the player's own rank and value, and the time until the weekly reset.
  Ranks are never shared: on equal values the player who reached the value first ranks higher, then the lower id.
  Staff characters (`group_id >= staffGroup`, 4) are left out of every board, title and reward.
- **Fastest-time boards** (mode `"min"`, the Cinderheart Solo / 2-3 / 4-5 boards of "Ascended Omens and the
  Cinderheart"): the lowest value (seconds) is kept and ranks first; `format = "time"` shows it as m:ss in the window;
  `byClass = true` adds class tabs ("All classes" first), filtered by the vocation stored with the score (the
  character's class at the record, else its current one) and ranked again within the class.
- **Week.** The weekly boards reset on Monday at 06:00 server time (`resetHour`). This is the bounty board's week rule:
  `ChaosLeaderboard.week` calls `ChaosBounty.week`. The week key is the YYYYMMDD of that Monday.
- **Sources.** `worldboss.lua` records every rewarded participant's damage when the boss dies (the shares of
  `computeShares`, so multi-client characters and those below `minDamagePercent` do not count; offline participants
  count too). `bounty.lua` records a contract when it pays (not when multi-clienting). The rift scripts call the API below.
- **Reset.** A once-a-minute check (and one at startup) runs the reset when the week key is later than the last
  processed one. It takes the top 3 (`top`) of every weekly board of the week that ended. They get the board's title
  (`title`: Bossbane, Warden of the Hunt, Riftwalker, Goblin Slayer, Siegebreaker, Duelist, Gladiator) for the week that starts. Their orbs (`rewards`: 1st 5 Divine +
  10 Chaos, 2nd 3 + 6, 3rd 1 + 3) go straight to the inbox. A player offline at the reset gets them at the next login:
  the `rewarded` flag is in the DB, so a restart loses nothing. The reset broadcasts the winners (also as a toast with
  `game_chaosnotify`). Score rows older than `keepWeeks` (8) are deleted. When the server was down over several
  Mondays, only the week just ended is scored.
  A board with `noReward = true` gives its title only, no orbs (the professions' Gatherers board: professions make no orbs,
  see "Professions").
- **Titles.** They show in the look text ("He holds the title Bossbane (1st)."; an `onLook` EventCallback registered
  at index 100, after the base server's `default_onLook` at index 0, which builds the "You see" text and ignores what came
  before it) and next to the name on every board (that board's title first, "+n" for more).
- **Class Ladder.** It reads the players table (`deletion = 0`, below the staff group), ordered by experience, and
  caches each class for `cacheSeconds` (300). Online characters count with their last saved level. Classes are grouped by base
  class through `ladder.baseOf` (nil = `Chaos.classes.baseOf` of the class rework). A vocation missing from the
  mapping is grouped through `Vocation(id):getDemotion()`. The class list holds the vocation ids of
  `data/XML/vocations.xml` that the engine knows. Names come from the server (`Vocation(id):getName()`), so renamed
  or new classes need no change here.

### API (rifts and any other script)

```lua
-- board: "worldboss" | "bounty" | "rift" | "goblin" | "siege" | "arena1v1" | "arena2v2" (a key of Chaos.leaderboardConfig.boards)
-- who:   a Player, a player guid, or {guid = n, name = s} (offline players are looked up)
-- value: integer >= 0; mode: "add" (sum) or "max" (keep the best); nil = the board's mode (rift: "max")
-- Every call also adds 1 to the board's count column (kills / contracts / runs).
-- Returns the player's entry {value, count, at} of this week, or nil (unknown board or player).
ChaosLeaderboard.record(board, who, value, mode)

-- e.g. at the end of a cleared rift, for every member:
if ChaosLeaderboard then ChaosLeaderboard.record("rift", player, tier) end
```

`ChaosLeaderboard.recordShares(shares)` (world boss shares), `ChaosLeaderboard.titlesOf(guid)` (titles held this week)
and `ChaosLeaderboard.checkReset(force)` are public too. A new weekly board is one more entry in `boards` (key, name,
mode, value/count labels, title, info); the client builds its tabs from the server.

Staff: `/leaderboard reset` runs the reset again for the week that just ended (it does not award twice),
`/leaderboard shift <days>` moves the leaderboard clock for tests (0 = real time), `/leaderboard` alone shows the state.

**Tests:** `tests/leaderboard_test.lua` (week key and reset time, record add/max, ranking and ties, the staff filter,
titles and rewards at the reset, look and broadcast text, class grouping).

Verified on the test server: a world boss killed with spell damage -> 18M damage, 1 kill on the board. A bounty
contract completed -> 1 contract. `record("rift", player, 7)` then `5` -> 7, 2 runs. Fake scores for 9 characters
through the API (guid path), a tie at 18M ranked by who reached it first. The reset (clock shifted 4 days): 9 titles,
the broadcast, 3 Orbs of Upheaval + 1 Orb of Fate in the online 3rd place's inbox, the offline winners' rows kept for their login.
Look text "You hold the title Riftwalker (3rd).". Restart: no second reset, titles and the new week's scores loaded
from the DB, the reward of an unrewarded row delivered at login. Tabs, class tabs, own rank, the top menu entry. Not
verified: the look text from another player's view ("He"/"She"; unit-tested), the real Monday 06:00 change (a
once-a-minute check of the week key), the rift source (the rift scripts do not call it yet).

## Competitive records (`records.lua`, `records_core.lua`, `records_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_records.sql`)

Fastest kills and best results of every competitive system, beside the weekly boards (owner request: "Faça uma
leaderboard de bosses, tower e essas coisas, pra gerar uma competição entre os players"). Client: the **Records** button of
the Leaderboards window (`game_leaderboard`, `recordsview.lua`); website: the Records box of the Leaderboards page.

- **Boards** (`records_config.lua` `boards`, built by `ChaosRecordsCore.catalogue` from the content configs, so a new
  boss of those lists gets its boards by itself). Bosses: World Boss Kill (fastest, per boss) and World Boss Damage (the
  best damage share of a kill, per boss), Omen Guardians, Ascended (the three Omens and the Cinderheart), the Guild Boss,
  the Sepulchre Clear, the Hollow Vault and every other dungeon, the deep dungeons 6-9 included (per difficulty). Infinity Tower: Highest Floor, Fastest
  Climb to floors 50 / 100 / 120. Rifts: Highest Tier, Fastest Seal per tier band (1-5, 6-10, 11-14, 15), Atlas
  Completion. Ember Descent: Deepest Room (the weekly seeded run). Vocation Trials: Trial Clear per difficulty. Arena:
  rating per bracket, Battleground wins. Filters: the variant (boss, difficulty, band, floor, bracket), the party size
  (Solo, 2-3, 4-5 where the content allows groups), the class (the class at the run), and the view.
- **Views.** This week (resets Monday 06:00 with the leaderboards), the season (the running server season of
  `season.lua`, else the calendar quarter) and all time. One row per character, slot ("board|variant|size") and period
  in `chaos_records`; a better result replaces it, a tie keeps the older one.
- **Ranking and ties.** Fastest first on the time boards, highest first on the others; a tie goes to the earlier time,
  then the lower character id (ranks are never shared). The "your rank" row counts the characters ahead of you in the
  same view and filters.
- **Anti-abuse** (`ChaosRecordsCore.validate`; a run that fails any rule is not recorded, the reason goes to the console):
  no staff character in the group (one gamemaster voids the run for everyone), no multi-client character, no debug run
  (a run flagged by its script, or the records clock shifted with `/records shift`), the party size inside the board's
  brackets (and at most `maxGroup`), the same difficulty from start to end (dungeons), a variant the board knows, a time
  of at least `minSeconds` (10). Staff and accounts held by the anti-bot review are left out of every view too.
- **Rewards.** The weekly top 3 of every slot hold the category title for the next week (Bossrunner, Spire Climber, Rift
  Sprinter, Depth Seeker, Trial Breaker, Warlord; `ChaosTitles` source `records`) and the **laurel** name plate frame as
  a badge (`ChaosTitles.registerFrame`); awarded at the Monday reset into `chaos_records_awards`, broadcast. A beaten
  all-time record is broadcast ("New record! ... (was ...)"). **Realm firsts:** the first player or party to defeat each
  boss in the season ("Realm first of Season of Ash! ...", `chaos_records_firsts`) holds the title "First: <boss>" for
  that season; the client and the site list them.
- **Sources.** No content script was edited for the bosses: `records.lua` wraps functions they already call, at load, at
  startup and again every minute (a `/reload` of the wrapped script replaces the function): `ChaosWorldBoss.computeRewards`
  (kill time from `W.state.fightStart`, the damage shares), `ChaosRiftCore.atlasSealed` (sealed rifts and Omen guardians:
  tier, omen, seconds, the finishers), `ChaosExclusives.bossKill` (the Ascended and the Cinderheart through the
  `ChaosAscended` run, the guild boss through the `ChaosGuildBoss` run), `ChaosLeaderboard.record` (`raid_clear`,
  `descent`, `arena*`, `battleground`), `ChaosTower.recordRun` (highest floor), `ChaosAchievements.set` ("trial_tier_<n>":
  the `ChaosTrials` run). One guarded line in `infinitytower_run.lua` (floor cleared -> `ChaosRecords.towerFloor`).
  **Not wired yet (the boss mechanics files were being edited):** the dungeons and the Hollow Vault need one line in
  `dungeons.lua` endRun, after `storeRun(...)`:
  `if ChaosRecords and ChaosRecords.dungeonClear then pcall(ChaosRecords.dungeonClear, {dungeonId = run.dungeonId, title =
  titleOf(run.dungeonId, dg), difficulty = run.difficulty, difficultyStart = run.difficultyStart or run.difficulty, ms =
  elapsed, members = memberInfo}) end` (and `run.difficultyStart = run.difficulty` where the run is made). Until then those
  boards stay empty. The world boss, the Ascended and the guild boss use the kill time as the scripts compute it; a
  boss-only time for the rift bands would need a hook in `rift.lua` (the band boards use the whole seal time).
- **Protocol** (opcode 229 `ChaosOpcodes.leaderboard`, a second extended-opcode event; `leaderboard.lua` ignores these
  actions): client `rmeta` | `rget {board, variant, size, period, group}` | `rfirsts`; server `rcat {cat, boards}` (the
  meta in parts of at most 6 boards, the window has no chunk joiner), `rmeta`, `rboard {rows, own, total, record,
  resetIn, seasonName}`, `rfirsts`. The server writes the catalogue to `chaos_records_boards` at startup for the website.
- **Staff:** `/records` (state), `/records reset` (award the last week again; INSERT IGNORE keeps it once), `/records shift
  <days>` (test clock: every run is a debug run meanwhile), `/records rebuild`.
- **Tests:** `tests/records_test.lua` (catalogue, periods and resets, brackets, validation, merge, ranking and ties, awards,
  titles, badge, realm firsts, texts; and `records.lua` on a mocked engine: every hook, the SQL order of the upsert, the
  broadcasts, the views and the meta parts), client `game_leaderboard/recordsview_test.lua`, website
  `chaos_leaderboards_page_test.php`. Live test 2026-10-14 (test server, two clients): a solo world boss kill (time and damage boards), an Omen guardian kill and Infinity Tower floors were recorded in all three views, the Records window showed them, the realm first was broadcast and listed; a kill with a second client of the same connection online was not recorded (the multi-client rule).

## Crafting (`crafting.lua`, `data/lib/chaos_crafting.lua`, `tools/install_crafting.py`)

Install: `python3 -I server/tools/install_crafting.py <server>/data` (idempotent, `--dry-run`), then
`python3 -I server/tools/install_orbs.py <server>/data` (orbs v2 and the new names, see "Crafting orbs v2") and the
`chaos_crafting_log` table of `sql/chaos.sql`. `crafting.lua` loads `data/lib/chaos_crafting.lua` itself, so `lib.lua`
needs no change. The client needs the multi-use flag on two orbs in its `Tibia.dat`:
`python3 -I client/tools/sprites/set_multiuse.py <client>/data/things/1098/Tibia.dat` (after `gen_effects.py`, which
writes a new dat).

**How an item carries modifiers (base server).** A rarity is the custom attribute `rarity` (stored ids 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 10 =
Common, Uncommon, Magic, Rare, Legendary, Divine; items from before 2026-10-18 may still carry 6-9 and 11-15, see "Item rarities").
The engine's C++ roll (`Item::applyRarityEffects`) used to make them; new items are now rolled by `ChaosCrafting.forge` (see "Item modifiers"), the same attributes and an item level
(`combatPowerLevel`, shown as "Level: N"), a small attack/defense/armor/hit chance bonus, and per rarity a fixed number
of modifiers, one custom attribute each: absorbs `rarity_<x>Absorb` (%), skills `rarity_<skill>Skill` (magic level is
`rarity_maglevelSkill`), critical / mana leech / life leech as chance + amount pairs, and on weapons without an element
of their own one `rarity_element<x>` (% extra damage). Everything is also written into the description attribute
("Level: 53, Holy +3%, Fishing +1, Critical Chance +1%, Critical Hit +1%"), which is what the look text and the client
tooltip show. With engine patch 0004 a critical / leech chance is (2 x roll + 1) / 3 of the pair's roll (1..6 -> 1, 1,
2, 3, 3, 4; the amount keeps the roll; the Orb of Grafting does the same, `ChaosCrafting.specialChance`). `customs/rarity/base_rarity.lua` turns the attributes into conditions and storages when the item is
equipped (and at login); the element and absorb combat scripts read those storages. Uniques (`chaos_unique_items.lua`)
are base items with the custom attribute `chaos_unique` and their stats as the same `rarity_*` attributes, without a
rarity. On top of these, items carry the Chaos modifiers of the next section (`chaos_mod_<key>`).

**Every orb is used directly on the item.** "Use with" on the orb, then click an item or a Rift Key in the backpack
(an `Action` per orb id in `crafting.lua`, `ChaosCraftingUseOrb`). The bench is optional. All seven orbs go through the
same `craft()` as the bench: the orb is owned, the item is in the backpack (equipped items and the ground are still
refused: the copy-making orbs would have to unequip and re-equip, and the equip scripts would have to follow), no
uniques, no stacks, the rules below, a line in `chaos_crafting_log`. Using an orb on nothing, a creature, the floor or
anything that can never carry modifiers only explains how to use it ("Use the Orb of Grafting on an item: choose
"Use with" on the orb, then click an item or a Rift Key in your backpack..."); it no longer opens the bench.

**How the two plain-use orbs became use-with (and why that way).** The three rune stones and the Orbs of Upheaval and Fate
were already use-with; the Orb of Awakening (29851, client 27195) and the Orb of Grafting (29855, client 27199) were
plain items. Use-with needs two flags: the client's multi-use flag in `Tibia.dat` (otherwise the client never starts
the crosshair) and the server's `useable` flag in `items.otb` (`Game::playerUseItemEx` refuses an item without it).
Chosen: set both flags on the existing ids (option a). `install_crafting.py` sets `FLAG_USEABLE` on the two otb nodes
(keeps `items.otb.bak`), `client/tools/sprites/set_multiuse.py` inserts flag byte 7 into the two items of the dat
(keeps `Tibia.dat.bak`; checks that the dat still parses exactly). The ids stay the same, so no migration: every orb
already in a backpack, depot, store offer, loot table, bounty chest and the character-upgrade costs
(`waystone_system/character_upgrades.lua` counts 29851 and 29855) keeps working. Moving the orbs to other multi-use ids
(option b) would have needed a migration of every existing stack and of all those references. With a dat that lacks
the flag the orbs still work on the bench; the engine answers a plain use of a `useable` item with "You cannot use this
object" (it refuses plain use of every use-with item, the rune stones included).

The Orbs of Upheaval and Fate are registered by `crafting.lua` too (same rules, the log, Rift Keys); `crafting.lua` loads
before `customs/rarity/reroll_rarity_stats.lua` (scripts load in path order), and the installer makes that script skip
its own two registrations when `ChaosCrafting.ownsStockOrbs` is set (otherwise the engine prints a duplicate warning
and keeps the first one, ours). The installer still adds the unique guard to its `isRerollable`.

**The orbs on gear.** A modifier is one line of the description (a leech or critical pair is one modifier, a Chaos
modifier is one). The maximum per rarity is two prefixes' worth of each side (2, 2, 4, 4, 4, 4, 6 ... 6, see "Item
modifiers"), Chaos modifiers included.

| orb | id | on gear |
|---|---|---|
| Orb of Awakening | 29851 (existing currency item) | normal item (no rarity, no modifiers) -> Common 65% / Uncommon 35%, rolled by `forge` at the item's level |
| Orb of Gilding | 24691 (rune stone, named by the installer) | normal item -> Magic 60% / Rare 30% / Legendary 10%, rolled by `forge` at the item's level |
| Orb of Grafting | 29855 (existing currency item) | item with a rarity and an open prefix or suffix: one new modifier it does not have yet, on an open side, its tier by the item level (weights per type in `ChaosCrafting.affixes()`) |
| Orb of Unmaking | 24697 (rune stone) | item with a rarity: one random modifier goes (rarity and item level stay) |
| Orb of Erasure | 24688 (rune stone) | item with a rarity: a plain copy of the base item (no modifiers; the item level stays) |
| Orb of Upheaval | 29856 | item with a rarity: a new copy of the same rarity and item level with a new set of modifiers |
| Orb of Fate | 29857 | a new copy one rarity rank up with new modifiers (Legendary: 5% Divine, else no change); the item level stays (since 2026-10-22, "Crafting orbs v2") |

Awakening, Gilding, Erasure, Upheaval and Fate make a new copy (like the stock orbs), so upgrade levels on the item
are lost; Grafting and Unmaking change the item in place and rewrite only the rarity part of the description (text in
front of "Level:" and `[...]` upgrade slots behind it are kept). Never touched: uniques (also an old unique without the
marker, recognised by its spec name), stacks, containers, non-gear, the boat items, equipped items, items outside the
backpack. There is no orb that copies an item. The Orb of Sockets changes the number of sockets: see "Gems
and sockets". The six orbs that came after (Tempering, Binding, Excision, Reforging, Ruin, the Whetstone) and the new names of
the old ones are in "Crafting orbs v2".

**The orbs on Rift Keys** (the map way; `C.keyCheck` / `C.keyApply`). The rift's own modifier pool, value ranges and
reward bonuses (`rift_config.lua` `mods`, `rift_core.lua`); the tier never changes; the key's `rift_mods` attribute,
name and description (modifiers, reward bonuses, level) are written again through `ChaosRift.applyKey`. Rarity, unique
and slot rules do not apply; the backpack rule and the log do.

| orb | on a Rift Key |
|---|---|
| Awakening | a key without modifiers gets 1 |
| Gilding | a key without modifiers gets 2 (60%) or 3 (40%) (`key.alchemyCount`) |
| Grafting | one more modifier the key does not have, up to `key.maxMods` (3) |
| Unmaking | one random modifier goes |
| Erasure | every modifier goes |
| Chaos | new modifiers, the count rolled with the drop weights (1: 50, 2: 35, 3: 15) |
| Divine | the same modifiers, new values inside their ranges (whole steps) |

`key.maxMods` also caps the decoded key (`R.decodeMods`); above 3 the crash refund marker would need more storages.

**Bench.** Economy > Crafting Bench in the top menu (the orbs no longer open it). Drag an item or
a Rift Key from an open backpack onto the slot, or click one in the grid (bags inside the backpack included, 64 at
most; keys have a violet frame). The bench shows rarity and item level (a key: tier, level and reward bonuses),
modifiers / maximum and every orb with your count and, when it fits, a preview of what it would do ("2 -> 3 of 5
modifiers", "Magic 60%, Rare 30%, Legendary 10%", "same modifiers, new values"; `C.preview`); a button is enabled only
when the server says the orb fits. The server checks again on every click: the item is found by its path from the
backpack plus its id and a signature of its modifiers (moved or changed -> "put it on the bench again"), the orb is
owned, the rules above, 250 ms between orbs. The last 8 crafts come from `chaos_crafting_log` (rows older than 60 days
go at startup); use-with crafts are logged too.

**Drops and rewards.** Chaos loot layer (`loot_config.lua` currency, per 10000 kills, normal / magic / rare / legendary /
boss): Awakening 30/200/700/2500/3500 (1-2), Gilding and Unmaking 10/80/300/1200/2000, Erasure
15/100/400/1500/2500, Grafting 4/30/120/600/1000; weights for the guaranteed legendary/boss draw 20/10/10/10/5 (Upheaval 70,
Fate 30). Simulated 10000 legendary kills: Upheaval 8513, Fate 4380, Awakening 7607, Gilding 1862, Unmaking 1864,
Erasure 2110, Grafting 945. The store does not sell these orbs (no orb with a random result is sold; see "Store"). Weekly bounty chest: + 3 Orbs of Awakening, 1 Orb of Unmaking, 5 Whetstones and 2 Orbs of Tempering (`weeklyExtra` in `bounty_config.lua`).

**Tested in game** (test server, cropped map, client with the patched dat): use-with of all seven orbs on items with no
bench open (the Orb of Awakening and the Orb of Grafting with the mouse: right click, then click the item; the others
by `g_game.useWith`, the same packet), the hint for an orb used on oneself and on the floor, the bench (select an item
and a key, previews, Grafting from the bench), every orb on a Rift Key by use-with and on the bench, then a rift opened
with the crafted key (Brutality 15, Withering, Swarm 2: damage x1.15, no regeneration, packs of 5-6), the log rows of
every path; earlier: refusals (unique, full item, no orb, equipped item), drag and drop onto the slot, the store
purchase and the loot simulation. `tests/crafting_test.lua` covers eligibility, each orb on a mocked item, slot limits,
the description, unique protection, the Chaos modifiers through the orbs, the previews and every orb on a Rift Key.
Not tested: the weekly bounty chest with the extra orbs (needs four finished contracts), a hotkey set to plain "use".

## Base crafting script (`tools/patch_base_crafting.py`, `tests/base_crafting_patch_test.lua`)

The base server ships its own crafting, separate from the Chaos bench: `data/scripts/customs/crafting/1crafting_mod.lua`
loads 7 categories (herbalist, woodcutting, mining, generalcrafting, armorsmith, weaponsmith, jewelsmith; 275 recipes in
the category files), registers tables with action ids 38820-38826 on the shipped map and talks JSON on extended opcode 91.
No client module of ours handles opcode 91, so only a modified client can open it or send a craft.

**The stock bugs.** Gold and materials were checked when the "craft" request arrived; the item was made 860 ms later in
an `addEvent`, and only after `addItemEx` were `removeMoney` / `removeItem` called, results unchecked. N requests inside
860 ms gave N items for one set of materials (the leftovers' removals simply failed). `Crafting:craft` never checked that
the player was at a table, so any client sending opcode 91 crafted from anywhere. `addItemEx` returns a ReturnValue, so
the stock "not enough space" branch never ran.

**What the patch changes** (the stock file is CRLF; line ends are kept):
- Using a table records its category, position and time (`CraftGuard.markTable` in the tables' `onUse`). A craft is
  refused unless the player used a table of that category in the last 5 minutes, stands on its floor within 2 tiles of
  it, and has no craft pending; 1 s between two requests ("You are already crafting. Wait a moment.").
- The delayed event finds the player again by id (a logout ends it), checks the table, recipe unlock, skill, gold,
  materials, capacity and backpack space again, then takes the gold and each material, every result checked. A failed
  removal gives back what that attempt took and crafts nothing. Only then is the item made and added; when it cannot be
  made or added, gold and materials are given back (materials with `addItem(id, count, true)`: a full backpack drops
  them at the player's feet).
- Unchanged: recipes, texts, the 860 ms delay, skill tries, the rarity roll (5% x the stock tier chances; with the
  duplication closed a rolled craft costs a full set of materials, so it is no cheap salvage source). For equipment,
  potions and runes `patch_base_crafting_bonus.py` replaces that roll later (see "Crafting bonus").

**Anchors.** `local CODE_CRAFTING = 91` (the guard block goes after it), the tables' `function actionEvent.onUse(player)`
+ `player:showCrafting(category)`, and the whole stock `function Crafting:craft` ... `end, 860)` / `end`, compared by
sha256 (line ends and trailing blanks ignored). Each must be found exactly once and in that order, else the tool says
"not the expected stock version" and writes nothing (exit 1). Markers `-- Chaos: crafting guard (patch_base_crafting.py)
v1 ...`; all three present: "already"; only some: refused. No crafting script in the base: skipped.

**Tests.** `tests/base_crafting_patch_test.lua` patches `tests/fixtures/base_crafting/1crafting_mod.lua` (the stock file,
LF) through the tool (twice, CRLF, another version, a partly patched file) and runs the patched script on a mock engine:
no table / 3 tiles away / another floor / table use over 5 minutes old / other category refused; 5 requests at once give
one craft and one set of materials; gold and materials are removed before the item is created; materials gone before
the event, a failed gold or material removal and a logout create nothing; a failed `addItemEx` refunds everything.
Against the stock script the same test gets 5 items for one set of materials.

## Base crafting recipes (`tools/patch_base_recipes.py`, `tools/patch_base_recipes_test.py`)

Owner (2026-10-22, on the Seraphic Charged Stone): "Coloque pra que servem". The base books have three class sets at
level 35: Myst Regalia (mage), Seraphic (paladin) and Dawnforged (knight). Every Seraphic and Dawnforged recipe asked
for the Myst Charged Stone (29921) and the Myst Emblem (29924), so the Seraphic and Dawnforged stones and emblems
(29922, 29923, 29925, 29926) that the level 1200+ bosses drop had no use. The tool (install step `baserecipes`, after
`basecraftingbonus`; idempotent, `--dry-run`, `--check`):

- **Own materials.** armorsmith, weaponsmith, jewelsmith: a Seraphic piece (29869-29877) takes the Seraphic Charged
  Stone and Emblem, a Dawnforged piece (29878-29890) the Dawnforged ones. Same counts, gold (60,000), level (35),
  Nyxdrath Heart and the other materials as the Myst piece of that slot. Belts and gloves stay (`patch_badges.py`
  retires them).
- **Myst amulet and ring.** The jewelsmith's "Myst Regalia Amulet" / "Myst Regalia Ring" made 29865 / 29866 (the Myst
  spellbook and wand, which the weaponsmith also makes); they make 29867 / 29868 now.
- **Trophy recipes** (generalcrafting, the crafting table; appended after the stock book in a marked block, so the stock
  recipes keep their places):

| Product | Materials | Gold | Level |
|---|---|---|---|
| Myst Charged Stone | Gargantuan Eye, Runic Claw | 25,000 | 25 |
| Seraphic Charged Stone | Verdant Scale, Vorsk Scale | 25,000 | 25 |
| Dawnforged Charged Stone | Frostbone Shard, Runic Stone Shard | 25,000 | 25 |
| Myst / Seraphic / Dawnforged Emblem | its line's Charged Stone, Runic Stone Shard | 25,000 | 30 |
| Myst Emblem | Brainforged, Runic Stone Shard | 25,000 | 30 |

  The trophies drop at 7-9% from the level 950-1150 hunts (`tools/loot_bands_data.lua`) and only sold to an NPC before;
  the Runic Stone Shard (25% from the level 1200+ monsters, the waystone shop) had no use at all. **Economy:** by the
  price table each recipe's materials sell for at most its product (75,000-107,000 against 80,000 / 115,000), so the
  table's craft floor leaves every price as it was; with the gold the inputs are worth more than the product, so no
  recipe makes money, and no recipe turns its product back into a material. The test checks both against
  `chaos_item_prices_data.lua`.
- **Descriptions.** items.xml: the stones, emblems, Nyxdrath Heart, trophies and the Runic Stone Shard say what they are
  for ("Crafting material for the Seraphic set and the Seraphic Emblem."); added, or appended to another description.

`item_prices_base.py` reads the books through `patch_book`, so `gen_item_prices.py survey` writes
`data/items/base_recipes.csv` as installed. The item finder reads the global `Crafting` at run time and shows every
recipe both ways; the tooltip's "Used in" line comes from it (see "Item finder").

**Audit (2026-10-22): base materials that drop and had no use.** Item finder rows of every system, the base books, every
base script and NPC: after this change the late boss materials above are all used. Still with no use beyond the sell
price of the item price table: the classic creature products (vendor loot by design) and the energy creature parts
26158-26179 and the scarab ocarina 27432, which no base NPC buys (the Loot Buyer pays the table's price).

## Crafting bonus (`tools/patch_base_crafting_bonus.py`, `chaos/craft_bonus*.lua`, `tests/craft_bonus_test.lua`, `tests/base_crafting_bonus_test.lua`)

**The stock roll.** The base script gave every product, potions and tools included, `rollRarity()`: 5% of crafts, then
the stock chance of each rarity id 1..15 in turn, made with `Game.createItemWithRarity` (the engine's own stats). The ids
are the rarities of ours (stored ids 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 10; the roll now walks `ChaosRarity.stockRolls`, step 21 of `patch_base_events.py`), but such an item has no item level, no modifier tiers, no
prefix / suffix split and no sockets: the item_mods layer never rolled it (the comment on `ChaosCrafting.createItem` says
to stop using that call). It duplicates our roll, so for equipment it is replaced. Any other product (tools, materials,
the flasks the herbalist makes for the armorsmith) keeps it unchanged; potions and runes keep it too and get the bonus
below on top.

**Mastery** = the crafter's skill in the recipe's category (`getEffectiveSkillLevel`, skills 7-13) minus the recipe's
required level, at least 0. Stock recipes need 10-35. All numbers are in `craft_bonus_config.lua`.

**Equipment** (`ChaosCraftBonus.kind`: `ChaosCrafting.isGear` of the result, one piece a craft, not a tool). On the
stock recipes: 164 of the armorsmith, weaponsmith and jewelsmith results (helmets, armors, legs, boots, weapons, shields,
rings and amulets, gloves and belts) and the two quivers (Haloed and Seraphic: off-hand equipment since
"Infinite arrows and quivers"). Not equipment: the profession tools and the mount scroll (`isGear` accepts them for
their skill bonus, but they are "other" items that fit only the hands: `toolSlots`), the backpacks, materials. One roll
over:

| Rarity | mastery 0 | mastery 25 | mastery 50+ (cap) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Common | 12% | 15% | 18% |
| Uncommon | 6% | 7.5% | 9% |
| Magic | 3% | 3.75% | 4.5% |
| Rare | 1.2% | 1.5% | 1.8% |
| plain | 77.8% | 72.25% | 66.7% |

Every chance x (1 + 1% per mastery point), at most x1.5; all together at most 35%; never above Rare (4); the old crafted Legendary (0.4%) was removed with the seven rarities. A
legendary monster's gear has floor 4 and a boss's floor 5 (`loot_config.lua` `gear.minRarity`), so a craft never beats a
boss drop; the test checks it against the real loot config. The item level is the recipe level + mastery / 2, never
below what the type's required level gives a plain item (as `ChaosCrafting.orbLevel`), at most 90: modifier tiers up to
T5 (`chaos_item_mods.lua` tierLevels: T6 needs 95; world boss gear is 145). The piece is made by
`ChaosCrafting.createItem(id, rarity, level)` (the drop roll: modifiers and tiers by item level) and gets sockets from
`ChaosGems.rollDropSockets` when it has a rarity. A plain piece gets the item level only.

**Potions and runes** (the herbalist potions 28076-28083 and 28088-28091 in `yield.ids`; any `ItemType:isRune()`; no
stock recipe makes a rune today). One roll: double the recipe's count with 0.08% per mastery point (at most 8%), else
+50% (rounded up) with 5% + 0.25% per point (at most 25%). Gold and materials stay the same.

| Mastery | +50% | x2 | extra per craft (5-potion recipe) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 5% | 0% | +0.15 |
| 25 | 11.25% | 2% | +0.44 |
| 50 | 17.5% | 4% | +0.73 |
| 75 | 23.75% | 6% | +1.01 |
| 100+ | 25% | 8% | +1.15 |

The recipe's own count is made and added as before; the extra pieces are given only after that add worked: into the
backpack (`Chaos.giveItem`), what does not fit to the store inbox (as the bestiary rewards), so a lucky roll never fails a
craft. A failed add refunds gold and materials and gives no extra.

**Order.** Both rolls run inside the guarded delayed craft (`patch_base_crafting.py`), after `CraftGuard.take` took the
gold and the materials, before `addItemEx`; a failed make or add gives both back as before, so the dupe fix holds.

**Texts** (window message, "ok"): "You crafted a Rare Crown Shield (item level 32)." / "You crafted a Crown Shield (item
level 32)." / "You crafted 7 Exalted Health Potions (bonus +2)." (+ "Your backpack was full: N went to your store
inbox."). Other products keep the stock texts.

**Window.** Each recipe of a `fetch` page carries `bonus` at the player's skill: `{kind = "gear", level, odds = [{rarity,
name, pct}]}` or `{kind = "stack", odds = [{extra, pct}]}`. The recipe panel shows it under the gold line: "Rarity at
item level 37: Common 18% / Uncommon 9% / Magic 4.5% / Rare 1.8%" or "Bonus yield: +3 at 17.5% / +5 at
4%"; the result's tooltip too.

**What the patch changes** (after both earlier patches, whose markers it needs): a `CraftingBonus` block before `local
LoginEvent = CreatureEvent("CraftingLogin")` (it calls `ChaosCraftBonus` and falls back to the stock roll and texts when
that is missing or fails); `bonus = CraftingBonus.odds(...)` after `storageText = craft.storageText or "",` in
`Crafting:sendCrafts`; the stock product block (`local rarityId = rollRarity()` ... `end`) of the guarded craft becomes
`CraftingBonus.make` and must come after `CraftGuard.take`; the two success texts become `CraftingBonus.finish` after
`CraftGuard.added(player:addItemEx(item))`. Each anchor exactly once and in that order, else nothing is written.
Markers `-- Chaos: crafting bonus (patch_base_crafting_bonus.py) v1 bonus / odds / make / text`.

**Tests.** `tests/craft_bonus_test.lua`: the odds, caps (against `loot_config.lua` and the item level gates), item level,
roll boundaries and rates, the yield, the texts, then `craft_bonus.lua` on a mock engine (which products count, odds,
make, finish, the store inbox). `tests/base_crafting_bonus_test.lua`: the tool on the fixture (needs both earlier
patches, idempotent, CRLF, partly patched, another version) and the patched script with the real `craft_bonus.lua`:
gold and materials before the roll, five requests give one item, the extra pieces only after the add, a failed add
refunds without extra, tools the stock way, the odds on the pages, the fallback without `craft_bonus.lua`.
Live test (full map, armorsmith and herbalist skill 65): 164 equipment and 24 potion recipes found, the tools and
backpacks stay stock; 15 Plate Legs (recipe level 10) came out at item level 37, 6 of them Common to Rare, each with
its modifiers and tiers (T1-T3) in the look text; Exalted Health Potion x5 gave 8 (bonus +3) for one set of materials.

## Crafting Table window (`tools/patch_base_crafting_ui.py`, `tests/base_crafting_ui_test.lua`, client `game_craftingtable`)

The client side of the base crafting tables ("Base crafting script"): using a table opens the Crafting Table window on
its category. The base protocol is kept as it is (extended opcode 91, JSON `{action, data}`; the client module registers
91, which no other Chaos script or client module uses):

| Direction | Action | Data |
|---|---|---|
| server -> client | `show` | `{category}`: a table was used (sent with `money` first) |
| server -> client | `money` | the gold the player carries (`getMoney`), after `show` and after a craft |
| server -> client | `chunkedFetch` | `{chunkData = {msgID, index, count, payload}}`: 512-byte pieces of the JSON text of `fetch` |
| (joined) | `fetch` | `{category, page, totalPages, crafts = [{index, name, id, clientId, level, cost, count, storage, playerStorage, storageText, materials = [{id, clientId, count, player, name}], bonus}]}`, 10 recipes a page, `player` = the player's count (`getItemCount`), `bonus` from "Crafting bonus" |
| server -> client | `craft` | `{success = true}`: accepted, the item comes 860 ms later; the recipe's page is sent again after it |
| server -> client | `message` | `{kind = "ok" / "error", text}` (this patch) |
| server -> client | `tip` | `{category, craftId, tip}` (this patch; `tip = false` without the Chaos item tooltip) |
| client -> server | `fetch` | `{category, page}` |
| client -> server | `craft` | `{category, craftId}` (`craftId` = the recipe's index in its category) |
| client -> server | `tip` | `{category, craftId}` (this patch) |

The base `show` from the client and the `materials` answer are not used. Categories and skills: herbalist (skill 10),
woodcutting (8), mining (9), generalcrafting (7), armorsmith (11), weaponsmith (12), jewelsmith (13); the client reads
the skill levels from the skills packet (base patch 0012, `g_game.onCraftingSkill(skill - 7, ...)`, `game_craftskills`).

**What the patch changes** (after `patch_base_crafting.py`, whose markers it needs; it refuses a file without them, so that
tool's hash of the stock `Crafting:craft` still matches when both run on a fresh file):
- Every `player:popupFYI(` of the script becomes `CraftingUi.notify(player, "ok" | "error", ...)`: the texts go to the
  window as `message` instead of popup boxes. All of them answer a `craft` request, which only a client with the window
  sends. "ok" for the two success texts, "error" for the rest (table, busy, unlock, gold, skill, materials, capacity,
  backpack, refunds).
- `tip`: the Chaos item tooltip (`ChaosItemTooltip.build`) of a new item of the recipe's result, made with
  `Game.createItem` and never placed (rarity and modifiers are rolled when the real item is crafted); 8 per second per
  player; an unknown category, a method name of `Crafting` or an unknown recipe gets no answer.
- `fetch`: each material carries its `name`.
- Anchors `Crafting = {}`, `elseif action == "craft" then`, `player = player:getItemCount(mat.id)`, each exactly once;
  markers `-- Chaos: crafting window (patch_base_crafting_ui.py) v1 ui / tip / names`.
- Request checks (marker `... v2 valid`, added on the next run to a file patched before): the JSON and its `data` must
  be tables, `fetch`, `show` and `craft` take only one of the seven categories (`CraftingUi.CATEGORIES`), `fetch` only a
  whole page 1..1000 (`CraftingUi.page`, "2" counts as 2). The stock check `Crafting[category]` let a fetch name a method
  ("craft"): `sendCrafts` took the length of a function and the console showed a Lua error. Anchors: the crafting window
  block's end line, the JSON check, `local data = json_data.data` and the three category checks, each exactly once.

**The window** (`client/overlay/modules/game_craftingtable/`, logic in `craftingtableview.lua`): the seven categories as
tabs (the table's own marked), the recipe list with a search over recipe and material names and a filter (All / Can
craft: unlocked, the skill, the gold and the materials the player carries), the recipe: result icon with the item tooltip,
count, skill needed against the player's, gold against what he carries, the materials with have/need in green or red,
Craft with a count (Craft x N sends the next request when the previous one succeeded and the 1 s cooldown passed, and
stops at the first refusal), a bar for the 860 ms and the server's answer under it. Craft is off, with the reason, for
another category's tab, when the player moved more than 1 tile from where the table opened the window, when the table
use is over 290 s old, and when the counts say something is missing (the counts come from the server: the window asks
for every page when a table opens it, the page again after a refusal, and on Refresh). Economy > Crafting Tables only
explains where the tables are: in the crafting hall around x 31650, y 32233; z 4 general crafting, jewelsmith,
armorsmith and weaponsmith (two tables each); z 5 mining (three); z 6 woodcutting (three) and herbalist (four).

**Tests.** `tests/base_crafting_ui_test.lua` (both tools on the stock fixture: refused without the guard patch,
idempotent, CRLF, partly patched refused; the patched script on a mock engine: refusal, success, busy, gold and skill
texts as `message`, no popup, material names, `tip` and its limit) and client `game_craftingtable/craftingtableview_test.lua`
(messages, chunks out of order, pages, have/need, unlock / skill / gold / material / table checks, how many, search and
filters, progress and repeat timing). **Tested in game** on the full map (test server with the patched script, MariaDB,
Linux client): a herbalist table used from the client opens the window with 34 recipes, the stats tooltip of a weapon of
another tab, Craft x2 (two items, 2,000 gold and two sets of materials taken, the skill rose, the counts refreshed),
the server's refusal for materials that were gone (stale counts), the walked-away state and the server's table refusal
for a request sent from 3 tiles away, the menu entry.

## Rune supply (`data/lib/chaos_rune_supply.lua`, `tools/install_rune_supply.py`, `sql/chaos_rune_supply.sql`, `tests/rune_supply_test.lua`)

Owner: "Tire as spells de fazer runa. Deixa as runas serem de vendedores e craft." No spell conjures a rune; every rune a
stock spell conjured (36, and the unscribed rune) comes from NPC vendors or the base crafting tables. Every number is in
`data/lib/chaos_rune_supply.lua`; the install tool, the crafting loader, the test and `check_content.py` all read it.

**What `install_rune_supply.py DATA_DIR [--dry-run]` does** (install step `runes`, after `npcnames`; idempotent):
- spells.xml: the 40 conjure entries (by script path: `conjuring/<rune>.lua`, `conjuring/blank_rune.lua` and
  `R.otherConjures`, whatever rename_spells.py called them) become comments marked `Chaos: no conjuring`. The `<rune>`
  entries stay. The server spellbook, the support runes and the combat log strip comments, so they no longer list them.
- Other conjure spells (owner, 2026-10-13: "Pode tirar, já que as ammos são infinitas"): Conjure Rations
  (`support/food.lua`), Hallow Spear (`conjuring/enchant_spear.lua`) and Charge Staff (`conjuring/enchant_staff.lua`) go
  the same way. The foods Conjure Rations made stay on sale, no shop change needed: meat, ham, bread and cheese at
  Yornath and Beline in Mirewake (meat and ham at 32 base NPCs), grapes and apples at Kestbert in Mirewake, cheese also
  in Cinderhold, rolls at 4 NPCs elsewhere. The enchanted spear and staff were only ever conjured.
- NPC shops: every NPC that sells one of these runes (XML `shop_buyable`, Lua `addBuyableItem`, `{id, buy}` tables; 27
  NPC files and one NPC script of the base) sells it at the config's price; nobody undercuts the table. Runes stack in this protocol, so the
  price is per rune (the subtype an NPC writes stays and changes nothing).
- Vendors: Raloth (Mirewake, town 1) and Isora (Cinderhold, town 2: the main city and the default home town, `hubTown`,
  `startTowns`, "Main city") sell all 36 runes and the unscribed rune (10 gold). Found by their Chaos name, or before the
  npcnames step by the hash in `data/npc/base_npc_names.csv`. A vendor that is missing, or has no XML shop list, stops
  the tool with exit 1 and nothing written. Raloth sold 25 of the 36 runes and Isora 20; the rest are added.
- Crafting: `data/scripts/customs/crafting/generalcrafting.lua` gets a loader block at its end (CRLF kept) that calls
  `ChaosRuneSupply.addRecipes(Crafting.generalcrafting)`: 36 recipes after the stock ones (their indexes stay), once per
  load. No crafting file: skipped.
- Learned spells: the stock entries had `needlearn="0"`, so nobody learned one; `sql/chaos_rune_supply.sql` deletes any
  `player_spells` row with a stock or Chaos name of the 40 removed spells (the engine keeps learned names as text and never checks them,
  so a login never fails either way). A hotkey with the old words only says them now.

**Prices** (gold a rune, at every NPC): conjure value = (mana x 0.5 + soul x 10 + blank rune 10) / runes conjured, the
mana at what mana potions cost; x1.0 for rune levels 1-24, x1.1 for 25-34, x1.2 for 35+; never below the lowest price a
base NPC asked; at least 2 for the 10-a-blank runes. Flagged for the owner (docs/OWNER_TODO.md).

A flat NPC price cannot follow the income curve: runes are a real sink from level 8 to about 300 (heaviest at 30-60,
where the strong runes unlock) and a token one past 500. The prices are per item in the base NPC shop module, so a
level-scaled price would need a scripted shop. Open for the owner.

**Crafting** (general crafting tables, skill 7, action id 38823; the crafting hall, z 4). A recipe turns 5 unscribed

herbalist and mining gathering; the Chaos professions feed no crafting, their owner rule):

| 25-34 | 18 | scarlet flower (26726) | piece of sapphire (26404) | the third tier of tools |
| 35+ | 25 | red lilly (26727) | piece of gold (26401) | the expert's tools |

Recipe gold + the 5 blank runes = 55% of the vendor price of what it makes (`goldShare`); the materials have no NPC
price, they cost gathering time, and the table takes 860 ms a craft and 1 s between crafts. "Crafting bonus" applies
(runes: +50% or x2 extra pieces by mastery: about +2.5% runes at mastery 0, +20% at 100), so the gold a rune falls from
55% to about 46% of the vendor price.

the rune lines and three runes that no NPC sold before change).

town; every rune has a recipe (band herb and ore, skill, blank runes) that costs less gold a rune than the vendor and at
least 40% of it; `addRecipes` once; the tool on a written data folder (rune, blank rune, food, spear and staff conjure
entries commented, the rune entry, another spell, another script of the same file name and an entry an earlier version
commented kept, every NPC repriced in XML and Lua, both vendors stocked without duplicates, the crafting loader on
a CRLF file, loading it gives every recipe once, a second run and a dry run change nothing, a missing vendor writes

tutorial's class spells) names a removed spell. Run on the base server's data (copy): 40 entries commented, 27 NPC files
and one NPC script repriced, Raloth and Isora complete, the 36 recipes loaded with LuaJIT and Lua 5.3; a second run did

**Client.** `gen_spell_data.py` writes `ChaosRemovedSpells` (old words -> Chaos words) into `spelldata.lua`: the 40
