spell id, which only the conjure entry of the rune carries (`Spells.getSpellByIcon`), and Chaos words the server list
knows keep `spellfix.lua` from moving those ids by +1000. Taking them out of the spell list (`chaosspells.lua`, by words,
any type: Conjure Rations is an "Instant" entry) is pending; the spell icon sheets keep their cells for the same reason.

## Crafting orbs v2 (`data/lib/chaos_orbs.lua`, `chaos_orbs_config.lua`, `tools/install_orbs.py`, `item_powers.lua`)

The second set of orbs, on top of the item level / tier / prefix and suffix rework ("Item modifiers"). They are registered
with `ChaosCrafting.addOrb{key, id, name, text, check, apply, preview, pick, keyCheck, keyPick, keyApply}` from
`data/lib/chaos_orbs.lua`, which `chaos_crafting.lua` loads at its end, so `crafting.lua` registers a use-with action and a
bench row for each of them like for the first eight. Every number is in `ChaosOrbsConfig` (`chaos_orbs_config.lua`).
Tests: `tests/orbs_test.lua` (8500 checks), `tests/powers_test.lua`.

**New names.** The currency items used the names of another game; every orb has a name of its own now. Only the names change:
ids, keys (`transmutation`, `exalted`, ...), storages and the character-upgrade shop stay.

| old name | new name | id |
|---|---|---|
| Orb of Transmutation | Orb of Awakening | 29851 |
| Orb of Augmentation | Ember Shard (character upgrades only; the Ember Orb of crafting is the new item 32258) | 29852 |
| Regal Orb | Crown Shard (character upgrades only; the Crown Orb of crafting is the new item 32259) | 29853 |
| Vaal Orb | Void Shard (character upgrades only; the Void Orb of crafting is the new item 32260) | 29854 |
| Exalted Orb | Orb of Grafting | 29855 |
| Chaos Orb | Orb of Upheaval | 29856 |
| Divine Orb | Orb of Fate | 29857 |
| Angel Orb | Dawn Orb (character upgrades only) | 29858 |
| Mirror of Kalandra | Orb of Echoes (character upgrades only; it never copied an item, and nothing here does) | 29859 |
| Orb of Alchemy | Orb of Gilding | 24691 |
| Orb of Annulment | Orb of Unmaking | 24697 |
| Orb of Scouring | Orb of Erasure | 24688 |

`install_orbs.py` writes the names (and plurals) into `items.xml` and replaces the old names in every base-server file that
lists items by name: the loot lists of the waystone monsters (`id = "vaal orb"` ...), monster XML, NPC lists, any script
outside `data/scripts/chaos` (case-insensitive, whole words; 220 references in 36 files of the test server's base data).
A base item name that holds an old name is kept: "blazing ember orb" (29520) holds "Ember Orb", and an older run wrote
"blazing ember shard" (no such item: Ashseer Dravok's loot failed to load, the general crafting recipes and the shops of
Khadin and Vazallia named it; live log 2026-10-21). The names come from items.xml; a form a rename made of one is put
back on the next run (`tools/install_orbs_test.py`). The
repository's own files carry the new names (a sweep over scripts, configs, tests, docs, the website). `check_names.py` has no
list of these names; the old ones are gone from the player-facing text.

**The orbs.**

| orb | id (sprite) | what it does | source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Orb of Tempering | 32251 (blue inlay stone) | rolls the values of every modifier that is not bound again, inside the current tiers; on a Rift Key: new values | drops, salvage 20 shards (not in the store) |
| Orb of Binding | 32252 (violet crystal) | binds one modifier (chosen on the bench; a random one by use-with): Tempering, Unmaking, Excision, Reforging and Upheaval leave it alone. At most 1 bound modifier up to Rare, 2 from Legendary (`ChaosItemMods.config.bind.max`). Only an Orb of Erasure frees it | store 30 (3 a week), drops (rare), salvage 75 |
| Orb of Excision | 32253 (red crystal) | removes the modifier you choose (a random one that is not bound by use-with); on a Rift Key: one modifier | store 25 (3 a week), drops, salvage 60 |
| Orb of Reforging | 32254 (gold crystal) | rolls the tier (by the item level) and the value of the one modifier you choose again | drops, salvage 50 (not in the store) |
| Orb of Ruin | 32255 (black stone) | the gamble, below | drops (very rare), salvage 150, no store |
| Ember Orb | 32258 (red crowned gem) | raises the one modifier you choose by exactly one tier (new value in the new tier; never past T8, not on bound modifiers; a random one by use-with) | drops, salvage 50, 1,500 Ember Shards, Candlemarks 10 (5 a week) |
| Crown Orb | 32259 (purple crowned gem) | lifts the item one rarity, Common up to Legendary (never Divine): every modifier stays, the base bonus becomes the new rarity's, the item gets one more modifier | drops (rare), salvage 100, 1,750 Crown Shards, Candlemarks 25 (2 a week) |
| Whetstone | 32256 (moonlight crystals) | +1% item quality, up to 20% (30% from Divine rarity) | store 10 for 20 (5 packs a week), bounty chest (5), drops, salvage 5 |
| Void Orb | 32260 (small enchanted amethyst) | corrupts a Rare or better item for good, then one weighted outcome (below) | drops (very rare), salvage 125, Orb Exchange; never Candlemarks or the store |

The sprites are the stock multi-use inlay stones, essence crystals and moonlight crystals (clients 24483, 25047, 25049, 25048,
24477, 22083; the Ember and Crown Orb use the crowned gems 25045 and 25044, the Void Orb the small enchanted amethyst 678,
a stock gem sprite like those `install_gems.py` copies): they have the multi-use flag in `Tibia.dat` already, so **no client dat change and no `set_multiuse.py` run**
is needed; the live dat pair is untouched. The server nodes are copies of the stock nodes with the `useable` flag (the same
way as the gems and the salvage shard, `install_gems.py`' helpers). Ids 32251..32260 are reserved for this set.

**Ember and Crown rework (2026-10-20).** The base server's Ember Orb (29852) and Crown Orb (29853) were currency of the
waystone upgrade window, which has no client window, and their sprites have no multi-use flag: they could not be spent and
the wiki explained nothing. They are now the **Ember Shard** and **Crown Shard** (still dropped, still shop currency), and
Ember Orb and Crown Orb are real crafting orbs, items 32258 and 32259 (`ChaosOrbsConfig.crown` = max rank 5 and modifiers
added). A server installed before keeps working: `install_orbs.py` renames by id and rewrites the old names in base data.
Since 2026-10-21 the shards also combine into their orb at the crafting bench's Salvage tab: 1,000 Ember Shards make an
Ember Orb, 1,000 Crown Shards a Crown Orb (see "Salvage", "Ember and Crown Shards into orbs", for the numbers).

**Void Orb rework (2026-10-21).** Beta: "The Void Orb is still broken, I think it has no use." It was the base server's
29854, currency of the same waystone upgrade window (no client window, no multi-use flag, no crafting key): the codex
said "no crafting use" and nothing spent it. 29854 is now the **Void Shard** (two rename rows like the Ember and Crown
Shard), and the **Void Orb** is item 32260, orb key `void`, a corruption orb (`ChaosOrbs.corrupt`, numbers in
`ChaosOrbsConfig.void`):

- **Refused** (the orb stays): no gear, a unique, a stack, a Rift Key, a ruined item, an item already corrupted
  (`corrupted`), a locked item (`chaos_locked`, the bench's Lock button: `locked`), a store item (`chaos_storebound` or
  the engine's store flag: `storeItem`), below Rare (`voidRarity`). The orb is taken only when it applied (crafting.lua).
- **Corrupted** (`chaos_corrupted` = 1): every orb refuses the item, the Orb of Sockets and the Void Orb included, and the
  Conquest refinement too (`corrupted`). It can still be worn, sold, listed, stashed, salvaged and socketed with gems.
  "Corrupted" in the description, `corrupted` in the bench state ("CORRUPTED", red) and the tooltip (a red line
  "Corrupted: no orb can change this item"). The market's free-slot search treats it like a ruined item (no free slot).
- **Outcomes** (weights, they add up to 100; one that cannot happen falls back as noted):

| outcome | weight | what happens | fallback |
|---|---|---|---|
| sealed | 28 | nothing else: only the lock | - |
| tier | 20 | one random unbound modifier one tier up (never past T8) | implicit |
| implicit | 20 | a corrupted implicit (`chaos_cimp` = its attribute key) at T7 or T8 from the pool of the item's kind (`void.implicits`: weapon Damage to Elites and Bosses, Attack Speed, Execute, Physical / Elemental Penetration; shield Block, Reflect, Damage Taken from Monsters; armour, helmet, legs, boots, jewel, other and quiver lists of their own); not one the item has. It is a normal modifier for the engine and the totals (caps apply) but takes no prefix or suffix slot: side "implicit", listed first ("Corrupted implicit: ...") | tier |
| quality | 8 | quality 30%, above the 20% cap of Rare and Legendary (`ChaosCrafting.setQuality`) | implicit |
| socket | 7 | one socket more, up to 3, past the limit of its kind and rarity | implicit |
| reroll | 8 | every unbound modifier rolls a new tier (by item level) and value | sealed |
| rarity | 4 | one rarity up, Rare to Legendary or Legendary to Divine (the only orb that makes Divine), base bonus of the new rarity, one modifier more | implicit |
| decay | 5 | the downside: one random unbound modifier two tiers down (not below T1) | sealed |

  On a good item 59% improve it, 28% only lock it, 8% are a coin flip and 5% hurt: worth it on an item one step from
  done, a gamble on a finished one. The result is announced like every orb ("Void Orb: <item> is corrupted: ...") with
  the dark `CONST_ME_MORTAREA` cloud (red on the downside). `ChaosOrbs.forceVoid` is the test hook.
- **Persistence.** `chaos_corrupted` and `chaos_cimp` are in `ChaosCrafting.attributeKeys()`, so the guild depot copy and
  the key-list item codec (market escrow and stash without engine patch 0017) keep them; the blob codec keeps every
  attribute anyway.
- **Sources and worth.** Loot weight 2 (chance 1 / 3 / 8 / 160 / 320 per 10000 kills, normal to boss), salvage recipe 125
  shards (a reference price of 50 coins, between Binding and Ruin) and whole-orb weight 1, the Orbs Pouch, the Orb
  Exchange (every crafting orb is listed). Candlemarks may never sell it (`forbiddenIds`). NPCs do not buy it (currency).
- **Client** (overlay only, updater): the tooltip line and the implicit heading (`game_itemtooltip`), "CORRUPTED" and
  the implicit rows on the bench (`game_crafting`), pt-BR strings. No dat, sprite or engine change.
- Tests: `tests/orbs_test.lua` (every outcome and fallback, the weights, every refusal, every orb refusing a corrupted
  item, the codec round trip), `item_tooltip_test.lua`, `market_test.lua`, `conquest_test.lua`, client
  `tooltiplogic_test.lua`. Not tested in game.

**The Orb of Ruin.** Odds in `ChaosOrbsConfig.ruin`, shown on the bench and in the orb's text: 40% the item **improves**,
60% nothing happens (since 2026-10-15, "Conquest Tokens": it never ruins an item any more; before, 45% nothing and 15% the
item was **ruined**, and those items stay ruined). An improvement is (60%) one tier more on every modifier that is not bound
(T8 stays; a new value inside the new tier; the item level does not limit it), else (or when nothing can go up) one **extra
modifier** above the side limit of its rarity, once per item (`chaos_ext`: the side that got it has one more slot from then
on, the bench shows the new limit). A **ruined** item (`chaos_ruined`, "Ruined" in the description, a red line in the
tooltip and on the bench) refuses every orb, the Orb of Sockets included; it can still be used, worn, sold and salvaged.
`ChaosOrbs.forceRuin = "improve" | "nothing" | "ruin"` and `ChaosOrbs.forceImprove = "tiers" | "slot"` are the test hooks (nil in
the game; the in-game test drove them with a test-only talkaction).

**Bound modifiers** (`cb_<attribute key>` = 1 on the item; "(T3, bound)" in the description, "bound" in the tooltip and on the
bench). `removeMod`, `rerollValues`, `rerollTiers`, `annul` and `upheave` skip them; `clearMods` (the plain copy of Erasure)
removes them. The Orb of Upheaval on an item with bound modifiers works **in place**: the bound ones stay, the rest is rolled
again up to the rarity's count (the upgrade levels of the item stay too). The Orb of Fate (a new copy with a new rarity) is
refused on an item with a bound modifier ("use an Orb of Erasure first"). The rule for the Orb of Fate itself: it keeps the old
rarity gamble (stock odds: 85% of the time no rarity at all), item level and quality stay; it is the "risky rarity" orb next to
the Orb of Ruin, no longer a value reroll (that is the Orb of Tempering). **Since 2026-10-22** (owner: "isso só transforma o
item em normal. não aumenta a raridade") it raises the rarity one rank with a new set of modifiers (Normal -> Common ..
Rare -> Legendary); a Legendary item becomes Divine at `fateDivineChance` 5%, else it stays as it is and the orb is spent;
a Divine item refuses it (`maxRarity`). Item level and quality stay.

**Item quality** (`chaos_quality`, 0..30). Every modifier value is multiplied by (100 + quality) / 100 and rounded to the nearest
whole number, never below the value itself: a T4 skill of 3 at 20% is 4, a value of 1 stays 1 (so very small values only move
with enough quality; the larger Chaos modifiers move earlier). The item stores the value as it was rolled inside the tier
(`cv_<attribute key>`) and the value it acts with; Tempering, Reforging and Ruin roll the raw value and scale it again; the
orbs that make a new copy (Upheaval, Fate, Erasure, Awakening, Gilding) carry the quality over. The bench has a quality bar,
the tooltip a line "Quality +9% (up to 20%)". Not scaled: the base attack / armour of the item, sockets and gems.

**The bench's modifier picker.** Every modifier row is clickable; the orbs that are aimed at one modifier (`pick` of the
orb: Binding, Excision, Reforging) are enabled once a modifier they may act on is selected and send it as `mod` (the server
checks it again: it must be an unbound modifier of that item). Rows show the tier and range, a gold "bound" mark, an orange
colour for legendary powers; the item panel shows the quality bar and "Mods 4/6 P2/3 S2/3 B1/2". The orb list scrolls (14
orbs), the Salvage tab's recipe grid too. Nothing else about the bench changed.
**An extended opcode message above 8192 bytes is dropped by the engine** (`NetworkMessage::addString` refuses a longer string).
With fourteen orbs the bench state passed that limit as soon as an item had many modifiers, so the protocol changed: the
bench sends an `info` message when it opens (the orbs with their texts, the reason texts) and every `state` carries only
counts, reason codes, the item and the lists; `sendState` drops the history and then the end of the item list until the JSON is
under 7600 bytes (opcode 232 documentation in `crafting.lua` / `game_crafting/crafting.lua`).

**Sources.** Drops: `loot_config.lua` currency entries with weights 18 / 14 / 6 / 5 / 3 / 1 (Whetstone, Tempering, Reforging,
Excision, Binding, Ruin; the Ember, Crown and Void Orbs are listed above) and chances per 10000 kills per monster tier (the Whetstone 25/180/600/2000/3000, Ruin 0/4/18/80/160 for
normal / magic / rare / legendary / boss); rifts and Omen guardians pay through the same currency roll. Store (Chaos Currency): Whetstone 10 for 20 coins
(5 a week), Excision 25 and Binding 30 (3 a week each); Tempering, Reforging and Ruin are not sold. Weekly bounty
chest: + 5 Whetstones and 2 Orbs of Tempering. Salvage: recipes (shards) Whetstone 5, Tempering 20, Reforging 50, Excision 60,
Binding 75, Ruin 150 (about 2.5 shards per coin of a reference price, the Orb of Ruin priced like a 60 coin item), and the whole-orb chance of a
salvaged item picks them with weights 14 / 12 / 4 / 3 / 2 / 1. Loot filter: orbs glow as before (the filter finds them in the
currency list); an item with a legendary power always glows.

**Achievements.** Bound by Oath (bind a modifier), Fortune's Favourite (an Orb of Ruin improves an item), Beyond Saving (it ruins
one; hidden), Honed to an Edge (20% quality), Legend Reborn (own an item with a legendary power; title Powerbearer).

**Install.** `python3 -I server/tools/install_orbs.py <server>/data [--dry-run]`. `install_all.py` is not changed yet: it needs
a step `orbs` after `crafting` (`'orbs'` in `STEPS`, and `def step_orbs(server, data, ctx): return
tool_result(run_tool([tool('install_orbs.py'), data], 'install_orbs.py'))` like `step_salvage`). Idempotent; keeps `items.otb.bak`; verifies
the written `items.otb`. **Tested in game** (test server, ASan engine build with patches 0001-0011, cropped map, client with the
unchanged live dat): bench with 14 orbs (scrolling), an Orb of Awakening on a plain sword, Binding of a picked modifier
(bound mark, Binding / Fate / Excision / Reforging disabled with the reason), Tempering that kept the bound value and rerolled
the other, Excision of the chosen one, Reforging (T4 -> T5), 9 Whetstones (quality bar, values x1.09), Ruin forced to improve
tiers (3 modifiers one tier up), improve slot (an extra prefix on a full Rare item, limit 2/2) and ruin (RUINED, every orb
disabled), Upheaval on a bound item (in place, the bound one stayed), Binding and Whetstone by use-with without the bench,
the tooltip with quality / bound / power, the store (page 2 with the new orbs, since cut to Whetstones, Excision and Binding), the Salvage tab recipes. Not tested in game:
orbs on a Rift Key (unit-tested), the drops of the new orbs (the loot simulation only), the weekly chest.

## Dark tile set (`data/lib/chaos_dark_tiles.lua`, `data/lib/chaos_dark_paint.lua`, `tools/install_dark_tiles.py`)

Our own dark environment tiles, drawn in code by `client/tools/sprites/gen_dark_tiles.py` (client/MANIFEST.md "Dark tile
set"): 9 grounds (cracked obsidian, magma-veined obsidian, ash soil, bone-strewn earth, wet black rock, mossy black rock,
dark moss, ruined dark stone floor, an animated cursed pool), 48 border pieces (edges, outer and inner corners for
obsidian, ash soil, wet rock and dark moss), 3 walls and 14 objects (dead trees, a dead bush, a boulder, a 2x2 rock
outcrop, ruined and broken pillars, an iron brazier and a standing torch that give light, violet and teal glowcaps,
blood crystals, bones, rubble).

- Ids: client ids 27484-27557 (appended after the last stock item), server id = client id + 3000 (30484-30557).
  `data/items/dark_tiles.csv` is the manifest (ids, names, size, ground speed, otb group / flags / top order, light,
  dat flags); `data/lib/chaos_dark_tiles.lua` maps the names to server ids. Both are written by the generator.
- Install: step 5d. `install_dark_tiles.py` appends one otb node per row (keeps `items.otb.bak` the first time, parses the
  file again and checks every node) and writes the `items.xml` names between two marker comments. A second run changes
  nothing; a server id that already belongs to another client id stops it before anything is written.
- Without the items (or with `dark.enabled = false`) every area uses its stock ids: `ChaosDarkTiles.id(name, fallback)`
  returns the fallback while `ItemType(id):getId()` is 0, and `ChaosDarkPaint.ready(style)` is false.
- Where it is used (`ChaosDarkPaint.plan` / `apply`; styles in `chaos_dark_paint.lua`): a main ground with accent
  variants, patches of a second ground with border pieces around them, loose walkable pieces on the floor and solid ones
  only against the walls, never near arrival, portal or spawn tiles.
  - Rifts (`rift_config.lua` `dark`): walls `obsidian_wall`, hub lights `brazier`; themes Abyssal Rift (`abyss`), Obsidian
    Hall (`hall`), Ashen Crypt (`crypt`), Forsaken Sanctum (`sanctum`).
  - World boss arena (`chaos_constants.lua` `worldBoss.dark`): `dark_wall`, `ruined_pillar` as cover, `brazier` lights,
    styles `arena` and `lobby`.
  - Ascension trial room (`ascension_quest_config.lua` `trial.dark`): `ruined_wall`, `brazier`, style `trial` (nothing
    solid on the floor).
  - Guild hall decoration tier 2 "Obsidian" (`guild_config.lua`): `obsidian_floor` and `obsidian_wall`.
- Tests: `tests/dark_paint_test.lua` (border pieces per neighbourhood, a planned room: borders next to patches, nothing
  solid near reserved tiles or away from the walls; the fallback when not installed; the Lua ids against the manifest).
  Checked in game on the test server: a tier 1 rift (Ashen Crypt), `/worldboss arena` (lobby, corners, pillars) and the
  trial room, with the set on and off, at normal size and with the client's HD upscaling (x2).

## Equipment sets (pair 28) (`data/lib/chaos_gear_sets.lua`, `data/lib/chaos_gear_sets_items.lua`, `tools/install_gear_sets.py`, `chaos/gear_sets.lua`, switch `ChaosGearSets.PAIR28`, on)

Seven themed equipment sets from the owner's own item sheets (client/MANIFEST.md "Equipment sets (pair 28)"), plus three
later-tier sets for level 1000 and up (see "Gear beyond level 1000"): 448
pieces, 64 a set, client ids 33995-34442, server ids 36995-37442 (client id + 3000). Unlike the themed sets of pair 24
these are real gear with stats. **Switch `ChaosGearSets.PAIR28`, ON as shipped**: pair 28 is live on windows-assets b37b983c
(2026-10-15). Off, installed pieces exist but nothing drops them and the transmog catalogue skips their
ids. On: the loot below and the pieces are ordinary transmog looks. Install: `install_all.py SERVER_DIR --only
files,gearsets` (step `gearsets`, after `assetsdecor` and after `vocations`, whose class names its lists use), restart.

| Set | Theme | Levels | Drops from (hunting level) | Bosses (15% per kill) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Blightfang | dark green, venom | 8-150 | Poison Spider, Swamp Troll, Cobra, Scorpion (8-11), Wailing Widow, Rot Elemental, Bog Raider, Giant Spider (34-48), Plaguesmith, Cobra Assassin, Blightwalker, Venom Spider (138-177) | Fennra, Snake God Essence |
| Wyrmscale | green dragon | 40-220 | Wyvern, Dragon Lord Hatchling, Dragon, Wyrm, Dragon Lord, Elder Wyrm, the Wyrmblood (36-104), Black, Mega and Netheria Dragon, Wardragon (163-180) | Shimmerscale |
| Cinderwrought | fire, ember | 120-450 | Hellhound, Lava Golem, Burning Gladiator, Hellflayer, Burning Book, Cinderclaw, Infernal Demon, Hellhunter Pyrarch, Blazefang (132-474) | Pyrevorn, Morgashal |
| Bloodmoon | crimson, blood | 300-650 | Elder Bloodjaw, Bloodfang Reaver, Bloodthirst Bulgeye, Bloodspark Adept, Bloodshade Reaper (326-501) | - |
| Rimewraith | teal frost, spectral | 450-1000 | Distorted, Capricious and Hazardous Phantom, Frost Hydra (406-449), Glacial Hellcharger, Frost Maiden, Ice Lich (612-1000) | - |
| Azure Vigil | blue and gold, holy | 800-1350 | Dawn Strayer, Spirit of Purity, Celestial Wyrm (980-1080; Rimecrown Depths, Slagmourn Foundry) | Ossivane the Gravecage |
| Gildcrown | gold | 1250-2000 | Winterstride, Bloodantler Fiend, Mirecoil Wyrm, Pyrewing Tyrant, Pyre Stork (1220-2000; the gilded owner looks) | Vaelith the Fallen Seraph, Azhkarrath the Chained Wyrm |

The bands overlap, so a character always has a set running and the next one starting.

- **Who wears what.** Every set dresses and arms every class. Armour pieces have a fit read off the art: heavy
  (Warrior and Templar lines), medium (Ranger, Thief and Monk lines), cloth (Mystic and Necromancer lines); boots,
  amulets, rings and Gildcrown's two legs anyone. Weapons follow the stock rules of their kind after `add_vocations.py`:
  one-handed swords Warrior, Juggernaut, Templar and Thief lines; two-handed melee the Warrior line (the Berserker only
  these); one-handed axes and clubs the Warrior without the Berserker (clubs also the Templar line); two-handed clubs
  also the Monk line (its staff); bows the Ranger line, crossbows the Ranger and Deadeye; wands the Mystic,
  Elementalist and Necromancer line, rods the Mystic, Illusionist and Necromancer line; shields the Warrior and
  Juggernaut and the Templar line; spellbooks the casters. The larger half of a melee kind (by art) is two-handed.
- **Levels (fluid).** The pieces of one track (kind and fit, e.g. the cloth helmets or the two-handed axes) spread over
  the band in sheet order, rounded to 5: a set's three heavy helmets of 8-150 are 8, 80 and 150. Each class finds the
  next piece of a slot a little higher, never a big jump. Stats are fixed by the level along curves anchored to the
  stock gear of the same level (`CURVES` in the tool; the stock gear stops growing after level 1000, the curves go on
  slowly to 2000): body armour 7 / 13 / 16 / 19 / 25 / 31 at 8 / 100 / 200 / 400 / 1000 / 2000 (medium x0.9, cloth
  x0.8), one-handed melee attack 16 / 46 / 49 / 53 / 61 / 69 (two-handed +3 and 3 s attacks, as `two_handed.py`), of
  it 35% the set's element; launchers the archery bands' attack (31 at level 8, 68 at 100, 85 at 2000) and hit
  chance, the set's missile; wands 16 / 62 / 85 / 98 / 118 / 138 mean damage of the set's element, mana 2-33; shields
  defense 14-55, spellbooks 8-33 with magic level +1 to +5; skills and magic level in steps by level; the set's
  resisted element on body armour and amulet (2-10%, a weakness of half on body armour), half on helmet, legs,
  shield and spellbook; rings physical 1-4%; boots speed 0-40. Bloodmoon weapons leech life (chance and amount 2-6).
- **RNG decides only the max.** The base above is the same for everybody. A dropped piece is forged like any gear
  (`ChaosCrafting.forge`): rarity, item level from the monster, modifiers and their tiers; the orbs work on it. No
  piece is a unique; any number of pieces may be mixed with other gear.
- **Set bonuses** (owner request 2026-10-15; `ChaosGearSets.bonuses`, only while the switch is on). The sets join the
  item set system ("Item sets") as *open* sets: `S.load` adds `ChaosGearSets.itemSets()`, a plain item is a piece by
  its base id (`S.openById`), any 2, 4 and 6 pieces of one set worn at their level give the tiers (weapons, shields and
  spellbooks count; the same item twice, e.g. in both hands, once; a two-handed weapon or launcher twice). Tiers add up.
  Each tier is about one modifier roll of the tier the band's items roll (T2-T3 for Blightfang up to T7 for Gildcrown),
  so a full set is worth three rolls: below the uniques and the ten item sets of the same levels (Bloodsworn at 300:
  bleed 10% and damage over time 15% at 2 pieces plus two effects) and far below a keystone. Modifier numbers go into
  the item totals before the caps; resistances count only half against players and their summons (`pvpShare` 50; the
  old sets keep 100), the other stats act on monsters or loot only, apart from dodge (cap 10) and maximum health.

| Set | 2 pieces | 4 pieces | 6 pieces |
|---|---|---|---|
| Blightfang (8-150) | Chance to Poison +4%, Earth Resistance +4% | Damage over Time +6% | Chance to Poison +4%, Damage over Time +4% |
| Wyrmscale (40-220) | Fire Resistance +5% | Maximum Health +3% | Fire Resistance +5%, Damage Taken from Monsters -2% |
| Cinderwrought (120-450) | Chance to Ignite +6% | Elemental Penetration +4% | Chance to Ignite +4%, Damage over Time +10% |
| Bloodmoon (300-650) | Health on Hit +8 | Life on Kill +40 | Health on Hit +8, Health Regeneration +10 per second |
| Rimewraith (450-1000) | Chance to Chill +8% | Dodge +2% | Ice Resistance +8%, Dodge +1% |
| Azure Vigil (800-1350) | Death Resistance +8% | Damage Taken from Monsters -3%, Healing Done +4% | Damage Taken from Monsters -2%, Maximum Health +4% |
| Gildcrown (1250-2000) | Gold Find +10% | Rarity Find +8%, Item Find +5% | Damage to Elites and Bosses +6% |

  The tooltip (server `tip.set` for a plain piece, client `tooltiplogic.lua`) and the look text show the set, the pieces
  worn (an open set lists only those), "Active tier: n of 3" and every bonus, active ones bright / "[active]".
  Nothing is stored: the bonuses are worked out from the equipment on every equip, unequip and swap, at login and every
  3 s; the set condition has one sub id and is replaced, never added twice; logout drops the cache and login starts
  from a clean one (a death that keeps the character's id does not keep a stale condition signature); a /reload
  works the same state out again.
- **Loot** (`ChaosGearSets.lootRows`, added to the monster types at startup by `chaos/gear_sets.lua` while the switch
  is on, as the fist weapons): per monster every piece of its set whose level is within 300 below and 50 above the
  monster's hunting level, sharing 0.6% per kill (bosses 15%), at least 0.01% each. The chaos loot layer's extra
  rolls, smart loot (a piece made for the killer's class weighs 3, see "Smart loot"), the Item Finder and the bestiary
  read `MonsterType:getLoot()` and see the rows. A monster or item missing on the server is reported and skipped. No
  talkaction, no shop.
- **Install** (`install_gear_sets.py DATA_DIR [--dry-run]`): items.otb nodes (the importer's group and flags), an
  items.xml block, an Equip / DeEquip pair per piece in movements.xml (slot, level, classes; ascended classes hidden
  next to their base class) and a melee / distance / wand entry per weapon in weapons.xml (level, classes; wands and
  rods damage, mana and element), each between marker comments, rewritten when a number changed; an id with an entry
  outside a block stops the tool. Launchers have no ammunition type: they fire on their own like every launcher after
  `patch_base_archery.py`. `--lua [--check]` writes `data/lib/chaos_gear_sets_items.lua` (levels, classes, stats per
  piece; CI checks it). Tried on a copy of a full test server (`--dry-run` of `install_all.py --only gearsets` and two
  runs of the tool): 448 nodes, the three files parse, the second run changes nothing.
- Tests: `tests/itemsets_test.lua` (the open sets: tiers, duplicates, hands, levels, condition, PvP share, logout,
  login, death, reload, tooltip and look text), `tests/gear_sets_test.lua` (pieces against the manifest, every set dresses and arms all 21 classes inside its
  band, levels only rise along a track, the loot rows and the monsters they name, the transmog catalogue off and on, the
  startup script on mocks), `tools/install_gear_sets_test.py`, `client/tools/sprites/gen_gear_sets_art_test.py`.
- **Prices.** `tools/gen_item_prices.py` prices every piece as plain equipment by its level and slot (the equipment
  formula and the gear scale: a level 8 helmet 140 gold, a level 120 one 8,400, from about level 1000 up 30,252, the
  Wandering Merchant's orb cap), so the Loot Buyer and the Auto Seller take them like other gear.
- **The Gambler** (`gamble_config.lua` `sets`, `K.setEntries` / `K.setCandidates` in `gamble_core.lua`, `P.setEntries` in
  `gamble.lua`; tests in `tests/gamble_test.lua`). While `ChaosGearSets.PAIR28` is on and `sets.enabled` is true, all 448
  pieces can appear in a stock (weapon kinds sword / axe / club / bow / crossbow / wand / rod into the weapon slot,
  spellbook and shield into the shield slot, the rest by kind; no quiver piece exists). The pieces are not in `pool`: each
  pick of a slot that has a usable set piece is one with `sets.share` percent (20, so about 3 of 14 pieces; a slot without
  a usable piece is as before), else a base type as before. The piece is one of the `sets.choices` (4) usable pieces with
  the highest level at or under the character's level (class and level by the installed movements.xml / weapons.xml, like
  the pool), so it is always inside the set's band, drawn with `sets.weight` of its set (10 each, 0 leaves a set out). Item
  level, price and rarity roll are those of any piece. Switch off or `enabled = false`: the stock is exactly the old one
  (the recorded stock of the test did not change). The Item Finder does not list the set pieces under the Gambler.
- **Recipes: none.** The crafting system (`crafting.lua`, `salvage_config.lua` recipes) works on orbs, shards and runes
  only; there is no recipe table that makes an item, so a set piece recipe has nothing to join. Not added.
- Open (owner): publish pair 28 with the regenerated `outfit_anchors.lua`. Not run in a client or on a live server.

### Gear beyond level 1000 (later-tier sets, level gear)

Beta 2026-10-24: "the monsters of the highest teleport hall spots (level 2000) drop the same equipment as level 800".
Cause: the seven art sets end at level 2000 but a monster type has one static loot table (`addLoot` at startup), and the
hall monsters share the base types, so their drops did not follow the spawn level. The weapon and gear tables thinned out
above level 800, and `chaos_class_loot.lua` fell back to the three highest bases whatever their level.

Fix, three parts:

- **Three later-tier sets** (`tools/install_gear_sets.py` `TIER2`, ids 52000-52191, 64 pieces each). They reuse the
  client ids (the looks) of three art sets, so no new sprites. Same stat curve as the other sets. Not in the transmog catalogue.

| Set | Levels | Elements | Looks of | Server ids |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Wintermourn | 1000-1350 | ice | Rimewraith | 52000-52063 |
| Lumenhallow | 1300-1750 | holy, death, earth | Azurevigil | 52064-52127 |
| Sunderthrone | 1700-2050 | energy | Gildcrown | 52128-52191 |

- **Three more Rimewraith legs (O285, 2026-10-28).** The art sets have one or two legs of a weight, at 450 or 1000, so the
  band 700-1000 held two options for the medium and cloth classes (`tools/gear_coverage.lua --check`, 15 gaps once the base
  monsters stood at their pool level). `tools/install_gear_sets.py` `EXTRA_LEGS` adds one per armour weight at level 800
  with the look (client id) of the Rimewraith legs of that weight: 52192 rimewraith greaves (heavy, armor 13, ice 4%),
  52193 rimewraith chausses (medium, armor 11, ice 4%), 52194 rimewraith skirt (cloth, armor 10, magic level 2, ice 4%);
  the stats are the curve's at 800, the same as Azure Vigil's legs. The Rimewraith monsters (Frost Maiden 820) drop them
  and level gear may. No new sprite. The block of the later tiers is 52000..52194.

- **Level gear** (`loot.lua` step 1d, `ChaosGearSets.rollLevelGear`). Every kill at hunting level 700 or more may add one
  piece of a set whose level is within 200 below and 50 above that level. A boss rolls more often. The class's own pieces
  weigh 3x. Config: `ChaosGearSets.config.open`. The window has a top cap, so level 2400 still drops the highest pieces.
  A hunt of 2000 and a hunt of 800 share no piece (`tests/loot_level_gear_test.lua`, `tests/gear_sets_test.lua`).
- **Class loot fallback** keeps only bases within `fallbackSpan = 200` levels of the highest one.

Audits: `weapon_coverage.lua` bands are now 800-1000, 1000-1300, 1300-1700, 1700-2400+ and `gear_coverage.lua` has
`fairEdges` up to 1200. Both count the level gear through `ChaosGearSets.levelDrop`. Two quiver uniques (levels 1400 and
2100) fill the quiver slot. Prices, unique specs, codex, wiki and card texts are regenerated.

## Pack art (pair 30) (`data/lib/chaos_pack30_art.lua`, `data/lib/chaos_pack30_items.lua`, `tools/install_pack30_items.py`, switch `ChaosPack30Art.PAIR30`, off)
Items of the third-party art packs imported into the client pair 30 (import-only; plan: weapons icons, flasks, corpses,
grounds, decoration, buildings, animated objects). Installer part:
- **Manifests.** The importer writes one `data/items/pack30_<cat>.csv` per category (columns of `art_items.csv`; extra
  `group=|gw=|gh=|piece=r,c` for big art cut in pieces of 4x4, `hideout=0|1`, `blank=1` for padding rows). Every file of
  that name whose header starts `client_id,server_id,key` is read (the outfit table is skipped), so an overflow building
  file works without a change. None exists yet: the installer does nothing and the generated files are empty.
- **Ids.** Server id = client id + 3000, allowed 37443..39999 and 40113..65535 (the donor items hold 40000..40112; the
  equipment sets 36995..37442). Blocks (client ids): items-A..D 34443..34758, corpses 34759..34858, grounds
  34859..35158, decoration 35159..36058, buildings 36059..36458, animated 36459..36758, reserve to 36999, overflow
  37113+. Padding rows (`blank=1`) get no items.otb / items.xml entry. An id or key twice, an id out of range, or a kind
  that contradicts its otb flags (weapon not pickupable, flask not stackable, wall not hangable, stump not blocking,
  decor blocking, ground outside the ground group) stops the script before anything is written.
- **Install.** `tools/install_pack30_items.py DATA_DIR [--dry-run]` (install_all step `pack30items`, after `gearsets`):
  items.otb nodes (same rules as `install_assets_decor.py`: identical left alone, same group and flags replaced, an id of
  another item refused, `.bak` the first time) and an items.xml block between two marker comments (name, article,
  description "A <kind> from the pack art (pair 30)."; corpses with container size 20, decay 0, duration 600 and the
  corpse type of their race). Idempotent.
- **Generated.** `--lua [--check]` writes `data/lib/chaos_pack30_items.lua` (key to id, size, kind; groups with their
  pieces for the gallery); `--hideout-lua [--check]` writes `data/scripts/chaos/hideout_pack30_config.lua`, a list of
  Hideout decoration entries (`p30_<key>`, store price 80 / 120 / 200 by size, category by key words, wall items on the
  wall layer, stumps block) for items with `hideout=1`, or by default decoration-block items of at most 2x2, kind decor or
  stump, not part of a group. `hideout_config.lua` appends that list (integrator). Keys are never renamed.
- **Switch.** `M.PAIR30 = false`: the items may be installed, nothing uses them until the owner switches it after the
  pair is pushed. `ChaosPack30Art.decorId(key, fallback)` and `lookOf(name, current)` fall back while off.
- Tests: `tools/install_pack30_items_test.py` (synthetic manifests, items.otb and items.xml; no base server needed).
  Not run against a real manifest or base server yet.

Owner, 2026-10-22: use the purchased monster art, "pode sobrescrever os nossos sprites por aqueles". The art is the
pack30 sheet looks 2237-2311 (client/MANIFEST.md "Pair 30 build"), live since pair 31 and in every pair after it. No

  a file is reported. Run on the base server copy: 9 matched, 9 updated, then 0.
- **The rows.** `apply_monster_looks.py` treats a `base` row on a sheet look like a gallery row: no file of ours may
  use it. The 10 earlier pack30 monsters (`pack30/*.xml` of 2026-10-20, ChaosPack30Art) still spawn nowhere.
- Tests: `tools/patch_base_looks_test.py` (synthetic folder: tint, kit look without colours, the Chaos folder untouched,
  idempotent, missing names), `tools/apply_monster_looks_test.py`. Not run in a game yet.

## Pair 33 cosmetics (`data/lib/chaos_pack33.lua`, `data/lib/chaos_pack33_cosmetics.lua`, `data/XML/chaos_auras_pack33.csv`, `tools/gen_pack33_cosmetics.py`, switch `ChaosPack33.PAIR33`, on)
Wings, head accessories and capes of the client pair 33 (four purchased packs, import-only; client/MANIFEST.md
"Pair 33 packs", "Pair 33 build"). Owner decisions of 2026-10-21: pair 33 approved; head accessories and capes become
**auras** (no engine change) with a store category each; the sci-fi and plainly modern pieces are not imported (the
list: `gen_pack33.py` DROP); the wings' x placement fixed against the body.
- **What.** 92 wings (client looks 2385..2476, wings.xml ids 30..121), 92 head accessories (looks 2477..2568, auras.xml
  ids 33..124) and 89 capes (looks 2569..2657, auras.xml ids 125..213). Heads and capes are two-layer aura things (back
  layer behind the body, front layer over it, client base patch 0006 GameAuraFrontAndBack), so a player wears **one aura,
  head accessory or cape at a time**; the store text says so. A step 2 (two outfit fields of their own, so they stack
  with wings and an aura) needs a server src-patch and a client base patch and is not planned yet. The kit of the same
  pair (looks 2658..2667, items 38093..38607) has no server use yet.

  (`client/tools/sprites/art_import/pack33_{wings,heads,capes}.csv`) and writes `data/lib/chaos_pack33_cosmetics.lua`

  name); CI runs `--check`. Names are the packs' piece names; ids follow ours in the client's look order.

  line with the store's other cosmetics (Wings 200-350, Auras 150-300; placeholder until the owner sets them,
  docs/PRICES.md):

  | list | category | price | count sold |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | wings 3x3 / larger (4x3, 4x4) | Wings (appended after the pair 26 wings) | 250 / 300 | 89 (42 / 47) |
  | head accessories 2x2 or smaller / larger | Head Accessories (new, under Cosmetics after Auras) | 150 / 200 | 90 (83 / 7) |
  | capes 2x2 or smaller / larger | Capes (new, after Head Accessories) | 200 / 250 | 88 (80 / 8) |

  The running "Launch sale" (20% off the Wings category until 2026-10-24) covers the new wings too while it lasts. In

  `client_chaos_charselect/outfit_anchors.lua` from pair 33 (prepared in the same branch as its own commit), set

## Haunted Harvest (pair 33 kit) (`harvest_event.lua`, `harvest_event_core.lua`, `harvest_event_config.lua`, `harvest_places.lua`, `data/lib/chaos_harvest_art.lua`, `data/lib/chaos_pack33_kit.lua`, switch `ChaosHarvestArt.PAIR33`, on)
A seasonal haunted event zone built from the harvest kit of the client pair 33 (`set33 kit`, docs/CREDITS.md; owner
2026-10-21: "Seria um mapa de Halloween/mal assombrado"): a cursed harvest village at night with a corn maze, a
ruined chapel, a graveyard and catacombs under the chapel that lead to the boss crypt, for levels 450-650. **Behind the
switch** `ChaosHarvestArt.PAIR33`, on since 2026-10-21 with pair 33 (windows-assets 1c7c58df; the cosmetics of the
same pair have their own switch, `ChaosPack33.PAIR33`, on too). Switch-on: the harvest rows of `harvest_picks.csv`
appended to `picks.csv` and `apply_monster_looks.py` run (the monster files carry the kit looks), then
`install_all.py --only pack33items,harvestevent,contentareas` and a restart. Off: nothing is placed, the event
never opens, the monsters keep stock looks.
- **Items.** `tools/install_pack33_items.py` (install_all step `pack33items`, after `pack30items`): the kit's 514 items
  and the boss corpse, server ids **41093-41607** (= client id + 3000), from `data/items/pack33_kit.csv`, which
  `--manifest` builds from the things file `client/tools/sprites/art_import/pack33_kit.csv` (CI `--check`), so no pair
  is needed on the server side. Flags reviewed from the draft: walls, fences, corn, big props and closed states block;
  decals, roofs, stairs, open doors and gates, seedlings, circles and the portal are walkable; the open coffin and
  sarcophagus, the dug grave and the emptied coffins block too (`REVIEW`). Light 3 / colour 206 on the 38 glowing
  items, the 37 strips animated. **Decay** (`DECAY`, items.xml decayTo + duration) drives the timed states: pumpkin
  stages 1 -> 5 (90, 90, 120, 120 s) and a woken pumpkin back to a mound (8 s), the seal (breaking 1 s -> open 240 s ->
  sealed), the grave (dug 2 s -> buried coffin; bursting 1 s -> empty 180 s -> mound), the upright coffin (opening 1 s
  -> open 180 s -> closed), the ritual circle (lighting 2 s -> flare 1 s -> portal 120 s -> closing 1 s -> dormant),
  the portcullis, the lantern post, the sarcophagus lid and the tolling bell. `--lua` writes `data/lib/chaos_pack33_kit.lua`
  (key -> id, size, kind, blocking, light, animation; the mechanics' states; the decay chains). A footprint over one
  tile blocks only its anchor (bottom-right) tile.
  `tools/install_harvest_event.py` (step `harvestevent`): **hollow candy** 41620 (the currency; a copy of the stock
  candy, stackable), **sexton's key** 41621 (bone key), **ritual candle** 41622 (candlestick), **hollow charm** 41623
  (ghost charm) from `data/items/harvest_items.csv` (copies of stock nodes: stock looks, no pair needed), and Widow
  Hessa in `data/npc`.
- **Map.** Two fixed plans in `tools/areaplan/events/` (docs/MAP_GUIDE.md "Haunted Harvest"), placed by step
  `contentareas` **only while the switch is on** (`install_content_areas.py` adds the folder then):
  `haunted_harvest` (156 x 132 at 15305, 14700, 7; biome `harvest`) and `harvest_catacombs` (112 x 96 at 15305,
  14880, 8; biome `harvest_crypt`), new biomes of the area planner on the kit's grounds, borders and crypt brick walls
  (`tools/areaplan_build.lua`), dressed by the kit's decoration overlay `areaplan/decor_pack33_kit.json` (merged by
  `area_plan_decor.py` only while the switch is on; off, the two biomes take the stock forest and crypt kits).
  The set pieces and the mechanics are not in the map: `tools/gen_harvest_places.py` compiles both plans (as with the
  switch on) and chooses their tiles into `data/scripts/chaos/harvest_places.lua` (CI `--check`), and
  `harvest_event.lua` puts them there at startup: the corn maze (corn walls on a 3-tile grid, a perfect maze opened
  wherever it cut a tile off), the ruined chapel's crypt stone walls, the graveyard's iron fence, a barn and three huts
  in the hamlet, haystacks, carts, scarecrows, giant pumpkins, autumn oaks and dead trees, gibbets, crypts, altars,
  black candles, jack-o'-lanterns and lantern posts (the lights), plus the mechanics below. Never on a spawn, the NPC,
  the arrival or a portal, no blocking piece on the walk to a zone (but the maze's own walls), and every tile the

- **Way in and out.** While open, a **Harvest Portal** stands next to the temples of Cinderhold and Mirewake

## Item rarities (`data/lib/chaos_rarity.lua`, `rarity_migrate*.lua`, `sql/chaos_zz_rarity_migrate.sql`)

Owner item 87 (2026-10-18): exactly **seven rarities**, in this order: **Common, Uncommon, Magic, Rare, Legendary, Divine,
Unique** (pt-BR: Comum, Incomum, Mágica, Rara, Lendária, Divina, Única). Before there were 15 (Common .. Transcendent).
`ChaosRarity` is the one module that names them, gives their colours and maps the old ones; every per-rarity table in the
scripts is an array of six entries (Unique, where a table has one, is the seventh) read through `ChaosRarity.at(tbl, id)`.
Tests: `tests/chaos_rarity_test.lua` (293 checks), `tests/rarity_migrate_test.lua`, `tools/rarity_stock_patch_test.py`.
Stackable items never carry a rarity (2026-10-20; "Throwing weapons"): the loot layer and the login walk clear it.

**Mapping.** The custom attribute `rarity` (and every column that mirrors it) stays in the old number space 1..15, so items
and engine tables keep loading. Six numbers are rarities of today (the *stored ids*), the others only exist on old items:

| stored id | rarity | old rarities that became it |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Common | Common |
| 2 | Uncommon | Uncommon |
| 3 | Magic | Rare |
| 4 | Rare | Epic |
| 5 | Legendary | Legendary, Exotic, Mythic, Chaos, Eternal (ids 5-9) |
| 10 | Divine | Divine, Phantasmal, Celestial, Cosmic, Abyssal, Transcendent (ids 10-15) |
| (none) | Unique | never stored: the item carries `chaos_unique` |

Thresholds stay monotone in the id, so "Legendary and up" (`>= 5`, shines in the client, `itemrarity.lua pulseFrom`) and
"Divine" (`>= 10`) mean the same for old and new items. `canon(n)` is the stored id of any number, `rank(n)` its place 1-6.

**Saved items keep working, nothing is lost.** (1) Every reader maps an old id on the fly, so the server needs no migration
to run. (2) `rarity_migrate.lua`: at a character's first login it walks equipment, backpacks, purse, inbox and the depot
chest of every town (one container per tick) and rewrites only the `rarity` number of an item with id 6-9 or 11-15 to 5 or
10 (`rarity_migrate_core.lua`); modifiers, tiers, values, item level, quality, sockets and gems are untouched; it is
idempotent, remembered in storage 7102490 (version 1), and a GM can repeat it with
`/lua ChaosRarityMigrate.walk(Player("Name"))`. (3) `sql/chaos_zz_rarity_migrate.sql` (installed by the `sql` step,
idempotent) canonicalises `chaos_market_offers`, `chaos_stash_items`, `chaos_market_history` and
`chaos_market_history_daily` (`UPDATE IGNORE`; the daily price history of merged rarities is not summed). The crafting orbs
and the forge also write the stored id.

**Numbers, before -> now.**

| | before (15) | now (7) |
|---|---|---|
| modifiers on a new item | 2,2,3,3,3,4,4,4,5,5,5,5,6,6,6 | 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 (Common .. Divine) |
| prefix / suffix limit each | 1 .. 3 | 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3 |
| stock drop roll (`ChaosRarity.stockRolls`, patched into `rollRarity` by `patch_base_events.py` step 21) | 43% of gear drops had a rarity | 33%: Common 10.5, Uncommon 8.3, Magic 6.1, Rare 4.5, Legendary 2.84, Divine 0.38 |
| Chaos loot floors (`loot_config.lua minRarity`) | rare 3 / legendary 5 / boss 7 | Magic / Rare / Legendary ids 3 / 4 / 5; `maxRarity` 5; `divineChance` rare 5%, legendary 30%, boss 150% (more than one roll) |
| sell price multiplier | 1 .. 32 | 1, 1.5, 3, 6, 12, 24 (`gen_item_prices.py`) |
| salvage shards (base) | 1 .. 18 | 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 12; whole-orb chance 0.5, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 3% |
| Orb of Transmutation / Alchemy / Gilding | Common-Uncommon / Rare-Epic-Legendary (55-30-15) | Common 65 Uncommon 35 / Magic 60 Rare 30 Legendary 10 / Magic, Rare or Legendary |
| Orb of Fate rarity | up to 15 | one rank up; Legendary to Divine at 5% (`fateDivineChance`, 2026-10-22) |
| Gambler (Legendary or better) | about 13% | about 4% (Common 70.0, Uncommon 12.2, Magic 8.4, Rare 5.4, Legendary 3.6, Divine 0.4) |
| Conquest refinement | one rarity up to Celestial | one rank up to Legendary (`perRarity` 60) |
| craft bonus (`craft_bonus_config.lua`) | up to old Legendary | up to Rare (`maxRarity` 4) |
| Auto Seller | 5 tier bits | 6 tiers (bit 4 Magic, 8 Rare, 16 Legendary, new 32 Divine; version bit 128: an older saved choice has Divine follow Legendary) |

Loot filter thresholds, pouch `minRarity` and the market filter are stored as canonical ids (a saved old id is clamped on
read). The achievements "rarity_7 / 9 / 12" are retired (points kept, `data.retired`), "rarity_15" is "Divine Find".

**Known limits.** The base files not in this repo are patched where they name rarities: the look text of
`default_onLook` takes `ChaosRarity.name` (`patch_base_events.py` step 23), the loot line translates the stock names
(`lootline_core.lua`) and reads a text rarity as a number (step 22), and `reroll_rarity_stats` is skipped for the Chaos
orbs (`install_crafting.py`). Server-built text shows English rarity names; pt-BR names come from the
client `tr()`. Gear set bonuses are not scaled by the value raise.

**Value raise (owner item 78).** Modifier ranges were small; every tier of every Chaos and engine modifier is now 1.5x to
3x higher by stat (the bigger raise on low flat values such as dodge and the ailment chances, the smaller on stats close
to a cap), T8 at or under the cap of the stat and of the engine (attack speed T8 13-15 with cap 15, dodge 5-7 with cap
10, bossdamage 18-22 with cap 30, thorns 120-190 with cap 250, life on kill 160-260 with cap 300; absorb 10-14, skill
7-10, critical 8-10, leech 7-10, weapon element 33-52). Examples before -> now, T1 / T8: dot 2-4 / 20-28 -> 4-7 / 36-48;
cdr 1-2 / 8-10 -> 2-3 / 13-16; experience 1 / 6-8 -> 1-2 / 8-11; absorb 1 / 5-7 -> 2 / 10-14; element 1-3 / 22-35 ->
2-4 / 33-52. The tables under "Item modifiers" are the current ones. Higher tiers keep scaling (tier weights are
unchanged); the old ranges stay in `ChaosItemMods.legacy` and `.legacyEngine`, so an item without a stored `ct_` tier keeps
its tier and its range (`ChaosCrafting.readMods`, `affix.legacy`). Charm ranges are unchanged (only the gear reference
`gearRef` of `charms_config.lua` was raised so a charm stays under the best gear roll).

### Level 500+ rarity (`loot.lua` `L.levelRarityChance`, `L.upgradeRarity`, `loot_config.lua` `gear.levelRarity`)

Beta 2026-10-20: two days at level 500+ and about 30 kills a minute gave orbs and plain gear, no Rare and no Legendary
item. The audit (monster levels, item levels, the 500+ loot tables, `tests/loot_level_rarity_test.lua`):

- For normal and magic monsters (98% of the kills: `monster_tiers.lua` spawn chances 6% magic, 1.5% rare, 0.25%
  legendary) the loot layer gave at most Magic (no floor, bonus steps from nothing): every Rare and Legendary of a
  normal hunt came from the base server's stock roll alone (`default_onDropLoot.lua`, 7.7% of the gear drops Rare+).
  That roll is not in this repository and its result in a live corpse was never measured; the beta's zero says it gives
  nothing there for these monsters, or that the gear never reaches the corpse with it. No level gate exists in the
  layer: item levels (`M.sourceLevel`, cap 150), the waystone and orb gates and the pace thinning were checked.
- The level 500+ loot tables (`data/monster/monsters/chaos`, `pack30`) hold gear at 4-7% a kill (16-20 entries of
  250-375 / 100000) against 23% at the level 380 Hollow Rider, and pack combat keeps it with chance 0.73-0.97
  (`pace_config.lua` `scaled.loot` x `scale.loot`).
- Fix: the layer's own roll by hunting level (`ChaosPace.levelOf`: the monster's level, a generated point's, else 2 x the
  bounty pool estimate). A gear drop of a monster at hunting level 500 gets at least Rare with 4% (6% at 1000, 8% at
  2000 and beyond; nothing below 450; x item find), 30% of those Legendary (`legendaryShare`). It runs in
  `L.upgradeRarity` after the tier's floor and steps, never lowers an item and stops at `maxRarity` (Divine stays the
  divine roll's). Rare monsters keep their Magic floor with the level roll on top.

Measured with the core (`L.simulate` on the real loot tables, the tier mix of `monster_tiers.lua`, the pace factor;
36,000 kills each, rare+ gear per hour at 30 kills a minute):

| Monster (level) | stock roll, before | stock roll, after | no stock roll, before | no stock roll, after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ashmaw Raider (540) | 7.0 | 8.9 | 1.4 | 3.1 |
| Mercenary (670) | 8.1 | 10.9 | 1.6 | 4.4 |
| Golden Lord (880) | 6.8 | 9.7 | 1.4 | 4.1 |
| Vyrm (1180) | 6.1 | 11.7 | 1.1 | 6.0 |
| Hollow Rider (380, under the curve) | 22.8 | 22.8 | 2.6 | 2.6 |

"No stock roll" is the beta's case (the base pass gives nothing): before, only the rare and legendary monsters' floors
gave a Rare now and then (1.1-1.6 an hour, mostly Magic); now 3-6 an hour from the layer alone. Not verified: why the
stock roll gives nothing on the live server (its script is the base server's); a live hunt with the loot channel open
would tell.

## Item modifiers (`data/lib/chaos_item_mods.lua`, `chaos_crafting.lua`, `item_mods.lua`)

Every item with a rarity is rolled by `ChaosCrafting.forge` (drops, rift chests, world boss, goblin, tutorial, and the new
copy of every orb): an **item level** from its source, **how many modifiers** from its rarity, the **tier** of each from the
item level, and a **prefix / suffix** split. The engine's own rarity roll (`Item::applyRarityEffects`) is no longer used for
new items. All numbers are in `ChaosItemMods.config`; tests: `tests/item_mods_test.lua` (catalogue, tiers, item level,
counts, every effect against a mocked engine), `tests/crafting_test.lua` (forge, orbs, prefix / suffix rules, orbs v2 API),
`tests/item_tooltip_test.lua`, `tests/salvage_test.lua`, `tests/lootfilter_test.lua`, `tests/supports_test.lua`.

**Item names** (owner 2026-10-28): a rolled item is named after its modifiers, "Vicious Longsword of Haste". Name = best
prefix word + stock name + best suffix phrase; best = highest tier, then the larger value, then the earlier affix
(deterministic); one side only gives one word. The words are `ChaosItemMods.config.names` (one `{word, top word}` per
affix, keyed by the Chaos key or the lower case engine attribute key; the top word shows from tier 7; prefixes are
adjectives, suffixes "of ..." phrases; a new affix needs a word, `tests/item_names_test.lua` fails without one and checks
the words are unique per side and hold no "orb"). `C.affixName(base, mods)` is the pure part; `C.applyName(item)` runs
at the end of `C.rewriteDescription` (so every orb, forge and quality change renames): it sets `ITEM_ATTRIBUTE_NAME`
and `ITEM_ATTRIBUTE_ARTICLE` ("an" before a vowel sound) from the **stock** name (`ItemType:getName()`, so it is
idempotent, title-cased), marks the item `chaos_aname = 1` (copied by the guild depot and the item codec through
`C.attributeKeys`), and removes name, article and mark when the item has no modifier left. Normal items, uniques,
waystones, rift keys and an item another script named (no mark) keep their name. Existing items get their name the next
time a modifier changes (there is no login pass). Readers audited: market (offer name and search use the new name; the
category comes from the gear kind), item links (name limit 56), tooltips, loot line and pouch line (one id with
different names merges into "2 longswords"), hunt summary (lists the stock name, one row per base), loot filter,
autosell (rarity items go by rarity, not by name), jewelry (name only matters for uniques), guild depot and codec (copy
name, article and mark). Item names are not translated to pt-BR (see "Still English on purpose" under internationalisation), so the
names stay English.

Kinds (`M.kindOf`): weapon, shield, helmet, armor, legs, boots, jewel, other, and **quiver** (the quiver bases of
`data/lib/chaos_archery_config.lua`, off-hand equipment). A quiver rolls only modifiers whose `kinds` name it
(its eight of `chaos_archery_config.lua` `mods`, added to the catalogue by `chaos_archery_core.lua`, and the shared ones);
see "Infinite arrows and quivers".

**Item level** (`M.sourceLevel`, `loot.lua L.dropLevel`). Stored as the custom attribute `chaos_ilvl` (1-150) and mirrored
into `combatPowerLevel`, which the client frame and the stock scripts read; items from before have only
`combatPowerLevel`, which counts as the item level. The level of a drop is the dropping monster's level
(`Monster:getMonsterLevel`; a monster without one: its hunting level in `bounty_pool.lua`, else 1.6 x sqrt(experience)
raised by health / 60, the estimate of `tools/gen_bounty_pool.py`) along the curve `itemLevel.curve` (level 1 -> 1, 50 ->
22, 100 -> 36, 200 -> 54, 500 -> 90, 900 -> 118, 1500 -> 136, 6000 -> 145), plus: Magic +2, Rare +4, Legendary +7 (Divine as Legendary), boss +10;
inside a rift +1 per rift tier (at most +15), an Omen guardian arena +15 more; capped at 150. World boss drops and rewards
are fixed at 145 (`worldBoss`), the tutorial's gear at 5 (`tutorial`), rift chest and coffer gear use the rift boss's
level (else the top of the tier's window) with the rift bonuses, the treasure goblin its area level as a Legendary.
`store` (60) is the fixed level for Chaos-store gear; the store sells no gear today, so nothing uses it yet
(`ChaosCrafting.createItem(id, rarity, ChaosItemMods.config.itemLevel.store)` is the call). Plain gear without a rarity
gets `chaos_ilvl` too, so an Orb of Awakening or Gilding on it uses the level it dropped with. Orbs keep the item's
level (Erasure and Fate too); an item without any level gets one from the item type's required level.

**Tiers.** Eight per modifier, T1 the lowest, T8 the highest. A tier needs an item level (`tierLevels`): T1 1, T2 15, T3 30,
T4 50, T5 70, T6 95, T7 120, T8 140. A modifier rolls among the best five tiers the item level allows
(`tierWindow`), weighted 100, 90, 80, 65, 50, 35, 22, 12 for T1..T8 (higher tiers are rarer): at item level 150 T8 comes
6.5%, T4 35%; at item level 40 T1 37%, T2 33%, T3 30%. The five ranges the modifiers had before (tier = ceil(rarity / 3))
were T2-T6; since the value raise of 2026-10-18 (owner item 78) every tier is 1.5x to 3x higher (see "Value raise" below)
and the old ranges are kept in `M.legacy` / `M.legacyEngine`. The tier is stored next to the value as `ct_<attribute key, lower case>`
(`ct_chaos_mod_dodge`, `ct_rarity_swordskill`); an item without it (every item from before) reads its tier from the value:
the lowest of T2-T6 whose OLD range (`M.legacy`) holds it, above T6 the top; its value is judged against the old ranges too,
so an old item neither loses its tier nor shows a value outside its range. The pair attributes (critical, leech) store one tier for both.

**How many, and the sides.** Rarity decides the count (`config.rarity`):

| rarity | modifiers on a new item | prefixes / suffixes at most (each) |
|---|---|---|
| Common | 1 | 1 |
| Uncommon | 2 | 1 |
| Magic | 3 | 2 |
| Rare | 4 | 2 |
| Legendary | 5 | 3 |
| Divine | 6 | 3 |

(Before 2026-10-18 there were 15 rarities with 2 to 6 modifiers; see "Item rarities".) (`config.rarity.count` / `.sides`.) The Orb of Grafting fills up to 2 x the side
limit. Prefixes are damage and defence, suffixes utility, resistances and speed; a new item is rolled until the count or
both sides are full. Old items keep what they have (an old item of before 2026-10-18 may carry more of one side than today's limit; the
orbs only add on a side that is open). **The Orb of Grafting** picks among the modifiers on an open side that the item does not
have and that suit its kind, **Unmaking** removes one at random, **Upheaval / Awakening / Gilding / Fate** make a new
copy and `forge` it (so the limits hold), **Erasure** makes a plain copy. An item's description lists them:
"Item Level: 57. Prefixes: Sword +2 (T3); Critical Chance +1%, Critical Hit +2% (T2). Suffixes: Fire +3% (T4)".

**The engine's types** (absorbs, skills, critical / leech pairs, weapon elements) have tiers too (`config.engine`), weighed
against the Chaos types in one list (`ChaosCrafting.affixes()`):

| element | prefix | 2 | 2-4 | 4-9 | 7-13 | 10-18 | 15-24 | 20-30 | 26-39 | 33-52 |

(skills: combat skills and magic level; profession skills are `profession`; critical is the amount, the chance part is about
two thirds of it, `ChaosCrafting.specialChance`.)

**How the new ones work** (`item_mods.lua`; all through the same totals and caps as the others):
- *Ailments* (bleed physical, ignite fire, poison earth): on every hit of yours on a monster the chance rolls; a hit
  starts a condition owned by you that deals 40% of the hit over 4 ticks of 1 s (`config.ailment`). Chill slows the monster
  by 30% for 3 s, shock makes it take 15% more damage from everyone for 4 s. Condition ticks never start ailments.
- *Penetration*: the monster's resistance (`MonsterType:getElementList`) counts that many points lower for physical /
  every other damage type, with the maths of the Sunder support (`M.penetrate`, never below 0, immune stays immune).
- *Execute*: a hit that leaves a non-boss monster at or below N% of its health kills it (not bosses, world bosses, rift or
  Omen guardians).
- *Damage over time*: +N% on the damage of conditions you own.
- *Health / mana on hit*: flat, on every landed hit on a monster. *Health regeneration*: N per second, healed every 3 s by
  the equipment check.
- *Block*: N% chance that a physical melee or ranged hit does nothing (spells are not blocked); shields only.
- *Cooldown / mana cost reduction*: the spell side. Through `ChaosSpellEvents` (below) the cost is reduced when the spell is
  checked and the spell's own cooldown shortened as it is set; they add to the Thrift and Quickening supports and stay
  under those supports' caps (30%) and the 1 s cooldown floor.

**Spell events.** `data/lib/chaos_spell_events.lua` is the one `ChaosSpellEvents` table the stubs of engine patch 0008 call
(`onSpellCost`, `onSpellPreCast`, `onSpellCast`, `onSpellCooldown`); `ChaosSpellEvents.set(kind, key, fn)` registers a
handler (kinds `cost`, `precast`, `cast`, `cooldown`) and the table chains them. `data/spells/chaos/_supports.lua` registers
the `supports` handlers: Thrift and Mana Cost Reduction become a real discount, Quickening and Cooldown Reduction cut the
spell cooldown (the group cooldown is left alone). `ChaosSpellEvents.live` turns true at the first event the engine sends;
until then the spell wrapper keeps its fallback (mana back and a rewritten cooldown condition a tick after the cast), so an
engine or `events.xml` without the events works as before. **To switch the events on**, run
`patch_base_events.py DATA --enable-spell-events` after building with patch 0008; `install_all.py` (step `events`) passes
that flag. **Verified in game** (engine with patches 0001-0011, a Ninja of group 1: a gamemaster group spends no mana and gets
no cooldowns): Soulward 150 mana / 40000 ms bare; with a helmet of T8 Cooldown Reduction +10% and T8 Mana Cost Reduction +13%
(the tooltip and the Codex tier table agree) 131 mana / 36000 ms on the cooldown condition, and Banner Call 250 -> 218 mana,
35000 -> 31500 ms, the 31500 also in the client's spell cooldown; the group cooldown stayed 2000 ms.

**Skipped on purpose**: none of the approved stats were dropped. Not done: mana-shield damage (dodge, block, reflect and the
reduction act on health damage only), and a stat that adds the ailment chance to spells that deal no damage to the target
(the chance needs a damaging hit).

**Loot filter, tooltips, bench, salvage.** The loot filter has a rule "glow on a modifier of tier T+" (settings bits 22-25,
`tier`); the rarity data of a corpse item (`x`) is "Item Level 57; Sword +2 (T3); ..." and `t` is its best tier. The rich
tooltip (`item_tooltip_core.lua`) sends `level`, `maxTier`, `sides = {p, s, max, mp, ms}` (mp / ms: the limit of a side with an extra slot), `quality = {q, cap}`, `ruined`, and per modifier `tr` (tier), `sd` (side), `bd` (bound), `pw` (a legendary power)
and `lo` / `hi` (the range of that tier); the client shows "Item Level 57  (up to T4)", then "Prefixes 2/2" / "Suffixes
1/2" with "T3 Sword +2 [1-3]" lines in a colour per tier (`game_itemtooltip`). The bench shows the same per modifier
(prefixes first, "T3  Sword +2  [1-3]") and the preview of each orb names the tiers the item level allows ("T1-T3").
Salvage yields `floor(base x (1 + 0.5 x item level / 150))` shards plus one per modifier of T6 or better
(`salvage_config.lua`). The guild depot copies the new attributes (`ChaosCrafting.attributeKeys`). The achievement
"Perfection" now asks for an item with 6 modifiers.

**Storage and caps on the character** (`item_mods.lua`). Like `base_rarity.lua`, the totals of the equipped items (in a slot
they fit, `M.equippedItems`) are worked out again when an item is put on or taken off (EventCallback onItemMoved, after
base_rarity), at login, on level up (speed) and by a check every 3 s (each player every 3 s; the players are checked in
12 groups by id, one group every 250 ms, see "Game loop stalls"). They live in memory (`ChaosItemModsCache`), capped per
modifier; nothing is written to storages. `ChaosItemMods.playerBonus(player, key)` is the API (loot.lua reads item and rarity
find with it).

**Drops and the engine's pass.** The engine rolls the rarity of corpse items in `Monster::dropLoot` after every Lua
callback, only for items whose `rarity` attribute is a number. The loot layer forges the item first (step 2b) and stores
the rarity as a text for the length of that pass (`ChaosCrafting.shield`); `ChaosItemMods.afterDrop` gives it back as a
number the next tick, and `ChaosCrafting.unshield` does the same for an item that is moved first (`onItemMoved`, autoloot).
Readers go through `tonumber`. Items that leave a corpse before the pass go through `ChaosLoot.finalizeRarity`
(autoloot, Rarity Autoloot, the pouch).

## Legendary powers (`data/lib/chaos_powers.lua`, `data/scripts/chaos/item_powers.lua`)

Twelve modifiers that change what the character does instead of adding a number. A power is a modifier of
`ChaosItemMods.config.mods` with `power = true` (chaos_powers.lua adds them): it has a tier (T1..T8, higher is stronger), a
value, a prefix or suffix side, a tooltip line, a cap, and it **counts against the modifier limits**. It only rolls on items of
rarity **Legendary or better** and at most **one per item** (`config.powers`), through the same forge / Orb of Grafting /
Reforging / Ruin paths as every modifier (`C.candidates` enforces the gate). The value of a tier is the chance of the proc, except
Last Breath (the health left), Bloodrush (percent per stack) and Smoldering Aura (damage per second). The capped totals of the
equipped items (`ChaosItemModsCache`) are what `item_powers.lua` reads; every proc has an internal cooldown (`ChaosPowers.config`)
and the damage of a power never starts another power (a guard), only monsters in clear sight that are not somebody's summon are
hit. A power's hit is a **proc** (2026-10-22): `strike()` raises `ChaosKeystones.depth` and `ChaosSpellFactor.depth`, so the
passive tree's damage, intelligence, the class line and spell factors, keystones, archetypes, supports and trials leave it alone,
and `ChaosPowers.depth`, so `item_mods.lua` rolls no Execute, ailment or life / mana on hit on it. What still applies: the
engine's critical hit, penetration, damage to elites, shock, gems, charms and blessings (like every keystone proc). The origin
stays ORIGIN_SPELL, so the monsters' own events (defences, the hall display guard) see the hit.

| power | side | what it does | tiers T1..T8 | cap | limit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Death Blast | prefix (weapon, jewel) | on kill: a fire explosion on up to 8 monsters around the corpse, 10% of its maximum health, at most 50 + level | 2-3% .. 12-16% | 25% | 1.5 s |
| Glacial Ward | prefix (shield, armour, legs, boots, other) | when you dodge or block a monster's hit: an ice nova (100 + level) that slows 35% for 3 s | 2-3% .. 12-16% | 30% | 4 s |
| Echo Shot | prefix (weapon) | a ranged hit that landed is repeated after 250 ms for 60% | 2-3% .. 12-16% | 25% | 0.8 s |
| Critical Echo | prefix (weapon, jewel) | a critical hit is repeated after 200 ms for 50% | 3-5% .. 18-25% | 30% | 1 s |
| Arc Lightning | prefix (weapon, jewel) | a hit arcs to 3 monsters within 3 sqm for 30% | 2-3% .. 12-16% | 30% | 0.7 s |
| Bloodrush | prefix (weapon, jewel, other) | every kill adds a stack (5, 6 s): +N% damage per stack | 1% .. 4-5% | 5% (25% at 5 stacks) | stacks |
| Shatter Splash | prefix (weapon) | the killing blow bursts onto up to 6 monsters within 2 sqm: N% of the health it took, shared by them | 2-3% .. 12-16% | 25% | 1 s |
| Crimson Burst | suffix (weapon, jewel, helmet) | a hit heals 4% of your maximum health | 2-3% .. 12-16% | 25% | 2.5 s |
| Last Breath | suffix (armour, helmet, shield, jewel, legs) | a lethal hit leaves you at N% health instead (the time of the last one is a player storage, 7101800: once per 5 minutes, also across logins) | 10-15% .. 45-50% | 50% | 5 min |
| Ember Step | suffix (boots, legs, armour, jewel) | a single hit of 20% of your health or more blinks you up to 3 sqm away (a free tile in clear sight with a walking path: never through a wall, door or bars) and burns where you stood (60 + 2 x level) | 4-6% .. 22-28% | 30% | 15 s |
| Hunter's Rush | suffix (boots, jewel, helmet, other) | on kill: haste +40 for 4 s | 4-6% .. 22-28% | 30% | 8 s |
| Smoldering Aura | suffix (armour, helmet, jewel, legs, other) | while you fight (you attacked a monster in the last 5 s) and stand outside a protection zone: every 3 s N x 3 fire damage to up to 6 monsters within 2 sqm, N at most 2 + level / 30 | 1-2 .. 28-35 per s | 40 | tick |

**Not done, on purpose.** *Culling strike* is the Execute modifier already (a hit that leaves a monster at or below N% health
kills it). *A chance to cast a class spell on a critical hit* needs an engine call that casts a spell by name; there is none, so
Critical Echo (the hit again) is the closest thing. *Summons* (a spectral ally and the like) need a monster per class and a
lifetime owned by the minion scripts (the Necromancer's); no power summons.

Engine pieces used: `onHealthChange` on the target (registered by `onTargetCombat`, like `item_mods.lua`; its 8th argument
`critical` comes from engine patch 0001), `onHealthChange` on the player (Last Breath, Ember Step), `onKill`, a hook
`ChaosItemMods.onAvoid` that `item_mods.lua` calls on a dodge or a block, conditions (haste, slow) and a repeating global event
(the aura). Tooltips: the power is an orange line "T8 Death Blast: 13% chance on kill to explode"; the bench shows "Death Blast
13%" with the full text as a tooltip.

**Tested in game** (same test server): Death Blast (fire on the trolls around the corpse, damage numbers on screen), Hunter's
Rush, Arc Lightning (energy on the monsters nearby) and Crimson Burst (+384 = 4% of 9600), Last Breath (a 99999 hit left a level
600 character at 3839 of 9600 = 40%), the totals and caps (`deathblast=25` from a value of 100). Unit-tested only: the other
powers' procs (Echo Shot, Critical Echo, Bloodrush, Shatter Splash, Ember Step, Glacial Ward, Smoldering Aura) and every
cooldown. `tests/powers_test.lua` (305 checks) covers the catalogue, the maths, each handler against a mocked engine, the
cooldowns, the guard and the dodge hook, the aura's fight / protection zone / sight / level rules, the proc guard and the reading
of live items; `tests/orbs_test.lua` the rarity gate, one power per item and the side limits.

**Balance pass (beta 2026-10-22, owner: Smoldering Aura "extremamente forte"; it also killed the teleport hall's display
monsters, fixed in `hunt_teleports.lua`).** Measured with the real code of `chaos_powers.lua`, `item_powers.lua`,
`item_mods.lua` and `passivetree_effects.lua` on a mocked engine (one aura tick on a pack of 8; the engine's crit and the gems /
charms / blessings, which honour no guard, applied as the engine and those scripts do). Compared with the single-target damage
per second of `data/spells/README.md` (C4: level 300 about 955, level 1000 about 2600; level 100 about 450 and 500 about 1350 from
`rotation_sim.py`'s ratios) and the median monster health of `tools/pace_scan.lua` (702 / 1785 / 3885 / 12915, scaled hunts at
1000 about 65000). Typical: a Mystic with a fire tree of its level, a gem, a little crit, one aura item at the top of the best
tier its level drops (T3 / T5 / T6 / T7). Maxed: a Beastmaster (spell factor 1.25), tree and intelligence at the caps, gems,
charms and blessing at the caps, the aura at its cap. Internal numbers.

| level | before: typical tick / target, pack per s, of 1t DPS | before: maxed | after: typical | after: maxed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100 | 123, 246, 55% | 2253, 4506, 1001% | 15, 31, 6.8% | 23, 47, 10% |
| 300 | 494, 988, 103% | 14444, 28887, 3025% | 39, 79, 8.2% | 73, 147, 15% |
| 500 | 943, 1886, 140% | 14706, 29413, 2179% | 62, 124, 9.2% | 112, 224, 17% |
| 1000 | 1771, 3541, 136% | 15097, 30194, 1161% | 100, 199, 7.7% | 224, 447, 17% |

Before, the pipeline put x1.2-2.4 (typical) and up to x8.4 (maxed) on the aura's ticks; a typical tick killed a median monster
in 4-8 ticks, a maxed one in 1. After, a typical character's aura deals 7-9% of its own single-target damage per second to a full
pack at every level (the level cap, 2 + level / 30 per second, is about 1.3% of it per monster); the maxed rows are above 10%
because crit, gems, charms and blessing still apply, and a maxed character's own damage is higher by the same factors.

The other powers, same model (typical character, top of the tier its level drops; 4 monsters in reach, kills per second from
`tools/pack_model.py`, 2 monster hits a second with 20% dodged or blocked, one hit of 20%+ health every 30 s, crit rate 10%), in
% of its single-target damage per second, levels 100 / 300 / 500 / 1000:

| power | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Death Blast | 9 / 21 / 43 / 76% | 3 / 5 / 10 / 12% |
| Glacial Ward | 14 / 38 / 65 / 95% | 4 / 7 / 9 / 10% |
| Ember Step (average; one blink per cooldown) | 2-17%; 46 / 86 / 119 / 147% | 1-3%; 16 / 20 / 24 / 25% |
| Shatter Splash | 192 / 363 / 474 / 477% | 8 / 13 / 15 / 13% |
| Echo Shot (more ranged damage) | +4 / +8 / +11 / +16% | +4 / +5 / +7 / +8% |
| Arc Lightning (more damage) | +6 / +12 / +17 / +23% | +5 / +8 / +10 / +12% |
| Critical Echo (more damage) | +0.5-2% | +0.5-1% |
| Bloodrush (more damage at 5 stacks) | +10-20% | unchanged |

Echo Shot, Critical Echo and Arc Lightning only lost the double dip (a share of a hit that had the tree took it again); Hunter's
Rush (+40 speed for 4 s), Last Breath (once per 5 minutes) and Crimson Burst (4% health, 2.5 s) are no damage and stay.
Bloodrush (+25% at most) is a damage modifier of the size of the other top rolls and stays. Computed with the model above, not
measured in game.

**Live items.** Smoldering Aura and Shatter Splash keep the ranges they had in `cutFrom`; `ChaosItemMods.read` reads a stored
value above its tier's new range as the top of that range (x the item's quality), so a T7 aura of 250 reads 28 and a T8 splash
of 75% reads 16%. The stored value and tier stay on the item (nothing is rewritten; tooltips, totals and the bench all go
through `read`). The other changes are formulas, so every item gets them at once. The aura's level cap applies to every
character: an old item never deals more than 2 + level / 30 per second.

## Veiled modifiers (`data/lib/chaos_veiled.lua`, `chaos_veiled_config.lua`, `chaos/veiled.lua`, client `game_unveil`)

A hidden modifier slot on rare and better drops of the high content, shown as **Veiled modifier** until an **Orb of
Unveiling** (item 32257) reveals it. The orb offers three modifiers of the **veiled pool** (stronger numbers, paired
modifiers, seven effects of their own), the player picks one and the choice is final. Numbers: `chaos_veiled_config.lua`.

- **Which drops.** Gear of rarity Rare or better (`minRarity` 3; `high` chance from Legendary, 5), never uniques, set pieces
  or Rift Keys. The source is the killer's content (`ChaosVeiled.contextOf`: rift, raid, Ascended, Descent runs), the first
  that applies in `sourceOrder`. Chance per item (Magic-Rare / Legendary+): raid 15% / 25%, Ascended 12% / 20%, Omen
  arenas 10% / 18%, Descent from depth 8 6% / 12%, rifts from tier 10 5% / 10%. Kills: `loot.lua` step 2c hands the corpse to
  `ChaosVeiled.onCorpse` after the forge. Rewards: the rift chest (`rift.lua`), the raid boss gear (`raid.lua`) and the
  Ascended spoils (`uber.lua`) call `ChaosVeiled.rollReward`.
- **The orb.** A row of `chaos_orbs_config.lua items` (client sprite 25046, an essence crystal with the multi-use flag), so
  `install_orbs.py` writes it into items.otb / items.xml with the orbs v2; registered with `ChaosCrafting.addOrb`, so the
  bench, the use-with action, the crafting log, the Orb Exchange and the Codex know it. Drops from kills in the same content:
  per 10000 per kill rift 5, Omen 12, raid 25, Descent 8, Ascended 30, times the monster tier (normal 1, magic 2, rare 4,
  legendary 8, boss 40). The raid vendor has a weekly bundle (`v_unveiling`: 2 orbs for 90 Sepulchre Marks, always in stock).
- **Tiers.** Veiled tiers V1..V4 need item level 1 / 90 / 115 / 135; an offer's tier is rolled among the best three the item
  level allows (weights 40 / 30 / 20 / 10). Some modifiers need an item level of their own (`minLevel`).
- **Offered choices.** The first use of the orb rolls three distinct modifiers for the item's kind and level and stores them
  (`chaos_veil_offer` = `key:tier:value;...`); every later opening shows the same three, so closing the window never rerolls.
  A stored text that is not valid for the item (unknown key, wrong kind, tier or value outside the gates) is rolled again.
- **Unveiling.** `crafting.lua craft()` sends an orb with `dialog` to the window instead of applying it (no orb taken). The
  client's choice (`choose {path, id, sig, choice}`, opcode **196**, `ChaosOpcodes.veiled`; free in the reference server and
  client and in every Chaos script, see "Opcode collision check") checks the item's path, id and signature, then runs the
  bench's `craft()` with `{choice = n}`: one orb taken, the crafting log, the community goal, the look text rewritten.
- **Item attributes.** `chaos_veil` (1 veiled, 2 unveiled), `chaos_veil_offer`, `chaos_veil_key`, `chaos_veil_tier`,
