  `chaos_veil_val`; in `ChaosCrafting.attributeKeys` (guild depot, market key list). The slot is not a prefix or suffix:
  `readMods` does not see it, no orb changes it, and `ChaosCrafting.recreate` copies it (Upheaval, Fate, Erasure keep it).
  Ruined items refuse the orb like every orb.
- **Totals.** `item_mods.lua` sums the unveiled modifiers of the equipped items (`ChaosVeiled.totals`): catalogue keys go into
  `ChaosItemMods.totals`' `extra`, so the catalogue caps hold; the hook keys get their own caps (`hookCaps`).
- **Hooks** (`item_mods.lua`): Veilpiercer and Last Ember scale your hits (target above 80% health, you below 50%; together
  at most +40%, `hook.maxDealt`); Gravebound,
  Hexbreaker and Ashen Ward take a share off hits taken (you below 35% / a boss / an elemental hit of a monster; together at
  most 40%); Blood Harvest and Soul Harvest restore health / mana on a kill.
- **Display.** The tooltip's `veil` block (`item_tooltip_core.lua`) in its own violet colour, the look text ("Veiled modifier:
  not revealed" / "Veiled: Wraithstride, ... (V4)"), the market rows (`market.lua addLooks`: "Veiled" / "Unveiled" in the
  row's sub line), the Codex orb page (sources, the pool with its ranges, the tier gates).

| modifier | gear | item level | V1 .. V4 | cap |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Veilpiercer | weapon, jewel | - | +8-11% .. +18-22% damage to monsters above 80% health | 40% |
| Last Ember | weapon, jewel, other | - | +10-13% .. +21-26% damage while below 50% health | 40% |
| Gravebound | armour, helmet, legs, shield, boots | - | 6-8% .. 13-16% less damage from monsters while below 35% health | 25% |
| Soul Harvest | helmet, jewel, weapon | 100 | kills restore 1% .. 2-3% of maximum mana | 5% |
| Blood Harvest | armour, jewel, other, boots | 100 | kills restore 1% .. 2-3% of maximum health | 5% |
| Hexbreaker | armour, helmet, shield | - | 4-6% .. 10-12% less damage from bosses | 20% |
| Ashen Ward | armour, legs, shield, helmet, boots | - | 3-4% .. 8-10% less elemental damage from monsters | 15% |
| Doombringer | weapon, jewel | 90 | Damage to Elites and Bosses +12-14% .. +20-24% | catalogue (30%) |
| Wraithstride | boots | - | Movement Speed +5-6% .. +8-10%, Dodge half of it | catalogue (12%, 10%) |
| Bloodtithe | weapon, jewel, other | - | Health on Hit +10-14 .. +25-32, Life on Kill 3x | catalogue |
| Spellweave | helmet, jewel | - | Cooldown and Mana Cost Reduction +3-4% .. +6-8% each | catalogue |
| Sundering | weapon | - | Physical and Elemental Penetration +5-7% .. +11-13% each | catalogue (25%) |
| Plaguebearer | weapon, other | - | Damage over Time +12-15% .. +23-28%, Chance to Poison half | catalogue |
| Stormcaller | weapon | - | Chance to Shock and to Chill +7-9% .. +13-16% each | catalogue (30%) |
| Gilded Omen | helmet, jewel | - | Rarity Find and Gold Find +8-11% .. +17-20% each | catalogue (40%) |
| Veiled Insight | helmet, jewel | 90 | Experience +4-5% .. +7-9% | catalogue (15%) |
| Bastion | shield | - | Block Chance and Reflect Damage +5-7% .. +10-12% each | catalogue (15%) |
| Briar Shroud | armour, legs, shield | - | Thorns +70-95 .. +150-190, Reflect Damage 4% of it | catalogue |
| Undying Root | armour, legs, helmet, jewel, shield | - | Health Regeneration +18-24 .. +39-48 per second, Damage Taken from Monsters a tenth | catalogue |
| Headsman | weapon | 110 | Execute below 3-4% .. 6-8% health, Chance to Bleed 2x | catalogue (10%) |

**Tests:** `tests/veiled_test.lua` (the pool and its caps, chances by source and rarity, uniques / set pieces / low rarity /
low content excluded, tier and level gates, offers fixed per item and the stored text checked, the orb through
`ChaosCrafting.check` / `apply`, the slot surviving Upheaval / Erasure / Tempering, totals under the caps, the hook maths, the
tooltip block, and `veiled.lua` against a mocked engine: contexts, a corpse in the raid, the window, a stale signature, a bad
choice, the choice); `tests/orbs_test.lua`, `tests/gems_test.lua` (orb counts); client `game_unveil/unveilview_test.lua`
(cards, confirm, the request, the tooltip block, the market tag). **Tested on a live test server** with the real client:
the veiled tooltip, the window (the same three after reopening it), two unveilings (orb count 2 -> 1 -> 0, tooltip and look
text after), Blood Harvest healing 2% of maximum health per kill (+290 of 14506), Plaguebearer's totals (dot 16, poison 8),
an Orb of Unveiling dropped by a kill in a raid context ("Chaos bonus loot of a rat: Orb of Unveiling"), a veiled item listed
on the market (row "Epic - iLvl 150 - Veiled", the offer's tooltip shows the veiled slot). Not run live: the rift chest, raid
boss and Ascended reward hooks (one line each, unit tested through `rollReward`) and the raid vendor bundle.

## Item sets (`data/lib/chaos_item_sets.lua`, `chaos_item_sets_config.lua`, `chaos/itemsets.lua`)

Ten sets of 4-6 pieces with bonuses at 2, 4 and 6 pieces, two per class family. A set gives a build its identity (a bleed
build, a dodge build, a summoner) without being needed: a full set is about as strong as a good mix of rares and
uniques, not above it. Every number and every set is in `chaos_item_sets_config.lua`; the pure part is
`chaos_item_sets.lua` (counting, totals, texts, tooltip block, unique entries, chase rolls), the game side
`itemsets.lua`. No new opcode, no storage, no table: the state is worked out again from the equipment.
Open sets: the seven equipment sets of pair 28 join while `ChaosGearSets.PAIR28` is on (plain items counted by base
id, any 6 pieces reach the last tier, PvP half of their resistances; "Equipment sets (pair 28)").

**Pieces.** A piece is a unique (`ChaosMakeUnique`): a copy of a stock base item with its own name, description and
stats from `data/items/chaos_items.xml` (attribute `set` = the set key; `tools/gen_unique_specs.py` writes it into
`chaos_unique_specs.lua`, and `ChaosMakeUnique` writes the custom attribute `chaos_set` on the copy). A stock copy of
the same base item is no piece; a set key on an item that is no piece of that set counts for nothing; the six old
Embers uniques (made before the key existed) are found by their spec. The base item's own equip rules stay
(`movements.xml`: level and classes), so each set uses base items its classes can wear and its level is at least the
highest equip level of its base items. As uniques the pieces take no orbs and keep their one socket; unlike other
uniques they can be salvaged (`salvage_config.lua` `setPieceShards` = 8, never by "salvage all"); a transmog look
(`chaos_tmog`) does not change the piece.

**Counting** (`S.count`): a piece counts when it is worn in a slot it fits (`ChaosItemMods.fits`), its wearer has its
level and it is another piece: the same piece twice (one dagger in each hand) counts once; a two-handed weapon
(`hands = 2`) counts as two, so a set with one reaches its last bonus with an item less. `item_mods.lua` asks
`ChaosItemSets.refresh(player)` on the path it already has (equip / unequip, login, every 3 s, so a level-up turns a
piece on); a change of the counts is part of its signature.

**Bonuses.**
- Modifier numbers (block, bleed chance, damage over time, penetration, cooldown reduction, healing done, a legendary
  power such as Death Blast...) are added to the equipped items' totals before the caps (`ChaosItemMods.totals(items,
  extra)`), so a set never lifts a cap and everything that reads `ChaosItemModsCache` (item_powers.lua, loot.lua, the
  spells' cooldown and mana cost) sees them.
- Skills, magic level, maximum health / mana (flat or percent): one `CONDITION_ATTRIBUTES`, sub id 7245.
- Resistances (`res_fire` ...): the wearer takes that much less of the element (`ChaosItemSetsTaken`).
- Signature effects, each with a cooldown or a limit and a recursion guard, only on monsters that are nobody's summon:

| Effect | Set | What | Hook |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pyre Bulwark | Embers 6 | a blocked or dodged hit sets the attacker ablaze: 40% of it as fire over 6 s (1 s) | `ChaosItemMods.onAvoid` (now passed the hit), chained after Glacial Ward |
| Hemorrhage | Bloodsworn 4 | a monster that dies bleeding from you passes a bleed (the ailment share of the last hit) to 3 monsters within 2 sqm | dealt (bleed ticks) + onKill |
| Red Harvest | Bloodsworn 6 | a critical hit opens a fresh bleed on the target (0.5 s) | dealt, `critical` (engine patch 0001) |
| Ashen Oath | Ashwarden 4 | a block heals you and party members within 3 sqm 2% of their health (2 s) | onAvoid |
| Hanging Verdict | Gallows 4 | ranged hits deal 20% more to monsters below 35% health | dealt |
| Thorn Volley | Thornwake 4 | a ranged hit splinters 30% onto another monster within 2 sqm (1.5 s) | dealt |
| Soul Siphon | Lichbound 4 | your damage over time heals you 6% of what it deals | dealt (condition ticks) |
| Mirror Grace | Mirrorweave 6 | heals on another player heal you 25% of the amount | heal on the healed player |
| Umbral Recoil | Duskstalker 6 | a dodge gives haste (3 s) and +40% on your next hit within 3 s (4 s) | onAvoid + dealt |
| Pack Bond | Hollowpack 4 | your summons deal 20% more; their kills heal you 2% | dealt (summon hits) + onKill |

The dealt event goes on a target through `onTargetCombat` (as item_mods.lua and item_powers.lua do), so it follows the
same engine rule: weapon hits count after the player attacks the monster.

**The sets.** Level = the level the pieces need to count; the drop sources are below.

| Set | Family, for | Level | Pieces | 2 | 4 | 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Embers of Aranoth | support: Illusionist, Elementalist with a shield | 70 (pieces 70-250) | the six old uniques (helm, coat, greaves, boots, shield, ring) | Magic Level +1, Fire Resistance +6% | Damage Taken from Monsters -5%, Block +4% | Max Health +6%, Pyre Bulwark |
| Bloodsworn Reaver | melee: Berserker | 300 | greataxe (two-handed), visage, hauberk, legplates, treads | Bleed Chance +10%, Damage over Time +15% | Hemorrhage | Axe +3, Red Harvest |
| Oath of the Ashen Warden | melee: Sentinel, Juggernaut, Templar | 800 | visor, cuirass, bulwark (shield), seal (amulet) | Block +5%, Max Health +4% | Damage Taken from Monsters -4%, Ashen Oath | - |
| Gallows Marksman | ranged: Deadeye | 600 | arbalest (two-handed), hood, coat, leggings | Distance +2, Physical Penetration +6% | Damage to Elites and Bosses +8%, Hanging Verdict | - |
| Thornwake Volley | ranged: Ranger, Beastmaster | 150 | longbow (two-handed), jerkin, striders, loop (ring) | Movement Speed +4%, Life on Kill +40 | Thorn Volley | - |
| Cinderstorm Court | caster: Elementalist | 400 | wand, crown, mantle, kilt, sandals, signet | Magic Level +2, Elemental Penetration +6% | Cooldown Reduction +6%, Mana Cost Reduction +8% | Chance to Ignite +10%, Death Blast 15% |
| Lichbound Vestments | caster: Lich, Necromancer | 400 | mask, robe, kilt, phylactery (amulet) | Magic Level +2, Damage over Time +15% | Chance to Poison +10%, Soul Siphon | - |
| Mirrorweave Raiment | support: Illusionist, Iron Sage | 300 | codex (spellbook), circlet, robe, skirt, slippers, band | Healing Done +6%, Magic Level +1 | Mana Cost Reduction +8%, Max Mana +5% | Healing Done +4%, Mirror Grace |
| Duskstalker Garb | hybrid: Ninja, Thief (Shadowfist without the blades) | 300 | fang and sting (daggers), cowl, jerkin, breeches, tabi | Dodge +4%, Movement Speed +4% | Chance to Poison +12%, Damage over Time +10% | Umbral Recoil |
| Hollowpack Covenant | hybrid: Beastmaster, Bone Lord | 250 | mask, hide, fang chain, bond (ring) | Max Health +4%, Health Regeneration +20 | Pack Bond | - |

**Drops.** Every piece of a set from every source the set lists (`sources`):
- World bosses (boss-only `ChaosUniqueItems` entries, added by `ChaosItemSets.register` from `chaos_unique_items.lua`):
  Vharok (Bloodsworn), Nyxareth (Gallows, Duskstalker), Kaelgor and Skaldra (Cinderstorm), the Rotmother (Mirrorweave,
  Hollowpack); chance 8 x the boss tier (0.48% per kill and piece) and the participation reward's boss unique roll.
- Monsters: Thornwake from the rare Wildwood beasts (Ancient Treant, Mushroom King, Mycelium Horror, Elk Guardian,
  Owlbear, Dire Bear: 0.06% per kill and piece from a rare one, 0.12% legendary); the Embers pieces keep their unique
  entries (fire monsters, rare tier).
- Rift chests by theme (`rift.lua` deliver, one roll per finisher, not Omen chests): Abyssal Rift (Duskstalker from
  tier 4, Cinderstorm from 6), Obsidian Hall (Gallows from 7), Ashen Crypt (Hollowpack from 4, Bloodsworn from 5),
  Forsaken Sanctum (Thornwake from 1, Mirrorweave from 5); 2.5% + 0.25% per tier above, at most 8%.
- Chase: the Ashen Sepulchre (Ashwarden from Ulthar and the Sovereign: 2% per boss loot, 5% from the final boss;
  `raid.lua` deliver) and the Ember Descent (Lichbound from depth 8: 3% + 1% per deeper room + 5% on a clear, at most 12%;
  `descent.lua`); these pieces drop nowhere else.
- Dungeon clears (`dungeons.lua`): Thornwake, Duskstalker, Hollowpack, 1.5% + 0.5% per difficulty step, at most 6%.
- Every roll x the player's item find; rift, raid, Descent and dungeon rolls only for characters of at least the set's
  level - 50 (`chase.levelBelow`). Every roll is under bad-luck protection (group "set", +5% of the base per miss, at most x4)
  and any piece can be bought at the Conquest vendor ("Conquest Tokens, the Conquest vendor and bad-luck protection"). `ChaosItemSets.grantChase(player, source, key, ctx)` makes, gives (inbox when the
  backpack is full) and announces the piece.

**Balance** (the reasoning; not measured on the dummies yet). A rolled Legendary or better item carries 3-4 modifiers
of tiers 4-7 (`chaos_item_mods.lua`), a power on some, quality on top; a unique carries 2-4 fixed stats. The pieces get
fixed stats at about 60-70% of a unique of their level (one or two skills or protections, a crit or leech pair on the
weapons), no rolled modifiers. The bonuses then hand back what the pieces lack: the numbers of a full set equal 4-6
modifier rolls of about tier 5 (Bleed Chance +10% and Damage over Time +15% are one T5 roll each, Block +5% a T5-T6
roll), and the signature effects are sized like a legendary power each: Hanging Verdict +20% on the last 35% of a
monster's health is about +7% damage over a whole fight; Red Harvest adds a bleed of 40% of a critical hit (about +4-8%
damage at 10-20% crit); Umbral Recoil gives one +40% hit at most every 4 s (+3-5% single target at 4-10% dodge); Pack
Bond is +20% on the summons' share (a Beastmaster's companion is about a third of its damage: +6-8%); Soul Siphon and
Mirror Grace are sustain, Hemorrhage and Thorn Volley pack clear. So 4-6 slots of a set trade 12-24 rolled modifiers
for about 10-15 fixed stats, 4-6 modifier rolls and one or two powers: level with a good rare / unique mix, below a
perfect one, and every number shares the item modifier caps. Partial sets (2 or 4 pieces) leave the other slots to rares
and uniques, which is the intended mixing. The world boss pieces are 0.48% per kill and piece; a full set is a long
chase, the raid and Descent sets more so.

**Tooltips and the client.** `item_tooltip_core.lua` `T.setInfo` (`tip.unique.set`) and the client's
`tooltiplogic.lua` `L.setLines`: the set name with the pieces that count (e.g. 3/6), every piece (worn: bright, worn
below its level: rust with the level, not worn: dim; a two-handed piece says it counts 2), every bonus (active: bright,
else dim). The title reads "Set ..." in the set green. The client drops every cached set piece's tooltip when the
equipment changes (`LocalPlayer.onInventoryChange`, `L.dropSetTips`), so the next hover is current. Item links and
Inspect Player count the pieces of the equipped ids (no level check). The look text adds "Set: <name> (n/total)" and
every bonus, "[active]" when the viewer has it (`onLook`, index 121). Character > Info & Services > Character Info
shows a line per worn set (command `sets`, `ChaosCommands`). The Codex has a Sets tab (pieces with links to their
unique pages, bonuses, sources and rules, filters family and level), generated by `tools/gen_codex_data.lua`.

**Install.** Nothing new: `install_all.py` step `files` copies the two libraries and `itemsets.lua`;
`chaos_unique_items.lua` loads the sets. After editing a set or a piece: `cd server && python3 -I
tools/gen_unique_specs.py && luajit tools/gen_codex_data.lua`.

**Tests and checks.** `tests/itemsets_test.lua` (luajit and lua5.3): the data (every piece has a generated spec with
its name, set key and level; families; thresholds; real rift themes, raid bosses and world bosses), counting
(duplicates once, a two-handed piece twice, the level, a helmet in the hand, swaps through `item_mods.lua`, the caps),
the condition (axe skill, percent health as 104), every signature effect with the set and the same call without it,
the tooltip block, the look text, the Character Info line, the chase chances and a granted piece, salvage and a
transmogged piece. Client: `game_itemtooltip/tooltipsets_test.lua` (the set block, wrapping, the cache drop),
`tooltiplogic_test.lua`, `game_codex/codexview_test.lua`; `tests/codex_gen_test.lua` (nine tabs, every set). On a live
test server (Thief level 1000): the tooltip at 3/6 and, after equipping the tabi, 4/6 without a new hover; the
Character Info line; the Codex tab; Umbral Recoil fired by real dodges against demons (five times in about 40 s at 10%
dodge) and its label and haste, then the "Recoil" hit on the next attack; a rift chase piece and its look text.
Not run live: Ashen Oath and Mirror Grace with a real party, the raid / Descent / dungeon calls.

**Found on the way, not changed.** Three old Embers uniques have base items with higher equip levels than their
description says (Emberveil Greaves 250, Bloodstep Boots 150, Cinderclaw Band 100) and three are Mystic / Necromancer
gear; the set counts them from those levels.

## Codex data (`tools/gen_codex_data.lua`, client `game_codex`)

The client's Codex (Economy > Codex, Alt+K; `client/MANIFEST.md` "game_codex") shows the item system without asking the
server: its data is one generated Lua table, `client/overlay/modules/game_codex/codex_data.lua`. `tools/gen_codex_data.lua`
builds it from the real data files, loaded as the server loads them (`chaos_item_mods.lua` with the legendary powers,
`chaos_crafting.lua` with the orbs v2 and the gems, `chaos_unique_items.lua` / `chaos_unique_specs.lua`,
`chaos_supports*.lua`, `rift_core.lua` and `loot_config.lua`, `salvage_config.lua`, `shop_config.lua`,
`bounty_config.lua`, `rift_config.lua`, `chaos_constants.lua` for the world bosses); only a few `ITEM_ATTRIBUTE_*`
constants are stubbed. Every name, number and source in the Codex comes from those tables (orb names from
`ChaosCrafting.config.orbs`, drop chances from the loot layer, shard costs from salvage, prices from the store), so the
Codex follows a change of the data once it is regenerated:

    cd server && luajit tools/gen_codex_data.lua            # writes the client file
    cd server && luajit tools/gen_codex_data.lua --check    # exit 1 when the client file is stale

The output has no clock and no `pairs()` order, and Lua 5.3 writes the same bytes as LuaJIT. CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`,
"Codex data is up to date") regenerates it with LuaJIT, checks Lua 5.3 gives the same file, and fails on `git diff` of
`codex_data.lua`, like the client spell data and the unique specs. `tests/codex_gen_test.lua` covers the pure helpers (number
and percent texts, the Lua writer, modifier value texts) and the build on the real data (every modifier, power, orb,
currency item, gem, unique, rift modifier and support present, unique ids, every link and shared section resolvable, eight
tiers per modifier, no old orb names in the player texts).

Lore tab: `data/scripts/chaos/lore_data.lua` (22 entries, English and Brazilian Portuguese: the world, rifts, Omens, the
Sepulchre, the world bosses, the Descent, the deep wardens) is the eleventh tab; the wiki's Lore tab comes from the same file.

## Item finder (`itemfinder.lua`, `itemfinder_core.lua`, `itemfinder_sources.lua`, `itemfinder_config.lua`, client `game_itemfinder`)

"Where does this drop": search any item by name, or right-click one, and see every source and every use. Extended
opcode **155** (`ChaosOpcodes.itemFinder`; free in `ChaosOpcodes`, in the reference server's list and in the base
client's `ExtendedIds`, checked by `tests/itemfinder_test.lua`). No storages, no tables.

**The index.** Built once at startup (GlobalEvent `ChaosItemFinderStartup`) and kept in memory; one record per server
item id with at least one row. Every name is read at runtime from the engine and the installed files, so they are the
renamed ones: items `ItemType(id):getName()`, monsters `MonsterType:name()`, NPCs the `name` attribute of their file,
towns `Game.getTowns()`. The sections and what fills them:

| Section | From |
|---|---|
| Monsters and bosses | `MonsterType:getLoot()` of every bestiary entry (its exclusions: scenery, summons, dummies), child loot included; the chance is the list chance x the loot rate (`rateLoot`, capped at 100%); the bestiary's level (left out when it is the capped estimate) and spawn places, the hunting-area level band of the map markers (`data/chaos_poi.lua`) |
| Chaos drops (first: any monster drops these) | the global drop tables as "Any monster" with "global drop, about 1 in N kills[, level X+]" from the real chances: `loot_config.lua` currency (chance by monster tier; legendary and boss monsters also draw one entry by weight, with its weight share), `chaos_gems_config.lua` gem drops (the quality's best share and the first monster level that rolls it), the Rift Key from monsters (`rift_config.lua` monsterKey, its level gate); uniques (`ChaosLoot.uniqueList()`: their monsters, minimum tier, boss only, season), omen fragments from rift monsters. Before the monster section and first in the tooltip's "Drops from" (live test winpkg-35: an Orb of Awakening from a Rat named only two monsters) |
| Chests and rewards | daily reward and login streak, bounty contracts and the weekly chest, rift chest and completion, Infinity Tower milestones and season chests, world bosses, invasions, arena, battleground, guild boss, the Descent, the raid uniques, dungeon loot lists, treasure goblins, achievements (hidden ones never: they are secrets), faction tokens, the Ascended Omens; quests (the tales of `tales_config.lua`), the Ember Cache, the guild siege, the weekly leaderboards, the community goal token, the referral gift, the class trials, charm drops (`charms_config.lua`), the nemesis trophy, starter kits and level gifts (`newplayer_config.lua`; the Everfull potions of `potions_config.lua` `everfull`), the raid's boss orbs and the raid vendor (Sepulchre Marks), the season pass free track and the season journey chapters |
| Crafted from | the base crafting tables (the global `Crafting` of the base crafting script: station, level, gold, materials), salvage and the shard recipes, gem combining, faction recipes, omen keys, Ascended sigils |
| NPCs that sell it / buy it | the NPCs of the map's spawn file: `data/npc/<name>.xml` (`shop_buyable`, `shop_sellable`, `shop_buyable_containers`) and their scripts (`addBuyableItem`, `addBuyableItemContainer`, `addSellableItem`; scripts with their own trade window: `{id, buy, sell}` tables); the town is the nearest temple to each place of the NPC. Plus the Material Broker (tools, materials), the Wandering Merchant and the faction quartermasters |
| Store and vendors | Chaos store item offers, bundle parts and the service offers that put an item in the backpack (the store pouches of `pouches_config.lua`, the Everfull Ration of `store_food_config.lua`), each with "Store > <category>" (`shop_config.lua`); the battleground vendor (honor); the Candlemark shop (`candlemarks_config.lua`: items and the random gems of a quality); the Mentor Marks shop (`mentor_config.lua`); the Conquest vendor (tokens) |
| The Gambler | `gamble_config.lua` pool: slot and level |
| Gathering | `professions_config.lua` materials: profession, tier, levels, the areas with nodes |
| Used to make, other uses | the recipes above the other way round; guild boss ember donations, faction token turn-ins |

Hidden (`itemfinder_config.lua` `hidden`): server item ids, monster names, NPC names and source names; monsters by name
patterns (dummies, training, summons) also without the bestiary. A source that throws while building is printed
(`[Chaos itemfinder] rewards <key>: ...`) and only its rows are missing.

**Audit** (`tests/itemfinder_test.lua`, live test winpkg-35: the store's Everfull Ration said "no known source"): every
item a config the index reads hands out (any `{kind = "item" | "items", id}`, any `{id, count}` / `{id, n}` of an
`items`, `equip` or `backpack` list, the store's item, bundle and service offers) must have at least one row. A new
reward in one of those configs without a source fails the test.

**Protocol** (JSON `{action, data}`; answers through `Chaos.sendChunked`): `search {q, p}` -> `results {q, p, pages,
total, rows = [{id, cid, name, n, kinds}]}`; `item {id}` or `item {cid}` -> `item {id, cid, name, total, secs = [{k, p,
pages, total, rows}]}` (or `none = true`); `page {id, k, p}` -> one page of one section; `busy {}` while the index is
missing. A row is `{n, d, v, c, i, l, b, m}`: name, detail, value (chance, price), count, linked item (client and
server id), boss, materials. Search: at least 2 characters, at most 40; exact name first, then names that start with
the text, then names whose words start with every word typed, then names containing the text, then names containing
every word; ties by the shorter name. 12 results a page, 15 rows a page per section. One request per player per 200 ms
(`Chaos.limited`, `ratelimit.lua`); a dropped request gets no answer and the window sends it once more after 0.9 s.

**Staff.** `/itemfinder` (items, rows, build time, memory), `/itemfinder rebuild` (after `/reload scripts`: the index
is not rebuilt by a reload), `/itemfinder <text>` (the first results in the console). Group 4 and up.

**Measured** on the test server (reference data, the full map's NPCs and spawn file, the machine under load from other
builds): 3,034 items with 30,092 rows; built in 0.49-0.54 s (monsters 0.15 s, NPC files 0.27-0.32 s, the rest under
0.05 s); the index takes about 9.5-10 MB of Lua memory (measured with `collectgarbage("count")` with and without it).
The spawn file parse (9 MB) takes 0.04 s.

**Client and Codex.** `game_itemfinder` (Economy > Item Finder; the game's right-click menu of an item: Where to find;
a right-click on a market row or a loot channel icon). The Codex has a "Where to find" link on the page of every item
it knows (orbs, currency, rift items, gems by tier, uniques, materials: `items` of the entries, written by
`tools/gen_codex_data.lua`), and the item finder a Codex button for those items. See `client/MANIFEST.md`.

**Tests.** `tests/itemfinder_test.lua`: the opcode is free; texts; the parsers (shop lists, NPC files, NPC scripts, the
spawn file, hunting bands, towns); the index from mocked sources (child loot, the loot rate, hidden items and sources,
duplicates, recipes both ways); every reward source on the real configs; search ranking and paging; sections and their
pages; the dispatch; the engine part on a mocked engine (build from the bestiary, NPC files and a spawn file, answers,
`Chaos.sendChunked` for long answers, the rate limit). Tested in game (one client): search, results, an item with its
sections, section pages, links between items, Back, the Codex both ways, the right-click menu of an inventory item, the
menu on a virtual item, the rate limit (3 requests at once: 1 answer).

**Tooltip sources (2026-10-15).** `K.brief(idx, id)` gives an item tooltip the first two sources (monsters by chance,
Chaos drops, rewards, recipes, shops, store) and, when the item comes only by luck, the best chance per kill (`row.p`:
the monster loot chance x the loot rate; a unique's chance x the tier multiplier of its weakest tier, `pk` legendary or
boss) below 1 in 5. `F.brief(id)` adds the Conquest vendor's price (`ChaosConquest.offerOf`, guarded) and caches per
server id until the index is rebuilt; `item_tooltip.lua` puts it in the tip as `src`, so the client's tooltip cache keeps
it. The client shows "Drops from: Dragon Lord (100%), Daily reward" and "~1 in 500 legendary kills, or 690 Conquest
Tokens" (`game_itemtooltip` `tooltiplogic.lua` `L.sourceLines`). Tests: `tests/itemfinder_test.lua` (brief),
`tooltiplogic_test.lua`.

**Used in (2026-10-22).** Owner, on the Seraphic Charged Stone that showed only its bosses: "Coloque pra que servem".
`K.brief` also gives `u = {n, m}`: the first `K.USED_SHOWN` (2) products of the item's "usedin" rows (every recipe and
exchange that takes it, lowest level first, one per name) and how many other products there are (`m`, left out at 0).
An item used in something but from nowhere now has a brief too (`s` empty). The client shows a dim "Used in: Seraphic
Emblem, Seraphic Bleeder +8 more" (pt-BR "Usado em: ... +8 outros") under the sources (`L.usedInText`). The field is
optional: an older client ignores it, an older server sends none. Tests: `tests/itemfinder_test.lua` (mocked recipes and
the real `data/items/base_recipes.csv`), `tooltiplogic_test.lua`.

**Not covered.** Base quest chests (their contents are items on the map, not data the scripts can read), the rift
chest's random item rolls (any rift monster's loot), cosmetic store offers, and the base NPCs placed by scripts instead
of the spawn file. The chances are the loot list's; the Chaos loot layer's extra rolls for magic, rare, legendary and
boss monsters come on top. The market right-click was checked with the same `attach` call on a test widget, not on a
real offer (the test database had none).

## Gems and sockets (`data/lib/chaos_gems.lua`, `chaos_gems_config.lua`, `gems.lua`, `tools/install_gems.py`)

Install: `python3 -I server/tools/install_gems.py <server>/data` (idempotent, `--dry-run`; `install_all.py` step
`gems`). It adds 35 items.otb nodes and an items.xml block (the gems and the Orb of Sockets). The client needs the
multi-use flag on the small diamond sprite: `client/tools/sprites/set_multiuse.py <client>/data/things/1098/Tibia.dat`
(its default list now holds client 3028 next to the two orbs). All numbers: `chaos_gems_config.lua`; tests:
`tests/gems_test.lua` (ids, effects, socket counts, socketing, totals and caps, description, the Orb of Sockets and the
other orbs, combining, drop and reward rolls, and `gems.lua` against a mocked engine).

**Items.** Seven gem types in five tiers, Chipped, Flawed, Polished, Flawless and Perfect. Each type and tier has its
own server id, 32001..32035 = 32001 + (type - 1) x 5 + (tier - 1): ruby 32001-05, sapphire 32006-10, emerald 32011-15,
amethyst 32016-20, topaz 32021-25, diamond 32026-30, onyx 32031-35. They are new items.otb nodes, each a copy of the
stock node of its sprite (same group and flags, plus "useable" for use-with). So the client needs no new sprite. Chipped
to Polished use the stock small gem (ruby 3030, sapphire 3029, emerald 3032, amethyst 3033, topaz 9057, diamond 3028,
onyx chip 22193); Flawless and Perfect ruby, sapphire, emerald and amethyst use the small enchanted gems (676, 675, 677,
678). Gems stack per tier, NPCs do not buy them as stock gems, and nothing in the stock data knows the ids. The dark
tile set uses 30484..30557 (client id + 3000), so the two id ranges stay apart. The Orb of Sockets is the unused
stackable use-with rune stone 24692 (named by the installer, like the crafting orbs).

**Orb of Sockets look** (`socketOrb.look` / `useLook`, pair 38, 2026-10-22). Owner: "Coloque arte de orb de verdade. Não
use as runas para isso. Deixe os sprites de runa só para as runas." The rune stone node 24692 drew client 22036, whose
only sprite (1317) is the great fireball rune's (client 3191): in the bags, the Orbs Pouch and its tooltip the orb was
a red rune stone. `install_gems.py` now sets that node's client id to 38641, our own orb (blue glass, a gold band, three
sockets lit violet, cyan and green; `client/tools/sprites/gen_orb_items_art.py`, client/MANIFEST.md "Orb looks").
Only the client id attribute changes (stackable, useable, the rest stay); the new thing copies 22036's dat flags. The
rune keeps its sprite. Every other orb of the loot list and the bench was checked against the 134 rune things of pair
37: no shared sprite and no near picture, so none else changed. A client older than pair 38 draws nothing for the orb:
ship pair 38 first. Rollback: `useLook = false` and the installer again (22036 back, byte for byte). Test:
`tools/install_gems_test.py`.

**Own looks** (`ownLook`, on since 2026-10-14): animated looks of our own for every gem and tier, client 33905-33939 =
`lookFirst` + (type - 1) x 5 + tier - 1 (client/tools/sprites/gen_gem_art.py, from the owner's gem set; client/MANIFEST.md
"Gem looks"). In things_custom25, on windows-assets at ebe1b2b2. Install step with the switch on:
`ownLook = true` in `chaos_gems_config.lua`, `python3 -I server/tools/install_gems.py <server>/data` (rewrites the 35
nodes with the new client ids, the rest of each node stays the stock gem's), restart. `ChaosGems.clientIdOf` follows
the switch. Rollback: false and the installer again (byte-identical to before). Test: `tools/install_gems_test.py`.
**Fixed 2026-10-16: own-look nodes are animated.** The own looks have 9 phases, so the client (GameItemAnimationPhase)
reads a phase byte after every gem; 27 of the 35 nodes were copies of still stock gems without `FLAG_ANIMATION`, so the
server sent no such byte and every packet holding one of those gems came out one byte short for the client:
"ProtocolGame parse message exception (126 bytes, 1 unread, last opcode is 0x6e ...): InputMessage eof reached"
(the owner opened a Loot Bag holding gems; the client drops the rest of that packet, the container never opens, and a
map or tile packet with such a gem on the ground is lost the same way). Second symptom (owner 2026-10-16, "the loot
bag and the backpack are conflicting": two windows titled "Backpack" with mixed loot): opening the Loot Bag in the
same window as a backpack, the server already holds the Loot Bag under that window's container id but the client drops
the open packet and keeps showing the backpack there; every later add / update / remove of the Loot Bag's slots then
lands in the "Backpack" window, and a move from it acts on the Loot Bag's slots. Same fix; the server never picks a
container id itself (the client asks for a free one, or the window's own one for "same window"). `install_gems.py` now sets `FLAG_ANIMATION` on
every own-look node (stock looks keep the stock flags); `install_gems_test.py` checks it and that every row of
`client/tools/sprites/art_import/gems.csv` has more than one phase. **Servers: run `install_gems.py` (or
`install_all.py --only gems`) again and restart** ("items.otb: 27 gem nodes updated" on the 2026-10-15 base).
Guard for any item: `python3 -I server/tools/check_item_wire.py <server>/data/items/items.otb <pair>/Tibia.dat` compares
the bytes the server writes per item (count or fluid byte, phase byte) with what the client reads (stackable / quiver /
fluid / splash, more than one phase); on things_custom28 with the fixed items.otb: 31147 nodes, 0 disagree (27 before).
Rules tested by `tools/check_item_wire_test.py` (CI).
The Codex gem pages and the wiki icons show the new art already (images, not sprites).

**Sockets on an item**: custom attributes `chaos_sockets` (count) and `chaos_gem1..3` (the gem's server id). The most
sockets is the lower of two limits. By kind: one-handed weapon 2, two-handed weapon 3, armour 3, shield, helmet and
legs 2, boots, amulets, rings and other gear 1. By rarity: none, Common-Rare 1; Legendary and Divine 2;
Unique 3 (`chaos_gems_config.lua rarityMax`). Sockets come from:
- drops: the Chaos loot layer (`loot.lua` step 2b) rolls them on every gear drop with a rarity. Weights for 0/1/2/3 by
  rarity (Common .. Divine): 80/18/2/0, 75/22/3/0, 70/25/5/0, 60/30/9/1, 45/35/16/4, 25/40/25/10, then capped by the item's maximum. The
  text is written once the engine's rarity pass is done (`ChaosItemMods.afterDrop`).
- the **Orb of Sockets** (eighth orb on the bench, use-with like the others): a new count from at least the number of
  socketed gems up to the item's maximum, weights 50/35/15 for 1/2/3. Gems stay and move to the front. It is refused
  when nothing could change. It drops from the loot layer (8/60/250/1000/1500 per 10000 kills, normal to boss) and is made from rune shards
  (Salvage, 60 shards); the store does not sell it.

Sockets and gems survive every orb that remakes an item (Awakening, Gilding, Erasure, Upheaval, Fate: `C.recreate`
copies them) and the loot layer's rolled copy (`ChaosLoot.finalizeRarity`). **Uniques** have one fixed socket
(`uniqueSockets`) without the attribute: gems can be socketed and taken out, no orb changes the count. The socket shows
in the look text from the moment the unique is made (`ChaosMakeUnique` is wrapped by `gems.lua`).

**The effects**: one per gem, by the group of the item it sits in (weapon; jewellery = amulets and rings; armour =
everything else, shields included). The values below are for Chipped / Flawed / Polished / Flawless / Perfect. The cap is the
most a character gets from all gems.

| gem | in a weapon | in armour | in jewellery |
|---|---|---|---|
| ruby | Fire Damage +2/4/6/9/12% | Max Health +20/45/80/130/200 | Fire Resistance +2/3/4/6/8% |
| sapphire | Ice Damage +2/4/6/9/12% | Max Mana +15/35/60/100/150 | Ice Resistance +2/3/4/6/8% |
| emerald | Earth Damage +2/4/6/9/12% | Movement Speed +1/1/2/2/3% | Earth Resistance +2/3/4/6/8% |
| amethyst | Critical Chance +1/1/2/3/3%, Critical Hit +5..25% | Death Resistance +2/3/4/6/8% | Death Damage +2/4/6/9/12% |
| topaz | Attack Speed +1/2/3/4/5% | Energy Resistance +2/3/4/6/8% | Energy Damage +2/4/6/9/12% |
| diamond | Holy Damage +2/4/6/9/12% | Elemental Resistances +1/1/2/3/4% (fire, ice, earth, death, energy, holy) | Holy Resistance +2/3/4/6/8% |
| onyx | Life Leech Chance +1/3/4/5/7%, Amount +1..5% | Physical Resistance +1/1/2/3/4% | Physical Damage +1/2/3/4/6% |

Caps: element damage 40% each, physical damage 12%, element resistances 30% each, physical resistance 10%, max health
2000, max mana 1500, critical 10% chance / 75% damage, life leech 20% / 15%, movement speed 12% (together with the
Movement Speed modifier, whose cap it shares), attack speed 15% on the weapon (modifier and gems together; 20% before 2026-10-28).
An offensive theme (critical, life leech, attack speed) sits in weapons with the gem's element damage in jewellery;
otherwise the element damage sits in weapons and the theme in armour.

**Applied on the same path as the item modifiers** (`item_mods.lua` works out `ChaosGems.totals` of the equipped items
whenever it works out the modifiers: equip / unequip, login, the 3 s check), handed to `ChaosGems.applyTotals`
(`gems.lua`):
- max health, max mana, critical chance and damage, life leech: one `CONDITION_ATTRIBUTES`, sub id 7240, replaced when
  the values change.
- element and physical damage: onHealthChange on the target, registered by onTargetCombat: hits by the player or their
  summons of that combat type, primary and secondary part.
- resistances: onHealthChange on the player.
- movement speed: added to the Chaos modifier in `item_mods.lua`.
- attack speed: the weapon's own attack interval (`ChaosItemMods.syncAttackSpeed`, modifier and topaz together).

Nothing is stored; the totals live in memory (`ChaosGemsCache`).

**Using gems** (all by "Use with" on the gem, `gems.lua`):
- on gear you carry (backpack or equipped): into the first free socket. The description, the weapon's interval and,
  for equipped gear, the totals are updated at once. An item without sockets says that an Orb of Sockets gives some;
  a full item points at the bench.
- on a gem of the same kind and quality: three become one of the next quality (Perfect does not combine). Different
  gems are refused. The target may be the used stack itself (right-click the stack, then click it again). The gems
  may be carried (equipment, backpack, bags, pouches) or sit in the purse (store inbox), the depot inbox or the depot
  chest: the engine's `player:getItemCount` / `removeItem` walk only inventory slots 1-10 and their containers, so
  `G.combine(player, id, used, target)` counts the clicked stacks outside that walk itself, takes them first and the
  rest from what is carried. Everything is counted before anything is taken; a removal that fails gives back what
  was taken. Refused: gems on the ground or someone else's ("Combine gems you own ..."), a locked stack (the item
  lock), fewer than three. The new gem goes to the backpack, else the depot inbox, else the player's feet (never
  lost; `G.give`, also used by Remove). The counting and taking live in `data/scripts/chaos/combine_core.lua`
  (`ChaosCombine.take`, `placeOf`, `give`), shared with the support runes (`supports.lua` `S.combine`, SUPPORTS.md).
  How to combine with the mouse, in the plain-use message (`G.COMBINE_HOW`), the items.xml text (`install_gems.py`;
  run it again to update a server) and the Codex: "use the stack, then left-click the same stack" (a right-click in
  the classic controls brings up the crosshair; a second right-click only cancels it). **Fixed 2026-10-21** (player report: "gem combine does not work", a stack
  used on itself): a stack in the purse or the depot was refused with "You need three gems" whatever its count,
  since the engine's count never sees those boxes. Tests: `tests/gems_test.lua` "combining against the engine's
  item walk".
- plain use: the gem's three effects and how to use it.

Every action is logged in `chaos_crafting_log` (the bench's "Recent crafts").

**Taking gems out** (crafting bench, Economy > Crafting Bench: the sockets are listed under the modifiers, extended opcode 232 action
`gem`): **Remove** returns the gem for 2000 / 6000 / 20000 / 60000 / 200000 gold by tier (bank first, then the
backpack); **Shatter** is free and destroys it. The 3-to-1 combining, the removal cost and shattering are the gem sinks.

**Description**: one section at the end, "Sockets (1/2): Flawless Ruby (Fire Damage +9%), empty." After the engine's
text it follows a full stop. `C.rewriteDescription` strips it and writes it again last, so it is never doubled. Items
without a rarity keep their own text (the items.xml description) in front. The loot filter's tooltip data (`x`) gets
"Sockets 1/2: ..." after the modifiers. The bench shows each socket: gem, effect, Remove (cost) and Shatter.

**Drops and rewards** (`chaos_gems_config.lua` `drop` / `rewards`):
- monster kills (`loot.lua` step 3b): chance per 10000 kills 25 / 150 / 500 / 1500 / 3000 (normal / magic / rare /
  legendary / boss), times the loot layer's rate and item find. Tier weights by the monster's level (the killer's when
  it has none): up to 49: 85/15/0/0/0, 149: 60/32/8/0/0, 299: 35/40/20/5/0, 599: 15/35/35/13/2, above: 5/25/40/24/6.
  Legendary monsters have a 25% chance, bosses 40%, that the gem is one tier better. Simulated in the engine (100,000
  kills each): normal 0.25%, magic 1.5%, rare 5%, legendary 15%, boss 30%. At level 700, a boss drops
  959/5020/10129/9140/4777 per tier.
- bounty contracts: a gem at 30% (hunt), 50% (elite), 100% (boss); tier weights by the level band (80/20 for band 1
  up to 0/10/40/38/12 for band 6). The weekly chest has 2 gems of the band's weights.
- rift chest: 1 + 0.2 x tier gems (the fraction is the chance of one more). Tier weights by rift tier: up to 3:
  50/40/10, up to 6: 20/45/30/5, up to 10: 5/30/45/17/3, above: 0/15/45/30/10.
- world boss: every rewarded participant gets 2 + 4 x share gems, weights 0/10/45/35/10 (`W.computeRewards`, so
  offline delivery includes them).

**Tested in game** (test server with the cropped map, client with the patched dat):
- socketing by mouse (right click on the gem, then the item: "Perfect Ruby socketed into magic sword (socket 1): Fire
  Damage +12%.") and by `g_game.useWith`; a full item refused.
- the look text of socketed gear and of a gem.
- equipping armour with two Perfect Rubies and a Perfect Diamond: max health 8487 -> 8887, critical from the armour's
  own rarity plus the amethyst; taking it off: back to 8487.
- 200 fire damage from the player on a Behemoth (through `Combat:execute`): 168 -> 188 with a Perfect Ruby in the
  weapon (+12%); 300 fire damage taken: 250 -> 230 with a Perfect Ruby in the amulet (-8%).
- combining three Chipped Rubies; on the bench, Remove (200k from the bank; refused without the gold) and Shatter.
- the Orb of Sockets on the bench (3 -> 1, the gem kept and moved to the front) and by use-with (an axe with no
  sockets got 1). The Orb of Upheaval on socketed armour: sockets and gem kept.
- a unique: one socket, a gem socketed, the orb refused.
- gem drops with a raised chance, sockets on rarity drops (5 of 8 gear drops of 100 demons had sockets, written after
  the engine's text), the rift chest and world boss rewards with gems.

The damage test used `Combat:execute` (the spell path, which runs onTargetCombat and so registers the event);
`doTargetCombatHealth` skips onTargetCombat (see "Open decisions" in ROADMAP.md) and showed no bonus until the event was
registered by hand. Not tested in game: a bounty payout and the weekly chest (unit tests of the rolls only), melee hits,
life leech and attack speed from gems in a fight.

## Vocation Trials (`trials*.lua`, `TRIALS.md`, client `game_passivetree/trials*.lua`)

**Limits** (`trials_config.lua` `limits`, "Instance limits"): 8 / 9 / 10 minutes by tier (unchanged) with warnings at 2 min, 1 min and 10 s; time up loses the trial (nothing is lost, the 60 s cooldown); at most 8 chambers, the wait and the waiting line when all are in use; a staff close ends a trial without a cooldown.

A layer on the passive tree: per vocation (21: 7 base classes and both ascensions of each, in 7 trial families) a
solo runtime-built challenge arena (x / y 9000+, 8 / 9 / 10 minutes, 3 / 3 / 2 lives, Normal / Cruel / Merciless at level
100 / 250 / 400) and 3 pairs of special nodes (126 in all); each cleared tier opens one pair, a character holds one node
per pair. The full design table (every trial, every pair with its numbers; no node has a downside since the owner decision, and Avatar of Iron is a Berserker node, the Juggernaut got Wall Unbroken) is `server/data/scripts/chaos/TRIALS.md`.
Entry: the Keeper of Trials NPC (temple) or the Trials button of the Passive Tree window (opcode 65 `extraActions`); the
run HUD is the rift HUD (opcode 228). A lethal hit costs a life instead of killing (no experience or item loss). First
clear: bank gold, Orbs of Upheaval and Fate and the pair; repeat: 1 Trial Token and a small reward (5 a week, unused ones
bank up to 15: `repeatBankWeeks` 3, storage 7101766, `M.repeatState`, 2026-10-15; the week is
the shared Monday 06:00 one, `ChaosBounty.week`, key YYYYMMDD of its Monday in storage 7101761: the old day-of-year keys
YYYYWW made 31 Dec a one-day week 53 and never match a new key, so the first clear after the switch counts from 0). Switching a
pick or giving a pair up (the Clear button of each pair row in the Trials window sends `trialChoose` with side 0, `clear {can, why}` in the state): 1 Trial Token + level x 250 gold, not in combat or during a run. A node's max health / mana (`vitality`, `spirit`, e.g. Steelblood +8%) is kept outside the tree's +50% cap (`trialVitality` / `trialSpirit` in the bonus table, like the Paragon share): at the cap it gave nothing (2026-10-20). Special nodes use their own
combat code (`trials_effects.lua`, about 40 keys, damage dealt bounded 0.25-2.5 and taken 0.3-2.0), are separate from the
passive points, survive every tree reset, and are not in build codes. Ten nodes use spell cost / cooldown keys and need
engine patch 0008. Crash recovery: a marker storage moves the character out at the next login. Tests:
`tests/trials_test.lua`, `trials_flow_test.lua`, client `trialsmath_test.lua`; tested in game (one Berserker slice:
runs, life loss, first clear, choose / refuse / switch, tree reset, crash recovery). Not exercised in game: the seal,
mark and fire mechanics and the evade / reflect / mana shield nodes. Balance: boss health (`hp` per tier) and the thrall
hit rate are first guesses.

**Marks and kill counts (O187, 2026-10-24).** Beta report: "In the Ninja's Merciless trial, the Marked Cutthroat keeps
reviving, so it is impossible to count the kills". A mark (the thief family's fast target) used to be removed after
`markSeconds` (16 / 13 / 10) whether or not it was being fought, and came back at full health for 20 s of the clock, without
a limit; its health is a share of the boss health (Merciless level 400: 7020 health, so 700 damage a second to kill it in
10 s). Now `ChaosTrialsCore.markStep` runs the clock: a tick that finds the mark lower than the last one starts the clock
again, an untouched mark flees at most `markMaxFlees` (3) times in a run and then stays until it dies. A mark that
vanishes without its death event is counted as a kill, `stageKills` fills the counter when the marks are done, a spawn
that fails does not use up a mark number, and a necromancer thrall that stood up again is not counted a second time.
`ChaosTrials.runAt(pos)` / `isTrialMonster(creature)` (like `ChaosDungeons.runAt`) keep the ambush copy
(`monster_tiers.lua`, also one queued before the trial opened), the tier roll and the Treasure Goblin out of a running
chamber, and the map's own respawn is refused there. Not on a live server: the thralls were already skipped by the tier
script (`skipTiers`), so an ambush was not the cause; the clock rule is. Tests: `tests/trials_test.lua` (block O187
reproduces the old rule with the numbers above), `trials_flow_test.lua`, `monster_tiers_test.lua`.

## Salvage (`salvage.lua`, `salvage_core.lua`, `salvage_config.lua`, `tools/install_salvage.py`, client `game_crafting`)


**Recycling (2026-10-20).** The recipe rows of the bench also work backwards: Shift+click a row turns the orbs of that kind in the backpack (up to 100 a click) into shards at `recycleShare` (0.4) of the recipe cost, rounded down (`K.recycleShards`, action `recycle`; always fewer shards than making one costs). Beta: a tester held ~2000 orbs nobody could use.

**Uniques (2026-10-15).** A unique on the bench salvages for Conquest Tokens: 10% of its Conquest vendor price (at least
25) plus `uniqueShards` (4) rune shards; a set piece keeps its `setPieceShards` (8) and gets the tokens too. The
character is saved before the tokens go into the database. "Salvage all" never takes a unique. See "Conquest Tokens,
the Conquest vendor and bad-luck protection".

Rolled gear you do not want becomes crafting currency instead of NPC gold. A **Salvage** tab on the crafting bench
(Economy > Crafting Bench, then the tab; or Economy > Salvage, or use a Rune Shard) breaks an item with a rarity into **Rune Shards**, with a
small chance of a whole orb, and turns shards into the existing orbs. Every number is in `salvage_config.lua`; the pure
rules are `salvage_core.lua` (tests: `tests/salvage_test.lua`, which also drives `salvage.lua` against a mocked engine).

**Install.** `python3 -I server/tools/install_salvage.py <server>/data [--dry-run]` (idempotent; `install_all.py` step
`salvage`, after `gems`). It adds one items.otb node, the **rune shard** (server id **32051**), a copy of the stock node
of the violet crystal shard (18414, client 16120: stackable, so the client needs no change), and its items.xml entry
between marker comments. Without it the bench says salvage is not installed and refuses. It also guards the stock rarity
remover against locked items (see "The item lock"). No SQL: salvage writes to
`chaos_crafting_log`.

**What can be salvaged.** Gear with a rarity, in the backpack or a bag inside it (never equipped, never the ground),
not locked, not unique, no gem in a socket (take gems out first on the bench: Remove for gold or Shatter; empty sockets
are fine and pay a shard each). Normal items, Rift Keys, stacks and containers are refused. **Uniques are never
salvaged** (`allowUniques = false`): they are chase items with their own drop table and no rarity tier to price them,
and a duplicate is still worth keeping for a season or a trade.

**Yield** (deterministic, so the preview is exact):
- shards = floor(base x (1 + 0.5 x position of the item level in its rarity's window)) + 1 per Chaos modifier + 1 per
  empty socket. The window of a rarity is the one of its first old id (10r-9..10r), so the top of the window gives up to +50%.
- base by rarity (Common .. Divine): 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 12 (a Divine at the top of its window: 18).
- whole orb on top, per item: 0.5, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 3%; which orb by weight:
  Awakening 35, Upheaval 25, Erasure 12, Gilding 10, Unmaking 8, Fate 5, Sockets 3, Grafting 2, Whetstone 14, Tempering 12, Reforging 4, Excision 3, Binding 2, Ruin 1.

**Shards into orbs** (one click makes 1, Ctrl+click up to 10): Awakening 12, Upheaval 25, Erasure 30, Gilding 40,
Unmaking 50, Fate 60, Sockets 60, Grafting 100, Whetstone 5, Tempering 20, Reforging 50, Excision 60, Binding 75, Ruin 150 shards, about 2.5 shards per Chaos Coin of a reference price (5, 10, 12,
15, 20, 25, 25, 40; Whetstone 2, Tempering 8, Reforging 20, Excision 25, Binding 30). The store sells only Whetstones,
Excision and Binding, with weekly limits; the other prices are reference values.

**Ember and Crown Shards into orbs (2026-10-21).** Beta: "How do I combine the shards into 1 orb? I looked in the crafting
bench but didn't find it." The same grid has two more rows, paid with the shards themselves (not rune shards):
**1,000 Ember Shards (29852) -> 1 Ember Orb (32258)**, **1,000 Crown Shards (29853) -> 1 Crown Orb (32259)** and (since the Void Orb rework) **1,000 Void Shards (29854) -> 1 Void Orb (32260)**
(`salvage_config.lua` `shardRecipes`, keys `embershard` / `crownshard`, action `combine {key, count}`). Same rules as the
rune shard rows: one click 1, Ctrl+click up to 10 (`maxCombine`), 300 ms between combines, the shards are taken from every
stack in the backpack and its bags at once (`player:removeItem` counts first and removes only when there are enough)
before the orb is given, the orb goes to the backpack, else the inbox, else the floor, a `Shards` row in
`chaos_crafting_log` ("1,000 Ember Shards -> 1x Ember Orb"). No recycling back into shards (Shift+click does nothing on
these rows). The shards stay currency of the character upgrades. The look text and the rich tooltip add "Combine 1,000 at
the Crafting Bench (Salvage tab) into an Ember Orb." (`ChaosSalvage.shardHint`, `item_tooltip_core.lua`); the Codex and
the wiki say it on the shard and in the orb's Sources. Client: `game_crafting/recipeview.lua` (the grid's logic, tested by
`recipeview_test.lua`): the row shows "1,000 Ember Shards" in amber and the tooltip "Your Ember Shards: 3,200.".

*The counts.* The owner set 1,000 for both (2026-10-21, "pode deixar 1000 shards por orb"). The model first proposed 1,500 and 1,750 (computed from the base server's monster files, not measured in game); its reasoning, kept for reference: The shards drop only from
the 30 monsters of the waystone maps (estimated level 470-610): per map tier the five monsters' loot entries give Ember
Shards at 10-46% (1-5 a drop) and Crown Shards at 8-40% (1-4). With the stock count multiplier by monster level (x2.25 up
to level 500, x2.70 above) and the pace loot thinning of those monsters (`pace_config.lua` base `loot` 0.20 x scale 1.2 =
0.24 at hunting level ~1000) a kill gives on average:

| Waystone map tier | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ember Shards per kill | 0.07-0.08 | 0.11-0.13 | 0.22-0.26 | 0.29-0.35 | 0.43-0.52 | 0.66-0.78 |
| Crown Shards per kill | 0.04 | 0.06 | 0.10-0.11 | 0.18-0.22 | 0.27-0.34 | 0.43-0.52 |

At the pace model's 1,400 kills an hour (band 300-600 and 600-1000) the middle tiers (3-4) give about 400 Ember and 210
Crown Shards an hour, tier 6 about 1,000 and 670. The loot layer drops about 0.25 Ember Orbs and 0.125 Crown Orbs an hour at
that pace (chance per kill 4 and 2 per 10000 against the Orb of Upheaval's 40, which gives the hunting model's 2.5 an hour).
So the costs give a shard hunter of the middle tiers about as many orbs again (Ember 400 / 1,500 = 0.27 an hour, Crown 210 /
1,750 = 0.12), about 3x in tier 6, and nothing to anyone who never hunts there; the same coins of reference value per
hour of shards for both (Ember 20 per 3.8 h, Crown 40 per 8.3 h; the Crown Orb is worth twice the Ember Orb and its shards
drop at 0.55x). For comparison: the rune shard rows (50 and 100 rune shards) and the Candlemark shop (an Ember Orb for 5
hours online, a Crown Orb for 12.5) stay the cheaper sure paths, and a stock of shards from before (they had no use) turns
into a few orbs, not a flood. Not counted: the waystone "Loot" upgrade (chance x(1 + level / 100)), magic and rare monster
extra rolls, the shards a character upgrade takes (5 Ember Shards a level for levels 4-6, 4 Crown Shards for 7-10).
`tests/salvage_test.lua` checks the recipes (names against `chaos_orbs_config.lua` renames, cost 1,000-3,000, the same
coins per hour within 20%), the mocked combine (stacks in two containers, one short, Ctrl x10 and x11, the rate limit, a full
backpack, the log row, no recycling) and the look text.

**Why these numbers.** With the stock rarity roll (70% of gear drops pass, then each rarity in order with its own chance)
an average rolled drop gives about 2.8 shards before modifiers and sockets (about 3.3 with them) and a 0.9% orb chance:
roughly a tenth of an Orb of Upheaval. Rolled drops come a few times more often than orbs from the loot layer (a normal monster
drops an orb on about 1.4% of kills), so salvaging everything adds a modest share to a player's orb income instead of
replacing the orb drops, and it competes with selling the item: salvage is a sink for unwanted rarity gear, not a mint.
`tests/salvage_test.lua` checks the average (2.2-3.5 shards, about 1% orbs) and that an Orb of Upheaval takes at least 8 rolled
items.

**Salvage all.** Choose a container (the backpack, the Loot Bag or one bag in the backpack, its direct contents) and the
highest rarity; the bench shows how many items it takes, the shards, the summed orb chance and what it skips (locked, unique,
with gems, above the rarity, over the limit) and marks the items in the gear grid. The button asks for a confirmation. At most
**255 items per action** (`batchCap`, was 50): a full Loot Bag in one click. One action removes up to 255 items in one tick and
writes up to 255 rows in one `INSERT` into `chaos_crafting_log`, with `batchIntervalMs` (2 s) between two actions; nothing in
the code needs a smaller number. The rest, if any, is listed as over the limit for the next one.
**The Loot Bag** (tester feedback 2026-10-28: "Salvage All por qualidade na Loot Bag"): the bench only knew paths inside the
main backpack (`ChaosCraftingBench.walk` / `itemAt`), but the Loot Bag lives in the purse (the store inbox) and never leaves it,
so it was never in the container list and its items failed the backpack check, and the only way was to move them out one by
one. Now `bagList` offers it second (after the main backpack, when `ChaosPouches.carried` finds it) under the bag key `loot`
(items are addressed `loot.N`), and the "in the backpack" check of `S.inScope` also accepts a direct child of the carried Loot
Bag. Locked, unique, socketed and above-rarity items are still kept. The confirmation carries a signature of the
previewed items (paths and item signatures); when anything changed in between the server refuses ("check the list and
confirm again").

**The item lock.** The bench's Lock / Unlock button (gear and Rift Keys in the backpack) sets the custom attribute
`chaos_locked` = 1. The game's item right-click menu has the same as "Lock item" / "Unlock item" (client `game_crafting`
`lockmenu.lua`, two `addMenuHook` entries; the menu shows the one that fits the `chaos_locked` key 3 the item packet carries): action
`lockAt {pos, cid, on}` on the salvage opcode. The server finds the item by its client position (inventory slot or open
container, `ChaosItemTooltip.decodePos`; never the ground), requires that it hangs on the player himself (`getTopParent`), that
its client id is `cid`, and that it is gear or a Rift Key (also when worn); it answers with a text message and one
rate-limited action per `singleIntervalMs`. The bench's `lock` action only takes a real `on = true`. **Locked items cannot be sold nor melted.** A locked item is refused by salvage, skipped by "salvage
all", and never sold by the **Auto Seller**, whatever rarities are ticked (`autosell.lua` reads the attribute,
`ChaosShopServices.sellBlocked` returns "locked"; "Auto seller: kept a locked item."). The look text says "It is locked:
it cannot be sold, salvaged or thrown away." (EventCallback onLook, index 120); the gear grid shows locked items dimmed,
the rich tooltips (engine patch 0003, key 3) show "Locked". The lock survives the orbs that make a new copy
(Awakening, Gilding, Erasure, Upheaval, Fate: `C.recreate` calls `ChaosSalvage.copyLock`). Orbs and gems still work
on a locked item: the lock protects from destruction and selling, not from crafting.

Engine patch `src-patches/0009-locked-items-never-sold.patch` closes the paths the scripts cannot see (an item is
"locked" when `chaos_locked` is non-zero; a container with a locked item anywhere inside counts as locked too, so a bag
is never sold or trashed with a locked item in it):

| Path | With 0009 |
|---|---|
| NPC trade window (every NPC with `module_shop`, Grimgan, the Wandering Merchant, NPCs with their own `onSell`) | The sale list does not count locked items (a locked-only item is not offered). A sale only locked copies could fill is refused by the engine before the NPC script runs: "Locked items cannot be sold." With one locked and one unlocked copy, selling 1 takes the unlocked one, selling 2 is refused. |
| `player:removeItem(id, n)` (NPC selling, quest and NPC turn-ins, exchanges, any script removing by id) | Skips locked items. Fifth argument `includeLocked = true` takes them too (only the staff panel's "Remove item" uses it). |
| `player:getItemCount(id)` (turn-in checks) | Does not count locked items; third argument `includeLocked = true` counts them. A turn-in with only locked copies fails as if the player had none. |
| Market (sell offer, accepting a buy offer) | Never takes a locked item (`Item::hasMarketAttributes()`; any custom attribute already kept rolled items off the market). |
| Trash holders (trash cans, lava, ...) | A locked item cannot be moved onto one ("This item cannot be moved there."), and a trash holder never destroys one. |
| The stock "Upgrade and Rarity Remover" (29623, makes a plain copy) | Refused: "This item is locked." (a guard added to `data/scripts/customs/upgrade/upgrade_slot_item.lua` by `tools/install_salvage.py`; Lua, works without the patch). |

Unchanged on purpose: scripts that act on one specific item object (`item:remove()`: using a Rift Key or a scroll,
the guild depot and the stash, which keep the item; salvage itself checks the lock), player-to-player trade and mail
(the item and its lock move to the other character), the season join's inventory wipe (confirmed by the player, "this
cannot be undone") and staff tools. Without the patch the NPC trade window and turn-ins still take locked items. The lock
never stops crafting.

**Protocol** (extended opcode 232, `ChaosOpcodes.crafting`, new actions handed from `crafting.lua` to `salvage.lua`):
client -> server `salvage {path, id, sig}`, `lock {path, id, on}`, `salvageScope {bag, maxRarity, mode}`,
`salvageBatch {bag, maxRarity, sig}`, `combine {key, count}` (`key` an orb key, or `embershard` / `crownshard`); the bench state gains `salvage` (shards, recipes, bags,
rarity names, the batch preview while the tab is open, the tab) and `locked` / `salvage` (preview) on the items. Answers
are the bench's `result` (orb `"salvage"`) and `state`.

**Server checks.** The item is found by its backpack path plus id and signature (moved or changed -> "put it on the bench
again"); `inBackpack` again before anything is removed; all rules again on every item of a batch; 300 ms between single
actions and locks, 2 s between batches, 300 ms between combines; shards and orbs go to the backpack, else the inbox (a
message says so), else the floor. **Log**: every salvaged item is one row of `chaos_crafting_log` (orb `Salvage`, item
name, "Rare (level 26): 2 rune shards [+ 1 Orb of Upheaval]"; a batch writes its rows in one INSERT), combines are `Shards`
rows ("75 rune shards -> 3x Orb of Upheaval"), lock changes `Lock` rows; the bench's Recent crafts shows them.

**Tested in game** (test server, client with the new tab): a single Common salvaged from the bench (1 shard, log row);
"salvage all" in the backpack up to Uncommon with the cap lowered to 5 (5 taken, 6 over the limit, the socketed and the
higher ones skipped), then a bag up to Legendary (4 Commons and a Rare: 6 shards; the locked Uncommon skipped); the
confirmation box; Awakening (12 shards) and Ctrl+click Chaos (3 orbs for 75 shards); Lock / Unlock from the bench,
the refusal of a locked item, the look text; a monster kill with a locked and an unlocked rarity fire sword on the auto
sell list with the rarity opt-in: the unlocked one sold (4000 gold to the bank), the locked one kept; an Orb of Upheaval on a
locked sword (new copy, still locked). Unit tests: yields, orb roll, checks, the lock, batch cap and skips, signature,
combine, the economy average, and `salvage.lua` single / batch / lock / combine / full backpack / look text against
mocks; `tests/shop_services_test.lua`: the auto seller keeps a locked item.

## Item attributes in packets and rich tooltips (`src-patches/0003-item-custom-attributes.patch`, `item_tooltip.lua`, `item_tooltip_core.lua`, client `game_itemrarity`, `game_itemtooltip`)

**Item custom attributes in item packets (engine patch 0003).** Our client already parses per-item custom attributes
when the feature `GameItemCustomAttributes` (126) is on: after each item (after the animation phase byte) it reads a
u16 count, then per entry a u16 key and a u64 value, and stores them on the item (`item:getCustomAttribute(key)`).
The feature is negotiated, not part of the client's 10.98 profile: our client sends, after `OTCv8` and its version in
the login packet, the strings `OTCv8TierByte` and `A`; only for such a connection does the server add feature 126 to
its feature packet (0x43, sent before any item) and write the attributes. Other OTC-family clients keep the plain item
format, and our client against a server without the patch never enables the feature (rarity falls back to the
description tag). The client turns the feature off at every logout (`game_itemrarity`), so a later login to another
server starts without it.

Every item the client reads with its item parser goes through `ProtocolGame::AddItem`: map tiles (also the login map
description), inventory, open containers (and the last item of a removed container slot), trade windows, text windows.
The market sends item ids only. A plain item costs 2 bytes (count 0); an item with any of the attributes below gets
its keys, 10 bytes each (a rolled rare with sockets: 52 bytes). The Lua `NetworkMessage:addItem` is unchanged (no
script uses it; a script that sends items by hand to our client would have to add the count itself).

| key | name | source (custom attribute) | value |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | rarity | `rarity` (else the item type's) | 1..15 |
| 2 | level | `combatPowerLevel` | item level |
| 3 | locked | `chaos_locked` | 1 (the item lock of salvage.lua) |
| 4 | unique | `chaos_unique` present | 1 |
| 5 | sockets | `chaos_sockets` | socket count (a unique's fixed socket is not stored, so 0) |
| 6 | id | `chaos_iid` | per-item id |
| 7 | version | (computed) | 32-bit hash, never 0 |

The keys are defined three times with the same numbers: `ChaosItemAttrKey` in the engine's `const.h` (patch 0003),
`Chaos.itemAttr` in `chaos_constants.lua`, `ChaosItemAttr` in the client (`game_itemrarity/itemrarity.lua`);
`tests/item_tooltip_test.lua` reads all three and fails when they differ. Keys 6 and 7 are sent only with at least one
of keys 1-5. Key 6: the engine has no per-item id (the `getRealUID` of the base server is never set), so the first
time an item with any of keys 1-5 is sent it gets the custom attribute `chaos_iid` = (unix time of the block) << 20 |
counter, saved with the item; a new block starts every 2^20 ids and at every start, so ids stay unique across
restarts and below 2^53 (exact as a Lua number). A clone of an item (`Item::clone`) keeps the id; the tooltip request
checks the item at the position anyway. Key 7 hashes the item id, every custom attribute (order-independent), the
attack / defense / extra defense / armour / hit chance / range / attack speed attributes and the name and description:
it changes whenever an orb, a gem or an upgrade changes the item.

The engine sends an item again only when it moves or its id or count changes, so a script that changes attributes
calls the new `item:sendUpdate()` (inventory slot, container page of every player who has it open, or the tile's
spectators; touches nothing on the item, unlike a transform to the same id, which would reset durations).
`ChaosItemMods.sendUpdate(item)` wraps it (no-op without the patch); `ChaosCrafting.rewriteDescription` and
`ChaosGems.writeDescription` call it, and every orb, socket and gem change ends there. `item:getClientAttributes()`
returns `{[key] = value}` as the client gets them (the tooltip uses keys 6 and 7 for its cache key).

Build: apply 0001, 0002 and 0003 in the server source root and rebuild everything (0003 adds members to
`ProtocolGame`, so objects built before it must not be linked with it). Built on the test server with a fresh CMake
build of the base source plus the three patches.

**Rich tooltips (extended opcode 242).** Hovering an item in the inventory or an open container asks the server for
its tooltip; holding Ctrl adds the equipped item(s) worn the same way (both hands for weapons and shields, the same kind
only: a weapon is not compared with a shield) as plates next to it, and the hovered tooltip lists the differences per
number in green (better) or red (worse); a shorter attack interval counts as better. A Rift Key (`ChaosItemTooltip.riftKey`)
shows its map modifiers with their tiers (boons in the Chaos colour), the level its tier needs, the reward bonuses and how
it is used, and offers no compare (it is not worn). Checked in game: a key and a legendary item with a power (Ctrl compare
with the worn helmet, the power line in orange).

- client -> server `get {items = [{pos = {x, y, z, s}, iid, cid, n}]}`, at most 3 items; `iid` is the decimal string of
  key 6 (JSON numbers lose digits past 14); `cid` the client id of the hovered item, `n` its count (stackables only).
- server -> client `tips {items = [{pos, iid, cid, tip} | {pos, iid, cid, gone = true}]}`.
- The item asked about (live test winpkg-35: a Rope showed "Cheese 62", a Training Wand "Gold coin 100"). A plain item
  is named only by its slot, and a container's items move one slot up when an item goes in at the front (loot): a
  request sent before the client saw that found the neighbour, and the client kept its tooltip under the hovered item.
  Now the server takes the item at the slot only when its client id (and count) match, else the nearest slot of the
  same container that matches (`ChaosItemTooltip.matchIndex`), else `gone`; the client keeps an answer only when its
  `id` / `count` are what it asked for (`tooltiplogic.lua` `L.tipMatches`) and asks again (twice, 300 ms apart).
- Positions: `{0xFFFF, slot, 0}` inventory (slots 1-10), `{0xFFFF, 0x40 + container id, slot}` a container the engine
  has open for this player (`player:getContainerById`, slot on the current page), or a map position with the stack
  position `s` on the player's floor, at most 8 x 6 tiles away and visible (`player:canSee`); the client asks only
  about inventory and containers. Anything else, or an item whose `chaos_iid` differs from `iid`, answers `gone`.
- Budget: a token bucket per player, 12 tokens, 6 per second, one per item; a request over it is dropped (the client
  asks again on the next hover).
- The tooltip (`ChaosItemTooltip.build`, pure, `tests/item_tooltip_test.lua`): name, client id, count, kind and slot,
  rarity name, tier (1-5) and item level, base numbers (attack, defense, extra defense, armour, hit chance, range,
  attack interval, element, and the item type's own skills, protections, max health / mana, magic level, speed),
  every modifier as `ChaosCrafting.readMods` lists it with its text, group and roll range (`absorbRange` /
  `elementRange` of the rarity for the engine's modifiers, `ChaosItemMods.range` for the Chaos modifiers, none for
  uniques), sockets with each gem's effect in this item, unique and set (the item set block: pieces worn, bonuses active; "Item sets"), requirements
  (level, the unique's level, magic level, vocations), weight, flavour text (a unique's text, else the item type's; a
  rolled item's description is its modifiers and is not repeated), the lock, a flat list of numbers for the compare and
  the compare slots.
- Client cache: by `<id>:<version>` (keys 6 and 7), so an orb that changes an item (new version through
  `sendUpdate`) makes the next hover ask again; items without the keys are cached for 30 s under position, id and count.

**Rarity frames.** `game_itemrarity` reads the rarity from key 1 (unique: key 4) and draws a frame in the rarity colour
(unique orange) on container and inventory slots; without the feature it falls back to the `[NAME]` tag of the
description. The loot filter keeps its glow and dim and leaves the frame to `game_itemrarity` where it drew one.

**Tested in game** (srv16 built from the base source with 0001-0003, client with the overlay): the feature negotiated at
login and every inventory, container and ground item carrying its keys (a rolled Chaos sword: rarity 8, level 73,
sockets 2, id, version); frames from the attribute in the backpack (Chaos red, Divine, unique orange) and on the
equipped unique; tooltips of a rolled rare weapon (modifiers with ranges, Chaos modifiers, a Flawless Ruby), of a
unique (Soulreaper) and of Divine armour with two gems; Ctrl compare of the rare sword against the equipped Soulreaper
with green and red rows; an Orb of Unmaking on the sword: the version changed at once and the next hover showed one
modifier less; the budget (12 of 20 requests at once answered), unopened container, slot 11, far map position and a
wrong `iid` all answered `gone`; the same client against the engine without the patch: feature off, no errors from it.
Screenshots: scratchpad `tooltips/`. Not tested: two players watching the same container, trade windows.

## Item links in chat (`itemlink.lua`, `itemlink_core.lua`, `tools/patch_help_itemlinks.py`, client `game_chatlinks`)

Players link items they carry into chat. Extended opcode `ChaosOpcodes.itemLink` = **249**. The server has no hook on every
chat path (local say, party and guild channels and private messages have no Lua callback), so the link is a capability
carried by the stock chat instead of a server-side broadcast: the client first registers the items, then sends the message
as ordinary speech with the link text in it.

**Wire format.** One link in a message is `[Item Name]{<r><id>}`: `r` is the rarity as one hex digit (`0` normal .. `f` = 15)
or `u` for a unique, `id` is 9 characters `a-z0-9`. ASCII only (the Tibia chat is Latin-1), so other clients just show
`[Magic sword]{4k7f2m9qax}`; Cinders of Chaos clients draw `[Magic sword]` in the rarity colour and keep the rest hidden. The
text of a link is made by the server (`ChaosItemLink.token`): the name has no brackets or braces, a capital first letter and
at most 40 characters. At most 3 links in a message (the client counts chips, the format allows more but the client draws
only 3); a message with its links written out must fit in 250 characters.

**Protocol (JSON `{action, data}`).**

| direction | action | data |
|---|---|---|
| client -> server | `register` | `{n, items = [{pos = {x, y, z}, iid}], ctx = {kind, id}}` up to 3 items; `pos` is the client position of the item (inventory `{0xFFFF, slot, 0}`, open container `{0xFFFF, 0x40 + container id, slot}`), `iid` its per-item id as a decimal string, `ctx` the chat tab (`say`, `party`, `guild`, `private`, `channel` with the channel id, `npc`, `loot`, `log`) |
| server -> client | `registered` | `{n, links = [{token, name, rarity, unique}]}` |
| server -> client | `refused` | `{n, reason}` |
| client -> server | `get` | `{id}` the 9 characters of a link id |
| server -> client | `link` | `{id, tip, owner, left}` or `{id, gone = true}`; `tip` is the tooltip of `item_tooltip_core.lua`, `left` the seconds the link lives |
| server -> client | `caps` | `{help}` sent 2 s after login: the player may link in the Help channel (tutor or above) |

**Rules.**
- The item must be carried: the item's top parent is the player (inventory and containers inside it). Ground, corpses,
  depot and trade windows are refused (`itemAt`); the position is decoded by `ChaosItemTooltip.decodePos` and a wrong `iid` (the
  item moved since the client looked) refuses. A locked item (salvage lock) is linked like any other; the tooltip says "Locked".
- The snapshot (`ChaosItemTooltip.build`: rarity, item level, tiers, modifiers, sockets, requirements, set info of the
  owner's equipment, no viewer-specific "Your Attack Interval") is stored in a cache under a random id from `/dev/urandom`
  (`math.random` if it cannot be read): 36^9 values. It lives 10 minutes (`ttl`), at most 2000 snapshots are kept (least
  recently used go first) and 40 per player (oldest first). Registering the same item in the same state again gives the same
  link and renews it. The snapshot is what the item was when linked: a changed or sold item does not change old links.
- "Only links that appeared in messages the player received": the id is the secret. A player who has not seen the message
  does not know the id; guessing is counted: 8 unknown or expired ids in 60 s block that player's lookups for 60 s. The client
  asks only for ids it has drawn in its console. This is a capability check, not a record of who received what: anybody who
  was handed the id (a pasted message) can read the snapshot until it expires.
- Budgets (token bucket per player): `register` 6 items at once then one per 4 s (every requested item costs one, found or
  not); `get` 20 at once then 10 per second.
- Contexts: no links in the Help channel for players below tutor, none in NPC conversations, the loot channel or the spell
  channel. The client enforces all of it when writing and again when sending (a chip in a Help message goes out as plain
  `[Name]`); for modified clients the Help channel script is patched: `python3 -I tools/patch_help_itemlinks.py <server>/data`
  (run by `install_all.py` with the events step, idempotent) makes `data/chatchannels/scripts/help.lua` call
  `ChaosItemLink.helpBlocks(player, message)` and refuse the message ("Item links are not allowed in the Help channel."). Other
  channel scripts are not patched: a modified client can still paste a link into World Chat, which only shows a name and a
