  snapshot the pasting player has to own the id of.
- Spam: the usual chat limits apply to the message itself; the link adds the budgets above.

A transmogged item keeps its look in the snapshot (`tip.look`); the tooltip icon draws the look ("Transmog"). A speaker's chat
name colour (cosmetic, "Cosmetics") is drawn over the link colours, never instead of them.

Tests: `tests/itemlink_test.lua` (ids, the format and its parser, names, cache limits, budgets, strikes, contexts, the handlers
against a mocked engine) and the client's `chatlinks_logic_test.lua`.

**Tested in game** (srv34: the base source with patches 0001-0011, the client with the overlay; two characters on two
accounts): Shift+click on an equipped unique and on backpack items put `[Name]` chips in the input, the fourth chip was
refused with "You can link up to 3 items in one message."; the message arrived in the other client in the rarity colours
(blue, purple, unique orange); hovering showed the rich tooltip with "Linked by X - 10 min left"; Ctrl showed the compare
view against the equipped sword; the same in a party channel and in a private channel (the sender sees the coloured link
in the own message too); in the Help channel the client refused a chip, and a raw link text sent with `talkChannel` was
refused by the server while plain text went through. Not tested: guild channel (the same chat path as the party channel),
a tutor account, the 10-minute expiry (unit test only).

## Inspect Player (`inspect.lua`, `inspect_core.lua`, client `game_playerinspect`)

A window with the public side of another player. Extended opcode `ChaosOpcodes.inspect` = **240**; the client module is
`game_playerinspect` because the base client already has a module `game_inspect` (Inspect Object).

**Protocol (JSON `{action, data}`).**

| direction | action | data |
|---|---|---|
| client -> server | `inspect` | `{cid}` the creature id of a player the player right-clicked, or `{name}` typed in the window |
| client -> server | `privacy` | `{}` asks for the own setting, `{allow = true / false}` sets it |
| server -> client | `result` | `{name, level, voc, vocId, ascended, guild = {name, rank}, ach, rift, trials, outfit = {type, head, body, legs, feet, addons, mount}, self, parts}` |
| server -> client | `equip` | `{name, rows = [{slot, tip}], part}` `parts` packets follow a `result`; slot 1-10 as the inventory, `tip` the rich tooltip. Each packet is at most 8000 bytes of JSON, the whole message counted (`ChaosInspect.equipPackets`, `config.packetBytes`), and goes through `Chaos.sendChunked`: a single row bigger than that arrives in `S`/`P`/`E` parts, joined by the client's `L.joinPart` like the tree |
| server -> client | `tree` | `{name, nodes, masteries = [{id, choice}], cls, line, vocation, spent, total}` the active passive tree, after the equipment (`ChaosInspect.treePayload` of `ChaosPassiveTree.publicView`), through `Chaos.sendChunked`; `result.tree` says one follows |
| server -> client | `denied` | `{code, text}` code: `notfound`, `private`, `range`, `rate`, `bad` |
| server -> client | `privacy` | `{allow}` |

**What is public** (and all that is ever sent): name, level, vocation and whether it is an ascended class, guild and rank,
achievement points of the character (`ChaosAchievements.pointsOf`), the best rift tier sealed (the achievement counter
`rift_tier`), the highest Vocation Trial tier cleared as the current vocation (`ChaosTrials.tierCleared`), the outfit, the
ten equipment slots with their tooltips and the active passive tree (node ids, the chosen mastery effects, class and line). No
health, mana, skills, storage, gold or backpack contents. The tree is sent only with an allowed `result`, so the privacy
setting covers it. The window's **Passive Tree (n)** button shows it read-only in the passive tree window
(`game_passivetree/viewother.lua`): that class's section and keystone variants, the effects in the tooltips, its bonuses
in "Info & Bonuses", no planning, refund or apply, a banner with "Back to my tree".

**Rules.**
- `cid` (right-click): the same floor, at most 10 tiles away in x and y and in view (`player:canSee`). `name` (the menu
  entry): any online player, any distance; the same public data.
- Not inspectable: staff (account type gamemaster or above, or a group with access) and players in ghost mode answer exactly
  like a name that is not online. Yourself is always allowed.
- Privacy: `Chaos.storage.inspectOff` (7100960), per character, 1 = refuses; default on, so nothing is stored for most
  characters. Set from the checkbox "Allow others to inspect me" in the window (the server also tells the player in the text
  line). A refusal says "<name> does not allow others to inspect them."
- Limits: one request per 1.5 s and a bucket of 6 (one more per 5 s) per player; names are 2-29 letters, spaces, `'` and `-`.
- Menu: Social > Inspect Player (the window asks for the name; no spoken command) and "Inspect Player" in the right-click
  menu of a player (`game_interface.addMenuHook`). The base client's own "Inspect <name> Prestige" entry is a different thing.

**Packet size.** An extended opcode message carries at most 8192 bytes (see "Extended opcode size limit" above). The equipment
used to be cut at about 12000 bytes of rows: a rich item (Transcendent, 7 modifiers, three gems, a veiled slot, every
protection) is 4.0-4.5 KB of JSON, so two of them made a packet of about 9 KB that `extended_opcode.lua` refused, and the
window showed no equipment at all. Measured in `tests/inspect_test.lua` with ten such items (45.5 KB of rows): before, five
packets of 8975-9964 bytes, all refused; now ten packets of 4518-5507 bytes, all delivered, and a single 9 KB row goes in
two parts.

Tests: `tests/inspect_test.lua` (names, who may be inspected from where, budget, packets, the handler against a mocked
engine: public fields only, equipment tooltips, privacy default / off / on, hidden staff and ghosts, rate limit; the wire
under the engine's limit, joined by the client's own logic, for the largest realistic equipment) and the client's
`playerinspect_logic_test.lua` (equipment and tree packets in parts).

**Tested in game** (two clients): right-click menu (Ctrl + right-click with the classic controls) > Inspect Player on a
player next to the inspector: outfit, level, class, achievement points, equipment with the rich tooltip on hover (slot name
under it); Social > Inspect Player and a typed name; the privacy checkbox switched off in one client and the other client's
request refused with the name in the text and no stale data in the window. Not tested in game: a hidden staff member, a player
out of range (unit tests), a character with a guild (the guild line is the stock `getGuild`), rift / trial records of a
character that has them (the fields were 0).

## Seasons (`season.lua`, `season_core.lua`, `season_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_season.sql`, `tools/patch_season_events.py`)

Roadmap item 12, phase 1: fresh-start season characters with their own ladder, season-only uniques and an account-wide
cosmetic reward track that is kept after the season. Client `game_season` (Adventure > Season in the top menu),
extended opcode 246 (`ChaosOpcodes.season`). Every rule and number is in `season_config.lua`.

**Install.** Run `sql/chaos_season.sql` (4 tables, and a fifth for "Season modes") and `python3 -I server/tools/patch_season_events.py <server>/data`
(idempotent, `--dry-run`). The tool enables `onTradeRequest` / `onTradeAccept` in `data/events/events.xml` (shipped
disabled, so no script could see a trade) and makes `Player:onMoveItem` (`data/events/scripts/player.lua`) ask
`ChaosSeason.onMoveItem` first: a script callback cannot refuse a move reliably, because the base dispatcher keeps only
the return value of the last `onMoveItem` callback. Without the tool the server logs a warning at startup and only the
party, bank and unique rules apply.

**How a character joins (and why this way).** Characters are created on the website (also from the client's Create
character, which goes through the website): the base server has no account manager and no in-game creation (the base ships `ADD_DEPOT_BOXES_NEW_PLAYERS.txt`,
a snippet for the website's `users.php`). A fresh character opts in in game (or at creation from the client, below):
Adventure > Season, Join, then the confirmation within 60 s (the window is the only way in: there is no chat command for
players). The window follows level ups, so an open confirmation closes by itself once the character passes `join.maxLevel`.
Allowed while a season runs for a character of level 7 or lower (`join.maxLevel`; level 8 comes within minutes) that never
joined a season, has an empty depot, inbox and store inbox, is not in a party and owns no house. Joining destroys every
carried item, empties the bank balance, the Chaos bank stars and the supply stash (so nothing a standard character handed
over before the join comes along), then gives the new-player kit again when the character had received it. The flag is a
row in `chaos_season_players`; the look text says "He is a Season of Ash character [S1]." (after the season: "a veteran
of ...").

**Joining at creation (the client's Create character).** The client's character creation (website/README.md "Client
API") can pick the running season and a mode. The website then writes a row in `chaos_season_requests` (player,
season, mode; `sql/chaos_season.sql`, also created at startup and by the website's plugin). At the character's first
login `S.applyRequest` (season.lua, from the login event) runs the in-game join: `S.joinCheck` for the character
now, the join itself (`doJoin`: nothing to wipe on a new character) and the mode (`S.modesPick` / `S.modesJoined`),
so the realm, mode and Hardcore caches are the in-game join's. The row is deleted either way; when the season ended
before the first login, or the character may no longer join (a depot filled by `CHAOS_DEPOT_BOXES=1`), the player is
told why (`S.requestOutcome` in `season_core.lua`, tested in `tests/season_test.lua`) and plays as a standard
character. The website accepts only the season running at creation and Hardcore modes only with "I understand".

**Season record.** `seasons = {{id, name, tag, start, finish, hour, modifier}}`: dates as YYYYMMDD (at `hour`, server
time) or unix time. The modifier is shown in the window; `expMult` multiplies the monster experience of that season's
characters (an `onGainExperience` callback, so it needs `patch_base_events.py` like every Chaos experience bonus).
Gods (account type god): `/season start [id]` starts the next season now, `/season end` ends the running one now (both
stored as `server_config` rows `chaos_season_<id>_start|_end`, which win over the config dates), `/season status`.

**Isolation.** While a season runs, a character's realm is its season id (standard characters: 0). Different realms
cannot exchange anything; gamemasters and up (`isolation.exemptGroup`) are never blocked.

| Way | Rule | Hook |
|---|---|---|
| Trade window | refused between realms (also the house trade of `!sellhouse`, which skips the request event) | EventCallback `onTradeRequest` / `onTradeAccept` |
| Items on the ground | an item a player drops is tagged with the dropper's realm (custom attribute `chaos_realm`, pickupable items only); another realm cannot move it or anything inside it. Own items lose the tag when they reach the inventory (they stack again) | `onItemMoved`, `ChaosSeason.onMoveItem` |
| Corpses | a monster corpse gets the realm of its owner (the engine's most-damage player), a player corpse the realm of the dead character: another realm cannot loot it | `onDropLoot`, `onDeath` |
| Mail | a parcel or letter dropped on a mailbox is refused when the receiver (first line of the label / letter) is of another realm | `ChaosSeason.onMoveItem` |
| Houses | taking items from, or putting items into, a house owned by another realm is refused | `ChaosSeason.onMoveItem` |
| Party | **not allowed** between realms (the joining character and the leader are told). Chosen over "allowed without shared loot and experience": the party is also what the bounty board, the dungeons and 2v2 arena use, so one rule covers all of them | EventCallback `onJoin` |
| Chaos bank transfer | refused between realms | `bank.lua` asks `ChaosSeason.transferBlocked` |
| NPC bank transfer | refused between realms (the NPC says "You cannot transfer money to this account.", the player gets the season reason) | `Player.transferMoneyTo` (`data/lib/core/player.lua`) asks `ChaosSeason.npcTransferBlocked`: put there by `tools/patch_season_events.py` (exact match, idempotent); without the patch `season.lua` wraps the function at runtime and warns |
| Market | separate markets: season characters list, see and buy only their season's offers; standard characters only the standard ones. Season markets trade for **gold only** (listing, buying and buy orders in Chaos Coins are refused for season characters: coins are account-wide) | `market.lua` (see "Market"); the coin rule: `season.lua` wraps `ChaosMarket.list` / `buy` / `orderPost` (no change in `market.lua`; wrapped again after a reload, as `ChaosLeaderboard.record`) |
| Store (account-wide Chaos Coins) | a season character gets only **cosmetics and account services**: wings, auras, shaders, outfits, addons, mounts, plate frames, portal styles, transmog sets, premium time, the class unlocks (account-wide anyway), the Chaos Pact and its storage extras, the season pass and packs, name and sex change. Refused: every item offer (supplies, runes, crafting, training, boosts, the Backpack of Holding), the starter packs and any bundle with such a part, stamina, blessings, the skull remover, the passive tree reset, the vocation token, world buffs, pouches, pets, the Auto Seller and Rarity Autoloot. The same rule for a gift to a season character (online, offline, and again when a gift queued before the receiver joined is delivered at login: refunded). Refused offers go to nobody: the account buys them with a standard character. Anything not listed in `season_config.lua` `store` is refused, so a new offer kind needs a decision there | `shop.lua` asks `ChaosSeason.storeProblem` (four small hunks marked "Seasons"), rule `ChaosSeason.storeRefusal` (`season_core.lua`) |
| Season pass items | the pass is the account's (pass XP of every character, the premium pass, tier skips): while the season runs its item rewards (gold, potions) are claimed by standard characters only; they stay claimable (also by the season character after the season, within the grace days). Coins, titles, looks and portal styles are claimed by anybody | `seasonpass.lua` `SP.claim` asks `ChaosSeason.passClaimProblem` |
| World buffs | World Experience, World Loot and World Training (bought with account-wide coins) skip season characters | `shop_services.lua` `buffMult(id, player)`, callers in `loot.lua` / `loot_config.lua` pass the corpse owner |
| PvP: open world, arena, guild siege | **allowed** between realms. Nothing changes hands: player corpses keep the dead character's realm, arena and siege rewards come from the server, and 2v2 arena teams are parties (same realm). Season characters can be in guilds (a guild shares no items) | - |
| Depot | per character, nothing to share | - |

Why the coin rules: store coins belong to the account, so a season character could otherwise spend coins its account
bought or earned with standard characters (the season pass coins, the Pact drip, referrals, market sales) on a head
start. Cosmetics are fine on both sides; nothing that affects season progress crosses. Not a leak, so left as is: the
daily reward (one claim a day per account, from the server; the streak counts logins), the new-player and referral
gifts (from the server, as for any new character), the account-wide Pact limits (stash tabs, listings: room, not items;
the stash itself is per character and emptied at the join). Items on the ground before a season starts are untagged
(free). The stock market is off for everybody (`tools/patch_market.py`); our market keeps the seasons apart (see "Market").

**Ladder.** While a season runs the leaderboard window shows a "[S1] only" toggle (`leaderboard.lua` adds
`ChaosSeason.leaderboardMeta` to its meta and passes `season` to `ChaosSeason.sendBoard`): the class ladder then lists
only that season's characters (players joined with `chaos_season_players`, cached 120 s), and the weekly boards (World
Boss, Bounty Hunter, Rifts, ...) only their scores. The normal view still lists everybody, and titles are won on the
normal boards only.

**Season uniques.** A `ChaosUniqueItems` entry with `season = <id>` (`data/lib/chaos_unique_items.lua`) drops for nobody
before that season, only for that season's characters during it, and for everybody after it. `loot.lua` passes the
corpse owner to `rollUniques`; rolls without an owner (rifts, treasure goblins, the goblin hoard) leave season uniques
out while the season runs. Season 1: Widowmaker, Riftcaller, Hellspite Arbalest, Mortis Cowl (existing uniques, no new
art; `chaos_unique_specs.lua` is unchanged).

**Reward track.** Milestones of a season character (`track`): level 100 (title Ashborn), 300 (Death Herald outfit),
600 (its addons), 1000 (Doom Skull mount), 25 bounty contracts (Revenant outfit), 5 world bosses (Nightglass Devourer
mount), and a tier 10 rift (title Ashen Riftwalker; listed only when `ChaosRift` exists). Season stats come from a wrapper
around `ChaosLeaderboard.record` (`stats`: bounty and goblin add, rift keeps the best, world boss counts), so the bounty,
rift, world boss and goblin scripts needed no change. A milestone unlocks the reward for the whole account forever
(`chaos_season_rewards`): every online character of the account gets outfits and mounts at once, every other character
(also ones created later) at its next login; titles show in the look text ("He holds the season title Ashborn (Season of
Ash)."). Every look type and mount id exists in the base server's XML.

**End of season.** When the finish has passed (once-a-minute check, and at login) or after `/season end`, every
unmigrated character of that season becomes a standard character: `migrated_at` is set once (`WHERE migrated_at = 0`,
so running it again does nothing) and logged in `chaos_season_log` and the console. Level, skills, items, passive tree
and season uniques stay; the realm rule already treats a character of an ended season as standard, so trade works at
once even before the row is updated.

**Tests.** `tests/season_test.lua` (LuaJIT and Lua 5.3): the date math and overrides, join eligibility, the trade /
move / party / mail decisions, realms and item tags, milestone detection and the track view, the migration decisions,
the season unique rule and the look text; the coin rules against every real offer of `shop_config.lua` (each category
decided, every item offer and bundle with an item refused, unknown kinds refused), the season pass item rewards and the
gold-only season markets. `tests/shop_test.lua` runs the store's season hunks against the real rule (buying, online and
offline gifts, a queued gift refunded at login after the receiver joined), `tests/shop_services_test.lua` the world
buffs for season and standard characters.

Verified on the test server with two clients (a season character and a standard one): `/season start` and the
broadcast, the window (time left, modifier, track, Join), the join confirmation and the wipe (backpack, gold, bank
5000 -> 0), trade refused between realms and allowed within the season, a standard drop that the season character could
neither push nor pick up (the standard one could), the season character's drop refused to the standard one and untagged
when picked up again, a standard kill's corpse refused to the season character, a parcel to a standard character refused
and to a season character delivered, party refused between realms and allowed within, level 301 -> two milestones,
the outfit, the look text with the title, 25 bounty records -> Revenant outfit, the reward delivered at login to another
character of the account, the "[S1] only" view of the Bounty Hunter board and the class ladder, the bank transfer and
unique rules (300 boss rolls: 23 season uniques for the season character, 0 for the standard one and without an owner),
`/season end` migrating both characters (online and offline) once, a second `/season end` migrating none, and trade
allowed afterwards.

Verified later (two clients, a season character and standard ones, one of them on the same account): the experience
modifier (the same kills at the same level: dragon 17 325 for the season character, 15 750 for the standard one, x1.10;
two cyclopes 7 424 / 6 750), the house rules (a season guest in a standard house and a standard guest in a season house
could neither take an item nor put one down, an untagged item included; the owners could), a player corpse in PvP (a season
character killed by a standard one: corpse tagged with the season realm, the killer could not loot it), the confirmation
closing by itself (the character levelled past 7 with it open), a natural start and end from the dates (broadcasts, the
online and an offline season character migrated once), and the coin rules: the store refused potions and the Novice Pack
to the season character and sold it an aura, the standard character of the same account bought the potions, a potion gift
to the season character was refused and a wings gift delivered, a pass item claim was refused to the season character
and taken by the standard one, the season market refused a coin listing, a coin purchase and a coin buy order and took a
gold listing, World Loot and World Training skipped the season character (loot x1.00 / x1.25, skill tries 2000 / 2500).
Fixed: the window did not follow level ups (track progress and the Join button stayed at the join level until reopened).
Not verified in game: a gift queued for a character that joins a season before its next login (unit test only).

## Season modes (`season_modes.lua`, `season_modes_core.lua`, `season_config.lua` `modes`, `sql/chaos_season.sql`)

Roadmap item 62. Self-Found and Hardcore for season characters, on top of "Seasons" (the realm rules stay; the modes add
rules inside a realm). The rules are pure functions in `season_modes_core.lua` (`ChaosSeasonModes`); the engine glue is
`season_modes.lua`, which `season.lua` calls through `ChaosSeason.modes*` hooks (small hunks marked "season modes").
Every number and text is in `season_config.lua` `modes`.

**Install.** Nothing new: `sql/chaos_season.sql` has the table `chaos_season_modes` (the script also creates it at
startup), the hooks of `tools/patch_season_events.py` are the ones the realm rules use. Small hunks elsewhere:
`loot.lua` (the loot bonus), `orbexchange.lua` (`X.place`), `leaderboard.lua` (the mode tab and the fallen mark),
`data/lib/chaos_buffs.lua` (two buff bar entries), `achievements_data.lua` (six achievements).

**Joining.** The join confirmation (client `seasonjoin.otui`) offers Standard, Self-Found, Hardcore and Hardcore
Self-Found, each with its warning; a Hardcore choice needs "I understand" ticked. The server checks the key
(`ChaosSeasonModes.pick`; no key from an older client = Standard) and stores one row per character in
`chaos_season_modes` (`ssf`, `hc`, `chosen_at`). The mode cannot be changed until the season ends. The Season window
says "Mode: Self-Found." (or the fall); the look text "He is playing Hardcore Self-Found." / "He fell in Hardcore at
level 88 (killed by a dragon lord)."

**Self-Found (SSF).** Item origin is tracked with the custom attribute `chaos_owner` (guid): an item a player drops (or
puts into a container lying in the world) gets the dropper's guid; a monster corpse gets its owner (the engine's corpse
owner); a player corpse the dead character. An item that reaches an inventory loses the tag (it is the holder's now;
own items stack again), items in the own depot are not tagged, a tagged item keeps its first owner when others move it.

| Way | Rule | Hook |
|---|---|---|
| Trade window | refused both ways (also SSF with SSF) | EventCallback `onTradeRequest` / `onTradeAccept` (season_modes.lua) |
| Ground / corpses | an SSF character moves only items whose chain (the item and every container around it) carries no other owner: map items, quest and chest rewards, its own drops and its own monsters' corpses. Another player's drop, another player's corpse (also an SSF party member's: loot stays personal) are refused ("loot"); putting an item into someone else's container or corpse is refused ("give"; dropping on a tile counts as into the container on top of it). Nobody else takes an item carrying an SSF owner, or puts one into an SSF character's container ("item") | `ChaosSeason.modesMove` (from `ChaosSeason.onMoveItem`), EventCallback `onItemMoved` / `onDropLoot`, death event |
| Mail | an SSF character sends no parcel or letter (also to itself); mail to an SSF receiver is refused | `ChaosSeason.modesMove` |
| Houses | items of a house owned by someone else (and into it) are refused for SSF; nobody moves items in an SSF owner's house | `ChaosSeason.modesMove` |
| Chaos bank / NPC bank transfer | refused from and to an SSF character | `ChaosSeason.transferBlocked` (season.lua) asks `modesTransferBlocked` |
| Market | listing, buying, buy orders and filling buy orders refused (cancel and collect stay open) | season.lua's market wrapper asks `modesMarketRefusal` (also wraps `fill` now) |
| Orb Exchange | no new orders | `orbexchange.lua` `X.place` asks `modesOrbRefusal` |
| Party | only with SSF characters (Hardcore SSF included); the realm rule stays | EventCallback `onJoin` |
| Store gifts with power | already refused for every season character (cosmetics and services only, "Seasons") | `shop.lua` |
| Guild bank and depot | already refused for every season character | `guild.lua` |
| Depot | per character in this engine (the stash too: `player_id`); no account-wide item storage exists, so characters of one account exchange items only through the ways above | - |

Reward: +25% Item Find and +25% Rarity Find (`modes.ssf`), added in `loot.lua` (`L.itemFindMult`, the bonus rarity
chance), shown on the buff bar as "Self-Found" (icon `buff:self_found`, `client/tools/gen_buff_icons.py`), and the
Self-Found ladder tab. Achievements: Self-Found level 100 (title the Self-Made), still Self-Found at the season end.

**Hardcore (HC).** One life: a real death (the death event; deaths that arena, siege, trials and the like cancel are no
deaths) makes the character fallen. `fallen_at`, `fallen_level` and `fallen_cause` ("killed by Dragon Lord", "slain by
Name") are written once, the character is migrated at once with the season's own migration (`ChaosSeason.migrateRow`,
reason "fallen"): from then on it is a standard character with everything it has; its corpse is put in the standard
realm so it can take its items back. The fall is broadcast (`modes.hc.announce`) and logged (`chaos_season_log`
event "fallen"). Achievements: Hardcore level 50 / 100 (the Unfallen) / 250 (Deathless), alive at the season end
(Season Survivor).

Protections against unfair deaths (`modes.hc`), each one a health-change event that drops the damage and a
prepare-death event that cancels a lethal hit (a safety net after other scripts), shown as "Hardcore Ward" on the buff
bar with the reason:
- **Login:** no damage for `loginSeconds` (10) after every login, and after a client takes over a character that was
  left without one.
- **Disconnect:** the engine keeps a character in the world without a client while it may not log out (in fight).
  When it has no client (`player:getIp() == 0`) it takes no damage, and after `pullSeconds` (8) it is pulled to its
  temple.
- **Ping loss:** a Hardcore character's client (`game_season`) sends a heartbeat every `heartbeatSeconds` (2). No
  heartbeat for `pingLossSeconds` (6) while the client is still attached counts as a lost connection (protected,
  pulled after `pullSeconds`), at most `pingLossPerHour` (3) times an hour. A client that never sent a heartbeat
  (an older client) is judged by the disconnect only. After a reconnect the client asks for its state (`sync`) and the
  server sends it, so the heartbeat starts again.
- **Restart:** no damage while the game state is not normal (closing / shutdown) and during `restartGuardSeconds` (120)
  before the daily restart, which is read at startup from `data/globalevents/globalevents.xml` (`serversave.lua`'s
  time) plus `serverSaveNotifyDuration`; at the start of that window and at shutdown every Hardcore character is saved.

Limits, honestly: the protections do not see the moment a connection breaks. Until the server notices (the socket
closes, or `pingLossSeconds` of silence) the character fights normally and can die, so a stall of a few seconds in a
dangerous fight is still dangerous. Pulling the cable is also an escape to the temple; for a real disconnect that is
accepted (the character could not act anyway), the ping-loss path has its hourly budget so a client that stops its
heartbeat on purpose cannot hide behind it for long (and it would be pulled out of its hunt each time). A crash of the
server (no shutdown event, no warning) is not covered: what happened since the last save is lost, and a death in that
time may or may not be kept. Damage to mana (mana drain, a mana shield) is not blocked, only health; a script that
kills outside the damage path (e.g. a GM command) still kills, and the death counts. A heartbeat is a client feature, so a
client without `game_season` gets the disconnect and login protections only.

**Ladders.** The Season view of the leaderboard window has mode tabs: All (as before), Standard, Self-Found, Hardcore,
HC Self-Found and Fallen (`ChaosSeasonModes.ladderTabs`, sent in the leaderboard meta). The class ladder of a tab
LEFT JOINs `chaos_season_modes` (`ladderClause`): the Hardcore tabs list living characters only, Fallen lists the
fallen ones of the season by the level they fell at, with the cause; the weekly boards filter their scores the same way.
A fallen character gets a skull next to its name on every ladder (also the all-time class ladder: `ChaosSeason.fallenMark`,
cached 5 minutes), the tooltip says the level and cause. The website's Seasons page has the same tabs and skulls
(`chaos_class_ladder($base, $limit, $season, $mode)`, `chaos_fallen_marks()`; the Leaderboards page shows the skulls).

**End of season.** The normal migration resets the mode (`reset_at`), the character keeps its items; a character still
playing Hardcore alive gets `season_hc_survived`, one still Self-Found `season_ssf_finished` (achievements, also
offline). Fallen rows stay for the ladder history.

**Tests.** `tests/season_modes_test.lua` (LuaJIT and Lua 5.3): the rules (every blocked trade / party / gold / market /
orb / move / mail / house path, the owner tags, rewards, the fall, every protection with its timing and the hourly
budget, the restart window, the ladder clauses and tabs) and `season_modes.lua` against a mocked engine (the join, the
callbacks, real item chains, a fall with its migration, protected hits, the pull, a reconnect, the shutdown save, the end
of season, the mode tabs). Client: `game_season/seasonjoin_test.lua` (the dialog's choices and the Hardcore
confirmation). Website: `website/tests/chaos_season_modes_test.php`.

Verified on a test server with two clients: the join dialog with the four modes (Join disabled for Hardcore until
"I understand" is ticked), an SSF join (row stored, Mode line, Self-Found buff), a trade request from the SSF character
refused ("Self-Found characters cannot trade."), a standard season character's drop refused to the SSF character (and
taken back by its owner, tag gone), a party join refused, the market / Orb Exchange / bank hooks refusing the SSF
character and its Item Find x1.25; Hardcore: 3000-damage hits absorbed during the login protection and while the
restart guard was on (the Hardcore Ward shown), a client killed in fight: the character took no damage without a
client and was pulled to the temple after 8 s; deaths after the protection: fallen at once (migrated, broadcast, the
Fallen tab with skulls, the Season window's fallen line); `/season end`-style migration: modes reset, Season Survivor
and Needed No One unlocked. Not verified in game: the ping-loss path with a real stalled connection (a heartbeat gap was
seen protecting a character while its client was attached), a real server save restart, mail between modes.

## Seasonal Journey (`season_journey.lua`, `season_journey_core.lua`, `season_journey_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_season_journey.sql`, client `game_season` Journey tab)

Roadmap item 67. A fixed, chaptered checklist per season and per season character that walks a fresh character through
the season's content once. It is neither the season pass (account-wide, repeatable pass XP with daily / weekly
challenges: the journey only feeds it pass XP when a chapter is finished) nor the season reward track (account-wide
milestones kept forever, `season_config.lua` `track`). Nothing of the pass was changed: its challenges are rolling
"do X today / this week" tasks, the journey is a one-time guide, so extending the pass would have mixed two models.

**Install.** `sql/chaos_season_journey.sql` (tables `chaos_season_journey_stats` and `chaos_season_journey`; the script
also creates them at startup). Nothing else: no storages, no base file. Small guarded hunks in `descent.lua` (end of a
run per player), `dungeons.lua` (a cleared dungeon per member) and `atlas.lua` (points after a credit), each
`if ChaosSeasonJourney and ChaosSeasonJourney.emit then ... end`. The client hunk is the Journey tab of the Season
window (`journey.lua`, `journeyview.lua`, `season.otui`) and the `journey` toast of `game_chaosnotify`.

**Who.** A character of the running season (`ChaosSeason.realmOfGuid`) walks that season's journey (one per season id
in `season_journey_config.lua` `journeys`). Every other character (standard, migrated, fallen, staff) sees the journey
of the running or next season as a read-only preview. A Hardcore fall migrates the character, so its journey stops.

**Chapters.** In order; a chapter opens when the one before it is finished and the character has the chapter's level.
Counters count from the join on, also while a chapter is locked: an objective is marked done once its chapter is open
and its counter reaches the target (so a chapter that opens late completes at once what was already done). Objectives
can be mode-specific (`only = "hc" | "ssf" | "nossf" | "nohc"`): Hardcore and Self-Found characters get their own
objectives, Self-Found is never asked to use the Orb Exchange. A finished chapter writes its row (`c:<key>`) first and
then gives its rewards once: pass XP to the account's pass of that season (`ChaosSeasonPass.addXp`, only while that
pass runs), orbs (backpack, inbox when full), one piece of the season's appearance set (transmog looks through
`ChaosTransmog.unlockLook`, account-wide; the outfit and mount on the character) and, at the end, a title (titles.lua
source `journey`, kept after the season).

Season of Ash, "The Ashen Pilgrimage" (set "Ashen Pilgrim"):

| # | Chapter | Level | Objectives (all modes; mode-specific in brackets) | Rewards |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | First Embers | 0 | level 100, tier 1 rift, a world boss, 5 bounties, a bestiary task, 50 tiered kills, 5 orbs used | 1500 pass XP, 3 Upheaval, Magma Monocle look |
| 2 | Ash and Iron | 150 | level 200, tier 4 rift, a dungeon, Trusted by a faction, a treasure goblin, an invasion fought, 500 party kills, 10 Atlas points [HC: a flawless rift] | 2000 pass XP, 5 Upheaval, Magma Coat look |
| 3 | The Burning Road | 250 | level 300, tier 6 rift, Descent room 6, 3 world bosses, Tower 10 floors in a run, an invasion defended, a unique, 500 community points [SSF: 50 orbs used] | 2500 pass XP, 2 Fate, Magma Legs look |
| 4 | Omens in the Ash | 350 | level 400, an Omen guardian, tier 8 rift, 25 bounties, Honored, a full Descent, 30 Atlas points [not SSF: an Orb Exchange order; SSF: 150 orbs used] | 3000 pass XP, 3 Fate, Magma Boots look |
| 5 | The Ashen Sepulchre | 450 | level 500, a raid boss, 3 Omen guardians, tier 10 rift, 10 bestiary entries, an Orb of Grafting, Tower 25 floors [HC: level 550] | 3500 pass XP, 1 Grafting, Fiery Spike Sword look |
| 6 | Ascended Omens | 600 | level 650, an Ascended Omen, a full raid clear, 50 Atlas points, 10 world bosses, Descent room 10 [SSF: an item with 5 modifiers] | 4000 pass XP, 2 Grafting, Fiery Rainbow Shield look |
| 7 | The Cinderheart | 700 | level 750, 3 Ascended Omens, the Cinderheart, 3 raid clears, tier 12 rift, Revered, Tower 40 floors [HC: 5 flawless rifts] | 5000 pass XP, 5 Fate, Retro Knight outfit |
| 8 | Ash Eternal | 850 | level 900, a flawless raid clear, 75 Atlas points, tier 15 rift, Exalted, 100 bounties, 25 world bosses [HC: level 1000; SSF: a legendary power] | 6000 pass XP, 3 Grafting, Fire Panther mount, title Ashen Pilgrim |

Per mode a chapter has 6 to 9 objectives. Look types, mount and items are from the base server's XML (Retro Knight
1248 / 1249, Fire Panther mount 122; looks 7900, 7899, 7894, 7891, 7744, 8906), not sold in the store and not used by
another reward.

**Counters** (`season_journey_config.lua` `stats`, "add" or "max"): the achievement counters it lists come from
wrapping `ChaosAchievements.progress` / `set` (rifts, Omens, Ascended Omens, the Cinderheart, world bosses, invasions,
the raid, bounties, the bestiary, orbs, uniques, goblins, party kills); `ChaosFactions.gain` (reputation, rank index),
`ChaosCommunity.contribute` (points), `ChaosOrbExchange.place` (an order placed) and `ChaosTower.recordRun` (floors in a
run) are wrapped too; the Descent, dungeons and the Atlas emit. The wrappers are installed at startup and again every
30 s (after a `/reload` of the other script), once per function. An offline character's counter (an invasion share, a
rift finisher) is written to SQL and counted at its next login. At login the counters are raised to the character's
achievement counters, Atlas points and Descent record: a season character starts fresh at the join, so those are its
season's numbers, and a journey added in the middle of a season counts what was done before.

**Protocol** (season opcode 246, so the Season window keeps one opcode): `journey` (client: the tab opened) ->
`journey` (header and chapter summaries) and one `journeyChapter` per chapter (objectives, rewards with client ids):
every message stays far below 8192 bytes. `journeyDone` flashes the open tab; the toast is the notifications opcode 79,
action `journey`. While the tab is open, progress is pushed at most every 2 s.

**Gods.** `/journey status [name]`, `/journey stat name, stat, value` (test helper), `/journey reset name` (deletes the
season's rows; rewards already given stay).

**Tests.** `tests/season_journey_test.lua` (LuaJIT and Lua 5.3): the shipped journey (6-8 chapters, 6-10 objectives per
mode, chapter 1 basics and endgame chapters, rewards per chapter, the title at the end, the validator), gating by
chapter and level, mode objectives (Hardcore stops on its own objective, Self-Found finishes without the Orb Exchange),
the window view and preview; then `season_journey.lua` with a mocked engine and a fake SQL store: counters from the
wrapped achievement API, the factions, tower, Orb Exchange and emit hooks, rewards given once (also after a relog), offline
counters (add and max), the preview for a standard character, the last chapter's mount, outfit and title. Client:
`game_season/journeyview_test.lua`. Offline client screenshots of the tab and the toasts; not run on a live server.

## Season pass (`seasonpass.lua`, `seasonpass_core.lua`, `seasonpass_config.lua`, `seasonpass_store.lua`, `sql/chaos_seasonpass.sql`, client `game_battlepass`)

An account-wide pass per season of `season_config.lua`: a free and a premium track of 50 tiers, pass XP from play,
daily and weekly challenges, claims in the client (Adventure > Season Pass, extended opcode 227
`ChaosOpcodes.seasonPass`), tier-up toasts, and three season packs. Every number, reward and pack is data in
`seasonpass_config.lua` (`passes[<season id>]`); a new season adds a pass there. Season and standard characters of the
account add to the same pass and share its rewards; it starts from zero with the next season.

**Install.** Nothing beyond `install_all.py`: the `files` step copies the scripts and the `sql` step runs
`sql/chaos_seasonpass.sql` (5 tables, `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`; `seasonpass.lua` also creates them at startup). The
store category comes from the season pass hunk of `shop_config.lua` (one `dofile` of `seasonpass_store.lua`). No base
file is patched; the experience hook is an `onGainExperience` EventCallback, so it needs `patch_base_events.py` like
every Chaos experience bonus.

**When.** The pass of a season progresses while that season runs (`ChaosSeason.current()`, so `/season start|end` moves
it too). After the season ends its rewards reached can still be claimed for `claimGraceDays` (14) days; then the
window shows the next season. Purchases only while the season runs.

**Pass XP (from play only).** One tier costs `1000 + 25 x (tier - 1)` (80 625 XP for all 50). Sources, each with a
daily cap per account (server midnight). The caps bank (2026-10-15, `bankDays` 3): a source may give today what the last
three days left of their caps (a rolling window of 3 x the daily cap, days before the season count as none; `P.sourceRoom`,
`SP.capWindow` reads the two days before), so a missed day is made up later; the window shows today's cap with the bank:

| Source | Pass XP | Daily cap | Hook (no other system edited) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Experience | 1 per 1% of the character's level, counted on the monster's base experience x the level's experience stage only (store potions, world buffs, stamina, the season modifier and other bonuses add nothing) | 300 | EventCallback `onGainExperience` |
| Bosses | 150 per credited kill of a boss of `bosspoints_config.lua` (world bosses, the Trial Warden, endgame bosses) | 600 | `ChaosBossPoints.grant` wrapped |
| Bounty contracts | 60 each | 600 | `ChaosLeaderboard.record("bounty")` wrapped |
| Rifts | 40 + 8 x key tier | 1200 | `ChaosLeaderboard.record("rift")` |
| Treasure goblins | 150 | 450 | `ChaosLeaderboard.record("goblin")` |
| Invasions | 120 per Defender record | 240 | `ChaosLeaderboard.record("defender")` |
| Daily challenges | 250 each, three a day | - | the same events and monster kills (kill event) |
| Weekly challenges | 1200 each, three a week (Monday) | - | |

Challenges: one of every slot of `challenges.daily` / `challenges.weekly`, picked from the season id and the day / week
(the same for every account), progress from any character of the account. Model: about 45 minutes of play a day with
most dailies and the weeklies gives some 9 000 pass XP a week, tier 50 in about 9 of the season's 13 weeks; capping
every source every day takes about 3 weeks. Staff (group >= `staffGroup` 4, as on the leaderboards) earn nothing.
Nothing bought gives pass XP except the 10 tier skips of the top pack (asked for by the owner; they move the cosmetic
track only).

**Rewards.** Free track (earned by play): gold, potions, the titles Ashwalker (15) and Ashbound (50). Premium track
(bought with Chaos Coins; owner rule 2026-10-13: cosmetics and convenience only, never power): **cosmetics and Chaos
Coins back only**: the titles Kindled (1), Ash-Touched (5), Emberwake (18), Smoulderkin (20), Pyrewarden (22), Ashen
Herald (28), Cinderborn (35), Flamebound (38), Cinderlord (42) and Ashen Sovereign (48), the outfit shaders Ash Drift
(10, shaders.xml id 25) and Cinder Crown (30, id 26), the Cinderwrought name plate frame (40), the Everblight outfit (15)
and its addons (32, 45), the Cinderfall Gate portal style (25), the Magma Skull mount (50) and 10 Chaos Coins on each of
the other 32 tiers (320 back, less than the 600 the pass costs). No gold, potions, experience or gear on the premium
track: the validator (`ChaosSeasonPassCore.validate`, run at startup and by the test) refuses any premium reward whose
kind is not in `P.PREMIUM_KINDS` (coins and the cosmetic kinds), any item but gold and potions on the free track (no
orbs, gems, keys, experience potions, stamina or gear) and pack-only kinds on the tracks. The two shaders and the frame
are new art of this season, sold nowhere: the shaders are `chaos_ash_drift` / `chaos_cinder_crown` (client
`data/shaders/chaos_outfit_ash_drift.frag`, `chaos_outfit_cinder_crown.frag`, registered by `game_chaosshaders`; the
`install_outfits.py` shaders.xml block reads them from `seasonpass_config.lua`; a claim leaves the store's shader mark,
`shopShaderBase` + id, like the store's shaders), the frame is `cinderwrought` (`nameplate_core.lua` `N.FRAMES`, client
`game_nameplate/images/plate_cinderwrought.png` from `client/tools/gen_nameplate_art.py`; shown through the pass's own
frame switch). **Late buyers** lose nothing: buying the premium track (or a pack that holds it) claims every premium
reward of the tiers already reached at once (`P.premiumBacklog`, `SP.claimPremiumBacklog`; an account that got it as a
gift while offline gets them at its next login). The price, 600 Chaos Coins, was decided 2026-10-14 (docs/PRICES.md). Items go to the character
that claims (refused without room: the claim is undone and stays claimable); coins to the account; outfits, mounts,
titles and portal styles to every character of the account at once and to the others at login, kept after the
season. Claim all claims everything it can and leaves items without room for later.

**Premium and season packs.** The premium pass costs 600 Chaos Coins, once per account and season. Three packs, each
holding the lower ones, only while the season runs, once per account:

| Pack | Price | Holds |
|---|---|---|
| Ember | 500 | Brotherhood outfit and addons, Cinderhoof mount, title Emberkin, the Arboreal transmog set |
| Blaze | 1500 | Ember, the premium pass, Doom Knight outfit and addons, Flamesteed mount, Pyre Gate portal style |
| Inferno | 2500 | Blaze, Chaos Acolyte outfit and addons, Wrathfire Pegasus mount, title Inferno-Crowned (fire red), 500 Chaos Coins, 10 tier skips |

A higher pack after a lower one costs the difference, and the premium pass bought on its own counts toward a pack that
holds it (Ember + pass -> Blaze = 200). The store sells the pass and each pack at full price to an account that owns
none of them (`noSale`); with something owned it names the upgrade price and points to the pass window's Packs page,
which charges it. Gifts: the Packs page's Gift button buys the pass or a pack for another character's account (online or
not; not staff, not the own account) at the price that account would pay; the receiver gets it at once or at login.
Store gifts of these offers are off (`gift = false`): the store's gift path runs unlock offers on the buyer.

**Exclusive cosmetics.** `seasonpass_config.lua` `cosmetics` is the one list of the looks the season pass claims (each
entry carries `reward` in the shape of `achievements_data.lua` / `season_config.lua`, so the store's exclusion walk can
read it). Season of Ash: outfits Everblight (974 / 973), Brotherhood (278 / 279), Doom Knight (1016 / 1017), Chaos
Acolyte (665 / 664); mounts Magma Skull (106), Cinderhoof (90), Flamesteed (47), Wrathfire Pegasus (116); portal styles
Cinderfall Gate (item 12509) and Pyre Gate (item 29637), route `season` in `townportal_config.lua` (ids 41, 42);
titles Kindled, Ashwalker, Cinderborn, Ashbound, Emberkin, Inferno-Crowned; the transmog set Arboreal (reward kind `transmog`,
`ChaosSeasonPass.ownsTransmog` for `transmog.lua`). No wings, auras, shaders or name plate
frames: every one of those is sold in the store, a later season needs new art for them (the kinds `shader` and `frame`
are supported). `tests/seasonpass_test.lua` checks that achievements, the season track and the class looks give none of
them and prints a warning for each one the store still sells.

**Safety.** A claim is a row with primary key (account, season, tier, track), written with a random token and read
back before anything is given: two characters of the account clicking at once give one reward (tested with two clients
sending three claims each). The premium pass and the packs work the same way (`premium_token`, the pack row); a lost
race is refunded. Coins are taken with `coins >= price` in the same Lua call that checks them. Progress lives in memory
per account while a character of it is online and is written every 10 s, at a tier up, a claim, a purchase and the
last logout, as `GREATEST` of the stored value (a late write cannot lower it).

**Commands.** Gods: `/seasonpass` (state of the own account), `/seasonpass xp <amount> [character]` (test helper, logged).

**Tests.** `tests/seasonpass_test.lua` (LuaJIT and Lua 5.3): the shipped config, no power items, coins back, the
packs, the exclusive looks, the store category, the season portal styles, the tier curve and skips, experience units
and caps, day / week keys, the challenge pick (pinned so both interpreters agree), claims, pack prices and grants,
cosmetics of an account. Client: `game_battlepass/passview_test.lua`.

Verified on the test server with two clients: the window (tiers, claim, claim all, the room check), the store category
and purchases (Ember, then the premium pass; Ember again and Inferno refused with the upgrade price), the window's
upgrade to Inferno for 1600 (500 coins and 10 tiers given once), outfits, mounts and the title on the name plate, a gift
of Blaze to an offline account delivered at its login, a claim race from two characters (one reward), pass XP from
monster experience (a level 1000 and a level 105 season character), bounty, rift and boss pass XP through the real
hooks, a daily challenge completed with its toast, the tier-up toast, staff earning nothing, the grace after
`season end` (claims yes, progress and purchases no) and the pass closed after it, the season portal styles in the
Portal Style window. Not verified in game: an invasion or treasure goblin record, the week rollover.

## Guild siege (`siege.lua`, `siege_core.lua`, `siege_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_siege.sql`)

**Limits** (`siege_config.lua` `limits`, "Instance limits"): the 25 minute match (unchanged) with warnings at 5 min, 1 min and 10 s to everyone inside; `/instances close siege siege` is `/siege stop`.

A weekly scheduled war between guilds for the Chaos Obelisk. Client: `game_siege` (HUD + sign-up window, extended
opcode 233, Adventure > Guild Siege in the top menu). Every number below is in `siege_config.lua`.

**Install.** Run `sql/chaos_siege.sql` (tables `chaos_siege_signups`, `chaos_siege_results`) and
`python3 -I server/tools/patch_base_events.py <server>/data` (its third patch puts the siege rules in front of the
base server's `Creature:onTargetCombat`, see "PvP inside"). The Chaos spells ask the siege through
`ChaosSiege.canAttack` in `data/spells/chaos/_common.lua` (reinstall the spells with `register_spells.py`).

**Schedule.** Saturday 20:00 server time (`weekday`, `hour`, `minute`). Broadcasts 60, 15, 5 and 1 minutes before (the
first and the last also as a toast), with the guilds signed up so far. The login-screen calendar and Adventure > Events show a
"Guild Siege" day: siege.lua adds that entry to `Chaos.events.list` when it loads (no edit of the calendar config).

**Sign-ups.** Adventure > Guild Siege / Adventure > Guild Siege (or the window's buttons) by the guild leader or a vice-leader
(`signupRank` 2); the guild needs `minMembers` (3) members in `guild_membership`. Sign-ups close `signupCloseMinutes`
(5) before the start and while a siege runs. Up to `perBracket` (4) guilds share an arena; more guilds run as parallel
brackets (`maxBrackets` 3, arenas side by side, sizes differ by at most one, never below `minGuilds`); beyond 12 the
latest sign-ups wait (first come). Fewer than `minGuilds` (2) at the start: the siege is cancelled and the sign-ups
dropped. Adventure > Guild Siege shows the status and opens the window (next siege, countdown, sign-ups, your guild, champions, rules).

**The arena (built in code, like the world-boss arena).** At the start one arena per bracket is built with
`Game.createTile` at `arena.origin` (5100,5000,7; bracket b is `stride` tiles further east), refused if any footprint
tile already exists in the map with another ground or a house. Each is a 31 x 31 floor of black marble with a stone
wall, the Chaos Obelisk (item 1560) on the centre tile, the capture area (white marble, 5 x 5 around the obelisk,
`capture.radius` 2), eight stone pillars for cover, coal basins, and four base rooms (7 x 5, stone floor, two flags,
two basins) outside the middle of each side, sharing the arena wall. A base has a gate forcefield next to the wall
(action id 47212) into the arena, and an exit forcefield at the back (47213) to the temple. Nothing connects a base to
the arena by walking, so no enemy can enter it. After the siege the arena is cleaned (monsters, corpses, loose
items); walls, obelisk and decoration stay for the next week (the footprint check accepts our own grounds).

**Event flow.** Start -> the Guild Siege Portals (action id 47211) next to every temple ("City portals":
`portalOffsets`, a look text and an effect; or `portalPositions`), broadcast + toast -> members (level 100+) step in and arrive in their guild's base; gates are shut
for `gatherSeconds` (180) -> gates open, broadcast + toast, `matchMinutes` (25) of war; with `lateJoin` the portals stay
open -> end: standings, rewards, results in `chaos_siege_results`, broadcast + toast with every arena's ranking, the
HUD shows the final score -> after `exitDelaySeconds` (30) everyone inside goes to their temple (`exitPosition`
overrides it) and the arena is cleaned. A player who logs in inside during the match goes back to the base; inside
after the siege, to the temple.

**PvP inside.** During the match, in the arena of the player's own bracket:
- members of different guilds can always attack each other: skulls, the target's secure mode and party do not matter.
  `ChaosSiege.targetCombat` decides; the base `Creature:onTargetCombat` refuses a target with secure mode on and party
  members before any script callback runs, which is why `patch_base_events.py` inserts the hook before those rules
  (the hook returns nil outside the siege, so nothing changes elsewhere). Your own secure mode still has to be off to
  attack, as anywhere: the engine checks it (`Combat::canTargetCreature`) before Lua is asked.
- guild mates, players in a base, a downed player, players of other brackets and non-participants cannot be attacked;
  nobody attacks during the gathering. Monsters and fields cannot hurt players in a base or downed.
- **no real death**: a `preparedeath` event cancels the lethal hit. The engine never runs the death, so there is no
  frag, no unjustified kill, no skull from the kill, no experience, skill or item loss and no blessing is used. The
  player is "downed" for `downedSeconds` (3): slowed, cannot attack or be attacked, does not count on the point, then
  wakes up in the guild's base with full health and mana, poison/fire/energy/bleeding/paralyze removed.
- skulls: the engine still gives an attacker a white skull on each hit on an unmarked player
  (`Player::onAttackedCreature`, no Lua hook). siege.lua takes it back right after the hit (health-change event on the
  participants) and every second; on leaving, the in-fight condition (pz lock) is removed for players who came in
  without a skull. A red or black skull from outside stays as it was.
- multi-client (`Chaos.isMultiClient`): refused at the portal with "Multi-client: another character from your connection
  is online. Log it out to join the siege."; a participant who becomes one is sent out.

**Scoring.** `points.kill` (20) to the guild (and the killer) for every enemy struck down; `points.holdPerSecond` (1)
per second to the guild holding the obelisk, and 1 per second to each of its members on the point. Holding = the most
members (not downed) within `capture.radius` of the obelisk; a tie contests it (`capture.exclusive = true`: any enemy
contests). Standings: score, then kills, then sign-up order; a full tie for first place, or nobody scoring, has no
winner. 15 minutes of holding (900) outweighs a few kills more for the other side.

**Rewards.** For players with at least `minPresenceSeconds` (300) inside while the match ran: the winning guild's
members 500,000 gold to the bank, 5 Orbs of Upheaval and 2 Orbs of Fate; everyone else 150,000 gold and 2 Orbs of Upheaval (inbox
when the backpack is full; offline players get it at their next login). The winning guild is "Siege Champions" for
`titleDays` (7): its members' look text gets "He is one of the Siege Champions (guild)." (an onLook callback after the
base text) and +5% experience from monsters (`buff.xp`, onGainExperience callback; needs the
`patch_base_events.py` experience dispatch). Champions are loaded from `chaos_siege_results` at startup.
Leaderboard: every participant's points (kills x 20 + seconds on the held point) go to
`ChaosLeaderboard.record("siege", player, points, "add")`: the weekly Guild Siege board of the leaderboards (title
Siegebreaker).

**HUD.** Sent every second to everyone inside: title (arena number when there are several), time left (or "Gates
open in"), who holds the obelisk in the guild's colour / contested / neutral, a row per guild (colour of its base:
north red, east blue, south green, west gold; members inside, kills, score) sorted by score, and "You: kills, downed,
points". Hidden when the player leaves.

**Commands.** Adventure > Guild Siege (status + window), Adventure > Guild Siege, Adventure > Guild Siege, `Adventure > Guild Siege status`. Staff (`/siege`, group with
access): `start` (now, with the upcoming siege's sign-ups; they are consumed when it ends), `match` (skip the
gathering), `end` (end now with results), `stop` (cancel, no results), `portal` (entry forcefield two tiles east of
you), `arena [n]` (build arena n and go there), `signup <guild>` (no rule checks), `clear` (drop the upcoming
sign-ups).

**The base server's guild wars.** The stock TFS tables are there (`guild_wars` with status, `guildwar_kills`), and the
base `playerdeath.lua` (twice: `creaturescripts/scripts` and `scripts/customs/znote`) writes a `guildwar_kills` row
when both guilds have an active war (status 1). There is no in-game way to declare or accept a war (no `/war` or
`!war` script): it is meant for the website (Znote AAC), and the engine reads a guild's wars only at login
(`IOLoginData::getWarList`), so a war accepted while members are online counts for them only after a relog; startup
deletes pending (status 0) declarations. The siege does not use these tables. Possible double `guildwar_kills` rows
from the two death scripts were not checked.

**Tested in game** (test server, cropped map, two clients from one IP, guilds Iron Wolves and Blood Ravens):
sign-up refusal with too few members and the sign-up by command and from the window; the window; the forced start and
the arena build; the multi-client refusal at the portal (blocks on) and the toast; entry into the right base; gates
shut during the gathering and refusing another guild's gate; PvP by melee against a target with secure mode on; a lethal
hit (no death row, no experience lost, back in the base after 3 s); holding the obelisk alone (+1 per second, HUD
"Obelisk: Iron Wolves"); the end with results and rewards (winner 500k + orbs, the other guild 150k + 2 Orbs of Upheaval);
the champion look text and the +5% experience; everyone sent out and the arena cleaned. Not tested: two guilds at once
on the point (contested; covered by the unit test), parallel brackets, the scheduled start at the real time,
`tests/siege_test.lua` covers the schedule, sign-up rules, brackets, the arena geometry, capture control, standings,
rewards and the champion title.

## Weapon coverage (`tools/weapon_coverage.lua`, `weapon_coverage_config.lua`, `survey_base_weapons.py`, 2026-10-23)
Owner question: does every class have enough weapons? The audit answers it from the real data, in CI, so a gap fails the build.
- **What it counts.** For each class (docs/CLASSES.md, all 21) and each level band (1-20, 20-50, 50-100, 100-200, 200-400,
  400-700, 700-1000, 1000-1500, 1500-2400+): the weapons the class can wield and can get, whose required level is in the band.
  Wield = the class lists of the stock entry or the unique `equipLines` (Berserker two-handed melee only, Beastmaster bows
  only, crossbows Ranger and Deadeye, rods Illusionist, Mystic and the Necromancer line). Get = at least one way: a shop sells
  it, a monster drops it (chance of 0.02% or more per kill), a recipe makes it or a reward gives it. Charge weapons do not
  count. Power = attack (wand: mean damage) against the tier, the gear set attack curve at the band's own level
  (two-handed +3, crossbow +3).
- **Inputs.** `data/items/base_weapons.csv` is a snapshot of the stock weapons of an installed server, made by
  `python3 -I tools/survey_base_weapons.py INSTALLED_DATA` (like `base_item_values.csv`, so CI needs no game data; run it
  again when `install_all.py` changes a weapon). The rest is in the repo: `chaos_items.xml`, `chaos_unique_specs.lua`,
  `chaos_unique_items.lua` (drops), `chaos_gear_sets_items.lua` and `chaos_gear_sets.lua` (sources), `chaos_fist_weapons.lua`,
  `chaos_weapons800.lua` (the 34 weapons above level 800, their own monster rows are the source it counts), the base recipes and the Chaos monster loot.
- **Check (CI).** `cd server && luajit tools/weapon_coverage.lua --check` (and `lua5.3`) fails when a class has fewer than
  `minOptions` (3) weapons in a band, or its best one is under `minPower` (80%) of the tier, unless the cell is listed in
  `weapon_coverage_config.lua` (`knownGaps`, `handledElsewhere`). It fails too when the table below is out of date. Tighten
  the numbers in that file. Other commands: `--md` (the table), `--list [Class]` (every weapon of a class by band), `--write`
  (rewrite the table below).
- **Gaps found and filled.** Before: Berserker had no weapon at 1500+, Elementalist and Illusionist one, the Ranger line,
  Beastmaster, Mystic and the Necromancer line two. Beastmaster had two bows at 20-50 and at 700-1000. Fixed with
  (a) three sources for the Gildcrown level 2000 pieces, which no monster could drop (Pyrewing Tyrant, Pyre Stork,
  Azhkarrath the Chained Wyrm), (b) the Gildcrown band 1250-2000 (was 1200), which moves the second wand and rod to level
  1500, and (c) seven uniques with built-in modifiers: Hoarfen Bow (40), Moonlit Gallows Bow (900), Hollow Throne Claymore
  (1550), Gravetide Arbalest (1800), Emberhowl Greataxe (1950), Wake-Heron Longbow (2100) and Bellringer of the Last Vigil
  (2200). Their power is 106 to 108% of the tier. Wands and rods have no new unique because a unique keeps the damage of
  its base item.
- **Not touched.** The Thief line (dual daggers and daggers) and the Monk line (Monk weapons) are filled by other changes.
  They have no gap now, so they are not in `knownGaps`.
- **Limits.** Quivers stop at level 1000 (`chaos_archery_config.lua`); the gear audit below fills the rest with uniques. A
  band can pass with 3 options of one kind.

## Gear coverage (`tools/gear_coverage.lua`, `gear_coverage_config.lua`, `data/lib/chaos_class_loot.lua`, `chaos/class_loot.lua`, 2026-10-22)
Owner request: review all the loot and make sure it is well distributed for every class, from level 1. The weapon audit
above does the weapons. This audit does the rest of the slots and adds a fairness check of the weapon drops.
- **What it counts.** Per class and level band (the weapon audit's 9 bands): helmet, armor, legs, boots, shield, spellbook,
  quiver, amulet and ring. An item counts for a class when the class wears it (armor weight, shield and spellbook hand,
  quiver for the launcher line, unique `equipLines`), when it has at least one way in (a shop, a monster drop of 0.01%
  or more per kill, the Gambler, a recipe, a reward), and from the level it can be had at: its required level, or the level
  of its easiest source when higher. A drop counts from the **hunting** level of its monster (the pool level for a
  base monster since O285, `pace_config.lua` `baseLevelMult` 1; twice it before). Power = armor or defense against the gear sets' curve of the class's weight. The
  stock items carry no armor value, so their power is unknown and counts as full strength.
- **Check (CI).** `cd server && luajit tools/gear_coverage.lua --check` (and `lua5.3`) fails when a class has fewer than
  `min` options in a band (3; quivers 2), when the table below is out of date, or when the weapon drops are not equal
  (next bullet). Allowances go in `gear_coverage_config.lua` `knownGaps`. Other commands: `--md`, `--list SLOT [Class]`,
  `--fairness [--detail]`, `--derive`, `--write`.
- **Equal weapon drops (owner, 2026-10-28: "Monk weapons are very rare to drop, they must all be equal").** `--fairness`
  counts, per class and **loadout**, the usable weapons dropped per 1000 kills in the hunting bands 100, 300, 500, 800,
  1000 and 1200 (a band is +-15% of the number; 800 and up are scaled hunts). A loadout is one kind of weapon a build
  wields: `melee1h`, `melee2h`, `fist`, `bow`, `crossbow`, `wand`, `rod` (`gear_coverage_config.lua` `loadouts`: the Warrior,
  Templar and Thief lines and the Samurai 1h and 2h, the Berserker 2h, the Monk line fist plus both melee, the Ranger and
  Deadeye bow and crossbow, the Beastmaster bow, the Elementalist wand, the Illusionist rod, the other casters both). Every
  real source counts: the stock loot tables of the pool monsters, the equipment sets' loot rows, the sets' level gear
  (from hunting level 700, the killer's class weighs 3x), the class loot rows and rolls below, and the fist weapons' loot.
  A weapon counts when its power is 60% of the weapon audit's curve and its required level is within 150 below and 20
  above the band (or the class loot picks it there), so a level 25 club is no drop at hunting level 300. **Rule: in every
  band the loadout that finds the fewest is at least 90% of the one that finds the most** (`fairRatio`; it was "no class
  below 20% of the median", which let a Beastmaster find a third of a Warrior). Throwing weapons are no loadout:
  stackable throws are out of the game (`chaos_throwables.lua`). Monks can wield melee weapons (docs/CLASSES.md "Skills
  and weapons"), so the old model did not mislabel them; it counted no fist drop and, with the old window, 129 stock
  melee drops per 1000 kills at hunting level 300, nearly all of them weapons of level 25 to 40.
- **What it found.** Before: no quiver at 1-20, 700-1000 and 1500+ (the stock quivers run 20 to 1000), one at 20-50 and
  1000-1500; two spellbooks at 1-20 and 1500+; helmet, armor and legs at 1500+ one or two options (the sets stop
  at 2000 and some pieces were out of reach); one amulet at 400-700; two rings at 20-50. The stock monsters never dropped
  a bow, a crossbow or a quiver, so a Ranger found 0 usable weapons per 1000 kills in every band while a Warrior found 12
  to 230. A caster found 1 to 54. Stock wands, rods and spellbooks dropped from few monsters.
- **Fix 1: class loot** (`data/lib/chaos_class_loot.lua`, `data/scripts/chaos/class_loot.lua`, test
  `tests/class_loot_test.lua`). The bounty pool monsters and bosses get one-handed and two-handed melee, fist, bow,
  crossbow, wand, rod, quiver and spellbook rows from the stock bases (`base_weapons.csv`, the Monk line's
  `chaos_fist_weapons.lua`, `chaos_weapons800.lua`'s bases (bow, crossbow, wand, rod and two-handed melee above level 800, "Weapons above level 800"), the archery quivers and the spellbook list; set looks of `transmog_config.lua` are left out),
  by hunting level, as `jewelry.lua` does for rings. The chance per kill of a weapon family is a curve of the monster's
  hunting level (`config.chance`, anchors at 100, 300 and 500, flat outside; derived, see below), shared by the bases within
  150 levels below and 20 above the monster (the three highest below that, within 200 of the top). Quivers and spellbooks
  keep 0.8% rising to 2.4% at 800. Bosses: 4% melee and fist and bows, 3% crossbows, 2.5% wands and rods, 2% quivers and
  books. The loot layer rolls rarity, item level and modifiers as for any gear drop.
- **Scaled hunts** (`config.scaled`, `loot.lua` step 1e `L.classWeapons`, `ChaosClassLoot.rollScaled`). A monster type has
  one loot table, so a kill hunted above the pool (hunting level 658 and up) would carry the rows of its pool level. It
  rolls the weapons of the killer's class instead, once per family the class wields (`L.classKinds`, equal to the
  audit's loadouts, tested), with the chance of `config.scaled.chance` (anchors 800, 1000, 1200) x rate x item find x pack
  scale (at most 3) x tier (magic 1.5, rare 2, legendary 3, boss 3).
- **Derived numbers.** `luajit tools/gear_coverage.lua --derive` fits the anchors of `config.chance` and
  `config.scaled.chance` so that every loadout finds `fairTarget` = 28 usable weapons per 1000 kills (2.8%) in the fitted
  bands (the classes whose sets or stock drops add more are fitted for the one that needs most). Paste its output into
  the file when a base, a set or the pool changes; `--check` fails when a loadout falls behind.
- **Result** (usable weapons per 1000 kills, every loadout of every class, bands 100 / 300 / 500 / 800 / 1000 / 1200).
  After: 28.0 to 28.4 everywhere (least / most 0.99 to 1.00). Before (same model, old rows): Warrior 1h/2h 15.6 / 13.8 at 100
  and 0.0 at 300 and 500 (stock melee drops of level 25 to 40 do not count at those levels), 2.5 / 2.1 at 800; Berserker
  13.8, 0.0, 0.1; Ranger bow 10.4 / 26.0 / 28.3 and crossbow 10.6 / 18.6 / 21.2; Beastmaster bow 10.4 / 26.0 / 28.3;
  Mystic and Necromancer line wand 37 / 34 / 34 and rod 18 / 21 / 27; Elementalist 18 / 21 / 27; Illusionist 36 / 34 / 27;
  **Monk, Shadowfist and Iron Sage fist 0.0 / 0.2 / 0.0** (nine boss and rare rows); at 800 to 1200 every loadout 0.0 to
  2.7 (level gear only; fists none). All weapons dropped by the monsters of the bands per 1000 kills (any weapon, usable or
  not): 116 / 237 / 243 before, 263 / 366 / 409 after at 100 / 300 / 500. A class sees two to three loadouts, so a Warrior
  finds a usable weapon on about 5.6% of the kills, a Monk on 8.4%.
- **Fix 2: 17 uniques** (`chaos_items.xml`, `chaos_unique_items.lua`). Quivers for the Ranger line at levels 6, 14, 38, 750,
  900, 1200, 1600 and 1900 (built-in modifiers from the shared catalogue: life on hit, physical penetration, boss damage).
  Spellbooks at 12 and 1650. A ring at 30. Amulets at 450 and 600. Helmets at 1550 and 1800, armor at 1600, legs at 1650,
  all classes, 106 to 135% of the set curve. Each is a copy of a stock base with its own `equipLevel`. Magic and rare ones
  drop from the monsters of the band; the 1500+ ones from legendary monsters of the top hunts and the boss Vhalkareth
  Mortal Shell. Chance before the tier multiplier: 30 for levels up to 38 (0.3% per kill of a magic monster), 12 for 450
  to 1200 (0.24% on a rare one), 6 above (0.24% on a legendary one). The bad-luck protection of `conquest_config.lua`
  `pity` (monster uniques: +1% per miss, up to 3 times) already covers every unique, so none waits forever; it needed
  no change.
- **Wands and rods.** A unique keeps the damage of its base item and no tool sets it, so no wand or rod unique was added.
  Wand and rod coverage comes from the class loot rows above and the weapon audit's sets.
- **Limits.** Ammunition is not audited (bows fire without it). Amulets and rings are judged by count only. The table
  counts a stock item as full strength.

## Item prices (`data/lib/chaos_item_prices.lua`, `tools/gen_item_prices.py`, `tools/install_item_prices.py`, the Loot Buyer)

Owner request (2026-10-14): every item a player can loot or craft sells to an NPC at a sensible price, and rarer and
higher-level items sell for more. Owner decisions of 2026-10-14: uniques are never sold to an NPC (salvage or market),
crafted equipment floors at 20% of its materials and at most an hour of hunting, the Wandering Merchant's Orb of
Gilding costs 250,000. One table holds every price; the Loot Buyer, the base NPC shops and the Auto Seller
all pay from it.

**The table** (`data/lib/chaos_item_prices_data.lua`, generated, committed; the same plain prices in
`data/scripts/chaos/sell_prices.lua` for the Auto Seller). `python3 -I server/tools/gen_item_prices.py` writes both,
`--check` fails when they are out of date or a rule breaks (CI step "Item prices"). Inputs, all in the repo:
`data/items/base_item_values.csv` (a snapshot of the base server: per item its category, slot, level requirement, the
NPC sell and buy prices of the NPCs in the game, and its loot sources as counts, levels and chances; no base names),
`data/items/base_recipes.csv` (the base crafting recipes), `data/items/item_price_rules.csv` (overrides: the quest items,
the base upgrade runes) and the Chaos sources (creature products and food of `art_items.csv`, `fist_items.csv`, gems,
supports, charms, uniques, orbs, omens, Ascended items, faction tokens, pouches, the Everfull Ration, the store's items
in `shop_config.lua`, every Chaos monster's loot, and the wearable bases the Chaos layers drop or give on top of the
stock tables: `data/lib/chaos_class_loot.lua` (bows, crossbows, wands, rods, quivers, spellbooks), the Gambler's pool in
`gamble_config.lua` and the spellbook list of `tools/gear_coverage_config.lua`; the snapshot only knows what stock monsters
drop, so these are priced as equipment by their level requirement and slot, under the same caps; a quiver counts as a
backpack; `--check` and `tests/item_prices_test.lua` fail when one of them has no price, because the Auto Seller keeps an
unpriced item as "noPrice" and never sells it, 2026-10-24). `gen_item_prices.py survey BASE_DATA` rewrites the snapshot from a
base server (2,840 items, 275 recipes); `report` prints the problem counts and the bands below; `income BASE_DATA`
the gold per hour.

**Price of a plain copy** (`base(id)`), in this order:
- Never sold to an NPC (`unsellable`, with the reason): currency (gold, platinum and crystal coins, the crafting orbs,
  rune and charm shards, faction tokens, base tokens and coins), keys (Rift Keys, omen items, the Ascended items), quest
  items (`item_price_rules.csv`), store items (the items of `shop_config.lua`, the Whetstone among them: no coin to gold
  path), store-bound items (the pouches, the Everfull Ration), the professions' materials (the Material Broker buys
  them at his weekly price) and uniques ("unique: salvage or market": every copy with `chaos_unique` and the four
  unique charms; chase items, an NPC floor would turn them into gold and undercut the market). 147 ids.
- A fixed price of a Chaos source: creature products and fist weapons (their csv `sell`, which their install steps also
  write; CI checks both agree), gems 400 / 1,200 / 3,600 / 10,800 / 32,400 by tier (three combine into one, so a tier is
  worth at most three of the one below), supports 500 to 40,500 by level, charms 2,000 / 4,000 / 8,000 by size.
- Else the base NPC price: the highest any NPC in the game pays (spawned in the map or created by a script; an
  unspawned staff NPC and table shops in another coin are left out). 1,336 items.
- Else a formula. Equipment: by its level requirement (200 gold at 0, 1,000 at 20, 8,000 at 50, 20,000 at 80, 30,000
  at 120, 45,000 at 200, 60,000 at 300, 90,000 at 500, 160,000 at 1000) x the slot (two-handed 1.2, body 1.1, weapon 1,
  shield, head, legs 0.9, feet, ring, amulet 0.8 ...). Other loot: by the level of the lowest monster that drops it
  (15 gold at 1, 150 at 50, 350 at 100, 900 at 200, 2,500 at 300, 6,000 at 500, 20,000 at 1200) x its best drop chance
  (x0.5 at 25%+, x1 at 5%+, x2 at 1%+, x4 at 0.2%+, x8 rarer): a rarer drop is worth more.
- Equipment (not fixed) x0.31, the gear scale: 1 / 3.27, the expected rarity multiplier of a monster's gear drop
  (`loot_config.lua` gear: 56% of gear drops have no rarity). An average drop is worth what it was, a rare copy much more.
- Floors: a drop of monsters of level 200+ is worth at least a quarter of its formula value (no late drop below early
  trash); a crafted item that is not equipment at least what its materials sell for; crafted equipment at least 20% of
  them (a crafted copy rolls a rarity and item level, at most x1.9 expected, `craft_bonus_config.lua`); 2 gold for
  anything sellable.
- Caps: crafted equipment at most an hour of hunting gold at its level band (`gamble_config.lua` `balance.hunting`; the
  band is its level requirement or the highest lowest-monster level of its materials; 14 items). Every piece of
  equipment at most 30,252 for a plain copy: the Wandering Merchant's Orb of Gilding (250,000) adds x4.25 on average
  to a plain copy and his Orb of Fate (120,000) x0.55, so at item level 150 neither pays off (90% margin; 150 items,
  the inferniarch weapons at 14.9M before among them). A base the Gambler sells keeps its expected sale (x3.45, his rarity odds, and the item level) under 90% of his
  price at every level he offers it (152 items); at most half of what the NPCs ask for the item (the median of their
  gold prices), a fifth for supplies (potions, runes, ammunition); goods an NPC sells for 1-2 gold sell for 1.

**Price of a copy** (`ChaosItemPrices.sellPrice(item)`): base x R x L, rounded down.
- R, the rarity: none or Common 1, Uncommon 1.5, Magic 3, Rare 6, Legendary 12, Divine 24 (an old id maps to its rarity). Charms: Faint 1, Glowing 1.5,
  Radiant 3. A unique copy (`chaos_unique`) is 0: never sold.
- L, the item level (`chaos_ilvl`, equipment and charms): 1 + item level / 200 (x1.18 at item level 36, a level 100
  monster's drop; x1.45 at 90, level 500; x1.75 at 150).
- Example: a level 1000 gear drop with a plain price of 17,500 (the median of that band) sells for 20,000 plain at item level
  30, 344,000 as a Legendary at item level 128 (3.6% of an hour of hunting at level 1000).

**Prices by band** (lootable items by the level of the lowest monster that drops them, plain copies):

| Lowest monster level | Items | Median | 75th percentile | Highest |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1-49 | 858 | 75 | 280 | 28,000 |
| 50-99 | 309 | 600 | 3,100 | 250,000 |
| 100-199 | 248 | 930 | 4,600 | 72,680 |
| 200-299 | 97 | 6,100 | 11,000 | 115,800 |
| 300-499 | 233 | 9,100 | 15,000 | 90,000 |
| 500-799 | 119 | 13,000 | 29,000 | 490,000 |
| 800+ | 322 | 17,500 | 33,000 | 5,400,000 |

**Problems found and fixed** (`gen_item_prices.py report`; before = the base NPC prices of the NPCs in the game):

| Problem | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| lootable or craftable items no NPC buys (what the Auto Seller could not sell) | 1,106 | 0 |
| an NPC sells an item for less than another one pays (arbitrage) | 4 (113 with the unspawned staff NPC) | 0 |
| real loot for 1 gold | 4 | 11 (goods an NPC sells for 1-2 gold) |
| one item, different prices at different NPCs | 63 | 0 |
| drops of level 300+ monsters under 100 gold | 413 | 2 (salmon and broccoli, sold by NPCs for 6 and 3) |
| recipes whose product sells for less than its materials (equipment: 20%) | 168 | 0 (+148 crafted equipment capped on purpose: the merchant cap, the Gambler's price, an hour of hunting) |
| crafted equipment whose expected sale beats materials + cost | 20 | 0 |
