| crafting loops (NPC-bought materials + cost < product) | 0 | 0 |

Also found: the old `gen_sell_prices.py` read the `{id, buy, sell}` tables of NPCs that trade in a coin of their own
(a crafting NPC's "dorn coins") as gold, and counted NPCs that are not in the game. `gen_sell_prices.py` now runs
`gen_item_prices.py`.

**Gold per hour** (`gen_item_prices.py income BASE_DATA --old <the previous sell_prices.lua>`, the "Respec" hunting
model; the items of the best hunt at the old and the new prices, a gear drop at its expected rarity and item level):

| Level | Best hunt | Coins / h | Items / h before | Items / h after | Total before | Total after | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | Rotworms | 119,901 | 53,653 | 54,622 | 173,554 | 174,523 | +1% |
| 40 | Rotworms | 138,478 | 61,966 | 63,085 | 200,443 | 201,563 | +1% |
| 100 | Dragons | 67,777 | 291,062 | 252,412 | 358,839 | 320,189 | -11% |
| 300 | Demons | 158,430 | 723,436 | 779,232 | 881,866 | 937,662 | +6% |
| 500 | Soul War | 1,383,928 | 3,895,144 | 4,345,026 | 5,279,072 | 5,728,954 | +9% |
| 1000 | Soul War | 2,374,515 | 6,683,208 | 7,455,106 | 9,057,723 | 9,829,621 | +9% |

The model overcounts kills at levels 8 and 40 (one DPS curve for every level); the change in percent is what counts.
Dragons lose 11%: their gear is a Gambler base, capped by his price. The uniques of the loot layer were never in
the model (no NPC bought them before either). The respec prices and the other gold sinks keep
their numbers.

**The Loot Buyer** (`data/npc/Loot Buyer.xml`, `data/npc/scripts/loot_buyer.lua`; placed (Cinderhold: in its stall in the hub; else next to the temple) at
startup by `item_prices.lua`, offsets in `item_prices_config.lua`).

**Startup NPC placement** (`npc_place.lua`, `npc_place_core.lua`, `data/lib/chaos_npc_focus.lua`; `tests/npc_place_test.lua`).
Live test 2026-10-14: no Loot Buyer at Nightwrack and Scorchveil (every fixed offset a wall or taken) and the Loot Buyer
next to the Gambler (one "hi" / "trade" opened both windows). The Loot Buyer, the Gambler, the Ascendant Oracle,
Archivist Maelis, the Material Brokers and the faction NPCs now place through `ChaosNpcPlace.place`: the configured
offsets first, then every tile a player can walk to from the temple (closed doors count as walkable, never as a spot),
nearest walking distance first, up to 14 tiles; never on or next to the temple tile, not in a one-tile corridor unless
nothing else is left, and at least 4 tiles (Chebyshev) from every other NPC: beyond the talk radius (3). The order is
fixed, so a restart gives the same spots. Start log 2026-10-16: still no Loot Buyer at Nightwrack. Its temple (floor 6)
is a room of about 25 tiles left only by stairs; a base NPC and the Material Broker stand in it and no tile keeps 4 tiles
from both. `item_prices_config.lua` `npc.place.depotFallback = true`: with no spot at the temple the same search runs
around the town's nearest depot of the map markers (`data/chaos_poi.lua`, same floor first, at most 64 tiles away;
`ChaosNpcPlaceCore.depotAnchors`, `tests/npc_place_test.lua`). On top of that our NPC scripts answer a player only when he talks to them
already or no other NPC within the talk radius stands nearer (a tie: the lower creature id), so one greeting never opens
two windows. "trade": the window lists only what the player
carries (backpack and its containers, not the equipped items) at the plain price; a sale pays every copy at its own
price, takes no locked item (the item lock), no unique and no container with items. "appraise": the most valuable
copies carried and what the bags are worth. Asked about uniques he sends the player to salvage or the market.
Asked about coins, orbs, keys, ores or herbs he says where they go.

**Install** (`install_all.py` step `itemprices`, after `runes`; `tools/install_item_prices.py DATA_DIR [--dry-run]`,
idempotent): copies the Loot Buyer; in every base NPC shop (XML `shop_sellable` / `shop_buyable`, Lua
`addSellableItem` / `addBuyableItem`, `{id, buy, sell}` tables of gold shops) the sell price of a priced item becomes
the table's price and a buy price under it is raised to twice it. Only the numbers change. On the base server: 136 NPC
files, 1,826 sell prices, 125 buy prices; a second run changes nothing. Items the table does not price keep their
entries (a base NPC that buys a token keeps doing so).

**API** (`ChaosItemPrices`, any Lua state): `sellPrice(itemOrId[, count])`, `basePrice(id)`, `unsellable(id)`,
`reasonText(id)`, `priceFor(id, {rarity, ilvl, unique, charmRarity})` (a unique: 0), `instanceInfo(item)`,
`minBuyPrice(id)`, `prices()`, `saleBlock(item)`, `carried(player[, id])`, `sell(player, items, amount)`.
**Auto Seller:** it reads `sell_prices.lua`, so it already pays the table's plain prices. To pay rolled copies their
own price, `autosell.lua` replaces `local gold = services().sellPrice(id, count, PRICES)` with
`local gold = ChaosItemPrices and ChaosItemPrices.sellPrice(item, count) or services().sellPrice(id, count, PRICES)`.

**Tests.** `server/tests/item_prices_test.lua` (LuaJIT and Lua 5.3): the data (every price whole and positive, no id
both priced and unsellable, every reason documented), the unsellable ids, `sell_prices.lua` = the table, the formula
(each rarity, item level, cap, a unique copy 0, charms, not-gear items), the sale rules on mocked items (locked, unique,
a full container, stacks, the backpack walk), no arbitrage against the Wandering Merchant (Gilding or Fate from him
on the best plain equipment, with the real orb tables) and the rune supply, the
Gambler's expected sale under his price for every base and level (with his real `K.odds`), the NPC placement.
`server/tools/install_item_prices_test.py`: the installer on synthetic NPC files. `gen_item_prices.py --check`: every
lootable or craftable item priced or unsellable, no sell price above a cap or a Chaos NPC's price, the product / fist
csv prices, the Auto Seller's table.

Live test 2026-10-14: the Loot Buyer stood next to 18 of the 20 temples (none free at Nightwrack); its trade window listed the carried items, four plate armours of different rarities and item levels sold at base x rarity x level (120 to 2,520 each), a unique was refused; no XML shop sells below the table's price. Not verified in game: "appraise".

## Junk loot (`tools/patch_junk_loot.py`, `tools/patch_junk_loot_test.py`, `data/items/item_price_rules.csv`)

Owner approval 2026-10-20: items that only sell (no gear, supply, food, currency, craft or quest use) leave the Chaos
monsters' loot. 52 are removed. **Six stay in their loot** (owner decision 2026-10-20): 27053 (cracked alabaster vase) and
29001 (colourful snail shell), never checked against the base server, and 6097 (hook), 6098 (eye patch), 6088 and 6090
(music sheets), which may be map quest items. Grep the real `actions`, `npc` and quest data for them before removing.
- `python3 -I tools/patch_junk_loot.py [DATA_DIR] [--check]` deletes the loot line of each listed id in
  `monster/monsters/chaos/**/*.xml` (inside `<loot>`) and `monster/lua/chaos/*.lua` (`monster.loot`), nothing else.
  Idempotent; `--check` exits 1 while a junk line is left; `--list` prints the ids. Run it after any tool that re-adds
  loot. `tune_monsters.py` and `late_game.py` do not write these ids (checked).
- The removed ids: 25380 and 25379 tokens, 21399, 9006, 23563, 28036 (items of another world or a floor tile), gems
  2145 and 2153-2158, 5879, 5913, 6500, 8303, 10567, 10603, 11231, 12401, 12409, 12436, 18425, 20102, 23569 and the creature
  products 36010-36035 (26 items).
- Nothing is deleted from the game: the items stay in `items.xml`, `art_items.csv`, `chaos_pack_items.lua`, Grimgan's
  shop list and the stash (tab 109 holds creature products a player already has; no monster fills it now). Copies the
  players hold keep selling: the price table is built from the loot, so seven ids that only a monster put there got a
  fixed price in `item_price_rules.csv` (25380 3800, 25379 300, 21399 98000, 9006 110000, 23563 88000, 28036 62000, 2157
  200; 2157 would have gone from 200 to 1600 by the formula). `gen_item_prices.py` was run: the table and
  `sell_prices.lua` hold the same 3393 prices as before.
- Income: the junk was about 1% of the expected sell value of the loot; watch the hunting income
  (`gen_item_prices.py income BASE_DATA`) and adjust gold if the hour of hunting drops.

## Badge slot (`badges.lua`, `badges_core.lua`, `tools/patch_badges.py`, `src-patches/0058-badge-slot-no-second-ring.patch`, client base patch 0113, client `game_badgeslot`)

Beta question 2026-10-22: a player found a Moon Amplifier Catalyst [1] and asked what a Moon Badge is. The base engine
has five extra inventory slots: deck (12), badge (13), ship (14), belt (15), gloves (16). Our client drew slots 1-10
only, so nothing worn there could be seen or taken off. The first answer (commit bf2919f7) retired the badges. Owner
decision 2026-10-21: "tire o slot extra de ring e coloque o badge" (take out the extra ring slot and put the badge
there). So the badges are back in slot 13, drawn where the ammunition slot (the second ring slot) was. A server that
installed bf2919f7's `badges` step needs a fresh base copy before this install: that step took the badges out of the
boss loot, the task rewards and the roulette, and no tool puts them back.

- **What badges are.** A base system: 40 badges (27803-27842), nine lines of four or five tiers (Raging, Furious,
  Tempest, Blazing, Eternal) of Exiled Spirit, Fury, Moon, Night Seeker, Earthshade, Reborn, Chaosfiend, Veins and
  Daybreak. Armour 2-5 and the line's stats: an absorb, skills, health and mana, life or mana leech, critical hits. 31
  amplifier catalysts (27843-27873) upgrade a badge one tier at 35 / 25 / 15 / 10% (the base action
  `badges_upgrade.lua`). 16 base bosses drop the Raging badges and the catalysts. The Eternal Moon Badge (27815) is a
  container of 10. A badge is gear for the Chaos systems (`ChaosCrafting.isGear`: item level, rarity, orbs; modifier
  kind "other").
- **Engine** (src-patch 0058, after 0001-0057): items.xml slot type `badge` is the badge bit only (`patch_badges.py`
  writes it on the 40 badges; the decks keep `deckbadge`, deck and badge bits). `Player::queryAdd`: slot 13 takes a
  badge and refuses an item with the deck bit; slots 10, 12, 14, 15 and 16 take nothing. `getSlotType` sends a badge
  to slot 13 (the equip hotkey, the right-click equip of 0024). 0023's ring swap between slots 9 and 10 and the
  hotkey's second ring go. `Player::queryDestination` asks `queryAdd` with flags 0, so `addItem` without a slot no
  longer reaches a hidden slot.
- **Client** (base patch 0113, client/BASE.md): `InventorySlotBadge` = 13; the inventory window's ammunition widget is
  the badge widget (`slot13`, position `{65535, 13, 0}`; the protocol carried slot 13 already, base patch 0012); the
  action bar, hotkeys, NPC trade and equipment presets look at slot 13. The art is generated (`client/tools/gen_skin.py`
  group `badge`). The overlay: `game_badgeslot` (tooltip "Badge"), the inspect window, the rarity glow, the shader
  effects and the right-click equip cover slot 13. On the server: the item tooltip compares a badge with slot 13 and a
  ring with slot 9 only; inspect, loadouts, the new-player kit and the slot loops of the Chaos scripts take 13, not 10.
- **The retired slots keep their items' other uses.** A deck the player carries holds the cards (`ChaosBadges.deckOf`
  in the base deck system). A carried ship sails from the docks and opens its trainer portal (`ChaosBadges.boardShip`
  in the base sea tiles). Belts and gloves (24 items, slot type `beltgloves`) have no other use: they can't be worn,
  and since 2026-10-22 the base armorsmith no longer crafts them (its only source; coordinator decision); the Loot
  Buyer buys the copies players hold. Decks and ships keep their sources (the monster loot, the task deck, the first
  ship), as they work when carried; only the roulette lost them ("Prizes into the backpack"). Veyra the Apothecary sells
  the three decks ("The Apothecary"). The items.xml
  descriptions say so. `Player:onMoveItem` refuses a move into a retired
  slot with a message (the engine refuses it too).
- **Migration at login**, idempotent, never deletes: every item in a slot no client draws (12, 14, 15, 16, a deck in
  13; `ChaosBadges.checkSlots`) and anything in slot 10 (a ring of the second ring slot included;
  `ChaosArchery.checkHands`, "Infinite arrows and quivers") moves to the store inbox ("Purse"), else the depot inbox
  (`ChaosPrizes.toInbox`: `moveTo` with `FLAG_NOLIMIT`, no stacking). The de-equip events run. The character is saved
  at once and told what moved. An item that fits nowhere stays and the next login tries again. Nothing to move:
  nothing changes. The base's "one badge at a time" storage (249578) is cleared at login when no badge with that id is
  worn, so a badge that left the slot without its de-equip can't lock the slot. No retired item leaves the game, so
  nothing is refunded.
- **The Eternal Moon Badge** in slot 13: its weight counts; loot goes into it like any open container; containers in
  it are ordinary bags. The base death loss (`droploot.lua`) looped over slots 1-10, so a badge never dropped and the
  Eternal Moon Badge was a death-safe bag of 10: `patch_badges.py` step 7 makes the loop take slot 13 (not 11, the
  store inbox, nor the retired slots). The right-click of src-patch 0024 opens it (a container is not equipped on use):
  drag it to the slot.
- **Fixes on the way:** the base boss loot named "exiled amplifier catalyst [3]" twice and the Fury catalyst [3] never
  (`patch_badges.py` step 2); a hand-only item without stats no longer counts as gear (a catalyst got an item level).
- **Balance** (`server/data/spells/README.md` "Badge slot"): the badge replaces the second ring. Its absorbs pass the
  75 percent ceiling of src-patch 0049 (`Player::blockHit` loops slots 1-13); its leech and critical hit add to
  the engine sums like any item; the stock chances were scaled to two thirds (`patch_base_events.py`). Every Chaos
  modifier a ring may roll still reaches its cap at tier 8 with one ring (`tests/archery_test.lua`).

`tools/patch_badges.py DATA_DIR [--dry-run] [--check]` (install_all.py step `badges`, after `itemnames`), idempotent:
1. items.xml: the badges get slot type `badge`; the decks, ships, belts and gloves get their description. The 76
   cards the deck system turns on (`CARDS`: 27482-27541 and the level 6 legendaries 27547-27631 every 6th, 27640) get the
   description of `data/items/card_descriptions.csv` ("Cards and decks"): what the card gives, with the Chaos name of the
   spell, then `CARD_HINT` ("Use it to put it in a deck you carry and turn it on, use it again to turn it off. Veyra the
   Apothecary sells decks."). A card the file lacks keeps its text with the hint appended. The legendary levels 1-5 only
   upgrade: no hint. English in items.xml (one text for every viewer); the tooltip and Character Info are in the player's
   language (pt-BR in `i18n_strings.lua`).
2. the boss loot's Fury catalyst [3].
3. `Player:onMoveItem` asks `ChaosBadges.onMoveItem` first.
4. the base deck system: the card action asks `ChaosCards.use` first, and the cards are looked for in the carried deck.
5. the base sea tiles: a carried ship sails.
6. the ship NPC says to carry the ship.
7. `droploot.lua`: the death loss takes slot 13.
8. the base crafting lists (`Crafting.<table> = {`): the 24 belt and gloves recipes of the armorsmith go into block
   comments (marked), the other 67 recipes keep their order.

**Tests.** `tests/badges_test.lua` (ids, texts and pt-BR, the move rule, the login moves into the store inbox, the
depot inbox, nowhere, once; the stale storage; the glue on a mocked engine), `tools/patch_badges_test.py` (a small
data folder, CRLF kept, the armorsmith list still loads without the gloves, a second run, `--check`), `tests/archery_test.lua` (slot 10: the ring and anything else to the
Purse; the jewel budget), `tests/item_tooltip_test.lua`, `tests/inspect_test.lua`, `tests/loadouts_test.lua`,
`tests/crafting_test.lua`; client `badgeslotlogic_test.lua`, `playerinspect_logic_test.lua`,
`rightclickequiplogic_test.lua`. The server chain 0001-0058 and the client chain 0001-0113 apply in order;
`g++ -fsyntax-only` of the changed engine files has no errors. The install on a copy of the base data: 23 files, a
second run changes nothing, the patched Lua parses in Lua 5.3 and LuaJIT. Not run on a live server or seen in a client.

## Prizes into the backpack (`prizes.lua`, `prizes_core.lua`, `tools/patch_prizes.py`, `tests/prizes_test.lua`)

User report 2026-10-21: the Boss Roulette said "you won The Awakener" (a ship) and the ship was in no bag and not in
the inbox. The base gives prizes with `player:addItem(id, count)` (index `INDEX_WHEREEVER`), and the engine puts a new
item into an empty inventory slot that takes it before any container: the ship went into the ship slot (14), which no
client draws. Any deck, ship, belt, gloves or badge prize could do it. Src-patch 0058 closes it in the engine (the
hidden slots take nothing); the base scripts that hand out prizes now go through `ChaosPrizes`, which never uses an
inventory slot:

- `ChaosPrizes.give(player, id, count[, charges])`: new items into the backpack or a container in it, else the store
  inbox ("Purse", `FLAG_NOLIMIT`), else the ground under the player; the player is told when it is not the backpack.
  Stacks split at 100. Returns the last place used, nil when nothing could be given (the caller falls back).
- `ChaosPrizes.stow(player, item)`: an item the script made, into the backpack or a container in it.
- `ChaosPrizes.toInbox(player, item)`: a worn item of a hidden slot into the store inbox, else the depot inbox.
- `ChaosPrizes.rouletteReward(playerId, config, position, label)`: the roulettes' reward.

`tools/patch_prizes.py DATA_DIR [--dry-run] [--check]` (install_all.py step `prizes`, after `badges` and
`basecrafting`), idempotent, CRLF kept, base scripts found by content:
1. **The roulettes** (every script with `local function rewardPlayer(playerId, leverPosition)` and a `prizePool`; the
   base has five: the boss, exercise and premium roulettes and the two crystal token roulettes). `rewardPlayer` asks
   `ChaosPrizes.rouletteReward` first: the prize on the winning tile goes in as above, the free spin storage is
   cleared, a rare prize is broadcast as before. The base looked up `chancedItems[#chancedItems - 3]` for the
   broadcast, the chance of another spin's item, nil after fewer than four spins (a Lua error before the reward). Now
   the pool's chance of the won item decides (`ChaosPrizesCore.isRare`). The winning tile's top thing can be nothing,
   a creature or the ground when the tile changed: then nothing is given, the storage stays and the next spin is free,
   with a message. `initiateReward` reads the tile the same guarded way. The base body stays as the fallback without the
   Chaos scripts, with both nil guards. The prize pool lines of the decks and ships are commented out: the boss roulette
   loses 27633, 27634 and 27797; the other four roulettes have no retired item.
2. **The task rewards** (`self:addItem(reward.Id, reward.Amount)`): `ChaosPrizes.give` first. One task gives a deck.
3. **The base crafting script** after `patch_base_crafting.py`: `ChaosPrizes.stow` first, then the base `addItemEx`
   (crafted belts and gloves went into their slots).
4. **The ship NPC** (`player:addItem(27799, 1)`): `ChaosPrizes.give` first.

No other base script hands out a deck, ship, belt or gloves (searched by id and by name). A badge prize lands in a
visible slot at worst.

**Boss roulette odds** (superseded by "Boss Roulette and uniques in the hunts (O148)" below; `ChaosPrizesCore.odds`: every entry rolls its chance in 10000, one of the hits is picked at
random, no hit rolls again; exact). The three retired entries were 27.8% of the spins. Their chances are left out and
the others keep theirs, so every remaining prize is about 1.35 times as likely: the Furious badges 15.7 / 14.9 / 13.8 /
11.0 / 10.5 / 8.8 / 7.4 / 6.3 / 5.2% (were 11.2 / 10.6 / 9.9 / 7.9 / 7.6 / 6.4 / 5.4 / 4.6 / 3.8%), each of the four
level-6 items 1.6% (was 1.2%; together 6.4%, was 4.8%). The token price is unchanged.

**Tests.** `tests/prizes_test.lua` (luajit and lua5.3): the winner rule (nothing, a creature, the ground, an ignored
decoration, charges), the rare rule, the pool cleaning, the odds against brute force and the boss pool's numbers; the
glue on a mocked engine whose `addItem` and `addItemEx` raise an error: the backpack, a bag in it, the Purse, the
ground, nowhere; stacks, charges; `toInbox`; `rouletteReward` with a prize, a rare prize, an empty, creature, ground or
decoration tile, no tile, a logged-out player, no room anywhere. `tools/patch_prizes_test.py`: a small data folder (two
roulettes, one it can't read left alone, CRLF, the pool lines, the hook's tile and label, the guards, the task, crafting
and NPC lines, a second run, `--check`, the patched Lua parses). On a copy of the base data: 8 files, a second run
changes nothing, every patched file parses in Lua 5.3 and LuaJIT. Not run on a live server.

## Boss Roulette and uniques in the hunts (O148)

Beta feedback 2026-10-23, two reports: (1) "I spun the Boss Roulette twice. One reward was the golden deck, the other a boat. The
roulette also shows lots of card rewards. Some rewards look useless on this server." (2) "I killed loads of Rare and Legendary
monsters standing in hunts (~1000) and never got a Unique, only gear they already drop, more orbs and gold. I understood Rare
monsters beyond some level had a chance at a Unique."

### The Boss Roulette (`boss_roulette_config.lua`, `tools/patch_roulette.py`, `prizes.lua`/`prizes_core.lua`, `tests/boss_roulette_test.lua`)

**What it was.** The base boss roulette (lever room, token 28033) had 16 prizes: three decks and a ship (27.8% of the spins, the
golden deck and The Awakener ship the player saw), nine Furious badges and four legendary level 6 cards. The prizes step of
2026-10-22 already took the decks and the ship out of the install, so a beta server that had not installed it still showed them;
what was left was 93.6% Furious badges (the second of five tiers) and 6.4% cards, no orb, no gold, no unique. Nothing in it came
from the loot models.

**What it is.** The pool is `data/scripts/chaos/boss_roulette_config.lua` (one line per prize: id, count, chance, kind). The install
step `roulette` (`tools/patch_roulette.py`, after `prizes`, idempotent, CRLF kept) writes those lines into the `prizePool` of the base
boss roulette script (found by its "Boss Roulette requires" text) and sets the broadcast threshold to the config's `rareThreshold`
(120: only the chase orbs are announced). The other four roulettes got their own pools in O151 (next section).
The base draw stays: every entry rolls its chance in 10000, one hit is picked at random (`ChaosPrizesCore.odds` is exact).

| Kind | Prizes | Share of the spins |
|---|---|---|
| Crafting orbs | 16 of the orbs the loot layer drops (`loot_config.lua` `currency.entries`): Awakening, Whetstone, Upheaval, Tempering, Gilding, Unmaking, Erasure, Fate, Grafting, Reforging, Excision, Binding, Ember, Crown, Void, Ruin, in stacks of 1-3 | 63.0% |
| Sockets | Orb of Sockets, 1-3 | 5.0% |
| Gold | three purses (1, 2 or 5 crystal coins on the tile) | 20.7% |
| Unique chest | one chest on the tile | 0.6% |
| Badges | the nine Furious badges | 5.4% |
| Amplifier catalysts | the first catalyst of each badge line | 4.3% |
| Cards | 2 of the 4 legendary level 6 cards | 1.0% |
| Decks, ships, belts, gloves, boats | none (the config's `retired` list and `patch_badges.py` are checked by the tests) | 0% |

- **Gold scales with the level.** The tile shows N crystal coins; the prize is N x `gold.perUnit` (0.2) of an hour of hunting gold at
  the winner's level (`gamble_config.lua` `balance.hunting`, the same curve, kept equal by a test), paid as coin stacks, at least one
  crystal coin: 1 unit is 1 cc at level 8, 7 cc at 100, 190 cc at 1000. `ChaosPrizes.bossPrize` pays it and says the amount.
- **The unique chest** gives a unique of the winner's item level (`unique.low` 0.5 to `high` 1.0 of the level; the nearest below when
  the band is empty), never a season, Ascended or boss-only one, made with `ChaosMakeUnique` like a drop and announced. Without the
  unique scripts loaded the chest is the plain chest.
- **Expected value of one spin** (`tests/boss_roulette_test.lua` prints it): in kills of a level 100+ monster that the loot layer needs
  for the same drops (`normal` chance of the orb; the Orb of Ruin by its magic chance / 3), gold in kills of the level 1000 hunt
  (9.5M an hour, 870 kills an hour). Before (badges and cards only): 0 orbs, 0 gold, 6.4% cards, 93.6% badges. Base pool with the decks
  and the ship: 27.8% useless. Now: 1.16 orbs and 717,000 gold at level 1000 per spin = 788 + 66 kills, 1.0% cards. Computed, not
  measured on a server. The numbers are guesses against an unknown token drop rate (a token is a level 509+ monster drop): a spin is
  worth about 40 minutes of orb hunting; `chance` in the config is the knob, `limits` in it what the test holds (cards at most 6%,
  orbs, sockets and gold at least 40%, gold at least 12%, the unique chest between 0.3% and 2%).
- **Tests.** `tests/boss_roulette_test.lua` (luajit and lua5.3): no retired id (decks, ships, belts, gloves), every id known to the
  committed item lists and the Chaos configs (a dead id fails), no repeated prize, the odds add up to 1, the card share, the orbs are
  the orbs the loot layer drops, the chase orbs stay under 1%, the gold curve equals `gamble_config.lua`, gold never falls with the
  level, the coin stacks add up, the chest has a unique at every level, the value of a spin before and after.
  `tests/prizes_test.lua`: gold and chest through `rouletteReward` on a mocked engine, other roulettes keep the plain item.
  `tools/patch_roulette_test.py`: the real config, a small data folder (boss roulette changes, exercise roulette and an unreadable
  one do not), the threshold, CRLF, a second run, a changed config, a retired id refused; with `CHAOS_ITEMS_XML=/path/items.xml` it
  also checks every id against an installed base `items.xml`.
- **Deploy.** `install_all.py SERVER_DIR --only files,roulette` and a server restart (the lever script reads the pool at load). The
  other items on the tiles are existing items; no client change, no new text.

### Uniques from Rare and Legendary monsters in the hunts (`loot.lua`, `loot_config.lua` `unique.open`, `tests/unique_hunt_test.lua`)

**Not a crash, three real causes** (found by reading `L.rollUniques` and the `processKill` unique step; no code path was broken, the
drop could not happen):
1. **The monster list.** Every unique has a `monsters` name list; the endgame uniques (item level 900-2400,
   `minMonsterLevel` 800-1000, the only ones for a level 1500 character) listed twelve waystone monsters and bosses and no hunt
   monster, so no Azure Dragon, Golden Lord or other monster of the level-scaled hunts could drop one. The lower uniques list
   stock monsters of level 20-150.
2. **The pack factor.** The unique roll was `item find x pace`, the loot factor of the pack (0.163-0.204 at level 1500, the thin
   per-kill factor that keeps gold per hour), while Rare gear keeps the `notable` share (1 from monster level 700). A unique was
   thinned to a fifth.
3. **The level.** The `minMonsterLevel` gate read `Monster:getMonsterLevel()`, which is 0 for a base monster and for a waystone
   map's monster (their level comes from `ChaosLoot.monsterLevel` and the waystone run), so even listed waystone monsters failed it
   where the engine level was 0.

**The fix.** (a) `unique.open` in `loot_config.lua`: an entry with a `minMonsterLevel` (not boss-only) drops from any Rare or better
monster of that level or more, whatever its name, at `mult` (0.5) x its chance (below the level nothing changes; the lists still
rule the lower uniques). (b) `ChaosLoot.uniquePace`: the unique roll reads the notable share of the corpse (`L.corpseFactors`), at
least the loot factor. (c) The roll gets `max(getMonsterLevel, ChaosLoot.monsterLevel)`. The Conquest bad-luck protection already
covered these rolls (group `monster`: +1% per miss, up to x3); an open drop now counts as an eligible roll, so it works for the
hunts too (`conquest_config.lua` `pity`, unchanged).

**Numbers** (level 1500, the hunt monsters of `late_game_spawns.csv`, Rare : Legendary kills 150 : 25 as spawned, exact sums over the
entries, sampled with `L.rollUniques`):

| | Uniques per 1000 Rare / Legendary kills | One per |
|---|---|---|
| Before (computed / sampled) | 0.65 / 0.9 (all of it from four stock names; any other monster 0) | about 1,100-1,500 kills |
| Open rule only, loot factor kept | 6.5 | 154 kills |
| Now (open x0.5, notable share) | 17.4 computed / 17.8 sampled | 57 kills |

A hunter in the late sets kills about 830 monsters an hour and about 17 of them are Rare or Legendary (spawn chance 1.5% and 0.25%),
so the farmer sees one unique about every 3.4 hours, plus the pity. The drops are 21 uniques of item level 900-2200, 8 of them wearable at
level 1500; the rest wait for a higher level or a trade. `tools/loot_model.lua --check`, `tools/gear_coverage.lua --check` and `tools/weapon_coverage.lua --check`
stay green (uniques are not in the gold or item model; the coverage tool reads the entries' own chance, unchanged).
`tests/unique_hunt_test.lua` (luajit and lua5.3) proves it: before below 1 per 1000, now 10-25, one every 2.5-6 hours, the level and
list rules, boss-only entries keep their bosses, `open.enabled = false` brings the old behaviour back.

## Roulette prizes against token drops (O151)

Follow-up of O148, which rebuilt the Boss Roulette and left "the other four roulettes untouched" and "Open: the roulette value against the
token drop rate". This section audits the four others the same way (stale prizes, decks and boats, too many of one kind, items that do not
scale with the level), puts them through the same config and idempotent patch route, and works out what one spin of each of the five is
worth against how long its token takes to earn. Computed from the configs, not run on a server.

### The five roulettes (`actionId` of the base script, token, spin cost)

| Roulette | Script | actionId | Token (one spin) | Where the token comes from |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Boss | `customs/roulette/roulette.lua` | 18562 | Boss Token (28033), 1 | 43 base bosses of level 509+, mean chance 8.4%, 1-2 per drop |
| Exercise | `customs/roulette/roulette2.lua` | 18563 | Exercise Token (28058), 1 | the same 43 bosses, mean chance 6.3% |
| Premium | `customs/roulette/roulette3.lua` | 18564 | Ticket Roulette (28057), 1 | 22 bosses of level 1018+, mean chance 5.4% |
| Crystal (two) | `customs/tower_defense/roulette_crystal_token.lua` and `_2.lua` | 18565, 18566 | Crystal Token (28372), 15 | 5 per completed Tower Defense run (the base script's reward) |

The token sources were read from the base monster files (the survey in `data/items/base_item_values.csv` counts the monsters and the first
level; the mean chances come from the same files, `roulette_value_config.lua` `tokens`). `tests/roulette_pools_test.lua` checks the counts
and the levels against the snapshot.

### What the four others were

- **Exercise** (21 prizes, 7 chests of each of three charge tiers). All exercise weapon chests. Six of the 21 are the sword, axe and club
  kinds that are one melee weapon since 2026-10-23 (the axe and club chests left the shop lists), and a class can train with only the kinds
  of its line: a Ranger could use 29% of the spins, a Mystic or Necromancer 43%, a Warrior or Monk 57%, a Templar 86%. The chests are worth
  100,000 / 360,000 / 2.8M gold at a vendor. The token is the second rarest: about 84 minutes of boss hunting. A spin was worth 2.6 minutes of
  hunting at level 1000.
- **Premium** (14 prizes): 5 auras and 9 wings, each a one-time unlock (a second copy says "you already have this" and sells for 65,000-98,000
  gold). Every spin was broadcast (threshold 10000). The token is the rarest: about 99 minutes. Nothing in the pool came from the loot models.
- **Crystal**, both scripts (23 prizes, the same pool in both): 21 "Moist" gear pieces (a sword with 56 attack, an armor of 25: fixed base
  items that do not scale with the level, most of them for a class the winner is not, one of them listed twice) and the two best Tower Defense
  units. The scripts were copies of the premium and exercise ones: they said "Premium Roulette requires" and "Exercise Roulette requires", and
  announced "from the premium roulette!" / "from the exercise roulette!" and passed that label to `ChaosPrizes`. The token cost is 3 Tower
  Defense runs.

### What they are now

The pools are `roulette_exercise_config.lua`, `roulette_premium_config.lua` and `roulette_crystal_config.lua` (the same shape as
`boss_roulette_config.lua`: one line per prize, `limits` for the tests, the gold and unique rules shared with the boss config).
`patch_roulette.py` (install step `roulette`) now writes all four pools, matching each base script to its config by the `actionId` of its
`config` table (the boss script also by its "Boss Roulette requires" text); a script whose `playItem` is not the config's token, or whose
`actionId` is unknown, is left alone; a pool with a retired id or one of the fixed base gear 28373-28393 is refused. The two crystal scripts
are named the Crystal Roulette (messages, broadcast, the label passed on). `prizes.lua` finds the config of a roulette by `config.actionId`
(`ChaosPrizesCore.configFor`; `ChaosRoulettePools`), so gold and the unique chest work on all five.

| Roulette | Entries | Spins | Theme kept |
|---|---|---|---|
| Exercise | 32 | orbs 43.1%, gold 36.4%, sockets 6.0%, chests 13.9%, unique chest 0.6% | the 15 exercise chests (melee, bow, rod, wand, shield x 3 tiers; no retired axe or club chest) |
| Premium | 36 | orbs 48.4%, gold 25.5%, sockets 6.3%, cosmetics 18.7%, unique chest 1.2% | all 14 auras and wings; chase orbs (Crown 0.5%, Void 0.3%, Ruin 0.08%) |
| Crystal (both) | 17 | orbs 55.3%, gold 30.0%, sockets 7.1%, units 7.0%, unique chest 0.5% | the Grimnir Slashbaiter and King Aldor Goldcrusher units (1-2 and 1) |

- **Orbs and sockets** are the loot layer's orbs (`loot_config.lua` `currency.entries`), in stacks that grow with the price of the token
  (exercise 1-5, premium 1-5). **Gold** is the crystal coins on the tile, each unit `gold.perUnit` (0.2) of an hour of hunting gold at the
  winner's level (the Boss Roulette's rule, `ChaosPrizes.bossPrize`): exercise 1 / 2 / 5 / 10 units, premium 2 / 5 / 10 / 20, crystal 1 / 2 / 5.
  **The unique chest** gives a unique of the winner's level.
- **The exercise chest is never dead.** The chest on the tile is a prize of its kind; when the winner's class cannot train with that kind, the
  chest becomes the chest of the same tier of a kind it can (`ChaosPrizesCore.classChest`, `ChaosExercise.allowed`; picked at random among the
  usable ones) and the player is told ("Your class cannot train with that weapon: the chest became ..."; pt-BR in `i18n_strings.lua`). The test
  walks every vocation, every chest and every pick.
- **Broadcasts.** Premium announces the chase orbs and the lasting exercise chests, the crystal one the Orb of Reforging; the gold, the unique
  chest, the cosmetics and the units never (the unique chest announces itself).
- **Nothing a spin can win is a deck, ship, boat, belt, gloves, a retired chest, or Moist gear.**

### The value of a spin against its token (`tools/roulette_model.lua`, `data/scripts/chaos/roulette_value_config.lua`)

`cd server && luajit tools/roulette_model.lua` prints the table; `--check` (luajit and lua5.3, in CI) fails when a spin leaves the band
0.80 - 1.35 of its token's cost at any of the levels 650 / 1000 / 1500 / 2000. Both sides are minutes of hunting at the winner's level.

**Cost of the token.** Boss, exercise and premium tokens drop from bosses: tokens per spin / (mean chance x mean count 1.5) boss kills, each
`minutesPerBossKill` = 8 minutes (walk in, fight, loot, walk out; the lever rooms stop a fight at 30 minutes; **a guess**, the one number to
measure on the beta). Crystal tokens: 15 / 5 per run = 3 Tower Defense runs of `minutesPerRun` = 15 minutes (the session lasts 20).

| Roulette | Token drops | Cost of a spin |
|---|---|---|
| Boss | 0.126 per boss kill (1 token = 8.0 kills) | 63.7 min |
| Exercise | 0.095 per kill (10.5 kills) | 84.0 min |
| Premium | 0.081 per kill (12.3 kills) | 98.6 min |
| Crystal | 5 per run (3.0 runs for 15) | 45.0 min |

**Value of the prizes.** Counted: crafting orbs and sockets in kills of a level 100+ monster that the loot layer needs for the same drops (the
O148 rule), divided by the hunter's kills per hour (`paceKillsPerHour.scaled` of `spawn_tuning.json`: 836 at level 650, 869 at 1000, 813 at
1600, 789 at 2000); gold in hours of hunting gold (0.2 h per unit, a minute count that does not depend on the level); an exercise chest as its
vendor price against the hunting gold per hour; a unique chest as 200 minutes (about one unique per 3.4 hours of Rare and Legendary kills at
level 1500, O148). Not counted: cards, badges, catalysts, cosmetics and units (they are not a time), so the figures are a floor.

| Roulette | Before (level 1000) | Now: 650 / 1000 / 1500 / 2000 | Value / cost at 1000 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Boss (O148, unchanged) | 60.1 min of 63.7 | 62.3 / 60.1 / 63.7 / 65.7 min | 0.94 |
| Exercise | 2.6 min of 84.0 (x0.03) | 81.8 / 79.4 / 83.1 / 85.1 min | 0.95 |
| Premium | 0 counted of 98.6 (14 cosmetics) | 99.8 / 96.8 / 101.9 / 104.6 min | 0.98 |
| Crystal | 0 counted of 45.0 (21 Moist pieces, 2 units) | 46.2 / 44.8 / 47.2 / 48.5 min | 0.99 |

At level 1000 one spin now pays on average: boss 1.16 orbs + 717,000 gold; exercise 1.32 orbs + 3.3M gold (and 2-5 sockets in 6% of the
spins); premium 1.44 orbs + 2.8M gold; crystal 0.96 orbs + 1.1M gold. The Boss Roulette needed no change: at 8 minutes per boss kill its
spin is 0.94 of its token, the value the others now match; the O148 note "a spin is worth about 40 minutes of orb hunting" is the orb half
of the 60 here (46 min of orbs, 9 of sockets, 4.5 of gold, 1.2 of the unique chest).

**Sensitivity.** The cost side scales with `minutesPerBossKill`: at 6 minutes the boss spin is worth 1.25 tokens' time and the premium one 1.3;
at 10 it is 0.75 and 0.8 (the band's floor; the figures stay inside the band for 7 to 10 minutes except the boss at 10). A measured value
replaces the guess in one place (`roulette_value_config.lua`) and `chance` / `count` in the three configs are the knobs; the Tower Defense
side is less uncertain (the reward and the 20 minute session are in the base script).

### Tests

- `tests/roulette_pools_test.lua` (luajit and lua5.3): per roulette no retired id (decks, ships, belts, gloves, retired chests, Moist gear),
  every id a known item, no repeated prize, a kind of that roulette, the odds add up, the shares in `limits`, the orbs are the ones the loot layer
  drops, the broadcast rules, the actionIds are the base roulettes' once each; exercise: chests are at most 18% and at least 5%, every chest of the
  table is in the pool, **every vocation of every class line gets a chest of the same tier it can train with for every chest and every pick**;
  premium: 14 auras and wings, at most 25% of the spins, the chase orbs at most 1% each; crystal: the units at most 12%, 15 tokens a spin; the value
  config equals what it copies (the pace of `spawn_tuning.json`, the gold curve of `gamble_config.lua`, the token sources of the snapshot); every
  roulette in the band at every level; the numbers before and after printed.
- `tests/prizes_test.lua`: `configFor` (by actionId, the boss label as fallback), `classChest` (every rule), the glue on a mocked engine: an
  exercise chest for a Ranger becomes a bow or shield chest and the player is told, a Warrior keeps the melee chest, gold on all four
  actionIds, the unique chest announced as the premium roulette's, an unknown actionId keeps the plain item.
- `tools/patch_roulette_test.py`: the three new configs parse and are clean, every id is known (and in an installed `items.xml` when
  `CHAOS_ITEMS_XML` points at it), a data folder with all five scripts (each gets its own pool, mark and threshold; the crystal ones lose the
  copied names; a wrong token, an unknown actionId and a script of another roulette's text are left alone), a second run, a changed config, CRLF,
  a retired or Moist id refused.
- `tools/roulette_model.lua --check` in CI; on a copy of the five installed base scripts: 5 files changed, a second run changes nothing, all
  five parse in Lua 5.3.

### Deploy

`install_all.py SERVER_DIR --only files,roulette` and a server restart (the scripts read the pools at load; `files` copies the new configs and
`prizes.lua`). No client change. Players see the Crystal Roulette named in the two Tower Defense rooms and the new prizes on the tiles.
Not run on a live server. To measure: kill a few boss rooms and time them (`minutesPerBossKill`), count the tokens per kill, and time a Tower
Defense run, then edit `roulette_value_config.lua` and rerun the model.

## Rings and necklaces as gear (`data/lib/chaos_jewelry.lua`, `chaos/jewelry.lua`, `tools/patch_base_jewelry.py`, `tests/jewelry_test.lua`)

Owner request 2026-10-22: "faça rings e necklaces iguais a equips normais. pra equipar, com affixo e suffixo" and
"distribua esses rings e necklaces na loot pool também".

**What the base had.** Most rings change id when worn (`transformEquipTo`: sword ring 2207 -> 2210 "sword fighting +4")
and the worn id runs out (`duration`, `decayTo` 0); most amulets have `charges` and vanish at 0. The engine keeps the
same item object through a transform (custom attributes survive), but a rolled copy still vanished when its time or
charges ran out, and the unworn id had no stats, so `L.isGearId` never rolled a rarity on it. Several unworn rings had
an Equip movement and no DeEquip (the worn id took the stats off).

**Install step `jewelry`** (`tools/patch_base_jewelry.py DATA_DIR [--dry-run] [--check] [--stock-looks]`, install_all.py after
`badges`, idempotent). For every `slotType` ring or necklace of `data/items/items.xml` that is not a consumable:

1. an unworn id whose worn id has stats gets those stats (the worn values win), loses `transformEquipTo`,
   `stopduration` and `showduration`, and gets `showattributes` 1;
2. a worn id (`duration`, `decayTo` 0, `transformDeEquipTo`) loses `duration`, `decayTo` and `showduration`, so a copy
   worn before the install keeps working and turns back when taken off;
3. `charges` and `showcharges` go.

`data/movements/movements.xml`: each unworn id of step 1 gets a DeEquip entry right after its Equip entry (fromid/toid
ranges count; both entries are added when it had none). On the base: 15 unworn ids merged, 15 worn ids without
duration, 15 without charges, 9 entries added (2166, 2168, 2207, 2208, 2209, 2214, 6300, 18408; Equip and DeEquip for
24717, whose 3% physical absorb never applied). No engine patch.

**Consumables** (`J.consumable`) keep the base rules and never carry a rarity: might ring, stealth, energy, time and
dwarven rings (both ids), amulet of loss, stone skin amulet and the four 5-charge elemental amulets (10218-10221). Worn
for ever they would break the game (invisibility, magic shield, haste, 80% absorbs, death protection).
`ChaosCrafting.isGear` and `L.isGearId` refuse them; `L.stripStackableRarity` takes off a rarity the stock roll gave.

**Gear gates.** `L.isGearId` (loot.lua `relevantType`) also counts a ring or necklace whose only stat is regeneration
or speed (life ring, ring of healing). The rest already treated the ring and necklace slots as kind `jewel`
(`chaos_item_mods.lua` `M.kindOfType`): the tooltip, crafting, gems, the market category, the stash, the gamble, the
loot filter and autoloot, the item codec and the Auto Seller.

**Old copies.** A ring or necklace made before the install may still carry `charges` or `duration` as item
attributes. `ChaosJewelry.normalize` removes them when the item type has none: on every move (EventCallback
`onItemMoved`, index 9, before `base_rarity.lua` and `item_mods.lua`) and at login (`ChaosJewelryLogin`, every slot).

**Affix pool.** Kind `jewel` of `chaos_item_mods.lua`, unchanged. Prefixes: boss damage, physical and elemental
penetration, damage over time, engine skills, critical, energy shield (flat and %). Suffixes: life and mana on kill and
on hit, regeneration, experience, gold, item and rarity find, healing, goblin chance, cooldown reduction, mana cost,
absorbs, leech, profession, energy shield recharge. Weapon-only mods (attack speed, execute, added element, ailment
chances) are not in it. The count per rarity (1-6), the prefix and suffix sides, the tiers by item level and the caps
are the same as every other slot, so a ring or necklace has one slot's power: two jewel slots out of ten, as in the
base.

**Loot** (`chaos/jewelry.lua`, startup GlobalEvent `ChaosJewelryLoot`). Every hunt monster and boss of
`bounty_pool.lua` gets loot rows by its hunting level (`ChaosPaceCore.entryLevel`, else 2x the pool level), added with
`MonsterType:addLoot` like `gear_sets.lua`; no monster file changes. The loot layer rolls rarity, item level, prefixes
and suffixes as for any gear drop. Numbers in `J.config`:

| | per kill (of 100000), each kind | split |
|---|---|---|
| hunt monster | 75 (0.075%) | over the eligible bases, at least 5 a row |
| bounty boss | 1900 (1.9%) | same |

75 is one slot's share of the equipment sets' 600 (eight slots); 1900 is 15000 / 8. A base is eligible when its level is
within the monster's level -200 / +50; above every window the three highest bases drop. On the real pool: 709 hunt
monsters, 30 bosses, 11549 rows. The stock loot tables keep their own rings and amulets (band 100: 2.5% ring, 1% amulet
per kill; band 800: 13.5% / 13.7%).

| hunting level | rings | necklaces |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | life, power, sword, axe, club, ring of healing | bronze, protection, strange talisman, silver, dragon, elven, garlic |
| 100 | the above, death, prismatic, temptation | the above, terra, glacier, lightning, magma, onyx, deep, gill, prismatic |
| 300 | prismatic, temptation, butterfly | deep, gill, prismatic, exotic, foxtail, rainbow, cobra |
| 500+ | prismatic, temptation, butterfly | foxtail, rainbow, cobra |

Bases stop at level 250; item level and rarity carry the power beyond.

**Looks** (`items.otb`, same step). Owner request 2026-10-22: "use sprites de rings e necklaces dos nossos assets". The
29 loot bases show their own icons of pair 35, client ids 38612-38640 in `J.bases` order (`look`; cut from a free icon
set of docs/CREDITS.md by `client/tools/sprites/gen_jewelry_art.py`; client/MANIFEST.md "Jewelry looks (pair 35)").
The step sets each base node's client id to its `look` and clears `FLAG_ANIMATION` (the stock lightning pendant is
animated; the own looks have one phase). Server ids, flags and the other attributes stay. It refuses, writing nothing,
when a base node is missing, has a client id other than `look` or `stock`, or when another node already uses the look.
`items.otb.bak` keeps the original once. A client still on pair 34 has no thing 38612+ and draws nothing there: ship
pair 35 with the server, or run `python3 -I tools/patch_base_jewelry.py DATA_DIR --stock-looks`, which puts the stock
client ids (`stock`) and the animation flag back (byte for byte the base file; checked on the real items.otb). Worn
ids of old copies (2210 and the like) keep the stock look until taken off.

**Side effects and open points.** NPC-sold life rings and the other merged rings are permanent plain gear now. Fangs of
the Ninth Circle (24790) is permanent.

**Uniques on consumable bases** (`J.uniqueBases`, same step). Ring of the Last Ember sat on the worn time ring 2206
(it decayed when worn, turned into a time ring 2169 when taken off and got the time ring's haste); Heart of Cinders
(10218) and Heartbleed Pendant (10221) sat on 5-charge amulets (gone after five absorbs, with 60% physical and 40%
element absorb from the type). They have bases of their own now, server ids **41640-41642** (reserved block
41640-41659): ember ring, cinder heart amulet, heartbleed pendant.
- items.otb: copies of the stock nodes 2206, 10218 and 10221 with the new server ids (same client ids 3090, 9301,
  9304 and flags), appended. A node with that id and another client id stops the step.
- items.xml: one marked block before `</items>` with weight, slotType and the unique's stats that no item attribute
  holds (`skipped` of `chaos_unique_specs.lua`: the ring's speed 20 and regeneration, the heart's max health 200);
  no duration, transform or charges. An item id 41640-41642 outside the block stops the step. movements.xml: Equip
  and DeEquip entries.
- `chaos_items.xml`, `chaos_unique_items.lua`, the test kit and the specs name 41640-41642.
- Old copies (`chaos/jewelry.lua`): a copy of the old base with the `chaos_unique` marker (or the unique's name) turns
  into the new id; name, stats, rarity and sockets are item attributes and stay, charges and time left go. In a
  container: when moved (not into a slot) and at login (the backpack, recursively). Worn: at login it is moved to the
  backpack first, so the engine removes the old type's stats (the worn time ring turns into 2169 on the way), then
  turns; a message asks to put it on again. A full backpack leaves it worn until a later login. Copies in a depot turn
  when moved out.

## Market (`market.lua`, `market_core.lua`, `market_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_market.sql`, `tools/patch_market.py`, engine patch 0017, client `game_market`)

Our own player market (auction house) for **gold** and **Chaos Coins**; the stock 10.98 market is switched off for
players. Client `game_market` (Economy > Market in the top menu, **Alt+E**; using the market item of a depot locker opens
it too), extended opcode **221** (`ChaosOpcodes.market`, JSON `{action, data}`; long answers through `Chaos.sendChunked`).
Every number is in `market_config.lua`; the pure rules are in `market_core.lua` (`tests/market_test.lua`).

**Install.** `install_all.py` does all of it: the `files` step copies the scripts, the `events` step runs
`tools/patch_market.py` (comments out the `function="market"` line of `data/actions/actions.xml`, idempotent, marker
`Chaos: stock market off`), the `sql` step runs `sql/chaos_market.sql` (4 tables and the columns of the modifier search,
safe to run again: `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, MariaDB's `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`; `market.lua` runs the same
statements at startup). Engine patch `src-patches/0017-item-serialization-lua.patch` (two Lua methods, only
`luascript.cpp` / `luascript.h`) gives the exact escrow below; without it the market still works with a key list and
says so at startup.

**Stock market off.** Without the action nothing puts a character into the stock market, so the client cannot browse,
create or accept stock offers (the engine refuses those packets outside the market). `market.lua` registers item 14405
(the depot locker's market item) instead: using it opens this market. The stock `market_offers` rows stay unreachable;
the base client's own market window (`mods/game_tibia_market`) never opens.

**Offers.** A seller picks an item from the backpack (or drags one onto the Sell tab's slot), a price in gold, in coins
or in both (the buyer chooses), and 1, 3 or 7 days. A stack can be listed in part (20 of 50 orbs). Never listed (server
checks, `ChaosMarketCore.itemRefusal`): equipped items, locked items (`chaos_locked`), store items (`isStoreItem`) and the
store pouches (`ChaosPouches.isPouch(item)` or the custom attribute `chaos_storebound`), containers with something inside
(an empty bag is fine), items that cannot be picked up or moved, quest items (a map unique id; `blockedActionIds`), items
that are wearing off (decay state), gold / platinum / crystal coins. Rolled gear is sold whole. Players who want an item
they cannot find post a buy order (below).

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Listing fee | gold from the bank, not refunded: 1% of the gold price (a coins-only offer: coins x 100 gold x 1%), at least 100, at most 1,000,000 |
| Sales tax | 5% of what the buyer pays (gold and coins), rounded down, taken from the seller's share |
| Prices | gold 100 - 2,000,000,000; coins 1 - 100,000 |
| Duration | 1, 3 or 7 days (default 3); then the item goes back to the seller's inbox |
| Limits | 20 active listings per character, 40 per account (sell offers and buy orders together; Chaos Pact slots raise both); level 8 to list or buy; you cannot buy from your own account |
| Rate limits | per character: browse 150 ms, list 1.5 s, buy / cancel 0.8 s, tooltip 60 ms (`ChaosRateLimit`) |

**Escrow.** The listed item leaves the seller and lives in its offer row (`chaos_market_offers.data`): with engine patch
0017 as the engine's own binary form of every attribute (`item:serializeAttributes()`, the same bytes the engine saves
items with; hex in the row, codec `blob`), else as a list of the standard attributes and every custom key the Chaos
scripts set (codec `attrs`, the guild depot's method; a custom attribute outside the list would be lost, the reason for
the patch). On purchase, cancel or expiry the item is created again (`Game.createItem` + `item:unserializeAttributes()`;
a stackable keeps the count it was created with) and its per-item id `chaos_iid` is removed, so the engine gives the
copy a new one when it is first sent: chat links and cached tooltips of the old copy never point at it. The offer also
keeps a tooltip snapshot (`ChaosItemTooltip.build`, JSON), the name, category (gear kind, orb, gem, key, misc), rarity,
item level and what the modifier search reads (below).

**Modifier search** (Browse > Modifiers, `ChaosMarketCore.offerIndex / modFilter / modClauses`). Per offer, written with
the offer row from its tooltip snapshot:
- `chaos_market_offer_mods (offer_id, mod_key, value, tier)`, primary key `(offer_id, mod_key)`, keys
  `(mod_key, value)` and `(mod_key, tier)`: one row per modifier and legendary power (key in lower case, a power as
  `chaos_mod_<power>`; value as the tooltip shows it, quality included; a critical / leech pair by its amount, the number
  its tiers are made of; a unique's modifiers tier 0). The rows of an offer are removed in the transaction that sells,
  cancels or expires it (and with a dropped pending listing), so the table holds only what is on the market.
- columns of `chaos_market_offers`: `sockets`, `quality`, `free_prefix` / `free_suffix` (the rarity's limit, plus the Orb
  of Ruin's extra slot, minus what is there; 0 on a unique or a ruined item: no orb changes those), `has_power`,
  `bound_mods`, `mods_indexed`.
- the offers listed before this existed are indexed once at startup from their snapshots (`ChaosMarket.backfillIndex`,
  batches of 200, the offers still `mods_indexed = 0`), recorded in `server_config` `chaos_market_modindex` = the
  version (`market_config.lua modIndexVersion`; raise it to build the index again).

A search has up to 6 rows (modifier, lowest value, lowest tier: T1 lowest, T8 best, "T5" = T5 or better) and needs all
of them (one `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM chaos_market_offer_mods WHERE offer_id = offers.id AND mod_key = ... AND value >= ...
AND tier >= ...)` per row; MariaDB turns them into semi-joins on the `(mod_key, ...)` keys) or at least N of them
(`id IN (SELECT offer_id ... WHERE (row 1) OR (row 2) ... GROUP BY offer_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= N)`, materialized once),
plus `sockets >=`, `quality >=`, a free prefix / suffix, a power, a bound modifier; the other filters, sorting and pages
are unchanged. The server refuses (the client says why) more than 6 rows, a modifier twice, rows that are not a list and
any key that is not a modifier or power of `ChaosCrafting.affixes()` (the same 81 keys as the Codex); numbers are
clamped (value 0 - 1,000,000, tier 0 - 8, sockets 0 - 8, quality 0 - 30, N 1 - rows; `market_config.lua modFilter`);
keys are checked before they reach SQL and quoted with `db.escapeString`, numbers are integers. A Browse of the old
client (`mod` = one key) is one row. The request stays far below the extended opcode limit (6 rows of a key and two
numbers); the answer is the usual page.

**Buying.** Gold comes from the bank (`players.balance`), coins from the account's Chaos Coins (`chaos_shop_coins`). The
item always goes to the buyer's inbox; the seller gets the gold minus the tax in the bank, the coins minus the tax on
the account, with a text message, a toast and a line in My Offers. A seller who is offline gets the gold, the returned
items and the notices at the next login.

**Sale notifications** (`market_notify_core.lua`, `tests/market_notify_test.lua`; flows in `tests/market_test.lua`). The
queue is the seller's "sold" rows of `chaos_market_deliveries` (one per sold offer or buy order fill; no other table):
`MK.deliver` tells a sale only when that call applied its row, so the row's deliverSeq / `delivered` mark also stops a
second notice (relog, a crash after the save). Seller online: at once one chat line and a toast with the header ITEM
SOLD (`ChaosNotify.send` kind `sale`), e.g. "Buyer bought your 2x Orb of Fate for 100,000 gold (fee 5,000):
+95,000 gold to your bank." Seller offline: at the next login (the market's login delivery, 1.5 s after login) one
toast "While you were away: 3 items sold for 4.2M gold: Sword, plate armor, 20x Orb of Fate." (proceeds after the fee,
gold and Chaos Coins summed, one decimal rounded down) and one chat line per sale. The lines are capped at
`market_config.lua` `notify.lines` (5) plus "... and N more sales (see My Offers)"; the toast's total counts every
sale. The rows themselves are never dropped (they carry the money). A buy order fill tells its seller the same way
("Orderer's buy order took your ..."). The Orb Exchange does the same with its own delivery rows (below).

**Crash safety.** Every money move is one database transaction, and every item / gold change of a character is tied to
a marker storage that the engine saves in the same transaction as the items (`player:save()`):
- listing: (1) the offer row is written as pending (state 9); (2) in memory the item leaves, the fee leaves the bank and
  storage 7100970 (listSeq) = the offer id; (3) `player:save()` writes all three at once; (4) the offer turns active.
  A pending row found at startup or at the seller's login is activated when the saved listSeq reached its id, else
  dropped (the item never left the seller in a saved state). A save that fails gives the item and the fee back.
- buying with gold: `player:save()` first (the database then holds exactly the character), then one transaction takes
  the price from `players.balance` (`balance >= price`), marks the offer sold (`state = 0 AND expires > now`, so a second
  buyer or a double click finds nothing) and writes the deliveries (item -> buyer, gold -> seller); only then the price
  leaves the bank in memory. Buying with coins: one transaction moves the coins between the accounts, marks the offer
  sold and writes the deliveries.
- delivery (`chaos_market_deliveries`, one row per item / gold / coin notice, unique per offer and kind): owed rows are
  applied in id order (item into the inbox, gold into the bank), storage 7100971 (deliverSeq) = the row id, then
  `player:save()`, then the rows are marked delivered. A row at or below the saved deliverSeq only gets marked (it
  reached the character before a crash). Characters with `players.save = 0` cannot use the market (nothing of theirs
  would be saved).
- cancel and expiry (a globalevent every 60 s, 200 offers per run): one transaction closes the offer and writes the
  item delivery; delivered at once when the seller is online.

Every listing, sale (price, tax, net, both characters), cancel, expiry, delivery, recovery and error is a row in
`chaos_market_log`. Staff: `/market sweep` (run the expiry now), `/market info <offer id>`.

**Seasons.** An offer is on its seller's market: the season market while that season runs (season characters see, buy
and get tooltips of only their season's offers), the standard market otherwise; when the season ends its offers join
the standard market with their sellers. A purchase checks the buyer's, the offer's and the seller's current realm.

**Client** (`game_market`, Chaos skin, 900 x 600, fits 1280x720): Browse (search by name, category, lowest rarity,
currency, sort, item level and price ranges, pages of 10, a collapsible Modifiers section: up to 6 rows of modifier (a
search box filters the Codex names; the list is grouped into prefixes, suffixes and legendary powers and scrolls),
lowest value and lowest tier, "All must match" or "At least N match", sockets, quality, free prefix, free suffix, power,
bound; checked in the client before it is sent (`MarketView.modRequest`) and kept while the character is logged in;
item rows with icon, rarity frame and colour, name, rarity / item level / category / seller / time left and the prices;
hovering a row shows the full rich tooltip through `game_itemtooltip.showTip` with the seller, the prices and the
modifiers the search matched ("Matches: ...") under it, Ctrl compares; Buy asks which currency to pay with), Sell (the backpack's items, greyed with the reason when they cannot
be listed; amount, prices, duration, the fee and the tax as the server computes them), My Offers (active with Cancel,
sold / expired / cancelled) and History (purchases and sales). Long names are shortened at a word with "..."
(`SupportsText.shorten`), other texts wrap. Logic without client API: `marketview.lua` (`marketview_test.lua`).

**Protocol.** client -> server `open | browse {filter: q, cat, rarity, cur, priceMin, priceMax, ilvlMin, ilvlMax,
sort, page, mods = [{k, min, t}], need, sockets, quality, freeP, freeS, power, bound} | tip {id} | buy {id, cur} | sellable | list {ref|pos, sid|cid,
iid, count, gold, coins, days} | cancel {id} | mine | history | wallet`; server -> client `meta | page {rows, page, pages,
total} | tip {id, tip, seller} | sellable {items} | mine {active, closed, owed} | history {rows} | wallet {gold, coins} |
done {what, text} | error {text} | openWindow`. `ref` is the server's path to an item in the backpack (`s3.0.5`), `pos`
the client position of a dragged item; both are checked against the item id and the per-item id.

**Buy orders** (`market_orders_core.lua` pure rules, the engine part in `market.lua`, table `chaos_market_orders`,
Market > Buy Orders). A buyer posts what it wants: an item kind (found by name in the order form: the exact name, a part
of the name of an item it carries or of any item ever listed), optionally the lowest rarity, the lowest item level and the
Browse tab's modifier filter (the same language: up to 6 rows of modifier / lowest value / lowest tier, all or at least N,
sockets, quality, free prefix / suffix, power, bound; checked by `C.modFilter`, stored as one text column,
`MO.encodeFilter`), how many (1 - 1,000) and the price per unit in gold OR Chaos Coins, for 1, 3 or 7 days.
- **Escrow at posting.** The whole payment (price x quantity; at most 2,000,000,000 gold or 1,000,000 coins per order)
  leaves the buyer when the order is posted and lives in the order row (`escrow`): gold from the bank, coins from the
  account. The listing fee is a sell offer's (1% of the total gold, a coins order: coins x 100 gold x 1%; at least 100,
  at most 1,000,000; gold from the bank, not refunded). `player:save()` first, then ONE transaction takes the gold
  (`players.balance`), the coins (`chaos_shop_coins`) and writes the order.
- **Filling.** Market > Buy Orders lists the open orders of the viewer's market (best price, newest, ending, name;
  currency; name search); *Sell* opens the seller's items of that kind from the backpack (and the bags in it), greyed
  with the reason when they do not fit the filter or cannot be listed (`ChaosMarketCore.itemRefusal`, the same rules as a
  sell offer). A stack fills in part (up to what the order still wants or what the seller types), a single item fills
  one. A fill is written like a listing that sells at once (crash safe the same way): an offer row with `order_id` =
  the order (pending), the item leaves the seller (escrow of the item: engine patch 0017 blob, as for offers),
  `player:save()`, then ONE transaction (`MK.completeFill`) adds the units to the order, takes their price from the
  escrow, marks the row sold and writes the deliveries: the item to the buyer's inbox (a new per-item id), the gold
  minus the 5% sales tax to the seller's bank (a delivery row) or the coins minus the tax straight to the seller's
  account (plus a notice row). A pending fill found later (login, startup) is completed, or its item goes back to the
  seller's inbox when the order closed meanwhile. Fills show in both characters' History (`(buy order)`), and the
  seller's My Offers.
- **End.** The buyer can cancel; at the end of its duration the sweep (`MK.sweepOrders`, the market globalevent) expires
  it. Both refund what the escrow still holds: gold as a delivery row (`offer_id` = minus the order id, reason
  `refund`; online at once, else at the next login), coins straight back to the account (plus a notice row). An order
  whose units are all bought closes as filled.
- **Rules.** Not on your own order or one of your own account; seasons apart as for offers (an order is on its buyer's
  market; season characters see and fill only their season's orders; season markets trade for gold only: season.lua
  wraps `orderPost`, a fill of a coins order on a season market is refused too, and `meta.coinsOk = false` makes the
  window hide the coin price and offer gold only); level 8; money (gold / platinum / crystal coins)
  cannot be ordered. **Listing limits:** buy orders count against the same active-listing limits as sell offers
  (`MK.activeCounts`, `MK.limitRefusal`; the Chaos Pact block `MK.maxActive` is unchanged and still sets the numbers),
  so a player cannot open 20 offers and 20 orders on a free account.
- **Admin.** The admin panel's Economy > *Market buy orders* (every active order, or every order of one character, with
  the escrow held), staff `/market orders [character]`, `/market sweep` expires offers and orders; every post, fill,
  cancel and expiry is a `chaos_market_log` row (`order`, `fill`, `ordercancel`, `orderexpire`, `fillback`).
- **Protocol** (221): `orders {q, cat, cur, mine, sort, page}` -> `orders {rows, page, pages, total}`, `myOrders` ->
  `myOrders {active, closed, used, max}`, `orderFind {q}` -> `orderFind {items}`, `orderPost {sid, quantity, price, cur,
  days, filter}`, `orderCancel {id}`, `fillable {id}` -> `fillable {id, order, items}`, `fill {id, ref, sid, iid,
  count}`; answers `done {what = orderPost | orderCancel | fill}` or `error`. Rate limits: list 150 ms, post 1.5 s, fill /
  cancel 0.8 s, search 300 ms.
- **Install:** `sql/chaos_market.sql` (the table and the `order_id` column of `chaos_market_offers`, both
  `IF NOT EXISTS`); `market.lua` runs the same statements at startup.

**Tests.** `tests/market_test.lua` (LuaJIT and Lua 5.3, a mocked engine with a small SQL interpreter): fees, tax, prices,
every refusal, seasons, the Browse query (escaping, filters, sorting, pages), the modifier search (the index of an offer,
rows with value and tier, all rows and at least N, sockets, quality, free prefix / suffix, power, bound, refused keys /
seven rows / a modifier twice / an injection attempt, the rows removed on sale and cancel, the backfill once and again
for a new version), both codecs, listing a rolled legendary and
part of a stack, browse and filters, tooltips, buying with gold and with coins (money and tax, the item identical but
for a new per-item id), own offer / own account / other season / not enough money / sold twice, cancel, expiry online and
offline, a rolled-back transaction, failed saves, a crash between save and mark, interrupted listings. The mocked SQL
runs the real statements (`EXISTS`, `IN (SELECT ... GROUP BY ... HAVING COUNT(*))`, `table`.`column`).
`client/.../game_market/marketview_test.lua` (the catalog and typeahead choices, the form -> request and its checks,
the matched lines). Buy orders in both: the order checks and limits, the filter text round trip and matching (rarity,
item level, rows all / at least N, sockets, quality, free slots, power, bound), fill counts, payment and tax, the list
query; posting with gold and with coins (escrow and fee in the database and in memory), parts of a stack, a filtered
coins order filled by a fitting sword (every attribute kept, new per-item id), refusals (own order, own account, money,
another kind, a season character, a sword that does not fit, a wrong per-item id), cancel and expiry refunds (offline
buyer refunded at login), a failed fill transaction (item returned), a failed save, pending fills completed / returned
at startup, the shared listing limit, the admin report and the money balance (fills + refund = escrow); the client's
order form check, cost text, filter text and order lines.

**Tested in game** (test server built with 0001-0014 + 0017, two clients and a season character): a Legendary magic
sword (four modifiers with tiers, a bound modifier, a legendary power, quality 15%, two sockets with a gem) listed for
250,000 gold (fee 2,500) and 20 of 50 Orbs of Upheaval for 100 coins; Browse, the filters (name, currency, a modifier,
a legendary power) and the hover tooltip; the sword bought by another character: buyer's bank -250,000, seller's
+237,500 (tax 12,500), every attribute identical (attribute dump and serialized size), no per-item id until first sent;
the orbs bought with coins (buyer's account -100, seller's +95); cancel (orbs back in the inbox); expiry by the
globalevent with the seller online and offline (delivered at the next login, toast); refusals of a locked item and of a
bag with items inside (greyed in the picker); a dragged item; the market item of a depot locker opening the window;
season isolation (each market sees only its own offers, buying across refused) and the NPC bank transfer refused from a
season character (a gamemaster is exempt, as for the other season rules); `kill -9` right after a purchase commit (after
the restart the buyer got the item once and the seller the gold once), between the pending row and the save (row
dropped, item kept), between the save and the activation (offer activated), and between a delivery's save and its mark
(one item, row marked at the next login). Screenshots at 1280x720 and 1920x1080.
The modifier search (test server with 0017, a copy of that database with the first market schema): the startup added
the columns and the table and indexed the two active offers once (`server_config` row written); five rolled items
listed (a Legendary sword with a power, a bound modifier, quality 15% and two sockets; a Legendary sword with a socket;
a Rare plate armor; a Mythic helmet with three sockets; an Uncommon sword) and searched from another client: two rows
all (Herbalism T5+ and Distance: 2 offers), a lowest value (Herbalism 3+: 1), at least 2 of 3 (Herbalism T7+,
Distance T4+, Smoldering Aura: 1) and at least 1 (2), an invalid "at least 4 of 3" (refused in the client), sockets 2+,
free suffix, free suffix + a socket, power + quality, bound, free prefix; the typeahead, the scrolling list (picking
with the mouse), six rows, the matched lines in the tooltip; an unknown key and seven rows sent by hand (refused by the
server); the rows removed on a purchase and a cancel; `EXPLAIN` of both query shapes (semi-join on the `(mod_key,
...)` keys; the count mode materialized). `sql/chaos_market.sql` run twice on the first schema and on an empty database. Not verified in game: the key-list
codec on a real engine (unit-tested), the per-account offer limit, a listing price at the limits, the base client's
account with several characters on the copy used (its login parser lacked base patch 0025; patched for the test).
Buy orders (test server with 0017, a copy of the test database, two clients on two accounts): the order form found Orb
of Upheaval by part of its name and the magic sword by its name; a gold order for 30 orbs at 2,000 (bank -60,600: 60,000
held + 600 fee, the same in `players.balance`) and a coins order for 2 Legendary+ iLvl 100+ magic swords with Execute 5+
T5+ taken from the Browse modifiers (account -100 coins, bank -100 fee); the other character saw both, filled 5 of a
stack of 12 orbs (+9,500 gold: 10,000 minus 500 tax), then 7 more; its two swords listed, the Rare one greyed ("Its
rarity is too low."), the server refused it when sent by hand, the Legendary one filled (+48 coins) and reached the
buyer's inbox with every modifier and tier; cancel of the coins order (50 coins back), expiry of the orb order by the
sweep (36,000 gold back at once: 12 bought); My orders with the listings used, History with "(buy order)", the admin
action listing both orders. Money balanced to the gold piece on both sides. `sql/chaos_market.sql` run twice on the copy.
Not verified in game: a crash in the middle of a fill (unit-tested), season characters filling (unit-tested), the
per-account limit.

### Price history (`market_history.lua`, `market_history_core.lua`, `market_history_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_market_history.sql`)

Every completed sale is kept with its price per unit: a bought offer (`MK.buy`) and a buy order fill (`MK.completeFill`)
call `ChaosMarketHistory.record(offer id, realm)` after their transaction committed (inside `pcall`: a history failure
never touches a sale; the offer id is unique in the table, so a sale is recorded once). The key of a price is the
realm (0 = standard, else the season id: season and standard prices never mix), the currency (gold and Chaos Coins
apart), the item type, the rarity and the item level band (`bandSize` 10: iLvl 60-69; no item level = band 0). A stack
counts as one sale at its price per unit (rounded down); its units are the volume.

Tables: `chaos_market_history` (one row per sale, kept `rawDays` = 7 full days) and `chaos_market_history_daily` (one row
per key and day: sales, units, median, low, high, trimmed mean; dropped after `keepDays` = 90). A globalevent
(`compactSeconds` = 1 hour, and once at startup) aggregates the finished days older than `rawDays` (one key-day per
transaction: the daily row written, its sales deleted; at most `compactGroups` per run) and drops old rows. At the first
startup the sold offers of the last 90 days are imported once (`server_config` `chaos_market_history`; their realm is
the one stored on the offer).

Stats of a key (`market_history_core.lua` `H.stats`, unit tested): last sale and its age; the 7-day median, lowest and
highest sale, sales and units; the usual range (the 7-day sales without `trimPct` = 10% at each end) and the trimmed
mean; the daily series of the last 30 days (median of each day, sales as the volume). **Typical price**: the 7-day
median once there are `minSamples` = 5 sales in 7 days; else the median of the daily medians of the 30 days weighted by
their sales, once those have 5 sales; else none ("not enough sales"). A median is the mean of the two middle values
rounded down when the count is even; one fat-finger sale moves neither the median nor the range. Stats are cached per
key for `cacheSeconds` (300 s); a new sale of the key clears its entry.

Protocol (opcode 221, `MH.actions` from the market's handler): `prices {id}` (the key of an offer) or `prices {sid,
rarity, ilvl}` (an item of the Sell form) -> `prices {seq, sid, rarity, band, bandText, gold, coins, marks, warn}` for the
viewer's realm (rate `rateMs`). `MK.browse` hands each page to `MH.markRows` (two queries for the whole page): each row
gets `typ` (typical price per unit of its first currency), `tcur` and `pm` = "low" / "high" when its price per unit is
at most `marks.low` (0.6) / at least `marks.high` (1.6) times the typical price.

Client (`game_market`, logic in `marketpriceview.lua`): a click on a Browse offer opens its price history (typical price,
last sale, 7-day median and volume, usual range with the lowest and highest sale, a 30-day chart of the daily medians
with the sales as bars, drawn by the Orb Exchange chart code `OrbExchangeView.chart`; a Coin prices / Gold prices
switch when the other currency has sales). Rows priced well under / over the typical price show "50% under typical"
(green) / "87% over typical" (red); the hover tooltip adds the typical price. The Sell form asks for the chosen item's
prices, shows the typical price and a suggested price (the typical price rounded down to 3 significant digits, times the
amount), a "Use typical" button, and a warning when the asking price per unit is at most `warn.low` (0.5) / at least
`warn.high` (2.0) times the typical price.

Tests: `tests/market_history_test.lua` (bands, keys, medians, trims, weighted medians, the daily aggregation, stats with
the minimum sample and the 30-day fallback, outliers, marks, cutoffs, compaction groups and a compaction that keeps the
series; the engine file compiles and its schema equals the SQL file), `game_market/marketpriceview_test.lua`. The engine
file was run against MariaDB 10.11 through a test harness (backfill of 44 sales, compaction of 12 key-days with every
sale kept, stats with an outlier, season and coins apart, a stack per unit, record once, Browse marks, the prices action,
retention). Screenshots of the item chart and the Sell suggestion: offline client render. Not run on a live server yet.

## Orb Exchange (`orbexchange.lua`, `orbexchange_core.lua`, `orbexchange_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_orbx.sql`, client `game_orbexchange`)

The crafting orbs are the economy's currency; the Orb Exchange is their order book. Pairs: any orb against gold (the
bank balance) and any orb against any other orb. Client `game_orbexchange` (Economy > Orb Exchange in the top menu, and
an "Orb Exchange" button in the Market window), extended opcode **209** (`ChaosOpcodes.orbExchange`, JSON
`{action, data}`, answers through `Chaos.sendChunked`). Numbers in `orbexchange_config.lua`; the pure rules in
`orbexchange_core.lua` (`tests/orbexchange_test.lua`).

**Install.** Nothing beyond `install_all.py`: the `files` step copies the scripts, the `sql` step runs
`sql/chaos_orbx.sql` (4 tables, safe to run again; `orbexchange.lua` creates the same tables at startup). No engine
patch, no base data change. The orbs on the exchange are every entry of `ChaosCrafting.config.orbs` (orbs v2 and the Orb
of Sockets included; 14 on the test server) that is a stackable item; `orbs` / `exclude` in the config narrow it.

**Orders.** An order gives `giveQty` of one currency and wants at least `wantQty` of another; its ratio (what it
wants per unit it gives) is its limit. The window shows a pair as base (an orb) / quote (gold or another orb) and turns
Buy / Sell, quantity and price each into that (a buyer's total is rounded up, a seller's down, by less than one unit).
The order is done when it has given everything: a better price means it receives more (a buyer of 50 Awakening at 0.05
Upheaval each who meets an ask at 0.04 gets 75 for the same 3 Upheaval).

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Sizes | orbs 1 - 100,000 per side, gold 1,000 - 2,000,000,000 per side (all products stay below 2^53) |
