| Fees (gold sinks) | 2% (`goldBps` 200) of the gold leg of every fill, rounded down, paid by the side that receives the gold; 500 gold from the bank for every orb-for-orb order when it is placed; never refunded |
| Duration | 1, 3, 7 or 14 days (default 7); then the rest goes back |
| Limits | 20 open orders per character, 40 per account; level 8; characters with `players.save = 0` cannot trade |
| Rate limits | per character: place 1 s, cancel 0.5 s, book 150 ms, my orders 300 ms, open 400 ms (`ChaosRateLimit`) |

**Matching** (`ChaosOrbExchangeCore.match`, `fillAmounts`). A new order (the taker) meets the open orders that give what
it wants and want what it gives and whose ratio crosses its own, cheapest first and the older first at the same ratio
(price-time priority; the database query reads the best `matchBatch` candidates, the exact order is made with integer
cross-products). Every fill is at the resting order's ratio: what a resting order has received since it went on the book
is `ceil(given since then x wantQty / giveQty)`, so it never gets less than its ratio and gets exactly `wantQty` when it
started on the book and gives everything. The taker's limit is checked on every fill (what it gets per unit it pays is
never worse than its own ratio); when the largest fill would break it by the rounding, smaller fills are tried. A fill
moves `a` from the resting order's escrow to the taker and `b` from the taker's escrow to the resting order, minus the
gold fee: nothing is created. What a taker had given before it went on the book is kept in `rest_given`, so a buyer that
bought cheaper keeps that price and its rest is priced at its own ratio again (found in the game test: the first version
paid the improvement back to the next seller). An order whose rest cannot buy one whole unit at its own ratio (a buyer
with a few coins left after better prices) closes as filled and the rest is refunded in the same transaction. Orders of
the same account never trade with each other (`selfTrade = false`); they are skipped and stay on the book.

**Escrow and crash safety** (the market's method and order of steps):
- An orb order: (1) the order row is written as pending (state 9); (2) the orbs leave the backpack (stacks of that orb
  in the backpack and the bags in it, locked orbs not), the orb-for-orb fee leaves the bank and the storage 7100950
  (placeSeq) = the order id, all in memory; (3) `player:save()` writes all three in one database transaction; (4) one
  transaction activates the row and matches it. A pending row found at login or startup is activated and matched when
  the owner's saved placeSeq reached its id, else deleted (the orbs never left in a saved state). Tested by a real
  `kill -9` with one pending order whose marker was saved (activated and matched at startup) and one whose was not
  (dropped), and with stale pending rows dropped at login.
- A gold order: `player:save()` first, then one transaction takes the gold from `players.balance` (only when it is
  there), writes the active order and matches it; then the same gold leaves the bank in memory.
- Matching, cancel and expiry run inside one transaction each: every resting order is updated only when its `given` is
  still what was read, every fill writes its trade row and the deliveries; any failure rolls all of it back.
- Deliveries (`chaos_orbx_deliveries`, unique per order, trade and reason): orbs to the inbox in stacks of 100 (all of a
  row or nothing), gold to the bank, in id order, with the storage 7100951 (deliverSeq) = the row id, then
  `player:save()`, then the rows are marked; a row at or below the saved deliverSeq is only marked. Offline characters
  get theirs at the next login (tested). A delivery with a fill (an order of the player traded) is an ITEM SOLD toast
  (kind `sale`, `market_notify_core.lua` `exchangeToast`): "Orb Exchange: your orders traded: ..." online, "While you were away: your Orb
  Exchange orders traded: +1,200 gold in your bank." at login; refunds only keep the plain Orb Exchange toast.

**Seasons.** An order carries its owner's realm (`ChaosSeason.realmOfGuid`). While a season runs, its characters trade
on the season's own book and see only its orders and trades; standard characters never see or meet them
(`ChaosMarketCore.realmClause`, the market's rule). When the season ends its open orders join the standard book: the
sweep (`ChaosOrbExchange.mergeEndedSeasons`) matches each once as a new order against the standard book and sets its
realm to 0 (tested: a season bid at 6,000 did not touch the standard asks at 5,200 while the season ran, and bought
from them after the end, the rest refunded).

**The window.** Book tab: a strip of the orbs (item sprites, the count you carry in the tooltip) picks the base,
"priced in" picks gold or another orb; the book (asks above the spread line, bids below, price / quantity / orders /
total with depth bars; a click on a level fills the form to buy at an ask or sell at a bid, with the price rounded so it
crosses), last price, 24h change, high / low, volume and turnover, an hourly average price chart (step line and volume
bars), the last 20 trades, and the order form with the totals and fees before placing. My Orders tab: open orders with
progress and Cancel, my fills (what I gave and got, the fee), closed orders. The book is asked again every 5 s while
it is open.

**Protocol.** client -> server `open | book {base, quote, seq} | place {give, giveQty, want, wantQty, days} |
cancel {id} | mine | wallet`; server -> client `meta {orbs [{k, n, item}], fees, min, max, durations, defaultDuration,
maxOpen, realm, realmName, gold, have, hours} | book {base, quote, asks, bids, last, open, high, low, change, vol,
volQuote, points [{h, p, v}], trades [{ago, p, q, side}], mine} | mine {open, closed, fills, owed, max} |
wallet {gold, have} | done {what, id, text} | error {text}`.

**Tables.** `chaos_orbx_orders` (state 0 active, 1 filled, 2 cancelled, 3 expired, 9 pending; `given`, `got`,
`rest_given`, `refunded`, `fee`), `chaos_orbx_trades` (one row per fill, the price history), `chaos_orbx_deliveries`,
`chaos_orbx_log` (place, take, fill, cancel, expire, deliver, recover, merge, error). Storages 7100950 - 7100954 are
reserved (two used). Staff: `/orbx sweep` (expiry and season merge now), `/orbx info <order id>`, `/orbx escrow`
(what the open orders hold per currency).

**Opcode.** 209 is free in the reference server (its opcodes: "Opcode collision check"), in every Chaos script and in
every client module of the reference client (grep for `sendExtendedOpcode`, `registerExtended*Opcode` and opcode
constants).

**Tests.** `tests/orbexchange_test.lua` (LuaJIT and Lua 5.3): order checks, exact integer division near 2^53, crossing
and priority, single fills (the maker's rounding, the taker's limit, the smaller fill found), whole matches (several
makers, self-trade skipped, fees on the gold leg, a buyer that rests after a better price), dust, the book levels in
both orientations, the price history, the makers query and the limits; then randomized runs (thousands of orders
between 2 to 6 traders over four currencies, and tiny orb-for-orb orders where rounding is the common case) that count
every orb and every gold coin after each step (holdings + escrow + fees never change), and check that no order trades
worse than its ratio and that no amount goes negative. Client `game_orbexchange/orbexchangeview_test.lua`. In game
(test server copy with MariaDB, two characters on two accounts): sells and buys against gold with partial fills,
the fee, selling into a bid, an orb-for-orb trade with the placing fee, cancel and expiry refunds, offline delivery at
login, a real crash with pending orders, rate limit and size refusals, a season character's book, and the totals of
gold and of every orb checked after each step (equal to the start minus the fees).

## Guild levels and guild halls (`guild.lua`, `guild_hall.lua`, `guild_core.lua`, `guild_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_guild.sql`)

Guilds earn guild XP (GXP) from what their members already do, level from 1 to 20, and unlock small perks and a
guild hall: a guild-owned instance built at runtime. Client `game_guild` (Social > Guild in the top menu),
extended opcode 252 (`ChaosOpcodes.guild`). Every number is in `guild_config.lua`; the pure rules (curve, caps, perks,
upgrade prerequisites and costs, rent, slots and layout, depot rules, attribute encoding, the weekly board) are in
`guild_core.lua` and tested by `tests/guild_test.lua`. Guilds themselves (founding, members, ranks) stay the base
server's (`guilds`, `guild_ranks`, `guild_membership`; made on the website); rank level 3 = leader, 2 = vice-leader.

**Install.** Run `sql/chaos_guild.sql` (7 tables; `guild.lua` also creates them at startup when missing). Experience
share and the experience perk need the `patch_base_events.py` experience dispatch, like every Chaos experience bonus.

**Guild XP.**

| Source | GXP | Hook |
|---|---|---|
| Experience from monsters | 1% of it counted in "level units": a full level's worth of experience at the member's level = 10 GXP; at most 60 a member a day | own `onGainExperience` callback, kept in memory and written every minute and at logout |
| Bounty contract | 15 | a wrapper around `ChaosLeaderboard.record` (as seasons does), so no other script changes |
| Rift sealed | 10 + 2 x tier (max 40) | same |
| World boss participation | 40 | same (`worldboss`, one call per rewarded participant) |
| Invasion defended | 20 | same (`defender`, invasion.lua; any later `invasion*` board too) |
| Guild siege, per participant | 10 + 2% of the points (max 40) | same (`siege`) |
| Treasure goblin | 5 | same (`goblin`) |
| Guild siege result | 500 to the bracket winner, 150 to every other guild | new rows of `chaos_siege_results`, once a minute (earlier sieges are skipped on the first run) |

A member gives at most 400 GXP a day from all sources (`dailyCapAll`); siege results are not capped. The wrappers stack
safely with the season wrapper (a guard runs the guild part once per call, and seasons is told its wrapper is still in
place). Curve: level L -> L+1 needs round(300 x L^1.5) GXP: 300, 850, 1,560 ... 24,850; 5,110 to level 5, 33,320 to 10,
201,410 to 20 (a ten-member guild hunting daily reaches level 5 in about a week and 20 in months).

**Perks** (for online members, while they are in the guild; totals capped by `caps`):

| Level | Perk | Level | Perk |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | +1% experience | 10 | +1% experience, the guild aura (aura 4, Fireflies) |
| 3 | a guild hall scroll every day (`Social > Guild scroll`) | 12 | respec 5% cheaper |
| 4 | +2% loot | 13 | +20 depot slots |
| 5 | a guild hall can be bought | 14 | +1% experience |
| 6 | +1% experience | 15 | +1% loot |
| 7 | respec 10% cheaper | 17 | respec 5% cheaper |
| 8 | +20 depot slots | 18 | +20 depot slots |
| 9 | +2% loot | 20 | +1% experience |

At 20: +5% experience, +5% loot, respec -20%, +60 depot slots. Experience: monsters only, multiplied after the other
bonuses that ran before it. Loot: wraps `ChaosLootConfig.rateMult` for the corpse owner (the Chaos loot layer's extra
rolls and currency). Respec: wraps `ChaosRespec.fullCost` / `nodeCost` (tree, Paragon and single-node refunds). The
aura is given with `addAura` and taken back when the member leaves the guild (not when it was bought in the store).
A level-up is told to every online member with the new perks, and logged. API: `ChaosGuild.levelOf(guildId)` (for
the name plates' level badge), `ChaosGuild.perksOf(guildId)`, `ChaosGuild.addXp(guildId, playerId, source, amount)`.

**Guild bank.** `Social > Guild deposit <gold>` (or the window): any member, at least 1,000, from carried gold then the bank
balance. `Social > Guild withdraw <gold>`: the leader only, to the leader's bank balance. The hall, its upgrades and its rent
are paid from it. Money safety: every change of the guild bank is one conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE bank >= x` checked
with `ROW_COUNT()` (never read-then-write); a purchase pays first and then writes its row with a conditional statement
(`INSERT IGNORE` on the guild's key, `UPDATE ... WHERE tier = n`, `UPDATE ... WHERE paid_until = old`), and refunds and
logs when that write changed nothing. Money requests are limited to one a second per player (`ChaosRateLimit`), the
window requests that read the database to one per 300 ms. Season characters cannot use the guild bank or depot while
their season runs. Staff log: `chaos_guild_log` (deposit, withdraw, hall, upgrade, rent, put, take, refund, level,
staff) and a console line for every gold movement; `/guild log <guild>` shows the last 20.

**The guild hall.** The leader buys it at guild level 5 for 5,000,000 gold, from the guild bank or with their own gold.
One slot per guild (`chaos_guild_hall.slot`), in a grid of 64 slots (8 columns, 40 tiles apart) from 9216, 9216, 7,
where the real map has no tiles (OTBM scan: no tile area between x/y 3000 and 16000 except two at x 1790; other runtime
areas: tower 2000+, tutorial 4600+, world boss 5000+, siege 5100+, PvP arena 6000+, rifts 8192-8447). A slot is a
21 x 15 floor with walls, built with `Game.createTile` the first time it is needed (a slot with a map tile in its
footprint is skipped). The engine cannot remove tiles, so slots stay built and are reused: the fixtures are placed
again whenever the owner or the active upgrades change. Entry: the **Guild Hall Portal** of every town ("City
portals": the portal gallery at Cinderhold's temple, a fixed spot next to every other temple, then
`portalOffsets`; `portalPositions` replaces all of that when set; a look text and a green effect every 4 s; placed at
startup and checked once a minute): members of a guild that owns a hall go to their hall,
everyone else is refused ("Only guild members may enter a guild hall."). The exit forcefield leads to the temple
(`exitPosition` overrides it). Players cannot attack players inside a hall (an `onTargetCombat` callback), a player who
is not a member of the hall's guild (left the guild, logged in inside) is sent to the temple within a minute.

| Upgrade | Guild level | Gold | Needs | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Teleport Hub | 6 | 2,000,000 | | 4 forcefields along the north wall to the hunting areas of `hall.hub` (lands on the nearest free walkable tile within 3; each area has a way back at its `back` tile, action id 47616, into the guild's hall, 2026-10-21). A portal's look text announces "level N+" and the step-in enforces it (`ChaosGuildCore.hubGate`: below the destination's `level` the player is pushed back with "<name> needs level N."); `tools/check_hub_destinations.py DATA_DIR` reads the map and lists the destinations with no landing tile (they would answer "This portal leads nowhere right now."); run it after the content areas are installed |
| Training Room | 7 | 1,500,000 | | 3 exercise dummies of the base server (27751/27752; the store's exercise weapons work on them) and a damage dummy monster (the first of `dummyMonsters` the server knows) |
| Crafting Bench | 8 | 1,000,000 | | an anvil that opens the crafting window (`crafting.lua`) |
| Guild Depot | 9 | 2,500,000 | | a large trunk shared by the members, see below |
| Trophy Room | 10 | 1,000,000 | Teleport Hub | statues whose look text shows siege wins, world bosses, rift record, bounties, invasions, level and top contributors |
| Decoration 1 / 2 / 3 | 12 / 16 / 20 | 1.5M / 3M / 6M | Trophy Room | floor and walls: white marble, obsidian (black marble), gilded stone |

**Rent.** 300,000 gold a week + 100,000 per upgrade tier, paid from the guild bank: at purchase for the first week,
then automatically when due (once a minute check). If the bank is short the hall has 24 hours of grace (members are
reminded once an hour); after that the upgrades lock: their fixtures disappear (hub portals, dummies, bench, trunk,
trophies, decoration) and the depot is closed, nothing is deleted. Paying (Social > Guild, the window's Pay rent, or the
automatic try after a deposit) unlocks everything at once; a locked hall starts a new week from the payment (the locked
weeks are not charged), a hall in its grace time keeps its period.

**Guild depot.** Drop an item on the trunk inside your own hall: it is stored in `chaos_guild_depot` (item id, count and
its attributes as text: description, name, text, charges, attack/defense/armor and the other standard attributes, the
rarity system's custom attributes `rarity`, `combatPowerLevel`, every `rarity_*` modifier key of `ChaosCrafting`, uniques,
rift keys) and removed. Take items back in the Guild window (in the hall). Containers are refused; 30 entries + the
depot perks; members take at most 20 entries a day (leader and vice-leaders without limit). A take deletes the row with
one conditional `DELETE` first and only then creates the item, so double clicks or repeated requests give one item; no
room in the backpack -> the inbox; no room there either -> the row is put back. The window shows the depot's put/take
log. Limitation: a custom attribute that is not in that list is not copied (the engine has no call to list them).

**Weekly top guilds.** The window's Top Guilds tab ranks guilds by the GXP earned in the week (Monday 06:00, like the
leaderboards; `chaos_guild_contrib` rows with the week key), then level; it also names last week's top guild. The
Members tab shows every member's GXP this week and in total.

**Commands.** Social > Guild (window), `Social > Guild deposit|withdraw <gold>` (`5k`, `2.5m` work), `Social > Guild scroll`,
`Social > Guild hall buy [bank|self]`, `Social > Guild upgrade <hub|training|crafting|depot|trophy|decor>`, Social > Guild,
`Social > Guild take <id>`, `Social > Guild info`. Staff (`/guild`, groups with access): `xp <guild>, <n>`, `bank <guild>, <+-n>`,
`info <guild>`, `log <guild>`, `rent <guild>, due|lock|paid` (test helper: moves the paid-until time), `hall <guild>`.

**Client** (`game_guild`, JSON on 252): server -> client `state` {guild, perks, members, hall, depot, log, top},
`none` (not in a guild), `message`, `openModule` (the bench); client -> server `open`, `refresh`, `deposit`,
`withdraw`, `buyHall`, `upgrade`, `payRent`, `take`, `scroll`. Tabs: Overview (perks, scroll, guild bank, log),
Members, Guild Hall (rent and upgrades, buttons for the leader and vice-leaders), Depot, Top Guilds.

**Tested in game** (test server, cropped map, guild Iron Wolves with a leader and a member on two accounts, one client):
guild XP from kills (the experience share, 60 a day cap reached) and from a completed bounty contract (+15 through the
leaderboard hook); a level-up to 10 (staff XP on top) with the broadcast and the aura; the experience perk (a Dragon kill
18,900 -> 19,467 experience at +3%); the loot perk (rateMult x1.04); deposit and withdraw (a triple-clicked withdraw
paid once); buying the hall from the guild bank (a triple click bought it once); entering through the portal and
leaving through the exit; a non-member refused at the portal and sent out when placed inside; the Teleport Hub and the
Guild Depot bought from the window; the hub portal; a stack of Orbs of Upheaval and a Mythic dragon scale mail put on the trunk
and taken back with every modifier (three take requests in a row gave one item); a member taking an item; the depot
log; rent paid from the window; rent past the grace time with an empty bank locking the upgrades (fixtures gone, depot
closed, window red) and paying it unlocking them; the training room, bench (opens the crafting window), trophies and
decoration tiers 1 and 3 (looked at with the upgrades set in memory); the guild hall scroll (refused in combat, a
second claim the same day refused, used -> the hall); the window and its tabs. Not verified in game: the respec
discount (the test server has no respec.lua), rift / world boss / invasion / siege XP (unit-tested amounts; the hook
is the one the bounty used), the siege result poll (no `chaos_siege_results` table on the test server), the real map's
temples and hunting-area positions (the cropped map has neither: the test server's config pointed the portal, the exit
and one hub destination at its tiles), several guilds' halls at once, a restart with a hall in use (the tiles are gone
after a restart; the first entry builds them again).

## Guild wars in game (`guildwar.lua`, `guildwar_core.lua`, `guildwar_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_guildwar.sql`, engine patch 0020, client `game_guildwar`)

The base server knows guild wars only through the website (rows of `guild_wars`, status 1 = running; its
`playerdeath.lua` logs every war kill in `guildwar_kills`). This adds the whole flow in game, on extended opcode
**197** (`ChaosOpcodes.guildWar`), window Social > Guild Wars (also a button in the Guild window). Numbers:
`guildwar_config.lua`; pure rules: `guildwar_core.lua` (`tests/guildwar_test.lua`, which also runs `guildwar.lua` against
a mocked engine and database).

**Declaring.** The leader or a vice-leader (rank level 2+) names the target guild, a frag limit (10 / 25 / 50 / 100 / 200
counted kills), a duration (6 h / 1 / 3 / 7 days) and an optional gold stake per side (0, or 100,000 - 500,000,000; only
the leader, who alone may withdraw from the guild bank). Refused: a target in another season realm (a guild belongs to
the realm of its owner), guilds whose owners share an account or last IP (`sameOwnerBlocked`: a war could move a stake
between their banks), fewer than 3 members on either side, an offer or war between the pair already (ours or a website
one in `guild_wars`), 24 hours after their last war, 3 wars and offers per guild, one declaration a minute, a guild bank
short of the stake, a season character's bank. The stake leaves the declarer's guild bank at once (escrow, one
conditional UPDATE through `ChaosGuild.spend`). The other guild's members are told; the offer is open 24 hours.

**Answering.** The other guild's leader or a vice-leader accepts or declines in the window (a war with a stake: the
leader accepts). Accepting takes the same stake from that guild bank, inserts the base `guild_wars` row (status 1, and
`znote_guild_wars` with the frag limit when the website's table exists) and refreshes the engine's war list of every
online member of both guilds: with engine patch 0020 (`Player:setGuildWarList`) the war emblems (green own, red enemy)
and the skull rules (no white skull, no unjustified kill against a war enemy) change at once; without it at the next
login, and the members are told so. A declined, taken back or expired offer returns the stake. Pending offers live only
in `chaos_guildwar` (the base startup deletes status-0 rows of `guild_wars`).

**Kills that count** (`kills`): a player killed by a player of the other side (last hit, a summon's master, else the
most damage) is a war kill. It counts for the killer's guild unless killer and victim share an IP or an account, the
victim is below level 100 or below half the killer's level, the same victim already counted within 30 minutes, or either
is of another realm than the war. Every war kill goes into `chaos_guildwar_kills` with its verdict (the window's Kill
log shows refused ones with the reason); both guilds see each kill and the score.

**The end.** First side to the frag limit wins; when the time is up the side with more counted kills wins (a tie is a
draw); a surrender (leader or vice-leader, confirmed) gives the war to the other side; a guild that disbands loses; a
base row ended elsewhere (the website) ends ours by the score. Every status change is one conditional UPDATE of the war
row checked with `ROW_COUNT()`, so an end is paid once. The winner's guild bank gets both stakes minus `feePercent` 10%
(the fee is burnt: a gold sink); a draw returns both stakes in full. `pay1 + pay2 + fee` is always what was held (tested
for every stake and side). The base row goes to status 4, the war lists are refreshed. Winners of a war ended by the frag
limit or the time with 10+ counted kills get 150 guild XP; trophy counters `wars` / `warWins` (chaos_guild_stats); a
broadcast at the start and the end. Bank changes appear in the guild log (action `war`).

**Board.** The window: offers (accept / decline / take back), running wars (score, time left, terms, kill log,
surrender), the guild's history; the War Board tab and the website page `page.php?plugin=chaos&p=guildwars` (website
README) show the running wars and the latest ended ones of the server. Staff: `/guildwar` (list), `/guildwar end, <id>`,
`/guildwar expire, <id>`, `/guildwar time, <id>`.

**Engine patch 0020** (`src-patches/0020-guild-war-list-lua.patch`): `player:getGuildWarList()` and
`player:setGuildWarList({guildIds})` (luascript.cpp / .h only); setting the list re-sends the emblem and skull of the
player to every player in view and theirs to the player.

**Tested** on a live test server (engine 0001-0020, two clients on one machine): the same-owner refusal, a declaration with
a 1,000,000 stake (escrow), the offer on the other side, accept (both stakes held, the base row, green / red emblems on
both clients without a relog), a kill refused for the same IP, a counted kill with the IP rule switched off for the test,
the kill log, a surrender (1,800,000 to the winner, 200,000 burnt), emblems gone, the War Board.

## The weekly guild boss (`guildboss.lua`, `guildboss_core.lua`, `guildboss_config.lua`, monsters `monsters/chaos/guildboss/`)

**Limits** (`guildboss_config.lua` `limits`, "Instance limits"): the boss's limit (13 minutes after it appears) with warnings at 5 min, 1 min and 10 s; time up is a failed attempt (half of the need stays as fuel, everyone back in the hall); at most 8 arenas, the wait and the waiting line when all are in use.

A guild-only instanced boss, Gorvath the Banner-Eater, once per guild and week (Monday 06:00). Window: the Guild Boss tab
of `game_guildwar` (opcode 197), also opened by using the **Summoning Stone**, an obelisk (1560, action id 47609) that
every guild hall gets on the east wall below the depot spot (`guild_hall.lua`'s `G.furnish` is wrapped, nothing edited
there). Numbers: `guildboss_config.lua`; pure rules: `guildboss_core.lua` (`tests/guildboss_test.lua`, also the engine
file against mocks: donations, the summon, a failed attempt, the lockout).

**Fuel (a gold sink).** The stone needs 500 + 25 x guild level embers (level 10: 750). Members feed it during the week:
gold (carried, then the bank balance; 10,000 gold = 1 ember, at least 100,000) and materials (every one carried, up to
100: rune shard 2, omen fragment 3, Orb of Upheaval 5, Orb of Fate 25, Orb of Grafting 60 embers). Each gift is logged per
member (`chaos_guildboss_contrib`, the window's "This week's fuel") and in the guild log (action `boss`). Fuel left at
the weekly reset is gone; after the kill the stone takes nothing more.

**Summon.** The leader or a vice-leader, standing in the guild hall with the stone full and the rent paid: one conditional
UPDATE takes the need (fuel >= need, not killed this week, fewer than 3 summons). Every member of the guild in the same
hall, level 150+, comes along (1 to 20; one member may summon alone, owner 2026-10-24: all content solo). Health: the XML's x (1 + 0.6 (n-1)); alone x `boss.soloHealthMult` = 0.8 (a solo kill takes 495 s like two, the unscaled 619 s would pass the enrage at 600). Lives, adds and hazards already scaled from one player; the gold pool is 250,000 per rewarded member, so a solo member gets the average share of a group, never more. A failed attempt (wipe, time, everyone left) gives back half of the need as fuel;
a server restart during a fight returns the whole need and the summon.

**The fight** reuses the Ascended arenas (`uber_core.lua`: layout, telegraph shapes and marks, phase machine, enrage,
shared lives, the lethal-hit catch) with this config: health 650,000 x (1 + 0.6 x (players - 1)); three phases (The Gnawed
Standard: cone / ring / marks; Torn Colours at 66%: cross / circle / half and Banner Wraith adds; The Last Rally at 33%:
five patterns, burning pools, adds that heal it); enrage at 10:00 (x1.6 damage, faster telegraphs, a pulse), the arena
closes at 13:00; shared lives 3 + 1 per 3 more players (a lethal hit sends the player to the Ember Gate in the
antechamber, back after 8 s). Balance model (level 600 characters, 1,400 dps at 75% uptime): about 495 s with 2, 420 s
with 5, 395 s with 10 (tests keep them within 10% and before the enrage). The rift HUD (opcode 228) shows the fight.

**Rewards.** Every participant present at the kill who dealt 1% of the damage or healed is rewarded: 3 Orbs of Upheaval
and 1 Orb of Fate each, and a share of one **gold pool** for the guild. The pool is 250,000 per rewarded participant,
counted up to 10 (2: 500k, 5: 1.25M, 10 or more: 2.5M; `reward.pool`). The kill is a net gold sink: the fuel is 525-1000
embers (5.25M-10M gold), so the largest pool is at most ~50% of the cheapest stone (before: 1.5M each, 15M and 6 + 2
orbs each for 10 players, more than the fuel). The split (`B.splitGold`): everyone first gets 25% of an even split
(`floorShare`; 62,500 with 5 and with 10 rewarded), the rest goes in proportion to the contribution,
damage to the boss + healing done to the other participants (only the missing health counts; `healWeight` 1). Shares
are rounded down and the remainder goes to the top contributor, so they sum to the pool exactly. Each share goes to the
bank balance (a member who logged out in the arena gets it by an UPDATE of `players.balance`), is shown in the kill
message ("x gold to your bank (y% of the guild's pool)"), kept in `chaos_guildboss_week.pool` and
`chaos_guildboss_contrib.spoils` / `contribution` (the Guild Boss tab's "This week's spoils") and in the guild log
(action `boss`). The guild: 400 + 20 per participant guild XP (at most 800), the counter
`guildBoss` (trophy room line, banner tiers Ember 1 / Cinder 4 / Blazing 10 / Undying Flame 20 kills shown on the hall
flags), the weekly lockout (`chaos_guildboss_week.killed_at`; storage 7101302 = the next reset for the members: the Boss
Spawns cooldown of the "Guild Boss" row). The boss also gives its XML experience and the loot system's boss bonus like
other bosses (unchanged by the pool).

**Board.** This week's guilds: kills first (fastest), then the damage of their attempts (`chaos_guildboss_week`, every
attempt in `chaos_guildboss_runs`).

**Arena area:** x 11264-11455, y 10000-10095, z 7 (4 x 2 slots of 48, built with `Game.createTile`), clear of the tower,
island, world boss, siege, arena, ascension trial, Ascended, rifts, trials, guild halls, the Ember Descent, the raid, the
battleground (x/y 11264-11455 at y 11264+) and the hideouts (12288+); `tests/guildboss_test.lua` checks the overlaps.
Staff: `/guildboss` (runs), `/guildboss fuel, <guild>, <n>`, `/guildboss reset, <guild>`, `/guildboss phase, <n>`,
`/guildboss end`. Tested on a live test server: the stone in the hall, gold and orb donations, the summon with two
members, telegraphs, falls to the Ember Gate, phase 2, the kill (rewards, 440 guild XP, the Ember Banner on the flags),
the lockout and the Boss Spawns row. The gold pool split is covered by the unit and mocked-engine tests only (not yet
on the live test server).

## Arena (`arena.lua`, `arena_core.lua`, `arena_config.lua`, client `game_arena`)

**Limits** (`arena_config.lua` `limits`, "Instance limits"): 10 s of countdown and 5 minutes of fight (unchanged) with warnings at 1 minute and 10 s; a pair that finds every slot in use is told once, with the wait, and starts when one frees up. `/instances close arena <id>` stops a match (not rated).

Ranked PvP: 1v1 and 2v2, an Elo rating per mode, matches in arena instances built at runtime. Settings are in
`arena_config.lua`, the pure part (ratings, matchmaking, level rule, death catch, timeout) in `arena_core.lua`
(`tests/arena_test.lua`), the runtime in `arena.lua` (`tests/arena_flow_test.lua` runs it on a mocked engine: 2v2,
parallel slots, disconnect, timeout).

**Queue.** `Adventure > Arena queue 1v1`, `Adventure > Arena queue 2v2` (a party of exactly two; either member queues both), Adventure > Arena
(leaves the queue, or forfeits a running match), Adventure > Arena (status and the window). The window (Adventure > Arena in the top
menu, or Adventure > Arena) shows the rating, W-L-D and best per mode, the queue buttons, the queue time and window, the level
range you can face, whether today's first-win bonus is taken and the last 10 matches. To queue (and again when the match
is found) every player must be level 50+, in a protection zone, out of combat (no fight lock), not multi-clienting
(`Chaos.isMultiClient`) and not inside a dungeon, the Infinity Tower, a rift, the world boss rooms or a siege
(`ChaosDungeonIsInside`, `ChaosTowerRun.isInside`, `ChaosRift.isInside`, `ChaosWorldBoss.inside`, `ChaosSiege.isInside`;
each is skipped when it does not exist). A player who fails the check when the match is found is dropped from the queue
with the reason; the other entry stays queued.

**Matchmaking.** Every 2 seconds, oldest entry first, each entry takes the closest rating it may face. Allowed rating
difference: 100, +50 for every 10 s waited, at most 600, measured on the entry that waited longer. 2v2 teams queue with
the average 2v2 rating of the two. Two 1v1 players in the same party, or two entries from the same connection, never
pair. **Level rule** (one rule for both modes, over every player of the match): the lowest level must be at least 80%
of the highest, or within 20 levels of it. 800 fights 1000, 300 never does; there is no stat normalisation.

**The match.** A free slot of a grid of 8 (`grid` in the config: origin 6000,6000,7, 4 columns, 24 tiles apart; the
world boss uses 5000-5048, the tower 2000-2660, rifts 8192-8448) is built once with `Game.createTile`: an 11 x 9 room
of black marble with two pillars and coal basins, and a gallery south of it behind a wall. The build is refused if any
tile of the slot already exists (runtime tiles are gone after a restart, so an existing tile is always the map's); a
refused slot is skipped (`/arena slots` lists them). Everyone is checked again, healed to full health and mana, freed of
damage-over-time conditions and teleported in, the teams 6 tiles apart. 10 seconds of countdown (no damage between
players at all), then 5 minutes of fight. The client module turns secure mode off for the match (the base PvP rules make
a player with secure mode on unattackable) and back on after it; a fighter who still has it on 15 s into the fight is
counted as defeated.

**No death, skull or frag inside.** Fighters get three creature events for the match. `onHealthChange` drops every hit
that is not allowed (countdown, team mate, defeated attacker or target, anyone from outside the match) and cuts a hit
that would kill to leave 1 health: that player is defeated and moved to the gallery, where nothing can hit them and they
cannot hit. `onPrepareDeath` is the safety net (a hit raised by a later script, an `ORIGIN_NONE` hit): it cancels the
death and defeats the player. `onManaChange` drops mana taken by players who may not hit. An EventCallback
`onTargetCombat` refuses attacks before the fight, on team mates and the defeated, and in or out of a match ("The fight
starts in N seconds."). Nobody dies, so there is no frag, unjustified kill, death loss or corpse; the white skull and the
fight lock of the fight are removed at the end (`removeCondition(CONDITION_INFIGHT)` clears both), the target is
cleared, and everyone goes back to where they stood when the match started (the temple for a missing position), healed.

**End.** One side has nobody standing: the other side wins. Time out: the side with the higher share of health left
(sum of health / sum of max health, the defeated count as 0) wins; equal (within 0.1%) is a draw. Leaving counts as a
loss: logging out (only possible in the countdown, the engine refuses a logout in fight), losing the connection for 3 s,
Adventure > Arena, being moved out of the slot, or another character of the same connection logging in. A leaver is sent
back at once and scores 0 even when the partner wins the 2v2. `/arena stop` (staff) ends every match unrated. So does a
server shutdown or a closed server (the daily restart): `onShutdown`, or the first kick of a closed server, stops every
match unrated before the players are kicked, so nobody gets a loss from the restart (`tests/arena_flow_test.lua`).

**Ratings.** Elo per mode, start 1000, floor 100, K 40 for a player's first 10 matches of the mode, then 24. Every player
is rated against the other team's average (1v1: the opponent). Both the window and the result toast show the change
(`Rating 1000 -> 1020 (+20)`); the chat gets the same line. `ChaosLeaderboard.record("arena1v1" / "arena2v2", player,
rating, "max")` is called after every rated match when the leaderboard module is loaded (board keys in
`arena_config.lua` `modes`): the weekly Arena 1v1 and Arena 2v2 boards of the leaderboards (best rating of the week;
titles Duelist and Gladiator; "arena3v3", title Triumvir). **3v3** (a party of exactly three) uses the same room (three
spawns and gallery spots a side). **PvP seasons**: every rated match also counts for the mode's season rating
(`arena_season.lua`, called at the end of `finish()`); the window shows the season tier or the placement per mode and the
result toast the season change. The arena matchmaking keeps the lifetime Elo above. See "Battleground and PvP seasons".

**Rewards.** A win: 1 Orb of Upheaval (at most 10 rewarded wins a day). The first win of the day on top: 1 Orb of Fate and 2
Orbs of Upheaval. A draw or a loss gives nothing. Backpack first, the rest to the inbox. Storages 7100340-7100342 (player:
first-win day, wins day, wins count); 7100340-7100349 are reserved for the arena.

**Database** (`sql/chaos.sql`): `chaos_arena_ratings` (player, mode, rating, wins, losses, draws, best),
`chaos_arena_matches` (one row per rated match: mode, slot, winner, reason, start, end) and
`chaos_arena_match_players` (every player of a rated match: team, result, rating before/after, opponents, partner,
reason; the window's recent matches).

**Client** (`game_arena`, opcode 236 JSON): `state` (window), `start` (HUD on, secure mode off), `hud` every second
(both teams' names and health %, countdown or fight clock, your team on the left), `end` (VICTORY / DEFEAT / DRAW toast
with the rating change and the reward, 8 s; secure mode restored, attack cancelled); client -> server `open`,
`queue {mode}`, `leave`.

**Test switch.** The test map has no protection zone and the engine has no Lua call to give a runtime tile the
protection-zone flag, so the queue's protection-zone rule can be switched off for tests only:
`Game.setStorageValue(Chaos.arenaConfig.testNoPzStorage, 1)` (global storage 7100345, in memory, gone after a restart).
Never set it on a live server.

**Tested in game** (srv6, two clients on one IP, multi-client blocks switched off for the fights): the multi-client and
protection-zone refusals, the level rule (562 vs 1000 stayed queued, 850 vs 1000 paired), queue and match start, the
countdown block (attack refused with the message, scripted damage dropped), the death catch from a real melee hit and
from a scripted 30000 hit (1 health, defeated, gallery, no death row, no skull after), the rating change on both sides
(+20/-20, +18/-18, the underdog +26), the timeout decision (an exact health-share tie gave a draw, -2/+2), a dropped
connection as a loss, `/arena stop` unrated, the footprint refusal over the test map's tiles and all 8 slots built, the
HUD, the result toast, the window and the top-menu entry. 2v2, the gallery in a 2v2 and parallel matches were run on the
mocked engine only (there were two client displays).

**Limits.** No spectators from outside. No stat normalisation between levels inside the 80% band. The engine refuses a
logout during a fight, so a logout mid-fight is a disconnect (counted after 3 s). Players keep their buffs, summons and
items (potions and runes are used up as normal). The world type must allow PvP (`worldType = "pvp"`); on a no-pvp world
the engine blocks the damage before the scripts see it.

## Battleground and PvP seasons (`battleground.lua`, `battleground_core.lua`, `battleground_config.lua`, `arena_season.lua`, `sql/chaos_battleground.sql`, client `game_battleground`)

**Limits** (`battleground_config.lua` `limits`, "Instance limits"): 30 s of preparation and 15 minutes (unchanged) with warnings at 5 min, 1 min and 10 s; teams found while every field is in use are told once, with the wait, and start when one frees up. `/instances close battleground <id>` stops a match (not rated).

**Ember Wells**, an objective battleground for 5v5 to 10v10, and **PvP seasons** for the arena brackets (1v1, 2v2, 3v3)
and the battleground. Every number is in `battleground_config.lua`; the pure part (season dates, Glicko-lite, decay,
soft reset, tiers, rewards, matchmaking, normalisation, capture, score, waves, AFK, honor, deserter, vendor, the map) is
`battleground_core.lua` (`tests/battleground_test.lua`); `battleground.lua` is the runtime and `arena_season.lua` the
season ratings (both run on a mocked engine in `tests/battleground_flow_test.lua`). Extended opcode 200
(`ChaosOpcodes.battleground`), JSON through `Chaos.sendChunked`. Storages 7100380-7100389 (+0 inside a match, +1..+3 the
return position, +9 a GLOBAL test switch, see below). Tables (`sql/chaos_battleground.sql`, also created at startup):
`chaos_pvp_players` (honor, record, weekly honor and first win, deserter), `chaos_pvp_ratings` (season, character,
bracket), `chaos_pvp_season_rewards`, `chaos_bg_matches`, `chaos_pvp_purchases`; server_config `chaos_pvp_season_done`.

**Queue.** Adventure > Battleground (window tabs Battleground, PvP Season, Honor Vendor). Level 100+, in a protection zone,
out of combat, not multi-clienting, not inside a dungeon / the tower / a rift / a siege / the Descent / a raid / an
Ascended Omen / the world boss rooms, not queued for or fighting in the arena (and the arena refuses players queued for or
inside the battleground), no deserter penalty. Solo, or the party leader queues the whole party (up to 5; everyone checked,
same level bracket and realm). A player queues as one of the class's roles (`party_finder_config.lua` `classRoles`; the
main role by default, Tank / Healer / DPS buttons when the class has several). The Party Finder has a "Battleground"
activity (party of 5) to gather a group; the window's Find a Group button opens it.

**Matchmaking** (every 5 s, `K.findMatches`). Entries are grouped by **realm** (standard or the running season,
`ChaosSeason.realmOf`) and **level bracket** (100-299, 300-599, 600-899, 900+); groups never mix. Oldest entry first: the
entries inside its rating window (250 + 50 per 15 s waited, at most 1200; the battleground season rating) fill up to 20
players; the largest even match whole parties can fill is taken (10v10 at once; 5v5 to 9v9 only once the oldest entry
waited 45 s). The split into two teams keeps parties whole and minimises |team average rating difference| + 120 x (tank
difference + healer difference): subset-sum starts in a few orders plus 8 fixed pseudo-random ones, each improved by
moving one entry against one of the same size or two that add up. Tested: solo queues always split tanks and healers
evenly with team averages within 50; random party queues cost at most 10 above the exhaustive optimum. The window shows
the estimated wait (the average of the last 10 waits of the group, sooner when enough are queued).

**Level normalisation.** There was no PvP damage scaling before (only the healing reduction of `healing_rules_core.lua`,
which stays). Inside a match every hit and heal between players is multiplied by `(ref / source level)^0.8 x (target level
/ ref)^0.8`, each factor clamped to 0.6-1.6, `ref` being the bracket's reference level (200, 450, 750, 1000). Health,
damage and healing grow about linearly with the level, so exponent 1 would erase the level; 0.8 leaves a small edge.
Gear, the passive tree and skill are not touched.

**The map** (built at runtime with `Game.createTile`, like the arena; never over an existing tile; `/bg slots` lists refused
slots). Grid of 4 slots at **x/y 11264-11455, z 7** (origin 11264,11264, 2 columns, 96 apart; each slot 65 x 33 tiles; the
guild boss grid is at y 10000+, the hideouts at 12288+). A 63 x 31 field of black marble with a 180-degree rotation
symmetry: each team's base (7 x 9, stone floor, a 3-tile gate, two flags) at its end with a closed graveyard behind a wall
above it; cover walls and pillars; three braziers (coal basins) on white marble circles: the West Well near team 1, the
Heart Well in the centre, the East Well near team 2. Teams: **Emberguard** (west) and **Ashbound** (east).

**The match.** 30 s preparation in the bases (no damage; anyone outside is put back), then up to 15 minutes.
**Capture:** alive players of one team only within 2 tiles of a brazier move its progress towards their side, 8 s alone
from neutral (x1.25 per extra player, at most x2); both teams inside = contested; an enemy brazier is neutral at the half
and yours after 16 s. **Score:** every 2 s a team gets 4 / 10 / 20 points for 1 / 2 / 3 braziers held (all three win in 100
s, one in 500 s), and 5 for every enemy downed. 1000 wins (both at once: the higher, equal = draw); at the time limit the
higher score wins. **Death catch** (as the arena): a hit that would kill leaves 1 health; the player is **downed**, goes to
the team's graveyard, cannot hit or be hit, and comes back at the base, healed, with the next **respawn wave** (every 15 s
from the start of the fight). Nobody dies: no item or experience loss, no frag; the white skull and the fight lock are
removed when everyone goes back where they stood (12 s after the end, healed). The killer gets the kill, everyone of the
other team who hit in the last 10 s an assist. An enemy stepping into a base is thrown back to their own. Team mates and
the downed cannot be attacked (`onTargetCombat`), nobody from outside the match can hit or heal into it.
**AFK:** no step, hit, heal or brazier hold for 60 s: a warning (the HUD counts down), at 120 s removed as a deserter.
**Deserter** (leave, logout, lost connection for 20 s, AFK, leaving the field): a loss for the season rating, no rewards,
no queue for 15 / 30 / 60 / 120 minutes for the 1st / 2nd / 3rd / 4th+ desertion in 24 hours. A team with nobody left
loses by forfeit. A shutdown, a closed server or `/bg stop` ends every match unrated; a crash inside sends the character back
to where the match started at the next login.

**Rewards.** **Honor** (per character, cap 50000): win 120, draw 80, loss 50, +4 per kill or assist (cap 40), +10 per
brazier taken while standing in it (cap 50); at most 6000 a week from matches; the **weekly first win** (Monday 06:00) adds
300 honor and 1 Orb of Fate + 3 Orbs of Upheaval. Deserters and players present for less than half the fight get nothing.
The weekly **Battleground** leaderboard counts wins (title Wellkeeper); achievements Kindle the Wells, Keeper of the Wells
(title), Ashes and Honor (stats `bg_wins`, `bg_matches`). **Honor vendor** (window tab): 50 great health / mana / spirit
potions (60) and 50 ultimate health potions (120), and three cosmetics (`cosmetics_config.lua` source `pvp`): kill effect
Honor Brand (3000), loot labels Warbanner (2000), chat name Gladiator Steel (2500). Nothing with power above PvE gear.

**PvP seasons** (`arena_season.lua`, `ChaosPvpSeason`). 8 weeks each from the epoch Monday 5 Oct 2026 06:00 (`season.weeks`,
`season.epoch`). A rating per bracket (`1v1`, `2v2`, `3v3`, `bg`): **Glicko-lite**, start 1500, deviation 350; one rated
match is one Glicko-1 period against the other team's average rating and root-mean-square deviation (a leaver scores 0);
the deviation never drops below 75 (about +/-15 between equals) and grows by 35 per idle week. The first **5 matches** of
a bracket are placement (the tier stays hidden). **Tiers:** Ashen (below 1400), Smouldering 1400, Kindled 1600, Blazing
1800, Infernal 2000, Cinder Sovereign 2200 (emblems from `client/tools/gen_battleground_art.py`). **Decay:** a rating of
2000 or more loses 30 per full week after 14 days without a rated match of that bracket, never below 2000 (applied when
read and at the season's end). **Season end** (checked every minute and at startup, idempotent): the best placed
bracket's tier decides the rewards: honor (200 / 400 / 700 / 1000 / 1500 / 2500), a name plate title "<Tier> (S<n>)" from
Smouldering on (title source `pvpseason`, with the plate frame ember / crimson / gold / violet from Kindled on), cosmetics
for the account (Blazing labels from Blazing, Infernal chat name from Infernal, the Cinder Throne kill effect for Cinder
Sovereign), achievement stat `pvp_season_tier` (achievements Blazing Season, Cinder Sovereign). Then every rating
**soft-resets** when first read in the new season: 1500 + (rating - 1500) / 2, deviation at least 200, placement again.
The arena keeps matching on its lifetime Elo; the battleground matches on its season rating.

**Client** (`game_battleground`): the window (queue with role buttons, status and estimated wait, the four season cards
with emblem / tier / rating or placement, honor and record; the season tab with the dates, rules and the rewards per tier;
the vendor), the HUD at the top of the map (both scores towards 1000, the clock, the three wells with owner, capture
progress or "contested", the respawn wave and AFK countdowns, a Scoreboard button), the scoreboard (kills, assists, downs,
wells, damage, healing per player, both teams) and the end summary (result, score, season change, honor). Secure mode is
turned off for the match and back on after it. Protocol: client -> server `open`, `query`, `queue {role}`, `role {role}`,
`leave`, `board`, `buy {key}`; server -> client `state`, `start`, `hud`, `board`, `alert`, `end`, `msg`.

**Staff / tests.** `/bg stop | slots | min <n> | off | on` (`min` lowers the smallest team in memory, TEST ONLY).
`Game.setStorageValue(7100389, 1)` (global, in memory) skips the protection-zone rule on test maps without one; never on a
live server. **Tested** on a live test server (two clients on one IP, multi-client blocks off, `/bg min 1`, season rows of
one character seeded in the DB for the window): queue window, the match start and runtime map, preparation, a West Well
capture and the score ticks, the HUD, real `ORIGIN_SPELL` hits (scaled, death catch, downed, graveyard, wave), the
scoreboard, the end (season rating 1500 -> 1662 in placement, honor 438 with the weekly first win and its orbs, the
achievement, the DB rows), the release to the start position, the season and vendor tabs and a purchase. 5v5 and larger
ran on the mocked engine only. Note: scripted damage with `doTargetCombatHealth` and no origin skips `onHealthChange` on
this engine (as for every Chaos system); real attacks carry an origin.

## The Scorched Marches (open-world PvP zone) (`pvpzone.lua`, `pvpzone_core.lua`, `pvpzone_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_pvpzone.sql`, client `game_pvpzone`)

Roadmap item 77. An open-world PvP zone with risk and reward. Client `game_pvpzone` (Adventure > Scorched Marches),
extended opcode 193 (`ChaosOpcodes.pvpZone`; 193 is free in the reference server, the reference client's own
`ExtendedIds` 140 / 144-146 / 210 / 212 / 213 / 230 / 246 and every Chaos module, tested). Every number is in
`pvpzone_config.lua`; the rules are pure functions in `pvpzone_core.lua` (`ChaosPvpZoneCore`).

**Install.** The scripts load with the others; `pvpzone.lua` creates its three tables at startup (also in
`sql/chaos_pvpzone.sql`). `tools/patch_base_events.py` step 11 (`install_all.py` step `events`) makes the base
`Creature:onTargetCombat` ask `ChaosPvpZone.targetCombat` right after the siege hook: the base rules refuse an attack on
a player whose secure mode is on before any script callback runs, so without it a player could hide behind secure mode
(the server warns at startup when the hook is missing). Small hunks elsewhere: `loot_config.lua` rateMult,
`data/spells/chaos/_common.lua` (`ChaosSpell.canAttack` asks `ChaosPvpZone.canAttack` after the siege), `townportal.lua` /
`townportal_core.lua` (no Town Portal inside), `cosmetics_config.lua` (three vendor cosmetics), `leaderboard_config.lua`
(board `marches`), `achievements_data.lua` (six achievements), `chaos_constants.lua`. `blessings.lua` asks
`ChaosPvpZone.isInside(player)` / `.inZone(pos or player)`.

**Where.** Decided: built at runtime (`mode = "build"`), like the battleground and the rifts: no base map edit, and the
same on the cropped test map and the live map. One instance per realm: standard characters in slot 0, a running season
in its own slot (season id 1..3, then reused), so season and standard characters never meet here and embers, piles,
the shrine and its buff never cross realms (the open-world rule of "Seasons" allows PvP between realms; here it is
simply never possible). Grid x/y 13312 - 13823, z 7 (74 x 58 per instance with the wall), clear of every other runtime
area (tested). The field (O275, redesigned from a flat black marble plain): scorched rock ground in six variants with
basalt fields and crack patches, the border pieces of the generated areas between them (basalt over rock, rock over the
cracks: `areagen_config.lua` families and `pieces`, `ChaosAreaGenCore.borderPieces`), two gate yards (south-west and
north-east, 180-degree fair) each with a safe exit (a white marble circle by two banners, four coal basins), flagstone
roads 3 wide from each yard to the Cinder Shrine plaza (stone floor, radius 6) and through the gap of the broken wall
beyond it, the Cinder Shrine in the centre (a coal basin in a radius-3 circle with four big coal basins at its corners and
four glowing skull pillars around the plaza as beacons), the ruins (stone walls, pillars, a paved ruined hall in the
corner) and about 300 pieces of cover in clumps: charred trees, scorched rock and rock spikes, bone fields, lava holes
(only on the crack ground), with lava cracks, rubble, pebbles and bones as non-blocking decoration; 37 spawn points away
from the exits and the shrine. All ids are stock items the generated hunting areas already use (grounds, borders,
obstacles and `areaplan/decor_kits.json` decoration), listed in `pvpzone_config.lua` `look`; nothing is placed on the
roads, the yards, the plaza, next to a spawn point or within 2 tiles of a gate yard. The cover is laid in one half and
turned for the other (fair), and every piece is accepted only if the field stays connected (a neighbour-ring test, a
flood fill when that is not enough), so every objective is reachable from the entry. The look is deterministic: integer
hashes of the tile's coordinates (no clock, no `math.random`), the same in LuaJIT and Lua 5.3, in every slot, and the
layout is cached per config. Built at startup by `buildTiles` (ground, border pieces, wall, decoration, cover, lights,
landmarks), so the new look applies on the next server start: **no install step** (nothing in the otbm).
`mode = "map"` uses an existing rectangle of the loaded map instead (`area`: its exits, shrine and the
one realm let in; the map's own monsters inside are scaled when they spawn); not tried on a live map.

**Entering.** Adventure > Scorched Marches: the window (rules, the shrine, the pledge, the vendor, the record), Enter
opens the confirmation: every rule, "you carry N embers, a defeat drops them all, your killer may take up to 800", an
"I understand" box; the server checks `accept` too. Level 150+, from a protection zone, out of combat, not
multi-clienting, not inside another instance (dungeon, tower, rift, siege, descent, raid, Omen, battleground, hideout,
arena queue or match), no defeat cooldown (90 s). The player arrives next to a random safe exit, protected for 10 s
(no damage, cannot be attacked; attacking a player ends it). Walking or being teleported in without the confirmation
(map mode, a staff teleport) puts the player out again with the confirmation.

**Hardcore.** Decided: Hardcore season characters cannot enter at all (`hardcore.allow = false`; the window shows why
and the Enter button of the confirmation stays disabled). In open PvP a player decides when you fall (ambush, gank),
which the Hardcore protections are built to avoid; and since nobody dies here, letting them in would also be a
Hardcore run that cannot end where the risk is highest. With `allow = true` a second box ("a defeat here may end my
Hardcore run", `hcAccept`) would be needed. Self-Found characters may enter but never take another player's pile.

**Inside.** Open PvP whatever the world type allows through the scripts: `ChaosPvpZone.targetCombat` (base hook,
an EventCallback and the Chaos spells) lets players of the same instance attack each other regardless of the target's
secure mode; refused: across the border, protected or held players, party members (allies), a multi-client attacker.
**The battle lock** (beta 2026-10-20: "the debuff lasts 3+ minutes and the player respawns on a safe zone"). The debuff
is the engine's `CONDITION_INFIGHT`: the PvP lock (no logout, no protection zone on foot, the Town Portal and the temple
cleanse refuse) with the white skull riding on it, renewed with the server's whole `pzLocked` time by every player hit.
Inside it is cut to `combatLock.maxSeconds` (60) every tick (`K.lockTicks`). Leaving (a safe exit, a defeat, any other
way out) removes it with the skull and the monsters' harmful conditions, and again 100 ms and 1 s later
(`combatLock.clearAfterMs`): a cancelled lethal hit still runs the engine's attack bookkeeping after `onPrepareDeath`
and put the lock back for the full `pzLocked` time, so a defeated player stood in a protection zone with a lock the
temple cleanse would not touch. The respawn point: the temple, as every other death (`K.defeatDestination`), never a
spot inside the zone (the 90 s cooldown would keep him waiting there) nor the protection zone he happened to enter from.
The client turns its own secure mode off inside (and back on when leaving). No white skull (taken back every second),
and since the lethal hit is cancelled, no unjustified kill, no frag, no item, experience or blessing loss. PvP damage is
scaled like the battleground (`normalise` of `battleground_config.lua`, the target's bracket sets the reference level:
a level 1000 hitting a level 200 deals x0.6, the other way x1.6). Monsters: x1.6 health, x1.35 damage to players,
x1.5 experience, x1.5 Chaos loot rate; a spawn point refills 90 s after its monster died. World type "no-pvp": the
engine refuses every player attack before any script is asked (`Combat::canDoCombat`), so the zone has no PvP there
(monsters, embers and the shrine work; the server says so at startup). The live config is "pvp".

**Embers.** Carried (storage 7100522, at most 2,500) and banked (`chaos_pvpzone_players`, at most 200,000).
Monster kills inside give the player with the most damage 2 / 6 / 15 / 40 / 150 by tier (normal .. boss), the
shrine's warden +100, a capture +200 to every pledged player of the capturing faction in the circle.
A defeat (`onPrepareDeath` cancels the lethal hit): the player is sent to his home town's temple (`death.respawn =
"temple"`, decided 2026-10-20; `"entry"` = back where he entered, the rule before), healed, 90 s cooldown; all carried embers fall as a pile (an ashes marker and fire effects) where he stood. The killer (the last
player hit within 10 s also counts when a monster lands the blow) alone may take it for 30 s, then anyone; at most 800
per pile and player and 4,000 a day from other players' piles, never past the carry cap; the victim may take his own
back; after 120 s the rest burns. Pickup: stand on the pile or next to it. Banking: stand in a safe exit circle for 5 s
without dealing or taking damage (the HUD shows "Leaving... n%"); the carried embers are banked, the player goes back
to where he entered. Leaving any other way (a teleport, a staff move) burns the carried embers; the Town Portal is
refused inside. Logged out inside (or a crash or restart): the next login holds the character for 3 s (no damage, not
attackable), then puts it at the nearest safe exit with 10 s of protection; carried embers are kept. A login script that
moves the character out during the hold (the tutorial) burns nothing.

**Anti-farming** (as guild wars). A defeat counts only if killer and victim do not share an account or an IP, the
victim is level 150+ and at least 60% of the killer's level, entered at least 20 s before, and this killer has not had
a counted defeat of this victim in the last 30 minutes. A defeat that does not count gives nothing and its pile burns at
once (the victim still loses the carry: feeding embers to an alt is impossible).

**Factions.** A player pledges the Marches to one faction (window, outside the zone): at least Neutral with it, a change
after 24 h. Unpledged players fight but earn no reputation and cannot take the shrine. A counted defeat of a player
pledged to another faction gives the killer's faction 40 reputation (sworn rival, `factions_config.lua` `rival`) or 20
(the two others), same faction nothing, at most 400 a faction day from the Marches; the gain goes through
`ChaosFactions.gain` (source `pvpzone`: diminishing returns, the weekly cap, the rival's loss).

**The Cinder Shrine.** 15 minutes after the start (or the build) and then every 2 hours the Shrine Warden (a Demon,
health x9.6) rises next to the shrine; the realm's pledged players and everyone inside are told. While it lives the
shrine cannot be taken. After it falls, pledged players of one faction alone in the circle raise its progress by
100 / 60 per second (x1.25 per extra player, at most x2); two factions inside = contested (no change); a faction with
nobody inside loses 0.5 per second. The first to 100 takes the shrine; a contest not won within 20 minutes ends without
a holder. The holder's faction (every character pledged to it, in that realm, anywhere) gets +10% experience from
monsters and +10% loot rate for 60 minutes (`chaos_pvpzone_control`, kept over a restart). Staff: `/marches status |
contest | window <s> | hold <faction|> | embers <n> | testip on|off | nopz on|off | cooldown` (the test switches are memory
only).

**Rewards.** The vendor (banked embers): Orbs of Upheaval x3 (300, 5 a week), Awakening x2 (350, 5), Gilding x2 (350,
5), Fate x1 (500, 3), 50 great health / mana / spirit potions (80), 50 ultimate health potions (150), and three cosmetics
(source "pvp"): kill effect Marchfire (4,000), loot labels Scorched Earth (3,000), chat name Marchember (3,500). No gear,
nothing above PvE gear (tested). Weekly board "Scorched Marches" (embers banked, title Marchlord, the boards' orb
rewards). Achievements: Ash in Hand, Ember Hoarder (10,000 banked), Heavy Pockets (1,000 at one exit), Blood on the Ash,
Scourge of the Marches (100 counted defeats, title), Shrinebearer (in the circle at a capture).

**What the player has to do (O275).** The goal is told four ways, all in English and pt-BR. (1) The window opens with
"How it works", four numbered steps: pledge outside, enter and kill for embers (carry cap), carried embers are lost on a
defeat (the killer takes up to the per-pile cap), bank them by standing in a white safe-exit circle for 5 s (vendor
below). (2) On entering, two messages: "Goal: earn embers from monsters and rival players, then bank them at a safe exit
before you are defeated." and "Embers carried: N. Bank them at a safe exit (the white circles by the banners, marked on
your map) before you die." (also after a login inside). (3) The HUD has an objective line (client `PvpZoneView.goalLines`):
embers carried and the way to the nearest safe exit ("23 tiles north-east"), "hold still" while leaving, and during the
shrine event what to do at the shrine (slay the Warden, stand in the circle with your faction, only pledged players can
take it). (4) The `enter` message carries `marks` (every safe exit and the shrine); the client puts them on the minimap
as flags (`widget:addFlag`, as the Next Goals "where" buttons) and takes them off when the zone is left, at the game's end
and, after a crash, at the next start (the flags it put are remembered in the setting `pvpzoneFlags`). Floating text
(`ChaosCombatFx.label`, every 5 s while somebody is inside) hangs over the shrine ("Cinder Shrine", "Slay the Warden!"
while the Warden lives, "Take the Shrine!" while it can be taken) and over both exits ("Safe exit: bank your embers"),
with a fire effect on the shrine. Messages: "+N embers (carrying M)..." for every monster kill (the pile pickup message
existed), a defeat says the embers fell where you stood, that the killer may take them and in how many seconds the rest
burns out, banking says how many were banked and that the vendor is under Adventure > Scorched Marches. The POI marks of
`game_mapmarkers` were not used: they are a fixed set of kinds for the map's own places (new kinds would touch the shared
poi_core, art and tests); the flag is per client and per visit. Not verified in a client: the flag icon (index 0) and the
minimap's `removeFlag` signature (the client tries `removeFlag(pos)` and then `removeFlag(pos, icon, text)`).
**Fixed while there:** the vendor (`buy`) could be used from inside the zone, so 50 ultimate health potions could be
bought in the middle of a fight; it is refused inside now ("Leave the Marches to use the vendor."). Looked at and fine:
`enter` and `accept` are checked by the server (protection zone, level, cooldown, realm), `pledge` and `buy` keys are
checked against the config, the opcode is rate limited per action, carried embers are zeroed before the pile is made and
kept over a logout (no copy on a relog or a death), a pile of a defeat that does not count burns at once.

**Tests.** `tests/pvpzone_test.lua` (LuaJIT and Lua 5.3, 9796 checks): opcode and storages free, the layout (slots per
realm, clear of every other area, paths, fairness, spawn points; O275: every objective, arrival spot and shrine-circle
tile reachable from the entry with the cover included, a paved road from the entry to the shrine and to the other exit,
varied ground and border pieces, cover only on natural ground away from spawns and gates and lava only on cracks, cover
and decoration turned, lights at the shrine and in both yards, the same field on a second run and in every slot, a
solid block of cover still leaves the field connected; the goal messages, the marks, the floating text, the kill and
bank and defeat messages, no vendor inside), entry rules (Hardcore refused, the confirmation),
login hold and the exit channel, embers (caps, the pile, owner window, per-kill and daily caps, Self-Found, the own pile,
banking), anti-farming, reputation and the pledge, PvP scaling equal to the battleground's, the shrine contest, vendor,
cosmetics, board and achievements; then `pvpzone.lua` on a mocked engine (entering, protection, attack rules, secure mode
ignored, party allies, damage scaling, monster embers and multipliers, a defeat with its pile, the killer's share and the
third player's wait, same-IP and repeat defeats, banking with a hit restarting the channel, the vendor, login inside,
leaving by teleport, a walk-in, the contest, warden, capture and the faction-wide buffs). Client:
`game_pvpzone/pvpzoneview_test.lua`.

**Tested in game** (test server, cropped map, two clients from one IP with the multi-client block and the same-IP rule
switched off for the test, level 512 and 702 characters): the window and the entry confirmation, the pledge, entering
(instance built at startup, arrival next to a safe exit), the HUD, an attack on a player whose secure mode was on, a
defeat (the lethal hit cancelled, the victim back where he entered with the 90 s cooldown, "640 embers fell"), the
killer's pickup ("You take 640 embers"), banking at a safe exit (channel, then "640 embers banked"; Ash in Hand and Blood
on the Ash unlocked), a walk-in thrown out with the confirmation, a Hardcore character refused (season modes stubbed for
the screenshot), the contest (warden, capture by one Vigil player in ~60 s, "Vigil hold the shrine"), the holder kept
over a restart, a logout inside and the login at the nearest safe exit with the carry kept. Not in game: two factions
contesting, the faction buff on real experience and loot, map mode, a season instance, reputation gains (the test
characters shared an IP).

## Hunt tracker (`hunt.lua`, `hunt_core.lua`, `hunt_config.lua`, `hunt_supplies.lua`, `tools/gen_supply_prices.py`)

Client `game_hunt` (opcode 241), opened with Hunt > Hunt Tracker in the top menu. `Hunt > Hunt Tracker pause`, `Hunt > Hunt Tracker resume`
and `Hunt > Hunt Tracker reset` work from the chat too. Settings: `hunt_config.lua` (loaded as `Chaos.huntConfig`). No DB tables.

**Why not the base client's analyser.** The base client ships an analyser (`mods/game_analyser`, menu Hunt > Hunt
Analyser). Its loot, supply, damage and kill panes are fed by game-protocol messages (kill tracker, loot stats, supply
tracker, impact tracker) that a 10.98 server never sends, and it prices items with the client's own price list, not
the server's NPC prices. Only its experience pane works here. The Chaos window is fed by the server instead. The base
analyser is left as it is.

**What it shows.** The session time, with Pause / Resume and Reset. Experience gained, exp/h, the time to the next
level (the experience left is in the tooltip) and the kill count. Loot value and loot/h, supplies used and supplies/h,
profit (loot minus supplies) and profit/h, in green or red. Damage dealt and healing, as totals and per second. Four
tabs list kills per monster (count and share), looted items (icon, count, gold), supplies used, and Chaos drops (orbs,
uniques and items with a rarity, in the loot filter's rarity colours). Copy puts a text summary on the clipboard.

**How it counts (server side).** Sessions are kept in memory by character. A session starts at login (`autoStart`).
Its clock only runs while the character is online and the session is not paused. After a logout it is kept for
`keepOfflineMinutes` (30), so a relog continues the same session. A server restart clears it.
- Experience: an `onGainExperience` EventCallback at index 1000, after every bonus, so the number is what the character
  really gets. It reads the value and returns it unchanged.
- Kills: a `kill` CreatureEvent. The engine runs it for the last hit and for the most damage. Summons are not counted.
- Loot: the corpses the character owns, read in `onDropLoot` before (1.9) and after (2.4) the index-2 callbacks. For
  each item the larger count is kept, so items the auto seller sells and coins or keys added at index 2 both count.
  Items are valued at the NPC sell price (`sell_prices.lua`, highest price any NPC pays). Coins count at face value.
  `extraValues` can price items no NPC buys. Orbs count at 0 gold unless priced there.
- Supplies: every `thinkMs` (2 s), the potions, runes, ammunition and thrown weapons in the inventory are counted. If
  there are fewer than at the last count, the difference was used. Nothing is counted in a protection zone, so the
  depot, NPC trades and bank are not "used". The baseline is taken again after a pause or a login. Prices come from
  `hunt_supplies.lua`, generated by `python3 -I server/tools/gen_supply_prices.py <server>/data`: the lowest price an NPC
  asks per item. Runes are stackable in this protocol, so the price is per rune. The staff test NPCs are skipped.
- Damage: a `healthchange` event registered from `onTargetCombat` (index 60) on whatever the character or its summon
  attacks. It is capped at the target's remaining health, so overkill does not count.
- Healing: a `healthchange` event on the character itself, capped at the missing health (healing received).
- The client gets a state when the window opens and then every 2 s while it is open. It ticks the clock in between.

**Protocol** (JSON `{action, data}`): client -> server `open | close | get | pause | resume | reset`. Server -> client
`state {open?, t, p, xp, xph, lvl, left, ttl, lv, lvh, sv, svh, pf, pfh, dmg, dps, heal, hps, kc, k, l, s, x}`.
The lists are arrays to keep the message short (see `hunt_core.lua` `H.state`). Each list is capped (`maxKills`
40, `maxLoot` 60, `maxSupplies` 30, `maxSpecials` 40); the totals always count everything.

**Tested in game** (test server, a level 599 paladin, bow and arrows, Dragons, Dragon Lords, Cyclops, Trolls, Orc
Warriors and a treasure goblin):
- Experience: the tracker showed 652,994, the same as the character's experience minus the saved value at login.
- Supplies: 30 health potions, 30 runes and 43 arrows used, matching the inventory.
- Loot: after a reset, 8 corpses held 306 items worth 7,789 gold, the same as the tracker. The goblin's hoard added
  14 crystal coins, 3 platinum coins and two demon helmets (Rare, Mythic) at 40,000 each, plus 5 Orbs of Upheaval in the
  Chaos drops tab.
- Damage and healing counted, pause / resume / reset worked, and the session continued after a relog.
- `tests/hunt_test.lua` covers the clock (pause, offline, relog, reset), the counters, the corpse merge, used supplies,
  the level formula against the engine's, the rates and the state. The client's `game_hunt/huntmath_test.lua` covers
  the formatting.

**Limits.**
- Loot is what dropped in the corpses the character owns, not what it picked up. In a party, the corpse owner's
  session gets the loot.
- A supply that leaves the inventory outside a protection zone counts as used: thrown on the floor, traded, or put in
  a container on the ground.
- Damage done by a script hit that skips `onTargetCombat` is not counted. That was seen with a scripted kill of the
  goblin.
- Healing is healing received from any source, not healing done to others. Mana is not tracked.
- The rates include idle time while the session runs: pause it when you stop hunting.

## DPS meter and combat log (`combatlog.lua`, `combatlog_core.lua`, `combatlog_config.lua`, client `game_dpsmeter`)

Part of the Hunt Tracker family. Client `game_dpsmeter`, extended opcode 204 (`ChaosOpcodes.combatLog`), opened with
Hunt > DPS Meter or the Meter button of the Hunt Tracker. Settings: `combatlog_config.lua` (`Chaos.combatLogConfig`).
No DB tables, no storages. The pure logic is `combatlog_core.lua`, tested by `tests/combatlog_test.lua`.

**What it shows.** A compact panel over the game view. It can be moved by its strip, resized by its corner grip and
locked. It has a bar per source with its icon (the spell's own icon from the spell sheet, a rune's item, the buff bar's
icons for damage over time, our icons from `client/tools/gen_dpsmeter_icons.py` for the rest), total, per second and
share. Tabs: Damage, Healing, Taken (by attacker), Received (by healer). A dropdown picks the current fight, the
session or one of the last 10 fights; boss fights carry the boss's name. Party mode lists every party member's DPS / HPS
for the current fight or the session. The Combat Log window adds hits, crit rate, average, max and overhealing per
source and the split by element. Copy puts a summary on the clipboard. "To chat" puts one line into the chat input;
nothing is sent unless the player sends it. Shown, position, size, tab, party mode, sharing and lock are kept in the
client's g_settings node `chaosDpsMeter`.

**Attribution** (first match wins, `CL.classify`):
- **Proc.** `doTargetCombat` and `doAreaCombat` are wrapped once (a `/reload` wraps the original again). A call made by
  a script listed in `procLabels` labels every hit dealt inside it. The label comes from the first Lua frame that is not
  `data/global.lua`, so `doTargetCombatHealth` works too. Labels: Spell supports, Keystones, Trial nodes, Thorns (item
  modifier reflect), Legendary powers, Item elements (rarity element shares), Arrow splash, Bloodrage cleave, Thief
  strikes, Templar smite, Descent boons, Companion, Pet, Minions, Potions. A helper library (`necro_lib.lua`) and an
  unlisted file only count outside a cast. Calls from `data/spells/**` are never labelled.
- **Summon.** The attacker is a summon of the character: the summon's name.
- **Cast.** The spells supports' cast context (`ChaosSupportsSpell.cast()`): every wrapped spell, also in the addEvent
  callbacks it starts (pulses, cast-time spells). Otherwise the spell or rune between the engine's `onSpellPreCast` and
  `onSpellCast` (patch 0008, `ChaosSpellEvents`). A failed cast never reaches `onSpellCast`; the context is cleared one
  dispatcher tick later. A spell's own delayed hits outside every cast context are named with
  `ChaosCombatLog.asSpell(pid, spellId, fn, ...)`, checked first: the snares' scheduler (Snare Trap, Seeker Mine,
  Detonate Mines). It names the hits only; no supports, no cast. Names, words and rune ids come from
  `data/spells/spells.xml`.
- **Origin.** `ORIGIN_CONDITION`: damage over time by element (Bleeding, Burning, Poison, Electrified, Freezing, Dazzled,
  Cursed, Drowning). The condition owner is the attacker. `ORIGIN_MELEE`: the weapon in hand (sword, axe, club, fist; the
  Monk's fist weapons count as fist). `ORIGIN_RANGED`: distance. Origin 5 (`ORIGIN_WAND`, no Lua constant): wand.
- Anything else is **Other** (healing: **Other healing**).
- **Taken.** By attacker: the monster's or player's name; no attacker (fields, traps) is "Environment". Plus the split by
  element. Damage a mana shield takes counts too (a `manachange` event; mana drain does not).
- **Healing.** Done by the healer's source, received by healer (own heals by their spell). Healing counts up to the
  missing health; the rest is overhealing.
- Damage counts up to the target's health, so overkill does not count.

**What cannot be attributed.**
- Hits dealt with `ORIGIN_NONE` run no health events in the engine. The wrapper measures the target's health before
  and after such a `doTargetCombat` instead (rarity element shares, pets, companion hits). It cannot do this for
  `doAreaCombat` with `ORIGIN_NONE` or for engine-internal ones.
- The wrapper passes the optional arguments on exactly as the caller gave them. Fixed 2026-10-12: it passed an origin
  the caller left out as an explicit nil, which the engine reads as 0 (`ORIGIN_NONE`) where a missing one is
  `ORIGIN_SPELL`; so from 2026-10-10 every `ChaosSpell.damageTarget` / `healTarget` hit (Forked Storm, Final Verdict,
  Hail of Dawn, Blessed Earth, Feral Command, both Consecrations, Purging Nova, Life Siphon, Umbral Stride and every
  Chaos heal that uses the helper) ran no health events: no tree bonus, class factor, keystone, Weaver's Grace or PvP
  healing reduction. `tests/combatlog_test.lua` checks the argument count; the balance effect is in
  `data/spells/README.md` "The combat log wrapper and the balance".
- Life and mana leech, regeneration conditions and `addHealth` heals run no events: not counted.
- Damage over time cannot be traced to the spell that applied it. It is listed by element.
- Hits of spells the supports do not wrap, when they come later from an addEvent, are "Other".
- A proc script that kept its own copy of `doTargetCombat` from before the wrap is "Other". None of the listed ones does.
- The amounts are what the health events see at this script's place in the chain. Handlers registered later on the
  same creature can still change a hit.

**Fights.** A fight starts with the first damage dealt or taken. It ends `idleMs` (6 s) after the last one. Healing
alone does not start or extend a fight, nor does damage taken from no attacker. A fight is named by its boss
