(`MonsterType:isBoss()`, the boss points list, the world bosses, the boss tier, `extraBosses`). Otherwise it is named by
its most damaged target and "+N" others, or by its main attacker. A fight shorter than `minFightMs` (1 s) counts as 1 s.
The last `keepFights` (10) fights are kept per character. The session follows the hunt session: a Hunt Tracker reset
starts it over (one hunk in `hunt.lua` `act`). It does not count while the hunt is paused. Its per second is over its
combat time (the sum of its fights). "Reset the meter" in the panel menu clears fights and session. Numbers are kept in
memory by character for `keepOfflineMinutes` (30) after a logout, not over a restart.

**Overhead.** A hit costs one Lua call (the health event) and one row update in a per-character buffer. The buffer is
folded into the fight and the session once per tick (`tickMs`, 1 s). Rows per tab and segment are bounded (`maxRows`
40, the rest goes to "Other"). Targets per fight (`maxTargets` 16), the buffer and the source cache (`maxSourceCache`)
are bounded too. An open meter gets a state at most every `pushMs` (1 s), and only when something changed. The state goes
through `Chaos.sendChunked`; 25 rows per tab are sent. The benchmark in `tests/combatlog_test.lua` runs 20 characters x 10
hits/s for 10 minutes (132,000 hits), a tick per character per second and a state per character per second. LuaJIT:
0.08 us per hit in the core, about 1.1 us per hit through the engine glue (mocked getters), 0.3 us per tick, 7 us per
state. That is about 0.4 ms of CPU per second, 0.04% of one core. Lua 5.3: 0.4 / 2.8 / 2 / 17 us, about 1 ms per second.
The engine's own cost per call into Lua is not in these numbers.

**Privacy.** Party mode shows totals only, never a breakdown. It lists members of the same party, of the same season
realm (`ChaosSeason.realmOf` while a season runs), who share. "Share my totals with my party" in the panel menu; the
default is `shareByDefault` (on). The viewer always sees itself.

**Protocol** (JSON `{action, data}`; server -> client through `Chaos.sendChunked`). Client -> server: `open {seg, party,
share}`, `close`, `seg {id}` ("c" current or last fight, "s" session, a fight id), `party {on}`, `share {on}`, `reset`.
Server -> client: `state {sel, segs, v, live, share, party?}`. `segs` = `[[id, label, dur, damage, healing, taken, live,
boss, received]]`. `v` = `{id, label, dur, live, boss, t = [damage, healing, taken, received]}`, each tab `{tot, ov,
el = {element = amount}, r = [[key, kind, name, icon, total, hits, crits, max, over]]}`. `party` = `[{n, self, fd, fh,
ft, fdur, live, sd, sh, st, sdur}]`. Requests are rate limited (150 ms).

**Tests.** `tests/combatlog_test.lua` (LuaJIT and Lua 5.3, 237 checks). It covers the spells.xml index, the attribution
order, buffer and fights, idle end, boss and target labels, the last 10, the bounds, the session with hunt pause and
reset, views, party brief and sweep. Against a mocked engine it covers weapons, damage over time, summons, precast and
supports contexts, delayed spell hits named by `CL.asSpell`, a failed cast, runes, procs labelled by file (through
`pcall`, `doTargetCombatHealth` and `doAreaCombat`), helper libraries, `ORIGIN_NONE` hits measured, thorns, damage
taken, mana shield, overkill, bosses, healing done / received / overhealing, potions, the opcode actions, party with
realms and sharing, pushes only on change and logout. It ends with the benchmark. Client: `game_dpsmeter/dpsmath_test.lua`.

**Tested in game** (test server copy, a level 584 Mystic and a level 512 Deadeye in a party). The fight against Pyrevorn
was labelled "Pyrevorn". Rows: Greater Arc Bolt, Supreme Arc Bolt, Supreme Frostbite, Reaper's Rune (its item icon),
fist attacks. A spell on a fire-immune Dragon Lord counted nothing, as it dealt nothing. Healing (Grand Mending) showed
in Healing and Received. Taken by Dragon / Pyrevorn / Environment (fire fields). Party mode showed both members. The
Combat Log window, the dropdown, To chat (the line in the chat input) and the Hunt Tracker's Meter button were checked.
Not in game: summons, support, keystone and item-power procs, pets, and a season realm split in a party.

## Death recap (`deathrecap.lua`, `deathrecap_core.lua`, `deathrecap_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_death_recaps.sql`, client `game_deathrecap`)

Client `game_deathrecap`, extended opcode 154 (`ChaosOpcodes.deathRecap`), Hunt > Death Recap (added with
`ChaosTopBar.addEntry`). Settings: `deathrecap_config.lua` (`Chaos.deathRecapConfig`). Table `chaos_death_recaps`
(`Chaos.tables.deathRecaps`), created at startup when missing and in `sql/chaos_death_recaps.sql`. No player storages:
the block 7101830 - 7101839 offered for it stays free. The pure logic is `deathrecap_core.lua`, tested by
`tests/deathrecap_test.lua`.

Self hits (O159): a mana potion is `doTargetCombat(player, who, COMBAT_MANADRAIN, +v)`, a restore. The combat log feeds the recap
only a negative (draining) mana change, and `R.onTaken` drops a manadrain or healing hit the character dealt itself, so
"Yourself" never lists a potion or a mana cost. Pay mana costs with `player:addMana(-x)`, never through combat.

**What it shows.** After a death the window opens by itself. It names the killer and the killing blow (attacker,
amount, element, critical). It lists every attacker of the last seconds with its look (`UICreature`), total damage,
share, health and mana part, hits, crit rate, max hit and the split by element. A bar shows the elements of all damage
taken. Under it are the time window, the number of hits and the last 6 hits. The header has the time, the level, the
mode (instance label) and PvP. It also shows the experience and levels lost. The left column lists the character's last
5 deaths; a click opens one. "Open after a death" (g_settings node `chaosDeathRecap`) turns the auto-open off.

**Where the hits come from.** No second damage hook: `combatlog.lua` calls `ChaosCombatLog.takenHook` for every hit a
character takes, with the same attribution as the meter's Taken tab. The hook gets the part a mana shield took
(`mana = true`) and mana drain (`"manadrain"`, which the meter itself does not count). The recap keeps a rolling log per
online character: a ring of `maxHits` (60) hits, and only hits within `windowMs` (20 s) of the death are shown. The log
is dropped at death, at a mode defeat, at login and at logout. With the combat log off (`combatlog_config.lua`
`enabled = false`) the log stays empty and a recap only names the killer.

**When a recap is made.**
- **A death** (`onDeath` of the character): rifts, dungeons, the tower, PvP, Hardcore season characters and every other
  real death. The recap is stored at once (`seen = 0`). The engine takes the experience after `onDeath`, so at the next
  login (`loginDelayMs`, 1.5 s after it) the experience and levels lost are filled in from the character as it logs in,
  the row is marked seen and the client opens it. A row older than `autoOpenMaxAgeSeconds` (7 days) is only listed.
- **A mode defeat.** The arena, the battleground, the Marches, the raid, the Ember Descent, the guild boss, Ascended
  Omens, trials and the Trial of Ascension cancel the lethal hit in their `onPrepareDeath`. The recap's own
  `onPrepareDeath` runs before theirs and never cancels. It notes the hit when the character stands in a
  `Chaos.registerInstance` instance. `defeatCheckMs` (100 ms) later, a character still alive gets the recap at once: the
  instance's label is the mode, nothing is lost, and the row is stored as seen. A cancelled hit outside every instance
  (the Hardcore protection) is no death.
- `hideModes` lists instance keys whose deaths and defeats get no recap on purpose. It is empty: every mode shows it.
- **Order of the prepare-death events.** The engine runs login events by name, so `ChaosDeathRecapLogin` registers the
  recap's prepare event before the Marches' (`ChaosMarchesLogin`). The other modes register theirs when a run starts.

**Killing blow.** The last health hit of the log (a mana shield hit cannot kill). When the engine's killer is another
attacker, or that hit is more than `killerGapMs` (1.5 s) before the death, the killer is named without an amount. That
happens when the lethal hit ran no health event (a script's `doTargetCombatHealth` with `ORIGIN_NONE`).

**Privacy.** Names are the ones the victim saw. A staff character in ghost mode the victim could not see
(`canSeeCreature`) is `hiddenName` ("Unseen attacker"), also as the master of a summon. Its look is not sent and it does
not mark the death as PvP. A character only reads its own rows (`player_id` = its guid in every query).

**Bounds.** Names are cut to `nameMax` (40). At most `maxAttackers` (8) rows; the rest are summed into "Others". One
recap is cut to `maxRecapBytes` (5000) of JSON: rows from the bottom into "Others", then the timeline. The history
message (5 summaries and the newest recap) stays under 8192 bytes and still goes through `Chaos.sendChunked`. Five rows
per character (`keep`); the older ones are deleted after each insert. Requests are rate limited (`rateLimitMs`, 300 ms).

**Protocol** (JSON `{action, data}`). Client -> server: `open {id?}`, `get {id}`. Server -> client: `history {list, sel,
recap}` and `recap {id, recap, auto}` (`auto`: open by itself). A summary: `{id, at, k (killer), kind, lvl, xl, ll, mode,
pvp, tot, real}`. A recap: `{v, at, real (1 death, 0 defeat), mode, mk, lvl, exp, xl, ll, kb = {n, kind, m, el, a, c, mp},
dur, win, tot, hp, mp, el, pvp, nh, att = [{n, kind, m, look, tot, hp, mp, h, c, x, el}], last = [{dt, n, el, a, c, mp}]}`.
Kinds: `c` monster, `u` player, `s` the character itself, `e` environment, `h` hidden, `o` others.

**Edits to shared files.** `chaos_constants.lua` (`ChaosOpcodes.deathRecap = 154`, `Chaos.tables.deathRecaps`).
`combatlog.lua`: three hunks (`dealt` passes the mana flag and calls `CL.takenHook`; the mana event passes `true` and
feeds mana drain to the hook).

**Tests.** `tests/deathrecap_test.lua` (LuaJIT and Lua 5.3, 328 checks): the opcode collision check (reference server,
base client `ExtendedIds`, every `ChaosOpcodes`, no client module on 154), the ring (order, count, age, a lowered cap),
looks, the recap math (totals, health and mana, elements, killing blow, engine killer after a gap, window, timeline,
"Others", PvP with a player or a player's summon), the payload bound with a real JSON encoder, the experience lost, the
history of 5, the SQL. Against a mocked engine: the hook, a death, the row, the login that fills the loss and opens it,
an arena defeat, a real death in an instance, a cancelled hit outside one, a hidden mode, 5 rows kept per character, the
window's `open` / `get`, another character's id refused, bad input. Client: `game_deathrecap/deathrecaplogic_test.lua`.

**Tested in game** (test server copy on the cropped map, two Linux clients, the engine without patches 0028-0030). A
death to rats on the tutorial island; at the next login the window opened with 44.7M experience and 5 levels lost. A
death to a Dragon, a player (Velka Dusk) and her War Wolf with a mana drain: three rows with their looks, health 1.95k
and mana 150, Fire / Physical / Energy / Mana drain, PvP, the killing blow 980 fire. A defeat in a test instance that
cancels the death like the arena: the window opened at once ("Defeated by", the mode, nothing lost). The same with the
attacker in ghost mode: "Unseen attacker", no name in the row. The history list (older recaps opened), the Hunt menu
entry, "Open after a death" off (no window), 5 rows kept. Not in game: the real arena, battleground and other modes,
Hardcore, a mana shield.

## Loot filter, loot channel, loot beams and loot rays (`lootfilter.lua`, `lootfilter_core.lua`, `lootfilter_config.lua`, client `game_lootfilter`)

Extended opcode 238 (`ChaosOpcodes.lootfilter`), Hunt > Loot Filter (or Hunt > Loot Filter) opens the window; Hunt > Loot Filter applies a preset.

**How rarity reaches the client.** It does not, natively. The base server stores rarity as the item custom attribute
`rarity` (stored ids 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 10 = Common .. Divine, old ids 6-9 and 11-15 map to 5 and 10, see "Item rarities"; rolled in `eventcallbacks/monster/default_onDropLoot.lua` and by the Chaos loot
layer); uniques carry `chaos_unique`. `NetworkMessage::addItem` sends only the client id, count and fluid, so a container
item in the client has no rarity. `game_itemrarity` reads a `[NAME]` tag out of `item:getTooltip()`, but the server never
fills that tooltip string (the 10.98 packets have no description field; the hover tooltip is a separate 0x9F/0x9E request
used by `game_itemtooltip`), and its table is id-keyed with the server's aliases now (seven rarities). So the filter asks the server: on
every container open/change the client sends `peek {cid}` and the server answers the rarity, unique flag, orb flag and
category of each slot of that container (`player:getContainerById`), and the item's Chaos modifiers as one line (`x`,
"Item modifiers"; also in the kill rows, shown in the loot channel tooltip). `game_itemrarity` / `game_itemtooltip` are
not changed.

**Rules** (`lootfilter_core.lua`, mirrored for drawing in the client's `lootfilterlogic.lua`):
- *Glow on gear from* rarity X (0 = off): equipment with rarity >= X gets a glow in its rarity colour. Uniques (orange) and
  orbs (teal) always glow.
- *Dim gear below* rarity Y (0 = off): equipment with a lower rarity (rarity 0 = no rarity) is dimmed. Dimming only, items are
  never hidden (hiding would shift container slot indexes); dimmed items stay lootable.
- *Show* per category (equipment, currency = orbs and coins, supplies = potions/runes/food, other): a category switched
  off is dimmed (gear at or above the glow line still glows).
- Items with a rarity that do not glow get a thin frame in their colour. Corpses dim; other containers only glow/frame.
- *Rare-drop message*: every glowing item (not orbs) gives a coloured line `Rare drop: [Legendary] Dawnforged Helmet`
  (`Unique drop: [Unique] ...`) over the map. TFS text messages have no colour, so these go through the opcode.
- *Rarity Autoloot* (store unlock, see below): *leave list gear below* Z keeps autoloot-list equipment of a lower rarity in
  the corpse; *also pick up gear from* W autoloots equipment with rarity >= W, and uniques, even when they are not on the
  autoloot list. Uniques, orbs and coins are never held back.
- Presets: *Show all* (Magic+ glows, nothing dimmed), *Hunter* (Rare+ glows, Common and plain gear dimmed, picks up Rare+),
  *Strict* (Legendary+ glows, gear below Rare dimmed, supplies and other dimmed, leaves list gear below Rare, picks up Legendary+).
  Thresholds are stored as stored ids (1-5, 10); a saved old id is clamped on read.
  Presets keep the two display options (icons, rare-drop message).
- Settings live in one storage value per character, `Chaos.storage.lootFilter` (7100500), packed by `F.pack`; the client
  mirrors them (pushed after login and asked for with `sync` at game start).

**onDropLoot order** (lower index first): -1 the kill's loot line opens (`lootline.lua`), 0 stock loot + "Loot of" text
(held back), 1 Chaos loot layer, **1.9 settle** (the loot line reads the corpse, "One loot line per kill"), 2 auto seller,
**2.5 snapshot** (the corpse contents for the loot channel; list items below the Rarity Autoloot minimum are moved into a
bag on the corpse tile for the rest of the chain), 2.7 store pouches ("Store pouches"), 3 base autoloot, **3.5 rarity
pickup**, **4.5 finish** (the held items go back into the corpse, the bag is removed, the loot row, rare-drop lines and rays start),
99 empty corpse check, **100** the kill's one loot line is sent ("One loot line per kill").

**One loot line per kill** (`lootline.lua`, `lootline_core.lua`, `tests/lootline_test.lua`; playtest 2026-10-16: a kill
printed "Loot of ...", "Chaos bonus loot of ..." and "Looted: ..."). At index -1 a record opens for the corpse owner;
while it is open the stock "Loot of ..." line (MESSAGE_LOOT to the owner, or `broadcastPartyLoot`) is held back
(`Player.sendTextMessage` and `Party.broadcastPartyLoot` are wrapped once; any other message passes). The Chaos loot
layer adds its bonus items (`ChaosLootLine.addBonus`) and the store pouches their line (`ChaosLootLine.addPouch`); at
index 100 one line is sent: "Loot of a dragon: 120 gold coins, a dragon ham, 2 ember shards, {Ashbringer}. Looted: 120
gold coins, {Ashbringer} (2 to your backpack)." The bonus items join the stock list ("nothing" is replaced by them),
uniques and rare pouch items keep their `{}` highlight, and the pouch part (with the Loot Bag notes) is the owner's: in a
party the other members get the line without it. The line still starts with "Loot of": the client's loot colouring and
short numbers (`client_chaos_numbers`) read loot messages by their mode, and the loot channel, the hunt tracker and the
Loot Filter get their data by opcode, not from this text. Each recipient reads the fixed parts in their language
(`Chaos.t`: "Loot of %s: %s", "nothing", "Looted: %s", the pouch notes such as "%d to your backpack"; pt-BR in
`i18n_strings.lua`, e.g. "Loot de a dragon: 120 gold coins. Coletado: ... (2 para sua mochila)."); item and monster
names stay as the engine gives them. The client's loot colouring keys on the message mode and the `{}` marks, not on the
words, so the translated prefix keeps it. Without `lootline.lua` each part sends its own line as before.
Rarity of stock items: the stock callback (index 0) writes its line with the rarity it rolled ("[Common] fire sword"),
and the Chaos loot layer (index 1) may raise that rarity afterwards. The raise goes to the record
(`ChaosLootLine.addUpgrade`: item name, old and new rarity name), and at the flush `K.annotate` rewrites that stock entry
to the final rarity (no second "[Rare] fire sword" entry) and wraps every stock entry from `lootLine.flagRarity` (3,
Magic; `pouches_config.lua`) on in `{}`, as the bonus items and the pouch part are: "Loot of a dragon: 120 gold coins,
{[Rare] fire sword}, [Uncommon] plate armor." A raise with no matching entry is listed as a bonus item. Without
`lootline.lua` the bonus line lists the raise with the same `{}` rule.
**The list is the corpse** (beta report 2026-10-21, Nightfang Widow and Shadowcrystal Widow: "it says it drops X items, but
neither the Loot tab nor the bag gets even half"; `tests/lootline_corpse_test.lua`). The stock line is written at index 0,
from the corpse the stock pass filled, and the Chaos loot layer (index 1) then took items out again: the pack thinning of
"Pack combat (pace)" (`L.thinCorpse`; for these two base monsters, bounty pool levels 509 and 480, hunting level 1018 and 960:
about 24% of the items stay and about 7% of the coins and NPC-sellable items), arrows and throwing weapons, the waystones of
low monsters; smart loot swaps a gear item for another. The held stock list still named every item, so the line said about
four times what the corpse, the loot channel row (snapshot at 2.5) and the autoloot got. The display scale ("inflação de
números") is not involved: the engine scales only the damage and heal message types (src-patch 0037) and no Lua site
scales a loot field (checked by the same test). Now `lootline.lua` reads the corpse at **index 1.9** (`settleIndex`: after
the loot layer, Echoing Spoils 1.5 and the dungeon difficulty loot 1.7, before the auto seller 2) and the line lists exactly
those items (`K.describe`: "100 gold coins", "a great mana potion", "[Uncommon] knight armor", `{}` from Magic on, a unique
`{Ashbringer}`, "Veiled" on a veiled item; one id with the same rarity is one entry with its counts added; the items of a bag
in the corpse too). The stock list, the bonus items and the rarity raises are not added again (they are in the corpse); an
empty corpse says "nothing" (low stamina keeps "nothing (due to low stamina)"). What leaves the corpse after 1.9 says so
itself: the auto seller ("Auto seller: sold ..."), the autoloot gold to the bank, the pet's fetch, the pouches and the Loot
Bag (the "Looted: ..." part, with "N left in the corpse, no room"), the Rarity Autoloot ("no room or capacity, left in the
corpse"). The gold finds (item modifiers, paragon, pet, blessing, index 2) add coins after the line. Without the settle step
(a corpse that is not a container) the line is built as before.
The loot layer's own adds (`L.addToCorpse`): the engine's `Container:addItem` cuts a stackable count to 100, so an extra
roll of 270 gold said "270x gold coin" and put 100 in; a larger count now goes in stacks of 100 and the text says what
arrived. A corpse that is full refused the item (an extra roll, an orb, a gem or a unique was gone without a word); it now
goes in past the corpse's size (`FLAG_NOLIMIT`, as Echoing Spoils and the dungeon loot do), so the line, the loot channel
and the autoloot see it.
Every step is in `pcall` and returns nothing, so the chain never stops. `autoloot.lua` and `autosell.lua` are unchanged; the
auto seller still sells first (sold items never show in the row; checked in game: "Auto seller: sold ..."). The rarity pickup
puts what it takes into the backpack; with no room it stays in the corpse (the retired Bottomless Loot Pouch used to send it to
the stash or inbox).
Treasure goblins add their hoard in their death event, which the engine runs before `dropLoot`, so the snapshot sees it
(rays included; the old `ChaosLootRays.beam` hook in `treasure_goblin.lua` was removed).

**Keystone rows (O255).** A keystone shows as its own row, "Keystone: Name", instead of the shared "Keystones" row. One central
hook does it: `keystone_labels_config.lua` lists the flags (name, tab, kind) and `keystone_labels.lua` gives the keystone scripts two
calls, `ChaosKeystoneLabels.run(flag, fn, ...)` (the hits `fn` deals count under the keystone) and `note(player, flag, amount)`.
`combatlog.lua` plugs in as the sink; without it, or with the meter off, both are plain calls. Kind `p` rows are real damage or
healing and add to the totals. Kind `k` rows are notes (a damage factor such as Deadeye, damage not taken such as Immovable, a
count such as Hundred Hands): they are drawn in violet, never add to the totals, sort after the real sources (at most
`maxNotesSent`, 10, of them) and are dropped, not merged into "Other", when the table is full. Row count and payload limits are
unchanged (`maxRows` 40, `maxRowsSent` 25; `Chaos.sendChunked` over 8192 bytes). Tests: `tests/keystone_labels_test.lua`,
`tests/combatlog_test.lua`, `tests/passivetree_keystones_test.lua`. Not labelled yet (no single hook): Pack Alpha, Inspiring
Illusion, Grave Covenant, Blackblood Creed, Living Shadow, Way of the Blade, Hoarded Souls, Bone Colossus, Flowing Mercy,
Bastion, Iron Tithe; and four flags without a visible effect (`observe = false` in the config).

### Loot channel (icons, click to loot)
- On each kill the corpse owner gets `kill {k, m, look, p, items = [{n, id, c, r, u, o, g, nm, left}], drops}`; an empty
  corpse sends `items = {}` (a row, nothing tracked). `look` is the monster's outfit as it died (`F.look`: `getOutfit()`, so
  rift looks and tier shaders, else its type's; item looks as `auxType`, no mount, the shader by name from
  `data/XML/shaders.xml`). The client opens the console's **Loot** tab and lays a panel over that tab's text while it is
  selected: one row per kill, icons only, no text: the monster icon (hover: name and kill time; an empty corpse gets a small
  mark) and the item icons (count, rarity glow / frame / dim, hover: name, rarity and how to loot). The rare-drop lines go over
  the map only. Uncheck "Loot tab shows item icons" to get the plain text back. The last 50 rows are kept (`historySize`,
  client `MAX_ROWS`). Checked in game: normal, tiered (shader drawn on the icon), a rift look (2102, 2106), empty corpses,
  a unique, click and Shift+click looting.
- The corpse gets the custom attribute `lf_kill = <kill id>` so it can be found again on its tile (it survives
  container-to-container decay stages). Entries are matched to corpse items by `id:rarity:unique name`
  (`F.signature`, `F.reconcile`); identical items are interchangeable.
- Click = loot all of that entry, Shift+click = one of a stack. `take {k, n, id, one}`: the server checks the kill belongs to
  the player, the corpse still exists and holds a matching item, the player may open it (owner or a party member of the
  owner, the engine's `canOpenCorpse` rule), same floor, within 7x5 squares (`reach`) and in clear sight (a corpse next to the player always). The item goes into the backpack
  and the bags inside it (capacity checked; never into an equipment slot), or first into a carried store pouch that collects
  that kind of item (`ChaosPouches.stow`), else it is refused ("You do not have enough capacity or room.", shown over the map; a split stack goes back).
- Greying: `update {k, left}` after autoloot (in the same drop), after a click, after any player move out of the corpse
  (`EventCallback.onItemMoved`, index 11), and from a 1 s timer while rays run / every 5 s otherwise; `decay {k}` when the
  corpse is gone (all icons of the row grey with a check mark). Records are dropped on logout, when nothing is left or the
  corpse decayed.

### Rarity Autoloot (store unlock)
Store -> Convenience -> "Rarity Autoloot", 300 Chaos Coins, `kind = "unlock"`, `unlock = "rarityAutoloot"`, storage
`Chaos.storage.shopRarityAutoloot` (7100106), handled by `S.unlocks` in `shop_services.lua`. Without it the two Rarity
Autoloot selectors are greyed in the window with a store hint and the server ignores them (`F.autoloot` returns nil);
glow, dim, rare-drop lines, rays and the loot channel are free. Checked in game: before buying, an Exotic sword off the list
stayed in the corpse; after buying (Strict) it was picked up and a Common list sword stayed.

### Loot beams
- Owner request: the old rays (below) read as a red splash over the corpse that covered the next tiles and the
  creatures on them. Now the client draws a thin light pillar with a glow pool (client `game_lootbeams`, base patch
  0069; client/MANIFEST.md). The server only says which items in a tracked corpse may beam: `beam {k, p = [x, y, z],
  i = [{r, u, o, pw, g, t}]}` on opcode 238, the entries still inside with `F.beamCandidate` (base rarity >=
  `beamMinRarity` (1), uniques (`beamUniques`), legendary powers, orbs (`beamOrbs`; the client shows them only with its
  orb option)). The client picks the best one its loot filter makes glow and colours the pillar by tier.
- Since pair 36 (2026-10-22, owner: "Use as spells, level up e loot beams") the client draws the beam as the animated
  loot beam effect of the purchased beam pack, one per colour group (effects 4090-4101, `beam_*` of
  `data/lib/chaos_pack36_fx_ids.lua`; client/MANIFEST.md "game_lootbeams"). The server messages did not change.
- Sent when the kill is recorded (`finish`) and again whenever that list changes (`refresh`: an item taken by hand,
  by click-to-loot, by autoloot or by a party member); `i = []` when the corpse is looted empty, decays, leaves the
  history (`historySize`) or its owner logs out (`stopTracking` / `beamOff`). Recipients: the owner and the party
  members at the kill (the players allowed to loot it), wherever they are; the client draws only what is on screen.
  Decay is seen by the sweep's decay check (every `decayCheckEvery` seconds); looting at once (`onItemMoved`).
- `beams = false` stops the messages. Tests: `server/tests/lootfilter_test.lua` (candidates, the list after looting).

### Loot rays (off: `rayEffects = false`)
- With `rayEffects = true` (for a client without `game_lootbeams`), a beam effect rises from the corpse tile while a
  qualifying item is still in it: uniques (`rayUniques = true`, orange beam
  `loot_ray_unique`) and items of rarity >= `rayMinRarity` (5 = Legendary): Legendary gold, Divine white-blue (`rayBands`; the red and violet
  beams of the old Mythic and Cosmic bands stay in `chaos_fx.lua`, unused). One beam per corpse: a unique
  wins, else the highest rarity left. Rare and below never get one.
- Resent every `rayIntervalMs` (1000; the effect is 900 ms) for at most `rayDurationS` (60) and stops as soon as the item
  leaves the corpse or the corpse decays (same tracking as the loot channel; checked in game: orange -> red after looting
  the unique, nothing after looting the last one).
- Visible to the looters only (`rayVisibleTo = "looters"`: the corpse owner and their party on the same floor nearby);
  `"all"` shows it to everyone who sees the tile.
- Art: effects 424..428 (`loot_ray_*`), style `lootbeam` in `client/tools/sprites/gen_effects.py` (a 2x2 single effect: a
  thin bright core, a soft halo, a ground flare and rising motes, 91 % of every frame transparent). Rebuild the client pair as
  in `data/spells/README_FX.md`; `data/lib/chaos_fx.lua` and `effects_catalog.csv` are regenerated. Without the new dat the
  ids show nothing (the server does not check).

### Rule counters and sounds
- **Rules** (`F.RULES`, the reasons an item glows, in this priority order): *Uniques*, *Legendary powers* (not on a
  unique), *Rarity glow* (gear at or above "Glow on gear from"; off when that is Off), *Modifier tier* (gear with a
  modifier of the "Glow on a modifier" tier or better; off when Off), *Orbs*. An item can match several rules (a Legendary
  with a power counts for both); a unique counts only as a unique. Counts are items: a stack of 3 orbs adds 3.
- **Counters.** In `finish` (4.5) the server counts what the kill dropped (the snapshot at 2.5, so also what the base
  autoloot or the Rarity Autoloot took; what the auto seller sold at 2 is not counted) with `F.countHits`, per rule:
  *session* (in memory per character, cleared at login and logout, survives `/reload scripts`) and *total* (player
  storages 7100502 - 7100506, `totalStorageBase` + rule index, capped at 2,000,000,000). The kill message carries
  `hits {rule = items}` and `counts {session, total}` when a rule matched.
- **Reset**: `reset {scope = session | total | all, rule}`: the window's *Reset session*, *Reset totals* (with a
  confirmation) and the x of a rule (both counters of that rule); the server answers `counts`.
- **Sounds.** Per rule one of five alert sounds or none (Chime, Bell, Ping, Drum, Fanfare), a volume (0 - 100 %) and *Mute
  all*, saved per character (the filter is per character) in storage 7100501 (`F.packSound`: 3 bits per rule, volume,
  mute, the hunt tracker flag). Defaults: Uniques Fanfare, Legendary powers Chime, the rest none, 70 %. A kill plays one
  sound: the first rule in priority order that matched and has a sound (`F.pickSound`, mirrored by the client's
  `LootFilterLogic.pickSound`), on the client's Effect sound channel (`g_sounds`). The sounds are our own: synthesised
  sine waves and noise, `client/tools/gen_lootfilter_sounds.py` -> `game_lootfilter/sounds/*.ogg` (no recorded or base
  client audio). The client must be built with its sound framework (client base-patch 0032, `FRAMEWORK_SOUND` ON); a
  client without it logs one warning and stays silent.
- **Hunt tracker.** *Show the counters in the Hunt Tracker* (default on) lists every rule with its session count (total
  in the tooltip) at the top of Hunt Tracker > Chaos Drops.
- Protocol additions on 238: `sound {s = {rules = {rule = sound id}, vol, mute, hunt}}`, `reset {scope, rule}`; the
  `settings` message carries `snd`, `rules`, `sounds` and `counts`.

**Tests:** `server/tests/lootfilter_test.lua` (packing, sanitizing, presets, glow/dim rules, Rarity Autoloot decisions,
ray choice with the real config, reconcile, reach, labels, drop lines; the rule hits and counts, the sound settings
packing and clamping, the sound pick, the reset plans, the storages inside the reserved range) and the client's
`game_lootfilter/lootfilter_test.lua`. Checked in game on the test server: glow / frame / dim in a corpse window and in the
loot channel, presets, the setting surviving a relog, click to loot (all, Shift = one, refused with a full backpack),
autoloot greying icons, decay greying a row, the store purchase, Rarity Autoloot hold-back and pickup, the rays of every band.
Rule counters and sounds (test server, a client built with base patch 0032): a kill with a unique, a Legendary with a
power, an Epic, 3 orbs and plain items counted Uniques 1, Legendary powers 1, Rarity glow 2, Orbs 3 in the window;
sounds and volume changed in the window, kept over a relog (session back to 0, totals kept); the next kill picked Bell
at 50% for the rarity rule and a unique Fanfare (`g_sounds` returned a playing source; every one of the five files
loads); Mute all: counted, no sound; reset of one rule, Reset totals with its confirmation; the counters in the Hunt
Tracker's Chaos Drops tab. The container has no sound card: the client ran with `ALSOFT_DRIVERS=null` (client/LINUX.md),
so nothing was heard; the base build without the sound framework logs one warning and stays silent.
**Not verified:** party members looting (rows and rays go to the corpse owner only; party members can click-loot only
corpses of their own kills), corpses moved by a player (the row greys as decayed), many players at once.

## Ground loot labels (`groundloot.lua`, `groundloot_core.lua`, client `game_groundlabels`)

ARPG-style name plates over the loot on the ground. The client sees the items on the tiles around it (ids, counts
and the item custom attributes of engine patch 0003: rarity, unique, per-item id) but not their names, categories or
decay, so it asks extended opcode 230 (`ChaosOpcodes.groundLoot`) about the tiles whose items changed and draws the labels
itself by the loot filter's rules (`game_lootfilter`, the same settings the server keeps for the corpse highlights).

- **Protocol** (JSON `{action, data}`): `look {t = [[x, y, z], ...]}` (at most 30 tiles) -> `tiles {t = [{p, i}]}` where
  every asked tile is answered (`i` may be empty) with an item row `{s, id, c, nm, r, u, o, pw, g, t, il, e}` (`s` its index
  on the tile, `id` the client id, the rest as the loot filter's `itemInfo`, `e` the seconds until it decays) or a corpse
  row `{s, id, k = 1, n, i = [{c, nm, r, u, o, pw, g, t}], e}`; `tip {p, s, id}` -> `tip {p, s, id, tip | gone}` (the
  rich tooltip `item_tooltip_core.lua` builds); `raise {p, s, id, c, iid}` -> `raised {p, id[, err]}`. Answers are split
  so no message passes 7000 bytes.
- **What the server reveals and checks.** Only tiles on the player's floor within 8 x 6 squares that the player can see; not
  the tiles of a house the player does not own; a corpse's contents only when the player may loot it (owner, party, or
  no owner: `ChaosLootFilter.canLoot`, the loot channel's rule); only items that can be picked up (furniture gets no
  label). A request budget per player (120 tiles at once, then 60 per second; a tooltip costs 2, a raise 4); a flood is
  dropped, the client asks again.
- **Picking up** is the engine's: the client sends the normal move to its backpack, so the engine walks there first,
  checks capacity and room, the corpse owner and every move rule (`Player:onMoveItem`, the season isolation). The engine
  only ever moves the top item of a ground pile (`Game::internalGetThing`, `STACKPOS_MOVE`), so for an item lower in a
  pile the client first sends `raise`: the server checks the tile is in view, on the floor and seen, the player has a line
  of sight to it or stands next to it, it is not another player's house, the item is still there with the same client id,
  count and per-item id (`chaos_iid`), it can be picked up, is no corpse and has no map unique id; then it moves that item
  through a bag that exists for this call only back onto the same tile, which puts it on top (a failed move back leaves the
  bag with the item on the tile; nothing is lost). Nothing leaves the tile there. A click on a corpse label opens the
  corpse with the normal use (the engine walks there and checks the owner).
- **Despawn.** Ground items have no owner and no timer in this server: `cleanMap()` only runs from `/clean` and the admin
  panel (the server save's clean is off in `globalevents/scripts/save.lua` and `serverSaveCleanMap = false`). So `e` is
  only sent for what decays (`ITEM_ATTRIBUTE_DECAYSTATE` = decaying, `ITEM_ATTRIBUTE_DURATION` left, exact with the decay
  manager of `src-patches/0006`): lit torches, special items and corpses. For a corpse it is the time until its loot is
  gone: a corpse decays in stages (a fresh demon 10 s, then "slain demon" stages of 900 and 600 s) and keeps its items as
  long as the next stage is a container, so the stages are summed until the first that is not (`G.lootExpiry`).
- **Client** (`client/overlay/modules/game_groundlabels`): labels of items the filter makes glow (framed in the colour),
  Rare+ items (rarity >= Rare, uniques, orbs, legendary powers; a setting), everything else only while Alt is held (items
  the filter hides then faded). Items the filter hides never get a label without Alt, Rare or not. "Corpse: N items" over
  a corpse holding items that glow or are Rare+. The despawn timer (`m:ss`) for corpses and for items worth it. Labels of
  one tile stack upwards over it, a block that would cover a neighbour's moves up past it (or down when that is too far);
  at most 40, the best first (uniques, rarity, glow, corpses, then the nearest). Each labelled tile carries one widget
  (`Tile:setWidget`), drawn by the engine on the tile every frame; clicks and hovering are matched on the map panel. Left
  click: pick up / open the corpse; right click: the item menu; hover: the rich tooltip or the corpse's list. The engine
  has no Lua callback for tile changes, so the tiles in view are compared every 400 ms and right after the player moves
  (ids and counts first; the candidate test only runs on a changed tile; under 1 ms with 50 labelled tiles in software
  rendering), and only changed tiles are asked about. Settings in the Loot Filter window's "Ground Labels" button (saved
  in `g_settings`, node `groundLabels`): on/off, Rare+, Alt, corpses, timers, label size.

**Tests:** `server/tests/groundloot_test.lua` (positions from client input, view range, budget, decay and corpse stages,
wire rows, the message split, and the handler on a mocked engine: what is and is not revealed, refused tiles answered
empty, tooltips, every refusal of `raise` and the reorder) and the client's `game_groundlabels/groundlabels_test.lua`
(settings, candidates, the label decisions with the real loot filter rules, text, timer, colour, priority and the cap, and
the layout: no two blocks overlap in a row of wide labels, a 4 x 3 cluster or on one tile). Checked in game at 1280x720 and
1920x1080: labels of 15 rarities, a unique, orbs, a corpse with its timer and contents, a real demon kill (orb in the
corpse), Alt showing everything, the strict preset hiding Common to Rare (faded with Alt), stacks on one tile and a row of
neighbours, 40 labels of 54 tiles, the timer counting down, pick up by click (top item, an item lower in a pile, a unique
two squares away: walked there), the item menu on right click, the rich tooltip and the corpse tooltip on hover, label
sizes, switching labels off and on. **Not verified:** two players at once, a season character facing another realm's
items (the engine refuses the move; the label still shows), labels while walking fast over many piles (positions follow
the engine, the scan lags at most 400 ms).

## Instance limits (`instance_limits.lua`, `instance_limits_core.lua`, `instance_limits_config.lua`, `tools/patch_base_bossrooms.py`, `tools/patch_base_dungeon.py`, `tools/patch_base_eventrooms.py`)

Owner request: a time limit on quests and dungeons, so the instances do not fill up or overload (roadmap item 108). Every
place with its own way in and out has a time limit, warnings before it runs out, a rule for the end, an idle rule, a cap
on parallel copies with a wait estimate, and a staff view. Each system keeps its own numbers in its config (`limits`);
`instance_limits_config.lua` has the shared defaults. No new opcode and no new table; one new storage (the tutorial's
`islandUsed`, 7100257, in the new player block).

- **Warnings** (`limits.warnAt`, default 5 min / 1 min / 10 s): a red status line and a chat line to everyone inside
  ("Rift: 1 minute left. Everyone inside is sent out when the time runs out."), the marks of a minute or more also as a
  toast. Each mark once per run; a mark already behind when a run starts is skipped (a 3 minute trial gets no "5
  minutes left"). The HUDs that already count down (rift HUD, arena, battleground, dungeon window) keep doing so.
- **The end** is each system's own failure rule (table below): nobody gets a reward for it, nothing is lost twice.
- **Idle**: the systems that end a run at once when its last player is out keep doing so. The rift (a fallen player who
  may come back kept it open until the timer), the raid and the base boss rooms close an empty instance after a grace.
- **Caps** (`limits.maxRuns`, default the grid's slots): a player who finds every copy busy hears the wait of the first
  to end ("All rifts are busy. Try again in ~4 min. You are 2nd in line: you will be told when one is free.") and waits in
  line (`waitlist`): when a slot frees up the first in line who is online and outside every instance is told (chat and a
  toast) and taken off the line; nobody is moved in automatically, so the key, sigil or party check stays the player's.
  An entry stays 15 minutes (`waitMinutes`, at most `waitMax` = 50), a logout leaves the line, a closing server tells
  nobody. Arena, battleground and dungeons have their own queue, which now also says the wait.
- **Staff** (`/instances`, group 4+, logged like every guarded command): `/instances` lists every running instance with
  its type, id, time left, players and the idle grace; `/instances <type>` one type; `/instances close <type> <id>` ends
  one by its system's failure rule; `/instances line [type]` shows who waits. The registry of `chaos_constants.lua`
  (`Chaos.registerInstance`) takes two optional fields for this: `runs()` and `close(id)`.

**Before and after** (time = the limit of one run; "out" = where the player is sent):

| Instance | Before | After | End of time | Idle | Cap | Logout inside, login | Restart |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rift | 10 min (Waning Veil -15-40%), no warnings, "Try again in a moment" | 12 / 13 / 15 min by map size (2026-10-12, "Rifts", Big maps), + warnings, idle 3 min, wait and line | fails: out to where the key was used, key spent | a run kept for fallen players closes after 3 min (fails) | 16 | out of the run, back at the entry; a fallen player returns at login while the run lives | key back once (unchanged) |
| Omen arena | 10 min, as rifts | as rifts | as rifts | as rifts | shares the 16 rift slots | as rifts | as rifts |
| Ember Descent | 45 min, no warnings | + warnings, wait and line | ends at the depth reached (its rewards), back at the entry | ends when the last player is out | 8 | ends for that player with its rewards; crash: temple | ends with rewards, temple |
| Raid (Sepulchre) | no session limit, idle 10 min | session 150 min with warnings at 10 / 5 / 1 min and 10 s, idle 5 min, wait and line | everyone back where they came from, progress saved for the week (a fight then is a wipe) | 5 min (was 10), to the temple | 4 | removed (back where they came from); crash: temple | closed, temple, progress kept |
| Ascended Omen | boss limit 13 min (Cinderheart 18) + 8 s | + warnings, wait and line | fails, out, sigil spent | ends when the last player is out | 4 | out | sigil back once |
