| Ascension trial | 3 min, a line every 30 s | + wait and line | lost (10 min cooldown), back to the Oracle | solo | 8 | ends (the cooldown) | out at login |
| Infinity Tower | 5 min a floor, no run limit | run limit 60 min with warnings, floor warnings at 1 min and 10 s, wait and line | ends like a lost floor: back at the entry, floors cleared recorded | ends when the last player is out | 16 | ends (floors recorded); login inside: temple | login inside: temple |
| Dungeon | queue: base DungeonTime 60 / 30 min; a relog stayed in the box (and held the next group's run back). Next to it the base modal entry (tile 26702): its own run in the same boxes, 60 / 30 min, no warning, a scan of every tile of the box on each use (37,074 / 61,325 tiles), an exit timer holding the player object, at its end every monster of the box removed (also a queue run's) | queue only: the entry tile opens the dungeon window (`patch_base_dungeon.py`); capped at 45 min, warnings, the queue shows the wait of the run inside, a relog inside goes to the temple (a failed attempt: the cooldown) | back where they entered, cooldown, monsters removed | ends when the last member is out | 1 per dungeon, queue | released; login: temple + cooldown | temple, no cooldown |
| World boss | 45 min after the boss | + warnings | the boss withdraws, temple after 90 s, arena cleaned | event (not per group) | 1 arena, 40 players | stays in the event | login inside an idle arena: temple |
| Guild siege | 25 min match | + warnings | results, temple after 30 s | event | one a week | rejoins through the portals | unchanged |
| Tutorial island | none | 30 min online (offline time does not count), warnings at 5 and 1 min | leaves as with Skip tutorial: kit, welcome, temple | shared island, no copies | none needed | time kept; a login past the limit leaves at once | unchanged |
| Base lever boss rooms (51) and step-in miniboss rooms (7) | the script's own kick 10-60 min, no warning; the lever (tile) free whenever nobody stood inside; the old kick timer also hit the next group; monsters stayed | lever locked while a group's session runs, limit = the room's own time at most 30 min, warnings, countdown bars over the entrance and the lever | everyone to the room's exit, monsters removed | empty room frees up after 2 min (at once after a kill) | 1 group per room | login inside a closed room: its exit; inside its own running room: stays | closed at shutdown (exit) |
| Soul pit | no limit, no lock against a second group with a core during the 5 s countdown, a group that left kept the run's state and loops going | soul core on the pit locked while a run is on, 15 min with warnings | everyone to the pit's lobby spot, waves removed, the pit's state reset | empty: 2 min; completed: 65 s | 1 | login inside a closed pit: lobby spot | closed at shutdown |
| Tower defence | no limit; anyone could walk in mid-run; a lever pull after the spawning restarted the run under the walking monsters | the lever starts a 20 min session for the players inside; entrance tile and lever locked meanwhile; warnings | everyone to the exit drop, spawning stopped, summon counters reset, monsters and core removed | empty: 2 min; won or lost: 65 s (at once when empty) | 1 | login inside a closed arena: exit drop | closed at shutdown |
| Invasions, Scorched Marches, hideouts | open world / personal | unchanged | | | | | |

**Base lever boss rooms** (`tools/patch_base_bossrooms.py`, install step `bossrooms`; `ChaosBossRooms` in
`instance_limits.lua`). 51 base scripts share one template (a `config` with bossArea, participantsPos and
kickParticipantAfterSeconds; a lever Action; a boss death that opens a teleport out). 7 more rooms use the same template
entered by a tile instead of a lever, several in one file (see "Step-in miniboss rooms" below). The tool adds three marked
lines to each room, the rest untouched: the room's config is registered at load (`ChaosBossRoomsPending["aid<actionId>"]`), the lever's
onUse first asks `ChaosBossRooms.leverUse` (refused with "A group is fighting in there. The room frees up in ~X at the
latest."), and after the group went in `ChaosBossRooms.started` takes over the kick: the script's own timer is stopped
(it was never stopped when a room emptied and so hit the next group), the time limit is the room's own time capped at
`bossRooms.maxSeconds` (30 min: one boss fight, twice the longest Chaos boss limit; 3 of the 51 rooms had more), warnings,
a "Time left" bar over the entrance and a "Room in use" bar over the lever (tilebars.lua). At the end everyone inside goes
to the script's exitPosition and every monster in the room is removed; after a boss kill the script's own exit runs and
the room frees up when it is empty. `leverUse` also refuses a pull when nobody (the puller, or a player in front) stands
on the room's participantsPos tiles (`ChaosBossRooms.groupReady`): the stock onUse then made the boss, teleported nobody
and the room showed "Room in use" until the 2 min idle close. `started` with an empty group closes the room at once
(boss removed), and brings in a participant the lever's teleport left outside (`ChaosBossRooms.bringIn`: a free tile
within 3 sqm of entrancePos, inside the room). **Leave Boss Room** (client Info & Services > Services > Other, command
`leaveroom` of `commands_ui.lua`; `ChaosBossRooms.leave`, pure rule `ChaosInstanceLimitsCore.leaveReason`): a player in
any running room (the lever rooms, the waystone boss rooms, the step-in miniboss rooms, the soul pit, the tower
defence) goes to the room's exitPosition (the tower defence: its drop) and leaves the group. Refused outside a running
room, in a fight (`isPzLocked()` or `CONDITION_INFIGHT`, as the dungeon queue and the arena: no free escape from a lost
fight) and within `bossRooms.leaveCooldown` (30 s) of the last leave. The last one out closes the room with
`BR.close(key, "idle")` (boss and monsters removed, the lever free). The button is enabled only inside a running room
(Services state `inBossRoom`). Without the Chaos scripts the rooms work as before. Left alone (of another shape):
about a dozen old XML quest levers and pits. Map check (the base map, the action and unique ids of every map item): the 7
step-in miniboss rooms are on the map (below); the soul pit (its
start lever aid 57392 at 31588,32269,8, the entrance aid 5896); the tower defence (aid 27931 twice, aid 25486); of 11
XML lever and pit scripts that teleport a group into a fight with a timer or a room check, 9 have their ids on the map
(annihilator, elemental spheres, the new frontier arena, the warzones and their lever, children of the revolution,
Pythius, the two Killing in the Name of boss rooms); the Payback Time lever (uid 3198) and the demon oak (item 8293, set at
runtime) are not. These are left for a later change.

**Step-in miniboss rooms** (the same tool and step). `extensions/fear_feaster/minibosses.lua` (Vok the Freakish twice,
Irgix the Flimsy; entry tiles aid 33717 / 33719 / 33721) and `extensions/lions/minibosses.lua` (Srezz Yellow Eyes, Yirkas
Blue Scales, Katex Blood Tongue, Utua Stone Sting; 33723 / 33725 / 33727 / 33729) hold 3 and 4 rooms of the lever
template: one `local config` each, a MoveEvent `onStepIn` with the lever's signature instead of the lever, a 10 minute
kick, an exit tile inside the room, no boss death script. All 7 entry tiles and exit tiles are on the map. The tool cuts
such a file into one room per `local config` and patches each room as a lever room (its tile's onStepIn gets the lock);
a file is patched only when every room in it is recognised, otherwise it is listed and left alone whole. Each room locks
on its own (the other rooms of the file stay free); the "Room in use" bar stands over the entry tile (participantsPos[1]).
With the Chaos scripts, a monster or a summon walking onto an entry tile starts nothing (`leverUse` refuses non-players;
the stock script made the boss for it and started the kick timer). The rooms have no boss death script, so after a kill
the session sends the group out 65 s later (the default 60 s of `teleportRemoveSeconds` + 5; before, they stayed until
the 10 minute kick or took the exit tile). The 51 lever rooms come out of the tool byte for byte as before (checked on
the base data).

**Soul pit and tower defence** (`tools/patch_base_eventrooms.py`, install step `eventrooms` after `bossrooms`). Neither is
built from the boss room template and neither had a time limit, so the tool gives each a room config of its own and the
same `ChaosBossRooms` session (lock, warnings, bars, idle rule, login rule, staff list and close, shutdown):
- Soul pit (`soulpit_system/soulpit.lua`, a soul core used on the pit, aid 57392). The box is the script's room joined
  with its spawn area (the spawn area reached 2 tiles past the room, so monsters there were outside the room's own
  check). The lock comes first when a core is used on the pit (a core used on anything else is not touched; a refused
  core is not spent); the session starts as soon as the core is taken (the 5 s countdown was open to a second group).
  Time: `bossRooms.ownSeconds.soulpit` = 15 minutes (5 short waves). At the end everyone goes to the spot the pit's
  entrance teleport leads to (31589,32281,8; not the start tiles, which the next group needs), the waves are removed and
  the script's `event` state is reset (a group that left mid-run used to leave it and its 1 s loops going, and the next
  group then shared them). A completed pit closes the room 65 s later, like a boss kill.
- Tower defence (`tower_defense/tower_defense.lua`, lever aid 27931 in the arena; `entrance_teleport.lua`, aid 25485).
  The arena box is the script's own (`fromPos` / `toPos`). The lever starts a session for the players inside (they came
  in before the start); while it runs the entrance tile sends a newcomer back where they came from (with the time) and
  the lever answers the group "Your run is still going" (a pull after the spawning used to restart the run under the
  walking monsters). Time: `bossRooms.ownSeconds.towerdefense` = 20 minutes (the stock waves take about 7). At the end
  spawning stops, every monster (core, waves, summons) is removed, the players' summon counters and marks are reset as
  the login does, and everyone goes to the drop of the arena's own exit tile (31206,32295,8). A win or a loss (the
  script's own rules) ends the session; after a loss the script has sent everyone out and the arena is free at once.
  The bar "Room in use" stands at that drop, next to the entrance.
Without the Chaos scripts both work as before (the test runs the stock and the patched pit and compares them). A script
of another shape is listed and left alone.

**Base modal dungeon entry** (`tools/patch_base_dungeon.py`, install step `dungeonentry`; `ChaosDungeonsOpen` in
`dungeons.lua`). The base server has a second way into the 4 dungeons of `DUNGEON_SYSTEM` (lib/core/dungeon.lua): a
step-in tile (item 26702, one on the map at 32365,32233,7; movements `dungeon.lua`) opens a modal window, and its answer
(creaturescripts `dungeon_mod.lua`) runs a dungeon of its own in the same boxes as the queue. Neither knew about the
other. Its weak spots: "a team is already inside" looked at every tile of the box on each Confirm (Bones 222 x 167 =
37,074 tiles, Master of the Elements 223 x 275 = 61,325; the same pattern as "Game loop stalls"); its exit timer held
the player object (stale after a logout); its 60 / 30 minutes had no warning and no cap; at the end it removed every
monster in the box, also those of a queue run that had started there; and its runs had no difficulty, records or
challenges. Owner decision: the tile opens the Chaos dungeon window instead (rather than a second patched entry). The
tool adds one marked line at the top of the step-in's `onStepIn`: `ChaosDungeonsOpen(player)` sends the dungeon list (at
most once a second per player, as the window's own fetch) and the new server action `open` (opcode
`ChaosOpcodes.dungeons`), and the client's `game_dungeons` shows the window. The modal window is never sent, so the
modal answer, its box scan and its timer never run; every run goes through the queue (one per box, the time cap and
warnings above). A monster on the tile does nothing. Without the Chaos scripts the tile works as before. The modal
scripts stay in the base data untouched. A script is recognised as the script of a StepIn movevent that sends the
`DUNGEON_SYSTEM` modal window and has one `onStepIn`; another shape is listed and left alone.

**Load.** Every runtime area is built once per slot and kept (the engine cannot remove a tile); a run removes its
monsters and loose items at the end. The rifts are the exception since the big maps of 2026-10-12 ("Rifts", Layouts and
the slot pool): each run gets a new generated map of 9,700-50,500 tiles (both floors), built in 10 ms steps by one
builder job at a time (0.3-1.8 s of game loop a map, measured), up to about 26 MB a slot and 420 MB for the 16 at the
worst; at most 260 + 12 monsters a run alive, only those near the party active. The numbers below are of the first
density pass. Tiles per slot, counted from the layouts: rift 1,657 (1,045 before the bigger rooms of 2026-10-12), Descent about 440, raid 3,574,
Ascended 486, guild boss 574, arena 182, battleground 2,145, trial 529, ascension trial 225, tower 441, world boss
about 1,220, tutorial about 680. All grids full: about 76,000 tiles, about 23 MB at roughly 300 bytes a tile with its
ground and wall items, next to a map of millions. The game loop cost of a run is its tick (1 s or 250 ms; the players of
the run, the HUD, a sweep for strangers every 3 s) and its monsters. Ticks: well under 1 ms each, under 10 ms a second
with every slot of every type running (about 85). Monsters: a run is about one hunting group (Descent at most 14 a
wave; tower at most 22; raid about 40 awake). A dense rift (2026-10-12, "Rifts", Density) has at most 60 monsters alive
solo and 100 for five, +12 extra (Veilbreach, thralls); the rest of its plan (up to about 380, or more with Teeming and
Swarm) waits in a queue. So all caps full is about 2,600 active monsters (16 rifts x 112 = 1,792 of them; before: 16 x 76
and about 2,000 in all), 260 in each of the engine's 10 creature-check tasks a second; at the measured 20-50 us a monster
that is 5-13 ms a task, far from the 100 ms slow task line and the 250 ms stalls of "Game loop stalls". The cap also
bounds the worst rift modifiers: Teeming and Swarm V used to put about 4,600 monsters in the grid at once (10-25 ms a
task); now their plans get longer, not wider. A rift's first packs (up to 100 monsters with name, look, tier and events,
estimated 0.2-0.3 ms each) cost 20-30 ms once, in the task that uses the key; reinforcements are at most 2 packs (14
monsters, 3-5 ms) a second per rift, each run in its own timer task; ground and storm hazards are a few effects and one
position check per player a second. The caps stay at 16 rifts. The one-off cost is building a slot the first
time (about 3 items a tile: estimated 16 ms for a rift, 30-60 ms for a raid slot) and clearing it at the end (a Tile
lookup per floor tile, a few ms). So the caps stay at the grid sizes, which were sized to free map areas; a full set of
every type holds more players than the 200-400 online the server was load tested with, so the cap binds only in a burst.
Not measured on a running server (no disk for a build this time); the slow task log (`slowTaskLogMs = 100`) on the test
server shows a slot build or a clean-up if one is slower than estimated.

**Tests.** `tests/instance_limits_test.lua` (the core: marks, idle, wait, line, texts; the glue on a mocked engine: the
warnings and toasts, busy and line, freed, `/instances`; the patch tool on a stock-shaped room in LF and CRLF, dry run,
idempotence, another shape left alone; the patched room script on the mocked engine: lock, the old timer stopped,
warnings, time up with the exit and the monsters removed, the idle grace, a kill, the login rules, staff close,
shutdown), `tests/instance_limits_systems_test.lua` (dungeons and the tutorial island on their real files), and an
"instance limits" part in `rift_refund_test`, `raid_test`, `uber_test`, `guildboss_test`, `trials_flow_test`,
`arena_flow_test`, `battleground_flow_test`, `infinitytower_run_test` and `worldboss_test` (each system's limit,
warnings, cap and line, idle close, staff list and close where it applies). `instance_limits_test` also patches a
stock-shaped miniboss file (two step-in rooms, CRLF) and runs it: each room locks on its own, the kick timer is stopped,
a monster on the tile starts nothing, time up sends each group to its room's exit and removes the monsters; a file with
one room of another shape is left alone whole. `tests/base_eventrooms_patch_test.lua`: the tool on the stock-shaped soul
pit and tower defence (made-up monsters; dry run, CRLF, idempotence, another shape), the stock and the patched pit without
the Chaos scripts (the same run), then both with them: lock, time, warnings, time up (exit, waves removed, state reset so
the next run starts fresh), a completed pit; the tower's lever session, the entrance sending a newcomer back, the
group's second pull, time up (exit, counters reset, spawning stopped), a win and both loss paths. `tests/base_dungeon_patch_test.lua`: the
tool on the stock entry (written there with made-up dungeons: dry run, idempotence, CRLF, another shape and a non
StepIn script left alone), then the stock and the patched entry on a mocked engine: without the Chaos scripts the same
modal window and answer; with `dungeons.lua` loaded no modal window, not one tile looked at, the list and `open` sent,
the queue runs the dungeon with its cap, a monster does nothing, the rate limit. The Descent, the ascension trial and the
siege got the same few lines (config, a warning call in the tick, the cap and the busy text, the registry) without an
engine test of their own. Not run in game.

## Waystone tiers (`waystone_tiers.lua`, `waystone_tiers_core.lua`, `waystone_tiers_config.lua`, `tools/patch_waystone_bosses.py`, `tools/install_waystone_items.py`)

The base waystone system (`data/scripts/customs/waystone_system/tier_maps.lua`) has six tiers of two maps each. Its
monster files have the same flat stats in every tier (hunting level about 468-612). Owner 2026-10-23: the first waystone
at monster level 1100, the last at 2500, new waystones in between, a gradual rise, and 2-3 scenarios each for the low,
middle and high levels. So:

| Band | Tiers | Monster level | Scenarios (maps of the base tiers) |
|---|---|---|---|
| low | I-V | 1100-1500 | 4: the water cave and the cave (base I), the plain and the cave (base II) |
| mid | VI-X | 1600-2000 | 4: the plain and the cave (base III), the forest and the underground (base IV) |
| high | XI-XV | 2100-2500 | 4: the desert and the ice (base V), the undead cave and the forest & desert (base VI) |

Each tier is +100 levels (`tiers` in the config). Tier I-VI are the base items (29845-29850); VII-XV are new items
41951-41959 (`tools/install_waystone_items.py`, install step `waystoneitems`: copies of the base tablet nodes with their
own server ids, looks of base III-VI, so no client pair is needed; a hotkey use of one picks the base item of the same
look, so use them from the backpack or on the device). `tools/patch_waystone_hideout.py` part 3 lets the base device take
them (`ChaosWaystoneTiers.tablets`), open a map of the tier's band (`optionsFor`), show each tier's level in the window
(client `game_waystone`) and call `startRun` when the pads open.

**Level.** A base tier's monster type (or boss) inside a map of that base tier counts at the level of the map's run: the
tier of the last waystone that opened it, else the band's first tier. `ChaosWaystoneTiers.levelOf` is read by `loot.lua`
`ChaosLoot.monsterLevel` (shown level, item level of drops, late-game damage boost, pack combat). Shown level:
`Chaos.spawnLevel` at onSpawn index 40. Max health x the engine's level factor at the first think, from the monster's
hunting level to the run's level (bosses: from the band's first tier level, their base health); experience x target /
native; damage to players x the engine's damage factor (`monster_damage.lua`), bosses also x `bossDamage` of their base
tier. `startRun` rescales the monsters already standing in the map (same health share, new shown level); respawns during
the run spawn at its level. Summons, other monsters and a type outside its maps are untouched.

**Drops.** After the level gate (`loot.lua` `gateWaystones`), `retierDrops` turns every waystone in a corpse into one of
the run's tier: T 60%, T+1 30%, T+2 10% (`drops.inside`, capped at XV); outside the maps a waystone is a Tier I. The run's
boss adds one waystone of tier T+1 (`drops.bossNext`).

**Bosses.** Morgrath (base V) took no damage away from a Katoi Pillar, and Nyxdrath (base VI) took only the adjacent
pillar's element. `tools/patch_waystone_bosses.py` (install step `waystonebosses`) makes their health events keep
`shieldedShare` (0.25) of such a hit and hint the attacker every `hintSeconds`. The same tool moves the Waystone III
Frostreaver entrance off a tar tile (32965 to 32964,33236,7). At startup `ChaosWaystoneTiers.clearPaths` removes the
items that block both base IV boss levers: a fir tree at 33217,33237,7 and nine rope railings on y 33412, floor 8.

Tests: `tests/waystone_tiers_test.lua`, `tools/install_waystone_items_test.py`, `tools/patch_waystone_hideout_test.py`,
`tools/patch_waystone_bosses_test.py`, client `waystonelogic_test.lua`. The website and codex levels still come from the
bounty pool. Balance numbers are first guesses. Not run in game.

Modifiers: see "Waystone modifiers". `retierDrops` also rolls a dropped waystone's rarity inside a run, and the
experience callback multiplies by the run's experience bonus.

## Waystone modifiers (`waystone_mods.lua`, `waystone_mods_core.lua`, `waystone_mods_config.lua`, `lib/chaos_crafting.lua`, `tools/patch_waystone_hideout.py` part 4)

Owner 2026-10-23: waystones work like the maps of the well-known action RPG: they take modifiers, each a buff for the
monsters or a debuff for the players, paid with experience and loot.

**Rarity.** Normal: no modifier. Magic: at most one prefix and one suffix. Rare: at most three of each (six). The
rarity follows the counts (`W.rarityOf`). Prefixes buff the monsters, suffixes debuff the players. The 25 modifiers are
the rift keys' (`rift_config.lua` mods copied by key, with their ranges, tiers I-V, groups and conflicts); the rift-only
ones (packs, goblin, coffer, twin guardians, double loot, time, lives) are left out. Modifier tiers follow the item's
tier through `modTiers` (tiers 1-5 roll I-III, 6-10 I-IV, 11-15 II-V).

**Storage.** Custom attribute `ws_mods` ("key:value,...", `R.encodeMods`). A waystone with modifiers gets its own name
("Rare Waystone Tier IV") and a description with the level, the modifiers and the rewards. Waystones are stackable, so
`WM.single` splits the crafted one off its stack; writing an empty list removes the attributes, so it stacks again.

**Orbs** (`lib/chaos_crafting.lua`, the crafting window lists waystones): Awakening Normal -> Magic (one modifier),
Gilding Normal -> Rare (4-6), Grafting +1 on an open side (a full Magic one needs Fate first), Fate Magic -> Rare (the new
modifier on the filled side) or rerolls a Rare one's values, Upheaval rerolls within the rarity, Unmaking removes one,
Erasure back to Normal. Sockets and the other orbs refuse with a reason (`ws*`).

**The device.** `tools/patch_waystone_hideout.py` part 4 replaces the base `player:removeItem(id, 1)` with
`ChaosWaystoneMods.take`: the waystone the player used on the device within `chosenSeconds` (300), else the carried one
of that tier with the fewest modifiers. Its modifiers go to `WT.startRun(area, serverId, mods)` -> `WM.begin`.

**The run.** `WM.runs[map] = {mods, fx, bonus, untilAt}` lasts `runSeconds` (31 min) or until the next waystone opens
the map. Effects run through `rift_core.lua` (`R.effects` with a shim config, `R.monsterHit`, `R.monsterTaken`):
monster health and speed are applied once and taken off when a run without modifiers starts; Elites raise the magic /
rare roll; brands, keen, festering, cinder, breach, dread on the boss; withering, parched, blight, hexes, ground and
storm on the players in the map (a 1 s tick).

**Rewards.** Each modifier's own `reward` (quantity, rarity, experience) plus `perMod.waystone` 12% waystone chance,
capped at `bonusCap` (120 / 110 / 80 / 72). Quantity: `loot_config.lua` rateMult; rarity: `loot.lua` rarityFind;
experience: `waystone_tiers.lua`; waystone: a second waystone chance in `retierDrops`. A waystone dropped inside a run
rolls `dropRarity` (Normal 55, Magic 30, Rare 15); outside the maps it is Normal.

Tests: `tests/waystone_mods_test.lua` (core and mocked engine), `tools/patch_waystone_hideout_test.py`. Balance numbers
are first guesses. Not run in game.

## Waystone Atlas (`waystone_atlas.lua`, `waystone_atlas_core.lua`, `waystone_atlas_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_waystone_atlas.sql`, client `game_riftatlas` waystone mode)

Owner 2026-10-23: the waystone maps get their own atlas, as the maps of the well-known action RPG. Opcode 159, table
`chaos_waystone_atlas` (created by the script when missing, as the Rift Atlas's), no storages. Window: Adventure >
Waystone Atlas.

**Points.** Killing a map's boss during a waystone run credits every player inside the map rectangle with the map x tier
cell (`m<map>.<tier>`, only the five tiers of the map's band: 12 maps x 5 = 60) and, when the run's waystone was Rare,
the Rare cell of the tier (`r<tier>`, 15). 75 points; the tree costs 108, so it can never be filled. Each cell counts
once per character.

**The tree.** 81 nodes, the Rift Atlas's shape and rules (`atlas_core.lua`: allocate next to a held node, one keystone,
refund 250k gold or an Orb of Upheaval per node, reset at 80%). Core nodes count everywhere; the north, east and south
branches count only in Low (tiers I-V), Middle (VI-X) and High (XI-XV) maps; the west branch (Cartography) everywhere.

**Effects** (`WC.resolve`, caps in the config): item quantity (20), rarity (25), experience (20), waystone chance
(30), modifier rewards (25, multiplies the modifiers' bonuses), tier up of dropped waystones (15), fewer Normal drops
(35), a second waystone from the boss (50). Keystones: Pure Stone (+40% quantity and experience on Normal waystones,
modifier rewards halved), Hunter's Vow (the boss drops two more waystones, half the others are lost), Ascendant Path
(dropped waystones one tier higher, the boss drops none), Rare Pursuit (no Normal drops, -20% quantity).

**Whose atlas.** The player who used the waystone (`WM.take` stores `opener`); `WT.startRun` calls `WA.beginRun` before
`WM.begin`, so a run without modifiers also gets the atlas. The effects last as long as the run (`runSeconds`).
Hooks: `WM.lootMult`, `WM.rarityFind`, `WM.expMult`, `WM.extraWaystone`, `WM.rollDrop` (`WC.dropRows`) and
`waystone_tiers.lua` `retierDrops` (`WC.dropTier`, keystones on the boss's drops).

Tests: `tests/waystone_atlas_test.lua` (core, mocked engine and the hooks). Balance numbers are first guesses. Not run in
game.

## Content rewards (`content_rewards.lua`, `content_rewards_core.lua`, `content_rewards_config.lua`, `tools/content_reward_model.lua`, `tools/audit_waystone_maps.py`)

Beta feedback 2026-10-23: inside a waystone "the monsters are the same as outside with the same drops", the boss dropped
almost nothing, and nobody knew what the content was for. Owner: rifts and waystones need separate drops.

**What each paid before (O143 audit).** Rift: the monsters' own loot x the key's quantity bonus (rateMult), the guardian's
chest per finisher (gold, Upheaval / Fate, item rolls, gems), the next key. Waystone: the same monsters' own loot x the
modifiers' quantity and rarity, one next-tier waystone from the boss. The base waystone monster files hold coins,
potions, materials and orbs and **no gear and no waystone at all** (`data/monster/lua/waystone_portals`), and the corpse
rule by monster level (`pace_core.lua`) thins a level 1100+ boss's table to a few coins. So the boss was worth less than
a hunted pack and a waystone could not even pay for the next one.

**Identity.** Rifts = crafting currency. Waystones = gear. Each keeps the other's reward out.

| | Rift (key tier 1-15) | Waystone (tier 1-15) |
|---|---|---|
| Every kill | an orb: 1.5% (tier 1) to 5.7% (tier 15) of normal kills, x2.5 magic, x5 rare, x12 legendary; drawn Upheaval 30, Awakening 20, Fate 18, Gilding 12, Grafting 8, Unmaking 6, Erasure 6 | a set piece (Azure Vigil / Gildcrown, level 0.45-1.0 x the run's) on 2.5% (tier 1) to 6.7% (tier 15), same tier multipliers; always Rare or better (Legendary 29%, Divine 1% + 0.2% per tier); the loot layer then rolls item level, sockets, modifiers; smart loot may turn it into the killer's class |
| Run bonus | the key's modifiers (unchanged) | quantity +10% + 1.5% per tier, rarity find +20% + 3.5% per tier, on top of the modifiers; 12% of the monsters are magic or rare (loot-tier name and look via `ChaosApplyTier`; `waystone_mods_config.lua` `elites.runBase`) |
| Boss | the guardian's corpse: 4 + 0.8 x tier orbs (same draw) and 1 + 0.1 x tier unique rolls at 2x find; the chest as before | 3 + 0.25 x (tier - 1) Legendary (85%) or Divine pieces, 2 + 0.2 x (tier - 1) unique rolls at 3x find (boss tier), Awakening 2-4, Gilding 1-2, Grafting 35%, Fate 25%, one waystone of the run's tier plus the tier + 1 one; pieces x the quantity |
| The loop | a sealed rift leaves a key (below) | 0.4% of the kills drop a waystone of the run's tier (x tier multiplier), the boss two |

Everything scales with the modifiers' quantity (`ChaosWaystoneMods.lootMult`, `ChaosRift.contentOf`). `loot.lua` calls
`ChaosContentRewards.onKill` after the extra rolls and before the gear quality step (a piece gets item level, sockets and
modifiers like any drop). Summons pay nothing. Omen arenas keep their own chest. `enabled = false` turns it all off.

**Key ladder (`rift_config.lua` `keyDrop.pity`, `R.keyGuarantee`).** Report: a level 800-1500 character ran Rift Level 1 six
times and never got a Level 2 key. The old rule is pure RNG (55% a key, 70% of those tier + 1: 38% per run for a one
modifier key, so six misses in a row happen to 6% of players). Now: (1) pity: `runs` = 2 sealed rifts in a row with no
stronger key (counter on the receiver, storage `riftRun + 5`) make the third leave tier + 1; (2) fast step: a finisher at
1.5x the tier's entry level or more always gets a key of the tier his level fits (`R.fitTier`), at least +1 and at most
+3 per run (level 1000 in tier 1: tier 4, then 7, 10). The Ashen Ascent keystone turns both off. Rift monsters stay at
the key tier's level window (a tier 1 rift is level 80-180 whatever the player's level): scaling them to the party would
make the low tiers a grind at a high level, so they are a quick step with a guaranteed key instead.

**Layout audit.** `tools/audit_waystone_maps.py BASE_SERVER_DIR --check` walks each of the 12 maps of `tier_maps.lua` on
the base `.otbm` (players walk onto fields; `clearPath` items taken off; the Frostreaver entrance moved): the arrival
region, every lever tile, the boss entrance and boss tile, that the boss room is closed, that 85% of the spawn points
are reachable and that at least four of the tier's five monster types spawn. Result 2026-10-23: all 12 pass; **maps 7
(tier IV forest) and 8 (tier IV underground) fail on the raw map** (lever cut off: a small fir tree; rope railings),
which `clearPath` fixes at each start (`waystone_tiers.lua` `clearPaths`; this was already in place). The monsters
Nexlurith, Nightflare Dreadknight and Inferno Juggernaut spawn in only one of their tier's two maps, which is not a
defect. `waystone_tiers_config.lua` `layouts` records the audit and `retired` lists maps `WT.optionsFor` must leave out
(none today). The base map is not in the repository: CI runs `tools/audit_waystone_maps_test.py` (synthetic maps,
parsers) and `tests/waystone_layouts_test.lua` (12 rows, rectangles, clearPath inside maps, a band keeps two maps); run
the audit by hand after a map or `clearPath` change. The generated rift layouts (including the fungus forest theme
"Forsaken Sanctum") are validated for every theme and size band by `tests/rift_layout_test.lua`.

**The model (`tools/content_reward_model.lua --check`, both interpreters).** Per hour at the pack model's kills (x0.85
waystone, x0.8 rift for the walking), against the richest stock hunting band (`richestBand`: the loot model's band with the most Rare+ gear an hour; 500 since
O285, 24.8 an hour at the old band 1000 before, 25.7 now; the base set ends at pool level 657):

| Content | Tier 1 | Tier 15 | With +60% quantity |
|---|---|---|---|
| Waystone Rare+ gear/h (hunting 25.7) | 43.5 (x2.7) | 132.9 (x6.2) | x3.7 / x9.0 |
| Rift orbs/h (hunting 69 / 51) | 47.8 (x1.7) | 135.1 (x3.7) | x2.1 / x5.2 |

`bounds` in `content_rewards_config.lua`: waystone gear gain at least x2 with no modifiers and at most x14 with them, rift
orbs at least x1.5 and at most x10. The gold and experience models are untouched (the contents add gear and orbs, no
coins; `loot_model.lua --check` stays green). Computed, not measured in game; the pieces are Rare or better, so their NPC
value is not in the gold model. Not done: waystone-exclusive or rift-exclusive items (new items need art and an
`items.xml` install; the pools are the set pieces and the unique pool) and faction materials (none exist).

Client: the device window, the Atlas window (under the map, per mode) and the rift HUD (label and tooltip) say what each
pays. Tests: `tests/content_rewards_test.lua`, `tests/waystone_layouts_test.lua`, `tools/audit_waystone_maps_test.py`.

## Rifts (`rift.lua`, `rift_core.lua`, `rift_config.lua`, `rift_layout_core.lua`, client `game_rift`)

**Limits** (`rift_config.lua` `limits`, "Instance limits"): 12 / 13 / 15 minutes a run by the size of its map (tiers 1-5 / 6-10 / 11-15, `layout.sizes`; was 10 for all; Omen arenas keep 10), warnings at 5 min, 1 min and 10 s; time up fails the rift (out to where the key was used, the key is spent); a run kept open only for fallen players who may come back closes after 3 minutes as a failed rift; at most 16 rifts and Omen arenas at once, a player who finds them busy (or none ready yet) hears the wait and waits in line.

Map devices (roadmap item 8). A consumable Rift Key opens a timed instance with random modifiers for the player and their
party. All numbers are in `rift_config.lua`; the pure logic (key rolls, rewards, key odds, slots and layout, the timer, the
experience cap) is in `rift_core.lua` and tested by `tests/rift_test.lua`. Extended opcode 228 (server -> client HUD),
storages 7100400-7100409, action ids 47401 (key), 47402 (reward chest) and 47403 (Sealed Coffer). No database table.

- **The key.** An existing non-stackable item, the "shadow orb" (10155), with action id 47401, the custom attributes
  `rift_tier` (1-15) and `rift_mods` (`"vitality:40,reflection:10"`), the name "Rift Key (Tier N)" and a description
  that lists the modifiers, the reward bonuses and the level needed, so looking at a key shows everything. One NPC (Black
  Bert) lists the shadow orb in his trade, so a player could sell a key there.
- **Modifiers** (1-3 per key, weights 50/35/15; a next-tier key from a sealed rift rolls 25/45/30). Each has a value
  range and gives reward bonuses per point of value:

  | Modifier | Effect | Reward bonus |
  |---|---|---|
  | Vitality | monsters +20-60% health | quantity 0.5x, experience 0.25x the value |
  | Brutality | monsters +15-40% damage (health and mana damage to players) | rarity 0.75x, experience 0.25x |
  | Haste | monsters +40-120 speed | quantity 0.15x |
  | Elites | +50-200% magic/rare/legendary monsters | rarity 0.15x, quantity 0.1x |
  | Reflection | monsters reflect 5-15% of the damage that lands (not overkill) as physical damage | experience 1.5x, quantity 1x |
  | Warding | monsters resist 10-30% of all non-physical damage | quantity 0.75x, rarity 0.5x |
  | Withering | players get no health regeneration (food regeneration is swapped for one with mana only; restored on leaving) | +15% experience, +15% quantity |
  | Swarm | +1-3 monsters in every pack | quantity 8x, experience 5x |

  Map modifiers (second set). These have a roll weight (the first eight weigh 100) and a lowest key tier; keys below
  that tier never roll them, from drops or from orbs (`R.addMods`). Boons are pure rewards with no bonus of their own,
  shown in gold on the HUD:

  | Modifier | Effect | Weight, tier | Reward bonus |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Teeming | +20-50% packs | 80, 1+ | quantity 0.5x, experience 0.3x |
  | Gilded Trail (boon) | 30-70% chance that the existing Treasure Goblin (`ChaosTreasureGoblin.spawn`) appears in a random open room after 25-60% of the kills, at the level of the strongest type | 40, 1+ | - |
  | Warbands | 10-30% of packs: every member rare, the first legendary | 60, 2+ | rarity 1x, quantity 0.3x |
  | Sealed Coffer (boon) | 40-100% chance of a coffer (big treasure chest 12664, action id 47403; "Reward chests") in an open room. Using it wakes 5 (+1 per extra player) magic+ rift monsters, which do not count towards the guardian. Once they are dead it opens with coins worth 2,000 x tier^2, Orbs of Upheaval 0.25 + 0.05 x tier, Orbs of Fate 0.03 x tier and 2 + 0.25 x tier item rolls, all x quantity and x the party's loot bonus (one coffer for the party). An unwoken coffer crumbles at the seal | 50, 1+ | - |
  | Twin Guardians | two guardians, each with 55-75% of the guardian health; both must die | 50, 3+ | rarity 0.25x, quantity 0.2x |
  | Echoing Spoils (boon) | 5-15% of kills: every corpse item is copied once (onDropLoot 1.5, before the loot snapshot so rays and autoloot see the copies; Rift Keys are not copied) | 35, 2+ | - |
  | Cinderdeath | 1.5 s after a kill, players within 1 sqm take fire damage: 5-15% of the monster's max health, at most 300 + 150 x tier | 70, 3+ | quantity 1.2x, rarity 0.8x |
  | Blighted Mending | players receive 20-50% less healing (spells, potions, runes) | 70, 2+ | rarity 0.5x, experience 0.3x, quantity 0.2x |
  | Waning Veil | the time limit is 15-30% shorter | 70, 1+ | quantity 1x, experience 0.5x |
  | Dread Guardian | the guardian(s) +50-150% health and damage | 60, 4+ | rarity 0.2x, quantity 0.1x |

  Map modifiers, third set (2026-10-12; appended after Fragile, indexes 20-36, so old keys and refund markers decode
  unchanged). Every modifier now has a side: a **prefix** makes the monsters or the guardian stronger, a **suffix** makes
  the players or the area worse (Withering, Blighted Mending, Waning Veil and Fragile are suffixes, the boons have no side;
  the HUD shows suffixes in violet). A key carries one modifier of a `group` at most and never an `excludes` pair: rolls,
  orbs (`R.addMods`) and the Ember Tides draw around them, and `R.decodeMods` drops the second of a pair. Values are the
  tier I-V range; reward per point of value as the older ones (each sums to 15-50% at the top of tier III, the band of the
  first eight):

  | Modifier | Side, group | Effect | Range (I-V), weight, tier | Reward bonus |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | Emberbrand / Frostbrand / Stormbrand | prefix, brand | rift monsters deal +10-50% of their hit again as fire / ice / energy (the free secondary slot of the hit, else on the primary) | 10-50, 40 each, 2+ | quantity 0.5x, rarity 0.3x |
  | Keen Fangs | prefix | 5-30% of monster hits deal x1.5 | 5-30, 60, 1+ | rarity 0.8x, quantity 0.4x |
  | Ironhide | prefix | monsters take 10-40% less physical damage (Warding's physical twin; hardest on melee, arrows, bolts) | 10-40, 60, 2+ | quantity 0.75x, rarity 0.5x |
  | Festering Wounds | prefix | 10-50% of monster hits fester: 40% of the hit again as earth over 6 s (a poison condition without an owner, so nothing scales it twice) | 10-50, 50, 3+ | quantity 0.4x, rarity 0.25x |
  | Spiteglass | prefix, reflect | monsters reflect 5-22% of the elemental damage that lands (energy back; hardest on casters) | 5-22, 50, 3+ | experience 1x, quantity 0.7x |
  | Single Brood | prefix | every pack is of the run's strongest kind | flat, 40, 2+ | +12% quantity, +8% rarity |
  | Wrathful Guardian | prefix, excludes Twin Guardians | every 8 s a ring of 3 sqm around each guardian is marked, 1.2 s later it hits for 10-30% of max health (death); every 20 s 2 thralls (husks of the weakest kind, at most 6) | 10-30, 50, 4+ | rarity 0.6x, quantity 0.4x |
  | Veilbreach | prefix | 5-25% of slain pack monsters tear open a breach: 2 more monsters 0.8 s later (elite and laden by the run's shares; they do not count towards the guardian and open no breach) | 5-25, 50, 3+ | quantity 0.8x, experience 0.5x |
  | Searing Hex / Flaying Hex | suffix, hex | players take +10-40% elemental / physical damage from rift monsters | 10-40, 50 each, 2+ | quantity 0.4x, rarity 0.4x |
  | Sapping Hex | suffix, hex | players (and their summons) deal 10-30% less damage to rift monsters | 10-30, 50, 3+ | quantity 0.7x, rarity 0.4x, experience 0.3x |
  | Parched Veins | suffix, regen (never with Withering) | no mana regeneration (food regeneration swapped for one with health only; back on leaving) | flat, 50, 2+ | +10% experience, +15% quantity, +5% rarity |
  | Scorched Earth / Rimefloor | suffix, ground | every 3 s a patch (a plus of 5 tiles) within 2 sqm of each player for 6 s; standing in one costs 2-6% of max health a second (fire / ice; Rimefloor also slows 40% for 1.5 s) | 2-6, 50 each, 2+ | quantity 4x / 4.5x, rarity 3x |
  | Veilstorm | suffix | every 6 s a marked strike within 2 sqm of each player, 1.2 s later 10-30% of max health (energy) within 1 sqm | 10-30, 50, 3+ | quantity 0.8x, rarity 0.4x |

  The hits are pure functions (`R.monsterHit`: the run's damage, x Dread Guardian or x the density's pack damage, Keen
  Fangs, the brand, the hexes, Festering Wounds; `R.monsterTaken`: Warding, Ironhide, Sapping Hex and the elemental part
  for Spiteglass). Ground, storm and nova damage is a share of the player's max health with no attacker, so the rift's
  damage rules do not scale it again; a player back from a lost life is spared for its shield seconds. Not ported (no
  engine hook without a patch): less cooldown recovery, shorter potion effects (Blighted Mending covers healing), no
  leech, lower resistance caps (the engine has no caps; Searing Hex does the same job), monster curses on skills.

  The summed bonuses of a key are capped (`bonusCap`): quantity 80%, rarity 75%, experience 60%. These caps sit above
  every three-modifier sum of the first eight modifiers.

  Quantity multiplies the Chaos loot rate of the rift's kills (`loot_config.lua` rateMult) and the chest's gold, orbs
  and rolls; rarity raises the chest's gear rarity; experience multiplies the kill experience in the rift.
- **Modifier tiers (I-V; higher is better).** Every modifier but Withering has five tiers inside its value range
  (`tiers` = the top value of each, rift_config.lua). Tiers I-III are exactly the old ranges (keys saved before decode
  unchanged, nothing new is stored: the tier follows from the value); IV and V extend them (Vitality 20-90, Brutality
  15-60, Haste 40-180, Elites 50-300, Reflection 5-22, Warding 10-40, Swarm 1-5, Teeming 20-70, Gilded 30-100, Warbands
  10-40, Twin 55-85, Echo 5-25, Cinderdeath 5-25, Blight 20-70, Waning 15-40, Dread 50-250; the Coffer stays at 3 tiers
  because it is a chance). A key rolls tiers by its own tier (`modTiers.window`): keys 1-5 I-III (as before), 6-10
  I-IV, 11-15 II-V; Orbs of Fate reroll inside the same window. Names show on keys and HUD ("Vitality IV"). Each tier IV /
  V modifier raises the bonus caps (+8/+8/+6 and +16/+16/+12).
- **Lives.** A run has shared lives: 3, +1 per extra player who entered, minus Fragile (new modifier, key tier 4+,
  1-2 fewer lives, quantity 7x / rarity 7x / experience 5x the value), at least 1. A death inside is the engine's
  normal death (experience / skill / item loss with blessings and the amulet exactly as anywhere, no reduction) and costs
  one life; the next login of that character puts it back at the rift's entrance with 5 s in which rift monsters do
  not hurt it. The death that takes the last life collapses the rift (everyone out, no chest, key spent). Fallen players
  who may still return keep a run open and share the chest. HUD shows "Lives: n / max". The Flawless Seal achievement now needs no deaths.
- **Key ladder (2026-10-23).** A sealed rift's key is pity-backed: two rifts in a row without a stronger key make the third leave tier + 1, and a finisher at 1.5x the tier's entry level or more always gets a key of the tier his level fits (at most +3 a run). See "Content rewards".
- **Omens.** Sealed rifts of tier 6+ add Omen Fragments (item 32071, copy of the red crystal fragment) to every finisher's
  chest: 2 + 1 per tier above 6, x quantity; rare / legendary monsters of those rifts carry one 8% / 25%. Using 60
  fragments binds an Omen Key (item 32072, copy of the eye of the storm; attribute omen_kind) of a random kind. The key
  opens a guardian arena: a rift slot with every side room shut, level 800+, 12 minutes (10 until 2026-10-13, "Solo kill times"), the rift lives, the guardian
  after 5 s, health from its XML (+100% per extra player; was +75%), +10% damage per extra player. Guardians (rift-exclusive outfits 2116, 2117, 2118 of things_custom11, see "Rift looks" below; 500k
  health each, `monsters/chaos/omens/`): Sangrith the Bloodmoon Herald, Morvane the Hollow Crown, Thalcyra the
  Stormbound Seer. Chest per finisher: 3,000 gold x the finisher's level (at least 800; 3M at level 1000; was a flat 5M),
  4 Orbs of Upheaval, 2 Orbs of Fate (were 12 / 6), 8 item rolls (boss tier, x1.5 rarity), gems and supports as a tier
  15 rift, and 2 unique rolls over every unique at boss tier x2 find; gold, orbs and rolls x the party bonus (see "Party
  scaling" below). Achievements omen_1 / omen_10
  and one per kind. Install: `tools/install_omens.py DATA_DIR` (items.otb / items.xml) and register the omens monster
  folder. `/rift omen [kind]`, `/rift fragments [n]`, `/rift lives n` for gamemasters.
- **Dungeon difficulty** (`dungeons_difficulty.lua`): the six difficulties now do what the client panel says (the test
  compares both): monster health 100/200/320/500/800/1300%, damage to the players 100/130/190/280/400/600%, experience
  +0/75/100/200/300/400%, gold coins +0/75/100/200/300/400%, extra loot roll +0/0/15/30/45/60% of each entry's chance.
  Applied to every monster in the dungeon box during a run (also respawns). Also fixed: the queue called a missing
  Game.getPlayerByGUID, so queued runs never started.
- **Invisible rift monsters (O309, 2026-10-29).** Tester report: "bastante bicho invisivel tambem, missing sprite
  provavelmente" (a Forsaken Sanctum). Cause: pair 51 (O269) retired 42 outfits nothing "uses", scanning monster files,
  NPCs, outfit lists and scripts; the rift looks are set at runtime from `rift_config.lua`, so the scan missed 13 of
  them, and pairs 52-56 keep them blank: 2101, 2102 (Abyssal brute, elite), 2105, 2106 (Obsidian), 2109, 2110 (Crypt),
  2112, 2113 (Sanctum minion, brute) and the five big guardians 2208-2212. Every monster of those ranks drew nothing
  (the Sanctum: two of its three ranks; only the 40% that wore a variant, looks 2200-2207, showed). Pool monsters,
  summons and Omen guardians are fine: the 709 hunt entries of `bounty_pool.lua` and every Chaos monster file are checked
  against the pair's blank outfits. Interim fix, no new pair needed: `looks.undrawn` maps each blank look to one the pair
  draws (our rank variants 2200, 2203, 2204, 2201, 2206 painted over the same bases, else the family's minion look) and
  `R.drawn` applies it in the look plan; `looks.bigGuardiansOn = false` (the guardians wear the family look again).
  The real fix is a pair 57 that restores the 13 outfits (`prune_pair.py restore --ids outfit:2101,...` from the pair 51
  archive on windows-assets; the rows moved from `pair51_removed.csv` to `pair51_keep.csv`), then delete `undrawn`, turn
  `bigGuardiansOn` back on and drop the 13 ids from `PAIR_BLANK` in `tools/ci/check_content.py`. CI: `check_content.py`
  now reads every look of `rift_config.lua` `looks` (families, variants, big guardians when on) through
  `tools/ci/rift_looks.py` and fails on a look above the pair or blank in it (after `undrawn`); the same check on the
  config of before fails with 13 problems. Test: `tools/ci/rift_looks_test.py`, `tests/rift_test.lua` (no look plan wears a
  blank look).

  Started on a local server, 2026-10-13 (base, src-patches 0001-0036, `install_all.py` without the map steps, all pair 24 switches on): no new console error. Through `ChaosRift._spawnOne` with a look plan per theme: the four family guardians came with looks 2208-2211
  and their rift names, Thalcyra as an Omen guardian with 2212; with the variant roll forced to 0 every rank with a
