- **Rift names** (`rift_config.lua` `looks.names`, `R.nameOf`). Each look shows a name of its own, family word first:

  | Theme | Minion | Brute | Elite | Guardian |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | Abyssal Rift | Abyssal Spawn | Abyssal Gazer | Abyssal Shade | Abyssal Sovereign |
  | Obsidian Hall | Obsidian Hound | Obsidian Brute | Obsidian Ravager | Obsidian Colossus |
  | Ashen Crypt | Crypt Thrall | Crypt Bonehulk | Crypt Reaper | Crypt Dreadknight |
  | Forsaken Sanctum | Sanctum Sporeling | Sanctum Creeper | Sanctum Blightstone | Sanctum Warden |

  No engine change. The base engine already has `Monster:rename(name[, nameDescription])` (luascript.cpp), but a rename
  after the placement does not reach clients that already know the creature: `Monster::setName` resends the tile, and a
  known creature goes out by id only, without its name. So the name is set in onSpawn, before the placement:
  `Chaos.createMonsterNamed(type, pos, extended, force, name)` (chaos_constants.lua) holds the name in `Chaos.spawnName`,
  and an onSpawn callback in monster_tiers.lua (index -100, before every other one) renames the monster with
  `nameDescription` "a crypt thrall" / "an abyssal spawn". The first creature packet then carries the name (with the
  level, "Crypt Thrall [812]"), and so do the look text, the damage and heal lines, "A legendary ... appears!", the
  monster bar, the hunt tracker's kill list, the loot channel row, the rift HUD's guardian line and "The rift guardian ...
  tears through the veil!". Loot lines: the stock "Loot of ..." (`patch_base_events.py` step 10) and "Chaos bonus loot of
  ..." ask `Chaos.monsterNameDescription`. Ambush copies of a rift monster keep its name.
  What a monster is stays its pool type: `Chaos.monsterTypeName` (the MonsterType's name) is used by the bestiary, the
  bounty board, unique drops, rift key drops and pool levels, the ascension quest, pets, resistances (supports, item
  mods), achievements and the monster tier boss / skip lists. Invaders (invasion.lua renames them the same way) now count
  for the bestiary too. `tests/rift_test.lua` checks the ranks, that every name is its own and that no monster file has
  a rift name; `tests/monster_names_test.lua` checks the helpers. Checked in game: an
  Abyssal Gazer (Blazebringer) shows its name over the look, in the monster bar and in "Loot of an abyssal gazer";
  killing it credits the Blazebringer bestiary entry; a Grove Keeper spawned as "Crypt Thrall" counted for a Grove Keeper
  bounty (1/50); the Ashen Crypt and Forsaken Sanctum guardians showed "Crypt Dreadknight" and "Sanctum Warden" in the
  HUD and their kill credited the Tundra Troll / Lacewing Moth entries; a forced ambush on a rare Crypt Reaper brought a
  "Magic Crypt Reaper" (monster bar, Brutal) in the rift look.
  Also fixed: an ambush copy got its tier in onSpawn, where the engine has not given the monster its id yet, so its tier
  state sat under id 0 (no modifier ticks, no monster bar tier). The ambush now applies the tier after the placement.
- **Tiers.** Tier N picks its monsters from the bounty pool (`bounty_pool.lua`, only monsters that spawn on the map, no
  bosses, at least 100 health) in a level window, and needs a level: 1: 80-180 (level 100), 2: 140-240 (150),
  3: 200-320 (200), 4: 280-420 (300), 5: 380-520 (400), 6: 480-640 (500), 7: 580-740 (600), 8: 680-840 (700),
  9: 780-940 (800), 10: 880-1100 (900). Tiers 11-15 keep the tier 10 window and add +15% monster health and damage and
  +10% rewards per tier (level +25 per tier). A window with fewer than three types is widened.
- **Opening.** Use the key in a protection zone, out of combat, not multi-clienting (`Chaos.isMultiClient`), not in a
  dungeon, the tower or the world boss arena, at the tier's level. Party members within 8 sqm on the same floor come
  along (up to 5 players; was 4); members who fail a rule stay behind and both are told why.
- **The instance** is a generated map per run (see "Layouts and the slot pool" below), built at runtime with
  `Game.createTile` in a grid of 16 slots (4 x 4, 256 sqm apart, floors z 7 and 8) at x/y 20480-21503, where the map has
  no tiles (checked in the OTBM of the full map: x/y 15360-30719 hold only 26 tiles, at 16735,16438,15 and near
  18944,18944,7; other runtime areas use 2000-15359). Until 2026-10-12 each slot was one fixed 19 x 19 hub with four 15 x 15
  side rooms (1,657 tiles) at x/y 8192-8447. The first build of a slot after a start looks at every position of its
  square on both floors and refuses a slot with a map tile (marked unusable, the next one is taken). The engine has no
  Lua call to remove a tile, so a slot's tiles stay; a new layout clears the old one first (every item and creature of
  its tiles) and a tile it does not use stays empty (no ground: not walkable, drawn black).
- **The run.** Packs: with the density (below, on by default) 80 + 8 x (tier - 1) monsters solo x the map's area
  factor (about 1.7-2.1), +25% per extra player, in packs of 5-7 (+ Swarm), about 100-165 alive (+10 per extra player,
  260 at most), the rest coming in ahead of the party as it advances. Without it (`density.enabled = false`): 6 + tier/3
  + 2 per extra player, of 3-4 monsters, all at once. One type per pack; the first pack in the section nearest to the
  arrival, the rest spread over the whole map. Every monster rolls magic 10% / rare 3% / legendary 0.6%
  (x (1 + 0.05 tier) x the Elites modifier) through `ChaosApplyTier` (monster_tiers.lua; the natural spawn roll and the
  ambush also still apply). After 75% of the monsters died the guardian appears in its arena in the far corner: the strongest type of the
  rift, legendary, with 3x its base health (+100% per extra player). With a party every pack monster gets more health
  too, so the rift's total monster health is +100% per extra player (see "Party scaling"). Time limit 12-15 minutes by the map's size. The HUD (top left, under the
  character plate) shows tier, theme, time left, kills / left, the guardian, the modifiers and the bonuses.
- **End.** Guardian killed in time: the rift is sealed, the remaining monsters vanish, a reward chest (32311, the own look, falling back to 21584; action id 47402,
  "Reward chests") appears where it died and every finisher may open it once within 60 s; whoever did not gets it delivered at the exit
  (or at the next login when offline). Time up: "the rift collapses", everyone is sent back to where they used the key,
  the key is lost. Death inside: the normal death rules (temple, losses), the player is out of the run. Logout inside: the
  player is put back at their entry position and is out of the run. A run whose last player left fails.
- **Density** (`rift_config.lua` `density`, `R.density` / `R.packHealth` / `R.guardianBase` / `R.clearSeconds` in
  `rift_core.lua`, glue in `rift.lua`; owner request 2026-10-12: "350-700 monsters per endgame map elsewhere, ours seem
  much lower"). Measured from the configs and spawn logic before this change (typical = the median class of the level
  1000 table in `data/spells/README.md`, area damage x(level/1000)^1.07, x1.15 for gear as the Ascended model, 60% of
  the time hitting; the pool's monsters at their level, the late-game set at 80-185k health):

  | Tier (level) | Monsters solo / party of 5, before | Health of a normal monster, before | Typical solo clear, before | Monsters solo / party of 5, now | Health, now | Typical solo clear, now |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 1 (100) | 21 / 49 | 6.4k | 7.7 min | 78 / 162 | 1.1k | 4.7 min |
  | 3 (200) | 24.5 / 52.5 | 17k | 11.3 min | 96 / 192 | 1.9k | 4.7 min |
  | 5 (400) | 24.5 / 52.5 | 35k | 11.8 min | 114 / 222 | 3.4k | 4.7 min |
  | 8 (700) | 28 / 56 | 108k | 23 min | 138 / 270 | 5.1k | 4.7 min |
  | 10 (900) | 31.5 / 59.5 | 167k | 31 min | 150 / 306 | 6.1k | 4.7 min |
  | 12 (950) | 35 / 63 | 217k | 42 min | 168 / 336 | 5.7k (x1.3) | 6.1 min |
  | 15 (1025) | 38.5 / 66.5 | 292k | 58 min | 192 / 384 | 5.4k (x1.75) | 8.2 min |

  So before, the rifts were not short of monsters by count alone: they held 3-6 monsters a 100 tiles (open hunts have
  2.7-4.4), but each late monster was 20-40 times what a typical player kills quickly, and from tier 3 a typical solo
  player could not seal a rift in its 10 minutes (tier 10 about 31 minutes, tier 15 about an hour; untested in game,
  "balance of tiers 8-15 against geared characters" was open). Against the reference: 350-700 monsters in about 5 minutes
  is 1-2 kills a second with one-hit monsters; our combat is auto attacks every second and area spells on 2 s group
  cooldowns, so the target is fewer but quick monsters: a pack of 5-7 falls to two or three area casts, about 0.3-0.5
  kills a second solo. The curve: 80 + 8 per tier solo (tier 1 78, tier 15 192 after rounding to packs; a party of 5
  twice that, 162-384: the lower half of the reference band for a full party, a third of it solo).
  - **Health budget.** Every pack monster gets the health a typical player needs: the packs up to the guardian take
    225 s of the tier's level area damage, the guardian 55 s of single-target damage (75% of the time hitting). So tiers
    1-10 take a typical solo player about 4.7 minutes, tiers 11-15 (their +15% health a tier on top) 5.4-8.2 minutes, a
    party of 5 (4.98x the damage, the Ascended model) the same, and a player with half the damage still makes tier 10
    (`tests/rift_test.lua` checks every tier). A kind keeps its share against the run's other kinds (XML health against
    their mean, 0.5-2x), its magic / rare / legendary tier, Vitality and the party share (+100% total health per extra
    player as before, split over 25% more monsters each). Pack monsters hit x0.6 (`density.damage`): a pack is about
    twice the size of before. The guardian's base is the budget too (tier 10 about 113k before Dread / Twin / the party,
    was about 500k).
  - **Reinforcements.** The run spawns packs up to the live cap (first pass: 60, +10 per extra player, 100 at most; on
    the big maps below 100-260); the rest wait in a queue. Each second up to 2 queued packs come in, away from the
    players (first pass: the open room farthest from them, at least 9 sqm; on the big maps: the farthest unreached
    section just ahead of the party, at least 16 sqm), until the guardian appears. The guardian comes after 75% of the whole plan
    (the HUD's total), so the party has to keep moving. A monster that cannot be created leaves the plan. Veilbreach and
    thralls are extra (12 above the cap at most).
  - **Spoils stay per run.** Of the monsters, the share old / new (about 0.2-0.27) decides: elite chances (and Warbands)
    x the share, so a run has as many magic+ monsters as before; normal monsters carry loot with the share that gives as
    many laden normals as before; the others are **husks** (`Creature:setDropLoot(false)`): experience only (under the
    rift's experience cap), no corpse loot, no bounty or bestiary credit (`ChaosRift.isHusk`, asked by `bounty.lua` and
    `bestiary.lua`). Teeming, Swarm and the atlas density keep their extra loot: the share is taken against the packs of
    before with the same modifiers. Orbs, uniques, keys and Omen Fragments from kills, the gold and items of corpses
    and kill credit per run are the same as before; the chest is unchanged.
  - **Orbs an hour.** The income model above already assumed four sealed tier 15 rifts an hour; before this change a
    typical player could not seal one. Now a run of tier 15 takes 8.2 minutes, so with 3-5 minutes around it (key, travel,
    the 60 s chest, town) 4.2-5.4 runs an hour: 24-33 Orbs of Upheaval and 12-16 Orbs of Fate solo, the model's 24 / 12 up
    to +34% for a player who turns runs around in 3 minutes (inside the test's 15x hunting bound). Tier 10 at 6-8 runs
    an hour gives 19-24 Upheaval, under the tier 15 model. Not changed: the chest, the atlas orb nodes (kept at the
    owner's earlier cut). If the fast turnaround should stay at the model, the lever is `reward.chaos.perTier` /
    `divine.perTier` (x0.75).
  - **Bigger slots** (earlier the same day): a 19 x 19 hub and 15 x 15 rooms, the live cap about 5.6 monsters a 100 open
    tiles. Replaced by the generated maps (below).
  - **Big maps** (2026-10-12, second pass; owner request: "make the rifts big, much bigger than those pictures"). The
    maps are 10-30 times the old slot (8,500 / 14,800 / 21,200 walkable tiles in a typical map of the three size bands,
    was 1,081), so the density grows with them, the health budget stays, and the walk is part of the clear time:
    - *Count*: the curve above x (walkable / 1,081) ^ 0.25 (`density.area`, 1 to 2.5): x1.67 / x1.92 / x2.10 for typical
      maps. Tier 1 solo 132 (was 78), tier 10 294 (150), tier 15 402 (192); a party of 5 about twice. A smaller or
      bigger map of the band gets fewer or more (a dungeon map has 30-40% less floor than a waste).
    - *Live cap*: 60 + 10 per extra player + 0.5 per 100 walkable tiles (`density.live.per100`), at most 260: 102 / 134
      / 166 solo in typical maps (was 60). About 1 alive a 100 tiles; the plan 1.5-2 a 100 tiles.
    - *Health*: the same budget (225 s of area damage for the packs, 55 s of single-target damage for the guardian),
      over more monsters: each pack monster has about half the health of the first density pass (tier 10 3.2k, was
      6.1k). Packs stay 5-7, so area spells still hit five at a time.
    - *Walk*: the clear time adds the map's walking distance from the arrival to the arena (200 / 265 / 340 steps in a
      typical map, measured over 48 maps) x 1.8 (side branches, packs off the way) at the tier's level (engine patch
      0018's speed: 3.7 tiles a second at level 100, 7.7 at 1000; `R.tilesPerSecond`, `R.walkSeconds`): 97 s at tier 1,
      62 s at tier 10, 80 s at tier 15.
    - *Placement*: the first packs (up to the live cap) go to the map's sections (16 x 16 cells with 24+ walkable,
      `RL.sectionOrder`): the one nearest to the arrival first, the rest shuffled, so the whole map is populated; they
      come 20 monsters a step every 100 ms (`density.populate`; one step costs about what the old run start did). No pack
      within 12 sqm of the arrival, none in the arena.
    - *Reinforcements* still come from the farthest area, now taken from the party's progress: sections a player came
      within 10 sqm of count as reached; a queued pack comes in the unreached section farthest from the players among
      those up to 90 walking steps past the farthest one reached (else the nearest unreached one ahead), at least 16 sqm
      (out of sight) from every player, around the section's centre (`RL.reinforceSection`, `density.reinforce`).
    - *Clear time and the limit* (typical solo player; a party of 5 the same within 2%; half damage in brackets):

      | Tier | Map | Monsters solo / 5 | Alive solo / 5 | Pack health | Walk | Clear solo | Limit |
      |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
      | 1 | 160 x 160 | 132 / 270 | 102 / 142 | 676 | 97 s | 6.3 min (11.0) | 12 min |
      | 5 | 160 x 160 | 186 / 378 | 102 / 142 | 2.1k | 58 s | 5.6 min (10.3) | 12 min |
      | 8 | 200 x 200 | 264 / 522 | 134 / 174 | 2.7k | 67 s | 5.8 min (10.5) | 13 min |
      | 10 | 200 x 200 | 294 / 582 | 134 / 174 | 3.2k | 62 s | 5.7 min (10.4) | 13 min |
      | 12 | 240 x 240 | 354 / 708 | 166 / 206 | 2.8k (x1.3) | 80 s | 7.4 min (13.5) | 15 min |
      | 15 | 240 x 240 | 402 / 810 | 166 / 206 | 2.7k (x1.75) | 80 s | 9.5 min (17.6) | 15 min |

      Why a longer limit and not less health: the fight stays the size the owner approved with the first density pass,
      the walk is new time on top (1-1.6 minutes in the model, more for a party that explores or gets lost on a map it
      has never seen: every run is a new one). 12 / 13 / 15 minutes keep the typical clear at 44-63% of the limit (the
      first pass had 47% for tiers 1-10 and 82% at tier 15), so a half-strength player still seals tiers 1-12 and Waning
      Veil V (-40%) still leaves 7.2-9 minutes. Tests: `tests/rift_test.lua` (every tier inside 70% of its band's limit,
      half strength up to tier 12, the counts and the live cap, the walking speeds against the patch 0018 table).
    - *Orbs*: per run unchanged (owner decision: the orb rates stay as they come out). Per hour a little lower at tier
      15 (9.5 minutes a run: 4.1-4.8 runs an hour with 3-5 minutes around each, was 4.2-5.4), about the same at tiers
      1-10 (5.3-7.0 an hour).
  - **Husk deaths** (a bug of the first density pass, found in game while testing the big maps): a monster that drops
    no loot (`setDropLoot(false)`, the husks) gets no death event from the engine (`Creature::dropCorpse` runs the
    death events only for a monster with loot or a master), so husks never counted: the guardian could not come.
    `rift.lua` now counts a husk from the kill event of the player who killed it (`ChaosRiftPlayerKill`, also through
    the player's summons) and, for any monster of the run that is gone without a death the script saw, in the tick's
    sweep; every monster counts once (`RF.dead`). The per-kill effects of a husk (Cinderdeath, Veilbreach) run from the
    kill event. Checked in game: 316 and 478 kills counted, the guardian at 75%, sealed. Note for tests: a kill by a
    gamemaster also clears the loot (the engine's NotGenerateLoot flag), so such a kill gets no death event either.
  - `density.enabled = false` brings back the packs, health and loot of before exactly (`tests/rift_test.lua` keeps the
    old checks on that path).
  - Tests: `tests/rift_test.lua` (the curve, the shares, elites and laden monsters per run as before, clear times of
    every tier solo and for 5, the live cap of 16 slots, the plan's packs, Warbands, Single Brood, the reinforcement
    room; the third set: sides, groups and exclusions over 20,000 keys and the orbs, decode, effects, `R.monsterHit` /
    `R.monsterTaken`, rewards in the band, the tier 15 pace and its orbs). `tests/rift_density_test.lua` (`rift.lua` on
    a mocked engine: first packs up to the cap, the queue, budget health, husks without loot, reinforcements away from
    the player and none when every room is near one, the guardian at 75% of the whole plan with its budget health,
    Veilbreach extras, Rimefloor and Veilstorm, the Wrathful Guardian's nova and thralls, Parched Veins, a brand on a
    hit). Not run in game (no build this time): a dense run, the hazards' look, the reinforcement feel.
- **The chest** (per finisher): gold to the bank 5,000 x tier^2, Orbs of Upheaval 0.5 + 0.085 x tier, Orbs of Fate
  0.06 x tier, item rolls 2 + 0.5 x tier (each draws one entry of a random rift monster's loot table weighted by its
  chance; gear gets a rarity from `ChaosLoot.upgradeRarity` at magic (tiers 1-3) / rare (4-6) / legendary (7-10) / boss
  (11+), x the rarity bonus), one Chaos currency roll and one unique roll at that tier; gold, orbs and rolls x (1 +
  quantity bonus), then the finisher's Rift Atlas, then the party bonus. Before the reward pass (2026-10-11) it was
  10,000 x tier^2, 1 + 0.5 x tier and 0.25 x tier. Measured with the old numbers: tier 1 10k gold, 2 Chaos, 1 Divine, a
  few items; tier 7 (+40% quantity) 686k gold, 6 Chaos, 3 Divine, an [Exotic] dragon robe, potions, 11 crystal coins;
  tier 10 1M+ gold. Finishers are recorded on the weekly Rifts leaderboard (`ChaosLeaderboard.record("rift", player,
  tier)`).
- **Party scaling** (`rift_config.lua` `party`, `R.party` / `R.applyParty` / `R.partyReward` in `rift_core.lua`, tested by
  `tests/rift_test.lua`). By the players who entered (n), rifts and Omen arenas alike:

  | Players | Total monster health | Guardian health | Damage taken | Chest per finisher | Kill loot and coffer |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | x1 | x3 (the guardian's base) | x1 | x1 | x1 |
  | 2 | x2 | x6 | +10% | +12.5% | +5% |
  | 3 | x3 | x9 | +20% | +25% | +10% |
  | 4 | x4 | x12 | +30% | +37.5% | +15% |
  | 5 | x5 | x15 | +40% | +50% (cap) | +20% (cap) |

  - **Health, +100% per extra player.** The packs already grow (+2 per extra player), so each pack monster gets the rest
    of the curve: x (n x solo packs / party packs), never below 1 (tier 15, 5 players: 19 packs instead of 11, each
    monster x2.89; tier 1: 14 instead of 6, x2.14). Guardians: +100% per extra player (`boss.perExtraPlayer`, the Omen
    guardian's `omen.healthPerExtraPlayer`, was +75%). The curve is linear and at least the party's damage: a party of
    5 (four damage dealers and a healer, the Ascended balance model: 4.98x a solo player's damage) clears a rift in about
    the time one player needs, so a run per hour per head is the same as solo.
  - **Damage, +10% per extra player** (`fx.damage`, every rift monster and guardian, Omens too): the extra hits a party
    soaks are spread over more players, so a bit more damage keeps the pressure.
  - **Reward, +12.5% per extra player, capped at +50%** (a full party of 5). Every finisher still gets the whole chest, x
    the bonus: gold, orbs, item rolls and Omen Fragments (`R.partyReward`, `R.partyCount`). Linear because each extra
    player adds the same work; capped so a full party ends at about 1.5x solo per head, not 5x.
  - **Loot, +5% per extra player, capped at +20%:** the Chaos loot rate of the rift's kills (`ChaosRift.lootMult`) and the
    Sealed Coffer. A modest bonus: corpses are shared, so kill loot per head stays lower in a party (tier 15, 5 players:
    1.7x the monsters for 5 players), and the chest bonus makes up for it.
  - The run start says it in chat ("Party of 3: monster health x3, damage +20%; every chest +25%, loot +10%.").
- **Income** (level 1000, per hour; hunting is the "Respec" model: 9.5M gold, and the audit's 2.5 Orbs of Upheaval and
  1.3 Orbs of Fate). Rifting model: four sealed tier 15 rifts an hour at +128% quantity (the highest key with tier V
  modifiers), chest only (no coffer, no kill loot). The loop row is three rifts and one Omen kill an hour (three tier 15
  chests give 75 fragments, more than one key). Per head; the party rows assume the same runs per hour (see the health
  curve above). Before = the numbers before 2026-10-11 (a party could be 4 at most and cleared faster than solo).

  | Per hour | Gold | Upheaval | Fate | Gold / hunting | Upheaval / hunting | Fate / hunting |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | Hunting | 9.5M | 2.5 | 1.3 | 1x | 1x | 1x |
  | Rifts solo, before | 30.8M | 116 | 51 | 3.2x | 47x | 39x |
  | Rifts solo, after | 15.4M | 24.3 | 12.3 | 1.6x | 9.7x | 9.5x |
  | Rifts, party of 5, after | 23.1M | 36.5 | 18.5 | 2.4x | 14.6x | 14.2x |
  | Loop solo (3 rifts + 1 Omen), before | 28.1M | 99 | 44.5 | 3.0x | 40x | 34x |
  | Loop solo, after | 14.5M | 22.2 | 11.3 | 1.5x | 8.9x | 8.7x |
  | Loop, party of 5, after | 21.8M | 33.4 | 16.9 | 2.3x | 13.4x | 13.0x |
  | Full atlas + Lone Ember solo, before | 61.6M | 197 | 92 | 6.5x | 79x | 71x |
  | Full atlas + Lone Ember solo, after | 30.8M | 26.5 | 13.8 | 3.2x | 10.6x | 10.6x |
  | Full Obsidian Hall atlas + Obsidian Crown solo, after | 19.2M | 53 | 27.4 | 2.0x | 21x | 21x |

  Before, a party of 4 got the solo chest each and cleared about 2.5x faster (3.9x the damage against 1.55x the
  monsters at tier 15), so about 2.5x solo per head; now a party of 5 gets 1.5x solo per head from the chests. The
  atlas's `goldMult` and the Lone Ember / Fleeting Sanctum `rewardMult` now raise gold and item rolls only, never the
  orbs. Obsidian Crown raises the orbs by 50% (`orbsMult` 1.5, about 16x hunting with a full Hall atlas; it was x2, 21x) for a guardian twice as strong.
  `tests/rift_test.lua` checks the solo and party rows against these bounds.
- **Keys.** A sealed rift drops one key (to the player who used the key, else a random finisher) with 30% + 10% per
  modifier (max 60%); of those 50% + 10% per modifier are the next tier (with more modifiers), the rest the same tier.
  Rare / legendary monsters inside a rift carry a key of its tier 2% / 6% of the time. Tier-1 keys: normal kills outside
  rifts (EventCallback onDropLoot, after the Chaos loot layer, before autoloot) with 50 in 100,000 per kill x (magic 3,
  rare 8, legendary 20, boss 40) when the monster (one of the bounty pool) has a hunting level (`Chaos.monsterHuntingLevel`)
  of at least max(60, killer level x 0.4) and the killer is level 100+ (O284; O285: `baseLevelMult` 1, so the pool
  level for a base monster); completed bounty contracts give one 25% (hunt) / 50% (elite) / 100% (boss) of the time (`bounty.lua` calls
  `ChaosRift.onBountyPaid`).
- **Crafting.** Every crafting orb works on a key (Awakening / Gilding on a key without modifiers, Grafting up to
  `key.maxMods` = 3, Unmaking, Erasure, Upheaval rerolls them, Fate rerolls their values; Tempering and Excision work on a key too), by "Use with" or on the
  bench; see "Crafting".
- **Experience** comes only from the kills, with a cap so a dense rift cannot beat open hunting: the base experience of a
  kill (monster experience x the monster-level bonus x the stage x the magic/rare/legendary multiplier) counts against
  an allowance of 1.1 x the leveling model's base rate at the player's level (the sorcerer hours of "The leveling model",
  the fastest vocation) per minute in the run; above it a kill gives 2% of its experience. Stamina, potions, the Chaos
  bonuses and the rift's Experience bonus apply on top, as when hunting. Measured at level 1000, tier 10: 32 monsters
  killed in the first second gave 13.8M experience instead of ~220M (the first minute's allowance is 3.2M base).
- **Restart and crash refund.** Using the key writes a "run in progress" marker (tier and modifiers, storages
  7100400-7100404) and saves the player before the teleport. It is cleared, and saved, when the key's owner leaves the run
  (end, death, logout) and set again when the owner returns after a death with lives left. The marker is the only record
  of the refund: it is cleared in the same step the key is given and saved with it, so a key comes back once.
  - *Clean shutdown or closed server* (the daily server save with `serverSaveShutdown`/`serverSaveClose`, SIGTERM/systemd
    stop, `/closeserver [shutdown]`, the admin panel's shutdown): an `onShutdown` event, and for a closed server (which
    has none) the first kick's `onLogout`, end every open run before the players are kicked (`ChaosRift.interrupt`). Everyone
    goes to the temple (and is saved there). Guardian still alive: the key's owner, if still in the run, gets the key back
    (same tier and modifiers; an omen arena its Omen Key) with "The server is restarting: your rift closes and its key is
    returned". Guardian dead (chest up): no key; unclaimed chest shares of the players online are handed out as at a normal
    exit. Without this the kick read as "logged out inside" and the key was lost.
  - *Crash* (`kill -9`, power loss: no event): the next login returns the key ("Your last rift was interrupted by a server
    restart ...") and a character saved inside a rift slot goes to its temple. A logout, a death or the timer clear the
    marker first, so none of them gives a key back, not even across a crash. A character removed without a logout event
    while the server keeps running gets nothing, then or after a restart (the marker is deleted from the database).
  - Not refunded: a run whose key owner had left (logout, or a death without returning) when the server stopped; chest
    shares of finishers who were offline at the exit live only in memory and are lost at a restart.
  - `tests/rift_refund_test.lua` (rift.lua against a mocked engine) covers all of these.
- **Other systems.** `ChaosRift.isInside(player)`; the temple scroll refuses inside a rift (`shop_services.lua`), a second
  character of the connection cannot log in while one is in a rift (`multiclient.lua`).
- **Layouts and the slot pool** (`rift_layout_core.lua`, `rift_config.lua` `layout` / `build`, the rift themes of
  `areagen_config.lua`; owner request 2026-10-12). Every run gets a map of its own from the area generator ("Generated
  areas"): the arrival in one corner, the guardian's arena (a chamber of radius 9 kept clear, in a dungeon a 21 x 21
  room) in the opposite one, loops and side branches, holes and ladders between two floors where the theme has them.
  - *Size by tier* (O309, 2026-10-29): tiers 1-5 144 x 144, 6-10 176 x 176, 11-15 208 x 208 (a two-floor map 0.72 x the
    side on each floor, about the area of one floor; an open waste 0.85 x, it fills more of its square). Was 160 / 200 /
    240, two floors 0.8, no kind scale. 48 maps measured (4 themes x 3 bands x 4 seeds, `tools/rift_layout_model.lua`),
    before -> now: walkable tiles 7,100-12,200 -> 4,800-6,900 (band 1), 11,700-19,200 -> 8,200-10,500 (band 2),
    15,200-27,700 -> 12,100-14,500 (band 3); a walk of up to 423 steps from the arrival to the arena (was up to 412, the way is not the problem); the
    hunting areas of item 109 are 66 x 52 to 100 x 80 with 1,000-5,000 walkable tiles.
  - *Size against monsters* (O309; tester report: "mapas absurdamente grandes e com densidade muito baixa pelo tamanho,
    fiquei 10min so andando", a tier 6 Forsaken Sanctum, 168 of 214 slain, mostly empty floor). The plan grew with the
    map only by (walkable / 1081) ^ 0.25, so a bigger map was a thinner one: before, 39-84 walkable tiles a planned
    monster (band 2 at tier 6: 54-65) and 101-140 a live one. Now `density.area.tilesPerMonster` = {33, 27} (tier 1, tier 15, linear) is a floor of the
    plan (`R.densityCount`: at least walkable / that many monsters solo, a party's growth on top; the tier's own count still
    rules on a small map), and `density.live.per100` is 1.0 (was 0.5): 27-33 tiles a monster and 45-71 a live one
    everywhere (band 1 144-222 monsters, band 2 264-360, band 3 420-534; the pack health budget is per run, so the
    monsters are weaker and the clear time is the same; the first tier of a band has weaker monsters than the last of
    the band before, its map holding more of them). The full sweep of a map (walkable / 8 steps of width at the
    tier's walking speed) took up to 410 / 359 / 449 s in the three bands (the same width on the old maps) and now takes at
    most 232 / 198 / 235 s. `layout.typical` was refitted (5,875 / 9,133 / 13,463 walkable, route 159 / 203 / 263).
    The model is `server/tools/rift_layout_model.lua` (no flag: the table per layout and band tier; `--check` in CI,
    both interpreters; `--typical` the new `layout.typical`), the limits `rift_layout_balance_config.lua` (tiles per
    monster 34, per live monster 75, sweep 300 s and 30% of the time limit, way to the arena 150 s, walkable per band,
    spread of a band 1.5x, `typical` within 15% of the mean); `tests/rift_layout_model_test.lua` pins the floor, the
    kind scale and that the layouts of before fail the check (271 problems on the 48 maps of before, 0 now).
  - *Kind and floors by theme* (`layout.themes`, weighted per run): Abyssal Rift an open waste (55) or a cave system
    (45), one floor; Obsidian Hall a ruined complex (65) or marble halls cut into rock (mixed, 35), one or two floors;
    Ashen Crypt catacombs: a cave with ruined chambers (50) or a ruined complex (50), always two floors; Forsaken
    Sanctum a cave system (65) or a cave with chambers (35), one or two floors. The palettes keep each theme's look: the
    old rift floors without the dark set; with it obsidian and magma with ash, moss and lava (Abyssal), black marble
    halls with pillars and braziers (Obsidian), ash soil and bone earth with moss, bones and catacomb rooms (Crypt),
    wet and mossy rock with moss and glowcaps and worn stone chambers (Sanctum). Every id is checked against the live
    items.otb and pair (`areagen_export.py check`: 211 ids stock, 280 with the dark set, 0 problems).
  - *Seeded*: the builder draws the seed of each layout; one seed always gives the same map (LuaJIT and Lua 5.3), and
    the run's log line names it, so `tools/areagen_export.py preview OUT ... --area "rift:<theme>:<band>:<seed>"`
    draws the map a player saw. A map the validator rejects (a link that did not fit) is made again with another
    seed (none in 48 + 36 test maps).
  - *The slot pool*: a slot is empty, building, ready, busy, dirty (a run ended there) or bad (a map tile in its
    square). A key takes a ready slot of the asked theme and size band, else another theme of the band, else the theme
    in another band, else any ready slot (the slot's map decides theme, size and time limit). The builder keeps
    `build.poolReady` = 6 slots ready from the start and rebuilds every slot a run left; the next layout's theme and band
    are the ones the keys asked for most against what is ready (decayed counts). No ready slot: the player hears the
    wait and waits in line ("Instance limits"), and is told when a slot is ready.
  - *Build cost*: one job at a time; the generator runs in a coroutine and yields every 10 ms of game loop
    (`build.sliceMs`; areagen_core.lua calls `opts.tick` in its long loops, never inside a sort), the clean-up and the
    tiles go in the same steps, one step every 40 ms (`build.everyMs`). Measured on the test server (cropped map, every
    Chaos script, a machine shared with other test servers at load 5-20 on 4 cores, so the times are high): a whole
    layout cost 0.30-1.35 s of game loop for 14,000-30,000 tiles and 1.45-1.8 s for 44,000-45,000 (clearing the old map
    included), spread over 27-130 steps in 3-15 s; the median step 15-21 ms, a few 30-80 ms under that load (in LuaJIT
    alone, unloaded, the longest stretch between two yields of the generator is 12 ms and a whole 240 x 240 layout
    generates in 0.3-0.5 s). Nothing comes near the 100 ms slow task line in normal load or the 250 ms stalls of "Game
    loop stalls". Building a 200 x 200 map in one task would have been 0.6-1.4 s: a stall, so the build is never done
    in the task that uses a key. Opening a run: the key use itself took 24 ms under that load (18 of them the database save of the
    refund marker, as before), then the first packs 20 monsters every 100 ms (one such step 28-93 ms under that load),
    reinforcements 2 packs a second in the rift's tick (30-66 ms under that load).
  - *Memory*: a layout keeps about 0.7 MB of Lua (sorted keys of its walkable cells and of its built tiles, the
    sections); the tile model (up to 50 MB of Lua while it is made) is dropped once built. In the engine a slot holds up
    to 50,500 tiles with 64,000 items (about 15 MB at the 300 bytes a tile of "Instance limits"); since tiles are never
    freed, a slot that saw many layouts holds at most its square on both floors (131,072 positions, about 26 MB with
    the empty ones). 16 slots: about 250 MB typical, 420 MB at the very worst, next to the 18.2 million tiles of the full
    map. Monsters: at most 260 + 12 per run, 4,350 for 16 runs, but only those near a player are active (the engine
    idles the others), so the creature checks see about one hunting group per rift as before.
  - *Cap*: 16 slots and 16 parallel runs (rifts and Omen arenas) as before, 6 kept ready. The cap stays because the
    load of a run is its active monsters near the party and its 1 s tick, not the size of its map; the memory above is
    the price of the size. A smaller grid (`grid.cols` / `rows`) and `limits.maxRuns` lower both.
  - *Omen arenas* take a ready map (their theme's when one is ready, any size): the party arrives at the mouth of its
    guardian's arena, the rest of the map stays empty.
  - The map overlay forgets the minimap of the slot's square on both floors at the start of every run (`map_marks.lua`).
  - Tests: `tests/rift_layout_test.lua` (every theme in every band, stock and dark: valid, the band's size inside its
    slot, the arena far, reachable and open, sections over the map, deterministic and varied; every kind a theme rolls;
    the typical numbers of the model; sections reached, reinforcements ahead, spawn cells; the pool on a mocked engine:
    built in many short steps, every tile built, a slot over a map tile refused, ready slots by theme and band, a slot
    rebuilt after its run with nothing of the old map left, the demand steering the next build). `rift_density_test`
    runs on a generated map (populate steps, every monster on a walkable cell, none near the arrival, packs over the
    whole map, husk kills). Checked in game (test server above, one client, a level 1000 character): the pool built at
    the start, a tier 8 run on a 200 x 200 Abyssal waste (269 monsters, 13 minutes, packs spread, the lives and the
    return at the arrival after a death), a tier 12 and a tier 13 Ashen Crypt (two floors, 383 and 478 monsters:
    every kill counted, reinforcements 15 a second ahead, the guardian at 75%, sealed with the chest), the slot
    rebuilt with a new map after the run. Screenshots and previews of the owner pass are not in the repository.
- **Commands.** Adventure > Rifts (dialog: the run status and every key carried with its modifiers). Gamemasters: `/rift key <tier>
  [count | mods]`, `/rift status` (runs, the state of every slot and its map, the builder), `/rift fail`; `key`, `omen`
  and `fragments` hand out value and need an administrator (group 5, `Chaos.staffCommand`).

**Edits to shared files** (one line or block each): `map_marks.lua` (the rift square per floor), `atlas_core.lua`
(the Swift time of a tier from the rift model, `A.swiftSeconds`; see "Rift Atlas"), `tools/gen_codex_data.lua` (the run text of the Codex),
`areagen_core.lua` / `areagen_config.lua` / `tools/areagen_dump.lua` / `tools/areagen_export.py` (see "Generated
areas"), `chaos_constants.lua` (`ChaosOpcodes.rift = 228`,
`Chaos.storage.riftRun = 7100400`), `loot_config.lua` (rateMult x `ChaosRift.lootMult(ctx)`), `shop_services.lua`
(`S.teleportBlocked`), `multiclient.lua` (`insideInstance`), `bounty.lua` (`payContract` calls `ChaosRift.onBountyPaid`),
`monster_tiers.lua` (an ambush copy wears the killed monster's outfit and name, so a rift look carries over; the onSpawn rename callback for `Chaos.createMonsterNamed`; the boss and skip lists by type name), `bounty.lua` and `bestiary.lua` (`B.onKill` / `X.onKill`: no credit for a density husk, `ChaosRift.isHusk`), and the type-name lookups (`Chaos.monsterTypeName`) in `bestiary.lua`, `bounty.lua`, `loot.lua`, `pets.lua`, `supports.lua`, `item_mods.lua`, `achievements.lua`, `ascension_quest.lua` (see "Rift names").

## New players (`newplayer.lua`, `newplayer_core.lua`, `newplayer_config.lua`, `newplayer_tutorial.lua`)

Roadmap items 21 and 22. Every number, item and text is in `newplayer_config.lua`; the pure logic (kit lookup, flags,
milestones, island layout, station state machine) in `newplayer_core.lua`, tested by `tests/newplayer_test.lua`. Storages
`Chaos.storage.newPlayer` = 7100250 - 7100269 (kit, welcome, tutorial stage / done mask / kills / orb count / flags,
+7 the tutorial island time of earlier sessions, +8 the wearable kit given, +9 the level 1 stats checked, milestones at
+10..+19); `Chaos.storage.tutorialSnapshot` = 7102750 -
7102779 (the character at the island's start, "Tutorial reset"; `tests/newplayer_reset_test.lua`). Tested in game on the test server (fresh level 1 characters, see "Verified" below).

- **The start** (owner design 2026-10-16: no tutorial island). A new character is created at level 8 with exactly that
  level's experience (4200), its class's level 8 health, mana, capacity and soul, its class look in its class's start
  colours, town Cinderhold and position 0,0,0 (the temple), on every creation path (see "Starting stats" below). Its
  first login, in the login event itself: the temple of the main city and the **full kit** (worn gear, weapon, the two
  Everfull potions, food, rope, shovel, temple scroll, gold), so its first frame shows it in Cinderhold wearing the kit.
  A moment later the welcome text goes to the chat and the welcome toast carries `openHelper` (`welcome.helper`): the
  client opens the Helper window with its Auto setup button blinking and the hint "Set up your helper in one click"
  (`game_helperrotation/onboarding.lua`; an older client shows only the toast). The welcome modal is off
  (`welcome.window`). The tutorial island is switched off (`tutorial.enabled = false`, its code kept): a character
  still on it leaves it at its next login (`tutorialFinish` "closed": the island's reset, the temple, the full kit,
  then the start level and stats). Next Goals has no "Reach level 8" any more (`goals_config.lua`).
- **Kit** (one time): a character logging in for the very first time (`lastLoginSaved` 0, kit storage unset) gets the kit of
  its class, in two parts (2026-10-16, owner report: "the character still starts in this ugly place without any
  equipment"; without the island both parts come at once at the first login). The **wearable part** (`NP.giveWearable`, storage +8) comes the moment it arrives on the tutorial island,
  before the island's snapshot: weapon and armour equipped (into the backpack when the slot is taken) and a backpack with
  the two Everfull potions (`ChaosPotions.giveAll`). The **rest** (`NP.giveKit`) comes when the island ends (exit, skip,
  time limit): the real weapon of a level-gated class (the Mystic's wand of vortex), the kit's own backpack rows (the
  Thief's throwing stars), 20 brown mushrooms, rope, shovel (the island needs neither), the store's Temple Teleport Scroll (3 uses, same item and attributes as `shop_services.lua`) and
  500 gold. Kits by class id (`Chaos.classes.ids`): Warrior / Juggernaut 4/8 jagged sword + dwarven shield + brass set;
  Berserker 14 battle axe (two-handed: the class takes no shield) + brass set; Ranger / Deadeye / Beastmaster 3/7/15 bow (no
  arrows: bows fire without ammunition) + chain helmet, ranger's cloak, studded legs; Mystic / Elementalist / Illusionist 1/5/10 wand of vortex (the scorcher
  is equipped below level 7, the wand waits in the backpack) + spellbook + magician's robe; Thief 11 dagger + 30 throwing stars
  + leather set; Ninja 12 the same plus a second dagger; Samurai 13 the same with a katana instead of the dagger; Monk /
  Shadowfist / Iron Sage 17-19 leather set, no weapon (they fight unarmed); Necromancer / Lich / Bone Lord 20-22 the Mystic's
  kit; Templar / Inquisitor / Sentinel 23-25 the Warrior's (one-handed sword and shield). A vocation without a row falls back to its base class (`Chaos.classes.baseOf`, then the engine's demotion), then to
  `default` (short sword, wooden shield). Every kit weighs under ~360 oz (a level 1 character carries 400-470); what does
  not fit goes to the inbox. No kit carries stock health or mana potions (owner 2026-10-16): the only starting potions
  are the two Everfull ones (`tests/newplayer_test.lua` checks every kit). Without the island both parts come at the
  first login; a character already on the island when this came gets the wearable part at its next login there (the
  snapshot's armor count follows it, `NP.snapshotAddItems`). `/newplayerkit <name>` gives both parts again. Existing characters never get a kit by logging in. Messages read the class name from `Vocation(id)`.
- **Starting stats** (`start_stats.lua`, one row per class with its level 1 values and its vocation gains;
  `tests/start_stats_test.lua`): the level 1 row follows the gains (Warrior 185 / 35 / 470, Ranger 165 / 60 / 440,
  Mystic 150 / 90 / 400, Thief and Monk 175 / 45 / 455, Necromancer 155 / 80 / 410, Templar 180 / 40 / 465; ascended
  classes like their base); a character starts at `startLevel` 8 with the row plus 7 levels of gains (Warrior 290 / 70
  / 645, Ranger 235 / 165 / 580, Mystic 185 / 300 / 470, Thief 259 / 115 / 609). Before, every creation path wrote ZnoteX's or the database's flat 150 health / 0 mana / 400 cap, so a
  level 1 Mystic could not cast or drink a mana potion. Every path reads this file: the website and the client's API
  (`plugins/chaos/lib.php` `chaos_apply_start_stats` on the `character.created` hook), the Linux package's
  `add-account.sh` (which also writes the class look and colours, the main city and position 0,0,0, as the website does;
  the test runs it), the Windows test accounts (`test_accounts.sql`, checked by the test). The login correction
  (`NP.fixStats`, once per character, storage +9): a new character or one the island had, without its kit and below
  the start level, gets exactly level 8's experience (`NP.raiseToStart`; an old character without a kit row keeps its
  level); then a character up to `fixUpToLevel` (8) below its class's values for its level is raised to them (never
  lowered) and filled up (an island snapshot gets the new values, `NP.snapshotSetStats`).
- **Inflated maximums** (live error 2026-10-24, `getNumber(). Argument 3 has out-of-range value` in the passive
  tree's `applyCharStats`): the flat max health / mana parameter of a fractional percent is clamped into int32
  (`ChaosPassiveFlatMax`, `passivetree_effects.lua`). Every login `NP.repairInflated` (`newplayer_core.lua`) resets a
  base maximum health or mana to the class's value for the level (`NP.statsFor`) when it is above both
  `inflated.floor` (1 000 000) and `inflated.factor` (20) x that value (`newplayer_config.lua`), and brings current
  health and mana down to the new maximum. No flag: a repaired character is under the margin, and a legitimate one
  is nowhere near it (tests: `start_stats_test.lua`, `passivetree_effects_test.lua`).
- **Start look** (owner report 2026-10-16, a website Ranger "Jokr" that looked like a mage in a blue robe and a
  headband): every path gave the right look type (the Ranger's hooded archer, 2163 / 2164; the website, the client API,
  `add-account.sh` and the first login all read `class_looks_core.lua`, and the classes' donor outfits are not worn at
  login). The class looks are colour templates, and the website's starter colours (head 78 yellow, body 68 blue) turned
  the archer's cloak into a blue robe. Each base class now has start colours (`L.startColors`, e.g. the Ranger forest
  green and browns), put on at creation (website `chaos_apply_class_look`, `add-account.sh`) and at the first login
  (`L.startOutfit`). `tests/start_stats_test.lua` checks every base class's start look (male and female) is its own,
  and add-account.sh's; the website test checks its looks and colours against the Lua.
- **Home town** (one time, `homeTown`): a brand-new character (no kit yet) moves to the main city, Cinderhold (town 2),
  at its first login, before the tutorial island; its temple, respawn and Town Portal are there from then on. Towns in
  `homeTown.keep` are kept as chosen; `id = 0` turns it off; characters with their kit keep their town. See "Main city".
- **Test characters** (the Windows package's `tools/windows/test_accounts.sql`, and the Linux package's with
  `CHAOS_TEST_ACCOUNTS=1`; test-only, the website's and the client's characters are not touched): Chaos Admin and
  Test Warrior / Ranger / Mystic / Thief start in town 2 at the temple of Cinderhold (32369, 32241, 7, `data/chaos_poi.lua`)
  with `lastlogin` 0 and the tutorial stage storage (7100252) at 101, skipped: their first login gives the kit of their
  class and level and the welcome at once, no island. Before (winpkg-35) they had town 1 and the island took them at the
  first login, so they started bare. To try the island with one: `/newplayerkit <name>, reset`, then `, tutorial`.
  `tests/newplayer_reset_test.lua` checks the SQL's key, stage, town and temple against the Lua side.
- **The base server's starting items:** `creaturescripts/firstitems.lua` only equips vocation 0, which the kit skips
  (`skipVocations`), so nothing is given twice. The base starter chest (`scripts/customs/actions/first_chest.lua`, action id
  and storage 33735, old vocation ids only) is marked as opened when the kit is given (`baseChestStorage`), so nobody collects
  both. **Starter chest removed (owner request 2026-10-27):** the chest is not needed any more, so `install_all.py` step
  `startchest` (`tools/patch_start_chest.py`, test `patch_start_chest_test.py`) cuts every map item with action id 33735
  (the chest, with its contents, whatever look it wears) off its tile and renames
  `data/scripts/customs/actions/first_chest.lua` to `first_chest.lua.chaos-off`, so the base script and its floating "Collect
  First Items!" text are not registered. Any other `.lua` / `.xml` file that still holds the text is only listed in the
  step's output (hint, never changed). The base files are not in this repo, so the text's exact source could not be read:
  the step finds it by scanning the installed data. Idempotent; `<map>.otbm.bak` is written first. `baseChestStorage` is
  now moot and harmless. VPS: run the `startchest` step (`install_all.py SERVER_DIR --only startchest`), then restart
  the server.
- **Welcome** (one time, after the kit): a server modal window (client `game_modaldialog`) with the next steps (Character > Spellbook, the

  `newplayer`, type NEW_PLAYER, added to `notifications.lua`). The tutorial island is the starter quest line.
- **Milestone gifts** at levels 20 / 50 / 100 / 200, once per character (a storage each, so a death and the same level-up
  again give nothing), on level-up (`onAdvance`; a jump over several milestones gives each): potions by role (each role gets
  only potions the base `potions.lua` lets it drink; the Thief line the unrestricted ones), 1 / 2 / 3 / 5 Orbs of Upheaval and 2
  Stamina Extensions (the store item) at 100. Backpack first, inbox when full; a message and a toast.
- **API:** `ChaosNewPlayer.kitFor(vocationId)` returns a copy of a class's kit; `ChaosNewPlayer.setKit(name, def, {ids})`
