- **Staff:** `/newplayerkit <name>` gives the kit again (ignores the flag); `, welcome` shows the welcome; `, milestone <n>`
  gives gift n; `, reset` clears every new-player storage (and the tutorial snapshot); `, tutorial` sends the character to the island's first station.
  Online characters only; every use in the admin audit log (`Chaos.staffCommand`); the kit, a milestone and `reset` need
  an administrator (group 5).

### Tutorial island (`newplayer_tutorial.lua`)

**Switched off since 2026-10-16** (owner design: the start above). Everything below holds when `tutorial.enabled` is
set back to true.

**Limits** (`newplayer_config.lua` `tutorial.timeLimitMinutes`, "Instance limits"): a character spends at most 30 minutes online on the island (offline time does not count; storage 7100257 keeps the time of earlier sessions), warnings at 5 and 1 minute; then it leaves as with Skip tutorial (the kit, the welcome, its temple). A login past the limit leaves at once. `/instances tutorial` lists the characters on the island; `/instances close tutorial <name>` sends one out.

Built at startup with `Game.createTile` like the world boss arena (nothing is saved to the map, base data is never
touched, a rebuild adds nothing twice): footprint x 4586-4654, y 4590-4620, z 7 (the map has no tiles within x/y
4500-5600; every tile is checked first and the island is not built over foreign tiles, then new characters get their
kit at the first login instead). The tiles come from `NP.islandModel` (`newplayer_core.lua`, pure, tested): five 7 x 9
grass pens side by side, closed by a wooden fence (pieces by neighbours, measured on the live map with
`tools/map/derive_borders.py`) with a gap in each divider as the gate (action id 47504); a dirt path along the pens with
a branch to each white marble lesson tile (47501), grass edges on the path; an angel statue (47502, use: read the
lesson again) and a signpost (same action) in every pen, coal basins, flowers and grass tufts along the fences; a
goblin statue (47503, skip) beside the arrival tile and a magic forcefield exit (47505) in the last pen. Around the
fence three tiles of land the player cannot reach (trees, bushes, flowers, lit street lamps by every gate), a shore
border all round, a wooden dock with a bollard, a barrel and a moored boat on the west shore, then water out to where
the client's largest view (29 x 21, `game_chaosview`) plus one tile ends from any pen tile: the view never shows an
unmapped (black) tile (2026-10-16; before, two rows of water left a black band on the west and north edges).
`tests/newplayer_test.lua` checks the footprint, the closed fence (from the arrival only the pens and gates are
reachable), the view corners and every id against the config. Preview with the map tools:
`python3 -I server/tools/areagen_export.py preview OUT ITEMS.otb ITEMS.xml Tibia.dat Tibia.spr --area tutorial`
(`tools/areagen_dump.lua tutorial` prints the model).

A brand-new character (first login, no kit yet, a class with a kit) arrives in the first pen instead of the temple,
wearing its class's starter gear. The first window is a choice (`NP.showArrival`, `tutorial.arrival`): **Start
tutorial** (lesson 1) or **Skip to Cinderhold** (the temple, the rest of the kit, gold), with a toast and a chat line
pointing at the goblin statue beside the arrival. Each station opens a lesson (modal window + toast) when entered; its gate opens east only when the task is done:
1. Moving and fighting: kill 3 rats (spawned in the first pen when the lesson is closed, the lesson tile is stepped on, or
   after 20 s; at most 3 alive). Detected with a `kill` CreatureEvent.
2. Spells: open Character > Spellbook (`ChaosSpellbook.sendTo` is wrapped at startup: the command and the client button both pass there)
   and cast the class spell (Warrior Salve of Scars `saen tin brak`, Ranger / Mystic Arcane Stitch `saen tin`), detected by
   the spell group cooldown condition (polled every 300 ms). A level 1 character with too little mana gets its maximum raised
   to the spell's cost once (no class needs it since the level 1 stats, `start_stats.lua`). The Thief line has no spell below level 20: opening the spellbook is enough.
3. Passive tree: one free passive point (`passiveExtraPoints` +1, taken back when the character leaves); allocating it and pressing Apply Plan completes the
   station (a listener in `ChaosPassiveTree.listeners`).
4. Orbs: an Orb of Upheaval and a Common (rarity 1) leather armor; the station completes when the orb is used (the character's orb
   count drops: the stock action and the crafting bench both consume it). The lesson mentions Economy > Crafting Bench when `ChaosCrafting`
   is loaded.
5. Keystones, Adventure > Bounty Board, the store and the top menu: information; the forcefield then sends the character to its temple with
   the kit and the welcome.

The arrival window's Skip to Cinderhold, Character > Services > Leave Tutorial, the goblin statue beside the arrival or
the station 1 lesson's "Skip tutorial" button leave at once with the kit. Characters that existed
before never enter the island. Safety: no PvP on the island (`EventCallback onTargetCombat`; runtime tiles cannot get the
protection-zone flag); nobody dies there (a hit that would kill leaves 1 health and the character is healed; a death anyway,
e.g. elsewhere, is answered at the next login); logging out and in, or a death, puts the character back in the pen of its
station; monsters cannot leave (water and walls, gates push monsters back); multi-client characters are welcome.

### Tutorial reset (`newplayer_core.lua` `NP.takeSnapshot` / `NP.tutorialReset`, owner report on winpkg-35)

**The bug.** Skipping the tutorial (or finishing it) kept what the island had given: the levels of the rats (x10 stage:
150 experience, level 2), the station 2 max mana raise, the free passive point, the Orb of Upheaval, the leather armor
and the backpack. The character reached the temple stronger than a new one, with the island's gear next to its kit.

**The fix.** What the island gives is lent, by the exit as by a skip, the time limit or `/instances close`:
- `NP.tutorialStart` stores the character as it is (`NP.takeSnapshot`): level, experience (hi x 1e9 + lo), every skill
  level and its tries, magic level and mana spent, max health, max mana, capacity, the leather armors and orbs it owns.
  Storages `Chaos.storage.tutorialSnapshot` = 7102750 - 7102779 (`NP.SNAP`). An existing snapshot is kept: a staff
  restart of the island never records what the first run gave. It lives in storages, so a logout keeps it.
- On the island no skill or magic level advances: an `EventCallback onGainSkillTries` at index 1000 (after every
  multiplier) returns 0 for a character in stages 1-5 (`NP.skillTriesFilter`). Lua cannot lower a skill, so the gain is
  stopped instead. Experience still comes (the rats show it) and is taken back.
- `NP.tutorialFinish` sets the final stage, then runs `NP.tutorialReset` before the temple and the kit:
  the free passive point back (`passiveExtraPoints` -1; a preset that now holds more nodes than the points is emptied
  for free, `NP.passiveRefund`); every item tagged with the custom attribute `tutorial.lentTag` (`chaos_tutorial`: the
  leather armor, and the backpack when the island made it, with what is in it), equipped, in a container or in the
  inbox, and the orb if station 4 was not done; experience set back exactly (an `addExperience` overshoot from bonus
  callbacks is removed again), skills and magic level raised back to the snapshot (what a death took; exact tries past
  every multiplier, `NP.exactTries`), max health, max mana and capacity from the snapshot, then full health and mana;
  the island's storages (done, kills, orbBase, flags, islandUsed) and the snapshot cleared. The stage stays 100 / 101.
- It runs once: `NP.tutorialFinish` returns at once for a character that is not on the island (a second skip, the
  statue's window and `!skiptutorial` both answered), and a second `NP.tutorialReset` finds nothing to undo.
- A death on the way (the island's guard keeps it rare): the login puts the character back at its station; the reset
  then raises level and skills back to the snapshot. A logout between the end and the kit (it comes 1 s later): the
  next login gives it (`NP.kitDueAfterTutorial`).
- A character that began the island before this change has no snapshot: its items, the point and the island storages
  go, its level stays (the console line says "no snapshot").
- The console logs each end: level before and after, skill levels raised back, items taken back, the passive point.
`tests/newplayer_reset_test.lua`: a mocked engine player (experience with a 50% bonus callback, skills with a x2 buff and
the island filter) through skip, exit, the orb used, an untagged armor, the character's own backpack, orbs and armor,
logout, a staff restart, a death with level, skill and magic level lost, a level 8 start, experience past 32 bits, no
snapshot, the second skip, and the Windows test characters' SQL. Not verified in game yet.

**Verified in game (test server, cropped map with a test-only temple floor):** first login lands on the island with lesson 1;
the death guard and the heal; logout / relog and death mid-tutorial resume at the station; each station's task (kills through
real kill events, Character > Spellbook + `saen tin brak`, a passive node applied in the client, the Orb of Upheaval used on the armor from the
client); the exit to the temple with the Warrior kit and the welcome; "Skip tutorial" (Ranger) and Character > Services > Leave Tutorial (Mystic:
scorcher equipped, wand in the backpack); relog gives no second kit; milestones 20, then 50 + 100 in one jump, nothing after
losing and regaining level 20; `/newplayerkit` and its options. Not verified: PvP block (needs two clients), the island build
refusal over foreign tiles, the full stations for the Thief line beyond 1-2.

## Patch notes (`patchnotes.lua`, `patchnotes_core.lua`, `data/patchnotes/*.md`, client `game_patchnotes`)

Weekly patch notes for players (roadmap item 23). Client: `client/overlay/modules/game_patchnotes` (Social > Patch Notes
in the top menu, or Social > Patch Notes), extended opcode 244 (`ChaosOpcodes.patchnotes`), table `chaos_patchnotes` (created at
startup if missing; also `sql/chaos_patchnotes.sql`). The notes live on the server, so new notes never need a client update.

- **Files.** One Markdown-ish file per week or version in `data/patchnotes/` (copy `server/data/patchnotes/` there), named
  `<id>.md` (e.g. `2026-10-08.md`; the id is the name without `.md`). Format (parser: `patchnotes_core.lua`):
  `# Title`, an optional `Date: YYYY-MM-DD` line (else the date at the start of the file name), free text before the first
  section (the intro), then `## New`, `## Changes`, `## Fixes`, `## Balance` (other headings are kept and drawn in plain
  colour). Bullets `- ` (or `* `, `+ `), sub-bullets indented by 2+ spaces, indented lines without a dash continue the
  bullet above, `- **Lead.** text` gives the bullet a highlighted lead, `<!-- ... -->` is ignored, `**`/`__`/backticks
  and `[text](link)` markers are removed. `README.md` and drafts (a name starting with `_`) are skipped. Write for
  players, and only about what is live. The folder is listed with `ls` (`dir /b` on Windows; `data/patchnotes/index.txt`,
  one file name per line, when the server cannot run commands) at startup and again at most every 60 s, so a new file
  shows up within a minute; `/patchnotes reload` (staff) reads it at once. Weeks are ordered by date, then id (newest
  first); the list shows up to 52.
- **The notes in the repository.** `2026-10-31.md` is the player-facing Open Beta note (what the game is, the systems to
  try, the beta warning: progress may be wiped, report bugs in game and on Discord); its date makes it the newest, so
  it opens at the first login of every account. `2026-10-08.md` and `2026-10-09.md` are the closed-test notes, kept as
  history (the beta note says so). A server that installs the folder before 31 October shows the beta note at once;
  where that is not wanted, delete `data/patchnotes/2026-10-31.md` after every `install_all.py` run (it copies the file
  again). docs/BETA.md lists the notes still to write for the beta and for launch.
- **Window.** Weeks on the left (date, title, NEW for unseen ones), the selected week on the right: title, date, intro,
  section headings in colour (New green, Changes gold, Fixes blue, Balance violet), bullets with a dot in the section
  colour, sub-bullets, bold leads. A long note is sent in parts of about 4 KB of text (`PN.parts`; one 9 KB message never
  arrived in the test client) and joined by the client.
- **Login.** Once per new week per **account** (`seen_key` = date|id of the newest week the account was shown; a week
  counts as seen when the client displayed it, opened by itself or by hand, and an older week never lowers it). "Don't
  show automatically" (`auto_open`, per account) stops the login opening; the menu and Social > Patch Notes still work. The login
  opening never stacks with the Daily Reward window: it is the `patchnotes` entry (order 30, after the daily's 20; set
  `Chaos.dailyStreak.loginOrder.patchnotes` to change it) of daily.lua's login window queue `ChaosLoginWindows`, so the
  server sends it only after the client reports the daily window closed (or when the daily is not due), and the window
  reports `closed` itself so the queue can go on. The client also refuses to show it over a visible Daily Reward window
  (and hides it again if one appears in the first 20 s), and game_daily waits while `patchNotesWindow` is on screen. On
  a server without that queue, the script falls back to its own timer (the daily's `openDelayMs` + 1.5 s) and tells the
  client whether a daily window is expected; the client then waits up to 6 s for it to appear and until it is closed.
- **Staff:** `/patchnotes reload` (read the folder now), `/patchnotes unseen` (forget the own account's last seen week, to
  test the login opening), `/patchnotes` (status).
- **Brazilian Portuguese (pt-BR).** Every note has a twin `<id>.pt-br.md` next to it (`2026-10-22.md` and
  `2026-10-22.pt-br.md`; same format, same `Date:` line, same sections and bullets, translated). `fileNames` skips the
  twins and `twinNames` pairs them by the id in front of `.pt-br.md`; a twin without its English file is ignored. Section
  headings are translated and still map to the same kinds (Novidades = New, Mudanças = Changes, Correções = Fixes,
  Balanceamento = Balance). The scan stores the twin on the note (`note.tr["pt-BR"]`); the week list and the note go out
  through `PN.localize(note, Chaos.lang(player))`, so a player whose client language is pt-BR (client hello, see "Server
  texts in pt-BR") reads the twin and everyone else, or any note without a twin, reads the English file. The id, date
  and "last seen" key always come from the English note. The scan logs a warning when a twin has a different number of
  sections or bullets. Names of spells, items, zones and menu paths stay as they are in game. No em dashes. The
  **Changelog tab is English only**: `gen_changelog.py` builds it from git commit subjects (English), so it is not
  translated.
- **Discord post.** At startup (30 s later, once `discord.lua` has made the queue table) and then hourly,
  `PN.postDiscord` takes the newest note that is dated today or earlier and not announced yet and queues rows of the new
  event `patchnotes` (channel `announce`; `ChaosDiscordCore.patchnotes`): first the English digest, then the pt-BR one
  (English only when there is no twin). A digest is the title, the intro and, per section, the top level bullets (bold
  lead plus the start of the text, sub-bullets left out), cut into messages of at most 1900 characters (the event text
  limit is 2000), at most 4 per language, the last one ending with "More in game: Social > Patch Notes." The worker
  (`discord_worker.php`, kind `patchnotes`) posts each row as one embed. **No repeat:** the key `date|id` of the note is
  saved in `server_config` (`chaos_discord_patchnotes`) before the rows are queued, so a restart, a `/reload` or the next
  hourly check posts nothing again (at most once: a crash between the save and the insert loses the post, it never
  doubles it). Older unannounced notes are never posted late, and a note dated in the future (the beta note before its
  day) waits for its day. A server that has never recorded a key announces its newest due note once. Switches in
  `discord_config.lua`: `enabled` and `events.patchnotes` (on by default), `patchnotes.enabled`, `postedKey`,
  `startDelaySeconds`, `checkSeconds`, `maxChars`, `maxParts`, `bulletChars`; channel `channels.patchnotes`. The webhook
  URLs stay in `/etc/chaos/discord.env` (`CHAOS_DISCORD_WEBHOOK_ANNOUNCE`); nothing here reads or prints them.
  `CHAOS_DISCORD_OFF=patchnotes` also switches the kind off at the worker. When Discord is off or `discord.lua` is not
  loaded nothing is queued and nothing is remembered, so the note goes out once Discord is on.
- **Tests:** `tests/patchnotes_test.lua` (parsing, limits, file list, ids, order, seen key, auto-open, the parts, the
  twins: pairing, headings, `compare`, `localize`, the Discord digest and dedupe; it also parses every real file of
  `data/patchnotes/` and fails when an English note has no pt-BR twin with the same sections and bullets, or a twin has
  no English note), `tests/patchnotes_discord_test.lua` (patchnotes.lua against a mocked engine: rows, once over
  restarts, future dates, switches, what a pt-BR and an English player receive) and the client's `patchnotesview_test.lua` (blocks and colours, joining
  parts, the login wait).

Verified on the test server: the window from the menu and with Social > Patch Notes, week list and switching weeks, the
formatted notes (four sections, leads, sub-bullets, scrolling), the login opening with the Daily Reward window first
(old timer path and the login window queue: the notes appear only after the daily window is closed), the opening at once
when the daily is already claimed, no second opening at the next login, "Don't show automatically" (no opening for a new
week, unticked again from the window), the seen key and setting in the database. Not verified: two characters of one
account online at once, the Windows `dir` listing and the `index.txt` fallback, the client stepping aside for a daily window that
appears in the first 20 s (cannot happen with the queue).

## Changelog (`tools/gen_changelog.py`, `changelog_core.lua`, `patchnotes.lua`, `data/changelog/changelog.json`, client `game_patchnotes`)

The weekly patch notes are written by hand and only about what players notice; the Changelog tab of the same window
lists every change that actually shipped to the server or the client (owner 2026-10-22). Same opcode 244, action
`changelog` (client -> server, no data; server -> client `changelog {available, server = {date}, published, entries}`).

- **Source.** The git history of the deployed checkout (main). `tools/gen_changelog.py` (stdlib only) reads the
  first-parent history: a merge "Merge pull request #N" (or "Merge PR N:") is one pull request whose own commits are its
  entries, dated by the merge (the day it reached main, which the kit update deploys; the date in the commit's own time
  zone); a commit pushed straight to main is an entry of its own. Each commit is tagged by the paths it touched:
  **server** (`server/data` but `patchnotes/`, `server/src-patches`, `server/sql`, the install steps `install_*`,
  `patch_*`, `add_*`, `adapt_*`, `apply_*`, `fix_*` of `server/tools`), **content** (monster, spell, item, NPC and XML data,
  the `*_config.lua` numbers), **client** (`client/overlay`, `client/base-patches`, `client/MANIFEST.md` when the subject
  names a sprite pair), **website** (`website/` but its tests, tools and README). A commit with none (docs, CI, tests,
  tools only) is left out.
- **What players read.** Only the subject line, never the body. Dropped: subjects that read as internal (CI, docs, tests,
  ROADMAP, refactors, patch notes commits, kit update, admin app, map master, installs, a file or identifier first, a
  script or file name, asset uploads to windows-assets), and any subject that could carry something private (an IPv4
  address, an e-mail, a link, a machine path, a hex string of 16+ digits or a token-like run, words like password,
  secret, token, key, SSH, VPS) or a name `tools/ci/check_names.py` refuses (its `name_hit` is loaded from the checkout;
  without it nothing is written). Cut: internal clauses after a ";" ("...; docs", "...; CI check for them", a short one
  about tests), patch numbers ("(base patch 0111)", "Client base patch 0116:" -> "Client:"), team parentheses (an upload,
  an approval, a commit hash, "(owner)"). At most 160 characters.
- **Client versions.** A client change reaches players with the first client update `winpkg-N` whose build commit
  contains it (the release tags point at the commit the package was built from, a branch commit too). The releases are
  the `winpkg-N` tags of the checkout, the lines `N COMMIT` of `--releases FILE`, and those the previous output kept
  (GitHub keeps only the newest 3 releases and deletes their tags; the kit never prunes local tags, and a version once
  found is kept by entry id). `--published-client N` (the live client update, `updates/live/manifest.json`): a change in a
  newer release, or in none yet, is `pending` and shows as "Client: next update".
- **Limits.** The last 90 days (`--days`) and at most 200 entries (`--max`); the file at most 200 KB (the oldest entries
  go). Written atomically (temporary file, fsync, rename, mode 0644) and only when the content changed: running it again
  is a no-op. A failure (no git, a bad ref, the names check missing) exits 1 and leaves the old file.
- **Deploy.** `deploy/chaos_kit_update.sh` runs it (function `changelog`) in step 5 after the checkout, `install_all.py`
  and the helper files, before the server starts; also when nothing else changed, and again after a client update was
  published (so its entries leave "next client update"). The kit's checkout may be shallow (docs/HOST_TRIAL.md clones with
  `--depth 1`): then one bounded fetch with `--shallow-since` of about 100 days brings the branch and the `winpkg-*` tags;
  a full checkout only fetches the tags. It never fails the update: a problem is logged ("WARN: the changelog was not
  written") and the old file stays. `deploy/chaos_update.sh` (the older non-kit path) does not run it; run it by hand
  there: `python3 -I server/tools/gen_changelog.py --repo /opt/chaos/repo --out /opt/chaos/server/data/changelog/changelog.json`.
  `--print` lists the entries without writing.
- **Server.** `patchnotes.lua` reads the file at most every 60 s (`PN.config.rescanSeconds`; `/patchnotes reload` at
  once), never more than 256 KB (read capped; larger is refused), decodes it in a pcall and rebuilds it from known fields
  only (`changelog_core.lua`: dates, integers in range, known tags, printable text cut to 200 bytes without splitting a
  UTF-8 character, at most 250 entries). A missing file gives an empty answer; a bad one keeps the last good one (logged
  once). The encoded answer is cached; over 8192 bytes it goes out through `Chaos.sendChunked`. One answer per player
  per 5 s (`changelogCooldown`) on top of the per-action rate limit.
- **Client.** Tabs Patch Notes / Changelog; a line "Server updated: <date>" and "Client: update N (build B)" (the
  updater's applied update or the package's baseline, `ChaosUpdater.status()`, `Services.update`); filters All /
  Server / Client / Content / Website; entries by date with coloured tags; NEW marks for changes newer than the last
  look (client setting `chaos-changelog-seen`; the first look marks nothing); the tab reads "Changelog (N new)". The
  module listens with `ProtocolGame.registerExtendedJSONOpcode` now (needed for the chunked answer; a single message is
  plain JSON as before).
- **Tests:** `tools/gen_changelog_test.py` (subject rules, path classes, a throwaway repository with a pull request,
  a release tagged on its branch, a direct commit, a pending change, dates, idempotence, a failure keeping the old file,
  a pruned tag, `--releases`, the window, a shallow and a deepened clone, the size cap), `tests/changelog_test.lua` (the
  validation and the serving with a mocked engine: chunking, rescan, bad and oversize files, cooldown),
  `deploy/chaos_kit_update_test.py` (the kit writes it), the client's `patchnotesview_test.lua` (rows, tags, filter,
  NEW, info line).

Not verified in game: the tab, the chunked answer in the real client, the layout in pt-BR, the kit's shallow deepening on
the VPS.

## Rift Atlas (`atlas.lua`, `atlas_core.lua`, `atlas_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_rift_atlas.sql`, client `game_riftatlas`)

The long-term progression of the rift loop (roadmap item 54). Sealing rifts fills a finite completion grid; every new
cell is worth points; points buy nodes of a map of 81 nodes. Every number and the whole graph are in `atlas_config.lua`;
the pure logic is `atlas_core.lua` (tested by `tests/riftatlas_test.lua`). Extended opcode 210 (`ChaosOpcodes.riftAtlas`),
table `chaos_rift_atlas`, no storages. Window: Adventure > Rift Atlas, or the Rift Atlas button of the rift HUD.

- **The grid (96 points).** First completions only, credited to every finisher of the run (an offline finisher's row is
  written straight to the database): each theme x tier (4 x 15 cells, 1 point each), Flawless per tier (sealed without a
  death, any theme; 15 x 1), Swift per tier (sealed within the tier's Swift time, below; 15 x 1) and each Omen
  guardian (Sangrith, Morvane, Thalcyra; 3 x 2). A message names the new cells.
- **Swift times** (since 2026-10-12, when the rifts became big generated maps; owner approved). The old rule, half of
  the base 10 minutes (5:00) for every tier, was out of reach on the big maps (the model's typical solo clear is about
  6 minutes at tiers 1-10, 7.4 at tier 12, 9.5 at tier 15). Now each tier has its own time, `A.swiftSeconds`: the rift
  model's clear time (`R.clearSeconds`: the packs up to the guardian, the guardian and the walk arrival -> arena) of
  the tier on its size band's typical map, for a solo player with `swiftDps` = 1.25 x the model player's damage,
  rounded down to `swiftRound` = 15 s (`atlas_config.lua`). It grows with the map size and the tier; a strong player
  can earn it at every tier, a typical one cannot. The run's own limit (Waning Veil, Fleeting Sanctum, atlas time)
  does not change it, and the map a run actually got (one or two floors) neither: the time is per tier, so the
  atlas tooltip and the HUD show the same number.

  | Size band | Map, limit | Tiers: Swift time | Model's typical solo clear |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | 160 x 160, 12:00 | 1-5: 5:15 (model 5:15 -> 4:30) | 6:17 -> 5:37 |
  | 2 | 200 x 200, 13:00 | 6-10: 5:15 (model 4:45) | 5:51 -> 5:42 |
  | 3 | 240 x 240, 15:00 | 11: 5:30, 12: 6:00, 13: 6:30, 14: 7:15, 15: 7:45 | 6:41 -> 9:29 |

  The model's times fall inside a band because the walk gets faster with the tier's level, so a tier never gets less
  time than a lower tier: each takes the most of its own and every lower tier's time (owner, 2026-10-12); a party of five (the party model)
  gets the same times. Without the generated layouts (or without `rift_core.lua` loaded) it is `swiftShare` (0.5) of
  `rift_config.lua` `timeLimit`, 5:00, as before. Swift cells already earned stay: the cells are stored by key and
  never re-checked. The window's tooltip names each tier's time (tree payload `grid.swiftTiers`; `grid.swift` stays
  5:00 for an older client); the rift HUD shows "Swift: seal within m:ss (m:ss to spare)" while the rift runs, then
  "Swift: missed" (HUD field `swift`, none in an Omen arena; client `RiftMath.swiftLine`). `atlas.lua` loads
  `rift_core.lua` when `rift.lua` has not yet (the hooks are kept).
- **The map.** A core (start, four spokes of three small nodes toward the branches, four notables between them) and
  four theme branches of 16 nodes (gate, attunement notable, two arms with a notable each, a trunk with a notable, a
  join, the keystone at the far end). Costs: small 1, notable 2, keystone 3; the whole map costs 108. A full grid buys
  every small node and notable (96) or a keystone and most of the rest: one keystone at a time (`keystoneMax`).
  Allocating is free; a node must touch the start or a held node.
- **Respec.** One node: 250,000 gold (carried first, then the bank) or 1 Orb of Upheaval, only when the rest stays
  connected. Everything: the per-node price x nodes x 0.8. Both are sinks.

| Branch | Small nodes | Notables | Keystone |
|---|---|---|---|
| Core | +3% packs (x2), +2% modifier rewards (x3), +4% chest gold, +2% next-key chance (x2), +3% key upgrade, +3% time (x2), +5% fragments | Second Wind (+1 life at tier 8+), Keywright (+4% key, +5% upgrade), Unbroken Line (+1 life at tier 12+, +4% time), Cartographer's Eye (+4% modifier rewards, +4% packs) | - |
| Abyssal Rift (north) | packs and elites in Abyssal Rifts, fragments, packs | Attunement (+60% theme weight), Teeming Abyss (+15% packs), Eye of the Abyss (+15% elites, +0.5 item rolls), Endless Tide (+8% packs everywhere) | Lone Ember: one shared life, every finisher's chest +60% gold and item rolls (not orbs) |
| Obsidian Hall (east) | chest gold, Orbs of Upheaval, item rolls | Attunement, Guardian's Hoard (+0.25 Upheaval, +0.25 Fate per chest in the Hall), Molten Coffers (+10% gold, +0.5 rolls), Forged in Obsidian (+6% modifier rewards in the Hall, +0.1 Fate); Molten Vein and Glimmering Orb +0.1 Upheaval each | Obsidian Crown: guardian +100% health and damage, the chest's orbs x2 |
| Ashen Crypt (south) | next-key chance and upgrade, time | Attunement, Rekindled Key (+15% upgrade in the Crypt), Crypt Warden's Mark (+1 life, +8% time in the Crypt), Ember Ward (keys from sealed rifts roll more modifiers) | Ashen Ascent: next-key chance halved, every key that drops is a tier higher |
| Forsaken Sanctum (west) | time, Treasure Goblin and Sealed Coffer chances | Attunement, Gilded Pilgrims (+20% goblin in the Sanctum), Reliquary (+20% coffer in the Sanctum), Sanctified Hours (+6% time, +3% modifier rewards) | Fleeting Sanctum: 35% less time, +40% packs, every finisher's chest +30% gold and item rolls |

- **How it reaches the rifts.** `rift_core.lua` has a hook table, `R.hooks.atlasMods(player, ctx)` -> the flat modifiers of
  `A.resolve` and `R.hooks.onSealed(info)`; `atlas.lua` sets both. Without the hooks every rift function behaves exactly as
  before (the tests compare the plans, keys and chests with and without). The key user's atlas shapes the run:
  attunements weigh the theme pick (`R.pickTheme`), then packs (`packMult`), elites, time (`timeMult`), lives
  (`R.startLives`: extra lives, or one with Lone Ember), the goblin and coffer chances (on top of the Gilded Trail and
  Sealed Coffer modifiers, so they can appear without them), the guardian (`boss`, as Dread Guardian), the modifier
  reward bonuses (`R.atlasBonus`) and the next key (`R.keyOdds` / `R.rollKeyDrop`). Each finisher's own atlas adds to
  their chest (`R.atlasReward`: gold, orbs, item rolls; `R.atlasFragments`); the keystone's chest multipliers come from
  the key user and count for every finisher (they share the risk). `goldMult` and the keystones' `rewardMult` raise gold
  (`rewardMult` the item rolls too), never the orbs; only the flat orb nodes and Obsidian Crown's `orbsMult` change those.
  The party bonus ("Rifts", Party scaling) applies after the atlas. Stats tied to a theme count only in rifts of that
  theme; "tier N+" stats only from that tier. Omen arenas take no atlas effects (they still credit their cell). The HUD
  shows an "Atlas: ..." line (keystone, packs, time, lives).
- **Caps** (`caps`, on the sum of all nodes; keystones on top): packs 25%, elites 40%, time 25%, modifier rewards 20%,
  chest gold 25%, next-key chance +15, key upgrade +25, fragments 25%, +0.6 Upheaval, +0.4 Fate (were +2 / +1.5, cut
  with the chest's orbs), +1.5 item rolls,
  goblin 40%, coffer 40%, 2 lives.
- **Totals and the reward economy.** The chest is `R.reward`: gold 5,000 x tier^2, Orbs of Upheaval 0.5 + 0.085 x tier,
  Orbs of Fate 0.06 x tier, item rolls 2 + 0.5 x tier, all x (1 + quantity), tiers 11-15 +10% per tier (the reward pass
  of 2026-10-11 halved the gold and cut the orbs about 4x; "Rifts", Income). A full atlas without a keystone (all 96
  points), at tier 15 with +50% quantity: gold 2.53M -> 3.16M (+25%), orbs 6.0 -> 6.2 (Abyss) or 6.9 (Hall, Guardian's
  Hoard), item rolls 21.4 -> 22.4-22.9; +24-25% packs (more kills, more loot from them), +25% time,
  +20% on the modifiers' bonuses (a +69% quantity key gives +83%: the chest about +8%), next key 50% -> 65% (two
  modifiers), tier-up 70% -> 84% (95% in the Crypt), +2 lives from tier 12. Roughly +30-40% income per run for a player
  who has sealed everything up to tier 15 in every theme; a tier-5 player with ~25 points gets about a quarter of it.
  Lone Ember (+60% chest gold and item rolls, one life) and Fleeting Sanctum (+30% chest gold and item rolls, +40%
  packs, 35% less time) are the big bets; Obsidian Crown raises the chest's orbs by 50% (about +3.5 orbs at tier 15) against a
  guardian twice as strong.
- **Persistence and seasons.** One row per character: `done` (cell keys `c<theme>.<tier>`, `f<tier>`, `s<tier>`,
  `o<kind>`) and `nodes` (ids), both comma lists; `atlas.lua` creates the table when it is missing. Loaded at login and
  checked against the current config (`A.sanitize`: unknown ids, extra keystones, nodes cut off from the start and nodes
  over the points are dropped, free). Season characters are characters of their own (season.lua), so each realm has its
  own atlas without extra rules; a migrated character keeps its atlas as it keeps its levels and items.
- **Protocol** (JSON {action, data}): client `open {tree}` (tree = true: send the graph again) | `alloc {id}` | `refund {id, pay = gold|orb}` | `reset {pay}`; server
  `tree` (the graph, positions, costs, tooltip lines, the grid's shape with `swiftTiers`, the Swift time of each tier;
  once per login, through `Chaos.sendChunked`),
  `state {earned, spent, points, max, alloc, done, refund, reset, orb, totals, msg}`, `credit {cells, points}`.
- **Staff:** `/atlas grant all` or `/atlas grant <cell key>`, `/atlas clear`, `/atlas` (status).
- **Opcode check:** 210 is in no Chaos script, no client module and none of the reference server's opcodes (1, 67, 73, 89,
  91, 92, 99, 106, 107, 136, 181, 201, 202).
- **Tests:** `tests/riftatlas_test.lua`: graph size and kinds, unique ids, known and symmetric links, no orphan node,
  keystones as leaves, every node reachable from the start, nodes at least 60 apart and links at least 24 from any
  other node; grid cells and points, run cells (flawless, swift at exactly the tier's time and a second over, omen), the Swift
  times per tier (pinned, the strong player's model time, under the typical clear, a party the same, 5:00 without
  layouts or the rift model, earned cells kept), credit once; allocate / refund /
  keystone limit / sanitize; resolve (themes, tier gates, caps, keystones); the effects in `rift_core.lua` (plan packs,
  time, lives, goblin and coffer rates, guardian, bonuses, chest, fragments, key odds and drops, theme pick, the same
  results without an atlas); `atlas.lua` against a mocked engine (open, credit online and offline, alloc, refund with gold
  and an orb, reset, relog). Client: `riftatlasview_test.lua` (the Swift tooltip per tier, the real tree's times) and
  `game_rift/riftmath_test.lua` (the HUD's Swift line). Rendered in the Linux client from payloads of the real core
  (offline, login screen); not run on a live server yet.

## Daily reward and login streaks (`daily.lua`, `daily_core.lua`, `daily_config.lua`)

Client `game_daily` (opcode 207), opened with Adventure > Daily Reward or Adventure > Daily Reward, and by itself at login while today's
reward is unclaimed. The 7 daily rewards and the week bonus stay in `Chaos.daily` (`chaos_constants.lua`). The streak
rules are in `daily_config.lua` (loaded as `Chaos.dailyStreak`). Table: `chaos_daily_account` (`sql/chaos.sql`).

**Account-wide.** One claim a day per account, whichever character claims it. The reward goes to that character. The
row holds the streak (consecutive claim days), the best streak ever, grace charges, the day of the last claim and the
total number of claims. It is cached in memory and written through on every claim.
- Migration: the first login of an account after the update builds its row from the old per-character storages
  (`dailyStreakDay`, `dailyLastClaim`) of all its characters. The most recent claim wins, then the higher slot. The
  old cycle only stored the slot, so that slot becomes the streak.
- The old storages are still written on each claim, but nothing reads them any more.
- If the table is missing, the server prints one warning and keeps streaks in memory until the next restart.

**Streak and the 7-slot cycle.** The window's 7 slots follow the streak: slot = ((streak - 1) mod 7) + 1, so day 8
of a streak is slot 1 again, and the week bonus comes with every slot 7. The window shows `Streak: N days`, the best
streak, the grace charges, the next milestone (days, how many claims away, and the reward), and the account's title.
An older client ignores the new fields.

**Grace day.** Missing one day does not break the streak if the account has a grace charge. One charge is used per
missed day. A charge is earned every 7 claimed days of a streak, 2 stored at most (`graceEvery`, `graceMax`). Two or
more missed days in a row always break the streak (`graceMaxMissed` = 1). The window marks the charges in gold on a
day when a charge will be used.

**Milestones** (all in `daily_config.lua`, paid together with the day's reward, all or nothing):

| Days | Reward |
|---|---|
| 7 | 2 Orbs of Upheaval, 1 Orb of Fate |
| 14 | 3 Orbs of Upheaval, 2 Orbs of Fate |
| 30 | 5 Chaos, 3 Divine, 1 Orb of Grafting and the title "the Devoted" |
| 60 | 8 Chaos, 5 Divine, 2 Orbs of Grafting |
| 100 | 12 Chaos, 8 Divine, 3 Orbs of Grafting, 10 crystal coins and the title "the Relentless" |
| 180 | 20 Chaos, 12 Divine, 5 Orbs of Grafting, 25 crystal coins and the title "the Undying" |

- A milestone is paid every time a streak reaches it.
- Titles use the leaderboards' mechanism: a line in the look text of every character of the account ("He holds the
  login streak title the Devoted (30 days in a row).", `onLook` at index 101, after the leaderboard titles). The title
  follows the account's best streak, so it is kept after the streak breaks.
- The first time an account reaches a title milestone, it is broadcast.
- No new art or items: the rewards are the existing orbs and coins.

**Login order (`ChaosLoginWindows` in `daily.lua`, the one place for it).** Windows that open by themselves at login go
through one queue, so they never stack on top of each other:
- Each window registers with `ChaosLoginWindows.register(key, order, wants(player), open(player))`. A lower order opens
  first. The daily window is `daily`, order 20 (`Chaos.dailyStreak.loginOrder`). The patch notes use it with order 30.
- At login, after `Chaos.daily.openDelayMs`, the wanted windows are sent one at a time.
- The next window is sent when the client reports the current one closed (`ChaosLoginWindows.closed(player, key)`;
  game_daily sends `{"action":"closed"}`), or after `loginWindowMaxWaitMs` (90 s) if the client never does.
- On the client, a window opened this way (`"Login":1`) waits while a server modal dialog (the new-player welcome, the
  tutorial) or another login window (`LOGIN_BLOCKERS` in game_daily) is on screen. This fixes the daily window that
  opened over the new-player welcome.
- The walk-away rule of the daily window (more than 3 tiles closes it) now ignores jumps (the placement at login, a
  teleport). Those move its anchor instead.

**Protocol additions** (the shipped protocol and its quirks are unchanged; see the header of `daily.lua`):
- `OpenDailyWindow` also carries `Streak, Best, Grace, GraceMax, GraceUse, Broken, Title, Next {Days, In, Reward,
  Title}` and `Login`.
- The client also sends `closed`.

Staff: `/daily` shows the own account's state, `/daily shift <days>` moves the daily clock (tests),
`/daily set <streak> [grace]` sets the own account's streak as if claimed yesterday (group access required).

**Tests:** `tests/daily_test.lua`.
- Pure part: days over month, year and DST ends, the slot cycle, claims, grace (use, earn, cap, two missed days),
  broken streaks, a clock that went back, milestones, titles and texts, the migration, the login order.
- Mocked `daily.lua`: the slot mapping of the client, the migration at login, an alt of the same account refused, a
  second account, a stale window, day 7 with the week bonus, milestone and grace charge, all or nothing with a
  milestone that does not fit, the look text, and the login queue moving on at "closed".

**Tested in game** (test server, clock moved with `ChaosDaily.offsetDays`):
- The migration from the old storages (slot 2 -> streak 2).
- A claim on the next day (streak 3, row written).
- Day 7 paid 3 Orbs of Fate plus the milestone (2 Orbs of Upheaval, 1 Orb of Fate), 2 crystal coins of the week bonus, and a
  grace charge.
- A missed day covered by the charge (charges shown in gold, streak 7 -> 8, charge used).
- Day 30: the title in the window and in the look text.
- The window waited behind a server modal dialog and opened when it closed. Closing it emptied the server queue.
- After a relog the window opened by itself. A teleport kept it open; walking 4 tiles closed it.

**Not verified in game.** The refusal for a second character of the same account. The test client cannot list two
characters of one account (a base client character-list error), so this is covered by the mocked test only.

## Ascension quest (`ascension_quest.lua`, `ascension_quest_core.lua`, `ascension_quest_config.lua`, the Ascendant Oracle)

**Limits** (`ascension_quest_config.lua` `trial.limits`, "Instance limits"): the Trial's 3 minutes (unchanged, a line every 30 s); at most 8 rooms, the wait and the waiting line when all are in use; a staff close ends a Trial without a cooldown.

Players ascend through a quest, not a command (docs/CLASSES.md "Ascension quest"). Install: step 4b (the NPC and the promotion
patch) plus the scripts (step 1) and the guardian monsters (`data/monster/monsters/chaos/ascension/`, registered with the
other Chaos monsters). Settings: `ascension_quest_config.lua` (`Chaos.ascensionQuest`); the level rule and the two ascended classes
of every line are read at run time from `Chaos.classes.ascension`, so a new class line gets the quest without code changes.

- **The Ascendant Oracle** is placed at startup in its stall in the hub (Cinderhold, "Hub NPC booths"; else next to the temple) of every town in `npc.townIds` (`{2}` since 2026-10-22: the main city only, "Main city"; first free tile
  of `npc.offsets`), unless an NPC of that name already stands there (placed with the map editor); `npc.positions` places it
  exactly. Its script runs in the NPC's own Lua state: it reads the storages and opens modal windows, whose answers
  (`ChaosAscensionModal`) are checked again in the scripts' state. "promotion" is answered with the pointer to the quest.
- **Stages** (storage `7101000`: 0 none, 1 Proof, 2 Trial, 3 Choice, 4 done; `7101001` Proof points, `7101002` Trial cooldown,
  `7101003` attempts, `7101004` Trial won): 1 the Calling (talk at level 100 as a base class: the two paths of the class),
  2 Proof of Strength (10 points: a rare monster 1, a legendary 3, counted when the monster's hunting level, from
  `bounty_pool.lua` or estimated from experience and health as `tools/gen_bounty_pool.py` does, is at least 0.6 x the player's
  level, min 40; `Q.minHuntingLevel`, against the kill's `Chaos.monsterHuntingLevel`: its own level, else the pool level
  x `Chaos.huntingMult()`. Before 2026-10-28 the pool level was compared, so the bar was 1.2 x the player's level: a
  level 202 Monk saw 242),
  3 the Trial, 4 the Choice (a list of the two classes, then a confirmation; near the Oracle, no PvP lock).
- **The Trial**: "trial" at the Oracle -> a modal -> a runtime-built room (13 x 13, slots at x/y 7000+, `Game.createTile`,
  refused when the footprint is not empty; 8 slots) with the class's guardian: `Ascension Warden` renamed and dressed per line
  (Warden of Iron, of the Hunt, of the Veil, of Shadows, of the Still Fist, of Bones, of Dawn; a default for new lines), health
  6000 x level/100 with the level clamped to 100-130, its own hits x the same factor, no experience, no loot, never a monster
  tier. Mechanics per line (`guardians[base].mechanics`): `stillness` (3 s on one tile: a slam of 20% max health, warned at 2 s),
  `adds` (2 shades every 15 s, at most 4), `zones` (5 marked tiles around the player burst 1.5 s later for 25%), `enrage`
  (x1.5 below 30% health). 180 s. A lethal hit is cut to 1 health (no death: no experience, item or blessing loss); death, the
  time limit, leaving the room or logging out fail the attempt: back to where the player stood, healed, retry after 10 min.
  A character saved inside a room (crash) is sent to its temple at login.
- **The ascension** is `ChaosAscension.ascend(player, word[, opts])` in `ascension_quest.lua`: the class lock
  (`ChaosClassUnlocks.canUseVocation`, staff included), then ascension.lua's own vocation change (`ChaosClasses.applyVocation`:
  health / mana / capacity recounted, the vocation resent to the client, dual wield synced, the companion / minions / chi
  HUD), storage `Chaos.classes.storage.ascended`, a toast (game_chaosnotify action `ascension`), a broadcast and the name plate
  title "Ascended <class>" (`ChaosTitles.register("ascension", ...)`, guarded: every ascended character holds it).
- **the Ascendant Oracle**: players get "Ascension is earned, not claimed. Speak with the Ascendant Oracle in the temple." Staff (group 4+)
  keeps the old command, and a migrated character's one free switch (the Ascendant Oracle) still works.
  `command = "open"` in the config restores the command for everyone. The store's Vocation Change is unchanged; a character
  it took back to a base class may choose again at the Oracle without redoing the quest.
- Character > Character Info shows a character's progress. Staff: `/ascendset <player>, <ascended class>` sets an ascended class of the
  character's own line (restores characters demoted by the old login bug; the class lock still applies; no broadcast).
  Characters ascended before the quest keep their class.
- Tests: `server/tests/ascension_quest_test.lua` (the pure rules). Verified on the test server: King Tibianus refuses; a level
  100 Warrior did the Calling, the Proof (a rare Dragon, level 42, did not count; legendary and rare Hydras did), failed the
  Trial twice (lethal hit caught, experience unchanged, cooldown), won it and became a Berserker; a Thief became a Ninja
  (dual-wield storage set); a locked Templar was refused at the confirmation; the Ascendant Oracle and `/ascendset` as documented.
  Not measured: the guardian's balance against geared characters (the numbers are first estimates).

## Ascension tracker (`ascension_tracker.lua`, `ascension_tracker_core.lua`, client `game_goals`)

The twin of the Next Goals tracker for the ascension quest (owner 2026-10-23, ROADMAP O123). Rows, in order: Hear the Calling
(0/1, stage 1+), Proof of Strength (points / `proof.needed`, full from stage 2), Win the Ascension Trial (0/1, stage 3+) and
Choose your ascended class (0/1). The quest's stages and storages (7101000 block) are read as they are; nothing new is stored.

- **Rule.** Shown for a base class whose line has an ascension, from `Chaos.classes.ascension.minLevel` until the character has
  ascended. Ascended classes, lines without an ascension and characters below the level get no rows, so the client hides the
  section. A character the store's Vocation Change took back to a base class sees the finished steps and the Choice again.
- **Protocol.** No new opcode: the goals opcode 178 carries `ascension {rows = [{key, title, progress, target, state}]}`
  (empty rows hide the section). Titles are sent in the player's language (pt-BR entries in `i18n_strings.lua`).
- **Refresh.** At login, when the client asks for `tracker`, and whenever the rows change: a 3 s sweep compares a signature
  per online character, so the Oracle NPC's own Lua state, the quest script, level ups, a Vocation Change and `/ascendset`
  all reach it without hooks. Nothing is sent while nothing changed.
- **Client.** The section sits below the goals in the same panel, with the same rows, wrapping and bars (done rows are green
  with "Done"). It shares the fold and the Goal Tracker switch (Adventure > Goal Tracker); with no open goals the panel is
  titled "Ascension".
- Tests: `tests/ascension_tracker_test.lua` (rules, languages, signature, mocked engine), client `goalsview_test.lua`.

## Line spell quests (`spellquest.lua`, `spellquest_core.lua`, `spellquest_config.lua`, `spellquest_tracker*.lua`)

Phases 1 to 5 of the 21 line spells (design: three quests per class line at level 500 attack, 800 buff, 1200 ultimate).
Built: the quest machine, the hunt, the fragments, the trial hook, the reward, the tracker, the NPC, the seven level 500 attack spells,
the seven level 1200 ultimates and the seven level 800 buffs (below), and the client's locked spells in the Spellbook. All 21 spell ids
of `spell_id_pool_config.lua` are in use. Phase 6 (2026-10-28) is the NPC in the game and the tester bot check `spell_quest` (below);
left for later: a live run of both and the balance from play data. Phase 7 (2026-10-28) is the drawn icons: the 21 spells have PixelLab
art in the Chaos frame in cells 349-369 of the three spell icon sheets and in the seven buff bar icons (client/MANIFEST.md "Line spell
quest icons"); no server file changed.

- **Level 500 spells (phase 2).** Keepfall 142, Moonshard Rain 149, Prismatic Rupture 152, Eclipse Edge 155, Soulflay Wave 158,
  Thousand-Echo Palm 172, Pyre of Absolution 177: the first id of each line's triple in the pool (quest 2 and 3 take the next two of
  the line). Rows in `attack_kit_config.lua` (`quest = 1`), `spells_chaos.xml` (`needlearn="1"`, level 500, cooldown 13 s, the base
  class and both ascensions), `chaos_supports_config.lua` `kindOverride` (all area), `rotation_model.csv`, scripts in
  `data/spells/chaos/<folder>/`. Numbers and the reference of each: server/data/spells/README.md "Line spell quests, level 500
  attacks" and docs/CLASSES.md. Every class has 12 attack spells (`check_attack_counts.py`), the spell cap is 24
  (`patch_spell_cap.py`). The cooldown ladder does not rank these (`rotation_sim.py` `QUEST_COOLDOWN`). Client: `spelldata.lua`
  `quest = 1`, icon cells 349-355 (placeholder glyphs), the helper's Auto setup data.
- **NPC install.** The NPC files (`data/npc/Archivist Odrenna.xml`, `scripts/archivist_odrenna.lua`; renamed from Archivist Ysolde on
  2026-10-28, a Warden Ysolde already exists) reach the server with every other NPC of `server/data/npc`: the class hook
  `tools/install_class_ascension.py` (install step `spells`) copies that whole folder, new or different files only. The NPC is placed
  at startup in the hub stall (`npc_booths_config.lua`). Test: `tools/install_class_ascension_test.py`.
- **Quests.** Quest n needs quest n - 1 done on the same line and the level (500 / 800 / 1200, checked at every step, so a
  level lowered by death stops it). Steps: 0 none, 1 hunt, 2 trial open, 3 done. Hunt 400 / 700 / 1000 kills and 20 / 30 / 40
  fragments; trial s1 / s2 / s3. Talk to **Archivist Odrenna** (her stall is next to the Keeper of Trials in the hub's south row, x 31628 y 32236,
  `npc_booths_config.lua`) to start; ask her again for the count and the trial. All numbers: `spellquest_config.lua`.
- **NPC in the game (phase 6).** Checked statically end to end: `spellquest.lua` places her at startup (1.1 s) with
  `ChaosNpcPlace.place(name, temple, offsets, opts)`; for the main city's temple that is her stall in the hub
  (`ChaosNpcBoothsCore.spotForTemple`, `npc_booths_config.lua`, the second stall of the south row, x 31628 y 32236, next to the Keeper of Trials), where
  `patch_hub_npcs.py` has cleared the base NPC (it clears every tile of `booths`); `data/npc/Archivist Odrenna.xml` and
  `scripts/archivist_odrenna.lua` follow the Keeper of Trials (same script header, the nearest-NPC focus rule, greeting and farewell in the
  player's language). She was missing from the POI list of the map (`poi_config.lua` `npcs`, where the Keeper and Maelis are): added,
  test in `tests/poi_test.lua`; `patch_hub_npcs_test.py` now requires her stall; the tester coverage table (`tester_scenarios.json`)
  brings a bot to her (`PLACES`, kind place) instead of calling the system staff only.
- **Lines.** Warrior, Ranger, Mystic, Thief, Necromancer, Monk, Templar, by the base class of `Chaos.classes`; the base class and
  both ascended classes share the three spells (their names are in the config, ids belong to the spell registration).
- **Kills.** A death event on every monster that is not a summon. A kill counts when the monster's hunting level
  (`Chaos.monsterHuntingLevel`: the level players see, the native level of a level-scaled monster, a generated area's point,
  else the pool level x `baseLevelMult`; the Proof of Strength's measure) and the killer's level are at least the quest's.
  Not counted: summons, monsters of rifts (and dense-rift husks), Trials, dungeons, Ascension guardians, monsters the pace layer
  does not know (event spawns), kills within 4 tiles of a protection zone. A boss kill counts 25 kills. Credit: the killers
  (last hit, most damage, summons resolved) and party members within 30 tiles who dealt damage.
- **Fragments.** A counter in storage, never an item. Each counted kill rolls 6% (rare x2, legendary x5, from the monster tier), a
  boss drops one for sure, the 41st counted kill without one is sure (pity 40). The chat message "Quest fragment found: n of N".
  The hunt is done with both the kills and the fragments; then the trial opens.
- **Trial.** The Trials engine (`trials.lua`, `trials_config.lua` `spellTiers`): the family and mechanics of the character's own
  line, one stage plus the guardian, `opts.spell = "s1"`. Guardian health = the Merciless hp x 0.8 / 1.0 / 1.2 x (level /
  tier level) ^ 1.5, the level clamped to 500-800 / 800-1200 / 1200-1600; hits 9 / 12 / 15% of the player's max health, thralls
  3.5 / 5 / 6.5%; 5 / 6 / 7 minutes, 3 / 3 / 2 lives. `ChaosTrials.spellHook` (set by `spellquest.lua`): `won` completes the quest,
  `failed` closes the door 60 s (not after a logout, abort or error). The run needs no tier cleared and pays no tier reward.
- **Reward.** The spell, a message, a toast, 2000 x level gold to the bank, once per quest (done time in +6; a second line later
  gets the spell but no gold).
- **Vocation Change.** The done flag is a bit per line in +7. `class_spells_core.lua` never teaches a quest spell (the `quest` hook of
  `plan`), forgets the ones of another line, and `ChaosSpellQuest.sync` (login, class change) teaches the done ones of the new line
  again for free. A change to another line shows quest 1 of that line (its own quest); the way back finds it done. A running hunt
  continues after a change (progress is per character).
- **Staff.** `/spellquest set <player>, <quest>, <step>[, kills[, fragments]]`, `show <player>`, `reset <player>` (staff only, like
  every talkaction; step 3 marks the line done without gold).
- **Tracker.** Rows on the Next Goals channel (opcode 178, `spellquest {rows}`), a third section of the client panel, titled
  "Spell Quest". Shown while the character can work on a quest (the next one not done on its line, its level reached).
- **Level 1200 ultimates (phase 3).** Judgment of Iron 148, Dawnbreaker Shot 151, Eclipse of Ruin 154, Death Between Heartbeats 157,
  Funeral of Kings 160, Heaven's Ninth Gate 174, Hammer of Ember Dawn 237: the third id of each line's triple. Rows in
  `attack_kit_config.lua` (`quest = 3`; extras `main` and `critAbove`, a second effect `vfx2`), `spells_chaos.xml` (`needlearn="1"`,
  level 1200, cooldown 35 to 50 s, mana 3 x the reference), `kindOverride`, `rotation_model.csv` (flag `ultimate`), scripts in
  `data/spells/chaos/<folder>/`, big effect swaps in `chaos_big_fx.lua`. Every class has 13 attack spells. Numbers per spell, the shapes
  by role (boss bursts for the Thief, Monk and Ranger lines, area for the Mystic and Necromancer, mixed for the Warrior and Templar)
  and the gain per class: server/data/spells/README.md "Line spell quests, level 1200 ultimates".
- **Level 800 buffs (phase 4).** Ironbound Oath 143, Unblinking Gaze 150, Veil of Whispers 153, Shroud of Knives 156, Dirge of the
  Legion 159, Lotus Stance 173, Mantle of Dawn 178: the second id of each line's triple. Support group, level 800, `needlearn="1"`
  (taught by the quest, never by the level), cooldown 90 s, group cooldown 2 s, a self buff with no pacify and no lock, the base class
  and both ascensions; `chaos_supports_config.lua` `kindOverride` = buff. Every number is in `quest_buffs_config.lua` (rules in
  `quest_buffs_core.lua`, the cast in `data/spells/chaos/_questbuffs.lua`, one script per spell in the line's folder). Each buff is a
  `CONDITION_ATTRIBUTES` on the caster with its own sub id 71075 - 71081 (`ChaosSpell.SUBID`, a buff bar row each in `chaos_buffs.lua`,
  icon `buff:<key>`); the skill parts are condition parameters, the rest is read from that condition by the combat scripts:

  | Buff | Time | Effect | Where it is read |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Ironbound Oath (Warrior) | 20 s | melee skill +20%, shielding +25% | condition parameters |
  | Unblinking Gaze (Ranger) | 20 s | distance skill +25%, critical chance +10 points | condition parameters (the special skill) |
  | Veil of Whispers (Mystic) | 20 s | magic level +15%, 1% of the maximum mana every second | magic level parameter, plus a `CONDITION_REGENERATION` of sub id 72077 |
  | Shroud of Knives (Thief) | 15 s | melee and distance skill +20%, evasion +10 points | condition parameters; `thief_combat.lua` adds the evasion to the line's (the Blackblood Creed still halves the sum) |
  | Dirge of the Legion (Necromancer) | 20 s | minion hits +25%, death spell damage +10% | `necro_lib.lua` `hitBonus` (with Banner of Bones' bonus), `passivetree_effects.lua` `ChaosPassiveDealt` (death damage of a spell, not a minion hit or a proc) |
  | Lotus Stance (Monk) | 15 s | +1 chi on a weapon or fist hit, evasion +10 points | `monk_combat.lua` (chi), `monk_chi_core.lua` `dodges(..., extra)` (Scarred Discipline still removes the evasion) |
  | Mantle of Dawn (Templar) | 20 s | damage taken -15%, the holy strike after a melee hit +20% | `templar_combat.lua`: `damageTakenFactor(..., extra)` and `radiantDamage(..., mult)` |

  The evasion is added to the line's chance (Thief 8%, Ninja 12%, Samurai 5%, Monk 6%, Shadowfist 8%, Iron Sage 4%). The buffs are
  outside the models: `rotation_sim.py` reads attack spells only (a support spell has no row in `rotation_model.csv`), every balance
  model measures a character without quest spells, and a buff of 15 to 20 s every 90 s is up for about a fifth of the time. Helper:
  `game_helpersupport/supportspells.lua` `KINDS` lists the seven as `auto = 'timer'`, so Auto setup puts the buff the character knows in
  its Timer section (first among the buffs: the highest level), cast in fights every 91 s. Test: `tests/quest_buffs_test.lua`.
- **Spellbook (phase 5).** The client's Spellbook shows an unlearned quest spell as locked: the row says "Locked", the tooltip and the
  description name Archivist Odrenna and the level of the quest, the detail panel has a "Quest" row; locked quest spells of the
  character's line are always in "Available soon", "My vocation" and "All spells" (client/MANIFEST.md `game_spellbook`).
- **Rotation cap exemption.** The ultimate is not one of the 5 attack spells of a rotation (owner 2026-10-28). The model flag
  `ultimate` (rotation_sim.py) keeps it out of every set and preset and adds its gain on top; `autorotation_data.lua` lists it per class as
  `ultimate = id`; the helper (`game_helperrotation/autorotation.lua`) puts it first, for one monster, when the character can cast
  it, and still fills the 5 below. `spellquest_config.lua` `rotationCapExempt = {false, false, true}` documents it (nothing reads it).
- **Quest gain, not a tax.** The class factor knots (`spell_factor_config.lua`) and the weapon power are the ones from before the quest
  spells: a character without quests keeps its damage, and every balance model measures that baseline. The quest spells are strengthened
  per class by `quest_spell_scale_config.lua` (a factor per class and spell, applied by the attack kit): Q1 adds about 4.5% to the best
  set at levels 500-800, Q3 about 9% on top at 1200. `python3 -I server/tools/rotation_sim.py --quest` prints the gains, `--check` keeps
  them in bounds (server/data/spells/README.md).
- Tests: `tests/spellquest_test.lua` (rules and the engine file on a mocked engine), `tests/spellquest_tracker_test.lua`,
  `tests/trials_test.lua` (spell tiers), `tests/class_spells_test.lua` (quest spells), `tests/quest_buffs_test.lua` (the level 800
  buffs), client `goalsview_test.lua`, `spellbook_core_test.lua`, `supportspells_test.lua`.

## Base scripts and the classes (`tools/patch_base_classes.py`)

The base server's scripts test the stock vocation ids (1-10) by number or with `Player.isSorcerer / isDruid / isKnight /
isPaladin / isMage`. The new lines (Thief 11-13, Berserker 14, Beastmaster 15, Monk 17-19, Necromancer 20-22, Templar 23-25)
were refused, indexed nil (script errors) or, at the vocation Oracles, put on the retired ids 2 and 9. The tool (install step
5b, run by `install_all.py` after `add_vocations.py`; exact match on the stock lines, idempotent, `--dry-run`) makes every
class count as one stock vocation:

| Class line | Counts as | Familiar |
|---|---|---|
| Warrior 4 / Juggernaut 8 / Berserker 14 | Knight / Elite Knight | Knight Familiar |
| Templar 23 / Inquisitor 24 / Sentinel 25 | Knight / Elite Knight | Paladin Familiar (holy) |
| Ranger 3 / Deadeye 7 / Beastmaster 15 | Paladin / Royal Paladin | Paladin Familiar |
| Thief 11 / Ninja 12 / Samurai 13 | Paladin / Royal Paladin | Paladin Familiar |
| Monk 17 / Shadowfist 18 / Iron Sage 19 | Paladin / Royal Paladin | Druid Familiar |
| Mystic 1 / Elementalist 5 | Sorcerer / Master Sorcerer | Sorcerer Familiar |
| Necromancer 20 / Lich 21 / Bone Lord 22 | Sorcerer / Master Sorcerer | Sorcerer Familiar |
| Illusionist 10 | Elder Druid | Illusionist Familiar |

- `lib/core/player.lua`: `CHAOS_STOCK_VOCATION` (the table), `Player.getStockVocationId()`, `Player.getStockBaseVocationId()`

## Class looks (`class_looks.lua`, `class_looks_core.lua`, `tools/install_outfits.py`)

Every class has its own look, male and female (list and looks per class: docs/CLASSES.md "Content per class"; art:
client/MANIFEST.md "Class looks pair", "things_custom19" and "Class looks pair 20").
- Given and worn. First login and every class change: the class's look and its base class's look are given and the
  class's look is put on. The website (form and the client's Create character) already writes the class look with
  both addons into a new character's row (website/README.md "Client API"), so the character lists show it before the
  first login; the first login then gives the look as above. Other logins: looks of the class not owned yet are given; the worn look stays. Colours and
  mount stay the player's. Nothing is taken away. A store outfit the player wears stays on; the class look is only the
  default.
- Addons. A class look is worn with both addons (`ChaosClassLooks.ADDONS` = 3). Each class look given comes with both
  its addons (`Player:addOutfitAddon(look, 3)`): only that look's addons, no other outfit's. The base outfits.xml
  cannot grant addons (`unlocked="yes"` would give the bare look to everyone), so the entries stay `unlocked="no"`
  and the script grants them. Existing characters get the addons at their next login. If the worn look is the one
  that just got its addons, it is put on with them, once; a later choice of fewer addons is kept.
- outfits.xml: `install_outfits.py` (install step `outfits`) writes the marked block "Chaos class looks" from
  `L.looks`, both sexes, locked. Re-run it after the list changes.
- Pair 19 switch: `L.PAIR19_LOOKS` in `class_looks_core.lua`, on since 2026-10-12 (things_custom19 on windows-assets
  at b36204f2). Keep it one plain line: `install_outfits.py` and the test read it. On, Juggernaut, Ranger,
  Beastmaster, Bone Lord, Shadowfist and Sentinel use outfits 2161-2172 of client pair things_custom19
  (`L.pair19Looks`). Off, no script, outfits.xml line or store list names 2161-2172. A client on things_custom18 or older draws nothing for
  them, and the pair's dat and spr signatures did not change, so the server cannot tell the pairs apart.
  With it on:
  - the replaced looks stay owned and wearable as "<class> Class (old)" in outfits.xml
  - they join `L.retired`, so the store never sells them (`gen_shop_cosmetics.py` excludes 2161-2172 either way)
  - a character wearing a replaced look of its class or base class gets the new look at its next login, colours kept,
    with both addons
- Flip step: done 2026-10-12, after the owner's approval and the push of things_custom19 to windows-assets
  (b36204f2, archive sha256 a203681267535b90cc420a6f6bed8931c7e59a8845d2cfcd6b9f27ac74a78c41). The switch line was
  set to true, with client/MANIFEST.md, ROADMAP.md C4 and this section. On each server, once the Windows package is
  rebuilt from the branch: `python3 -I tools/install_all.py SERVER_DIR --only outfits`, then restart. On a base
  outfits.xml it writes 27 class looks: the 21 looks and the six "(old)" ones. A second run changes nothing.
  Rollback: set it back to false and re-run the step. The old looks are the class looks again; nobody lost them. A
  character still wearing 2161-2172 keeps that look type until it changes outfit, so roll back only while the clients
  still have things_custom19.
- Tests: `tests/class_kit_test.lua` (wear, login, addons, sources listed for every look, the switch both ways: on
  as shipped, off on a second copy of the core loaded with the switch line set to false).
- Pair 20 switch: `L.PAIR20_LOOKS` in `class_looks_core.lua`, on since 2026-10-12 (things_custom20 on windows-assets
  at 77b9cc9b; client/MANIFEST.md "Class looks pair 20"). On, the Lich, Inquisitor, Necromancer, Thief, Ninja and
  Templar use outfits 2173-2184 (`L.pair20Looks`): matched pairs for the Lich and the Inquisitor (one look for both
  sexes before) and the Necromancer (two unrelated outfits before). Off, no script, outfits.xml line or store list

- Pair 20 flip step: done 2026-10-12, after the owner approved the picks and things_custom20 went to windows-assets
  (77b9cc9b, archive sha256 4ec97152be8b54f2ede683ee27dfdfe7944b6c36ee9190785e7f069355d11202). The switch line was

## Class signature effects (`data/lib/chaos_class_fx.lua`, `data/lib/chaos_class_fx_ids.lua`, hooks in `data/spells/chaos/_common.lua`)
Each class line's signature spells send an effect of their own (ROADMAP C4 "effects"), so the classes read differently
in combat. Art: client/MANIFEST.md "Class signature effects" (things_custom22, effects 593-627, our own procedural
art); looks per effect: `data/spells/README_FX.md` "Class signature effects".
- `ChaosClassFx.swaps`: class key -> spell id -> {effect the script sends = the class effect}. A class takes its
  line's swaps (`lineOf`), its own win (the Juggernaut's Iron Bellow is not the Warrior's). No spell script changes:
  during a cast (the supports wrapper's `ChaosSupportsSpell.cast()`, also in the cast's addEvent callbacks)
  `ChaosSpell.vfx`, `ChaosSpell.fx` and the wrapped `Fx` ask `ChaosClassFx.swapFor(pid, spellId, name)`. Order: a
  cosmetic spell skin the player chose, then the class effect, then the default. `Fx` (an id only, e.g. the per-tile
  hit of an area) takes a class effect only when it sits on the tile itself (offset 0,0: ranger_arrowfall,
  ninja_smoke); the 3x3 ones go through `Vfx` at the target + (1, 1).
- Swaps: Warrior line: Earthbreaker and Colossus Fall warrior_quake, Reaping Gyre warrior_gyre, Iron Bellow
  warrior_bellow (Juggernaut juggernaut_bulwark); Berserker: Red Frenzy and Bloodrage berserker_rage, Skyfall Cleave
  berserker_cleave. Ranger line: Dawnpiercer ranger_pierce, Hail of Dawn ranger_arrowfall (each tile), Blessed Earth
  ranger_thornseal, Lightward ranger_canopy; Deadeye: Final Verdict deadeye_mark; Beastmaster: Wild Bond
  beast_spirit. Mystic line: Purifying Wellspring mystic_mend (each healed ally), Hall of Mirrors illusion_mirror
  (each clone), Umbral Stride illusion_shatter; Elementalist: Falling Pyre elementalist_glyph; Illusionist: Mirror
  Mend mystic_mend (the mirror heal). Thief line:
  Shadow Veil and Shadow Mend thief_vanish; Ninja: Shadow Step ninja_vanish, Smoke Bomb ninja_smoke (each tile);
  Samurai: Counter Stance samurai_parry, Bushido Focus samurai_focus. Necromancer line: Withering Curse necro_curse;
  Lich: Soul Rot lich_rot (the Bone Lord keeps its own bone effects 586-592). Monk line: Whirling Heel monk_heel;
  Shadowfist: Pressure Points shadowfist_mark; Iron Sage: Chi Ward ironsage_ward. Templar line: Vow of Mending
  templar_mend; Inquisitor: Zealotry inquisitor_zeal; Sentinel: Aegis of Faith sentinel_aegis, Lay on Hands
  templar_mend. Banner Call and Soulward (every class) keep the shared effects.
- Snares and vigils: snare_jaws, snare_blast, vigil_wrath, vigil_iron, vigil_haste, vigil_clarity are in the pair
  (`ChaosClassFx.unwired`) but not sent yet: `_snares.lua` and `_vigils.lua` send stock effects. To wire them, those
  scripts call `ChaosClassFx.send(pos, name, stockFallback)` (the stock effect while the switch is off).
- Pair switch: `C.PAIR22_FX` in `chaos_class_fx.lua`, **on** (2026-10-12; things_custom22 on windows-assets, 13e289c7).
  Off, `chaos_class_fx_ids.lua` is never loaded and every spell sends what it sent before. Flip step, after the
  owner approves the push and the Windows package is rebuilt from the branch: set the line to true (and flip the
  check in `tests/class_fx_test.lua`), `python3 -I tools/install_all.py SERVER_DIR --only files`, restart. Rollback:
  set it back to false; a client on things_custom21 would only log "invalid effect id" and show nothing in their place.
- Tests: `tests/class_fx_test.lua` (vocations equal `Chaos.classes.ids`; every swap is a spell the class may cast,
  a name its script sends, an effect in the spec and the ids; line inheritance; switch off: nothing changes; on: the
  hooks send the class effect at its offset, a skin wins, the default outside a cast, `Fx` only for 0,0 effects).
- Skyfall Cleave fix, 2026-10-13. Its swap name `ground_slam` was only the combat's `COMBAT_PARAM_EFFECT`. That id is
  fixed when the script loads, outside any cast, so no class effect was sent. The cast now sends it on the slammed
  spot, unless a skin is chosen. The test checks that every swapped name is also asked during the cast.
- Checked in a live client, 2026-10-13, pair things_custom23: every class's signature spells were cast; the server
  sent each class effect at its offset. Berserker and Ranger were cast again after the fix. Skyfall Cleave sends 598 at the target + 1,1. Hail of Dawn sends 600 on all
  12 hits. A cosmetic skin still wins: Red Frenzy with Voidborn War Cries sends 526, without it 597. Hail of Dawn's
  cast effect at the caster uses the same name, so the Ranger also gets the arrowfall on its own tile while it casts:
  kept on purpose (owner, 2026-10-13).

Item powers, snares, rift modifiers, world bosses and the reflect sent stock effects. With the switch on they send
animated effects of the oblique spell effect set instead. Effects only: no damage, chance, timing or target changes.

## Mystic line effects (`data/lib/chaos_mystic_fx.lua`; Tier A of the 2026-10-16 effect pass)

Owner: "I found the effects of the Mystic spells very poor." Effects only, all from the client pair already live
(pair 28): no damage, area, timing or target changes. What each spell sends: server/data/spells/README_FX.md
"Mystic line effects". The rules:
- A large or shaped effect that covers an area replaces its 1x1 tile effects (`ChaosMysticFx.tileFx`): Rime Bloom,
  Blightswarm, Falling Pyre, Frozen Crypt (pulses with the nova), Doomtide, Primordial Squall, Nightburst, Tear in the
  Weave. Without the effect in the pair (a switch off, an older pair) the tile effects stay.
- Impacts land when the missile arrives (`ChaosMysticFx.flightMs`: 150 ms x sqrt(tiles), the client's missile time):
  Witchfire Bolt, Shattered Psyche, Forked Storm, Umbral Stride, Mirror Mend.
- Swaps changed: `ChaosBigFx.spells` 230 `shadow_smoke` (the eruption) and 231 `arcane_circle` (the implosions);
  the pair 27 Tear in the Weave rift is no longer `first` (the large rift wins, the script adds the pair 27 core);
  `ChaosClassFx` 208 and 96 swap `heal_sparkle` (the allies, the mirror heal) so the caster and the healed ally keep
  the larger pack healing_bloom / regenerating.
- Effect names: every spell and script asks ChaosFx only for names it has (`tests/spell_fx_names_test.lua` scans
  all of data/; a missing name is silent at runtime, Fx() sends the stock fallback). The `aura_ring` and
  `poison_cloud` aliases of `_common.lua` are gone: Mystic `poison_cloud` -> `poison_burst`, `aura_ring` ->
  `arcane_aura`; Warcry `blood_ring`; Whirlwind and Blade Flurry `blood_slash`; Consecration and Divine Ward
  `holy_cross`; Rallying Cry `holy_spiral`; Sense Prey `frost_ripple`. Piercing Volley asked for `blood_spear`, a
  missile only, as its tile effect and sent the stock hit area: now `blood_splash`.
