## Condition auras, blasts and fireworks (pair 29) (`data/lib/chaos_pack29_vfx.lua`, `data/lib/chaos_pack29_vfx_ids.lua`, `scripts/chaos/pack29_vfx.lua`, switch `ChaosPack29Fx.PAIR29`, off)

The five effect packs the owner bought on 2026-10-16 (client/MANIFEST.md "Condition auras, blasts and fireworks
(pair 29)", effects 780-829, missiles 170-185; credits in docs/CREDITS.md). Effects only: no damage, chance, timing,
target or reward changes. Same switch as the Mystic effects of the pair (`ChaosPack29Fx.PAIR29`, off until pair 29 is
on windows-assets).
- **Condition auras** (`C.auras`, 16 states; small, over the head, sent again while the state lasts):
  - damage conditions, by the engine (src-patch 0045, `C.conditionTicks`, set once at startup by
    `ChaosPack29Vfx.applyEngine`): each tick of fire burning, earth poison, energy shocked, physical bleeding, ice
    frozen, death cursed shows that aura instead of the stock hit sparks;
  - `C.hold(creature, state, ms)` (one addEvent chain per creature and state, at most `C.maxHeld`, re-sent when the
    aura ends): `ChaosSpell.slow` slowed; Iron Palm stunned (a big monster: slowed); the Monk's PvP stun stunned; the
    item chill frozen and the item shock shocked (`item_mods.lua`); a status word on a creature (`C.words`, 3 s:
    frozen, stunned, fear, cursed, blessed, shocked, slowed);
  - `C.show` (throttled to the aura's length) from the boss fight tick: invulnerable while an immune adds phase lives,
    enraged after the soft enrage (`boss_mechanics.lua`);
  - the online players' scan every `C.scanMs` (`scripts/chaos/pack29_vfx.lua`): paralyze slowed, drunk confused, a
    spell's regeneration (CONDITIONID_COMBAT, not the food one) regeneration.
  - Silenced and petrified have no game mechanic: imported, unused (`C.unused`). Monsters slowed by a stock rune or a
    monster spell show nothing (no Lua call site and no scan of monsters, which would cost too much).
- **Hit splashes** (engine, `C.raceHits`): a physical hit on a blood creature (players too) `hit_blood`, on a fire
  creature `hit_blood_spray`. The pack is red only: venom, undead and energy creatures keep the stock hit. The splash
  item under the creature and the corpse pools are unchanged.
- **Element blasts**: the engine's direct element hits (`C.elementHits`: fire, ice, energy, earth, death, arcane;
  holy keeps the stock sparks), the small hits and procedural bursts a spell sends during its cast (`C.names`, asked in
  `_common.lua` after the Mystic swaps; per-tile area effects sent by id stay), boss deaths (`bosspoints.lua`, every
  listed boss: `blast_boss`, `blast_massive` from 1,000,000 max health). Unused: `blast_fire5`.
- **Missiles** (engine, `C.missiles`): the stock fire, energy, energy ball, death, sudden death, ice, small ice, earth,
  small earth, poison, holy, small holy and explosion missiles and the procedural Chaos bolts (`fx:fire_bolt` ...) are
  sent as the pack's bolts, from spells, runes, wands, monsters and Lua alike. Weapon ammunition keeps its look. Unused:
  `bolt_ultimate`, `bolt_water`, `bolt_wind`.
- **Celebrations** (`C.celebrate(pos, kind, fallback)`): the level-up `fw_grand` (`scripts/chaos/pack29_vfx.lua`; the
  base advance_save.lua sends no firework: its `config.effect` is false), an achievement `fw_star`, a boss point, a
  world boss, guild boss or raid reward `fw_rainbow`. Off, the old stock firework.
- Off (as shipped): the ids file is not loaded, `applyEngine` only clears the overrides, every call site sends what it
  sent before. An engine without 0045: nothing is set (the Lua checks `Game.setHitEffect`). Flip step: the pair 29
  switch (above) and the engine built with 0045. Rollback: the switch off and a restart (startup clears the
  overrides).
- Tests: `tests/pack29_vfx_test.lua` (switch off; every table name in the client spec and the ids file, every spec name
  sent or unused, the engine-sent auras and splashes at offset 0, 0, missiles fit u8; the engine rows; off: nothing sent
  or set; on: auras, holds, words, celebrations, boss blasts; the call sites wired), `tools/effect_overrides_patch_test.py`
  (the patch and a model of its rules). A local run with the switch on passed the server test set (client/MANIFEST.md
  "Pair 29 build"). Not run on a server or in a client.

## Purchased effect packs (pair 36) (`data/lib/chaos_pack36_fx.lua`, `data/lib/chaos_pack36_fx_ids.lua`, switch `ChaosPack36Fx.PAIR36_FX`, on)
Owner 2026-10-22: "Use o máximo de assets de lá por favor. São todos comprados", "Use as spells, level up e loot
beams", use everything usable. Pair 36 (client/MANIFEST.md "Purchased effect packs (pair 36)") brings the purchased
effect packs of docs/CREDITS.md into the game. Effects only: no damage, area, timing, target or reward changes.
- **Redrawn in place** (no server change needed): 141 effects and 35 missiles keep their ids and show pack art. These
  are the stock ids our generated effects redrew (`fx_custom.csv`), the procedural 372-428, the combat feedback
  (173 and 415 crit: a critical hit burst; 416 dodge: a smoke poof; 417 and 628 reflect: parry and block flashes; no
  words, as the owner wants the animation, not the word), and the stock and procedural missiles. Every engine
  `CONST_ME_*` / `CONST_ANI_*` send, every monster `areaEffect` / `shootEffect` and every `ChaosFx` name on those ids
  now shows the new art. `combat_fx.lua` sends what it sent before. The pack's word pop-ups (`w_text_*`, English) are
  appended but sent by nothing.
- **Send offsets of the in-place art** (2026-10-22, owner: "a animação amarela está totalmente fora de centro", Banner
  Call's `holy_spiral` 405, a 5x5 judgement pillar kept as 4x4, drawn two tiles up and left; again 2026-10-23, "efeito
  fora de centro. mesma coisa com o efeito amarelo": the blue teleport 11, the login effect, and the yellow holy 201 and
  262, drawn about a tile down and right). The in-place art keeps its bottom-right tile on the tile it is sent to, and
  `gen_pack36_fx.py` moved art reaching past that tile up and left as a whole, so each effect's pivot (the ring's
  middle, the spot the pack author meant) sits a few to some 60 pixels up and left of its place. The first table (23
  ids) moved every 3x3 / 4x4 art by the size of the art from its appended twin, which was a whole tile too much where
  the pull was small: the teleport ring was pulled 4, 10 px and got a tile. Now the build records the pull of each
  effect (`art_import/pack36_replace_pivots.csv`, from the pack art) and
  `data/lib/chaos_fx_send_offsets.lua` (`ChaosFxSendOffset[id] = {dx, dy}`, generated by
  `client/tools/sprites/gen_fx_send_offsets.py`, `--check` and a unit test in CI) holds the whole-tile offset that brings
  the pivot nearest to its place: 15 ids, and every one of the 141 in-place effects ends within 15 px of its place
  (the old table left 15 of them 17-31 px off, the teleport 11 by 28, the holy 262 by 31; 96 now are within 4 px).
  Ids no longer listed, because they sit where they were drawn: 3 puff of smoke, 7 fire area, 11 teleport, 167 red
  smoke, 201 and 262 holy, 226 fire, 309 arcane, 416 dodge. 405 (the 4x4 pillar) goes one tile now, 15 px up and left of
  the middle (two tiles were 17 px past it); it and 409, 399 and 4 (13-15 px) would fit exactly only with the art re-cut
  in a new pair. No pair or client change is needed: a server restart is enough, with or without the engine patch.
  `Position:sendMagicEffect` (the guard of
  `chaos_constants.lua`, `fx_send_offset_core.lua`) sends there, so every
  Lua send (`ChaosSpell.fx`, `Fx`, scripts) is centred. Engine sends
  (src-patch 0060): `fx_send_offset_core.lua` hands the same table to the engine at every load of
  `chaos_constants.lua` (`Game.setFxSendOffsets(ChaosFxSendOffset)`, read anew on a reload), and
  `ProtocolGame::sendMagicEffect` sends every packet of a listed id at the centring tile: combat
  `COMBAT_PARAM_EFFECT` areas and targets, monster `areaEffect` / `shootEffect` impacts, the crit 173 / 415, poffs,
  teleports, Lua sends. Kept on the map, same floor; a player who sees the target but not the centring tile gets the
  effect at the target, as before. Once the engine took the table the Lua guard sends at the target tile, so nothing
  is shifted twice; an engine without 0060 has no `Game.setFxSendOffsets` and the Lua guard shifts the Lua sends as
  before. The pair 29 hit overrides (src-patch 0045) carry their own dx, dy on `ChaosVfx` ids, none in the table.
  Tests: `client/tools/sprites/gen_fx_send_offsets_test.py` (the rounding, synthetic pivots, every in-place effect has a
  pivot and ends within 15 px, the Lua table is the generated one), `tests/fx_send_offset_test.lua` (405 one tile, 11, 201
  and 262 at their own tile, no `ChaosVfx` id shifted twice),
  `tests/magic_effect_guard_test.lua`, `tests/fx_send_offset_engine_test.lua` (the hand-over, no double shift, an
  engine without the patch), `tools/chaosfxoffsets_test.cpp` (lookup, map clamp, viewers at the edge; CI).
- **Appended:** effects 855-4101 and missiles 189-250, named in `data/lib/chaos_pack36_fx_ids.lua` (generated by
  `client/tools/sprites/import_fx_art.py`; catalog `data/spells/pack36_fx_catalog.csv`). `C.live()` loads them into
  `ChaosVfx` / `ChaosVfxMissile`; any script may send them by name.
- **Spells:** `_common.lua` `pack36(kind, name)` (`ChaosSpell.pack36`), asked by `pack27()` after pair 27 and pair 29
  have no swap: 42 spells pair 27 does not touch get pack art (`C.spells`, same kinds as pair 27: fx, missile, dir,
  fxdir). Examples: Dawnpiercer w_impact_holy_strike, Final Verdict w_impact_divine_judgment, Blightswarm
  mega_venom_wasps, Iaijutsu cone_steel_crescent_<dir>, Mistborne Step w_impact_gale_cut (fxdir), Corpse Explosion
  w_impact_corpse_explosion. `C.names` holds each spell's name, checked against `spells_chaos.xml`.
- **Client:** the level-up effect (`w_fx_level_up`, "Level-up effect") and the loot beams (`beam_*`, "Loot beams")
  are sent by the client by id; the server's level_up use of pair 27 (`catchup.lua`) is gone.
- **Switch off** (`C.PAIR36_FX = false`): the ids file is not loaded and every spell sends what it sent before. The
  in-place art stays, as it is in the pair. A client on pair 35 or older logs "invalid effect id" for appended ids.
- **Tests:** `tests/pack36_fx_test.lua` (specs, ids from 855 / 189 in order, every spell and name against
  `spells_chaos.xml`, no overlap with pair 27, the switch, the wiring in `_common.lua`); `tests/pack27_fx_test.lua`
  (no level_up use). Client: `levelwingsmath_test.lua`, `lootbeams_test.lua` (ids against the ids file).
  Not run on a live server or in a client.

### Pair 41 / 42 missile wiring (O239)
`ChaosSpell.pshoot(from, to, pname, vname, name, fallback)` (`data/spells/chaos/_common.lua`) sends the ChaosVfxMissile
`pname` at its send offset. It loads the ids through `ChaosPack36Fx.live()` (switch `PAIR36_FX`). It sends the old
missile (`vshoot(vname ..)`, else `shoot(name ..)`, else nothing) when the ids are not known, when the caster chose a
skin for it, or when a pair 27 / 29 swap exists for the old name (those switches stay in charge). So a client or a
config without the art draws what it drew before. Attack kit specs take `pshot` (and `pshotBy`, a vocation name to
missile map) in `attack_kit_config.lua`. The elemental extra projectile of a bow (`chaos_archery_core.lua` `ELEMENTS`,
`vmissile`) is sent by `weapon_styles.lua`; the ordinary shot of a bow is the engine's ammunition missile and is not
touched. The table of what flies where, checked by `tests/pack41_fx_test.lua`:

| Missile | Sent by |
|---|---|
| `proj_arrow_fire` 251, `proj_arrow_frost` 252 | extra projectile of a bow or crossbow with a fire or ice quiver |
| `proj_piercing_arrow_holy` 253 | Ranger line: Sunspear, Dawnpiercer, Hail of Dawn, Final Verdict, Twin Verdict |
| `proj_ball_lightning_thunder` | Forked Storm |
| `proj_boulder_magma` | Falling Pyre |
| `proj_wind_blade_storm` | Iaijutsu |
| `proj_razor_leaf_sakura` | Razor Rain, Samurai only (Thief and Ninja keep the razor disc) |
| `proj_blood_spike_necrotic` | Marrow Bolt |
| `proj_venom_glob_necrotic` | Blightbrand |
| `proj_flame_lance_spirit` | Soulrend Beam |
| `proj_shadow_bolt_blood` | Life Siphon (the drain flies back to the Lich) |
| `proj_soul_skull_spirit` | Raise Dead |
| `proj_spirit_wisp_arcane` | Mirror Mend (heal to an ally) |
| `proj_void_orb_abyss` | Umbral Stride |
| `proj_poison_dart_necrotic` | Soul Rot (the rot flies as a dart; the Beastmaster dart is earth and keeps its dart) |
| `proj_spirit_arrow_blood` | Skewering Line (a caster with the blood spear store skin keeps the skin, `pshoot` yields to it) |
| `proj_spirit_arrow_gold` | Radiant Smite (Templar holy filler) |
| `proj_water_bolt_abyss` | Dreamrot (Illusionist; no spell is water, this is the abyssal one; it sent no missile before, so a client without the art sees none) |

Monster files are base data and are not edited. Energy and earth quivers keep the flash and earth arrow.

## Pack farming spell effects (`data/lib/chaos_pack27_fx.lua`, `data/lib/chaos_pack27_fx_ids.lua`, switch `ChaosPack27Fx.PAIR27_FX`, on)
The nine pack farming spells borrowed their effects from other spells. A local trial pair 27 (client/MANIFEST.md
"Pack farming spell effects (pair 27 trial)", effects 674-758, missiles 154-160 on top of things_custom26) gives them
their own. It also gives 34 spells of the other class lines new impacts, plus vigil, stun, buff, game feel, Town Portal
and boss telegraph effects. Effects only: nothing else changes.
- Spells: during a cast `_common.lua` asks `ChaosPack27Fx.swapFor(spellId, kind, name)` in `ChaosSpell.fx` / `vfx` /
  `vfxDir` / `shoot` / `vshoot`. A skin always wins. A large effect and a class signature effect win too, unless the
  spell lists the name in `first` (`swapFor` then also returns true): the new art is the point of those swaps.
  - Pack farming: Palm Shockwave palm_quake; Blade Flurry flurry_petals (the Ninja and Samurai keep their class
    effects); Iaido Sweep iaido_dash_<dir>; Shadow Ricochet ricochet_bolt + ricochet_burst; Iron Chain chain_disc +
    chain_sparks; Bone Shrapnel shrapnel_shards + shrapnel_burst; Sanctified Ground sanctified_seal; Shield Wave
    shieldwave_bash_<dir> (kind `fxdir`: turned from the caster towards its tile); Fan of Knives fan_knife; Hunter's
    Instinct hunter_focus.
  - Mystic: Rime Bloom nova_frost; Falling Pyre meteor_fall (first); Forked Storm storm_chain on each jump (first);
    Tear in the Weave rift_void (first).
  - Templar: Radiant Smite smite_radiant + holy_orb; Judgement judgment_holy, Purging Nova nova_radiant, Vow of Mending
    mend_holy, Zealotry zeal_oath, Aegis of Faith aegis_radiant (all first).
  - Warrior: Reaping Gyre gyre_steel, Earthbreaker slam_earth, Colossus Fall terra_strike, Iron Bellow bellow_cry, Red
    Frenzy and Bloodrage berserk_blood (all first); Skyfall Cleave and Vaulting Cleave cleave_blood_<dir>.
  - Thief: Shadow Step backstab_shadow, Counter Stance parry_steel, Shadow Veil veil_stealth (first); Poison Blades
    venom_flurry; Shuriken Toss and Shuriken Barrage shuriken_steel.
  - Necromancer: Life Siphon drain_blood; Raise Dead summon_necro + soul_skull; Withering Curse curse_mark (first) +
    soul_skull; Soul Rot soul_skull.
  - Monk: Shadowfist Flurry claws_shadow_<dir> (fxdir); Ashen Fist punch_fire; Iron Palm hammer_steel; Kindled Breath
    healing_burst. Shared: Soulward ward_shield.
- Uses (`C.uses`, `ChaosPack27Fx.send(pos, use)`, on the player): `catchup.lua` rested, returning, catchup (login
  messages), low_stamina (the daily notice) (level_up, levelup_rise on a new level, removed 2026-10-22: the client
  now plays the pair 36 level-up effect, see "Level-up effect");
  `embercache.lua` embercache (each reward toast); `candlemarks.lua` candlemarks (Candlemarks earned); `_vigils.lua`
  vigil_wrath / iron / haste / clarity (a vigil switched on); `ironsage/iron_palm.lua` stun (a monster really
  stunned). Loot beams (`C.rays`, `lootfilter.lua` emitRay): legendary gold, divine steel, cosmic amethyst, unique
  emerald; the other rays stay.
- Town Portal (`C.portals`, `C.portal(name)`, tried first in `townportal.lua` fx): the channel arcane_circle
  portal_pad, the Waygate teleport_in portal_in and teleport_out portal_out.
- Boss telegraph (`C.telegraph(tiles)`, `boss_mechanics.lua` first pulse): a round telegraph of 5 tiles across gets
  boss_telegraph at its centre (`C.telegraphCentre`, via `ChaosBigFx.circleOf`); any other shape keeps
  `ChaosBigFx.telegraph`.
- On (shipped since 2026-10-15, pair 27 live on windows-assets 51a26d26). Off: the ids file is not loaded, `send`
  sends nothing, `ray`, `portal` give nil and `telegraph` false, so every call site sends what it sent before; set it
  off for clients still on pair 26 or older (`install_all.py SERVER_DIR --only files`, restart).
- The swaps are keyed by spell id; `C.names` holds each spell's name and `tests/pack27_fx_test.lua` checks both against
  spells_chaos.xml, so a moved id fails the test (update `C.spells` and `C.names`).
- Tests: `tests/pack27_fx_test.lua` (switch line on; ids and names in spells_chaos.xml; each script sends the
  swapped name; every new name in the client spec and the ids file; missile ids fit u8; the loot rays, portal names
  and telegraph exist; the `first` flag; off: no swap, no use effect, rays, portals and telegraph unchanged; on: the
  names, the gold beam, the level up effect, the 5 vs 7 tile telegraph; `_common.lua` and every call site wired). Not
  run on a server or in a client.

## Class lock (`class_unlocks.lua`, `class_unlocks_core.lua`, `sql/chaos_class_unlocks.sql`)

The Necromancer, the Monk and the Templar (docs/CLASSES.md, classes five to seven) need an account-wide unlock. The method is one
table, `ChaosClassUnlocksCore.config` (`class_unlocks_core.lua`): per class key (`necromancer`, `monk`, `templar`) the vocation ids,
`locked`, and the unlock methods (`store`, `level`, `quest`, `achievement`, or a new kind registered with `registerMethod`). One
method since 2026-10-15: `level = {min = 200}` (free for the whole account once any of its characters reaches level 200, checked at
login and on level advance). History: 2026-10-14 the store (category "Classes", 500 coins each) or level 500; 2026-10-15 level 200
("Time-friendly progression") and the store offers removed (owner rule "follow your recommendations": classes are earned by play,
never sold; nobody had bought one). The `store` method and `ChaosClassUnlocks.storeUnlock` stay in the code, unused: a class offer
in `shop_config.lua` with a matching `store` entry in the config would sell it again. The unlock is written to
`chaos_class_unlocks` at once (not the engine's account storage, which is only saved at server save). The lock message, the
character creation (client and website) and the cancel text name the level, not the store.

- Gates: the Ascendant Oracle (ascension.lua) and Character > Services (shop_services.lua; the token is kept) refuse a locked class; at login a
  character on a locked vocation goes to its temple, cannot attack and gains no experience or skills until the account unlocks
  the class (the store works in that state). Staff (group 4+, or account type 5+) is never locked.
- Character > Character Info shows the account's state; staff: `/classunlock <character>, <class>[, revoke]`
  (an unlock needs group 5, a revoke group 4; `Chaos.staffCommand`).
- Characters are created on the website (the base server has no in-game character creation): it should offer the three classes
  only to unlocked accounts; the login check holds even if it does not.
- Tested in game (2026-10-09): a locked account's Necromancer logs in to its temple with the warning (also as a window, one
  sentence per line) and can neither cast nor attack; the Ascendant Oracle refuses a locked Templar; Character > Services refuses
  a locked class and keeps the Vocation Change token; buying the Necromancer in the store (Classes, 750 coins) unlocks it at once
  for every character of the account, and the Oracle then ascends it.

## Achievements (`achievements.lua`, `achievements_core.lua`, `achievements_data.lua`, client `game_achievements`)

Long-term goals across every system: 178 achievements in 10 categories (Combat & Leveling, Monsters, World Bosses, Rifts,
Raids, Bounties, Items & Crafting, PvP, Exploration & Social, Secrets), 4280 points in all (counted from
`achievements_data.lua` on 2026-10-14; the five deep dungeon ones, in Raids: a clear of each of the four, 10 / 10 / 15 /
25 points, and the hidden "Into the Last Fire", all four on difficulty 6, 50 points, title "the Unchained"; their
counters `dungeon_<area id>`, `_top`, `_d6` come from `areagen.lua` at a won run). Client `game_achievements` (Chaos ->
Achievements in the top menu, or Character > Achievements), extended opcode 250 (`ChaosOpcodes.achievements`), tables
`chaos_achievements` and `chaos_achievement_stats` (`sql/chaos_achievements.sql`; also created at startup).

- **The list** is `achievements_data.lua`, one line each: `id`, `name`, `desc`, `cat`, `points`, `stat` + `target` (or `all =
  {stats}`: each at least once), optional `hidden`, `title` (24 characters at most) and `reward` (`gold`, `items`, `outfit =
  {name, female, male, addons}`, `mount = {name, id}`; outfits and mounts the base server already has). Bad entries are
  printed at startup and left out. Never rename a live `id`: it is what the database stores.
- **Counters** (per character, they only go up): `ChaosAchievements.progress(who, key, amount)` and `.set(who, key, value)`
  (the higher value is kept); `who` is a Player, a guid or `{guid, name}`. Offline characters are written straight to the
  database and checked at their next login. Online counters are saved every 30 s, at logout and at shutdown; unlocks at once.
  An achievement unlocks once per character (`INSERT IGNORE`), with a chat line, a toast (game_chaosnotify action
  `achievement`, header ACHIEVEMENT UNLOCKED, trophy icon), its reward and its title; the window refreshes if it is open.
  The toast (`achievements_core.lua` `K.toast`) reads "The Thousandth Step: +50 points. Title: the Unbroken. Reward:
  mount Doombringer."; the quiet login check sends one summary (`K.summaryToast`: "3 achievements unlocked: +30 points:
  A, B, C. Rewards: ..."). Every path toasts: a live counter, the 30 s sweep, level up and a staff grant (one toast each),
  the login check and offline counters (the summary). The unlock row is written first; when that write fails nothing is
  given or shown and a later check tries again, so a relog never unlocks, rewards or toasts twice. A class unlocked by
  achievements ("Class unlocked") and a reward track cosmetic (cosmetics.lua, "Reward track") toast with the same header.
- **Where the counters come from.** Nothing in the other systems was rewritten:
  - level, Paragon level (`level - Chaos.paragon.startLevel`), ascension, tutorial island finished, guild: login, level up
    and a 30 s sweep of the online characters;
  - kills (a `kill` event on every player, the tier from `ChaosTierOf`): magic / rare / legendary, party kills, Treasure
    Goblins, the secrets; ambushes from `ChaosTierDead[id].depth` (one line added to `monster_tiers.lua`);
  - `ChaosLeaderboard.record` is wrapped at runtime, like `season.lua` does: `bounty` (contracts), `rift` (tier, runs; the
    modifiers and "nobody lost" from `ChaosRift.runOf`), `arena1v1` / `arena2v2` (wins and best rating from
    `ChaosArena.ratingOf`), `siege` (played; won when the player's bracket winner is their guild);
  - `ChaosWorldBoss.computeRewards` is wrapped: every rewarded player (offline ones too), the boss by name, top damage = rank 1;
  - `ChaosCrafting.apply` is wrapped: orbs used on the bench and by the crafting orbs' use-with, Orbs of Grafting, the most
    modifiers on an item. **Not counted:** the base server's own Upheaval / Fate use-with (`reroll_rarity_stats.lua`,
    local functions, no hook);
  - `ChaosTreasureGoblin.tick` is wrapped: a goblin removed by its timer after being hit = "escaped" for its attackers;
  - an `onDropLoot` callback at index 2.4 (before the loot filter's snapshot and the base autoloot): uniques found, best
    rarity, modifiers. Only monster corpses count (not rift chests, goblin hoards or world boss rewards);
  - the weekly bounty chest: `Chaos.storage.bountyWeekBonus` holds the week of the last chest; a newer week = one more.
  - the bestiary (`bestiary.lua`, guarded calls): `bestiary_known`, `bestiary_completed`, `bestiary_points` (set at a new
    stage and 2 s after login, so they are retroactive) and `bestiary_tasks` (a completed kill task);
  Any other script: `if ChaosAchievements then ChaosAchievements.progress(player, "my_stat", 1) end` and an entry with
  `stat = "my_stat"`.
- **Retroactive** at every login (quietly, one summary toast): level, Paragon, ascension, tutorial, guild, completed contracts
  in `chaos_bounty` (`status = 1`), the last weekly bounty chest, arena wins and best rating in `chaos_arena_ratings`. Kills,
  orbs, rifts and world bosses have no history to read and start at 0.
- **Points.** Character points are the sum of its unlocks. Account points count each achievement once, whichever character
  of the account earned it (alts do not add the same achievement twice). The window shows both.
- **Titles** go to the name plates: `ChaosTitles.register("achievement", ...)` (titles.lua, colour teal), key
  `achievement:<id>`. Players pick one with the Achievements window or the window's title box (it says the Achievements window for them).
  Nothing happens while titles.lua is not loaded.
- **Reward track** (cosmetics earned by playing, never sold). Account achievement points unlock a cosmetic at 100 / 250 /
  500 / 1000 / 1750 / 2500 / 3500 points (3880 exist), and a category whose every achievement the account has (any of its
  characters, hidden ones too) gives a title and a cosmetic. The cosmetics are entries of `cosmetics_config.lua` (source
  `achievement` with `points` or `category`, table in "Cosmetics"); the titles are `categoryRewards` in
  `achievements_data.lua` (titles.lua source `achievement`, key `achievement_cat:<key>`, the frame while it is the active
  title; account-wide, so every character of the account holds them):

  | Category | Title (frame) | Cosmetic |
  |---|---|---|
  | Combat & Leveling | Warmaster (ember) | War Surge, kill effect |
  | Monsters | Beastwarden (verdant) | Thornbloom, kill effect |
  | World Bosses | Titanfeller (bone) | Titan's Pyre, kill effect |
  | Rifts | Riftwarden (violet) | Rift Sigil, kill effect |
  | Raids | Sepulchre Lord (bone) | Sepulchre Labels, label accent |
  | Bounties | the Relentless (ember) | Huntsman's Copper, chat colour |
  | Items & Crafting | Forgewright (frost) | Tempered Labels, label accent |
  | PvP | the Unconquered (violet) | Bloodsteel Name, chat colour |
  | Exploration & Social | Wayfarer (verdant) | Lantern Name, chat colour |
  | Secrets | Keeper of Secrets (frost) | Falling Stars, kill effect |

  Grants go through cosmetics.lua (`ChaosCosmetics.sync`): at login, when the Cosmetics window opens and after every new
  unlock (`ChaosAchievements.syncTrack`, also after a staff `grant`); idempotent and never taken back. Staff re-sync:
  `/cosmetic <character>, sync`. A new category in the list needs its `categoryRewards` entry and a cosmetic, or it simply
  has none (the validators name a bad one). Window: a reward track bar under the summary (account points to the next
  milestone, one pip per milestone with a preview tooltip: name, kind, description, colour or label background, points to
  go), a "Reward track" entry in the category list (a row per milestone and per category, chat colours drawn in their
  colour, label accents behind the kind line), and each category's tooltip names its completion reward. Protocol: `track
  {ap, steps = [{p, n, k, d, c, a, o}], cats = [{key, cn, dn, t, ti, n, k, d, c, a, o, x}]}` after `state`
  (`ChaosCosmeticsCore.trackView`, one message under 7 KB). Nothing is sent while cosmetics.lua is not loaded.
- **Class unlock method.** achievements.lua replaces the `achievement` kind of `ChaosClassUnlocksCore` with a superset of it:
  `achievement = {points = 500}` (the account has 500 achievement points), `achievement = {name = "rift_t10"}` (any
  character of the account has that achievement), or both (either is enough). It is checked at login and on level up by
  class_unlocks.lua, and after every unlock by achievements.lua. **No class uses it**: every class keeps `store` only. To
  offer it, add it next to the store in `class_unlocks_core.lua`, e.g.
  `unlock = {store = {offer = "unlockMonk", cost = 750}, achievement = {points = 500}}` (any listed method unlocks; the lock
  message lists both).
- **Protocol** (opcode 250, JSON `{action, data}`): client `open` / `get`; server `state` (points, account points, counts,
  categories, recent, titles, active title), then `list` in parts of 30 rows (`{i, n, d, c, p, h, u, v, t, ti, r}`; hidden
  locked rows come as "???" with no progress, title or reward), and `unlock` (the open window asks again).
- **Commands.** Character > Achievements (summary + window). Staff (`/achievements`, on yourself): `grant <id>`, `stat <key> <value>`,
  `add <key> <n>`, `reset`.
- **Tests:** `tests/achievements_test.lua` (the list, thresholds, unlocking once, hidden rows, points and account points, the
  retroactive stats, titles, the class unlock method plugged into class_unlocks_core.lua, SQL; the reward track's category
  completion, titles and frames, and achievements.lua on a mocked engine: the sync after new unlocks only, the track
  message, a second character's category titles) and the client's `game_achievements/achievementsview_test.lua` (the
  track bar, pips, tooltips and rows).
  **Reward track tested in game** (test server copy, one client, a level 1000 character with 62 achievements, 1285 account
  points): the 4 milestones and 4 complete categories granted at login, the bar and pips, the milestone tooltip, the Reward
  track view, a category's tooltip, the four category titles in the title box. Screenshots outside the repository.

**Tested in game** (test server, cropped map): retroactive unlocks at login (level 562: levels 50-500, ascension, with the
level 500 orbs; a level 1000 character: the Doombringer mount, arena 1v1 wins / rating 1200 and bounty contracts read from
the database), a live level up (level 700 + its orbs) with the toast, a legendary ambush copy (Legend Slayer, It Was a
Trap, the hidden Out of the Frying Pan, Legendary Find from its corpse), a rare kill, an Orb of Upheaval on the crafting bench, a
tier 1 rift sealed with Brutality / Withering / Swarm (6 achievements), a death, a bounty record and the weekly chest
storage, world boss shares for an offline character (unlocked at its next login), the window (categories, progress,
"???", recent), the title box and the title on the name plate, the class unlock method with a test config. Not tested in
game: arena and siege matches, a real world boss fight, a Treasure Goblin escape, party kills (unit-level only or not at
all).

## Late game (`tools/late_game.py`, `tools/late_game_spawns.csv`, 17 monsters in `data/monster/monsters/chaos/`)

Goal agreed with the owner: a dedicated sorcerer reaches level 1000 in about 100 hours, knights and paladins in about 150
or less. Before, the model gave ~155 h (sorcerer) and ~285 h (knight, paladin), 80% of it between 700 and 1000.
`python3 -I server/tools/late_game.py <server>/data [--config PATH] [--spawn PATH] [--dry-run] [--remove]` does both parts
below; it is idempotent and `--remove` restores the stock stage table and every replaced spawn.

### Experience stages (`config.lua`)

Levels 1-700 are the smooth table since 2026-10-23 ("Progression smoothness (O135)"); the table below is the late game (701+), which did not change.

| Level | 1-650 | 651-700 | 701-750 | 751-800 | 801-850 | 851-900 | 901-950 | 951+ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| before (as written) | unchanged | 15 | 12 | 9 | 6 | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| before (as the engine used it) | unchanged | 15 | 12 | 9 | 6 | **5** | **5** | **5** |
| after | unchanged | 15 | 15 | 15 | 14 | 14 | 13 | 13 |

The stock last stage `{ minlevel = 851, multiplier = 3 }` has no maxlevel. This engine's `loadLuaStages` reads a missing
maxlevel as 0, so the stage never matched and levels 851+ fell back to `rateExp` (5). The new table gives its last stage
`maxlevel = 999999`. Checked on the test server: `Game.getExperienceStage` 700 -> 15, 750 -> 15, 800 -> 15, 801 -> 14,
900 -> 14, 901 -> 13, 1000 -> 13 (before the fix in the tool, 951 and 1000 returned 5).

### The monsters

The imported level-scaled monsters of the 650-1300 band that render in the client (Dawn Strayer, which drew broken, joined
later on its new art 2122; Cunning Hyaena's art does not match it, Mercenary and Mercenary Ranger have no sprite; see `data/monster/CUSTOM_MONSTERS.md`).
The engine scales a monster at level L: health x(1 + 0.0074 L), speed x(1 + 0.0085 L), damage x(1 + 0.0015 L),
experience x0.03 L (`data/events/scripts/player.lua`), black skull from 401 and loot x2.7 from 501. At their old levels
(up to 1300) they had 300k-900k health and 3000-7000 speed. Now:
- levels clamped to 650-1000, narrow ranges, three tiers;
- base health, experience and speed rewritten so the values at the level land where they should (speed 380-480 like the
  existing 500+ monsters, 350-450);
- attack damage scaled per monster so that a level 1000 knight in the best level 1000 gear takes about as much per second as
  from the strongest existing late-game monsters (Embermaw Archon and Inferno Juggernaut ~1550/s, Pitlord Incarnate ~1070/s,
  Aegis Sentinel ~780/s); player spells used as monster attacks (Reaver's Spin, Thornlash, an unknown "death wave",
  "arc bolt") became plain combat attacks, `lenght` typos fixed, slows capped at -900, hastes at +300 (that tuning was with
  the stock armour; with the percent armour, `monster_damage.lua` adds +30% to their physical hits on players at runtime,
  see "Late-game damage boost", so the XML values stay as measured);
- elements: physical and holy -15% (weakness), fire, energy, ice and earth +20%, death +10%. This is the lever that gives
  knights and paladins a hunt where they keep up (see the model);
- the donor events (`auto_loot`, `orb_bonus`, `crusd_chest_bonus`, unknown here, one warning per spawn) were removed, and
  the donor's "one of" loot lines (`id="a;b;c"`, which this engine reads as item 0 and drops) became one line per item with
  the chance split.

Values at the middle of the level range (health, speed and experience per health point as measured in game on fresh
normal-tier spawns; damage per second and the largest 100 ms hit measured with 45 s of a monster attacking a level 1000
two-handed knight in full level 1000 gear):

"Largest hit" is the largest health drop in one 100 ms sample, so attacks that land on the same tick add up: Blazebringer's
12k and Swamp Snapper's 8.9k are such peaks (Blazebringer peaked at 3.4k in an earlier 40 s run with nearly the same
scale); most attacks land at 1-3k. A level 1000 knight standing in Nightglass Core without healing went from 18k to 9k in
about 2 s against a pull of 6-8 and died in the next area: these are not monsters to pull in packs of five.

Tier averages of experience per health point: 1.19 (levels 650-750), 1.80 (760-850), 2.20 (860-1000). Today's best
spawned monsters give 1.0-1.45 (Soul War 1.02, Helm Hunter 1.43, Aegis Sentinel 1.45), so the first tier is no faster than
the existing 650-700 hunts. The Chaos monster tiers (magic/rare/legendary) still apply on top, as everywhere.

### The 1300-2000 set (2026-10-14, owner approved; `tools/tune_monsters.py` `HIGH_BAND`)

Facetis (1260-1300) was the strongest hunting monster, so the 1300-1500 plans ran on more of the 1140-1280 set and
nothing existed above. Eight monsters of our own, one every 100 levels, continue the curves of the 1000-1280 set

experience per health 1.15 + 0.0039 (L - 670), speed at the level 380 + (L - 650) / 6.5, the strongest hit 800 + 0.8
(L - 650) before the level bonus, heals 10% of the base health). `tune_monsters.py --check` (and check_content.py) keep the
files on the curve; each has its own speed step. Elements: two of its own at 55%, one weakness at 0, the rest 35% (on
average 36%, like the 35% of the 1000-1280 imports), so a hunter of the right element kills faster.

Computed, not measured in game. Damage/s at L: the sum of chance x average / interval of the damage attacks, x the
engine's 1 + 0.0015 L, without conditions and before armour and resistances; physical hits on players get the late-game
boost (+30%, "Late-game damage boost") on top. Per second they take 13-17% of a knight's health at their level (15 x L +
185), Facetis 17%. Solo kill time (health / 0.64 / the one-target damage 2,600 + 2.41 (L - 1000), "Solo kill times";
heals and armour left out): 137 s at 1300 to 166 s at 2000, on the line of the 1000-1280 set (112 s at 1000, 134 s
Facetis at 1280). The strongest hit is 20% of that knight's health at 1300 and 25% at 2000 (Facetis 20%).

- **Looks** (no new art, no pair push): outfits of the live pair (things_custom24) that no monster, mount, wing or aura
  used: donor B 1532, 1543, 1544, 1546, 1547 (`client/tools/sprites/donor_b_selection.csv`: red dragon, skeleton
  warrior, frost skeleton, minotaur warlord, werewolf) and stock 1369, 1449, 1462. Checked against every monster file,
  every Lua look in `data/`, the picks csvs and the base server's monsters and XML lists; rendered from the pair.
  Without colour layers, so the files carry no colours.
- **Loot**: the 1000-1280 set's coin lines (platinum 55-90 by level) and equipment pool, a titanium token 50-85 in 100,000,
  and one equipment item of the tier 1 pool at 600 as the monster's own drop (Ravager skullcracker armor, Revenant frozen
  plate, Reaver skull helmet, Fiend demon shield, Juggernaut great shield, Stalker crystal boots, Wyrm swamplair armor,
  Tyrant elite draken mail; every id priced already). Item level and rarity follow the level (`loot.lua`
  `L.monsterLevel`).
- **Telegraphs**: Mirecoil Wyrm and Pyrewing Tyrant have a light `boss_mechanics_config.lua` profile (two small shapes, a
  fifth of max health, one every 16 s, 2.9 s warning; no `ref`, so no health change); "Boss mechanics" auto-attaches it
  by name. The other six have none.
- **Where**: the plans gravehorn_deeps (1500-1750) and duskmarrow_crater (1750-2000), docs/MAP_GUIDE.md "Content
  plans"; the bounty board and bestiary know them once a plan is placed and `gen_bounty_pool.py` /
  `gen_bestiary_spawns.py` run again.

### The leveling model and the hours

The model of the earlier analysis: rotation DPS from `data/spells/README.md` (5-target values, interpolated 300 -> 1000),
0.47 of it turning into kills, the best hunt per level (generic 1.25 exp/health, Soul War with its task from 500), tasks as
flat experience. Added: the new monsters from the level a player can hunt them (tier 1 from 650, tier 2 from 725, tier 3 from
800) at their exp/health, with fewer targets per pull (3 instead of 5: they are 5-8 times bulkier than the area's old
monsters and hit as hard as the strongest existing ones) and their elements (knights and paladins x1.15, sorcerers x0.80).
"Boosted" = premium stamina x1.5, double experience potion, Soul Pit; "+hooks" also the Chaos callbacks (Blood Moon,
passive tree, store World Experience +25%, waystone upgrade) as in the earlier analysis.

| sorcerer | after | 0.3 | 2.6 | 7.3 | 21.8 | 17.2 | 21.1 | 25.5 | **96** |

Levels 1-700 are unchanged (no stage changed there, and the first tier is not better than the existing 650-700 hunts). In

84 -> 38, 82 -> 34 h.

Checked on the test server: all 268 entries spawn (a monster of the new name within 6 sqm of every row, 268/268 walkable);
experience per kill at a level 900 knight = XML exp x 0.03 x level x stage x 1.5 (premium stamina) x 1.25 (the store's World
Experience buff that was active), i.e. exactly 1.875 x the model for all 17. Not measured: real hunting speed (the 0.47
efficiency and the 3-target assumption), the one-handed knight (~14% less damage than two-handed), druids and
illusionists (earth/ice/death are resisted too).

Pack combat (2026-10-14) multiplies these kills by its `scaled` experience curve on top. Its points must count the
x0.03 L: the 2026-10-20 points did not and paid 5-10x this model per hour until O108 ("Pack combat (pace)", Scaled
experience re-fit: 500 -> 1000 in 112 h for the median class again, the model's 111 h; it was 40 h).

## Progression smoothness (O135, `tools/progression_model.lua`, `progression_config.lua`, `tools/late_game.py` `SMOOTH_STAGES`, 2026-10-23)

Owner request (pt-BR): "Faça a progressão ser mais fluída". Read as the leveling journey from the start level (8) to 2200:
find the walls, dead zones and spikes, measure them with the repo's own models, and smooth them.

**The model (computed from the repo's data, not measured in game).** Minutes per level at level L = the experience to the
next level (the engine's `50 L^2 - 150 L + 200`) / (the median experience per hour of the pool hunts whose hunting level is
within 0.8-1.1 L, x the chain bonus 1.3, x the experience stage of L). A hunt pays its `pace_config.lua` experience per kill
at the pack model's kills per hour (`spawn_tuning.json` `paceKillsPerHour`). `luajit tools/progression_model.lua` prints the
table, `--check` is the CI gate, `--spells` lists the unlock gaps. Limits and windows: `progression_config.lua`. The absolute
hours differ from "The leveling model and the hours" (that one is the fastest class with the best hunt; this is the median
hunt, so it is slower); only the shape matters here, and the band hours of 100+ did not change.

**What the measurement found.**

| Finding | Where | Before | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cliff in the stage table | level 20 to 21 | x10 up to 20, x50 from 21: levels 8-20 took 1.1-2.7 minutes a level, levels 21-50 0.35-0.6 (a 5x jump, 10-level blocks fall to 0.37x) | `SMOOTH_STAGES`: x30 at level 8 rising to x36 at 20, x38 at 28, x40 at 40, x45 at 51 |
| Steps of 3 every 50 levels | 301 to 700 | each 50th level paid 8-20% less per kill (x36, 33, 30, ... 15) | one multiplier per step, rows of 14-17 levels, the same averages (hours of 300-700 within 0.5%) |
| Paragon track ends | level 1282 to 2200 | 282 points, one a level, all spent at 1282: 900 levels of level-ups with no new choice | one point a level up to 1100, then one every 6 levels: all 282 at level 2192; points already owned stay |
| Hall hunt gaps | levels 163-233, 386-518 (by a window of 0.8-1.1 L) | 0-2 hall hunts, the nearest 22% above | fixed by O139 (below, "Hall coverage (O139)"): 8 new hunts, `--check` also fails on fewer than 3 within 0.8-1.1 L in the listed ranges |
| Gold per hour | 300 to 800 | 469k (300), 393k (500), 2.5M (800): a dip, then a 6x jump (`tools/loot_model.lua`) | fixed by O141 ("Balance follow-ups (O141)"): 469k, 860k (500), 2.5M; reported at first |
| Spell unlock gaps | levels 130-380 | longest stretches without a new spell below 300: Ninja 180 to 360, Beastmaster 220 to 380, Berserker 130 to 260, Lich 170 to 300, Shadowfist 150 to 250 | fixed by O141 for the attack spells (4 unlock levels moved); `--spells` prints all 21 and counts supports too |

Before and after (minutes a level, mean of 3 levels; stage):

| Level | Before | After | Stage before / after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 1.88 | 0.61 | x10 / x30 |
| 12 | 2.21 | 0.68 | x10 / x32 |
| 16 | 2.74 | 0.79 | x10 / x34 |
| 20 | 1.08 | 0.63 | x10 / x36 |
| 21 | 0.44 | 0.61 | x50 / x36 |
| 30 | 0.35 | 0.46 | x50 / x38 |
| 50 | 0.59 | 0.61 | x50 / x45 |
| 100 | 0.85 | 0.84 | x45 / x44 |
| 300 | 2.90 | 2.75 | x39 / x39 |
| 500 | 7.49 | 7.37 | x27 / x26 |
| 650 | 13.17 | 12.81 | x18 / x17 |
| 700 | 15.11 | 15.11 | x15 / x15 |
| 1000 | 18.19 | 18.19 | x13 / x13 |
| 2000 | 41.15 | 41.15 | x13 / x13 |

Hours (model): 8-20 0.46 to 0.14; 20-50 0.25 to 0.28; 50-100 0.55 to 0.56; 100-300 5.87 to 5.85; 300-500 15.6 (same);
500-700 35.9 to 35.7; 700-1000 80.9 (same); 8-1000 139.5 to 139.0. The worst 10-level change of the minutes a level over
8-2200 went from 0.37x (a cliff) to 0.78x, and the worst rise from 1.26x to 1.18x. The largest step of the stage table went
from 5x to 1.077x (15 to 14, 14 to 13 in the late game; unchanged). From 700 the curve is flat (15-18 minutes a level to 1000,
19-21 to 1400) and rises 5% every 50 levels from 1500 to 2200 (23 to 50 minutes): smooth, and it matches the experience
needed per level growing with L^2 against hunts that pay linearly.

**`--check` (CI, `luajit` and `lua5.3`, `tests/progression_test.lua`).** Fails when: a stage row steps more than 8% from the
one before or the table has a hole; the mean minutes a level of consecutive 10-level blocks change by less than 0.75x or more
than 1.25x (25-level blocks 0.88x to 1.35x) between 8 and 2200; fewer than 4 pool hunts are in reach of a level; fewer than 3
hall hunts are within 0.7-1.3 L of a level. The test also feeds it the table from before O135 and expects the x50 step at
level 21 and the time cliff to be named.

**Not fixed, and why.**
- (Done in O139, "Hall coverage (O139)".) The hall had levels 163-233 and 386-518 with fewer than 3 hunts within 0.8-1.1 L;
  200 and 450 had the nearest hunt 22% above.
- Class power dips at levels 30 / 60 / 100 and spikes at 200 (spells/README.md "Attack spell parity"): the damage factors
  belong to the combat numbers; unlock levels of the attack kit are the cheapest lever and are listed by `--spells`.
- Gold per hour (above) and the costs of potions per band: loot tables and prices are other work.
- `catchup_config.lua` `model` and `rift_config.lua` `exp.model` keep their hours per band (the fastest class); levels
  8-20 are 20 minutes faster in the model, which they do not show.

**Install.** The stage table is written by `tools/late_game.py` (install step `lategame`, `install_all.py --only lategame`,
which the kit update runs): config.lua is read at the engine's start, so restart the server. A table with the old rows is
replaced; `chaos-ctl.sh xp-rate` keeps its factor (it scales the release table). Paragon needs only the script reload.
No client update and no engine rebuild.

engine rebuild. Not run on the real map: `tools/install_content_areas_test.py` (synthetic map) and the planner's compile and
QA of the twelve plans pass; the dry run on the live map is the owner's first step (`install_all.py --only contentareas
--dry-run`).

## Pack combat (pace) (`pace.lua`, `pace_core.lua`, `pace_config.lua`, 2026-10-14)

Owner request (pt-BR, paraphrased): players must feel strong and kill several monsters at once, not one by one, with
some danger left; more monsters, experience compensated; dungeons at most 10-15 minutes. Design and model:
`scratchpad/rebal/DESIGN.md` of the session (not in the repo); this section is what was built.

**Class identity pass (2026-10-28).** The pack cleave shares below `pace_config.lua` `cleave.byVocation` were all changed so that the
classes farm packs by role (pure area 1.00-1.10, mixed and tanks 0.88-0.95, healers 0.85-0.93, burst 0.80-0.86 of the median class
before the pass): docs/CLASSES.md "Class identity (2026-10-28)", `tools/pack_model.py --check` (`packLimits` in
`data/scripts/chaos/boss_balance_config.lua`). The Berserker has none (`percent = 0, high = 0`: `P.cleaveOf` returns nil). Fan of
Knives (`_packtools.lua` `fan.pack` 0.5) and Iaido Sweep (`_blades.lua` `sweep.pack` 0.9) hit the rest of the pack for less, and
`rotation_model.csv` follows (t5 = 1 + 4 x pack): run `python3 -I server/tools/rotation_sim.py --write` after changing a pack tool, it
rewrites the helper's Auto rotation data. The class damage factors that came with the pass are in `class_tree.lua` `classDamage`; the
Infinity Tower health lines were re-derived (`tools/tower_model.py --derive`).

**Rebalance 2026-10-20 (beta feedback).** (1) `scaled` curves: a level-scaled monster gave 1/15 of the experience and had
  1/4.6 of the health of a base monster of the same hunting level, so lvl 500 spiders (base) paid more than lvl 800
  monsters. New points follow the base monsters (`luajit tools/pace_scan.lua` prints the median experience and health by
  hunting level: now rising with the level in every band). That comparison (and `pace_scan.lua` then) left out both
  engine factors of a level-scaled monster, x0.03 L experience and x(1 + 0.0074 L) health ("Late game", checked on the
  test server), so the "1/15" and "1/4.6" were artefacts; the experience points paid 5-10x the model per hour, see
  "Scaled experience re-fit" below (O108). Generated area / dungeon points keep their old points as the new
  `generated` set (the queue dungeons' 10-minute model is calibrated on them). (2) New `gold` factor (`pace_config.lua`, base and scaled,
  0.30 from hunting level 450): a second thinning of coins and NPC-sellable items that are not gear (`L.isGoldLike`,
  `L.thinCorpse(corpse, f, g)`); orbs, gems, keys and gear keep only `loot`. Reason: gold per hour at level 500-600 was
  about 16M against the income model's 5.5-6.3M. Check it with the hunt tracker in the beta. Replaced 2026-10-21 by
  the smooth `coins` / `junkKeep` / `notable` curves of "Loot by monster level" below (same gold per hour). (3) Rifts: time limit
  1000 / 1100 / 1260 s per band, pack health model exponents `dps5Exp` 1.35 / `dps1Exp` 1.1 (tier 1 packs have half the
  health), completed-rift key chance 45% + 10% per modifier (cap 75%), rare / legendary in a rift 4% / 10%, tier 1 key
  from a normal kill 250 per 100000.

**One runtime layer.** Base monsters are about 95% of the spawns and their XML is not ours, so nothing is edited per
monster: `pace.lua` scales health, experience, loot and damage by the monster's hunting level at runtime, for base and
Chaos monsters alike. `pace_config.lua` `enabled = false` switches every part off (health, experience, loot, damage,
ambush and goblin chances, kill goals, multikill, cleave); the spawn side (fill, respawn) is install data and stays.
`scale` (`{xp = 1.0, loot = 1.0}`) multiplies the experience and loot curves for calibration (see the live check).

- **Hunting level** (`pace_core.lua` `P.levelOf`): `Monster:getMonsterLevel()` for a level-scaled monster; the spawn
  point's level for a generated area or dungeon monster (`ChaosAreaGen.pointOf`); else `baseLevelMult` (1 since O285,
  2026-10-28; 2 before) x `ChaosLoot.monsterLevel` (the bounty pool's fair-hunt estimate: the hunting level of a base
  monster is its pool level, "Level bands and capacity"). A monster with a level of its own uses the `scaled` curves.
- **O285: the base curves re-fitted to the pool level (2026-10-28).** With the x2 rule a pack at hunting level L was made
  of pool level L/2 monsters; now it is made of pool level L ones, whose stock health is about 2.5-3.5x and experience
  about 3-4x (the pool: health about 65 a level from level 300, experience about (level / 1.6)^2). The `base` health, xp
  and loot points were re-fitted so that, at every hunting level, what the models measure is what they measured before:
  health {20: 1.00 -> 0.28, 100: 0.36 -> 0.105, 250: 0.21 -> 0.095, 600: 0.21 -> 0.105} (`tools/pack_model.py`: the median
  class's pack dies in 2.3-4.6 s from level 20 to 600, as before, within 10%); xp {20: 1.00 -> 0.20, 100: 0.32 -> 0.082,
  250: 0.17 -> 0.075, 600: 0.16 -> 0.066} (`tools/progression_model.lua`: minutes per level within 0.93-1.08 of the old
  curve up to level 400, 7-17% shorter at 450-650); the goals did not change (the kills per hour did not). Levels
  under 10 (health) and 6 (xp) stay untouched, as the pool levels under 10 / 5 were. The base set ends at the pool's
  highest level (657): above it only level-scaled monsters are hunted, so `tools/pack_model.py --check` compares the late
  packs (670+) with a base pack of the top monsters whose health grows with the level, 2.0-2.7x (limit 3.0). O297: the shared
  `damage` curve was left as it was, so every base monster hit up to 41% harder than before (pool 450: x0.425 -> x0.60).
  `base.damage` is that curve at twice the level, so a base monster of pool level P hits as before O285 (`tests/pace_test.lua`
  pins P = 10 to 657); level-scaled and generated monsters keep the shared curve. A base hunt at hunting level L now has
  pool L monsters, whose stock hits are harder than the pool L/2 ones of before: that is the monsters' own strength.
- **O298: loot curves smoothed (2026-10-28).** The O285 re-fit left `base.loot`, `base.coins`, `base.cheapPrice` and
  `base.junkKeep` zigzagging (loot 0.19 / 0.068 / 0.032 / 0.078 at 300 / 350 / 400 / 450, coins one point at 550, cheapPrice
  535 at 200 then 62 at 250 and 11 at 300). They are now smooth, one point per 50 levels from 150 on: loot {150: 0.116 ->
  0.087, 200: 0.159 -> 0.110, 250: 0.19 -> 0.148, 300: 0.19 -> 0.151, 350: 0.068 -> 0.060, 400: 0.032 -> 0.052, 450: 0.078 ->
  0.068, 500: 0.089 -> 0.083, 550: 0.036 -> 0.084, 600: 0.091 -> 0.099, 650: 0.248 -> 0.100}; cheapPrice {200: 535 -> 22,
  250: 62 -> 20, 300: 11 -> 20, 400: 241 -> 31, 500: 603 -> 61, 600: 150 -> 97, 650: 228 -> 115}; coins {150: 0.145 -> 0.476,
  200: 0.128 -> 0.334, 250: 0.074 -> 0.269, 300: 0.220 -> 0.270, 350: 0.18, 400: 0.117, 500: 0.114 -> 0.120, 650: 0.106 ->
  0.114} (a smaller loot x a larger coins share: the same value of coins and junk); junkKeep 0.83-1.27, rising from 200 on.
  The band models still hold (`tools/loot_model.lua --check`, no tolerance changed): gold an hour at 100 / 300 / 500 / 650
  138.0k / 469.0k / 859.8k / 1.340M -> 137.8k / 456.5k / 836.6k / 1.293M (and 350 / 400 / 450 / 550 / 600 966k / 1.216M / 1.014M /
  943k / 1.317M -> 937k / 1.257M / 1.045M / 920k / 1.367M, the targets are 965k / 1.215M / 1.015M / 945k / 1.315M); items an
  hour 541 / 688 / 377 / 546 -> 555 / 700 / 354 / 508; Rare+ gear an hour 3.8 / 9.6 / 25.7 / 5.5 as before. Outside the
  checked bands (unpinned) the gold an hour at 125-275 moves by at most 10%, the items an hour at 175 / 200 / 225 fall from
  610 / 409 / 453 to 388 / 190 / 225: the 535 `cheapPrice` spike at 200 was what held them up (the 2026-10-20 rule had 420 /
  294 / 304 there), and the stock loot of the pool levels 200-230 has little cheap junk. The cliff of `loot` from 300 to 350
  stays (0.151 -> 0.060): from 350 the Rare+ gear and rare drops stay whole and are worth 0.4-0.7M gold an hour on their own,
  so the thinned share must fall there to keep the gold targets.
- **Which monsters**: natural map spawns (`onSpawn` with `artificial = false`), generated areas and dungeons (their
  boss never), base dungeon monsters (`dungeons.lua` marks them) and ambush copies of a paced monster
  (`monster_tiers.lua`). Never: bosses (isboss, rewardboss, the tier list), summons, and every script-made monster of the
  instanced modes (rifts, the Ember Descent, the tower, invasions, arena, battleground, raid, world and guild bosses,
  Ascended Omens): they are created with `Game.createMonster` and not marked. PvP is not touched.
- **Health**: at the monster's first think (`ChaosPaceInit`; script-made monsters get `ChaosPaceProbe`, which paces
  only a generated area's point), max health x the curve, full health. The tier (also at the first think) multiplies in
  either order.
- **Experience**: `onGainExperience` at index -10 (after the xpcap recorder, before every bonus): x the curve with
  random rounding (a kill worth 1+ gives at least 1). `xpcap.lua` multiplies its base by the same curve, so the 4.0 cap
  is 4 x the paced base.
- **Multikill** (`pace_config.lua` `multikill`): kills of one player, each within 3 s of the one before, form a chain;
  the whole chain's experience gets +10% at 4 kills, +20% at 6, +30% at 8, +40% at 9 (the kill that reaches a step also
  pays the step on the chain's earlier kills, divided by its own tier multiplier). From 6 kills a status line
  "Multikill x6: +20% experience on the chain." (pt-BR in `i18n_strings.lua`). It counts against the cap. The experience
  curve is already divided by 1.30, the median pack's bonus.
- **Loot** (`loot.lua`): the stock corpse is thinned by the monster's level only ("Loot by monster level" below:
  `L.thinCorpseByLevel`, `pace_core.lua` `P.levelPlan`; with `lootLevel.enabled = false` the 2026-10-20 method with the `coins` share: a stack
  keeps count x factor rounded at random, gold included, any other item stays with that chance, `L.thinCorpse`), and the Chaos extra rolls, currency, gems,
  supports and uniques roll x the factor, outside the `maxRate` / `maxScale` caps. The thinning runs after the stock
  "Loot of ..." list was written; the kill's loot line lists the corpse as it is after it (index 1.9, "One loot line per
  kill", beta 2026-10-21: the line used to name the whole stock list). An empty paced corpse decays after
  30 s (`emptyCorpseSeconds`). The check runs at the end of the drop (`loot_config.lua` `emptyCorpseIndex` 99), after
  the Loot Bag, the base autoloot and the Rarity Autoloot, so a corpse the autoloot emptied decays fast too. A corpse
  with anything left in it decays after 120 s (`corpseSeconds`, owner 2026-10-18; every monster, never longer than the stock
  decay; 0 = stock). The ambush chance (`monster_tiers.lua`), the treasure goblin roll of a respawn
  (`treasure_goblin.lua`) and the faction token chance (`factions.lua`) are x the loot factor too.
- **Damage to players** (`monster_damage.lua`): a paced monster's hits, and its summons', x the `damage` curve: every
  element, conditions, mana shield hits and mana drain (healing never). The late-game physical boost stays on top.
- **Kill goals**: bounty hunt and elite counts (`bounty.lua` `cfg.goalMult`), bestiary stages after Discovered and kill
  tasks (`bestiary.lua` `cfg.goalOf`, family tasks `cfg.familyGoalOf`) x the monster's goal factor; the generic counters
  (achievements: tiered, party and witching kills; the season pass "kill"; community contributions; faction contracts
  and kill reputation) count a paced kill as 1 / goal, summed per player (`ChaosPace.killCredit`). Ambush and goblin
  counters stay (their chances were cut already).
- **Pack cleave** (`pace_config.lua` `cleave`, PvE only): the classes with little area damage hit packs too. A direct
  hit (melee, ranged, spell; not damage over time) of such a character on a paced monster also deals a share of it to
  the nearest monsters within 1 sqm of that monster (never a boss, a player or a player's summon; no cleave from a
  cleave): Thief, Samurai, Necromancer 25% to 3; Monk, Iron Sage 20% to 3; Deadeye, Shadowfist 20% to 2; Ninja 15% to 2.
  It is class-wide (every spell and the auto attack), so `rotation_model.csv` and the helper's auto rotation are
  unchanged (`rotation_sim.py --write` / `--check`: up to date). Second pass (2026-10-15, owner decision: the top
  pack class untouched, every other class raised to about 0.92 of it or more; data/spells/README.md "Pack farming for
  every class"): the Thief line got two area spells (Blade Flurry, Iaido Sweep), the classes that needed a large cleave
  pack spells of their own (Fan of Knives, Palm Shockwave, Shadow Ricochet, Iron Chain, Bone Shrapnel, Sanctified
  Ground, Shield Wave: `data/spells/chaos/_packtools.lua`); every class but the Elementalist cleaves to 4 monsters (at
  most 26%, the Juggernaut); the share grows from level 300 (`percent`) to 1000 (`high`, `pace_core.lua`
  `P.cleavePercent`); a summon's hit cleaves by its master's class and level.

Experience, gold and goal pace per hour are the O108 ones (`progression_model.lua --check`, `loot_model.lua --check`).
Generated area points and bosses are unchanged. Deploy: `files` and `spawns` install steps and a server restart; the client codex page (`codex_data.lua`) and the website wiki data were regenerated.

These come on top of the engine's x(1 + 0.0074 L) health and x0.03 L experience of a monster with a level of its own.
Loot: `pace_config.lua` (and "Loot by monster level").

**Scaled experience re-fit (2026-10-22, O108; owner: "pode fazer").** The `scaled` xp points of 2026-10-20 (0.70 at 650,
0.58 at 800, 0.52 at 1000, 0.46 at 2000) were fitted on the file experience. The base `player.lua` also gives a
level-scaled kill x0.03 L (a level 900 knight on the test server: XML exp x 0.03 x level x stage x stamina x buff), so a
kill paid 81k at hunting level 670, 157k at 800 and 296k at 1000 before the stage, 17-40x a base monster there
(4.8k-7.6k), and the 800+ bounty band always hit its 20-level cap. Two ways to make the curve and the factor agree: a
`patch_*.py` that takes the factor out of the base `player.lua` for paced monsters, or new curve points with the factor
counted. The points were chosen: one config line (and the `generated` one), no base file and no install step change,
and the factor stays for everything that already counts on it: the late sets' XML experience was tuned with it ("Late
game"), and rifts (`rift.lua` cap), invasions, the Ember Descent, the tower, world, guild and pocket bosses, `xpcap.lua`
and the bounty and kill task rewards (`B.monsterKillBase`) read the same factor and are not paced, or follow the curve.

The model: the leveling model of "The leveling model and the hours" as the pack model carried it on 2026-10-14/15 (the
median class about 130 h from 1 to 1000; the old `scaled` points held a late set's experience per hour on it). Experience
per hour at a level = the pace model's kills per hour (`spawn_tuning.json` `paceKillsPerHour`; for the late sets x the
median class's kills per hour with the health curve of 2026-10-20 / with the old one, `tools/pack_model.py`, since the
monsters became bulkier) x the median kill (base: the bounty pool's monsters of that hunting level; late sets: their
level-scaled health and experience, with the engine factors) x `scale.xp` 1.3 x the stage; the hunt is the better of
the base hunt and the late set from 650 (tiers and the multikill bonus of the model; boosts and Chaos bonuses left
out). Each new point is the old one x the old / new kills per hour: about 0.086 at every level.

out until now). With both engine factors a level-scaled monster's experience per health point is cut like a base

  what such a kill can pay fell with the curve (155k x stage before, 23k x stage now, the pool median at 800+). The experience cap

**More monsters, faster respawn** (the spawn side):
- Base map fill (`tools/gen_spawn_density.py`, `tools/spawn_density.json`, regenerated on a scratch install of the base
  server): from hunting level 30 (the audit's level 15) every hunt under 4.3 per 100 region tiles is raised to 4.5, at
  most x2.5 its entries and +600 monsters, in spawn blocks of 3 (radius 2) whose centres are 5+ sqm apart (falling back
  to 3 when the region is full). Hunts under level 30 keep the earlier fill (3.25 -> 3.4, one-monster spawns). The
  planned areas (`chaoscontent` / `chaoshunt` blocks of install step contentareas) and the entries the spawns step took
  out are left out of the count. 765 hunts filled with 21,469 monsters in 8,982 blocks (the earlier fill: 570 hunts,
  10,922 one-monster spawns). The spawns step (`patch_base_spawns.py`) writes a row `[x, y, like, dx, dy, ...]` as one
  spawn block with a monster at the centre and at each offset.
- Respawn (`tools/spawn_tuning.json` `bandRespawn`): hunting level 300-599 45 s (was 90), 600+ 75 s (was 120; the
  late-game rows of `late_game.py` included, marked `chaosst` like any other). Below 300 unchanged (60 s).
- Dynamic respawn (`respawn_config.lua`): a hunter alone 80% (`soloPercent`, new), 2 hunters 70%, 3 60%, 4 50%, 5 or
  more 45% (was 100 / 85 / 70 / 55 / 50). With `soloPercent` a single hunter makes a zone too.
- Generated areas (`areagen_config.lua`: Emberdeep, Ossuary, Cinderfall): density 4.5 (band 4.0-5.0), 60% of the
  points packs of up to 4, points 6+ sqm apart, 75 s respawn: 1,023 monsters (was 740).
- Planned areas (`tools/areaplan/plans/*.json`): counts raised to 4.1-4.6 per 100 walkable tiles (was 3.2-3.5), packs
  of 3, respawn 45 s (300-599) / 75 s (600+); no zone above the validator's 8 per 100 (0 errors, 0 warnings). A server
  that installed the earlier plans restores its map from `<map>.otbm.bak` before install step contentareas (the step

### Loot by monster level (2026-10-21)

Owner (pt-BR): "Ajuste o loot de acordo com o lvl só monstro" (adjust the loot by the monster's level only). Beta: almost
nothing dropped from Nightfang Widow and Shadowcrystal Widow (monster level 1018 / 960 on the hunting scale): the
2026-10-20 rule kept about 24% of the items (each one at random) and about 7% of the coins and NPC-sellable items, so
about half their corpses came out empty.

**What decides.** Only the monster: its level (`P.levelOf`: its own level for a level-scaled monster, a generated
point's, else the pool estimate (2 x until O285), read at its first think) and its kind (the `base` / `scaled` / `generated` curve
set), times a pocket's factor (`pocketboss.lua`, a property of the monster). The killer's level, party, stamina and
place are not read (`P.levelPlan(ll, f, items, rnd)` has no player argument; `tests/lootline_corpse_test.lua` gives a
level 100 hunter alone and a level 1500 hunter in a party the same corpse with the same rolls). The stock pass before
it (its own chances, low stamina) and the Chaos extra rolls after it are unchanged.

**The rule** (`pace_core.lua` `P.levelPlan`, `loot.lua` `L.thinCorpseByLevel`; numbers in `pace_config.lua`):
- *Notable drops* stay whole with the `notable` share: gear the stock roll made Rare or better (stored rarity >=
  `lootLevel.notableRarity` 4, so Legendary and Divine too; 7.72% of stock gear drops) and any item whose loot-table
  chance is at most `lootLevel.notableChance` (1000 per 100000: 1% or rarer). `notable` is the loot factor up to monster
  level 650 and 1 from 700 (smooth in between) in the scaled set; in the base set (O285) it is its own curve: the rule
  from before the pool scale (the old loot share, 0.44 at pool level 50, 0.32 at 88, 0.24 at 125-225, 0.23 at 300-325)
  and 1 from level 350 (hunting 700 before).
- *Coins*: their value x `loot` x `coins` comes back as coins (`P.coinStacks`, crystal / platinum / gold, through
  `L.addToCorpse`), rounded at random to whole gold. A corpse that had coins shows coins (before: 4 crystal coins x
  0.07 rounded to nothing 71% of the time).
- *Junk* (NPC-sellable, not gear: `L.isGoldLike`) is worth `loot` x `coins` of its NPC price. It stays in kind with
  chance `loot` x `junkKeep` (a stack keeps count x the rest of the share, rounded at random; a single item at most the
  value share); taken out, the rest of its value share is paid as coins.
- *Floor*: a corpse that would show nothing although junk dropped gets that junk's value x the share as coins (at least
  1 gold). The `coins` curve pays for it.
- *Plain gear and other items* (orbs, gems, keys, unsellables): the loot factor as before, so their per hour is
  unchanged.

**The curves** (smooth: `P.smooth`, monotone cubic through the points, flat beyond the ends). Base set; the scaled set
has the same points from 450 on and the old ramp x 0.963 below; the generated set keeps the 2026-10-20 shares (its
queue model is calibrated on them) with the coin pay and the floor:

**O285 (2026-10-28): the base curves re-fitted to the pool level, items per hour restored.** The pool's base monsters now
stand at their own level (the highest is 657) and a level 500 monster carries about 8.5x the NPC gold of the level 250
monster that stood there before (and 1.8x the items: 0.6 a kill against 0.33). Holding the gold per hour
(`lootLevel.goldPerHour`) with the old knobs would have cut the items per hour by half (100-300) to four fifths (450+). The
owner (2026-10-28) asked for the items per hour back at the same gold, so the two are decoupled with one new knob:
`cheapPrice` (a curve of the base set, `pace_core.lua` `P.factors` `cheap`, `P.levelPlan`): junk worth at most that many
gold a unit (its NPC price) stays in the corpse whole, whatever `loot` and `coins` say. The items per hour come from the
cheap junk (potions, pearls, trinkets, 20-600 gold), the orbs and the notable drops; the gold from the dearer junk and the
coins, which `coins` pays thin. `notable` is the rule from before the pool scale on the pool scale (first O285 fit: it was
set to the new `loot` curve, 0.2 from 250 to 650, which cut every monster of pool level 350-657 from every drop to a fifth
of its Rare+ gear: the owner's "rare rates as before" was broken, 24.8 Rare+ pieces an hour at the old band 1000 became
about 1-5). Now `notable` follows the old rule point by point (`loot_model.lua` `M.OLD_RULE`: the old base `loot` curve
x `scale.loot` 1.2 at 2 x the pool level, and 1 from hunting level 700 = pool level 350, a ramp from 325 to 350), so the
Rare+ gear per hour of a band is the old rule's on the same monsters: `lootLevel.rarePerHour` 3.9 / 9.65 / 25.7 / 5.5 at
100 / 300 / 500 / 650, held within 5% by `--check` (every band of the check, also 350 / 400 / 450 / 550 / 600, is held to
the old rule's figure) and pinned in `tests/loot_by_level_test.lua` (24.8 and 5.5 are what the old model gave for the old
bands 1000 and 1300; a thinned `notable` curve fails the test). `loot` (plain gear, orbs, gems) stays under 0.19 up to
level 325 so that it is under `notable` there (a `loot` above the notable share would raise the Rare+ gear; O298 smoothed the curve), `coins`,
`junkKeep` and `cheapPrice` were fitted again band by band (`tools/loot_model.lua`, coins for the gold per hour, `cheapPrice`
and `junkKeep` for the items per hour; `--derive` solves the constant per band). `lootLevel.itemsPerHour` holds the bands to
539 / 692 / 380 / 540 an hour at 100 / 300 / 500 / 650 (the figures from before, `--check` and
`tests/loot_by_level_test.lua`); between them the bands are 350 -> 503, 400 -> 436, 450 -> 400, 550 -> 368, 600 -> 490.
The gold per hour at 100 / 300 / 500 / 650 is unchanged (138k / 469k / 860k / 1.34M; 650 was 1.5M in the first O285
fit): bands 600 and 650 are the same 9-16 monsters of the pool's top, so their gold cannot differ by more than 1.28x.
The bands in between could not keep the 600k / 625k / 785k / 1.005M / 1.055M they had at 350 / 400 / 450 / 550 / 600:
with the Rare+ gear back the stock gear of the pool levels 350-410 (Apparitions, Courage Leech, Branchy Crawler ...) is
worth 0.5-1M gold an hour on its own, so even with no coins at all the band 400 pays 1.03M. They are 965k / 1.215M / 1.015M
/ 945k / 1.315M now (`goldPerHour`). The no-dip rule of O141 reads the gold without the notable drops (the "trade gold"
of the model: 363k at 300, 523k at 350, 531k at 400, 583k at 450, 711k at 500, 851k at 550, 1.05M at 600, 1.26M at 650,
growing); the whole gold per hour may fall from 400 to 500 (1.22M to 860k) because of the luck-driven Rare+ gear, and
never rises by more than 2.3x from one band to the next 150 levels up. The scaled set keeps its own points. The weapon
drops of the weapon fairness work start at hunting level 658 (`loot.lua` step 1e), above every base monster, so they are
not in these bands.

**The economy model** (`tools/loot_model.lua`; `luajit tools/loot_model.lua` prints it, `--check` is in CI, `--fit`
proposes the points). Input: `tools/loot_bands_data.lua`, the stock loot tables of the bounty pool monsters of each band
(+-15% of the band level on the hunting scale, which is the pool level since O285; no base monster is above 657, so the
bands stop at 650 and the data holds every base monster from level 40), written by `python3 -I server/tools/loot_bands.py BASE_DATA` from an installed base server (`--check` compares;
coin / gear / junk / other by `items.xml` and the item price table). Per entry the chance, the stock count (uniform
1..max, x the stock level multiplier of a level-scaled monster) and both rules' shares, as expected values; the Rare+
share from `ChaosRarity.stockRolls`; kills per hour from `spawn_tuning.json` `model.paceKillsPerHour` by the monster's
level; weights the pool's spawn counts. Gold is coins plus plain NPC prices (the "Respec" measure: rarity, item level,
the Chaos extra rolls, gold finds and item find are left out, the same under both rules), so the absolute gold per hour
is the stock corpse's only and lower than the "Respec" column; the economy target is the ratio: the 2026-10-20 rule is
what the beta calibrated (16M -> the 5.5-6.3M model at 450-600), and the new curves keep it. Tolerances of `--check`:
gold per hour 5%, items (non-coin corpse entries) per hour 7%, Rare+ gear per hour 5% (O285), at the four bands (100, 300,
500, 650) and every fit point (100 ... 650 in steps of 50, 350 / 400 / 600 on top). The Rare+ gear per hour is the stock
gear chances x the Rare+ share x the `notable` share of the monster's level; the check holds every band to
`lootLevel.rarePerHour` or, for the bands between, to the rule from before the pool scale on the same monsters.

some pay one: at about 3,100 gold a kill that is one crystal coin in about three kills. Other monsters keep

Not measured: no live server ran it; the band tables come from one installed base copy (`loot_bands.py` on another base
copy may differ: rerun it, then `--fit` / `--check`); the stock count of a monster with a player loot bonus (storage
76855) and the waystone loot upgrade are left out of the model; Rare+ gear now drops about 4x as often from level 700
monsters (it was thinned to 24%), which the gold model counts at its plain price only (its rarity value, salvage and
the crafting market are not modelled: watch them in the beta).

100-monster floor), `areagen_test` (densities, packs, the run model with pace, 100+ monsters per dungeon),
`gen_spawn_density_test.py` (blocks, spacing, the low-level rule), `instance_limits_systems_test` (15 minutes).

## Spawn density and respawn (`tools/patch_base_spawns.py`, `tools/spawn_tuning.json`, `respawn.lua`, `respawn_core.lua`, `respawn_config.lua`, engine patch 0022)

Measured on 2026-10-11 on the loaded map and its spawn file after `late_game.py`, with a one-off script that read the
`.otbm` tile by tile (not in the repo). Areas are named by id and position only.

### The map

- Map header 34800 x 34200. The world lies in x 30700-34600, y 30900-33850, floors 0-15. A few small test and event
  areas lie outside it.
- 5.36 million walkable tiles: floor 7 has 2.86 million, floors 8-15 0.13-0.41 million each, floors 0-6 8,000-200,000.
  120,000 of them are protection zone and 48,000 are house tiles. 20 towns (ids 1-14, 28, 29, 31-34).

### The spawns

- 50,338 spawn blocks (908 empty), 74,071 monster entries and 960 NPCs. 85% of the entries respawn after 60 s and 15%
  after 120 s (mostly the level 300+ areas). Some have long timers on purpose (rare spawns, 200-3,600 s).
- **913 entries never spawned.** `monsters.xml` names 10 monsters twice. The engine keeps the first line of a name, and
  that line's file name has the wrong case (the base server was made on Windows). On Linux the file is not found, the
  monster never loads and the console prints 913 "Can not find" warnings. Most of them are level 300-600 monsters.
- **111 entries had 30,976-32,768 s** (about 9 hours) from the map editor, so in practice they came once a day. Their
  monsters respawn after 60 s everywhere else.
- **99 entries sat on a tile that blocks** (a wall, or no ground).
- No entry is in a protection zone or a house, and every other monster name is defined.
- 1,688 entries sit in small closed pockets: under 400 walkable tiles with no stairs, ladder, hole or teleport tile.
  Most are quest rooms reached by a scripted teleport or a lever, so they were left alone (see "Not done").
- The engine never respawns a monster while a player sees its spot (the timer then starts again), and `rateSpawn`
  (1 in the base server) is how many monsters one spawn block brings back per check. A pack of five took five
  spawntimes to refill. Engine patch 0041 lifts the view rule (see "Respawn near players"); the tables below were
  measured before it.

### Level bands and capacity

Spawn blocks on one floor within 12 sqm of each other and of a similar level form an area. Areas with 12+ monsters are
hunting areas (1,195, with 42,300 monsters that load); the other 28,100 are scattered single spawns. A monster's hunting
level is the bounty pool's "fair hunt" estimate (`gen_bounty_pool.estimate_level`), or the middle of its range for
a level-scaled monster (twice the estimate from 2026-10-14 to 2026-10-28, O285: the owner retired the x2 rule; the base
monsters now end at level 657). That puts the leveling model's hunts at about 40, 125 and 325 for the hunts that were
at 85, 250 and 650 before, and the late levels are the level-scaled sets'. Density is monsters per 100
walkable tiles within 6 sqm of a spawn, as in docs/MAP_GUIDE.md (2.7-4.4 is normal).

Capacity is a simple model: a spot holds N hunters while N x one hunter's kills per hour stays at or below the kills
per hour its respawn can feed.
- One hunter: 3600 x 0.47 x the 5-target rotation DPS at the area's level (`data/spells/README.md`, as in "Respec") /
  (the monster's health x 1.11 for the tier spawns), at most 900 kills per hour. Level-scaled late-game monsters are
  pulled 3 at a time (x0.75).
- The respawn of a spawn block: the sum of 1 / spawntime of its monsters, at most rateSpawn / its shortest spawntime,
  divided by 1.25 for the player-in-view rule (gone with patch 0041 and spawnNearPlayers: no division).
- A party of four kills about as fast as three solo hunters, so N hunters is about N / 3 parties.
- Rule of thumb: under 60% of the capacity a hunter finds a free spot; above 80% players fight over spots.

Before: as the engine ran it (dead monsters, rateSpawn 1). After: install step `spawns` and rateSpawn 3, without the
dynamic respawn. Only the hunting areas are counted.

**Expected population.** No owner estimate was written down, so this assumes 400 online at the evening peak of
