The one real shortage was the 300-600 band in the first week: half the players pass through it then, it had the
fewest areas, and almost a fifth of its monsters never spawned. The 1000+ band has 6 areas: those players also hunt the
hunting level 900+ areas of the band below (253 hunters) and are pointed at the instanced endgame (rifts of tier 10-15,
Omens, Ascended Omens, the Ember Descent, the weekly raid). At 150 online every band stays under 40%.

### What the spawns step changes (`tools/patch_base_spawns.py`, `tools/spawn_tuning.json`)

`python3 -I server/tools/patch_base_spawns.py <server>/data [--config PATH] [--spawn PATH] [--tuning PATH] [--dry-run]
[--remove] [--report]`, install step `spawns` (after `monsters`). Every change carries a marker; a run first undoes the
last run and then applies the JSON, so a second run changes nothing and `--remove` gives the stock files back.
`--report` prints the band table of the spawn file as it would be written (monster entries of all spawns, not only
hunting areas). Monster names are never written in the JSON: entries are named by position, and a new spawn copies
the monster of an existing entry.

| Change | Count | How |
|---|---|---|
| Dead registrations | 10 lines (913 entries) | the dead first line of a monster in `monsters.xml` is commented out when another line of the name has a file |
| Glitched spawntimes | 111 | an entry with 30,000 s or more gets the median spawntime of the same monster elsewhere (10+ other entries) |
| Band respawn | 2,539 (9,051 since pack combat) | entries of a monster with a hunting level of 300-599 and a spawntime of 91-300 s respawn after 90 s (was 120); since pack combat 300-599 after 45 s and 600+ after 75 s; not the display monsters of the content areas (`chaoshunt`, their own spawntime) |
| Blocking tiles | 99 moved | to the nearest free walkable tile within 3 sqm (no protection zone, house, floor change or teleport) |
| Thin 300-600 areas | 93 added in 12 areas (`H4-01`..`H4-12`) | raised to 3.0 monsters per 100 walkable tiles, at most +50% |
| Thin level 900+ areas | 91 added in 9 areas (`H5-01`..`H5-09`) | outdoors at 0.8-1.1 per 100; raised to 1.5, at most +60% |
| Fill (2026-10-14) | 10,922 added in 570 hunts (`F0001`..`F0570`, `tools/spawn_density.json`) | every hunt under 3.25 per 100 raised to 3.4, at most x2 its entries and +400 (see "Fill") |
| Emptied spawns (2026-10-16) | 339 | a stock `<spawn>` whose every entry was taken out (`remove`, `dungeons`) becomes one comment `<!-- chaosemptied: <spawn ...>...</spawn> -->`; before, the engine printed "Empty spawn at position ... radius 1" for each at every start |

New spawns hold one monster each and sit on free walkable tiles of their area, at least 3 sqm from any spawn and
connected to it. Each copies the nearest ordinary entry: no boss, no rare spawn, a monster with 10+ entries on the map.
`late_game.py` and this tool leave each other's entries alone, in either order.

`prod_config.py` sets `rateSpawn = 3`: most packs come back in one or two spawntimes instead of one monster per
spawntime. That is the biggest change below level 300 (+20-55% respawn there).

### Spawns on fire fields (`tools/patch_spawn_fields.py`, 2026-10-21)

The start log printed "Couldn't spawn monster" for eight base spawn entries, each line twice: three monster types of
the fire lairs (floors 4, 5 and 12) that the base server made immune to fire. Not the base server: with its fire
immunity none of them fails. Since C7 ("Monsters are not immune to fire") they are not immune, and at start the
engine places a monster unforced (`Map::placeCreature`, `extendedPos`): `Tile::queryAdd` refuses a tile with a magic
field that does damage of an element the monster is not immune to, then tries the 12 tiles around. For these eight the
spot and all 12 tiles hold a burning fire field (items 1487, 1488) or block (wall, lava, hole). The line comes twice
because `Spawn::spawnMonster(spawnBlock_t)` tries a one-monster block again after the first try fails; there is one
entry per position, no duplicate in the spawn file. The respawn places monsters forced, so they came 60 s later anyway.

Install step `spawnfields` (after `spawns`): on the map, a burning fire field on one of nine spots becomes the small
fire 1489 (field fire, no damage: every monster may stand on it). The ninth spot, (32078, 32605, 5), is a neighbour
whose own tile burns: once the eight were free, its start search took (32078, 32603) first and pushed another entry
out. Only the item id changes; the rest of each lair keeps its fire. The ids are checked in `items.xml` first.
`<map>.otbm.bak` is written first when missing; a second run finds nothing. `--dry-run` lists, `--out FILE` writes a
copy. Measured on the base map with the engine's placement rules (damaging fields only): with fire immunity no entry
fails, without it exactly the eight of the log, after the step none (a simulation of the start order, 3000 runs).
Test: `tools/patch_spawn_fields_test.py` (synthetic map).

### Fill: every hunt full (`tools/gen_spawn_density.py`, `tools/spawn_density.json`, 2026-10-14)

Owner request (2026-10-14): every hunt big and full of monsters. The map's geometry is not changed; the thin hunts get
more spawns. `spawn_tuning.json` names the file (`"fill": "spawn_density.json"`) and the spawns step adds its rows like
the `add` rows (marker `chaosadd="F...."`; `--remove` takes them out with the rest).

`python3 -I server/tools/gen_spawn_density.py SCRATCH/data [ITEMS_OTB] [--map PATH] [--check] [--stats PATH]` writes the
file from a scratch install (docs/CONTENT.md: steps files, lib, monsternames, lategame, monsters, spawns), the map
(tools/map/otbm.py, numpy; about 2 minutes and 3.5 GB of memory) and items.otb / items.xml. It ignores its own earlier
spawns, so a second run gives the same file byte for byte (`--check`). Rules:
- Hunts as in `tools/content_audit.py`: entries of monsters that give experience on one floor, at most 12 tiles apart,
  10 or more.
- Region of a hunt: walkable tiles within 6 sqm of an entry and connected to one, without protection zone, house, floor
  change, teleport or door tiles and without town tiles (8 sqm around a house tile, 5 around a protection zone tile).
- Skipped: closed pockets (the walkable set around the hunt ends under 400 tiles with no floor change or teleport: quest
  rooms behind a lever or a scripted teleport; 79 hunts), regions under 60 tiles (4), no monster to copy (1).
- Density = entries per 100 region tiles. Under 3.25 it is raised to 3.4, at most x2 the hunt's entries and 400 spawns.
- A new spawn holds one monster on a free walkable tile (no NPC within 3 sqm, no floor change next to it), 3+ sqm from
  every entry of the floor and every new spawn: always the tile farthest from all of them. It copies the nearest ordinary
  entry of the hunt (no boss, a monster with 10+ entries on the map, spawntime up to 300 s, not moved or added by this
  tool), with that entry's final spawntime (so the 90 s of the 300-600 band and every respawn timer stay as they were).

**Experience per hour.** In the model one hunter's kills per hour come from its damage, not from the monsters around,
so a denser hunt holds more hunters at the same rate and does not raise a solo hunter's rate, except where the
respawn was the limit. In the filled hunts the respawn feeds x1.45 (level 1-50), x1.40 (50-150), x1.21 (150-300) and
x1.87 (300-600) the kills; a solo hunter was respawn-bound in 175 of 353 filled hunts of level 1-50 and 36 of 140 of
50-150, which gives +16% and +5% experience per hour there and nothing above level 150. Less walking between packs
adds an estimated +5-10% in the hunts that were under 2.0 per 100 (146 hunts). So: about +5-25% for a solo hunter in
thin low-level hunts, about +5-10% in thin hunts above level 150, 0 in the hunts that were full; crowded hunts lose
less to sharing. Measure it with the hunt tracker in the betas.

### Dynamic respawn (`respawn.lua`, `respawn_core.lua`, `respawn_config.lua`, `src-patches/0022-dynamic-respawn.patch`)

The stock engine reads a spawn's interval once and has no way to change it, so engine patch 0022 adds
`Game.setSpawnIntervalPercent(percent[, fromPosition, toPosition])`: every spawn, or every spawn whose centre lies in
the box, respawns after that percent of its spawntime (10-1000, never under the engine's 10 s). The percent is kept
per spawn; when it drops, a pending check runs after 1 s. The view rule and rateSpawn stay as they are.

Every 20 s `respawn.lua` counts the hunters: online, not staff, not in a protection zone, in fight. Characters behind
one IP count once. Where 2 or more hunt within 10 sqm on one floor, the spawns in that 16 x 16 sqm cell (plus 8 sqm
around it) respawn faster: 2 hunters 85%, 3 70%, 4 55%, 5 or more 50%. Since pack combat (`soloPercent`, "Pack combat (pace)") one
hunter alone 80%, 2 70%, 3 60%, 4 50%, 5 or more 45%. When they leave, the cell goes back to 100%.
The tick makes no engine call while nothing changes. Without patch 0022 it logs one line and does nothing. Every
number is in `respawn_config.lua`; `globalPercent` (100) changes the whole map, for an event. With engine patch 0027
the tick hands its zones to `Game.setSpawnIntervalZones` in one call, which touches only the spawns of the old and new
zones through an index; before, each zone was one pass over all ~50,000 map spawns (6-10 ms each, see "Game loop
stalls").

- `tools/gen_spawn_density_test.py`: the fill's rules on synthetic grids and a synthetic map (pockets, region, town and
  NPC margins, spacing, the farthest tile first, the caps, the same file twice). The real map: the second run gave the
  same file; the spawns step wrote 10,922 spawns, a second run changed nothing, `--remove` and a new run gave the same
  bytes.
- `tests/base_spawns_patch_test.lua`: the tool on a fixture with placeholder monsters (every rule, the fill, markers, a second run,
  `--remove` byte for byte, CRLF files, bad positions). `tests/respawn_test.lua`: the percent, the counts, the zones,
  the plan and the glue against a mocked engine.
- The real base data: the first run wrote the changes above, the second changed nothing, `--remove` restored both files
  byte for byte, and `late_game.py` still found its 277 entries.
- The engine with patches 0001-0022 built and ran on the full map (test database, no players): the 913 "Can not find"

## Generated areas (`areagen.lua`, `areagen_core.lua`, `areagen_config.lua`, `tools/areagen_export.py`)

A seeded generator builds hunting areas and dungeons that need no map edit (roadmap item 109; owner approval: a
"generated" look for caves, wastes and rifts; towns and story areas stay hand-made). Item 89 left level 1000-1300 with
6 hunting areas; three generated areas for that band are ready to go live.

**Design.** One pure Lua core makes a tile model (every tile with its ground and items, the spawns, links, arrival,
exit). Two users read the same model:
- `areagen.lua` builds it at startup with `Game.createTile` / `Game.createItem`, like the rifts and the tutorial
  island. It works on an installed server and needs no install step.
- The rifts (2026-10-12): `rift_layout_core.lua` makes a map per run with the same core and the rift themes below, and
  `rift.lua` builds it in short steps ("Rifts", Layouts and the slot pool).
- `tools/areagen_export.py` runs the same core through LuaJIT (`tools/areagen_dump.lua`). It writes an OTBM piece and
  a spawn file for the map editor and renders previews.
Why runtime first: no map edit, no merge with the 197 MB world file, and a config change ships with a restart. The OTBM
writer stays so the owner can open, review or hand-place an area in the map editor.

**Layouts** (`areagen_core.lua`):
- `cave`: cellular automata. Pockets under `minRegion` tiles are filled. The rest are joined by winding tunnels.
- `dungeon`: rooms joined by a spanning tree of L-shaped corridors, plus loop corridors between rooms that are 3+ steps
  apart in the tree.
- `waste`: the cave method with a low fill: an open field with rock islands. Enclosed rock islands are filled whole,
  so there are no void holes inside an area.
- Several floors are joined by a hole (8972) and a ladder (1386) at the same x, y. The stock ladder action climbs to
  the tile south of the hole, and that tile is kept walkable.
- Required points (arrival, holes, ladders, boss) are carved first and joined. Only the arrival's region is kept.
- The walkable set is checked as one connected set over all floors, from the arrival through holes and ladders.
- Options for big layouts (the rifts; an area without them comes out byte for byte as before, the fixed checksums of
  the four areas are unchanged):
  - `layout.scale` / `smooth`: the automaton runs on a grid `scale` times coarser, is scaled up and smoothed `smooth`
    times, so a 200 x 200 cave gets wide caverns and tunnels instead of a fine maze (rifts: cave and mixed 2, waste 3).
  - kind `mixed`: a cave with `rooms` rectangular chambers (corners cut) carved in and joined like any pocket; with the
    theme's `mixedFloors` they get a floor of their own.
  - `byKind = {kind = {...}}` in a theme (and in its `dark` part): overrides for one layout kind, so one theme serves
    every kind its rift rolls.
  - `bossAt` (the boss point, default the south-east corner), `layout.bossAnchor` (the boss room of a dungeon there),
    `boss.clear` (no decoration, patch or obstacle within that many cells: an open arena), `linkAvoid` (no hole near
    these points), `noExit` (no exit portal), `fastPaths` (the paths kept free from one search instead of one per
    target: a dungeon of 40 rooms in 0.1 s instead of 0.7 s).
  - `opts.tick` (A.generate, A.validate): called in the long loops (rows, every 1,024 steps of a search, never inside
    a sort) and never drawing a random number, so a caller can run the generator in a coroutine and yield there.

**Borders and walls.**
- Every ground family has a z order. The higher family draws its 12 border pieces on the lower tile. The piece comes
  from the 8-neighbour pattern, as the map editor's auto-border does: n/e/s/w, outer corners c*, inner corners d*
  (`A.borderPieces`). All 256 patterns are tested.
- The piece sets and the wall piece table were measured on the live map with `tools/map/derive_borders.py`. The
  winning piece of each pattern has an 85-100% share for most sets.
- Rock (earth 101, mountain 919) borders the floor with blocking edge pieces (dirt walls 5631-5654, gravel
  4468-4479). That is how the live map draws cave walls.
- Dungeon walls take their piece from the 4-neighbour pattern, as on the live map: an east-west run is horizontal, the
  north-west room corner is the pole, the south-east corner the corner piece.

**Dressing.**
- Grounds are picked by weight inside a family, so a 16x16 block mixes 5 ids.
- Patches of a second ground are rounded blobs that never touch another patch family. Lava pools are blocking ground,
  2+ cells wide, with their corners cut.
- Decoration comes as clusters plus an even scatter, never on the paths from the arrival to the links, the boss and
  the rooms.
- Obstacles have a fully walkable ring. Lights and wall furniture stand against walls, in dungeon rooms only (never in
  a corridor). Every blocking piece passes a "simple point" test, so it never cuts a path.
- With the dark tile set installed the themes use its patches and props (dark moss, ash soil, glowcaps, braziers, dead
  trees). Without it the stock palette is used.
- `areagen_export.py check` checked all 244 ids against the live items.otb (3.57) and things_custom18. Each id exists,
  has a sprite and has the right kind. With the rift themes (2026-10-12) it checks 211 ids stock and 280 with the dark
  set (now also the `byKind` overrides), against an items.otb with the dark set and things_custom19: 0 problems.
- Rift themes (`rift_abyss`, `rift_hall`, `rift_crypt`, `rift_sanctum`; "Rifts", Layouts and the slot pool): families
  `riftfloor` (the old rift floor 25549, 25704-25709), `crypt` (dark sandy 13189, rutted stone 12237), `gilded` (415),
  and with the dark set `obsidian` (obsidian / magma floor, its border set over any ground) and `wetrock` (wet / mossy
  rock, its border set). Every transition between bordered families carries its pieces (the test checks it for every
  theme in every band, stock and dark).

**Spawns.**
- Poisson-disc points at `minDistance`. Packs of 2-3 come with `packChance`. The density is per 100 walkable tiles
  outside the arrival's safe radius.
- Dungeon rooms fill before corridors, with a cap per room (`roomCap`, monsters per 100 room tiles).
- The monsters are the level-scaled late-game set (README "Late game"). They are scaled to the area's level with the
  engine's own formulas (`A.levelScale`):
  - health x(1 + 0.0074 T)/(1 + 0.0074 L) at the spawn;
  - damage x(1 + 0.0015 T)/(1 + 0.0015 L) in the player health and mana events;
  - experience x T/L in an onGainExperience callback (index 1).
  The engine has no Lua call to set a monster's level, so the name still shows its native level (960-1000).
- Respawn: the dynamic respawn of item 89 changes engine spawns only. Runtime monsters have none, so `areagen.lua` runs
  its own respawn with the same rules:
  - the spawntime (120 s);
  - no respawn while a player sees the spot (the timer starts again);
  - the dynamic respawn's percent for the hunters near the point (`ChaosRespawn.percentFor`, `respawn_config.lua`:
    2 hunters 85% down to 50%).
- A monster more than 14 tiles from its point with no target is walked back (leash).
- Boss: a stronger copy in its own room, by its shown name (`Chaos.createMonsterNamed`), health x8, damage x1.25,
  respawn 1 hour.

**Entrances and exit.**
- A magic forcefield (1387) with action id 47950 is placed on the live map at startup. It sends players of `minLevel`
  and above to the arrival; others are pushed back.
- The exit forcefield (47951) stands next to the arrival and leads back beside the entrance (an area without an
  entrance: the temple). Runtime tiles cannot be protection zones, so the arrival is a safe radius with no spawns.
- An entrance tile that is not free and walkable is skipped with a log line; `/areagen goto <id>` still works.

  x 14400-14495 y 14400-14475, Ossuary x 14560-14689 y 14400-14501, Cinderfall x 14400-14544 y 14560-14675, Vault

- Capacity (2026-10-14): 738 monsters + 3 bosses at 120 s (was 205), about 145 hunters at the 158 : 31 ratio below.
- Capacity before the growth: 205 monsters + 3 bosses at 120 s. That is +130% over the 158 monsters of the 1000+ band, so about 40 more

  The waste has 1.6 lights per 100 tiles against the lava band's 5+; it is under the sky, and the lava pools glow
  (light 4) but are grounds the scorer does not count. The Vault has 0 small loops (one big circuit).

**The generated dungeon.**
- `dungeon = {...}` registers the area in `DUNGEON_SYSTEM.Dungeons` and `Chaos.dungeons.extra` at startup.
- `extra.populate` fills every point at each run start and closes the boss room gate (`AG.gateTiles`: every walkable
  tile of the ring just outside the boss room, the doorways, gets a wall piece of the theme's wall brush; the test walks
  from the boss and never leaves the room). That is the hook in `dungeons.lua` `startRun`; the run's teardown removes
  the monsters. At 85% (`progressNeeded`) `extra.unlock` opens the gate and spawns the boss at its spot, so it cannot
  be seen, pulled or hit before. `extra.bossType` gives the client list the boss look.
- The base entry window (modal) path does not call the hook yet.

**The deep dungeons 6-9** (2026-10-14, owner request: four more queue dungeons for the levels after the Vault, 1000 /
1300 / 1600 / 2000, built like it).
- Where: a block of their own outside the world, x/y 24576-25599 (the 14336-15359 block is full of planned hunts). The
  full map read with `tools/map/otbm.py` (18,388,336 tiles) has no tile and no spawn there; the nearest tile is 5,315
  sqm away; the rift slots use 20480-21503. Cells of 256 sqm: Marrow Crypts 24576, 24576; Iron Crucible 24832, 24576;
  Fallen Sanctum 24576, 24832; Pyre Throne 24832, 24832 (z 9; 52 x 42 each since the 15 minute runs). docs/MAP_GUIDE.md
  "Content plans".
- Each has its theme (`marrow`, `crucible`, `sanctum`, `throne`: only ids of the checked palettes, so nothing new for
  `areagen_export.py check`), trash of its band scaled to the dungeon's level (the 1600 and 2000 dungeons use the
  1300-2000 hunting monsters, "Late game"), and a boss of its own monster file (its own look, its loot table, `isboss`):
  Ossivane the Gravecage (look 863), Forgewarden Kharzun (1281), Vaelith the Fallen Seraph (1148), Azhkarrath the
  Chained Wyrm (1535: a one-facing look, so the boss is chained, speed 0). All four looks are unused outfits of the
  current pair: no pair change. Mechanics: "Boss mechanics".
- Solo (party 1) like the Vault, six difficulties, the boss on the Vault's curve 100-225%, speed and flawless
  challenges, records boards (`dungeon_<id>`, per difficulty, by themselves from the dungeon list).
- Run length: 15 minutes, speed 6 (owner: "dungeons of 10-15 minutes"): 8-11 monsters in packs (their trash takes
  75-101 s alone each, the Vault's 44 s), bosses of 2:30 alone, own trash and boss curves ("Solo kill times").
- Boss chest (`dungeon.chest`, `AG.giveChest`, numbers `dungeons_difficulty.lua` `D.chest`): at the end of a won run
  every finisher gets, straight into the backpack (the inbox when full; the run sends everyone out 10 s after the kill):
  the dungeon's gold x (1 + the difficulty's gold bonus) to the bank (150,000 / 200,000 / 250,000 / 300,000 at
  difficulty 1, x5 at 6); 1 / 1 / 2 / 2 / 3 / 3 pieces of the boss's own gear at the boss level's item level (tier boss)
  + 0..5, rarity at least Magic / Magic / Rare / Rare / Legendary / Legendary (the loot layer's bonus steps of tier rare /
  rare / legendary / legendary / boss / boss on top, item find counts); 1 / 1 / 1 / 2 / 2 / 3 currency rolls of that tier.
  The Vault keeps no chest (unchanged). One hook in `dungeons.lua` `endRun` calls `extra.onClear` per finisher.
- Achievements: the counters `dungeon_<area id>`, `_top`, `_d6` ("Achievements").
- Codex / wiki: the lore entry "The Four Deeper Doors" (`lore_data.lua`); the wiki's Dungeons tab lists every generated
  dungeon with its level, theme, size, monsters, run, boss mechanics, chest and challenges (`tools/gen_wiki_data.lua`).
- The client's queue window needs nothing: the list, the boss look (`extra.bossType`), the loot panel and the
  challenges come from the server. The banner falls back to the stock "Underworld" art (as for the Vault).

**Install / enable.** Nothing to install. The areas are built when `enabled = true` (globally and per area); a
refused area logs why. Disabling an area at a restart drops its tiles; a character saved inside goes to its temple.
`/areagen status | goto <id> | fill <id>` (group 4+).

## Decoration of pair 48 (`tools/install_decor48_items.py`, `data/items/decor48_items.csv`)
352 decoration items for the ice (58), swamp (150), lava (16) and cave (128) biomes, art of a donor pair ("source B") appended to the
client pair as items 38759-39110 (client/MANIFEST.md "Decoration of the ice, swamp, lava and cave biomes (pair 48)").
- **Ids.** Server id = client id + 4000 (**42759-43110**), key `decor48_<biome>_<client id>`, name "<biome> prop <n>". The usual +3000
  would run into the Waystone Tier items (41951-41959); nothing else uses 42759-43110 (the test reads every other manifest of
  `data/items/`).
- **Install.** Step `decor48items` of `install_all.py`, after `rewardchest`: one items.otb node and one items.xml entry per row (the
  rules of `install_donor_items.py`: a node of the same bytes is left alone, another client id on a server id stops it, `.bak`
  of the original, the written file parsed back; items.xml block between two marker comments, an id outside the block stops it).
  Idempotent. Run on a copy of the installed server data: 352 nodes and entries added, a second run changes nothing. Without a
  client on pair 48 the items show as nothing.
- **Flags.** None is pickupable, moveable or a container. Trees, big rocks and crystals block (otb solid: the dat flags notwalkable
  or blockpath), bushes, flowers, snow piles, logs and the like do not. 26 are animated (9 of the 16 lava props, 14 cave, 2 swamp, 1 ice) and 34 more carry a light; `--kit-json OUT.json` writes biome -> [{server_id, size, kind static / animated / light, blocks}] for the map studio kits.
- **Use.** Nothing places them by itself. The area planner kits and the map studio can list them once the client pair is shipped.
- **Tests.** `python3 -I server/tools/install_decor48_items_test.py` (the shipped manifest, id and biome rules, a clash with another
  manifest, nodes and XML on synthetic files, the command line twice).

## Pair 50 items (`tools/install_pair50_items.py`, `data/items/pair50_items.csv`)
5198 ground, wall, stairs, decoration and corpse items of two purchased sprite sources ("source G", "source F"), appended to the
client pair as items 39198-44395 (client/MANIFEST.md "pair 50").
- **Ids.** Server id = client id + 4000 (**43198-48395**), key `pair50_<category>_<client id>`, category ground, wall, stairs, decor
  or corpse. They follow pair 49's block with no gap; the test reads every other manifest for clashes.
- **Install.** Step `pair50items` of `install_all.py`, after `decor49items`: same rules as the other item steps (node of the same
  bytes left alone, another client id on a server id stops it, `.bak`, written file parsed back, items.xml block between two marker
  comments). Idempotent. Install only together with a client on pair 50 or newer.
- **Floor changes.** Stairs up: `floorchange` north or west (the direction the treads climb on screen; a guess from the art).
  Stairs down and holes: `down`. Ladders: no floor change; `data/scripts/chaos/pair50_items.lua` registers an Action on the ids of
  `data/lib/chaos_pair50_items.lua` (written by `install_pair50_items.py --lua`) and calls `Position:moveUpstairs()` of the base lib
  (protection zone rule kept). Source G has no role in its selection: its 41 steps and pits carry no floor change, so a map maker
  must place a teleport or choose the pieces by hand. Doors are art only (no open / close script).
- **Flags.** `notwalkable` is solid, a dat `blockpath` alone only asks the path finder to avoid the tile (stair pieces carry it and
  stay walkable), borders sit on top, animated items carry the animation flag.
- **Corpses (139).** Containers of 20 slots that decay to nothing after 600 s, set up like the pack corpses. A corpse placed on a
  map as decoration decays too (one stage, no chain), so use them for monster corpses only.
- **Monsters and effects.** Outfits 2682-3360 are listed in `data/items/pair50_outfits.csv`. Effects 4102-4701 are in
  `data/items/pair50_effects.csv`; `data/lib/chaos_pair50_fx_ids.lua` (`client/tools/sprites/gen_pair50_fx_ids.py`) merges them into
  `ChaosVfx` with their send offset. No missile fits (one byte, 254 is the weapon-type constant, 253 are in use).
- **Tests.** `install_pair50_items_test.py`, `tests/pair50_items_test.lua`, `import_pair50_test.py`, `gen_pair50_fx_ids_test.py`.

## Reward chests (`rift_config.lua`, `descent_config.lua`, `reward_sparkle*.lua`, `tools/patch_reward_chests.py`)

Owner request 2026-10-20: the plain wooden chest was hard to see on dark cave floors. Every chest a player takes a reward
from is now one of two big chests of the 10.98 item set, picked from a rendered contact sheet of every chest of the
sprite pair (gold and readable on dark floors, 2x2, not moveable, not pickupable):

| Chest | Item | Was | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| reward chest (own look: a gold chest overflowing with coins and gems; container 32) | 32311 (client 38758, pair 53; 32310 and client 38657 are the retired 2 x 2 look); falls back to 21584 (the stock gold chest on a stone plinth) while 32311 is not installed | 1740, then 21584 | the rift chest where the guardian died (`rift_config.lua` `chest`), the Ember Descent's treasure room chest (`descent_config.lua` `objects.chest`), the quest chests of every planned area (`tools/areaplan_build.lua` hands the rift chest to the planner), and every quest chest of the base server's map (see "Install") |
| treasure chest (blue and silver, container 20) | 12664 | 1746 | the rift's Sealed Coffer (`rift_config.lua` `coffer`): it must be a container, its spoils go inside |

**Own look (owner request 2026-10-26: "make a reward chest and give every quest chest this sprite"; pair 45).** The stock
21584 is a gold chest on a stone plinth. Item **32310** "reward chest" is a copy of its node (group container, flags,
attributes; container 32, not moveable, not pickupable) with the client id **38657**, a PixelLab painting of our own: a
gold chest overflowing with coins and gems, the lid open, mirrored left-right at the owner's request (2 x 2, a still; client/MANIFEST.md
"Reward Chest look", `client/tools/sprites/gen_reward_chest_art.py`). The block 32310-32319 is reserved for it (32301-32309
are the charms, 32351-32399 the professions). `install_all.py` step `rewardchest` (`tools/install_reward_chest.py`, modelled on
the Cursed Chest's; before `rewardchests`) writes the otb node and an items.xml entry between two marker comments. Until it
is installed `rift_config.lua` `chest.fallbackId` and `descent_config.lua` `objects.chestFallback` (21584) are what the rift
and the Descent create (`ItemType(id):getId() ~= 0`, as the Cursed Chest does); the map step refuses to run without the id.
Ship pair 45 and a client build before the `rewardchest` step: a client on pair 44 or older draws nothing for the new
client id. `tools/install_reward_chest_test.py` (synthetic items.otb / items.xml; also checks the configs and the client
things file).

**Two looks (2026-10-26, pair 47).** The base map's quest chests were one tile big and many sit in tight quest rooms (31 of
about 297 next to another chest), where a 2 x 2 chest overlaps walls and neighbours. Item **32311** "reward chest" (client
**38758**, a 32 x 32 PixelLab version of the same chest: owner pick "use o 15"; client/MANIFEST.md "Reward Chest look, one
tile") is a second copy of the 21584 node with the same attributes, installed by the same step in the same block. The big
32310 stays the rift chest, the Descent's and the planned areas' quest chest, and the base's own 21584 chests (2 x 2
already); the small 32311 is what the base map's quest chests and quest boxes get (`rift_config.lua` `chest.smallItemId`,
read only by `patch_reward_chests.py`; no script uses it). Ship pair 47 before the `rewardchest` step.

**One look (2026-10-27, pair 53; O280).** Owner request: every reward chest wears the one-tile look. Client **38758** (server
**32311**) is redrawn in place in pair 53 as a chest of a purchased prop sheet (docs/CREDITS.md), fitted to 32 x 32 by taking 6 rows and 3 columns out of the 35 x 38 cut-out (client/MANIFEST.md "Pair 53"; the pixels are
not in git). The rift (`chest.itemId`), the Descent (`objects.chest`), the planned areas and every swapped chest of the base map use
32311; `chest.fallbackId` (21584) stays for a server that has not run the `rewardchest` step. The 2 x 2 **32310** is retired:
`install_reward_chest.py` still installs both nodes (a map or a character's history may hold 32310), `rift_config.lua`
`chest.legacyItemIds` lists it, and `patch_reward_chests.py` moves every placed 32310 to 32311 on the next run (planned areas
too; the `contentareas` step sees a changed plan and updates the placed area). The base's own 21584 chests are swapped to 32311
(they were 32310). `smallItemId` no longer exists. The area planner leaves the 8 tiles around a chest empty
(`area_plan_decor.Dresser.clear_around`, kept: floor, walls, path edging), so a chest never sits behind a statue or a barrel.
Ship pair 53 with the client before the map step.

The old ids could be moved and picked up (1740 and 1746 are pickupable in items.otb); the new ones cannot. Neither id
is used by another system (the base server's own handler of 21584 is commented out in its actions.xml; the plaza's
daily chests are 29327). The reward chests of the other systems are not map items: dungeon boss chests
(`areagen.lua` AG.giveChest), world bosses, invasions, arenas, pocket bosses and trials give straight to the backpack
or inbox; the Infinity Tower season chests (`chaos_constants.lua`) and the bounty chest (1990) are items sent to the
inbox, so they keep their small looks.

- **Sparkle:** `reward_sparkle.lua` (one GlobalEvent every `intervalMs`, 2.5 s) sends `CONST_ME_YELLOW_RINGS` over each
  registered chest. The rift registers its chest (while a finisher has not taken their share) and the coffer (while it
  is sealed). An entry ends when its check says so, when the item is no longer on its tile, after `maxAge` (30 min), or
  past `maxEntries` (200). The planned areas' quest chests do not glint: they are per character and on the map always.
  Rules: `reward_sparkle_core.lua`, `tests/reward_sparkle_test.lua` (also checks the ids of the configs).
- **Install** (`install_all.py` step `rewardchests`, right before `contentareas`, after `rewardchest`): `tools/patch_reward_chests.py
  DATA_DIR [--dry-run] [--map FILE] [--out FILE] [--items-otb FILE]` turns the quest chests on the map into the reward chest
  of `rift_config.lua` (`chest.itemId`, 32311, one tile, for every kind of chest below). It rewrites only the item id of the node: action id, unique id, the contents (a quest chest
  holds its rewards as child items), the tile and the rest stay, so the base quest scripts work as before (they look at the
  unique / action id, never at the item id; 21584 is a container like the old ones). What counts as a quest chest:
  1. **Planned areas:** a chest 1740 or 21584 with an action id of the quest chest block (47960-47999, or a plan's own
     `chest_action`). They are swapped, not only the old 1740, so a map that already holds 21584 chests catches up; the
     `contentareas` step sees its placed areas unchanged instead of refusing them as changed plans.
  2. **The base server's own quest chests** (`BASE_CHEST_IDS`: chest looks 1740, 1746-1749, 8587, 12664, 18472-18474) that the base
     quest system opens (`data/actions/actions.xml`, `scripts/quests/`): an action id of `system.lua` (2000, 2016, 2215,
     10544, 12374, 12513, 26300, 27300, 28300; the unique id is the storage key) **and** items inside (system.lua hands out
     the contents; a chest with nothing inside would hand out a copy of itself, so an empty one is no quest chest); action id
     2001 with a unique id of `system2.lua`'s table (a fixed reward); a unique id a quest script owns (Inquisition
     1300-1308, In Service of Yalahar 3088-3090, Bigfoot's Burden 3147-3150, Children of the Revolution 3164, Wrath of
     the Emperor 3200, Demon Oak 9008-9011, warzone 9172-9174); the base's own reward chest 21584 with an action id (the
     starter chest 33735, the Soul War chest 33733).
  3. **Quest boxes** (`BOX_IDS`: 1738 and 1741, "box"): the base quest systems open some boxes as reward containers, and the
     owner asked that every container that gives a quest reward wears the look. A box counts under the first two base rules
     only: an action id of `system.lua` with a unique id and items inside, or action id 2001 with a unique id of
     `system2.lua`'s table. An empty box, one without a unique id, one with only a quest-script unique id stays a box.
  4. **Not touched, on purpose:** the other containers that carry the quest action id are themed hiding places and keep
     their look: corpses and slain creatures, coffins, sarcophagi, chests of drawers, bookcases, barrels, the bamboo shelf
     (1716-1721, 1410, 1419 ...). Also not touched: chests no script owns (a unique id nothing handles, no action id:
     decoration or loot containers, e.g. the 12 of uid 61907-61918, and the mechanisms 61900-61918, 65207 and the action id
     41762 / 41763 / 12503 treasure chests: they trigger levers and doors, they hand out no reward), the plaza's royal
     chests (29327), the runtime chests (rift, coffer, Descent, Cursed Chest), and containers players keep things in
     (houses and depots carry no quest action id), a bare 21584 without an action id.
  5. **Migration:** a server that ran an earlier version of this step has chests as 32310 (and boxes as 1738 / 1741). The next
     run moves every 32310 (`chest.legacyItemIds`) to 32311, planned areas included, and swaps the boxes.
  On the base map of 2026-10 the step finds **301** nodes, all of which become 32311 (one tile): 4 starter / Soul War chests (21584) and **297**
  more: 265 by `system.lua` (140 x 1740, 3 x 1746, 7 x 1747, 6 x 1748, 18 x 1749, 3 x 8587, 5 x 12664, 3 x
  18473 chests, plus 51 x 1738 and 29 x 1741 boxes), 11 by `system2.lua` (5 x 1740, 5 x 1738, 1 x 1741), 21 by a quest script
  (14 x 1740, 3 x 1748, 12664, 18472, 18473, 18474): 86 boxes and 211 chests in all. A simulated earlier run (215 as 32310)
  followed by this one gives byte for byte the same map as one run (211 moved, 86 boxes swapped). 32311 is exactly one tile,
  so nothing on the map shifts (the earlier 2 x 2 chests of 21584 and 32310 are gone).
  Refused when either new id is not in `items/items.otb` (`--items-otb` names another file: `install_all.py --dry-run` reads its
  copy's, where the `rewardchest` step just ran). A second run changes nothing. `<map>.otbm.bak` is written first when
  missing. `tools/patch_reward_chests_test.py` (synthetic map with contents: every rule and every exception, boxes, the
  migration).

## Area planner (`tools/area_planner.py`, `tools/area_plan_*.py`, `tools/areaplan_build.lua`, `tools/areaplan/`)

A semantic plan (JSON, `tools/areaplan/schema.json`, version `chaos-area-plan/1`) becomes an OTBM piece for the map
editor through the area generator above (owner approval, 2026-10-13). The plan names a biome, zones, paths,
connections, spawns, boss, NPCs, chests, entry, exit, PZ zones, decoration and light; it never holds an item id.
Details and rules: docs/MAP_GUIDE.md "Area planner".
Production plans for the thin level bands live in `tools/areaplan/plans/` (ten, 200-1300; origins and placing:
docs/MAP_GUIDE.md "Content plans"). CI validates and compiles them with the examples; none is placed on the world map yet.

- **Commands:** `validate`, `compile` (`<id>.otbm`, `<id>-frame.otbm`, `<id>-spawn.xml`, `<id>.json` manifest, `data/...` stubs;
  `--no-dress` without decoration), `render` (floor PNGs and a marked minimap; needs items.otb/xml and the pair),
  `stats`, `approve`, `suggest`, `similar`, `catalogue`, `plan --from-prompt`, `place`, `install`, `check-kits`.
  Nothing runs on the live server; the world map is never written (`place` writes a copy).
- **Generator hooks** (`areagen_core.lua`): `def.layout.plan[floor]` (zones, paths, landing spots, anchor) carves a
  planned layout instead of a random one, and `def.links` gives the hole points. The four areas and the rifts are
  unchanged (same checksums).
- **Catalogue:** `tools/areaplan_build.lua` maps biomes to our themes and reads ids only from `areagen_config.lua`,
  `chaos_dark_tiles.lua`, `chaos_theme_items.lua` (pair 24 grounds, only with `ChaosThemeArt.PAIR24` on or
  `--pair24 on`), `data/items/art_items.csv` (pack grounds, borders, trees) and `rift_config.lua` (chest); stock
  snow, ice and grass grounds with their border sets for `ice` and `forest` (no install step needed; `forest_pack`
  and `ice_pack` need the packitems step). Monsters and levels: `bounty_pool.lua` and `monster/monsters/chaos`;
  tiers: `bounty_config.lua` bands (the open top band 800+ also takes monsters up to the plan's own top + 100, past the
  bounty window's 1500, for the 1300-2000 set); NPCs: `data/npc`; reward items: `data/items/base_item_names.csv`,
  `chaos_items.xml`, `data/lib/chaos_orbs_config.lua`, `art_items.csv`.
- **Decoration** (`tools/area_plan_decor.py`, kits `tools/areaplan/decor_kits.json`): 107 groups (267 stock 10.98
  ids, each checked on the pair for sprite, blocking and light by `check-kits`), one kit per biome. Placed by rules:
  hall pillar rows, throne and braziers in boss rooms, corner statues, torches and tapestries on north and west
  walls, light props, corner pieces, wall props, clusters of 2-5, path edging, floor detail denser near walls. Never on
  a spawn, teleport, link, chest, NPC or boss tile; nothing blocking on the routes or the planned paths; the QA checks
  that no walkable tile is cut off. `decoration` sparse/normal/dense = x0.55/x1/x1.5, `light` scales the lights.
- **Stairs:** connection `stairs` uses our stair brush (stairs ground 411 above, stone stairs 3687 below: down lands
  south of the stairs, up north of the stairs ground); hole and ladder when the tiles do not allow it.
- **Roofs:** a dungeon floor at z 7 or above gets a flat roof (920) on the floor over it; underground areas need none.
- **View frame** (2026-10-22, owner screenshot "hunt com mapa preto": Gallowroot Wilds showed grey rock, then black). The
  generator builds only a rock rim of `rimWidth` (2) past the floor, and deep rock that reaches the grid border stays
  unbuilt (Gallowroot: 12,795 tiles of its 163 x 131). The client shows 15 x 11 tiles, so a player near the rim saw void.
  The compile adds `<id>-frame.otbm`: bare ground on every spot within `area_plan_core.VIEW` (9 x 7, the screen's 7 x 5
  plus big sprites) of a walkable tile that has no tile, on each floor of the plan (`area_plan_core.view_frame`). The
  ground is the theme's rock family (the rim's own ground: mountain 919 or earth 101, unwalkable, so no border is
  wanted); a dungeon gets earth 101 behind its walls (a wall closes the edge, the border QA skips wall tiles next to
  the frame). The QA counts the frame with the area: borders, unknown ids, and an ERROR for any spot in view of a
  walkable tile without ground. The manifest's `frame` gives its tile count, family and ground. The frame is a file of
  its own because it is not the area: `install_content_areas.py` and `place` lay it only where the map has no tile and
  no area or room goes, so it never replaces a tile; the 66 plans of 2026-10-22 add 359,383 frame tiles and no frame
  touches another plan.
- **Quest chests:** the reward chest (rift_config.lua `chest.itemId`, 32311; "Reward chests"; nothing else is placed on the 8 tiles around it, `Dresser.clear_around`) with the area's action id (block **47960-47999**, plan `chest_action` or one from the
  block by the area id) and one player storage per chest (block **7101200-7101299**, by the quest key). The compile
  writes `data/scripts/chaos_areaplan/<id>_chests.lua`: a revscript Action that gives the plan's `reward` (item names
  from our item tables, gold, experience) once per character, keyed by the chest's offset from the area's ORIGIN.
- **New NPCs** (`"new": true` in the plan): `data/npc/<Name>.xml` and `data/npc/scripts/<name>.lua` stubs (greeting
  and "keyword: answer" lines); edit the look before going live.
- **Install a planned area** (owner, after the review):
  1. `compile` the plan with `origin` set to where it will go (or any place, then step 2 moves it).
  2. `place OUT/<id>.otbm WORLD.otbm COPY.otbm --at X Y Z --spawn WORLD-spawn.xml COPY-spawn.xml`: a copy of the map and
     of the spawn file; refused when a tile lands on a world tile. The view frame goes in where the copy has no tile.
  3. Check the copy in the map editor, then use it (and the spawn copy) as the server's map.
  4. `install OUT SERVER_DIR [--dry-run]`: the chest script and NPC stubs into `data/`; idempotent, refuses a clash
     of action id, storage or file. Restart the server.
- **Knowledge base:** SQLite outside git, `$AREAPLAN_KB` or `~/.local/share/cinders-of-chaos/area_planner/kb.sqlite3`.
- **AI adapter** (`area_plan_ai.py`, optional): only with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `AREAPLAN_LLM_MODEL` (no model name is kept in the repo) or
  `AREAPLAN_LLM=openai` with `AREAPLAN_LLM_ENDPOINT` / `AREAPLAN_LLM_MODEL` (a local Ollama needs no key) set by the
  user. Keys are read from those variables only, never stored or printed. Up to 3 fix rounds with the validator's errors.
- **Tests:** `tools/area_planner_test.py` (CI; validator rules, reachability maths, layout, the four examples compiled
  with QA, determinism, decoration rules and rates, stairs, roofs, chest script run on a mocked engine, place and
  install on synthetic maps, pair 24 switch, knowledge base, AI fix loop on a fake endpoint). Previews of the examples
  were rendered with things_custom23 for review only.

## Map inbox (`tools/area_inbox.py`, `tools/areaplan/inbox/`, `chaos-ctl.sh areas-publish`, O192)

Areas the owner asks for in chat wait here as plans until they are approved (docs/MAP_GUIDE.md "Map inbox").
- `tools/areaplan/inbox/<id>/plan.json` + `meta.json` (status pending / approved / installed). No binaries in git: the compile
  is deterministic, `area_inbox.py build ID OUT_DIR` makes the `.otbm`, frame, spawn xml, manifest and (with render inputs)
  pictures again. Commands: `new`, `list`, `check`, `approve`, `build`, `publish`, `promote`, `remove`. Test:
  `python3 -I tools/area_inbox_test.py` (CI step "Area planner"; `area_inbox.py check` validates every entry).
- `promote` moves an approved plan to `tools/areaplan/plans/` (needs an `origin`; refuses a box that meets another plan's).
  It wires nothing else: `hunt_teleports_config.lua` `plans` is optional (it names the display monster; an unlisted plan
  gets its most frequent monster), the slots come from the level band. Remaining: `install_content_areas.py` on the live
  map (`install_all.py --only contentareas`), `progression_model.lua --check`, `tests/hunt_teleports_test.lua`.
- `chaos-ctl.sh areas-publish [--pictures] [--rotate]` (admin app: Comandos > Mapas pedidos > Publicar áreas / Novo
  endereço): needs `CHAOS_REPO` to hold the entries (update-apply), python3 and LuaJIT (as the content install). Writes
  `CHAOS_DL_DIR/areas-<TOKEN>/`, the token in `CHAOS_AREAS_STATE` (default `/var/lib/chaos/areas/token`, mode 600), prints
  `areas-published: N area(s)` and `url=<CHAOS_SITE_URL>/dl/areas-<TOKEN>/`. Nothing runs on the game server and the map
  is not touched. `tools/windows/package/fetch-areas.bat` fetches from that url.
- Assumption: the web server serves files of `dl/` as they are (the downloads page already relies on it) and does not list
  the folder. The site has no login for static files, hence the secret path.

, `hunt_teleports_core.lua`, `hunt_teleports_config.lua`, `tools/install_content_areas.py`)
The way into the ten planned content hunts (`tools/areaplan/plans/`, docs/MAP_GUIDE.md "Content plans"): new teleports
in the base server's teleport room. Owner: "Coloque um teleporte pra elas na sala de teleports"; "Aumente a sala de
teleports mantendo o mesmo design dela. O teleport na frente de um monstro dela".

**The room.** The hub the "Teleports" portals beside Cinderhold's temple (town 2, temple 32369, 32241, 7) lead to: a
hall on three floors (z 5, 6, 7) at x 31627-31669, y 32251-32261, the stairs in the middle (31648, 32257). Each floor
has 16 teleports in alcoves of 4 columns along a carpet corridor (north row y 32254, south row y 32258), a counter with
a sign behind each teleport, two closed one-tile cells beside the counter with a monster of the hunt in each (spawn file,
radius 1; the cells are not PZ, the corridor is) and a teleport to the temple at each end. **Display monsters are
harmless** (owner, 2026-10-16): a monster without a master on a cell row (`room.cellRows`) of floors 5-7 inside
`display.x` is a display (`ChaosHuntTeleports.isDisplay` / `isDisplaySpot`; Lua cannot read the spawn file's
`chaoshunt` mark, so the spot is the tag). `onTargetCombat` refuses every hit of it, the engine asks that for melee,
target and area combat alike. **Nobody hurts a display either** (beta 2026-10-22: the Smoldering Aura item power killed them): `onTargetCombat` also refuses every hit on it, and direct damage that skips that check (`doTargetCombatHealth` of scripted hits) is dropped by `ChaosHallDisplayGuard` (onHealthChange, registered in `onSpawn` on a display spot; heals pass). Boss mechanics, the monster tier roll, the treasure goblin and the item powers skip it. Every slot was taken. The
hunts take floor 6 ("More Teleports"), which has no tile around it.

**Install** (`install_all.py` step `contentareas`, after houses and before poi; on its own
`python3 -I server/tools/install_content_areas.py <server>/data [--dry-run] [--only ID,...] [--no-room]`):
- Compiles every plan (`area_planner.py compile`, read at run time: size, origin and arrival are never copied) and
  pastes it into the map at its own origin; refused when a tile lands on a map tile. Then each placed area's view
  frame (Area planner "View frame") fills the spots where the map has no tile and no area, room or hall tile goes
  (two frames on one spot: the first plan by id); it never replaces a tile, and a second run adds nothing. An area
  placed before the frame existed (`placed already`) gets its frame on the next run. A plan placed later on another
  area's frame takes those tiles when they still hold the bare frame ground (they are cut and written again).
- Grows floor 6 by `modules` (6) alcove modules on each side: the columns of `room.east.module` / `room.west.module`
  are copied one after another past the old end, and the end (`cap`, with its temple teleport and destination) moves
  out by 24. Only the old end's 34 tiles are replaced (cut from the map file); the 504 other new tiles land where the map
  has none, else nothing is written. The copies have no teleport and blank signs: 24 new slots (x 31606-31626 and
  31670-31690, both rows); floor 6 spans x 31602-31694 instead of 31626-31670. A floor grown before by fewer modules
  (5 until 2026-10-25, when Sunken Mirewood made 38 hunts on floor 6) grows on from its ends where they stand: only the
  missing modules are new, the ends move on (log "floor 6 is grown by east 5 / west 5 modules already"). The same holds
  for the wings. `hall.capacity` names each floor's slot count; `install_content_areas_test.py` counts the hunts per
  floor (base hunts and plans, by level) and fails CI with "grow the room" before a deploy would.
- Spawn file: the plans' spawn blocks (marked `chaoscontent="ID"`) and two display monsters per used slot in the cells
  beside its counter (`chaoshunt="ID"`, spawntime `displaySpawntime`), the same way the room shows its own hunts. A
  display monster is a frequent monster of the plan whose look renders in the client pair (checked:
  Deathrattle 1150, Hellflayer 856, Nightfang Widow 1404, Ashfang Wrym 1418, Hellmaw Brute 1409, Black Stag 686,
  Ironhook Corsair 1492, Elite Tidecrest Serpent 675, Black Vixen 1475) and at most 2x2 tiles (owner, 2026-10-16:
  bigger sprites spilled over the cell walls; swapped: Celestial Wyrm 3x3 -> Spirit of Purity, Scaleborn 5x4 ->
  Twisted Shaper, Bonecrusher 3x3 -> Sopping Carcass; Wyrmspine Hollows has only 4x4 and 5x5 monsters: since
  2026-10-22 the base server's 2x2 Elder Wyrm stands in, `standIn = true`). Display blocks of a slot no longer used are removed. A base display block whose monster stands off its centre (centre on the
  corridor, monster one tile north in the cell) is taken over too (before, only the centre counted: two monsters on one
  cell, "Couldn't spawn monster" for Hellspawn, Warlock and Fleshcarver at every start; playtest 2026-10-16;
  `tools/install_content_areas_test.py`).
- Chest scripts (`area_planner.py install`) and `data/lib/chaos_hunt_places.lua`: per plan its teleport, sign,
  arrival, exit, band and the tile in front of its teleport (`front`, where its exit sends players back).
- Idempotent: a placed plan (same tiles) and a grown room are left alone. A plan changed after it was placed, on the
  same footprint, is written again: its tiles and its `chaoscontent` spawn blocks are replaced (a new spawn list moves
  the decoration, which keeps off the spawn points; the 11 plans of pack 30 on the live map, 2026-10-22). A changed
  footprint is refused; a map master keeps an area edited by hand ("Map master"). `<map>.otbm.bak` is written before
  the first change when missing. The
  map goes through `<map>.otbm.tmp` and its tile count is checked before it replaces the old one. The action id must not
  be on the map (checked). Measured on a copy of the live map: 127,827 tiles added, 34 replaced, 1,417 spawn blocks +
  20 display spawns, 87 s; a second run changes nothing.

**In game.** At startup `hunt_teleports.lua` puts a magic forcefield (1387) with action id **47930** (block
**47930-47939**, the rest free; the ways back of the added hunts share it, "Hall order") on each slot of a placed plan, gives it a description and writes the sign behind it
("Widowmere, levels 480-640" and the pt-BR line). Every `floatText.interval` ms the label floats over each teleport for
the players near it, each in their own language (the base room labels its teleports the same way). Stepping in below
the floor of the band (`minLevel` overrides it): back where the player came from, a poff and "Widowmere is for level
480 and above." (pt-BR: "Widowmere é para nível 480 ou mais."); else the teleport effect, the arrival tile and the band.
The camp portal of a placed plan (action id 47951, `areagen.lua`) sends players back to the tile in front of the
plan's own teleport, on its floor (`front` of its places entry, written by the install; else computed from
`room.teleportRows`: below a north-row teleport, above a south-row one, towards the stairs for an end-row one), through
`ChaosHuntTeleports.backFor`; other areas keep their exits. (Before 2026-10-20 every exit led to the middle of floor 6,
(31648, 32256, 6), though the hunts of levels 200-500 stand on floor 7: beta report "the teleports inside the hunts
take you to random places".) Slot order (owner, 2026-10-16: "ordered by level"):
the plans by level band ascending (the plan file's `level`: floor, ceiling, id), along the corridor from west to east,
north before south in each column; the config's order does not count, so a new hunt lands in its band's place on the
next install (the display spawns follow). `slot` pins one (1 = the westmost north teleport). A plan missing from
`plans` gets its most frequent monster on display (the install log names it: check its look, then list the plan to
choose). With `tools/hall_hunts.csv` the whole hall is ordered, the base server's teleports too: see "Hall order".
Tests: `tests/hunt_teleports_test.lua` (core and the engine file against a mock), `tools/install_content_areas_test.py`
(synthetic map: dry run, grow, place, spawns, places file, second run, refusals, reorder, --only).
- **Hall fill** (owner, 2026-10-22: "And the hunts of the upper floors? Did we fill all the ones that were
  missing?"). No: z 6 had 6 hunts on 37 slots, z 5 8 on 18 (dry run on the base map). 41 new plans fill them: 31 on
  z 6 (bands 500-615 up to 950-1050, 15 levels apart, about 115 wide) and 10 on z 5 (1050-1200 up to 1850-2000, four of
  them on two floors). They sit in their own block, x 15616-17663, y 14336-15359 (the schema's `origin.x` reaches
  17663), a grid of 204 tiles. Their monsters are the level-scaled ones of the chaos folder (no new monster); every
  display monster is 2x2 or smaller. 26 of them have a reward chest (action ids 47960-47999, storages 7101200-7101299,
  no clash). XP and gold per hour on the pace model (`paceKillsPerHour`, the engine's level factors, coins x 2.7) sit
  on the curve of the older plans of the same levels: XP within 25% (the furthest, Hexwood Thicket and Voidscar
  Chasm, are older plans whose monsters sit low in their bands), gold 1.1-2.3 M/h against 1.2-2.0. Install on a
  copy of the base map: z 7 48 on 48, z 6 37 on 37, z 5 18 on 18, 0 rooms closed, 829,327 tiles added, a second run
  changes nothing; `check_hunt_returns.py`: 45 base hunts, 0 without a way back, every plan back through its camp
  portal. Not played in a client.
- **Assumption:** the base room lives on floors 5-7 above the open ground of z 7, so the new wings of floor 6 hang over
  grass seen from z 7 outside the hall like the rest of the hall's upper floors.

## Hall order (`tools/hall_order.py`, `tools/hall_quests.py`, `tools/hall_hunts.csv`, `install_content_areas.py`, `hunt_teleports.lua`)
Owner, 2026-10-16: the teleport hall of Cinderhold ordered by level, floors going up as the monsters get stronger.
Hunting levels (owner 2026-10-27): the base hunts of `hall_hunts.csv` are on the pool scale; the install multiplies their `level`, `lo` and `hi` by `baseLevelMult` (`hall_order.hunting_rows`), so signs, labels, the order and the floors use the hunting level like the plans. **Retired 2026-10-28 (O285):** `baseLevelMult` is 1, so the shown level is the pool level again and the multiplication changes nothing; the floor boundary is back at 500 (560 was only needed for the doubled levels).
Owner, 2026-10-18 (after the first order overwrote some quest teleports of the ground floor): the **ground floor z 7
holds the hunts of levels 1-500 (560 on 2026-10-27 only, see "Hunting levels in the hall"), z 6 of 500-1000, z 5 of 1000 and up** (`hall.levels` in the config), and the base
quests are back, in their own hall. Every hunt teleport of the hall, the base server's and the planned hunts', takes a
slot of the floor its level belongs on, by its level (below), then band floor, ceiling and id: along the corridor from
west to east (north before south in a column). A floor with too few slots is grown (`room.wings`; below). A new hunt
(a plan file, or a row of the CSV) lands in its place on the next install.
- **Floors by level.** `hall.levels = {{z = 7, max = 500}, {z = 6, max = 1000}, {z = 5}}`: a hunt whose level is at most
  `max` goes on that floor, the last floor takes the rest. The floor labels say it ("Floor 7: levels 1-500", "Floor 5:
  levels 1000+"). `hall_order.assign` refuses with the floor's name when it has fewer slots than hunts; the z 7 wings
  (`room.wings`, copied from the room's alcoves of floor 6, 8 modules on each side, `sweep = true`: they take the place
  of the impassable lawn beside the hall, only decoration; `check_swept` refuses a tile with an action id, a unique
  id, a teleport, a sign or contents) hold the content hunts of 200-500 that the floor's rule puts there. On the
  test copy of the base map: z 7 48 hunts on 48 slots, z 6 37 on 37, z 5 18 on 18 (6 on 37 and 8 on 18
  before the hall fill of 2026-10-22, "Hunt teleports").
- **Level and band (the rule).** A hunt's level is the weighted median of its monsters' hunting levels (a plan: the
  middle of its `level`); its band, on its sign and label, is the weighted 20th-80th percentile, to 5s. One strong
  monster in a mixed area moves neither.
- **Quest hall** (`tools/hall_quests.py`, CSV kind `quest`, config `hall.quests`). The 16 base quest teleports of z 7
  (each an alcove of 4 x 3 tiles: the quest's name on the sign, the rewards on show in the two cells beside the teleport,

  base server's unmarked blocks in the hall's cells are taken over, `chaoshunt="base_Z_X_Y"`), and the places file
  gets `hall = true`, the base hunts (`base`), the floors' bands (`floors`) and the quest hall's label (`quests`). The
  tile flags (PZ) of existing tiles are never touched; the quest hall copies the hall's own. A tile attribute we cannot
  write back (a container) is refused.
  `--remove-hall` puts every base hunt back where the CSV says it stood, the quests in their old alcoves and the planned hunts in the wings again;
  the map backup `<map>.otbm.bak` is written before the first change as for every content install. Idempotent both ways.

## Map fixes (`tools/patch_map_fixes.py`, `tools/teleport_fixes.csv`, install step `mapfixes`)
Owner report of 2026-10-21 (live server): "many teleports lead nowhere", "hunts whose teleport has no teleport back",
"teleports in the hub with no monsters behind them", "black spots in the teleport hub", "the new NPCs are scattered".
Found on a copy of the base map with every install step (the live map is that), 2026-10-21; one tool fixes the map
parts in one pass after `contentareas` (before `poi`), idempotent like the other map steps (`<map>.otbm.bak` first,
`.tmp`, tile count checked; `--dry-run`, `--out`, `--only teleports,hub,temples`; test `tools/patch_map_fixes_test.py`).

  items.xml or items.otb calls a teleport (2,014 on the installed map) and its destination attribute:

## Lava edge strips (`tools/patch_lava_edges.py`, install step `lavaedges`, O288)

Owner, 2026-10-28: "some hunts have wrong floors", brown strips and an ochre bar on the grey rock of Ironhorn Slagworks.

- **Cause.** The lava decoration kit (`areaplan/decor_kits.json`, group `lava_cracks`) held the stock items 5840 to 5843,
  named "small lava cracks". They are the old lava edge pieces: a narrow brown strip with a crack line (5840, 5841, 5843)
  and a flat bar (5842), made to sit on the rim of a lava pool, not alone on a floor. The kit laid them as floor detail
  in every lava or waste hunt (`lava`, `waste` biomes): all 12 plans use the kit. The PvP zone (`pvpzone_config.lua`
  `decor.cracks`) used them too, now the thin cracks 22509 and 25834.
- **Fix.** The group is gone, the kit uses `cracks` (22509, 25834) instead. `area_planner_test.py` rejects any id of
  the four decoration kits or of the `areagen_config.lua` themes that is a ground, border, shore or lake piece (the
  `data/items/*.csv` tables, the area generator's own pieces and grounds, the stock edge items above); floor decals the
  tables mark `family=decals` or `cata_ground` are meant to lie alone and pass.
- **Placed hunts.** A placed area keeps its tiles (`install_content_areas.py` never replaces one), so a rerun of
  `contentareas` does not clean the live map. Step `lavaedges` (`patch_lava_edges.py`, after `deadholes`) takes the
  items 5840 to 5843 off every tile of a lava or waste plan (all its floors); ground and other items stay. Idempotent,
  writes `<map>.otbm.bak` first. Test `tools/patch_lava_edges_test.py`.
- **Owner step.** On the VPS: `python3 -I server/tools/install_all.py SERVER_DIR --only lavaedges` with the server
  stopped (`--dry-run` first lists the count). The admin app (`android/`) has no button for install steps.

Owner, 2026-10-28, with a screenshot of the Hollow Crypt hunt: the corridor floor alternates tile by tile between dark
streaked tiles and round reddish-brown pebble discs, so it reads as broken.

- **Cause.** The area generator's `crypt` ground family (`areagen_config.lua`, used by the themes `rift_crypt` and
  `marrow`) held `{13189, 3}` and `{12237, 2}`: 13189 "dark sandy floor" and 12237 "rutted stone floor". 12237 is one
  of the stain family 12234 to 12237 (the Map Studio cave kit lays them as small `stain` patches); it is a round pebble
  tile that does not tile with 13189, so a weighted pick laid the two side by side. The planner's `catacomb` biome
  (theme `rift_crypt`) put it on every corridor and floor stretch of 5 hunts: Hollow Crypt, Bonechoir Catacomb, Bonewright
  Galleries, Graveknell Catacombs, Lanternless Catacombs. The Marrow Crypts dungeon and the Ashen Crypt rifts build from
  the same family at run time and are fixed by the same change. The `crypt` biome (theme `ossuary`: slate) and
  `harvest_crypt` (pair 33 kit floors) never used it.
- **Fix.** The family is 13189 only (listed twice with the old weights so the seeded draws, and every layout, stay). `area_planner_test.py` checks the family and that the five catacomb plans
  compile with no 12234 to 12237 ground. The Ember Descent's Ashen Crypt look (`rift_config.lua` themes) and the arena
  look's small crypt patches (`arenalook_core.lua`) still use 12237 as patches, not as the floor.
- **Placed hunts.** A placed area keeps its tiles. Step `cryptfloors` (`patch_crypt_floors.py`, after `lavaedges`)
  sets the ground of every 12237 tile inside a catacomb plan (all its floors) to 13189; items stay. Idempotent, writes
  `<map>.otbm.bak` first, leaves house tiles alone. Test `tools/patch_crypt_floors_test.py`.
- **Owner step.** On the VPS, server stopped: `python3 -I server/tools/install_all.py SERVER_DIR --only cryptfloors
  --dry-run`, then the same without `--dry-run`. The admin app (`android/`) has no button for install steps.

## Dead holes (`tools/check_dead_holes.py`, `tools/patch_dead_holes.py`, `tools/dead_holes.csv`, install step `deadholes`, O264)
Owner report of 2026-10-26 with a screenshot: "esse buraco nao leva a lugar nenhum" (this hole leads nowhere): a dirt hole
on a patch of grass beside grey stone ruins and jungle plants. No coordinates. The checker and the patch below came out
of it; the base server's own map is where the holes are (see "Found").
- **The checker** (`python3 -I server/tools/check_dead_holes.py MAP.otbm [--items items.otb] [--xml items.xml] [--plans DIR]
  [--csv FILE] [--all] [--quiet]`; about a minute for the base map; items.otb and items.xml are looked for beside the map,
  else `../items/`). It reads the map with `tools/map/otbm.py`, finds every tile with a floor change item and works out where
  the engine puts a creature that steps on it, from the floor change values of items.xml (`floorchange`; items.otb bits 8-12
  too) and the item names:
  - `down` (holes, pitfalls, trapdoors, stairs down, ground-type holes): the same x,y one floor below, moved by the floor
    change of that tile as the engine does (the first of south-alt, east-alt, south, east, west: a stair below pushes the
    landing off its foot; a north stair below does not);
  - `north` / `south` / `east` / `west` (ramps, stairs up, corkscrew stairs): one floor up and one tile that way (alt: two);
  - ladders, rope-ladders and the rope spots (384, 418, 8278, 8592): the tile above or any of its 8 neighbours;
  - sewer grates: the tile below or any of its 8 neighbours.
  A landing is `void` (no tile, or a tile without a ground) or `blocked` (a ground with an item that blocks: flag block solid;
  block path only steers path finding, stairs and holes have it). A change is dead when every candidate landing is. A tile
  nobody can stand on (no ground, or a blocking item: roof pieces, rails) is no hole and is not listed. The area of a dead
  change is the plan box (origin, size, floors) of `areaplan/plans`, `chronicle`, `rooms`, `events` and `inbox` it lies in,
  else `base map`. The engine side is read from the usual TFS 1.4 floor change rules (the base source is not in the repo);
  run it again after an engine change that touches floor changes.
- **Not in CI on a map:** it needs the map. `tools/check_dead_holes_test.py` runs in CI on a synthetic map (down, up, ladder,
  grate, rope spot, stair offsets, void and blocked, roofs, items.xml ranges, a tiny OTBM, the CSV rows).
- **Found** on the installed map (the winpkg-80 release, 25,909 floor change tiles): 445 dead,
  all in the base map. By kind: stairs down 215 (ground-type stairs over nothing or over a wall), ramps and stairs up 111,
  sewer grates 45 (the cities' sewers are not mapped), pitfalls 18, holes 13, trapdoors 12, ladders and rope-ladders 12,
  ramps down 3, rope spots 3, and 13 others (9 ice huts and 2 coffins that carry a floor change, 2 open pitfalls drawn as
  "grass"). By floor: 114 on floor 7, 57 on 6, 55 on 3, the rest over 0 to 15. 246 land on no tile, 199 on a wall. None
  in our areas: the 73 plans of `areaplan/plans`, `chronicle`, `rooms` and `events` compiled alone
  (`area_planner.py compile`, deterministic) hold 18 floor change tiles and none is dead; the teleport hall and the placed
  areas of the installed map have none either (`area` is `base map` in every row). One dead hole lands on our view frame's
  rock (31339,30999,7: a large hole of the base map over the bare rock of an area's frame; the hole is the base server's).
- **The screenshot:** most likely 32396,31518,7 (item 293, a "grass" ground that is a pitfall, no tile on floor 8): jungle
  grass, shallow water, a mossy stone wall, carved stone, a broken lizard statue, stone pillars, bamboo and an umbrella
  plant within six tiles. Another 15 pitfalls on jungle grass (32675-32729, 32965-33038, floor 7) are dead too. The owner
  gave no position, so this is a match by description, not confirmed.
- **The patch** (`tools/patch_dead_holes.py DATA_DIR [--dry-run] [--map FILE] [--out FILE] [--csv FILE]`, install step
  `deadholes` after `mapfixes`, before `poi`; test `tools/patch_dead_holes_test.py`). `tools/dead_holes.csv` (made by
  `check_dead_holes.py --csv`; positions and item ids only) has one row per floor change item of a dead tile: `remove` takes
  the item off (the ground stays), `ground` turns a floor change that IS the ground (stairs, an open pitfall) into the
  commonest plain walkable ground round it, `none` where none is near. A row is applied only while the tile is still dead
  on the map the tool reads, so a lower floor mapped later keeps its hole. Idempotent like `mapfixes` (`.bak`, `.tmp`, tile
  count checked, `--dry-run`, `--out`). On the installed map: 195 items removed, 243 grounds replaced, 7 left alone (4 on house
  tiles, which the writer does not rewrite, 3 with no plain ground near); the checker finds those 7 and nothing else after.
- **A new dead hole in one of our areas** is fixed in its plan (`areaplan/plans/*.json`) or in the install tool that
  placed it, not by this patch: run the checker on the compiled area (`area_planner.py compile PLAN OUT`, then
  `check_dead_holes.py OUT/ID.otbm --items items.otb --xml items.xml`). To refresh the list after a new base-map change: `check_dead_holes.py MAP --csv server/tools/dead_holes.csv`.

## Map master (`tools/map_master.py`, `deploy/chaos_kit_update.sh` step `map`, branch `windows-assets` `world/`)
Owner request 2026-10-21: hand edits made in the map editor must survive the next build and reach the VPS. Before,
every build started from the base map and the install steps, so an edit lived only in one folder.
- **What it is.** The `.otbm` the owner edited (taken from the newest `CindersOfChaos-Windows.zip`, which holds the
  installed map; docs/MAP_GUIDE.md "Editing the live map"), kept on the private branch `windows-assets` under `world/`:
  `map-master.otbm.xz.partNN` (xz, cut at 95 MiB like `base-client.tar.xz.partNN`), `SHA256SUMS` (one line per part,
  `sha256sum -c` reads it) and `MAP_MASTER.json` (format, version 1, 2, ..., date, SHA-256 and size of the `.otbm` and
  of the `.xz`, the parts in order, the map header, the previous version, a note). Never on `main`: it is large and it
  is the live map.
- **The tool.** `pack OTBM OUT_DIR` checks the header (OTBM identifier, root node, map data), compresses, cuts, writes
  the sums and the metadata, bumps the version (the same map as the current version is refused, `--force`), removes
  parts an earlier version had and decompresses the result once to check it. `unpack DIR OUT` checks every part, the
  joined `.xz` and the map against the metadata and writes through `OUT.tmp`. `verify DIR [--deep]`. `install DIR
  SERVER_DIR`: the map of config.lua's `mapName` is replaced, the old one moved to `--backup-dir` (default
  `SERVER_DIR/map-backups`) as `<map>.otbm.<YYYYmmdd-HHMMSS>`, the newest 3 kept; the marker
  `data/world/<map>.otbm.master.json` records the version; the same version again is skipped (`--force`). The header
  names the spawn and house files the engine loads: a map saved under another name gets `<map>-spawn.xml` /
  `<map>-house.xml` back, else the server would start without monsters and houses. `<map>.otbm.bak` (the base map the
  install steps keep) is left alone. `installed SERVER_DIR` prints the version. Test: `tools/map_master_test.py`
  (synthetic maps with escaped header bytes).
- **Only the `.otbm`.** The spawn file and the house file stay the install steps'. The map editor writes a spawn file
  without the steps' markers (`chaosadd`, `chaoscontent`, `chaoshunt`, `chaosst`), so the next install would add every
  spawn twice. Monster and NPC spawns and house changes go in as a request (docs/MAP_GUIDE.md says so).
- **Builds.** `windows-package.yml` checks out `world` with the other assets and passes it to
  `tools/windows/prepare_server.sh BASE_SERVER_DIR [MAP_MASTER_DIR]`, which installs the master over the base map
  (the base map is not kept in the package) before `install_all.py`. No `world/MAP_MASTER.json` on the branch: the base
  map, as before. The Windows zip, the Linux server package and so the VPS's kit carry the marker.
- **Install steps over the master.** The master is an installed map, so every map step must find its work in place:
  `towns`, `worldtexts`, `servername`, `houses`, `spawnfields`, `rewardchests`, `contentareas` (each placed area
  checked tile by tile; a tile the owner changed inside a placed area refuses that area with the reason), `mapfixes`,
  `poi`, the `ownerdecor` / `assetsdecor` items. Three steps were not stable on a second run and are fixed (2026-10-22):
  `archery` moved its quiver block in `movements.xml` to the end on each run, so it traded places with the unique equip
  block (`tools/patch_base_archery.py` rebuilds the block where it stands; `tests/base_archery_patch_test.lua`);
  `spawns` took its added blocks out and appended them at the end, behind the blocks `contentareas` adds, so the two
  reordered the spawn file on every run (`tools/patch_base_spawns.py` puts them back where the first one was;
  `tests/base_spawns_patch_test.lua`); `spawns` also gave the display monsters of `contentareas` (`chaoshunt`) the
  band respawn, and `contentareas` put their own spawntime back at the end of the file (now `spawns` leaves those blocks
  alone). Several steps still rewrite each other's files during a run (`weapons`, `packitems`, `themeitems`,
  `pack30items`, `pack33items`, `archery`, `corpses` in `items.xml`: attack speed, corpse durations, launcher
  attributes; `outfits`, `auras`, `worldtexts`); the files at the end of a run are the same, so the report lists them
  but nothing changes.
- **Measured (2026-10-21, the real map after a full install).** `pack`: the 200 MB `.otbm` gives 28 MB of xz in one
  part, in about 2 minutes. `install`: 3 seconds. A full `install_all.py --no-sql` over the installed master: about
  5 minutes, no file different at the end (git status of the server folder clean, the `.otbm` byte for byte the
  master).
- **The VPS.** `chaos_kit_update.sh` step 3 `map` (`--no-map` skips it): `git ls-remote` for `CHAOS_MAP_BRANCH`
  (default `windows-assets`), a shallow fetch without blobs (`--depth=1 --filter=blob:none`: git fetches only the
  blobs it reads, so the base client and the other large files never come down; the checkout's `origin` becomes a
  promisor remote), the version of `world/MAP_MASTER.json` against the marker. Newer: `world/` and the branch's
  `map_master.py` into the work folder, `verify --deep`; a refusal ends the update before anything stops. Step 5
  (`install`, server stopped) runs `map_master.py install` before `install_all.py`, the old map going to
  `CHAOS_MAP_BACKUP_DIR` (default `$KIT/map-backups`, state `map_backup`); the restart of step 6 loads it. A failed
  start, or `update-rollback`, copies that backup back (the marker comes back with `data/` from the backup archive).
  `check` prints `map_master`, `installed_map`, `needs_map`; the admin app shows a "Mapa" line and the step "Conferindo
  o mapa mestre". Test: `deploy/chaos_kit_update_test.py` (a `windows-assets` branch packed by the real tool).
- **Publishing a master.** `python3 -I server/tools/map_master.py pack <the owner's .otbm> <windows-assets>/world
  --note "..."`, then commit `world/MAP_MASTER.json`, `world/SHA256SUMS` and every `world/map-master.otbm.xz.part*`
  on `windows-assets` (removed parts too) and push. The next package build and the next "Atualizar servidor" take it.

## Monster levels in the name (`monster_levels.lua`, `monster_levels_core.lua`, engine patch 0040)
Owner, 2026-10-16: "Black Stag [777]" showed its level, Hellflayer and Ashfang Wyrm did not. Cause: the engine rolls a
level only for a monster type with both `min` and `max` of `<level>` in its XML (our level-scaled monsters, written by
`tools/tune_monsters.py`) and puts " [level]" after the name only when that level is above 0; stock monsters have no
`<level>`. Giving them one would change them: the engine's level adds health (`monsterBonusHealth` x level), speed,
damage and a skull colour. So patch 0040 adds a display level instead (`monster:setDisplayLevel` /
`getDisplayLevel`), shown after the name and in the look text only. At every spawn (`onSpawn`, before the
placement) `monster_levels.lua` gives a monster without a level of its own its **hunting level** (owner 2026-10-27, "O272"):
`ChaosLoot.monsterLevel`, the bounty pool's "fair hunt" level of its type (else the experience / health estimate), times
`pace_config.lua` `baseLevelMult` (`Chaos.huntingLevel`, `ChaosMonsterLevelsCore.huntingLevel`), the level pace
uses to hunt it. **Since 2026-10-28 (O285) `baseLevelMult` is 1** (the owner retired the x2 rule: the planned hunts pick
monsters by pool level and showed double), so the shown level is the pool level; the multiplication stays in the code. Item level, monster damage and loot still read the pool level (display only). A generated area point's
level and a waystone run's level are hunting levels already and are not multiplied. Not for a player's summon (a Necromancer minion shows its owner's level, see "Summons: targets, walk-through,
levels"). Display monsters of the teleport room get it like any monster. Without patch 0040
nothing changes.

**Monsters outside the pool and summons in a high hunt (beta 2026-10-27).** A type that is not in `bounty_pool.lua` (fewer
than six spawn entries, scenery, a boss: Sheep, Dog, Mirror Image, Tornado, Rift Lord ...) only had the estimate of its
experience and health, so a Sheep stood in a level 240 hunt as "level 2". Now `ChaosMonsterLevels.apply` raises it to the
lower end of the hunting area it stands in (the nearest hunt mark of `data/chaos_poi.lua` within 60 sqm on its floor,
`ChaosMonsterLevelsCore.areaFloor`); a type of the pool is raised only when it shows less than a tenth of that lower end
(`farBelow`: a Badger in a level 120 hunt). The summon of a monster shows at least its master's level. The monster bar
(`monster_tiers.lua`) shows the nameplate level. `tests/hunt_display_levels_test.lua` crosses the pool, the spawn data and
the marks and fails when a monster of a hunt of 100+ would show less than a tenth of its lower end.

**Scaled monsters** show the level their system scaled them to, not their type's. The system passes it to
`Chaos.createMonsterNamed(type, pos, extended, force, shownName, shownLevel)` (or sets `Chaos.spawnLevel` around
`Game.createMonster`); `monster_levels.lua` uses it once in the same `onSpawn`, before the placement, so the first
creature packet carries it. Patch 0044 lets a set display level win over a level of the monster's own (a level-scaled
type in a rift showed its rolled "[777]"). Display only, as above.
- Rifts with density (`rift_core.lua R.displayLevel`): every pack monster and the guardian show the tier's level
  (`tiers[t].minLevel`, + `beyond.minLevelStep` a tier above the table), the player level their health budget is
  sized for. Without density, and an Omen guardian, keep their own level (their own health x multipliers).
