- Invasions (`invasion_core.lua I.displayLevel`): waves, boss and occupiers show the area level they are scaled to.
- Generated areas and dungeons (`areagen.lua`): each monster shows its spawn point's level (`A.levelScale`).
- Base dungeons (`dungeons.lua`) are not level-scaled: a difficulty multiplies health and damage by percents after the
  placement, so their monsters keep their level.

**Level of a scripted boss (O177, beta 2026-10-24: Kaelgor showed "Lv 10182" in its pocket).** The estimate of a world
boss species' experience and health is only meant to rank monsters and is far above any level. Two guards, both
display only (health, loot, pace and monster damage read other values: `MD.levelOf` uses the engine level, which a
display level does not change):
- The estimate is shown at most at the top hunting level, `ChaosMonsterLevelsCore.maxEstimate` = 2200
  (`progression_config.lua` `limits.toLevel`; the test keeps them equal). A level a system passes
  (`Chaos.spawnLevel`, the Infinity Tower's floors, which may be higher) is not clamped.
- The scripted boss spawns pass the level of their fight through `Chaos.createMonsterNamed(..., level)`: pocket boss
  (below), world boss and raid boss (their `minLevel`: 300 and 800), guild boss (`minLevel`), Ascended / uber bosses
  (`def.minLevel`), Trial Warden (`scale.level`, the player's level within the tier). Left to the clamp: dungeon and
  map monsters, nemesis, treasure goblins, the ascension quest guardian, adds and totems (stock monsters, no huge
  estimate).

Tests: `tests/monster_levels_test.lua`.

## Stop request file (`stop_request.lua`, `stop_request_core.lua`, `stop_request_config.lua`)
Windows ends a closed console window after about 5 seconds, too soon for the engine's save, so closing the game server
window of the Windows package could lose progress. The packages' stop scripts now ask the server to stop with a file:
- `stop-server.bat` (Windows package) writes `server\stop.request` while ChaosServer.exe runs, then waits up to 200 s
  for the process to exit before it stops the database, as before.
- `stop-server.sh` (Linux package) writes `server/stop.request` first and waits up to 20 s for the server to take it;
  without an answer (an older server) it removes the file and sends SIGTERM as before. It still touches `run/stop`
  so `start-server.sh` does not start the server again.
- The globalevent `ChaosStopRequest` checks the server folder (the engine's working folder) every `intervalMs`
  (2.5 s). Found: it removes the file, broadcasts `message`, and after `graceMs` (3 s) runs `saveServer()` and
  `Game.setGameState(GAME_STATE_SHUTDOWN)` (every player saved at the kick, a clean exit with code 0, which the start
  scripts take as a stop, not a crash).

Safety: the name is fixed by the config and must be a bare file name (letters, digits, `_`, `-`, `.`; no folder, no
`..`; else `stop.request`), so only a file in the server's own folder counts. Its content is never read. A file that
cannot be removed stops nothing (logged once), so a stuck file never stops every later start. A leftover file is
removed at startup (and by both start scripts) instead of being obeyed. Anyone who can write into the server folder
can stop the server, the same people who can already end its process. Tests: `tests/stop_request_test.lua`.

## Help channel assistant (`helpai.lua`, `helpai_core.lua`, `helpai_config.lua`, `tools/helpai.py`, `tools/patch_help_ai.py`)
Owner, 2026-10-20: "put an AI in the chat's Help tab to answer the players' questions". Ember answers in the Help
channel (channel 7) from the game's own wiki data. It is off until the owner gives it an API key; without one the
Help channel works exactly as before.

**How it works.** The game server never waits on the network; the model is called by a sidecar process, the same
idea as the login-screen services and the remote admin file.
- `tools/patch_help_ai.py` (install step `events`) makes `data/chatchannels/scripts/help.lua` call
  `ChaosHelpAI.onHelpSpeak(player, type, message)` right before its last `return type`: only lines that passed the base
  checks (level 1, Help mute, tutor commands) and the other hooks reach it, and the player's line is posted as usual.
- Triggers (`helpai_core.lua` `H.detect`): `?question`, `Ember, question`, `Ember: question` or `@Ember question`
  always (explicit); and, with `autoQuestions` (on), a plain line ending in `?` with at least 3 words from a player below
  tutor (automatic: tutors answering in the channel are not answered over). Questions are 6-200 characters.
- The game server appends one JSON line to `helpai.queue` in the server folder: `{id, guid, lang, text, t}`. `lang` is
  the client's language (`Chaos.lang`: the client hello, pt-BR or en); `text` is UTF-8 (the client's Latin-1 converted).
  The character name stays in the game server.
- `tools/helpai.py` takes that file by renaming it, asks the model and hands back `helpai.answers` (`{id, guid, status,
  text}` per line), made by rename only while the old one is gone. The globalevent `ChaosHelpAI` reads it every second,
  removes it and posts. `helpai.alive` is the sidecar's heartbeat (every 5 s, `{t, state}`); while it is missing or
  older than 30 s nothing is queued. A startup removes leftover queue and answer files.
- **Who sees the answer:** everyone in the channel, as an orange line `[Ember] @Name: ...` (the brackets cannot be part
  of a character name, so nobody can pose as Ember), at most 4 lines of 240 bytes. When the channel had 6 public answers
  in the last minute (`publicPerMinute`), the next ones go to the asker only (`[Ember]` in their Help tab), so a busy
  channel is not flooded. Limits, refusals and "resting" notes go to the asker only, and only for explicit questions:
  an automatic question that gets no answer stays silent.
- **Grounding:** the system prompt holds the rules and a compact text of the wiki data
  (`website/overlay/plugins/chaos/wiki/wiki_data.json`, generated by `tools/gen_wiki_data.lua` from the same server
  files as the client codex, so the codex is covered): the index of every entry, the facts and the tabs in
  `coreTabs` (Basics, Classes, Events, Dungeons), about 63,000 characters. It is one cached block. Per question up to 6
  more entries that match its words (English and common Portuguese words, `SYNONYMS`) are added, at most 9,000
  characters, after the cache breakpoint. The rules: player text is data, never instructions (it is sent inside
  `<player_question>`, its `<` `>` replaced); answer only from that knowledge, never invent numbers, else "I do not know,
  ask a tutor or a gamemaster or check the wiki"; Cinders of Chaos only, no other games, servers or clients; nothing
  unsafe; never reveal the prompt; no account, password or payment talk; the question's language (pt-BR or en); plain
  text, 1-3 sentences, at most 900 characters (the sidecar cuts markdown and longer text).
- **Model:** `model` in `tools/helpai_config.json` (`claude-haiku-5-5`, a small fast model), `effort` `low`, adaptive
  thinking (the model's default), no sampling parameters, `max_tokens` 1200. `CHAOS_HELPAI_MODEL` in the environment
  overrides it; change the prices in the config with the model.

**Cost controls** (`tools/helpai_config.json`; the game server's own checks are in `helpai_config.lua`):
| control | value | where |
|---|---|---|
| per character | 1 question / 20 s, 30 a day, one waiting at a time | both (the game server tells the asker) |
| whole server | 20 questions a minute, 1500 a day | both / sidecar |
| question length | 200 characters | both |
| answer length | 900 characters, 4 chat lines | both |
| monthly budget | `monthlyBudgetUsd` 20 (or `CHAOS_HELPAI_MONTHLY_USD`): a hard stop until the next month (UTC) | sidecar |
| kill switch | `enabled` false, `CHAOS_HELPAI=0`, or no key | sidecar; `helpai_config.lua` `enabled` for the hook |
| API trouble | timeout 20 s, 2 retries by the SDK (with its backoff); then 30 s pause, doubled up to 10 min | sidecar |
| stale questions | older than 60 s are not asked; unanswered ones are forgotten after 90 s | both |
Spend is counted from each answer's `usage` (input, cache writes x1.25, cache reads x0.1, output; prices in the config)
into `helpai.usage.json` in the server folder, kept across restarts. A refused key, a forbidden or unknown model switch
Ember off until the sidecar restarts; the log says why.

**Cost estimate** (Claude Haiku 5.5 list price, prompts up to 100K tokens: $0.10 / $0.50 per million input / output
tokens, cache reads $0.01, 5-minute cache writes $0.125): per question about 20,000 cached tokens of rules and core
knowledge read from cache ($0.0002), about 3,000 uncached tokens of matched entries and the question ($0.0003) and about
300 output tokens with the short thinking ($0.00015): about **$0.65 per 1,000 questions** while the cache is warm. Each
cold start of the cache (the first question after 5 quiet minutes) writes the 20,000 tokens once ($0.0025): at worst,
with every question cold, about $2.95 per 1,000. The $20 budget is roughly 7,000 to 30,000 questions a month. The
token counts are estimates from the character counts, not measured: check `cr=`/`in=`/`out=` in the log after the first
answers and the month total in `helpai.usage.json`.

**Turning it on (Linux package on the VPS, /opt/chaos-trial):**
```
cd /opt/chaos-trial
python3 -m venv helpai-venv && helpai-venv/bin/pip install anthropic
echo 'CHAOS_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=<your key>' >> chaos.env     # chaos.env stays mode 600; never commit it
./stop-server.sh && ./start-server.sh -d                   # prints "Help channel assistant on"
tail -f logs/helpai.log                                    # "Ember is on: model ..., budget $20.00/month"
```
`start-server.sh` hands the key to the sidecar only and removes it from the environment before the game server starts.
Off: `CHAOS_HELPAI=0` in chaos.env (or remove the key) and restart. systemd install (docs/LAUNCH.md): the optional
`server/deploy/chaos-helpai.service` with the key in its own `/etc/chaos/helpai.env`, so `chaos-server.service` never
reads it. The package ships `server/tools/helpai.py`, `helpai_config.json` and `wiki_data.json`; regenerate the wiki
data (`tools/gen_wiki_data.lua`) and rebuild the package when the game data changes, or Ember answers from the old data.

**Privacy.** The API receives the question text, the language and the matched wiki text; never the character name,
the guid, the account or the IP. The sidecar logs the question id, the outcome, tokens and cost; never names, guids or
accounts. With `logQuestions` true (or `CHAOS_HELPAI_LOG_QUESTIONS=1`) it also logs the question and the answer, cut to
120 characters, for quality review: off by default. The key is read from the environment only
(`CHAOS_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, else `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) and never written or logged. Players' questions go to an outside
service: the privacy policy (docs/legal/) should say so before Ember is switched on for the public.

**Tests:** `tests/helpai_test.lua` (triggers, limits, the flat JSON lines, chat lines, the channel's audience, the
engine file against a mocked engine: nothing queued without the sidecar, a question queued without the name, the answer
public or private, wrong guid dropped, budget and switch) and `tools/helpai_test.py` (config and key, knowledge and
retrieval, the request (model, effort, one cached system prompt, injection-safe question tag), limits, back-off, every
API error class, budget stop, logging without names, `patch_help_ai.py`), with a fake API client: no network.
Also checked by hand against the real SDK (anthropic 1.16.0) talking to a local fake endpoint: request shape (`system`
with the cache breakpoint, `output_config.effort`), 200, 401, 404, 429, 529 and a refused connection map to ok, off,
off, busy, busy, busy. **Not verified:** no real API call (no key here), no live server: the hook in the base
`help.lua`, `sendChannelMessage(7, TALKTYPE_CHANNEL_O, text)` showing an author-less orange line in the client, the
answer quality and the real token counts and cost.

## Remote admin commands (`remote_cmd.lua`, `remote_cmd_core.lua`, `remote_cmd_config.lua`)
Owner, 2026-10-20: full control of the live server from a phone (docs/ADMIN_APP.md). The phone app talks ssh to the VPS
and runs `server/deploy/chaos-ctl.sh`; for the things only the engine can do it appends one line to `remote.cmd` in the
server folder (the engine's working folder), the same idea as the stop request file above.
- The globalevent `ChaosRemoteCmd` checks every `intervalMs` (2.5 s). The file is renamed to `remote.cmd.work` first (a
  writer that appends later makes a new file, nothing is lost), read (at most 8 KB, 20 lines) and removed.
- Lines are a whitelist, nothing else is ever run: `broadcast TEXT` (1-200 characters, a warning message to everyone),
  `kick NAME` (a character name: letters, spaces, `'` and `-`, 3-29 characters; an offline name does nothing), `save`
  (`saveServer()`), `open` and `close` (`Game.setGameState` NORMAL / CLOSED: login open or closed; players online stay).
  `spectate NAME` (same name rule) starts or renews the live view of a character (see "Live spectator"); a renewal is
  not logged. `cast NAME` (same name rule) names the player of the cast port and `caststop` clears it (src-patch 0064;
  an engine without it answers "this engine has no cast port"). Control characters, long lines and every other word are refused and logged.
- The whole admin panel (`chaos/admin`, 179 actions) is reachable too, through two more lines: `catalog ACTOR` writes the
  catalog of the panel for ACTOR's group to `remote.catalog` (JSON, same as the in-game panel gets), and
  `panel RID ACTION|ACTOR|JSON` runs one action (`ChaosAdmin.execute`: group check, parameter validation, audit log) and
  appends `{"rid","ok","message","lines"}` to `remote.result` (restarted above `maxResultBytes`). ACTOR is an admin
  character, online or not: online it is the real player; offline it is a stand-in built from its `players` row
  (`K.virtualActor`: name, group, guid, account, audit log). Either way the action runs with that character's group, so
  `minGroup` limits hold. A stand-in has no body: actions that use the actor's position, teleport, ghost mode, speed or
  conditions answer "this action needs NAME in the game".
  `chaos-ctl.sh catalog|panel` queues the line and waits up to 15 s for the answer (the app's Comandos tab).
- Every command and every refusal is logged as `[ChaosRemoteCmd] ...` in the console log (`chaos-ctl.sh logs`).
- Safety: the file name is a bare name from the config (same rule as the stop request file). A leftover file at startup is
  removed, not obeyed. A file that cannot be renamed runs nothing (logged once). Anyone who can write into the server
  folder can run these five commands, the same people who can already end the process. The folder is not reachable from
  the network. The `panel` line is the strongest: it can do anything the admin panel does, so the folder must stay
  closed to everyone but the server's own user and root.
- Tests: `tests/remote_cmd_test.lua` (core and engine file against a mocked engine, a real file), and
  `server/deploy/chaos_ctl_test.py` for the script that writes the lines. Untested: the engine calls (`Player(name)`,
  `player:remove()`, `Game.setGameState`) have not run on a real server.

## Live spectator (`spectate.lua`, `spectate_core.lua`, `spectate_config.lua`, `tools/spectate_render.py`)
Owner, 2026-10-20 (ROADMAP "Open decisions": a live view of a player in the admin app). Phase 1: the owner watches one
online character from the phone (docs/ADMIN_APP.md "Assistir jogador"), drawn with the real client sprites. Read only:
the player is not told and nothing in the game changes. No engine patch: the snapshot comes from the Lua API.
- **Engine side.** The remote command `spectate NAME` (see "Remote admin commands") starts a watch that lasts
  `watchSeconds` (20 s); the same name again only renews it, another name replaces it (one watch at a time). While a
  watch runs, the globalevent `ChaosSpectate` (every `intervalMs`, 1 s) writes `remote.spectate` in the server folder,
  atomically (`.tmp` then rename): JSON `{v, watch, t, online, name, level, voc, hp, maxhp, mp, maxmp, cap, soul,
  stamina, skull, pos, x0, y0, w, h, tiles, creatures}`. The area is the 15 x 11 client view plus a margin for tall
  things (`area`: 8 left, 9 right, 6 up, 7 down: 18 x 14 tiles) on the character's floor only. Each tile lists client
  item ids in draw order (ground, top items, down items oldest first; stackables, fluid containers and splashes as
  `[id, subtype]`; at most `maxItemsPerTile`, the newest kept). Each creature: tile, name, outfit (look type or item
  look, head / body / legs / feet, addons, mount), direction, health %, skull, kind, and `me` for the watched one;
  invisible creatures and players in ghost mode are left out (the watched character always shows); at most
  `maxCreatures`. An offline name writes `{watch, online:false}`.
- **VPS side.** `chaos-ctl.sh spectate NAME` checks the name (letters, single spaces, `'` and `-`, 3-29), takes a lock
  (another view running: `busy`, exit 75), keeps at most one view every 0.8 s, queues `spectate NAME` when the name
  changed or 5 s passed, waits up to 8 s for a `remote.spectate` of that name at most 2 s old, then runs
  `tools/spectate_render.py render` under `timeout 25`. The renderer reads the client pair with
  `client/tools/sprites/datspr.py`, draws the 15 x 11 view around the character in the client's order (ground, bottom,
  common items, creatures, top items, with elevation; outfits with colours, addons and mounts; health bars and names
  in the client's colours) and prints one JSON line: `{ok, name, level, voc, hp, maxhp, mp, maxmp, cap, soul, pos, age,
  w, h, png}` (480 x 352, base64, 256 colours). Errors: `{"ok":false,"error":"offline" | "stale" | "bad-snapshot" |
  "no-pair" | "busy" | "no-answer" | "timeout","message"}`. The name is passed as one argument everywhere, never
  through a shell string. The dat index (about a second to parse a real dat) is cached in
  `CHAOS_SPECTATE_STATE/dat-index.json` (`/var/lib/chaos/spectate`, mode 0700), rebuilt when the dat changes.
- **The pair.** The renderer reads `CHAOS_SPECTATE_PAIR` (default `$CHAOS_ROOT/pair`, `/opt/chaos/pair`: the same
  folder as the site's `CHAOS_SPRITE_PAIR`). `chaos-ctl.sh spectate-pair fetch` (the app: Baixar sprites) fetches the
  branch `CHAOS_PAIR_BRANCH` (`windows-assets`) shallow and without other files' contents, reads
  `things/things-1098.tar.xz.part*` and `SHA256SUMS.parts`, checks every part's sum, unpacks only the regular files
  `Tibia.dat` and `Tibia.spr` (no links, no paths) into `pair.new` and swaps it in; then builds the index. It runs in
  the background (log `CHAOS_SPECTATE_LOG`, `/var/log/chaos/spectate-pair.log`; `spectate-pair log`), one at a time,
  and needs about 2.3 GB of free disk while it runs. `spectate-pair status` prints `branch=`, `fetching=`, `pair=`,
  `dat_md5=` and `index=`. The VPS needs `python3-numpy` and `python3-pil`.
- **App.** Comandos > Ações rápidas > Assistir jogador (`android/.../SpectateCard.java`): name, Ao vivo / Foto / Parar.
  Foto asks for one picture (phase 1), scaled without smoothing, with name, level, vocation, health, mana and position
  under it. Ao vivo is phase 2, below.
- **Draws stock art.** Unlike the website (which never shows stock sprites), the view draws everything the pair has:
  it is private to the owner's phone.
- Tests: `tests/spectate_test.lua` (core and engine file against a mocked engine: names, watch, tile order, limits,
  creatures, ghosts, snapshot, JSON shape, atomic write), `tests/remote_cmd_test.lua` (the `spectate` line),
  `tools/spectate_render_test.py` (a synthetic pair: index cache, snapshot checks, draw order, elevation, outfits,
  mounts, PNG, the pair archive with traversal, links and wrong sums), `server/deploy/chaos_ctl_test.py` (refusals,
  quoting, lock, rate limit, renewal, no answer, pair status). Untested: the engine calls on a real server, a real
  pair (pair 37's spr is over 1 GiB), the fetch from `windows-assets`, the app on a phone.

**Phase 2: the live cast (src-patch 0064, `tools/cast_relay.py`, `chaos-ctl.sh cast NAME`).** Owner, 2026-10-23: "Eu
quero ver o gameplay em tempo real. Faça o patch na engine." The phone shows the game as the player sees it, moving.
- **Engine (src-patch 0064).** `config.lua` keys: `castPort` (default 0: off), `castMaxSpectators` (3, 1-8),
  `castQueueKb` (1024). With a port the engine listens on 127.0.0.1 only, on its own thread
  (`src/chaoscastserver.cpp`). `Game.setCastTarget(name)` names the watched player ("" clears it);
  `Game.getCastTarget()` returns the name, the spectators and whether the port is open. `ProtocolGame::writeToOutputBuffer`
  hands the watched player's messages to the port. `src/chaoscast.h` keeps only the game view (map, tiles, creatures,
  moves, effects, missiles, animated text, health, light, the player's stats, speech on screen, the typed numbers).
  Private and channel messages, VIP, modal windows, store, market, trade, containers, inventory, extended opcodes and
  pings never leave the engine. A frame is u16 length (little endian) + one message body, plain. A new spectator gets a
  hello frame (opcode 0x00, "CAST", version 1, player id, client marker, item / text flags, aware range, name), then
  the view a login sends (`Player::writeCastView`), then the live messages. The game thread never waits: a spectator
  more than `castQueueKb` behind is dropped. Everyone is dropped when the target changes, logs out or reconnects.
- **Enable.** `install_all.py` step `castport` (`tools/patch_cast_port.py`) sets `castPort = 7179`, then restart the
  server. `chaos-ctl.sh` reads the port from `config.lua` (or `CHAOS_CAST_PORT` in `/etc/chaos/ctl.conf`).
- **Relay.** `tools/cast_relay.py --port N --dat --spr [--otb] [--name] [--max-seconds]` reads the port and keeps the
  world our client would keep (the same parse rules: floors, stack order, our item attributes, typed numbers, wings /
  aura / shader). It writes JSON lines on stdout: `wait`, `hello`, `spr` (a sprite sheet PNG, once per run, at most
  600), `full`, `d` (changes, at most about 20 a second), `hb`, `resync`, `end`. The docstring has the format. Broken
  input never crashes it: a broken frame starts the view again. It stops when stdin closes, stdout breaks or after
  `--max-seconds`.
- **VPS.** `chaos-ctl.sh cast NAME` checks the name (same rule), the port (`cast-off`) and the pair (`no-pair`),
  takes a lock (`busy`, exit 75), queues `cast NAME` and runs the relay for at most 30 minutes. On exit it queues
  `caststop`. Errors are `{"ok":false,"error",...}` lines like `spectate`.
- **App.** Ao vivo runs `chaos-ctl.sh cast NAME` on one ssh channel (`Ssh.stream`) and `CastView.java` draws the lines
  at about 30 frames a second: the 15 x 11 tiles of the player's floor with item patterns and animation, elevation,
  creatures walking between tiles with their walking frames, effects, missiles, health bars, names, numbers and
  speech, scaled without smoothing. The camera follows the player's steps. Level, health and mana show under it. It
  stops on Parar, on leaving the tab or the app, on an error and after 30 minutes. Phase 3 (below) adds the other
  floors and the light. Not drawn: the client's own interface.
- Tests: `tools/chaoscast_test.cpp` (the message whitelist, frames, hello bytes; CI), `tools/cast_relay_test.py`
  (synthetic frames for every opcode, both client markers, sheets, the loop with a local port, a fuzz; CI),
  `tests/remote_cmd_test.lua` (`cast`, `caststop`), `server/deploy/chaos_ctl_test.py` (cast refusals, lock, quoting),
  `tools/patch_cast_port_test.py`. The patched engine compiles (chain 0001-0064). The app compiles.
  Live run (2026-10-23, the sanitizer build, the real pair, 3 load test bots walking, talking and hunting): the port
  listened on 127.0.0.1 only, `cast Loadbot Aaa` through `remote.cmd`, and in 45 s the relay wrote hello, 170 sheets,
  the full view and 76 changes (walks, effects, numbers, speech) with no resync and no sanitizer report. The full view
  drawn from those lines matched the game. Untested: the app on a phone, `chaos-ctl.sh cast` on the VPS.

**Phase 3: the other floors and the light (O152, `cast_relay.py` protocol 3, `CastView.java`, `CastMath.java`).**
Owner, 2026-10-23, same request as phase 2: the view should be what the client shows. No engine change: src-patch 0064
already mirrors the floors (map, `0x4B`, floor changes), world light (`0x82`), creature light (`0x8D`), magic effects
(`0x83`) and distance missiles (`0x85`); phase 2 drew effects and missiles of the camera floor only and dropped the rest.
- **Version.** The hello line carries `"v":3` (phase 2 had no `v`, read as 2). Every addition is a new key or a new
  field after the old ones; `tiles`, `fx`, `mi` and `cr` keep their meaning (the camera floor). An older app ignores the
  new keys and shows the camera floor as before; a newer app on an older relay (no `v`, no `fl`) draws one floor, unlit.
- **Floors the client draws.** `World.floors()` = `[first, last]`: `last` is 7 above ground (the camera floor + 2
  underground, at most 15); `first` is 0 above ground (camera - 2 underground), raised for every floor a roof or
  ceiling closes over the camera. The rule is the client's `calcFirstVisibleFloor` as remembered: for the camera tile
  and the open (look-possible, nothing that blocks a missile) tiles north, south, east and west of it, walk up one floor
  at a time; the tile straight above and the tile one east and one south per floor (the geometric cover) end the walk
  when a tile limits the view (`limitsFloorsView`: a ground, or for a tile seen from an open one also a bottom item such
  as a wall; things with the don't-hide flag never do). The base client tree is not in the repo, so this is an
  approximation of the real rule; a wrong floor shows as a roof drawn or hidden by mistake.
- **Lines.** `full` has `fl` and `ft`; `d` has `fl` when the range changed, `fc` (floors that came into view whole:
  the app drops their old tiles first) and `ft`. `ft` is a list of `[z, x, y, under, over, elevation]` (the tile format
  of `tiles` with the floor first; an empty tile clears the app's). Only floors in `fl` and tiles in the window the app
  can show (floor f is drawn `camera z - f` tiles up and left, so tile x sits at cell x - (camera z - f)) are sent;
  a change on a hidden floor is not sent, the floor comes back whole (`fc`) when it is shown again. `fxf` is
  `[x, y, sheet key, pattern, z]` and `mif` `[fx, fy, tx, ty, key, pattern, ms, z]` for floors other than the camera's
  (dropped when their floor is not drawn). Numbers and speech stay on the camera floor, as in the client.
- **Light data.** The `spr` line of an item sheet has `gr` (a ground) and `lt` `[intensity, colour]` when the dat thing
  shines; effect and missile sheets have `lt` likewise; a creature in `cr` has `lt` when its light is on (the key is
  absent when off); the `light` key (`[intensity, colour]`) was already in phase 2. Item lights need no tile change:
  the app looks the sheet of each drawn entry up.
- **App.** `CastView.java` keeps tiles of every floor, draws the floors from the lowest to the highest (a floor above
  over the ones under it, creatures, effects and missiles of a floor in that floor's pass; health bars and names for the
  camera floor only), skips the cells a ground on a floor above covers (the client does this too, and it keeps 8 floors
  cheap), and then lights the frame as the client's light view does: a quarter-size bitmap filled with the ambient
  light (the world light's colour at intensity / 255; underground 0, the sun does not reach), a round glow added for
  every source (creatures, item entries of the drawn floors, effects and missiles that shine; radius intensity x 32 px
  capped at 8 tiles, brighter the stronger), multiplied over the frame and smoothed up. The player gets a light of 2 of
  his own in the dark (world light under 64) and underground, as the client does. Full daylight (every channel of the
  ambient at 94% or more) draws nothing. `CastMath.java` holds the arithmetic (cells of other floors, 8-bit colours, the
  light numbers) without Android classes.
- Tests: `cast_relay_test.py` now also covers the visible-floor rule (open sky, roof above, geometric roof, a roof that
  is not above, don't-hide ground, wall, open and blocked neighbour tiles, underground, the lowest floor), the full and
  delta lines of other floors (window, empty tile, roof appears and goes, hidden floor silent, whole floors again with
  `fc`), effects and missiles on other floors (and their cap, and dropped when hidden), creature, item and effect light,
  the `v` field. The app compiles against the Android API jar with `javac` (there is no Android SDK on the build
  machine, so no gradle build was run); `CastMath` was run on a JVM. Untested: the drawing itself (the floors, the
  light overlay and its speed) on any device, the cover rule against the real client, a live run of the new lines on a
  server.

**Black Ao vivo view (O265, owner 2026-10-26).** In Comandos > Ações rápidas > Assistir jogador > Ao vivo only names and
health bars showed; ground, items and outfits were black. The sprites were on the VPS (Sprites na VPS showed the pair).
- **Root cause (by reading; no phone or live server here).** `CastView.applyLight` multiplied the light view over the
  whole frame and drew names and bars after it. The game's own darkness is nearly black: `Game::checkLight` (day/night
  cycle) sends world light 40 of 255 at night, and `CastMath.ambient` returned 0 on every underground floor (hunts are
  mostly underground), so only a 2-tile glow around the player was lit. The names and bars were the only things not
  darkened, which is exactly the report. Candidates read and cleared: sheet field names (`key`, `png`, `cw`, `ch`, `ax`,
  `ay`, `np`, `nf`, `fd`, `ni`, `nw`, `el`, `gr`, `lt`) match between `cast_relay.py` and `CastView.sheet`; tile entries
  `[key, pattern, lift]` and tiles `[x, y, under, over, elev]` match; sheets go out before the `full` line; `Ssh.stream`
  takes lines up to 8 MiB; the relay test with the synthetic pair draws every sheet. A second silent path made the same
  picture: a sheet that failed to draw (`Sheets.need` swallowed the exception) or to decode (`BitmapFactory` null)
  left no trace, and `CastView.creature` draws the name and bar even without a body sheet.
- **Fix.** `CastMath.ambient(..., minimum)` and `READABLE` (104 of 255): the map is never darker than about 40% by
  default; the button Luz clara / Luz do jogo switches to the game's real darkness (a state line then says "Escuro como
  no jogo"). Item lights (torches, lamps) now add their glow; they were described here but not drawn. `Sheets.need`
  returns `{"t":"sprerr","key","why"}` (why: `none`, `limit` or the error) instead of nothing; the app counts those and
  the sheets it cannot decode and shows "Sprites: N sprite(s) não vieram (chave: motivo)", or "Nenhum sprite chegou da
  VPS" when a map has no sheet at all.
- Tests: `cast_relay_test.py` `test_black_view_is_not_silent` (PIL failure gives `sprerr` lines, the full line still
  goes out), `android/app/src/test/java/.../CastMathTest.java` (plain JVM: night and caves are dark, the minimum lifts
  them, day untouched). The app classes were compiled with `javac` against the Android API jar (only the generated `R`
  is missing there). Not run on a phone or against a live relay: if the view is still black, the state line now says
  why.

**chaos-ctl.sh settings file (`/etc/chaos/ctl.conf`).** Owner, 2026-10-20: the app showed "service not found, codigo 5"
on the beta VPS. The kit there runs from `/opt/chaos-trial` (`tools/linux/server/start-server.sh`) with no systemd
unit, and `systemctl` exits 5 for a unit that does not exist. Setting `CHAOS_UNIT` in the environment never helped: the
script re-runs itself with `sudo -n`, which drops the environment.
- The script now reads `/etc/chaos/ctl.conf` first. Keys: `CHAOS_UNIT`, `CHAOS_ROOT`, `CHAOS_SERVER_DIR`, `CHAOS_REPO`,
  `CHAOS_ENV`, `CHAOS_LOG`, `CHAOS_UPDATE_LOG`, `CHAOS_ADMIN_USER`, `CHAOS_PID_FILE`, `CHAOS_DB_SOCKET`, `CHAOS_MYSQL`,
  `CHAOS_BACKUP_DIR` (and the publish-update keys below). Order: the environment, then the file, then the default.
- Safety: the file is parsed, never sourced. Plain `KEY=VALUE` lines, optional quotes, `#` comments. A value may only
  hold `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ / @ : + -`. Other keys and values are skipped with a warning. The whole file is ignored unless
  it is a plain file owned by root (or by the user running the script) and not writable by group or others.
  `CHAOS_CTL_CONF` names another file, honoured only outside sudo (tests).
- Missing unit: `start`, `stop` and `restart` check `LoadState` first. `not-found` exits 5 with
  `chaos-ctl: unit-not-found: ...` naming `CHAOS_UNIT` and the file. `status` adds `unit=`, `unit_state=` and `pid=`.
- Database client: `CHAOS_MYSQL`, else `mysql`, else `mariadb`, else `CHAOS_ROOT/mariadb/bin/mariadb` (the kit's).
  None found: exit 127 with `chaos-ctl: mysql-not-found: ...`; `status` then says `players=?`. `CHAOS_DB_SOCKET` (in
  ctl.conf or the env file) connects over that socket instead of host and port; `backup.sh` honours it too and uses
  `mariadb-dump` when there is no `mysqldump`. The kit's game user is `'chaos'@'127.0.0.1'`, so on the kit keep TCP
  (`CHAOS_DB_PORT=3307` in its `chaos.env`) and leave the socket empty.
- `errors [N] [all]`: the console log has no time stamps, so errors are grouped by server start (the kit's
  `Starting the game server (DATE)` line, else the engine's `Loading config`; the newest start without a date takes the
  unit's start time). Default: only the current start, so old errors (a database shutdown days ago) no longer look
  current. Identical entries are counted once (`56x ...`, a leading time stamp kept apart as `[stamp]`), a Lua error
  joins its next two lines. Output: `@run DATE [current]`, the entries, `@older K` (earlier starts with errors).
  `status errors=` counts the error lines of the current start. Tested with mawk, gawk and busybox awk.
- `vps [info]`, `vps upgrade`, `vps upgrade-log [N]`, `vps reboot MINUTES`, `vps reboot-cancel` (2026-10-22): the
  machine. `info`: key=value lines (host, os, kernel, uptime, load, cpus, memory, disk of /, pending packages from
  `apt-get -s upgrade` and how many of them are `php*`, the `php*-fpm` or `libapache2-mod-php*` package and version, reboot_required from /run/reboot-required, reboot_at of a planned shutdown). `upgrade`:
  `apt-get update` then `upgrade` with `--force-confold` (config files kept), detached, log `CHAOS_VPS_LOG`
  (/var/log/chaos/vps-upgrade.log), one at a time. `reboot`: a broadcast, a save (SIGUSR1 to the engine), then
  `shutdown -r +MINUTES` (1 to 60); `reboot-cancel`: `shutdown -c` and a broadcast.
- `services`, `service NAME start|stop|restart`, `service-log NAME [N]` (2026-10-22): the `chaos-*` units (and
  `CHAOS_UNIT`) and the web server units `apache2`, `nginx`, `php*-fpm` (restart them after a PHP update). NAME must
  be one of those, `chaos-[a-z0-9-]+` with an optional `.service` / `.timer`, and a loaded unit; nothing else is
  started or stopped. `service-log` tails the unit's `StandardOutput=append:` file, else its journal.
- `errors clear`: appends `[chaos-ctl] list cleared by the owner DATE` to the log. `errors` and `status errors=` count
  only what comes after the newest such line (also with `all`). Nothing in the log is deleted; `logs` and the tester
  report still read every line. The marker has no word the error filters match. Admin app: Logs > Erros > Limpar lista.
- `publish-update TAG [--version N] [--min-package N]` and `publish-log [N]` (2026-10-20): runs
  `server/deploy/publish_client_update.sh TAG` in the background (log `CHAOS_PUBLISH_LOG`,
  `/var/log/chaos/publish-update.log`). It publishes the release's `CindersOfChaos-Client-Windows.zip` as the signed
  client update in `CHAOS_SITE_DIR/updates/live` with the key `CHAOS_UPDATE_KEY` (docs/LAUNCH.md "Publishing a client
  update": the owner's commands, the version and min_package rules). More ctl.conf keys, passed on to that script:
  `CHAOS_SITE_DIR`, `CHAOS_UPDATE_KEY`, `CHAOS_UPDATE_PUBLIC`, `CHAOS_UPDATE_REPO`, `CHAOS_UPDATE_URL`,
  `CHAOS_WORK_DIR`, plus `CHAOS_PUBLISH_LOG`; `CHAOS_ENV` (the env file) is passed too. Release tags only: the admin
  user cannot hand the script a file of its own to sign. **Since client build 13 the update files are encrypted**
  (client/BASE.md "Encrypted updates"): the script needs the client guard key `CHAOS_CLIENT_KEY`, read from the
  `CHAOS_CLIENT_KEY=` line of `/etc/chaos/chaos.env` (the game server's own; never printed), opens a packed package's
  `chaos.pack` with it and encrypts every blob; without it nothing is published, and min_package must be 13 or more.
  Tests: `chaos_ctl_test.py` (refusals, the arguments and settings reaching a stub) and `publish_client_update_test.py`
  (the real script on synthetic loose and packed packages with throwaway keys: the manifest verifies, every blob is
  ciphertext that decrypts to its signed content, version and min_package, unsafe zips, key mismatches, a missing or
  wrong client key, a development pack and a build-12 package refused, old plain blobs removed, the rotation key
  picked, the web server check against a local HTTP server).
- Kit update from GitHub (owner, 2026-10-21: "fetch GitHub and, if newer, apply the update and restart; also the client
  and the site's downloads"): `update-check`, `update-apply [--no-client] [--no-downloads] [--no-site]`,
  `update-status`, `update-rollback`, `update-downloads [--force]` (O165: only step 9, the site's `dl/` packages, when
  the release is newer than `downloads.json` or with `--force`; no stop, no restart, no signed update) run
  `server/deploy/chaos_kit_update.sh` (check / apply / downloads / rollback; apply and
  rollback in the background into `update-log`, one at a time by a lock in `CHAOS_KIT_STATE`). On the kit
  (`CHAOS_KIT_DIR`, or `CHAOS_ROOT` holding `start-server.sh`) the old `update TAG` is refused and `rollback now` runs
  `update-rollback`. Order (O198, "Faster server update"): backup with the server up, `install_all.py --no-sql` on a copy
  of the server folder while the game runs, stop, swap the folders, start (the kit's MariaDB runs inside the unit),
  `install_all.py --only sql`, restart, `Server Online` within `CHAOS_BOOT_TIMEOUT`, else an automatic rollback (the old
  folder renamed back; without a swap: engine `tfs.antes-N`, `config.lua` and `data/` from the backup's archive, previous
  commit). The
  XP rates survive `install_all.py` (`server/deploy/chaos_config_rates.py save` / `restore`: the `experienceStages`
  table and `rateExp`, `rateSkill`, `rateLoot`, `rateMagic`, `rateSpawn`). Then the client update, the client
  downloads of the site (`CHAOS_DL_DIR`: `.prev`, `.sha256`, `downloads.json` read by the downloads page) and
  `website/install_site.sh`. Details: docs/ADMIN_APP.md "Atualizar servidor", docs/LAUNCH.md "Updating the kit server".
  New ctl.conf keys: `CHAOS_KIT_DIR`, `CHAOS_UPDATE_BRANCH` (main), `CHAOS_RELEASE_REPO`, `CHAOS_KIT_STATE`,
  `CHAOS_BOOT_TIMEOUT`, `CHAOS_STAGING`, `CHAOS_CACHE_DIR`, `CHAOS_DL_DIR`, `CHAOS_SITE_ENV`, `CHAOS_SITE_LOG`. With `CHAOS_KIT_DIR` set, `CHAOS_ROOT`,
  `CHAOS_ENV` and `CHAOS_LOG` default to the kit's (`KIT`, `KIT/chaos.env`, `KIT/logs/server.log`).
- Frequent commands (2026-10-21): `xp-rate [show | set N | reset] [restart]` (the release's stages x N, 1..100, backup
  `config.lua.before-xp-<time>`), `backups` (the newest dumps and data archives), `site-install` / `site-log`, `health`
  (unit, engine, database, web units, disk, memory, cleanup size), `cleanup [--yes]` (a day old update and publish work
  folders and `srvNN` folders in `CHAOS_WORK_DIR`, `tfs.antes-*` beyond the newest 2, `config.lua.before-*` beyond the
  newest 5), `account-create NAME` / `account-password NAME` (the password on stdin, a PBKDF2 hash with config.lua's
  `passwordHashIterations`, the SQL to the client on stdin: never on a command line), `gm-logs [N] [PLAYER]` (the base
  server's `data/logs/<name> commands.log`, newest first, a link out of the folder is not read; the admin panel's
  `chaos_admin_log` rows). Coins and groups stay in the in-game panel (`store.give_coins`, `players.set_group`). Tests:
  `chaos_ctl_test.py`, `chaos_kit_update_test.py`.
- `players` prints the class name (`VOCATIONS` in the script: every id of `docs/CLASSES.md`, 0 None; the retired 2, 6 and
  9 print `vocation N`); `vocations` lists the map. The test checks it against `docs/CLASSES.md` and
  `server/data/XML/chaos_vocations*.xml`.
- Save and backup: with a live engine pid in `CHAOS_PID_FILE` (default `CHAOS_ROOT/run/server.pid`, written by the
  kit's `start-server.sh`; the process must be named `tfs`), `save` sends SIGUSR1 to that pid and `backup` passes
  `--save-pid`. Otherwise `systemctl kill --kill-who=main`. Under the kit's unit the main process is `start-server.sh`,
  and SIGUSR1 would end it.
- Kit layout: `server/deploy/chaos-trial-server.service` (install as `/etc/systemd/system/chaos-server.service`, set
  `User=` to the owner of `/opt/chaos-trial`) and `server/deploy/ctl.conf.trial.example` (copy to `/etc/chaos/ctl.conf`,
  mode 644, owner root). Stop a run started by hand (`./stop-server.sh`) before enabling the unit.
- Tests: `chaos_ctl_test.py` (file keys, environment first, unsafe lines never run, group-writable file ignored, not
  under sudo, missing unit, missing client, socket, engine pid, the errors report, the class names). Not verified: the
  unit and the kit's database client on the real VPS.

## Respawn near players (engine patch 0041, config `spawnNearPlayers`, `spawnMinPlayerDistance`)
Owner, 2026-10-16: monsters must respawn even with players nearby. The stock engine skipped a spawn block while a
player could see its spot (`Spawn::findPlayer`, same floor, the client's view) and started its timer again, so a busy
hunt never refilled; only a boss with `isIgnoringSpawnBlock` came back in view.

**The rule** (`spawnNearPlayers = true`, the engine default): with a player in view a block still respawns when
- its tile has a ground, no creature (a ghost staff character counts), no blocking item and no protection zone. The
  spawn places a monster forced (on its exact spot, over anything), so the engine checks this itself now;
- no player the monsters see (`PlayerFlag_IgnoredByMonsters` excepted) is closer than `spawnMinPlayerDistance` sqm
  (default 2: never on a tile next to a player; the larger of dx and dy, same floor; 0 or 1: only the tile itself; at
  most 7).

A respawn a player sees shows the teleport effect (`CONST_ME_TELEPORT`), so it never pops up silently. When the tile
is taken or a player is too close the stock rule holds for that check: only an `isIgnoringSpawnBlock` boss spawns
(silently, as before) and the timer starts again. Startup spawns are unchanged. `spawnNearPlayers = false` is the
stock engine. `tools/prod_config.py` writes both keys (`--spawn-near-players yes|no`, `--spawn-min-distance N`;
without them the values in config.lua are kept, true and 2 on a first run); `tools/prod_config_test.py` (CI).

**Cost.** The extra work is one small spectator search (the distance box) per block whose spot a player sees, at its
check; blocks without a player in view cost what they did. The real cost is more monsters: spawn checks now succeed in
busy areas, so those stay full while hunted (more monsters alive, thinking, pathing and sending packets near players).
The capacity model of "Spawn density and respawn" loses its 1.25 view divisor: about +25% respawn where players
hunt, more with the dynamic respawn (4 hunters: 50% of the spawntime, now also in view). Watch the game loop
(`slowTaskLogMs`) on a full server; `spawnMinPlayerDistance` up or `spawnNearPlayers = false` brings it back.

**Our spawn systems** (checked 2026-10-16):
- `onSpawn` callbacks (`monster_levels.lua`, tiers, archetypes, bounty, bestiary, boss mechanics, ...) run as before:
  the tile and distance check comes before the monster is made, so a refused spot runs no Lua. Level-scaled monsters
  (`late_game.py`, `tools/tune_monsters.py`) roll their level at creation as before.
- `patch_base_spawns.py` output: entries on blocking tiles were moved and none is in a PZ or a house, so every entry
  qualifies. Its fill blocks of 3 refill while hunted now.
- Dynamic respawn (`respawn.lua`, patch 0022/0027): unchanged; its percent now also applies in view.
- Display monsters of the teleport hall: their one-tile cells are not PZ and closed, so a killed display comes back
  after `displaySpawntime` with the effect once nobody stands next to the cell (before: only when the hall was
  empty). `HT.isDisplaySpot` in `onSpawn` sees the same spot as before.
- Rifts, invasions, the tower, trials and pocket bosses use `Game.createMonster`: not affected.
- Generated areas (`areagen.lua`) respawn their points in Lua with the same rule: in view, a point fills when
  `configKeys.SPAWN_NEAR_PLAYERS` is on, its tile is free (ground, no creature, no blocking item, no PZ) and no player
  is within `SPAWN_MIN_PLAYER_DISTANCE` - 1 sqm (+2 for a point of several monsters, which land up to 2 sqm away),
  never with the forced placement, with the teleport effect. Without the keys (an engine without 0041) or with the
  option off: the old rule (the timer starts again). Tests: `tests/areagen_test.lua`.
- Base dungeons (map spawns in the dungeon box): a spot the party left out of view respawned before too; now
  a spot in view also comes back after its spawntime (60-120 s). The kill counter never goes back, so a slow party
  may need a few more kills for 85%.
- Lair bosses (map spawns, `bossspawns_config.lua` rule `timer`) now come back after their spawntime with a party in
  the lair, not only once it is empty.

Needs a live check: a hunt refilling in view with the effect, no spawn next to a player or on a player / summon /
box, the teleport hall's displays, a lair boss camp, and the game loop on a busy server.

## PZ guard (`pz_guard_core.lua`, installed by `chaos_constants.lua`)
Scripted damage never lands on a player in a protection zone. The engine's own combat skips PZ (a monster never
targets a player there, area attacks skip PZ tiles), but `doTargetCombat` / `doTargetCombatHealth` from a script hit
whoever they are given. `chaos_constants.lua` wraps both globals once, before any system keeps a local copy: damage (a
negative amount, any type but healing) to a player on a PZ tile is dropped. Passed: healing and mana gain, a creature
hurting itself (a self cost), a caster with `PlayerFlag_IgnoreProtectionZone`. `combatlog.lua` wraps the guarded
function, so its log keeps working.
Boss mechanics leave PZ out on their own too: an auto-attached arena has no PZ tile, a player in PZ gets no cast bar,
no mark and no hit. Owner's bug (2026-10-16): the display Mirecoil Wyrm (level 1880-1920) in its closed cell of the
Cinderhold teleport room auto-attached its light profile (`boss_mechanics.lua`: every monster with a profile gets one,
arena = a radius 8 box round its spawn). The box took in the PZ carpet, and Mire Spit (20% of max health through
`doTargetCombat`) killed a level 8 player there (58 earth).
Tests: `tests/pz_guard_test.lua` (the guard, its install, and static checks over every Chaos script: a load-time copy
of the combat functions comes after `chaos_constants.lua`; direct `addHealth(-x)` only in reviewed places),
`tests/boss_mechanics_test.lua` (the display wyrm beside a PZ carpet).

## Name plates and titles (`nameplate.lua`, `nameplate_core.lua`, `titles.lua`, client `game_nameplate`, base patch 0022)

Over every player the client draws three lines, like a name plate: the **active title** (coloured by where it comes from),
the **guild** in braces (`{Ashen Covenant}`), and the **name** in gold on a small framed plate. A line that has nothing to
show is left out (no title, no guild). The health bar stays where the client always draws it, right under the name, so
players read it in the same place as on monsters; the plate is lifted 2 px so the frame does not touch the bar. Monsters
and NPCs keep the normal look. Extended opcode 248 (`ChaosOpcodes.nameplate`), `sql/chaos_nameplate.sql` (also created at
startup).

- **Titles** come from a registry: `ChaosTitles.register(source, fn)`, `fn(player)` returns the titles the player holds
  now (`{text, key?, color?, at?, frame?, priority?}`; see the head of `titles.lua`). Registering a source again replaces
  it. Sources today: `staff` (group: Tutor, Senior Tutor, Game Master, Community Manager, Administrator; red, gold
  frame, always listed first), `leaderboard` (weekly top 3, `ChaosLeaderboard.titlesOf`; gold), `champion` (Siege
  Champions while the guild holds it, `ChaosSiege.champions`; orange, crimson frame), `season` (season title rewards,
  `ChaosSeason.titlesOf`; violet), `streak` (login-streak milestone title, `ChaosDaily`; green); achievements register
  `achievement` (teal) from `achievements.lua`; arena titles have a colour (steel blue) waiting. Each source reads the
  other system's tables at call time and returns nothing while that system is not loaded, so `leaderboard.lua` and the
  rest were not edited (the leaderboard's look-text title stays).
- **Active title**: the one picked with the Achievements window (prefix and case do not matter), stored per character in
  `chaos_player_titles`; otherwise staff titles first, then the most recently earned. the Achievements window lists, No title in the Achievements window hides,
  `the Achievements window auto` goes back to the default. A picked title that is gone falls back to the default.
- **Frames**: `default` (blackened iron with ember studs) for everyone, `gold` while a staff title is active, `crimson`
  for Siege Champions, plus `violet` and `frost` unused yet. `ChaosTitles.registerFrame(source, fn)` lets the store or
  seasons hand out a cosmetic frame (`fn(player)` -> frame id), which wins over the title's frame. The images are
  16x15 9-slices from `client/tools/gen_nameplate_art.py`.
- **Traffic**: plain text, one line per player: `cid|title|RRGGBB|guild|frame` (about 40 bytes). Sent to everyone who
  sees the player (`Game.getSpectators`, all floors) at login, and the plates around to the player who logs in; the
  client asks `q|id,id,...` (batched every 250 ms, at most 40 ids) for players that appear without a plate or with one
  older than 60 s, and asks again (3 s, 4 tries) when no answer came. Every 5 s the server rebuilds the plates of the
  online players and sends only the ones that changed (new or lost title, guild joined or left, frame), so systems that
  grant titles need no hook; `ChaosNameplate.refresh(player)` sends at once.
- **Guild**: the name from the engine (`player:getGuild()`); the rank stays in the look text (the engine already says
  "He is Leader of the ..."). The engine's emblems and war colours are untouched; the guild line turns red-orange for a
  war enemy (red emblem).
- **Client**: patch `client/base-patches/0022-chaos-nameplate.patch` adds `Creature:setNameplate(guild, font, guildColor,
  nameColor, frameImage, border)` to `drawInformation` (the title line is the engine's own `setTitle`; 9 textured quads
  and one text more per player, nothing per frame in Lua). A client without the patch shows title and guild as one block
  above the name, without the frame. **The Windows client must be rebuilt with patch 0022.**

**Tests:** `server/tests/nameplate_test.lua` (title order, pick and find, colours and frames, wire format, queries, the
registry with mocked leaderboard / siege / season / login-streak tables) and `game_nameplate/nameplatemath_test.lua`
(parsing, batching, retries). Checked in game on the test server with two clients: all three lines (staff
"Administrator", guild, gold frame), a player without a title, a leaderboard title appearing live within 5 s, the guild
line disappearing live after leaving the guild, the Achievements window list / switch (Bossbane, Siege Champions with the crimson frame)
/ none / auto, the choice kept after a relog, monsters unchanged. Not checked: 30 players on screen (the drawing cost is a
few quads per player), war colours (no guild war on the test server).

## Beastmaster companion (O306, 2026-10-29; `beastmaster.lua`, `classes.lua`, `companion_balance_config.lua`)

Tester report (Beastmaster near level 400): the wolf was 4% of the damage, died in 3 hits and 5 s of 2 monsters of the hunting level,
died again right after Wild Bond, and was shown at level 12 or 300.

* **Level bug, root cause.** The monster-level callback (`monster_levels.lua`, `onSpawn`) runs when the monster is created,
  before Wild Bond binds it to its owner, so it never sees a player's summon. It gave the War Wolf the level of a wild War
  Wolf (the bounty pool's 12), or, when the wolf stood in a hunt whose lower level is above 120 (a pool level below a tenth
  of the hunt: `raisedLevel`), the lower end of that hunt (300). Hence 12 near a town and 300 in a hunt. The Necromancer fixed the same
  thing for its minions (`necro_lib.lua showLevel`); the Beastmaster never did, and set the health once at the spawn only,
  so a level-up or a call-back left the wolf behind. Now every path calls `ChaosClasses.syncCompanion(owner, companion, fresh)`:
  Wild Bond's spawn, Wild Bond's call-back of a wolf already out, and the 0.5 s tick of `beastmaster.lua` (level-ups,
  logins). It sets the shown level to the owner's level and the maximum health to `companionHealth(level)` (the same share of
  health kept on a level-up). Tested in `tests/classes_test.lua` with a mock monster born at level 12 and 300.
* **Survival.** Health is `800 + 30 x level` (was `500 + 15 x level`) and a hit on a companion is x0.6 (`companion.taken`,
  `ChaosClasses.companionDamageTaken`, applied in the guard before Pack Alpha's extra 20% cut).
* **Damage.** The companion's own bite (every 2 s, physical, dealt as the owner) is `level x 1.1 + distance skill x 2.0`
  (`autoLevel`, `autoSkill`; was `0.12` and `0.6`). Feral Command and Pack Frenzy keep the old bite (`biteLevel`,
  `biteSkill`: their rotation numbers are unchanged). The measured class totals held the old bites (4-8%), so the class damage
  factor (`class_tree.lua classDamage.beastmaster`, now 0.85-1.05 by level) takes the gain back and the cleave's high end
  (`pace_config.lua`, Beastmaster, the companion's hits cleave too) went from 1 to 2: the pack and boss bands of
  `boss_balance_config.lua` hold (`pack_model.py --check`, `boss_model.py --check`). `pack_model.py damage()` calls
  `companion_model.apply` for the Beastmaster.
* **Model.** `server/tools/companion_model.py --check` (CI) with `companion_balance_config.lua`: seconds alive under 2
  monsters of the hunting level (the necro model's `monsterDps` x a burst of 1.5), hits taken, the share of the pack fight
  alive, the bites' share of the Beastmaster's damage (20-30%), the class total against before. No flag prints the table,
  `--legacy` the numbers before. Computed, not measured in game.

| Level | Alive under 2 monsters | Bites (alive, in contact) | Share of damage | Health |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100 | 5.7 s -> 18.2 s | 18 -> 81 dps | 6% -> 24% | 2000 -> 3800 |
| 400 | 6.7 s -> 22.0 s | 70 -> 402 dps (2 wolves) | 6% -> 27% | 6500 -> 12800 |
| 1000 | 5.3 s -> 17.4 s | 122 -> 828 dps (2 wolves) | 4% -> 21% | 15500 -> 30800 |

Class total with the change, against before: 1 target +9..+15%, pack of 5 within 1%. Assumptions: contact 0.6 and burst 1.5 are
fitted to the report (the old model said 6% and 7 s, the tester saw 4% and under 5 s); the model counts the companion's own bites only
(the spells' mauls are in the rotation model). Needs a live check: the shown level on a spawn, a level-up and Wild Bond
on a wolf already out; a hunt of 2 attackers at level 400.

## Pets (`pets.lua`, `pets_core.lua`, `pets_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_pets.sql`, client `game_pets`)

A pet is a small companion that cannot fight and cannot be fought. One is out at a time; it follows its owner, levels from
the owner's kills and has two small abilities (the first from pet level 1, the second from level 20). Client `game_pets`
(Character > Pets in the top menu), extended opcode 254 (`ChaosOpcodes.pets`), table `chaos_pets` (one row per
character and species: name, total XP, out or not, source; `sql/chaos_pets.sql`, also created at startup). Every number
is in `pets_config.lua`; the pure rules in `pets_core.lua`.

- **The creature.** The pet is a monster type of `data/monster/monsters/chaos/pets/` (registered by the installer's
  monsters step), created next to the owner and made the owner's summon, so the engine makes it follow. The types are not
  attackable, have no attacks, no loot, 40 health (below the monster tiers' minimum, and `pets.lua` puts them in
  `ChaosTierConfig.skip`), every immunity and speed 600. They are **passable** (`<flag passable="1" />`, engine patch
  `src-patches/0005-passable-pets.patch`): players (the owner and everyone else), monsters and NPCs walk through a pet and
  path through it, so a pet never blocks anyone; the pet itself still moves only to free tiles. Without the patch the
  engine warns "Unknown flag attribute: passable" for the eight types and pets block as ordinary monsters. A renamed pet
  carries its name (`Monster:rename`); its look text says whose pet it is.
- **Following.** Every 500 ms (`thinkMs`): a pet farther than 6 squares from its owner or on another floor is put next to
  it; a pet the engine removed (a long teleport) comes back next to its owner. The pet **rests** (removed with a puff,
  back by itself when the reason ends) while the owner stands in a protection zone, in a banned zone, or has another
  summon that is not a class companion. No anti-block step-aside: pets are passable for players and monsters (patch 0005).
- **Coexistence with class summons.** Beastmaster companions (`Chaos.classes.companion.monsters`) and Necromancer
  minions (`ChaosNecroConfig.minions`) count only their own monster types, so a pet never lowers their caps, and the
  pet stays out next to them. Any other summon (the stock summon spells and Convince Creature, Moonfang Pack, the base
  server's own familiars) makes the pet rest while it is out, so the stock limit of two summons and Moonfang's cap of
  four are never reduced by a pet. The base server's familiar command refuses while any summon is out, so a player
  dismisses the pet before calling a familiar.
- **Levels.** 1 to 50; XP from level L to L+1 = floor(8 x L^1.4): 8 at level 1, 200 at 10, 724 at 25, 1,859 at 49;
  736 in all to level 10, 7,180 to 25, 38,871 to 50. A kill of the owner while the pet is out (monster with experience,
  not a summon) gives 1 XP, plus 1 / 3 / 7 / 10 for a magic / rare / legendary / boss monster. A normal monster only
  counts when its experience is at least 2 x the owner's level (no farming of trivial monsters): a Dragon (700) counts up
  to level 350, a Dragon Lord (2,100) up to 1,050. At about 700 counted kills an hour, level 20 (4,149 XP) takes about 6 hours, level 50
  about 45 hours of hunting.
- **Abilities** (value at pet level 1 -> 50; L = pet level):

  | Ability | Kind | Value | Rule |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Mend | combat | 4% -> 7.9% of max health (+0.08 per level) | below 50% health; every 30 s at most |
  | Ward | combat | 6% -> 11.9% less damage from monsters (+0.12 per level) | below 60% health, for 6 s; every 45 s at most |
  | Spark Aura | combat | owner level x 0.25 + L x 4, +/-20% (owner 300 / pet 50: about 275; owner 1000: about 450) | every 2 s, up to 3 monsters next to the pet that target the owner or are its target; dealt as the owner in the pet's element (resistances apply) |
  | Gold Sniffer | utility | +2% -> +6.9% gold coins in the corpse (+0.1 per level) | corpses the owner owns (onDropLoot index 2) |
  | Treasure Sense | utility | +1% -> +5.9% item find (+0.1 per level) | added to the item find of the Chaos loot layer (`loot.lua` `L.itemFindMult`) |
  | Fetch | utility | 3 -> 5 squares (+0.05 per level) | coins of a corpse within range of the pet go to the bank (index 2.45, after the hunt tracker's read) |

  Combat abilities pause in PvP combat (`ChaosHealing.inPvp`) and in "utility" zones; the aura never hits players or
  summons.
- **Zones** (`zones`): banned (the pet waits until the owner leaves, cannot be called there): ranked arena, guild siege,
  PvP-zone tiles. Utility only (no Mend, Ward or Aura): rifts, the world boss arena and lobby, Infinity Tower runs,
  dungeons (their own rankings). Seasons: a season character keeps its own pets; achievement pets come only from
  achievements the season character earned itself (store pets are per character anyway).
- **Species** (looks are existing outfits of our dat):

  | Species | Look | Abilities | How |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Ember Whelp | 272 (red hatchling) | Spark Aura (fire), Ward | 1 in 2,500 kills of dragons, dragon lords and their hatchlings |
  | Frost Whelp | 283 (frost hatchling) | Ward, Spark Aura (ice) | 1 in 2,500 kills of frost dragons, frost dragon hatchlings, ice dragons |
  | Duskwing | 122 (bat) | Fetch, Gold Sniffer | 1 in 20,000 counted kills of any monster (x2 / x4 / x8 / x10 magic / rare / legendary / boss) |
  | Lantern Wisp | 294 (wisp) | Mend, Ward | Store, Pets: 400 Chaos Coins |
  | Hoarder Squirrel | 274 (squirrel) | Gold Sniffer, Treasure Sense | Store, Pets: 400 Chaos Coins |
  | Ash Cat | 276 (cat) | Fetch, Mend | Achievement Hired Blade (`bounty_25`) |
  | Gilded Goblin | 61 (goblin) | Gold Sniffer, Fetch | Achievement Greed Is Good (`goblin_10`) |
  | Riftling | 232 (lost soul) | Treasure Sense, Spark Aura (death) | Achievement Deeper Wounds (`rift_t5`) |
  | Ember Parrot | 217 (parrot) | Mend, Ward | Store, Pets: 400 Chaos Coins |
  | Rime Penguin | 250 (penguin) | Gold Sniffer, Treasure Sense | Store, Pets: 400 Chaos Coins |
  | Ashen Hare | 262 (silver rabbit) | Mend, Ward | Store, Pets: 400 Chaos Coins |
  | Bog Frog | 224 (frog) | Gold Sniffer, Treasure Sense | Store, Pets: 400 Chaos Coins |
  | Dusk Moth | 213 (butterfly) | Mend, Ward | Store, Pets: 400 Chaos Coins |
  | Rotling | 314 (ooze) | Gold Sniffer, Fetch | Boss drop: the Rotmother (`exclusives_config.lua`, account-wide) |
  | Ashweaver Spiderling | 350 (spider) | Treasure Sense, Mend | Boss drop: the Ashen Sepulchre's first four bosses (account-wide) |

  The store pets reuse the two ability pairs of the first store pets (Mend + Ward, Gold Sniffer + Treasure Sense), so
  coins buy no new power (`pets_test.lua` checks it). A boss pet is unlocked for the account by `exclusives.lua`, which
  calls `ChaosPets.grant` on each of its characters (at once for the ones online, at login for the others;
  `ChaosPets.owns` skips a character that has it).

  A drop goes straight to the character (message, fireworks, console line). A second copy of an owned species gives that
  pet 400 XP. Achievement pets are account-wide like achievements: checked at login, when the window opens and every
  60 s. Store offers are `kind = "unlock"` with the keys of `pets_config.lua` `store`; `shop_services.lua` asks
  `ChaosPets.storeUnlock`, and an owned pet cannot be bought again (no coins taken).
- **Rules.** 5 s between summon / dismiss / switching, 30 s between renames (2-16 letters and single spaces, capitalised;
  never the name of a monster type, so a pet cannot pass for a class companion or a boss). The owner's death: the pet
  flees (dismissed) and cannot be called for 60 s (kept over a relog). Logout: XP and name are saved, the pet that was out
  comes back 2 s after the next login. XP is saved on level up, dismiss, logout, death, every 60 s and at shutdown.
- **Commands.** Character > Pets (window), `Character > Pets summon <name or species>`, `Character > Pets dismiss`, Rename (the pet that is
  out), `Character > Pets list`. Staff (`/pet`, access groups): `give <species>[, character]`, `xp <n>`, `level <n>`, `reset`, `species`.
- **Protocol** (JSON `{action, data}`): client -> server `open | get | close | summon {species} | dismiss | rename {species,
  name}`; server -> client `state` (owned pets with level, XP, abilities and their unlock state, the catalogue with how to
  get each species, the active pet, out / resting text, zone rule, cooldowns) and `xp` (after a kill while the window is
  open).
- **Shared-file lines.** `chaos_constants.lua` (`pets = 254`), `loot.lua` (one line in `L.itemFindMult`),
  `shop_services.lua` (`unlockEntry` asks `ChaosPets.storeUnlock`), `shop.lua` (an unlock offer with `look` shows that
  outfit), `shop_config.lua` (category "Pets").
- **Tests:** `tests/pets_test.lua` (config sanity, the curve numbers above, kill XP, ability values and unlocks, zone rules,
  drops with a seeded run, names, cooldowns, gold, rest reasons, the window view, every pet monster file passable and not
  attackable) and
  `game_pets/petsview_test.lua` (list, texts, buttons).
- **Tested in game** (test server with the scripts of this repo, one client): staff give; summon from the window (the pet
  follows); rename (`Character > Pets rename`) shown over the pet; kill XP (Dragon Lords and Heroes count at level 500, Dragons do
  not) with the window's XP bar updating live; Spark Aura hitting Heroes next to the pet (about 100-115 each 2 s at owner
  500 / pet 1; Dragon Lords take nothing from the fire aura, they are immune); Mend (+475 at pet level 21, 8,496 max
  health) and Ward (a fixed 1,000 hit: 860 without, 787 with ward 8.4%); forced drops (a new Frost Whelp from a Frost
  Dragon, a Duskwing from a Hero, a duplicate Ember Whelp -> +400 XP); Fetch (coins to the bank with a message) and Gold
  Sniffer (with the value raised to 102% for the test: 40 coins in the corpse -> 81 fetched); rest while a non-class
  summon is out and back after it; banned zone (arena check forced on): pet sent home and "Pets are not allowed here (the
  arena)"; leash after a teleport; owner death: pet gone, "still recovering from your death: 34 s" after the respawn;
  store purchase (400 coins taken, pet owned, second purchase refused); achievement pet (Ash Cat after `bounty_25`);
  logout and server restart: name, XP and the pet that was out come back. Passable (server built from the base source
  with patches 0001-0005, two clients): the owner steps onto the pet's tile in all 8 directions, and so does a second
  player; right after a teleport and return with the pet on the east tile, 5 of 5 steps east go through; a Fire
  Elemental and a Dragon Lord (pushes creatures) in a 1-wide corridor path through the pet (the path is computed through
  its tile), share its tile for a step and reach the owner at the dead end, the pet untouched; following and the leash
  still work; attacking the pet from either client is refused. **Not tested in game:** the protection-zone
  rest (the test map has no protection-zone tile; same code path as the other rests), PvP
  pause, the rift / tower / world boss / dungeon utility rule. The stock loot message ("Loot of ...") is
  written before Fetch runs, so it still lists the coins the pet carried to the bank.

## Bestiary and kill tasks (`bestiary.lua`, `bestiary_core.lua`, `bestiary_config.lua`, `bestiary_spawns.lua`, client `game_bestiary`)

A bestiary entry for every monster the server knows, unlocked by kills, plus personal kill tasks and a task tracker HUD.
Client `game_bestiary` (Hunt > Bestiary / Kill Tasks / Task Tracker in the top menu, Hunt > Bestiary, Hunt > Kill Tasks),
extended opcode 253 (`ChaosOpcodes.bestiary`), tables `chaos_bestiary` (kills per character and monster) and
`chaos_bestiary_tasks` (accepted and finished tasks) in `sql/chaos_bestiary.sql` (also created at startup), storages
7100870-7100879 (`Chaos.storage.bestiary`: +0 task points, +1 / +2 the day and level of the day's board). Every number
is in `bestiary_config.lua`; the pure rules in `bestiary_core.lua`.

- **The catalogue** is built at startup from every name in `monster/monsters.xml` plus the Lua-registered types
  (`MonsterType(name)` loads each one: this engine loads monster files on first use, so `Game.getMonsterTypes()` alone
  lists only those already spawned). Left out: experience below 1, no outfit, `excludeNames` / `excludePatterns`
  (dummies, spell summons). When two registered names show the same name (the quest copy "Demon (Goblin)" is called
  "Demon"), the type registered under that name wins. On the test server: 1,396 entries. Loading every monster at
  startup also prints the base server's broken `monsters.xml` lines once (missing files such as Charger, Vexclaw).
- **Categories:** Bosses (boss flag), Chaos (defined under `monsters/chaos/`), then by the words of the name from the last
  one (the head noun: "Giant Spider" is vermin, "Frost Dragon" a dragon) against the category word lists (`word*` prefix,
  `*word` suffix), else by race (undead, fire / energy -> Elementals, venom -> Insects & Arachnids), else Other. 18
  categories.
- **Difficulty and stages.** The estimated hunting level is the bounty pool's (`<level min max>` middle, else
  1.6 x sqrt(experience), raised by health), capped at 1500. Kills for stage 1 Discovered / 2 Studied / 3 Mastered /
  4 Completed and the bestiary points of each stage:

  | Difficulty | Level | Kills | Points | Completion bonus |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | Harmless | up to 14 | 1 / 10 / 50 / 250 | 1 / 1 / 2 / 4 | +1% damage, +1% experience |
  | Easy | 15-49 | 1 / 25 / 100 / 500 | 1 / 2 / 3 / 6 | +1% / +1% |
  | Medium | 50-149 | 1 / 25 / 250 / 1000 | 2 / 3 / 5 / 10 | +2% / +2% |
  | Hard | 150-399 | 1 / 25 / 200 / 800 | 2 / 4 / 6 / 12 | +2% / +2% |
  | Challenging | 400-799 | 1 / 20 / 150 / 600 | 3 / 5 / 8 / 15 | +3% / +3% |
  | Deadly | 800+ | 1 / 15 / 100 / 400 | 3 / 6 / 10 / 20 | +3% / +3% |
  | Boss | boss flag | 1 / 2 / 3 / 5 | 5 / 5 / 10 / 20 | +3% / +3% |

  Monsters with 1-5 spawn entries on the map (`bestiary_spawns.lua`) need x0.2 of the kills (at least the stage number).
  Stage 1 shows the outfit, level, health and experience; 2 the elements (as damage taken), immunities, where it lives
  (the 3 busiest 160x160 squares of its spawns, named after the nearest temple, with the depth) and the 4 rarest loot
  items; 3 the whole loot (40 at most, with chances) and the Chaos uniques that list the monster (`ChaosLoot.uniqueList`);
  4 activates the bonus. The bonus: damage through a healthchange event on the monster (registered from
  `onTargetCombat`, like `item_mods.lua`), experience through `onGainExperience` (needs the experience dispatch of
  `tools/patch_base_events.py`).
- **Ranks.** Bestiary points (stages + kill tasks) give a rank with experience from every monster: Novice 0, Tracker 100
  (+0.5%), Hunter 300 (+1%), Slayer 750 (+1.5%), Lorekeeper 1500 (+2%), Bestiarch 3000 (+2.5%), Monster Sage 6000 (+3%).
- **Kills.** A death event on every monster without a master (EventCallback `onSpawn`); the last hit and the most damage
  (summons count for their master) and their party members within 30 tiles on the same floor (`ChaosBounty.credit`) each
  get the kill once. Kills are kept in memory and written every 120 s, at a new stage and at logout. A party member's
  credit counts for its kill tasks only when the task's level is within the member's board window (`C.partyCountsTask`,
  2026-10-22): a low character cannot finish a task of strong monsters next to a strong one; the bestiary stages still
  count it.
- **Kill tasks.** A hunt task (kill N of one monster) comes from the daily board or from a discovered entry whose level is
  in the character's take window (0.4 x level to 1.5 x level + 20; up to level 30 anything below that). A family task
  (kill N of a category within a level window) only from the board. The board: 3 hunts and 3 families from monsters that
  spawn in the board window (0.6 x level to 1.25 x level + 10), seeded by task day and character, rolled for the level
  of the character's first look that day. Kills needed: harmless 100, easy / medium 150, hard 120, challenging 100,
  deadly 80 (half, rounded to 5, for monsters with fewer than 20 spawn entries); families 1.8 x the hunt count of the
  window's middle level. Limits: 3 at once, 4 completed a day, 20 a week (done + held; the task day starts at 06:00 like
  the bounty board, the week on Monday). No expiry: a task stays until done or abandoned; progress is written every
  10 kills, at the milestones (25/50/75%) and at logout.
- **Rewards** (paid at once; gold to the bank, orbs to the backpack or the inbox): a share of the bounty board's hunt
  reward of the band of min(task level, character level) (`bounty_config.lua` bands): hunt 40% gold, 50% Orbs of Upheaval,
  5 x the difficulty's stage-1 points; family 60% gold, 75% Chaos, 50% Divine, 8 x points. So: level 120, hunt 20k gold,
  1 Orb of Upheaval, 10 points; family 30k, 1 Chaos, 16 points; band 800+: hunt 800k, 3 Chaos; family 1.2M, 4 Chaos,
  1 Divine. **Experience** (2026-10-22, as the bounty board; it was 1.5% / 2% of a level, 10.7k at level 120 while the
  task's kills gave millions): `expShare` 20% (half a bounty hunt's: up to 4 a day, on a monster the character picks) of
  the base experience of the task's kills at the character's stage, required x one kill's base
  (`C.taskKillBase`: `ChaosBounty.monsterKillBase` of the hunt's monster, for a family the median of the category's
  spawning monsters in the window) x `Game.getExperienceStage`; at least the old `expPercent` (1.5 / 2) and at most
  `expCap` 1000 (10 levels) percent of level L to L + 1 (L = the character's level capped at the band's top). The window
  and the tracker show the amount for the current level. Model (30 boards per level from the bounty pool as the
  catalogue, median, min-max):

  | Level | Hunt old -> new (min-max) | Hunt kills' experience | Family old -> new | Family kills' experience | New, levels (hunt / family) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 8 | 43 -> 18k (2.4k-29k) | 91k | 58 -> 15k | 76k | 6.3 / 5.2 |
  | 30 | 654 -> 342k (121k-436k) | 1.7M | 872 -> 436k (cap) | 4.0M | 7.9 / 10 |
  | 100 | 7.4k -> 4.3M (2.1M-5.0M) | 21.3M | 9.9k -> 5.0M (cap) | 42.7M | 8.6 / 10 |
  | 250 | 47k -> 9.7M (4.7M-18.5M) | 48.7M | 62k -> 18.4M | 91.8M | 3.1 / 5.9 |
  | 400 | 120k -> 17.0M (5.2M-32.8M) | 84.8M | 160k -> 43.0M | 215M | 2.1 / 5.4 |
  | 650 | 186k -> 13.5M (5.4M-211M) | 67.5M | 422k -> 25.9M | 130M | 0.6 / 1.2 |
  | 900 | 478k -> 261M (8.5M-405M) | 1.30B | 809k -> 25.8M | 129M | 6.4 / 0.6 |

  Repeat farming: 4 tasks a day and 20 a week, each a share of kills the character makes anyway; the cap bounds a task
  of a monster with outsized experience. Four a day pay at most 4.8M gold at 800+,
  against 24M for the twelve bounty contracts of a day. Multi-client: as the bounty board, a task that got a kill while
  multi-clienting pays nothing (`mcReward = false`).
- **Bounty board split.** The bounty board (`bounty.lua`) stays the shared daily board per level band with the big
  rewards and the weekly chest. Kill tasks are personal, longer-lived, smaller and pay bestiary points; a kill counts for
  both. Nothing in `bounty.lua` was changed: `bestiary.lua` wraps `ChaosBounty.sendBoard` (accept, abandon, completion)
  and `ChaosBounty.onKill` at runtime to refresh the tracker, and reads `ChaosBounty.players` for the tracker rows.
- **Task tracker HUD**: kill tasks (T), then the active bounty contracts (B), 8 rows at most, pushed after every change
  (one push per player per 150 ms). Client side it sits at the bottom right of the visible map: left of the right side
  panels, above the chat (the rift / invasion HUDs are top left, siege / arena / monster bar top centre, toasts top right,
  monk chi bottom centre).
- **Achievements** (guarded `ChaosAchievements.set` / `.progress`): `bestiary_known`, `bestiary_completed`,
  `bestiary_points`, `bestiary_tasks`; 4 entries in the Monsters category (Field Notes, Know Thy Enemy, Monster Scholar
  with the title Lorekeeper, Exterminator with its title).
- **Protocol** (opcode 253, JSON `{action, data}`): client `open | summary | list | entry {id} | board | take {id} |
  accept {key} | abandon {key} | query`; server `summary` (totals, categories, rank, limits), `list` (rows `[id, name,
  category, difficulty, level, kills, stage, lookType]` in parts of about 6.5 KB, one per 50 ms), `entry` (what the stage
  reveals, the task offer), `kill` (one entry's kills and stage after each kill), `board`, `tracker`, `show {tab}`.
- **Spawn data:** `bestiary_spawns.lua` is generated by `python3 -I server/tools/gen_bestiary_spawns.py <server>/data` from
  the loaded map's spawn file (871 names from the full map in the repo). Rerun it after spawn changes, with
  `gen_bounty_pool.py`.
- **Shared-file lines.** `chaos_constants.lua` (`bestiary = 253`, `Chaos.storage.bestiary`), `achievements_data.lua` (4
  entries and the stats comment), client `client_chaos_topbar` (3 Hunt entries), `game_chaosnotify` (toast type
  `BESTIARY`, action `bestiary`), `docs/tools/gen_readme_art.py` (the README card).
- **Tests:** `tests/bestiary_test.lua` (config sanity, levels, difficulties, thresholds with few spawns, stages and points,
  ranks, categories, the catalogue and summary, task windows, the seeded board, matching, party credit, milestones, the
  accept limits, rewards against the bounty bands, the task experience (kill base of a hunt and a family, share, floor,
  cap, the party rule for tasks), views, packets, the spawn data) and the client's
  `game_bestiary/bestiaryview_test.lua`.
- **Tested in game** (test server with the scripts of this repo, cropped map, monsters created next to the character,
  one client): discovery and stage messages and toasts, the window (categories, search, pages, an undiscovered, a studied
  and a completed entry with elements, areas and loot icons), the board, accepting hunt and family tasks, progress on the
  tracker with every kill, completion (20,000 gold to the bank, 1 Orb of Upheaval, 10,711 experience = 1.5% at level 120 by the old rule, 10
  points), the active cap and the daily limit (Accept greyed with the reason; a forced accept refused), progress kept
  over relog and restart, bounty contracts on the tracker and gone when completed, the completion bonus (a dragon: 45,601
  experience with the bonus, 45,150 without, x1.01; 360 holy damage -> 363) and the damage event registered by real melee,
  the achievement counters. **Not tested in game:** party credit with two players (unit-tested), the 06:00 day change and
  the weekly limit (unit-tested), multi-client tasks.

**Board rerolls** (2026-10-15, for the Candlemarks shop). `ChaosBestiary.addRerolls(player, n)` adds charges (storage
`rerollStorage` 7102404). The task board then shows "Reroll board (N)" (action `reroll`): today's open offers are drawn
again (`C.offers` with a salt, the rerolls used today in storages +1 / +2), the tasks held stay. Tests:
`tests/bestiary_test.lua` (another board, salt 0 is the day's board, a salted board is stable, the charges),
`tests/candlemarks_apis_test.lua`.

**No Prey, no base Task Hunt** (2026-10-16). The base client's Prey and Task Hunt windows (bounty tasks, preferred list,
talisman, weekly tasks, task shop) read packets of newer protocols; this 10.98 server sends none and has no prey, so
