they stayed empty. The client leaves Task Hunt out and has no Prey entry (client/BASE.md, patch `0058`). The task
systems are these kill tasks and the bounty board (opcodes 253 and 223); no server change and no new opcode.

The Monk line's fist weapons (docs/CLASSES.md "Monk"). Owner 2026-10-23: "creio que o monk nao tem armas pra ele. se nao
tiver, faca por favor".

* **The gap found.** The Monk did have six fist weapons (levels 8 to 650), but: nothing for levels 1 to 7 and 9 to 59 (the
  kit was empty hands); one unique (level 650) and none to level up with; after level 650 nothing, so a Monk from level 650
  to 2400+ wore the same talons or went bare (bare fists reach their cap of 60 at level 800 and nothing beat them); the

  the skill factor of "Auto attack power", fists did not); the Monk's starter kit had no weapon.

little lower attack. The Pyre Saint's base is 62 / 22.)

* **Balance.** Bare fists are 40 + level x 0.025 (at most 60, from level 800). A plain tier is 1 to 7 attack above them at its
  own level: **x1.00 .. x1.12 damage** (asserted in `fist_weapons_test.lua`: a gain over 1 and at most 1.12 at the level of
  each plain tier; the old tiers measured x1.047 at level 300, 979 against 933 per hit on a dummy). The Monk's auto attack
  is 53-62% of its single-target spell rotation (`weapon_sim.py --power`, below) and a plain claw adds at most 12% to it,
  so the share stays where the other weapon classes are (30-60%). The family is an upgrade path and a gear slot, not a new
  damage tier. The uniques go further on purpose (the Pyre Saint's grasp 64, Gravewind Talons 68, Dawnless Gauntlets 70,
  up to +17% over the bare cap) and carry their value in modifiers.
* **Fist skill scales the hit (new).** `weapon_power_config.lua` has a fourth kind `fist` (`POWER_KINDS['fist'] = (0.30,
  'Monk', 1.5)` in `weapon_sim.py`: lifted to 30% of a Monk's rotation, a lift that never cuts; the Monk is already at
  53-62%, so the level factor is **1.00 at every level**). The skill factor `(fist skill / typical skill)^0.5`, clamped to
  0.7 .. 1.6, now applies to bare fists and fist weapons too (`monk_combat.lua`: `WP.hitFactor("fist", level, fist skill)`
  after `unarmedFactor`). It is 1 at the typical skill (no balance number moves) and +10 skill at level 1000 is +9.3%
  where the engine alone gave +5.6%. The Monk's attack speed is not touched.
* Rarities, item levels, modifiers: drops get the stock rarity roll and the chaos gear pass like any gear;
  `chaos_item_mods.lua` treats a shield with an attack as a weapon, so they roll weapon modifiers (attack speed,
  ailments, penetration, ...). A unique is a copy of its own base item with the attributes of `chaos_items.xml`
  (`gen_unique_specs.py` maps `skillFist` to the stock rarity attribute `rarity_fistSkill` and the `mods` attribute to
  built-in Chaos modifiers, two to four per unique). Slot `"fist"` in `chaos_unique_items.lua`; the leveling pair drops
  as magic from ordinary monsters (chance 25), the endgame pair as rare or better from monsters of level 1000+ (chance
  6, `minMonsterLevel`). The base item of a unique is in no shop and no loot.
* Prices: `gen_item_prices.py` reads both manifests (`fist_rows()`); the csv `sell` is the table price, the NPC buy is at
  least twice the sell (no buy-below-sell loop) and the gear price cap (33,834) holds. The cheap tiers are sold by the 17
  weapon dealers; the rest only drops, and Grimgan buys it.
* Starter kit: the Monk's new-player kit (`newplayer_config.lua`) gets the pair of splinter claws in the right slot (the
  shield hand), given at level 1 and worn from level 1. The admin test kit (`admin/testkit.lua`) gets the cinderforged

## Iron Palm stun on players (`monk_combat.lua`, `monk_chi_core.lua`, spell `ironsage/iron_palm.lua`)

The Iron Sage's Iron Palm stuns a player as well as a monster, built from what the engine already has (no source patch):
- **When:** only when the strike's damage lands. The spell writes the chi it spent into the caster's storage
  `ChaosMonk.ids.storage.palmChi` (7100804) for the length of its `doTargetCombat`; the victim's `ChaosMonkCombat`
  onHealthChange sees physical damage with `ORIGIN_SPELL` from that caster, after the Monk evasion and Chi Ward, and stuns.
  So every PvP rule that can stop the damage stops the stun: no-PvP world, protection / no-PvP zones, protection level, party
  members, secure mode, the multi-client rule, the arena guard and the guild siege (`ChaosSpell.canAttack` and the
  `onTargetCombat` callbacks). A dodged, fully warded or lethal hit does not stun. The hit fight-locks and skulls the Monk as
  any attack on a player does, and both are then in PvP combat, so the -30% heal rule (`healing_rules.lua`) applies to them.
- **What:** `creature:setMovementBlocked(true)` (no walking, cannot be pushed) and `creature:setNoMove(true)` (a walk already
  queued stops), both undone by an `addEvent` at the exact end and only when this file set them (another script's block
  stays); `CONDITION_PACIFIED` with the default condition id and sub id 0 for the stun's length (the engine's
  `Creature::hasCondition` only sees sub id 0 and checks the end time to the millisecond): no auto attack
  (`Player::doAttacking`) and no aggressive spell or rune ("You are exhausted."); healing spells and potions still work. A
  cast-time spell in progress is interrupted (`ChaosCasting.interrupt`, result `paralysed`). A creature think event
  (`ChaosMonkStunThink`, registered only while stunned) frees a stun whose timer was lost (a script reload).
- **Numbers** (`ChaosMonk.cfg.stun.pvp`): 0.5 s + 0.1 s per chi spent, at most 1 s (0.6 s at 1 chi, 1 s at 5). Then 6 s of
  immunity (condition timer `subId.stunImmune`, 71035) and a 15 s window (`subId.stunDr`, 71038) in which the next stun lasts
  half as long (at least 0.3 s). Iron Palm's own cooldown is 8 s, so one Monk stuns 1 s, then 0.5 s; a second Monk inside the
  immunity gets "X cannot be stunned again yet."
- **Shown:** "Stunned!" over the victim (orange, seen by everyone) and the stun effect; the victim reads "You are stunned for
  1.0 s by X.", the Monk "X is stunned for 1.0 s."; the buff bar gets the debuff **Stunned** (source `stun`, from
  `ChaosMonk.pvpStun`) and the buff **Stun Immunity** (condition 71035) at once (the bar is pushed, not left to its 1 s
  look), and the party frames show them on the member.
- Tests: `tests/monk_pvp_stun_test.lua` (numbers, and `monk_combat.lua` against a mocked engine: stun, release on time,
  immunity, the shorter second stun, no stun on a melee hit / heal / lethal / empty hit, another script's block kept, the
  think fallback, logout), `tests/buffs_test.lua` (the two buff bar rows). Tested in game with two characters (Iron Sage and
  Sentinel, two clients, local test server and database): the stun at 5 chi, the victim's walk refused during it and allowed
  after, an attack spell refused ("You are exhausted."), the bar's Stunned row for 1 s, the second stun 8 s later for 0.5 s,
  a second Iron Palm inside the immunity refused, the multi-client rule refusing the attack before its test switch was on.

## Buff bar and party frames (`buffbar.lua`, `data/lib/chaos_buffs.lua`, `partyframes.lua`, `partyframes_core.lua`, client `game_buffbar`, `game_partyframes`)

Two client HUDs fed by the server. Opcodes (`ChaosOpcodes` in `chaos_constants.lua`): **234** `buffs` and **235** `partyFrames`
(both were free: 224-227, 230, 231, 234 and 235 were unused; 249 and 240 went to the chat links and the inspect window in the
meantime). The server is the authority: the client draws what it is told and counts the time down by itself.

### Buff bar (opcode 234)
- `data/lib/chaos_buffs.lua` is the registry (`ChaosBuffs.entries`: `key`, `name`, `kind` buff / debuff, `icon`, `desc`, `prio`)
  and the rules (`collect`, `diff`, `full`, `wire`, `brief`, `validate`). An entry is backed either by a **condition**
  (`cond = {type, sub, ids}`: found with `player:getCondition(type, id, sub)`, the time left is the condition's ticks, -1 = no
  timer) or by a **source** (`B.sources[name](player, nowMs, def)`, a function that returns a list of items; it reads the other
  modules' globals guarded, so a module that is not loaded adds nothing). To add a buff: one `cond(...)` or `source(...)` line,
  its icon name in `client/tools/gen_buff_icons.py` (the tool refuses to run when the two disagree), done.
  The Ember Descent's entries `descent_boon` / `descent_curse` (source `descent`, one item per boon or curse held, icons
  `descent_b_<key>` / `descent_c_<key>`) are drawn by `client/tools/gen_descent_icons.py`; `gen_buff_icons.py` leaves the
  `descent_*` names to it.
- Covered (90 entries): the engine conditions haste, regeneration, food ("Well Fed", regeneration with the default id), mana
  shield, invisible, light, spell / potion buffs (attributes without a sub id), poison, burning, energy, bleeding, drowning,
  freezing, dazzled, cursed, paralyze (shown as "Slowed"), drunk, pacified, muted, in fight (also the PZ lock, the engine keeps
  one condition for both), white / red / black skull with the time the engine keeps it; the class buffs by sub id (Red Frenzy, Banner Call, Ironbark Hide, Lightward, Soulward, Wraithshroud, Flickerdash, Iron Bellow, Shadow Veil,
  Poison Blades, Counter Stance, Bushido Focus with its stacks, Bloodrage, Banner of Bones, Bone Offering, the Monk's Focus /
  Chi Ward / Mantra of Stone / Kindled Breath, Aegis of Faith, Moonfang Pack, Hall of Mirrors); the sources: the three world buffs
  (global storages of `shop_services.lua`), the Victory buff (server-wide, or only inside its area), Golden Hour and Chaos Storm
  (only for a character standing in the area, `ChaosWorldEvents.active`), the day's events with a bonus (no timer),
  the double experience potion (storage 6000), Vocation Trials kill stacks (Bloodlust, Zeal and the other stack nodes: the stacks
  from `ChaosTrials.nodeState`, named after the held node, the timer is the oldest kill falling off), the Monk's chi (stacks =
  chi, timer = the decay), the Berserker's Rage (a passive: stacks = the bonus percent, no timer), the Reprisal window
  (storage of `supports.lua`), the Iron Palm stun on a player and its immunity (section "Iron Palm stun on players") and the
  **Templar aura** (source `templarAura`, from `ChaosTemplar.auraState` of `templar_combat.lua`): "<Templar>'s Aura" (or
  "Your Sentinel Aura"), stacks = the damage it takes off in percent, the text names the Templar, the class, the reduction,
  the Sentinel's regeneration and Bastion; no timer (it lasts while the Templar is near), so it is sent when it starts, when
  another Templar's aura takes over or the numbers change, and when it ends, never while it simply holds; the **vigils**
  (source `vigils`, section "Vigils"): a row per vigil that covers the player and Iron Tithe's health row, stacks = the
  effect in percent, no timer. `tests/buffs_test.lua` checks the sub ids against the spell files and the class configs.
- **Support spells** (owner report 2026-10-17, "a support spell does not show on the buff bar"): every support-group spell
  that puts a timed state on the caster is on the bar. Three gaps were closed. (1) Moonfang Pack (40 s) and Hall of Mirrors
  (10 s) made summons / decoys but no condition on the caster, so they never showed: the two spells now add a timer-only
  condition (`ChaosSpell.buffTimer`, sub ids 71070 / 71071 in `ChaosSpell.SUBID`) and have the rows `moonfang_pack` and
  `mirror_image` (their own spell art as the icon). (2) Mantra of Stone of an Iron Sage with Deep Mantra puts the timer 71037
  instead of 71032, which had no row: an entry can now name several sub ids (`cond.subs`), and `mantra` looks for both.
  (3) The stock support spells that are not in this repo (the base `spells.xml`: Haste, Strong Haste, Charge, Swift Foot,
  Bloodlust, Bulwark, Hawkeye, the party Communions) are engine conditions with the combat id; the plain ones (sub id 0) were
  shown already, but a base script that gives its condition a small sub id was not, so `spellbuff` looks for the attribute
  sub ids 0-9 and `haste` for 0-3 (the exact ids of the base scripts could not be checked: the base tree is not committed,
  they show under the generic names "Spell Buff" / "Haste"). Not on the bar on purpose: the summons without a timer (Raise
  Dead, Bone Golem, Wild Bond), what a spell does to monsters (Smoke Bomb, Rebuke, Judgement, Iron Palm), instant spells
  (Town Portal, Hunter's Instinct, Detonate Mines), and the Reprisal / vigil states, which have their own sources. The
  test `tests/buffs_test.lua` fails when a sub id of `ChaosSpell.SUBID` has no row.
- Not on the bar: the passive tree's own conditions (permanent, sub ids 7200-7240); the item ailments of `item_mods.lua`
  (bleed, ignite, poison, chill, shock), which are only ever put on monsters, so they cannot appear on a player; what a monster
  does to a player (poison, burning, slow ...) is an engine condition and is covered. Hex / Brand marks sit on monsters (the
  `hexes` table of `supports.lua` is local to it): the optional row under the monster bar for the player's own marks is **not done**.
- Icons (`icon` of an entry): always `buff:<name>`, our own 26x26 pixel art at the bar's cell size
  (`client/overlay/data/images/game/buffs/`, 86 icons from `client/tools/gen_buff_icons.py`, one per registry key). Buffs sit in
  an ember-gold frame, debuffs in a blood-red frame with thorns in the corners (the same colours as the client's border). The
  class buffs that come from a Chaos spell show that spell's pixel-art icon inside the buff frame; everything else is drawn by
  the tool. No stock condition art and no spell sheet lookup any more: `validate` refuses any other form, and
  `tests/buffs_test.lua` checks that every entry's icon and key PNG exist at 26x26. The client still reads an older server's
  `spell:` / `cond:` spec, but draws the key's own icon for it.
- Protocol: client -> server `sync` (start, or ask for the full list; at most one per `cfg.requestMs` = 2 s) and `off`; server ->
  client `full {list}` and `diff {add, upd, del}`, an entry `{k, n, d, i, t (0 buff / 1 debuff), l (ms left; none = no timer),
  s (stacks)}`. Only a client that sent `sync` is looked at, once per `cfg.tickMs` (1 s); a diff is sent only when something
  changed (stacks changed, the end moved by more than `cfg.toleranceMs` = 1.5 s, a new or gone buff), so a quiet bar costs no
  traffic; a full list goes out every `cfg.resyncMs` = 30 s (a lost message heals itself). The list is cached for 0.9 s per
  character, so the bar and the party frames never collect it twice. At most `cfg.maxEntries` = 24 entries.

### Party frames (opcode 235)
- Every `cfg.tickMs` = 500 ms a character whose client sent `open {buffs}` is told the state of its **own** party
  (`P.state` in `partyframes_core.lua`): per member the id, name, level, vocation, outfit, health and mana, floor difference,
  distance, flags (leader, in fight, dead, connection lost, you) and the first `cfg.partyEntries` = 5 buffs / debuffs
  (debuffs first; only when the client asked for them; each with its name, which the frame's tooltip lists, e.g. "Cf
  Sentinel 300's Aura"). **Range rule:** a member within `rangeSqm` = 50 squares and
  `rangeFloors` = 2 floors gets exact health, mana, distance and buffs; a farther one only a health percent in steps of
  `farStep` = 10 and the floor difference (the minimap already shows where party members are), no mana, no distance, no
  buffs. Nothing is ever sent about a character outside the viewer's party, and a viewer without a party gets one empty
  state (the client hides the frames). An unchanged state is repeated only every `heartbeatMs` = 2 s (the client calls a
  state older than 4.5 s "connection lost"); within one tick every member is read once, whoever of the party asks.
- Actions (`kick {id}`, `lead {id}`, `invite {name}`; at most one per 0.5 s, an invitation per 2 s, `ChaosRateLimit`): the
  leader removes a member (`party:removeMember`), a member cannot; the leader passes the leadership (the client uses the
  engine's own `g_game.partyPassLeadership` from the menu, `lead` is the same check for other callers); `invite` takes a
  name, starts a party for a character that has none (`Party(player)`) and refuses yourself, a character already in a party
  or already invited, an unknown name and a full party (20). The checks are `P.canKick`, `P.canPassLeadership`,
  `P.canInvite`. Accepting an invitation stays the engine's (the invite window of `game_chaosnotify`, or `partyJoin`).
- The engine removes a character from its party when it logs out, so "offline" on a frame means a lost connection (IP 0, the
  character still in the game) or no state for 4.5 s; "dead" is health 0 for a moment (a dying character leaves the map).

### Tests and checks
- `tests/buffs_test.lua` (registry, conditions by type / id / sub id, every source, order and cap, wire, diff, cache),
  `tests/partyframes_test.lua` (range, far health, flags, state, signature, action checks) and
  `tests/buffparty_glue_test.lua` (the two scripts loaded against a mocked engine: login, opcode, ticks, what a viewer is and
  is not told, kick / lead / invite) run with luajit and lua5.3 from `server/`. Client: `game_buffbar/buffmath_test.lua`,
  `game_partyframes/partymath_test.lua`.
- Tested in game on a test server (the engine with patches 0001-0011, the cropped test map) with three characters in one
  party: the bar with about 20 buffs and debuffs at once (stack number on Bushido Focus, countdown, red borders, tooltips with the
  live time left), dragging and the saved position, the gear window (since replaced: the bar is now fixed under the
  character plate and follows it, rows as wide as the plate, see client/MANIFEST.md `game_buffbar`), hiding from the top menu (the server stops sending), a
  world buff, the Victory buff, Golden Hour; the frames with three members, a member on another floor (arrow and count), one
  70 squares away (rough health, no mana), left click follows and a second click stops, shift+click, the right-click menu,
  removing a member and passing the leadership, inviting by name, the leader crown moving, the frames hiding on leaving the
  party. Not tested in game: Vocation Trials stacks (the test server runs with the trials off; the source is covered by the
  unit test), Chaos Storm, the Monk's chi and the Berserker's Rage on a real character, skull timers, a dead member.
- Limits: the client's stock status icons (the arcs around the character and the row under the plate) are the base client's
  and stay as they are, so the stock states show twice; the order of the icons is the server's after a full list and the
  order of arrival between two (nothing jumps about); the party frames' outfit is the character's whole outfit in a small
  square (class outfits are larger than a tile, so they are drawn small); Hex / Brand marks on the target are not done.

## Level-up effect (`levelwings.lua`, `levelwings_core.lua`, `levelwings_config.lua`, client `game_levelwings`)

When a character gains a level, everyone on screen sees the level-up effect of the purchased game feel pack (pair 36,
`w_fx_level_up` = 4047, about 1.4 s: a ring, a rising star and the words LEVEL UP in English baked into the art). The
client plays it with `Effect.create` + `g_map.addThing` on the character's tile + (1, 1) (client/MANIFEST.md
"game_levelwings"). Since 2026-10-22 (owner: "Use as spells, level up e loot beams"); until then a pair of golden wings
(our PNG frames, `gen_levelwings_art.py`, both retired). The server side did not change. The stock level-up text and
magic effect are the engine's and stay as they were. A client on a pair older than 36 draws nothing.

- **Trigger:** a `CreatureEvent` `onAdvance` (`ChaosLevelWingsAdvance`, registered at login) for `SKILL_LEVEL` with a
  higher new level. Several levels from one experience gain are one `onAdvance` call, so they play once; a level lost on
  death plays nothing.
- **Message:** extended opcode **191**, JSON `{"action": "play", "data": {"id": <creature id>, "lv": <new level>, "n":
  <levels gained>}}` (about 60 bytes), to every player `Game.getSpectators(pos, false, true)` returns (the character
  itself included; this floor only, `multifloor` in the config).
- **Throttles** (`levelwings_config.lua`): one play per character per 4 s (`playerCooldownMs`; a staff `set_level` pressed
  again and again, kills that each give a level), at most 3 plays per viewer per second (`viewerMax`), at most 40
  broadcasts per second for the whole server (`globalMax`). A dropped play costs nothing and does not spend the
  character's cooldown. Entries are pruned after a minute and dropped at logout.
- **Client settings:** Options > Graphics > Effects, "Level-up wings on my character" and "Level-up wings on other
  characters" (client base patch 0036), both on by default. The server sends to everyone; each client decides.
- **Opcode:** 191 is free in the reference server, the base client (`ExtendedIds`) and every Chaos script and module
  (189 / 190 client guard, 199 the Gambler). No storages, no tables.
- **Tests:** `tests/levelwings_test.lua` (opcode unique and not a base one, the payload, the per-character cooldown, the
  server-wide and per-viewer budgets with their windows, prune and forget, and `levelwings.lua` against a mocked engine:
  the events, one message per spectator, cooldown, other skills and a lost level, an engine error caught); client
  `game_levelwings/levelwingsmath_test.lua` (the effect id and offset against `chaos_pack36_fx_ids.lua`, the tile,
  settings rule, message check). The wings were tested on a live test server with two Linux clients (a real level-up
  through `addExperience` showed them to the character and to a second player; each setting turned off hid them on
  that client only). The pair 36 effect is not yet run in a client.

## Boss spawns (`bossspawns.lua`, `bossspawns_core.lua`, `bossspawns_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_boss_spawns.sql`, client `game_bossspawns`)

A window (Adventure > Boss Spawns, extended opcode 217, `ChaosOpcodes.bossSpawns`) with every boss of the server, grouped by
category, with its place and when it comes back. The list is `bossspawns_config.lua` plus what the owning systems hold, read
at the first spawn of the map (so they never drift): the world bosses (`Chaos.worldBoss.bosses`), the invasion bosses
(`invasion_config.lua` factions), the Infinity Tower bosses (`ChaosTowerRunConfig.bosses`), the Vocation Trial bosses
(`trials_config.lua` families), the Ascension Warden and the dungeon bosses (`Chaos.dungeons.extra` with the base
`DUNGEON_SYSTEM`: level, entrance, party size, cooldown storage).

| Category | Bosses | Respawn rule shown |
|---|---|---|
| World Bosses | Kaelgor, Skaldra, The Rotmother, Nyxareth, Vharok (arena at 5016, 5016, 7; portals at every temple) | rotation slots 03/09/15/21:00: the time of each boss's next slot; "Alive" while the event runs |
| Island Bosses | Dreadscale (Sun 00:00), Aquatic Overlord Thalassa (Mon 16:00), Drak'thul (Tue 20:00), Thalador (Wed 20:00), Vorondor (Thu 20:00), Azazel (Fri 20:00), Mortis and Dreadbone (Sat 12:00), Tymagron (Sat 20:00), Gor'gul (Sun 20:00) | the base server's weekly timer (they stay until slain): next weekly time |
| Raid Bosses | 25 single-spawn bosses of the base `data/raids/raids.xml` (Vhalkareth, Vharagoth, Morgashal, Moloveth, Ul'thazmor, Kazmorath, Ssylvath, The Ashen Count, The Grey Widow, ...) | "Random", about every `interval2` minutes and at least `margin` after the last raid; numbers and positions read from the installed raid files at startup, raids the server does not have are left out |
| Lair Bosses | map spawns of the real map: Apocalypse, Ul'thazmor, Vhalkareth Mortal Shell, Morgashal, Pyrevorn (x3), the seven Inquisition bosses, Koshei, The Collector, Tibb the Butcher | spawntime after the tracked kill (countdown), "Respawn due" after that (the engine waits while a player sees the spot) |
| Invasion Bosses | Warchief Grashnak, Goblin Chieftain, Mushroom King, Sanguidrake the Unburied, Ancient Treant, Morgashal, The Ashen Count, Ironbrow the Gorer, Moloveth | the next announced invasion whose area and faction pick this boss (`invasion_core.lua` upcoming + planBoss), else "Random" |
| Rift Guardians and Omens | Rift Guardian, Sangrith, Morvane, Thalcyra | on demand (Rift Key, Omen Keys); the Omens' last kill is tracked |
| Dungeon Bosses | Prince Skeletal, Master of the Elements, Forbidden Chevalier, The Rootmaw | on demand (dungeon queue); the player's own dungeon cooldown counts down |
| Infinity Tower Bosses | the 12 tower bosses, floor 10, 20 ... 120, repeating every 120 floors | on demand |
| Trial and Quest Bosses | the seven Vocation Trial bosses and the Ascension Warden | on demand; the player's trial / ascension cooldown counts down |
| Rare Spawns | Treasure Goblin | 1 in 3000 natural respawns; "Alive" while one is up |

**Tracking.** An `EventCallback onSpawn` sees every monster the engine creates (map spawns, raids, `Game.createMonster`); a
monster whose type is in the list gets the death event `ChaosBossSpawnsDeath`, and 100 ms later (the creature id exists only
once the engine has placed it) the monsters of that type within `scanRadius` of the spawn point are matched by
`ChaosBossSpawnsCore.match`: same type, the shown name for the renamed invasion bosses, and the place (within `radius` sqm and
one floor of `pos`, inside a dungeon box, or anywhere). So a tower or rift copy of Morgashal never counts for the raid or the
lair, and a map Orc Warlord is no Warchief Grashnak (only the running invasion's boss is). The death stores the time, the
player with the most damage (else the last hit) and the kill count in `chaos_boss_spawns` (one row per boss key, created at
startup too); a boss removed without dying is dropped from "alive" when the list is built. Lair, island and raid entries
whose monster type is not loaded on the server are left out (logged once).

**Places.** `loc` from the config; without one, "near <town>" from the closest temple of `Game.getTowns()`. Rows send the
coordinates of open-world bosses; instance bosses send a note instead.

**Protocol.** Client `open` / `refresh` (rate limited, `requestMs`); server `list {now, refresh, cats, rows}` (about 20 KB, so
`Chaos.sendChunked`). Times are seconds from the moment of sending (the client counts down by itself) plus "Wed 19:30" for
waits of 6 hours or more. Fields: server/data/scripts/chaos/bossspawns.lua header.

**Opcode.** 217 is free in the reference server and in every Chaos script and client module (checked by grep, as in "Opcode
collision check"); `tests/bossspawns_test.lua` checks that no two `ChaosOpcodes` share a number. No player storage is used
(the cooldowns shown are read from the dungeon's, the Trials' 7101764 and the Ascension Trial's 7101002 storages).

**Tests.** `tests/bossspawns_test.lua` (luajit and lua5.3): the list from the real configs, raid file parsing, matching,
every rule's status, the payload and its size, and `bossspawns.lua` against a mocked engine (spawn, scan, death, SQL row,
the list with the player's cooldown, rate limit). Client: `game_bossspawns/bossspawnsview_test.lua`. The window was rendered
in the Linux client with a payload built by the core; not run against a live server (the island bosses' and raid bosses'
looks and the lair positions come from the base data and the real map's spawn file: check them on the live server after
the first install).

**Pocket button.** World, island and raid boss rows carry a Pocket button with the player's charges ("Pocket 2/3"); it
opens that boss's pocket (below). The server sends `pocket {bosses = {key = {l, m, b, lv, ok}}, reset, inside}` after every
`list` and when the charges change; the client sends `pocketEnter {k}`; a refusal comes back as `pocketError {text}` (in the
player's language) and shows in the window's bottom line for 8 s. `bossspawns.lua` hands every `pocket*` action to
`ChaosPocketBoss.actions` (one handler on 217). Every pocket row also carries `pl` (its pocket level; "Pocket: level N+"
under the name of a boss without a level of its own) and the Raid Bosses category is sorted by it, then by name
(`ChaosPocketBoss.tidy`, `pocketboss_config.lua` `sortSpawns`), so the 25 raid bosses stay tidy.

## Pocket bosses (`pocketboss.lua`, `pocketboss_core.lua`, `pocketboss_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_pocketboss.sql`, client `game_bossspawns`)

Owner decision (2026-10-15): every boss that is time-gated or contested gets a private copy, the **pocket**, open any time
for less reward. The scheduled and contested fights stay the full-reward social events. Decided (2026-10-15, delegated by
the owner; `docs/OWNER_TODO.md` "Decided"): 60% experience and loot, the level floors below, pockets for all 25 raid bosses
(listed by pocket level in the Boss Spawns window), no Ashen Sepulchre pockets, the no-stacking hour persisted, multi-client
characters allowed (each spends its own charges).

**Which bosses.** Read from the systems that own them (`pocketboss_core.lua K.list`): the five world bosses
(`Chaos.worldBoss.bosses`, keys `world_1` .. `world_5`), the ten island bosses and the 25 bosses of the random base raids
(Moloveth among them) from the Boss Spawns list (`bossspawns_config.lua` keys; a monster type the server does not have is
left out). Not pocketed: the Ashen Sepulchre (open any time; its loot is the weekly lockout and its fights live in
`raid.lua`), dungeon bosses (queue any time), the guild boss (the guild's weekly fuel), lair bosses (back within seconds to
an hour), and the rift, Omen, Ascended, tower, trial and Descent bosses (already private).

**Opening.** Only from the client: the Pocket button of the Boss Spawns window (owner rule: no player talkaction or
command). From a protection zone, out of combat, not inside another instance, at the boss's level (world bosses: the
event's 300; island 250, raid 150, Moloveth 250: the open-world fights have no level, so a floor is set), with a charge
left and not rewarded by that boss's event in the last `noStackSeconds` (3600). Party members within `party.range` (8) sqm
on the same floor come along (5 in all); a member who fails a rule (level, charges, far, combat, another instance, the
event hour) stays behind and both are told why. `enterCooldown` (10 s) between two openings by one player.

**Charges.** `charges.daily` (3) per character, boss and day; the day turns at `charges.resetHour` (0: midnight, the day
of `Chaos.dayKey`, as the daily reward and the Descent's free run). Every member who comes along spends one. Bonus charges
(`ChaosPocketBoss.addCharges`) are spent after the daily ones, stay over the reset, at most `bonusPerDay` (3) added per
boss and day and `bonusMax` (6) held. Table `chaos_pocketboss` (player, boss key: day, used, bonus, bonus_day, bonus_added,
kills, event_at), created at startup too. A charge is written with a synchronous query when it is spent, before anyone moves: a
logout, a death, a crash or leaving early never give it back. Only a server shutdown with the pocket open does
(`refundOnRestart`), and a boss that could not be created.

**The arena.** `uber_core.lua`'s runtime-built slot layout (as the guild boss), 23 x 23 with the antechamber south of it
and the way out (forcefield, action id 47620; 47620-47629 reserved) there. Grid x 11520-11903, y 10000-10095, z 7: 8 x 2
slots of 48, east of the guild boss arenas, clear of every other runtime area (`tests/pocketboss_test.lua` checks it).
Registered with `Chaos.registerInstance("pocketboss")` (`/instances`, the Town Portal and the hideout see it), at most
`limits.maxRuns` (16) at once with the waiting line of `instance_limits.lua`, warnings at 5 / 1 min / 10 s, strangers
swept out every 3 s, a character that logs in inside the grid without a run goes to its temple.

**The fight.** The boss appears `startDelay` (6 s) after the arrival, the boss's own monster type with
`boss_mechanics.lua`'s profile when it has one (world bosses), health x `health` of its category by party size (world:
3% solo of the 16-22 M event health, +2.5% per extra player, at most 15%; island 50% +25%, raid 60% +25%, at most 150%),
the hits of the pocket's monsters on players x `damage` (world 0.5 solo +0.1 per extra player; island 0.75, raid 0.8).
Time limit `minutes` (world 15, island 12, raid 10); the boss walks back to its spot when nobody is in the arena. A lethal
hit is caught (`catchLethal`): the player goes back where they came from, healed, no death and no loss; the charge stays
spent. The last one out ends the pocket. After the kill the corpse can be looted for `exitDelay` (30 s), then everyone is
sent back and the slot is cleaned.

**Rewards.** Experience x `xpMult` (0.6; `EventCallback onGainExperience` at index -5, rounded at random). The corpse x
`lootMult` (0.6): `loot.lua` multiplies its pack factor by `ChaosPocketBoss.lootMultOf(monster)`, so the stock loot is
thinned (a stack keeps count x 0.6, any other item stays with chance 0.6: even the items that always drop are not sure)
and the Chaos rolls, gems and uniques are x0.6 too. A pocket world boss drops at the world boss item level. Conquest
Tokens per player and kill (`tokens`: world 3, island 2, raid 1, Moloveth 2) through `ChaosConquest.grant(player,
"pocketboss:<key>", n)` when that module is loaded. World bosses also give each player present a reduced share of the
event reward: the base orbs x0.6 (rounded at random), one roll of the boss's gear list (its sets) at `gearChance` x 0.6
(9%) and one boss-only unique roll at `uniqueChance` x 0.6; no bank gold, no pool, no podium, no title. The **boss passive
point** comes from `bosspoints.lua` as for any kill of that type (damage map and party): the five world boss points and
Moloveth's are no longer locked behind the clock or a random raid, and each is earned once either way.

**No stacking.** A character rewarded by a boss's scheduled or contested fight (the world boss event's `W.deliver`,
wrapped at startup; an island or raid boss's corpse owner or personal loot) cannot open that boss's pocket for
`noStackSeconds`. Kept in `chaos_pocketboss.event_at` (the boss's row of that character, created when needed): a restart
keeps it.

**Personal loot of the contested fights** (`contested`). The island bosses and the random raid bosses spawned by the base
server (not a pocket, not a lair spawn of the same type: the place decides, through `ChaosBossSpawnsCore.match`) count
the damage each player deals them and, from the players within `healRange` (10) sqm, the healing done on players fighting
them (capped at the missing health). At the death every player other than the corpse owner whose damage + healing reaches
`minPercent` (2%) of the boss's max health (at most `maxPlayers` 30) gets a personal roll of the boss's own loot table
(each entry at its chance x `lootMult` 1.0, count 1..max) into the backpack, the rest to the store inbox; gear gets the stock
rarity roll and the kill's item level. The corpse owner keeps the corpse.

**After the kill** (beta 2026-10-20, "Shadow of ..." pocket: no drop, stairs that cannot be entered). A pocket spawns
the boss's own monster type away from its home. Two things of the home came with it: a reward boss (the base server's
`rewardBoss` flag) drops no corpse loot, its loot goes to the reward chest of its home room, which a pocket does not
have; and a boss whose own death script opens the way on (stairs, a teleport) put that way into the pocket, where it
leads nowhere. Now `bossDeath` records the corpse (items in it, `MonsterType:isRewardBoss`, the loot table) and, for
island and raid bosses (`K.needsFallbackLoot`: a reward boss, no corpse or an empty one), every player of the run gets a
personal roll of the loot table x `lootMult` (gear with the stock rarity roll and the boss floor of the loot layer, the
kill's item level; backpack, else inbox; "Pocket loot of ..."). Any teleport or floor-change tile of the pocket other
than its two forcefields is cleared at the kill and again 1 s and 5 s later (`K.foreignExits`; a floor-change ground
becomes the arena ground). The arena's own forcefield (b89d8cad) is chosen before the room is painted
(`K.arenaGate`) and reserved from the dark paint; it was placed after the paint, on whatever decoration landed there.
The kill message says the way out is the forcefield by the arrival. Which boss "Shadow of ..." is cannot be read here:
the name is the base server's (the renamed raid and island bosses, `base_monster_names.csv` holds only hashes); the
fix is for every pocket boss.

**The corpse after the loot** (beta 2026-10-22, Weakened Slurgoth: no drop and a stair that cannot be entered). Its
monster type's corpse is item 18982, a ramp: no container, so the engine drops no loot into it, and it looks like a way
down. The engine also runs the death event before it drops the loot, so the item count `bossDeath` read there was 0 for
every corpse (every island and raid pocket got the personal roll on top of a full corpse). `bossDeath` now records the
corpse's position and id; `settleCorpse` reads it again in `success()`, one tick later: a container's real item count
decides `K.needsFallbackLoot`, and a corpse that is no container is taken away and the run gets the personal roll
(`tests/pocketboss_test.lua`: the ramp corpse, and a corpse filled after the death event).

**API.** `ChaosPocketBoss.bosses()` -> `{{key, name, minLevel}}` (every pocket boss);
`ChaosPocketBoss.addCharges(player, bossKey, n)` -> added, reason (bonus charges, capped as above; the online-time shop);
`ChaosPocketBoss.charges(player, key)`, `.view(player)`, `.isInside(player)`, `.lootMultOf(monster)`,
`.isWorldBoss(monster)`, `.noteEvent(player, key)`. Staff: `/pocketboss` (open pockets), `/pocketboss charges, <name>,
<key>, <n>`, `/pocketboss reset, <name>`, `/pocketboss end`.

**Anti-abuse.** Charges live on the server and are written before the teleport; the opcode actions are rate limited
(`requestMs`, `ChaosRateLimit` key `pocketboss`) and take only a string key of at most 48 bytes; the pockets are
instances (no Town Portal or hideout way in, intruders swept out); the re-entry cooldown; no stacking with the event
hour; logout and death never refund.

**Level of the boss (O177).** The boss is created with an explicit level (`K.bossLevel`, `Chaos.spawnLevel`), shown after
its name; without it the bar showed the estimate of the species ("Lv 10182" for Kaelgor). World pocket: the world boss
entry level (`Chaos.worldBoss.minLevel`, 300; the corpse is fixed at the world boss item level, so the monster level
does not move the drop). Island and raid pockets: the level the drops already use (`ChaosLoot.typeLevel`: the bounty
pool's hunting level, else the estimate), at least the pocket's entry level and at most 2200, so the number shown is
the one the item level is rolled at. Display only: health (the pocket's factor), damage and loot are unchanged; the
monster damage layer reads the engine level (`MD.levelOf`), not the display level.

**Tests.** `tests/pocketboss_test.lua` (luajit and lua5.3): the list from the real configs, charges and the reset, bonus
caps, refunds, the entry and party checks, scaling, the world reward rates over 20,000 rolls, no stacking, personal loot
eligibility and rolls, the grid; then `pocketboss.lua` against a mocked engine: solo and party pockets (each member pays,
the one without charges stays), the kill (tokens, experience, loot factor), logout without refund, the lethal-hit catch, a
restart refund, the event blocking its pocket, the island boss's personal loot. `tests/opcode_fuzz_test.lua` fuzzes the
`pocket*` actions through the Boss Spawns handler. Client: `game_bossspawns/bossspawnsview_test.lua` (the button). Not
run against a live server: the island and raid bosses' health and damage scaling are guesses until measured (their XML
lives in the base data).

**Island reward (O142, beta 2026-10-23: "the second section only gives the cards as reward, and the cards did not work").**
The island bosses' corpse is the stock loot table x `lootMult` 0.6, where the sure items were cards. Now every player at an
island kill also gets `islandReward` (`pocketboss_config.lua`, `K.islandReward`, `islandRewardOf` in `pocketboss.lua`):
Orb of Upheaval x2 and Orb of Fate x1 (x0.6, rounded at random) and 2 picks of a weighted pool: a piece of the boss's own
loot table gear (Magic or Rare, kill item level; skipped when the table has none), a deck card (tier 40/30/20/10), Mythic
Essence, Legendary Abyssal or Ancestral Essence, Orb of Upheaval, crystal coins. Cards are about a sixth of the picks. A
failure is logged and never blocks the kill. The Item Finder lists the items (`pocketisland`). Tests: `K.islandReward`
weights and skips, an island pocket kill. Gear comes from the existing table, so `loot_model` and `gear_coverage` do not move.

## Map markers (`partymarkers.lua`, `poi.lua` and their `_core` / `_config` files, `tools/gen_poi.py`, `sql/chaos_poi.sql`, client `game_mapmarkers`)

Markers on the minimap and on the full map (the same minimap widget, Ctrl+Shift+M): where the other party members are,
and the points of interest. One opcode, **153** (`ChaosOpcodes.mapMarkers`), JSON `{action, data}`, shared by the two
scripts: the client sends `hello {party, poi}` at login and `set {party}` / `set {poi}` when an option changes; each
script answers its own part. Client: `client/overlay/modules/game_mapmarkers/` (view rules in `markermath.lua`, tested by
`markermath_test.lua`), art from `client/tools/gen_mapmarker_art.py`. Settings: top menu Hunt > More > Map Markers
(party members on / off, points of interest on / off, one check box per category; g_settings node `mapMarkers`).

### Party members (`partymarkers.lua`, `partymarkers_core.lua`, `partymarkers_config.lua`)
- **What is sent.** To every party member whose client asked for markers ("watcher"): `party {m = [{i, n, x, y, z, p}]}`,
  every member it may see with its name, position, floor and health in 10% steps (0 only when dead, never 100 when
  hurt), the viewer included (the client leaves itself out, so one list serves the whole party and is encoded once per
  party). Far members and members on other floors are listed too: the minimap can be scrolled and the client draws an
  up / down triangle. An empty list clears the markers (left the party, party disbanded).
- **When.** A tick every `tickMs` (1 s) looks at the parties that have a watcher; a watcher is sent a list only when it
  differs from the last one it got (`P.plan`: positions, floors, health steps, who is in the party, the leader order).
  Joining, leaving, a disbanded party, a member logging in or out are seen by the next tick (at most 1 s later: the base
  party events live in the base data and are not hooked). The hello at login and switching the option on are answered at
  once (`P.sendNow`). Nothing is sent to clients without the module or with the option off.
- **Who sees whom** (`P.visibleTo`). A member in ghost mode (invisible staff) is listed to nobody. A member inside a
  battleground match has the scope `bg:<match>:<team>` and is listed only to watchers of the same match and team, so a
  match's positions stay inside its team; members outside are listed to everyone of the party. The Scorched Marches and
  the battleground have no other privacy rule: party members stay allies in the Marches, and the battleground keeps
  parties whole on one team, so enemies are never in the same party.
- **Throttle** (`P.tick`). At most `maxPartiesPerTick` (300) parties are read and `maxSendsPerTick` (600) messages sent
  per tick; the next tick goes on after the last party handled (round robin), so a crowded server spreads the work over
  a few ticks instead of stalling one.
- **Cost.** Unit benchmark (`tests/partymarkers_test.lua`, 100 parties of 4, the core plus a JSON-like encode, LuaJIT):
  0.5 ms per tick when nothing moved, 1.5 to 1.9 ms when every member moved (400 messages, about 200 bytes each, about
  80 KB per tick). Live (TFS built with src-patches 0001-0026, full map, 395 bots in 98 parties of 4 walking a step every
  second, on a shared 4-core machine with a load of 13): a tick that finds nothing changed takes 2.5 ms (reading 392
  members through the engine), one that re-sends all 392 lists 13 to 14 ms; the sends dominate (about 30 us each, the
  `NetworkMessage` of `extended_opcode.lua`), so `maxSendsPerTick` = 600 caps a tick near 20 ms.
- **Client.** A pin per member in a party colour (a member keeps its colour while it stays; a newcomer takes the
  lowest free one), tinted from one white image; an up or down triangle when the member is on another floor than the
  one shown; outside the shown part of the map the pin becomes an arrow on the edge pointing toward the member (8
  directions, kept clear of the minimap window's zoom and floor controls). The markers glide to the new place in
  0.8 s (a jump for a teleport or a floor change). Hover: "Name, 80% health, 2 floors up, 140 squares north-east". The
  markers never take the mouse (clicks, drags and the wheel stay the minimap's); the hover text comes from a hit test
  in the minimap's mouse move. No screen-edge indicator on the game view: the edge arrows of the minimap cover it, and
  the game view's tile geometry would need the probing that `game_mapoverlay` does.

### Points of interest (`poi.lua`, `poi_core.lua`, `poi_config.lua`, `data/chaos_poi.lua`, `sql/chaos_poi.sql`)
- **Data.** `tools/gen_poi.py SERVER_DIR` (install step `poi`, after `towns`, `npcnames` and `worldtexts`, which rename
  what it reads) writes `data/chaos_poi.lua` from the installed server: temples (the map's towns, named from
  `tools/base_towns.csv`), depots (the map's depot lockers: lockers within 30 tiles on one floor, at least 4), the base
  crafting tables (action ids 38820-38826; three or more within 20 tiles are a "Crafting hall"), the service NPCs of the
  spawn file (travel, bank, blessings, shop, by their NPC file and script), hunting areas (the bounty pool's monsters at
  the busiest spots of the bestiary spawn data, spots within 40 tiles merged, the level band from the middle 70% of the
  spawn entries (printed as the **hunting level**, the pool level times `pace_config.lua` `baseLevelMult`, since 2026-10-27; `baseLevelMult` is 1 since 2026-10-28, O285, so the pool level: "Terror Bird (level 20-30)"; `gen_poi.py` reads the multiplier, `data/chaos_poi.lua` was halved back with the reverse transform and is byte-identical to its state before O272), at least 12 entries, the 300 biggest) and the island, raid and lair bosses of `bossspawns_config.lua`.
  Every name is checked against the rename lists (sha256 of each phrase); a mark that would still carry an old-world
  name is left out. The committed `server/data/chaos_poi.lua` is the output for the shipped map (800 marks: 20 temples,
  45 depots, 4 crafting halls, 27 banks, 19 blessings, 63 travel, 272 shops, 50 bosses, 300 hunting areas);
  `tools/gen_poi_test.py` (CI) builds a small map and checks the generator. At runtime `poi.lua` adds what the systems
  place at startup (found 20 s after the start and every 5 minutes, `poi_config.lua`): the Chaos NPCs within 12 tiles
  of a temple (Material Broker, the Gambler, the Keeper of Trials, the Ascendant Oracle, the faction quartermasters),
  the Chaos NPCs in the stalls of the hub (`npc_booths_config.lua`, looked for `hubRadius` = 1 tile around each stall; the
  temple scan cannot reach them, the stalls are about 700 tiles away; fixed 2026-10-28: before, the 16 hub NPCs had no
  mark; `P.hubMarks`, name from `npcs` else the NPC's own),
  the portals there by action id (hideout, guild hall, the Ember Descent, the Ashen Sepulchre, the Ember Gate, the world
  boss and siege portals while they stand) and the dungeons of the base dungeon system at their entry point. On the
  shipped map: 90 runtime marks. The Marches, the battleground, rifts, the arena and the tower have no place on the map
  (they are entered from their windows), so they have no mark.
- **Discovery.** Known from the start (`r = 0`): temples, depots, crafting, the Chaos NPCs, the portals next to the
  temples and the shops, banks, travel and blessing NPCs within 80 tiles of a temple. Discovered (`r = 1`): hunting
  areas, boss places, dungeons and the service NPCs out in the world, when the character comes within 20 tiles on the
  same floor (checked every 2 s for every online character, also with the option off, so turning it on later shows what
  was found), with "Discovered on your map: ..." and the new marker. Why: a new character needs the town services at
  once, while the hunting grounds and lairs are worth finding; a first-kill rule would miss the areas you only pass
  through, and the distance rule needs no hook in the kill path. The discoveries are one row per character in
  `chaos_poi_seen` (keys of 10 characters, a kind letter and the position in hex, comma-separated: about 6 KB with every
  mark found), read at login, written at most every minute and at logout. A key names a place, so regenerating the data
  keeps the discoveries of the places that stayed. Staff: `/poi status | reset | all | rescan`.
- **What is sent.** At the hello: `poi {v, marks = [{k, x, y, z, n}]}` (what is known: about 330 marks, 25 KB, through
  `Chaos.sendChunked`); then `reveal {marks}` for each discovery. Undiscovered marks are never sent.
- **Cost.** The reveal check looks only at the marks of the 3 x 3 cells of 32 tiles around each character: 2.2 ms per
  check of about 400 characters on the live test (every 2 s); the unit test checks 1000 characters in about 7 ms.
- **Client.** One 14 px icon per kind (temple, depot, bank, npc, shop, travel, bless, craft, guild, portal, boss, dungeon,
  hunt) on the shown floor, only inside the shown area (at most 160, nearest first), under the party markers; the name
  on hover. Categories: temples, depots and banks / Chaos NPCs / shops, travel and blessings / crafting / guild hall /
  entrances and portals / dungeons / boss places / hunting areas.
- **Tested** on a live test server (full map, committed src-patches 0001-0026, private MariaDB) with two clients and a
  bot in a party, and 395 bots for the cost: pins, the floor triangle after a teleport to another floor, the edge arrow
  for a member 600 tiles east with its hover text, the full map view, leave and disband clearing the markers, the
  option off and on, a hunting area discovered on approach with the message, the discoveries kept over a relog, a
  category switched off. Screenshots were taken but are not in the repository.

## Party Finder (`party_finder.lua`, `party_finder_core.lua`, `party_finder_config.lua`, client `game_partyfinder`)

Looking-for-group window, Social > Party Finder (opcode **208**). A leader posts a listing; others browse it, apply with
a role, and the leader accepts (a real party invite) or declines.

**Listing.** Activity: Rift (tier range, max from `rift_config.lua` `maxTier`), Dungeon (from `Chaos.dungeons.extra`),
World Boss (`Chaos.worldBoss.bosses`), Omen (the guardians of `rift_config.lua` `omen.kinds`), Infinity Tower (floor
range), Raid, Trial (`trials_config.lua` tiers), Other (a free title). Wanted tank / healer / DPS counts (0-6 each, leader +
party + wanted at most 10; a raid: see below), the leader's own role, minimum level, a note (80 printable characters; bad words become
asterisks, link-like words are cut), expiry (15 / 30 / 60 / 120 min), "auto-accept quick joins". One listing per
character; posting again updates it (ids and applications kept; a role can not drop below the slots already taken).
Only a party leader (or a character without a party) can post.

**Raid listings of 15.** An activity may set its own size and caps (`party_finder_config.lua` `activities`: `maxParty`,
`perRole`, `suggest`). The Raid sets 15 (raid_config.lua `maxPlayers`; `tests/party_finder_test.lua` checks they match),
up to 3 tanks, 4 healers and 12 DPS wanted (the leader's own role comes on top), and the form proposes 2 / 3 / 9 (15 with
the leader). Every other activity keeps 10 and 0-6 per role. The listing stores its size (`L.max`, `K.maxOf`); post,
update (a raid of 12 cannot become a rift) and accept (`partyFull`) check against it, and rows carry `max`; init `acts`
carry `max`, `per` and `suggest`. The engine side needs nothing new: TFS 1.4.2 parties have no member cap (`Party`
holds a plain member list; `invitePlayer` and `joinParty` never count it), and the raid uses one engine party: `raid.lua`
`groupOf` takes the opener's party members within `partyRange` (12 sqm, same floor), up to `maxPlayers`. So the listing's
15 slots are that one party's 15 members; no raid roster is needed. Party frames list up to 20 and wrap a raid of 15.

**Roles.** `party_finder_config.lua` `classRoles`, by vocation id, from docs/CLASSES.md "Roles in a group": tanks are the
Juggernaut, Sentinel and Samurai (and the Warrior and Templar base classes); healers the Illusionist, Iron Sage, Sentinel
and the Mystic base class; everyone may play DPS except the Sentinel. The first role is the class's main role, used for
party members who joined without a listing slot. Applications and posts are checked against the character's real class.

**Flow.** Apply (one role, the level, a free slot of that role; at most 5 open applications per character and 20 per
listing; 120 s before a declined character may apply again to the same listing). The leader gets a toast, a console line
and a badge (on the Social menu, the menu entry and the My Group tab), also with the window closed. Accept takes the slot,
withdraws the character's other applications and sends `party:addInvite` (a party is started with `Party(leader)` when
needed); the invited player has 90 s to join, else the slot opens again. Every 2 s a GlobalEvent compares each listing with
the engine party: joined (slot filled), left (slot opens), and the listing closes when every slot has joined (full),
when it expires, when the leader logs out, is no longer the party leader, or the party broke up after members joined.
Applicants of a closed listing are told. "Join as" (quick join) puts a character in a queue (30 min) for the oldest listing
with its role open, its level, realm and the chosen activity; the match is an application marked "quick", or a direct
invite when the listing auto-accepts.

**Seasons and staff.** A listing carries its leader's realm (`ChaosSeason.realmOf` while a season runs): it is shown to and
joinable by its own realm only, like the season's party rule (`season.lua` onJoin, `ChaosSeason.partyAllowed`). Staff
(group >= 4, the season's `exemptGroup`) see every realm and can close any listing (`unlist {id}`).

**State.** In memory only (`ChaosPartyFinder.state`): listings are transient and a restart clears them. No storage keys,
no table. Rate limits: `ChaosRateLimit` 800 ms for open / refresh, 400 ms for every other action, plus 20 s between two new
listings and 3 s between two updates of one character.

**Protocol (JSON {action, data}).** Client `open`, `hide`, `refresh`, `post {a, lo, hi, t, title, want, minLevel, note, exp,
role, auto}`, `unlist {id?}`, `apply {id, role}`, `withdraw {id}`, `accept {id, g}`, `decline {id, g}`, `queue {role, a}`,
`unqueue`. Server `init {acts, roles, my, lv, exp, defExp, lim}`, `list {rows, mine, badge, applied, queue}` (pushed to open
windows on every change, `Chaos.sendChunked`), `badge {n}`, `notice {text, kind}`.

**Opcode.** 208 is free in the reference server (its opcodes: "Opcode collision check"), in every Chaos script and in every
client module of the reference client (checked by grep for `sendExtendedOpcode`, `registerExtended*Opcode` and opcode
constants); `tests/party_finder_test.lua` checks that no two `ChaosOpcodes` share a number.

**Tests.** `tests/party_finder_test.lua` (luajit and lua5.3): roles of every class, the activities from the real configs,
the note filter, every post / apply / decide refusal, the reconcile cases, realms and staff, the queue, the payloads, and
`party_finder.lua` against a mocked engine (post, apply, toast and badge, decline, accept with the party invite, join,
quick join, full, staff close, logout); raid listings of 15 (sizes and role caps, a crew counting against 15, 14
accepts, the 16th refused, full at 15, an update to a rift refused). Client: `game_partyfinder/partyfinderview_test.lua`
(limits per activity, the slot grid: 15 boxes wrap into 8 + 7). The 15-slot raid listing was rendered offline too. The window was rendered in
the Linux client with payloads built by the core (offline); not run against a live server.

## Anti-bot and player reports (`antibot.lua`, `antibot_core.lua`, `antibot_config.lua`, `reports.lua`, `reports_core.lua`, `sql/chaos_reports.sql`, `tools/patch_report_chat.py`, client `game_antibot`)

Extended opcode **211** (`ChaosOpcodes.antibot`; free: not in the base server's list under "Opcode collision check", not
used by any Chaos module, `tests/antibot_test.lua` checks both). Storages 7100890 - 7100899 (`Chaos.storage.antibot`:
+0 last presence check, +1 its day, +2 checks that day, +3 grace until, +4 score x 10). Tables `chaos_reports`,
`chaos_antibot_log`, `chaos_antibot_holds` (`sql/chaos_reports.sql`; the scripts also create them at startup).
**Nothing here bans or punishes on its own.** The detection asks for a presence check and writes a staff log; staff decide.
The client base had its bot, cavebot and script modules removed already (client base patch 0015); there was no
anti-cheat or player report feature on the server before this (the base server's `Player:onReportRuleViolation` now
lands in `chaos_reports` too, reason "other").

### Behaviour detection (`antibot_core.lua`, numbers in `antibot_config.lua`)

Per online character a few bounded ring buffers, filled by cheap hooks; staff (group >= 4) are never sampled.

| Signal | Samples (hook) | 0 (human) .. 1 (bot) |
|---|---|---|
| timing | per kind of action (each spell id from the spell events of engine patch 0008, own heals from `healthchange`): the intervals, at most 32 per kind, 8 kinds. A cast within 150 ms of its spell / group cooldown ending (a held hotkey, from the engine's `onSpellCooldown`) gives no interval; own heals without the events: intervals within 120 ms of a multiple of 1 s are left out | robust spread 1.4826 x MAD / median of the most regular kind: >= 0.15 -> 0, <= 0.05 -> 1 (20 intervals needed) |
| reaction | an own heal with no own heal in the 2.5 s before it, within 1.5 s of a hit taken: its latency (server side, so ping included), 24 kept | share under 250 ms (0.5 -> 0, 0.9 -> 1) times tightness (standard deviation 90 ms -> 0, 40 ms -> 1); 10 needed |
| loop | position every 2 s (`GlobalEvent`), 8 x 8 tile cells per floor, only cell changes, none while fighting (a hit or an action in the last 4 s), 192 kept | for each step between two cells the distance back to its last occurrence; the share of repeated steps that come back after about 1, 2 or 3 laps of the most common lap (4 - 60 steps, at least 5 cells, at least 40% of the steps repeated): 0.7 -> 0, 0.92 -> 1. Runs at most every 5 minutes |
| loot | items moved by hand out of a corpse into the inventory (`EventCallback onItemMoved`): the gaps inside one looting burst (< 2.5 s), 32 kept | CV >= 0.22 -> 0, <= 0.08 -> 1 (16 needed) |
| nonstop | activity minutes (any action, move, loot); a streak ends after 20 minutes without activity or offline | one streak 8 h -> 0, 14 h -> 1; or active hours in the last 24: 18 -> 0, 22 -> 1 |

**Score.** Every 60 s per character: `score = score x 0.5^(60 s / 60 min) + sum(weight x signal)`, weights timing 1.2,
reaction 1.2, loop 0.8, loot 0.8, nonstop 0.6; when fewer than two signals are at 0.5 or more, the add is multiplied by
0.35. The steady score of a constant add is about 87 x add, so **one signal alone, even at 1, stays at most near 37**,
under every threshold (a human with one odd habit: a fixed route, very long sessions, fast reflexes). Thresholds:
**60** asks for a presence check, **120** writes a `score` entry in `chaos_antibot_log` (again after 6 h or when the score
doubled). Online staff get a console line for every log entry.

**Cost.** Memory: about 300 numbers and short strings per online character, kept 30 minutes after logout (a relog keeps
the stats; a restart clears them, the score survives in a storage). CPU: one `getPosition` per character every 2 s, a
table write per hook event, one evaluation per character per minute (rings of at most 32 numbers per kind; the loop
search, at most every 5 minutes, is one pass over 192 cells with a table lookup each). The healthchange event on every
character is one more Lua call per hit or heal.

### The presence check (client `game_antibot`)

A small modal: "Click the picture of: Fishing Rod" and four item pictures (stock items, `check.pool`: food, tools,
weapons, potions; two of one group, like Bag and Backpack, never together), positions shuffled. The client gets client
ids and random keys only; which key is right stays on the server, and the client has no item names. 75 s
(`timeLimitSeconds`), the bar counts down. **Accessibility:** one retry: a wrong click shows a new picture (at least 45 s
more), or "Another picture" before choosing. A pass multiplies the score by 0.4 and starts an 8 h grace; a failure (wrong
twice or no answer) adds 40 and runs `failAction`: `"log"` (default) or `"temple"`; never a kick (see "Bot detection"),
always with a `check_fail` log entry. **Never during PvP or boss fights:** a hit from or on a player in the last 60 s
(also summons, also a PZ lock or a player as target), a hit from or on a boss in the last 45 s (the boss points list,
the world bosses, `MonsterType:isBoss()`), or a rift run in progress defer it; a check deferred 30 minutes is dropped.
**Rate limits:** at least 4 h between two checks, at most 2 a day per character. Logging out during a check is no
failure: it comes again after the next login. Staff: `/reports check <name>` sends one at once (for tests).

### Player reports (`reports.lua`, `reports_core.lua`)

Report Player (right-click a player or System > Report a Player; no spoken command, see "Player commands: the menu"): name, reason (botting, cheating /
exploiting, harassment, scam, offensive name, other) and a note (200 characters; "other" needs one). The server checks
the name (online or offline character, not staff, not yourself), the reporter's level (8+) and the limits: 60 s between
two reports, 5 a day per account, one report per target per 24 h. The row: reporter, target, reason, note, the target's
position when online (else the reporter's; `target_online` says which), time, the target's suspicion score and its last
10 lines in **public channels only** (World Chat, English Chat, Advertising, Help; `tools/patch_report_chat.py` adds one
line to those channel scripts; private messages and the default local chat are never read). The lines live in memory and
leave 30 minutes after the target's logout. Optional Discord webhook: `reports.discordWebhook` is empty in the repository;
set the environment variable `CHAOS_REPORTS_WEBHOOK` (only `https://discord.com/api/webhooks/...` URLs; the post carries
the report id, reason and the two names, never chat or note; sent with `curl` in the background).

**Leaderboards.** `log.holdLeaderboards = true` (off by default): a `score` or `check_fail` entry holds the account in
`chaos_antibot_holds` until staff clear it; held accounts are left out of the weekly boards and their titles / orbs
(`leaderboard.lua`), the class ladder, the season ladder (`season.lua`) and the website boards. Switching it off again:
clear the open holds too (`/reports clear <name>` or `UPDATE chaos_antibot_holds SET cleared_at = UNIX_TIMESTAMP()`),
the website does not read the flag.

### Staff guide

1. **New report:** online staff see `[Report #12] A reported B: botting. /reports show 12`. In game: `/reports` (open
   reports), `/reports list closed|all`, `/reports show <id>` (note, position, public chat lines). The admin panel has
   the same under Accounts & Security (Player reports, Show report, Close report, Anti-bot log, Anti-bot score); the
   website has `page.php?plugin=chaos&p=reports` for the admin accounts (filters, close / note / reopen, the anti-bot log).
2. **Look before deciding:** `/reports score <name>` shows the score and each signal with its numbers (`timing 1.00 cv
   0.006` = an action at a fixed delay; `reaction 1.00 fast 1.00 sd 6` = heals within a few ms of every hit; `loop 0.95
   period 43` = the same 43-cell route again and again; `loot 1.00 cv 0.02`; `nonstop streak 16.2h`). `/reports log
   <name>` lists its log entries (scores, checks passed / failed). One signal alone is never evidence; a failed check
   can be someone who stepped away.
3. **Watch** the character, talk to it, `/reports check <name>` for a fresh presence check.
4. **Decide** with the normal staff tools (admin panel: kick, ban, notes), then `/reports close <id>, <what you
   found>`. `/reports clear <name>` resets the score and lifts a leaderboard hold after a review that found nothing.

### Bug reports

System > Report a Bug in the client (the base `game_bugreport` dialog: Map, Typo, Technical, Other and a text) sends
the engine's bug report packet; the engine calls `Player:onReportBug(message, position, category)` of the base
`data/events/scripts/player.lua`. That function handed it to the stock callback
(`scripts/eventcallbacks/player/default_onReportBug.lua`), which returned at once for a normal account
(`ACCOUNT_TYPE_NORMAL`: no message, nothing stored) and wrote text files under `data/reports/bugs/` for tutors and up.
The base client also lost the text (its Lua passed three values to a one-string binding, so the category digit was
sent as the text); client base patch 0040 sends the category, the text and, for a map report, the position.

- **Install:** `tools/patch_base_events.py` step 12 (`install_all.py` step `events`) puts `ChaosReports.onReportBug`
  first in `Player:onReportBug` (marker comment, idempotent; the stock path still runs when `reports.lua` is missing).
- **What is stored** (`reports.lua` `RP.submitBug`, pure part `reports_core.lua`): a `chaos_reports` row with reason
  `bug`, reporter and target = the character, note `[category] text` (control characters folded, non-ASCII removed, at
  most `bugs.textMax` = 240 characters; the player is told when it was shortened), the position (the reported tile of
  a map report, else the character's), the time, and in `chat` the details: category, the character's position, the
  reported tile, level and class. Every account type may report.
- **Limits** (`antibot_config.lua` `reports.bugs`): fewer than 6 characters is refused (also what a client without
  patch 0040 sends); `Chaos.limited` one per character every 5 s; per account 30 s apart and 10 a day (kept over a
  relog). Each refusal tells the player why.
- **Player answer:** "Thank you. Your bug report #15 was sent to the staff." (or the reason it was refused). The client
  also shows its own "Bug report sent." line.
- **Staff:** online staff see `[Bug #15] Name (map) at x, y, z. /reports show 15`; `/reports list bugs` lists the open
  ones; `/reports show` shows the text, position and details; the admin panel's Player reports has the filter "Bug
  reports (open)"; the website staff page has the reason "Bug report". The reports webhook (`CHAOS_REPORTS_WEBHOOK`)
  gets "New bug report #15 (map) from Name at x, y, z." (never the text). Close them like player reports.
- **Suggestions:** category `suggestion` (4 in `R.bugCategories`; a client that sends 4 is accepted). The base
  dialog (`game_bugreport`, not in this repository) has only Map, Typo, Technical and Other and patch 0040 clamps the
  category to 0..3, so a player writes `suggestion:` (or `sugestao:` / `sugestão:`, any case) at the start of the text in
  "Other"; `R.suggestionPrefix` strips it and the note becomes `[suggestion] text`. A map report keeps its category.
- **Reading them (owner):** `chaos-ctl.sh feedback [--days N] [--all] [--category C] [--names]` prints the open bug
  reports and suggestions of the last N days (default 30) as plain text, newest first, max 200: `#id | date UTC |
  category | open | pos x,y,z | lvl N class`, the text indented below (closed ones with the staff note under `--all`).
  `feedback-close ID [NOTE]` closes one open report with a staff note. The admin app has the card Painel > Bugs e
  sugestões (docs/ADMIN_APP.md) with "Copiar tudo" to paste the list to Claude. Safety: the query is fixed text with a
  checked number of days and one category word from a fixed list; it never selects an account id, IP or e-mail, and the
  character name only with `--names` (the app never passes it); `server/tools/feedback_format.py` strips control and
  format characters and caps the text; `feedback-close` takes a digits-only id and sends the note as a hex literal built
  from sanitised text (no quote or backslash can reach the SQL). Tests: `server/deploy/chaos_ctl_test.py`
  (`test_feedback`), `android/app/src/test/java/com/cindersofchaos/admin/FeedbackInfoTest.java`.
- **Tests:** `tests/bugreport_test.lua` (validation, categories, the cap, positions, limits, staff lines, webhook,
  `RP.onReportBug` with a normal account against a mocked engine, `/reports list bugs`, the patch tool on the stock
  function and the patched function's dispatch); `website/tests/chaos_reports_page_test.php` (the bug filter).

### Protocol (JSON `{action, data}` on 211)

- server -> client: `check {t, w, o = [{k, c}], s, a, r}` (token, word, options with key and client id, seconds left,
  attempt, retries left), `checkResult {ok, retry, text}`, `reportOpen {name, reasons = [{k, n}], noteMax}`,
  `reportResult {ok, text}`
- client -> server: `answer {t, k}`, `another {t}`, `reportOpen {name}`, `report {name, reason, note}` (rate limited)

### Tests and checks

`tests/antibot_test.lua` (luajit and lua5.3, about 2700 checks): helpers, each signal on small traces (fixed rhythm,
held hotkey left out, instant reactions, heal trains, a 10-cell loop, walking between two cells, a 15 h streak and a
break), the single-signal bound, the decisions (PvP / boss deferral, drop after 30 min, gap, grace, daily limit, log
cooldown), the pictures (200 challenges: four distinct, groups apart, the payload without words or the answer), answer /
retry / fail / timeout, reports (validation, limits, chat lines and their expiry, webhook URL and body), and
`antibot.lua` + `reports.lua` against a mocked engine (login, healthchange, cooldown-aware casts, loot moves, a check
passed, a check unanswered -> temple + log + staff told, logout during a check, report rows with the public lines,
refusals, `/reports close`, leaderboard filtering). Synthetic traces (a position every 2 s, fights, hits,
heals, attack spells, looting, an evaluation every minute) with the real config:

| Trace | Runs | Reached the check | Highest score |
|---|---|---|---|
| normal human, 6 h | 24 | 0 | 0.2 |
| heal-spamming tryhard (held hotkeys), 6 h | 16 | 0 | 0.4 |
| fast reflexes on a 15 ms ping, 6 h | 16 | 0 | 19 |
| human walking one fixed circle (loop at 1.0 alone), 6 h | 12 | 0 | 24 |
| 14 h grinder with breaks | 8 | 0 | 0.3 |
| bot: fixed delays, instant heals, waypoint loop, 6 h | 12 | 12 (median 24 min) | 336 |
| bot with fixed loot timing, 6 h | 6 | 6 (median 23 min) | 333 |
| bot with jittered attack and loot timing, 16 h | 6 | 6 (median 59 min, by reactions + loop + nonstop) | 216 |

`luajit tests/antibot_test.lua -v` prints this table with the signals of the worst run of each trace. Client:
`game_antibot/antibot_logic_test.lua`. Website: `website/tests/chaos_reports_page_test.php`.

**Not verified on a live server** (no TFS in this environment): the hooks' real event rates, `onItemMoved` with corpse
containers, `MonsterType:isBoss()`, the channel scripts after `patch_report_chat.py` (checked on a copy of the base
scripts: patched, idempotent, `luac -p` clean), the webhook post. The synthetic traces are models, not recordings:
real false-positive rates have to be watched in the log after launch (raise `check.at` or lower a weight if needed). A
careful bot with human-like random delays on every signal is not caught by this; reports and staff are the answer there.

## Moderation record purge (`moderation_purge.lua`, `moderation_purge_core.lua`, `moderation_purge_config.lua`)

The Privacy Policy (docs/legal/privacy.*.md section 4) keeps reports, bug reports, anti-cheat and staff logs for
`[PRAZO DOS REGISTROS DE MODERAÇÃO]`. This job keeps that promise: once a day it deletes rows older than
`days.<table>` of `moderation_purge_config.lua` (default 730 for each; 0 = never purged) from `chaos_reports`,
`chaos_antibot_log`, `chaos_antibot_holds` and `chaos_admin_log`. **Set `days` to the period the owner writes in the
policy** (docs/legal/README.md "Placeholders"); the test checks the policy still names the placeholder or the number.

- **Kept, whatever their age:** an open report (a closed one counts from `closed_at`); an uncleared hold (a cleared one
  counts from `cleared_at`); every row about an account whose ban is active (base `account_bans`, `expires_at` 0 =
  permanent) or ended less than `appealDays` (30) ago (`account_bans` rows not yet moved, `account_ban_history`), so an
  appeal on Discord still has its evidence: reports on that account's characters, its anti-bot log and holds, admin log
  lines whose target is one of its characters, its account name or id; the `security.ip_ban` admin log line of an IP ban
  that is active or ended less than `appealDays` ago.
- **When:** a globalevent looks every `checkSeconds` (1 h) and runs when `runEverySeconds` (1 day) passed since the last
  run (`server_config` row `chaos_moderation_purge`), so the daily restart neither skips nor repeats it. Rows are read
  in id order, `batch` (500) at a time, at most `maxBatches` (200) per table and run, and deleted by id; a report
  reopened or a hold set again between the read and the delete stays. The console gets one line:
  `[Chaos moderation purge] reports 3 deleted, 5 kept; ... (2 accounts protected by a ban)`.
- **Not touched:** the base ban tables and `players.lastip` (docs/legal/README.md "Check" 2), mutes (not stored).
- **Install:** nothing beyond the revscripts folder; the tables exist from `sql/chaos_reports.sql` and
  `sql/chaos_admin.sql`.
- **Tests:** `tests/moderation_purge_test.lua` (config, due check, cutoffs, every keep rule, the SQL, then the engine
  file on an in-memory database: a full run over batches, no second run the same day, the appeal window running out,
  a table at 0 days, a bad config deleting nothing). **Not run on a live server** (no MySQL here): the queries use
  `UNION`, `LEFT JOIN` and `IN` lists only.

## Shadow mute (`shadow_mute.lua`, `shadow_mute_core.lua`, `tools/patch_shadow_mute.py`)

Staff panel actions `players.shadow_mute` (player, 1-1440 minutes) and `players.shadow_unmute` (admin panel, group 4+, in
the admin log like the other Players actions). A shadow-muted character keeps seeing its own lines in the PUBLIC chat
channels (`public="1"` in `chatchannels.xml`), but nobody else does, and it gets no message, so a spammer does not switch
account. `patch_shadow_mute.py` (install step `events`, after `patch_report_chat.py`, idempotent) adds one hook to the top of
each public channel's `onSpeak`; the line goes back to the speaker with `Player:sendChannelMessage`.
Limits, stated plainly: say, yell, whisper and private messages are engine paths with no Lua hook, so they are not covered
(use the plain Mute, `CONDITION_MUTED`, for those); the mute lives in memory and a restart clears it; the hook runs before the
report hook, so a muted character's lines are not kept for reports while it is muted. No player commands.
**Tests:** `tests/shadow_mute_test.lua` (state, caps, expiry, list, the patch tool on a copy of a channel script and its
idempotence) and the shadow mute block of `tests/admin_panel_test.lua`. Not run on a live server.

## Absorb ceiling (engine `src-patches/0049-absorb-ceiling.patch`)

Owner decision 2026-10-20: one global ceiling of **75 percent** absorb per combat type, in the engine. Before it, nothing
capped the sum: the passive tree stopped at `maxAbsorb = 80` for its own share only and equipment added on top, so one
element could pass 100 percent.

- **Where absorb is taken off today (three layers):** (1) `Player::blockHit`: the item abilities (`absorbPercent`), each one
  applied to what the previous left; (2) after it, the base event `rarity_onHealthChangeAbsorb`
  (`data/scripts/customs/rarity/rarity_onCombat_absorbs.lua`): the SUM of two storages per type, 977544-977553 / 977572 /
  977574 (gear rarity rolls) and 977562-977575 (passive tree and Paragon, `passivetree_effects.lua`), no cap.
- **The patch:** in `Player::blockHit` (`player.cpp`) the equipment part is raised back so that equipment and the storages
  together never remove more than `CHAOS_ABSORB_CEILING_PERCENT` (75, **the one place to change it**). The storages are read
  with `Player::getStorageValue` (a fixed table of the 12 types), so equipment may take at most `25 / (100 - storage)` of the
  hit; with storages at 75 or more, equipment takes nothing more. Negative absorbs (weakness) are not touched.
- **The base event:** install step `absorbceiling` (`tools/patch_absorb_ceiling.py`, idempotent, keeps CRLF, refuses when the
  expected code is missing; test `tools/patch_absorb_ceiling_test.py`, which runs the patched event against a mock) limits
  the SUM of the storages in `rarity_onCombat_absorbs.lua` to 75 per type, so the engine and the event agree. Without that
  step the event takes the full storage sum after `blockHit`. The tree/Paragon share is also clamped by
  `maxAbsorb` in `passivetree_effects.lua` (**still 80: set it to 75**, together with the "at most 80 percent" texts in
  `passivetree_stats_config.lua` lines 84-95 and the asserts at `tests/passivetree_stats_test.lua:83` and
  `tests/passivetree_effects_test.lua:39,52`); gear rarity rolls in storage 9775xx are summed with it and can still pass 75
  alone only if a character stacks more than 75 of them, which the item caps (T8 absorb 10-14 per line) make unlikely.
- **Lua side:** `ChaosItemMods.config.absorbCeiling = 75` and `ChaosItemMods.effectiveAbsorb(items, storage)` (the same
  arithmetic as the patch, for tooltips and tools); the Codex text of every absorb modifier says the 75% cap
  (`tools/gen_codex_data.lua`, regenerated `game_codex/codex_data.lua`).
- **Tests:** `tests/absorb_ceiling_test.lua` (the arithmetic, and that the patch constant equals the config).
- **Apply:** after 0001-0048, `patch -p1 < 0049-absorb-ceiling.patch`, then rebuild. A dry run over 0001-0049 on the base
  source applies cleanly; **not compiled**, not run in game.

## Typed impact numbers (engine `src-patches/0051-typed-impact-numbers.patch`, client base patch `0100`, client `game_damagescatter`)

Slice B of the damage number work (slice A: client base patch `0081`, the random shift and speed, no protocol change).
The server now tags every number it shows over the map, so the client can pick a font per kind, let the number float
with its creature and show it as a percent later.

- **Wire layout (0xB4, text message).** For modes 23, 24, 27 (damage dealt / received / others): position, u32 + u8
  (physical value, colour), u32 + u8 (element value, colour), **u16 percent, u8 type, u32 creature id**, string text.
