  For 25, 28 (healed, healed others) and 26, 29 (experience, experience of others): position, u32 + u8,
  **u16 percent, u8 type, u32 creature id**, string text. The same three fields, in the same order, after the pairs and
  before the text, for every mode; one set per message (both numbers of a hit share it). The mode ids are this
  engine's `MessageClasses` and the client's 10.98 table (`protocolcodes.cpp`: 23..29); mana gain and loss travel as
  healed / damage modes (the client's mana mode 43 is never sent; the client reads the fields for it too).
- **Fields.** `percent`: the value as a share of the target's maximum, x100, rounded up (10000 = 100%): health for
  damage and heals, mana for the mana shield, mana drain and mana gain, health for the energy shield, the level's
  experience for an experience gain (0 for a loss and for a summon's experience). `type` (`ChaosImpactType` in
  `const.h`, `Chaos.impactType`, client `DamageScatterLogic.TYPE`): 0 normal, 1 critical (`CombatDamage::critical`, which
  `combat.cpp` sets where it rolls the crit), 2 condition tick (origin `ORIGIN_CONDITION`), 3 mana drain (mana shield,
  mana loss), 4 mana gain, 5 energy shield (patch 0015), 6 and up free for scripts. `creature id`: the target (the healed
  player, the player who gained experience, the summon); every spectator's copy carries it.
- **Condition ticks after a script.** `combatChangeHealth` / `combatChangeMana` run the onHealthChange / onManaChange
  scripts, set `origin` to `ORIGIN_NONE` and call themselves again (so the scripts do not run twice). The patch keeps the
  origin in `CombatDamage::firstOrigin` first, so a tick stays type 2 after any script.
- **A critical hit on a mana shield:** the mana part is type 3, the rest of the hit type 1.
- **Who gets it (compatibility).** Our client sends, in the login packet after its markers, a capability byte; base
  patch `0100` sets bit 7 (`CHAOS_CAPABILITY_IMPACT_TEXT`). Only then `sendFeatures` announces `GameChaosImpactText`
  (155) and `sendTextMessage` writes the three fields. Any other client (the current release client included) gets the
  old layout from the new engine, and the new client gets the old layout from the old engine (it clears 155 before each
  login). So there is **no hard requirement**: the live beta keeps working while the engine and the client are updated
  one after the other, but the new look (crit font, numbers following the creature) needs **both** the new engine
  (`windows-package.yml`, the release package) and the new client. Ship them in the same release.
- **Lua.** `player:sendTextMessage(type, text, pos, value, color, secondaryValue, secondaryColor, percent, typeId,
  creature)`: arguments 9-11 are new (a script number with its own type, e.g. 6 for a script label, attached to a
  monster). Arguments 7 and 8 stay the element pair of this engine, so the new ones come after them (pass `0,
  TEXTCOLOR_NONE` to skip the pair). A creature (or id) that is gone answers false and sends nothing. No Chaos or base
  script sends damage, heal or experience text messages today (checked with grep: the Chaos labels such as "DODGE" go
  through the animated text packet 0x84 in `combat_fx.lua`, `item_powers.lua` and `tile_labels.lua`, untouched), so no
  caller needed a change; any later caller goes through `ProtocolGame::sendTextMessage` and gets the right layout.
- **Display scale** (patch 0037) still scales the values and the text; the percent is a ratio and is not scaled.
- **Tests:** `tests/impact_text_test.lua` reads the engine patch, the client patch, `chaos_constants.lua` and the client
  module and checks the types, the feature ids (155, 156, `LastGameFeature` 157), the capability bit, the field order
  of the writer and of both readers, that the text is read last and that every impact message names its creature.
- **Build:** the engine with patches 0001-0049 and this one was built and linked on Linux (CMake Release, g++ 13, no
  warnings). Not run against a live client yet. Apply after 0001-0050 (0050 is the item lock patch, in flight); rebuild
  everything (TextMessage, CombatDamage and ProtocolGame change layout).

## Terms acceptance notice (`legal_notice.lua`, `legal_notice_core.lua`, `legal_notice_config.lua`)

The website records each acceptance of the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy in `chaos_legal_acceptance` (account, texts'
version, time; no IP): at sign-up and, for accounts without a row for the current version (the beta accounts made
before the checkbox, everyone after the texts change), on `page.php?plugin=chaos&p=accept`, which the site opens before
any other page at the next website login (website/README.md "Legal pages"). The game login cannot be held for a web
form cleanly, so at login (after `delayMs`, 2.5 s) such an account gets two lines (English, Portuguese) and a window
(`Player:popupFYI`) naming that page, at every login until it accepts. Nothing is blocked.

- The current version is the `server_config` row `chaos_legal_version`, written by `website/setup/chaos_setup.php`
  (run by `install_site.sh`) from the installed texts; read again every `cacheSeconds` (300). No row: no notice.
- **Tests:** `tests/legal_notice_test.lua` (version check, SQL, texts with the link, the mocked login: notice, none for an
  accepted account, none without a version, the cache); website `tests/chaos_legal_accept_test.php`.
- **Not verified on a live server:** `Player:popupFYI` (base 1.4 binding; skipped when missing).

## Beta starter coins (`beta.lua`, `beta_core.lua`, `beta_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_beta.sql`)

Owner request (beta only): testers start with 5,000 Chaos Coins so they can try every store feature. One switch,
`Chaos.beta` (`beta_config.lua`): `enabled` (true now; **set it to false on the launch server**, docs/LAUNCH.md section 11)
and `starterCoins` (5000).

- **Once per account.** Chaos Coins belong to the account (`chaos_shop_coins`), so the grant does too. At a character's
  first login (`Player:getLastLoginSaved() == 0`; `firstLoginOnly`) `beta.lua` writes the account's row in
  `chaos_beta_grants` with `INSERT IGNORE` and adds the coins only when that insert made the row (`ROW_COUNT() = 1`).
  A second character, a relog, a restart or two characters logging in at once: no second grant, so alts cannot farm
  coins. A character made before the switch was on gets nothing; its account gets the coins with its next new character.
- The player gets one line (English / pt-BR, `Chaos.t`) after `delayMs` (3 s): these are beta test coins, wiped at launch.
- **Season characters:** the coins go to the account like any other; what a season character may buy with them is the
  season store rule (`season_config.lua` `store`, "Seasons").
- **Payments stay off in the beta** (docs/BETA.md section 4). The coins and everything bought with them are wiped at
  launch: docs/BETA.md section 9 truncates `chaos_shop_coins`, the purchase tables and `chaos_beta_grants`.
- **Tests:** `tests/beta_test.lua` (config, due check, SQL, then the engine on an in-memory table: first character
  granted once, relog, second character, restart, a second account in pt-BR, an older character, beta off, store missing).

## Ascended Omens and the Cinderheart (`uber.lua`, `uber_core.lua`, `uber_config.lua`, `tools/install_ascended.py`)

**Limits** (`uber_config.lua` `limits`, "Instance limits"): the boss's own limit (13 minutes after it appears, the Cinderheart 18) with warnings at 5 min, 1 min and 10 s; time up fails the run (out, the sigil is spent); at most 4 arenas, the wait and the waiting line when all are in use.

The top challenge above the Omen Keys (roadmap item 57): Ascended versions of the three Omen guardians and one final
boss, Ysgrath the Cinderheart. ("uber" is only in the file names; players read "Ascended" and "Cinderheart".) Every
number is in `uber_config.lua`; the pure logic (kinds, the item chain, scaling, the phase machine, enrage, telegraph
shapes and timing, hazards, the caught lethal hit, rewards, the balance model) is `uber_core.lua`, tested with
`uber.lua` against a mocked engine by `tests/uber_test.lua`. No opcode of its own: the run shows on the rift HUD
(opcode 228, `game_rift`). Storages 7100460-7100469 (`Chaos.storage.ascendedRun`). Monsters:
`data/monster/monsters/chaos/ascended/` (registered by the `monsters` step).

- **Access.** Omen guardian kills give every finisher an Ascended Shard of that omen 40% of the time
  (`shardChance.omen`); sealed rifts of tier 13 / 14 / 15 give 4 / 7 / 10% of a shard of a random omen (rift.lua calls
  `ChaosAscended.onRiftSealed` after the Rift Atlas hook; online finishers). Both chances x the party bonus of the
  run (below; 40% -> 60% for a party of 5). Four shards of one omen (use one) bind an
  **Ascended Sigil** of it. The sigil opens that omen's Ascended arena (protection zone, out of combat, level 900, the
  party within 8 sqm comes along, up to 5). Every finisher of an Ascended kill gets that omen's **Ascended Relic**; one
  relic of each omen (use one while carrying all three) binds a **Cinderheart Sigil** (level 1000).
- **Items** (`install_ascended.py`, step `ascended` after `omens`): items.otb copies of stock nodes with new server ids,
  so the client needs no change: shards 32073 / 32074 / 32075 (magma clump, violet and blue crystal shard; stackable),
  the sigil 32076 (soul stone) and the relic 32077 (burning heart), both carrying the custom attribute `ascended_kind`.
  Without the items the actions are not registered and the console says so.
- **The arena.** A runtime-built grid (4 slots, x/y 7600-7700, between the ascension trial grid and the rift grid; the
  footprint must be empty on first use): a 19 x 19 arena and, behind a wall south of it, the antechamber with the
  **Ember Gate** (a portal tile, action id 47411). The dark tile set paints it when installed.
- **Lives.** Shared: Ascended 3 + 1 per extra player, the Cinderheart 2 + 1. A lethal hit is caught (the energy shield
  counts): the player lands in the antechamber, healed, and the run loses a life. The Ember Gate lets the player back
  after 8 s with 3 s in which the arena cannot hurt them. No real death, no loss: the cost is the life and the time.
  The fall that takes the last life ends the run (the sigil is spent).
- **The fight.** The boss comes 8 s after the arrival. Health: the XML's x (1 + healthPerExtraPlayer x (players - 1))
  (1.0 for every boss; was Ascended 0.45, Cinderheart 0.58), adds x (1 + 0.5 x (players - 1)) and one more add per
  player in each wave (so the adds' total health grows about +150% per extra player). The boss's and the adds' hits
  x (1 + 0.10 x (players - 1)) (`party.damagePerExtraPlayer`), times the enrage; telegraphs, hazards and the enrage
  pulse hit a share of the victim's max health and do not scale. **Phases** at health thresholds (Ascended
  100 / 70 / 35%, Cinderheart 100 / 75 / 50 / 25%), each entered once and in order (a big hit through two thresholds
  enters both): a yell, a burst, adds, a hazard. **Telegraphs** every 9-6 s by phase (a random pattern of the phase):
  the tiles are marked at once (warning_zone 451) and one turn later (warning_fill 450), and 2 s after the first mark
  every player still on a marked tile takes 55% of their max health (80%, with only one warning turn of 1 s, when
  enraged). The 3x3 warning pictures go only on tiles whose neighbours are marked too; the edges get a one-tile effect,
  so a safe tile never looks marked. Patterns: cone (towards the target), ring (safe next to the boss and far away),
  circle, marks (under every player: spread out), cross (through the boss), half (one side of the boss), lines (rows /
  columns), eye (everything but a circle round one tile: stack). **Hazards**: blood / burning pools (move every
  18-20 s), storm columns (move every 9-10 s), the creeping dark (the arena edge, one ring deeper every 18-20 s, up to
  3); 7% of max health per second while stood on. **Harvest** (Bloodmoon 35%, the Last Cinder): the boss heals 1%
  (0.5%) of its health per living add every 5 s. **Enrage** at 10:00 (Cinderheart 15:00): boss and add hits x1.75,
  telegraphs twice as often, a pulse of 8% of max health on everyone every 4 s; the arena closes at 14:00 (20:00; 13:00 / 18:00 until 2026-10-13).
- **The bosses.** Ascended Sangrith (Bloodmoon; look 2116; adds Bloodmoon Thrall): Red Night (cone, ring, marks),
  Blood Pools (pools, a thrall wave), Harvest (+cross, thralls every 30 s, the heal). Ascended Morvane (Hollow Crown;
  2117; Hollow Wraith): Empty Throne (cross, circle, half), Wraith Court (wraiths every 35 s), Creeping Dark (+ring, the
  edge). Ascended Thalcyra (Storm; 2118; Storm Shard): Gathering Storm (marks, lines, eye), Storm Columns, Shattered Sky
  (+circle, shards every 30 s). Their XML is the omen's with 1.2M health, hits x1.3, without the omen's untelegraphed
  radius 6 hit, self-heal and invisibility. **Ysgrath the Cinderheart** (its own look 2126, a donor-library creature,
  client/MANIFEST.md "The Cinderheart look"; adds Cinderspawn): Red Night Remembered (the Bloodmoon set + burning pools),
  The Hollow Court, Storm of Cinders (fire columns), The Last Cinder (every pattern, the creeping edge, Cinderspawn, the
  heal). The bosses and adds get no random tier or boss modifiers (`ChaosTierConfig.skip`).
- **Rewards** (per finisher, into the backpack, the rest to the inbox): Ascended 15,000,000 gold to the bank, 20 Orbs of
  Upheaval, 10 Orbs of Fate, 1 Exalted Orb, 4 gear rolls of the boss's loot at the boss tier, 2 rolls (x6 find) over
  the Ascended uniques, the relic; Cinderheart 40,000,000, 40 / 20 / 3, 6 gear rolls, 3 unique rolls (x10 find). The
  corpse loot (loot.lua) comes on top. **Ascended uniques** (`chaos_items.xml` -> `gen_unique_specs.py`,
  `chaos_unique_items.lua` with `ascended = true`, never in a rift or Omen chest): Sanguine Crescent (two-handed sword;
  Sangrith and the Cinderheart), Hollow Crown of Morvane (helmet; Morvane, Cinderheart), Eye of the Unbroken Storm
  (amulet; Thalcyra, Cinderheart), Cinderheart Signet (ring; the Cinderheart only); level 1000. **Achievements**
  (rifts category): Beyond the Omen, one per Ascended Omen, Three Relics (title "the Ascendant", orbs), Cinderbreaker
  (title "Cinderbreaker" with the ember name plate frame, orbs; unlocks the kill effect **Cinderheart Crown**,
  cosmetics id 108), Alone Against the Ember (solo, title "the Last Light"), Not One Spark Lost (no life lost), Keeper
  of the Ashes (10 kills, title "Ashkeeper"). A Cinderheart kill is broadcast.
- **Party bonus** (`uber_config.lua` `party`, `U.party` / `U.reward` in `uber_core.lua`). Every finisher still gets the
  whole spoils and the relic. Gold, orbs (Exalted too) and gear rolls x (1 + 12.5% per extra player, at most +50% at 5
  players), the unique find x (1 + 5% per extra player, at most +20%); the relic stays one. Per kill and finisher:

  | Players | Ascended gold | Upheaval / Fate / Exalted | Cinderheart gold | Upheaval / Fate / Exalted |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 1 | 15M | 20 / 10 / 1 | 40M | 40 / 20 / 3 |
  | 2 | 16.9M | 22.5 / 11.3 / 1.1 | 45M | 45 / 22.5 / 3.4 |
  | 5 | 22.5M | 30 / 15 / 1.5 | 60M | 60 / 30 / 4.5 |

  Before, a party of 5 got the solo spoils each and killed 1.8x faster than one player (health x2.8 against 5x the
  damage); a sigil is spent per run, so each run paid the whole party. Now a party of 5 kills in the solo time and each
  finisher gets 1.5x. The start of a run says it in chat ("Party of 5: boss health x5, damage +40%; spoils +50%.").
- **Leaderboards.** Three weekly boards of the fastest Cinderheart kill (mode `min`: the lowest time wins; shown m:ss):
  Solo, 2-3 and 4-5 players, each with class tabs (the class at the kill; "All classes" first). Titles Lone Cinder,
  Emberwarden, Ashen Vanguard and the usual orbs for the top 3. See "Leaderboards".
- **Boss Spawns.** Category "Ascended Omens" (on demand, kill tracking anywhere).
- **Crash and shutdown.** The sigil is spent at the start; the opener's marker gives it back at the next login after a
  crash; a clean shutdown ends every run first (everyone to the temple, the sigil back while the boss lives). A login
  inside a slot without a run goes to the temple. Logout inside: out of the run, back where the player came from.
- **Staff.** `/ascended` (the runs), `/ascended sigil, <kind>`, `/ascended shards, <kind>[, n]`, `/ascended relic, <kind>`,
  `/ascended phase, <n>` (your boss to that phase), `/ascended enrage`, `/ascended end`. Kinds: bloodmoon, hollow, storm,
  cinder. `sigil`, `shards` and `relic` need an administrator (group 5, `Chaos.staffCommand`).

### Balance

Health and enrage are set from the measured level 1000 damage of the classes (data/spells/README.md "Classes with the
passive trees": one target 2000-4800, median about 2700): a well-geared level 1000 character with the boss and
Ascended uniques deals `model.refDps` 3000 to one target, the healer of a party 2000; the share of the fight spent
hitting (moving out of telegraphs, adds, the gate) is 75% alone and 80% in a party. `U.killTime` (tests/uber_test.lua
keeps every target within 5%):

| Players | Ascended Omen health | Kill time | Cinderheart health | Kill time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1.20M | 8:53 | 1.65M | 12:13 |
| 2 | 2.40M | 10:00 | 3.30M | 13:45 |
| 3 | 3.60M | 9:22 | 4.95M | 12:53 |
| 4 | 4.80M | 9:05 | 6.60M | 12:30 |
| 5 | 6.00M | 8:55 | 8.25M | 12:16 |

At the measured median 2,600 (2026-10-13, "Solo kill times"): Ascended solo 10:15 / party of 5 10:05, Cinderheart
14:06 / 13:52; at the weakest class's 1,950: 13:41 / 12:45 and 18:48 / 17:32. The arena now closes at 14:00 / 20:00
(was 13:00 / 18:00), so the weakest builds finish inside it after the enrage; `model.refDps` stays 3,000 (a geared
character with the uniques).

Targets: Ascended solo 9:00 / party of 5 9:00 (enrage 10:00), Cinderheart solo 12:10 / party 12:15 (enrage 15:00), so a
well-geared player or party kills before the enrage and a weaker one meets it. Health is +100% per extra player since
the party pass of 2026-10-11 (was +45% / +58%: a party of 5 took 5:00 / 8:09). The model gives every party one healer,
so a duo of a damage dealer and a healer meets the Ascended enrage (10:00); two damage dealers need 8:20. Measured on the test server (2026-10-10, the
`ztest` harness of "Late game": the boss next to a level 1000 Juggernaut in the best level 1000 set, 17,023 health,
health sampled every 100 ms for 40 s, telegraphs, hazards and enrage off): the bosses' own attacks deal Sangrith 807,
Morvane 652, Thalcyra 614, the Cinderheart 996 damage per second (largest single hit 2.4-3.6k). A telegraph that is not
dodged costs 55% of max health (a Mystic's 5,145 health: 2,830; a Warrior's 15,065: 8,286), the enrage pulse adds 8% every
4 s. Not measured: a full kill with a real party (the kill times are the model's), the adds' damage.

**Checked in game** (test server copy, the reference client with the things_custom13 pair, 2026-10-10): opening an
Ascended Sigil, the HUD (phase, health, enrage, lives, players at the gate), a marks and a cross telegraph (warning,
second turn, hit), a lethal hit caught into the antechamber and the way back through the Ember Gate, phase 2 (storm
columns) and phase 3 (Storm Shard adds), the kill with its spoils and relic, three relics into the Cinderheart Sigil,
the Cinderheart on look 2126 with a ring telegraph and burning pools, its kill with the achievements and titles, and
the Cinderheart Solo board with its time. Not checked in game: a party (2+ players), the creeping edge, the enrage pulse,
a crash refund, the shutdown path.

## Factions (`factions.lua`, `factions_core.lua`, `factions_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_factions.sql`, `tools/install_factions.py`, client `game_factions`)

Four powers that fight over what the Cinders left, each with a home NPC who is also its quartermaster. Reputation is per
character (a season character is a character of its own and starts at Neutral everywhere: season isolation needs nothing
more; its gear and tokens follow the season's trade rules like any item). Every number is in `factions_config.lua`; the
pure logic (ranks, gains, caps, rivalry, contracts by seed, offer states, gear values, titles, the window payload) is
`factions_core.lua`; `tests/factions_test.lua` checks it and runs `factions.lua` against a mocked engine. Extended opcode
215. No player storages: three tables (`chaos_factions` standing, `chaos_faction_contracts` progress,
`chaos_faction_purchases` unlocks and weekly counts), also created at startup.

| Faction | Lore | Monster families (bestiary) | Rift theme | Invaders | World boss | Rival | NPC (town) | Token |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| The Ashen Vigil | pyre-wardens who burn what will not stay dead | undead, humans | Ashen Crypt | Undead Legion | Vharok | Veiled Choir | Warden Ysolde (Cinderhold) | pyre ash sigil 32091 |
| The Cinderforge Compact | smiths and sellswords of the obsidian forges | demons, constructs, humanoids | Obsidian Hall | Orc Warband, Minotaur Horde | Kaelgor | Thornbound Circle | Forgemaster Brannoc (town 1) | cinderforge seal 32092 |
| The Veiled Choir | seers who listen at the rifts and bargain with what answers | magic, dragons, aquatic, elementals | Abyssal Rift | Infernal Host | Nyxareth, Skaldra | Ashen Vigil | Cantor Velith (Bellwatch) | veiled eye 32093 |
| The Thornbound Circle | wardens of root and rot who cut the blight out of the Sanctum | plants, beasts, vermin, reptiles, birds, slimes | Forsaken Sanctum | Goblin Tribe, Wildwood Uprising | The Rotmother | Cinderforge Compact | Elder Bramwyn (Thornmere) | thornbound leaf 32094 |

**Ranks** (reputation from -6,000 to 36,000; the bar fills to the next threshold): Hostile -6,000, Wary -2,000, Neutral 0,
Trusted 2,500, Honored 8,000, Revered 18,000, Exalted 36,000 (the ceiling). Nothing locks content: a Hostile faction still
talks, offers contracts and takes tokens; only its quartermaster's rank offers wait.

**Earning** (`sources`, `contracts`):

| Source | Reputation | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Daily contracts (2 per faction) | 300 each | kill N (120-200) of one of the faction's families at 40%+ of your level; seal a rift of its theme at (your top tier - 1)+; deliver 15-25 rune shards and gold (150 per level, 20k-150k): a material and gold sink |
| Weekly contract (1 per faction) | 1,200 | take part in a world boss kill; stand against an invasion; seal 3 rifts of its theme at (top tier - 2)+; deliver 60-90 shards and gold (500 per level, 60k-500k) |
| Kills of its families | 1 per 10 points | points by tier: normal 1, magic 3, rare 8, legendary 25; monster hunting level at least 40% of yours (O284); party members in range share it (the bestiary rule) |
| Bounty contract | 60 | the contract's monster's family decides the faction |
| Rift seal of its theme | 30 + 6 x tier | not Omen guardians |
| Invasion reward | 100 | the factions that fight that invader |
| World boss share | 150 | the boss's faction |
| Token turned in at its NPC | 40 each | Turn in button in the window, next to the NPC |

Contracts are generated from a seed of (character, period, faction, slot) with a Park-Miller generator (the same numbers in
LuaJIT and Lua 5.3, tested), so a character sees the same contracts all day / week; the level at the first look is stored
with the progress and used again. A kind that cannot be made (no family with monsters in the level window, no rift tier
yet) is skipped. Contracts reset with the faction day (06:00) and week (Monday 06:00), the bounty board's rule.

**Diminishing returns, cap, rivalry** (`K.gain`). Activity reputation (everything but contracts) of one faction and day:
the first 600 at full value, the next 600 at half, the rest at a fifth (fractions carry over, so single kill points
count). Every source together stops at the weekly cap of 7,500 per faction (contracts alone give 5,400 a week; at the cap
Exalted takes about five weeks per faction). The cap rolls over (2026-10-15, `rolloverWeeks` 3): what a week leaves
unused, and a whole cap for every week skipped, carries into the next week (`entry.bank`, column `week_bank`), so a
week's cap is at most 22,500; a player who misses two weeks catches up in the third, the long-run pace is unchanged.
The window gets the faction's own cap (`wc`). Tests: `tests/factions_test.lua`, client `factionsview_test.lua`. Every gain lowers the rival by a quarter of it (fractions carry), never
below -2,000 (Wary) and never once the rival holds you Exalted (sworn): choosing a side costs, both sides stay possible.

**Tokens** (`tokenDrop`): per kill of the faction's families at hunting level 60+ (and the 40% rule), per 10,000: normal 4,
magic 25, rare 120, legendary 600, into the corpse (the loot owner's); a rift seal of its theme gives 1 + tier / 5; its
world boss 5; an invasion of its invaders 2. Tokens are stackable items (copies of stock stackable nodes, client sprites
unchanged) and can be traded.

**Quartermasters** (`offers`; every purchase needs the faction's NPC within 6 tiles; gold carried or in the bank):

| Rank | Ashen Vigil | Cinderforge Compact | Veiled Choir | Thornbound Circle |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Trusted | 5 Orbs of Upheaval, 150k (3/week) | 10 Whetstones, 120k (3/week) | 3 Orbs of Gilding, 140k (3/week) | 5 Orbs of Awakening, 80k (3/week) |
| Honored | Recipe: Pyre Distillation 100k (40 shards + 3 tokens + 10k -> 1 Orb of Fate) | Recipe: Cinder Tempering 100k (15 shards + 2 tokens + 5k -> 2 Orbs of Tempering) | Recipe: Veiled Binding 100k (50 shards + 3 tokens + 10k -> 1 Orb of Binding) | Recipe: Thorn Reforging 100k (35 shards + 3 tokens + 10k -> 1 Orb of Reforging) |
| Honored | helm (crown helmet), ilvl 100, Rare: monster damage taken T5, regeneration T5, life on kill T5; 250k + 10 tokens | sword (warlord sword), ilvl 100: boss damage T5, physical penetration T5, attack speed T5 | circlet (charmer's tiara), ilvl 100: monster damage taken T5, cooldown reduction T5, mana cost T5 | boots (terra boots), ilvl 100: dodge T5, movement speed T5 |
| Revered | 2 Orbs of Fate, 300k (2/week) | 1 Orb of Grafting, 900k (1/week) | 2 Orbs of Fate, 300k (2/week) | 10 Orbs of Upheaval, 280k (2/week) |
| Revered | armor (crown armor), ilvl 115: monster damage taken T6, thorns T6, regeneration T6; 600k + 20 tokens | legs (demon legs), ilvl 115: dodge T6, thorns T6, regeneration T6 | amulet (star amulet), ilvl 115: elemental penetration T6, cooldown reduction T6, mana on kill T6 | legs (golden legs), ilvl 115: dodge T6, regeneration T6, gold find T6 |
| Revered | tabard aura Pyrelight Mantle (aura 25), 300k + 15 tokens | Forgeflame Ring (aura 26) | Veiled Eyes (aura 27) | Thornfire Wreath (aura 28) |
| Exalted | shield (mastermind shield), ilvl 125: block T7, reflect T7, regeneration T7; 1.5M + 40 tokens | axe (royal axe), ilvl 125: boss damage T7, physical penetration T7, attack speed T7 | wand (wand of starstorm), ilvl 125: elemental penetration T7, damage over time T7, mana on hit T7 | amulet (platinum amulet), ilvl 125: boss damage T7, life on kill T7, healing done T7 |
| Exalted | Pyrewarden Charger (mount 142), 2M + 60 tokens | Forgeborn Emberwolf (mount 143) | Veilrunner (mount 144) | Thornbound Stag (mount 145) |

Gear is deterministic: the base item gets rarity Rare (old Epic), the item level, the base bonus and exactly these modifiers at these
tiers, each value the middle of its tier's range, through `ChaosCrafting.writeAffix` (so tooltips, orbs, salvage, the
market and transmog treat it like any rolled item); it carries the offer's name and `chaos_faction`. The test holds every
gear offer to `chaos_item_mods.lua` (the kind may carry the modifier, the tier is allowed at the item level, count and
prefix / suffix limits of the rarity) and to the faction limits (item level 125, Rare, T7 at most): a catch-up and
target-farm path below the top drops (item level 145-150, up to six modifiers, T8). Orbs can change it afterwards like any
item. Each faction has its own aura and mount (client pair things_custom14, client/MANIFEST.md "Raid boss and faction
looks"): auras 25..28 (`data/XML/chaos_auras_donor.csv`: Pyrelight Mantle, Forgeflame Ring, Veiled Eyes, Thornfire
Wreath; looks 2136..2139) and mounts 142..145 (`tools/install_outfits.py` MOUNTS: Pyrewarden Charger, Forgeborn
Emberwolf, Veilrunner, Thornbound Stag; looks 2132..2135), both given with `addAura` / `addMount` and remembered in
`chaos_faction_purchases`; none is sold in the store (`gen_shop_cosmetics.py` leaves out the factions_config.lua mounts).
The former placeholders (auras 14, 15, 24, 23; mounts 46, 30, 50, 54) are store offers only again. A character that
bought a placeholder keeps it; the offer's key is unchanged, so it cannot buy the new reward again (a staff `addAura` /
`addMount` of the new id if wanted).

**Titles, achievements, board.** Rank titles through `ChaosTitles.register("faction")`: Honored, Revered and Exalted each
give one (Vigil: Pyrewarden, Bellkeeper of the Vigil, Ashen Saint; Compact: Forgesworn, Anvilguard, Cinderlord; Choir:
Veilsinger, Voice of the Rift, Abyss-Tongued; Circle: Thornwarden, Rootkeeper, Heart of the Thorn); the Exalted title
brings the faction's plate frame (bone, ember, violet, verdant) and stays once earned. Achievements (category Exploration
& Social): one per faction for Exalted (25 points, 3 Orbs of Fate and an Orb of Grafting) and Oath of Four Banners for all
four (50 points, title Oathbound); stats `faction_exalted_<key>` and `faction_exalted`, set at the rank-up and at login.
The weekly board "Reputation" (`leaderboard_config.lua`, title Banner-Sworn) gets the reputation gained, every minute and
at logout.

**NPCs and install.** `tools/install_factions.py DATA_DIR [--dry-run]` (`install_all.py` step `factions`, after
`ascended`) adds the four tokens to `items.otb` / `items.xml` (stackable copies of stock stackable nodes: holy ash 20130,
copper token 25378, eye of corruption 12627, four-leaf clover 15546; the run stops when a source is not stackable, since
the client would misread the count) and copies the NPCs (`data/npc/<name>.xml`, their scripts and the shared
`npc/scripts/chaos_faction_npc.lua`). `factions.lua` places them at startup on the first free tile of `npcOffsets` around
the temple of their town (by name, else `townId`; a ring further out than the Ascendant Oracle and the Keeper of Trials).
Their dialogue runs in the NPC state: "contracts", "quartermaster", "tokens", "reputation" (and the like) open the
client window on that faction (opcode 215, action `npc`); "lore" and the rival's name answer in text. Every action is
checked again by `factions.lua`, which also checks that the NPC stands close.

**Hooks** (nothing in the other systems was edited): a death event on every monster without a master (family from
`ChaosBestiary.cat()`, tier from `ChaosTierDead`), `ChaosLeaderboard.record` wrapped for "bounty" and "rift" (the run's
theme from `ChaosRift.runOf`), `ChaosWorldBoss.computeRewards` and `ChaosInvasion.deliver` wrapped; each wrapped once
(flag on the table, installed again at login after a /reload) and counted once per event even if wrapped twice.
Staff: `/faction <character>[, <faction>, <reputation>]` shows or sets a standing.

**Protocol** (JSON `{action, data}`): client -> server `open {f?}`, `close`, `turnin {f}`, `deliver {key}`, `buy {key}`,
`craft {key}`; server -> client `state` (about 12 KB, `Chaos.sendChunked`; shape in `factions_core.lua` `K.payload` and
the client's `factionsview.lua`), `msg {text, ok}`, `npc {f}`. Item ids in the payload are client ids.

**Not verified:** nothing ran on a live server (the NPC placement, the extended opcode from the NPC state, `addAura` /
`addMount`, the gear through the real crafting library). The window was rendered in the reference client with a payload
from the real core (screenshots kept outside the repository).

## The Ember Descent (`descent.lua`, `descent_core.lua`, `descent_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_descent.sql`, client `game_descent`)

**Limits** (`descent_config.lua` `limits`, "Instance limits"): 45 minutes a run (unchanged) with warnings at 5 min, 1 min and 10 s; the end gives the rewards of the depth reached, back at the entry; at most 8 runs, the wait and the waiting line when every hall is taken.

A roguelike trial (roadmap item 59). Every number is in `descent_config.lua`; the pure logic (the seeded generator, the
room chain, escalation, waves, boon offers, picks, stacks and curses, the hit maths, embers, prices, rewards, titles,
free runs) is `descent_core.lua`, tested by `tests/descent_test.lua` with LuaJIT and Lua 5.3, including fixed values of
the generator that both interpreters must give (so a weekly run is the same run everywhere). Extended opcode **205**.

**Entry.** A portal (magic forcefield 1387, action id 47701) is placed for each town of `portal.townIds` (Cinderhold, the main city, and Mirewake): Cinderhold's at its fixed tile in the temple's portal gallery (`portal.positions` 32363, 32245, 7), Mirewake's (and a taken fixed tile) next to the temple at startup (the first
free tile of `portal.offsets`); stepping in opens the Descent window, and Adventure > Ember Descent opens it anywhere. The
window shows the free runs, the sigils carried, the best depths and the forge. A run starts in a protection zone, out of
combat, level 100+, not multi-clienting; the party within 8 sqm comes along (up to 4). Each member pays for himself:
the free normal run of the day (server day; unused days bank up to `freeBankDays` 3, 2026-10-15: `free_day` is the
clock of the free runs, `D.freeState` / `D.spendDaily`, and with one banked it reads as before), the free weekly run of the week (the leaderboard week, Monday 06:00) or one
**Ember Sigil**. A sigil is a stock "red power core" (10074, used by nothing else) with action id 47710 and the custom
attribute `descent_sigil`, forged in the window for 25 rune shards (salvage) and 50,000 gold (carried or bank): a sink.

**The hall.** The rift slot functions of `rift_core.lua` (`slotCenter`, `allocSlot`, `slotOfPos`) on the Descent's own
grid (x 10000-10255, y 10000-10127, z 7, 8 slots; no map tiles there) and the rift way of building (`Game.createTile`,
walls, lights): one square hall of 19 x 19 per slot. Every room re-themes the floor with a rift
theme (never the same twice in a row; the floor is the shared arena look since O276, see "Arena looks") and fills it again, so one slot serves a whole run.

**Rooms.** 8-12 rooms from the run's seed (`generate`): the first is combat, the last the boss, the one before the boss
a merchant; the others by weight combat 50, elite 18, treasure 10, shrine 12, merchant 8 (no elite before room 3, no
treasure / shrine / merchant twice in a row).

| Room | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Combat | 2 + depth / 4 waves (up to 4) of 4 + depth / 3 monsters (+2 per extra player, up to 14) |
| Elite | one wave of 2 + depth / 4 (+1 per extra player) rare or legendary monsters (legendary 25% + 5% per depth), health x1.5 |
| Treasure | 3 guards (+1 per extra player), then the chest: 40 + 10 x depth embers and 2,000 + 800 x depth gold (bank) per player |
| Shrine | the altar takes 20% of the maximum health (never the last point) for a boon choice; Continue or the gate goes on |
| Merchant | Ember Draught (full health and mana, 20 + 3 x depth embers), Boon Cache (a choice, 55 + 5 x depth), Ash Cleanse (the newest curse and its bonus, 40 + 4 x depth), Cinder Shell (a ward of 25% max health, 15 + 2 x depth) |
| Boss | the strongest type of the room's window, legendary, health x(6 + 2 per extra player), the rift guardian look of the theme and a name of its own (Hollow Archon, Obsidian Tyrant, Pyre Lich, Blighted Matriarch) |

Monster types come from the bounty pool (`bounty_pool.lua`), three per room, in the level window party level x
(0.55 + 0.05 x depth) .. x (0.8 + 0.05 x depth), clamped to 20-1500 and widened when too few. Health x(1 + 0.08 x
(depth - 1)), damage to players x(1 + 0.06 x (depth - 1)); the tier mix (monster_tiers.lua) magic 8 + 3 x depth %, rare
2 + 1.5 x depth %, legendary 0.8 x depth - 3.2 %. Embers (the run currency, per player): 2 a kill (6 in an elite room),
15 a cleared room. The run has 45 minutes.

**Boons.** After a combat, elite or treasure room every player picks one of three cards (40 s, else the first). Picking a
boon again stacks it. All numbers per stack; the boons work through the hit and kill events of descent.lua and show on
the buff bar (source `descent`, icons `buff:descent_b_<key>` / `buff:descent_c_<key>`):

| Boon | Effect | Max |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ember Edge | +12% damage to Descent monsters | 3 |
| Searing / Rime / Grave Brand | 50% of physical damage becomes fire / ice / death, that part +15% (one brand at a time) | 1 |
| Blood Drinker | heal 5% of the damage dealt | 3 |
| Pyre Burst | a slain foe bursts for 20% of its max health as fire within 2 sqm | 3 |
| Soul Harvest | 3% health and mana a kill | 3 |
| Echo Strike | 20% chance a hit strikes again for 50% | 3 |
| Ember Ward | a ward of 10% max health, renewed every 20 s | 3 |
| Quickstep | +40 speed | 2 |
| Keen Eye | 10% chance of +60% damage | 3 |
| Executioner | +35% damage below 30% health | 2 |
| Stoneskin | 10% less damage taken (60% at most) | 3 |
| Thornmail | 30% of a monster's hit back | 2 |
| Phoenix Ember | once a run a lethal blow leaves 40% health | 1 |
| Ember Tithe | +50% embers | 2 |

From room 2, a combat or elite room's choice carries a curse 30% of the time; taking it with the boon adds its reward
to the player's final rewards and gives embers at once: Frailty (+20% damage taken; +25%, 30 embers), Withering (healing
-30%; +20%, 25), Swarm (rooms +30% monsters for the party; +25%, 30), Frenzied Foes (monsters +60 speed; +20%, 25),
Ashen Purse (-40% embers; +15%).

**The end.** A lethal hit is caught (the health event, `onPrepareDeath` as the safety net): the player is out with
the rewards of the depth reached, healed, at the place he entered from; nothing is lost. The run ends when nobody is
left, at the time limit or with the boss (a full clear). Logging out (not in a fight) or Leave ends it for that player
with his rewards. Rewards per player (x the curse bonuses): gold to the bank (3,000 x depth + 400 x depth^2) x
(1 + level / 400), Orbs of Upheaval depth / 2, Orbs of Fate depth / 4, Dawn Orbs depth / 6; x1.5 on a full clear; from
depth 6 a roll for one of five run-exclusive uniques (150 per 10000 per room past 5, +800 for the boss, at most 2500):
Emberfall Blade (sword, depth 6), Ashwalker Treads (boots, 6), Heart of the Descent (amulet, 8), Sigil of the Ninth Room
(ring, 9), Pyre Cleaver (two-handed sword, 10). They are in `data/items/chaos_items.xml` (so `gen_unique_specs.py` makes
their specs) but not in `ChaosUniqueItems`: no monster, chest or boss drops them. Titles (name plate source `descent`):
Ashwalker (depth 5), Emberdelver (depth 9), Heart of the Descent (a full clear). The weekly run (seed from the week key)
records its depth on the weekly leaderboard "Ember Descent" (title Emberlord, the board's top 3 rewards).

**Persistence.** `chaos_descent_players` (best depth, full clear, the day / week of the free runs, the weekly best, runs,
clears) and `chaos_descent_runs` (one row per player and run). Storages 7100410 (a run in progress: the next login after
a crash goes to the temple) and 7100411 (when the next free run is ready: the Boss Spawns window's cooldown of the new
row "Ember Descent Boss", category "The Ember Descent"). A clean shutdown ends every run first.

**Staff.** `/descent status | sigil | reset | clear | skip | boon <key> | offer | portal`.

**Tested.** `tests/descent_test.lua` (130,000 checks: 3,000 seeds of room chains, 400 x 12 offers, tier draws, hits,
rewards, wiring of opcode, storages, action ids, specs, board, Boss Spawns row, buff registry and icons) and
`game_descent/descentmath_test.lua`. On a live test server with the client: the portal and window, daily, weekly and sigil
runs to the boss and to a fall, the shrine, the merchant (Boon Cache), curses, the buff bar icons, the HUD, the end
summary, the database rows, the weekly board and the Boss Spawns row. Not tested in game: a party of 2-4, the
crash marker, a clean shutdown during a run.


**Empty rooms (2026-10-24).** `descent_core.lua` `pickTypes` picks the room's monsters from the bounty pool; when the level window
(clamped to `escalation.maxLevel`) lies above the pool (it ends at level 980) it takes the nearest levels, so a room always has
monster types while the pool has one valid monster. `spawnSet` lets a type the engine cannot create give way to the others. A wave that
made 0 monsters is retried (`spawn.retries`, `spawn.retrySeconds`) with the types picked again and is never a cleared room; after the
retries the run ends with result `error` (depth rewards) and one `[Chaos descent] ERROR` line in the log.
## The Ashen Sepulchre, the weekly raid (`raid.lua`, `raid_core.lua`, `raid_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_raid.sql`, client `game_raid`)

**Limits** (`raid_config.lua` `sessionMinutes`, `idleMinutes`, `limits`, "Instance limits"): one opening lasts at most 150 minutes, warnings at 10, 5 and 1 minute and 10 s; then everyone goes back where they came from, the slot closes and the progress stays saved for the week (a fight still going ends as a wipe). An empty raid closes after 5 minutes (was 10). At most 4 raids, the wait and the waiting line when every wing is taken.

Guild content for 5 to 15 players (roadmap item 61): five bosses in sequence in one instanced raid zone, trash between
them, a loot lockout per character, boss and week, and a raid that is saved so a group can continue it another day of
the same week. Every number is in `raid_config.lua`; the pure logic (the lockout week, lockouts and loot eligibility, the
saved raid and its doors, scaling, the layout, cones and circles, the mechanic state machines, loot, the seeded vendor,
the journal, the HUD payload) is `raid_core.lua`, tested by `tests/raid_test.lua` (LuaJIT and Lua 5.3) together with
`raid.lua` against a mocked engine. Extended opcode **213** (`ChaosOpcodes.raid`). Storages 7100440-7100449
(`Chaos.storage.raid`: +0 inside a raid instance, the crash marker; +1 .. +5 the end of this week's lockout of boss 1 .. 5,
the Boss Spawns cooldown). Monsters: `data/monster/monsters/chaos/raid/` (registered by the `monsters` step).

**Entry.** A portal (magic forcefield 1387, action id 47801) for each town of `portal.townIds` (Cinderhold, the main city, and Mirewake): Cinderhold's at its fixed tile in the temple's portal gallery (`portal.positions` 32375, 32245, 7), Mirewake's (and a taken fixed tile) next to the temple, the first free tile of
`portal.offsets`) and Adventure > Raid: Ashen Sepulchre open the raid window. "Open New Raid" (or "Continue" on a saved
raid of this week) in a protection zone, out of combat, level 800+, not multi-clienting: the opener's party within 12 sqm
comes along, 1 to 15 of them (owner 2026-10-24: all content solo; `minPlayers` 1, `basePlayers` 5 is the group the boss numbers were measured for; staff may still open with `/raid open[, id]`). **Solo scaling** (`raid_core.lua`): under 5 raiders the boss, trash and add health is x (the group's damage / five raiders' damage) from the balance model (`K.smallMult`; solo x0.217, 2 x0.43, 3 x0.65, 4 x0.87), so one raider takes the same time as five and the enrage fits; from 5 up the old +18% / +12% / +10% per raider. Mechanics for one: Ember Brand needs `min(need, raiders)` inside and its total scales with that need (solo: one circle on you, 50% of max health, stand in it), Sundering Blows fades the stacks instead of a Crushing Verdict when nobody else is in the room (`sunderDecide(..., alone)`), packs are 3 monsters alone. Loot is personal and the weekly lockout per character as before, so a solo run pays what one member of a group gets. A lethal hit still throws the player to the hall; alone that is a wipe (the boss resets). Each member's own
problem (level, a fight, another instance) leaves only that member behind. "Join" puts a member of a raid that is open
right now (or the party of someone inside) into it, up to 15.

**The zone.** The rift slot functions of `rift_core.lua` (`slotCenter`, `allocSlot`, `slotOfPos`) on the raid's own grid:
x 10400-10911, y 10000-10511, z 7, 2 x 2 slots of 256 (checked free of the tower, island, world boss, siege, arena,
ascension trial, Ascended, rift, trials, guild hall and Ember Descent areas by the test; no map tiles there). One slot is a
row west to east, 176 tiles long: the entry hall (11 x 11, the exit portal, where players land and the fallen wake), then
per boss a corridor (10 x 5, the trash) and the boss room (23 x 23). Tiles are built with `Game.createTile` like the rift
slots and painted with the dark tile set (style "hall") when it is installed. Doors (iron bars, 1546) close the
corridors: a corridor's west door opens when the boss before it is slain, its east door when its trash is cleared; a boss
fight seals its room. The rooms of the bosses that cast hexes have a Font of Ash (fountain 1360, action id 47803) in each
corner. A slot nobody stands in closes after 5 minutes (its progress stays saved; was 10).

**Trash.** Each corridor holds 2-3 packs of the raid's trash (Sepulchre Ghoul, Bone Lancer, Hex Cultist, Cinder Hound,
Marrow Knight, Ashen Reaper; stock looks, 42-60k health, level 900 hits), 3 + 1 per 3 raiders each (at most 8: 4 at five,
8 at fifteen), health x(1 + 0.12 per raider over 5), 30% magic and 10% rare (monster_tiers.lua). A corridor's trash wakes
when its west door opens; clearing it is saved.

**The fight.** A raider within 8 sqm of a boss in its room (or damage to it with the door open) pulls it: raiders in the
corridor in front are drawn in, the room seals, the boss takes the raid's size into its health: the XML's (set for five)
x(1 + 0.18 per raider over 5). Phases at health thresholds, each entered once and in order (a yell, a call-out); every
mechanic of the phase runs on its own timer. Telegraphs are uber_core.lua's: the tiles are marked at once and every 1.1 s
until the hit 2.2 s after the first mark (circles of radius 1 get the 3 x 3 warning picture on their centre). A lethal hit is
caught: the raider lands in the entry hall, healed, and stays out of the fight until it ends (no death, no loss). Nobody left
standing in the room for 4 s is a wipe: the boss heals, its adds and effigies go, the doors open. Enrage (time after the
pull): boss and add hits x1.75, mechanics 40% more often, 10% of max health on everyone every 4 s.

| Mechanic | What to do | Numbers (share = of the hit player's max health) |
|---|---|---|
| Sundering Blows (tank swap) | Two tanks: the boss's melee stacks Sundered on its target (buff bar, 20 s). At 4 stacks the boss turns to the raider in melee range with the fewest stacks; with nobody there, Crushing Verdict falls on its target | +15% damage taken from the boss per stack (up to 8); Verdict 55% x (1 + 15% per stack), 2 s warning; turning away in time avoids it |
| Frontal Cleave (positional) | Stand beside or behind | a cone 7 long in front, every 11 s, 60% to everyone in it but the target |
| Rear Sweep (positional) | Never stand behind | a cone 6 long behind, every 9 s, 55% |
| Ember Brand (split soak) | Groups stack in the circles | every 17 s one circle per 7 raiders (1 / 2 / 3 at 5 / 10 / 15) near players, 4 s warning; 150% split among those inside; fewer than 3 inside (+1 per 5 raiders over 5) and everyone else in the room takes 35% |
| Cinder Acolytes (add priority) | Kill them first | 1 + 1 per 4 raiders every 40 s (90k health, +10% per raider over 5); each living one: the boss takes 15% less damage (at most 60%) and heals 1% every 5 s |
| Bone Bloom (spread) | Step out of your circle, not onto another's | a 3 x 3 circle under every raider, 45% |
| Hex Effigy (kill the totem) | A kill team | 1 + 1 per 8 raiders every 38 s (70k health); each living one adds a Hexed stack (buff bar) to everyone in the room every 3 s, 2% per stack (at most 10), the stacks fall when none lives; not killed in 22 s it detonates for 60% on everyone |
| Withering Hex (dispel) | Cleanse: use the Font of Ash (the cure curse spell is retired) | 1 + 1 per 5 raiders every 26 s; not lifted in 8 s it bursts for 45% on everyone within 2 sqm of the hexed |

| Boss | Look | Phases (health) | Mechanics | Enrage |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gravewarden Ulthar | 2127 (hooded black plate warden, red ember glow) | The Watch 100%, Last Watch 40% | sunder, cleave; + Bone Bloom | 9:00 (was 8:00) |
| Morwen the Ash-Sister | 2128 (hooded violet-robed sister in ember soul fire) | The Ash Choir 100%, Requiem 50% | soak, Cinder Acolytes; + Bone Bloom | 10:00 (was 8:00) |
| The Marrow Colossus | 2129 (many-legged pale bone colossus) | Grinding Bones 100%, Shattering 50% | sweep, Bone Bloom; + cleave | 11:00 (was 8:00) |
| Vhoss the Hexmaw | 2130 (coiled violet maw with a blue hex glow) | The Effigies 100%, Hexfall 45% | Hex Effigies, Withering Hex; + cleave | 11:00 (was 8:30) |
| Varkhul the Ashen Sovereign (final) | 2131 (ash-grey winged sovereign, 4x4) | The Throne 100% (sunder, cleave), Court of Ash 70% (sunder, soak, acolytes), The Last Sovereign 40% (sunder, effigies, hex, sweep) | seven | 16:00 (was 13:00) |

The looks are their own donor-library creatures (client pair things_custom14, client/MANIFEST.md "Raid boss and faction
looks"; picks.csv rows `raid_*`, written into the XMLs by `tools/apply_monster_looks.py`, family `raid`). Until
2026-10-11 they were the unused stock looks 1281, 354, 863, 1369, 1445; a client on an older pair draws nothing for them. Health and kill times (the balance model `K.killTime`: a well-geared level
1000 character deals 3,000 to one target, a fifth of the raid supports at 60% of that, 75% of the fight is spent hitting):

| Boss | 5 players | 10 players | 15 players |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gravewarden Ulthar | 4.00M, 6:26 | 7.60M, 6:07 | 11.20M, 6:00 |
| Morwen the Ash-Sister | 4.40M, 7:05 | 8.36M, 6:43 | 12.32M, 6:36 |
| The Marrow Colossus | 4.80M, 7:43 | 9.12M, 7:20 | 13.44M, 7:12 |
| Vhoss the Hexmaw | 5.00M, 8:03 | 9.50M, 7:38 | 14.00M, 7:30 |
| Varkhul the Ashen Sovereign | 7.20M, 11:35 | 13.68M, 11:00 | 20.16M, 10:49 |

At the measured median 2,600 (data/spells/README.md) 5 raiders take 7:26 / 8:11 / 8:55 / 9:17 / 13:23, so since
2026-10-13 the enrage is at 9 / 10 / 11 / 11 / 16 minutes (was 8 / 8 / 8 / 8:30 / 13): 18-23% to spare
(tests/raid_test.lua keeps 15-25%). At the weakest class's 1,950 they take 9:55 / 10:55 / 11:53 / 12:23 / 17:51 and
meet the enrage; the five fights then take about 63 minutes of the 150-minute session (unchanged).

Not measured: a real raid's kill times and the boss melee against a full set of tanks (the XML hits are first estimates
near the Ascended Omens').

**The lockout and the saved raid.** The lockout week starts Monday 06:00 (`resetDay` / `resetHour`, the rule of every
other weekly reset). A character may loot each boss once a week: at a kill every raider in the room (or fallen in that
fight) whose lockout of that boss is free gets personal loot and the lockout (`chaos_raid_lockouts`, one row per
character, week and boss); the others helped (a line, no loot). The kill counts for the raid either way. A raid
(`chaos_raid_instances`: week, opener, bosses slain and corridors cleared as bits, cleared) and its members
(`chaos_raid_members`) are saved at every kill and trash clear; its leader or any member may continue it later the same
week (the slain bosses stay dead, the cleared corridors stay empty, the next boss waits); a new week ends it. A crash: the
marker storage puts the character in the temple at the next login ("continue it from the raid window"); a clean shutdown
closes every instance first.

**Loot** (personal, into the backpack, the rest to the inbox): bosses 1-4: 2,500,000 gold to the bank, 6 Orbs of Upheaval,
2 Orbs of Fate, 2 gear rolls, 20 Sepulchre Marks; the final boss: 6,000,000 gold, 12 Upheaval, 5 Fate, 1 Exalted Orb, 3
gear rolls, 45 marks. A gear roll is one of the boss's base items (the late-game sets 29861-29890: Myst Regalia, Seraphic,
Dawnforged, a different mix per boss) made by `ChaosCrafting.createItem` at item level 120-130 with the boss-tier rarity
roll x1.5 (so tiers and modifier counts follow chaos_item_mods.lua). A unique roll: 1.5% (the final boss 4%) for one of
the five raid uniques that name the boss (`chaos_items.xml` -> `gen_unique_specs.py`; never in `ChaosUniqueItems`, so no
monster or chest drops them): Gravewarden's Verdict (club, Ulthar), Shroud of the Ash-Sister (armor, Morwen), Marrowforged
Greaves (legs, the Colossus), Eye of the Hexmaw (ring, Vhoss), Crown of the Last Sovereign (helmet, Varkhul only); the
final boss can give all five; level 800. A unique is broadcast. The corpse holds only coins.

**The final boss** also gives: the achievement The Last Door (title Sovereign's Bane), which unlocks the kill effect
**Sovereign's Pyre** (cosmetics id 109, `dome_blast_violet`); a guild trophy for the guild of every eligible raider, once
per guild and kill (`ChaosGuild.addStat(gid, "raidClears")`, shown on the trophy room's second statue, and 300 guild XP
that also count for the weekly top guilds); a broadcast; and, when all five bosses fell in one sitting (a raid that was
not continued), the weekly board **Sepulchre Clear** (`raid_clear`, mode `min`, m:ss; title Sepulchre Breaker) gets the
time from the first pull for everyone present. Achievements (category Raids): Into the Sepulchre, one per boss, The Last
Door, Nobody Kneels (nobody fell in the final fight, hidden, title the Unbowed), Through Every Door (a clear under 30
minutes, hidden), Keeper of the Sepulchre (10 clears, title Sepulchre Keeper); stats `raid_kills`, `raid_<boss key>`,
`raid_clears`, `raid_flawless`, `raid_speed` for every raider present.

**The vendor** (the window's Vendor tab, in a protection zone or inside the raid): Sepulchre Marks are a per-character
balance (`chaos_raid_players`, with bosses looted, clears and the best clear; spent with one conditional UPDATE). Each week
it shows the two orb bundles (10 Upheaval for 40, 3 Fate for 60) and five of the gear offers picked by the week's seed
(the same for everyone; `K.vendorStock`), each at most `weekly` times a week (`chaos_raid_purchases`). Gear is fixed like
the faction quartermasters' (Rare, item level 130, three T7 modifiers at the middle of their range, `factions_core.lua`
`gearProblems` checks every offer against chaos_item_mods.lua): helm, plate, legs, boots, a two-handed cleaver, a wand,
an amulet, a shield (100-180 marks); and an Exalted Orb for 150. A catch-up below the world boss drops (item level 145).

**Window, HUD, buff bar.** Client `game_raid`: This Week (the lockouts with the time to the reset, the raids of the week
with Continue / Join), Boss Journal (per boss its intro, the role hint, phases, every mechanic with its numbers from
`raid_core.lua` `K.mechText`, the loot preview), Vendor. Inside: a HUD under the character plate (raid id, the boss and
its health, phase, enrage clock, bosses slain, raiders / fallen / adds / effigies, the player's own Sundered / Hexed /
Withering Hex, the last call-outs) and the call-outs over the map ("TANK SWAP", "SOAK the circles", "Hex Effigy rises: KILL
IT!"). The buff bar source `raid` (`data/lib/chaos_buffs.lua`, icons `buff:raid_*` by `client/tools/gen_raid_icons.py`)
shows Sundered and Hexed with stacks and the hex with its timer. Party frames: a raid of 15 wraps into columns
(`PartyMath.grid`). Boss Spawns: the category "The Ashen Sepulchre (Raid)", a row per boss with the character's lockout as
its cooldown. Party Finder: the activity Raid offers "The Ashen Sepulchre" (`party_finder.lua` `src.raids`); a raid
listing holds 15 (`party_finder_config.lua` raid `maxParty`; "Party Finder", "Raid listings of 15").

**Protocol** (JSON `{action, data}`, `Chaos.sendChunked`): client -> server `open | start | continue {id} | join {id} |
leave | buy {key} | journal | query`; server -> client `info` (lockouts, saved raids, marks, records, the vendor's stock),
`journal {bosses}`, `hud` (`K.hud`), `alert {text, kind}`, `loot {boss, eligible, lines}`, `end {text}`, `msg {text, ok}`,
`closeInfo`.

**Staff.** `/raid status | open[, id] | trash | kill | phase, n | mech, <cleave|sweep|soak|adds|marks|totem|hex> |
stacks[, n] | reset | marks[, n] | close | portal`.

**Opcode.** 213 is free in the reference server (its opcodes: "Opcode collision check"), in every Chaos script
(`ChaosOpcodes`, `tests/raid_test.lua`) and in the client modules (a search for `sendExtendedOpcode`,
`registerExtended*Opcode` and opcode constants).

**Tested.** `tests/raid_test.lua` (674 checks): the week and the reset (the bounty board's week for Monday 06:00 over two
weeks of hours), lockouts, eligibility and helpers, the saved raid, continuation and expiry, doors, the session clear,
scaling, the layout inside its slot (and `slotOfPos` agreeing), cones and circles, every mechanic, loot and uniques, the
vendor's stock and every gear offer against chaos_item_mods.lua, the journal, the wiring (opcode, storages, tables, SQL,
grid, XMLs and looks, specs, board, Boss Spawns rows, achievements, cosmetic, buff registry and icons, Party Finder); and
`raid.lua` on a mocked engine with 5 raiders: the size rule, trash and doors, the pull and the seal, the tank swap and the
Verdict, a cleave, a caught lethal hit, a wipe, a kill with loot and lockouts, a member continuing two days later, a
second raid the same week without loot, the new week, the vendor, a full clear (board, guild trophy, achievements) and the
hex with the Font of Ash. Client `game_raid/raidview_test.lua`, `game_partyframes/partymath_test.lua` (the grid). On a
live test server (one character, opened by staff): the portal and the window (lockouts, journal, vendor buys of orbs and
fixed gear), a raid opened and joined, trash and doors, pulls, Sundered stacks on the buff bar and the HUD, the Verdict, a
cleave, phase 2 and Bone Bloom, an Ember Brand circle and its overflow, the hex and an effigy with the Hexed stacks, a
caught lethal hit and wipes, a kill with personal loot (gear at item level 125-127) and the lockout (window and Boss Spawns
cooldown), a continued raid after a restart, the database rows. Not tested in game: a real group of 5-15, the guild trophy
and the board (unit tested only), the Font of Ash by hand, the Party Finder pick.

## Community goals and the weekly world modifier (`community.lua`, `community_core.lua`, `community_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_community.sql`, client `game_community`)

One bar the whole server fills together, and a world that changes every week. Every number is in `community_config.lua`;
the pure logic (weeks and periods, points and caps, stages and their buff windows, the ranking and rewards, the seeded
draw of the week, every hook value) is `community_core.lua`; `tests/community_test.lua` checks it (LuaJIT and Lua 5.3 must
draw the same weeks) and runs `community.lua` against a mocked engine. Extended opcode 203. No player storages: five
tables (`chaos_community_goal`, `_buffs`, `_contrib`, `_week`, `_history`), also created at startup, so a restart keeps
the goal, the open buff windows, every contribution and the week.

**The goal** ("Fuel the Brazier", target 1,500,000 points, `goal.periodDays` = 7: the week of the leaderboards, Monday
06:00; any other number of days counts periods from `goal.epoch`):

| Source | Points | Daily cap (per character) | Hook |
|---|---|---|---|
| Monsters slain | 1 (magic 2, rare 4, legendary 8) | 4,000 | a `kill` event on every player; summons and monsters with a hunting level under 40% of the character's level give nothing (O284) |
| Rifts sealed | 120 + 15 x tier | 3,000 | `ChaosLeaderboard.record("rift", ...)` wrapped (every finisher) |
| Invasion waves repelled | 40 per wave of a won invasion | 2,500 | `ChaosLeaderboard.record("defender", ...)` wrapped (every rewarded defender; liberations do not count) |
| World bosses slain | 400 | 2,000 | `ChaosLeaderboard.recordShares` wrapped (every share) |
| Crafting orbs used | 12 | 1,500 | `crafting.lua` craft() calls `ChaosCommunity.onOrbUsed` |
| Gold given to the Brazier | 1 per 1,000 gold | 5,000 (5,000,000 gold) | the Brazier dialog |

All sources together count at most 12,000 points per character and day (the day turns at 06:00). Only characters online
at the moment are credited (an offline world boss share or invasion reward adds nothing). Staff (group 4+) add nothing,
cannot give gold and are never ranked.

**Stages** (each opens its buff for everyone for `hours` from the moment it is reached, on the buff bar with its own icon,
broadcast in chat and listed on the website; a window outlives the period it came from):

| Stage | Buff | Hours | Applied through |
|---|---|---|---|
| 25% Kindled Brazier | +10% experience from monsters | 24 | `community.lua`'s `onGainExperience` callback |
| 50% Ashen Bounty | +10% Chaos loot quantity | 24 | `loot_config.lua` `rateMult` (`ChaosCommunity.lootMult`) |
| 75% Rift Beacon | +5% Rift Key chance on a sealed rift | 24 | `rift_core.lua` `R.hooks.world` (merged into the key user's atlas modifiers) |
| 100% Brazier Ablaze | +20% faction reputation, +5% experience | 48 | `factions.lua` `F.gain` (`ChaosCommunity.repMult`), the experience callback |

Steps of 10% and 90% are broadcast too. Staff: `/community add <points>` and `/community stage <n>` (tests, events).

**Rewards** when a period ends (handed out at the character's next login, marked on its `chaos_community_contrib` row):
the top 3 get the title "Keeper of the Flame" for 7 days (name plates, `ChaosTitles.register("community")`); everyone with
1,500 points or more gets 2 Orbs of Upheaval and an Orb of Fate (backpack, else the inbox). The end is broadcast with the
top three and written to the history.

**Season realms** (`goal.realms`): `"together"` (the default) is one goal; season characters add to it and get its buffs
like everyone else. `"separate"` gives every realm (0 = standard, the season id for season characters, `season.lua`
`ChaosSeason.realmOf`) its own goal, ranking, stage buffs and rewards; the website shows each realm's bar. The weekly
modifier is always the same for every realm.

**The Great Brazier**: a coal basin (the dark tile set's brazier when installed) placed at startup on the first free tile
of `brazier.offsets` around the temple of town `brazier.townId` (or exactly at `brazier.pos`), action id 47901. Using it
opens the donate dialog; gold is taken from the backpack and the bank (`Chaos.pay`), in whole thousands, 1,000 to
10,000,000 per donation, while the character stands within 4 tiles. Every donation is logged.

**The weekly world modifier**: one (55%) or two (45%) modifiers of the pool, drawn by the week's seed (Park-Miller over a
hash of the week key: the same draw on every start, in LuaJIT and Lua 5.3; never two of one group). Staff override for the
current week: `/community modifier <key>[,<key>]` (stored in `server_config` `chaos_community_override`, ignored once the
week is over), `/community modifier auto` goes back to the seed. The week is announced at login (as runtime events of the
event calendar, so `!events` and the calendar's login lines name it), in the window, on the buff bar (with the week's time
left) and on the website (`chaos_community_week`).

| Modifier | Effect | Hook |
|---|---|---|
| Ember Tides | rifts open with one more modifier, chests 15% richer | `R.worldKeyMods` in `rift.lua` (after the refund marker, so a crash refunds the key as it was); `rewardMult` through `R.hooks.world` |
| Champions' Week | magic / rare / legendary monsters x1.5 as often | `ChaosEvents.dynamic` bonus `tierChance` (`monster_tiers.lua`) |
| Restless Dead | undead +30% experience and +30% Chaos loot | the experience callback, `ChaosCommunity.lootMult`; the family is the bestiary's (`ChaosBestiary.cat()`), else `week.familyWords` |
| Gilded Week | treasure goblins x2 | `ChaosEvents.dynamic` bonus `goblin` (`treasure_goblin.lua`) |
| Forgefire | crafting orb cost -20%: each orb used has a 20% chance to be kept | `ChaosCommunity.onOrbUsed` in `crafting.lua` |
| Dragonfall | dragons +25% experience and loot | as Restless Dead |
| Ambush Season | ambush chance x1.5 | `ChaosEvents.dynamic` bonus `ambush` (`monster_tiers.lua`) |
| Banner Week | +20% faction reputation | `F.gain` |
| Tower Echoes | Infinity Tower points x1.5 | `ChaosEvents.dynamic` bonus `towerPoints` (`infinitytower.lua`) |

Every hook is a guarded call that returns 1 / nil / false when no stage window is open and no modifier is active; the test
checks each modifier alone against every hook and the shared hook points with no hook installed.

**Protocol** (opcode 203, JSON `{action, data}`; the state with `Chaos.sendChunked`): client `open | close | donate {gold}`;
server `state {now, goal, stages, sources, mine, top, week, brazier}` (`community_core.lua` `C.payload`, again every 20 s
while the window is open and at every stage) | `msg {text, ok}` | `brazier {}` (the Brazier was used: the client opens its
dialog).

**Edits to shared files** (small guarded hunks): `chaos_constants.lua` (`ChaosOpcodes.community = 203`), `data/lib/chaos_buffs.lua`
(entries `community_goal`, `wmod_week`, source `community`), `loot_config.lua` (`rateMult`), `rift_core.lua` (`R.hooks.world`,
`R.mergeWorld`, `R.worldKeyMods`; `R.atlasMods` merges the world answer), `rift.lua` (one call before the run's effects),
`factions.lua` (`F.gain`), `crafting.lua` (craft(): the orb hook), `client/tools/gen_buff_icons.py` (leaves `community_*` /
`wmod_*` to `client/tools/gen_community_icons.py`).

Assumptions (not run on a live server): the base server's `kill` CreatureEvent fires for the killer; `Chaos.pay`
takes from the backpack and the bank; the main city's temple (town 2, Cinderhold, "Main city") has a free tile at one of the offsets (else set `brazier.pos`).

## The Ashen Chronicle (`chronicle.lua`, `chronicle_core.lua`, `chronicle_config.lua`, `chronicle_text.lua`, `sql/chaos_chronicle.sql`, client `game_chronicle`)

Owner-approved design (2026-10-14): a server-wide story per season that advances with what the whole realm does. The
pure logic is `chronicle_core.lua` (`tests/chronicle_test.lua`, LuaJIT and Lua 5.3, also `chronicle.lua` against a
mocked engine); every number is in `chronicle_config.lua`; the story is `chronicle_text.lua` (English and Brazilian
Portuguese, one file of our own so the lore writers' `lore_data.lua` stays theirs). Extended opcode 171 (shared with
"The Capital Memorial"). Tables `chaos_chronicle_state`, `_chapters`, `_progress`, `_contrib`, `_record`, `_levels`,
also created at startup. No player storages; global storages 7102100-7102119; action ids 47920-47929.

**Chapters.** A season with an arc (`arcs`, season id -> arc key; Season 1 tells `s1`) has 4-6 chapters. One is open at
a time; it is written when every goal is met. Only the open chapter counts; a met goal takes no more and gives no more
points. Season 1:

| Chapter | Goals (`chapters.s1`) | When it is written |
|---|---|---|
| I. The Ash Thickens | 250 characters reach level 300; 1,200 rifts sealed in tiers 1-5 | ash drifts and cracks around the capital's temple |
| II. The Wound Beside the Walls | 20 world bosses; 1,200 rifts in tiers 6-10 | the Cinderscar Breach opens (levels 440-560); rubble near the temple |
| III. Omens in the Ashfall | 180 Omen guardians; 600 rifts in tiers 11-14 | ward-fires (candles) around the temple |
| IV. The Sepulchre Stirs | 12 Ashen Sepulchre clears; 30 Ascended Omens | the Ossuary Stair opens (levels 400-520) |
| V. Embers Rekindled | 10 Cinderheart kills; 80 characters reach level 600; 6 invasions repelled | ash and rubble cleared, flowers: the capital rebuilt |

The story text and these sizes were approved on 2026-10-14 (owner delegated, docs/OWNER_TODO.md "Decided"). The
Chronicler is Archivist Maelis (one name; she answers "chronicle" and "cronista", `archivist_maelis.lua`).

**Goal sizes** (2026-10-14, after pack combat; computed, not measured). Assumptions: Season 1 starts with the launch
(20 Nov) and ends 31 Jan (72 days); 150 online at the evening peak (the middle of the expected 100-300), about 2.5 x
that many players a day and 13 x it in player-hours a day (1,950 at 150); the leveling model of "Pack combat (pace)"
(level 300 in 3-7 hours of play, 600 in 20-45, 800 in about 40, 925+ in about 55-70; boosted about 40% less). Only
the open chapter counts, so each goal counts what happens in its own window (a level goal counts characters that cross
the level while the chapter is open). Target: each chapter takes days at any population of 100-300, the arc about 5-6
weeks at 150, so a quieter server still finishes before the season ends.

| Goal | Rate at 150 online (where it comes from) | Days at 150 | at 100 | at 300 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| I: 250 reach level 300 | ~600 different players in the first 3 days, most pass 300 in 3-7 hours of play | ~2 | ~3 | ~1 |
| I: 1,200 rifts tiers 1-5 | ~1,200 player-hours/day at levels 100-500, 15% in rifts, ~4.5 runs/h, 1.5 players a run: ~500/day | ~2.5 | ~3.5 | ~1.2 |
| II: 20 world bosses | 4 spawns a day (every 6 h), ~85-100% killed; does not grow with players | ~5-6 | ~6 | ~5 |
| II: 1,200 rifts tiers 6-10 | ~580 player-hours/day at 500-900, 20% in rifts, 4 runs/h, 1.5 a run: ~300/day | ~4 | ~6 | ~2 |
| III: 180 Omens | rifts 6+ give 2 + (tier - 6) fragments each finisher, 60 a key: ~65 keys/day, about half used at 800+ | ~6 | ~8 | ~3 |
| III: 600 rifts tiers 11-14 | 20-60 characters at 925+, ~1.5 h/day there, 4 runs/h, 1.7 a run: ~120/day | ~5 | ~7.5 | ~2.5 |
| IV: 12 Sepulchre clears | 80-120 characters at 800+, groups of 5-15, about one clear per group a week: ~8/week | ~10 | ~17 | ~4-5 |
| IV: 30 Ascended | ~33 shards/day (40% per Omen finisher, 4-10% per high rift), 4 a sigil, some fails: ~5/day | ~6 | ~9 | ~3 |
| V: 10 Cinderheart | every finisher of an Ascended kill gets a relic, 3 kinds a sigil; level 1000; ~1-2 kills/day | ~7 | ~10 | ~4 |
| V: 80 cross level 600 | late joiners, casual players and alts crossing 600 in weeks 4-6: ~6-10/day | ~10 | ~14 | ~5 |
| V: 6 invasions repelled | 2 scheduled a week + 35% of days a random one = ~4.5/week, ~80% repelled | ~12 | ~13 | ~11 |

The slowest goal closes a chapter: I ~2.5 days, II ~5-6 (world bosses), III ~6, IV ~10 (the raid), V ~12-14
(invasions): about 37 days at 150 online (written around 27 Dec), about 50 at 100 (9 Jan), about 28 at 300. The
earlier sizes left chapter I to the first hours (150 characters at level 100 in under an hour of play each) and IV and V
to 4-5 weeks each (40 raid clears at ~8 a week, 10 invasions at ~3.5 a week). Players can keep Omen keys and sigils
from the chapter before; that only speeds a chapter up. Recheck after beta weekend 2 (`/chronicle` shows the progress)
and before the season starts; a target is one number in `chapters.s1`.

**Sources** (no content script was edited; each hook is wrapped once through `ChaosWrapChain`, `wrapchain_core.lua`,
with the same contract built in when that file is absent):

| Event | Hook |
|---|---|
| world boss kill, sealed rift (tier -> band), Omen guardian, Ascended Omen, the Cinderheart | `ChaosRecords.submit(run)` when it returns true (the records' anti-abuse: staff, multi-client and debug runs never count) |
| Ashen Sepulchre clear | `ChaosAchievements.progress(p, "raid_clears")` (raid.lua, every player present), once per raid run (`ChaosRaid.runOf`); wrapped once at load, under season_journey.lua's wrapper |
| invasion repelled | `ChaosInvasion.deliver(player, r)` (not a liberation), once per invasion and 30 minutes |
| character reaching a goal's level | an advance event; once per character, level and season (`chaos_chronicle_levels`); staff never |
| any other world event | `ChaosChronicle.event(key, players)` (dedupe is the caller's) |

Points per contribution (`points`): world boss 10, rift 1 / 2 / 4 / 6 by band, Omen 8, Ascended 15, Cinderheart 40,
raid 6, level 5, event 4. The other members of a run counted once get the points in the chapter that run counted for.

**The world.** The world of a season is replayed from its written chapters (`ChaosChronicleCore.worldOf`), so a start,
a restart, a written chapter and a new season are the same diff (`worldDiff`): a written chapter's `open` areas get
their gate portal (item 1387 with action id 47920 + the area's index; a step-in moves the player to the area's arrival
from `minLevel` up), its `town` sets of non-blocking stock decoration are placed on the first free tile of each piece's
offsets around the capital's temple (action id 47929, found again after a `/reload`) or taken away, optional ground
swaps (`swaps`, `from` -> `to` and back) turn, and the global storages say how many chapters are written (7102110),
which (7102100 + n) and for which season (7102111). An NPC script reads them and answers with
`ChaosChronicleText.npcLine(arc, done, lang)` (dofile `chronicle_text.lua` in the NPC's state). A broadcast in each
player's language (`Chaos.broadcast` of i18n.lua when loaded, else English) and a Discord row (`ChaosDiscord.queue`,
kind `chronicle`, when discord.lua is loaded and its config switches the kind on) go out. After a season ends its world
stays until the next season starts, which starts from nothing.

**The areas.** `server/tools/areaplan/chronicle/chronicle_cinderscar_breach.json` (waste, 128x104, levels 440-560, origin
14910, 15140, 7) and `chronicle_ossuary_stair.json` (crypt, 120x104, levels 400-520, origin 15100, 15140, 9), planned
with the area planner. Install step `contentareas` (`tools/install_content_areas.py`) places both at their origins with
their spawns, as fixed areas: no hunt teleport (decided 2026-10-14). `areas[i].at` is that origin and `gate` an optional
fixed world tile of the portal (a staff override; unset since 2026-10-16). The gates: the **Chronicle Gates** of
`gateTowns` (Cinderhold and Mirewake), placed by "City portals" beside the temple (Cinderhold: the temple's portal
gallery), with the area's name in the look text (they stood in the upper hall of Cinderhold's temple, 32362 / 32358,
32240, 6, before; the owner found that odd). Without `at` (and `gate` or `gateTowns`) a chapter opens an area in the
story only: the window says so and the console names the missing setting. Their exit
portal (47951) leads to the temple. `tools/chronicle_areas_test.py` checks the plans (validate, compile, QA) and the
arrival offsets of the config.

**The record.** At the season's end the top `topRecorded` (10) of every chapter go to `chaos_chronicle_record`
(aggregated: a total per chapter and character, no event log). The client's Record tab and the website's Chronicle
page show them; a name follows the character's Memorial choice ("records"): "A hero who keeps their name" otherwise.

**Protocol** (opcode 171, JSON): client `open` | `close`; server `state` (`ChaosChronicleCore.payload`: chapters with
both languages, goal bars, own points, top contributors, past seasons), through `Chaos.sendChunked`. The login line,
the Memorial's question and its answers follow the player's language (`Chaos.lang`, i18n.lua). The client also
reads the chapter pages in the Codex's Lore tab (`tools/chronicle_pages.lua`).

**Staff:** `/chronicle` (status, areas placed or not), `/chronicle world` (apply again), `/chronicle complete` (write the
open chapter) and `/chronicle reset` (this season's Chronicle from the start, the world reset): group 5, logged.

**Not verified:** not run on a live server; the gate portal and the town decoration only in the mocked engine (the
decoration ids are the area planner's kit ids, checked on the pair by `check-kits`). Hooks wanted: see the list at
the end of "The Capital Memorial".

## The Capital Memorial (`memorial.lua`, `memorial_core.lua`, `memorial_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_memorial.sql`, client `game_chronicle` Memorial tab)

Owner-approved design (2026-10-14): a plaza in the capital with statues and memorial stones for the season's realm
firsts, its top records and the fallen Hardcore characters, each only with the player's consent, refreshed each season
and archived on the website (page.php?plugin=chaos&p=memorial). Pure logic `memorial_core.lua`
(`tests/memorial_test.lua`, also `memorial.lua` on a mocked engine); numbers `memorial_config.lua`. Tables
`chaos_memorial_optin`, `chaos_memorial_entries`. Action ids 47940-47949 (they were 47930-47939, the hunt teleports'
block: moved 2026-10-14), modal window 7480.

**Entries** (every `refreshSeconds`, 600, for the season key: "s<id>", else the quarter, as the records): realm firsts
from `chaos_records_firsts` (one row per member), the season's best of each board of `boards` from `chaos_records`
(any party size; ties to the earlier, then the lower id), the season's Hardcore falls from `chaos_season_modes`
(name, level, class, cause, date). Staff are never on it. Rows of past seasons stay: the website's archive.

**Consent.** `chaos_memorial_optin` per character: records and realm firsts are shown unless turned off; a Hardcore fall
only after a yes. `ChaosSeason.modesFall` is wrapped: the fall asks at the next login (a modal window; the client's
Memorial tab shows the question too). The choice is in Adventure > Chronicle > Memorial, any time; a change updates
the `shown` column of every season's rows at once, the plaza's statues too. A first counts its hidden members without
naming them; a record whose holder hides stays, without the name; a hidden fall is not there.

**The plaza.** `server/tools/areaplan/chronicle/capital_memorial.json` (hall, 48x40, z 7 with a flat roof, every zone
protected, no monsters): the hall of firsts (west), the hall of records (east), the garden of the fallen (north), the
plaza with the Memorial stone, the approach with the exit portal. Install step `contentareas` places it at its origin
(14800, 14800, 7) as a fixed area; `plaza.at` is that origin (decided 2026-10-14). The way in (moved 2026-10-16: the owner found the old tile
in the temple's upper hall odd): the **Memorial Portal** (1387, action id 47944) of Cinderhold and Mirewake
(`portalTowns`), placed by "City portals" beside the temple (Cinderhold: the temple's portal gallery, 32361, 32245, 7;
Mirewake 32960, 32073, 7), with a look text and
a purple effect, at startup and at every tick when missing (`plaza.portal` set: one fixed tile instead); stepping in
leads to the plaza's arrival (`plaza.at` + `plaza.arrival`, 23, 33); the plaza's exit portal leads to the character's
temple. `memorial.lua` places 8 guardian statues (8836, 8837), 8 statues (1443, 1448, 1450), 12 grave stones
(1407, 1408) and the stone circle (1421) on the plan's `slots`, each with its entry as the look text (item
description, at most 255 characters); an empty slot holds nothing. More entries than statues: the pages turn every
`rotateSeconds` (600); the stone says the page. `tools/chronicle_areas_test.py` checks that every slot is free floor
in its hall and that no walkable tile is cut off with every statue placed.

**Protocol** (opcode 171, JSON, beside the Chronicle's actions): client `mem` | `memset {records, fallen}` (booleans
only; staff refused; 1 s rate limit); server `mem` (`ChaosMemorialCore.payload`). **Staff:** `/memorial`, `/memorial
refresh`.

## Idle Hall (`idlehall.lua`, `idlehall_core.lua`, `idlehall_config.lua`, `tools/areaplan/rooms/idle_hall.json`)

Owner request (2026-10-15): characters idle for some minutes in a town are moved to a trainer room, so the temple does
not get crowded. Every online character earns Candlemarks, idle or not ("Candlemarks"), so many idle characters are
