expected. Pure logic `idlehall_core.lua` (`tests/idlehall_test.lua`, also `idlehall.lua` on a mocked engine); numbers
`idlehall_config.lua`; the room's plan `tools/areaplan/rooms/idle_hall.json` (`tools/idle_hall_test.py`). No player
storages, no table, no opcode of its own, no command. Action ids 47910-47919 (the hall's fixtures: 47910).

**Idle.** No action of the player for `idleMinutes` (10). Actions: a step or a turn (sampled; see Cost), an item moved
(EventCallback `onItemMoved`: containers, ground, equipment), a trade request or accept, pushing someone
(`onMoveCreature`), a spell (`ChaosSpellEvents` "cast", engine patch 0008 with the spell events on), a public chat line
(`ChaosReports.onChannelSpeak`, wrapped once with `ChaosWrapChain`), and the requests of the windows a player works in
while standing (`activityOpcodes`: market, Orb Exchange, store, stash, bank, crafting, transmog, Candlemarks, Town
Portal; their handlers in `Chaos.opcodeDispatch` are wrapped once, so no extra call runs for any other opcode). Other
extended opcodes do not count: some modules send on their own. **Being pushed is no action**: the tile
someone pushed the character onto (`onMoveCreature`) is not a step, so a crowd in the temple does not keep idle
characters there. Not seen: local chat (the default channel has no script hook) and NPC talk while standing still; the
engine's own idle time would see them (`Player.getIdleTime` is used when the engine has it; no src-patch exposes it
today).

**Where.** Only in a town: a protection zone tile within `town.radius` (60) sqm of a temple of `Game.getTowns()`, at most
`town.floors` (2) floors up or down (the temple, the depots, the town square, the shops), not a house tile, not in a
`town.exclude` box; a `town.include` box counts as town too (still a protection zone). Never: hunts and anything without
a protection zone, houses, staff (`Chaos.isStaff`), any instance (`Chaos.inAnyInstance`: rifts, dungeons, tower, arena,
hideouts, raids, ...; guild halls and the other runtime areas lie far from every temple anyway), a character in exercise training (the base script's storage 37100 is 1),
the Idle Hall itself (no temple near it: nobody is moved out). Trade and the market count as actions (above).

**Warning and move.** `warnSeconds` (60) before the move: "You are idle in town: you will be moved to the Idle Hall in 1
minute. Take a step to stay." (pt-BR in `i18n_strings.lua`). The move never comes without that warning, and never
sooner than a minute after it. Then the character is teleported to the hall's arrival with a teleport effect where it
leaves and where it lands, and a message. Logging out and in inside the hall is fine; its exit portal leads to the
temple of the character's town (its own action id 47911 since 2026-10-16, re-tagged from areagen's 47951 at startup,
idempotent; a look text and an effect: "City portals"). Candlemarks, offline training (beds), the stamina trainer tile and the market are not
touched: the character stays online and keeps earning; exercise training works on the hall's dummies.

**The hall.** `tools/areaplan/rooms/idle_hall.json`: biome hall, 44 x 28, z 7, flat roof, three protected rooms
(training west, hall with the arrival, rest east), no monsters. One shared hall for every town (cheaper map work than a
hall per town; the exit sends each character to its own temple). Install step `contentareas` places the
`tools/areaplan/rooms/` folder like the chronicle folder: a fixed area at its origin **14600, 14760, 7** (the free band
west of the Memorial's plaza: 73+ tiles from every plan and generated area, docs/MAP_GUIDE.md "Content plans"),
without a teleport. At startup and once a minute `idlehall.lua` puts on the config's slots: 4 exercise dummies (27751,
27752; the store's exercise weapons work on them) in the training room, 4 benches (1662) in the rest room and a sign
(1429, read from afar) beside the arrival with the rules in English and pt-BR; each carries action id 47910 and is found
again after a reload. `tools/idle_hall_test.py` (CI): the plan validates and compiles without a QA error, `hall.at` is
its origin and `hall.arrival` its arrival, every slot is free floor in its room with room to stand beside it, no
walkable tile is cut off with every fixture placed, the origin keeps 10 tiles from every other area, the installer
reads the folder. Until the hall is on the map nobody is warned or moved (one console line).

**Cost.** One GlobalEvent every `thinkMs` (1 s) looks at one of `slices` (10) groups of the online characters by creature
id: one `getPosition` and one `getDirection` each, so every character is sampled every 10 s (400 players: 40 per tick).
The town rule (one `Tile`, a flag, a house lookup, the temple list) and the exemptions (staff, instances, the training
storage) run only for a character that is due, then at most once per `recheckSeconds` (60) while it stays due and is
left alone. Each action above is one table write. Precision: the warning and the move come within 10 s of their time.

**Open.** The base `config.lua` has `kickIdlePlayerAfterMinutes = 15`: the engine warns a character 15 minutes after its
last action and kicks it a minute later (`Player::onThink`; moving it to the hall is no action; only staff and tiles
with the no-logout flag are spared), which also stops its Candlemarks. Raised to 1440 by
`tools/patch_base_idle_kick.py` (install step `idlekick`, "Candlemarks"); 0 is no "off": the engine then kicks after
one minute.

## Loadouts (Armory) (`loadouts.lua`, `loadouts_core.lua`, `loadouts_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_loadouts.sql`, client `game_loadouts`)

Save a whole build and switch between builds without paying the respec again. Client `game_loadouts` (Character > Loadouts,
and a Loadouts button the module adds at runtime to the passive tree window), extended opcode 206 (`ChaosOpcodes.loadouts`).
Every number is in `loadouts_config.lua`; the rules are in `loadouts_core.lua` (pure, `tests/loadouts_test.lua`).

**What a loadout holds.**

| Part | Stored as | On a switch |
|---|---|---|
| Passive tree nodes | `tree` column ("2,3,9") | the live tree (`chaos_passive_tree`, the active preset) is replaced |
| Paragon allocation | `paragon` column ("damage=3,health=4") | `ChaosParagon.save`, then `ChaosPassiveTree.apply` |
| Support runes in the spells' sockets | the runes themselves: the live sockets for the active loadout, player storages `7112000 + (slot - 1) * 2000 + spell id * 4 + socket` for the others (`supports` column: a summary) | the runes move between the live sockets and the loadout's own storages; never into the backpack, never copied |
| Class / vocation | `voc` column (vocation id at the save) | a requirement: nodes another class cannot hold are refunded for free on load; ascension itself is not part of a loadout (it changes only through the store's vocation change) |
| Equipment set | `gear` column: per equipment slot the item's per-item id (`chaos_iid`) or, for a plain item, its type (the de-equipped form: an equipped ring is another id); "empty" for an empty hand | the set's items are moved onto the character (below) |
| Action bar profile | client only: `g_settings` node `loadouts`, per character and slot | the client switches to the profile after a load (`client_settings.changeActiveHotkeyProfile`) |

Not part of a loadout: the Vocation Trial node picks (`trials.lua`; changing a held node costs a Trial Token and gold, which a free
switch would dodge) and the trial nodes themselves (they are kept through every tree change anyway).

**Slots.** 3 for everyone, a 4th at level 200 and a 5th at level 500 (`baseSlots`, `earned`, `maxSlots`), and one more while the
Chaos Pact (the VIP) is active (`pactSlots`, owner approval 2026-10-13; `ChaosPactPerks.loadoutBonus`; a slot over the limit
keeps its loadout, as below). The earned slots are never sold on their own in the store. The Pact's slot is a paid slot in
effect (a loadout slot is worth respec gold: each one keeps a tree that would otherwise cost a full reset); the owner kept it
on 2026-10-13 ("Pode manter"), which replaces the old rule that loadout slots are never sold. A character whose level drops below
an unlock keeps the loadout in that slot (it can be deleted, not saved or loaded, until the level is back). The Chaos Pact's saved
builds (`pact.lua`) are a different thing and stay as they are: account-wide build codes that are applied through the build-code
preview at the respec prices.

**The rules (no respec dodge).** Exactly one loadout is active: the live build is that loadout.
- Save copies the live build into a slot. The server reads the build itself (tree, Paragon, equipped items); the client never sends
  nodes or items. The first save makes that slot active. Saving into another slot is a copy; support runes are not copied (a
  copy keeps the runes it already holds, a new slot holds none).
- A tree only changes while it is live, in the passive tree window, at the normal prices (adding is free; a single-node refund or a
  reset costs what `respec.lua` says). So every tree a loadout holds was paid once; switching between saved loadouts costs nothing.
- Load (switch) parks the live tree, Paragon and runes into the active loadout (nothing is lost, nothing is refunded) and puts the
  target's live. Without an active loadout a switch is refused while the live build holds anything ("save it first"), so a switch
  can never drop a build for free.
- Delete: an inactive loadout that holds support runes cannot be deleted (load it and take them out at the normal price); deleting
  the active loadout leaves the live build as it is. A save over a slot that holds runes of its own is refused while no loadout is
  active.
- The randomized check in `tests/loadouts_test.lua` runs thousands of save / load / delete / priced-edit steps and checks that no
  tree shape ever appears that a priced edit did not make, and that no rune is created or lost.

**Switching.** Out of combat (no fight condition, not PZ-locked), level 8+, not inside an instance (arena, rift, Vocation Trial,
raid, Ember Descent, Infinity Tower, Ascended Omen, siege), `cooldownSeconds` (60) after the last switch. In a protection zone it
is instant; elsewhere it is a `castMs` (3 s) channel: moving or entering combat interrupts it; the bar is drawn by `game_castbar`.

**Validation on load** (against the tree data and the character now; the window shows it before loading). Nodes that left the
tree, nodes that no longer connect (a balance pass moved them), nodes the class may not hold (`ChaosClassTree.allowed`) and nodes
over the owned points (the farthest from the start go first, the rest stays connected) are refunded for free and the player is
told how many and why; Paragon points over the owned points are refunded for free (as at login). Support runes of a spell that
left the game come back as items; a rune type that left the game is dropped. Item level and vocation requirements are the
engine's own (the equip check of the movement scripts).

**Gear.** The set's items are looked for in the equipment, the backpack (every container in it) and, while switching in a
protection zone, the store inbox. First every slot that changes is emptied into the backpack (never merged into a stack), then the
set's items are put on: the engine places a copy in the slot and the item itself is removed in the same step, so it is one item
moved (per-item id and attributes kept), never a duplicate. A two-handed weapon the set does not want is put away when it blocks
the set's shield. Items in a depot are not taken out: the engine saves a depot chest only after the depot was opened in that
session, so an item taken from an unopened depot could come back after a crash. They are named instead ("sword: in your depot
(<town>)"); a missing item is reported and its slot keeps what it had. The supply stash only holds stackable plain items, so no
gear is ever there.

**Season realms.** Loadouts belong to a character (`player_id`); season characters are separate characters, so they have their
own loadouts, and a season character's set only finds that character's items.

**Crash safety.** A switch writes the database first (the slot 0 row: switch serial + 1 and an undo record with the previous live
tree, Paragon and the parked slot's row), then the player storages (runes, active slot, serial), then saves the player at once.
At login a database one serial ahead of the storages (the save never happened) is undone from the undo record; any other mismatch
(a restored backup) takes the database serial.

**Storages and table.** 7100570 active slot, 7100571 switch serial, 7100572 time of the last switch (7100570 - 7100579 reserved);
7112000 - 7127999 the runes of the inactive loadouts (8 slots of 2000, above the live sockets 7110000 - 7111999). Table
`chaos_loadouts`: one row per character and slot (1..5), slot 0 is the character's switch record; `loadouts.lua` also creates it at
startup.

**Protocol** (JSON `{action, data}`): client `open`, `save {slot, name, icon}`, `load {slot}`, `rename {slot, name, icon}`,
`delete {slot}`, `cancel`; server `state` (through `Chaos.sendChunked`), `result {ok, text, lines}`, `cast {ms, slot}`,
`castEnd {result}`. Rate limits per action (`rate`).

**Tests.** `tests/loadouts_test.lua` (LuaJIT and Lua 5.3): slots and unlocks, names and icons, tree validation against the real tree
data (budget trim stays connected for every budget, unknown, class and moved nodes), Paragon, keystone names, the switching gate
and channel, the plans and the randomized no-dodge check, crash recovery, rune layouts and the storage ranges, the gear planner
(per-item id, plain items, one item used once, items from the other hand); then `loadouts.lua` against a mocked engine: save,
copy, switch in a protection zone and through the channel (moving interrupts it), cooldown, combat, runes parked and back, the
sword moved back from the backpack (one sword), a missing item named in the depot, free refunds of a changed tree, a crash
rollback, rename, delete rules, the two-handed weapon put away. Client `game_loadouts/loadoutsview_test.lua`.
Tested on a live test server copy with the client: two loadouts of a Juggernaut (90 nodes with Immovable and 3 runes, 80 nodes
with Bulwark, 2 runes and a two-handed sword), switching in the temple and through the channel outside it, runes and gear moving
both ways without duplicates, the state kept over a server restart, an item left in the depot reported, a saved tree with nodes
that left the tree refunded for free, the Loadouts button in the passive tree window.

## Ember Blessings (`blessings.lua`, `blessings_core.lua`, `blessings_config.lua`)

A monster kill may bless its loot owner for one minute. Numbers live in `blessings_config.lua`, rules in
`blessings_core.lua` (pure, tested), the engine glue in `blessings.lua`. Nothing to install beyond the scripts: no
database table, no storage, no opcode (the buff bar carries it).

**The ember (O243).** A proc drops an ember on the ground instead of blessing at once; see "Ground pickups and globes (O243)".
The roll below is unchanged, and the 20 s cooldown starts at the roll.

**Who rolls.** One roll per kill, in `EventCallback onDropLoot`, for the corpse owner only: the player who dealt the most
damage, or the master of the summon that did. That is the player the Chaos loot is for. Party members do not share the
roll; a party hunt still procs often, since every member owns some of the corpses. No roll for a summon's death, without
stamina for loot (`ChaosLootConfig.minStamina`), or in a PvP place (battleground, arena, siege, a PvP-zone tile, the open
PvP zone module when installed). Season realms make no difference.

**The chance.** By the monster's tier: normal 1.5%, magic 4%, rare 8%, legendary 15%, boss 25% (capped at 40%). A monster at
most 10 levels under the character counts in full; past that its level as a share of the character's level decides:
0.75 or more full, 0.6 half, 0.45 a fifth, below that nothing. The monster level is `ChaosLoot.monsterLevel`. After a proc
no other proc for 20 s (`cooldownMs`), whatever the kind.

**The pool** (weight, one minute each):

| key | name | weight | effect | how |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| xp | Ember of Insight | 20 | +25% experience from monsters | `onGainExperience`, index 6 |
| gold | Ember of Avarice | 18 | +50% gold coins in the corpse | `onDropLoot`, index 2 |
| damage | Ember of Fury | 16 | +15% damage dealt to monsters | `onHealthChange` on the monster, registered by `onTargetCombat` |
| ward | Ember of Warding | 14 | -15% damage taken from monsters | `onHealthChange` / `onManaChange` on the player |
| speed | Ember of Haste | 14 | +25% of the base speed | `CONDITION_HASTE`, sub id 7260 |
| regen | Ember of Renewal | 12 | 2% of max health and mana every 2 s | `CONDITION_REGENERATION`, sub id 7261 |
| crit | Ember of Precision | 12 | +10% critical chance, +25% critical damage | `CONDITION_ATTRIBUTES`, sub id 7262 |
| loot | Ember of Plenty | 10 | +40% Chaos loot (extra rolls, currency, gems, runes) | `loot_config.lua` `rateMult` |
| rarity | Ember of Fortune | 8 | +60 rarity find on gear drops | `loot.lua` rarity find |
| orb | Ember of the Forge | 6 | orbs x2 | `loot.lua` `rollCurrency` |

Damage and ward touch only fights with monsters: no PvP effect.

**Stacking.** The same kind never stacks. A proc of an active kind refreshes it to the full 60 s; the value stays.
Different kinds run side by side, at most 3 (`maxActive`). A new kind past the cap replaces the one with the least time
left, so a proc is never lost.

**Feedback.** A floating label on the player (`ChaosCombatFx.label`, palette byte colours from the config, never hex
strings), a magic effect and a status line. The buff bar shows one row per kind (`blessing_<key>` in
`data/lib/chaos_buffs.lua`, source `blessings`) with its countdown and the effect text. Icons `buff:blessing_<key>`
come from `client/tools/gen_buff_icons.py`: the motif plus a small ember flame in the corner.

**Ends.** A once-a-second look removes what ran out. State lives in memory only: logout, login and death clear it.
Entering a PvP place takes every blessing away, with a message.

**Staff.** `/blessing <key>` gives one now (refresh and cap rules apply). `/blessing list` shows the active ones and the
pool, `/blessing clear` takes them all. `/blessing roll <tier>, <monster level>[, n]` prints the chance for you and n
simulated kills at one kill every 2 s.

**Tests.** `tests/blessings_test.lua` (LuaJIT and Lua 5.3): the config (palette bytes, labels, formats), the chance by tier
and level gap, the cap, the roll reasons, the cooldown, the weighted draw, refresh without stacking, the cap and its
replacement, expiry. Then `blessings.lua` against a mocked engine: a kill blesses the corpse owner (label, effect,
message), no proc inside the cooldown, for a summon, a trivial monster, without stamina or in a PvP place; every effect on
and gone after 60 s; the buff bar rows; logout and `/blessing`.
Tested on a live test server copy with one client: a proc label on a kill, three blessings on the bar with their
countdowns and tooltip, a refresh of the same kind by a kill (48 s back to 58 s, one icon), the cap replacing the
weakest, +25% experience (145 to 181) and +25% speed (2228 to 2785) measured. Not run live: the PvP-place fade, ward, gold.

## Ground pickups and globes (O243) (`pickups.lua`, `pickups_core.lua`, `pickups_config.lua`, `globes.lua`, `globes_core.lua`, `globes_config.lua`, `tools/install_pickups.py`)

Two things lie on the ground for a short time and are taken by walking onto them: the health and mana globes of a kill
and the ember of an Ember Blessing proc. Both use one framework. Server only: no client part, no client build, no opcode,
no storage key, no database table.

**The framework** (`pickups_core.lua` pure and tested, `pickups.lua` the engine glue, `pickups_config.lua` the items and
the shared numbers). A pickup is an item on a tile plus a record in memory (owner, birth, end, callback). `ChaosPickups.drop`
takes the nearest tile with ground, no solid block and no pickup of ours (the corpse tile, then the ring around it, 13
tiles tried), creates the item, starts a glow. Rules:
- **Who takes it.** The owner (the killer, the corpse owner) at any time; the owner's party members once the owner window
  has passed (`ownerWindowMs`: 0 for the globes, so the party at once; 6 s for the ember); **nobody outside the party, ever**,
  and nobody after the end. The party is the owner's party when the step happens (an owner who logged out has none: only they
  could take it). A stranger who steps on it gets "This is not meant for you." and nothing is taken. Monsters and summons
  walk over it untouched.
- **Once.** The step takes the record out first, then runs the callback; a second step or a second creature finds nothing.
  The callback may refuse (it returns false): the record goes back and the pickup stays. The globes refuse a full bar, so
  it stays for a hurt party member; the ember refuses a PvP place.
- **Lifetime.** A half-second look-out (`tickMs`) ends a pickup at its time: the item goes with a fade effect
  (`CONST_ME_POFF`) and grants nothing. The glow pulses (a red, blue or violet magic effect) every 1.5 s so it is easy to see.
- **Not an item to keep.** The nodes are neither pickupable nor moveable (`install_pickups.py`), so they cannot go into a
  bag, be pushed, traded or sold; they hold no game value. Nothing is saved: the record is in memory, and a map save does
  not keep ground items outside houses. **After a restart or a reload** the record is gone; an item that is still on a tile
  (a crash, a reload) is removed by the first step on it and grants nothing, and its items.xml entry decays by itself after
  90 s (`failsafeSeconds`, `item:decay()` at creation). Relogging does not change a pickup (it lies on the ground, not in
  the character).

**The items** (new items.otb nodes, installed by `python3 -I tools/install_pickups.py DATA_DIR`, step `pickups` of
`install_all.py`, idempotent, test `tools/install_pickups_test.py`; server ids 32088-32090, 32087 stays free):
| id | item | look |
|---|---|---|
| 32088 | health globe | a red glass globe on a dark base (client item 44397 of pair 55, `gen_portal_art.py`; the node is copied from the stock health potion node of client id 7618 with the client id 44397 written, `stockClientId` in `pickups_config.lua`; stackable) |
| 32089 | mana globe | the same globe in blue (client item 44398, the owner-approved recolour of the health globe, red hues turned to blue; node copied from client id 7620; stackable) |
| 32090 | ember | the violet portal in a stone ring (client item 44396 of pair 55, `gen_portal_art.py`; the node is copied from the Ember Orb node of client id 25045 with the client id 44396 written, `stockClientId` in `pickups_config.lua`), the name and text per blessing (item attributes); glow `CONST_ME_PURPLEENERGY` |
All three pickups wear looks of ours (pair 55, client/MANIFEST.md "Pair 55"; PixelLab art, `gen_portal_art.py`): **the step
installs only while `chaosClientPair` is 55 or more** ("Client pair guard"; below it the step prints a warning and writes
nothing), else they would show as unknown items. An older install's nodes (the
globes on the potion looks 7618 / 7620, the ember on 25045) are rewritten to the new client ids by the same step. The potion
items and the Ember Orb (server 32258) keep their own client ids. The glow is a magic effect pulsing on the tile (red, blue, violet). The pickup effect is a magic effect and
the heal number is the game's own (green for health, blue for mana). A pickup sound would need an event in `game_chaossound`
(its heal sounds are keyed by magic effect themes); none is added.

**The globes** (`globes_core.lua` pure and tested, `globes_config.lua` every number, `globes.lua` the hook).
- **The drop.** `EventCallback onDropLoot` (index 8), for the corpse owner (the player who dealt the most damage, or the
  master of the summon that did: **a minion's kill counts for its owner**, a Necromancer's raised minion included). Two
  independent rolls, health and mana, on the **lowest share of max** among the owner and the party members within 12 tiles on
  the same floor. The curve: 0% at 60% of max or more, 35% at 30%, 50% at 10% (linear between, flat below); plus a flat 3% for
  rare, 5% legendary, 10% boss monsters (`flat`), whatever the bars; at most 60% (`maxChance`). A character with under 30
  maximum mana gets no mana globe (and no flat chance for it).
- **The pickup.** 18% of the maximum health or mana (`healthPct`, `manaPct`). Health goes through `doTargetCombat` with
  `COMBAT_HEALING`, as the Everfull potions do, so the passive tree's Healing and the PvP healing rule apply to it; mana adds
  the stored tree Healing percent (`potions_config.lua storage.healingPct`, 7102481). 15 s on the ground (`lifetimeMs`).
- **Anti-abuse.** Per killer and kind: no new globe for 5 s (`cooldownMs`), at most 2 of a kind on the ground (`maxAlive`).
  Monsters more than 10 levels under the character and under 0.45 of its level drop none (`levelGap`: no farming trivial
  packs), nor does a character without stamina for loot, nor a summoned monster that dies (the Necromancer's raised
  minions cannot be farmed). One item a tile. State is in memory.
- **Where nothing drops** (`pickups_config.lua blocked`): the registered instances `arena`, `battleground`, `siege`,
  `tower` (the Infinity Tower), `trials`, `tutorial` (`Chaos.inAnyInstance`), PvP-zone tiles (`ChaosBlessings.pvpPlace`), and
  any `boxes` entry (`{x1, y1, x2, y2, z}`). **The Tower Defense of the base script is no registered instance**
  (`instance_limits.lua` knows it only as the boss room `towerdefense`), so its room is a box: `{31180, 32239, 31236, 32277, 8}`,
  the `fromPos` / `toPos` of the base script (the same values `tests/base_eventrooms_patch_test.lua` mirrors; the patch
  `patch_base_eventrooms.py` hands them to the boss rooms as `bossArea`). `tests/globes_test.lua` checks the corners, the
  middle and one tile outside on every side and on the floor above. If a base script change moves the room, change the box.
  Dungeons, rifts, boss rooms and the open map drop globes (owner 2026-10-26: "Mantenha os globos").

**The Ember Blessings on the ground** (`blessings.lua`, `blessings_config.lua pickup`). A proc no longer blesses at once:
the same roll (chance, level gap, PvP-place exclusion, stamina, the 20 s cooldown **which now starts at the roll**) drops an
ember named after the drawn blessing ("Ember of Insight": look at it for the effect). Whoever takes it gets the blessing
exactly as before (one minute, the cap, the buff bar, the label): the corpse owner at once, the owner's party after 6 s
(`pickup.ownerWindowMs`), nobody else; it lies 30 s (`pickup.lifetimeMs`), then goes out and gives nothing. Taking it in a
PvP place leaves it on the ground. The owner gets "A dying ember drops: <name>. Step on it within 30 seconds."; the pickup
message is the old proc line, now translated. If the pickup cannot be made (`pickup.enabled = false`, `install_pickups.py`
not run, no free tile) the blessing goes to the owner at once, as before. `/blessing <key>` still gives one directly.

**Install.** `python3 -I server/tools/install_all.py SERVER_DIR --only pickups`, then `files` (the scripts) and a restart. Before
the step runs the globes do nothing and the blessings work as before.

**Tests.** `tests/globes_test.lua` (LuaJIT and Lua 5.3): the configs, the take rule (owner, party after the window, strangers,
expiry, once), the curve and the flat chance (and about 35% of 20000 kills at 30%), amounts, level gap and cooldown; then
`pickups.lua` and `globes.lua` against a mocked engine: a drop near the corpse, the step (monster, stranger, owner, party
member, full bar, a leftover item), the lifetime and fade, the pulses, the cooldown and the limit of two, mana with the tree
percent, every blocked place and no free tile. `tests/blessings_test.lua` has the ember path. `tools/install_pickups_test.py`.
Not run live: the glue's engine calls (`Tile`, `Game.createItem`, `MoveEvent`, `Item:setAttribute` / `decay`, `Party`) are the
ones other scripts here use, but this has only run against the mock.

**To check live.** Run the install step and restart. Take a character to 25% health, kill monsters (raise the chance with
`globes_config.lua` for a test): a red globe glows on the corpse, a step heals 18%; a second character outside the party
cannot take it; wait 15 s and it fades; a character in the arena gets none. Force an ember with `/blessing roll` (simulation
only) or many kills of rare monsters: the ember shows the blessing's name when looked at.

## Charms (`charms.lua`, `charms_core.lua`, `charms_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_charms.sql`, `tools/install_charms.py`, client `game_charms`)

A second, small place for minor bonuses: the 10.98 client has no free equipment slot, so charms go into a per-character
**charm grid** in a window of its own (Character > Charms, extended opcode **198**, `ChaosOpcodes.charms`). Every number is in
`charms_config.lua`; the rules are pure in `charms_core.lua` (`tests/charms_test.lua`, LuaJIT and Lua 5.3).

**Items.** `tools/install_charms.py` (`install_all.py` step `charms`) adds copies of stock nodes (their client looks, no client
change): 32301 small charm (1x1, arcane insignia), 32302 tall charm (1x2, elven brooch), 32303 wide charm (2x1, heavy medal),
32304 grand charm (2x2, golden figurine), the uniques 32305 Gravewarden's Seal (1x2, frost charm), 32306 Wanderer's Compass
(2x1, hero's medal), 32307 Eye of the Hoard (2x2, oracle figurine), 32308 Ashen Tally (1x1, royal medal), and the stackable
32309 charm shard (onyx chip). Charms are never stackable. A rolled charm keeps its rarity, item level and modifiers as custom
attributes (`charm_r`, `chaos_ilvl`, `charm_k1/charm_v1`, `charm_k2/charm_v2`; a unique only its item level) and a look text
("Radiant, item level 100, 2x2 cells. Damage to Undead +9%. ..."). They are ordinary items: they trade, and the market lists
them (its key-list codec carries the charm keys too, `market.lua` customKeys).

**Grid and unlocks.** 5 x 4 cells. Open from the start: columns 1-3 of rows 1-2 (6 cells); level 200: columns 4-5 of rows 1-2
(+4); level 400: row 3, columns 1-3 (+3); level 600: row 3, columns 4-5 (+2); level 800: row 4, columns 1-3 (+3); the achievement
"Edge of Ruin" (`rift_t10`, seal a tier 10 rift; account-wide like every achievement): row 4, columns 4-5 (+2). A charm needs
all its cells open, inside the grid and free; at most 20 charms. A charm on a cell that closes again (a lost level) stays
placed and gives nothing until it opens again (shown dimmed). Place, move and take out: level 8+, out of combat (no fight
condition, not PZ-locked), anywhere.

**Rolls.** Shape by weight (small 50, tall 20, wide 20, grand 10); rarity Faint (60, 1 modifier, x0.7), Glowing (30, 1
modifier, x0.85), Radiant (10, 2 modifiers, x1.0); item level 1-100 scales the roll from x0.5 to x1.0. A modifier rolls its
1x1 range x the shape (small 1.0, tall / wide 1.7, grand 3.0: bigger charms roll stronger but less per cell) x rarity x item
level, rounded, at least 1; two modifiers of one charm are never the same key nor two of one group (families, elements).

| Modifier (charm pool) | 1x1 range | Best roll (grand) | Charm cap (all charms) | One gear slot's best | Where it acts |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Damage to Dragons / Demons / Undead / Humans / Humanoids / Beasts / Elementals / Insects and Arachnids | 1-3% | 9% | 15% each | 16% (Elites and Bosses T8) | `charms.lua` onHealthChange on the monster; the family is the bestiary category of the monster's type name |
| Fire / Ice / Energy / Earth / Death / Holy Resistance | 1-2% | 6% | 8% each | 7% (absorb T8) | `charms.lua` onHealthChange on the player, that element only |
| Life on Kill | 4-10 | 30 | 60 | 150 | the gear totals (`item_mods.lua`), under the gear cap 300 too |
| Gold Find | 1-2% | 6% | 10% | 20% | the gear totals, under the gear cap 40% too |
| Orb Find | 1-3% | 9% | 20% | 12% (Item Find T8) | `loot.lua`: the currency layer's chances (orbs, whetstones) x (1 + total) |
| Movement Speed out of Combat | 1-2% | 6% | 8% | 11% (Movement Speed T8) | a 1 s think: +N% of the base speed while not in combat |
| Reputation | 1-3% | 9% | 15% | - | `factions.lua` F.gain: positive gains + N% |
| Rift Time | 5-12 s | 36 s | 90 s | - | `rift.lua`: the opener's total lengthens a new run |

No charm beats a gear slot: `charms_core.lua` C.validate (run at startup and by the test) fails a pool key whose best roll is
not below its `gearRef` (the matching gear modifier's T8 top, which the test reads from `chaos_item_mods.lua`), and a unique
whose fixed values are not.

| Unique | Shape | Modifiers | Signature |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gravewarden's Seal | 1x2 | Damage to Undead +6%, Death Resistance +4% | Last Ember: once every 10 minutes a hit that would kill you leaves you at 1 health (storage 7100471) |
| Wanderer's Compass | 2x1 | Movement Speed out of Combat +5%, Rift Time +20 s | Wayfarer's Rest: out of combat 1% of your health and mana every 2 s |
| Eye of the Hoard | 2x2 | Orb Find +8%, Gold Find +5% | Hoard Sense: +15% Treasure Goblin Chance (gear totals, cap 15 from charms) |
| Ashen Tally | 1x1 | Life on Kill +12 | Harvester: Mana on Kill = half the charms' Life on Kill (cap 30 from charms) |

**Totals.** The placed charms whose cells are all open are summed per key and capped by the charm cap. The keys of the gear
catalogue (Life on Kill, Gold Find, Treasure Goblin Chance, Mana on Kill) go to `item_mods.lua` as an extra source of
`M.refresh` (one guarded hunk, like the item set bonuses: `ChaosCharms.extra`), so the gear caps still hold over items + sets
+ charms; the other keys stay in `ChaosCharms` and are read by the hooks above. The window shows the totals (a capped one is
marked).

**Drops** (only online characters; backpack, else the store inbox; `ChaosCharms.onSource` from one guarded line per source):

| Source | Chance per player | Item level |
|---|---|---|
| A sealed rift of tier 6+ (each finisher; not omens) | 6% + 1% per tier above 6, at most 15% | 40 + 4 x tier |
| A completed bounty contract | 4% | level / 10, 30-80 |
| A rewarded invasion defender / liberator | 10% (rank 1: 25%) | area level / 10, 40-90 |
| A cleared dungeon (each member) | 8% + 2% per difficulty | 50 + 5 x difficulty |
| An Ember Descent room cleared (each player in the run) | 3% (the boss room 15%) | 40 + 3 x depth |

2% of the charm drops are a unique instead (equal odds). Staff: `/charm give <small|tall|wide|grand|gravewarden|compass|hoard|tally> [rarity] [item level]`.

**Shards.** Salvage (the window's button, a charm of your backpack; a locked item is refused): small 2, tall / wide 4, grand 8
shards (+2 for Radiant), a unique 15. Reforge: rolls a charm's values again (same modifiers, rarity and item level) for small 6,
tall / wide 12, grand 24 shards; uniques cannot be reforged.

**Safety: a placed charm is never an item too (no duplication).** The approach of the market's escrow (`market.lua`), the
safest the repo has for moving an item out of a character: a placed charm leaves the character and lives only in its
`chaos_charms` row: `data` = the item's attributes in the engine's own binary form (`item:serializeAttributes()`, engine patch
0017, hex, codec `blob`; without the patch the charm's attribute list, codec `attrs`), `charm` = its summary for the totals.
Taken out, the item is made again from the row (`unserializeAttributes`, a new per-item id) and the row is deleted. Moving a
charm only changes the row's x, y. A hidden container was not used: the engine saves a depot chest only after it was opened
in that session ("Loadouts", Gear), and an item in any container can still be moved, traded or changed by other scripts; a
row cannot.
Every place / take is crash safe (`charms_core.lua` C.place / C.take, the market's listing order): 1. the row is written
"pending" (state 9 placing, 8 taking) with the next serial of storage 7100470; 2. the item leaves (or is made) in memory and
the storage takes the serial; 3. `player:save()` writes items and storage in one transaction; 4. the row is marked placed (or
deleted). A failed save puts everything back. At login a pending row is settled by the saved serial (C.recoverAction):
placing and serial <= saved -> placed, else dropped (the item never left the saved inventory); taking and serial <= saved ->
dropped (the item reached the saved inventory), else back in the grid. Characters with `players.save = 0` cannot use the grid.
`tests/charms_test.lua` crashes the simulated world at every step of both operations and checks that exactly one charm
exists after the login; the mocked-engine part crashes `charms.lua` inside the save and after it, for a place and a take.

**Protocol** (JSON `{action, data}`): client `open`, `place {ref | pos, sid, iid, x, y}` (`ref`: the server's path in the
backpack, `s3.0.5`; `pos`: an item dragged in from an open container), `move {id, x, y}`, `take {id}`, `salvage {ref, sid,
iid}`, `reforge {ref, sid, iid}`; server `state {cols, rows, cells, placed, bag, groups, totals, level, shards, max}` (through
`Chaos.sendChunked`) and `result {ok, text}`. Rate limits per action (`rate`).

**Storages and table.** 7100470 the place / take serial, 7100471 the Last Ember cooldown (7100470 - 7100479 reserved). Table
`chaos_charms` (id, player_id, state, seq, x, y, item_id, codec, data, charm, placed_at; `sql/chaos_charms.sql`, also created
by `charms.lua` at startup).

**Client** (`game_charms`, Chaos skin, 640 x 520): the grid (open cells, locked cells with a padlock and the reason as tooltip,
placed charms sized by their shape with the rarity colour as border and their icon), the Cells list (each unlock, open or
locked), Your Charms (the charms in the backpack), Totals, Salvage / Reforge / Close. Drag a charm from the list onto the grid
(the cells it would cover light up green or red under it), drag a placed charm to move it or onto the list to take it out; an
item dragged in from an open backpack works too. Each charm has a tooltip (name, rarity, item level, shape, modifiers,
signature, inactive, salvage / reforge cost). Looks: each charm is drawn as an item sprite of the live pair (a UIItem),
picked by its `icon` key (the unique, else its first modifier) in `charmsview.lua` `V.LOOKS`: one trinket per modifier and
unique, none shared (dragon necklace for Damage to Dragons, glacier amulet for Ice Resistance, compass for the Wanderer's
Compass, ...). A key without an entry shows the charm item's own look (`item`, the client id the state carries). 32 px; a
2x2 charm 64 px (twice, whole pixels). Cells and charms sit in the skin's slots (`gen_skin.py` `charmslot_1x1/2x1/1x2/2x2`,
drawn at the exact tile size); the rarity is the frame colour, and Glowing, Radiant and Unique charms also glow; locked
cells are dimmed slots with the depot padlock. The server side is unchanged. Logic without client API: `charmsview.lua`
(`charmsview_test.lua`: one look per key of `charms_config.lua`, none shared, a slot image per shape at the right size).

**Tested on a live test server** (own server copy and database, one client, a level 1000 character): six charms placed through
the protocol and by dragging with the mouse (the green preview, a drop on the locked achievement cells refused with the
reason, a placed charm dragged back onto the list and taken out, then placed again), the rows in `chaos_charms` with codec
`blob`, the totals (Gold Find reached `ChaosItemMods.playerBonus`, out-of-combat speed +5% applied), the grid kept over a
server restart, salvage and reforge with shards, the look text, 60 tier 15 rift drops (8 charms). Not run in game: a real
crash, the drop hooks from real rifts, bounties, invasions, dungeons and Descent rooms (called directly), the market listing of
a charm.

## The Gambler (`gamble.lua`, `gamble_core.lua`, `gamble_config.lua`, `tools/install_gamble.py`, client `game_gamble`)

Mordecai Ashwager, the Gambler, sells sealed equipment for gold: the base type, the slot and the item level are shown, the
rarity is hidden until the piece is bought. Every number is in `gamble_config.lua`; the rules are pure in `gamble_core.lua`.

**The stock.** Each character sees its own stock of 14 pieces (`stock.size`). It is new at fixed times every 4 hours: 00:00,
04:00, 08:00, 12:00, 16:00 and 20:00 of the **server's time zone** (the clock of the machine, as every other daily and weekly
reset). `refresh.utcOffsetHours = -3` pins the times to UTC-3 (the owner's clock) whatever the machine is set to; with the
machine on UTC and the default `nil`, the stock changes at 21:00, 01:00, 05:00, ... UTC-3. The window shows the time of the
next stock, the zone and a countdown. The stock is computed, not stored: a Park-Miller generator seeded by the character, the
window number and the early refreshes bought in it (`K.seed`), the same under LuaJIT and Lua 5.3, after a relog and after a
restart (the test pins one stock). Five player storages (7101900 - 7101904) hold the window the stock belongs to, the level
and vocation it was made for (frozen at the first look in a window, so a level up does not reshuffle it), the sold slots (a
bit mask) and the early refreshes. No database rows.

**Equipment set pieces** (pair 28, `sets` in the config): see "Equipment sets (pair 28)", The Gambler.

**What is offered.** Each piece draws a slot (weights weapon 3, armour / helmet / legs / boots 2, shield / amulet / ring /
quiver 1) and a base type from `gamble_config.lua` `pool` (246 stock bases of the base server, each with the level it
belongs to; the 12 quiver bases of "Infinite arrows and quivers" since that change, priced like a helmet, offered only to the
bow classes, whom their movements.xml entries name: for anyone else the slot is drawn again, so their stocks are unchanged):
the 4 bases with the highest level the character can use (`base.choices`). "Can use" is read from the installed
`data/movements/movements.xml` (Equip entries: level and vocations, as rewritten by `add_vocations.py`) and
`data/weapons/weapons.xml` (level, vocations); items with charges or a duration, uniques and non-gear never come. A slot with
nothing usable is drawn again. The **item level** is between gate - 6 and the gate, where the gate is what a kill of a monster
of the character's level gives (`ChaosItemMods.sourceLevel`, tier normal: 36 at 100, 90 at 500, 123 at 1000): never above
the drops' own curve.

**Prices** (gold, `price.curve` x `price.slot`, rounded to 100). An armour piece costs about 18% of an hour of hunting at the
level whose kills give that item level (the hunting model of `professions_config.lua`; the test checks every level 8-1500
stays between 8% and 35%). A whole stock costs about two and a half hours of hunting, so nobody buys every crate of every
window. Gold comes from the backpack first, then the bank (`Chaos.pay`).

| Level | Gate | Weapon x1.3 | Armour x1.15 | Amulet, ring x1.1 | Helmet, legs, shield x1 | Boots x0.9 | Early refresh | Hunting / h |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 4 | 3,900 | 3,400 | 3,300 | 3,000 | 2,700 | 1,700 | 19,000 |
| 50 | 22 | 26,000 | 23,000 | 22,000 | 20,000 | 18,000 | 11,500 | 129,000 |
| 100 | 36 | 72,800 | 64,400 | 61,600 | 56,000 | 50,400 | 32,200 | 358,839 |
| 200 | 54 | 126,100 | 111,500 | 106,700 | 97,000 | 87,300 | 55,700 | 620,352 |
| 300 | 67 | 195,000 | 172,500 | 165,000 | 150,000 | 135,000 | 86,200 | 881,866 |
| 500 | 90 | 1,105,000 | 977,500 | 935,000 | 850,000 | 765,000 | 488,700 | 5,548,330 |
| 700 | 106 | 1,430,000 | 1,265,000 | 1,210,000 | 1,100,000 | 990,000 | 632,500 | 7,136,882 |
| 1000 | 123 | 1,950,000 | 1,725,000 | 1,650,000 | 1,500,000 | 1,350,000 | 862,500 | 9,519,711 |
| 1500 | 136 | 2,145,000 | 1,897,500 | 1,815,000 | 1,650,000 | 1,485,000 | 948,700 | 9,519,711 |

(Prices at the gate; a piece a few item levels lower costs a little less.)

**Early refresh** ("Fresh Crates", next to the Gambler): a new stock now for half an armour piece at the gate, doubled for each
earlier one in the same window, three per window (`reroll`). It only changes which bases and item levels are offered (the
rarity is rolled at the purchase), and it clears the sold marks: every crate is still paid in full, so it is another sink.

**The rarity** is rolled only after the gold is taken, the slot is marked sold and the character is saved
(`Chaos.saveCharacter`, the shared "save before a database credit" rule): a failed save gives the gold back (to the bank),
unmarks the slot and rolls nothing; a crash after the save loses at most the piece, never duplicates it. The roll is the loot
layer's own (`ChaosLoot.stockRarity` then `ChaosLoot.upgradeRarity`, the API monster drops and the rift, raid and goblin
rewards use) as a magic monster's gear drop, raised to at least Common and capped at Divine (`odds`; no item find). The piece
is made with `ChaosCrafting.createItem(id, rarity, item level)` (modifiers, tiers, prefixes and suffixes as on drops) and
gets sockets like a drop (`ChaosGems.rollDropSockets`); a full backpack sends it to the inbox. Odds per crate (exact,
`ChaosGambleCore.odds`, checked by the test against 200,000 rolls of the real `loot.lua` functions):

| Rarity | Gamble | Normal monster gear drop | Magic monster gear drop |
|---|---|---|---|
| plain | 0% | 67.31% | 60.58% |
| Common | 70.03% | 10.50% | 13.49% |
| Uncommon | 12.17% | 8.33% | 10.15% |
| Magic | 8.36% | 6.14% | 7.01% |
| Rare | 5.45% | 4.50% | 4.78% |
| Legendary | 3.62% | 2.84% | 3.62% |
| Divine | 0.38% | 0.38% | 0.38% |
| **Legendary or better** | **3.99%** | 3.21% | 3.99% |

So a crate is always at least as good as a magic monster's gear drop at every rarity up to Divine, never plain, and Legendary
is exactly as rare as from a magic monster's drop (about one crate in 28; before the seven rarities Legendary or better was 13%). A Divine
reveal is told to the players within 8 tiles (`announceFrom`).

**Safety.** Rate limited (`Chaos.limited`, 300 ms per player). A purchase holds a per-character lock, so a second request
while one runs (or from inside the save) is refused; the sold bit is set before the save, so the same slot cannot be paid
for twice. The client sends the window number and the item id it saw: a purchase across a refresh or of another piece is
refused ("The stock has changed"). Buying and the early refresh need the Gambler within 4 tiles; the window opens anywhere
(to look and to see the countdown).

**The NPC** (`data/npc/Mordecai Ashwager.xml`, script `mordecai_ashwager.lua`, installed by `tools/install_gamble.py`,
`install_all.py` step `gamble`): placed at startup (3 s after the other temple NPCs) in its stall in the hub for the towns of `npc.towns` (`{2}`; else next to the temple)
(Cinderhold, the main city, then Mirewake), on the first free tile of `npc.offsets` (none of the Material Broker's, the Ascendant Oracle's, the Keeper of Trials',
the Great Brazier's or the Descent / raid / world boss portals' offsets). "gamble" / "trade" / "crates" / "buy" opens the
window (opcode 199 `npc`); "odds" and "refresh" answer in the NPC channel.

Protocol (opcode 199, JSON `{action, data}`): client -> server `open` | `close` | `buy {i, w, id}` | `reroll {w}`; server ->
client `state` (`K.payload`, through `Chaos.sendChunked`: `w`, `items {i, id, c, n, s, sn, l, p, sold}`, `level`, `gate`,
`near`, `money`, `left`, `hours`, `at`, `tz`, `reroll`, `rerolls`, `rerollMax`, `odds {r, n, p}`, `npc`, `last`), `result {ok,
text, reveal {r, rn, id, c, n, l, s, i}}`, `npc {}`. Staff: `/gamble Name` (window, level, gate, sold, refreshes), `/gamble
Name, new` (a new stock now), `/gamble odds`.

**Client** (`game_gamble`, Economy > The Gambler): a grid of crates (look with a "?" seal, name, slot, item level, price in red
when you cannot pay, Buy), the countdown to the next stock and its time and zone, "Fresh Crates" with its price, the odds line,
and the reveal of the last crate in its rarity colour.

**Tests:** `tests/gamble_test.lua` (LuaJIT and Lua 5.3): config check; window boundaries (03:59:59 / 04:00:00 / 07:59:59 /
08:00:00 at UTC-3, six windows a day, the server's own zone on 4-hour marks); prices, their rounding and rise, the share of
hunting gold per hour at every level 8-1500, the early refresh price; bases (the best four, usable, at or below the level),
stock determinism (same character and window, another window / character / refresh), item levels never above the gate at
any level, a pinned stock; the sold mask; the exact odds (sum 1, never plain, cap, Legendary no more often than a magic drop,
at least as good as normal and magic drops at every rarity, 200,000 real rolls); every purchase refusal; and `gamble.lua`
against a mocked engine: reading movements.xml / weapons.xml, the NPC placement, the window state (no rarity sent), a
purchase (gold from the backpack then the bank, the sold mark, two saves, the item at its item level with its rarity, the
reveal), the same slot again, an old window, a wrong piece, too little gold, a failed save (gold back, nothing rolled), two
requests at once and a re-entrant one, a full backpack, away from the Gambler, the rate limit, a relog and a restart (same
stock, same sold slots), a level up inside a window, the early refresh (price, doubling, three at most, away), the next
window, a Mystic's stock. Client: `game_gamble/gambleview_test.lua`.

**Tested in game** (test server on the full map with a private MariaDB, one client with the things_custom15 pair, a level
1000 Warrior): the Gambler placed next to the main temple (the first four offsets taken, he stood on {1, 5}), "hi" and
"gamble" opening the window, 14 Warrior pieces at item level 117-123 with prices of 1.33M-1.95M, eight purchases (Common,
Common, Rare, Epic, Exotic, ...; storages and bank balance saved at once; a full inventory sending pieces to the inbox), the
same stock and sold slot after a server restart and a relogin, the window from Economy > The Gambler, Fresh Crates (862,500
gold, a new stock, the next one 1.73M), the Buy buttons off and a forced request refused away from the Gambler. Not seen: a
refresh at the 4-hour mark with the window open, the Divine announcement, two characters at once.

## Candlemarks (`candlemarks.lua`, `candlemarks_core.lua`, `candlemarks_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_candlemarks.sql`, `tools/install_candlemarks.py`, NPC `data/npc/Osric the Chandler.xml`, client `game_candlemarks`)
A currency for time online (owner decision 2026-10-15): one Candlemark for every 30 minutes a character is online,
spent on help to progress. The brief called it "Vigil Coins"; the name is Candlemarks because "Vigil" is taken twice
already (the Vigils auras, `vigils*.lua`, `ChaosVigils`, buff keys `vigil_*`; and the Vigil faction). The name lives in
`candlemarks_config.lua` messages, `i18n_strings.lua` and the client's pt-BR table, so the owner can rename it.

- **Earning.** A GlobalEvent every minute (`tickSeconds`) adds the time since the last tick to every online character
  that earns. Owner rules: every online character earns, idle or not (no activity or AFK rule), several characters of
  one account each earn, training online counts (offline training is logged out). Limits: at most `earn.maxPerIp` (2)
  characters per IP address earn at once: per IP the earliest logins (then the lower character id); when one of them
  logs out, the next in that order earns from the next tick; the others keep their progress, frozen
  (`ChaosCandlemarksCore.pickEarners`). A character without a connection (IP 0) is not limited. Staff (group 4+)
  never earn; `earn.minLevel` (1) and `earn.dailyCap` (0, none) are there for the owner.
- **The idle kick.** The stock `config.lua` has `kickIdlePlayerAfterMinutes = 15` (the engine warns 15 minutes after a
  character's last action and kicks it a minute later; 0 is no "off", it kicks after one minute), which would end an
  idle character's Candlemarks. `tools/patch_base_idle_kick.py SERVER_DIR [--minutes N]` (step `idlekick` of
  `install_all.py`, right after `candlemarks`; idempotent, only that line changes, a trailing comment kept, the key
  appended when missing) sets it to 1440 (a day). `prod_config.py` leaves it alone. Test:
  `tools/patch_base_idle_kick_test.py` (a copy of the stock text, CI).
- **Scope.** The balance is per ACCOUNT (`chaos_candlemarks`): every character of the account sees and spends it, and
  every earning character adds to it. The progress to the next coin is per CHARACTER (`chaos_candlemark_progress`) and
  survives logouts and restarts. A tick credits at most `maxTickSeconds` (a server stall gives no burst).
- **Writes.** A coin: the account's balance and the character's progress in one transaction. The progress also every
  5 ticks and at logout, so a crash loses at most a few minutes of progress and never adds a coin.
- **Shop** (`C.offers`; prices and limits decided, docs/OWNER_TODO.md "Decided"): pocket boss charges
  (one offer per boss of `ChaosPocketBoss.bosses()`, sharing one weekly limit, the boss's own level counts; delivered with
  `ChaosPocketBoss.addCharges`, 0 added = refunded with its reason), the common orbs (Awakening, Ember, Tempering,
  Unmaking, Grafting once a week; the chase orbs Echoes, Fate, Dawn and the Orb of Ruin are refused by
  `K.validate`), Whetstones, Chipped and Flawed gems of a random type, Rune Shards, four supply bundles and four Supply
  Crates sharing one limit (a crate is four bundles of its tier for three bundles' price; tier IV at level 200: supreme
  health and ultimate mana potions; 2026-10-23), and offers for other systems' APIs that show only while the API exists (`kind = "call"`: a rested vial
  `ChaosRested.addVials`, bounty and kill task rerolls `ChaosBounty.addRerolls` / `ChaosBestiary.addRerolls`; none exist
  yet), and three cosmetics of our own, once per account (`ChaosCosmetics.grant`, source `"candlemarks"` in
  `cosmetics_config.lua`: never sold for Chaos Coins, no exclusive): Candle Seal (kill effect, 150), Candlelight Name
  (chat colour, 120), Tallow Labels (loot labels, 100). Every offer has a weekly limit per account (Monday 06:00, the
  bounty board's week) and a minimum level. Prices and limits decided by the owner on 2026-10-15.
- **Buying only at Osric** (owner 2026-10-15, `npc.buyNearNpc = true`). The window, the counter and the catalogue work
  anywhere; a purchase needs Osric the Chandler within `npc.range` (3) tiles on the same floor, checked by the server
  (`ChaosCandlemarks.near`); otherwise "Visit Osric the Chandler at the temple to buy." and nothing is written. The state
  carries `near`, so the window shows where to buy and turns Buy off; an owned cosmetic shows "Owned".
- **Buying, the write order (no duplicate on a crash).** One purchase at a time per character, one a second. (1) the
  checks; (2) one transaction: the balance taken with `UPDATE ... WHERE balance >= price` (`ROW_COUNT`) and the purchase
  row written pending with what it delivers; (3a) items: given (backpack, the rest to the inbox), the delivery mark
  (storage 7102460) set to the row id, the character saved (items and mark in one save), the row done; (3b) a pocket
  boss charge, a call or a cosmetic: the mark set and the character saved first, then the API; a failure refunds.
  At login, pending rows at or under the mark were delivered (row settled), rows over it were not (items given now,
  other kinds refunded, never called). The one loss case: a crash between 3b's save and its call; staff refund it.
- **Client** `game_candlemarks`: a counter next to the Chaos menu bar (balance, minutes to the next coin counted down
  in the client, "paused" with the reason as tooltip; a click opens the shop) and the shop window (Economy >
  Candlemarks; Osric the Chandler's trade opens it too (its stall in the hub in town 2, next to the temples of towns 1, 3-5); buying only next to him). No player talkaction (owner rule:
  commands live in the menu). Opcode 176 (free in the reference server, the base client and every Chaos module;
  "Opcode collision check"): `open`, `buy {k}`; `hud` every minute, `state`, `result`, `npc`.
- **Staff.** `/candlemarks <name>` (look, group 4); `/candlemarks <name>, give <n>`, `take <n>`, `refund <purchase id>`
  (group 5, logged by `Chaos.staffCommand`).
- **Install.** `tools/install_candlemarks.py DATA_DIR` (step `candlemarks` of `install_all.py`, after `gamble`) copies the
  NPC; the tables come from the sql step (also created at startup).
- Tests: `tests/candlemarks_test.lua` (blocks, the daily cap, the IP limit as characters log in and out, offers and
  guards, checks, gems, recovery; the engine against a mocked engine and database: earning per character into the
  account, progress across a relog, purchases, weekly limits, the inbox, the transaction order, both crash cases,
  the guarded offers, refunds, staff), `opcode_fuzz_test.lua`, client `candlemarksview_test.lua` and the client
  fuzz test. Not run on a live server or in a client yet.
- **Empty list fixed (2026-10-23).** The window's offer list sits inside `listFrame`, and `render()` read `window.list`,
  which is nil (the engine sets only direct children as fields): the header showed, the list stayed empty and the
  error was swallowed by `safe()`. It now reads `window.listFrame.list`. `tools/ci/check_modules.py` refuses a
  `window.<id>` whose id is only nested in the module's `.otui` (it also found the Chronicle's tab buttons).

## Conquest Tokens, the Conquest vendor and bad-luck protection (`conquest.lua`, `conquest_core.lua`, `conquest_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_conquest.sql`, `tools/install_conquest.py`, NPC `data/npc/Iselde Varrow.xml`, client `game_conquest`)

The owner's rule (2026-10-15): everything a player needs has a deterministic path; luck only decides the maximum
(perfect rolls, top rarities, the best legendary power). Three parts: a currency for every boss and clear, a vendor
that sells any unique or set piece the character has seen, and bad-luck protection on every chase roll.

**Tokens.** A per-character balance (`chaos_conquest`; every grant and purchase in `chaos_conquest_log`, kept
`logKeepDays` = 60 days). Per character, not per account, so a season character or an alt starts at 0 like the raid's
Sepulchre Marks. Decided 2026-10-15: per character (alts already have the experience catch-up, and no mule can
funnel tokens); a season character is a character of its own, so it earns and spends its own tokens. Public API for other systems:
- `ChaosConquest.grant(player, sourceKey, amount)`: gives the tokens under the source's daily cap; safe to call as often
  as wanted (an unknown source, a non-player or a reached cap gives 0); logged; tells the player once in the loot channel.
  The returning-player bonus of the catch-up system (`ChaosCatchup.tokenMult(player)`, e.g. x1.5) multiplies the amount
  first (rounded to the nearest token, before the cap; never on salvage).
- `ChaosConquest.reward(player, sourceKey, ctx)`: the same with the source's amount for `ctx` (tier, difficulty,
  depth, share, cleared).
- `ChaosConquest.balance(player)`, `pityMult(player, group)`, `pityRecord(player, group, hit, itemId)`,
  `saw(player, itemId)`, `offerOf(itemId)`.

Sources (`conquest_config.lua` `sources`; per character and day, the day turns at midnight server time):

| Source | Tokens | Per day |
|---|---|---|
| World boss | 12 | 72 |
| Island boss | 10 | 60 |
| Base server raid boss | 4 | 40 |
| Lair boss | 3 | 45 |
| Invasion boss | 8 | 48 |
| Omen guardian | 15 | 90 |
| Ascended Omen / the Cinderheart | 25 / 50 | 150 |
| Dungeon boss | 5 | 60 |
| Tower boss | 4 | 48 |
| Trial boss | 6 | 36 |
| Descent boss | 8 | 64 |
| Guild boss | 12 | 48 |
| Sepulchre boss / the Sovereign | 15 / 35 | 120 |
| Any other boss (type flag) | 2 | 30 |
| Sealed rift | 4 + 0.5 x tier, at most 12 | 300 |
| Dungeon clear | 5 + 2 x difficulty, at most 15 | 90 |
| Ember Descent run | 4 + 0.5 x depth (+6 on a full clear), at most 18 | 90 |
| Invasion reward | 5 + 10 x share, at most 15 | 60 |
| Pocket boss (called by the pocket boss system) | 4 | 60 |
| Next Goals goal (called by the goals system, `reward(player, "goals", {tier = band})`) | 3 + 2 x band, at most 15 | 60 |
| Salvaged unique | 10% of its price, at least 25 | 400 |

Boss kills: one death event on every monster whose type is a boss of the Boss Spawns window (its category picks the
source) or carries the boss flag; credit like the boss points (damage map, summons for their master, last hit, most
damage, their party within 30 sqm). `boss.byName` gives the Omen guardians, the Ascended bosses, the Cinderheart and the
Sovereign their own amounts. Clears: `rift.lua` `RF.deliver` (not the Omen chest, its guardian kill counts),
`dungeons.lua` (the clear, with the difficulty), `descent.lua` (every finisher by depth), `invasion.lua` `V.deliver`.

**Income model** (the reasoning; not measured on a live server):

| Player | Play | Tokens an hour | A week |
|---|---|---|---|
| Casual, level 100-300 | 1.5 h a day: dungeons (7-9 + a dungeon boss 5 every ~20 min), low rifts (5-7), two world bosses and three invasions a week | about 30 | about 360 |
| Dedicated, endgame | 4 h a day: tier 12-15 rifts (10-11 every ~8 min), Omen guardians, the weekly raid (4 x 15 + 35), bosses | about 60 | about 1,800 |

**The vendor.** Iselde Varrow next to the main temple (`npc` in the config; placed at startup like the Gambler) or
Economy > Conquest Vendor; buying needs a protection zone or the vendor in sight (no new player command). Every unique of
`ChaosUniqueItems`, every set piece and every raid unique is on sale for a character that has seen it: it dropped for
the character (`chaos_conquest_seen`, written on every pity hit and every purchase), the character's bestiary has a
kill of a monster that drops it, or its level is at most the character's level + 50 (`vendor.levelBand`). Grasp of the
Pyre Saint (the Monk's top fist weapon) is always on sale (`vendor.always`). A bought item is made like a drop
(`ChaosMakeUnique`): the same stats, sockets and rules; the maximum stays with luck on the crafting side. Season uniques
follow `ChaosSeason.uniqueBlocked`. The purchase: the item is made, the tokens go with one conditional UPDATE (a failed
one removes the item), then it is given (inbox when full) and the character saved.

| Group | Price (tokens) | Examples | Casual weeks | Dedicated weeks |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Monster unique | 600 + 1.5 x level | level 60: 690, 100: 750, 300: 1,050; Grasp of the Pyre Saint (650): 1,580 | 2-3 | under 1 |
| Boss unique | 1,000 + 3 x level | level 120: 1,360 | 3.7 | under 1 |
| Set piece | 900 + 1.2 x level | level 70: 980, 300: 1,260, 800: 1,860 | 2.7-3.5 | 1 |
| Raid unique | 2,400; Crown of the Last Sovereign 3,600 | | | 1.3-2 |
| Ascended unique | 4,200; Cinderheart Signet 5,400 | | | 2.3-3 |

The Cinderheart chain (`cinder`): an Omen Key of the kind you choose (150; level 800 like the keys), your carried Omen
Key attuned to another kind (40), an Ascended Shard of the kind you choose (300), and conversions: 2 shards of one kind
into 1 of another, 2 duplicate relics into the missing one (no fee). `uber.lua` exports `ChaosAscended.relicsOf`.

Refinement (`refine`): a worn item with a rarity (not a unique, not ruined) rises one rarity (Common to Legendary, never into Divine), keeps every modifier and
gains one random modifier that fits the new rarity (none when full); 60 + 60 x the new rank tokens (`refine.base`, `perRarity`; Rare to
Legendary 300), never above Legendary: Divine stays luck. The Orb of Fate stays the cheap gamble.

**Bad-luck protection** (`pity`). Per character and group, in player storages: every roll of the group that misses
raises the next chance to base x (1 + step x misses), at most x cap; a drop of the group resets it (a drop of another
item of the same group resets it too; decided 2026-10-15: per group, not per item). The window's Progress tab shows the misses and the multiplier.

| Group | Rolls | Step | Cap | Expected rolls to a drop (plain -> with pity) | 90% of players have one after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Monster uniques | magic / rare / legendary kills of listed monsters (`loot.lua`, the corpse owner) | +1% | x3 | 312 -> 155 (a 0.32% roll) | 718 -> 306 rolls |
| Boss uniques | boss corpses (`loot.lua`), the Ascended spoils' unique rolls | +10% | x4 | 83 -> 31 (1.2%) | 191 -> 59 |
| Set pieces | their unique entries (`loot.lua`) and every chase roll (`itemsets.lua` `grantChase`: rift, raid, Descent, dungeon) | +5% | x4 | 208 -> 72 (0.48%) | 479 -> 142 |
| Raid uniques | the Sepulchre's unique roll per boss loot (`raid.lua`, `raid_core.lua` `K.rollUnique` mult) | +25% | x5 | 67 -> 19 (1.5%) | 152 -> 37 |

Also under pity (2026-10-15): the world boss participation reward's unique roll (`worldboss.lua`
`W.computeRewards(..., pityOf)`: every chance of the player x its "boss" multiplier; a set piece drawn from the pool
resets "set", any other unique "boss", a miss counts for "boss") and the rift chest's unique roll (the finisher is the
owner of `L.rollUniques`, so it counts like a corpse drop: monster, boss and set groups, the season rule too). The Omen
chest's rolls had the finisher as owner already.

**Also changed by this rework.** The Orb of Ruin never ruins an item any more (`chaos_orbs_config.lua` `ruin`:
40 improve / 60 nothing / 0 ruin; items ruined before stay ruined). Uniques may be salvaged: `salvage_config.lua`
`uniqueTokens` gives 10% of the vendor price in tokens (at least 25) plus `uniqueShards` (4) rune shards, a set piece
keeps its 8 shards and gets the tokens too; the character is saved before the tokens are credited. The Codex (a Basics
page "Conquest Tokens", a Conquest vendor and a bad-luck row on every unique and set), the wiki and the Item Finder (a
"Conquest vendor" shop row per item, the Omen Key and the shards) show the new paths.

**Protocol** (opcode 167, `ChaosOpcodes.conquest`): client -> server `open`, `close`, `buy {k}` (`u:<id>`,
`omen:<kind>`, `attune:<kind>`, `shard:<kind>`, `conv:shards|relics:<from>:<to>`, `refine:<slot>`); server -> client
`state` (through `Chaos.sendChunked`), `result {ok, text}`, `npc {}`. One request per 400 ms (`Chaos.limited` before any
database read). Storages 7102640 - 7102689 ("Storage keys"). Staff: `/conquest Name` (balance, misses), `/conquest Name,
give, n` (an administrator, logged), `/conquest Name, pity` (clears the misses).

**Tests.** `tests/conquest_test.lua` (LuaJIT and Lua 5.3): the config, amounts, caps and the day turn, boss sources,
the pity curve with a deterministic roll sequence and the expected rolls, the catalog over the real uniques, sets and
raid uniques, visibility, refusals, refinement, conversions, salvage tokens, the design targets (1-3 weeks dedicated,
1.5-6 weeks casual), and the engine on a mocked engine (grants, caps, the log, pity storages, buying, Omen Keys,
conversions, refinement, the window, the rate limit). Extended: `orbs_test.lua` (Ruin), `itemfinder_test.lua` (the
vendor rows), `i18n_test.lua` (the new texts and the NPC); client `game_conquest/conquestview_test.lua`. Not run on a
live server.

## Professions (`professions.lua`, `professions_core.lua`, `professions_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_professions.sql`, `tools/install_professions.py`, client `game_professions`)

The owner's rule: professions gather materials **to sell to NPCs** and give an **experience bonus**. They make no gear and no
orbs and feed no crafting, so they never compete with the crafting orbs or salvage. Every number is in `professions_config.lua`.

**Four gathering professions**, each with its own level 1-100 per character (table `chaos_professions`):

| Profession | Gathers | Tool (stock item, sold by the broker) | Channel |
|---|---|---|---|
| Delving | ore veins (node items) | pick 2553 | 3 s |
| Wortcunning | herb patches (node items) | sickle 2405 | 3 s |
| Flaying | fresh corpses of beasts and reptiles (bestiary families `beasts`, `reptiles`) | obsidian knife 5908 | 2.5 s |
| Angling | water: the base server's own fishing, extended | fishing rod 2580 / 10223 | none (the stock cast) |

They are separate from the base server's engine skills of the same trades (the skills window's Mining, Herbalist, Fishing, ...),
which stay as they were: gear and passive nodes raise those skills, never a profession level, so the experience bonus cannot be
pumped with items. The base server's own veins, plants, trees and its crafting tables are not touched.

**Gathering.** Delving and Wortcunning: "use" a node with the tool in the backpack, or "use with" the stock pick / sickle on it.
Flaying: "use with" the obsidian knife on a corpse. A gather is a channel on the cast bar (opcode 231, client `game_castbar`;
clicking the bar cancels it): moving, attacking (a target set) or taking damage interrupts it (healing does not). The stock tool
scripts ask `ChaosProfessions.onTool` first (one line each, `install_professions.py`); it handles only our nodes and tagged
corpses and returns false for everything else, so the stock pick, sickle and knife work as before. Angling: every stock fishing
cast on fishable water calls `ChaosProfessions.onFishCast` (one line right before the stock skill try): one roll per character
every 3 s at most, 10% chance of a material; the stock catch (fish, the Fishing skill, worms) is unchanged.

A gather yields a material of tier **min(the place's tier, the profession's tier, the character's tier)**, `1 + 1 (chance
min(60%, (profession level - the tier's level) / 100)) + 1 (3%)` units, profession experience (x0.6 one tier below the
profession's own, x0.25 two or more), and a little character experience (0.1% of what the character needs for its next level,
no stages, no bonuses: a level 1000 character gets 49,850). A flay can miss (40% chance of a hide; a miss gives half the
experience); each corpse once, only the corpse owner and the owner's party (`ChaosLootFilter.canLoot`). The corpse is tagged at
the death (EventCallback `onDropLoot` index 4: custom attribute `chaos_flay` = serial x 10 + tier, tier by the monster's
hunting level `ChaosBestiaryCore.estimateLevel`; summons and `flaying.exclude` (rabbit: the stock skinning keeps it) are not).

| Tier | Profession level | Character level (= the places' hunting level) | Base price | Profession experience |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Common | 1 | 1 (8) | 20 | 10 |
| 2 Fine | 20 | 40 | 80 | 18 |
| 3 Rare | 40 | 100 | 350 | 30 |
| 4 Grim | 60 | 250 | 800 | 45 |
| 5 Infernal | 80 | 500 | 4,000 | 65 |

Level curve: level L -> L+1 needs floor(30 + 8 L + 0.45 L^2) (38 at 1, 5,232 at 99; 190,295 in all): about 4,000 gathers of the
right tier, 35-45 hours per profession.

**Items** (`install_professions.py`, copies of stock nodes: their looks, no client change): materials 32351..32370, stackable
(Delving: ashstone ore, bloodiron ore, duskglass shard, wraithsilver ore, emberheart crystal; Wortcunning: gravemoss, bitterroot,
nightshade bloom, wraithcap, emberbloom; Flaying: matted pelt, tough hide, scaled hide, dire pelt, wyrmscale; Angling: mudfin,
gloomcarp, bloodfin trout, dusk pike, drowned pearl), nodes 32371..32375 (veins, the base server's vein looks) and 32376..32380
(herb patches, its plant looks). Range 32351..32399 is reserved for the professions.

**Nodes and places.** Chosen: a **per-player node cooldown**, not shared depletion. A node never disappears; after a character
gathers it, it is ready again for that character after 6 minutes (`respawnMin`; in memory, a restart makes every node ready).
Nobody can camp or steal a node, players hunting the same ground do not compete, and the node's look never has to change. Node
items are put at startup (and by `/professions nodes`) on tiles of the areas of `professions_config.lua` `areas`: existing
hunting grounds of the real map (centres from `bestiary_spawns.lua`), a box centre +- r on one floor, `nodes` per profession on
walkable ground with nothing on it (no protection zone, house, teleport or stairs), at least 3 tiles apart, picked by a seed from
the area key (the same tiles after every restart; fixed `pos` spots first). `fishing = true` makes the water in the box fish at
the area's tier; any other water fishes tier 1.

| Area | Tier | Centre | Nodes | Fishing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gutworm Burrows | 1 | 32224, 32746, 8 | Delving 10 | |
| Wolf Meadows | 1 | 32580, 32036, 7 | Wortcunning 10 | yes |
| Cyclops Crags | 2 | 32448, 32073, 8 | Delving 10 | |
| Lion's Rest | 2 | 32661, 32103, 7 | Wortcunning 10 | yes |
| Dragon Scar | 3 | 33215, 31297, 7 | Delving 10, Wortcunning 10 | yes |
| Behemoth Depths | 4 | 33521, 31643, 13 | Delving 12 | |
| Hydra Fens | 4 | 33700, 31657, 14 | Wortcunning 12 | yes |
| Infernal Rift | 5 | 33841, 31312, 12 | Delving 10, Wortcunning 10 | |

**Selling.** One Material Broker stands next to every temple, in Cinderhold in its stall in the hub (`data/npc/Material Broker.xml`, placed at startup like the faction
NPCs; `broker.towns = "all"`). "trade" opens his trade window with the four stock tools; "sell" / "demand" / "materials" opens the
Professions window on its broker board (opcode 195 `npc`). The sale is checked by `professions.lua` (a broker within 4 tiles, the
items in the backpack) and paid to the **bank account**. Per material, character and day (days start at 06:00, like the bounty
board): the full price for the first 100 units, then 50% up to 200, then nothing more that day (`chaos_professions_sales`).
**Weekly demand**: per profession and week (Monday 06:00) the five materials get the multipliers x1.5, x1.25, x1, x1, x0.75 in an
order drawn from the week key (`K.demand`: Park-Miller generator, the same draw under LuaJIT and Lua 5.3, after a restart and for
every character). Season characters are characters of their own (levels and caps per character); Self-Found characters sell to
the broker like everyone (selling to an NPC is not trading).

**Gold per hour** (`K.balance`, checked by the test): the best case per tier (profession 100, the best demand week, no daily cap)
against hunting gold per hour at the tier's character level ("Respec" table: 358,839 at 100, 881,866 at 300, 5,548,330 at 500;
levels 8 and 40 from the same model on Gutworm / Troll / Orc and Cyclops / Dwarf Guard / Minotaur Guard hunts: 19,000 and 83,000).
Pace model: node professions min(3600 / (channel + 12 s walking), nodes of the tier x 60 / 6 min) = 100 gathers an hour (one area
of 10 nodes); Flaying 3600 / (2.5 s + 10 s per kill) x 40%; Angling 1,200 rolls x 10%.

| Tier | Delving | Wortcunning | Flaying | Angling | Hunting / h | One material's best day |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Common | 4,890 (26%) | 4,890 (26%) | 5,633 (30%) | 5,868 (31%) | 19,000 | 4,500 |
| 2 Fine | 19,560 (24%) | 19,560 (24%) | 22,533 (27%) | 23,472 (28%) | 83,000 | 18,000 |
| 3 Rare | 85,575 (24%) | 85,575 (24%) | 98,582 (27%) | 102,690 (29%) | 358,839 | 78,800 |
| 4 Grim | 205,920 (27%) | 205,920 (27%) | 197,683 (26%) | 205,920 (27%) | 751,109 | 180,000 |
| 5 Infernal | 738,000 (13%) | 738,000 (13%) | 850,176 (15%) | 885,600 (16%) | 5,548,330 | 900,000 |

Every cell stays below `balance.maxShare` (40%) of hunting, and one material's best day (100 at full price + 100 at half, x1.5)
stays below one hour of hunting at its level. Flaying comes on top of a beast hunt but costs the channel time per corpse.

**Experience bonus.** +0.0253% monster experience per profession level above 1, all four together, at most +10%: every
profession at 100 (396 levels) reaches the cap, a new character has +0%; all at 50 give +4.96%. EventCallback `onGainExperience`
at index 6 (after the world buff, before the dungeon / rift caps), monster kills only (no summons, no other sources). Shown on the
buff bar as one passive entry "Profession Mastery +N%" (`chaos_buffs.lua` source `professions`, icon `buff:professions` from
`client/tools/gen_buff_icons.py`, the whole percent as stacks on the icon, no timer; hidden at +0%).

**Also:** achievements (`achievements_data.lua`, category Exploration): each profession at 50 and 100 (titles Master Delver,
Master Herbwife, Master Flayer, Master Angler), 200 profession levels in total, all four at 100 (title Master of the Wilds); stats
`prof_<key>` and `prof_total`, set at login (retroactive) and at each level up. Weekly leaderboard "Gatherers" (materials
gathered, `leaderboard_config.lua` key `professions`, flushed every minute and at logout): the title Gatherer of the Week only,
no orbs (`noReward = true`, new in `leaderboard.lua` / `leaderboard_core.lua`). Codex: a Materials tab (every material: profession,
tier, where, price, the daily rule; and a page about the professions with the bonus table), `tools/gen_codex_data.lua`.

**Client** (`game_professions`, Economy > Professions): the four professions (level, experience bar, the tier they gather, tool and
total in the tooltip), the bonus line, "Where to Gather" (every area with its tier, your ready nodes per profession, fishing, the
nearest town; position and monsters in the tooltip), the broker board of the week (look, price x demand, sold today of the cap,
carried, Sell; Sell All with the estimate; enabled only next to a broker), the daily rule and the time to the next day and week.

Protocol (opcode 195, JSON `{action, data}`): client -> server `open` | `close` | `sell {id, n}` | `sellAll`; server -> client
`state` (`K.payload`, through `Chaos.sendChunked`), `result {ok, text}`, `levelup {k, lv}`, `npc {}` (from the broker's NPC script).
Staff: `/professions Name[, profession, level]` (show / set), `/professions nodes` (place the nodes again). Test or event areas:
`ChaosProfessions.addArea{key, name, tier, center, r, nodes, fishing}` places them at once.

**Tests:** `tests/professions_test.lua` (635 checks under LuaJIT and Lua 5.3): config, curve, tiers and yields, the bonus and its
cap, the demand draw of a fixed week (exact values), weeks and days, prices, the daily cap, the gold per hour bound against
hunting, node spots (deterministic, spaced), fishing places; and `professions.lua` against a mocked engine: placing an area twice,
a node gather through the action and the cast bar, the profession tier cap, the per-player cooldown, another character on the same
node, moving / damage interrupting (healing not), the wrong tool, the stock pick's own uses, flaying a tagged wolf (and once only,
the owner rule; a dragon is no beast), the angling roll limit, selling away from / at the broker, the full / late price and the cap,
a new day, Sell All, the bonus on monster experience only (+10% at the cap), the buff entry, the weekly board, the title-only
board. Client: `game_professions/professionsview_test.lua` (45 checks).

**Tested in game** (test server with the cropped map, a runtime test area next to the temple, one client): a vein by "use" with the
pick in the backpack (cast bar, "You gathered 1 duskglass shard (+30 Delving experience)", 49.8k character experience at level
1000), a herb patch with the stock sickle by "use with" (the tier capped by Wortcunning 31, with the message), Angling with the
stock rod in the test water (bloodfin trout, +18), flaying two wolves with the obsidian knife (a miss with half the experience, a
matted pelt; full backpack -> inbox), the broker placed at the temple, "sell" in the NPC channel opening the window, one Sell
(26 duskglass shards, 9,100 gold to the bank, 26 / 200 today) and Sell All (135 materials, 29,885 gold, the estimate's number),
