"trade" with the tools, the window from the menu away from the broker (selling disabled), the buff bar entry and its tooltip,
levels kept over a relogin, the bonus on monster experience: Demons 175,500 -> 193,050 with +10% (exactly x1.10).
Not tested: the real map (the area centres come from the spawn data; the tile picks there are not seen), more than one broker,
the weekly leaderboard reset and the achievements unlocking at 50 / 100.

## Client guard (engine `src-patches/0021-client-guard.patch`, `clientguard.lua`, `clientguard_core.lua`, `clientguard_config.lua`, client base patch 0035, client `game_chaosguard`)

Only the official Cinders of Chaos client may play. **What it is and is not:** no client check is unbreakable. The key
the client proves with is inside every client binary (only obfuscated), and a determined attacker can reverse the exe or
proxy the traffic of a real client. The guard stops stock and third-party clients (other OTClient builds, the base
client, Tibia clients, bots that speak the protocol themselves) and casually modified clients (edited Lua, a client
rebuilt without our patches), logs every attempt, and makes the rest work for it. Three layers:

1. **Login gate (engine, both logins).** Both login packets already carry a u32 "client version" field that the engine
   skipped. Our client (base patch 0035) sends `0x4343 << 16 | build` there (stock clients send 1098). The login server
   and the game server refuse anything else with **"Please use the official Cinders of Chaos client: <download URL>"**
   (`clientGuardDownloadUrl`): the account login before the password check, the game login before the character is
   loaded (with the guard on, a client of another protocol version gets this message too instead of "Only clients
   with protocol 10.98 allowed!"). The build must be in `clientGuardBuilds` (empty: any build), and when `clientGuardManifest` names the
   updater's `manifest.json` on this machine, not below its `min_package` (re-read when the file changes).
2. **Challenge-response (C++ on both sides).** Right after the game login, before the login packets, the server sends a
   16-byte random nonce on extended opcode **189** (`cg1:<hex>`). The client answers from C++ (the challenge never
   reaches Lua) with `cg1:<build>:<hex>` of
   `HMAC-SHA256(key, nonce || u16le #account || account || u16le #character || character || u16le build)` (account =
   the session key's account, character = the name this login sent; server: Crypto++ and a constant-time compare;
   client: OpenSSL). A wrong answer, or none within `clientGuardTimeout` seconds (10), is logged and the player gets the
   same message and is logged out (`Player::kickPlayer`: logout scripts run, the character is saved). Every other
   extended opcode the client sends before its answer is held back (at most 64) and handed to the scripts right after
   it, so no module loses its first request; after a failure they are dropped. The official client answers within one
   round trip, before its modules send anything.
3. **Module hello (Lua, cheap).** A checked connection must send the hello of client module `game_chaosguard` on
   extended opcode **190** within 30 s (`clientguard_config.lua` `helloTimeout`): `{"action": "hello", "data": {"build":
   n, "modules": n}}`, the same build as the login and at least 20 of our modules (`game_*`, `client_chaos_*`) loaded.
   It catches our exe running with its overlay stripped or replaced. A failure goes through `player:clientGuardFail`.

**Modes** (`clientGuardMode`): `"off"` (the engine's default, so an older config.lua and the test servers change
nothing), `"log"` (every check runs and every failure is logged, nobody is refused or kicked: for a first week, or an
emergency) and `"enforce"` (any other value counts as enforce, so a typo does not open the server). Switch with
`/reload config` or a restart.
**Staff:** nobody is exempt by default. Accounts of type gamemaster or higher that log in from an IP listed in
`clientGuardStaffIps` skip the gate, the handshake and the hello (logged as such); from any other IP staff are checked
like everyone.
**Log:** one line per refusal, kick, staff pass and log-only pass, on the console and in `clientGuardLogFile`
(`data/logs/clientguard.log`), e.g. `[ClientGuard] 2026-10-11 16:37:51 kicked ip=1.2.3.4 account=x character=Y build 7:
wrong answer (another key, or not our client)`. At startup the console shows the mode, how many keys and from where,
the accepted builds and an HMAC self-test; enforcing without a usable key prints an error (then every handshake fails:
fail closed).

**Keys.** The key is 32 random bytes as 64 hex digits (`openssl rand -hex 32`). The server takes the first non-empty of
`clientGuardKey` (config.lua), the file `clientGuardKeyFile`, the environment variable `CHAOS_CLIENT_KEY`; several keys
separated by commas are all accepted (a key rotation: old and new until every player has the new client). The public
**development key** (`DEV-KEY-cinders-of-chaos-UNSAFE!`, what a client built without the secret gets) is refused unless
`clientGuardAllowDevKey = true` (test servers only); an answer made with it says so in the log.

**What the owner must set up (once):**
1. Make the key on your own machine: `openssl rand -hex 32`. Keep it out of the repository, chats and screenshots.
2. GitHub: Settings -> Secrets and variables -> Actions -> New repository secret, name **`CHAOS_CLIENT_KEY`**, value the
   64 hex digits. `windows-package.yml` (the Windows and the Linux client) and `windows-client.yml` build the client
   with it (without it `windows-package.yml` fails unless its input `allow_dev_key` is ticked; then, and in
   `windows-client.yml`, the client gets the development key, which a production server kicks). The
   Linux server download of `windows-package.yml` writes `clientGuardMode` as "enforce" when its `chaos.env` sets
   `CHAOS_CLIENT_KEY` and "off" otherwise (`tools/linux/package_server.sh`); a rerun of `prod_config.py` makes it
   "enforce" again.
3. Game server: the same value as `CHAOS_CLIENT_KEY=` in `/etc/chaos/chaos.env` (`server/deploy/chaos.env.example`,
   mode 0600), then `server/tools/prod_config.py ... --url https://<site> [--client-url URL] [--client-builds 4,5]
   [--client-manifest /path/updates/live/manifest.json] [--client-staff-ips IP,...]`. It writes `clientGuardMode =
   "enforce"`, `clientGuardKey = os.getenv("CHAOS_CLIENT_KEY") or ""`, `clientGuardAllowDevKey = false`,
   `clientGuardTimeout = 10` and the four values of the options. Restart and look for `>> Client guard: enforce, 1 key(s)`.
4. Every new client exe: run the workflow with a higher `client_build` (it also sets `Services.update.package`), then
   either list both builds (`clientGuardBuilds = "4,5"`) for an update window and drop the old one later, or publish an
   update with `--min-package 5` and let `clientGuardManifest` follow it (`docs/LAUNCH.md` "Client updates").

**Config keys** (`config.lua`, all read on `/reload config`): `clientGuardMode` ("off"), `clientGuardKey` (""),
`clientGuardKeyFile` (""), `clientGuardAllowDevKey` (false), `clientGuardBuilds` (""), `clientGuardManifest` (""),
`clientGuardDownloadUrl` (""), `clientGuardStaffIps` (""), `clientGuardTimeout` (10, 2..120), `clientGuardLogFile`
("data/logs/clientguard.log", "" = console only).
**Updater:** the build number is the updater's package number (`Services.update.package`, `--min-package`): the exe is
what the guard identifies. The Lua update number (`--min-version`) stays a client-side rule of the updater.
**Lua:** `player:getClientGuard()` -> `{mode, state = "none" | "pending" | "verified" | "bypass" | "logged" | "failed",
official, build}`; `player:clientGuardFail(reason)` (logged; in "enforce" the message and a logout, returns true).
**Load test:** `tools/loadtest.py run` sends the stock version by default (a server in "off" or "log" lets the bots in);
`--dev-key` (with `clientGuardAllowDevKey = true`) or `--client-key HEX` / `CHAOS_CLIENT_KEY` and `--client-build N` make
the bots send the identifier, answer the challenge and say hello like the client.
**Opcodes:** 189 (handshake, engine only) and 190 (hello) are free in the base server, in every Chaos script and in every
client module (`tests/clientguard_test.lua` checks `ChaosOpcodes`).
**Limits, honestly:** the identifier is plain in the packet (it only stops stock clients); the key can be dug out of a
client binary with a debugger, after which a custom client can answer; a proxy in front of a real client can inject
packets after the handshake; Lua-level checks can be faked by anyone who reads `game_chaosguard`. What raises the bar
further, if ever needed: rotating the key with every client build (old and new key during the window), and server-side
behaviour checks (the anti-bot system).
**Tests:** `tests/clientguard_test.lua` (Lua 5.3 and LuaJIT: which states are checked, the hello rules, timeout,
logout, the engine glue against a mocked engine, the opcodes); `client/tools/chaosguard_test.cpp` (CI: RFC 4231 and the
handshake vector, the same one `loadtest.py` computes with Python's `hmac`, so client, server and load test agree).
**Tested end to end** (engine 0001-0021 built on Linux, client chain 0001-0035 assembled from the `windows-assets` base and
built on Linux, test server with the cropped map): the official client (test key, build 7) logs in, is `verified`, stays
past the 10 s and 30 s checks, the daily reward, store and passive tree windows work (their first requests went through
the hold-back); the same client built with another key is kicked at once with the message (the box now survives the
logout, base patch 0035); an exe without patch 0035 and a stock base client build (made to speak 10.98) are refused at
the account login with the message; a hacked Lua account login with a stock game login is refused at the game login;
bots: no answer -> kicked after 10 s, no hello -> kicked after 30 s, a hello sent before the answer is held and accepted,
development key refused (and accepted with `clientGuardAllowDevKey`), build outside `clientGuardBuilds` and below the
manifest's `min_package` refused, two keys (rotation) both accepted, key from config, file and environment, staff account
from a staff IP let in and a normal account from that IP refused, enforce without a key fails closed with the startup
error. Log mode: the stock-id client and the wrong-key client play, every check logged. `loadtest.py`: 6 bots for 40 s in
log mode (stock id) and in enforce with `--dev-key`, all logged in, no disconnects. Not run: the Windows workflows.

## Login encryption (RSA, XTEA) (engine `src-patches/0046-own-rsa-login-key.patch`, client base patch 0072, `tools/rsa_key.py`, `client/tools/set_rsa_key.py`)

The 10.98 login sends the account name, the password and the session's XTEA key in one 128-byte RSA block (the game
login sends the password again, in its session key). After that both sides use XTEA with the client's key. Audit
2026-10-16 (docs/SECURITY_CHECKLIST.md):
- **The RSA key was the public default open-server key** (`key.pem` of the base download, `OTSERV_RSA` of the client,
  fingerprint `69bbc82b7c9073de`). Its private key is public: anyone on the path (a shared Wi-Fi, a hostile network,
  a provider) reads every account and password and can pose as the server. **Fixed:** our own key (below).
- **The client's XTEA key was guessable.** `Protocol::generateXteaKey` seeded `mt19937` with the current second, so a
  recorded login gave its session key away after a few hundred tries: the session could be read and forged whatever
  the RSA key. **Fixed:** client base patch 0072 takes it from OpenSSL `RAND_bytes`.
- XTEA is on both ways for the login and the game protocol from the first answer on; a login block no key opens is
  refused (disconnect), and the server never reads a plain packet after it. Only the status protocol (7171, the
  online count) and the game port's first challenge are plain, as in every 10.98 server. No change needed.
- **Limits of the protocol** (not fixable without breaking 10.98): RSA without padding, 1024 bits (within reach of a
  well-funded attacker, far beyond a casual one), XTEA without a MAC (a bit flipped on the path is not detected, only
  the game's own parsing catches nonsense). TLS in front of the game would need a client and server change of the
  transport (not planned). The client guard (above) is separate: it proves the client, not the channel.

**Our own key.** `config.lua` `rsaKeyFile` (default `"key.pem"`, as before): one or more PKCS#1 PEM files, comma
separated; the first is the current key, the others are still accepted (a rotation). `prod_config.py` writes
`rsaKeyFile = os.getenv("CHAOS_RSA_KEY_FILE") or "key.pem"`, so the path is in `/etc/chaos/chaos.env` (or the Linux
package's `chaos.env`); an empty value means `key.pem`. The engine tries each key and takes the first whose result
starts with the 0 byte the protocol requires (a wrong key gives that by chance once in 256 tries; that login then
fails and a retry works). Read at startup only: restart after a change. At start: `>> RSA key 1: <file> (fingerprint
<16 hex>)` per key, and a WARNING for the public default key. A key that is not 1024 bits stops the start.
- Make it on the game server, as the user the engine runs as (or as root with `--owner chaos`):
  `python3 -I server/tools/rsa_key.py gen --out /etc/chaos/rsa/login-YYYYMMDD.pem --owner chaos`. It writes a 1024-bit
  key (exponent 65537) with `openssl genrsa`, mode 600, in a folder of mode 700, refuses a path inside a git work tree
  and an existing file, and prints only the public modulus (decimal) and the fingerprint. `rsa_key.py public --key F`
  prints them again, `check --key F [--owner chaos]` checks format, size, exponent, mode, owner and that it is not
  the default key, `fingerprint MODULUS` the fingerprint of a modulus.
- The client: the modulus (public, not secret) goes into the GitHub secret or variable **`CHAOS_RSA_PUBLIC`**;
  `windows-package.yml` writes it into the separate client downloads' `init.lua` (`Services.rsa`) with
  `client/tools/set_rsa_key.py`, which prints the same fingerprint in the build log. Without it the run fails unless
  `allow_dev_key` is ticked (then the default key and a warning). The full Windows zip keeps the default key: its own
  server folder has the stock `key.pem`.
- Order: build and publish the client with the new modulus **before** the server uses only the new key. During the
  switch list both: `CHAOS_RSA_KEY_FILE=/etc/chaos/rsa/login-new.pem,key.pem` (the old clients keep working), then drop
  the old file once every player has the new client (with `clientGuardBuilds` / `--min-package` the old exe is refused
  anyway).
- **Rotation** (a key leaked, or once a year): `gen` a new file, publish clients with its modulus, list
  `new,old` in `CHAOS_RSA_KEY_FILE`, restart; after the update window list only `new`, restart, delete the old file
  (`shred -u`). A leaked key: do the same at once and shorten the window; anyone who had it could read the logins made
  with it, so ask players to change their passwords on the website.
- The private key never leaves the game server: not in the repository, not in a GitHub secret, not in a chat.
  `backup.sh` does not copy `/etc/chaos`; keep the key on the machine only, and if it is lost make a new one and build
  a new client (the same steps as a rotation, without the window).
- `tools/loadtest.py --key FILE` reads the modulus of any of the key files for the bots.
- Tests: `tools/rsa_key_test.py` (gen, modes, refusals, PKCS#8, the default key), `client/tools/set_rsa_key_test.py`
  (the modulus checks, init.lua, and the const.lua hunk of patch 0072 run under LuaJIT and Lua 5.3). The engine part
  was built from the chain 0001-0046 (the touched files compile) and checked with a small program against
  `src/rsa.cpp`: two keys loaded, a block for each key opened by the right one, a random block refused, a 2048-bit
  key refused, the fingerprints the same as the tools print. Not run in a full server build.

## Failed-login limits (engine `src-patches/0047-login-failure-limit.patch`, `src/loginlimit.h`)

Audit 2026-10-16: the game's account login (7171) and game login (7172) let anyone try passwords as fast as it could
reconnect. The stock throttle only stops 6 connections within 500 ms; nothing counted wrong passwords (the website
has its own limit, website/README.md "Passwords"). Each guess also costs a PBKDF2 run on the login worker.
- After `loginFailMaxPerIp` (20) failed logins from one IP, or `loginFailMaxPerAccount` (50) on one account name from
  any IP, within `loginFailWindow` (600) seconds, that IP or account name is refused for `loginFailBlock` (900)
  seconds with "Too many failed logins. Please wait N minutes ...", before the password check (no PBKDF2 for it). 0
  turns a limit off. Read on every login, so `/reload config` changes them.
- Account names are compared without case. A good login clears its account's count, never the IP's: an attacker
  cannot reset his IP's count with an account of his own. Each map holds at most 100,000 entries (expired ones are
  swept). Behind the gateways the IP is the player's own (patch 0025).
- **Accepted trade-off:** someone who knows an account name can block its game login for 15 minutes with 50 wrong
  passwords from 3 or more IPs (one IP is stopped by its own limit after 20). The account's owner then waits or uses
  the website. 50 keeps that hard and still stops guessing spread over many addresses.
- One console line when a block starts: `[Login limit] ip|account blocked after failed logins: ip a.b.c.d, account x`.
- Test: `tools/loginlimit_test.cpp` (CI takes `loginlimit.h` out of the patch: the IP and account limits, the window,
  a good login, limits off, bounded memory). The chain 0001-0047 applied; `protocollogin.cpp`, `protocolgame.cpp` and
  `configmanager.cpp` compile. Not run in a full server build.

## Pre-auth connection limits (O200) (engine `src-patches/0067-preauth-limits.patch`, `src/chaospreauth.h`)

Hardening against connection floods before login. The stock engine accepts any number of connections and holds each for
up to 30 s before it has said a word; its only throttle stops 6 connections of one IP within 500 ms. Now a connection
that has not logged in yet is counted, and the count is limited. All keys are read at start (`config.lua`; 0 turns a
limit off; not written by the install tools, the defaults hold):

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `preAuthMaxPerIp` | 5 | connections of one IP that have not finished their login |
| `preAuthMaxTotal` | 200 | the same over all IPs |
| `preAuthDeadline` | 15 | seconds; a connection not logged in by then is closed (0: no deadline) |
| `preAuthRateMax`, `preAuthRateWindow` | 10, 10 | new connections one IP may open within the window (seconds) |
| `preAuthCooldown` | 30 | seconds an IP over the rate is refused |
| `preAuthExemptLoopback` | true | 127.0.0.0/8 is not counted (admin tools, watchdog, health check) |

- A refused connection is closed at once, before a packet is read. The check runs in `ServicePort::onConnectionReady`,
  before the old ban-list throttle. One console line per kind per 10 s: `[Pre-auth limit] ... : a.b.c.d (N more
  refused since the last line)`.
- Counted: every connection of the login (7171), game (7172) and status ports. A login or status connection ends by
  closing; a game connection ends its pre-auth state when its login went through (`ProtocolGame::login` / `connect`).
  The count is given back exactly once per connection, on every close path and in the destructor, behind the
  connection's lock and a flag; the limiter itself is one mutex over a bounded table (100,000 IPs, expired
  ones swept; a table full of live entries refuses new IPs).
- Not counted: loopback (above) and the trusted gateways of patch 0025 (their clients are counted by their own address
  from the PROXY header, as the old throttle does). The live cast port has its own acceptor and is not covered.
- **Trade-offs:** several players behind one address (a family, an event, carrier NAT) share the per-IP and rate
  limits: one login is 2 connections (login server, then game) plus status checks, so 5 open and 10 per 10 s allow
  about 4 players logging in at the same moment from one address. Raise `preAuthMaxPerIp` / `preAuthRateMax` for an
  event, or set them to 0. A load test with many bots from one non-loopback IP needs the same. The 15 s deadline
  must stay above the slowest login (PBKDF2 queue on the login worker) under load.
- Test: `tools/chaospreauth_test.cpp` (CI takes `chaospreauth.h` out of the patch: per-IP and global caps, release
  without leaks, loopback, rate and cooldown, limits off, bounded table, log throttling, 8 threads; also clean under
  ThreadSanitizer). The chain 0001-0067 applies to the base; `configmanager.cpp`, `connection.cpp`, `server.cpp` and
  `protocolgame.cpp` compile with the build flags. Not run in a full server build or against a live flood.

## Leech from real damage (engine `src-patches/0048-leech-real-damage.patch`)

Report C1 (2026-10-20): "mana leech does not work on the Templar (item / buff)". Life and mana leech (patches 0004, 0011, 0015)
ran for hits that dealt nothing. Fixed in `Combat::doTargetCombat` (one target: weapon hit or spell) and `Combat::doAreaCombat`:
- A target that cannot be attacked (`!isAttackable()`, which `Game::combatChangeHealth` reports as done) gives no leech.
- The leech value is rounded first; a value of 0 (zero damage, a hit that rounds to 0) heals nothing and no longer takes the
  900 ms leech window of patch 0011 (a wasted roll used to block the next real hit).
- Area: a target that took 0 damage or cannot be attacked is not counted in `totalTargets` and `maxDamageFound`; the divisor
  is never 0 (the block already needs `maxDamageFound > 0`), and the window is taken only when the area leech is above 0.
- Not changed: the `getMana() < getMaxMana()` gate (mana leech at full mana does nothing, by design: the most common reason a
  Templar "sees no leech"), the rule that a leech heal is not leeched again, `ORIGIN_CONDITION` damage never leeching.
- A Templar-only cause was not found: no Lua, item or buff path treats the Templar differently (`templar_combat.lua` has no leech
  logic); `passivetree_stats_config.lua` lists `@manaLeech` as irrelevant for the Templar and Sentinel, a stat-pool choice for the
  tree, not for items. Re-test in game with mana below the maximum.
- Apply after 0001-0047: `patch -p1 < 0048-leech-real-damage.patch`, then rebuild (applies cleanly to the 0047 tree; not run in
  a full server build). Test: `tests/leech_real_damage_test.lua` (a Lua mirror of the old and new rule for a weapon hit, a single
  spell and an area spell, zero damage, an unattackable target, the window, and the patch text).

## Poison Blades with ranged weapons (C3, 2026-10-20)

Reported: the weapon poison does not work with a bow, crossbow or thrown weapon. Checked: `thief_combat.lua` `onOffence`
counts `ORIGIN_RANGED` as a weapon hit like `ORIGIN_MELEE` (`isWeapon`), the engine sets `ORIGIN_RANGED` for `WEAPON_DISTANCE`
and `WEAPON_AMMO` (weapons.cpp), and Shuriken Toss strikes with `ORIGIN_RANGED`. `tests/thief_poison_test.lua` pins it: melee and
ranged poison with the buff; a spell hit (`ORIGIN_SPELL`), zero damage, healing and a non-thief do not; Blackblood Creed needs no
buff. No code change: the failure did not reproduce in the script layer, so the root cause is not proven (the engine side needs a
run in game with a bow and the buff active). The Thief line itself carries no bows or crossbows (stackable throwing weapons left
the game, "Throwing weapons").

## Gateways and the PROXY protocol (engine `src-patches/0025-proxy-protocol.patch`, `deploy/gateway/`, `deploy/firewall/`)

Owner decision: "put game proxies in front of the game server, and add per-IP connection limits." Players connect to
2 or 3 DDoS-protected **gateways** (HAProxy in TCP mode) that forward 7171 and 7172 to the real server with a PROXY
protocol v2 header; the real server's IP is never published and its firewall takes the game ports from the gateways
only. Owner steps, DNS, limits and how to replace a gateway: docs/LAUNCH.md "Gateways and DDoS".
**Why the engine needs a patch:** behind a proxy every connection comes from a gateway. The engine uses the connection's
IP (`Connection::getIP`) for bans, its connection throttle (`Ban::acceptConnection`: 5 quick reconnects block the IP for
3 s), the status query limit, `player:getIp()` (the 2-characters-per-IP rule of `multiclient.lua`, mentors), the client
guard's `clientGuardStaffIps`, `players.lastip` and the logs. Without the header, all of that would see 2 or 3 addresses.
**Config (config.lua, `tools/prod_config.py --proxy-trusted LIST --proxy-required yes|no`):**
- `proxyProtocolTrusted = "1.2.3.4,5.6.7.0/24"`: the gateways, IPv4 or a.b.c.d/nn, separated by commas or spaces. Empty
  (the default): off, every connection is direct as before. A bad entry is named at startup and ignored. Read again after
  `/reload config`.
- `proxyProtocolRequired = false`: true refuses every address that is not a trusted gateway at accept, except
  127.0.0.0/8 (`chaos_watchdog.py` and `chaos_health.py` ask the status protocol on 127.0.0.1). Then the real server
  cannot be played directly even when its firewall is wrong. True with an empty list: only 127.0.0.0/8 can connect (the
  console says so at startup).
**What the engine does** (`src/proxyprotocol.cpp`, `connection.cpp`, `server.cpp`):
- a connection from a trusted address must start with a PROXY header, v2 or v1 (`PROXY TCP4 ...`), within 5 s. It is
  read in steps (8 bytes, then exactly what the parser asks for), so none of the client's own bytes are taken. Its source
  address becomes the connection's IP. Only then do the ban and throttle checks run (on the real IP) and the protocol
  start, so the game port's challenge goes out after the header.
- LOCAL (HAProxy's health checks), UNSPEC and v1 UNKNOWN keep the gateway's own address. A gateway's own address skips
  the per-IP throttle: the gateways limit their clients themselves, and each client is throttled by its own IP.
- IPv6 clients are refused: the engine stores IPv4 addresses only (an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address counts as IPv4). Publish
  A records only.
- a trusted address without a valid header is closed: `[PROXY protocol] no valid PROXY header from a trusted gateway,
  closed: <ip> (<why>)`.
- from any other address a PROXY header is never believed: a first packet that starts with `\r\n` or `PR` (lengths of
  2573 and 21072 bytes, which no real first packet has) is closed: `[PROXY protocol] PROXY header from an address that is
  not in proxyProtocolTrusted, refused: <ip>`. With `proxyProtocolRequired`: `[PROXY protocol] direct connection refused
  (proxyProtocolRequired): <ip>`.
- each kind of console line at most once every 10 s, with the number left out, so a flood cannot fill the log.
- startup: `>> PROXY protocol off ...` or `>> PROXY protocol from N trusted gateway entries (...); direct connections
  allowed | refused (proxyProtocolRequired), except from 127.0.0.0/8`.
**Gateway** (`deploy/gateway/setup_gateway.sh BACKEND_IP [--admin-ips LIST|any]`, idempotent, Debian / Ubuntu): installs
HAProxy and nftables and writes `/etc/haproxy/haproxy.cfg` (from `haproxy.cfg.template`), `/etc/nftables.d/chaos-gateway.nft`
(from `gateway.nft.template`) and `/etc/sysctl.d/90-chaos-gateway.conf` (SYN cookies, backlogs, conntrack size), each
checked (`haproxy -c`, `nft -c`) before use. HAProxy: per-IP stick-tables (open connections and new connections per 10 s
for each port, a silent drop for floods), 5 s for the first bytes on 7171 and 8090 (slow connections), 90 s idle
timeout (the game pings every few seconds), TCP health checks of both backend ports, tcplog to syslog. 8090 (the
login-screen services) is forwarded too, without a header, so the client names only the gateways. nftables: drop invalid
and malformed SYNs, per-IP new-connection rate and open-connection cap on the game ports.
**Backend** (`deploy/firewall/setup_backend_firewall.sh GATEWAY_IPS --admin-ips LIST|any [--services LIST|any|off]
[--extra-ips LIST] [--web-ports LIST]`, idempotent): table `inet chaos_backend` from `backend.nft.template`; 7171 / 7172
from the gateways (at most 300 new connections/s each) and the `--extra-ips` only; 8090 open with a per-IP rate or from
a list; SSH from the admin addresses; everything else, MariaDB included, closed.
**World address:** the login server sends `ip` (config.lua) as text in the character list and the client resolves it,
so it is the gateways' DNS name (`prod_config.py --public-host`), and a DNS change needs no restart. The gateways listen
on the same ports as `loginProtocolPort` / `gameProtocolPort`, because the client is told the game port.
**Not covered:** a client-side list of gateway hosts (try the next one when a gateway does not answer) needs a client
patch: proposal only. The base client's DNS handling (does it try every address of a round-robin answer?) is not in this
repository and was not checked.
**Tested** (engine 0001-0025 built on Linux from the `windows-assets` base; the patches apply cleanly in order to a fresh
base; the full map; MariaDB on a private port; HAProxy 2.8 in front with the rendered gateway config, `send-proxy-v2`,
backend source address as the only trusted one; `tools/loadtest.py` through it):
- 20 bots from 20 loopback addresses logged in through the proxy, walked and talked for 40 s, no disconnects;
  `players.lastip` and `clientguard.log` hold each bot's own address, not the proxy's;
- 5 bots from one address through the proxy: 2 logged in, 3 refused (the 2-per-IP rule counts the real IP);
- `clientGuardMode = "enforce"`, `clientGuardStaffIps` = one bot's address, two staff accounts: the one from the staff
  address got in (account and game login), the other was refused;
- `proxyProtocolRequired = true`: direct status and game connections from a non-loopback address closed at accept,
  127.0.0.1 status (the watchdog's own check) answered, status and game through the proxy worked;
- a forged v2 and v1 header from an untrusted address (login, status and game port): closed, never used; a trusted
  address without a header: closed; v1 header and v2 LOCAL from the trusted address: status answered; a header cut off
  after a few bytes: closed after 5 s;
- the status protocol through the proxy answered; its 5 s limit now applies per real IP;
- HAProxy: 50 fast connections from one address on 7171: 42 refused by HAProxy, 8 passed (open cap), the flooder stayed
  refused while another address was served; 7172: 40 of 50 refused; health checks logged `DOWN` while the server
  restarted and `UP` after; 8090 forwarded;
- nftables rules (in a network namespace, never on the host): the gateway table, 50 parallel SYNs from one address:
  20 passed (burst), 30 dropped; a held-connection cap of 24; the backend table: game ports from the gateway and the extra
  address only, 8090 open, 3306 and SSH from others dropped; both load twice without error (idempotent);
- `tools/proxyprotocol_test.cpp` (CI builds it from the patch's `proxyprotocol.cpp` with the stand-ins in
  `tools/proxyprotocol_stubs/`; also run under AddressSanitizer): v1, v2, LOCAL, IPv6 mapped and not, TLVs, a header
  read in the engine's steps never takes a byte of the client's data, every malformed case, the trusted list with
  ranges and bad entries, loopback, required. CI also renders and checks both setup scripts with `--dry-run`.
Not run: `setup_gateway.sh` and `setup_backend_firewall.sh` for real (apt, systemd, files under /etc; their dry runs,
which render and check every file, were run), a gateway on a real VPS with real DDoS filtering, the Windows build.

## Display scale (`display_scale.lua`, `display_scale_core.lua`, `display_scale_config.lua`, engine `src-patches/0037-display-scale.patch`, client `game_chaosscale`)

**Off since 2026-10-23** (owner: "Tire, por favor, a inflação artificial de números que a gente colocou"): the curve is
`{{1, 1}}`, x1 at every level, so every player sees the internal numbers. The code, the engine patch and the client
module stay (a factor of 1 changes nothing and needs no new client build); the tests run it on the old curve and check
that the shipped curve is x1. The rest of this section describes the scale as it was.

Owner request (2026-10-13): end-game damage in the millions, as a **visual** scale. Every combat number a player sees is
the internal number x a factor of a level; the internal numbers (health, damage, the balance of
`data/spells/README.md`, everything in the database) stay exactly as they are and the engine keeps int32 health.

**The curve** (`display_scale_config.lua` `curve`): factor 1 up to level 100, then exponential (a straight line of
log(factor)) to x1000 at level 1000, then slower (x10 over 500 levels) to the cap x10000 at level 1500 and above. The
factor is rounded to a whole number. The first steps are 1 -> 2 at level 153, 3 at 220, 4 at 264, 5 at 296, 10 at
394; from about level 400 one level adds under 10%. Median single-target DPS: measured at levels 300 (913) and 1000
(2598, the 21 classes of `data/spells/README.md` "Class damage factor"); the other levels are estimates on the power
law through those two (DPS ~ level^0.87).

| Level | Factor | Median DPS (internal) | Median DPS shown |
|---|---|---|---|
| 50 | 1 | about 190 (estimate) | about 190 |
| 100 | 1 | about 350 (estimate) | about 350 |
| 200 | 2 | about 640 (estimate) | about 1.3k |
| 300 | 5 | 913 (measured) | 4.6k |
| 500 | 22 | about 1420 (estimate) | about 31k |
| 700 | 100 | about 1900 (estimate) | about 190k |
| 1000 | 1000 | 2598 (measured) | 2.6M |
| 1500 | 10000 (cap) | about 3700 (estimate) | about 37M |

**Why a whole-number factor.** Shown numbers then add up exactly: the shown parts of a hit (primary + secondary) are
the shown total, the shown hits of a fight are the meter's shown total, and a shown health minus the shown hits is the
next shown health (no rounding drift; `tests/display_scale_test.lua` checks it at x1 to x10000). The price is the first
steps (x1 -> x2 at level 153); from level 400 on they are small.

**Mana is never scaled** (since 2026-10-21, "Fixed spell costs"; engine `src-patches/0052`): the own mana and max
mana, the mana drain and mana gain messages, spell costs, party members' mana and the mana rows of item tooltips show
the numbers the engine counts, so a spell costs the same shown number at every level.

**Whose level.** The viewer's own level, for everything that viewer sees: its damage dealt and taken, heals, its own
health, monster and boss health numbers, the DPS meter and combat log, the death recap, party frames (health), damage
boards, the bestiary's monster health. Percentages stay percentages (monster bars, boss
HUDs, party frame bars and every percent stat send percents anyway). Edge cases:
- **PvP:** each side sees its own scale. A level-1000 hit on a level-300 player reads x1000 to the attacker, x5 to the
  victim and x(own) to every bystander; the engine scales each spectator's message on its own (`sendTextMessage` runs
  once per receiving player).
- **Party members and party frames:** a member's health in the frames is in the VIEWER's scale (its mana as it is) (the same as
  that member's damage numbers the viewer sees), so two members of different levels see each other's bars with
  different numbers but the same percents. The combat log's party view and the battleground scoreboard likewise.
- **Spectators:** a bystander sees a fight in its own scale, like the PvP case.
- **Death recap:** at the level the character had at that death (`recap.lvl`), the numbers it saw while dying, also
  when it is opened after a level up; a recap stored before this change without a level uses the viewer's factor.
- **Items traded between players of different levels:** an item's tooltip uses the factor of the item's level
  requirement (`req.level`), not the viewer's. Why: an item is the same thing for everybody; its tooltip reaches
  players of every level (the market, chat links, Inspect, trade, ground labels) and has to read the same for the
  seller and the buyer, and chat links and market offers keep one snapshot for every reader. `tip.ds` carries that
  factor and the client's compare view brings a worn item's flat rows to the hovered item's scale (`L.toScale`), so
  two items of different levels compare by their real numbers. Only flat health / damage / heal rows are scaled
  (`itemFlatKeys`: max health, thorns, life on kill and on hit, health regeneration, the Smoldering Aura power, flat
  health gems); attack, defence, armour, skills, speeds, every percent and every mana row (max mana, mana on kill and on
  hit, mana gems; since 2026-10-21) stay. The price: such a row is not
  in the wearer's scale (a level-500 wearer of a level-1000 helmet's "+200,000 Max Health" gains x22 on its bar, not
  x1000).
- **Consistency on one screen:** everything the viewer sees about combat uses one factor, its own (the boss bar's
  numbers, the damage numbers, its health, the meter); item tooltips are the one exception above.

**Where the numbers come from, scaled at the last step before sending.**
- Engine (`src-patches/0037`, `src/chaosdisplay.h`): the damage and heal text messages (MESSAGE_DAMAGE_DEALT /
  _RECEIVED / _OTHERS, MESSAGE_HEALED / _OTHERS: both values, uint32 clamped, and the numbers of the text that count
  hitpoints, mana, energy shield or health; "1 hitpoint" shown as more becomes "hitpoints"), the player's own health
  and max health in the stats packet (uint32, clamped), and the energy shield's "es:" message (patch 0015). Patch 0052
  takes mana out again: mana and max mana in the stats packet as they are, and a message of type mana drain / mana gain
  (patch 0051) at factor 1. A C++ patch because TFS 1.4.2 has no Lua event per spectator message: the text is built once per hit and sent
  to every spectator. The factors come from Lua once at load (`Game.setDisplayScale(table)`, levels 1..1500, a higher
  level uses the last entry; `player:getDisplayScale()`); without the table every factor is 1.
- Lua, right before each json.encode (`ChaosDisplayScale.apply(site, viewer, payload)`, a scaled copy: shared and cached
  payloads stay raw): `combatlog.lua` (totals, rows, max hits, elements, the party's totals; the factor is part of the
  push signature, so a level up re-sends), `deathrecap.lua`, `partyframes.lua`, `hunt.lua` (damage, DPS, healing),
  `leaderboard.lua`, `season.lua`, `season_modes.lua` (the World Boss, Boss Healer and Boss Tank boards only:
  `leaderboardBoards`), `battleground.lua` (scoreboard damage and healing), `guildwar.lua` (the guild boss damage
  board), `bestiary.lua` (monster health), the item tooltips of
  `item_tooltip.lua`, `inspect.lua`, `itemlink.lua`, `groundloot.lua` and `market.lua` (`DS.itemTip`), and the text
  "Your pet mends you (+N)" of `pets.lua`.
- Client (`game_chaosscale`, opcode 157): the server sends `scale {level, f}` at login, at a level up that changes the
  factor, and as the answer to the client's `hello` (sent at every game start, when the module loads in game and when
  the own level differs from the last factor's: a reattach to a lingering character runs no onLogin, and a lost level
  runs no onAdvance). The client keeps the factor (`chaosDisplayFactor()`, `chaosDisplayValue(n)`); it no longer
  scales the mana costs in `SpellInfo` (2026-10-21, "Fixed spell costs"). The short numbers
  (`client_chaos_numbers`, base patch 0018 above the map) already write k / M / B / T with three significant digits;
  the DPS meter and the hunt tracker wrote "kk" / "kkk" and now use M / B / T too.
- Opcode 157 is free in the base server, the base client and every Chaos module ("Opcode collision check").

**Never scaled:** gold, experience, levels, skills, item counts, prices, timers and durations, hits and crits counts,
percentages, ratings, points, kills, and anything stored (the combat log's own numbers, death recaps, market snapshots,
chat link snapshots, boards in the database). Not scaled on purpose or not reached: the passive tree's flat stat texts
(client tree data, read as stats like skills), the Codex and the website wiki (reference tables in the internal numbers,
which are what a level 1-100 character sees; the wiki's FAQ has the factor of a few levels from this config, see
`tools/gen_wiki_data.lua` facts `scale.*`), the item look text of the engine (the description attribute, written once
into the item), the market search filters (typed against the internal values), the base server's own inspect opcode 107
(no module of our client reads it).

**Tests:** `tests/display_scale_test.lua` (the curve against this table, whole and monotone factors, smoothness, the
rounding, the 2^53 and uint32 clamps, additivity at x1 to x10000, the text rule, the engine table; every site function
on payloads made by the real cores: combat log, death recap, party frames, hunt tracker, plus the boards, battleground,
guild boss, bestiary, spellbook and item tooltips; the engine glue against a mocked engine: the table to the engine,
the opcode at login, at a level change that changes the factor and at hello; a scan that every hook site calls its
function right before it sends), hook sites against the mocked engines of `tests/combatlog_test.lua` (a level-1000 and
a level-300 viewer of one meter, the push at a level change), `tests/deathrecap_test.lua` (a recap at its death's
level, the stored row unchanged) and `tests/item_tooltip_test.lua` (a built tooltip as sent), the engine header in
`tools/chaosdisplay_test.cpp` (CI, the header cut out of the patch), the patch guard `tools/display_scale_patch_test.py`
(CI: the chain is numbered without gaps, 0037's hunks are well formed, the last patch writing each function scales it,
the Lua binding and the opcode), client `game_chaosscale/scalelogic_test.lua`, `game_itemtooltip/tooltiplogic_test.lua`
(the compare across scales), `client_chaos_numbers/numbers_test.lua`, `game_dpsmeter/dpsmath_test.lua` and
`game_hunt/huntmath_test.lua` (M / B / T).

**Checked live (2026-10-13):** the base server source with src-patches 0001-0037 (the chain applies to the base and
builds without warnings), `install_all.py`, the Linux client with the overlay, the live sprite pair. A Warrior at level
1000 hitting a target with raw 2600 fire and 1800 physical saw "2.6M" and "1.8M" above it, "A rat loses 2.6M hitpoints
due to your attack." in the Server Log, "You lose 300k hitpoints" and "You healed yourself for 450k hitpoints", its
health as 15.9M / 15.9M and mana 5.36M, and the DPS meter at 66M in 18 s (3.5M DPS; the meter's raw total was exactly
66,000). The same character at level 100 saw 260, 180, 45, health 2.47k and the meter at a few hundred DPS; at level
300 its health read 21.9k / 27.3k (x5) and at level 700 1.14M (x100). A level lost (removed experience) and a reattach
after the client was killed brought the right factor to the client. Not checked live: two players at once (PvP, a
party), the item tooltips and the energy shield in a client, the Windows build.

## Nemesis (`nemesis.lua`, `nemesis_core.lua`, `nemesis_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_nemesis.sql`, client `game_nemesis`)

A regular monster that kills a character may become that character's personal Nemesis. Client `game_nemesis`, extended
opcode 163 (`ChaosOpcodes.nemesis`; free in the reference server, the base client and every Chaos module), a
"Nemesis" tab put into the Bestiary window's tab row at runtime (`game_bestiary` is not edited) and Hunt > Nemesis.
Settings: `nemesis_config.lua` (`ChaosNemesisConfig`). Table `chaos_nemesis` (`Chaos.tables.nemesis`), created at
startup when missing and in `sql/chaos_nemesis.sql`. Storages 7102300 - 7102309. Pure logic: `nemesis_core.lua`,
tested by `tests/nemesis_test.lua` (core and `nemesis.lua` against a mocked engine) and the client's
`game_nemesis/nemesisview_test.lua`.

- **Birth.** The victim's death event. The killer must be a regular monster: no boss (isboss, `ChaosTierConfig.bosses`,
  tier boss), summon, treasure goblin, renamed monster (rift, invader: an event or instance monster) or nemesis, no
  player in the kill (PvP), the victim outside every `Chaos.registerInstance` instance and of level 50 or more. Then
  25% (`birth.chance`). One active nemesis per character; none for 6 h after the last one ended. Server-wide the chance
  falls linearly above 200 active nemeses (`softCap`) to none at 300 (`serverCap`); the count is read at startup and
  every hour.
- **The nemesis.** A generated name (syllables, `names`) with an epithet from the kills and the victim's name: "Varkh,
  Bane of Varek", then "Twice-Slayer of", "Thrice-Slayer of", "Doom of" (pt-BR: "Flagelo de", "Duas Vezes Algoz de",
  ...; the shown monster name is one string for every viewer, `nameLang` = English). Level = the killer's
  (`ChaosLoot.monsterLevel`, else max health / 20) + 10-20%; health x1.5 x (level / base level), damage x1.0 and
  experience x2.5 (owner 2026-10-18: was x3, x1.3, x4; a kill takes about half as long, config only, applies to every
  nemesis at its next spawn) through its own monster_tiers.lua tier `nemesis` (label "Nemesis" in the monster bar). Look: the
  Heartblood outfit shader (23), a black skull, a death effect when it appears. No new sprite.
- **Traits.** One at birth, a second at the second kill: Vengeful (the berserker modifier), Swift, Thorned
  (reflective), Regenerating, Stalker (steps next to its victim when more than 7 tiles away, every 8 s). `nemesis.lua`
  sets `ChaosTiers.nemesis` and the `ChaosTierState` entry, so monster_tiers.lua's damage, reflect and experience
  handlers do the work (wrapped, not edited); its tick runs the regeneration. Depth = `maxChain`: never an ambush copy.
  Before its own stats it is paced (`ChaosPace.apply(monster, true)`): a script-made monster is never paced on its own,
  and unpaced a level 1000 nemesis skipped the pace damage x0.40 and health x0.42 of its level, so it hit 2.5x harder
  than its own type and one-shot its victim (beta, 2026-10-21). Its health, damage and experience now start from the
  paced numbers of its type.
- **Appearing.** The kill event is registered only on characters with a nemesis. A kill of the same type, or of a
  monster within 25% of its base level, rolls 4%: "You feel a familiar hatred watching you...", then 3 s later the
  nemesis 3-6 tiles away (no protection zone, house or instance). At most every 30 min (15 until 2026-10-22: in a pack
  farm the 4% comes up within a few dozen kills, so it showed at every cooldown). It fades after 5 min, when its
  victim logs out, dies, changes floor or runs 30 tiles off. Never for anybody else.
- **No griefing.** Health- and mana-change events on every player cancel its damage to anybody but the victim and
  the victim's party; one on the nemesis cancels damage from anybody else (and their summons). It retargets its victim.
- **Growth.** It kills its victim again: one more kill (up to 4), +10% of the base level, the second trait, the next
  epithet. A nemesis not seen for 14 days is gone (login check, startup and hourly `DELETE`).
- **Rewards** (`K.reward`). The victim slays it: a trophy (`rewards.trophy.id` 7393, a stock hunting trophy; named
  "nemesis trophy", the engraved name in the description and the custom attribute `chaos_nemesis_name`, owner
  `chaos_nemesis_owner`, `chaos_storebound` and `chaos_locked`: the market and NPCs refuse it, a house takes it), the
  title Avenger of Self (`ChaosTitles` source `nemesis`) and gold in its corpse (5000 + 150 per level, once per 20 h).
  A party member slays it: the Nemesis Hunter bounty to the bank (10000 + 200 per level, once per 6 h per hunter, never
  for the victim's account or connection, never for a nemesis younger than 10 min), the title Nemesis Hunter after 3,
  and a notice to the victim. Killed by the world (no player credit): no reward, it comes back. The row is deleted
  before anything is paid, so a second death event pays nothing. Hardcore: a Hardcore character can have one; a
  Hardcore slayer gets the trophy only.
- **Optional hooks, all guarded:** `Chaos.t` / `Chaos.lang` (texts: the English texts of `nemesis_config.lua` are the
  keys; until `i18n_strings.lua` has them a pt-BR player reads the config's `texts.pt`), `ChaosAchievements.progress`
  (stats `nemesis_marked`, `nemesis_avenged`, `nemesis_hunted`; the achievements themselves are not written yet),
  `ChaosLeaderboard.record` (board `nemesis` once `leaderboard_config.lua` lists it), `ChaosNameplate.refresh`,
  `ChaosSeason.modesOf`.
- **Performance.** Per death: a few table checks and, on a birth, one INSERT. Per kill: only characters with a nemesis
  run the kill event (a table lookup and one roll). Per hit on a player: one table lookup. Login: one SELECT by
  `player_id` (indexed).
- Not run on a live server yet.

## Tales (`tales.lua`, `tales_core.lua`, `tales_config.lua`, `lore_data.lua`, npc `Archivist Maelis`)

Story quests from level 8 to 2000: 27 tales (2026-10-22: 23 added to the first 4). The giver is Archivist Maelis
(`data/npc/Archivist Maelis.xml`, `npc/scripts/archivist_maelis.lua`), placed next to the first temple at startup;
`install_class_ascension.py` copies the NPC folder. She gives and closes every tale.

| 12 | The Lantern Road | vigil | Teeth in the Cellars |
| 15 | The Troll Toll | compact | |
| 20 | The Deserters of Anvildeep | compact | |

| 130 | Outcasts of the Pit | compact | |

- **Steps.** kill (party members within 30 squares share the kill), visit, talk, deliver, report. The last step is
  always deliver or report at the Archivist; `M.problems` refuses any other config and the startup logs it.
- **Visit.** Stand within `radius` of a place: a hunting mark of `data/chaos_poi.lua`. Only characters with an open
  visit step are watched (`T.watch`); the global event `ChaosTalesVisit` checks them every `visitMs` (3 s) and sweeps
  all players every `visitSweep` ticks. The place is revealed on the map when the step opens (`ChaosPoi.seen`, opcode
  153 `reveal`).
- **Talk.** Ask a faction NPC for "tales" (Warden Ysolde, Forgemaster Brannoc, Cantor Velith, Elder Bramwyn).
  `npc/scripts/chaos_faction_npc.lua` loads `tales_core.lua` and does the step in its own Lua state; with nothing
  pending the faction dialogue runs as before.
- **Chains.** `requires` names a tale that must be done first. A locked tale is not offered, and a forged accept is
  refused.
- **Rewards.** Experience, bank gold, orbs, faction reputation and a lore book. The experience is a share of the next
  level, measured at most at the top of the tale's band (`M.xpLevel`), so a high character gets no huge reward from a
  low tale.

Every text is English and Brazilian Portuguese: a player says "portugues" or "english" to the Archivist, or `Chaos.t`'s
language decides. The Archivist also answers lore questions from `lore_data.lua`. The list shows tales in progress
first, then new ones, then done ones. Modal windows 7170-7171. Storages 7101500 - 7101549 (slots 1-19) and 7101560 -
7101599 (slots 20-39); a slot per tale, append only, never reuse one. No spoken `!command`. Pure logic:
`tales_core.lua`; tests: `tests/tales_test.lua`. Not run on a live server.

## First hour (`firsthour.lua`, `firsthour_core.lua`, `firsthour_config.lua`)

Hints for a character, English and Brazilian Portuguese, at levels 1, 4, 8, 12, 20, 30, 50 and 100: hunting marks,
the next gear, the bounty board at 8, the unlocks at 30, 50 and 100; and (2026-10-15) at every band where the next system
unlocks: 120 (the Next Goals panel), 150 (pocket bosses, guild bosses, the Scorched Marches), 200 (the hunt teleports,
tales), 250 (Cruel Trial, island pocket bosses, Conquest Tokens), 300 (world bosses, boss passive points), 400, 500,
700, 800 (raid, Omens, The Hollow Vault), 900 (Ascended Omens), 1000 (Cinderheart, Marrow Crypts, Paragon), 1300, 1600
and 2000. At levels 1, 8, 20, 35, 50, 80, 120, 160, 200, 300, 400, 500, 700, 800, 1000, 1150, 1300, 1500 and 1750 it
marks the 3 nearest hunts of the character's level on its map (`data/chaos_poi.lua`) and names the content hunts of the
teleport room of Cinderhold for its level (`F.planNames`: the placed plans of `hunt_teleports.lua`, else
`goals_config.lua` `hunts`). Characters above level 20 when the module first sees them get every hint marked as given,
silently. Hints and reveals are bits by index: new ones go at the end of the lists. A character that knew a shorter list
(storage +2 / +3, else `legacy` = 8 hints, 6 reveals) gets the new entries of levels it already passed marked as given,
silently, at its next login (`M.sync`); the rest come at their level. Storages 7101550 - 7101559 (+0 hints, +1 reveals,
+2 hints known, +3 reveals known). Tests: `tests/firsthour_test.lua`.

**O240, the first hour walked to level 30.** A character starts at level 8 (no tutorial island), wearing its kit. The model
(`tools/progression_model.lua`) puts levels 8 to 20 at 0.70 - 0.74 minutes a level, so level 25 comes about 12 minutes in.
`--spells` shows the gap: every class has spells at 1 and 8, then nothing until 25 (Mystic and Elementalist 20; the Necromancer
line 12, 16 and 20). Weapon coverage has 4 or more weapons in the 1-20 band for every class, so the upgrade exists; what was
missing was telling the player. Changes: (1) the hints came together (a new character had three due at its first login, level 8,
beside the welcome and the Helper): `F.run` now says one per run (`cfg.pace.perRun`) and `F.later` schedules the next after
`cfg.pace.gapMs` (75 s); a hint with hunt names reads them from the map (`F.peekMarks`) when the reveal came in an earlier run;
(2) `dueHints` orders by level, so hints added at the end of the list can sit at a lower level: `upgrade` (10, the town shops
and the Item Finder) and `nextspells` (16, the next spells at about level 25); (3) Next Goals `spells25` (unlocks at 12, "Reach
level 25: new spells", opens the Spellbook), so the tracker has a next step between the passive point and level 20; (4) the
Portuguese hints used `Aventura >`, `Economia >` and an English `Next Goals`: they now use the menu names the client shows.
Left alone on purpose: spell unlock levels (spells_chaos.xml, rotation data, icons and tests change together), the top menu
(then showed every system from the start; O259 and O262 hide entries below their level, see "The top menu reveals systems by level"), and the milestone gifts (10 of 10 storages used).

**O241 (2026-10-25): a spell between levels 12 and 20 for every class.** The O240 audit left the unlock levels alone; this
moves them. Chaos spells (`spells_chaos.xml`): Reaping Gyre 30 -> 16 (Warrior, Juggernaut, Berserker), Dawnpiercer 30 -> 12
and Snare Trap 40 -> 16 (Ranger, Deadeye, Beastmaster; Snare Trap is shared, so the Thief, Ninja and Samurai get it at 16
too), Rime Bloom 20 -> 16 (Mystic, Elementalist), Sundering Palm 30 -> 16 (Monk, Shadowfist, Iron Sage), Consecration 40 -> 16
(Templar, Inquisitor, Sentinel). The Illusionist had no Chaos attack spell before 110, so the base Arcane Ripple (also the
Mystic's) goes 40 -> 16 through `data/spells/spell_timings.csv` (`patch_spell_timings.py`, install step `spells`) and
`stock_spells.csv`. The Necromancer line keeps 12, 16 and 20. Damage formulas are unchanged: they scale with level and magic
level or weapon skill, so the spells hit softly at 16; the mana check (`rotation_sim.py --mana --check`) still passes. The
cooldown ladder is by damage, not level, so no cooldown moved. Regenerated: `spelldata.lua`, `autorotation_data.lua`
(`rotation_sim.py --write`), `wiki_data.json`. The first-hour tip `nextspells` and the goal `spells25` now say "a new spell
between levels 12 and 20, more around 25". `luajit tools/progression_model.lua --spells` has a new column, the longest
stretch without a new spell in levels 8-30 (was 17 levels, 8 to 25, for 16 classes; now 10 at most, 25 to 35). No CI limit:
`progression_config.lua` has no spell-gap number.

**O248 (2026-10-26): the 25 to 35 stretch.** 15 classes still waited from 25 to 35 (about 7 minutes). Only shared spells sit
there (Hunter's Instinct is at 25, Flickerdash at 35), so two moves cover all 21 classes without touching a kit, the rotation
data or the icon sheets (neither is an attack spell): Flickerdash 35 -> 30 and Vigil of Clarity 40 -> 35 (`spells_chaos.xml`;
Vigil of Haste stays at 40). Moving Flickerdash alone only shifted the gap to 30-40. Every class now has a spell at 25, 30, 35
and 40. Longest stretch in levels 8-35 (`--spells`): was 10 levels (25 to 35) for 15 classes, now 9 at most (16 to 25, for 18
classes; 5 for the Necromancer, Lich and Bone Lord). The 16 to 25 stretch is not closed: it would need a class spell moved to
about 20. Regenerated: `spelldata.lua`. The tip `nextspells` and goal `spells25` say "more at levels 25, 30 and 35" (en,
pt-BR). The Clarity vigil reserves 20% of the mana, so at 35 it is a real choice, not a free buff (not played).

**O250 (2026-10-26): a new spell around level 20 for every class.** `--spells` showed 9 levels without a new spell (16 to 25)
for 18 classes, and behind it a second gap the table did not show: 8 to 16, since the O241 spells sit at 16. Two moves per
line close both, to at most 6 levels in 8-35 (was 9; the Ranger line 4, 2, 6, 5; the Necromancer line 5). A second spell
from the line's own kit at 20, an attack spell where the mana runway allows: Earthbreaker 60 -> 20 (Warrior, Juggernaut,
Berserker), Sanctum Burst 50 -> 20 (Ranger, Deadeye, Beastmaster; base spell, `stock_spells.csv` and a level in
`spell_timings.csv`), Witchfire Bolt 30 -> 20 (Mystic, Elementalist), Blade Flurry 50 -> 20 (Thief, Ninja, Samurai), Palm
Shockwave 50 -> 20 (Monk, Shadowfist, Iron Sage). Two lines get a heal because no attack spell fits. Templar line: Vow of
Mending 30 -> 20; Hallowed Cut (80) was the other candidate, but its 115 mana (and Consecration's 95) leaves a Templar or
Sentinel pool of 192 with 14.9 s of casting at level 20, under the 15 s runway of `rotation_sim_test.py` (the Inquisitor
passes: it regenerates more). Illusionist: Purifying Wellspring 40 -> 20 (the Mystic's too); Bewitching Hex (60) was
the only attack candidate and it is far above the other classes (Illusionist 26 -> 136 damage a second on one target at
level 20, Mystic 55 -> 206; the median class is about 25), so it stays at 60. The O241 spells move from 16 to 14 so the first wait
(8 to 14) is 6 levels: Reaping Gyre, Rime Bloom, Arcane Ripple, Sundering Palm, Consecration, Snare Trap (also the Thief
line's; the Ranger line keeps Dawnpiercer at 12 and gets Snare Trap at 14). Attack counts per class do not change
(`check_attack_counts.py` counts the total, 10 each). Damage formulas are unchanged and scale with level, so the moved
spells hit softly at 20 and grow with you; cooldowns stay (the ladder is by damage). Regenerated: `spelldata.lua`,
`autorotation_data.lua` (`rotation_sim.py --write`: a preset at 20 for the lines with an attack spell there), `wiki_data.json`, the Spellbook hero
image of the wiki. `--spells` now covers levels 8-35. The tip `nextspells` and goal `spells25` say "around levels 12-14
and 20, more at 25, 30 and 35" (en, pt-BR).

## Next Goals (`goals.lua`, `goals_core.lua`, `goals_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_goals.sql`, client `game_goals`)

Owner goal (2026-10-15): item acquisition and progression must be clear: how to evolve, what the goal is, what to do
next, noob friendly. Every character (not only season characters) has a panel, Adventure > Next Goals (Próximos
objetivos), and a compact tracker on screen (Adventure > Goal Tracker or the window's box toggles it). No talkaction.

- **Bands.** 13 level bands from 1 to 2000+ (`goals_config.lua` `bands`: 1, 20, 50, 100, 200, 300, 500, 800, 900, 1000,
  1300, 1600, 2000). Each has a name and a line, a gear path (where the next gear comes from: hunts, dungeons, vendors,
  crafting; each line with a button) and the content hunts of the teleport room whose band holds the level
  (`hunts`, checked against `tools/areaplan/plans/*.json` and `hunt_teleports_config.lua` by the test).
- **Goals.** 73 goals, each with a title, why it matters, where (a button: a client window, an Info page, the kill
  tasks, the Item Finder, or a mark on the minimap at an NPC, the nearest hunting ground of the level, a teleport of the
  room or the temple: the server resolves the position), progress, the expected effort and a small reward. They cover
  the unlocks: passive tree (12), bounty (8), kill tasks, crafting orbs, invasions, arena, ascension (100), rifts, the
  Vocation Trials, the Ember Descent, factions (Trusted, Honored, Revered, Exalted), dungeons, pocket bosses and Conquest
  Tokens (150, shown only while `ChaosPocketBoss` / `ChaosConquest` exist: `requires`), the Infinity Tower, uniques,
  world bosses (300), Orbs of Grafting, the raid and Omens (800), The Hollow Vault (800), Ascended Omens (900), the
  Cinderheart and The Marrow Crypts (1000), Paragon (1001), legendary powers, The Iron Crucible (1300), The Fallen
  Sanctum (1600), The Pyre Throne and difficulty 6 (2000), and a "reach level N" goal closing each band.
- **The panel** lists the open goals of the band, then up to 6 open goals of the bands below (the nearest first, "and N
  more"), then the band's goals done; the side column has the gear path, where to hunt and the next 3 unlocks
  ("Level 500: Reach level 800"). Season characters get a Seasonal Journey button: the Journey stays the season's own
  checklist (`season_journey*.lua`), Next Goals is the character's level path.
- **Progress** is what the other systems already count, read live: every achievement counter
  (`ChaosAchievements.stats`: kills by tier, rift tier, world boss and Omen kills, bounties, kill tasks, dungeon clears
  per generated dungeon `dungeon_<id>`, trials, raid, uniques, orbs, Paragon ...); `ChaosAchievements.progress` / `set`
  are wrapped (`ChaosWrapChain`, marker `goals_*`) so a change checks the goals; a level up (onAdvance) does too. Own
  stats (`goals_config.lua` `own`, rows `s:<stat>`): `faction_rank` (ChaosFactions.gain wrapped), `pocket_kills` and
  `conquest_earned` (ChaosConquest.grant wrapped: a `pocketboss:<boss>` grant is a pocket boss kill), `tower_floor`
  (ChaosTower.recordRun), `descent_*`, `dungeon_clears`, `atlas_points` (ChaosSeasonJourney.emit wrapped: the lines
  descent.lua, dungeons.lua and atlas.lua already call for every character), `passive_spent` (ChaosPassiveTree
  .hasAllocation at login, panel open and from a `ChaosPassiveTree.listeners` entry after every save). Other scripts
  may call `ChaosGoals.emit(player, stat, value)` (guarded). No other file was edited for the tracking.
- **Live refresh** (`G.schedule`, `G.refresh`): a change waits `checkMs` (250 ms) so one kill's counters merge, then
  the goals are checked and the tracker, and the panel while open, are pushed only when what they show changed
  (`K.sig`, `K.panelSig`). At most one run per `pushMs` (1 s) per character (`K.queuePush`); a done goal leaves the
  tracker and the next open one takes its place. Bounty contracts arrive through `bounty.lua`
  `ChaosLeaderboard.record("bounty")`, which `achievements.lua` turns into `bounty_done` (paid contracts only).
- **Rewards** once per goal and character: experience (`reward.xpPct` = 4% of the experience to the next level), gold
  to the bank (`goldPerLevel` 25 x level, at least 200) and Conquest Tokens by band (0-10) through
  `ChaosConquest.grant(player, "goals", n)`, given only while `conquest_config.lua` has a `goals` source (open item for
  the Conquest owner). The row `g:<key>` is written before the reward. A character first seen by the module (no rows)
  gets the goals of the bands below its own that it already did marked done without a reward (`K.retro`, value 2).
- **Messages:** a text and a toast (notifications opcode 79, action `journey`) per goal done; entering a band says
  "New goals at level N" with the band's name.
- **Protocol** (opcode 178, `ChaosOpcodes.goals`; free in the reference server, the base client and every Chaos
  module, checked by the test): client -> server `open | close | tracker`; server -> client `goals {header, goals,
  upcoming, gear, hunts, hereWhere}` (Chaos.sendChunked; under 24 KB at its largest band), `tracker {rows}`,
  `done {text}`. Requests rate limited per action (400 ms).
- **State:** `chaos_goals` (player_id, entry, value, at). No player storages.
- **Tests:** `tests/goals_test.lua` (config, hunts against the plans, stats against the counters, windows against
  the client modules, NPCs against data/npc, the guide's sections, bands, retro, evaluation, rewards, the panel, the
  tracker, effort texts; goals.lua on a mocked engine: login, rewards once, the hooks, the panel, the resolver, the band
  message, logout), client `game_goals/goalsview_test.lua`. Not run on a live server.

## Server texts in pt-BR (Chaos.t)
`i18n_core.lua` (ChaosI18n, pure) puts the helpers on `Chaos`: `Chaos.t(player, "English %s pattern", ...)`, the text in
the player's language; `Chaos.lang(player)` / `Chaos.setLang(player, lang)`; `Chaos.broadcast(type, key, ...)` (or a
deferred text, or a function(lang)): each player reads it in their own language; while nobody online reads pt-BR it is
the one `Game.broadcastMessage` of before. `ChaosI18n.msg(key, ...)` is a deferred text (tostring = English) for
helpers that send one text to many players (rift and raid `say` / `alert`, world boss, invasion and world event
announcements, mentor and referral `say`) or that return a reason the caller shows (store refusals). The key is the
English pattern itself; `i18n_strings.lua` has the pt-BR table (one table, no key twice; the translation keeps the %
conversions of its key in the same order). The client says its
language in the display scale hello on opcode 157 (`i18n.lua`; a hello without `lang` changes nothing); it is kept in
storage 7101830 for the next login. A file that calls the helpers starts with
`if not Chaos.t then dofile("data/scripts/chaos/i18n_core.lua") end`. Pure cores take an optional last `lang` argument
(`T(lang, key, ...)`: through ChaosI18n when it is loaded, English otherwise), so their tests stay English.
A reason a party member "stays behind" with (rift, Ascended arena, Descent, raid) is a deferred text in the third
person ("is in a fight", "needs level %d"); `ChaosI18n.you(why)` gives the second person ("are in a fight") for the
member's own line and the "You %s." refusal. The rift HUD notes are deferred texts too, resolved per player when the
HUD is sent.

NPC scripts run in their own Lua state, which never sees the hello: `ChaosI18n.langOf(player | cid)` reads the stored
language, `ChaosI18n.npcText(cid, key, ...)` translates a line, and `ChaosI18n.npcMessages(npcHandler)` (called after
the script's own `setCallback` lines) gives the XML's `message_greet` / `farewell` / `walkaway` / `sendtrade` in the
