## Smart loot (`smartloot.lua`, `smartloot_core.lua`, `smartloot_config.lua`)

Owner goal (2026-10-15): drops should feel relevant. A gear drop that nobody near the corpse can wear (a wand in a Warrior
party) may become a gear item of the same monster's loot table that someone near can wear.

- **Who is near.** The corpse owner and the owner's party members on the same floor within `partyRange` (30) squares.
  A mixed party gets drops for any of its classes.
- **Who can wear what.** The equip rules of `movements.xml` and `weapons.xml` (class, level), read once by the Gambler's
  parser (`ChaosGamble.rules`, `gamble.lua`). An item without a rule fits every class and is never swapped. By default
  only the class counts (`checkLevel = false`): a drop can be kept for later.
- **The swap.** With `swapChance` (60%) per unwearable drop, at most `maxSwapsPerCorpse` (3) per corpse. The new item is
  drawn by the loot table's own chances among the wearable gear, of the same kind first (weapon, shield, quiver, head,
  armour, legs, feet, ring, necklace), else any kind (`anySlotFallback`). Nothing wearable in the loot table: the drop
  stays. Items never come from outside the monster's loot table, so the Item Finder, the wiki loot lists and each item's
  drop chance stay true.
- **Where.** `loot.lua` step 1b, after the extra rolls and before the gear quality step: the swapped item (`Item:transform`,
  the stock rarity kept) still gets its rarity floor, item level, modifiers and sockets.
- **Class weighting** (owner answer 2026-10-15: "a Templar gets more Templar items than Thief items"). Among the loot
  table's gear, an item made for the class (its equip rule names it) weighs 3, an item any class wears 2, an item of
  another class 1 (`weights`). The Chaos extra rolls (`loot.lua` step 1) use a copy of the table with the gear chances
  reweighted for the corpse owner and scaled so their sum stays the same: as many gear drops as before, more of them for
  the class. Swap candidates are weighted the same way for the classes near. The stock roll keeps the table's chances.
  The Item Finder and the wiki show the table's own chances; for one class the real chance of an extra-roll item is
  shifted by these weights.
- Tests: `tests/smartloot_test.lua` (with the class weighting) (rules, candidates, pick, plan, the engine side on a mocked corpse and party).
  Not run on a live server.

## Gentle deaths and blessings (`gentledeath.lua`, `gentledeath_core.lua`, `gentledeath_config.lua`)

Owner goal (2026-10-15): noob friendly. Owner decision (2026-10-15, death and blessings): nobody loses items on death,
experience is lost by the base formula with a softening for new characters, the classic blessings are easy to get.

**Items.** No equipped item, backpack or container drops on death, at any level (`keepItems`). Only a red or black skull
drops items, by the base rules. `tools/patch_base_events.py` step 19 makes the base `droploot.lua` return before its item
loss when `ChaosGentleDeath.keepAll(player)`: the amulet of loss is not used up and is no longer needed (it still works
the base way for a skulled character). Step 15's hook (`ChaosDeathKeep.beforeDrop`) asks `keepAll` too, as a second
guard. Hardcore season characters keep their own rule (base item loss, and the fall of `season_modes.lua`); gentle
deaths does not touch them at all.

**Experience.** The engine computes the loss by the base formula (a percentage of the experience, lower with each
blessing: x0.92 per blessing, and x0.7 for an ascended class, as the base `getLostPercent`). Step 18 hands that loss to
`ChaosGentleDeath.onLoseExperience`, which softens it:

| Level | Share of the base loss |
|---|---|
| 1-30 | none |
| 100 | half |
| 250+ | full |

Linear between the points of `xpLoss`; the first death of a day (the day turns at 06:00) is x0.5 on top
(`firstDeathOfDay`; storage 7102740). Skills and magic level follow the engine. The player is told what was eased.
Only a death is eased: the engine also runs `onLoseExperience` for every script's `player:removeExperience`, and a
character with health above 0 there is not dying (the tutorial reset takes the island's experience back that way;
before the 2026-10-16 playtest it could not below level 30 and said "Gentle death" without a death). `tests/gentledeath_test.lua`.

**!bless** (owner exception 2026-10-15 to the no-commands rule; the only Chaos player command, `tests/commands_ui_test.lua`
allows it by name). Buys every missing classic blessing (the five base ones, `Chaos.shopServices.blessings`; not the
Ember Blessings of `blessings.lua`) for gold, carried first, then the bank. Anywhere but in combat (battle sign or
protection zone lock); one try per 2 s (`Chaos.limited`); every answer in the player's language. Price of ONE blessing:

| Level | 1-30 | 50 | 120 | 200 | 500 | 920+ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gold | 2,000 | 6,000 | 20,000 | 28,000 | 58,000 | 100,000 |

The base NPC price to level 120 (2000, +200 a level from 30, at most 20,000: the priests of `patch_base_npcs.py`), then
+100 a level, at most 100,000 (all five: 500,000, about 3 minutes of hunting gold at level 1000). Numbers in
`gentledeath_config.lua` `bless`; review in docs/OWNER_TODO.md.

**Eternal Blessing** (store, Premium & Services > Blessings, next to All Blessings; service `eternalBlessing`, registered into
`ChaosShopServices.services` at startup). One purchase per character: the character gets all five blessings, and at
every login after a death the missing ones come back (storage 7102741). Per character, not per account (recommended:
the value grows with each character's level and the other blessing offers are per character too; an account-wide
version would be one flag on the account). Not for season characters (`seasonBlocked`: a season ladder is not bought;
`!bless` still works there). Placeholder price 750 coins (docs/OWNER_TODO.md).

- Tests: `tests/gentledeath_test.lua` (curve, items rule, prices, !bless in and out of combat, money, the rate limit, the
  store service, the login after a death, the offer, pt-BR keys), `tools/gentle_death_patch_test.py` (steps 18 and 19 on
  stock copies, idempotent; run with LuaJIT: no item and no amulet lost without a skull, all three with a red skull).
  Assumption: the base engine calls `Player:onLoseExperience` and removes blessings on death (TFS 1.4 does). Not run on
  a live server.

## Ember Cache, Daily Spark and the day book (`embercache.lua`, `embercache_core.lua`, `daybook_core.lua`, `embercache_config.lua`, client `game_embercache`)

Owner goal (2026-10-15): fluid and fun for heavy and light players, everyone rewarded for effort, no chore lists. Every
activity gives **Ember points**; any mix fills the same bar. Adventure > Ember Cache opens the window. No command.

| Source | Points | Daily cap |
|---|---|---|
| Monster kills (party members near count each kill too) | 1 per 20 kills | 60 |
| Rare / legendary monster | 1 / 3 | 30 |
| Dungeon cleared, rift run | 12 | |
| Ember Descent run | 10 | |
| Infinity Tower run, Vocation Trial run | 8 | |
| Bounty done, kill task done, invasion fought, battleground or siege | 6 | |
| World boss | 15 | |
| Ashen Sepulchre boss, Omen or Ascended Omen guardian | 10 | |
| Treasure goblin | 5 | |
| Crafting orb used | 1 | 15 |
| Junk orbs offered (the window's button) | 1 per 10 orbs | 60 |

- **Junk orb offering** (beta 2026-10-20: a player held about 2,000 low-value orbs with no use for them). The window's
  **Offer junk orbs** button asks the server for a quote (`offerQuote`: the junk orbs in the backpack and the bags in it,
  what an offer takes and gives, the points left today); a box shows it, Yes sends `offer`. The client sends no number:
  the server counts again, takes the orbs (`offering.orbs`: Orb of Upheaval, Orb of Awakening, Whetstone, Orb of Erasure,
  the four most common drops, taken in that order) and only then credits the points through `E.credit` like any
  activity (the day's double points and the Spark included). Whole points only (`offering.perPoint` 10 orbs a point; a
  rest stays in the backpack), at most the source's daily cap (60 points, 600 orbs; storage +12, kept with the other
  capped sources). Never counted: locked orbs (`chaos_locked`) and store orbs. A removal the engine refuses credits only
  what left (the part that is no whole point goes back, the backpack else the inbox). Rate limit `offering.requestMs`
  (1.5 s) per player on top of the window's 300 ms per action. Pure plan `embercache_core.lua K.offerPlan`. It is a sink:
  10 orbs (about 20 minutes of hunting income by the value of the rewards above) buy one point.
- **Daily Spark.** The first 40 points of a day count double. 30 points (counted) in a day light the Spark. About 15
  minutes of hunting, or two dungeons.
- **Ember Cache (weekly).** Milestones at 120 / 300 / 600 points (counted), the week from Monday 06:00.
- **Rewards** (owner answer 2026-10-15: our estimate; the Spark worth 10-15 minutes of normal hunting, the milestones
  about 1 / 2 / 4 hours). A reward is hours of hunting gold at the character's level plus a few orbs. Hunting gold per
  hour: the "Respec" table (`gamble_config.lua` `balance.hunting`) x 1.12 (pack combat's gold per hour against the old
  model, 1.10-1.16 by band, "Pack combat"): 21k at 8, 93k at 40, 402k at 100, 988k at 300, 6.2M at 500, 10.7M at 1000
  (`income`). Orbs sell to no NPC; a median hunt finds per hour about 1.5 Upheaval, 1.5 Awakening, 1.5 Whetstone, 0.6
  Tempering, 0.5 Fate, 0.3 Sockets; counting orbs as 30% of an hour's income, shared by kind and worth more the rarer
  they are, one orb is 0.05 / (found per hour) hours (Upheaval, Awakening, Whetstone 2 minutes, Tempering 5, Fate 6,
  Sockets 10).

| Reward | Gold (hours of hunting) | Orbs | Total | Gold at 100 / 300 / 1000 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Daily Spark | 0.15 h | 1 Awakening | 11 min | 60k / 148k / 1.6M |
| Milestone 1 | 0.9 h | 1 Upheaval, 1 Awakening, 1 Whetstone | 1.0 h | 362k / 889k / 9.6M |
| Milestone 2 | 1.7 h | 2 Upheaval, 1 Fate, 1 Whetstone, 1 Tempering | 2.0 h | 683k / 1.7M / 18.1M |
| Milestone 3 | 3.4 h | 4 Upheaval, 1 Fate, 2 Whetstone, 1 Tempering, 1 Sockets | 3.95 h | 1.4M / 3.4M / 36.3M |

  Model: 30 minutes a day is about 60 counted points (milestone 1 after two days, 2 after five); three hours a day
  reaches milestone 3 in three or four days. A whole week (three milestones and seven Sparks) is about 8 hours of income on top of
  the play itself. Rewards are given at once with a toast (gold to the bank, items to the backpack, else the inbox); the state is
  written first. `tests/embercache_test.lua` checks the 10-15 minutes and the 1 / 2 / 4 hours.
- **Day book.** What the character did today: experience, levels, kills, loot value, supplies, profit, orbs / uniques /
  rarity items, deaths, time played, Ember points. At the first login of a new day the last day of play is told once
  (a toast, when it had 5+ minutes). Loot and supplies come from the hunt tracker and count while it runs.
- **Where the points come from.** Kills: a `kill` creature event (monsters without a master; each kill once per
  character). Counters: `ChaosAchievements.progress` wrapped (`stats` of the config), `ChaosSeasonJourney.emit` wrapped
  (`dungeon_clears`, `descent_runs`), `ChaosTower.recordRun` wrapped. Day book: an `onGainExperience` callback at index
  1001, `ChaosHunt.addLoot` / `addSupply` wrapped. Hooks through `ChaosWrapChain`, again every minute.
- **Storage.** Player storages 7102700-7102719 (cache) and 7102720-7102739 (day book; experience and gold as hi x 1e9 +
  lo so a day past 2^31 fits). No tables.
- **Opcode.** 174 (`ChaosOpcodes.emberCache`), free in the reference server, the base client's `ExtendedIds` and every
  Chaos module. `open` / `close` / `get` / `offerQuote` / `offer` in, `state {open?, week, day, src, book}` and `offer
  {orbs, points, room, per, carried}` out.
- Tests: `tests/embercache_test.lua` (days, weeks, caps, bonus, Spark, milestones, rewards, storages, day book, the engine
  on mocks with a party, counters, a new day's recap, pt-BR; the offering plan, a backpack with a locked stack and a bag,
  the quote, the offer, the daily cap and the next day), client `game_embercache/cacheview_test.lua` (the confirmation
  texts). Not run on a live server.

## Restock (`restock.lua`, `restock_core.lua`, `restock_config.lua`, client `game_hunt` Restock button)

Owner goal (2026-10-15): fewer dead trips. Back in town, the **Restock** button of the Hunt Tracker buys back the potions,
runes and spears this hunt session used, at the NPC price (`hunt_supplies.lua`, the lowest base NPC price; a rune by
its charges) plus a 10% convenience fee for the walk it saves (`priceMult` 1.10, owner answer 2026-10-15), paid from
the gold carried and then the bank.

- The click asks for a quote; a box lists what it buys, the gold and the fee in it; Yes buys exactly that quote (a changed or older than
  60 s quote is quoted again). Most gold first, at most 5000 units a click; without enough money it buys what the money
  pays for.
- Only in a protection zone, outside every instance. What was bought back is noted on the hunt session: a second click
  buys nothing until more is used; a session reset starts over. Items go to the backpack, else the inbox.
- Shares the hunt opcode 241 with `hunt.lua` (actions `restockQuote` / `restock`). No storages.
- Tests: `tests/restock_test.lua`. Not run on a live server.

## Party shared experience: why it is off (`party_xp.lua`, `party_xp_core.lua`, `tests/party_xp_test.lua`)

Owner report 2026-10-17: "Exp share não parece estar funcionando". The sharing is the engine's (`party.cpp`, no Chaos
engine patch touches it) plus the stock `Party:onShareExperience` of `data/events/scripts/party.lua` (only patched by
`tools/patch_base_classes.py` to count the class lines, at most 5). Findings, no Chaos script is in its way (the
experience callbacks only read the kill's experience and source; the shared share reaches them like any gain):

- The leader must switch it on (party shield menu), and then it works only while EVERY member, the leader included,
  passes all of these at once; one member failing one rule switches it off for the whole party, and the only sign is the
  shield icon: the party has 2 or more members; nobody below ceil(2/3 x the highest level of the party); everyone within 30
  tiles and 1 floor of the leader; everyone attacked a monster or healed a party member in the last pzLocked seconds.
  A buff, an aura or a shield does not count, so a support that only buffs (or an idle, far or low level member) keeps the
  share off for the others.
- The share itself is `exp x bonus / members` (bonus 1.2, or 1 + n(5(n-1)+10)/100 for n class lines, capped at x2.5 by
  the Chaos patch); with equal damage it is only the bonus (+20% to +150%) over what each member gets alone, so a working share
  is easy to miss.

`party_xp.lua` (EventCallback `onGainExperience`, index 2000, never changes the experience) makes the cause visible: when
a member gains experience from a monster in a party whose leader switched sharing on but the engine has it off, the
leader gets a chat line naming the member and the rule ("Ana has not attacked a monster or healed a member lately (buffs do
not count)", "Bob is below level 267 ...", "... is too far from the leader (30 tiles, 1 floor)"), at most once per two minutes
per party and reason; a leader who never switched it on gets a hint once per half hour. No timer and no scan: it runs only
for such members, on their own gains. The rules are in `party_xp_core.lua` (`diagnose`, pure, tested). Changing the engine
rule itself (for example counting only the members near the kill, or an aura cast as activity) is a C++ change
(`server/src-patches`, a new number) and an owner decision.

## XP gain rate display (`xp_rate_display.lua`, `xp_rate_display_core.lua`)

The "XP gain rate" line of the client's Skills window is the engine's base XP gain (plus low level bonus, boost and
stamina), and the Chaos bonuses (world, self, passive tree, item mods, party, ...) are multipliers in the
`onGainExperience` chain, so it stayed at 100%. A callback at index 999 (after every bonus, before the hunt tracker at 1000)
sets the player's base XP gain (`Player:setBaseXpGain`, which resends the stats) to what the last monster kill really
gave over its base experience (`ChaosXpCap.baseOf`: the monster's experience x level factor x stage x tier), with the
stamina bonus taken out (the client multiplies it in again). The first kill after a login updates the line; between kills
it keeps the last value. Assumed engine API, guarded and not verified on a running server: `Player:setBaseXpGain`,
`Player:getStaminaXpBoost`. Tests: `tests/xp_rate_display_test.lua` (the percent maths).

Owner 2026-10-18 ("mande todo o gold que for auto looted pro banco"): when a coin (gold, platinum or crystal coin) is on
the character's autoloot list, the coins of a kill's corpse are paid into the bank account (`ChaosAutolootGold.toBank`, an
`onDropLoot` callback at index 2.6: after the auto seller at 2, before the store pouches at 2.7 and the base autoloot at 3)
instead of being looted into the backpack. No coin stacks to convert, no weight. The chat line reads "Auto loot: N gold to your
bank." (pt-BR in `i18n_strings.lua`); the economy telemetry counts it as faucet `autoloot_gold`.

coins into the bank, with or without a coin on the list or a Loot Bag (`G.wanted` is always true). Coins inside a bag of
the corpse (two levels deep) are paid in as well. The Loot Bag's "gold" rule no longer gets coins from kills.

## Server hardening: systemd sandbox, no secret core dumps, SQL integer guards (O196)

Live server, no gameplay change. Files: `server/deploy/*.service`, `server/deploy/chaos_units_test.py`,
`data/scripts/chaos/admin/core.lua` (`ChaosAdmin.sqlInt`), `admin/actions_security.lua`, `admin/actions_players.lua`,
`bank.lua`, `tests/sql_key_guard_test.lua`, `tests/bank_test.lua`, `tests/admin_panel_test.lua`. Not run on the live server
here: only `systemd-analyze verify` and `security --offline`, the unit test (CI) and the Lua tests ran.

**chaos-server.service.**

| Line | Why |
|---|---|
| `LimitCORE=0` | a core holds the whole engine memory: database password, RSA key, client guard key, players' data. Nothing in the repository reads a core (`chaos_crashlog.sh` keeps the log tail, the watchdog the hang; `coredumpctl` appeared only in a runbook line, now changed). |
| `PrivateDevices`, `ProtectKernelModules`, `ProtectKernelLogs`, `ProtectClock`, `ProtectHostname`, `ProtectProc=invisible` | the engine needs none of them (it reads `/dev/urandom`, which a private `/dev` has). |
| `RestrictNamespaces`, `RestrictRealtime`, `RestrictSUIDSGID`, `LockPersonality`, `SystemCallArchitectures=native` | nothing uses them. Not `MemoryDenyWriteExecute` (LuaJIT needs writable + executable pages) and no `SystemCallFilter`. |
| `RestrictAddressFamilies=AF_INET AF_INET6 AF_UNIX AF_NETLINK` | AF_UNIX: the MariaDB socket when `mysqlHost` is `localhost`; AF_NETLINK: the resolver and interface lookups (could not be proven unused, so it stays). |
| `CapabilityBoundingSet=`, `AmbientCapabilities=` | the ports are 7171, 7172 and the cast on 127.0.0.1:7179, all above 1024, and the user is `chaos`. `curl` and `ls` started from Lua need none. |
| no `UMask=` | the website (www-data) reads `/opt/chaos/server/data` (`CHAOS_SERVER_DATA`) and `chaos-ctl` / the admin app read the logs; 0077 could hide files they read. |
| `ProtectSystem=full`, no `ReadWritePaths` | `strict` needs the full list of what the engine writes. The Lua side was audited: in `/opt/chaos/server` only `data/chaos_clientservices.json` (+ `.tmp`, renamed), `data/chaos_tree_picks_*.csv`, `helpai.queue` / `helpai.answers` / `helpai.alive`, `data/logs/clientguard.log` (engine patch 0021); `os.tmpname` files in `PrivateTmp`; the console log is opened by systemd. But the base engine's C++ is not in the repository, so "writes nowhere else" cannot be proven, and a wrong guess stops saves on the live server. If you want `strict` later: `ProtectSystem=strict` and `ReadWritePaths=/opt/chaos/server` (a drop-in), test on the test server through a daily save, a `/treestats export` and a stop / start. |

`systemd-analyze security --offline=true` exposure (systemd 255): chaos-server 8.0 EXPOSED -> 3.0 OK; clientservices,
helpai, discord, payworker 6.5 each -> 2.9 OK; health 6.9 -> 5.9; backup 8.6 -> 7.5; watchdog 9.4 -> 6.4;
chaos-trial-server 8.8 -> 7.5. A score is not a test: the unit test checks the lines, the live start checks the rest.

**The root `ExecStopPost`.** `chaos_crashlog.sh` runs as root (`+`) from `/opt/chaos/repo`. If the service user could write
that file (or its directories), a crashed engine would be a root shell. The checkout steps create it as root, and
`chaos_update.sh` / `chaos-ctl.sh` run as root and chown only `/opt/chaos/server`, so it is root-owned today. The unit now
checks it at every stop: `find` over the script and its three directories; owned by `chaos`, group `chaos`, or writable by
group or others (`-perm /022`), or any `find` error (no such user), and the script is skipped with one line in the
journal (`chaos-server: ... crash record skipped`), the service restarts as before. Fails closed. `chaos_units_test.py`
runs the guard on a throwaway tree. The other root units (`backup`, `health`, `watchdog`) execute files of the same
checkout: the same rule protects them.

**Other units.** `LimitCORE=0` in every unit; `clientservices`, `helpai`, `discord`, `payworker` (unprivileged, no port
below 1024) get the same restrictions as the game server and an empty capability set; the root oneshots (`backup`,
`health`, `watchdog`) keep their capabilities and get the kernel / clock / hostname / realtime / SUID / personality /
architecture lines; `watchdog` also gets `NoNewPrivileges`, `PrivateTmp`, `PrivateDevices`, `ProtectSystem=full`,
`ProtectHome` and the kernel protections; the kit unit (`chaos-trial-server`) gets `LimitCORE=0` and the safe subset.

**One core, on purpose.** To debug one crash: install `systemd-coredump` and cap it, root only:
`/etc/systemd/coredump.conf.d/chaos.conf` with `[Coredump]` `Storage=external`, `Compress=yes`, `ProcessSizeMax=6G`,
`ExternalSizeMax=6G`, `MaxUse=8G`, `KeepFree=4G` (files in `/var/lib/systemd/coredump` are readable by root only), and a
runtime drop-in that goes away at reboot: `/run/systemd/system/chaos-server.service.d/60-core.conf` with `[Service]`
`LimitCORE=infinity`, then `systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl restart chaos-server`. After the crash:
`coredumpctl list tfs`, `coredumpctl gdb tfs`, then `coredumpctl` is cleaned with `rm /var/lib/systemd/coredump/core.tfs.*`
and the drop-in removed (`rm` it, `daemon-reload`). Never copy a core off the machine, never attach one to a ticket.

**Owner steps on the VPS (once).** First get the new checkout there: admin app, Painel > card "Atualizar servidor" >
"Aplicar e reiniciar" (`chaos-ctl.sh update-apply`). That updates the checkout, the engine and the data, but it does not
copy unit files to `/etc/systemd/system`. Two parts:
- **The game server unit.** Admin app, Comandos > Ações rápidas > card "Servidor como usuário chaos" > Ver, then
  Corrigir (or "Corrigir e reiniciar (5 min)"). It installs the unit of the right layout with `User=chaos` and keeps the
  old one ("Server user (O271)" below). An older version of these steps copied the unit and set `User=` to the owner of
  `/opt/chaos-trial`: that owner is root on the live server, which is why the engine warned "executed as root user".
  Do not set `User=` by hand to the folder's owner.
- **The helper units** (no app button for these; as root on the VPS, only the ones already installed):
```
REPO=/opt/chaos/repo                       # CHAOS_REPO in /etc/chaos/ctl.conf
for n in clientservices watchdog health backup helpai discord payworker; do
  [ -f /etc/systemd/system/chaos-$n.service ] && cp "$REPO/server/deploy/chaos-$n.service" /etc/systemd/system/
done
systemctl daemon-reload
```
The server unit takes its new settings (sandbox, `LimitCORE=0`) when the unit restarts: `systemctl restart chaos-server`
at a quiet moment (it saves, players are disconnected; admin app, Painel > "Reiniciar em..."). On the Linux kit the
daily server save restarts only the engine inside `start-server.sh`, not the unit, so it does not apply a new unit.
Then `systemctl status chaos-server`, the server log's last lines (map loaded, no `Lua Script Error`), a login from the
client and `systemctl show chaos-server -p LimitCORE`. If the engine does not start: `journalctl -u chaos-server -n 50`,
`/opt/chaos/repo/server/deploy/chaos-ctl.sh server-user rollback` (puts the kept server unit back) and `systemctl restart
chaos-server`. The other units are picked up at their next start (timers: next run).

**SQL integer guards.** The admin actions `security.ip_unban`, `security.ip_ban`, `security.account_info`,
`players.ban` and `players.unban` write the address or account id through `ChaosAdmin.sqlInt` (a finite whole number as
`%d` text, `nil` otherwise; the action refuses). `bank.lua` writes the transfer amount and ids with `sqlInt` as well
(`%d`, raises on anything else), and `doTransfer` rejects an amount that `ChaosBankCore.checkAmount` does not accept (the
opcode handler already did: `Chaos.toInt` and an exact compare); before this, a star transfer relied on that single entry
check. The three cores with `'%s'` keys (`achievements_core.validKey`, `class_unlocks_core.validKey`,
`legal_notice_core.cleanVersion`) never escape the key: `tests/sql_key_guard_test.lua` feeds them quotes, backslashes,
semicolons, comment markers, newlines, NUL, unicode, spaces, empty and 1000-character strings and non-strings and checks
that no statement is built. Tests: `tests/sql_key_guard_test.lua`, `tests/bank_test.lua`, `tests/admin_panel_test.lua`.

## Server user: the engine runs as chaos, not root (O271) (`chaos-ctl.sh server-user`, `deploy/chaos_ctl_test.py`)

Finding (tester run 2026-10-27): the live log said "Warning: Cinders of Chaos has been executed as root user, please
consider running it as a normal user." Cause: the live unit (`chaos-trial-server.service` installed as
`chaos-server.service`) ran with `User=root`. The shipped unit says `User=chaos`; the O196 owner steps told the owner to
replace `User=` and `Group=` with the owner of `/opt/chaos-trial` (`stat -c '%U %G'`), and root extracted the kit, so that
owner is root. An unit with no `User=` (very old install) runs as root too. The engine is the main process of the kit's
`start-server.sh`, so it takes the unit's user.

`chaos-ctl.sh server-user`, all as root through the admin app's sudo rule:
- `server-user [status]`: key=value lines. `unit_user` (systemd's `User=`, root when empty), `engine_pid` / `engine_user`
  (the live process: `engine_pid` is the pid file's, else the unit's main process), `runs_as_root`, `user_exists`,
  `server_owner`, `foreign_files` (entries of the writable folders not owned by the user; -1 while the user does not
  exist), `repo_root_owned`, `db_admin` (kit: the database's socket admin; `n/a` on the repo layout), `unit_current`
  (the installed unit equals the rendered one), `unit_backup`, `needs_fix`, `restart_needed`. Changes nothing.
  `status` also prints `engine_user=`. `update-apply` prints a warning when the unit runs as root, and the kit update
  (`chaos_kit_update.sh`, `chaos_update.sh`) logs one at its start; `update-check` has `runs_as_root=`.
- `server-user fix [--restart SECONDS]` (30 to 900), in this order, stopping at the first refusal:
  1. Refusals before anything changes: the installed unit is not a plain file; its layout (it starts `start-server.sh`
     = kit, else repo) differs from the settings (`layout-mismatch`: the wrong unit stops the server); the repo layout
     under another root than `/opt/chaos`; the checkout (`CHAOS_REPO`, `server/`, `server/tools`, `server/deploy`) owned
     by the user or writable by group or others (`repo-not-root-owned`: the same rule as the `ExecStopPost` guard of
     `chaos-server.service`); a folder to chown that is a symbolic link or contains the checkout; the kit folder not
     enterable by others; the new unit not passing `systemd-analyze verify`.
  2. The system user `chaos` (`useradd --system --user-group`, home `/var/lib/chaos`, no login shell) when missing.
  3. Kit only: the kit's MariaDB has no password admin. `start-server.sh` connects as the system user it runs as, over
     the socket (unix_socket), and the database was created for root. The fix creates `'chaos'@'localhost' IDENTIFIED VIA
     unix_socket` with all privileges (what a fresh install as chaos would have), by running the client as the owner of
     `database/` (root: `-u root`). The game's own TCP account `'chaos'@'127.0.0.1'` is not touched. The database must be
     up (`database-down` otherwise). Without this step the engine would start but `start-server.sh` would wait 60 seconds
     for a database it cannot ping and give up.
  4. `chown -R` of only the folders the service writes: kit: `server/`, `database/`, `run/`, `logs/`, `crashes/`, plus
     `chaos.env` (owner only, mode kept); repo layout: the server folder. Never the checkout, the kit root or the
     binaries (`mariadb/`, `start-server.sh`), which stay root-owned.
  5. The unit: the repository's unit of the same layout with `User=` and `Group=` set (the kit folder replaced when it is not
     `/opt/chaos-trial`), written next to the old one and moved in; the old one is kept as
     `CHAOS_SERVER_USER_STATE/chaos-server.service.before-DATE` (default `/var/lib/chaos/server-user`, the newest 5),
     `daemon-reload`, then `systemctl show -p User` must say the user (a drop-in that keeps `User=root` puts the old unit
     back: `unit-user-not-applied`). A unit that already has `User=chaos` is left as it is.
  6. The restart. Without `--restart` nothing restarts: the engine keeps running as root until the unit restarts, and
     the output says `restart: needed`. (The daily server save does not help on the kit: it restarts only the engine.)
     With `--restart SECONDS`, a detached run (`server-user log` shows it) warns the players like `restart SECONDS`,
     stops the unit (the engine saves), chowns again (the root engine may have written files meanwhile), starts it and
     waits up to 300 s for an engine running as the user. If the chown fails or the engine does not come up as the user,
     it puts the old unit back, `daemon-reload`, restarts it and logs `RESULT rolled-back`.
  Idempotent: a second run creates nothing, keeps the unit and only chowns again what is not the user's. Output ends with
  `RESULT ok: prepared` or `RESULT ok: nothing to change`.
- `server-user rollback`: the newest kept unit back, `daemon-reload`, no restart (`restart SECONDS` applies it).
- `server-user log [N]`: the log of `fix --restart` (`CHAOS_SERVER_USER_LOG`, `/var/log/chaos/server-user.log`).
- Settings (`ctl.conf`): `CHAOS_SERVER_USER_STATE`, `CHAOS_SERVER_USER_LOG`, plus the layout keys it already reads
  (`CHAOS_KIT_DIR`, `CHAOS_ROOT`, `CHAOS_SERVER_DIR`, `CHAOS_REPO`, `CHAOS_SYSTEMD_DIR`, `CHAOS_MYSQL`). The user is
  always `chaos` (`CHAOS_SERVER_USER` in the environment is for the tests and is dropped by sudo).

Assumptions to watch on the first real run: an existing user named `chaos` is used as it is (one with uid 0 is refused); the kit extract is readable and executable by others (`mariadb/`, `server/tfs`); another program
that writes into the kit as root (a hand-run `start-server.sh`, a root `tar`) leaves root-owned files, which `server-user
status` shows as `foreign_files` and `fix` repairs; the engine as chaos can now use the database socket as admin of the
kit's private MariaDB (the same as on a fresh install), which holds only the game database.

Tests: `deploy/chaos_ctl_test.py` `test_server_user` (stubs for `systemctl`, `getent`, `useradd`, `chown`, `runuser`,
`ps`, `systemd-analyze` and the database client: the refusals leave the unit and the owners untouched, the fix, again, a
failed apply, the repo layout, the restart success and both rollbacks), `deploy/chaos_units_test.py` (both game server
units keep `User=chaos`), `deploy/chaos_update_test.py` and `chaos_kit_update_test.py` (the warnings), and
`android/app/src/test/.../ServerUserInfoTest.java` (the card). Not run on the live server.

## Engine hardening (sanitizers, fuzzing) (`tools/build_sanitized.sh`, `tools/fuzz/`, `tools/netfuzz.py`, `src-patches/0061`-`0063`)

ROADMAP "Open decisions and loose ends", owner 2026-10-20: harden the engine instead of a Rust rewrite. Parts (1) a
sanitizer build under a bot load test and (2) fuzzing of the packet parsers are done; (3) Rust for new services is
open. Goal: a malformed packet is an error, never a crash.

**Sanitizer build.** `server/tools/build_sanitized.sh BASE_TAR_OR_DIR WORK_DIR [--jobs N] [--cxx g++|clang++]
[--clean-objects]` extracts only the engine source (CMakeLists.txt, cmake/, src/) of the base download into
`WORK_DIR/src-tree`, applies every `src-patches/*.patch` in order, and builds `WORK_DIR/build/tfs` with
`-O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer` (Ninja). Its own copy of CMakeLists.txt drops `-Werror`
and link-time optimisation; the base download is not changed. Idempotent: a stamp (sha256 of the patches and the base)
keeps the tree, ninja rebuilds what changed; a new patch set starts a clean tree. A full build takes about 25 minutes
on 4 cores and about 3 GB with objects (`--clean-objects` keeps only the binary). Run it from a test server folder:

```
ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0:quarantine_size_mb=64:malloc_context_size=15:log_path=asan \
UBSAN_OPTIONS=print_stacktrace=1:log_path=ubsan  WORK_DIR/build/tfs
```

Leak checking is off: the engine does not free its world at exit, every global would be a report. UBSan keeps running
after a report (set `halt_on_error=1` to stop at the first). On the full map the server needs about 5.7 GB RSS at idle
and starts in about 2 minutes 15 seconds (ASan shadow memory and the slower allocator). Never on the live server.

**Fuzz harnesses** (`server/tools/fuzz/`, libFuzzer entry points that also build as plain regression tests):

| Harness | What it feeds | Engine code |
|---|---|---|
| `fuzz_proxyprotocol` | PROXY v1 / v2 headers read in the engine's steps, the trusted list, `looksLikeHeader` | `proxyprotocol.cpp` of 0025 |
| `fuzz_clientguard` | guard answers (`checkAnswer`, with a MAC that must pass), `gateReason` with build lists and a manifest file | `clientguard.cpp` of 0021 |
| `fuzz_loginlimit` | sequences of failures, successes and checks per IP and account; the block never longer than configured, the table bounded | `loginlimit.h` of 0047 |
| `fuzz_netmsg` | whole connections: framing, checksum, the login and game server's first-packet reads (RSA block as plain), XTEA and the in-game reads; traps on a read past the received bytes | the real `networkmessage.h`, `getString`, `getPosition`, `adlerChecksum`, `XTEA_decrypt`, mirrors of `Connection::parseHeader` / `parsePacket` and the login reads |

`server/tools/fuzz/build_fuzz.sh OUT_DIR [--src ENGINE_DIR] [--libfuzzer] [--run] [--only NAME,...]`. Without `--src`
it takes the new files out of the patches (what CI does) and builds the first three; `--src WORK_DIR/src-tree` (the
sanitizer build's tree) also builds `fuzz_netmsg`, and checks the engine still has the lines the harness mirrors.
Default: g++ with ASan + UBSan and `standalone_main.cpp`, which runs each file of `corpus/<name>/` once (CI);
`--libfuzzer` builds with clang `-fsanitize=fuzzer` for real fuzzing:

```
server/tools/fuzz/build_fuzz.sh /tmp/fz --src WORK_DIR/src-tree --libfuzzer
/tmp/fz/fuzz_netmsg -max_total_time=300 /tmp/fz/new-corpus server/tools/fuzz/corpus/netmsg
```

`python3 -I server/tools/fuzz/gen_corpus.py [--check]` writes the seed files (`seed-*`, deterministic). An input that
found a bug is kept by hand as `regress-*` and runs with the seeds. Needs clang's libFuzzer runtime
(`libclang-rt-18-dev` on Ubuntu 24.04), Crypto++ and fmt.

**Network fuzzer.** `python3 -I server/tools/netfuzz.py --key SERVER/key.pem --dev-key --server-pid PID [--duration
1800] [--workers 4] [--seed N] [--bots 900,20] [--log FILE]` sends malformed traffic to a running TEST server (its
docstring lists every case): raw bytes and lying length headers, every protocol id, the status protocol, PROXY headers
from an untrusted address, login packets with bad or mutated RSA blocks, game logins with broken sessions, names and
OTCv8 markers, and in-game sessions of the loadbot accounts (`loadtest.py setup`) that send 5-60 game packets with random
fields, cut-short packets, extended opcodes to every Chaos and base opcode with random bytes or odd JSON, bad client
guard answers and XTEA frames with lying sizes. Every case has its own seed (`--replay SEED:CASE`) and a loopback source
address of its own (the per-IP limits never see two cases as one player). A probe logs in every 5 seconds; 3 misses in
a row, or the process gone, is a hit: exit code 1 and the last 40 cases. It logs bots in and makes them act at random:
never against a live server. `server/tools/netfuzz_test.py` (CI) runs the raw, login and game cases against a stand-in
server and checks that a seed sends the same bytes again.

**What was run (2026-10-23, a private test server on the base full map (197 MB .otbm), 4 cores, 15 GB).**
- Run 1, engine 0001-0059 with 0061-0063 not yet written: 100 load test bots (`loadtest.py run --count 100 --hunt`)
  for 1200 seconds, all 100 in game, no failure, no disconnect; RSS 5.68 GB idle, 5.80 GB max; CPU 103% avg of one
  core; at the same time `netfuzz.py` for 1500 seconds, seed 2, 4 workers: 7489 cases (1889 raw, 1831 login, 1946
  game, 1823 in-game sessions), no hit. One ASan report (at shutdown) and one UBSan report (at start): fixed below.
- Run 2, engine 0001-0059 with 0061-0063 and the `jsonguards` step: 50 load test bots for 1500 seconds, all 50 in
  game, no failure, no disconnect; RSS 5.68 GB max; at the same time `netfuzz.py` for 1563 seconds, seed 3, 4
  workers, now also to the base opcodes: 7382 cases (1788 raw, 1883 login, 1840 game, 1871 in-game sessions), no hit,
  no ASan or UBSan report (start and shutdown included), no Lua error.
- Run 3, the full chain 0001-0063 (with 0060, written on another branch at the same time): built with the sanitizers,
  started, `netfuzz.py` for 300 seconds, seed 4: 1542 cases, no hit, no report, a clean shutdown.
- libFuzzer (clang 18, ASan + UBSan, 300 seconds each): `fuzz_proxyprotocol` 4.5 million inputs, `fuzz_clientguard`
  1.8 million, `fuzz_loginlimit` 2.1 million, no finding; `fuzz_netmsg` found the over-read below in its first
  seconds, then 600 seconds with 0063: 22 million inputs, no finding.
- In all: about 62 minutes of the server under ASan with bots or the network fuzzer at work, 56 of them with the
  network fuzzer (16413 cases, three seeds).

**Found and fixed.**
- `src-patches/0061-scheduler-timers-before-service.patch` (ASan, every shutdown): heap-use-after-free in
  `~Scheduler`. `scheduler.h` declared the map of pending timers before the `io_context`; members die in reverse
  order, so the timer service was freed first and each pending timer read it in its destructor. A shutdown (the daily
  restart) could crash or corrupt the heap after the save. The map now comes after the `io_context`.
- `src-patches/0062-lua-environment-built-first.patch` (UBSan, every start): `luascript.cpp` "member call on address
  ... which does not point to an object of type 'LuaEnvironment'". The `LuaScriptInterface` constructor called
  `g_luaEnvironment.initState()` while `g_luaEnvironment` was still being built. The `LuaEnvironment` constructor now
  makes its state at its end; no change in behaviour.
- `src-patches/0063-first-packet-reads-zeros.patch` (`fuzz_netmsg`): `NetworkMessage::canRead` allows reads up to 8
  bytes past `info.length`. For a decrypted message that is inside the message; for a connection's first, plain packet
  (the login packet of both servers) it is past the bytes received, so a lying string length read the end of an
  earlier packet or, since 0032 took the buffer's zeroing out, memory never written in this connection. No crash, but
  stale bytes could enter an account name, password or character name. `Connection::parseHeader` now zeroes the 8 bytes
  after each body. Regression input: `tools/fuzz/corpus/netmsg/regress-first-message-overread`.
- Install step `jsonguards` (`tools/patch_base_json_guards.py`, test `tools/patch_base_json_guards_test.py`;
  netfuzz.py, run 1): a store request (opcode 201) with valid JSON that is not an object (`1`) gave "Lua Script Error
  ... game_store.lua:350: attempt to index local 'json_data' (a number value)". The same flaw was in the base handlers
  of tasks (92), upgrades (181), inspect (107), character stats (106) and the waystone device (202, which did not even
  catch a decode error). Each now returns, as for bad JSON, unless the decoded value is a table. A Lua error is caught
  by the engine (no crash), but each such packet wrote an error to the log.

No suppression file is used: every report above was a real bug in our engine or scripts.

**Rust for new services** (part 3): see "Rust services (O153)" at the end of this file.

**Not run / not covered.** The Windows build; a sanitizer run with real players or on the VPS; MemorySanitizer and
ThreadSanitizer (the dispatcher, scheduler and network threads were not checked for data races); the client; the
`fuzz_netmsg` harness in CI (it needs the base engine source, not in git; `build_fuzz.sh --src` runs it locally). The
harness mirrors the engine's read sequences rather than calling `ProtocolLogin` / `ProtocolGame` (they need the whole
game), and `build_fuzz.sh` stops when those lines change. In-game packets were fuzzed through the network only, as
full-engine handlers. The server never reassembles chunked extended opcodes (`Chaos.sendChunked` is server to client
only), so there is no server-side chunk parser to fuzz.

## Rust services (O153) (`services/clientservices-rs/`, `chaos-ctl.sh clientservices-impl`)

ROADMAP "Open decisions and loose ends", engine hardening part (3), owner 2026-10-20: new services outside the engine
may be written in Rust, one at a time. The first is the login-screen services endpoint, a port of
`tools/clientservices.py`.

**Which service, and why.** The three candidates in the roadmap text were checked in the repository:
- the **login gateway** is HAProxy (`deploy/gateway/haproxy.cfg.template`) plus nftables, not a Python program: nothing
  to port;
- the **payment worker** is PHP (`website/overlay/plugins/chaos/pay/worker.php`, `deploy/chaos-payworker.service`), and
  it only makes outgoing calls (the provider's webhook goes to the website): no listener of its own;
- the **Help assistant** is Python (`tools/helpai.py`) but exchanges small files with the game server and calls the
  Claude API: it never accepts a connection.

The Python program with the largest untrusted network surface is therefore `tools/clientservices.py`: the only one that
listens on a public port. `chaos-clientservices.service` binds `0.0.0.0:8090`, the nftables template opens that port to
everyone (rate limited), and every client, scanner and bot can send it HTTP. It is small (one JSON file, three
answers), which makes it a good first port. The cast relay (`tools/cast_relay.py`) listens only on 127.0.0.1 and reads
the engine's own frames, so it has no outside surface.

**The crate** (`server/services/clientservices-rs/`, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, one runtime dependency: `serde_json`
and its four small crates; `proptest` for tests only; `Cargo.lock` committed, built with `--locked`; credits in
docs/CREDITS.md):
- `src/lib.rs`: the protocol, no sockets. `read_head` (any `BufRead`), `plan` / `finish`, `render`. Same rules as
  `http.server`: ISO-8859-1 head, `\n` or `\r\n` line ends, 65536-byte lines (414 / 431), at most 100 header lines
  counting the empty one, the first `Content-Length` wins and a line that is not a header ends the headers, POST body
  at most 64 KiB (413), bad JSON 400 `{"error": "invalid json"}`, unknown type 400 `{"error": "unknown type",
  "types": [...]}`, GET with the last `type=` of the query (not percent-decoded) or all three parts, OPTIONS 204, other
  methods 501, HTTP/2 505. The file is read on every request; a part that is not an object (Lua writes `[]` for an
  empty table) becomes the empty answer. CORS headers on every answer; HTTP/1.0 style, one request per connection.
- `src/main.rs`: sockets, threads and the clock. Same command line as the Python tool (`FILE --host --port`,
  `--port=N`), same start line, same log prefix `[clientservices]`. One thread per connection.
- `build.sh OUT`: `cargo build --release --locked` into a temporary target folder, the binary replaced by a rename.

**Differences from the Python service, all stricter** (none changes an answer the client can get):
the whole request must arrive in 30 s (Python: 10 s per read, so a trickle held a thread for ever); at most 256 open
connections (more are closed at once); all header bytes together at most 128 KiB; a data file over 16 MiB is ignored;
the request line `GET /` without a version (HTTP/0.9) is 400, not served; the 204 of OPTIONS has no body (Python sent
`{}` with a 204) and the error answers of 414, 431, 501 and 505 are JSON, not an HTML page; the log line is cut at 200
characters and its control characters escaped; the answer carries a `Date` header. JSON is compared as data, not as
text (key order, `\u` escapes). Not reproduced: Python's `json` accepts `NaN` and `Infinity`, keeps integers beyond 64
bits exact and accepts a BOM; `serde_json` does not (a data file the Lua writer produces has none of these).

**Switch** (`chaos-ctl.sh clientservices-impl [status | rust | python]`, admin app: Comandos > Serviços da tela de
login (Rust) > Ver / Ligar Rust / Voltar ao Python). Python stays the default. `rust` builds first (needs `cargo` on the
VPS, rustup; a failed build changes nothing), installs `CHAOS_ROOT/bin/clientservices-rs`, writes the systemd drop-in
`/etc/systemd/system/chaos-clientservices.service.d/10-rust.conf` (`ExecStart=` reset, then the binary with the data
file, `--host 0.0.0.0 --port 8090`; same sandbox, user and log as the unit), reloads and restarts only that unit; a unit
that is not active 2 seconds later is put back on python. `python` removes the drop-in. While the drop-in exists,
`chaos_update.sh` (and so `update-apply`) rebuilds the binary after the questions and before the game stops, and
restarts the unit; a failed build warns and keeps the old binary. The drop-in directory is `CHAOS_SYSTEMD_DIR` in
`ctl.conf` (default `/etc/systemd/system`). The Linux kit (`start-server.sh`, no systemd unit) keeps the Python service.

**Tests.**
- `cargo test --locked` (CI): unit tests of the parser, the limits, the content-length rule, the query, the date and
  the rendering, and proptest properties: `read_head` on arbitrary bytes and on request-shaped text never panics and
  never reads past its input; `plan` stays inside the 64 KiB limit; `finish` on arbitrary bodies answers 200 or 400;
  any data file gives objects. `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are in CI too.
- `compare_test.py` (CI): starts `tools/clientservices.py` and the binary on free ports and sends the same 50 raw requests
  to both (well-formed and broken: every method, Content-Length padded, negative, huge, short, repeated, bare LF, 70 KB
  lines, 100 and 101 headers, junk bytes, empty connections), against 10 shapes of the data file; status and JSON must
  match. The stricter cases are checked on the Rust side alone. Also the command line and a half-sent request.
- `chaos_ctl_test.py`: the switch (python by default, rust builds then writes the drop-in, a failed build changes
  nothing, python removes it, rebuild only while on, no unit refused).

**Fuzzing** (`clientservices-rs/fuzz/`, cargo-fuzz and libFuzzer, nightly Rust, run by hand, not in CI). Own crate with
its own `Cargo.lock` and an empty `[workspace]`, so stable `cargo test --locked`, fmt and clippy never build it. The
invariants are plain functions in `src/fuzz_checks.rs`, shared by the targets and by `tests/fuzz_seeds.rs`, which
replays the small seed corpus (`fuzz/seeds/`, 11 + 8 files) on stable in CI.
- `read_head`: arbitrary bytes as one connection. `read_head`, then `head_error_reply` or `plan`, then `finish` on the
  bytes after the head as the body. Checks: the cursor stays inside the input, fewer than 100 headers, a body request
  within 64 KiB, `finish` answers 200 or 400, and every `render` starts with `HTTP/1.`, has a `Content-Length` equal to
  the body, a JSON body (empty for 204).
- `parse_misc`: the same bytes as a data file (`parse_data`, `answer`, `answer_all`), a target (`query_type`, the result
  is part of the input), a `Content-Length` value, a log line (`log_safe`: at most 200 characters, no control
  characters), a POST body and a timestamp (`http_date`).
- Run (from `server/services/clientservices-rs/fuzz`, once `cargo install cargo-fuzz --locked`):
  `mkdir -p corpus/read_head && cp seeds/read_head/* corpus/read_head/` then
  `cargo +nightly fuzz run read_head -- -max_total_time=600 -max_len=262144 -timeout=10`; the same with `parse_misc`.
  `corpus/`, `artifacts/` and `target/` are git-ignored; a crash lands in `artifacts/<target>/`: minimise it with
  `cargo +nightly fuzz tmin`, fix the cause, add a unit test in `tests/protocol.rs` and a small seed file.
- Result 2026-10-27: 10 minutes per target, both at once: `read_head` 2,294,629 runs, `parse_misc` 1,816,311 runs; no
  crash, panic, timeout or broken invariant.

**Not covered.** A real `cargo build` on the VPS (the script and the switch are tested with a stub build); longer fuzz
runs than the 10 minutes above (and any in CI); the unit under systemd with the real sandbox; a load test of the
thread-per-connection design against the Python server; IPv6 hosts; the Linux kit.


## Stock level ranges on Lua monsters (O163) (`loot.lua` `L.ownLevel`, `tests/stock_level_range_test.lua`)

Owner 2026-10-24 (live screenshot, Sorcerer hunting): "Grimeleech [158]" next to "Giant Hornet [3]", "[4]", "[6]", "[7]" and "Reflect Spider [9]", all as strong as the others.

**Root cause.** The base server's Lua monster types of `data/monster/lua/azure_portals/` (20 types with `getLevel {minLevel = 1, maxLevel = 10}`, 8 with 1-50) carry the stats of a level 150+ monster (Giant Hornet 11,500 health, 8,250 experience). The engine rolls a level between the two numbers, `monster_levels.lua` keeps an own level (`displayLevel(own > 0)` returns nil), and `loot.lua` `L.baseMonsterLevel` and `pace.lua` `PC.levelOf` read `Monster:getMonsterLevel()` first. So the name showed the roll, and the loot item level, orb gate, waystone and nemesis levels, monster damage curve and the pace layer (scaled curve at level 3 instead of the base curve at 2 x pool level) used it too. In generated areas `areagen.lua` scaled health by (1 + 0.0074 T) / (1 + 0.0074 x 3) and experience by T / 3 (measured in the mock: health x8.4, experience x340 at T about 1000), and treasure goblins took 3 as the area level. The bounty pool had the right level (192) all along: `gen_bounty_pool.py` reads no Lua level.

**Fix.** `ChaosLoot.ownLevel(monster)` returns the engine level only when it is real. The bounty pool level of a type that is not level-scaled equals the estimate of its experience and health (`ChaosItemMods.estimateMonsterLevel`, the rule of `P.entryLevel`); a level-scaled type has the middle of its range there. When they are equal the engine level is a stock roll and counts as 0. Read through it: `L.baseMonsterLevel` (so `monsterLevel`, loot, orbs, waystones, damage, nemesis), `PC.levelOf`, the display level (`monster_levels.lua` sets the pool level, which wins over the own level with patch 0044), `areagen.lua` `spawnPoint`, `treasure_goblin.lua`. Not changed on purpose: `xpcap.lua` and the rift cap mirror the engine's own experience factor (x0.03 L only above 1, so none at 1-10). The engine keeps its tiny health, damage and speed bonus of the rolled level (under 8% at level 10). Rift, invasion and generated area spawns still show the level their system scaled them to.

Install: server files and a restart. No client change, no engine rebuild.
Tests: `tests/stock_level_range_test.lua` (name at the spawn, loot / orb / waystone level, pace level), `tests/areagen_test.lua` (generated area scaling).

## Faster server update: staging copy, step times, plan compile cache (O198)

Problem (2026-10-24): `chaos-ctl.sh update-apply` took over 5 minutes with the game down for most of it, because
`install_all.py` ran with the server stopped.

Flow of `chaos_kit_update.sh apply` (step names and `RESULT` lines unchanged):

1. Backup with the game up. The save wait ends at the engine log line `> Saved in steps:` (patch 0026), `--save-wait` is only the maximum. New option `--save-log FILE` of `tools/backup.sh`.
2. A manifest of the live folder (`deploy/chaos_stage_sync.py manifest`), then `cp -a --reflink=auto` of the server folder to `SERVER.new` (not `data/logs`, `data/reports`), same filesystem.
3. `install_all.py --no-sql` into `SERVER.new` with the game running, at low priority. A failing install removes the copy and never stops the game.
4. Stop. `chaos_stage_sync.py sync` brings what the game wrote since the manifest into the copy. A file that the install and the game both changed is a conflict: the swap is refused, the game keeps running from the live folder. `config.lua` is handled by `chaos_config_rates.py` (rates only; any other change is a conflict).
5. Swap by rename: `SERVER` becomes `SERVER.old`, `SERVER.new` becomes `SERVER`. Rollback state (`prev_commit`, `old_server`, ...) is written only after the swap.
6. Start, `install_all.py --only sql`, restart, `Server Online` check within `CHAOS_BOOT_TIMEOUT` (polls every 1 s now). On failure the rollback renames `SERVER.old` back. The next update removes old failed folders.

Downtime is stop + sync + swap + start + sql + restart, no longer the install. Fallback to the old flow (stop first, install in place, archive rollback) when `CHAOS_STAGING=0`, there is no room for a copy, `SERVER` is a mount point or the sync helper is missing.

Step times: `install_all.py` prints `(x.x s)` per step, a `Time:` line and `Slowest steps:`. Snapshot digests are cached per (size, mtime_ns) with a 2 s racy window.

Plan compile cache (`install_content_areas.py --cache-dir`, `CHAOS_CACHE_DIR`, default `CHAOS_KIT_STATE/cache`, outside the repo):
- Key: sha256 of the cache format, the contents and names of the compile inputs (`COMPILE_INPUTS` globs), the Python version, the `LUAJIT` env and the plan file bytes.
- A change in any input gives a new key, so stale entries are never used. Entries carry `CACHE_OK.json` (file list, sha256, size), are written through a `.partial-PID` folder and an atomic rename, and are checked on read. Full runs prune old keys.
- A strace-based test checks that `COMPILE_INPUTS` covers every file a real compile opens.

Measured on a copy of the real server (197 MB map), `--no-sql --quiet`: fresh 554 s, steady state without cache 410 s, cold cache 424 s, warm cache 339 s (`contentareas` 173 s to 98 s). Left: map load and area state of `contentareas` (about 98 s), `gearsets` 65 s, `mapfixes` 46 s. These now run while the game is up.

Tests: `deploy/chaos_kit_update_test.py` (`test_staging`), `deploy/chaos_stage_sync_test.py`, `deploy/backup_save_wait_test.py`, `tools/install_content_areas_test.py` (cache), `tools/install_all_snapshot_test.py`. Live not run here.
VPS: no action. The first update that brings this still runs the old script. Needs free disk for one more copy of the server folder.


## Combat hot paths (O199) (`tools/hotpath_bench.lua`, `tests/pack29_scan_test.lua`)

Audit of the callbacks that run per hit, per step or per tick in `data/scripts/chaos`.

- Creature events put on a target from `onTargetCombat`: already registered once per monster through `Chaos.registerOnce` and `Chaos.eventKnown` (chaos_constants.lua). Every callback that registers uses it. Players are registered at every call on purpose (events do not survive a login). No change.
- `mana_flow.lua`: the think read level, mana, maximum, health and the Parched Veins run for every player each second. `ChaosManaFlow.thinkPlayer` (core, tested against `regenAmount`) reads mana and maximum first, returns at once on a full pool, and caches the rounded regen per level (`clearCache()` after a config change).
- `pack29_vfx.lua`: the aura scan did up to 5 `_G[...]` lookups per player per second. The condition constants are resolved once per `V.scan` table.
- `gems.lua`: `ChaosGemsDealt` and `ChaosGemsTaken` built `"dmg_" .. name` strings at every hit. Prebuilt key tables now.
- Looked at, left: `pocketboss.lua` contest health (spectator scan already throttled to every 3 s), `weapon_styles.lua` `_G[element.combat]` (only on a bow hit with an element), `reward_sparkle.lua` (one `_G` lookup per 2.5 s), `supports.lua`/`cards.lua` context storage reads (one read, the value is needed), `charms.lua`/`item_powers.lua` storage reads (behind a cheap guard).

Measured with `luajit tools/hotpath_bench.lua` and `lua5.3 tools/hotpath_bench.lua` (mocked engine; ns per call, old / new). Engine calls cost more than the mock, so the real gain of the mana think is larger (5 engine calls per full-pool player become 2).

| Case | LuaJIT 2.1 | Lua 5.3 |
|---|---|---|
| mana think, full pool | 13.5 / 7.5 | 333 / 128 |
| mana think, mana missing | 59.5 / 50.5 | 686 / 358 |
| pack29 scan of one player | 100 / 57 | 420 / 256 |
| gems hit, two lookups | 3.1 / 2.4 | 133 / 62 |

VPS: no action. A normal update brings it.

## Build flags and allocator (O201) (engine `src-patches/0068-build-flags-mimalloc.patch`, `src/chaos_build.cmake`, `tools/linux/check_engine_hardening.sh`)

Owner decision: **the hardening flags ship; the allocator and `-O2` do not.** How the Linux engine is built: the only
Linux engine build in the repository is the `engine-linux` job of `.github/workflows/windows-package.yml` (Ubuntu 22.04,
g++ 11, `cmake -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DSKIP_GIT=ON`, `-Werror` stripped); `docs/LAUNCH.md` section 1 says
the same for a by-hand build. The base `CMakeLists.txt` adds `-Wall -Wextra -Wnon-virtual-dtor -pedantic -Werror -pipe
-fvisibility=hidden -fno-strict-aliasing` and turns link-time optimisation on (`check_ipo_supported`).

| | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| build type, optimisation | Release (CMake's `-O3 -DNDEBUG`) | unchanged (`CHAOS_OPT_LEVEL` empty; `-DCHAOS_OPT_LEVEL=-O2` would replace it, never measured better) |
| LTO / IPO | on (base `CMakeLists.txt`) | on, unchanged |
| `-march` | none | none (the engine is built on one machine, run on another) |
| stack protector, FORTIFY_SOURCE, PIE, RELRO, BIND_NOW | only what Ubuntu's g++ turns on by itself (not in the repo, not checked) | set by the build, same on any toolchain: `-fstack-protector-strong -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2 -fstack-clash-protection -fcf-protection=full -fPIE`, link `-pie -Wl,-z,relro,-z,now,-z,noexecstack`; checked in CI |
| allocator | glibc malloc | glibc malloc (mimalloc is opt-in, off) |

Patch 0068 adds `src/chaos_build.cmake`, included first by `src/CMakeLists.txt` (so the patch touches `src/` only, like
the others, and the base `CMakeLists.txt` stays as it is). It does nothing for Windows, macOS, Debug, or a build with no
build type (the sanitizer build passes `-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=None -DCHAOS_MIMALLOC=OFF`). Options: `CHAOS_HARDEN` (ON;
each flag is added only when the compiler accepts it), `CHAOS_OPT_LEVEL` (empty), `CHAOS_MIMALLOC` (OFF),
`CHAOS_MIMALLOC_DIR` (prefix of the secure mimalloc, used with `CHAOS_MIMALLOC=ON`).

**Check.** `tools/linux/check_engine_hardening.sh build/tfs` reads the binary with `readelf`: PIE, RELRO, BIND_NOW, stack
protector, FORTIFY, non-executable stack. The `engine-linux` job runs it after the build and on a cache hit (cache key
`engine-linux-bin-v4`). If a mimalloc is linked, the script also starts the engine once in an empty folder with
`MIMALLOC_VERBOSE=1` and requires a secure level, so a plain mimalloc fails. Result of a full build with the defaults
(g++ 13.3, `-Werror` kept, 0 warnings, 4,348,792 bytes, LTO): all six properties ok. On this Ubuntu toolchain the
unflagged build already had them by default; the flags make it independent of the toolchain.

**Allocator, measured and not shipped.** mimalloc 2.1.7 was linked and tried (the engine starts, LuaJIT GC64 works
through it). Micro benchmark of pure allocation churn (4 threads, `make_shared` objects and strings, the worst case, 5
runs each, 4 cores, the library preloaded):

| allocator | seconds per run |
|---|---|
| glibc malloc | 0.55 to 0.75 |
| mimalloc, plain (distro package) | 0.34 to 0.52 |
| mimalloc, secure (`MI_SECURE`: guard pages, randomised allocation, encoded free lists, double-free detection) | 0.90 to 1.07 |

The plain build is faster but has no heap-corruption checks glibc has, which the owner's no-security-trade-off rule
excludes; the secure build is about 40% slower than glibc on this loop. So neither ships and nothing about the
allocator changed. **Opt in, to experiment:** `bash tools/linux/build_mimalloc.sh /opt/chaos/mimalloc` (builds the
pinned upstream release v2.1.7, checking its commit and source sha256, into that prefix as `libmimalloc-secure`), then
`-DCHAOS_MIMALLOC=ON -DCHAOS_MIMALLOC_DIR=/opt/chaos/mimalloc` on the CMake call; the library is first in the link line
and the engine finds it through an rpath (bundle `lib/` with `tools/linux/bundle_libs.sh` for a package). Only the
secure build is accepted. Not measured on a live server.

VPS: no action. A normal update brings it.

## Packet compression (O209) (engine `src-patches/0069-packet-compression.patch`, `src/chaospacketcompress.h`, client base patch `0131`, `tools/packet_compress_bench.py`, `tools/packet_compress_test.cpp`)

Fewer bytes per second to the player. The server deflates its game packets. **Off by default**: `config.lua`
`packetCompression = true` turns it on (read at start; restart or reload the config as for the other engine keys).

What the client engine already had (read in the base client source, `framework/net/protocol.cpp`, `inputmessage.cpp`):
with the checksum on, a server packet whose checksum word is `0` is "compressed". The client XTEA-decrypts it, appends
`00 00 FF FF` and runs `inflate(Z_SYNC_FLUSH)` on ONE stream per connection (`inflateInit2(-15)`), so the stream carries
its dictionary from packet to packet. The feature flag `GamePacketCompression` (compress every packet) is not used.
No client change is needed to receive it; a client of an older release of ours inflates too.

What the server does (`Protocol::onSendMessage`): body -> raw deflate with `Z_SYNC_FLUSH`, last 4 bytes cut -> u16 length
-> XTEA (padded to 8) -> u32 `0` instead of the adler word -> u16 length. One `z_stream` per connection, fed in send
order (the call runs under the connection lock). Window 2^14 and memLevel 7: about 128 KB per compressing connection
(25 MB at 200 online).

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `packetCompression` | false | switch |
| `packetCompressionMin` | 128 | smallest body (bytes) that is deflated; never below 16; bodies over 60000 stay plain |
| `packetCompressionLevel` | 3 | zlib level 1-9 |

Who gets it: only a connection whose login packet carries the markers of our client (`OTCv8TierByte` + `A`, the same test
as `chaosClient`). Other clients, the login and status protocols, and the live cast keep plain packets. Not an explicit
capability bit: the capability byte of the login block is full (bits 0-7 are used) and the RSA block is a fixed 128
bytes, so one more byte could overflow it for long account + password + name.

Security:
- Server to client only. The server never inflates anything, so there is no decompression bomb on the server. The
  client's packet reader is unchanged for what the client sends.
- The client inflates into a buffer: stock code gave inflate 320 KB and took a full buffer for success (silent cut).
  Base patch `0131` caps one packet at 65536 bytes (output space cap + 1) and closes the connection with an error line
  when the result is over the cap or input is left over. Worst case before: 320 KB of output from a 320 byte packet.
- XTEA stays outermost, so the order the client expects is kept: checksum word, XTEA, inflate.
- The adler word is not sent on compressed packets (0 replaces it). It was never a security check (no key). Known, from
  before this patch: a plain packet whose adler is exactly 0 (about 1 in 4 billion) would be read as compressed by the
  client and close that connection; unchanged and not fixed here.
- A deflate error switches compression off on that connection (later packets plain); nothing is lost.
- Hardening, `src-patches/0073-compression-hardening.patch` (review findings in 0069): if the deflated block does not fit
  `replaceBody`, the stream had advanced for a block the client never gets, so the deflater is dropped as on a deflate
  error (that packet and later ones plain). And compression is switched on after the password check, not on the first
  packet, so a connection that never logs in holds no zlib state (about 130 KB). The client needs no signal for it (a zero
  checksum word means inflate). The reset path lives in `protocol.cpp`, which cannot be built standalone: not covered by
  `packet_compress_test.cpp`; checked with `g++ -fsyntax-only` only. Client side: base patch `0135` (footer bound).
- A body that was deflated is sent deflated even if it did not shrink (the client's stream must see every block). The
  expansion is a few bytes at most; `tools/packet_compress_test.cpp` checks it, the round trip against the client's way
  of inflating, 4000 packets including a 60000 byte one and noise.

Measured (`python3 -I server/tools/packet_compress_bench.py`, this sandbox's CPU, Python's zlib 1.x; bytes are wire
bytes: length word, checksum word, XTEA padding; TCP/IP headers not counted). The packets are built with the byte layouts
of `protocolgame.cpp` (tile, item with the Chaos attribute word, creature, floor, step, effect, shot, text message,
extended opcode JSON). With `--map` the tiles are the real tiles of the base server's world map (.otbm) (236,916
tiles of sampled areas, items through `items.otb` client ids). Creatures, effects, damage values and the JSON are
generated. **It is not a capture of a live session.** Level 3, min 128:

| Traffic | Real map | Synthetic map | us per compressed packet |
|---|---|---|---|
| login / teleport: 8 floors of one view | 81.4% saved | 74.5% | 56 / 129 |
| walking: one step per packet (row or column + move) | 70.1% | 67.2% | 8 / 17 |
| fighting: effects, shots, health, damage text, stats, one 10 ms flush per packet | 26.2% | 26.4% | 12 |
| module JSON on extended opcodes | 76.3% | 77.4% | 11 |
| mixed hunt minute (1 view, 200 steps, 3000 fight flushes, 120 JSON; assumed mix) | 35.7% | 37.0% | 12 |

Sensitivity of the mixed minute (synthetic): level 1 34.9%, level 3 37.0%, level 6 38.9% (CPU per packet 12 / 13 / 18
us); min 64: 50.2% (more packets compressed, 2939 instead of 1669 per minute); min 256: 16.8%; window 2^15 + memLevel 8:
37.3%; window 2^12 + memLevel 5: 35.4%. The small fight packets are the weak part: most are under 128 bytes and stay
plain. Level 3 and min 128 are the default; min 64 is the next step if the owner wants more and has CPU for it.

CPU: about 12 us per compressed packet. The mixed minute holds about 1700 of them: roughly 20 ms of CPU per hunting
player per minute (0.03% of one core), about 7% of one core at 200 hunting players. The call runs on the thread that
calls `Connection::send` (the game loop when the connection is idle), so it counts against the 20 ms task class of "Game
loop stalls". Not measured on a live server.

Verified: the patch applies after 0001-0068 with no fuzz; `protocol.cpp`, `outputmessage.cpp`, `connection.cpp`,
`protocolgame.cpp`, `configmanager.cpp` pass `g++ -std=c++17 -fsyntax-only` with the boost, fmt, crypto++ and LuaJIT
headers of this sandbox; the `Deflater` round trip test passes. Not run: a full engine build and link, a real client
against the patched server, a live load test.

Install: apply the patch with the others, add zlib to a Visual Studio project by hand (CMake finds it), build the new
client with base patch `0131` (optional for the feature: the stock client inflates already, only the size cap is new).
Then `packetCompression = true` in `config.lua`. Check in a client: map loads, walking, a hunt, relog; if anything is
wrong set it back to false. VPS: the admin app (`android/`) has no key editor for it; edit `config.lua` and restart.

## Cheaper monster pathfinding (O211) (engine `src-patches/0070-cheaper-pathfinding.patch`, `src/chaospathing.h`, `tools/path_bench.cpp`, `tools/chaospathing_test.cpp`, `tools/path_bench_grid.py`)

Monsters chase, summons follow, players auto-walk: all of it ends in `Map::getPathMatching`. This is what the audit of
the stock engine (with patches 0001-0069) found, and what was changed.

**How often it runs.** Less than expected. A monster searches from `Creature::goToFollowCreature`, which runs from
`Creature::onThink`, and a monster's think is the 1 s creature think. A search is triggered by the 2 s refresh, by a step
of the monster or of its target while it has a path (`isUpdatingPath`), by a failed step (`forceUpdateFollowPath`) or by
a new target. The first three only set a flag that the next think reads, so a monster searches at most once a second
and in the benchmark's packs 0.5 to 0.9 times a second. A throttle of "one search per 500 ms" would change nothing. Players
search once per click (auto-walk). So the lever is the cost of one search, not the number of searches.

**What one search costs.** Stock `AStarNodes` (`map.h`, `map.cpp`): `nodes(), openNodes()` zero 12.8 KB on the stack at every
construction; every node goes into a `std::unordered_map<uint32_t, AStarNode*>` (one heap allocation per node, one more for
the bucket array, all freed again at the end of the search); `getBestNode` scans every node ever created, closed ones
too, once per expansion, so a search that reaches the 512 node cap costs about 130,000 comparisons. The tile tests are
not the cost for monsters: `Map::canWalkTo` reads the creature's local walk cache first.

**What changed (patch 0070, same answers).** `ChaosPath::NodeStore` (`src/chaospathing.h`, header only): arrays that are
not cleared, the node table as open addressing with a generation stamp (no clearing between searches either), the open list
as a binary heap ordered by (f, node index) with lazy deletion. The old scan took the lowest f and, among equal f, the
lowest index; the heap pops exactly that node, so every path, every failed search and every node count stays the same.
`ChaosPath::Lease` hands one store per thread to each search (a search that starts while another holds it, which does not
happen today, gets a store of its own). `AStarNodes` keeps its interface and forwards to the store; `Map::getPathMatching`
and every caller are untouched. Player auto-walk and the Lua `getPathTo` calls get the same store (safe reuse, same paths).

**Measured** (`path_bench.cpp`; this sandbox, g++ 13 -O2, one core; the world is 8 windows of 96 x 96 tiles of the base
server's real map, floor 7, tiles with the solid or path-blocking flag as walls, cut by `tools/path_bench_grid.py`, nothing
of it kept in git; a melee monster, search radius 12, as `Monster::getPathSearchParams` sets it).

| Single searches | searches | nodes taken from the open list per search | stock | new | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| target reachable | 16000 | 67 | 19.8 us | 13.2 us | 1.50x |
| target not reachable (hits the 512 node cap now and then) | 10547 | 147 | 48.5 us | 29.4 us | 1.65x |

| A pack chases for 120 game seconds (12 monsters; think 1 s, step 500 ms, they block each other, the player walks, stands, or cannot be reached) | searches/s | nodes/s | search time per game second, stock | new | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| player walks | 9.9 | 420 | 128 us | 75 us | 1.71x |
| player stands | 9.3 | 229 | 60 us | 36 us | 1.65x |
| player unreachable | 6.0 | 1553 | 590 us | 322 us | 1.78x |

With 40 monsters (60 game seconds): 1290 / 672 us (1.92x) walking, 1094 / 575 us (1.90x) standing, 2012 / 1034 us (1.95x)
unreachable. The searches, the nodes and the monsters' distance to the player are identical in both columns (the
benchmark's `--check` fails otherwise). `chaospathing_test.cpp` runs the old and the new store through the same port of
`getPathMatching` on 16,000 random searches (walls, crowds, the 512 node cap, the 100 node budget of `maxSearchDist 0`,
ranged and fleeing parameters, no diagonals) and compares the found flag, the walk list, the end tile, the nodes expanded and
the tile tests; it also runs under ASan and UBSan.

Reading the numbers: the search time of the stock store at 40 monsters is about 32 us per monster per game second, so
500 hunting monsters would spend about 16 ms of every second (1.6% of one core) in the search, and the new store about
8 ms. That is the order of the saving on the live server, not a promise: the tile tests, `isSightClear` and the creature scan
of the real engine cost more than the grid lookups of the benchmark, and they are unchanged, so the real share of the
store is smaller and the real saving is below the 1.7x of the benchmark. The rest of the pathing cost (the think
bookkeeping, `addEventWalk`'s scheduler events, `getDanceStep`) is not in the benchmark and was not touched.

**Measured and not shipped: a search memo** (`tools/path_memo_experiment.h`, the third row of each chase in the benchmark).
A monster that remembers its last search skips the next one when the target stands on the same tile and either the walk
list still leads to the old goal (up to 1500 ms) or the last search from the same tile found nothing (up to 3000 ms).
Result on the real-map windows: 3% fewer searches while the player walks, 5% while he stands, 20% against an unreachable
player (the monsters wander, so the start tile changes and the failure is not reused); 1.15x to 1.25x less search time on
top of the store. In the synthetic dungeon the mean distance of the pack to the player grew from 7.2 to 8.2 tiles while
it walked, because monsters follow an older route round their own members until a step is blocked. Under the 20% line and
it changes how a pack moves, so it stays out. The early exit for an unreachable target with a negative cache has the same
problem (a failure is only reused when nothing moved) and a smaller search radius or node cap would change the paths; neither
was done. If the live server shows the search near the top of the profile, the next step is a negative cache keyed by the
set of tiles a failed search closed.

**Not verified.** No full engine build or link, no run on the live server, no profile of the real server (the numbers
are an offline reproduction of the search with grid lookups for the tile tests; the world is a 96 x 96 window of the real
map, the packs are 12 or 40 monsters). Verified: the chain 0001-0070 applies to the base source with `patch -p1`, 0 FAILED,
0 fuzz; `map.cpp`, `creature.cpp`, `monster.cpp`, `game.cpp` and `npc.cpp` pass `g++ -std=c++17 -fsyntax-only` with the
boost, fmt, crypto++ and LuaJIT headers of this sandbox; the unit test and `path_bench --check` pass (CI "Native checks").

Install: apply the patch with the others and build. No key, no config, nothing to turn on; a restart brings it. To compare on
a test server, watch the tick time (`slowTaskLogMs`) with a big pack chasing before and after. VPS: no action beyond the
normal update (the admin app has nothing to set for this).

Re-run the benchmark: `python3 -I server/tools/path_bench_grid.py --map DIR/data/world/WORLD.otbm --items DIR/data/items/items.otb --out grid.txt`
(about 50 s), then build the patch's header out (`awk` line of the CI step) and
`g++ -std=c++17 -O2 -I DIR server/tools/path_bench.cpp -o path_bench && path_bench --grid grid.txt`; without `--grid` it
plays synthetic rooms and corridors.

## Cheaper spectator queries (O212) (engine `src-patches/0071-cheaper-spectators.patch`, `src/chaosspectators.h`, `tools/spectator_bench.cpp`, `tools/chaosspectators_test.cpp`)

Every creature step (`Map::moveCreature`: two queries and a union), magic effect, distance effect, health bar and area
spell calls `Map::getSpectators`. This is what the audit of the stock engine (with patches 0001-0070) found, and what was
changed.

**What the stock code paid.** The QTree sector walk is not the cost (about 180 ns for a screen with 45 creatures, 30
leaves of 8 x 8 tiles). The cost around it was:
- `SpectatorVec` reserved 32 pointers on the heap in its constructor: one allocation and one free for every caller, used
  or not. A step builds two (plus the union), an effect one, a distance effect two.
- The two caches were `std::map<Position, SpectatorVec>`: a tree node and a vector copy per store. `Tile::addThing`,
  `removeThing` and `internalAddThing` clear them for every creature that is added or removed, which is every step, so in a
  hunting pack each query stored an entry that the next step freed. A query that missed cost 5 allocations; a hit still
  built a `SpectatorVec` (2).
- `SpectatorVec::addSpectators` (the union of the old and the new position of a step and of a distance effect) searched
  the first list for every element of the second: 1800 compares for 45 and 40 creatures, 70,000 for a crowd of 260.
- `Map::moveCreature` grew its `std::vector<int32_t>` of stack positions one `push_back` at a time (4 to 7 allocations).

**What changed (patch 0071, same answers).** `src/chaosspectators.h`, header only: `ChaosSpec::SmallVec` (48 pointers inline,
heap beyond), `ChaosSpec::SpectatorList` (the stock interface; `spectators.h` makes `SpectatorVec` an alias of it, same
element order, `erase` still swaps with the last), `ChaosSpec::appendMissing` (the same union in the same order, a
pointer set when both lists are long) and `ChaosSpec::Cache` (open addressing, generation stamped slots over a pool of
vectors that are reused; `clear()` is O(1) and frees nothing; a burst of thousands of centres is trimmed back). `map.h` /
`map.cpp`: the caches are `ChaosSpec::Cache`, `getSpectators` looks up and stores by a packed position key, the stack
positions are a `SmallVec`. What a cache holds, when it is looked up, stored and cleared is exactly as before, so a query
returns the same creatures in the same order.

**Not done on purpose: skip the cache clear when nothing in range changed.** The leaf lists remove by swapping with the
last element, so a kept entry could differ in order from a fresh walk (and `onlyPlayers` answers come from the all-creature
entry or from `player_list` depending on what is cached), which would change the order creatures are notified in. And in a
pack everything is in range of everything, so the clear would almost never be skipped where it matters. Collapsing the old
and new query of a step into one is the same problem (the order of the union). The sector walk itself was left alone.

**Measured** (`spectator_bench.cpp`; this sandbox, g++ 13.3 -O2, one core, best of 3, `--seconds 1.0`). The world copies the
