engine's QTree (8 x 8 leaves, `leafS` / `leafE` links, some missing sectors around the area, real map coordinates), creature
and player lists, `getSpectators` / `getSpectatorsInternal` / the cache rules of `map.cpp`, `moveCreature` without the tile
and the packets. One template runs twice, with the stock pieces (the unchanged `SpectatorVec`, `std::map` cache, `std::vector`)
and with the new ones; heap allocations are counted with a global `operator new`. A tick: every creature steps once
(`steps`), or one area spell (one area query, 3 queries per target, 25 tile effects), or 20 effects and distance effects,
or all three (`mixed tick`). The hunt is 40 monsters and 5 players in one screen, the city 100 players spread over 160 x 110
tiles, the crowd 200 monsters and 60 players in 60 x 50 tiles (a boss event, the Tower).

| Per tick | stock | new | | allocations stock -> new |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| hunt, steps (90 queries) | 57.2 us | 43.1 us | 1.32x | 457 -> 0 |
| hunt, spell (61 queries) | 2.6 us | 1.2 us | 2.21x | 66 -> 5 |
| hunt, effects (15 queries) | 0.9 us | 0.4 us | 2.14x | 15 -> 0 |
| hunt, mixed tick (141 queries) | 69.7 us | 48.7 us | 1.43x | 590 -> 1 |
| city, steps (200 queries) | 80.3 us | 64.8 us | 1.24x | 945 -> 0 |
| city, effects (60 queries) | 6.5 us | 2.8 us | 2.33x | 60 -> 0 |
| city, mixed tick (286 queries) | 114.2 us | 80.4 us | 1.42x | 1160 -> 0 |
| crowd, steps (520 queries) | 2299 us | 997 us | 2.31x | 4853 -> 1302 |
| crowd, mixed tick (668 queries) | 2471 us | 1107 us | 2.23x | 5180 -> 1317 |

That is 28% to 30% less time in the spectator code of a mixed hunt or city tick, and 55% less in a crowd (the 1302
allocations left are lists longer than 48, which spill to the heap). Parts of one query in the hunt (ns per call):

| | stock | new |
|---|---|---|
| sector walk alone, 45 creatures | 277 | 179 |
| query, cache miss (walk + store) | 405 (5 allocations) | 216 (0) |
| query, cache hit | 33 (2 allocations) | 17 (0) |
| query, players only, cache hit | 72 | 35 |
| union of 45 and 40 (copy + merge) | 307 | 176 |

The answers are identical: `--check` (CI "Native checks") runs both worlds on the same random operations (steps,
teleports, queries with the default range and with own ranges, one floor and multifloor, players only, a non empty target
vector, the union, `erase`) and compares every list element by element, in order, 6 seeds x 3 scenarios; the timing run
also compares the sums of the first 30 ticks of every phase. A broken union or a cache that clears too rarely makes
`--check` fail (tried). `chaosspectators_test.cpp` checks the pieces against std containers (ASan and UBSan too).

Reading the numbers: the saving is a share of the spectator code, and that code is small in absolute terms. A hunting
pack of 40 monsters spends about 115 us of every second in it (two steps per monster per second at the hunt row), so 500
hunting monsters cost about 1.4 ms per second (0.14% of one core) and the patch takes about 0.4 ms of that. The crowd is
where it shows: 260 creatures stepping twice a second cost about 4.6 ms per second stock and 2 ms now. The engine's own
work around each query (the tile moves, the packets, the Lua events) is unchanged and larger than the benchmark's
stand-ins, so the share on the live server is smaller than the percentages above, not larger.

**Not verified.** No full engine build or link, no run on the live server, no profile of the real server. The benchmark is
a copy of the walk and the cache rules (kept in step with `map.cpp` by hand, not compiled from it). Verified: the chain
0001-0071 applies to the base source with `patch -p1` (root `CMakeLists.txt` and `cmake` copied in for 0069), 0 FAILED, 0
fuzz; `map.cpp`, `game.cpp`, `creature.cpp`, `tile.cpp`, `combat.cpp`, `monster.cpp`, `player.cpp`, `npc.cpp`,
`luascript.cpp`, `condition.cpp`, `container.cpp` and `spawn.cpp` pass `g++ -std=c++17 -fsyntax-only` with the boost, fmt and
LuaJIT headers of this sandbox; the unit test and `spectator_bench --check` pass (CI "Native checks").

Install: apply the patch with the others and build. No key, no config, nothing to turn on; a restart brings it. To compare
on a test server, watch the tick time (`slowTaskLogMs`) with a big pack or a crowd stepping before and after. VPS: no action
beyond the normal update (the admin app has nothing to set for this).

Re-run the benchmark: build the patch's header out (`awk` line of the CI step), then
`g++ -std=c++17 -O2 -I DIR server/tools/spectator_bench.cpp -o spectator_bench && spectator_bench` (about 1 minute;
`--seconds N` sets the time per row, `--check` the CI mode).

## Cheaper map description (O213) (engine `src-patches/0072-cheaper-map-description.patch`, `src/chaosmapdesc.h`, `tools/mapdesc_bench.cpp`, `tools/chaosmapdesc_test.cpp`, `tools/mapdesc_world.h`)

A map description is sent on login, teleport and every floor change, and a row or a column of it on every step of a
player (`ProtocolGame::GetMapDescription` -> `GetFloorDescription` -> `GetTileDescription`). Audit of the stock engine
(with patches 0001-0071), what was found and what was left alone.

**Found.** `GetFloorDescription` called `Map::getTile` for every tile of the rectangle. Each call walks the quad tree from
the root (`QTreeNode::getLeafStatic`, 12 pointer hops down to an 8 x 8 leaf) and then the leaf's floor, although 64
neighbouring tiles share that one leaf and floor. A full description is 18 x 14 tiles on up to 8 floors: about 2000 walks
into memory that is cold on a big map. The sibling costs were checked and are small: `NetworkMessage` writes are a bounds
check and a `memcpy` (patch 0032 already removed the 90 KB zeroing), and the strings and creature fields of a tile are
needed bytes.

**Changed (patch 0072, same bytes).** `src/chaosmapdesc.h`, header only: `ChaosMapDesc::describeFloor` is the stock loop
(same order: x outer, y inner; same skip counter and the 0xFE flush) with the `Floor` resolved once per 8 x 8 block
through four slots keyed by block (a column of up to 25 tiles spans at most four block rows, so the next column finds
them again): an 18 x 14 floor needs 9 walks instead of 252. The coordinates are narrowed to `uint16_t` and the floor to
`uint8_t` first, as `getTile`'s parameters did, so a rectangle past the map edge behaves the same. `map.h`: `Map::getFloorAt`
(`getTile` without the last index). `protocolgame.cpp`: `GetFloorDescription` calls `describeFloor`.

**Left alone on purpose.** The known creature list (`knownCreatureSet`, an `unordered_set`): its eviction after 1300
entries follows the container's iteration order, so a different container could drop another creature and change the
bytes. It is also touched once per creature in view, not per tile. The tile writer (`GetTileDescription`) is needed work.

**Measured** (`mapdesc_bench.cpp`; this sandbox, g++ 13.3 -O2, one core, best of 7 rounds of 2000 random positions on a
400 x 400 city and cave, both versions on the same positions, interleaved).

| Description | stock | new | |
|---|---|---|---|
| city, full 18 x 14 (z 7, 8 floors, 11.2 KB) | 97-101 us | 67-72 us | 1.41-1.44x |
| cave, full 18 x 14 (z 11, 5 floors, 14.1 KB) | 93-99 us | 71-75 us | 1.30-1.32x |
| city, step: row of 18 | 9-13 us | 7-10 us | 1.28-1.29x |
| city, step: column of 14 | 5-6 us | 4-5 us | 1.21-1.28x |
| sea, full 18 x 14 (almost all empty) | 10.2 us | 4.4 us | 2.29x |

The tile writer of the benchmark is a stand-in (ground and a few items, a table lookup each, into a `std::vector`), much
lighter than the engine's (creature visibility checks, outfits, the known creature list), and that part is the same before
and after. So the share saved of a whole description in the engine is smaller than the table, probably 10 to 25%, not
measured. In absolute terms: a step saves 2 to 4 us per player and a floor change or login about 30 us.

The bytes are identical: `chaosmapdesc_test.cpp` compares the new loop with a copy of the stock one on 60 synthetic maps
(dense, sparse, empty, one tile per leaf, rectangles on the 16 bit coordinate edges and across them, floors that do not
exist, z out of range, a skip carried in from a previous floor, columns with more than 254 empty tiles) for 24,000
single floors and 24,000 whole descriptions (ASan and UBSan too), and checks the count of walks (9 for 18 x 14).
`mapdesc_bench.cpp --check` compares every byte of every position it times and fails when a full description is not at
least 1.15x faster (CI "Native checks").

**Not verified.** No engine build or link, no run on a live server, no profile of a real server. `protocolgame.cpp` and
`map.cpp` were not compiled: the sandbox has no Lua or Boost headers, so the patched files were not even syntax-checked
(`describeFloor` itself is compiled by the test with the same lambda shapes). The world of the benchmark is a copy of the
quad tree and the loops, kept in step with `map.cpp` and `protocolgame.cpp` by hand. Verified: the chain 0001-0072 applies
to the base source with `patch -p1`, 0 FAILED, 0 fuzz, 0 reversed.

Install: apply the patch with the others and build. No key, no config, nothing to turn on; a restart brings it. To compare
on a test server, time a login or a teleport (`onLogin` to the first map packet) before and after. VPS: no action.

## Cheaper line of sight (O218) (engine `src-patches/0074-cheaper-line-of-sight.patch`, `src/chaossight.h`, `tools/sight_bench.cpp`, `tools/chaossight_test.cpp`, `tools/sight_world.h`)

`Game::isSightClear` -> `Map::checkSightLine` decides every ranged shot: each attacking monster asks once a second
(`Creature::onAttacking`), `Monster::canUseAttack` asks for every target of a target search, spells that need a clear
shot and a player's throw ask too. Audit of the hot paths left after 0070-0073: pathfinding, spectators and the map
description are done; the other candidates were weighed by cost per call times calls per second. `Creature::executeConditions`
copies its `std::list` of conditions once per creature per second, measured at about 50 ns for three conditions (a
micro test, not kept): not worth a patch. `Monster::searchTarget` builds a `std::list` of candidates, but its cost is the
`canUseAttack` sight lines it already pays for, so the sight line is the better place.

**Found.** `checkSteepLine` / `checkSlightLine` called `Map::isTileClear` for each tile of the line, and that is
`Map::getTile`: a walk down the quad tree from the root (13 pointer hops to an 8 x 8 leaf; patch 0072's text says 12,
the engine's `createLeaf` runs levels 15 down to 3), then the leaf's floor, although the tiles of a line inside one 8 x 8
block share both.

**Changed (patch 0074, same answers).** `src/chaossight.h`, header only: `ChaosSight::Line` is the stock stepping (same
float arithmetic, argument swaps for the steep case, loop bounds, early exit on the first blocking tile) with the `Floor`
of the current block kept in two words on the stack of one call (`key = x >> 3, y >> 3`; a missing leaf or floor is
cached as nullptr, so a tile lookup is still `nullptr` -> clear). `map.cpp`: `Map::checkSightLine` builds a `Line` over
`Map::getFloorAt` (patch 0072) and `Tile::hasProperty(CONST_PROP_BLOCKPROJECTILE)`. `isTileClear` and `isSightClear` are
untouched. Bounds: no allocation and nothing kept between calls, so a tile or floor created later is always seen and
there is nothing to invalidate or to grow.

**Left alone on purpose.** `Tile::hasProperty` (it walks the item list, needed work), the float arithmetic (changing
it could move a line by one tile), and any cache across calls (a stale tile would change what a monster can shoot at).

**Measured** (`sight_bench.cpp`; this sandbox, g++ 13.3 -O2, one core, best of 7 rounds of 4000 random lines on a
400 x 400 city and cave, both versions on the same lines, interleaved).

| Line | stock | new | |
|---|---|---|---|
| city, 4-7 tiles | 254 ns | 199 ns | 1.27-1.28x |
| city, 7-10 tiles | 375-381 ns | 285-288 ns | 1.31-1.32x |
| city, 11-15 tiles | 547-557 ns | 400 ns | 1.37-1.39x |
| cave, 7-10 tiles | 376-381 ns | 289-294 ns | 1.29-1.30x |
| sea, 7-10 tiles (almost all empty) | 96 ns | 87 ns | 1.11x |

The tile test of the benchmark is a stand-in (a flag table lookup for the ground and each item), lighter than the
engine's item list walk, which is the same before and after, so the share saved in the engine is smaller than the table,
not measured. In absolute terms about 60 to 150 ns per sight check. A small gain: a monster asks once a second.

The answers are identical: `chaossight_test.cpp` compares the new check with a copy of the stock one for 72,000 lines
(60 synthetic maps: dense, sparse, many blockers, empty, floors that do not exist, z out of range, the edges of the 16
bit coordinates; every slope, both directions, zero length, straight and diagonal lines; ASan and UBSan too), checks
the walk count (4 for a 40 tile line, stock 39), that a blocker or a floor created after a check is seen by the next one,
and that a wrong block key is caught (tried by hand). `sight_bench.cpp --check` compares every answer it times and fails
when a line of 7 tiles or more is not at least 1.15x faster (CI "Native checks"). `tools/sight_world.h` has its own quad
tree of 13 levels: `mapdesc_world.h` has 12, so a leaf there covers 16 x 16 tiles that share one 8 x 8 floor, which is
wrong for a test that sets neighbouring blocks (harmless for 0072's byte comparison, left as it is).

**Not verified.** No engine build or link, no run on a live server, no profile of a real server. `map.cpp` and
`game.cpp` pass `g++ -fsyntax-only` against the patched base source. The world of the benchmark is a copy of the quad tree
and the stock functions, kept in step with `map.cpp` by hand. Verified: the chain 0001-0074 applies to the base source with
`patch -p1`, 0 FAILED, and 0074 itself with 0 fuzz and no offset.

Install: apply the patch with the others and build. No key, no config, nothing to turn on; a restart brings it. VPS: no action.

## Extended opcode protocol audit (O220) (engine `src-patches/0075-extended-opcode-size-cap.patch`, `chaos_constants.lua`, `tests/opcode_dispatch_test.lua`)

Audit of the server side of the JSON-over-extended-opcode protocol (client to server). Each question and what the code did:

| Question | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Size cap before decode | `Chaos.opcodeRequestMax` (16,384 bytes) in the Lua dispatcher only, after the engine had read the string (up to 90 KB), copied it into a dispatcher task and, with the client guard of patch 0021, queued up to 64 of them per connection. The base handlers and any event left with the engine had no cap. | Patch 0075: `ProtocolGame::parseExtendedOpcode` returns for a string over 16,384 bytes before any of that (at most 64 x 16 KB held per connection). The Lua cap stays (reloads, tests). |
| Rate limit | Engine: `maxPacketsPerSecond` (50, all packet types, average, closes the connection). Lua: per action keys through `Chaos.limited` in the handlers that touch the database; nothing in the dispatcher. | `Chaos.opcodeBudget`: a bucket of 250 requests per player refilled 60 a second, taken in `D.dispatch` before any handler; dropped over it with one console line per player a minute. Looser than the engine on purpose (a login sends a few dozen at once), so a real client never reaches it. Cleared at logout. |
| `pcall` around decode | `Chaos.decode` and the admin, market, loadouts, charms, remote command and patch note decodes use `pcall`. The six base handlers are guarded by `patch_base_json_guards.py`. | Unchanged. |
| Depth and element limit | None. The base `json.lua` recurses once per `[` or `{` (two Lua calls per level): a 16 KB request of `[` is 16,000 levels, a stack overflow error per packet. Elements are bounded by the byte cap (16 KB is at most about 8,000 values, about 1.4 ms to decode). | `Chaos.guardJson` wraps `json.decode` once: text nested over `Chaos.jsonMaxDepth` (32; real messages nest 2-6) fails with "json nested too deeply" before the decoder runs, for `Chaos.decode`, the admin panel and the base handlers alike. The scan skips strings and allocates nothing. |
| Field validation | `Chaos.toInt` (rejects NaN, inf, beyond 2^53, fractions floored, ranges), `sqlInt` / `db.escapeString` for SQL; `tests/opcode_fuzz_test.lua` feeds every field of every handler (92 handlers, 576 actions) negative, fractional, NaN, inf, huge, wrong type and checks that no client string reaches SQL unescaped. | Unchanged. A spot check of the `db.*` calls built with `..` found each value escaped, passed through `tonumber` / an integer helper or taken from the database. |
| Unbounded memory | Unknown opcode: no handler, no state. Chunked reassembly (`Chaos.sendChunked`) exists on the client side only: the server never joins parts, and a client request is one string under the cap. `ChaosRateLimit` keys are capped at 512 per player and cleared at logout. The client guard queue is 64 entries. | The 64-entry queue is now bounded in bytes too (patch 0075). Dispatcher state per player (`warned`, `bucket`, `warnedRate`) is cleared at logout (`D.forget`). |

Limits: `Chaos.opcodeRequestMax` 16,384 bytes (the client's largest request, a passive tree plan, is about 3 KB), `Chaos.opcodeBudget` {burst 250, perSecond 60}, `Chaos.jsonMaxDepth` 32. Raise them in `chaos_constants.lua`; the engine constant `EXTENDED_OPCODE_MAX_BYTES` (patch 0075) must stay at least as large as `opcodeRequestMax`.

Not done: no element-count limit beyond the byte cap (it would add a scan per request for no gain at 16 KB); the base `json.lua` itself is not edited (the wrapper is in `chaos_constants.lua`). A modified client can still send 50 packets a second of valid small requests: each runs its handler, and the handlers that read or write the database carry their own `Chaos.limited` keys.

Tests: `tests/opcode_dispatch_test.lua` (budget: burst, refill, per player, backwards clock, logout, flood through the dispatcher; JSON depth: limit, strings, escapes, unterminated text, the wrapper) under luajit and Lua 5.3. Patch: 0001-0075 applied in order to the base with 0 FAILED and 0 fuzz; `g++ -std=c++17 -fsyntax-only` on the patched `protocolgame.cpp`. Not built or run in an engine.

## Cheaper walk map refresh (O225) (engine `src-patches/0076-cheaper-walk-map-refresh.patch`, `src/chaosstrip.h`, `tools/strip_bench.cpp`, `tools/chaosstrip_test.cpp`)

Audit of the monster think and target code by reading, for the hottest waste that can be proved and keeps behaviour
exactly. Weighed:

- `Monster::searchTarget` collects its candidates in a `std::list` (a heap node each). Replaced by a stack array in a
  trial and tested for identical choices (same checks, same random draw): the whole search got only 1.04-1.12x faster
  against the engine's own attack test (distance, then the sight line of O218), because the sight lines are the cost.
  Under the 1.1x bar for a real gain, so dropped, not shipped.
- `Monster::updateTargetList` calls `updateIdleStatus` after every spectator. Looks redundant but is not: while the
  target list is still empty it sets the monster idle, which clears the friend list, so skipping calls would change
  which friends a monster ends with. Left alone.
- `getDanceStep` (a `std::vector` of directions, up to five sight lines), `isTarget`, `selectTarget` (a `std::find` in a
  short list), `onCreatureFound`: small, and dominated by the sight lines or the item list walks.

**Found.** Every step of a monster that walks (`Monster::useCacheMap`, anything that is not a random stepper) runs
`Creature::onCreatureMove` for the mover, which shifts its 33 x 25 grid `localMapCache` and fills the new edge: a row of
33 or a column of 25 tiles, each with `Map::getTile`, a walk down the quad tree from the root (13 pointer hops) although
neighbouring tiles of an 8 x 8 block share one leaf and one `Floor`. `Creature::updateMapCache` (first think of every
monster, teleport, floor change) does it for all 825 tiles. A hunting pack steps about once a second per monster.

**Changed (patch 0076, same tiles).** `src/chaosstrip.h`, header only: `ChaosStrip::TileReader::at(x, y, z)` is
`Map::getTile` (the ints are narrowed to 16, 16 and 8 bits the same way, a missing leaf, floor or z out of range gives
`nullptr`) with the `Floor` of the last 8 x 8 block kept in two words (block key and z), so a column or a row walks the
tree 4 to 5 times instead of 25 or 33. `creature.cpp`: the four edge loops of `onCreatureMove` and the loop of
`updateMapCache` read through a reader over `Map::getFloorAt` (patch 0072); `updateTileCache` and its `queryAdd` are
untouched. The reader lives on the stack of one refresh: nothing is kept between calls and nothing is allocated, so a
tile or floor created later is always seen.

**Left alone on purpose.** `Tile::queryAdd` (it walks the items and creatures of the tile, needed work), the shift of the
grid, and the refresh for other creatures' moves (they update two tiles with the tiles they were given).

**Measured** (`strip_bench.cpp`; this sandbox, g++ 13.3 -O2, one core, best of 7 rounds of 3000 random places on a
400 x 400 city and cave, both versions on the same places, interleaved, every cache compared byte for byte).

| Refresh | stock | new | |
|---|---|---|---|
| city, step north (row of 33) | 1.8 us | 0.97 us | 1.87x |
| city, step east (column of 25) | 0.93-1.0 us | 0.55-0.59 us | 1.70-1.73x |
| cave, step south (row of 33) | 1.6 us | 0.85-0.87 us | 1.84-1.91x |
| cave, step west (column of 25) | 0.95 us | 0.52-0.53 us | 1.79-1.82x |
| city, whole grid (825 tiles) | 33 us | 17-18 us | 1.83-1.88x |
| sea, step north (almost all empty) | 0.2 us | 0.11-0.13 us | 1.67-1.73x |

The tile test of the benchmark is a stand-in (a flag table lookup for the ground and each item), lighter than
`Tile::queryAdd`, which is the same work before and after, so the share saved in the engine is smaller than the table,
not measured. The map of the benchmark (400 x 400) fits the cache better than a real one, which favours the stock walk
less than the engine would. Absolute: about 0.5 to 0.9 us per step of a walking monster, 15 us per full refresh.

The tiles are identical: `chaosstrip_test.cpp` compares `Map::getTile` with the reader for 3.5 million reads (60
synthetic maps: dense, sparse, empty, floors that do not exist, z out of range, the edges of the 16 bit coordinates where
`x - 16` and `x + 16` wrap; every edge of a step, the full grid, random reads that change block in any order; ASan and
UBSan too), checks the walk count (4 for a column of 25, 5 for a row of 33, stock 25 and 33), that a tile or floor
created after a read is seen by the next reader, and that two floors with the same block do not share a cached floor.
`strip_bench.cpp --check` compares every cache it times and fails when a step in the city or the cave is not at least
1.15x faster (CI "Native checks"). It reuses `tools/sight_world.h`. The patch chain 0001-0076 applies to the base source
with 0 FAILED and 0 fuzz; `creature.cpp` passes `g++ -fsyntax-only` on the patched source. Not built or linked, not run
on a live server.

## Eight-direction facing (O283) (engine `src-patches/0077-eight-direction-facing.patch`, `src/chaosfacing.h`, `tools/chaosfacing_test.cpp`)

Owner request 2026-10-28: "pode fazer o patch de 8 direções do motor e fazer as gerações em 8 direções". The client half is
base patch 0160 (client/BASE.md): it draws a look's diagonal columns when the look has 8. The looks of pair 54 (3361-3363,
"AutoSprite looks (pair 54)") are the first with 8.

**What the server sends.** `Creature::direction` stays four-way: spell areas and waves, the tile in front, `getDirection` in
Lua and everything else the server decides with it are unchanged. Next to it, `Creature::facing` is the way the clients draw
the creature:
- `setDirection` sets both, so every stock turn faces its direction.
- `Map::moveCreature`: a diagonal step faces its diagonal (`ChaosFacing::ofStep`); the direction stays east or west as before.
  The client already draws a diagonal walk from the move packet; the facing matters when the creature comes into view later
  (the creature description carries it).
- `Monster::updateLookDirection`: the same four-way turn as before, and the facing of the target's diagonal when the target
  stands nearer a diagonal than an axis (`ChaosFacing::toward`: the smaller offset over 0.4 of the larger, tan 22.5 degrees =
  0.414; 2 by 1 faces the diagonal, 3 by 1 the axis). With no target it does nothing (stock: a turn to the same direction).
- `Game::internalCreatureTurn(creature, dir, facing = DIRECTION_NONE)` sends the turn when the direction or the facing changes.
  A plain turn (a player, an NPC, Lua `setDirection`, a teleport) faces `dir`, so it also clears a diagonal.
- The turn packet (0x6B) and `AddCreature` send `ChaosFacing::wire(facing)`: the client's order is north-east 4, south-east 5,
  south-west 6, north-west 7 (the server's own diagonal values are south-west 4, south-east 5, north-west 6, north-east 7).
  Lua `setDirection` with a diagonal now reaches the client as that diagonal (stock sent the server value, which the client
  read as another diagonal).

**Old clients and other looks.** A client without base patch 0160, and a look with 4 columns, draw a diagonal east or west:
what they drew before. The web cast viewer (`tools/cast_relay.py`) draws the client's diagonals east or west the same way
(`facing4`; it took the low two bits before, which turned north-east into north).

**Checked.** `tools/chaosfacing_test.cpp` (CI "Eight-direction facing", also under ASan and UBSan): the 8 steps, that a
diagonal step keeps the stock east or west direction and that a 4-column look draws what it drew before, `toward` on and
around the 0.4 line and for every offset up to 8 tiles, the wire bytes. `tools/cast_relay_test.py`: the four diagonal turns.
The chain 0001-0077 applies to the base source with `patch -p1 --fuzz=0`, 0 FAILED; `map.cpp`, `monster.cpp`, `game.cpp` and
`protocolgame.cpp` pass `g++ -std=c++20 -fsyntax-only -Wall` on the patched source with no new warning. Not built or linked,
not run on a live server: in game, confirm a monster of looks 3361-3363 walks and stands on the diagonals and turns to a
diagonal target, and that spells still point the four ways.

## Cursed Chest (`cursedchest.lua`, `cursedchest_core.lua`, `cursedchest_config.lua`; O244)

Owner request 2026-10-25: a chest that any monster can leave; opening it wakes 5 hordes one at a time; kill them all and the chest gives loot.

- **Chance.** One roll per kill for the corpse owner (EventCallback onDropLoot, index 5): normal 0.3%, magic 0.8%, rare 1.5%, legendary 2.2%, boss 3% (`spawn.chance`, at most 6%). The Ember Blessings level rule applies (a monster 10 levels under the player counts in full; at 75% / 60% / 45% of the player's level the chance is x1 / x0.5 / x0.2, below nothing). One chest at a time per player, 360 s cooldown, at most 25 on the server, 150 s before an unopened one crumbles.
- **No chest from:** summons, PvP places (battleground, arena, siege, PvP zones), any instance (`Chaos.instanceAt` / `inAnyInstance`, rift runs, areas the treasure goblin excludes), protection zones and houses, monsters under 40 max health, no stamina, `spawn.excludeNames` / `excludedAreas`, and monsters of other systems (treasure goblins, rifts, invasions, generated areas, this event's own).
- **One look (2026-10-27, pair 53; O280).** Owner request: one look. A chest is now always server item **32281** (client 38642),
  redrawn in place in pair 53 as K3, a 32 x 32 PixelLab chest of ours: 1 x 1, one phase, no animation (client/MANIFEST.md "Pair 53";
  `chest.itemIds = {32281}`). `chest.legacyItemIds = {32282, 32283}` are never drawn but still count as a cursed chest
  (`K.allChestIds`, `K.isChestId`), so a chest already on a map works. `install_cursed_chest.py` still installs all three nodes;
  only 32283 keeps FLAG_ANIMATION, and a node that an older run wrote with the flag on 32281 is rewritten without it. With 32281 not
  installed the chest is 12664 as before. The text below is the first version.
- **Looks (pair 43).** Each chest wears one of three own looks at random, server items **32281-32283** (client 38642-38644, art from PixelLab, client/MANIFEST.md "Cursed Chest looks"; `chest.itemIds`): A idles in 5 phases, B is a still, C chews in 8. Installed by `tools/install_cursed_chest.py` (step `cursedchest`, test `tools/install_cursed_chest_test.py`): items.otb copies of node 12664 (container, blocks, not moveable; A and C with FLAG_ANIMATION) and items.xml entries "cursed chest". An id the server does not have (`ItemType(id):getId() == 0`) is left out of the draw; with none installed the chest is 12664 as before. All four ids count as a cursed chest (`K.isChestId`); the use is found by action id and tile. **Item id block 32281-32299 is reserved for this set** (32251-32270 are orbs and potions; 32271-32280 stay free; 32284-32299 free). Ship pair 43 before the install step: older clients draw nothing for the new ids.
- **Chest.** The Sealed Coffer's item (12664, the fallback look, not moveable) with action id **47730** (free: 47720-47729 are the Harvest Portals), placed on the corpse's tile or the nearest free one. A dark loop (`CONST_ME_MORTAREA`, every third `CONST_ME_PURPLEENERGY`, 1.5 s) plays over it. The owner gets a text, a toast and a floating "CURSED CHEST" label (en and pt-BR). Only the owner and the owner's party may use it.
- **Event.** The use locks the chest. The opener and the party members within 9 tiles take part. The hordes (all in `event.hordes`) are 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 monsters (+35% per extra player, at most x2), health x1.0 / 1.1 / 1.2 / 1.35 / 1.5, damage x1.0 / 1.05 / 1.1 / 1.2 / 1.3; the share of magic and rare monsters grows from 0% to 70%, and horde 5 has a rare (70%) or legendary (30%) leader. The next horde comes 3 s after one is dead, or 45 s after the last came (not while 30 live). Progress "Horde 3/5" shows as a message, a toast and a label over the chest. Monsters are the killed monster and the non-boss monsters within 10 tiles (up to 4 kinds), padded from a themed list by level band; they are scaled to 90% of the opener's level (areagen's `levelScale`: health, damage; capped x3 / x2), paced like a hunt (`ChaosPace.apply`: experience as normal) and appear 2-5 tiles from the chest.
- **Fail.** 270 s total; or nobody who took part is alive, online and within 16 tiles for 10 s (warning after 4 s). The chest crumbles with no loot and the event's monsters are removed.
- **Win and loot.** After horde 5 the chest unseals for 120 s. Each participant (by creature id, recorded at the use) takes one roll, delivered to the backpack (inbox when full): gold = 3 minutes of hunting gold at the chest's level (the Respec table, same numbers as `gamble_config.lua`, checked by the test), 1 Orb of Upheaval (+1 per 400 levels, at most 4), 3% Orb of Fate, Rune Shards (4 + level/25, at most 30), 1 crafting orb, 1-2 gear pieces rolled at rarity floors Magic / Rare / Legendary (30 / 50 / 20) with the hunting level's rarity roll and item find x1.5, and the unique roll as a rare kill. A party's rolls are x1.0 / 0.75 / 0.6 / 0.5 / 0.45 by size.
- **Economy.** About 4-5 chests an hour of hunting (the cooldown caps 10). The gold is about 22% of an hour's, and the fights (about 3 minutes, monsters are husks) cost the same in lost corpse loot, so gold is neutral; orbs are about 5 an hour, against 24-33 from tier 15 rifts. No model config was changed; `store_model`, `roulette_model`, `progression_model`, `skill_model`, `pack_model` pass.
- **Abuse.** Event monsters are husks (`Monster:setDropLoot(false)`, as rift husks): no corpse loot, so no `onDropLoot` (no chest, blessing, Chaos roll) and they are never treasure goblins (artificial spawns). They are also tagged and refused by the chest roll. One claim per participant (the mark is set before the loot). Everything is checked on the server. Nothing is stored (no storage keys, no table): after a restart or `/reload` no monster remains and a chest item left on the map is unknown to the table and crumbles at its next use.
- **Outcome messages (O308).** Tester report: chests opened with no loot and no line. Every claim now ends with an event line and a toast (`MESSAGE_LOOT` is kept off the game screen by `game_lootscreen`, so it is not the only line): the loot list, or "held nothing for you". Each part of the roll (gold, orbs, shards, crafting orbs, gear, uniques) is its own step, so one error is logged and the rest is still given; a roll that breaks as a whole gives the claim mark back and tells the player to use the chest again. Backpack full: the inbox, else the ground at the player's feet, and the line says which. A won chest reminds players who have not claimed `event.remindSec` (30) before it crumbles and tells them when it does; a chest item that disappears mid-event fails the event with a line. An error in the use itself is a cancel message, not silence.
- **Staff.** `/cursedchest` makes a chest next to you; `/cursedchest roll <tier>, <level>[, <n>]` shows the chance.
- **Not done / assumptions.** Damage scale needs `ChaosAreaGen` (its hit hook); without it only health is scaled. Without `Monster:setDropLoot` the monsters would drop loot. Untested on a live server. No client part: server texts only. Tests: `tests/cursedchest_test.lua` (rules, state machine, loot against the gold model, and the glue on a mocked engine).

## Progress metrics (O253) (`metrics.lua`, `metrics_core.lua`, `metrics_config.lua`, `sql/chaos_progress_metrics.sql`, `tools/progress_metrics.py`)

Owner request 2026-10-26: see where players stop playing and where they die, so balance is tuned from real data. The admin app shows it (Painel > "Métricas dos jogadores" > "Atualizar métricas"; command `chaos-ctl.sh metrics [--json]`, read only).

- **What is measured.**
  - **Churn** per level band: characters whose last login is older than `churnDays` (14) against the active ones. One `GROUP BY` over `players` (`lastlogin`, `level`) at startup (after `churnDelaySeconds`, 60) and every 24 h; the answer is one row per band, written to the table as a snapshot (`churn` rows, replaced each time). A character that never logged in is left out. This counts characters, not accounts.
  - **Deaths** per area and per killer, each per level band (the level at the death). Area: the `Chaos.registerInstance` label when the character stood in an instance (rift, dungeon, arena, ...), else the nearest hunt of `data/lib/chaos_hunt_places.lua` (a hunt's arrival tile or a base hunt's destination) on the same floor within `areaRadius` (80) tiles, else "Outside hunts, floor N". Killer: the monster's name; a player is counted as "Player (PvP)", a player's summon as "Player's summon", no killer as "Environment or unknown". A player's name never reaches a counter. A defeat a mode cancels (arena, battleground, ...) is not a death and is not counted.
  - **First session** of a new character (first login ever, `getLastLoginSaved() == 0`): minutes from login to logout, in the buckets of `sessionBuckets` (5, 10, 20, ... 480, then "inf"). A crash loses that one count; a relog starts the rest of the play, not a second first session.
  - **Time to level**: when a character first reaches 10, 25, 50, 100 or 200 (`milestones`), its played minutes (`players.onlinetime` at the last logout plus this session) are added to a histogram bucket (`timeBuckets`, 5 minutes to 40 days). The report reads the median inside its bucket by linear interpolation (`progress_metrics.py`), so it is exact to the bucket width, finer in the first hours. A bit mask in player storage 7102830 (+0) records which milestones a character has had, so a level lost at a death and gained again counts once; at login every milestone below the character's level is marked without counting, so characters that existed before the install do not skew the medians. 7102831 - 7102833 are used by the funnel (O258, below); 7102834 - 7102839 free. Nine milestones since O258 (10, 25, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000; the first five keep their bits).
- **Who is left out.** Tester bots (`Chaos.isTester`, storage 7102900; in SQL `Chaos.notTesterSql`) and staff (`group_id` above `maxGroupId`, 1). They get no session state, so no counter at all.
- **Cost.** Counters are plain Lua table increments (one per death, one per milestone, one per new character's logout). Every `flushSeconds` (300) and at shutdown they are added to the table with one `INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE n = n + VALUES(n)` per 200 rows (`db.asyncQuery`; `db.query` at shutdown). `maxKeys` (4000) bounds the memory between flushes; a new key beyond it is dropped. The churn query runs once a day. The one SQL read in play is `onlinetime` of one character when it reaches a milestone.
- **Privacy.** The table `chaos_progress_metrics` (kind, k1, k2, n) holds only counters keyed by band, area, monster name, minute bucket or milestone. No character name, account id, IP or chat is read into a counter, stored, sent to the app or kept in a log; the churn query reads `level`, `lastlogin`, `group_id` and the tester storage of `players` and returns counts. The only per-character value is the milestone bit mask in the character's own storage, a game flag that no report reads. The table has no row per character, so the tester cleanup and account deletion have nothing to remove from it. Small numbers are suppressed: a count of 1 to 4 (a churn band or one side of it, an area, a monster, a first-session bucket, a milestone) is written `<5` in the text and as the string `"<5"` in the JSON, with its share and median left out (`null`) and the top band of a hidden death count empty; 0 stays 0 (`MIN_SHOWN` in `progress_metrics.py`, `minShown` in `metrics_config.lua`, `M.suppress`; the admin app shows `<5`).
- **Install.** `install_all.py` step `sql` creates the table from `sql/chaos_progress_metrics.sql` (idempotent, every `sql/*.sql` runs); the script also creates it at startup when it is missing. The scripts reach the server through the `files` step. Restart once. The admin app needs a new build for the card; the ssh command works without it. The table is empty until players play (counters after 5 minutes, the churn snapshot a minute after the start).
- **Report.** `chaos-ctl.sh metrics` prints text, `--json` one line (`ok`, `churn` {days, at, gone, active, bands}, `deathAreas` and `deathMonsters` (top 10: name, deaths, topBand), `firstSession`, `milestones` {level, medianMinutes, characters}); `{"ok": false, "error": "no-table" | "database"}` and exit 1 when it cannot read. The query is fixed and takes no argument.
- **Limits and assumptions.** `players.onlinetime` is assumed to be seconds saved at logout (the mentor system reads it the same way); the engine fork is not run here. Hunt areas are named by the nearest arrival tile, not by the hunt's real boundary, so a death far inside a large hunt may fall to "Outside hunts" (raise `areaRadius`; not measured on the real map). Changing `bands` later leaves old rows under their old labels. Deaths are counted when the character has a session, so a death during the first seconds of a login is counted and a `/reload` loses the open sessions' first-session counts. Not run on a live server.
- **Tests.** `tests/metrics_test.lua` (bands, buckets, counters and flush SQL, churn SQL and rows, areas, milestone mask, tester and staff exclusion, privacy of every statement, the engine file against a mocked engine), `tools/progress_metrics_test.py` (report, medians), `deploy/chaos_ctl_test.py` (the command, errors, refusals).

## Opcode input audit (O252) (`partyframes_core.lua`, `mentor.lua`, `nameplate_core.lua`, `monster_tiers.lua`)

Every committed handler of a client extended opcode was read against a client that sends arbitrary bytes at any time. The protocol layer (size cap, token bucket, JSON depth, one `xpcall` per handler) is O220; `tests/opcode_fuzz_test.lua` feeds every field of every handler. This round checked what the fuzz cannot: ids that must belong to the player, atomic money, and replies about other players.

Checked and found sound: shop and gifts (guarded `UPDATE` plus `ROW_COUNT`, refund on failure), bank and guild deposits (`Chaos.toInt`, save before credit), stash, market (guarded transaction, own-item checks), factions, crafting, professions, autosell, donations (`shop_payments.lua`: orders are read by account), item tooltip, loot filter, town portal, hideout, atlas, candlemarks, commands UI, admin (group check on every message), death recap, leaderboard, records, party finder, inspect (staff and ghosts answer "not found"). Website PHP (prepared statements, escaped output, CSRF tokens, admin gates, signed webhooks) and the deploy scripts (validated names, password on stdin) showed no injection path.

| Handler | Issue | Severity | Fixed | Test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| party frames invite | the reply told apart an online hidden player from an offline one | low | yes | `partyframes_test.lua` |
| mentor invite | same | low | yes | covered by the shared `canSeeCreature` rule, `mentor_test.lua` |
| name plate query | plates of players out of view, on another floor or hidden were answered for any creature id | low | yes | `nameplate_test.lua` (`N.mayQuery`) |
| monster bar query | distance check ignored the floor and sight | low | yes | `monster_tiers_test.lua` |
| Infinity Tower claim | the claimed mask is written after the items are given, the DB result is not checked | low | no | not reachable by a client request |
| admin throttle log | one log row per non-admin sender every 5 s | low | no | none |

**The base server's own handlers (second round).** The base tree is not in the repo, so this was read on a read-only copy of a base server (every Lua handler of an extended opcode: `onExtendedOpcode` creature events; 12 files). The engine layer of O220 already applies to them (16 KB cap, depth limit, 50 packets a second). Install step `opcodeinputs` (`tools/patch_base_opcode_inputs.py`, right after `jsonguards`, test `tools/patch_base_opcode_inputs_test.py`: synthetic excerpts in LF and CRLF, idempotence, refusal of unknown text, all anchors on a real base folder with `CHAOS_BASE_DATA`) fixes what a modified client could do. Each file gets the marker `-- Chaos: opcode input checks (patch_base_opcode_inputs.py)`; a file with other text is refused, nothing written.

| Base handler | Finding | Severity | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| store `gift_coins` (201) | the amount was any positive number: 1.5 coins left the sender as `- 1.5` and reached the recipient as `+ 1.5`, and the database rounds both sides to a whole number (net plus 1 coin per request, repeatable at the packet rate); the debit was not conditional | high | whole amounts 1 to 2,000,000,000; `UPDATE ... WHERE points >= amount` read back with `ROW_COUNT()`; the credit read back too and the debit given back when the recipient account has no points row |
| store (201), all actions | `data` that is a number made `data["category"]` a Lua error | low | `data` must be an object |
| highscores (73) | `entriesPerPage` and `page` unbounded: one request listed the whole players table (reply and query cost), and `1e999` or a fraction broke the `%d` of the query | medium | whole numbers, page 1-10000, 1-100 entries |
| highscores (73) | `vocations` went into the SQL text as typed (SQL injection) when `patch_base_classes.py` had not run, and a non-list value was a Lua error | high without the class step, low with it | only numbers reach the query (64 at most), a non-table is dropped |
| highscores (73) | unknown category was `error("invalid category")` (a log line per packet); a hidden (ghost) staff character was listed as online | low | falls back to experience; `online` uses `canSeeCreature` |
| inspect (107) | any online player was inspected by name from anywhere, a hidden (ghost) staff character too (presence leak) | low | "not found" for a player the asker cannot see; the name must be a string |
| character stats (106) | add or remove with an unknown stat name called `getCharacterStat(nil)` | low | unknown name returns |
| upgrades (181) | actions `points` and `upgrade_points` called `onUpgradesUpdatePoints`, which exists nowhere (a Lua error per packet); `data` that was not an object was indexed | low | calls `gameUpgradesUpdatePoints(player)`; `data` must be an object |
| tasks (92) | `start` without a number in `kills` was `math.max(nil, ...)` | low | non-number becomes the minimum, fractions floored |
| item fusion (67) | JSON decoded without `pcall`; `item` and the entries of `items` indexed without a type check | low | `pcall`, tables with a whole-number `clientId` |
| waystone device (202) | `teleport` opened the portal pads before taking the tier tablet, so a client naming a tablet it did not own got the pads | high | already fixed by `patch_waystone_hideout.py` part 2 (checked here, the pick is refused before any pad); not repeated |
| crafting (91) | `fetch` naming one of the script's own functions, wrong types in `data`, double crafts | medium | already fixed by `patch_base_crafting.py` and `patch_base_crafting_ui.py` v2 (checked here) |
| item fusion (67) | any 3 identical items the player holds (also cheap equipment, the server has no list) become an Upgrade Rune v1-v4 or the Upgrade and Rarity Remover; the client window may offer only some items, a modified client any id | medium | no: design decision of the owner (a list of fusable ids would change the feature); the three items are really taken (`removeItem` result checked) |
| party icons (136) | one request sends the party list (names, vocations, positions) to every member, so one packet costs the party size | low | no: members only, bounded by the packet rate |
| tier maps `wrap` (202) | the device chosen by `show` is kept as a Lua object until `wrap` or `teleport`, even when it was moved meanwhile | low | no: changes only the device's own look |
| reputation (99) | none: no field is read | none | none |

Checked and sound in the base handlers: upgrades `purchase` (price and level from the server's tables, points and item count checked before the level is raised, single game thread), store `buy` (offer, category and price compared with the server's tables), tasks `cancel`, tier maps `choice_apply` (ownership of the visual per storage), the base `extendedopcode.lua` (DB read throttled by `patch_base_stalls.py`).

Verification: `patch_base_json_guards.py`, the class, tester, crafting and hideout patches and then `patch_base_opcode_inputs.py` were run twice on a copy of the base data folder (second run: nothing to change); every changed file loads in LuaJIT (`luajit -bl`) and Lua 5.3 (`loadfile`); the highscores handler was run against a mocked engine with hostile requests under both interpreters (only numbers in the SQL, page and size clamped). Not run on a live server.

## Funnel metrics (O258) (`metrics.lua`, `metrics_core.lua`, `metrics_config.lua`, `tools/progress_metrics.py`)

Part of the retention pass (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-26-retention-design.md): measure where new characters leave, so the next steps (O259 - O261) are chosen from data. It extends the progress metrics (O253, section above); same table, same flush, same exclusions (tester bots and staff), no opcode, no new table. Admin app: Painel > card "Funil dos jogadores" (filled by the same "Atualizar métricas" button of the card above); `chaos-ctl.sh metrics [--json]`.

- **Milestones.** `milestones` is now 10, 25, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000 (nine bits in storage 7102830; the old five keep their bits). A character past a new milestone is marked silently at login (`maskAtLogin`). `timeBuckets` goes on to 180 days for the high levels (the last bucket "inf"; a median in the open bucket is a lower bound).
- **Return.** The first login ever (`getLastLoginSaved() == 0`) stores `day * 8` in storage 7102831 (day = whole days since the epoch in server time, `X.today`) and counts `cohort / YYYYMMDD`. A later login on calendar day first + 1, + 3 or + 7 (or later) counts `return / dN / <cohort YYYYMMDD>` once each; the flags live in the low 3 bits of the same value. A character from before the install has no value and is not counted. The report groups cohort days into weeks (Monday) and gives the share that came back; a share is shown only when the whole week is old enough for that day (Sunday + N <= today), so a young week does not look like churn.
- **First use.** `ChaosMetrics.firstUse(player, key)` counts `first / <system> / "<level band>|<played-minutes bucket>"` once per character and system (bit in storage 7102832). Played minutes = `players.onlinetime` (one read per session, at the first use) + the session so far. Hooks (`X.installHooks`, wrapped through `ChaosWrapChain` at startup and every minute, like `community.lua`):
  - dungeon: `ChaosSeasonJourney.emit(player, "dungeon_clears")`, which `dungeons.lua` `endRun` calls for every member of a clear;
  - rift, bounty, invasion, world boss: `ChaosLeaderboard.record` with the boards `rift` (a sealed rift), `bounty`, `defender` (a repelled wave) and `worldboss` (every share);
  - tower: `ChaosTower.recordRun` with at least one floor cleared; waystone: `ChaosWaystoneAtlas.beginRun` (the opener of a map); market: `ChaosMarket.list` or `.buy` that returned true; craft: `ChaosCrafting.apply` that succeeded (the item's owner);
  - pocket boss: a direct call in `pocketboss.lua` `success` (no public hook there);
  - party and guild have no hook: every `memberCheckSeconds` (60) the open sessions are looked at (a party with at least one other member, a guild). A character already in a guild at login is marked silently (a join during the session counts).
- **Where they stop.** Characters log out in town, so the last saved position says little. Instead the last hunt is remembered: on a kill of a monster (creature event `ChaosMetricsKill`, registered at login) by a counted character, at most once per `huntSeconds` (60), only when the tile is not a protection zone, the character is in no instance and a hunt's arrival tile (`data/lib/chaos_hunt_places.lua`, `places` and `base`, as `areaFor` reads them) is within `areaRadius`, the hunt is written to player storage 7102833 (`huntStorage`) when it differs from the cached value (the cache is read at login; one write per change, none per kill). The stored number is not an index of the places list (the installer orders plans by level band, so a new plan shifts every index) but `ChaosMetrics.stableId(place.id)`, a hash of the place's `id` string (`h * 33 + byte` modulo 1073741789, plus 1; the same in Lua 5.3 and LuaJIT). At startup the spots get their number; two ids that collide are logged and the second is not remembered. With the churn snapshot one grouped query joins `player_storage` (key 7102833) to the gone characters (last login older than `churnDays`, testers and staff out as before): a character with a hunt is grouped by that hunt, one without it by the 8-tile cell (`stopCell`) of `posx / posy / posz`, named by `areaFor` (nearest hunt within 80 tiles, else "Outside hunts, floor N"). A stored id no place has any more reads as "Hunt no longer listed" (`removedArea`). The answer is rows of `stop / <area> / <band>` (a snapshot: the old `stop` rows are deleted first). No row belongs to a character; the one storage value is a game flag of the character, like the other three.
- **Report.** `progress_metrics.py` gets `returns` (week, cohort, d1 / d3 / d7 and their shares), `firstUse` (system, characters, share of all characters = churn gone + active, median played minutes, most common level band) and `stops` (top 10 areas: gone, top band), in text and JSON; the milestones list is longer. Counts of 1 to 4 are `<5` (text) / `"<5"` (JSON) with their shares and medians left out; a hidden stop area also hides its band.
- **Limits.** Characters from before the install count their first use of a system at their current level and played time, which skews the first weeks; the cohort and return figures are clean (only characters created after the install). A first use inside one 60 s window that ends before the next check (a party that forms and disbands) is missed. The "where they stop" area is the last hunt a character killed in (a kill check at most every 60 s), so a character that never hunted, or left before the install, falls back to its last saved position, which is mostly the town; the hunt is the area nearest a place's arrival tile within `areaRadius`, so a kill far inside a large hunt is not remembered. Characters that last hunted before the install have no hunt until they log in again. `waystone` counts the first waystone opened by the character, not the first map cleared. Not run on a live server.
- **Tests.** `tests/metrics_test.lua` (day maths, return flags, first-use bits, stop rows and SQL, the wrapped hooks against fake systems, tester and staff left out), `tools/progress_metrics_test.py` (cohort weeks and maturity, first use, stops, suppression). The Android card is not built here (no SDK); CI `admin-app.yml` compiles it.

## The top menu reveals systems by level (O259) (`unlocks.lua`, `unlocks_core.lua`, `unlocks_config.lua`; client `client_chaos_topbar`)

**Why.** The top menu showed about 60 entries to a character that has just left the tutorial. The retention pass (design
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-26-retention-design.md`, section O259) shows a system in the menu when the character reaches
the level where that system opens, announces it, and hides the rest.

**One table.** `unlocks_config.lua` `entries`: `{key, level, menu, source, title, why, go}`. `menu` is the English text of the
entry in the client's top menu; `title` and the two `why` lines are English and pt-BR; `go = {open = <client module>}` (the
Go button runs the menu entry, which opens that module). The bits of the storages are by index: never reorder or insert,
add at the end (up to 30). Eleven entries now: Bounty Board 8, Market 8, Passive Tree 12 (the first point), Events 30 (invasions),
Arena 50, Rifts 100, Guild Siege 100, Infinity Tower 100, Dungeons 150, and (O262) Crafting Bench 20, Salvage 20 (the same gate), Pets 25.

**The level is the system's own.** Nothing here gates a system; each keeps its own check, and this table only says when the menu
shows it. `tests/unlocks_test.lua` has a reader per entry and fails when a level differs from the one the system enforces:

| Entry | Level from |
|---|---|
| bounty | `bounty_config.lua` `bands[1].min` |
| market | `market_config.lua` `minLevel` |
| passive | `Chaos.passive.startLevel + levelsPerPoint` (`chaos_constants.lua`: the first point is at level 12) |
| events | `invasion_config.lua` `minLevel` |
| arena | `arena_config.lua` `minLevel` |
| rifts | `rift_config.lua` `tiers[1].minLevel` |
| siege | `siege_config.lua` `minLevel` |
| tower | `infinitytower_run.lua` `cfg.minLevel` (read from the file text: the number is a local of the run file) |
| dungeons | `bossspawns_config.lua` `dungeons.defaults[1].level` (the first base dungeon, mirrors the base's own `Level`) |
| crafting | `data/lib/chaos_crafting.lua` `config.minLevel` (read from the file text: the lib needs the engine libs to load) |
| pets | `pets_config.lua` `minLevel` |

The test also checks that every entry has a reader and the other way round, that the menu text is an `entry('<text>', ...)` of
`chaos_topbar.lua`, that the Go module exists in `client/overlay/modules`, that both languages and two lines are there, and
that the changed level of a copy of the table is found. Systems of the menu without a gate the repo can read (Skills, Bank, Stash, ...) are not in the table and always show; add one
when its own config has a level.

**Two gates added for the menu (O262).** Crafting and Pets had no level check, so they showed from level 1. Now the systems
enforce one and the table follows: Crafting at level 20 (`ChaosCrafting.config.minLevel` in `data/lib/chaos_crafting.lua`,
rule `ChaosCrafting.levelGate(level)`) and Pets at level 25 (`pets_config.lua` `minLevel`, rule `ChaosPetsCore.levelGate`). Crafting:
below the level the bench opcode (232: open, select, apply, gem, clear and Salvage) answers nothing but a line on `open`
("Crafting opens at level 20.") and the orbs' "Use with" is refused with the same line (a plain use of an orb still explains
how it works); the tutorial island's orb station (a level 1 character, `ChaosNewPlayer.onTutorial`) is let through. Salvage has
its own top menu entry (`salvage`, the same level). Pets: below the level the opcode answers nothing but a line on `open` ("Pets open at level 25."), no pet is
called out at login (a pet a character already owns is kept and comes back at the level), the staff `/pet` command is not
gated. Both lines are in en and pt-BR (`i18n_strings.lua`). Bank and the Supply Stash are NOT gated on purpose: a new
character needs them from level 1, so they stay out of the table and always show.

**What the server does.**
- Login: a character with no storage yet gets masks: above `quietAbove` (20) every entry of its level is unlocked and seen,
  silently; at or below it nothing, so a new character at level 8 is told about the Bounty Board and the Market (20 s after the
  login, then 75 s apart). A returning character gets entries added to the table since silently when it already passed
  their level (`known`, like the first hour's `hintsKnown`).
- `run` (login after `delayMs` 20 s, and every level change, up or down): the entries at or below the level and not unlocked
  yet, lowest level first; one per run (`pace.perRun`), the rest after `pace.gapMs` 75 s (the first hour's pace, checked by the
  test). The bit is set first, then `new` and `state` go out. A level lost never takes an entry back.
- `state` carries the whole table (the client keeps none), the unlocked and seen keys and the `next` entry: the lowest level
  above the character's that is not unlocked. Staff (group 4 and up) and a switched-off module get `all = true`.
- `seen {key}` sets the seen bit of an unlocked entry; the badge goes. `hello` answers with `state` (rate limited 1 s).

**Opcode 115** is free: not in the reference server's list ("Opcode collision check"), not one of the base client's `ExtendedIds`,
not a `ChaosOpcodes` value and not named by any client module other than `client_chaos_topbar` (the test checks all four).
**Storages 7103000-7103009** are used by no other file (the test scans `data/scripts/chaos` and `data/lib`).

**Client** (`client/MANIFEST.md`, `client_chaos_topbar`): a menu entry whose key the table names is hidden until unlocked; the next
one shows grey with a padlock and "Level N" and says "Unlocks at level N" when clicked; its hotkey (Alt+J, Alt+E, Alt+P) says the
same instead of opening. On `new`: a big text "New: <title>!", a gold "New" badge on the entry (and a gold category button)
until it is opened, and a small window with the two lines, Go and Close. The option "Show the whole menu" (System > Options >
Interface, client base patch `0154`, `showWholeMenu`, off by default, kept in g_settings by client_settings like the other options)
turns the filter off. Without the patch the filter stays on.

**Assumptions / not run.** Nothing here ran on a live server or in a client. The base patch `0154` applies in order on the
clean base client (`client/tools/assemble_client.sh`, all patches). The Go button only opens the window (`go.open`); a map mark
(`go.mark` of the design) is not built: every entry so far is a window, not a place.

## The Weekly Chest, group nudges and a visible party bonus (O261) (`weeklychest.lua`, `weeklychest_core.lua`, `weeklychest_config.lua`, `groupnudge.lua`, `groupnudge_core.lua`, `groupnudge_config.lua`, client `game_weeklychest`)

Retention pass of 2026-10-26 (design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-26-retention-design.md`, part 4): a reason to come back every week, and a push towards each other. Nothing here is run on a live server or in a client.

### The Weekly Chest

- **Six activities, once each per week:** a dungeon (`ChaosSeasonJourney.emit` `dungeon_clears`), a rift (`ChaosAchievements.progress` `rift_runs`), a waystone run (`ChaosWaystoneTiers.startRun`, the run's opener `mods.opener`), an Infinity Tower floor (`ChaosTower.recordRun` with a floor cleared), a world boss or an invasion share (`wb_kills`, `invasion_fought`) and a bounty contract (`bounty_done`). The hooks go through `ChaosWrapChain` at startup and again every minute, as the Ember Cache does. The week is the bounty board's (`ChaosBounty.week`, Monday at `resetHour` 6; the test compares both).
- **4 of 6 open the chest, all unlocked ones add a bonus roll.** The chest is given at once (gold to the bank, orbs to the backpack, else the inbox) with a toast, once per week; the bonus roll picks one of three options. An activity the character cannot do yet is left out: each locked one takes one off the 4, but never below 2, and the bonus roll needs more activities open than the chest asks (`K.targets`). An activity the character did anyway counts as open, so a wrong gate never hides progress. Testers and staff bots earn nothing.
- **The gates** (`weeklychest_config.lua` `activities`): dungeon 150 (`bossspawns_config.lua` `dungeons.defaults[1].level`), rift 100 (`rift_config.lua` `tiers[1].minLevel`), waystone 1100 (`waystone_tiers_config.lua` `tiers[1].level`), tower 100, world boss or invasion 30 (`invasion_config.lua` `minLevel`; the world boss needs `Chaos.worldBoss.minLevel` 300), bounty 8 (first band of `bounty_config.lua`). This is a local table that mirrors each system's own gate; `tests/weeklychest_test.lua` reads rift, bounty, waystone and invasion configs and fails when one differs, and checks dungeon, rift and tower against the top menu's unlock table (`unlocks_config.lua`, O259).
- **Rewards by level band** (the bounty board's six bands): `hours` of hunting gold (the Ember Cache's `income` table, one source) plus orbs (counts x 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3 by band). Chest: 1.0 h of gold, 2 Orbs of Upheaval, 1 Awakening, 1 Whetstone, 1 Tempering. Bonus roll, one of: 0.8 h of gold; 0.3 h + Orb of Fate + Orb of Tempering; 0.4 h + Orb of Sockets. Orb values in hours are the Ember Cache's (2, 2, 2, 5, 6, 10 minutes). Limits checked by `tests/weeklychest_test.lua` at every band: chest at most 2.0 h, one bonus option at most 1.0 h, both at most 3.0 h, under the Ember Cache's top weekly milestone (3.95 h). The store and roulette models (`tools/store_model.lua`, `tools/roulette_model.lua --check`) do not read this table and stay green: the chest pays no coin or token value, and its gold is the same hours-of-income unit as the Ember Cache's.
- **Protocol (opcode 117, `ChaosOpcodes.weeklyChest`):** client -> server `open` / `close` / `get`; server -> client `state {open?, endsIn, acts = [{k, done, open, lv}], got, need, bonusNeed, open, chest = {given, gold, it}, bonus = {given, lo, hi}, chests}`. 117 is not in the reference server's list, not one of the base client's `ExtendedIds` and not named by another module (the test checks it).
- **Storages 7103020 - 7103029:** +0 the week, +1 the activities done (bit mask in the order of `activities`), +2 the chest was given, +3 the bonus roll was given, +4 chests given in all. The state is written before anything is given.
- **Client:** Adventure > Weekly Chest, `game_weeklychest` (client/MANIFEST.md). Tests: `tests/weeklychest_test.lua`, `weeklyview_test.lua`.

### The group nudge

Entering a dungeon (`dungeons.lua`, after `startRun`) or a rift (`rift.lua`, after `enter`) alone calls `ChaosGroupNudge.onEnter(player, "dungeon" | "rift", detail)` behind a guard. `groupnudge_core.lua` counts the players that look for a group for that content in the Party Finder: the people (leader, party, accepted members) of open listings that cover it (a rift listing's tier range, a dungeon listing's target or any dungeon) and the quick-join queue entries for that activity; the player's own listing and party, closed or full listings and other realms do not count. If the count is above zero and the player has not been nudged in the last 10 minutes (`cooldownSeconds`, in memory, spent only when there is something to say), the server sends `nudge {text, a, n}` on the Party Finder opcode 208 ("2 players look for a group for Rift T5.") and the client adds a [Join] to the toast; a click opens the Party Finder on the browse tab. A player already in a party is not nudged. Tests: `tests/groupnudge_test.lua`.

### The party bonus on the party frame

`party_xp_core.lua` `bonusPercent(lines)` is the stock share rule (`Party:onShareExperience`, the class lines counted by `tools/patch_base_classes.py`): +20% for one class line, else n x (5 (n - 1) + 10) percent for n lines, at most 5 lines (+150%). `partyframes.lua` adds `xp {p, on}` to the party state (`on` 1 the share works, 2 the leader switched it on but a member breaks its rules, 0 not switched on) and the frame header shows "+20% XP" in green, "XP share broken" in red or "XP share off" in grey, with a tooltip. The state signature includes it, so a change is sent at once. Tests: `tests/party_xp_test.lua`, `tests/partyframes_test.lua`, client `partymath_test.lua`.

## Early spike, pity, drop feed and personal records (O260) (`retention_loot.lua`, `retention_loot_core.lua`, `retention_loot_config.lua`, `tools/patch_drops_channel.py`, client `game_dropfeed`)

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-26-retention-design.md`. Why: the first hours had no moment where the character got
stronger by luck, a long dry streak had no end, a big drop was told to the people on the same screen only, and a record of
your own was not kept. Rules in `retention_loot_core.lua` (tests `tests/retention_loot_test.lua`), numbers in
`retention_loot_config.lua`, the engine side in `retention_loot.lua`. `loot.lua` calls it from `processKill` three times
(begin, once per gear drop, finish), each call in a `pcall`: a failure never costs a kill its loot.

- **First unique.** The character's 150th kill (every kill that gives it a corpse, bosses too) adds a leveling unique of its
  class to that corpse, once per character, up to level 60, never for tester bots. It is in the corpse, so the loot beam,
  the unique sound and the autoloot of the loot filter treat it like any unique drop. The candidates per class are
  `firstUnique.byClass` (ascensions use their line, `lineOf`; an unknown class uses `default`): the one with the highest level
  requirement the character already meets, else the lowest. The test checks that every candidate is a real unique of
  `chaos_unique_items.lua` and that every class has some. Storage 7103010.
- **Pity.** A hidden counter, storage 7103011, of the normal hunting kills in a row without a gear drop of Rare or better (a
  unique counts as one). At 400 the next gear drop of Magic or better is raised one rarity (Magic to Rare, Rare to Legendary;
  not above Legendary) and the counter starts again. Boss kills, summons, rifts, waystone maps, pocket bosses and testers
  neither count nor are raised. The raise is made in step 2 of `processKill` through `ChaosRetentionLoot.adjustRarity`; the
  counter is written in `finish` from the corpse as it is then (forged items keep their rarity as text until a tick later,
  `ChaosCrafting.rarityOf` reads both).
- **Drop feed.** A legendary or divine gear drop or a unique posts `Name (Lv N) found [Item]{...}!` in the channel **Drops**
  (id 21) and in the Default tab of everyone online, in each player's language (`i18n_strings.lua`). The item is an item link
  (`ChaosItemLink.linkFor`, "Item links in chat"): hover shows the tooltip for 10 minutes. The best find of a kill posts
  (unique over divine over legendary). Limits: one line per character per `feed.perCharSeconds` (60) and
  `feed.maxPerMinute` (12) server-wide; the rest is dropped silently. Staff and testers post nothing. The local broadcast
  of `loot.lua` (`broadcastText`) stays. The Discord relay gets the same line (`discord.lua` `X.drop`, event `drop`, channel
  key `drops`, 6 a minute; `website/overlay/plugins/chaos/discord_lib.php`). The first unique of the gift never posts.
- **Drops channel.** `tools/patch_drops_channel.py` (install step `events`, idempotent) adds
  `<channel id="21" name="Drops" public="1" script="drops.lua" />` to `data/chatchannels/chatchannels.xml` (a taken id or name
  is an error, nothing is written) and writes `data/chatchannels/scripts/drops.lua`, a read-only channel whose join and leave
  tell `ChaosRetentionLoot`. Test `tools/patch_drops_channel_test.py` (also checks the id and name against the config).
- **Client option.** System > Drop Feed (`game_dropfeed`): Off, Unique and Divine only, or Legendary and better (default).
  The client keeps it in its settings and sends `feedopt {mode}` on the records opcode 229 at login and on a change; the
  server keeps it in memory per player and filters the lines (`C.shown`). Until the client has sent one, every kind shows.
- **Personal records.** `records.lua` and `records_core.lua` got two hidden personal boards, `drop_rarity` (rank 1..7) and
  `drop_value` (NPC sell price), category `loot` (`records_config.lua`). A personal board keeps the all-time value of the
  character only: no weekly top 3, no title, no broadcast, no website publish, no realm first. `ChaosRecords.personalBests`
  reads a character's all-time rows once per `personal.cacheSeconds` (600). `ChaosRecords.submit` sends "New record: <what>:
  <value> (was <old>)" to a member whose own best of a board improved (any board: a boss time, a Tower floor, a rift tier
  too) and updates the cache. `K.personalRows` lists the best drop rarity, the best drop value, the highest Tower floor, the
  highest rift tier and the fastest boss kills (at most 12, the fastest party size of each boss). Shown in Inspect (a
  `records` packet after the result; the Records button next to Passive Tree swaps the equipment for the rows) and in the
  Leaderboards Records view as the tab **My Records** (`rmine` on opcode 229, `R.sendMine`).
- **Opcodes.** None new: the feed is chat and text messages, `feedopt` and `rmine` ride on 229, `records` on 240.
- **Install.** `install_all.py --only events` (the channel); the Lua files come with the `scripts` step.
- **Assumptions, not run on a live server.** `Player:sendChannelMessage` and the channel id 21 are free on the base copy; a
  public channel with a script is listed to every player; the base `onDropLoot` pass finishes before `loot.lua` (it does, it
  is index 1). The item value of the record is `ChaosItemPrices.sellPrice` (0 when the file is not loaded).

## Brand runes add damage (O277)

Owner 2026-10-27 (pt-BR): "em vez de ser 30% se torna x elemento, faça que os 30% seja adicionais de tal elemento".
The five brand supports (Emberbrand fire, Rimebrand ice, Dawnbrand holy, Gravebrand death, Stormbrand energy; 20/30/40/50/60%
by rune level) no longer convert. Before: X% of the spell's primary damage moved to the element (the total stayed). Now: the
hit stays whole and X% of it is added on top as extra damage of the element ("X% of the spell's damage is added as extra ice
damage"). Same percentages.
- Core: `ChaosSupports.addElement` (`data/lib/chaos_supports.lua`; `convert` stays for the spell cards); the event is `supports.lua` `ChaosSupportsHit`.
- The extra goes into the hit's secondary slot (or onto the primary part when that already is the element), in the same combat
  event: leech, crit and on-hit procs see one hit, nothing fires twice. Only when the secondary slot holds another element is the
  extra dealt as a hit of its own from the flush (guarded like Echo, so it can trigger nothing).
- Resistance: the extra part is X% of the hit with the primary element's resistance taken out and the brand element's put in.
- Brands add up (the window still allows one per spell); each is a share of the original hit. Keen Edge crits both parts.
- Monsters only: against a player nothing is added (PvP damage does not rise).
- Balance: a buff of +X% of the spell's damage before resistances (+20 to +60%), on a rune that dropped as a total-neutral
  rune. No balance model reads support values (store, roulette, weapon_power, skill, progression checks pass unchanged).
  Echo at Mythic is about +17.5% expected, so Mythic brands are now the best damage rune; watch it and cut `values` in
  `chaos_supports_config.lua` if hunts speed up.
- Texts changed (item description, tooltip, supports window, codex, wiki): `pt_br.lua` keys, `gen_codex_data.lua`,
  `gen_wiki_data.lua` regenerated. Tests: `tests/supports_test.lua`.

## Client pair guard (`config.lua` `chaosClientPair`, `tools/client_pair.py`, `chaos-ctl.sh client-pair`)

Why: the owner's admin app "Update" runs every `install_all.py` step. Steps that write `items.otb` nodes pointing at client
ids of a sprite pair the players' client does not have yet (the pair ships only when the owner publishes the client update;
the pair archive is owner-gated on `windows-assets`) would make those items show as unknown things. Before the guard only this
README warned.

* **The record.** One line in the server's `config.lua`: `chaosClientPair = 54`, the number of the sprite pair
  (client/MANIFEST.md "Pair N") that the SHIPPED client is on. The engine ignores the key (as `castPort` on an older engine).
  `update-apply` and `install_all.py` keep `config.lua`, so the number stays. A missing key counts as "unknown": every guarded
  row is held back until the owner sets it.
* **The rule.** A step that needs pair N reads the record (`client_pair.allows(data_dir, N, label)`; the tools get the data
  folder, `config.lua` is its parent's). Record lower than N or missing: the rows are skipped, `install_all.py` prints a
  warning line (`WARNING: ... skipped, it needs client pair N or newer and the recorded pair is ...`, always shown in the
  report), the step succeeds. Record N or more: the step runs as normal. Skipping never removes anything an install already has;
  a second run changes nothing in either state. Guarded today:

  | Step | Needs | Below it |
  |---|---|---|
  | `pickups` (health / mana globe, ember portal) | 55 | the whole step is skipped (the globes and the ember are not installed; `pickups.lua` already does nothing for a missing item) |
  | `fistweapons`, rows of mode `repoint` (claws and uniques 40003-40012) | 56 | written with the donor looks (client id = server id - 12000, as before pair 56): the items keep working on a pair 54 / 55 client |
  | `fistweapons`, rows of mode `new4` (48409-48411) | 56 | not installed (no node, no `items.xml` entry, no shop, no equip entry) |
  | `weapons800` (the 34 weapons above level 800, "Weapons above level 800") | 56 | the whole step is skipped |

  The Lua side needs no switch: the loot layers (`fist_weapons.lua`, `class_loot.lua`, `weapons800.lua`) add a row only when
  `ItemType(id)` exists, and the scaled class roll (`loot.lua` `classWeapons`) drops an id the server has no item for.
* **Setting it (owner).** When a client update with a new pair is published, record the pair, then run the update:
  1. **Admin app** (docs/ADMIN_APP.md): tab Comandos > card "Par do cliente" > field "Par" > **Ver** (`client-pair show`) /
     **Gravar** (`client-pair set N`, asks to confirm), the card pattern of "Taxa de XP".
  2. **Shell fallback** on the VPS: `chaos-ctl.sh client-pair set 56` (`client-pair show` prints `chaosClientPair=56` or
     `chaosClientPair=missing`); a number lower than the record is refused. Without the kit: `python3 -I
     server/tools/client_pair.py set SERVER_DIR 56 [--force] [--dry-run]`.
  3. Then the admin app **Update** (or `install_all.py`) installs the held rows; no restart is needed for the record itself.
* **Adding a guard.** A new step with items of pair N: `import client_pair`, `ok, why = client_pair.allows(data_dir, N, 'step')`,
  print `why`, return 0 when not `ok`; in `install_all.py` run the tool with `tool_result_warn` so the warning reaches the
  report; add the row to the table above and to `tools/client_pair_test.py`.
* Tests: `tools/client_pair_test.py` (key read / written, lowering refused, a missing or low record skips and writes nothing, a
  high enough one installs, a second run changes nothing; pickups and fist weapons end to end on a synthetic server),
  `deploy/chaos_ctl_test.py` (the `client-pair` command and its refusals), `tools/install_pickups_test.py`.

## Base raid fixes (`tools/patch_base_raids.py`, install step `baseraids`)

Owner log 2026-10-28: `[Error] Raids: Cant create monster Orc Armor`. `data/raids/thais/orcs.xml` has three `<singlespawn>` lines
for "Orc Helmet", "Orc Shield" and "Orc Armor". No monsters.xml line and no Lua monster has those names (base or installed), so
the engine refuses each spawn (the first failing event is the one the log shows). `patch_base_raids.py DATA_DIR [--dry-run]`
points the three at the "Orc Leader" (registered in the base), only while the old name is not a known monster and the new one is;
with no known replacement the line becomes an XML comment. Idempotent; `FIXES` in the tool is the place for more. Test:
`tools/patch_base_raids_test.py` (CI). Install: Update in the admin app (all steps), or `install_all.py SERVER_DIR --only
baseraids`. A scan of all 90 base raid files against every registered monster (monsters.xml, Lua monsters, our installs, the
monster renames) found five more unknown names, now in `FIXES`: "Orc Sambackpack" (a `<monster>` line of an area spawn in
`venore/orc_backpack.xml`) -> Orc Warlord, "White Pale" -> Spectre, "Chayenne" -> Dragon Lord, "Ocyakao" -> Yeti, "Hirintror" ->
Frost Dragon. Targets are base monsters of the same theme and about the same health that `monsternames` does not rename. The
raid files name no items, so no item errors can come from them.

## Unique loot names (`tools/install_decor49_items.py`, `tools/install_owner_decor.py`)

Owner log 2026-10-28: `Non-unique loot item "witch broom"` / `"witch hat"`, then `Cant load loot. witch.xml`: the Witch had no loot at
all. Monster XML names loot by item name, and the engine refuses a name that more than one item has. The stock items 10569 and 10570
are "witch broom" and "witch hat"; the pair 49 decoration manifest (`decor49_items.csv`, written by `gen_decor49.py`) named items
43171 and 43174 the same. The pair 33 kit had hit the same problem once (`witch_hat` -> "crooked witch hat"). Two more clashes of
the same kind were found by comparing every manifest name with the loot names of the monster files: the decor49 "Pumpkin" (43194,
loot of the Mutated Pumpkin) and the owner art "prickly pear" (36977, loot of the Ogre Shaman); they would have broken those two
loots the same way. The installs now rename them: `RENAMES` in `install_decor49_items.py` ("Cursed witch broom", "Cursed witch hat",
"Cursed pumpkin") and in `install_owner_decor.py` ("prickly pear cactus"; `data/lib/chaos_owner_decor.lua` regenerated). The art
sheets and manifests keep their names. Tests: `install_decor49_items_test.py` (the renames, and no manifest name equals a loot name
of our monsters), `install_owner_decor_test.py`. Owner, VPS: Update in the admin app, or `install_all.py SERVER_DIR --only
decor49items,ownerdecor` and a restart; the blocks in items.xml are rewritten, no SQL, no client change (the names show in the
client tooltips only).

## Item tooltips: who may use it (O307)

The engine's vocation string hides an ascended class whose base class is listed, so a crossbow read "For rangers" while
the Beastmaster (a bow class) cannot wield it. `T.vocationText` in `item_tooltip_core.lua` expands a listed Ranger or
Warrior into the classes of the install rule (`add_vocations.py`): Ranger, Deadeye, and the Beastmaster only for bows,
arrows and non-weapon gear; Warrior, Juggernaut, and the Berserker only for two-handed swords, axes, clubs and non-hand
gear. Unknown names stay as the engine wrote them. Test: `tests/item_tooltip_test.lua`. Client spell lists: a Chaos
spell matches the exact server vocation ids (`ChaosSpellFix.allowsVocation`); `tools/ci/check_rotation_kit.py` compares
spelldata.lua with the server spell XML.
